nodes.proof: Proof. Given a minimizing line \( \lambda  : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow  X \) , define \( {\lambda }_{ \pm  } : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  X \) by \( {\lambda }_{ + }\left( t\right)  = \lambda \left( t\right) \) and \( {\lambda }_{ - }\left( t\right)  = \lambda \left( {-t}\right) \) . Then we have the Busemann functions \( {B}_{ + } = {B}_{{\lambda }_{ + }} \) and \( {B}_{ - } = {B}_{{\lambda }_{ - }} \) . Proposition 2.3 applies to both \( {B}_{ + } \) and \( {B}_{ - } \) and shows that \( \Delta \left( {{B}_{ + } + {B}_{ - }}\right)  \leq  0 \) . On the other hand, using the fact that \( \lambda \) is distance minimizing, we see that for any \( s, t > 0 \) and for any \( x \in  M \) we have \( d\left( {x,\lambda \left( t\right) }\right)  + d\left( {x,\lambda \left( {-s}\right) }\right)  \geq  s + t \) , and hence \( {B}_{ + }\left( x\right)  + {B}_{ - }\left( x\right)  \geq  0 \) . Clearly, \( {B}_{ + }\left( x\right)  + {B}_{ - }\left( x\right)  = 0 \) for any \( x \) in the image of \( \lambda \) . Thus, the function \( {B}_{ + } + {B}_{ - } \) is everywhere \( \geq  0 \) , vanishes at least at one point and satisfies \( \Delta \left( {{B}_{ + } + {B}_{ - }}\right)  \leq  0 \) in the weak sense. This is exactly the set-up for the maximum principle, cf. [57], p. 279.

DEFINITION 2.16. Suppose that we have a fixed metric \( {g}_{0} \) on a manifold \( M \) and an open submanifold \( X \subset  M \) . We say that another metric \( g \) on \( X \) is within \( \epsilon \) of \( {\left. {g}_{0}\right| }_{X} \) in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  1/\epsilon \right\rbrack  } \) -topology if, setting \( k = \left\lbrack  {1/\epsilon }\right\rbrack \) we have

(2.1)

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  X}}\left( {{\left| g\left( x\right)  - {g}_{0}\left( x\right) \right| }_{{g}_{0}}^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\ell  = 1}}^{k}{\left| {\nabla }_{{g}_{0}}^{\ell }g\left( x\right) \right| }_{{g}_{0}}^{2}}\right)  < {\epsilon }^{2},
\]

where the covariant derivative \( {\nabla }_{{g}_{0}}^{\ell } \) is the Levi-Civita connection of \( {g}_{0} \) and norms are the pointwise \( {g}_{0} \) -norms on

\[
{\operatorname{Sym}}^{2}{T}^{ * }M \otimes  \underset{\ell  - \text{ times }}{\underbrace{{T}^{ * }M \otimes  \cdots  \otimes  {T}^{ * }M}}.
\]

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  X \times  I}}\left( {{\left| g\left( x, t\right)  - {g}_{0}\left( x, t\right) \right| }_{{g}_{0}\left( t\right) }^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\ell  = 1}}^{k}{\left| {\nabla }_{{g}_{0}}^{\ell }g\left( x, t\right) \right| }_{{g}_{0}}^{2}}\right)  < {\epsilon }^{2}.
\]

nodes.content: REMARK 2.17. Notice that if we view a one-parameter family of metrics \( g\left( t\right) \) as a curve in the space of metrics on \( X \) with the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  1/\epsilon \right\rbrack  } \) -topology then this is the statement that the two paths are pointwise within \( \epsilon \) of each other. It says nothing about the derivatives of the paths, or equivalently about the time derivatives of the metrics and of their covariant derivatives. We will always be considering paths of metrics satisfying the Ricci flow equation. In this context two one-parameter families of metrics that are close in the \( {C}^{2k} \) -topology exactly when the \( {r}^{th} \) time derivatives of the \( {s}^{th} \) - covariant derivatives are close for all \( r, s \) with \( s + {2r} \leq  {2k} \) .

DEFINITION 2.18. Let \( \left( {N, g}\right) \) be a Riemannian manifold and \( x \in  N \) a point. Then an \( \epsilon \) -neck structure on \( \left( {N, g}\right) \) centered at \( x \) consists of a diffeomorphism

\[
\varphi  : {S}^{2} \times  \left( {-{\epsilon }^{-1},{\epsilon }^{-1}}\right)  \rightarrow  N,
\]

with \( x \in  \varphi \left( {{S}^{2}\times \{ 0\} }\right) \) , such that the metric \( R\left( x\right) {\varphi }^{ * }g \) is within \( \epsilon \) in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  1/\epsilon \right\rbrack  } \) -topology of the product of the usual Euclidean metric on the open interval with the metric of constant Gaussian curvature \( 1/2 \) on \( {S}^{2} \) . We also use the terminology \( N \) is an \( \epsilon \) -neck centered at \( x \) . The image under \( \varphi \) of the family of submanifolds \( {S}^{2} \times  \{ t\} \) is called the family of 2-spheres of the \( \epsilon \) -neck. The submanifold \( \varphi \left( {{S}^{2}\times \{ 0\} }\right) \) is called the central 2-sphere of the \( \epsilon \) -neck structure. We denote by \( {s}_{N} : N \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) the composition \( {p}_{2} \circ  {\varphi }^{-1} \) , where \( {p}_{2} \) is the projection of \( {S}^{2} \times  \left( {-{\epsilon }^{-1},{\epsilon }^{-1}}\right) \) to the second factor. There is also the vector field \( \partial /\partial {s}_{N} \) on \( N \) which is \( {\varphi }_{ * } \) of the standard vector field in the interval-direction of the product. We also use the terminology of the plus and minus end of the \( \epsilon \) -neck in the obvious sense. The opposite (or reversed) \( \epsilon \) -neck structure is the one obtained by composing the structure map with \( {\operatorname{Id}}_{{S}^{2}} \times   - 1 \) . We define the positive half of the neck to be the region \( {s}_{N}^{-1}\left( {0,{\epsilon }^{-1}}\right) \) and the negative half to be the region \( {s}_{N}^{-1}\left( {-{\epsilon }^{-1},0}\right) \) . For any other fraction, e.g., the left-hand three-quarters, the right-hand one-quarter, there are analogous notions, all measured with respect to \( {s}_{N} : N \rightarrow  \left( {-{\epsilon }^{-1},{\epsilon }^{-1}}\right) \) . We also use the terminology the middle one-half, or middle one-third of the \( \epsilon \) -neck; again these regions have their obvious meaning when measured via \( {s}_{N} \) .

An \( \epsilon \) -neck in a Riemannian manifold \( X \) is a codimension-zero submani-fold \( N \) and an \( \epsilon \) -structure on \( N \) centered at some point \( x \in  N \) .

The scale of an \( \epsilon \) -neck \( N \) centered at \( x \) is \( R{\left( x\right) }^{-1/2} \) . The scale of \( N \) is denoted \( {r}_{N} \) . Intuitively, this is a measure of the radius of the cross-sectional \( {S}^{2} \) in the neck. In fact, the extrinsic diameter of any \( {S}^{2} \) factor in the neck is close to \( \sqrt{2}\pi {r}_{N} \) . See FIG. 1 in the introduction.

\]

in the sense of forward difference quotients. Suppose that \( G\left( t\right) \) satisfies the differential equation

\[

nodes.label: Definition 3.1

nodes.content:
DEFINITION 3.1. The Ricci flow equation is the following evolution equation for a Riemannian metric:

(3.1)

\[
\frac{\partial g}{\partial t} =  - 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( g\right) .
\]

A solution to this equation (or a Ricci flow) is a one-parameter family of metrics \( g\left( t\right) \) , parameterized by \( t \) in a non-degenerate interval \( I \) , on a smooth manifold \( M \) satisfying Equation (3.1). If \( I \) has an initial point \( {t}_{0} \) , then \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) is called the initial condition of or the initial metric for the Ricci flow (or of the solution).

nodes.content:
DEFINITION 3.2. We introduce some notation that will be used throughout. Given a Ricci flow \( \left( {{M}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) defined for \( t \) contained in an interval \( I \) , then the space-time for this flow is \( M \times  I \) . The \( t \) time-slice of space-time is the Riemannian manifold \( M \times  \{ t\} \) with the Riemannian metric \( g\left( t\right) \) . Let \( \mathcal{H}T\left( {M \times  I}\right) \) be the horizontal tangent bundle of space-time, i.e., the bundle of tangent vectors to the time-slices. It is a smooth, rank- \( n \) subbundle of the tangent bundle of space-time. The evolving metric \( g\left( t\right) \) is then a smooth section of \( {\operatorname{Sym}}^{2}\mathcal{H}{T}^{ * }\left( {M \times  I}\right) \) . We denote points of space-time as pairs \( \left( {p, t}\right) \) .

Given \( \left( {p, t}\right) \) and any \( r > 0 \) we denote by \( B\left( {p, t, r}\right) \) the metric ball of radius \( r \) centered at \( \left( {p, t}\right) \) in the \( t \) time-slice. For any \( {\Delta t} > 0 \) for which \( \left\lbrack  {t - {\Delta t}, t}\right\rbrack   \subset  I \) , we define the backwards parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {x, t, r, - {\Delta t}}\right) \) to be the product \( B\left( {x, t, r}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {t - {\Delta t}, t}\right\rbrack \) in space-time. Notice that the intersection of \( P\left( {x, t, r, - {\Delta t}}\right) \) with a time-slice other than the \( t \) time-slice need not be a metric ball in that time-slice. There is the corresponding notion of a forward parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {x, t, r,{\Delta t}}\right) \) provided that \( \left\lbrack  {t, t + {\Delta t}}\right\rbrack   \subset  I \) .

nodes.content: EXAMPLE 3.3. The standard metric on each of \( {S}^{n},{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , and \( {\mathbb{H}}^{n} \) is Einstein. Ricci flow is contracting on \( {S}^{n} \) , constant on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , and expanding on \( {\mathbb{H}}^{n} \) . The Ricci flow on \( {S}^{n} \) has a finite-time singularity where the diameter of the manifold goes to zero and the curvature goes uniformly to \( + \infty \) . The Ricci flow on \( {\mathbb{H}}^{n} \) exists for all \( t \geq  0 \) and as \( t \) goes to infinity the distance between any pair of points grows without bound and the curvature goes uniformly to zero.

EXAMPLE 3.5. Let \( {h}_{0} \) be the round metric on \( {S}^{2} \) with constant Gaussian curvature \( 1/2 \) . Set \( h\left( t\right)  = \left( {1 - t}\right) {h}_{0} \) . Then the flow

\[
\left( {{S}^{2}, h\left( t\right) }\right) , - \infty  < t < 1,
\]

is a Ricci flow. We also have the product of this flow with the trivial flow on the line: \( \left( {{S}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R}, h\left( t\right)  \times  d{s}^{2}}\right) , - \infty  < t < 1 \) . This is called the standard shrinking round cylinder.

The standard shrinking round cylinder is a model for evolving \( \epsilon \) -necks. In Chapter 1 we introduced the notion of an \( \epsilon \) -neck. In the case of flows, in order to take smooth geometric limits, it is important to have a stronger version of this notion. In this stronger notion, the neck not only exists in one time-slice but it exists backwards in the flow for an appropriate amount of time and is close to the standard shrinking round cylinder on the entire time interval. The existence of evolving necks is exploited when we study limits of Ricci flows.

2.2. Solitons. A Ricci soliton is a Ricci flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,0 \leq  t < T \leq \; \infty \) , with the property that for each \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) there is a diffeomorphism \( {\varphi }_{t} : M \rightarrow  M \) and a constant \( \sigma \left( t\right) \) such that \( \sigma \left( t\right) {\varphi }_{t}^{ * }g\left( 0\right)  = g\left( t\right) \) . That is to say, in a Ricci soliton all the Riemannian manifolds \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) are isometric up to a scale factor that is allowed to vary with \( t \) . The soliton is said to be shrinking if \( {\sigma }^{\prime }\left( t\right)  < 0 \) for all \( t \) . One way to generate Ricci solitons is the

following: Suppose that we have a vector field \( X \) on \( M \) and a constant \( \lambda \) and a metric \( g\left( 0\right) \) such that

(3.2)

\[
- \operatorname{Ric}\left( {g\left( 0\right) }\right)  = \frac{1}{2}{\mathcal{L}}_{X}g\left( 0\right)  - {\lambda g}\left( 0\right) .
\]

We set \( T = \infty \) if \( \lambda  \leq  0 \) and equal to \( {\left( 2\lambda \right) }^{-1} \) if \( \lambda  > 0 \) . Then, for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) we define a function

\[
\sigma \left( t\right)  = 1 - {2\lambda t}
\]

and a vector field

\[
{Y}_{t}\left( x\right)  = \frac{X\left( x\right) }{\sigma \left( t\right) }.
\]

Then we define \( {\varphi }_{t} \) as the one-parameter family of diffeomorphisms generated by the time-dependent vector fields \( {Y}_{t} \) .

nodes.proof:
Let's sketch the proof due to DeTurck [16], cf, Section 3 of Chapter 3 starting on page 78 of [13] for more details. First, we compute the first variation at a Riemannian metric \( g \) of minus twice the Ricci curvature tensor in the direction \( h \) :

\[
{\delta }_{g}\left( {-2\operatorname{Ric}}\right) \left( h\right)  = \bigtriangleup h - \operatorname{Sym}\left( {\nabla V}\right)  + S
\]

where:

(1) \( V \) is the one-form given by

\[
{V}_{k} = \frac{1}{2}{g}^{pq}\left( {{\nabla }_{p}{h}_{qk} + {\nabla }_{q}{h}_{pk} - {\nabla }_{k}{h}_{pq}}\right) ,
\]

(2) Sym \( \left( {\nabla V}\right) \) is the symmetric two-tensor obtained by symmetrizing the covariant derivative of \( V \) , and

(3) \( S \) is a symmetric two-tensor constructed from the inverse of the metric, the Riemann curvature tensor and \( h \) , but involves no derivatives of \( h \) .

Now let \( {g}_{0} \) be the initial metric. For any metric \( g \) we define a one-form \( \widehat{W} \) by taking the trace, with respect to \( g \) , of the matrix-valued one-form that is the difference of the connections of \( g \) and \( {g}_{0} \) . Now we form a second-order operator of \( g \) by setting

\[
P\left( g\right)  = {\mathcal{L}}_{W}g
\]

the Lie derivative of \( g \) with respect to the vector field \( W \) dual to \( \widehat{W} \) . Thus, in local coordinates we have \( P{\left( g\right) }_{ij} = {\nabla }_{i}{\widehat{W}}_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}{\widehat{W}}_{i} \) . The linearization at \( g \) of the second-order operator \( P \) in the direction \( h \) is symmetric and is given by

\[
{\delta }_{g}P\left( h\right)  = \operatorname{Sym}\left( {\nabla V}\right)  + T
\]

where \( T \) is a first-order operator in \( h \) . Thus, defining \( Q =  - 2\mathrm{{Ric}} + P \) we have

\[
{\delta }_{g}\left( Q\right) \left( h\right)  = \bigtriangleup h + U
\]

where \( U \) is a first-order operator in \( h \) . Now we introduce the Ricci-DeTurck flow

(3.4)

\[
\frac{\partial g}{\partial t} =  - 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( g\right)  + P.
\]

The computations above show that the Ricci-DeTurck flow is strictly parabolic. Thus, Equation (3.4) has a short-time solution \( \bar{g}\left( t\right) \) with \( \bar{g}\left( 0\right)  = {g}_{0} \) by the standard PDE theory. Given this solution \( \bar{g}\left( t\right) \) we define the time-dependent vector field \( W\left( t\right)  = W\left( {\bar{g}\left( t\right) ,{g}_{0}}\right) \) as above. Let \( {\phi }_{t} \) be a one-parameter family of diffeomorphisms, with \( {\phi }_{0} = \mathrm{{Id}} \) , generated by this time-dependent vector field, i.e.,

\[
\frac{\partial {\phi }_{t}}{\partial t} = W\left( t\right)
\]

Then, direct computation shows that \( g\left( t\right)  = {\phi }_{t}^{ * }\bar{g}\left( t\right) \) solves the Ricci flow equation.

nodes.proof:
The Ricci flow equation tells us that non-negative Ricci curvature implies that \( \partial g/\partial t \leq  0 \) . Hence, the length of any tangent vector in \( M \) , and consequently the length of any path in \( M \) , is a non-increasing function of

t. Since the distance between points is the infimum over all rectifiable paths from \( x \) to \( y \) of the length of the path, this function is also a non-increasing function of \( t \) .

Proposition 3.19. The evolution of the curvature operator \( \mathcal{T}\left( t\right)  = \; {\Phi }_{t}^{ * }\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is given by

\[
\frac{\partial {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }}{\partial t} = \Delta {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta } + {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{2} + {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{\sharp },
\]

where \( {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{2} = {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \gamma }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \beta } \) is the operator square; \( {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{\sharp } = {c}_{\alpha \gamma \zeta }{c}_{\beta \delta \eta }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \delta }{\mathcal{T}}_{\zeta \eta } \) is the Lie algebra square; and \( {c}_{\alpha \beta \gamma } = \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{\varphi }^{\alpha },{\varphi }^{\beta }}\right\rbrack  ,{\varphi }^{\gamma }}\right\rangle \) are the structure constants of the Lie algebra \( \operatorname{so}\left( n\right) \) relative to the basis \( \left\{  {\varphi }^{\alpha }\right\} \) . The structure constants \( {c}_{\alpha \beta \gamma } \) are fully antisymmetric in the three indices.

nodes.proof:
We work in local coordinates that are orthonormal at the point. By the first Bianchi identity

\[
{R}_{abcd} + {R}_{acdb} + {R}_{adbc} = 0,
\]

we get

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e, f}}{R}_{abef}{R}_{cdef} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e, f}}\left( {-{R}_{aefb} - {R}_{afbe}}\right) \left( {-{R}_{cefd} - {R}_{cfde}}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e, f}}2{R}_{aebf}{R}_{cedf} - 2{R}_{aebf}{R}_{cfde}
\]

\[
= 2\left( {{B}_{abcd} - {B}_{adbc}}\right) .
\]

Note that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e, f}}{R}_{abef}{R}_{cdef} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e, f}}{\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }{\varphi }_{ab}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{ef}^{\beta }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \lambda }{\varphi }_{cd}^{\gamma }{\varphi }_{ef}^{\lambda }
\]

\[
= {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }{\varphi }_{ab}^{\alpha }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \lambda }{\varphi }_{cd}^{\gamma }{\delta }^{\beta \lambda }
\]

\[
= {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{2}{\varphi }_{ab}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{cd}^{\beta }
\]

Also,

\[
2\left( {{B}_{acbd} - {B}_{adbc}}\right)  = 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e, f}}\left( {{R}_{aecf}{R}_{bedf} - {R}_{aedf}{R}_{becf}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e, f}}\left( {{\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }{\varphi }_{ae}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{cf}^{\beta }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \lambda }{\varphi }_{be}^{\gamma }{\varphi }_{df}^{\lambda } - {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }{\varphi }_{ae}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{df}^{\beta }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \lambda }{\varphi }_{be}^{\gamma }{\varphi }_{cf}^{\lambda }}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e, f}}{\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \lambda }{\varphi }_{ae}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{be}^{\gamma }\left( {{\varphi }_{cf}^{\beta }{\varphi }_{df}^{\lambda } - {\varphi }_{df}^{\beta }{\varphi }_{cf}^{\lambda }}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{e}{\mathcal{I}}_{\alpha \beta }{\mathcal{I}}_{\gamma \lambda }{\varphi }_{ae}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{be}^{\gamma }{\left\lbrack  {\varphi }^{\beta },{\varphi }^{\lambda }\right\rbrack  }_{cd}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{e}{\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \lambda }{\left\lbrack  {\varphi }^{\beta },{\varphi }^{\lambda }\right\rbrack  }_{cd}\left( {{\varphi }_{ae}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{be}^{\gamma } - {\varphi }_{be}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{ae}^{\gamma }}\right)
\]

\[
= {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }{\mathcal{T}}_{\gamma \delta }{\left\lbrack  {\varphi }^{\beta },{\varphi }^{\lambda }\right\rbrack  }_{cd}{\left\lbrack  {\varphi }^{\alpha },{\varphi }^{\gamma }\right\rbrack  }_{ab}
\]

\[
= {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{\sharp }{\varphi }_{ab}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{cd}^{\beta }.
\]

So we can rewrite the equation for the evolution of the curvature tensor given in Lemma 3.18 as

\[
\frac{\partial {R}_{abcd}}{\partial t} = \bigtriangleup {R}_{abcd} + {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{2}{\varphi }_{ab}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{cd}^{\beta } + {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{\sharp }{\varphi }_{ab}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{cd}^{\beta },
\]

or equivalently as

\[
\frac{\partial {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }}{\partial t} = \Delta {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta } + {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{2} + {\mathcal{T}}_{\alpha \beta }^{\sharp }.
\]

We abbreviate the last equation as

\[
\frac{\partial \mathcal{T}}{\partial t} = \bigtriangleup \mathcal{T} + {\mathcal{T}}^{2} + {\mathcal{T}}^{\sharp }
\]

Proposition 3.21. Let \( {t}_{0} \in  \mathbb{R} \) and let \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) be a Ricci flow defined for \( t \) in an interval containing \( {t}_{0} \) with \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) complete for every \( t \) in this interval. Fix a constant \( K < \infty \) . Let \( {x}_{0},{x}_{1} \) be two points of \( M \) and let \( {r}_{0} > 0 \) such that \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  \geq  2{r}_{0} \) . Suppose that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) for all \( x \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \cup  B\left( {{x}_{1},{r}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Then

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} \geq   - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{0} + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

If the distance function \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) \) is not a differentiable function of \( t \) at \( t = {t}_{0} \) , then this inequality is understood as an inequality for the forward difference quotient.

nodes.proof:
The first step in the proof is to replace the distance function by the length of minimal geodesics. The following is standard.

CLAIM 3.23. Suppose that for every minimal \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) from \( {x}_{0} \) to \( {x}_{1} \) the function \( {\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) \) which is the \( g\left( t\right) \) -length of \( \gamma \) satisfies

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} \geq  C.
\]

Then

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} \geq  C,
\]

where, as in the statement of the proposition, if the distance function is not differentiable at \( {t}_{0} \) , then the inequality in the conclusion is interpreted by replacing the derivative on the left-hand side with the liminf of the forward difference quotients of \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) \) at \( {t}_{0} \) .

The second step in the proof is to estimate the time derivative of a minimal geodesic under the hypothesis of the proposition.

CLAIM 3.24. Assuming the hypothesis of the proposition, for any minimal \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) from \( {x}_{0} \) to \( {x}_{1} \) , we have

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} \geq   - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{0} + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

Proof. Fix a minimal \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -geodesic \( \gamma \left( u\right) \) from \( {x}_{0} \) to \( {x}_{1} \) , parameterized by arc length. We set \( d = {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) \) , we set \( X\left( u\right)  = {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( u\right) \) , and we take tangent vectors \( {Y}_{1},\ldots ,{Y}_{n - 1} \) in \( {T}_{{x}_{0}}M \) which together with \( X\left( 0\right)  = {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \) form an orthonormal basis. We let \( {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) \) be the parallel translation of \( {Y}_{i} \) along \( \gamma \) . Define \( f : \left\lbrack  {0, d}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) by:

\[
f\left( u\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} u/{r}_{0}, & 0 \leq  u \leq  {r}_{0}, \\  1, & {r}_{0} \leq  u \leq  d - {r}_{0}, \\  \left( {d - u}\right) /{r}_{0}, & d - u \leq  {r}_{0} \leq  d, \end{array}\right.
\]

and define

\[
{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( u\right)  = f\left( u\right) {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) .
\]

See FIG. 2. For \( 1 \leq  i \leq  n - 1 \) , let \( {s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right) \) be the second variation of the \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -length of \( \gamma \) along \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i} \) . Since \( \gamma \) is a minimal \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -geodesic, for all \( i \) we have

(3.12)

\[
{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  \geq  0
\]

![019eafd6-18e6-7ba5-b83e-6cdf48ce6b88_89_527_519_748_309_0.jpg](images/019eafd6-18e6-7ba5-b83e-6cdf48ce6b88_89_527_519_748_309_0.jpg)

Figure 2. \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i} \) along \( \gamma \) .

Let us now compute \( {s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right) \) by taking a two-parameter family \( \gamma \left( {u, s}\right) \) such that the curve \( \gamma \left( {u,0}\right) \) is the original minimal geodesic and \( {\left. \frac{\partial }{\partial s}\left( \gamma \left( u, s\right) \right) \right| }_{s = 0} = \; {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( u\right) \) . We denote by \( X\left( {u, s}\right) \) the image \( D{\gamma }_{\left( u, s\right) }\left( {\partial /\partial u}\right) \) and by \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( {u, s}\right) \) the image \( D{\gamma }_{\left( u, s\right) }\left( {\partial /\partial s}\right) \) . We wish to compute(3.13)

\[
{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\left. \frac{{d}^{2}}{d{s}^{2}}\left( {\int }_{0}^{d}\sqrt{X\left( {u, s}\right) , X\left( {u, s}\right) }du\right) \right| }_{s = 0}
\]

\[
= {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\left( {\int }_{0}^{d}\langle X\left( u, s\right) , X\left( u, s\right) {\rangle }^{-1/2}\left\langle  X\left( u, s\right) ,{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( u, s\right) \right\rangle  du\right) \right| }_{s = 0}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{d} - \langle X\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) {\rangle }^{-3/2}{\left\langle  X\left( u,0\right) ,{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( u,0\right) \right\rangle  }^{2}{du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{d}\frac{\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right) ,{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   + \left\langle  {X\left( {u,0}\right) ,{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle  }{\langle X\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) {\rangle }^{1/2}}{du}.
\]

Using the fact that \( X \) and \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i} \) commute (since they are the coordinate partial derivatives of a map of a surface into \( M \) ) and using the fact that \( {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) \) is parallel along \( \gamma \) , meaning that \( {\nabla }_{X}\left( {Y}_{i}\right) \left( u\right)  = 0 \) , we see that \( {\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right)  = \; {\nabla }_{X}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( {u,0}\right)  = {f}^{\prime }\left( u\right) {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) \) . By construction \( \left\langle  {{Y}_{i}\left( u\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = 0 \) . It follows that

\[
\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}\left( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\right) \left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {{f}^{\prime }\left( u\right) {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = 0.
\]

Also, \( \langle X\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) \rangle  = 1 \) , and by construction \( \left\langle  {{Y}_{i}\left( {u,0}\right) ,{Y}_{i}\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = 1 \) . Thus, restricting to \( s = 0 \) and, for simplicity of notation, leaving the variable \( u \) implicit, Equation (3.13) simplifies to

(3.14)

\[
{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{0}^{d}\left( {{\left( {f}^{\prime }\right) }^{2}\left\langle  {{Y}_{i},{Y}_{i}}\right\rangle   + \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\nabla }_{X}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  }\right) {du}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{d}\left( {\left\langle  {R\left( {{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right) {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   - \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   + {\left( {f}^{\prime }\right) }^{2}}\right) {du}.
\]

We have

\[
\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   = \frac{d}{du}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   - \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i},{\nabla }_{X}X}\right\rangle   = \frac{d}{du}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  ,
\]

where the last equality is a consequence of the geodesic equation, \( {\nabla }_{X}X = 0 \) . It follows that

\[
{\int }_{0}^{d}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  {du} = {\int }_{0}^{d}\frac{d}{du}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   = 0,
\]

where the last equality is a consequence of the fact that \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i} \) vanishes at the end points.

Consequently, plugging these into Equation (3.14) we have

(3.15)

\[
{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{0}^{d}\left( {\left\langle  {R\left( {{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right) {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   + {\left( {f}^{\prime }\left( u\right) \right) }^{2}}\right) {du}.
\]

Of course, it is immediate from the definition that \( {f}^{\prime }{\left( u\right) }^{2} = 1/{r}_{0}^{2} \) for \( u \in \; \left\lbrack  {0,{r}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and for \( u \in  \left\lbrack  {d - {r}_{0}, d}\right\rbrack \) and is zero otherwise. Also, from the definition of the vector fields \( {Y}_{i} \) we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}\left\langle  {R\left( {{Y}_{i}, X}\right) {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right\rangle   =  - {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) ,
\]

so that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}\left\langle  {R\left( {{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right) {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right\rangle   =  - {f}^{2}\left( u\right) {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) .
\]

Hence, summing Equalities (3.15) for \( i = 1,\ldots , n - 1 \) and using Equation (3.12) gives

\[
0 \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left\lbrack  {\frac{{u}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left( {-{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{{r}_{0}}^{d - {r}_{0}} - {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) {du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{d - {r}_{0}}^{d}\left\lbrack  {\frac{{\left( d - u\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left( {-{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}.
\]

Rearranging the terms yields

\[
0 \leq   - {\int }_{0}^{d}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) {du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 - \frac{{u}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{d - {r}_{0}}^{d}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 - \frac{{\left( d - u\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}.
\]

Since

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} = {\left. \frac{d}{dt}\left\lbrack  {\left( {\int }_{0}^{d}\sqrt{\langle X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) \rangle }dt\right) }^{1/2}\right\rbrack  \right| }_{t = {t}_{0}}
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{0}^{d}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) {du},
\]

we have

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} \geq   - \left\{  {{\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 - \frac{{u}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+{\int }_{d - {r}_{0}}^{d}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 - \frac{{\left( d - u\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}}\right\}  .
\]

Now, since \( \left| {X\left( u\right) }\right|  = 1 \) , by the hypothesis of the proposition we have the estimate \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right)  \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) on the regions of integration on the right-hand side of the above inequality. Thus,

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} \geq   - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}{r}_{0}K + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

This completes the proof of Claim 3.24.

Claims 3.23 and 3.24 together prove the proposition.

Fix a minimal \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -geodesic \( \gamma \left( u\right) \) from \( {x}_{0} \) to \( {x}_{1} \) , parameterized by arc length. We set \( d = {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) \) , we set \( X\left( u\right)  = {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( u\right) \) , and we take tangent vectors \( {Y}_{1},\ldots ,{Y}_{n - 1} \) in \( {T}_{{x}_{0}}M \) which together with \( X\left( 0\right)  = {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \) form an orthonormal basis. We let \( {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) \) be the parallel translation of \( {Y}_{i} \) along \( \gamma \) . Define \( f : \left\lbrack  {0, d}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) by:

\[
f\left( u\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} u/{r}_{0}, & 0 \leq  u \leq  {r}_{0}, \\  1, & {r}_{0} \leq  u \leq  d - {r}_{0}, \\  \left( {d - u}\right) /{r}_{0}, & d - u \leq  {r}_{0} \leq  d, \end{array}\right.
\]

and define

\[
{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( u\right)  = f\left( u\right) {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) .
\]

See FIG. 2. For \( 1 \leq  i \leq  n - 1 \) , let \( {s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right) \) be the second variation of the \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -length of \( \gamma \) along \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i} \) . Since \( \gamma \) is a minimal \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -geodesic, for all \( i \) we have

(3.12)

\[
{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  \geq  0
\]

![019eafd6-18e6-7ba5-b83e-6cdf48ce6b88_89_527_519_748_309_0.jpg](images/019eafd6-18e6-7ba5-b83e-6cdf48ce6b88_89_527_519_748_309_0.jpg)

Figure 2. \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i} \) along \( \gamma \) .

Let us now compute \( {s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right) \) by taking a two-parameter family \( \gamma \left( {u, s}\right) \) such that the curve \( \gamma \left( {u,0}\right) \) is the original minimal geodesic and \( {\left. \frac{\partial }{\partial s}\left( \gamma \left( u, s\right) \right) \right| }_{s = 0} = \; {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( u\right) \) . We denote by \( X\left( {u, s}\right) \) the image \( D{\gamma }_{\left( u, s\right) }\left( {\partial /\partial u}\right) \) and by \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( {u, s}\right) \) the image \( D{\gamma }_{\left( u, s\right) }\left( {\partial /\partial s}\right) \) . We wish to compute(3.13)

\[
{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\left. \frac{{d}^{2}}{d{s}^{2}}\left( {\int }_{0}^{d}\sqrt{X\left( {u, s}\right) , X\left( {u, s}\right) }du\right) \right| }_{s = 0}
\]

\[
= {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\left( {\int }_{0}^{d}\langle X\left( u, s\right) , X\left( u, s\right) {\rangle }^{-1/2}\left\langle  X\left( u, s\right) ,{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( u, s\right) \right\rangle  du\right) \right| }_{s = 0}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{d} - \langle X\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) {\rangle }^{-3/2}{\left\langle  X\left( u,0\right) ,{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( u,0\right) \right\rangle  }^{2}{du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{d}\frac{\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right) ,{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   + \left\langle  {X\left( {u,0}\right) ,{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle  }{\langle X\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) {\rangle }^{1/2}}{du}.
\]

Using the fact that \( X \) and \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i} \) commute (since they are the coordinate partial derivatives of a map of a surface into \( M \) ) and using the fact that \( {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) \) is parallel along \( \gamma \) , meaning that \( {\nabla }_{X}\left( {Y}_{i}\right) \left( u\right)  = 0 \) , we see that \( {\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right)  = \; {\nabla }_{X}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( {u,0}\right)  = {f}^{\prime }\left( u\right) {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) \) . By construction \( \left\langle  {{Y}_{i}\left( u\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = 0 \) . It follows that

\[
\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}X\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}\left( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\right) \left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {{f}^{\prime }\left( u\right) {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = 0.
\]

Also, \( \langle X\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) \rangle  = 1 \) , and by construction \( \left\langle  {{Y}_{i}\left( {u,0}\right) ,{Y}_{i}\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   = 1 \) . Thus, restricting to \( s = 0 \) and, for simplicity of notation, leaving the variable \( u \) implicit, Equation (3.13) simplifies to

(3.14)

\[
{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{0}^{d}\left( {{\left( {f}^{\prime }\right) }^{2}\left\langle  {{Y}_{i},{Y}_{i}}\right\rangle   + \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\nabla }_{X}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  }\right) {du}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{d}\left( {\left\langle  {R\left( {{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right) {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   - \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   + {\left( {f}^{\prime }\right) }^{2}}\right) {du}.
\]

We have

\[
\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   = \frac{d}{du}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   - \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i},{\nabla }_{X}X}\right\rangle   = \frac{d}{du}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  ,
\]

where the last equality is a consequence of the geodesic equation, \( {\nabla }_{X}X = 0 \) . It follows that

\[
{\int }_{0}^{d}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  {du} = {\int }_{0}^{d}\frac{d}{du}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right\rangle   = 0,
\]

where the last equality is a consequence of the fact that \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{i} \) vanishes at the end points.

Consequently, plugging these into Equation (3.14) we have

(3.15)

\[
{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{0}^{d}\left( {\left\langle  {R\left( {{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right) {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( {u,0}\right) , X\left( {u,0}\right) }\right\rangle   + {\left( {f}^{\prime }\left( u\right) \right) }^{2}}\right) {du}.
\]

Of course, it is immediate from the definition that \( {f}^{\prime }{\left( u\right) }^{2} = 1/{r}_{0}^{2} \) for \( u \in \; \left\lbrack  {0,{r}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and for \( u \in  \left\lbrack  {d - {r}_{0}, d}\right\rbrack \) and is zero otherwise. Also, from the definition of the vector fields \( {Y}_{i} \) we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}\left\langle  {R\left( {{Y}_{i}, X}\right) {Y}_{i}\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right\rangle   =  - {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) ,
\]

so that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}\left\langle  {R\left( {{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}, X}\right) {\widetilde{Y}}_{i}\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right\rangle   =  - {f}^{2}\left( u\right) {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) .
\]

Hence, summing Equalities (3.15) for \( i = 1,\ldots , n - 1 \) and using Equation (3.12) gives

\[
0 \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}{s}_{{\widetilde{Y}}_{i}}^{\prime \prime }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left\lbrack  {\frac{{u}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left( {-{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{{r}_{0}}^{d - {r}_{0}} - {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) {du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{d - {r}_{0}}^{d}\left\lbrack  {\frac{{\left( d - u\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left( {-{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}.
\]

Rearranging the terms yields

\[
0 \leq   - {\int }_{0}^{d}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) {du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 - \frac{{u}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{d - {r}_{0}}^{d}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 - \frac{{\left( d - u\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}.
\]

Since

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} = {\left. \frac{d}{dt}\left\lbrack  {\left( {\int }_{0}^{d}\sqrt{\langle X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) \rangle }dt\right) }^{1/2}\right\rbrack  \right| }_{t = {t}_{0}}
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{0}^{d}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) {du},
\]

we have

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} \geq   - \left\{  {{\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 - \frac{{u}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+{\int }_{d - {r}_{0}}^{d}\left\lbrack  {\left( {1 - \frac{{\left( d - u\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right) }\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {du}}\right\}  .
\]

Now, since \( \left| {X\left( u\right) }\right|  = 1 \) , by the hypothesis of the proposition we have the estimate \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {X\left( u\right) , X\left( u\right) }\right)  \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) on the regions of integration on the right-hand side of the above inequality. Thus,

\[
{\left. \frac{d\left( {{\ell }_{t}\left( \gamma \right) }\right) }{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} \geq   - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}{r}_{0}K + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

This completes the proof of Claim 3.24.

THEOREM 3.29. Fix the dimension \( n \) of the Ricci flows under consideration. Let \( K < \infty \) and \( \alpha  > 0 \) be given positive constants. Fix an integer \( l \geq  0 \) . Then for each integer \( k \geq  0 \) and for each \( r > 0 \) there is a constant \( {C}_{k, l}^{\prime } = {C}_{k, l}^{\prime }\left( {K,\alpha , r, n}\right) \) such that the following holds. Let \( \left( {U, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,0 \leq  t \leq  T \) , be a Ricci flow with \( T \leq  \alpha /K \) . Fix \( p \in  U \) and suppose that the metric ball \( B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) has compact closure in \( U \) . Suppose that

\[
\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  K\;\text{ for all }x \in  U\text{ and all }t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{\beta }\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,0}\right) }\right|  \leq  K\;\text{ for all }x \in  U\;\text{ and all }\;\beta  \leq  l.
\]

Then

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{k}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {y, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{{C}_{k, l}^{\prime }}{{t}^{\max \{ k - l,0\} /2}}
\]

for all \( y \in  B\left( {p,0, r/2}\right) \) and all \( t \in  (0, T\rbrack \) . In particular if \( k \leq  l \) , then for \( y \in  B\left( {p,0, r/2}\right) \) and \( t \in  (0, T\rbrack \) we have

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{k}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {y, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{k, l}^{\prime }.
\]

Then for each integer \( k \geq 0 \) and for each \( r > 0 \) there is a constant \( {C}_{k, l}^{\prime } = {C}_{k, l}^{\prime }\left( {K,\alpha , r, n}\right) \) such that the following holds. Let \( \left( {U, g\left( t\right) }\rig...

nodes.proof:
The first remark is that establishing Theorem 3.29 for one value of \( r \) immediately gives it for all \( {r}^{\prime } \geq  {2r} \) . The reason is that for such point \( y \in  B\left( {p,0,{r}^{\prime }/2}\right) \) has the property that \( B\left( {y,0, r}\right)  \subset  B\left( {p,0,{r}^{\prime }}\right) \) so that a curvature bound on \( B\left( {p,0,{r}^{\prime }}\right) \) will imply one on \( B\left( {y,0, r}\right) \) and hence by the result for \( r \) will imply the higher derivative bounds at \( y \) .

Thus, without loss of generality we can suppose that \( r \leq  \pi /2\sqrt{K} \) . We shall assume this from now on in the proof. Since \( B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) has compact closure in \( M \) , for some \( r < {r}^{\prime } < \pi /\sqrt{K} \) the ball \( B\left( {p,0,{r}^{\prime }}\right) \) also has compact closure in \( M \) . This means that the exponential mapping from the ball of radius \( {r}^{\prime } \) in \( {T}_{p}M \) is a local diffeomorphism onto \( B\left( {p,0,{r}^{\prime }}\right) \) .

The proof is by induction: We assume that we have established the result for \( k = 0,\ldots , m \) , and then we shall establish it for \( k = m + 1 \) . The inductive hypothesis tells us that there are constants \( {A}_{j},0 \leq  j \leq  m \) , depending on \( \left( {l, K,\alpha , r, n}\right) \) such that for all \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  B\left( {p,0, r/2}\right)  \times  (0, T\rbrack \) we have

(3.17)

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{j}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {A}_{j}{t}^{-\max \{ j - l,0\} /2}.
\]

Applying the inductive result to \( B\left( {y,0, r/2}\right) \) with \( y \in  B\left( {p,0, r/2}\right) \) we see that, replacing the \( {A}_{j} \) by the constants associated with \( \left( {l, K,\alpha , r/2, n}\right) \) , we have the same inequality for all \( y \in  B\left( {x,0,{3r}/4}\right) \) .

We fix a constant \( C \geq  \max \left( {4{A}_{m}^{2},1}\right) \) and consider

\[
{F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  = \left( {C + {t}^{\max \{ m - l,0\} }{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\left( x, t\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{\max \{ m + 1 - l,0\} }{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\left( x, t\right) \right| }^{2}.
\]

Notice that bounding \( {F}_{m} \) above by a constant \( {\left( {C}_{m + 1, l}^{\prime }\right) }^{2} \) will yield

\[
{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\left( x, t\right) \right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{{\left( {C}_{m + 1, l}^{\prime }\right) }^{2}}{{t}^{\max \{ m + 1 - l,0\} }},
\]

and hence will complete the proof of the result.

Bounding \( {F}_{m} \) above (assuming the inductive hypothesis) is what is accomplished in the rest of this proof. The main calculation is the proof of the following claim under the inductive hypothesis.

CLAIM 3.32. With \( {F}_{m} \) as defined above and with \( C \geq  \max \left( {4{A}_{m}^{2},1}\right) \) , there are constants \( {c}_{1} \) and \( {C}_{0},{C}_{1} \) depending on \( C \) as well as \( K,\alpha ,{A}_{1},\ldots ,{A}_{m} \) for which the following holds on \( B\left( {p,0,{3r}/4}\right)  \times  (0, T\rbrack \) :

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq   - \frac{{c}_{1}{\left( {F}_{m}\left( x, t\right)  - {C}_{0}\right) }^{2}}{{t}^{\mathrm{s}\{ \max \{ m - l + 1,0\} \} }} + \frac{{C}_{1}}{{t}^{s\{ \max \{ m - l + 1,0\} \} }},
\]

where

\[
s\{ n\}  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll}  + 1, & \text{ if }n > 0, \\  0, & \text{ if }n = 0, \\   - 1, & \text{ if }n < 0. \end{array}\right.
\]

Let us assume this claim and use it to prove Theorem 3.29. We fix \( C = \max \left\{  {4{A}_{m}^{2},1}\right\} \) , and consider the resulting function \( {F}_{m} \) . The constants \( {c}_{1},{C}_{0},{C}_{1} \) from Claim 3.32 depend only on \( K,\alpha \) , and \( {A}_{1},\ldots ,{A}_{m} \) . Since \( r \leq  \pi /2\sqrt{K} \) , and \( B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) has compact closure in \( U \) , there is some \( {r}^{\prime } > r \) so that the exponential mapping \( {\exp }_{p} : B\left( {0,{r}^{\prime }}\right)  \rightarrow  U \) is a local diffeomorphism onto \( B\left( {p,0,{r}^{\prime }}\right) \) . Pulling back by the exponential map, we replace the Ricci flow on \( U \) by a Ricci flow on \( B\left( {0,{r}^{\prime }}\right) \) in \( {T}_{p}M \) . Clearly, it suffices to establish the estimates in the statement of the proposition for \( B\left( {0, r/2}\right) \) . This remark allows us to assume that the exponential mapping is a diffeomorphism onto \( B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) . Bounded curvature then comes into play in the following crucial proposition, which goes back to Shi. The function given in the next proposition allows us to localize the computation in the ball \( B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) .

Proposition 3.33. Fix constants \( 0 < \alpha \) and the dimension \( n \) . Then there is a constant \( {C}_{2}^{\prime } = {C}_{2}^{\prime }\left( {\alpha , n}\right) \) and for each \( r > 0 \) and \( K < \infty \) there is a constant \( {C}_{2} = {C}_{2}\left( {K,\alpha , r, n}\right) \) such that the following holds. Suppose that \( \left( {U, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,0 \leq  t \leq  T \) , is an n-dimensional Ricci flow with \( T \leq  \alpha /K \) . Suppose that \( p \in  U \) and that \( B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) has compact closure in \( U \) and that the exponential mapping from the ball of radius \( r \) in \( {T}_{p}U \) to \( B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) is a diffeomorphism. Suppose that \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,0}\right) }\right|  \leq  K \) for all \( x \in  B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) . There is a smooth function \( \eta  : B\left( {p,0, r}\right)  \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) satisfying the following for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   : \)

(1) \( \eta \) has compact support in \( B\left( {p,0, r/2}\right) \) .

(2) The restriction of \( \eta \) to \( B\left( {p,0, r/4}\right) \) is identically 1 .

(3) \( \left| {{\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }\eta }\right|  \leq  {C}_{2}\left( {K,\alpha , r, n}\right) \) .

(4) \( \frac{{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}}{\eta } \leq  \frac{{C}_{2}^{\prime }\left( {\alpha , n}\right) }{{r}^{2}} \) .

For a proof of this result see Lemma 6.62 on page 225 of [14].

We can apply this proposition to our situation, because we are assuming that \( r \leq  \pi /2\sqrt{K} \) so that the exponential mapping is a local diffeomorphism onto \( B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) and we have pulled the Ricci flow back to the ball in the tangent space.

Fix any \( y \in  B\left( {p,0, r/2}\right) \) and choose \( \eta \) as in the previous proposition for the constants \( {C}_{2}\left( {\alpha , n}\right) \) and \( {C}_{2}^{\prime }\left( {K,\alpha , r/4, n}\right) \) . Notice that \( B\left( {y,0, r/4}\right)  \subset \; B\left( {p,0,{3r}/4}\right) \) so that the conclusion of Claim 3.32 holds for every \( \left( {z, t}\right) \) with \( z \in  B\left( {y,0, r/4}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . We shall show that the restriction of \( \eta {F}_{m} \) to \( P\left( {y,0, r/4, T}\right) \) is bounded by a constant that depends only on \( K,\alpha , r, n,{A}_{1},\ldots ,{A}_{m} \) . It will then follow immediately that the restriction of \( {F}_{m} \) to \( P\left( {y,0, r/8, T}\right) \) is bounded by the same constant. In particular, the values of \( {F}_{m}\left( {y, t}\right) \) are bounded by the same constant for all \( y \in  B\left( {p,0, r/2}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

Consider a point \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  B\left( {y,0, r/2}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) where \( \eta {F}_{m} \) achieves its maximum; such a point exists since the ball \( B\left( {y,0, r/2}\right)  \subset  B\left( {p,0, r}\right) \) , and hence \( B\left( {y,0, r/2}\right) \) has compact closure in \( U \) . If \( t = 0 \) , then \( \eta {F}_{m} \) is bounded by \( \left( {C + {K}^{2}}\right) {K}^{2} \) which is a constant depending only on \( K \) and \( {A}_{m} \) . This, of course, immediately implies the result. Thus we can assume that the maximum is achieved at some \( t > 0 \) . When \( s\{ \max \{ m + 1 - l,0\} \}  = 0 \) , according to Claim 3.32, we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - {c}_{1}{\left( {F}_{m} - {C}_{0}\right) }^{2} + {C}_{1}.
\]

We compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\eta {F}_{m}}\right)  \leq  \eta \left( {-{c}_{1}{\left( {F}_{m - {C}_{0}}\right) }^{2} + {C}_{1}}\right)  - {\Delta \eta } \cdot  {F}_{m} - 2\nabla \eta  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m}.
\]

Since \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is a maximum point for \( \eta {F}_{m} \) and since \( t > 0 \) , a simple maximum principle argument shows that

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \eta {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Hence, in this case we conclude that

\[
0 \leq  \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\eta \left( x\right) {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  \leq  \eta \left( x\right) \left( {-{c}_{1}{\left( {F}_{m}\left( x, t\right)  - {C}_{0}\right) }^{2} + {C}_{1}}\right)
\]

\[
- {\Delta \eta }\left( x\right)  \cdot  {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  - 2\nabla \eta \left( x\right)  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) .
\]

Hence,

\[
{c}_{1}\eta {\left( {F}_{m}\left( x, t\right)  - {C}_{0}\right) }^{2} \leq  \eta \left( x\right) {C}_{1} - {\Delta \eta }\left( x\right)  \cdot  {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  - 2\nabla \eta \left( x\right)  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) .
\]

Since we are proving that \( {F}_{m} \) is bounded, we are free to argue by contradiction and assume that \( {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  2{C}_{0} \) , implying that \( {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  - {C}_{0} \geq \; {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) /2 \) . Using this inequality yields

\[
\eta \left( x\right) \left( {{F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  - {C}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{{2\eta }{C}_{1}}{{c}_{1}{F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) } - \frac{{2\Delta \eta }\left( x\right) }{{c}_{1}} - \frac{4}{{c}_{1}{F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) }\nabla \eta \left( x\right)  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{\eta {C}_{1}}{{c}_{1}{C}_{0}} - \frac{{2\Delta \eta }\left( x\right) }{{c}_{1}} - \frac{4}{{c}_{1}{F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) }\nabla \eta \left( x\right)  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) .
\]

Since \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is a maximum for \( \eta {F}_{m} \) we have

\[
0 = \nabla \left( {\eta \left( x\right) {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  = \nabla \eta \left( x\right) {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  + \eta \left( x\right) \nabla {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) ,
\]

so that

\[
\frac{\nabla \eta \left( x\right) }{\eta \left( x\right) } =  - \frac{\nabla {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) }{{F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) }.
\]

Plugging this in gives

\[
\eta \left( x\right) {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{{C}_{1}}{{c}_{1}{C}_{0}} - \frac{{2\Delta \eta }\left( x\right) }{{c}_{1}} + 4\frac{{\left| \nabla \eta \left( x\right) \right| }^{2}}{{c}_{1}\eta \left( x\right) } + \eta {C}_{0}.
\]

Of course, the gradient and Laplacian of \( \eta \) are taken at the point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) . Thus, because of the properties of \( \eta \) given in Proposition 3.33, it immediately follows that \( \eta {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) \) is bounded by a constant depending only on \( K, n,\alpha , r,{c}_{1},{C}_{0},{C}_{1} \) , and as we have already seen, \( {c}_{1},{C}_{0},{C}_{1} \) depend only on \( K,\alpha ,{A}_{1},\ldots ,{A}_{m}. \)

Now suppose that \( s\{ \max \{ m - l + 1,0\} \}  = 1 \) . Again we compute the evolution inequality for \( \eta {F}_{m} \) . The result is

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\eta {F}_{m}}\right)  \leq  \eta \left( {-\frac{{c}_{1}}{t}{\left( {F}_{m} - {C}_{0}\right) }^{2} + \frac{{C}_{1}}{t}}\right)  - {\Delta \eta } \cdot  {F}_{m} - 2\nabla \eta  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m}.
\]

Thus, using the maximum principle as before, we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \eta {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Hence,

\[
\frac{\eta \left( x\right) {c}_{1}{\left( {F}_{m}\left( x, t\right)  - {C}_{0}\right) }^{2}}{t} \leq  \frac{\eta \left( x\right) {C}_{1}}{t} - {\Delta \eta }\left( x\right) {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  - 2\nabla \eta \left( x\right)  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) .
\]

Using the assumption that \( {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  2{C}_{0} \) as before, and rewriting the last term as before, we have

\[
\eta {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{\eta \left( x\right) {C}_{1}}{{c}_{1}{C}_{0}} - \frac{{2t\Delta \eta }\left( x\right) }{{c}_{1}} + \frac{{4t}{\left| \nabla \eta \left( x\right) \right| }^{2}}{{c}_{1}\eta \left( x\right) } + \eta {C}_{0}.
\]

The right-hand side is bounded by a constant depending only on \( K, n,\alpha , r \) , \( {c}_{1},{C}_{0} \) , and \( {C}_{1} \) . We conclude that in all cases \( \eta {F}_{m} \) is bounded by a constant depending only on \( K, n,\alpha , r,{c}_{1},{C}_{0},{C}_{1} \) , and hence on \( K, n,\alpha , r,{A}_{1},\ldots ,{A}_{m} \) .

This proves that for any \( y \in  B\left( {p,0, r/2}\right) \) , the value \( \eta {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right) \) is bounded by a constant \( {A}_{m + 1} \) depending only on \( \left( {m + 1, l, K, n,\alpha , r}\right) \) for all \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in \; B\left( {y,0, r/2}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( \eta \left( y\right)  = 1 \) , for all \( 0 \leq  t \leq  T \) we have

\[
{t}^{\max \{ m + 1 - l,0\} }{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\left( y, t\right) \right| }^{2} \leq  {F}_{m}\left( {y, t}\right)  = \eta \left( y\right) {F}_{m}\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  {A}_{m + 1}.
\]

This completes the inductive proof that the result holds for \( k = m + 1 \) and hence establishes Theorem 3.29, modulo the proof of Claim 3.32.

CLAIM 3.32. With \( {F}_{m} \) as defined above and with \( C \geq  \max \left( {4{A}_{m}^{2},1}\right) \) , there are constants \( {c}_{1} \) and \( {C}_{0},{C}_{1} \) depending on \( C \) as well as \( K,\alpha ,{A}_{1},\ldots ,{A}_{m} \) for which the following holds on \( B\left( {p,0,{3r}/4}\right)  \times  (0, T\rbrack \) :

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq   - \frac{{c}_{1}{\left( {F}_{m}\left( x, t\right)  - {C}_{0}\right) }^{2}}{{t}^{\mathrm{s}\{ \max \{ m - l + 1,0\} \} }} + \frac{{C}_{1}}{{t}^{s\{ \max \{ m - l + 1,0\} \} }},
\]

where

\[
s\{ n\}  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll}  + 1, & \text{ if }n > 0, \\  0, & \text{ if }n = 0, \\   - 1, & \text{ if }n < 0. \end{array}\right.
\]

nodes.proof:
In this argument we fix \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  B\left( {p,0,{3r}/4}\right)  \times  (0, T\rbrack \) and we drop \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) from the notation. Recall that by Equations (7.4a) and (7.4b) on p. 229 of \( \left\lbrack  \mathbf{{13}}\right\rbrack \) we have

(3.18)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| {\nabla }^{\ell }\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| {\nabla }^{\ell }\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{\ell  + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{\ell }{c}_{\ell , j}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{\ell  - i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{\ell }\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|
\]

where the constants \( {c}_{\ell , j} \) depend only on \( \ell \) and \( j \) .

Hence, setting \( {m}_{l} = \max \{ m + 1 - l,0\} \) and denoting \( {c}_{m + 1, i} \) by \( {\widetilde{c}}_{i} \) , we have

\[
\text{ (3.19) }\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ {t}^{{m}_{l}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{{m + 1}}{\widetilde{c}}_{i}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1 - i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  + {m}_{l}{t}^{{m}_{l} - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\widetilde{c}}_{0} + {\widetilde{c}}_{m + 1}}\right) {t}^{{m}_{l}}\left| \mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ {t}^{{m}_{l}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{m}{\widetilde{c}}_{i}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1 - i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  + {m}_{l}{t}^{{m}_{l} - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Using the inductive hypothesis, Inequality (3.17), there is a constant \( A < \infty \) depending only on \( K,\alpha ,{A}_{1},\ldots ,{A}_{m} \) such that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{m}{\widetilde{c}}_{i}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1 - i}\operatorname{Rm}}\right|  \leq  A{t}^{-{m}_{l}/2}.
\]

Also, let \( c = {\widetilde{c}}_{0} + {\widetilde{c}}_{m + 1} \) and define a new constant \( B \) by

\[
B = c\left( {\alpha  + K}\right)  + {m}_{l}.
\]

Then, since \( t \leq  T \leq  \alpha /K \) and \( {m}_{l} \geq  0 \) , we have

\[
\left( {\left( {{\widetilde{c}}_{0} + {\widetilde{c}}_{m + 1}}\right) t\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  + {m}_{l}}\right) {t}^{{m}_{l} - 1} \leq  \frac{B{t}^{{m}_{l}}}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}.
\]

Putting this together allows us to rewrite Inequality (3.19) as

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  \leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ A{t}^{{m}_{l}/2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|
\]

\[
+ \left( {{ct}\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  + {m}_{l}}\right) {t}^{{m}_{l} - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{B}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + A{t}^{{m}_{l}/2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| .
\]

Completing the square gives

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  \leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {B + 1}\right) {t}^{{m}_{l} - s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + \frac{{A}^{2}}{4}{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }.
\]

Let \( {\widehat{m}}_{l} = \max \{ m - l,0\} \) . From (3.18) and the induction hypothesis, there is a constant \( D \) , depending on \( K,\alpha ,{A}_{1},\ldots ,{A}_{m} \) such that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  \leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ {\widehat{m}}_{l}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + D.
\]

Now, defining new constants \( \widetilde{B} = B + 1 \) and \( \widetilde{A} = {A}^{2}/4 \) we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left\lbrack  {\left( {C + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack   \leq
\]

\[
\left( {C + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {\widetilde{A}{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) } - 2{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + \frac{\widetilde{B}{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}{{t}^{s\left\{  {m}_{l}\right\}  }}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {-2{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + {\widehat{m}}_{l}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + D}\right) {t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- 2{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} + {m}_{l}}\nabla \left( {\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}\right)  \cdot  \nabla \left( {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}\right) .
\]

Since \( C \geq  4{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \) , this implies

\[
\left( {3.20}\right) \;\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - {10}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} + {m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- 8{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} + {m}_{l}}\left| {{\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  - 2{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} + {m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4}
\]

\[
+ \left( {C + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {\widetilde{B}{t}^{{m}_{l} - s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + \widetilde{A}{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\widehat{m}}_{l}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + D}\right) {t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Now we can write the first three terms on the right-hand side of Inequality (3.20) as \( - {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} + {m}_{l}} \) times

(3.21)

\[
{\left( \sqrt{10}\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  + \frac{4}{\sqrt{10}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2} + \frac{2}{5}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4}.
\]

In addition we have

(3.22)

\[
C + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  C + {A}_{m}^{2}.
\]

Let us set \( \widetilde{D} = \max \left( {\alpha /K,1}\right) D \) . If \( {\widehat{m}}_{l} = 0 \) , then

(3.23)

\[
{\widehat{m}}_{l}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + D = D \leq  \frac{\widetilde{D}}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }} = {\widehat{m}}_{l}{A}_{m}^{2} + D \leq  \frac{{\widehat{m}}_{l}{A}_{m}^{2} + \widetilde{D}}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}.
\]

On the other hand, if \( {\widehat{m}}_{l} > 0 \) , then \( s\left( {\widehat{m}}_{l}\right)  = s\left( {m}_{l}\right)  = 1 \) and hence

\[
{\widehat{m}}_{l}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l} - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + D \leq  \frac{1}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{\widehat{m}}_{l}{A}_{m}^{2} + D \leq  \frac{{\widehat{m}}_{l}{A}_{m}^{2} + \widetilde{D}}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}.
\]

Since \( {\widehat{m}}_{l} = {m}_{l} - s\left( {m}_{l}\right) \) , Inequalities (3.21),(3.22), and (3.23) allow us to rewrite Inequality (3.20) as

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - \frac{2}{5{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{t}^{2{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{4}
\]

\[
+ \left( {C + {A}_{m}^{2}}\right) \left( {\frac{\widetilde{B}{t}^{{m}_{l}}}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + \widetilde{A}{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}\right)  + \frac{{\widehat{m}}_{l}{A}_{m}^{2} + \widetilde{D}}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Setting

\[
{B}^{\prime } = \left( {C + {A}_{m}^{2}}\right) \widetilde{B} + \left( {{\widehat{m}}_{l}{A}_{m}^{2} + \widetilde{D}}\right) ,
\]

and \( {A}^{\prime } = \widetilde{A}\left( {C + {A}_{m}^{2}}\right) \) we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - \frac{2}{5{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{\left( {t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{{B}^{\prime }}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + {A}^{\prime }{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }.
\]

We rewrite this as

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - \frac{2}{5{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{\left( {t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} - \frac{5{B}^{\prime }}{4}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{5{\left( {B}^{\prime }\right) }^{2}}{8{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }} + {A}^{\prime }{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) },
\]

and hence

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - \frac{2}{5{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}{\left( {t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;R}\mathrm{m}\right| }^{2} - {B}^{\prime \prime }\right) }^{2} + \frac{{A}^{\prime \prime }}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}
\]

where the constants \( {B}^{\prime \prime } \) and \( {A}^{\prime \prime } \) are defined by \( {B}^{\prime \prime } = 5{B}^{\prime }/4 \) and

\[
{A}^{\prime \prime } = {\left( \max \{ \alpha /K,1\} \right) }^{2} + 5{\left( {B}^{\prime }\right) }^{2}/8.
\]

(Recall that \( t \leq  T \leq  \alpha /K \) .) Let

\[
Y = \left( {C + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) .
\]

(Notice that \( Y \) is not a constant.) Of course, by definition

\[
{F}_{m} = Y{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Then the previous inequality becomes

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - \frac{2}{5{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }{Y}^{2}}{\left( Y{t}^{{m}_{l}}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} - {B}^{\prime \prime }Y\right) }^{2} + \frac{{A}^{\prime \prime }}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}.
\]

Since \( C \leq  Y \leq  {5C}/4 \) we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - \frac{32}{{125}{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }{C}^{2}}{\left( {F}_{m} - {B}^{\prime \prime }Y\right) }^{2} + \frac{{A}^{\prime \prime }}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}.
\]

At any point where \( {F}_{m} \geq  {5C}{B}^{\prime \prime }/4 \) , the last inequality gives

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - \frac{32}{{125}{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }{C}^{2}}{\left( {F}_{m} - 5C{B}^{\prime \prime }/4\right) }^{2} + \frac{{A}^{\prime \prime }}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}.
\]

At any point where \( {F}_{m} \leq  {5C}{B}^{\prime \prime }/4 \) , since \( {F}_{m} \geq  0 \) and \( 0 \leq  {B}^{\prime \prime }Y \leq  {5C}{B}^{\prime \prime }/4 \) , we have \( {\left( {F}_{m} - {B}^{\prime \prime }Y\right) }^{2} \leq  {25}{C}^{2}{\left( {B}^{\prime \prime }\right) }^{2}/{16} \) , so that

\[
- \frac{32}{{125}{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }{C}^{2}}{\left( {F}_{m} - 5C{B}^{\prime \prime }/4\right) }^{2} \geq   - 2{\left( {B}^{\prime \prime }\right) }^{2}/5{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }.
\]

Thus, in this case we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq  \frac{{A}^{\prime \prime }}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }} \leq   - \frac{32}{{125}{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }{C}^{2}}{\left( {F}_{m} - 5C{B}^{\prime \prime }/4\right) }^{2} + \frac{{A}^{\prime \prime } + 2{\left( {B}^{\prime \prime }\right) }^{2}/5}{{t}^{s\left( {m}_{l}\right) }}.
\]

These two cases together prove Claim 3.32.

nodes.content:
DEFINITION 3.34. By space-time we mean a smooth \( \left( {n + 1}\right) \) -dimensional manifold \( \mathcal{M} \) (possibly with boundary), equipped with a smooth function \( \mathbf{t} : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) , called time and a smooth vector field \( \chi \) subject to the following axioms:

(1) The image of \( \mathbf{t} \) is an interval \( I \) (possibly infinite) and the boundary of \( \mathcal{M} \) is the preimage under \( \mathbf{t} \) of \( \partial I \) .

(2) For each \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) there is an open neighborhood \( U \subset  \mathcal{M} \) of \( x \) and a diffeomorphism \( f : V \times  J \rightarrow  U \) , where \( V \) is an open subset in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) and \( J \) is an interval with the property that (i) \( \mathbf{t} \) is the composition of \( {f}^{-1} \) followed by the projection onto the interval \( J \) and (ii) \( \chi \) is the image under \( f \) of the unit vector field in the positive direction tangent to the foliation by the lines \( \{ v\}  \times  J \) of \( V \times  J \) .

Notice that it follows that \( \chi \left( \mathbf{t}\right)  = 1 \) .

nodes.content:
DEFINITION 3.35. The time-slices of space-time are the level sets \( \mathbf{t} \) . These form a foliation of \( \mathcal{M} \) of codimension 1. For each \( t \in  I \) we denote by \( {M}_{t} \subset  \mathcal{M} \) the \( t \) time-slice, that is to say \( {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( t\right) \) . Notice that each boundary component of \( \mathcal{M} \) is contained in a single time-slice. The horizontal distribution \( \mathcal{H}T\mathcal{M} \) is the distribution tangent to this foliation. A horizontal metric on space-time is a smoothly varying positive definite inner product on \( \mathcal{H}T\mathcal{M} \) .

Notice that a horizontal metric on space-time induces an ordinary Riemannian metric on each time-slice. Conversely, given a Riemannian metric on each time-slice \( {M}_{t} \) , the condition that they fit together to form a horizontal metric on space-time is that they vary smoothly on space-time. We define the curvature of a horizontal metric \( G \) to be the section of the dual of the symmetric square of \( { \land  }^{2}\mathcal{H}T\mathcal{M} \) whose value at each point \( x \) with \( \mathbf{t}\left( x\right)  = t \) is the usual Riemann curvature tensor of the induced metric on \( {M}_{t} \) at the point \( x \) . This is a smooth section of \( {\operatorname{Sym}}^{2}\left( {{ \land  }^{2}\mathcal{H}{T}^{ * }\mathcal{M}}\right) \) . The Ricci curvature and the scalar curvature of a horizontal metric are given in the usual way from its Riemann curvature. The Ricci curvature is a smooth section of \( {\operatorname{Sym}}^{2}\left( {\mathcal{H}{T}^{ * }\mathcal{M}}\right) \) while the scalar curvature is a smooth function on \( \mathcal{M} \) .

nodes.label: Remark 3.37

nodes.content:
REMARK 3.37. Let \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) be a generalized Ricci flow and let \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Pulling \( G \) back to the local coordinates \( V \times  J \) defined near any point gives a one-parameter family of metrics \( \left( {V, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  J \) , satisfying the usual Ricci flow equation. It follows that all the usual evolution formulas for Riemann curvature, Ricci curvature, and scalar curvature hold in this more general context.

Of course, any ordinary Ricci flow is a generalized Ricci flow where space-time is a product \( M \times  I \) with time being the projection to \( I \) and \( \chi \) being the unit vector field in the positive \( I \) -direction.

nodes.content: DEFINITION 3.38. Let \( \mathcal{M} \) be a space-time. Given a space \( C \) and an interval \( I \subset  \mathbb{R} \) we say that an embedding \( C \times  I \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) is compatible with the time and the vector field if: (i) the restriction of \( \mathbf{t} \) to the image agrees with the projection onto the second factor and (ii) for each \( c \in  C \) the image of \( \{ c\}  \times  I \) is the integral curve for the vector field \( \chi \) . If in addition \( C \) is a subset of \( {M}_{t} \) we require that \( t \in  I \) and that the map \( C \times  \{ t\}  \rightarrow  {M}_{t} \) be the identity. Clearly, by the uniqueness of integral curves for vector fields, two such embeddings agree on their common interval of definition, so that, given \( C \subset  {M}_{t} \) there is a maximal interval \( {I}_{C} \) containing \( t \) such that such an embedding, compatible with time and the vector field, is defined on \( C \times  I \) . In the special case when \( C = \{ x\} \) for a point \( x \in  {M}_{t} \) we say that such an embedding is the flow line through \( x \) . The embedding of the maximal interval through \( x \) compatible with time and the vector field \( \chi \) is called the domain of definition of the flow line through \( x \) . For a more general subset \( C \subset  {M}_{t} \) there is an embedding \( C \times  I \) compatible with time and the vector field \( \chi \) if and only if for every \( x \in  C, I \) is contained in the domain of definition of the flow line through \( x \) .

We say that \( t \) is a regular time if there is \( \epsilon  > 0 \) and a diffeomorphism \( {M}_{t} \times  \left( {t - \epsilon , t + \epsilon }\right)  \rightarrow  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( \left( {t - \epsilon , t + \epsilon }\right) \right) \) compatible with time and the vector field. A time is singular if it is not regular. Notice that if all times are regular, then space-time is a product \( {M}_{t} \times  I \) with \( \mathbf{t} \) and \( \chi \) coming from the second factor. If the image \( \mathbf{t}\left( \mathcal{M}\right) \) is an interval \( I \) bounded below, then the initial time for the flow is the greatest lower bound for \( I \) . If \( I \) includes \( ( - \infty , A\rbrack \) for some \( A \) , then the initial time for the generalized Ricci flow is \( - \infty \) .

DEFINITION 3.40. Suppose that \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) is a generalized Ricci flow and that \( Q > 0 \) is a positive constant. Then we can define a new generalized Ricci flow by setting \( {G}^{\prime } = {QG},{\mathbf{t}}^{\prime } = Q\mathbf{t} \) and \( {\chi }^{\prime } = {Q}^{-1}\chi \) . It is easy to see that the result still satisfies the generalized Ricci flow equation. It is also possible to translate a generalized solution \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) by replacing the time function \( \mathbf{t} \) by \( {\mathbf{t}}^{\prime } = \mathbf{t} + a \) for any constant \( a \) , leaving \( G \) and \( \chi \) unchanged.
