- 2{C}_{0}\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}{ds} \leq  \frac{d\left| {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right| }{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }} + \left| {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right| } \leq  2{C}_{0}\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}{ds}.
\]

Suppose that \( {s}_{0} < {s}_{1} \) . Integrating from \( {s}_{0} \) to \( {s}_{1} \) gives

Given \( {\bar{\tau }}_{0} < \infty ,{C}_{0} < \infty ,\epsilon  > 0 \) , and \( {l}_{0} < \infty \) , there is a constant \( {C}_{2} \) depending only on \( {C}_{0},{l}_{0},\epsilon \) and \( {\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) such that the following holds. Let \( \gamma \) be an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic defined on \( \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) with \( {\tau }_{1} + \epsilon  \leq  \bar{\tau } \leq  {\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) and with \( \left| {\nabla R\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{0} \) and \( \left| {\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{0} \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . Suppose also that \( l\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  {l}_{0} \) . Then, we have

\[
\mathop{\max }\limits_{\tau }\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\left| {{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right| }\right)  \leq  {C}_{2}.
\]

From the definition \( \mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{\sqrt{{\tau }_{1}}}^{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}}\left( {2{s}^{2}R + \frac{1}{2}{\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {ds} \) . \[

\]

\[
\mathop{\min }\limits_{\tau }\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\left| {{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right| }\right)  \leq  {C}^{\prime }
\]

for some constant \( {C}^{\prime } \) depending only on \( {C}_{0},{l}_{0},\epsilon \) and \( {\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) . The result is now immediate from Lemma 6.60.

LEMMA 6.62. Given constants \( \epsilon  > 0,{\bar{\tau }}_{0} < \infty ,{C}_{0} < \infty \) , and \( {l}_{0} < \infty \) , there are \( {C}_{3} < \infty \) and \( 0 < {\delta }_{2} \leq  \epsilon /4 \) depending only on the given constants such that the following holds. Let \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) be a point with \( \mathbf{t}\left( y\right)  = {t}_{0} = T - \bar{\tau } \) where \( {\tau }_{1} + \epsilon  \leq  \bar{\tau } \leq  {\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) . Suppose that there is a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) from \( x \) to \( y \) with \( {l}_{x}\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  {l}_{0} \) . Suppose that \( \left| {\nabla R}\right| \) and \( \left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| \) are bounded by \( {C}_{0} \) along \( \gamma \) . Suppose also that the ball \( B\left( {y,{t}_{0},\epsilon }\right) \) has compact closure in \( {M}_{{t}_{0}} \) and that there is an embedding

\[
\iota  : B\left( {y,{t}_{0},\epsilon }\right)  \times  \left( {{t}_{0} - \epsilon ,{t}_{0} + \epsilon }\right) \overset{ \cong  }{ \rightarrow  }\widetilde{P}\left( {y,\epsilon ,\epsilon }\right)  \subset  \mathcal{M}
\]

compatible with time and the vector field so that the sectional curvatures of the restriction of \( G \) to the image of this embedding are bounded by \( {C}_{0} \) . Then for any point \( b \in  B\left( {y,{t}_{0},{\delta }_{2}}\right) \) and for any \( {t}^{\prime } \in  \left( {{t}_{0} - {\delta }_{2},{t}_{0} + {\delta }_{2}}\right) \) there is a curve \( {\gamma }_{1} \) from \( x \) to the point \( z = \iota \left( {b,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) , parameterized by backward time, such that

\[
l\left( {\gamma }_{1}\right)  \leq  l\left( \gamma \right)  + {C}_{3}\sqrt{{d}_{{t}_{0}}{\left( y, b\right) }^{2} + {\left| {t}_{0} - {t}^{\prime }\right| }^{2}}.
\]

Proof. Let \( {C}_{2} \) be the constant depending on \( {C}_{0},{l}_{0},\epsilon \) , and \( {\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) from Corollary 6.61, and set

\[
{C}^{\prime } = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\epsilon }}{C}_{2}
\]

Since \( \bar{\tau } \geq  \epsilon \) , it follows that \( \bar{\tau } - \epsilon /2 \geq  \epsilon /2 \) , so that by Corollary 6.61 we have \( \left| {{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right|  \leq  {C}^{\prime } \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{\tau } - \epsilon /2,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . Set \( 0 < {\delta }_{0} \) sufficiently small (how small depends only on \( {C}_{0} \) ) such that for all \( \left( {z, t}\right)  \in  \widetilde{P}\left( {y,\epsilon ,{\delta }_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
\frac{1}{2}g\left( {z, t}\right)  \leq  g\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {2g}\left( {z, t}\right) ,
\]

and define

\[
{\delta }_{2} = \min \left( {\frac{\epsilon }{8},\frac{\epsilon }{8{C}^{\prime }},\frac{{\delta }_{0}}{4}}\right) .
\]

Let \( b \in  B\left( {y,{t}_{0},{\delta }_{2}}\right) \) and \( {t}^{\prime } \in  \left( {{t}_{0} - {\delta }_{2},{t}_{0} + {\delta }_{2}}\right) \) be given. Set

\[
\alpha  = \sqrt{{d}_{{t}_{0}}{\left( y, b\right) }^{2} + {\left| {t}_{0} - {t}^{\prime }\right| }^{2}},
\]

set \( {t}_{1} = {t}_{0} - {2\alpha } \) , and let \( {\tau }_{1} = T - {t}_{1} \) . Notice that \( \alpha  < \sqrt{2}{\delta }_{2} < \epsilon /4 \) , so that the norm of the Ricci curvature is bounded by \( {C}^{\prime } \) on \( \iota \left( {B\left( {y,{t}_{0},\epsilon }\right)  \times  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{0} + {2\alpha }}\right) }\right) \) .

CLAIM 6.63. \( \gamma \left( {\tau }_{1}\right)  \in  \widetilde{P}\left( {y,\epsilon ,\epsilon }\right) \) and writing \( \gamma \left( {\tau }_{1}\right)  = \iota \left( {c,{t}_{1}}\right) \) we have \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {c, b}\right)  \leq  \left( {4{C}^{\prime } + 1}\right) \alpha . \)

Proof. Since \( \left| {{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right|  \leq  {C}^{\prime } \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{\tau } - {2\alpha },\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) , and \( {\delta }_{2} \leq  {\delta }_{0}/4 \) , it follows that \( {2\alpha } \leq  {\delta }_{0} \) and hence that \( {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) } \leq  2{C}^{\prime } \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{\tau } - {2\alpha },\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( \gamma \left( \bar{\tau }\right)  = y \) , this implies that

\[
{d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y, c}\right)  \leq  4{C}^{\prime }\alpha
\]

The claim then follows from the triangle inequality.

Now let \( \bar{\mu } : \left\lbrack  {\bar{\tau } - {2\alpha }, T - {t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  B\left( {y,{t}_{0},\epsilon }\right) \) be a shortest \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -geodesic from \( c \) to \( b \) , parameterized at constant \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -speed, and let \( \mu \) be the path parameterized by backward time defined by

\[
\mu \left( \tau \right)  = \iota \left( {\bar{\mu }\left( \tau \right) , T - \tau }\right)
\]

for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{\tau } - {2\alpha }, T - {t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) . Then the concatenation \( {\gamma }_{1} = {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {\tau }_{1},\bar{\tau } - 2\alpha \right\rbrack  } * \mu \) is a path parameterized by backward time from \( x \) to \( \iota \left( {b,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) .

CLAIM 6.64. There is a constant \( {C}_{1}^{\prime } \) depending only on \( {C}_{0},{C}^{\prime } \) , and \( {\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) such that

\[
l\left( {\gamma }_{1}\right)  \leq  l\left( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {\tau }_{1},\bar{\tau } - 2\alpha \right\rbrack  }\right)  + {C}_{1}^{\prime }\alpha
\]

Proof. First notice that since \( \bar{\tau } = T - {t}_{0} \) and \( \left| {{t}^{\prime } - {t}_{0}}\right|  \leq  \alpha \) we have \( \left( {T - {t}^{\prime }}\right)  - \left( {\bar{\tau } - {2\alpha }}\right)  = {2\alpha } + \left( {{t}^{\prime } - {t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  \alpha \) . According to Claim 6.63 this implies that the \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) -speed of \( \mu \) is at most \( \left( {4{C}^{\prime } + 1}\right) \) , and hence that \( {\left| {X}_{\mu }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{g\left( {T - \tau }\right) } \leq \; 8{C}^{\prime } + 2 \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{\tau } - {2\alpha }, T - {t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) . Consequently, \( R + {\left| {X}_{\mu }\right| }^{2} \) is bounded above along \( \mu \) by a constant \( \widetilde{C} \) depending only on \( {C}^{\prime } \) and \( {C}_{0} \) . This implies that \( \mathcal{L}\left( \mu \right)  \leq  \widetilde{C}\alpha \sqrt{T - {t}^{\prime }} \) . Of course, \( T - {t}^{\prime } \leq  \bar{\tau } + \epsilon  < 2\bar{\tau } \leq  2{\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) . This completes the proof of the claim.

On the other hand, since \( R \geq   - 3{C}_{0} \) in \( P\left( {y,\epsilon ,\epsilon }\right) \) and \( {\left| X\right| }^{2} \geq  0 \) , we see that

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {\tau }_{1},\bar{\tau } - 2\alpha \right\rbrack  }\right)  \leq  \mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  + 6{C}_{0}\alpha \sqrt{{\bar{\tau }}_{0}}.
\]

Together with the previous claim this establishes Lemma 6.62.

LEMMA 6.72. Let \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) be a generalized Ricci flow and let \( x \in  {M}_{T} \subset \; \mathcal{M} \) . Fix \( Q > 0 \) and let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{\prime },{G}^{\prime }}\right) \) be the \( Q \) scaling and shifting of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) as described in the previous paragraph. Let \( \iota  : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  {\mathcal{M}}^{\prime } \) be the identity map. Suppose that \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) is a path parameterized by backward time with \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = x \) . Let \( \beta  : \left\lbrack  {0, Q\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  Q\mathcal{M} \) be defined by

\[
\beta \left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right)  = \iota \left( {\gamma \left( {{\tau }^{\prime }/Q}\right) }\right) .

Then \( \beta \left( 0\right)  = x \) and \( \beta \) is parameterized by backward time in \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{\prime },{G}^{\prime }}\right) \) , and \( \mathcal{L}\left( \beta \right)  = \sqrt{Q}\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right) \) . It follows from the first equation in Corollary 6.74 that

\[
J\left( \iota \right) \mathcal{J}\left( {Z,\tau }\right)  = J\left( \sqrt{{Q}^{-1}}\right) {\mathcal{J}}^{\prime }\left( {\sqrt{{Q}^{-1}}Z,{\tau }^{\prime }}\right) ,
\]

where \( J\left( \iota \right) \) is the Jacobian determinant of \( \iota \) at \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x}\left( {Z,\tau }\right) \) and \( J\left( \sqrt{{Q}^{-1}}\right) \) is the Jacobian determinant of multiplication by \( \sqrt{{Q}^{-1}} \) as a map from \( {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) to itself, where the domain has the metric \( G \) and the range has metric \( {G}^{\prime } = {QG} \) . Clearly, with these conventions, we have \( J\left( \iota \right)  = {Q}^{n/2} \) and \( J\left( \sqrt{{Q}^{-1}}\right)  = 1 \) . Hence, we conclude

\[
{Q}^{n/2}\mathcal{J}\left( {Z,\tau }\right)  = {\mathcal{J}}^{\prime }\left( {\sqrt{{Q}^{-1}}Z,{\tau }^{\prime }}\right) .
\]

Letting \( \gamma \) be the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic in \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) with initial condition \( Z \) and \( \beta \) the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic in \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{\prime },{G}^{\prime }}\right) \) with initial condition \( \sqrt{{Q}^{-1}}Z \) , by Lemma 6.72 we have \( \gamma \left( \tau \right)  = \beta \left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) \) . From Corollary 6.74 and the definition of the reduced length, we get

\[
{\widetilde{l}}^{\prime }\left( {\sqrt{{Q}^{-1}}Z,{\tau }^{\prime }}\right)  = \widetilde{l}\left( {\gamma ,\tau }\right) .
\]

Plugging these in gives the result.

Putting these computations together gives the following.

Proposition 6.78. Let \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) be a generalized Ricci flow and let \( x \in \; {M}_{T} \subset  \mathcal{M} \) . Then, for any \( A < \infty \) , there is \( \delta  > 0 \) such that the map \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x} \) is defined on \( B\left( {0, A}\right)  \times  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) , where \( B\left( {0, A}\right) \) is the ball of radius \( A \) centered at the origin in \( {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) . Moreover, the map \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x} \) defines a diffeomorphism of \( B\left( {0, A}\right)  \times  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) onto an open subset of \( \mathcal{M} \) . Furthermore,

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\tau }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\widetilde{l}\left( {Z,\tau }\right) }\mathcal{J}\left( {Z,\tau }\right)  = {2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| Z\right| }^{2}},
\]

where the convergence is uniform on each compact subset of \( {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) .

nodes.proof:
First notice that since \( T \) is greater than the initial time of \( \mathcal{M} \) , there is \( \epsilon  > 0 \) , and an embedding \( \rho  : B\left( {x, T,\epsilon }\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {T - \epsilon , T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) compatible with time and the vector field. By taking \( \epsilon  > 0 \) smaller if necessary, we can assume that the image of \( \rho \) has compact closure in \( \mathcal{M} \) . By compactness every higher partial derivative (both spatial and temporal) of the metric is bounded on the image of \( \rho \) .

Now take a sequence of positive constants \( {\tau }_{k} \) tending to 0 as \( k \rightarrow  \infty \) , and set \( {Q}_{k} = {\tau }_{k}^{-1} \) . We let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{k},{G}_{k}}\right) \) be the \( {Q}_{k} \) -rescaling and shifting of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) as described at the beginning of this section. The rescaled version of \( \rho \) is an embedding

\[
{\rho }_{k} : {B}_{{G}_{k}}\left( {x, T,\sqrt{{Q}_{k}}\epsilon }\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {T - {Q}_{k}\epsilon , T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {\mathcal{M}}_{k}
\]

compatible with the time function \( {\mathbf{t}}_{k} \) and the vector field. Furthermore, uniformly on the image of \( {\rho }_{k} \) , every higher partial derivative of the metric is bounded by a constant that goes to zero with \( k \) . Thus, the generalized Ricci flows \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{k},{G}_{k}}\right) \) based at \( x \) converge geometrically to the constant family of Euclidean metrics on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Since the ODE given in Equation (6.5) is regular even at 0, this implies that the \( \mathcal{L} \) -exponential maps for these flows converge uniformly on the balls of finite radius centered at the origin of the tangent spaces at \( x \) to the \( \mathcal{L} \) -exponential map of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) at the origin. Of course, if \( Z \in  {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) is an initial condition for an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic in \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) , then \( \sqrt{{Q}_{k}^{-1}}Z \) is the initial condition for the corresponding \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic in \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{k},{G}_{k}}\right) \) . But \( {\left| Z\right| }_{G} = {\left| \sqrt{{Q}_{k}^{-1}}Z\right| }_{{G}_{k}} \) , so that if \( Z \in  {B}_{G}\left( {0, A}\right) \) then \( \sqrt{{Q}_{k}^{-1}}Z \in  {B}_{{G}_{k}}\left( {0, A}\right) \) . In particular, we see that, for any \( A < \infty \) and for all \( k \) sufficiently large, the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics are defined on \( {B}_{{G}_{k}}\left( {0, A}\right)  \times  (0,1\rbrack \) and the image is contained in the image of \( {\rho }_{k} \) . Rescaling shows that for any \( A < \infty \) there is \( k \) for which the \( \mathcal{L} \) -exponential map is defined on \( {B}_{G}\left( {0, A}\right)  \times  \left( {0,{\tau }_{k}}\right\rbrack \) and has image contained in \( \rho \) .

Let \( Z \in  {B}_{G}\left( {0, A}\right) \) , and let \( \gamma \) be the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\sqrt{\tau }{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  = \; Z \) . Let \( {\gamma }_{k} \) be the corresponding \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic in \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{k},{G}_{k}}\right) \) . Then

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\sqrt{\tau }{X}_{{\gamma }_{k}}\left( \tau \right)  = \sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}Z = {Z}_{k}.
\]

Of course, \( {\left| {Z}_{k}\right| }_{{G}_{k}}^{2} = {\left| Z\right| }_{G}^{2} \) , meaning that, for every \( k,{Z}_{k} \) is contained in the ball \( {B}_{{G}_{k}}\left( {0, A}\right)  \subset  {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) . Hence, by passing to a subsequence we can assume that, in the geometric limit, the \( \sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}Z \) converge to a tangent vector \( {Z}^{\prime } \) in the ball of radius \( A \) centered at the origin in the tangent space to Euclidean space. Of course \( {\left| {Z}^{\prime }\right| }^{2} = {\left| Z\right| }_{G}^{2} \) . By Claim 6.77, this means that we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{1}^{-n/2}{e}^{-{\widetilde{l}}_{k}\left( {\sqrt{{Q}_{k}^{-1}}Z,1}\right) }{\mathcal{J}}_{k}\left( {\sqrt{{Q}_{k}^{-1}}Z,1}\right)  = {2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| Z\right| }^{2}},
\]

with \( {\mathcal{J}}_{k} \) the Jacobian determinant of the \( \mathcal{L} \) -exponential map for \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{k},{G}_{k}}\right) \) . Of course, since \( {\tau }_{k} = {Q}_{k}^{-1} \) , by Lemma 6.75 we have

\[
{1}^{-n/2}{e}^{-{\widetilde{l}}_{k}\left( {\sqrt{{Q}_{k}^{-1}}Z,1}\right) }{\mathcal{J}}_{k}\left( {\sqrt{{Q}_{k}^{-1}}Z,1}\right)  = {\tau }_{k}^{-n/2}{e}^{-\widetilde{l}\left( {Z,{\tau }_{k}}\right) }\mathcal{J}\left( {Z,{\tau }_{k}}\right) .
\]

This establishes the limiting result.

Since the geometric limits are uniform on balls of finite radius centered at the origin in the tangent space, the above limit also is uniform over each of these balls.

nodes.content: COROLLARY 6.79. Let \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) be a generalized Ricci flow whose sectional curvatures are bounded. For any \( x \in  {M}_{T} \) and any \( R < \infty \) for all \( \tau  > 0 \) sufficiently small, the ball of radius \( R \) centered at the origin in \( {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) is contained in \( {\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) .

For any \( x \in {M}_{T} \) and any \( R < \infty \) for all \( \tau > 0 \) sufficiently small, the ball of radius \( R \) centered at the origin in \( {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) is contained in \( {\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) .

nodes.proof:
According to the last result, given \( R < \infty \) , for all \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small the ball of radius \( R \) centered at the origin in \( {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) is contained in \( {\mathcal{D}}_{x}^{\delta } \) , in the domain of definition of \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x}^{\delta } \) as given in Definition 6.17, and \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x} \) is a diffeomorphism on this subset. We shall show that if \( \delta  > 0 \) is sufficiently small, then the resulting \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) is the unique minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic. If not then there must be another, distinct \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic to this point whose \( \mathcal{L} \) -length is no greater than that of \( \gamma \) . According to Lemma 6.60 there is a constant \( {C}_{1} \) depending on the curvature bound and on \( \delta \) such that if \( Z \) is an initial condition for an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic, then for all \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) we have

\[
{C}_{1}^{-1}\left( {\left| Z\right|  - \frac{\left( {C}_{1} - 1\right) }{2}\sqrt{\delta }}\right)  \leq  \sqrt{\tau }\left| {X\left( \tau \right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{1}\left| Z\right|  + \frac{\left( {C}_{1} - 1\right) }{2}\sqrt{\delta }.
\]

From the formula given in Lemma 6.60 for \( {C}_{1} \) , it follows that, fixing the bound of the curvature and its derivatives, \( {C}_{1} \rightarrow  1 \) as \( \delta  \rightarrow  0 \) . Thus, with a given curvature bound, for \( \delta \) sufficiently small, \( \sqrt{\tau }\left| {X\left( \tau \right) }\right| \) is almost a constant along \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics. Hence, the integral of \( \sqrt{\tau }{\left| X\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2} \) is approximately \( 2\sqrt{\delta }{\left| Z\right| }^{2} \) . On the other hand, the absolute value of the integral of \( \sqrt{\tau }R\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is at most \( 2{C}_{0}{\delta }^{3/2}/3 \) where \( {C}_{0} \) is an upper bound for the absolute value of the scalar curvature.

Given \( R < \infty \) , choose \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small such that \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x} \) is a diffeomorphism on the ball of radius \( {9R} \) centered at the origin and such that the following estimate holds: The \( \mathcal{L} \) -length of an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic defined on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\delta }\right\rbrack \) with initial condition \( Z \) is between \( \sqrt{\delta }{\left| Z\right| }^{2} \) and \( 3\sqrt{\delta }{\left| Z\right| }^{2} \) . To ensure the latter estimate we need only take \( \delta \) sufficiently small, given the curvature bounds and the dimension. Hence, for these \( \delta \) no \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic with initial condition outside the ball of radius \( {9R} \) centered at the origin in \( {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) can be as short as any \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic with initial condition in the ball of radius \( R \) centered at the same point. This means that the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics defined on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\delta }\right\rbrack \) with initial condition \( \left| Z\right| \) with \( \left| Z\right|  < R \) are unique minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) - geodesics.

basis \( \left\{  {Y}_{\alpha }\right\} \) for \( {M}_{T - \tau } \) at \( {\gamma }_{Z}\left( \tau \right) \) . Notice that, letting \( {\tau }^{\prime } \) range from 0 to \( \tau \) and taking the push-forward of the \( {\partial }_{\alpha } \) under the differential at \( Z \) of \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x}^{{\tau }^{\prime }} \) produces a basis of \( \mathcal{L} \) -Jacobi fields \( \left\{  {{Y}_{\alpha }\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right\} \) along \( {\gamma }_{Z} \) . With this understood, we have:

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\ln \mathcal{J}{\left. \right| }_{\tau } = \frac{d}{d\tau }\ln \left( \sqrt{\det \left( \left\langle  {{Y}_{\alpha },{Y}_{\beta }}\right\rangle  \right) }\right)
\]

\[

\]

where \( {\widetilde{Y}}_{\alpha }\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) \) is the adapted vector field along \( \gamma \) with \( \widetilde{Y}\left( \tau \right)  = {Y}_{\alpha }\left( \tau \right) \) . Summing over \( \alpha \) as in the proof of Proposition 6.43 and Claim 6.44 yields

nodes.content: LEMMA 7.2. Assume that \( M \) is connected. Given \( {p}_{1},{p}_{2} \in  M \) and \( 0 \leq \; {\tau }_{1} < {\tau }_{2} \leq  T \) , there is a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic: \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},{\tau }_{2}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) connecting \( \left( {{p}_{1},{\tau }_{1}}\right) \) to \( \left( {{p}_{2},{\tau }_{2}}\right) \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 7.2. Assume that \( M \) is connected. Given \( {p}_{1},{p}_{2} \in M \) and \( 0 \leq \; {\tau }_{1} < {\tau }_{2} \leq T \) , there is a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic: \( \gamma : \left\lbrack {{\tau }_{1},{\tau }_{2}}\right\rbrack \rightarrow M \times \left\lbrack {0, T}\right\rbrack \) connecting \( \left( {{p}_{1},{\tau }_{1}}\right) \) to \( \left( {{p}_{2},{\tau }_{2}}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
For any curve \( \gamma \) parameterized by backward time, we set \( \bar{\gamma } \) equal to the path in \( M \) that is the image under projection of \( \gamma \) . We set \( A\left( s\right)  = {\bar{\gamma }}^{\prime }\left( s\right) \) . Define

\[
c\left( {\left( {{p}_{1},{\tau }_{1}}\right) ,\left( {{p}_{2},{\tau }_{2}}\right) }\right)  = \inf \left\{  {\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  \mid  \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},{\tau }_{2}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M,\bar{\gamma }\left( {\tau }_{1}\right)  = {p}_{1},\bar{\gamma }\left( {\tau }_{2}\right)  = {p}_{2}}\right\}  .
\]

From Equation (6.2) we see that the infimum exists since, by assumption, the curvature is uniformly bounded (below). Furthermore, for a minimizing sequence \( {\gamma }_{i} \) , we have \( {\int }_{{s}_{1}}^{{s}_{2}}{\left| {A}_{i}\left( s\right) \right| }^{2}{ds} \leq  {C}_{0} \) , for some constant \( {C}_{0} \) , where \( {s}_{i} = \sqrt{{\tau }_{i}} \) for \( i = 1,2 \) . It follows from this and the inequality in Equation (7.1) that there is a constant \( {C}_{1} < \infty \) such that for all \( i \) we have

\[
{\int }_{{s}_{1}}^{{s}_{2}}{\left| {A}_{i}\right| }_{g\left( 0\right) }^{2}{d\tau } \leq  {C}_{1}.
\]

Therefore the sequence \( \left\{  {\gamma }_{i}\right\} \) is uniformly continuous with respect to the metric \( g\left( 0\right) \) ; by Cauchy-Schwarz we have

\[
{\left| {\bar{\gamma }}_{i}\left( s\right)  - {\bar{\gamma }}_{i}\left( {s}^{\prime }\right) \right| }_{g\left( 0\right) } \leq  {\int }_{{s}^{\prime }}^{s}{\left| {A}_{i}\right| }_{g\left( 0\right) }{ds} \leq  \sqrt{{C}_{1}}\sqrt{s - {s}^{\prime }}.
\]

By the uniform continuity, we see that a subsequence of the \( {\gamma }_{i} \) converges uniformly pointwise to a continuous curve \( \gamma \) parameterized by \( s \) , the square root backward time. By passing to a subsequence we can arrange that the \( {\gamma }_{i} \) converge weakly in \( {H}^{2,1} \) . Of course, the limit in \( {H}^{2,1} \) is represented by the continuous limit \( \gamma \) . That is to say, after passing to a subsequence, the \( {\gamma }_{i} \) converge uniformly and weakly in \( {H}^{2,1} \) to a continuous curve \( \gamma \) . Let \( A\left( s\right) \) be the \( {L}^{2} \) -derivative of \( \gamma \) . Weak convergence in \( {H}^{2,1} \) implies that \( {\int }_{{s}^{\prime }}^{s}{\left| A\left( s\right) \right| }^{2}{ds} \leq  \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}{\int }_{{s}^{\prime }}^{s}{\left| {A}_{i}\left( s\right) \right| }^{2}{ds} \) , so that \( \mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{i}\right) \) . This means that \( \gamma \) minimizes the \( \mathcal{L} \) -length. Being a minimizer of \( \mathcal{L} \) -length, \( \gamma \) satisfies the Euler-Lagrange equation and is smooth by the regularity theorem of differential equations. This then is the required minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic from \( \left( {{p}_{1},{\tau }_{1}}\right) \) to \( \left( {{p}_{2},{\tau }_{2}}\right) \) .

\[
{\nabla }_{{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right)  = 2{s}^{2}\nabla R - {4s}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) , \cdot  }\right) .
\]

This is an everywhere non-singular ODE. Since the manifolds \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) are complete and their metrics are uniformly related as in Inequality (7.1), to show that the solution is defined on the entire interval \( s \in  \lbrack 0,\sqrt{T}) \) we need only show that there is a uniform bound to the length, or equivalently the energy of \( \gamma \) of any compact subinterval of \( \lbrack 0, T) \) on which it is defined. Fix \( \epsilon  > 0 \) . It follows immediately from Lemma 6.60, and the fact that the quantities \( R,\left| {\nabla R}\right| \) and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \) are bounded on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {\epsilon , T}\right\rbrack \) , that there is a bound on \( \max \left| {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right| \) in terms of \( \left| {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right| \) , for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\sqrt{T - \epsilon }}\right\rbrack \) for which \( \gamma \) is defined. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is complete, this, together with a standard extension result for second-order ODEs, implies that \( \gamma \) extends uniquely to the entire interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,\sqrt{T - \epsilon }}\right\rbrack \) . Changing the variable from \( s \) to \( \tau  = {s}^{2} \) shows that the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic extends uniquely to the entire interval \( \left\lbrack  {0, T - \epsilon }\right\rbrack \) . Since this is true for every \( \epsilon  > 0 \) , this completes the proof.

Proof. If \( \left( {q, T - \tau }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{U}}_{x} \) , then \( {l}_{x} \) is smooth near \( \left( {q, T - \tau }\right) \) , and the result is immediate from the first inequality in Corollary 6.51.

Now consider a general point \( \left( {q, t = T - \tau }\right) \) with \( 0 < t < T \) . According to Lemma 7.2 there is a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) from \( x = \left( {p, T}\right) \) to \( \left( {q, t = T - \tau }\right) \) . Let \( \gamma \) be any minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic between these points. Fix \( 0 < {\tau }_{1} < \tau \) let \( {q}_{1} = \gamma \left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \) and set \( {t}_{1} = T - {\tau }_{1} \) . Even though \( {q}_{1} \) is contained in the \( {t}_{1} \) time-slice, we keep \( \tau  = T - t \) so that paths beginning at \( {q}_{1} \) are parameterized by intervals in the \( \tau \) -line of the form \( \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},{\tau }^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) for some \( {\tau }^{\prime } < T \) . Consider \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\left( {q}_{1},{t}_{1}\right) } : {T}_{{q}_{1}}M \times  \left( {{\tau }_{1}, T}\right)  \rightarrow  M \times  \left( {0,{t}_{1}}\right) \) . According to Proposition 6.31 there is a neighborhood \( \widetilde{V} \) of \( \left\{  {\sqrt{{\tau }_{1}}{X}_{\gamma }\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right\}   \times  \left( {{\tau }_{1},\tau }\right\rbrack \) which is mapped diffeomorphically by \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\left( {q}_{1},{t}_{1}\right) } : {T}_{{q}_{1}}M \times  \left( {{\tau }_{1},\tau }\right)  \rightarrow  M \times  \left( {0,{t}_{1}}\right) \) onto a neighborhood \( V \) of \( \gamma \left( \left( {{\tau }_{1},\tau }\right) \right) \) . (Of course, the neighborhood \( V \) depends on \( {\tau }_{1} \) .) Let \( {L}_{\left( {q}_{1},{t}_{1}\right) } \) be the length function on \( V \) obtained by taking the \( \mathcal{L} \) -lengths of geodesics parameterized by points of \( \widetilde{V} \) . Let \( {\varphi }_{{\tau }_{1}} : V \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be defined by

\[
{\varphi }_{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {{q}^{\prime },{\tau }^{\prime }}\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }}}\left( {\mathcal{L}\left( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  0,{\tau }_{1}\right\rbrack  }\right)  + {L}_{\left( {q}_{1},{t}_{1}\right) }\left( {{q}^{\prime }, T - {\tau }^{\prime }}\right) }\right) .
\]

Clearly, \( {\varphi }_{{\tau }_{1}} \) is an upper barrier for \( {l}_{x} \) at \( \left( {q,\tau }\right) \) . According to Lemma 6.49 we have

\[
\frac{\partial {\varphi }_{{\tau }_{1}}}{d\tau }\left( {q,\tau }\right)  + \bigtriangleup {\varphi }_{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {q,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{n}{2\sqrt{\tau }\left( {\sqrt{\tau } - \sqrt{{\tau }_{1}}}\right) } - \frac{{\varphi }_{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {q,\tau }\right) }{\tau } + \frac{1}{2{\tau }^{3/2}}\mathcal{L}\left( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  0,{\tau }_{1}\right\rbrack  }\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{{K}_{{\tau }_{1}}^{\tau }\left( \gamma \right) }{2{\tau }^{3/2}} - \frac{{\mathcal{K}}_{{\tau }_{1}}^{\tau }\left( \gamma \right) }{2\sqrt{\tau }{\left( \sqrt{\tau } - \sqrt{{\tau }_{1}}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
- \frac{1}{2}{\left( \frac{{\tau }_{1}}{\tau }\right) }^{3/2}\left( {R\left( {{q}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  + {\left| X\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) .
\]

By Lemma 6.47, it follows easily that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{\tau }_{1} \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{\partial {\varphi }_{{\tau }_{1}}}{\partial \tau }\left( {q, t}\right)  + \bigtriangleup {\varphi }_{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {q, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{\left( {n/2}\right)  - {l}_{x}\left( {q, t}\right) }{\tau }.
\]

This establishes the result.

Furthermore, for every compact interval \( I \subset  \left( {0, T}\right) \) the subset of \( \left( {q,\tau }\right)  \in  M \times  I \) for which \( {l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right)  = {l}_{\min }\left( \tau \right) \) is a compact set.

nodes.proof:
Proof. In the case when \( M \) is compact, the claim is obvious. We consider the case when \( M \) is complete and the flow has bounded curvature. Since the curvature on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) is bounded, according to Inequality (7.1) there is a constant \( C \) such that for all \( t,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) we have

\[
{C}^{-1}g\left( {t}^{\prime }\right)  \leq  g\left( t\right)  \leq  {Cg}\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) .
\]

For any compact interval \( I \subset  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , there is \( {l}_{0} < \infty \) such that \( {l}_{\min }\left( \tau \right)  \leq  {l}_{0} \) for all \( \tau  \in  I \) . According to Corollary 6.61, for every \( \bar{\tau } \in  I \) and all \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics from \( x \) to points \( \left( {q, T - \bar{\tau }}\right) \) of lengths at most \( 2\left| {l}_{0}\right| \) there is an upper bound, say \( {C}_{2} \) , to \( \left| {\sqrt{\tau }{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right| \) . Thus, \( \left| {{X}_{\gamma }(\tau }\right|  \leq  \frac{{C}_{2}}{\sqrt{\tau }} \) , and hence

\[
{\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{g\left( T\right) } \leq  {C}_{2}\sqrt{C}/\sqrt{\tau }
\]

for these geodesics. Thus,

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}{\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{g\left( T\right) }{d\tau } \leq  2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}{C}_{2}\sqrt{C}.
\]

This shows that there is \( A < \infty \) such that for each \( \bar{\tau } \in  I \) and for any \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) defined on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) of length at most \( 2\left| {l}_{0}\right| \) the following holds. Letting \( q \in  M \) be such that \( \gamma \left( \bar{\tau }\right)  = \left( {q, T - \tau }\right) \) , the point \( q \) lies in \( {B}_{T}\left( {p, A}\right) \) . This implies that the endpoints of all such \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics lie in a fixed compact subset of \( M \) independent of \( \bar{\tau } \in  I \) and the geodesic. Since the set of \( \left( {q,\tau }\right) \) where \( {l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right)  = {l}_{\min }\left( \tau \right) \) is clearly a closed set, it follows that the subset of \( M \times  I \) of all \( \left( {q,\tau }\right)  \in  M \times  I \) for which \( {l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right)  = {l}_{\min }\left( \tau \right) \) is compact. The last thing to show is that for every \( \tau  \in  I \) the function \( {l}_{x}\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right) \) achieves its minimum. Fix \( \tau  \in  I \) and let \( {q}_{n} \) be a minimizing sequence for \( {l}_{x}\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right) \) . We have already established that the \( {q}_{n} \) are contained in a compact subset of \( M \) , and hence we can assume that they converge to a limit \( q \in  M \) . Clearly, by the continuity of \( {l}_{x} \) we have \( {l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{n \rightarrow  \infty }}{l}_{x}\left( {{q}_{n},\tau }\right)  = \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{{q}^{\prime } \in  M}}{l}_{x}\left( {{q}^{\prime },\tau }\right) \) , so that \( {l}_{x}\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right) \) achieves its minimum at \( q \) .

COROLLARY 7.12. Suppose that \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) is a generalized \( n \) -dimensional Ricci flow and that \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) is given and set \( {t}_{0} = \mathbf{t}\left( x\right) \) . We suppose that there is an open subset \( U \subset  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( {-\infty ,{t}_{0}}\right) \) with the following properties:

(1) For every \( y \in  U \) there is a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic from \( x \) to \( y \) .

(2) There are \( r > 0 \) and \( {\Delta t} > 0 \) such that the backward parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {x,{t}_{0}, r, - {\Delta t}}\right) \) of \( x \) exists in \( \mathcal{M} \) and has the property that \( P \cap  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( {-\infty ,{t}_{0}}\right) \) is contained in \( U \) .

(3) For each compact interval (including the case of degenerate intervals consisting of a single point) \( I \subset  \left( {-\infty ,{t}_{0}}\right) \) the subset of points \( y \in  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( I\right)  \cap  U \) for which \( \mathcal{L}\left( y\right)  = \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{z \in  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( {\mathbf{t}\left( y\right) }\right)  \cap  U}}\mathcal{L}\left( z\right) \) is compact and non-empty.

Then for every \( t < {t}_{0} \) the minimum of the restriction of \( {l}_{x} \) to the time-slice \( {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( t\right)  \cap  U \) is at most \( n/2 \) .

nodes.label: Theorem 7.13
nodes.document_title: John Morgan and Gang Tian - Ricci Flow and the Poincare Conjecture
nodes.content:
THEOREM 7.13. Let \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,0 \leq  t \leq  T < \infty \) , be a Ricci flow, complete and of bounded curvature, and let \( x = \left( {p, T}\right)  \in  M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . The last two inequalities in Corollary 6.51, namely

\[
\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau } - \bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^{\tau } \geq  0,
\]

\[
- {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{{l}_{x}^{\tau } - n}{\tau } + 2\bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^{\tau } \leq  0
\]

hold in the weak or distributional sense on all of \( M \times  \{ \tau \} \) for all \( \tau  > 0 \) . This means that for any \( \tau  > 0 \) and for any non-negative, compactly supported, smooth function \( \phi \left( q\right) \) on \( M \) we have the following two inequalities:

\[
{\int }_{M\times \{ \tau \} }\left\lbrack  {\phi  \cdot  \left( {\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right)  - {l}_{x}^{\tau }\bigtriangleup \phi }\right\rbrack  d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq  0,
\]

\[
{\int }_{M\times \{ \tau \} }\left\lbrack  {\phi  \cdot  \left( {-{\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{{l}_{x}^{\tau } - n}{\tau }}\right)  + 2{l}_{x}^{\tau }\bigtriangleup \phi }\right\rbrack  d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Furthermore, equality holds in either of these weak inequalities for all functions \( \phi \) as above and all \( \tau \) if and only if it holds in both. In that case \( {l}_{x} \) is a smooth function on space-time and the equalities hold in the usual smooth sense.

The last two inequalities in Corollary 6.51, namely \[ \frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau } - \bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^...

nodes.proof:
Proof. Let \( \phi  : M \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a non-negative, smooth function of compact support. Cover \( M \) by open subsets of the form \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) as above. Using a partition of unity we can write \( \phi  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{i}{\phi }_{i} \) where each \( {\phi }_{i} \) is a non-negative smooth function supported in some \( {B}_{\left( {q}_{i}, t\right) }^{\prime } \) . Since the inequalities we are trying to establish are linear in \( \phi \) , it suffices to prove the result for each \( {\phi }_{i} \) .

This allows us to assume (and we shall assume) that \( \phi \) is supported in \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) for some \( q \in  M \) .

Since \( {l}_{x}^{\tau } \) is a locally Lipschitz function, the restriction of \( {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} \) to \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) is an \( {L}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) -function. Similarly, \( \partial {l}_{x}/\partial \tau \) is an \( {L}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) -function. Hence

\[
{\int }_{{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }}\phi  \cdot  \left( {\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{{\left( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }\right) }^{ * }}\phi \left( {\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

On the other hand, by Corollary 7.24 we have

\[
{\int }_{{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }}{l}_{x}^{\tau }\bigtriangleup {\phi d}\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  {\int }_{{\left( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }\right) }^{ * }}\phi \bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^{\tau }d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

Putting these together we see

\[
{\int }_{{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }}\phi \left( {\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right)  - {l}_{x}^{\tau }\bigtriangleup {\phi d}\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {\int }_{{\left( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }\right) }^{ * }}\phi \left( {\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau } - \bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^{\tau }}\right) d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

It follows immediately from the second inequality in Corollary 6.51 that, since \( \phi  \geq  0 \) and \( {\left( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }\right) }^{ * } \subset  {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) , we have

\[
{\int }_{{\left( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }\right) }^{ * }}\phi \left( {\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau } - \bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^{\tau }}\right) d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq  0.
\]

This proves the first inequality in the statement of the theorem.

The second inequality in the statement of the theorem is proved in the same way using the third inequality in Corollary 6.51.

Now let us consider the distributions

\[
{D}_{1} = \frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau } - \bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^{\tau }
\]

and

\[
{D}_{2} =  - {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{{l}_{x}^{\tau } - n}{\tau } + 2\bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^{\tau }
\]

on \( M \times  \{ \tau \} \) . According to Corollary 6.51 the following equality holds on \( {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \)

\[
2\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{{l}_{x}^{\tau }}{\tau } = 0.
\]

By Proposition 7.5 the open set \( {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) has full measure in \( M \) and \( {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} \) and \( \partial {l}_{x}/\partial \tau \) are locally essentially bounded. Thus, this equality is an equality of locally essentially bounded, measurable functions, i.e., elements of \( {L}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty }\left( M\right) \) , and hence is an equality of distributions on \( M \) . Subtracting \( 2{D}_{1} \) from this equality yields \( {D}_{2} \) . Thus,

\[
{D}_{2} =  - 2{D}_{1},
\]

as distributions on \( M \) . This shows that \( {D}_{2} \) vanishes as a distribution if and only if \( {D}_{1} \) does. But if \( {D}_{2} = 0 \) as a distribution for some \( \tau \) , then by elliptic regularity \( {l}_{x}^{\tau } \) is smooth on \( M \times  \{ \tau \} \) and the equality is the naïve one for smooth functions. Thus, if \( {D}_{2} = 0 \) for all \( \tau \) , then \( {l}_{x}^{\tau } \) and \( \partial l/\partial \tau \) are \( {C}^{\infty } \) functions on each slice \( M \times  \{ \tau \} \) and both \( {D}_{1} \) and \( {D}_{2} \) hold in the naïve sense on each slice \( M \times  \{ \tau \} \) . It follows from a standard bootstrap argument that in this case \( {l}_{x}^{\tau } \) is smooth on all of space-time.

nodes.document_title: John Morgan and Gang Tian - Ricci Flow and the Poincare Conjecture
nodes.content:
REMARK 7.14. The terms in these inequalities are interpreted in the following way: First of all, \( \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau } \) and \( \bigtriangleup {l}_{x}^{\tau } \) are computed using only the spatial derivatives (i.e., they are horizontal differential operators). Secondly, since \( {l}_{x} \) is a locally Lipschitz function defined on all of \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , we have seen that \( \partial {l}_{x}/\partial t \) and \( {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} \) are continuous functions on the open subset \( {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) of full measure in \( M \times  \{ \tau \} \) and furthermore, that they are locally bounded on all of \( M \times  \{ \tau \} \) in the sense that for any \( q \in  M \) there is a neighborhood \( V \) of \( q \) such that the restriction of \( {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} \) to \( V \cap  {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) is bounded. This means that \( \partial {l}_{x}/\partial t \) and \( {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} \) are elements of \( {L}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty }\left( M\right) \) and hence can be integrated against any smooth function with compact support. In particular, they are distributions.

Since \( \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau } \) is a smooth, locally bounded vector field on an open subset of full measure, for any compactly supported test function \( \phi \) , integration by parts yields

\[
\int {\Delta \phi } \cdot  {l}_{x}^{\tau }d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  =  - \int \left\langle  {\nabla \phi ,\nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }}\right\rangle  d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

Thus, formulas in Theorem 7.13 can also be taken to mean:

\[
{\int }_{M\times \{ \tau \} }\left\lbrack  {\phi  \cdot  \left( {\frac{\partial {l}_{x}}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right)  + \left\langle  {\nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau },\nabla \phi }\right\rangle  }\right\rbrack  d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq  0,
\]

\[
{\int }_{M\times \{ \tau \} }\left\lbrack  {\phi  \cdot  \left( {-{\left| \nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{{l}_{x}^{\tau } - n}{\tau }}\right)  - 2\left\langle  {\nabla {l}_{x}^{\tau },\nabla \phi }\right\rangle  }\right\rbrack  d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  0.
\]

LEMMA 7.15. There is a continuous function \( C : M \times  \left( {0, T}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) such that for each point \( \left( {q, t}\right)  \in  M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , setting \( \tau  = T - t \) , the following holds. There is an upper barrier \( {\varphi }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) for \( {L}_{x}^{\tau } \) at the point \( q \) defined on a neighborhood \( {U}_{\left( q, t\right) } \) of \( q \) in \( M \) satisfying \( \left| {\nabla {\varphi }_{\left( q, t\right) }\left( q\right) }\right|  \leq  C\left( {q, t}\right) \) and

\[
\operatorname{Hess}\left( \varphi \right) \left( {v, v}\right)  \leq  C\left( {q, t}\right) {\left| v\right| }^{2}
\]

for all tangent vectors \( v \in  {T}_{q}M \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. By Proposition 7.5, \( L \) is a locally Lipschitz function on \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , and in particular is continuous. The bound \( C\left( {q, t}\right) \) will depend only on the bounds on curvature and its first two derivatives and on the function \( L\left( {q, t}\right) \) . Fix \( \left( {q, t}\right) \) and let \( \gamma \) be a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic from \( x \) to \( \left( {q, t}\right) \) . (The existence of such a minimizing geodesic is established in Lemma 7.2.) Fix \( {\tau }_{1} > 0 \) , with \( {\tau }_{1} < \left( {T - t}\right) /2 \) , let \( {t}_{1} = T - {\tau }_{1} \) , and let \( {q}_{1} = \gamma \left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \) . Consider \( {\varphi }_{\left( q, t\right) } = \mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{\left\lbrack  0,{\tau }_{1}\right\rbrack  }\right)  + {L}_{\left( {q}_{1},{t}_{1}\right) }^{\tau } \) . This is an upper barrier for \( {L}_{x}^{\tau } \) at \( q \)

defined in some neighborhood \( V \subset  M \) of \( q \) . Clearly, \( \nabla {\varphi }_{\left( q, t\right) } = \nabla {L}_{\left( {q}_{1},{t}_{1}\right) }^{\tau } \) and \( \operatorname{Hess}\left( {{\varphi }_{\left( q, t\right) } = \operatorname{Hess}\left( {L}_{\left( {q}_{1},{t}_{1}\right) }^{\tau }\right) .}\right. \)

According to Corollary 6.29 we have \( \nabla {L}_{\left( {q}_{1},{t}_{1}\right) }^{\tau }\left( q\right)  = 2\sqrt{\tau }{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \) . On the other hand, by Corollary 6.61 there is a bound on \( \sqrt{\tau }\left| {{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right| \) depending only on the bounds on curvature and its first derivatives, on \( \tau \) and \( {\tau }_{1} \) and on \( {l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right) \) . Of course, by Shi’s theorem (Theorem 3.27) for every \( \epsilon  > 0 \) the norms of the first derivatives of curvature on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {\epsilon , T}\right\rbrack \) are bounded in terms of \( \epsilon \) and the bounds on curvature. This proves that \( \left| {\nabla {\varphi }_{\left( q, t\right) }\left( q\right) }\right| \) is bounded by a continuous function \( C\left( {q, t}\right) \) defined on all of \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) .

Now consider Inequality (6.11) for \( \gamma \) at \( \bar{\tau } = \tau \) . It is clear that the first two terms on the right-hand side are bounded by \( C{\left| Y\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2} \) , where \( C \) depends on the curvature bound and on \( T - t \) . We consider the last term, \( {\int }_{{\tau }_{1}}^{\tau }\sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }}H\left( {X, Y}\right) d{\tau }^{\prime } \) . We claim that this integral is also bounded by \( {C}^{\prime }{\left| Y\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2} \) where \( {C}^{\prime } \) depends on the bounds on curvature and its first and second derivatives along \( {\gamma }_{1} \) and on \( T - t \) . We consider \( {\tau }^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},\tau }\right\rbrack \) . Of course, \( \sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }}\left| {X\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right| \) is bounded on this interval. Also,

\[
\left| {Y\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right|  = \left( \frac{\sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }} - \sqrt{{\tau }_{1}}}{\sqrt{\tau } - \sqrt{{\tau }_{1}}}\right) \left| {Y\left( \tau \right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{\sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }}}{\sqrt{\tau }}\left| {Y\left( \tau \right) }\right| .
\]

Hence \( \left| {Y\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right| /\sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }} \) and \( \left| {Y\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right| \left| {X\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right| \) are bounded in terms of \( T - t,\left| {Y\left( \tau \right) }\right| \) , and the bound on \( \sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }}\left| {X\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right| \) along the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic. It then follows from Equation (6.12) that \( H\left( {X, Y}\right) \) is bounded along the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic by \( C{\left| Y\left( \bar{\tau }\right) \right| }^{2} \) where the constant \( C \) depends on \( T - t \) and the bounds on curvature and its first two derivatives.

Of course, if \( \left( {q, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) , then this argument shows that the Hessian of \( {L}_{x}^{\tau } \) is bounded near \( \left( {q, t}\right) \) .

At this point in the proof of Theorem 7.13 we wish to employ arguments using convexity. To carry these out we find it convenient to work with a Euclidean metric and usual convexity rather than the given metric \( g\left( t\right) \) and convexity measured using \( g\left( t\right) \) -geodesics. In order to switch to a Euclidean metric we must find one that well approximates \( g\left( t\right) \) . The following is straightforward to prove.

CLAIM 7.20. Fix \( \left( {q, t}\right)  \in  M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , and let \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } : {B}_{\left( q, t\right) } \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be as above. Let \( S \subset  M \) be the singular locus of \( {L}^{\tau } \) , i.e., \( S = M \smallsetminus  {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) . Set \( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) } = {B}_{\left( q, t\right) } \cap  S \) . Of course, \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) is smooth on \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) } \smallsetminus  {S}_{\left( q, t\right) } \) . Then there is a sequence of smooth functions \( {\left\{  {f}_{k} : {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}\right\}  }_{k = 1}^{\infty } \) with the following properties:

(1) As \( k \rightarrow  \infty \) the functions \( {f}_{k} \) converge uniformly to \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) on \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) .

(2) For any \( \epsilon  > 0 \) sufficiently small, let \( {\nu }_{\epsilon }\left( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) }\right) \) be the \( \epsilon \) -neighborhood (with respect to the Euclidean metric) in \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) } \) of \( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) } \cap  {B}_{\left( q, t\right) } \) . Then, as \( k \rightarrow  \infty \) the restrictions of \( {f}_{k} \) to \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \smallsetminus  \left( {{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \cap  {\nu }_{\epsilon }\left( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) }\right) }\right) \) converge uniformly in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) -topology to the restriction of \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) to this subset.

(3) For each \( k \) , and for any \( z \in  {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) and any \( v \in  {T}_{z}M \) we have

\[
\operatorname{Hess}\left( {f}_{k}\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  \leq   - {\left| v\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}/2.
\]

That is to say, \( {f}_{k} \) is strictly convex with respect to the metric \( g\left( t\right) \) .

Proof. Fix \( \epsilon  > 0 \) sufficiently small so that for any \( z \in  {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) the Euclidean \( \epsilon \) -ball centered at \( z \) is contained in \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) } \) . Let \( {B}_{0} \) be the ball of radius \( \epsilon \) centered at the origin in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) and let \( \xi  : {B}_{0} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a non-negative \( {C}^{\infty } \) - function with compact support and with \( {\int }_{{B}_{0}}{\xi d}{\operatorname{vol}}_{h} = 1 \) . We define

\[
{\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\epsilon }\left( z\right)  = {\int }_{{B}_{0}}\xi \left( y\right) {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }\left( {z + y}\right) {dy},
\]

for all \( z \in  {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) . It is clear that for each \( \epsilon  > 0 \) sufficiently small, the function \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\epsilon } : {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is \( {C}^{\infty } \) and that as \( \epsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) the \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\epsilon } \) converge uniformly on \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) to \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) . It is also clear that for every \( \epsilon  > 0 \) sufficiently small, the conclusion of Corollary 7.19 holds for \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\epsilon } \) and for each Euclidean straight-line segment \( \alpha \) in \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) . This implies that \( {\operatorname{Hess}}^{h}\left( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\epsilon }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  \leq   - 3{\left| v\right| }_{h}^{2}/2 \) , and hence that by Inequality (7.2) that

\[
\operatorname{Hess}\left( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\epsilon }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  \leq   - {\left| v\right| }_{h}^{2} =  - {\left| v\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}/2.
\]

This means that \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\epsilon } \) is convex with respect to \( g\left( t\right) \) . Now take a sequence \( {\epsilon }_{k} \rightarrow  0 \) and let \( {f}_{k} = {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }^{{\epsilon }_{k}} \) . Lastly, it is a standard fact that \( {f}_{k} \) converge uniformly in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) -topology to \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) on any subset of \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) whose closure is disjoint from \( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) } \) .

Proof. Since \( {f}_{k} \rightarrow  {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) uniformly on \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) we have

\[
{\int }_{{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }}{\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }\bigtriangleup {\phi d}\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\int }_{{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }}{f}_{k}\bigtriangleup {\phi d}\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

Since \( {f}_{k} \) is strictly convex with respect to the metric \( g\left( t\right) ,\bigtriangleup {f}_{k} \leq  0 \) on all of \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) . Since \( \phi  \geq  0 \) , for every \( \epsilon \) and \( k \) we have

\[
{\int }_{{\nu }_{\epsilon }\left( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) }\right)  \cap  {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }}\phi \bigtriangleup {f}_{k}d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Hence, for every \( k \) and for every \( \epsilon \) we have

\[

\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \smallsetminus  \left( {{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \cap  {\nu }_{\epsilon }\left( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) }\right) }\right) }\phi \bigtriangleup {f}_{k}d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

Taking the limit as \( k \rightarrow  \infty \) , using the fact that \( {f}_{k} \rightarrow  {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) uniformly on \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \) and that restricted to \( {B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \smallsetminus  \left( {{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \cap  {\nu }_{\epsilon }\left( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) }\right) }\right) \) the \( {f}_{k} \) converge uniformly in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) -topology to \( {\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) } \) , yields

\[
{\int }_{{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime }}{\beta }_{\left( q, t\right) }\bigtriangleup {\phi d}\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  {\int }_{{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \smallsetminus  \left( {{B}_{\left( q, t\right) }^{\prime } \cap  {\nu }_{\epsilon }\left( {S}_{\left( q, t\right) }\right) }\right) }\phi \bigtriangleup {\beta }_{q}d\operatorname{vol}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

Now taking the limit as \( \epsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) establishes the claim.

By symmetry we can assume that \( x = \left( {0, T}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , where \( 0 \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) is the origin. Thus, identifying \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) with \( {T}_{0}{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , for any \( X \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) we have \( {\gamma }_{X}\left( \tau \right)  = 2\sqrt{\tau }X \) , and hence \( \mathcal{L}\exp \left( {X,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}X \) . Thus, for any \( \tau  > 0 \) we have \( \mathcal{U}\left( \tau \right)  = {T}_{p}M \) , and for any \( X \in  {T}_{0}{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) we have \( \mathcal{J}\left( {X,\tau }\right)  = {2}^{n}{\tau }^{n/2} \) . \[

\]

THEOREM 7.26. Let \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,0 \leq  t \leq  T \) , be a Ricci flow of bounded curvature with the property that for each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) the Riemannian manifold \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is complete. Fix a point \( x = \left( {p, T}\right)  \in  M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . For every \( 0 < \tau  < T \) the reduced volume

\[
{\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right)  = {\int }_{M}{\tau }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-{l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right) {dq}
\]

is absolutely convergent and \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right)  \leq  {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{\frac{n}{2}} \) . The function \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right) \) is a non-increasing function of \( \tau \) with

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right)  = {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{\frac{n}{2}}.
\]

By Proposition 7.5, \( {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) is an open subset of full measure in \( M \) . Hence,

\[
{\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right)  = {\int }_{{\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) }{\tau }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-{l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right) {dq}.
\]

Take linear orthonormal coordinates \( \left( {{z}^{1},\ldots ,{z}^{n}}\right) \) on \( {T}_{p}M \) . It follows from the previous equality and Lemma 6.71 that

\[
{\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right)  = {\int }_{{\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) }f\left( {Z,\tau }\right) d{z}^{1}\cdots d{z}^{n},
\]

where \( f\left( {Z,\tau }\right)  = {\tau }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\widetilde{l}\left( {Z,\tau }\right) }\mathcal{J}\left( {Z,\tau }\right) \) . By Proposition 6.81 for each \( Z \) the integrand, \( f\left( {Z,\tau }\right) \) , is a non-increasing function of \( \tau \) and the function converges uniformly on compact sets as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) to \( {2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} \) . This implies that \( f\left( {Z,\tau }\right)  \leq  {2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| Z\right| }^{2}} \) for all \( \tau  > 0 \) , and hence that

\[
{\int }_{{\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) }f\left( {Z,\tau }\right) d{z}^{1}\cdots d{z}^{n}
\]

converges absolutely for each \( \tau  > 0 \) , and the integral has value at most \( {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{n/2} \) .

Fix \( 0 < {\tau }_{0} < T \) . According to Theorem 6.80 (with \( A = M \times  \left( {T - {\tau }_{0}, T}\right) \) ), the reduced volume \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right) \) is a non-increasing function of \( \tau \) on \( \left( {0,{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Since this is true for any \( 0 < {\tau }_{0} < T \) , it follows that \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right) \) is a nonincreasing function of \( \tau \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . (This of course is a consequence of the monotonicity of \( f\left( {Z,\tau }\right) \) in \( \tau \) and the fact that \( {\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}}_{x}\left( \tau \right)  \subset  {\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}}_{x}\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) \) for \( \left. {{\tau }^{\prime } < \tau \text{ . }}\right) \)

To show that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right)  = {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{n/2} \) we need only see that for each \( A < \infty \) for all \( \tau  > 0 \) sufficiently small, \( {\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}}_{x}\left( \tau \right) \) contains the ball of radius \( A \) centered at the origin in \( {T}_{p}M \) . Since the curvature is bounded, this is exactly the content of Corollary 6.79.

Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) ,0 \leq  \tau  \leq  T \) , is a solution to the backward Ricci flow equation, complete and of bounded curvature. Let \( x = \left( {p, T}\right)  \in  M \times  \{ T\} \) , and suppose that \( 0 < \bar{\tau } < T \) . If \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{n/2} \) , then the backward Ricci flow on the interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) is the trivial flow on flat Euclidean space.

If \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\bar{\tau }}\right) = {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{n/2} \) , then the backward Ricci flow on the in...

nodes.proof:
If \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{n/2} \) , then by Lemma 7.25, \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right) \) is constant on the interval \( (0,\bar{\tau }\rbrack \) . Hence, it follows from the proof of Theorem 7.26 that the closure of \( \widetilde{\mathcal{U}}\left( \tau \right) \) is all of \( {T}_{p}M \) for all \( \tau  \in  (0,\bar{\tau }\rbrack \) and that \( f\left( {Z,\tau }\right)  = {e}^{-{\left| Z\right| }^{2}}{2}^{n} \) for all \( Z \in  {T}_{p}M \) and all \( \tau  \leq  \bar{\tau } \) . In particular,

\[
\frac{\partial \ln \left( {f\left( {Z,\tau }\right) }\right) }{\partial \tau } = 0.
\]

From the proof of Proposition 6.81 this means that Inequality (6.20) is an equality and consequently, so is Inequality (6.19). Thus, by Proposition 6.37 (with \( {\tau }_{1} = 0 \) ) each of the vector fields \( {Y}_{\alpha }\left( \tau \right)  = {\widetilde{Y}}_{\alpha }\left( \tau \right) \) is both a Jacobi field and adapted. By Proposition 6.43 we then have

\[
\operatorname{Ric} + \operatorname{Hess}\left( {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right)  = \frac{g}{2\tau }.
\]

In particular, \( {l}_{x} \) is smooth. Let \( {\varphi }_{\tau } : M \rightarrow  M,0 < \tau  \leq  \bar{\tau } \) , be the one-parameter family of diffeomorphisms obtained by solving

\[
\frac{d{\varphi }_{\tau }}{d\tau } = \nabla {l}_{x}\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right) \;\text{ and }\;{\varphi }_{\bar{\tau }} = \mathrm{{Id}}.
\]

We now consider

\[
h\left( \tau \right)  = \frac{\bar{\tau }}{\tau }{\varphi }_{\tau }^{ * }g\left( \tau \right) .
\]

We compute

\[
\frac{\partial h}{\partial \tau } =  - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{{\tau }^{2}}{\varphi }_{\tau }^{ * }g\left( \tau \right)  + \frac{\bar{\tau }}{\tau }{\varphi }_{\tau }^{ * }{\mathcal{L}}_{\frac{d\varphi \tau }{d\tau }}\left( {g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  + \frac{\bar{\tau }}{\tau }{\varphi }_{t}^{ * }2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {g\left( \tau \right) }\right)
\]

\[
=  - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{{\tau }^{2}}{\varphi }_{\tau }^{ * }g\left( \tau \right)  + \frac{\bar{\tau }}{\tau }{\varphi }_{\tau }^{ * }2\operatorname{Hess}\left( {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right)  + \frac{\bar{\tau }}{\tau }{\varphi }_{\tau }^{ * }\left( {\frac{1}{\tau }g\left( \tau \right)  - 2\operatorname{Hess}\left( {l}_{x}^{\tau }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= 0\text{ . }
\]

That is to say the family of metrics \( h\left( \tau \right) \) is constant in \( \tau \) : for all \( \tau  \in  (0,\bar{\tau }\rbrack \) we have \( h\left( \tau \right)  = h\left( \bar{\tau }\right)  = g\left( \bar{\tau }\right) \) . It then follows that

\[
g\left( \tau \right)  = \frac{\tau }{\bar{\tau }}{\left( {\varphi }_{\tau }^{-1}\right) }^{ * }g\left( \bar{\tau }\right) ,
\]

which means that the entire flow in the interval \( (0,\bar{\tau }\rbrack \) differs by diffeomorphism and scaling from \( g\left( \bar{\tau }\right) \) . Suppose that \( g\left( \bar{\tau }\right) \) is not flat, i.e., suppose that there is some \( \left( {x,\bar{\tau }}\right) \) with \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,\bar{\tau }}\right) }\right|  = K > 0 \) . Then from the flow equation we see that \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\varphi }_{\tau }^{-1}\left( x\right) ,\tau }\right) }\right|  = K{\bar{\tau }}^{2}/{\tau }^{2} \) , and these curvatures are not bounded as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) . This is a contradiction. We conclude that \( g\left( \bar{\tau }\right) \) is flat, and hence, again by the flow equation so are all the \( g\left( \tau \right) \) for \( 0 < \tau  \leq  \bar{\tau } \) , and by continuity, so is \( g\left( 0\right) \) . Thus, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is isometric to a quotient of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) by a free, properly discontinuous group action. Lastly, since \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {M,\tau }\right)  = {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{n/2} \) , it follows that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is isometric to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) for every \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . Of course, it then follows that the flow is the constant flow.

nodes.section_title: 8.1. A non-collapsing result for generalized Ricci flows
nodes.content:
THEOREM 8.1. Fix positive constants \( {\bar{\tau }}_{0} < \infty ,{l}_{0} < \infty \) , and \( V > 0 \) . Then there is \( \kappa  > 0 \) depending on \( {\bar{\tau }}_{0}, V \) , and \( {l}_{0} \) and the dimension \( n \) such that the following holds. Let \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) be a generalized \( n \) -dimensional Ricci flow, and let \( 0 < {\tau }_{0} \leq  {\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) . Let \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) be fixed. Set \( T = \mathbf{t}\left( x\right) \) . Suppose that \( 0 < r \leq  \sqrt{{\tau }_{0}} \) is given. These data are required to satisfy:

(1) The ball \( B\left( {x, T, r}\right)  \subset  {M}_{T} \) has compact closure.

(2) There is an embedding \( B\left( {x, T, r}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {T - {r}^{2}, T}\right\rbrack   \subset  \mathcal{M} \) compatible with t and with the vector field.

(3) \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) on the image of the embedding in (2).

(4) There is an open subset \( \widetilde{W} \subset  {\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}}_{x}\left( {\tau }_{0}\right)  \subset  {T}_{x}{M}_{T} \) with the property that for every \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) with initial condition contained in \( \widetilde{W} \) , the l-length of \( \gamma \) is at most \( {l}_{0} \) .

(5) For each \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , let \( W\left( \tau \right)  = \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x}^{\tau }\left( \widetilde{W}\right) \) . The volume of the image \( W\left( {\tau }_{0}\right)  \subset  {M}_{T - {\tau }_{0}} \) is at least \( V \) .

Then

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {B\left( {x, T, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}^{n}\text{ . }
\]

See FIG. 1.

In this section we denote by \( g\left( \tau \right) ,0 \leq  \tau  \leq  {r}^{2} \) , the family of metrics on \( B\left( {x, T, r}\right) \) induced from pulling back \( G \) under the embedding \( B\left( {x, T, r}\right)  \times \; \left\lbrack  {T - {r}^{2}, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) . Of course, this family of metrics satisfies the backward Ricci flow equation.

nodes.content:
Proposition 8.2. There is a positive constant \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \leq  1/{4n}\left( {n - 1}\right) \) depending on \( {\bar{\tau }}_{0} \) and \( {l}_{0} \) such that if \( \varepsilon  \leq  {\varepsilon }_{0} \) then, setting \( {\tau }_{1} = \varepsilon {r}^{2} \) , we have \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {W\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right)  < 3{\varepsilon }^{\frac{n}{2}}. \)

Given this proposition, it follows immediately that either \( \varepsilon  > {\varepsilon }_{0} \) or

\[
\varepsilon  \geq  {\left( \frac{{\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {W\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right) }{3}\right) }^{2/n} \geq  \frac{1}{{3}^{2/n}{\bar{\tau }}_{0}}{V}^{2/n}{e}^{-2{l}_{0}/n}.
\]

Since \( \kappa  = {\varepsilon }^{n} \) , this proves the theorem.

Proof. We divide \( \widetilde{W} \) into

\[
{\widetilde{W}}_{\mathrm{{sm}}} = \widetilde{W} \cap  \left\{  {Z \in  {T}_{x}{M}_{T}\left| \right| Z \mid   \leq  \frac{1}{8}{\varepsilon }^{-1/2}}\right\}
\]

and

\[
{\widetilde{W}}_{\mathrm{{lg}}} = \widetilde{W} \smallsetminus  {\widetilde{W}}_{\mathrm{{sm}}},
\]

(see FIG. 2).

![019eafd8-fdc6-7b80-ae12-d1283dd2df0a_13_470_452_857_452_0.jpg](images/019eafd8-fdc6-7b80-ae12-d1283dd2df0a_13_470_452_857_452_0.jpg)

We set \( {W}_{\mathrm{{sm}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right)  = \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x}^{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {\widetilde{W}}_{\mathrm{{sm}}}\right) \) and \( {W}_{\mathrm{{lg}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right)  = \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{x}^{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {\widetilde{W}}_{\mathrm{{lg}}}\right) \) . Clearly, since \( W\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \) is the union of \( {W}_{\mathrm{{sm}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \) and \( {W}_{\mathrm{{lg}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \) and since these subsets are disjoint measurable subsets, we have

\[
{\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {W\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right)  = {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {{W}_{\mathrm{{sm}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right)  + {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {{W}_{\mathrm{{lg}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right) .
\]

We shall show that there is \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \) such that either \( \varepsilon  > {\varepsilon }_{0} \) or \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {{W}_{\mathrm{{sm}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right)  \leq \; 2{\varepsilon }^{n/2} \) and \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {{W}_{\lg }\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right)  \leq  {\varepsilon }^{n/2} \) . This will establish Proposition 8.2 and hence Theorem 8.1.

1.1. Upper bound for \( {\widetilde{V}}_{x}\left( {{W}_{\mathrm{{sm}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) }\right) \) . The idea here is that \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics with initial vector in \( {\widetilde{W}}_{\mathrm{{sm}}} \) remain in the parabolic neighborhood

\[
P = B\left( {x, T, r}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {T - {r}^{2}, T}\right\rbrack
\]

for all parameter values \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{r}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Once we know this it is easy to see that their \( \mathcal{L} \) -lengths are bounded from below. Then if the volume of \( B\left( {x, T, r}\right) \) was arbitrarily small, the reduced volume of \( {W}_{\mathrm{{sm}}}\left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \) would be arbitrarily small.

Then for any \( {t}_{0} \leq  T \) , any \( r > 0 \) with \( {r}^{2} \leq  {t}_{0} \) and any \( \left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  M \times  \left\{  {t}_{0}\right\} \) , if \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {q, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) on \( B\left( {p,{t}_{0}, r}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) then \( \operatorname{Vol}B\left( {p,{t}_{0}, r}\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}^{3} \) .

nodes.proof:
Fix any \( x = \left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . First, we claim that we can suppose that \( {t}_{0} \geq  1 \) . For if not, then rescale the flow by \( Q = 1/{t}_{0} \) . This does not affect the curvature inequality at time 0 . Furthermore, there is \( {\omega }^{\prime } > 0 \) depending only on \( \omega \) such that for any ball \( B \) at time 0 and of radius 1 in the rescaled flow we have Vol \( B \geq  {\omega }^{\prime } \) . The reason for the latter fact is the following: By the Bishop-Gromov inequality (Theorem 1.34) there is \( {\omega }^{\prime } > 0 \) depending only on \( \omega \) such that for any \( q \in  M \) and any \( r \leq  1 \) we have Vol \( B\left( {q,0, r}\right)  \geq  {\omega }^{\prime }{r}^{3} \) . Of course, the rescaling increases \( T \) , but simply restrict to the rescaled flow on \( \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

Next, we claim that we can assume that \( r \leq  \sqrt{{t}_{0}}/2 \) . If \( r \) does not satisfy this inequality, then we replace \( r \) with \( {r}^{\prime } = \sqrt{{t}_{0}}/2 \) . Of course, the curvature inequalities hold for \( {r}^{\prime } \) if they hold for \( r \) . Suppose that we have established the result for \( {r}^{\prime } \) . Then

\[
\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {p, T, r}\right)  \geq  \operatorname{Vol}B\left( {p, T,{r}^{\prime }}\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{3} \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{r}{2}\right) }^{3} = \frac{\kappa }{8}{r}^{3}.
\]

From now on we assume that \( {t}_{0} \geq  1 \) and \( r \leq  \sqrt{{t}_{0}}/2 \) . According to Proposition 4.11, for any \( \left( {p, t}\right)  \in  M \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{2}^{-4}}\right\rbrack \) we have \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {p, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  2 \) and \( \operatorname{Vol}B\left( {p, t, r}\right)  \geq  {\kappa }_{0}{r}^{3} \) for all \( r \leq  1 \) .

Once we know that \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \) is universally bounded on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{2}^{-4}}\right\rbrack \) it follows that there is a universal constant \( {C}_{1} \) such that \( {C}_{1}^{-1}g\left( {q,0}\right)  \leq  g\left( {q, t}\right)  \leq \; {C}_{1}g\left( {q,0}\right) \) for all \( q \in  M \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{2}^{-4}}\right\rbrack \) . This means that there is a universal constant \( C < \infty \) such that the following holds. For any points \( {q}_{0}, q \in  M \) with \( {d}_{0}\left( {{q}_{0}, q}\right)  \leq  1 \) let \( {\gamma }_{{q}_{0}, q} \) be the path in \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {{2}^{-5},{2}^{-4}}\right\rbrack \) given by

\[
{\gamma }_{{q}_{0}, q}\left( \tau \right)  = \left( {{A}_{{q}_{0}, q}\left( \tau \right) ,{2}^{-4} - \tau }\right) ,0 \leq  \tau  \leq  {2}^{-5},
\]

where \( {A}_{{q}_{0}, q} \) is a shortest \( g\left( 0\right) \) -geodesic from \( {q}_{0} \) to \( q \) . Then \( \mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{{q}_{0}, q}\right)  \leq  C \) .

By Theorem 7.10 there is a point \( {q}_{0} \in  M \) and an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( {\gamma }_{0} \) from \( x = \; \left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right) \) to \( \left( {{q}_{0},{2}^{-4}}\right) \) with \( l\left( {\gamma }_{0}\right)  \leq  3/2 \) . Since \( {t}_{0} \geq  1 \) , this means that there is a universal constant \( {C}^{\prime } < \infty \) such that for each point \( q \in  B\left( {{q}_{0},0,1}\right) \) the path which is the composite of \( {\gamma }_{0} \) followed by \( {\gamma }_{{q}_{0}, q} \) has \( \widetilde{l} \) -length at most \( {C}^{\prime } \) . Setting \( {\tau }_{0} = {t}_{0} - {2}^{-5} \) , this implies that \( {l}_{x}\left( {q,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \leq  {C}^{\prime } \) for every \( q \in  B\left( {{q}_{0},0,1}\right) \) . This ball has volume at least \( {\kappa }_{0} \) . By Proposition 7.5, the open subset \( {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) \) is of full measure in \( M \times  \left\{  {2}^{-5}\right\} \) . Hence, \( W\left( {\tau }_{0}\right)  = \left( {B\left( {{q}_{0},0,1}\right)  \times  \left\{  {2}^{-5}\right\}  }\right)  \cap  {\mathcal{U}}_{x}\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) \) also has volume at least \( {\kappa }_{0} \) . Since \( {r}^{2} \leq  {t}_{0}/4 < {\tau }_{0} \) , Theorem 8.1 now gives the result. (See FIG. 3.)

nodes.content: DEFINITION 9.2. An ancient solution is a Ricci flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) defined for \( - \infty  < t \leq  0 \) such that for each \( t,\left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a connected, complete, non-flat Riemannian manifold whose curvature operator is bounded and non-negative. For any \( \kappa  > 0 \) , an ancient solution is \( \kappa \) -non-collapsed if it is \( \kappa \) -non-collapsed on all scales. We also use the terminology \( \kappa \) -solution for a \( \kappa \) -non-collapsed, ancient solution.

nodes.content: EXAMPLE 9.3. Let \( \left( {{S}^{2},{g}_{0}}\right) \) be the standard round 2-sphere of scalar curvature 1 (and hence Ricci tensor \( {g}_{0}/2 \) ). Recall that from Equation 6.15 we have

\[
H\left( X\right)  =  - \frac{\partial R}{\partial \tau } - \frac{R}{\tau } - 2\langle \nabla R, X\rangle  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) .
\]

Using Hamilton’s Harnack’s inequality (Theorem 4.37) with \( \chi  =  - X \) , we have

\[
- \frac{\partial R}{\partial \tau } - \frac{R}{{\tau }_{0} - \tau } - 2\langle \nabla R, X\rangle  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Together these imply

\[
H\left( X\right)  \geq  \left( {\frac{1}{\tau  - {\tau }_{0}} - \frac{1}{\tau }}\right) R = \frac{{\tau }_{0}}{\tau \left( {\tau  - {\tau }_{0}}\right) }R.
\]

\[
H\left( X\right)  \geq   - \frac{{c}^{-1}}{\tau }R
\]

\[

\[

\]

for all \( 0 < \tau  \leq  \left( {1 - c}\right) {\tau }_{0} \) . This is an equation of smooth functions on the open dense subset \( \mathcal{U}\left( \bar{\tau }\right) \) but it extends as an equation of \( {L}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) -functions on all of \( M \) .

As to the second inequality in the statement, by the first equation in Theorem 6.50 we have

\[

\]

\[
R\left( {q,\tau }\right)  - \frac{\left( {1 + {c}^{-1}}\right) {l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right) }{\tau } \leq  \frac{\partial {l}_{x}\left( {q,\tau }\right) }{\partial \tau }.
\]

This establishes the second inequality.
