nodes.proof:
Suppose that the result does not hold. Take a sequence of \( {\beta }_{n} \) tending to zero and counterexamples

\[
\left( {{N}_{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{0, n},0}\right\rbrack  ,{g}_{1, n}\left( t\right) }\right) ;\left( {{N}_{n}^{\prime } \times  \left( {-{t}_{1, n}, - {t}_{0, n}}\right\rbrack  ,{g}_{2, n}\left( t\right) }\right) \text{ . }
\]

Pass to a subsequence so that the \( {t}_{0, n} \) tend to a limit \( {t}_{0,\infty } \geq  0 \) . Since \( {\beta }_{n} \) tends to zero, we can take a smooth limit of a subsequence and this limit is an evolving cylinder \( \left( {{S}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R}, h\left( t\right)  \times  d{s}^{2}}\right) \) , where \( h\left( t\right) \) is the round metric of scalar curvature \( 1/\left( {1 - t}\right) \) defined for some amount of backward time. Notice that, for all \( \beta \) sufficiently small, on a \( {\beta \epsilon } \) -neck the derivative of the scalar curvature is positive. Thus, \( {R}_{{g}_{1, n}}\left( {x, - {t}_{0, n}}\right)  < 1 \) . Since we have a strong neck structure on \( {N}_{n}^{\prime } \) centered at \( \left( {x, - {t}_{0, n}}\right) \) , this implies that \( {t}_{1, n} > 1 \) so that the limit is defined for at least time \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1 + {t}_{0,\infty }}\right) \) . If \( {t}_{0,\infty } > 0 \) , then, restricting to the appropriate subset of this limit, a subset with compact closure in space-time, it follows immediately that for all \( n \) sufficiently large there is a strong \( \epsilon \) -neck centered at \( \left( {x,0}\right) \) . This contradicts the assumption that we began with a sequence of counterexamples to the proposition.

Let us consider the case when \( {t}_{0,\infty } = 0 \) . In this case the smooth limit is an evolving round cylinder defined for time \( ( - 1,0\rbrack \) . Since \( {t}_{1, n} > 1 \) we see that for any \( A < \infty \) for all \( n \) sufficiently large the ball \( B\left( {{x}_{n},0, A}\right) \) has compact closure in every time-slice and there are uniform bounds to the curvature on \( B\left( {{x}_{n},0, A}\right)  \times  ( - 1,0\rbrack \) . This means that the limit is uniform for time \( ( - 1,0\rbrack \) on all these balls. Thus, once again for all \( n \) sufficiently large we see that \( \left( {x,0}\right) \) is the center of a strong \( \epsilon \) -neck in the union. In either case we have obtained a contradiction, and hence we have proved the result. See FIG. 1.

nodes.content:
It follows from Assumption (2) that for any time \( t \) in the time-interval of definition of a Ricci flow with surgery, with \( t \) being distinct from the initial and final times (if these exist), for all \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small, the only possible singular time in \( \left\lbrack  {t - \delta , t + \delta }\right\rbrack \) is \( t \) . Suppose that \( t \) is a singular time. The singular locus at time \( t \) is a closed, smooth subsurface \( {\sum }_{t} \subset  {M}_{t} \) . From the local model, near every point of \( x \in  {\sum }_{t} \) we see that this surface separates \( {M}_{t} \) into two pieces:

\[
{M}_{t} = {C}_{t}{ \cup  }_{{\sum }_{t}}{E}_{t}
\]

where \( {E}_{t} \) is the exposed region at time \( t \) and \( {C}_{t} \) is the complement of the interior of \( {E}_{t} \) in \( {M}_{t} \) . We call \( {C}_{t} \) the continuing region. It is the maximal subset of \( {M}_{t} \) for which there is \( \delta  > 0 \) and an embedding

\[
{C}_{t} \times  (t - \delta , t\rbrack  \rightarrow  \mathcal{M}
\]

compatible with time and the vector field.

Assumption (4). Topology of the exposed regions: At all singular times \( t \) we require that \( {E}_{t} \) be a finite disjoint union of 3-balls. In particular, \( {\sum }_{t} \) is a finite disjoint union of 2-spheres.

nodes.proof:
Fix \( {t}^{\prime } < t \) but sufficiently close to \( t \) . By Assumption (4) every component of \( {E}_{t} \) is a 3-ball and hence every component of \( \partial {E}_{t} = \partial {C}_{t} \) is a 2-sphere. Since \( {C}_{t} \) is diffeomorphic to \( {C}_{{t}^{\prime }} \subset  {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) we see that every component of \( \partial {C}_{{t}^{\prime }} = \partial {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) is a 2-sphere. Since every component of \( {E}_{t} \) is a 3-ball, the passage from the smooth manifold \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) to the smooth manifold \( {M}_{t} \) is effected by removing the interior of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) from \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) and gluing a 3-ball onto each component of \( \partial {C}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) to form \( {M}_{t} \) .

By Assumption (5) every point of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) has a strong \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -canonical neighborhood. Since \( \epsilon \) is sufficiently small it follows from Proposition A. 25 that every component of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) that is also a component of \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) is diffeomorphic either to a manifold admitting a metric of constant positive curvature (a 3-dimensional space-form), to \( \mathbb{R}{P}^{3}\# \mathbb{R}{P}^{3} \) or to a 2-sphere bundle over \( {S}^{1} \) . In the passage from \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) to \( {M}_{t} \) these components are removed.

Now let us consider a component of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) that is not a component of \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) . Such a component is a connected subset of \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) with the property that every point is either contained in the core of a \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -cap or is the center of an \( \epsilon \) -neck and whose frontier in \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) consists of 2-spheres that are central 2-spheres of \( \epsilon \) -necks. If every point is the center of an \( \epsilon \) -neck, then according to Proposition A.19, \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) is an \( \epsilon \) -tube and in particular is diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{2} \times  I \) . Otherwise \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) is contained in a capped or double capped \( \epsilon \) -tube. Since the frontier of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) is non-empty and is the union of central 2-spheres of an \( \epsilon \) -neck, it follows that either \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) is diffeomorphic to a capped \( \epsilon \) -tube or to an \( \epsilon \) -tube. Hence, these components of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) are diffeomorphic either to \( {S}^{2} \times  \left( {0,1}\right) \) , to \( {D}^{3} \) , or to \( \mathbb{R}{P}^{3} \smallsetminus  {B}^{3} \) . Replacing a 3-ball component of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) by another 3-ball leaves the topology unchanged. Replacing a component of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) that is diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{2} \times  I \) by the disjoint union of two 3-balls has the effect of doing a surgery along the core 2-sphere of the cylinder \( {S}^{2} \times  I \) in \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) . If this 2-sphere separates \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) into two pieces then doing this surgery effects a connected sum decomposition. If this 2-sphere does not separate, then the surgery has the topological effect of doing a connected sum decomposition into two pieces, one of which is diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{2} \times  {S}^{1} \) , and then removing that component entirely. Replacing a component of \( {D}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) that

is diffeomorphic to \( \mathbb{R}{P}^{3} \smallsetminus  {B}^{3} \) by a 3-ball, has the effect of doing a connected sum decomposition on \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) into pieces, one of which is diffeomorphic to \( \mathbb{R}{P}^{3} \) , and then removing that component.

From this description the proposition follows immediately.

nodes.label: Corollary 15.4
nodes.document_title: John Morgan and Gang Tian - Ricci Flow and the Poincare Conjecture
nodes.content:
COROLLARY 15.4. Let \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) be a generalized Ricci flow satisfying Assumptions (1) - (7) with initial conditions \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) . Suppose that for some \( T \) the time-slice \( {M}_{T} \) of this generalized flow satisfies Thurston’s Geometriza-tion Conjecture. Then the same is true for the manifold \( {M}_{t} \) for any \( t \leq  T \) , and in particular M satisfies Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture. In addition:

(1) If for some \( T > 0 \) the manifold \( {M}_{T} \) is empty, then \( M \) is a connected sum of manifolds diffeomorphic to 2-sphere bundles over \( {S}^{1} \) and 3- dimensional space-forms, i.e., compact 3-manifolds that admit a metric of constant positive curvature.

(2) If for some \( T > 0 \) the manifold \( {M}_{T} \) is empty and if \( M \) is connected and simply connected, then \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{3} \) .

(3) If for some \( T > 0 \) the manifold \( {M}_{T} \) is empty and if \( M \) has finite fundamental group, then M is a 3-dimensional space-form.

Suppose that for some \( T \) the time-slice \( {M}_{T} \) of this generalized flow satisfies Thurston’s Geometriza-tion Conjecture. Then the same is true for the manifold \( {M}_{t} \) for any \( t \leq T \) , and in particular M...

nodes.proof:
Suppose that \( {M}_{T} \) satisfies the Thurston Geometrization Conjecture and that \( {t}_{0} \) is the largest surgery time \( \leq  T \) . (If there is no such surgery time then \( {M}_{T} \) is diffeomorphic to \( M \) and the result is established.) Let \( {T}^{\prime } < {t}_{0} \) be sufficiently close to \( {t}_{0} \) so that \( {t}_{0} \) is the only surgery time in the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{T}^{\prime }, T}\right\rbrack \) . Then according to the previous proposition \( {M}_{{T}^{\prime }} \) is obtained from \( {M}_{T} \) by first taking the disjoint union of \( {M}_{T} \) and copies of 2-sphere bundles over \( {S}^{1} \) and 3-dimensional space forms. In the Thurston Geometriza-tion Conjecture the first step is to decompose the manifold as a connected sum of prime 3-manifolds and then to treat each prime piece independently. Clearly, the prime decomposition of \( {M}_{{T}^{\prime }} \) is obtained from the prime decomposition of \( {M}_{T} \) by adding a disjoint union with 2-sphere bundles over \( {S}^{1} \) and 3-dimensional space forms. By definition any 3-dimensional space-form satisfies Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture. Since any diffeomorphism of \( {S}^{2} \) to itself is isotopic to either the identity or to the antipodal map, there are two diffeomorphism types of 2-sphere bundles over \( {S}^{1} : {S}^{2} \times  {S}^{1} \) and the non-orientable 2-sphere bundle over \( {S}^{1} \) . Each is obtained from \( {S}^{2} \times  I \) by gluing the ends together via an isometry of the round metric on \( {S}^{2} \) . Hence, each has a homogeneous geometry modeled on \( {S}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) , and hence satisfies Thurston’s Geometrization Conjecture. This proves that if \( {M}_{T} \) satisfies this conjecture, then so does \( {M}_{{T}^{\prime }} \) . Continuing this way by induction, using the fact that there are only finitely many surgery times completes the proof of the first statement.

Statement (1) is proved analogously. Suppose that \( {M}_{T} \) is a disjoint union of connected sums of 2-sphere bundles over \( {S}^{1} \) and 3-dimensional space-forms. Let \( {t}_{0} \) be the largest surgery time \( \leq  T \) and let \( {T}^{\prime } < {t}_{0} \) be sufficiently close to \( {t}_{0} \) . (As before, if there is no such \( {t}_{0} \) then \( {M}_{T} \) is diffeomorphic to \( M \) and the result is established.) Then it is clear from the previous proposition that \( {M}_{{T}^{\prime }} \) is also a disjoint union of connected sums of 3-dimensional space-forms and 2-sphere bundles over \( {S}^{1} \) . Induction as in the previous case completes the argument for this case.

The last two statements are immediate from this one.

(i) \( \mathbf{r} = {r}_{0} \geq  {r}_{1} \geq  {r}_{2} \geq  \cdots  > 0 \) , with \( {r}_{0} = \epsilon \) ,

(Assuming Theorem 15.9) Choose a metric \( g\left( 0\right) \) so that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is normalized. This is possible by beginning with any Riemannian metric on \( M \) and scaling it by a sufficiently large positive constant to make it normalized. According to Proposition 4.11 and the definitions of \( {T}_{i} \) and \( {\kappa }_{0} \) there is a Ricci flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) with these initial conditions defined for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  {T}_{2} \) satisfying Assumptions (1) - (7) and the three conditions of the previous theorem. The assumption that \( M \) has no embedded \( \mathbb{R}{P}^{2} \) with trivial normal bundle is needed so that Assumption (1) holds for this Ricci flow. Hence, by the previous theorem we can extend this Ricci flow to a Ricci flow with surgery defined for all \( 0 \leq  t < \infty \) satisfying the same conditions.

Showing that after surgery Assumptions (1) - (7) continue to hold and that the curvature is pinched toward positive is direct and only requires that \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right) \) be smaller than some universal positive constant.

nodes.proof:
It is immediate from the construction and Lemma 14.11 that the result of performing the surgery operation at time \( T \) on a Ricci flow with surgery produces a new Ricci flow with surgery. Assumptions (1) - (3) clearly hold for the result. and Assumptions (4) and (5) hold because of the way that we do surgery. Let us consider Assumption (6). Fix \( {t}^{\prime } < T \) so that there are no surgery times in \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime }, T}\right) \) . By flowing backward using the vector field \( \chi \) we have an embedding \( \psi  : {C}_{t} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime }, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \) compatible with time and the vector field. For any \( p \in  {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \smallsetminus  \psi \left( \right. \) int \( \left. {{C}_{T} \times  \left\{  {t}^{\prime }\right\}  }\right) \) the limit as \( t \) tends to \( T \) from below of the flow line \( p\left( t\right) \) at time \( t \) through \( p \) either lies in \( \Omega \left( T\right) \) or it does not. In the latter case, by definition we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {T}^{ - }}}R\left( {p\left( t\right) }\right)  = \infty \text{ . }
\]

In the former case, the limit point either is contained in the end of a strong \( {2\epsilon } \) -horn cut off by the central 2-sphere of the strong \( \delta \) -neck centered at one of the \( {y}_{i} \) or is contained in a component of \( \Omega \left( T\right) \) that contains no point of \( {\Omega }_{\rho }\left( T\right) \) . Hence, in this case we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {T}^{ - }}}R\left( {p\left( t\right) }\right)  > {\rho }^{-2} > {r}_{i}^{-2}.
\]

Since \( {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \smallsetminus  \psi \left( {\operatorname{int}{C}_{T} \times  \left\{  {t}^{\prime }\right\}  }\right) \) is compact for every \( {t}^{\prime } \) , there is \( {T}_{1} < T \) such that \( R\left( {p\left( t\right) }\right)  > {r}_{i}^{-2} \) for all \( p \in  {M}_{{t}^{\prime }} \smallsetminus  \psi \left( \right. \) int \( \left. {{C}_{T} \times  \left\{  {t}^{\prime }\right\}  }\right) \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{1}, T}\right) \) . Hence, by our assumptions all these points have strong \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -canonical neighborhoods. This establishes that Assumption (6) holds at the singular time \( T \) . By hypothesis Assumption (6) holds at all earlier singular times. Clearly, from the construction the Ricci flow on \( \left\lbrack  {T,{T}^{\prime }}\right) \) is maximal. Hence, Assumption (7) holds for the new Ricci flow with surgery.

From Theorem 13.2 the fact that \( \delta \left( T\right)  \leq  {\delta }_{i} \leq  {\delta }_{0} \leq  {\delta }_{0}^{\prime } \) and \( h\left( T\right)  \leq  {R}_{0}^{-1/2} \) imply that the Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{M}_{T}, G\left( T\right) }\right) \) has curvature pinched toward positive for time \( T \) . It then follows from Theorem 4.32 that the Ricci flow defined on \( \left\lbrack  {T,{T}^{\prime }}\right) \) with \( \left( {{M}_{T}, G\left( T\right) }\right) \) as initial conditions has curvature pinched toward positive. The inductive hypothesis is that on the time-interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) the Ricci flow with surgery has curvature pinched toward positive. This completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.content: PROPOSITION 16.1. Suppose that for some \( i \geq  0 \) we have surgery parameter sequences \( {\delta }_{0} \geq  {\delta }_{1} \geq  \cdots  \geq  {\delta }_{i} > 0,\epsilon  = {r}_{0} \geq  {r}_{1} \geq  \cdots  \geq  {r}_{i} > 0 \) and \( {\kappa }_{0} \geq  {\kappa }_{1} \geq  \cdots  \geq  {\kappa }_{i} > 0 \) . Then there is \( 0 < \kappa  \leq  {\kappa }_{i} \) and for any \( 0 < {r}_{i + 1} \leq  {r}_{i} \) there is \( 0 < \delta \left( {r}_{i + 1}\right)  \leq  {\delta }_{i} \) such that the following holds. Suppose that \( \bar{\delta } : \left\lbrack  {0,{T}_{i + 1}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {\mathbb{R}}^{ + } \) is a non-increasing function with \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right)  \leq  {\delta }_{j} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{j},{T}_{j + 1}}\right) \) and \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right)  \leq  \delta \left( {r}_{i + 1}\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1},{T}_{i + 1}}\right) \) . Suppose that \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) is a Ricci flow with surgery defined for \( 0 \leq  t < T \) for some \( T \in  \left( {{T}_{i},{T}_{i + 1}}\right\rbrack \) with surgery control parameter \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right) \) . Suppose that the restriction of this Ricci flow with surgery to the time-interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{T}_{i}}\right) \) satisfies the hypothesis of Theorem 15.9 with respect to the given sequences. Suppose also that the entire Ricci flow with surgery \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) satisfies Assumptions (1) - (7) and the strong \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -canonical neighborhood assumption with parameter \( {r}_{i + 1} \) . nodes.proof:
Since \( R\left( x\right)  \geq  {r}_{i + 1}^{-2} \) , by assumption any such \( x \) has a strong \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -canonical neighborhood. If this neighborhood is a strong \( \epsilon \) -neck centered at \( x \) , then the result is clear for a non-collapsing constant \( \kappa \) which is universal. If the neighborhood is an \( \epsilon \) -round component containing \( x \) , then \( x \) is contained in a component of positive sectional curvature. Likewise, if \( x \) is contained in a \( C \) -component, then by definition it is contained in a component of its time-slice with positive sectional curvature.

Lastly, we suppose that \( x \) is contained in the core \( Y \) of a \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -cap \( \mathcal{C} \) . Let \( {r}^{\prime } > 0 \) be such that the supremum of \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \) on \( B\left( {x, t,{r}^{\prime }}\right) \) is \( {\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{-2} \) . Then, by the definition of a \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -cap, \( \operatorname{vol}B\left( {x, t,{r}^{\prime }}\right)  \geq  {C}^{-1}{\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{3} \) . Clearly, \( {r}^{\prime } \leq  r \) and there is a point \( y \in  \overline{B\left( {x, t,{r}^{\prime }}\right) } \) with \( R\left( y\right)  = {\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{-2} \) . On the other hand, by the definition of a \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -cap, we have \( R\left( y\right) /R\left( x\right)  \leq  C \) , so that \( {r}^{\prime }/r \geq  {C}^{-1/2} \) . Thus, the volume of \( B\left( {x, t, r}\right) \) is at least \( {C}^{-5/2}{r}^{3} \) .

This completes an examination of all cases and establishes the proposition.

Proposition 16.4. For each \( {r}_{i + 1} \) with \( 0 < {r}_{i + 1} \leq  {r}_{i} \) , there is \( \delta  = \; \delta \left( {r}_{i + 1}\right)  > 0 \) (depending implicitly on \( {t}_{0}, C,\epsilon \) , and i) such that if \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right)  \leq  \delta \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1},{T}_{i + 1}}\right\rbrack \) then the following holds. Let \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) be a Ricci flow with surgery satisfying the hypothesis of Proposition 16.1 with respect to the given sequences and \( {r}_{i + 1} \) , and let \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) have \( \mathbf{t}\left( x\right)  = T \) with \( T \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i},{T}_{i + 1}}\right) \) . Suppose that for some \( r \geq  {r}_{i + 1} \) the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {x, r, T, - {r}^{2}}\right) \) exists in \( \mathcal{M} \) and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) on this neighborhood. Then there is an open subset \( U \) of \( {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \) contained in the open subset of smooth manifold points of \( \mathcal{M} \) with the following properties:

(1) For every \( y \) in \( U \) there is a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic connecting \( x \) to \( y \) .

(2) \( {U}_{t} = U \cap  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( t\right) \) is non-empty for every \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \) .

(3) For each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \) the restriction of \( \mathcal{L} \) to \( {U}_{t} \) achieves its minimum and that minimum is at most \( 3\sqrt{\left( T - t\right) } \) .

(4) The subset of \( U \) consisting of all \( y \) with the property that \( \mathcal{L}\left( y\right)  \leq \; \mathcal{L}\left( {y}^{\prime }\right) \) for all \( {y}^{\prime } \in  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( {\mathbf{t}\left( y\right) }\right) \) has the property that its intersection with \( {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( I\right) \) is compact for every compact interval \( I \subset  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \) .

Proposition 16.5. Given \( A < \infty ,{\delta }^{\prime \prime } > 0 \) and \( 0 < \theta  < 1 \) , there is \( {\delta }_{0}^{\prime \prime } = {\delta }_{0}^{\prime \prime }\left( {A,\theta ,{\delta }^{\prime \prime }}\right) \left( {{\delta }_{0}^{\prime \prime }\text{ also depends on }{r}_{i + 1}, C,\text{ and }\epsilon ,\text{ which are all now }}\right. \) fixed) such that the following holds. Suppose that \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) is a Ricci flow with surgery defined for \( 0 \leq  t < T \) with surgery control parameter \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right) \) . Suppose that it satisfies the strong \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -canonical neighborhood assumption at all points \( x \) with \( R\left( x\right)  \geq  {r}_{i + 1}^{-2} \) . Suppose also that \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) has curvature that is pinched toward positive. Suppose that there is a surgery at some time \( \bar{t} \) with \( {T}_{i - 1} \leq  \bar{t} < T \) with \( \bar{h} \) as the surgery scale parameter. Set \( {T}^{\prime } = \min \left( {T,\bar{t} + \theta {\bar{h}}^{2}}\right) \) . Let \( p \in  {M}_{\bar{t}} \) be the tip of the cap of a surgery disk. Then, provided that \( \bar{\delta }\left( \bar{t}\right)  \leq  {\delta }_{0}^{\prime \prime } \) one of the following holds:

(a) There is an embedding \( \rho  : B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},{T}^{\prime }}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) compatible with time and the vector field. Let \( {g}^{\prime }\left( t\right) ,\bar{t} \leq  t < {T}^{\prime } \) , be the one-parameter family of metrics on \( B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right) \) given by \( {\rho }^{ * }G \) . Shifting this family by \( - \bar{t} \) to make the initial time 0 and scaling it by \( {\bar{h}}^{-2} \) produces a family of metrics \( g\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t < \min \left( {\left( {T - \bar{t}}\right) {\bar{h}}^{-2},\theta }\right) \) , on \( {B}_{g}\left( {p,0, A}\right) \) that are within \( {\delta }^{\prime \prime } \) in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  1/{\delta }^{\prime \prime }\right\rbrack  } \) -topology of the standard flow on the ball of radius \( A \) at time 0 centered at the tip of its cap.

(b) There is \( {\bar{t}}_{ + } \in  \left( {\bar{t},{T}^{\prime }}\right) \) and an embedding \( B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},{\bar{t}}_{ + }}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) compatible with time and the vector field so that the previous item holds with \( {\bar{t}}_{ + } \) replacing \( {T}^{\prime } \) . Furthermore, for any \( t < {\bar{t}}_{ + } \) but sufficiently close to \( {\bar{t}}_{ + } \) the image of \( B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right)  \times  \{ t\} \) is contained in the region \( {D}_{t} \subset  {M}_{t} \) that disappears at time \( {\bar{t}}_{ + } \) .

The method of proof is to assume that the result is false and take a sequence of counterexamples with surgery control parameters \( {\delta }_{n} \) tending to zero. In order to derive a contradiction we need to be able to take smooth limits of rescaled versions of these Ricci flows with surgery, where the base points are the tips of the surgery caps. This is somewhat delicate since the surgery cap is not the result of moving forward for a fixed amount of time under Ricci flow, and consequently Shi's theorem does not apply.

nodes.content: LEMMA 16.8. Suppose that we have a sequence of 3-dimensional Ricci flows with surgeries \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{n},{G}_{n}}\right) \) that satisfy the strong \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -canonical neighborhood assumption with parameter \( {r}_{i + 1} \) , and have curvature pinched toward positive. Suppose that there are surgeries in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{n} \) at times \( {t}_{n} \) with surgery control parameters \( {\delta }_{n}^{\prime } \) and scales \( {h}_{n} \) . Let \( {p}_{n} \) be the tip of a surgery cap for the surgery at time \( {t}_{n} \) . Also suppose that there is \( 0 \leq  {\theta }_{n} < 1 \) such that for every \( A < \infty \) , for all \( n \) sufficiently large there are embeddings \( B\left( {{p}_{a},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{n},{t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n}}\right)  \rightarrow  {\mathcal{M}}_{n} \) compatible with time and the vector field. Suppose that \( {\delta }_{n}^{\prime } \rightarrow  0 \) and \( {\theta }_{n} \rightarrow  \theta  < 1 \) as \( n \rightarrow  \infty \) . Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{n}^{\prime },{G}_{n}^{\prime },{p}_{n}}\right) \) be the Ricci flow with surgery obtained by shifting time by \( - {t}_{n} \) so that surgery occurs at \( \mathbf{t} = 0 \) and rescaling by \( {h}_{n}^{-2} \) so that the scale of the surgery becomes 1. Then, after passing to a subsequence, the sequence converges smoothly to a limiting flow \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) ,\left( {{p}_{\infty },0}\right) }\right) ,0 \leq  t < \theta \) . This limiting flow is isomorphic to the restriction of the standard flow to time \( 0 \leq  t < \theta \) .

nodes.proof: Let \( Q < \infty \) be an upper bound for the scalar curvature of the standard flow on the time interval \( \lbrack 0,\theta ) \) . Since \( {\delta }_{n}^{\prime } \rightarrow  0 \) , according to the previous corollary, there is a smooth limit at time 0 for a subsequence, and this limit is the standard initial metric. Suppose that, for some \( 0 \leq  {\theta }^{\prime } < \theta \) , we have established that there is a smooth limiting flow on \( \left\lbrack  {0,{\theta }^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) . Since the initial conditions are the standard solution, it follows from the uniqueness statement in Theorem 12.5 that in fact the limiting flow is isomorphic to the restriction of the standard flow to this time interval. Then the scalar curvature of the limiting flow is bounded by \( Q \) . Hence, for any \( A < \infty \) , for all \( n \) sufficiently large, the scalar curvature of the restriction of \( {G}_{n}^{\prime } \) to the image of \( {B}_{{G}_{n}^{\prime }}\left( {{p}_{n},0,{2A}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{\theta }^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) is bounded by \( {2Q} \) . According to Lemma 11.2 there is an \( \eta  > 0 \) and a constant \( {Q}^{\prime } < \infty \) , each depending only on \( Q,{r}_{i + 1}, C \) and \( \epsilon \) , such that for all \( n \) sufficiently large, the scalar curvature of the restriction of \( {G}_{n}^{\prime } \) to \( {B}_{{G}_{n}^{\prime }}\left( {{p}_{n},0, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left( {{\theta }^{\prime } + \eta ,{\theta }_{n}}\right) }\right) \) is bounded by \( {Q}^{\prime } \) . Because of the fact that the curvature is pinched toward positive, this implies that on the same set the sectional curvatures are uniformly bounded. Hence, by Shi's theorem with derivatives (Theorem 3.29), it follows that there are uniform bounds for the curvature in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) -topology. Thus, passing to a subsequence we can extend the smooth limit to the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{\theta }^{\prime } + \eta /2}\right\rbrack \) unless \( {\theta }^{\prime } + \eta /2 \geq  \theta \) . Since \( \eta \) depends on \( \theta \) (through \( Q \) ), but is independent of \( {\theta }^{\prime } \) , we can repeat this process extending the time-interval of definition of the limiting flow by \( \eta /2 \) until \( {\theta }^{\prime } + \eta /2 \geq  \theta \) . Now suppose that \( {\theta }^{\prime } + \eta /2 \geq  \theta \) . Then the argument shows that by passing to a subsequence we can extend the limit to any compact subinterval of \( \lbrack 0,\theta ) \) . Taking a diagonal sequence allows us to extend it to all of \( \lbrack 0,\theta ) \) . By the uniqueness of the standard flow, this limit is the standard flow.

For all \( n \) sufficiently large \( {\theta }_{n} > \theta  - {\eta }^{\prime } \) , and consequently for all \( n \) sufficiently large there is an embedding \( {B}_{{G}_{n}}\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{n},{t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}\left( {\theta  - {\eta }^{\prime }}\right) }\right\rbrack \) into \( {\mathcal{M}}_{n} \) compatible with time and with the vector field. For all \( n \) sufficiently large, we consider the restriction of \( {G}_{n}^{\prime } \) to \( {B}_{{G}_{n}^{\prime }}\left( {{p}_{n},0, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\theta  - {\eta }^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) . These converge smoothly to the restriction of the standard flow to the ball of radius \( A \) on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,\theta  - {\eta }^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) . In particular, for all \( n \) sufficiently large, the restrictions to these time intervals are within \( {\delta }^{\prime \prime } \) in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  1/{\delta }^{\prime \prime }\right\rbrack  } \) -topology of the standard flow. Also, for all \( n \) sufficiently large, \( {\theta }_{n} - \left( {\theta  - {\eta }^{\prime }}\right)  < \eta \) . Thus, by Lemma 11.2, we see that the scalar curvature of \( {G}_{n}^{\prime } \) is uniformly bounded (independent of \( n \) ) on \( {B}_{{G}_{n}^{\prime }}\left( {{p}_{n},0, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{\theta }_{n}}\right) \) . By the assumption that the curvature is pinched toward positive, this means that the sectional curvatures of the \( {G}_{n}^{\prime } \) are also uniformly bounded on these sets, and hence so are the Ricci curvatures. (Notice that these bounds are independent of \( {\eta }^{\prime } > 0 \) .) By Shi’s theorem with derivatives (Theorem 3.29), we see that there are uniform bounds on the curvatures in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) -topology on these subsets, and hence bounds in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) -topology on the Ricci curvature. These bounds are independent of both \( n \) and \( {\eta }^{\prime } \) . Thus, choosing \( {\eta }^{\prime } \) sufficiently close to zero, so that \( {\theta }_{n} - {\eta }^{\prime } \) is also close to \( \theta \) for all \( n \) sufficiently large, we see that for all such large \( n \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\theta  - {\eta }^{\prime },\theta }\right) \) , the restriction of \( {G}_{n}^{\prime } \) to \( {B}_{{G}_{n}^{\prime }}\left( {{p}_{n},0, A}\right)  \times  \{ t\} \) is arbitrarily close in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  1/{\delta }^{\prime \prime }\right\rbrack  } \) -topology to \( {G}_{n}^{\prime }\left( {\theta  - {\eta }^{\prime }}\right) \) . The same is of course true of the standard flow. This completes the proof of the corollary.

CLAIM 16.10. Suppose that \( {\theta }_{n} < \min \left( {\theta ,\left( {{T}_{n}^{\prime } - {t}_{n}}\right) /{h}_{n}^{2}}\right) \) . Let \( {\sum }_{1},\ldots ,{\sum }_{k} \) be the 2-spheres along which we do surgery at time \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) . Then for any \( t < {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) sufficiently close to \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) the following holds provided that \( {\delta }_{n}^{\prime } \) is sufficiently small. The image

\[
{\rho }_{n}\left( {{B}_{{g}_{n}}\left( {x,{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right)
\]

is disjoint from the images \( \left\{  {{\sum }_{i}\left( t\right) }\right\} \) of the \( \left\{  {\sum }_{i}\right\} \) under the backward flow to time \( t \) of the spheres \( {\sum }_{i} \) along which we do surgery at time \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) .

nodes.proof:
There is a constant \( {K}^{\prime } < \infty \) depending on \( \theta \) such that for the standard flow we have \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {K}^{\prime } \) for all \( x \in  B\left( {{p}_{0},0, A}\right) \) and all \( t \in  \lbrack 0,\theta ) \) for the standard solution. Consider the image

\[
{\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{n},{t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n}}\right) }\right) .
\]

After time shifting by \( - {t}_{n} \) and rescaling by \( {h}_{n}^{-2} \) , the flow \( {G}_{n}^{\prime } \) on the image of \( {\rho }_{n} \) is within \( {\delta }^{\prime \prime } \) of the standard flow. Thus, we see that for all \( n \) sufficiently large and for every point \( x \) in the image of \( {\rho }_{n} \) we have \( {R}_{{G}_{n}^{\prime }}\left( x\right)  \leq  2{K}^{\prime } \) and hence \( {R}_{{G}_{n}}\left( x\right)  \leq  2{K}^{\prime }{h}_{n}^{-2} \) .

Let \( {h}_{n}^{\prime } \) be the scale of the surgery at time \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) . (Recall that \( {h}_{n} \) is the scale of the surgery at time \( {t}_{n} \) .) Suppose that \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right)  \times  \left\{  {t}^{\prime }\right\}  }\right) \) meets one of the surgery 2-spheres \( {\sum }_{i}\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) at time \( {t}^{\prime } \) at a point \( y\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) . Then, for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n}}\right) \) we have the image \( y\left( t\right) \) of \( y\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) under the flow. All these points \( y\left( t\right) \) are points of intersection of \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {p,{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \) with \( {\sum }_{i}\left( t\right) \) . Since \( y\left( t\right)  \in  {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {p,{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \) , we have \( R\left( {y\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  2{K}^{\prime }{h}_{n}^{-2} \) . On the other hand \( R\left( {y\left( t\right) }\right) {\left( {h}_{n}^{\prime }\right) }^{2} \) is within \( O\left( \delta \right) \) of 1 as \( t \) tends to \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) . This means that \( {h}_{n}/{h}_{n}^{\prime } \leq  \sqrt{3{K}^{\prime }} \) for all \( n \) sufficiently large. Since the standard solution has non-negative curvature, the metric is a decreasing function of \( t \) , and hence the diameter of \( B\left( {{p}_{0}, t, A}\right) \) is at most \( {2A} \) in the standard solution. Using Corollary 16.9 we see that for all \( n \) sufficiently large, the diameter of \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {p,{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \) is at most \( A{h}_{n} \leq  4\sqrt{{K}^{\prime }}A{h}_{n}^{\prime } \) . This means that for \( {\delta }_{n}^{\prime } \) sufficiently small the distance at time \( t \) from \( {\sum }_{i}\left( t\right) \) to the complement of the \( t \) time-slice of the strong \( {\delta }_{n}\left( {{t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n}}\right) \) -neck \( {N}_{i}\left( t\right) \) centered at \( {\sum }_{i}\left( t\right) \) (which is at least \( {\left( {\delta }_{n}^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}{h}_{n}^{\prime }/2 \) ) is much larger than the diameter of

\[
{\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \text{ . }
\]

Consequently, for all \( n \) sufficiently large, the image \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right)  \times  }\right. \; \{ t\} ) \) is contained in \( {N}_{i}\left( t\right) \) . But by our choice of \( A \) , and Corollary 16.9 there is an \( \epsilon \) -neck of rescaled diameter approximately \( A{h}_{n}/2 \) contained in \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \) . By Corollary A. 3 the spheres coming from the neck structure in

\[
{\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right)
\]

are isotopic in \( {N}_{i}\left( t\right) \) to the central 2-sphere of this neck. This is a contradiction because in \( {N}_{i}\left( t\right) \) the central 2-sphere is homotopically non-trivial whereas the spheres in \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{\bar{h}}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \) clearly bound 3-disks.

Since \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \) is disjoint from the backward flow to time \( t \) of all the surgery 2-spheres \( {\sum }_{i}\left( t\right) \) and since \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {{p}_{n},{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \) is connected, if there is a flow line starting at some point \( z \in  B\left( {p,{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \) that disappears at time \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) , then the flow from every point of \( B\left( {p,{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \) disappears at time \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) . This shows that if \( {\theta }_{n} < \min \left( {\theta ,{T}_{n}^{\prime } - {t}_{n}/{h}_{n}^{2}}\right) \) , and if there is no extension of \( {\rho }_{n} \) to an embedding defined at time \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) , then all forward flow lines beginning at points of \( B\left( {p,{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \) disappear at time \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) , which of course means that for all \( t < {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) sufficiently close to \( {t}_{n} + {h}_{n}^{2}{\theta }_{n} \) the entire image \( {\rho }_{n}\left( {B\left( {p,{t}_{n}, A{h}_{n}}\right) \times \{ t\} }\right) \) is contained in the disappearing region \( {D}_{t} \) . This shows that for all \( n \) sufficiently large, the second conclusion of Proposition 16.5 holds, giving a contradiction.

Proposition 16.13. For any \( \ell  < \infty \) there is \( {A}_{0} = {A}_{0}\left( \ell \right)  < \infty ,0 < {\theta }_{0} = \; {\theta }_{0}\left( \ell \right)  < 1 \) , and for any \( A \geq  {A}_{0} \) for the constant \( {\delta }^{\prime \prime } = {\delta }^{\prime \prime }\left( A\right)  = {\delta }_{0}^{\prime \prime }\left( {A,{\theta }_{0},{\bar{\delta }}_{0}}\right)  > \) 0 from Proposition 16.5, the following holds. Suppose that \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) is a Ricci flow with surgery defined for \( 0 \leq  t < T < \infty \) . Suppose that it satisfies the strong \( \left( {C,\epsilon }\right) \) -canonical neighborhood assumption at all points \( x \) with \( R\left( x\right)  \geq \; {r}_{i + 1}^{-2} \) . Suppose also that the solution has curvature pinched toward positive. Suppose that there is a surgery at some time \( \bar{t} \) with \( {T}_{i - 1} \leq  \bar{t} < T \) with \( \bar{\delta }\left( \bar{t}\right) \) as the surgery control parameter and with \( h \) as the surgery scale parameter. Then the following holds provided that \( \bar{\delta }\left( \bar{t}\right)  \leq  {\delta }^{\prime \prime } \) . Set \( {T}^{\prime } = \min \left( {T,\bar{t} + {h}^{2}{\theta }_{0}}\right) \) . Let \( p \in  {M}_{\bar{t}} \) be the tip of the cap of a surgery disk at time \( \bar{t} \) . Suppose that \( P\left( {p,\bar{t},{Ah},{T}^{\prime } - \bar{t}}\right) \) exists in \( \mathcal{M} \) . Suppose that we have \( {t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},\bar{t} + {h}^{2}/2}\right\rbrack \) with \( {t}^{\prime } \leq  {T}^{\prime } \) , and suppose that we have a curve \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) parameterized by backward time \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime } - {t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) so that \( \gamma \left( \tau \right)  \in  {M}_{{T}^{\prime } - \tau } \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime } - {t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) . Suppose that the image of \( \gamma \) is contained in the closure of \( P\left( {p,\bar{t},{Ah},{T}^{\prime } - \bar{t}}\right)  \subset  \mathcal{M} \) . Suppose further:

(1) either that \( {T}^{\prime } = \bar{t} + {\theta }_{0}{h}^{2} \leq  T \) or that \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  \subset  \partial B\left( {p,\bar{t},{Ah}}\right)  \times  \left\{  {T}^{\prime }\right\} \) ; and

(2) \( \gamma \left( {{T}^{\prime } - {t}^{\prime }}\right)  \in  B\left( {p,\bar{t},{Ah}/2}\right)  \times  {t}^{\prime } \) .

Then

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{T}^{\prime } - {t}^{\prime }}\left( {R\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( t\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {dt} > \ell .
\]

See FIG. 2.

The logic of the proof is as follows. We fix \( \ell  < \infty \) . We shall determine the relevant value of \( {\theta }_{0} \) and then of \( {A}_{0} \) in the course of the argument. Then for any \( A \geq  {A}_{0} \) we define \( {\delta }^{\prime \prime }\left( A\right)  = {\delta }_{0}^{\prime \prime }\left( {A,{\theta }_{0},{\bar{\delta }}_{0}}\right) \) , as in Proposition 16.5.

The integral expression is invariant under time translation and also under rescaling. Thus, we can (and do) assume that \( \bar{t} = 0 \) and that the scale \( h \) of the surgery is 1 . We use the embedding of \( P\left( {p,0, A,{T}^{\prime }}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) and write the restriction of the flow to this subset as a one-parameter family of metrics \( g\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t \leq  {T}^{\prime } \) , on \( B\left( {p,0, A}\right) \) . With this renormalization, \( 0 \leq  {t}^{\prime } \leq  1/2 \) , also \( {T}^{\prime } \leq  {\theta }_{0} \) , and \( \tau  = {T}^{\prime } - t \) .

Let us first consider the case when \( {T}^{\prime } = {\theta }_{0} \leq  T \) . Consider the standard flow \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{3},{g}_{0}\left( t\right) }\right) \) , and let \( {p}_{0} \) be its tip. According to Proposition 12.31, for all \( x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \) and all \( t \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) we have \( {R}_{{g}_{0}}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  c/\left( {1 - t}\right) \) . By Proposition 16.5 and since we are assuming that \( \bar{\delta }\left( \bar{t}\right)  \leq  {\delta }^{\prime \prime } = {\delta }_{0}^{\prime \prime }\left( {A,{\theta }_{0},{\bar{\delta }}_{0}}\right) \) , we have that \( R\left( {a, t}\right)  \geq  c/2\left( {1 - t}\right) \) for all \( a \in  B\left( {p,0, A}\right) \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\theta }\right\rbrack \) . Thus, we have

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{\theta }_{0} - {t}^{\prime }}\left( {R\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } \geq  {\int }_{{t}^{\prime }}^{{\theta }_{0}}\frac{c}{2\left( {1 - t}\right) }{dt}
\]

\[
= \frac{-c}{2}\left( {\log \left( {1 - {\theta }_{0}}\right)  - \log \left( {1 - {t}^{\prime }}\right) }\right) {dt}
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{-c}{2}\left( {\log \left( {1 - {\theta }_{0}}\right)  + \log \left( 2\right) }\right) .
\]

LEMMA 16.15. Given \( {L}_{0} < \infty \) , there is \( {\bar{\delta }}_{1} = {\bar{\delta }}_{1}\left( {{L}_{0},{r}_{i + 1}}\right)  > 0 \) , independent of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) and \( x \) , such that if \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right)  \leq  {\bar{\delta }}_{1} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \) , then for any curve \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) ,0 \leq  \tau  \leq  {\tau }_{0} \) , with \( {\tau }_{0} \leq  T - {T}_{i - 1} \) , parameterized by backward time with \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = x \) and with

\[
{\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{0}^{{\tau }_{0}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } < {L}_{0},
\]

the following two statements hold:

(1) Set

\[
{\tau }^{\prime } = \min \left( {\frac{{r}_{i + 1}^{4}}{\left( {256}\right) {L}_{0}^{2}},\ln \left( \sqrt[3]{2}\right) {r}_{i + 1}^{2}}\right) .
\]

Then for all \( \tau  \leq  \min \left( {{\tau }^{\prime },{\tau }_{0}}\right) \) we have \( \gamma \left( \tau \right)  \in  P\left( {x, T, r/2, - {r}^{2}}\right) \) .

(2) Suppose that \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {T - {\tau }_{0}, T}\right) \) is a surgery time with \( p \) being the tip of the surgery cap at time \( \bar{t} \) and with the scale of the surgery being \( \bar{h} \) . Suppose \( {t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},\bar{t} + {\bar{h}}^{2}/2}\right\rbrack \) is such that there is an embedding

\[

\]

compatible with time and the vector field. Then the image of \( \rho \) is disjoint from the image of \( \gamma \) . See FIG. 3.

Here, \( {A}_{0}\left( \ell \right) \) and \( {\theta }_{0}\left( \ell \right) \) are the constants in Proposition 16.13. Lastly, we require \( {\bar{\delta }}_{1} \leq  {\delta }^{\prime \prime }\left( A\right) \) from Proposition 16.13. Notice that, by construction, \( {\delta }^{\prime \prime }\left( A\right)  = {\delta }_{0}^{\prime \prime }\left( {A,\theta ,{\bar{\delta }}_{0}}\right) \) from Proposition 16.5. Thus, if \( p \) is the tip of a surgery cap at time \( \bar{t} \) with the scale of the surgery being \( \bar{h} \) , then it follows that for any \( {\Delta t} \leq  \theta \) , if there is an embedding

\[
\rho  : B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},\bar{t} + {\bar{h}}^{2}{\Delta t}}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathcal{M}
\]

compatible with time and the vector field, then the induced flow (after time shifting by \( - \bar{t} \) and scaling by \( {\bar{h}}^{-2} \) ) is within \( {\bar{\delta }}_{0} \) in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  1/{\bar{\delta }}_{0}\right\rbrack  } \) -topology of the standard solution. In particular, the scalar curvature at any point of the image of \( \rho \) is positive and is within a multiplicative factor of 2 of the scalar curvature at the corresponding point of the standard flow.

Recall that we have \( r \geq  {r}_{i + 1} \) and that \( P\left( {x, T, r, - {r}^{2}}\right) \) exists in \( \mathcal{M} \) and that \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) on this parabolic neighborhood. We begin by proving by contradiction that there is no \( \tau  \leq  {\tau }^{\prime } \) with the property that \( \gamma \left( \tau \right)  \notin \; P\left( {x, T, r/2, - {r}^{2}}\right) \) . Suppose there is such a \( \tau  \leq  {\tau }^{\prime } \) . Notice that by construction \( {\tau }^{\prime } < {r}_{i + 1}^{2} < {r}^{2} \) . Hence, for the first \( {\tau }^{\prime \prime } \) with the property that \( \gamma \left( {\tau }^{\prime \prime }\right)  \notin  P\left( {x, T, r/2, - {r}^{2}}\right) \) the point \( \gamma \left( {\tau }^{\prime \prime }\right)  \in  \partial B\left( {x, T, r/2}\right)  \times  \left\{  {T - {\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right\} \) .

Claim 16.17. \( {\int }_{0}^{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\left| {{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right| {d\tau } > r/2\sqrt{2} \) .

Proof. Since \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {x, T, r, - {r}^{2}}\right) \) , it follows that \( \left| \mathrm{{Ric}}\right|  \leq  2{r}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {x, T, r, - {\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right) \) . Thus, for any tangent vector \( v \) at a point of \( B\left( {x, T, r}\right) \) we have

\[
\left| \frac{d\left( {\langle v, v{\rangle }_{G\left( {T - \tau }\right) }}\right) }{d\tau }\right|  \leq  2{r}^{-2}\langle v, v{\rangle }_{G\left( {T - \tau }\right) }
\]

for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack \) . Integrating gives that for any \( \tau  \leq  {\tau }^{\prime \prime } \) we have

\[
\exp \left( {-2{r}^{-2}{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right) \langle v, v{\rangle }_{G\left( T\right) } \leq  \langle v, v{\rangle }_{G\left( {T - \tau }\right) } \leq  \exp \left( {2{r}^{-2}{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right) \langle v, v{\rangle }_{G\left( T\right) }.
\]

Since \( {\tau }^{\prime \prime } \leq  {\tau }^{\prime } \) and \( r \geq  {r}_{i + 1} \) by the assumption on \( {\tau }^{\prime } \) we have

\[
\exp \left( {2{r}^{-2}{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right)  \leq  \exp \left( {2\sqrt[3]{2}}\right)  < 2
\]

This implies that for all \( \tau  \leq  {\tau }^{\prime \prime } \) we have

\[
\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{G\left( T\right) } < {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{G\left( {T - \tau }\right) } < \sqrt{2}{\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{G\left( T\right) },
\]

and hence

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\left| {{X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right| {d\tau } > \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}{\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{G\left( T\right) } \geq  \frac{r}{2\sqrt{2}},
\]

where we use the fact that \( {d}_{T}\left( {\gamma \left( 0\right) ,\gamma \left( {\tau }^{\prime \prime }\right) }\right)  = r/2 \) .

Applying Cauchy-Schwarz to \( {\tau }^{1/4}\left| {X}_{\gamma }\right| \) and \( {\tau }^{-1/4} \) on the interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack \) yields

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } \geq  {\int }_{0}^{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\sqrt{\tau }{\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}{d\tau }
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{{\left( {\int }_{0}^{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| d\tau \right) }^{2}}{{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}{\tau }^{-1/2}{d\tau }}
\]

\[
> \frac{{r}^{2}}{{16}\sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}} \geq  {L}_{0}
\]

Of course, the integral from 0 to \( {\tau }^{\prime \prime } \) is less than or equal to the entire integral from 0 to \( {\tau }_{0} \) since the integrand is non-negative, contradicting the assumption that \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  {L}_{0} \) . This completes the proof of the first numbered statement.

We turn now to the second statement. We impose a further condition on \( {\bar{\delta }}_{1} \) . Namely, require that \( {\bar{\delta }}_{1}^{2} < {r}_{i + 1}/2 \) . Since \( {r}_{i} \leq  {r}_{0} \leq  \epsilon  < 1 \) , we have \( {\bar{\delta }}_{1}^{2}{r}_{i} < {r}_{i + 1}/2 \) . Thus, the scale of the surgery, \( \bar{h} \) , which is \( \leq  {\bar{\delta }}_{1}^{2}{r}_{i} \) by definition, will also be less than \( {r}_{i + 1}/2 \) , and hence there is no point of \( P\left( {x, T, r, - {r}^{2}}\right) \) (where the curvature is bounded by \( {r}^{-2} \leq  {r}_{i + 1}^{-2} \) ) in the image of \( \rho \) (where the scalar curvature is greater than \( {\bar{h}}^{-2}/2 > 2{r}_{i + 1}^{-2} \) ). Thus, if \( {\tau }^{\prime } \geq  {\tau }_{0} \) we have completed the proof. Suppose that \( {\tau }^{\prime } < {\tau }_{0} \) . It suffices to establish that for every \( {\tau }_{1} \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }^{\prime },{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) the point \( \gamma \left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \) is not contained in the image of \( \rho \) for any surgery cap and any \( {t}^{\prime } \) as in the statement. Suppose that in fact there is \( {\tau }_{1} \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }^{\prime },{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) with \( \gamma \left( {\tau }_{1}\right) \) contained in the image of \( \rho \left( {B\left( {p,\bar{t},\left( {{A}_{0} + {50}}\right) \bar{h}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},{t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) where \( \bar{t} \leq  {t}^{\prime } \leq  \bar{t} + {\bar{h}}^{2}/2 \) and where \( p \) is the tip of some surgery cap at time \( \bar{t} \) . We estimate(16.2)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }_{0}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } \geq  {\int }_{{\tau }^{\prime }}^{{\tau }_{0}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
\geq  \sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }}{\int }_{{\tau }^{\prime }}^{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

Let \( {\Delta t} \leq  T - \bar{t} \) be the supremum of the set of \( s \) for which there is a parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}, s}\right) \) embedded in \( {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( {( - \infty , T\rbrack }\right)  \subset \; \mathcal{M} \) . Let \( \Delta {t}_{1} = \min \left( {\theta {\bar{h}}^{2},{\Delta t}}\right) \) . We consider \( P\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h},\Delta {t}_{1}}\right) \) . First, notice that since \( \bar{h} \leq  {\bar{\delta }}_{1}^{2}{r}_{i} < {r}_{i + 1}/2 \) , the scalar curvature on \( P\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h},\Delta {t}_{1}}\right) \) is larger than \( {\bar{h}}^{-2}/2 > {r}_{i + 1}^{-2} \geq  {r}^{-2} \) . In particular, the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {x, T, r, - {r}^{2}}\right) \) is disjoint from \( P\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h},\Delta {t}_{1}}\right) \) . This means that there is some \( {\tau }^{\prime \prime } \geq  {\tau }^{\prime } \) such that \( \gamma \left( {\tau }^{\prime \prime }\right)  \in  \partial P\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h},\Delta {t}_{1}}\right) \) and \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {\tau }^{\prime \prime },{\tau }_{1}\right\rbrack  } \subset \; P\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h},\Delta {t}_{1}}\right) \) . There are two cases to consider. The first is when \( \Delta {t}_{1} = \; \theta {\bar{h}}^{2},{\tau }^{\prime \prime } = T - \left( {\bar{t} + \Delta {t}_{1}}\right) \) and \( \gamma \left( {\tau }^{\prime \prime }\right)  \in  B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right)  \times  \left\{  {\bar{t} + \Delta {t}_{1}}\right\} \) . Then, according to Proposition 16.13,

(16.3)

\[
{\int }_{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}^{{\tau }_{1}}{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right) {d\tau } > \ell .
\]

Now let us consider the other case. If \( \Delta {t}_{1} < \theta {\bar{h}}^{2} \) , this means that either \( \bar{t} + \Delta {t}_{1} = T \) or, according to Proposition 16.5, at the time \( \bar{t} + \Delta {t}_{1} \) there is a surgery that removes all of \( B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right) \) . Hence, under either possibility it must be the case that \( \gamma \left( {\tau }^{\prime \prime }\right)  \in  \partial B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right)  \times  \left\{  {T - {\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right\} \) . Thus, the remaining case to consider is when, whatever \( \Delta {t}_{1} \) is, \( \gamma \left( {\tau }^{\prime \prime }\right)  \subset  \partial B\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h}}\right)  \times  \left\{  {T - {\tau }^{\prime \prime }}\right\} \) . Lemma 16.13 and the fact that \( R \geq  0 \) on \( P\left( {p,\bar{t}, A\bar{h},\Delta {t}_{1}}\right) \) imply that

\[
\ell  < {\int }_{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}^{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {R\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } = {\int }_{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}^{{\tau }_{1}}\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }.
\]

Since \( \ell  = {L}_{0}/\sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }} \) and \( {\tau }^{\prime \prime } \geq  {\tau }^{\prime } \) , it follows from Equation (16.2) that in both cases

\[
{\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  \geq  {\int }_{{\tau }^{\prime \prime }}^{{\tau }_{1}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } > \ell \sqrt{{\tau }^{\prime }} = {L}_{0},
\]

which contradicts our hypothesis. This completes the proof of Lemma 16.15.

DEFINITION 16.18. Suppose that \( \bar{t} \) is a surgery time, that \( {\tau }_{1} > 0 \) , and that there are no other surgery times in the interval \( \left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . Let \( {\left\{  {\sum }_{i}\left( \bar{t}\right) \right\}  }_{i} \) be the 2-spheres on which we do surgery at time \( \bar{t} \) . Each \( {\sum }_{i} \) is the central 2-sphere of a strong \( \delta \) -neck \( {N}_{i} \) . We can flow the cylinders \( {J}_{0}\left( \bar{t}\right)  = { \cup  }_{i}{s}_{{N}_{i}}^{-1}\left( {-{25},0\rbrack }\right) \) backward to any time \( t \in  \left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . Let \( {J}_{0}\left( t\right) \) be the result. There is an induced function, denoted \( \mathop{\coprod }\limits_{i}{s}_{{N}_{i}}\left( t\right) \) , on \( {J}_{0}\left( t\right) \) . It takes values in \( ( - {25},0\rbrack \) . We denote the boundary of \( {J}_{0}\left( t\right) \) by \( \mathop{\coprod }\limits_{i}{\sum }_{i}\left( t\right) \) . Of course, this boundary is the result of flowing \( \mathop{\coprod }\limits_{i}{\sum }_{i}\left( \bar{t}\right) \) backward to time \( t \) . (These backward flows are possible since there are no surgery times in \( \left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right) \) .) For each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right) \) we also have the region, \( {D}_{\bar{t}} \) , that disappears at time \( \bar{t} \) . It is an open submanifold whose boundary is \( \mathop{\coprod }\limits_{i}{\sum }_{i}\left( t\right) \) . Thus, for every \( t \in  \left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right) \) the subset \( J\left( t\right)  = {J}_{0}\left( t\right)  \cup  {D}_{t} \) is an open subset of \( {M}_{t} \) . We define

\[
J\left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right)  = { \cup  }_{t \in  \left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right) }J\left( t\right) .
\]

Then \( J\left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right) \) is an open subset of \( \mathcal{M} \) . See FIG. 4.

\[

if follows that \( \gamma \left( 0\right) \) is separated from the boundary of \( {s}_{{N}_{i}}^{-1}( - {25},0\rbrack \) by distance at least \( {20}\bar{h} \) . Since the \( {J}_{0}\left( t\right) \) are contained in the disjoint union of strong \( \delta \) -necks \( {N}_{i} \) centered at the 2-spheres along which we do surgery, and since \( {\tau }_{1} \leq  {\bar{h}}^{2}/\ell  < {\bar{h}}^{2} \) , it follows that, provided that \( \delta \) is sufficiently small, for every \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1},\bar{t}}\right) \) , the metric on \( {J}_{0}\left( t\right) \) is at least \( 1/2 \) the metric on \( {J}_{0}\left( \bar{t}\right) \) . It follows that, for \( \delta \) sufficiently small, if there is a \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }_{1}}\right\rbrack \) with \( \gamma \left( \tau \right)  \in  J\left( t\right) \) then \( {\int }_{0}^{{\tau }_{1}}\left| {X}_{\gamma }\right| {d\tau } > {10}\bar{h} \) . Applying Cauchy-Schwarz we see that

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }_{1}}{\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}{d\tau } \geq  {\left( {10}\bar{h}\right) }^{2}/{\tau }_{1}.
\]

Since \( {\tau }_{1} \leq  {\ell }^{-1}{\bar{h}}^{2} \) , we see that

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }^{\prime }}{\left| {X}_{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}{d\tau } > \ell ,
\]

contradicting our hypothesis.

DEFINITION 16.20. Fix \( \ell  < \infty \) . Let \( {\theta }_{0} = {\theta }_{0}\left( \ell \right) \) be as in Proposition 16.13. For each surgery time \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right\rbrack \) , let \( h\left( \bar{t}\right) \) be the scale of the surgery. Let \( {p}_{1},\ldots ,{p}_{k} \) be the tips of the surgery caps at time \( \bar{t} \) . For each \( 1 \leq  j \leq  k \) , we consider \( {B}_{j}\left( \bar{t}\right)  = B\left( {{p}_{j},\bar{t},\left( {{A}_{0} + {10}}\right) h\left( \bar{t}\right) }\right) \) , and we let

\[
\Delta {t}_{j} \leq  \min \left( {{\theta }_{0},\left( {T - \bar{t}}\right) /{h}^{2}\left( \bar{t}\right) }\right)
\]

be maximal subject to the condition that there is an embedding \( {\rho }_{j} : {B}_{j}\left( \bar{t}\right)  \times \; \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},\bar{t} + {h}^{2}\left( \bar{t}\right) \Delta {t}_{j}}\right) \) into \( \mathcal{M} \) compatible with time and the vector field. Clearly, \( {B}_{j}^{\prime } = B\left( {{p}_{j},\bar{t},\left( {{10} + {A}_{0}}\right) h}\right)  \cap  {C}_{\bar{t}} \) is contained in \( J\left( \bar{t}\right) \) . Let \( {\bar{t}}^{\prime } \) be the previous surgery time if there is one, otherwise set \( {\bar{t}}^{\prime } = 0 \) . Also for each \( \bar{t} \) we set \( {\tau }_{1}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right)  = \min \left( {h{\left( \bar{t}\right) }^{2}/\ell ,\bar{t} - {\bar{t}}^{\prime }}\right) \) . For each \( t \in  \left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right) ,\bar{t}}\right) \) let \( \widetilde{J}\left( t\right)  \subset  J\left( t\right) \) be the union of \( {D}_{t} \) , the disappearing region at time \( t \) , and \( \mathop{\coprod }\limits_{i}{B}_{i}^{\prime }\left( t\right) \) , the result of flowing \( \mathop{\coprod }\limits_{i}{B}_{i}^{\prime } \) backward to time \( t \) . Then we set

\[
\widetilde{J}\left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right) ,\bar{t}}\right)  \subset  J\left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right) ,\bar{t}}\right)
\]

equal to the union over \( t \in  \left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right) ,\bar{t}}\right) \) of \( \widetilde{J}\left( t\right) \) .

By construction, for each surgery time \( \bar{t} \) , the union

\[
{\nu }_{\text{ sing }}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right)  = \widetilde{J}\left( {\bar{t} - {\tau }_{1}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right) ,\bar{t}}\right)  \cup  { \cup  }_{i}{B}_{i} \times  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},\bar{t} + {h}^{2}\left( \bar{t}\right) \Delta {t}_{i}}\right)
\]

is an open subset of \( \mathcal{M} \) containing all the exposed regions and singular points at time \( \bar{t} \) .

We define \( Y\left( \ell \right)  \subset  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right\rbrack  \right) \) to be the complement of the \( { \cup  }_{\bar{t}}{\nu }_{\text{ sing }}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right) \) where the union is over all surgery times \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right\rbrack \) . Clearly, \( Y\left( \ell \right) \) is a closed subset of \( {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right\rbrack  \right) \) and hence \( Y\left( \ell \right) \) is a compact subset contained in the open subset of smooth points of \( \mathcal{M} \) . (Notice that \( Y\left( \ell \right) \) depends on \( \ell \) because \( {\tau }_{1}\left( {\ell ,\bar{t}}\right) \) and \( {\theta }_{0} \) depend on \( \ell \) .)

Proposition 16.21. Fix \( 0 < L < \infty \) . Set

\[
{L}_{0} = L + 4{\left( {T}_{i + 1}\right) }^{3/2}.
\]

Suppose that for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1},{T}_{i + 1}}\right\rbrack \) , the surgery control parameter \( \bar{\delta }\left( t\right)  \leq \; {\bar{\delta }}_{1}\left( {{L}_{0},{r}_{i + 1}}\right) \) where the right-hand side is the constant from Lemma 16.15.

Suppose that \( {\gamma }_{n} \) is a sequence of paths in \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, G}\right) \) parameterized by backward time \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) with \( \bar{\tau } \leq  T - {T}_{i - 1} \) , with \( {\gamma }_{n}\left( 0\right)  = x \) and with

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{n}\right)  \leq  L
\]

for all \( n \) . Then:

(1) After passing to a subsequence, there is a limit \( \gamma \) defined on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . The limit \( \gamma \) is a continuous path and is a uniform limit of the \( {\gamma }_{n} \) . The limit is contained in the open subset of smooth points of \( \mathcal{M} \) and has finite \( \mathcal{L} \) -length satisfying

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{n \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{n}\right) .
\]

(2) If there is a point \( y \in  {M}_{T - \bar{\tau }} \) such that \( {\gamma }_{n}\left( \bar{\tau }\right)  = y \) for all \( n \) , and if the \( {\gamma }_{n} \) are a sequence of paths parameterized by backward time from \( x \) to \( y \) with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{n \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{n}\right) \) being no greater than the \( \mathcal{L} \) -length of any path from \( x \) to \( y \) , then the limit \( \gamma \) of a subsequence is a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic connecting \( x \) to \( y \) contained in the open subset of smooth points of \( \mathcal{M} \) .

(3) There is \( \ell  < \infty \) depending only on \( L \) such that any path \( \gamma \) parameterized by backward time from \( x \) to a point \( y \in  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \right) \) whose \( \mathcal{L} \) -length is at most \( L \) is contained in the compact subset \( Y\left( \ell \right) \) given in the previous definition.

nodes.content: CLAIM 16.25. The subset \( {Z}^{\prime } = \left\{  {z \in  Z \mid  {\mathcal{L}}_{x}\left( z\right)  \leq  L/2}\right\} \) has the property that for any compact interval \( I \subset  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \) the intersection \( {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( I\right)  \cap  {Z}^{\prime } \) is compact.
nodes.content_excerpt: CLAIM 16.25. The subset \( {Z}^{\prime } = \left\{ {z \in Z \mid {\mathcal{L}}_{x}\left( z\right) \leq L/2}\right\} \) has the property that for any compact interval \( I \subset \left\lbrack {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \) the intersection \( {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( I\right) \cap {Z}^{\prime } \) is compact.

nodes.proof:
Fix a compact interval \( I \subset  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{i - 1}, T}\right) \) . Let \( \left\{  {z}_{n}\right\} \) be a sequence in \( {Z}^{\prime } \cap  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( I\right) \) . By passing to a subsequence we can assume that the sequence \( \mathbf{t}\left( {z}_{n}\right)  = {t}_{n} \) converges to some \( t \in  I \) , and that \( {\mathcal{L}}_{x}\left( {z}_{n}\right) \) converges to some \( D \leq  L/2 \) . Since the surgery times are discrete, there is a neighborhood \( J \) of \( t \) in \( I \) such that the only possible surgery time in \( J \) is \( t \) itself. By passing to a further subsequence if necessary, we can assume that \( {t}_{n} \in  J \) for all \( n \) . Fix \( n \) . First, let us consider the case when \( {t}_{n} \geq  t \) . Let \( {\gamma }_{n} \) be a minimizing

\( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic from \( x \) to \( {z}_{n} \) . Then we form the path \( {\widehat{\gamma }}_{n} \) which is the union of \( {\gamma }_{n} \) followed by the flow line for the vector field \( \chi \) from the endpoint of \( {\gamma }_{n} \) to \( {M}_{t} \) . (This flowline exists since there is no surgery time in the open interval \( \left( {t,{t}_{n}\rbrack \text{ .) If }{t}_{n} < t\text{ , then we set }{\widehat{\gamma }}_{n}\text{ equal to the restriction of }{\gamma }_{n}\text{ to the interval }}\right) \; \left\lbrack  {0, T - t}\right\rbrack \) . In either case let \( {\widehat{y}}_{n} \in  {M}_{t} \) be the endpoint of \( {\widehat{\gamma }}_{n} \) . Since \( {M}_{t} \) is compact, by passing to a subsequence we can arrange that the \( {\widehat{y}}_{n} \) converge to a point \( y \in  {M}_{t} \) . Clearly, \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{n \rightarrow  \infty }}{z}_{n} = y \) .

It is also the case that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{n \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathcal{L}\left( {\widehat{\gamma }}_{n}\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{n \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{n}\right)  = D \leq  L/2 \) . This means that \( y \in  U \) and that \( {\mathcal{L}}_{x}\left( y\right)  \leq  D \leq  L/2 \) . Hence, the greatest lower bound of the values of \( {\mathcal{L}}_{x} \) on \( {U}_{t} \) is at most \( D \leq  L/2 \) , and consequently \( {Z}^{\prime } \cap  {U}_{t} \neq  \varnothing \) . Suppose that the minimum value of \( {\mathcal{L}}_{x} \) on \( {U}_{t} \) is \( {D}^{\prime } < D \) . Let \( z \in  {U}_{t} \) be a point where this minimum value is realized, and let \( \gamma \) be a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic from \( x \) to \( z \) . Then by restricting \( \gamma \) to subintervals \( \left\lbrack  {0, t - \mu }\right\rbrack \) shows that the minimum value of \( {\mathcal{L}}_{x} \) on \( {U}_{t + \mu } \leq  \left( {{D}^{\prime } + D}\right) /2 \) for all \( \mu  > 0 \) sufficiently small. Also, extending \( \gamma \) by adding a backward vertical flow line from \( z \) shows that the minimum value of \( {\mathcal{L}}_{x} \) on \( {U}_{t - \mu } \) is at most \( \left( {{D}^{\prime } + D}\right) /2 \) for all \( \mu  > 0 \) sufficiently small. (Such a vertical flow line backward in time exists since \( z \in  U \) and hence \( z \) is contained in the smooth part of \( \mathcal{M} \) .) This contradicts the fact that the minimum values of \( {\mathcal{L}}_{x} \) on \( {U}_{{t}_{n}} \) converge to \( D \) as \( {t}_{n} \) converges to \( t \) . This contradiction proves that the minimum value of \( {\mathcal{L}}_{x} \) on \( {U}_{t} \) is \( D \) , and consequently the point \( y \in  {Z}^{\prime } \) . This proves that \( {Z}^{\prime } \cap  {\mathbf{t}}^{-1}\left( I\right) \) is compact, establishing the claim.

Suppose that for some \( i \geq  0 \) we have surgery parameter sequences \( {\delta }_{0} \geq  {\delta }_{1} \geq  \cdots  \geq  {\delta }_{i} > 0,\epsilon  = {r}_{0} \geq  {r}_{1} \geq  \cdots  \geq  {r}_{i} > 0 \) and \( {\kappa }_{0} \geq  {\kappa }_{1} \geq  \cdots  \geq  {\kappa }_{i} > 0 \) .
