Proof. We first remark that continuity has already been established. To show the inequality, we begin with a claim.

CLAIM 19.5. It suffices to prove the following for every \( \delta  > 0 \) . There is a \( {C}^{2} \) -family \( \widehat{c}\left( {x, t}\right) \) of immersions within \( \delta \) in the \( {C}^{2} \) -topology to \( c\left( {x, t}\right) \) defined on the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{ - },{t}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) such that

\[
A\left( {t}^{ + }\right)  \leq  {\psi }_{\delta ,\widehat{c}}\left( {t}^{ + }\right)
\]

where \( {\psi }_{\delta ,\widehat{c}} \) is the solution of the ODE

\[
{\psi }_{\delta ,\widehat{c}}^{\prime }\left( t\right)  =  - {2\pi } + {2\delta }{L}_{\widehat{c}}\left( t\right)  - \frac{1}{2}{R}_{\min }\left( t\right) {\psi }_{\delta ,\widehat{c}}\left( t\right)
\]

with value \( A\left( {\widehat{c}\left( {t}^{ - }\right) }\right) \) at \( {t}^{ - } \) , and where \( {L}_{\widehat{c}}\left( t\right) \) denotes the length of the loop \( \widehat{c}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) .

Proof. (of the claim) Suppose that for each \( \delta \) there is such a \( {C}^{2} \) -family as in the statement of the claim. Take a sequence \( {\delta }_{n} \) tending to zero, and let \( {\widehat{c}}_{n}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) be a family as in the claim for \( {\delta }_{n} \) . Then by the continuity of the infimum of areas of the spanning disk in the \( {C}^{1} \) -topology, we see that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{n \rightarrow  \infty }}A\left( {{\widehat{c}}_{n}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{ \pm  }}\right) }\right)  = A\left( {c\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{ \pm  }}\right) }\right) .
\]

Since the \( {\widehat{c}}_{n}\left( {x, t}\right) \) converge in the \( {C}^{2} \) -topology to \( c\left( {x, t}\right) \) , the lengths \( L\left( {{\widehat{c}}_{n}\left( t\right) }\right) \) are uniformly bounded and the \( A\left( {{\widehat{c}}_{n}\left( {t}^{ - }\right) }\right) \) converge to \( A\left( {c\left( t\right) }\right) \) . Thus, the \( {\psi }_{{\delta }_{n},{\widehat{c}}_{n}} \) converge uniformly to \( \psi \) on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{ - },{t}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) , and taking limits shows the required inequality for \( A\left( {c\left( t\right) }\right) \) , thus proving the claim.

Now we return to the proof of the lemma. Let \( \widehat{c}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be a generic \( {C}^{2} \) -immersion sufficiently close to \( c\left( {x, t}\right) \) in the \( {C}^{2} \) -topology so that the following hold:

(1) the difference of the curvature of \( \widehat{c} \) and of \( c \) at every \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is a vector of length less than \( \delta \) ,

(2) the difference of \( \partial \widehat{c}/\partial t \) and \( \partial c/\partial t \) is a vector of length less than \( \delta \) ,

(3) the ratio of the arc lengths of \( \widehat{c} \) and \( c \) at every \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is between \( \left( {1 - \delta }\right) \) and \( \left( {1 + \delta }\right) \) .

The generic family \( \widehat{c}\left( {x, t}\right) \) consists of embedded curves for all but a finite number of \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{ - },{t}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) and at the exceptional \( t \) values the curve is immersed. Let \( {t}_{1} < {t}_{2} < \cdots  < {t}_{k} \) be the values of \( t \) for which \( \widehat{c}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) is not embedded. We set \( {t}_{0} = {t}^{ - } \) and \( {t}_{k + 1} = {t}^{ + } \) . Notice that it suffices to show that

\[
A\left( {\widehat{c}\left( {t}_{i + 1}\right) }\right)  - A\left( {\widehat{c}\left( {t}_{i}\right) }\right)  \leq  {\psi }_{\delta ,\widehat{c}}\left( {t}_{i + 1}\right)  - {\psi }_{\delta ,\widehat{c}}\left( {t}_{i}\right)
\]

for \( i = 0,\ldots , k \) . To establish this inequality for the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i},{t}_{i + 1}}\right\rbrack \) , by continuity it suffices to establish the corresponding inequality for every compact subinterval contained in the interior of this interval. This allows us to assume that the approximating family is a family of embedded curves. Let the endpoints of the parameterizing interval be denoted \( a \) and \( b \) . Fix \( {t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) and let \( D \) be a minimal disk spanning \( \widehat{c}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) , and let \( {\varphi }_{t} \) be an isotopy as in the argument given the proof of Lemma 19.2. According to this argument we have

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{dt}A\left( \widehat{c}\left( t\right) \right) \right| }_{t = {t}^{\prime }} \leq   - {2\pi } - \frac{1}{2}{R}_{\min }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) A\left( {c\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{c\left( {x,{t}^{\prime }}\right) }\left\lbrack  {{k}_{\text{ geod }}\left( \widehat{c}\right)  - \left( {\frac{d{\varphi }_{t}}{dt}{ \mid  }_{t = {t}^{\prime }}}\right)  \cdot  n}\right\rbrack  {ds}
\]

in the sense of forward difference quotients. The restriction of \( {\left. \frac{d{\varphi }_{t}}{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}^{\prime }} \) to the boundary of \( D \) agrees with \( \partial \widehat{c}\left( {x, t}\right) /\partial t \) . Hence, by our conditions on the approximating family, and since for \( c\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) the corresponding quantities are equal,

\[
\left| {{k}_{\text{ geod }}\left( \widehat{c}\right)  - \left( {\left. \frac{d{\varphi }_{t}}{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}^{\prime }}\right)  \cdot  n}\right|  < {2\delta }.
\]

Integrating over the circle implies that

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{dt}A\left( \widehat{c}\left( t\right) \right) \right| }_{t = {t}^{\prime }} \leq   - {2\pi } - \frac{1}{2}{R}_{\min }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) A\left( {c\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right)  + {2\delta }{L}_{\widehat{c}}\left( t\right) .
\]

The result is then immediate from Lemma 2.22.

nodes.content:
LEMMA 19.6. Assume that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,{t}_{0} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{1} \) , is a Ricci flow and that \( c = c\left( {x, t}\right) \) is a solution to the curve-shrinking flow. We have vector fields \( X = \partial /\partial x \) and \( H = \partial /\partial t \) defined on the domain surface. We denote by \( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2} \) the function on the domain surface whose value at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is \( {\left| \left( X\left( x, t\right) \right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2} \) . We define \( S = {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{-1}X \) , the unit vector in the \( x \) -direction measured in the evolving metric. Then,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  =  - 2{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {X\left( {x, t}\right) , X\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - {\left. 2{k}^{2} \mid  X\left( x, t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2},
\]

and

\[
\left\lbrack  {H, S}\right\rbrack  \left( {x, t}\right)  = \left( {{k}^{2} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {S\left( {x, t}\right) , S\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) }\right) S\left( {x, t}\right) .
\]

We have vector fields \( X = \partial /\partial x \) and \( H = \partial /\partial t \) defined on the domain surface. We denote by \( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2} \) the function on the domain surface whose valu...

nodes.proof:
Notice that as \( t \) varies \( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2} \) is not the norm of the vector field \( X \) with respect to the pullback of a fixed metric \( g\left( t\right) \) . On the other hand, when we compute \( {\nabla }_{H}X \) at a point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) we are taking a covariant derivative with respect to the pullback of a fixed metric \( g\left( t\right) \) on the surface. Hence, in computing \( H\left( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2}\right) \) the usual Leibniz rule does not apply. In fact, there are two contributions to \( H\left( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2}\right) \) : one, the usual Leibniz rule differentiating in a frozen metric \( g\left( t\right) \) and the other coming from the effect on \( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2} \) of varying the metric with \( t \) . Thus, we have

\[
H\left( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  =  - 2{\operatorname{Ric}}_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) }\left( {X\left( {x, t}\right) , X\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + 2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{H}X\left( x, t\right) , X\left( x, t\right) \right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) }.
\]

Since \( t \) and \( x \) are coordinates on the surface swept out by the family of curves, \( {\nabla }_{H}X = {\nabla }_{X}H \) , and hence the second term on the right-hand side of the previous equation can be rewritten as \( 2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{X}H\left( x, t\right) , X\left( x, t\right) \right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) } \) . Since \( X\left( {x, t}\right) \) and \( H\left( {x, t}\right) \) are orthogonal in \( {c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) \) and since \( X = {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}S \) , computing covariant derivatives in the metric \( {c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) \) , we have

\[
2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{X}H, X\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) } =  - 2{\left\langle  H,{\nabla }_{X}X\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) }
\]

\[
=  - 2\langle H,{\left| X\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}{\nabla }_{S}S{\rangle }_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) } - 2{\left\langle  H,{\left| X\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }S\left( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}\right) S\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) }
\]

\[
=  - 2\langle H, H{\rangle }_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) }{\left| X\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
=  - {\left. 2{k}^{2}{\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2}\right| }^{2}
\]

This proves the first inequality. As for the second, since \( X \) and \( H \) commute we have

\[
\left\lbrack  {H, S}\right\rbrack   = \left\lbrack  {H,{\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{-1}X}\right\rbrack   = H\left( {\left( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2}\right) }^{-1/2}\right) X = \frac{-1}{2{\left( {\left| X\right| }_{g}^{2}\right) }^{3/2}}H\left( {\left| X\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}\right) X.
\]

According to the first equation, we can rewrite this as

\[
\left\lbrack  {H, S}\right\rbrack  \left( {x, t}\right)  = \left( {{k}^{2} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{{c}^{ * }g\left( t\right) }\left( {S\left( {x, t}\right) , S\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) }\right) S\left( {x, t}\right) .
\]

Using the same conventions as above for the function \( {\left| H\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g} \) and leaving the metric implicit, we have

(19.1)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{k}^{2} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\left| H\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2}\right)  =  - 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {H, H}\right)  + 2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{H}H, H\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g}.
\]

Now we compute (using the second equation from Lemma 19.6)

\[
{\nabla }_{H}H = {\nabla }_{H}{\nabla }_{S}S
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{S}{\nabla }_{H}S + {\nabla }_{\left\lbrack  H, S\right\rbrack  }S + \mathcal{R}\left( {H, S}\right) S
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{S}{\nabla }_{S}H + {\nabla }_{S}\left( \left\lbrack  {H, S}\right\rbrack  \right)  + {\nabla }_{\left\lbrack  H, S\right\rbrack  }S + \mathcal{R}\left( {H, S}\right) S
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{S}{\nabla }_{S}H + {\nabla }_{S}\left( {\left( {{k}^{2} + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {S, S}\right) }\right) S}\right)  + \left( {{k}^{2} + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {S, S}\right) }\right) {\nabla }_{S}S
\]

\[
+ \mathcal{R}\left( {H, S}\right) S
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{S}{\nabla }_{S}H + 2\left( {{k}^{2} + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {S, S}\right) }\right) H + S\left( {{k}^{2} + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {S, S}\right) }\right) S + \mathcal{R}\left( {H, S}\right) S.
\]

Using this, and the fact that \( \langle H, S{\rangle }_{{c}^{ * }g} = 0 \) , we have

(19.2)

\[
2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{H}H, H\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g} = {2g}\left( {{\nabla }_{S}{\nabla }_{S}H, H}\right)  + 4{k}^{4} + 4{k}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {S, S}\right) ) + 2\operatorname{Rm}\left( {H, S, H, S}\right) .
\]

On the other hand,

(19.3)

\[
S\left( {S\left( {\langle H, H{\rangle }_{{c}^{ * }g}}\right) }\right)  = 2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{S}{\nabla }_{S}H, H\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g} + 2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{S}H,{\nabla }_{S}H\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g}.
\]

We write

\[
{\nabla }_{S}H = {\left( {\nabla }_{S}H\right) }^{ \bot  } + {\left\langle  {\nabla }_{S}H, S\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g}S.
\]

Since \( H \) and \( S \) are orthogonal, we have \( {\left\langle  {\nabla }_{S}H, S\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g} =  - {\left\langle  H,{\nabla }_{S}S\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g} = \; - \langle H, H\rangle \) . Thus, we have

\[
{\nabla }_{S}H = {\left( {\nabla }_{S}H\right) }^{ \bot  } - \langle H, H{\rangle }_{{c}^{ * }g}S.
\]

It follows that

\[
- 2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{S}H,{\nabla }_{S}H\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g} =  - 2{\left\langle  {\left( {\nabla }_{S}H\right) }^{ \bot  },{\left( {\nabla }_{S}H\right) }^{ \bot  }\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g} - 2{k}^{4}.
\]

Substituting this into Equation (19.3) gives

\[
\text{ (19.4) }2{\left\langle  {\nabla }_{S}{\nabla }_{S}H, H\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g} = S\left( {S\left( {\left| H\right| }_{{c}^{ * }g}^{2}\right) }\right)  - 2{\left\langle  {\left( {\nabla }_{S}H\right) }^{ \bot  },{\left( {\nabla }_{S}H\right) }^{ \bot  }\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g} - 2{k}^{4}\text{ . }
\]

Plugging this into Equation (19.2) and using Equation (19.1) yields

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{k}^{2} =  - 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {H, H}\right)  + S\left( {S\langle H, H{\rangle }_{{c}^{ * }g}}\right)  - 2{\left\langle  {\left( {\nabla }_{S}H\right) }^{ \bot  },{\left( {\nabla }_{S}H\right) }^{ \bot  }\right\rangle  }_{{c}^{ * }g}
\]

\[
+ 2{k}^{4} + 4{k}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {S, S}\right)  + 2\operatorname{Rm}\left( {H, S, H, S}\right) .
\]

Of course, \( S\left( {S\left( {\langle H, H{\rangle }_{{c}^{ * }g}}\right) }\right)  = {\left( {k}^{2}\right) }^{\prime \prime } \) so that this gives the result.

\frac{\partial k}{\partial t} \leq  {k}^{\prime \prime } + {k}^{3} + {C}_{1}k

From the equation in Claim 19.11, we see that for \( {C}^{\prime } \) an upper bound for the norm of the Ricci curvature, we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{e}^{{C}^{\prime }t}u}\right)  \geq  {\left( {e}^{{C}^{\prime }t}u\right) }^{\prime \prime }.
\]

It now follows from a standard maximum principle argument that the minimum value of \( {e}^{{C}^{\prime }t}u \) is a non-decreasing function of \( t \) . Hence, if \( c\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) is a ramp, then each \( c\left( t\right) \) is a ramp and in fact \( u\left( {x, t}\right) \) is uniformly bounded away from zero in terms of the minimum of \( u\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) \) and the total elapsed time \( {t}_{1} - {t}_{0} \) .

Then there is a curve-shrinking flow \( c\left( {x, t}\right) \) defined for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) with \( c \) as the initial condition at time \( t = {t}_{0} \) . The curves \( c\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) are all ramps.

nodes.proof:
The real issue here is to show that the curve-shrinking flow exists for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . Given this, the second part of the statement follows from the previous corollary. If the curve shrinking flow does not exist on all of \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) then by Claim 19.1 there is a \( {t}_{1}^{\prime } \leq  {t}_{1} \) such that the curve-shrinking flow exists on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}^{\prime }}\right) \) but \( k \) is unbounded on \( {S}^{1} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}^{\prime }}\right) \) . Thus, to complete the proof we need to see that for any \( {t}_{1}^{\prime } \) for which the curve-shrinking flow is defined on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}^{\prime }}\right) \) we have a uniform bound on \( k \) on this region.

Using Claim 19.8 and Claim 19.11 we compute

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( \frac{k}{u}\right)  = \frac{1}{u}\frac{\partial k}{\partial t} - \frac{k}{{u}^{2}}\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{{k}^{\prime \prime } + {k}^{3} + {C}_{1}k}{u} - \frac{k}{{u}^{2}}\left( {{u}^{\prime \prime } + \left( {{k}^{2} + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {S, S}\right) }\right) u}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{{k}^{\prime \prime }}{u} - \frac{k{u}^{\prime \prime }}{{u}^{2}} + \frac{{C}_{1}k}{u} - \frac{k}{u}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {S, S}\right) .
\]

On the other hand,

\[
{\left( \frac{k}{u}\right) }^{\prime \prime } = \frac{{k}^{\prime \prime }u - {u}^{\prime \prime }k}{{u}^{2}} - 2\left( \frac{{u}^{\prime }}{u}\right) \left( \frac{{k}^{\prime }u - {u}^{\prime }k}{{u}^{2}}\right) .
\]

Plugging this in, and using the curvature bound on the ambient manifolds we get

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( \frac{k}{u}\right)  \leq  {\left( \frac{k}{u}\right) }^{\prime \prime } + \left( \frac{2{u}^{\prime }}{u}\right) {\left( \frac{k}{u}\right) }^{\prime } + {C}^{\prime }\frac{k}{u},
\]

for a constant \( {C}^{\prime } \) depending only on a bound for the norm of the sectional curvature of the ambient Ricci flow. A standard maximum principle argument shows that the maximum of \( k/u \) at time \( t \) grows at most exponentially rapidly in \( t \) . Since \( u \) stays bounded away from zero, this implies that for ramp solutions on a finite time interval, the value of \( k \) is bounded.

LEMMA 19.15. Suppose that the dimension, \( n \) , of \( M \) is at least 3 . Let \( {c}_{1}\left( {x, t}\right) \) and \( {c}_{2}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be ramp solutions in \( \left( {M, g}\right)  \times  \left( {{S}_{\lambda }^{1}, d{s}^{2}}\right) \) with the image under the projection to \( {S}_{\lambda }^{1} \) of each \( {c}_{i} \) being of degree 1 . Let \( \mu \left( t\right) \) be the infimum of the areas of annuli in \( \left( {M \times  {S}_{\lambda }^{1}, g\left( t\right)  \times  d{s}^{2}}\right) \) with boundary \( {c}_{1}\left( {x, t}\right)  \cup \; {c}_{2}\left( {x, t}\right) \) . Then \( \mu \left( t\right) \) is a continuous function of \( t \) and

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mu \left( t\right)  \leq  \left( {{2n} - 1}\right) \mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right| \mu \left( t\right) ,
\]

in the sense of forward difference quotients.

nodes.proof:
Fix a time \( {t}^{\prime } \) . First assume that the loops \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) are disjoint. Under Ricci flow the metrics on the manifold immediately become real analytic (see [3]) and furthermore, under the curve-shrinking flow the curves \( {c}_{1} \) and \( {c}_{2} \) immediately become analytic (see [21]). [Neither of these results is essential for this argument because we could approximate both the metric and the curves by real analytic objects.] Establishing the results for these and taking limits would give the result in general. Since \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) are homotopic and are homotopically non-trivial, there is an annulus connecting them and there is a positive lower bound to the length of any simple closed curve in any such annulus homotopic to a boundary component. Hence, there is a minimal annulus spanning \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \coprod  {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) According to results of Hildebrandt ([40]) and Morrey ([52]) any minimal annulus \( A \) with boundary the union of these two curves is real analytic up to and including the boundary and is immersed except for finitely many branch points. By shifting the boundary curves slightly within the annulus, we can assume that there are no boundary branch points. Again, if we can prove the result for these perturbed curves, taking limits will give the result for the original ones. Given the deformation vector \( H \) on the boundary of the annulus, extend it to a deformation vector \( \widehat{H} \) on the entire annulus. The first order variation of the area at time \( {t}^{\prime } \) of the resulting deformed family of annuli is given by

\[
\frac{d\operatorname{Area}A}{dt}\left( {t}^{\prime }\right)  = {\int }_{A}\left( {-\operatorname{Tr}\left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}^{T}\left( {g\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right) }\right) }\right) {da} + {\int }_{\partial A} - {k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds},
\]

where \( {\operatorname{Ric}}^{T} \) is the Ricci curvature in the tangent directions to the annulus. (The first term is the change in the area of the fixed annulus as the metric deforms. The second term is the change in the area of the family of annuli in the fixed metric. There is no contribution from moving the annulus in the normal direction since the original annulus is minimal.) If \( A \) is embedded, then by the Gauss-Bonnet theorem, we have

\[
{\int }_{\partial A} - {k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds} = {\int }_{A}{Kda}
\]

where \( K \) is the Gaussian curvature of \( A \) . More generally, if \( A \) has interior branch points of orders \( {n}_{1},\ldots ,{n}_{k} \) then there is a correction term and the formula is

\[
{\int }_{\partial A} - {k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds} = {\int }_{A}{Kda} - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{k}{2\pi }\left( {{n}_{i} - 1}\right) .
\]

Thus, we see

\[
\frac{d\operatorname{Area}A}{dt}\left( {t}^{\prime }\right)  \leq  {\int }_{A}\left( {-\operatorname{Tr}\left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}^{T}\left( {g\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right) }\right)  + K}\right) {da}.
\]

On the other hand, since \( A \) is a minimal surface, \( K \) is at most the sectional curvature of \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right)  \times  \left( {{S}_{\lambda }^{1}, d{s}^{2}}\right) \) along the two-plane tangent to the annulus. Of course, the trace of the Ricci curvature along \( A \) is at most \( 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left| {\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,{t}^{\prime }}\right) }\right| \) . Hence,

\[
\frac{d\operatorname{Area}A}{dt}\left( {t}^{\prime }\right)  \leq  \left( {{2n} - 1}\right) \left| {\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,{t}^{\prime }}\right) }\right| \mu \left( {t}^{\prime }\right) .
\]

This computation was done assuming \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) is disjoint from \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) . In general, since the dimension of \( M \) is at least 3, given \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) we can find \( {c}_{3}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) arbitrarily close to \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) in the \( {C}^{2} \) -sense and disjoint from both \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) . Let \( {A}_{3} \) be a minimal annulus connecting \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) to \( {c}_{3}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {A}_{2} \) be a minimal annulus connecting \( {c}_{3}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) to \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) . We apply the above argument to these annuli to estimate the growth rate of minimal annuli connecting the corresponding curve-shrinking flows. Of course the sum of these areas (as a function of \( t \) ) is an upper bound for the area of a minimal annulus connecting the curve-shrinking flows starting from \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) . As we choose \( {c}_{3}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) closer and closer to \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) , the area of \( {A}_{2} \) tends to zero and the area of \( {A}_{3} \) tends to the area of a minimal annulus connecting \( {c}_{1}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {c}_{2}\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) . This establishes the continuity of \( \mu \left( t\right) \) at \( {t}^{\prime } \) and also establishes the forward difference quotient estimate in the general case.

COROLLARY 19.21. Let \( \Gamma  : {S}^{2} \rightarrow  {\Lambda M} \) be a continuous map with the property that \( \Gamma \left( c\right) \) is homotopically trivial for all \( c \in  {S}^{2} \) . Fix \( \zeta  > 0 \) . For any \( n \) sufficiently large denote by \( {\Gamma }_{n} \) the family of loops defined by setting \( {\Gamma }_{n}\left( c\right) \) equal to the \( n \) -polygonal approximation to \( \Gamma \left( c\right) \) . There is \( N \) such that for all \( n \geq  N \) we have:

(1) \( {\Gamma }_{n} \) is a continuous family of \( n \) -polygonal loops in \( M \) .

(2) For each \( c \in  {S}^{2} \) , the loop \( {\Gamma }_{n}\left( c\right) \) is a homotopically trivial loop in \( M \) and its length is within \( \zeta \) of the length of \( \Gamma \left( c\right) \) .

The total curvature of \( \widetilde{\Gamma }{\left( c\right) }^{\lambda } \) is the sum over the intervals \( \left\lbrack  {{\xi }_{n}^{k},{\xi }_{n}^{k + 1}}\right\rbrack \) of the total curvature on these intervals. On any one of these intervals we have a curve in a totally geodesic, flat surface: the curve lies in the product of a geodesic arc in \( M \) times \( {S}_{\lambda }^{1} \) . Let \( u \) and \( v \) be unit tangent vectors to this surface, \( u \) along the geodesic (in the direction of increasing \( x \) ) and \( v \) along the \( {S}_{\lambda }^{1} \) factor. These are parallel vector fields on the flat surface. The tangent vector \( X\left( x\right) \) to the restriction of \( \widetilde{\Gamma }{\left( c\right) }^{\lambda } \) to this interval is \( L{\psi }_{n}\left( x\right) u + \left( {\lambda /{2\pi }}\right) v \) , where \( L \) is the length of the geodesic segment we are considering. Consider the first-half subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {{\xi }_{n}^{k},{\xi }_{n}^{k} \cdot  \exp \left( {{\pi i}/n}\right) }\right\rbrack \) . The tangent vector \( X\left( x\right) \) is \( \left( {\lambda /{2\pi }}\right) v \) at the initial point of this subinterval and is \( L{\psi }_{n}\left( {{\xi }_{n}^{k} \cdot  \exp \left( {{\pi i}/2}\right) }\right) u + \; \left( {\lambda /{2\pi }}\right) v \) at the final point. Throughout this interval the vector is of the form \( a\left( x\right) u + \left( {\lambda /{2\pi }}\right) v \) where \( a\left( x\right) \) is an increasing function of \( x \) . Hence, the tangent vector is always turning in the same direction and always lies in the first quadrant (using \( u \) and \( v \) as the coordinates). Consequently, the total turning (the integral of \( k \) against arc-length) over this interval is the absolute value of the difference of the angles at the endpoints. This difference is less than \( \pi /2 \) and tends to \( \pi /2 \) as \( \lambda \) tends to zero, unless \( L = 0 \) in which case there is zero turning for any \( \lambda  > 0 \) . By symmetry, the total turning on the second-half subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {{\xi }_{n}^{k} \cdot  \exp \left( {{\pi i}/n}\right) ,{\xi }_{n}^{k + 1}}\right\rbrack \) is also bounded above by \( \pi /2 \) . Thus, for any \( \lambda  > 0 \) , the total turning on one of the segments is bounded above by \( \pi \) . Since there are \( n \) segments this gives the upper bound of \( {n\pi } \) on the total turning of \( \widetilde{\Gamma }{\left( c\right) }^{\lambda } \) as required.

nodes.proof:
All the constants in this argument are allowed to depend on \( {t}_{1} - {t}_{0} \) , on the curvature bound of the sectional curvature of the Ricci flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,{t}_{0} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{1} \) , on the original family \( \Gamma \) and on \( \zeta \) but are independent of \( \lambda , c \in  {S}^{2} \) , and \( {t}^{\prime } < {t}^{\prime \prime } \) with \( {t}_{0} \leq  {t}^{\prime } \) and \( {t}^{\prime \prime } \leq  {t}_{1} \) . First, let us consider the surface \( {S}_{c}^{\lambda }\left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack \) in \( M \times  {S}_{\lambda }^{1} \) swept out by \( c\left( {x, t}\right) ,{t}^{\prime } \leq  t \leq  {t}^{\prime \prime } \) . We denote by \( \operatorname{Area}\left( {{S}_{c}^{\lambda }\left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) the area of this surface with respect to the metric \( g\left( {t}^{\prime \prime }\right)  \times  d{s}^{2} \) . We compute the derivative of this area for fixed \( {t}^{\prime } \) as \( {t}^{\prime \prime } \) varies. There are two contributions to this derivative: (i) the contribution due to the variation of the metric \( g\left( {t}^{\prime \prime }\right) \) with \( {t}^{\prime \prime } \) and (ii) the contribution due to enlarging the surface. The first is

\[
{\int }_{{S}_{c}^{\lambda }\left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack  } - \operatorname{Tr}{\operatorname{Ric}}^{T}{da}
\]

where \( {\operatorname{Ric}}^{T} \) is the restriction of the Ricci tensor of the ambient metric \( g\left( {t}^{\prime \prime }\right) \) to the tangent planes to the surface and \( {da} \) is the area form of the surface in the metric \( g\left( {t}^{\prime \prime }\right)  \times  d{s}^{2} \) . The second contribution is \( {\int }_{c\left( {x,{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right) }\left| H\right| {ds} \) . According to Lemma 19.9 there is a constant \( {C}^{\prime } \) (depending only on the curvature bound for the manifold flow, the initial family \( \Gamma \left( t\right) \) and \( \zeta \) and \( {t}_{1} - {t}_{0} \) ) such that the second term is bounded above by \( {C}^{\prime } \) . The first term is bounded above by \( {C}^{\prime \prime } \) Area \( {S}_{c}^{\lambda }\left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack \) where \( {C}^{\prime \prime } \) depends only on the bound on the sectional curvatures of the ambient Ricci flow. Integrating we see that there is a constant \( {C}_{1}^{\prime } \) such that the derivative of the area function is at most \( {C}_{1}^{\prime } \) . Since its value at \( {t}^{\prime } \) is zero, we see that \( \operatorname{Area}{S}_{c}^{\lambda }\left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack   \leq  {C}_{1}^{\prime }\left( {{t}^{\prime \prime } - {t}^{\prime }}\right) \) . It follows that the area of \( {p}_{1}{S}_{c}^{\lambda }\left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack \) with respect to the metric \( g\left( {t}^{\prime \prime }\right) \) is at most \( {C}_{1}^{\prime }\left( {{t}^{\prime \prime } - {t}^{\prime }}\right) \) .

Now we compute an upper bound for the forward difference quotient of \( A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) }\right) \) at \( t = {t}^{\prime } \) . For any \( {t}^{\prime \prime } > {t}^{\prime } \) we have a spanning disk for \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime \prime }\right) \) defined by taking the union of a minimal spanning disk for \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) and the annulus \( {p}_{1}{S}_{c}^{\lambda }\left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack \) . As before, the derivative of the area of this family of disks has two contributions, one coming from the change in the metric over the minimal spanning disk at time \( {t}^{\prime } \) and the other which we computed above to be at most \( {C}_{1}^{\prime } \) . Thus, the derivative is bounded above by \( {C}_{2}^{\prime }A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right)  + {C}_{1}^{\prime } \) . This implies that the forward difference quotient of \( A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right) \) is bounded above by the same quantity. It follows immediately that the areas of all the minimal spanning surfaces are bounded by a constant depending only on the areas of the minimal spanning surfaces at time \( {t}_{0} \) , the sectional curvature of the ambient Ricci flow and \( {t}_{1} - {t}_{0} \) . Hence, there is a constant \( {C}_{4} \) such that the forward difference quotient of \( A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is bounded above by \( {C}_{4} \) . This proves the claim.

Lemma 19.24. Let \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,{t}_{0} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{1} \) , be a Ricci flow. Then there exist constants \( \delta  > 0 \) and \( {\widetilde{C}}_{i} < \infty \) for \( i = 0,1,2,\ldots \) , depending only on \( {t}_{1} - {t}_{0} \) and a bound for the norm of the curvature of the Ricci flow, such that the following holds. Let \( c\left( {x, t}\right) \) be a curve-shrinking flow that is an immersion for each \( t \) . Suppose that at a time \( {t}^{\prime } \) for some \( 0 < r < 1 \) such that \( {t}^{\prime } + \delta {r}^{2} < {t}_{1} \) , the length of \( c\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) is at least \( r \) and the total curvature of \( c\left( {\cdot ,{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) on any sub-arc of length \( r \) is at most \( \delta \) . Then for every \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime } + \delta {r}^{2}}\right) \) the curvature \( k \) and the higher derivatives satisfy

\[
{k}^{2} \leq  {\widetilde{C}}_{0}{\left( t - {t}^{\prime }\right) }^{-1}
\]

\[
{\left| {\nabla }_{S}H\right| }^{2} \leq  {\widetilde{C}}_{1}{\left( t - {t}^{\prime }\right) }^{-2}
\]

\[
{\left| {\nabla }_{S}^{i}H\right| }^{2} \leq  {\widetilde{C}}_{i}{\left( t - {t}^{\prime }\right) }^{-\left( {i + 1}\right) }.
\]

The first statement follows from arguments very similar to those in Section 4 of [2]. Once \( {k}^{2} \) is bounded by \( {\widetilde{C}}_{0}/\left( {t - {t}^{\prime }}\right) \) the higher derivative statements are standard, see [1]. For completeness we have included the proof of the first inequality in the last section of this chapter.

Now let us return to the proof of Lemma 19.25. Recall that \( c \in  {S}^{2} \) is fixed. We shall apply the above claims to the curve-shrinking flow \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) \) and thus prove Lemma 19.25. Now it is time to fix \( B \) . First, we fix \( \widetilde{A} = W\left( \Gamma \right)  + \zeta \) , we let \( {C}_{2} \) be as in Corollary 19.10, \( {C}_{4} \) be as in Claim 19.23, \( {C}_{5} \) be as in Equation (19.9), and \( {C}_{6} \) be as in the proof of Claim 19.26. Then we have \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) depending on \( {C}_{6},{C}_{4},\widetilde{A} \) as in Claim 19.26. We fix \( B \) so that:

(1) \( B \geq  3{C}_{5}{\left( {\delta }^{\prime }\right) }^{-1} \) ,

(2) \( B \geq  3{e}^{{C}_{2}\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }{\zeta }^{-1} \) , and

(3) \( B > {C}_{2}/\left( {\log 4 - \log 3}\right) \) .

The first step in the proof of Lemma 19.25 is the following:

CLAIM 19.28. After passing to a subsequence of \( \left\{  {\lambda }_{n}\right\} \) , either:

(1) for each \( n \) sufficiently large there is \( {t}_{n} \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) with the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{n}\right)  < {\delta }^{2}{B}^{-1} \) , or

(2) for each component \( {J}_{i} = \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) of \( {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) , after composing \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {x, t}\right) \) by a reparameterization of the domain circle (fixed in \( t \) but a different reparameterization for each \( n \) ) so that the \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) have constant speed, there is a smooth limiting curve-shrinking flow denoted \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}\left( t\right) \) , for \( t \in  {J}_{i} \) for the sequence \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) ,{t}_{i}^{ - } \leq  t \leq  {t}_{i}^{ + } \) . The limiting flow consists of immersions.

Proof. Suppose that the first case does not hold for any subsequence. Fix a component \( {J}_{i} \) of \( {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) . Then, by passing to a subsequence, by the fact that \( {J}_{B}\left( c\right)  \subset  {J}_{B}\left( {c,{\lambda }_{n}}\right) \) for all \( n \) , the curvatures and all the derivatives of the curvatures of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) are uniformly bounded independent of \( n \) for all \( t \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) . We reparameterize the domain circle so that the \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) have constant speed. By passing to a subsequence we can suppose that the lengths of the \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) converge. The limit is automatically positive since we are assuming that the first case does not hold for any subsequence. Denote by \( {S}_{n} = {S}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) the unit tangent vector to \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) and by \( {u}_{n} \) the inner product \( \left\langle  {{S}_{n}, U}\right\rangle \) . Now we have a family of loops with tangent vectors and all higher derivatives bounded. Since \( {u}_{n} \) is everywhere positive, since \( \int {u}_{n}{ds} = {\lambda }_{n} \) , since the length of the loop \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) is bounded away from 0 independent of \( n \) , and since \( \left| {\left( {u}_{n}\right) }^{\prime }\right|  = \left| \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{S}_{n}}{S}_{n}, U}\right\rangle  \right| \) is bounded above independent of \( n \) , we see that \( {u}_{n} \) tends uniformly to zero as \( n \) tends to infinity. This means that the \( \left| {{p}_{1}\left( {S}_{n}\right) }\right| \) converge uniformly to 1 as \( n \) goes to infinity. Since the ambient manifold is compact, passing to a further subsequence we have a smooth limit of the \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) . The result is an immersed curve in \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) }\right) \) parameterized at unit speed. Since all the spatial and time derivatives of the \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) are uniformly bounded, by passing to a further subsequence, there is a smooth map \( f : {S}^{1} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) which is a smooth limit of the sequence \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) ,{t}_{i}^{ - } \leq  t \leq  {t}_{i}^{ + } \) . If for some \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) the curve \( {\left. f\right| }_{{S}^{1}\times \{ t\} } \) is immersed, then this limiting map along this curve agrees to first order with the curve-shrinking flow. Thus, for some \( t > {t}_{i}^{ - } \) the restriction of \( f \) to the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - }, t}\right\rbrack \) is a curve-shrinking flow. We claim that \( f \) is a curve-shrinking flow on the entire interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) . Suppose not. Then there is a first \( {t}^{\prime } \leq  {t}_{i}^{ + } \) for which \( {\left. f\right| }_{{S}^{1} \times  \left\{  {t}^{\prime }\right\}  } \) is not an immersion. According to Claim 19.1 the maximum of the norms of the curvature of the curves \( f\left( t\right) \) must tend to infinity as \( t \) approaches \( {t}^{\prime } \) from below. But the curvatures of \( f\left( t\right) \) are the limits of the curvatures of the family \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) and hence are uniformly bounded on the entire interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) . This contradiction shows that the entire limiting surface

\[
f : {S}^{1} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

is a curve-shrinking flow of immersions.

REMARK 19.29. Notice that if the first case holds, then by the choice of \( B \) we have a point \( {t}_{n} \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) for which the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{n}\right) \) is less than \( {e}^{-{C}_{2}\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }\zeta /3 \)

For each \( n \) , the family of curves \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) in \( M \) all have \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = \widetilde{\Gamma }\left( c\right) \) as their initial member. Thus, these curves are all homotopically trivial. Hence, for each \( t \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) the limiting curve \( \widetilde{\Gamma }\left( c\right) \left( t\right) \) of the \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) is then also homotopically trivial. It now follows from Lemma 19.4, Claim 19.28 and Remark 19.29 that one of the following two conditions holds:

(1) for some \( t \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) the length of \( \widetilde{\Gamma }\left( c\right) \left( t\right) \) is less than or equal to \( {e}^{-{C}_{2}\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }\zeta /3 \) or

(2) the function \( A\left( t\right) \) that assigns to each \( t \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) the area of the minimal spanning disk for \( {p}_{1}\widetilde{\Gamma }\left( c\right) \left( t\right) \) satisfies

\[
\frac{{dA}\left( t\right) }{dt} \leq   - {2\pi } - \frac{1}{2}{R}_{\min }\left( t\right) A\left( t\right)
\]

in the sense of forward difference quotients.

By continuity, for any \( {\delta }^{\prime \prime } > 0 \) then for all \( n \) sufficiently large one of the following two conditions holds:

(1) there is \( {t}_{n} \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) such that the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{n}\right) \) is less than \( {e}^{-{C}_{2}\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }\zeta /2 \) , or

(2) for every \( t \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) , the areas of the minimal spanning disks for \( {p}_{1}\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfy

\[
\frac{{dA}\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) }\right) }{dt} \leq   - {2\pi } - \frac{1}{2}{R}_{\min }\left( t\right) A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) }\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime \prime }
\]

in the sense of forward difference quotients.

Suppose that for every \( n \) sufficiently large, for every \( t \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) is at least \( {e}^{-{C}_{2}\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }\zeta /2 \) . We have already seen in Claim 19.23 that for every \( {t}^{\prime } < {t}^{\prime \prime } \) in \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) the areas satisfy

\[
A\left( {{p}_{1}\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}^{\prime \prime }\right) }\right) }\right)  - A\left( {{p}_{1}\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right) }\right)  \leq  {C}_{4}\left( {{t}^{\prime \prime } - {t}^{\prime }}\right) .
\]

Since the total length of the complement \( {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) in \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) is at most \( 3{C}_{5}{B}^{-1} \) , it follows from our choice of \( B \) that this total length is at most the constant \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) of Claim 19.26. Invoking Claim 19.27 and the fact that \( A\left( {\widetilde{\Gamma }\left( c\right) }\right)  \leq  W\left( {\Gamma \left( c\right) }\right)  + \; \zeta  \leq  W\left( \Gamma \right)  + \zeta  = \widetilde{A} \) , we see that for all \( n \) sufficiently large we have

\[
A\left( {{p}_{1}\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{{\lambda }_{n}}^{c}\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right) }\right)  - {v}_{c}\left( {t}_{1}\right)  < \zeta /2.
\]

The other possibility to consider is that for each \( n \) there is \( {t}_{n} \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) such that the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{n}\right)  < {e}^{-{C}_{2}\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }\zeta /2 \) . Since \( {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) is contained in \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1} - {B}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) , in this case we invoke the first inequality in Corollary 19.10 to see that the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right)  < \zeta /2 \) for every \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1} - {B}^{-1},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . This completes the proof of Lemma 19.25.

CLAIM 19.26. Fix \( {C}_{4} \) as in Claim 19.23 and fix a constant \( \widetilde{A} > 0 \) . Given \( \zeta  > 0 \) there is \( {\delta }^{\prime } > 0 \) depending on \( {C}_{4},{t}_{1} - {t}_{0} \) , and \( \widetilde{A} \) as well as the curvature bound of the ambient Ricci flow such that the following holds. Suppose that \( f : \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a function and suppose that \( J \subset  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) is a finite union of intervals. Suppose that on each interval \( \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) of \( J \) the function \( f \) satisfies

\[
f\left( b\right)  \leq  {w}_{f\left( a\right) , a}\left( b\right) .
\]

Suppose further that for any \( {t}^{\prime } < {t}^{\prime \prime } \) we have

\[
f\left( {t}^{\prime \prime }\right)  \leq  f\left( {t}^{\prime }\right)  + {C}_{4}\left( {{t}^{\prime \prime } - {t}^{\prime }}\right) .
\]

Then, provided that the total length of \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack   \smallsetminus  J \) is at most \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) and \( 0 \leq \; f\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{A} \) , we have

\[
f\left( {t}_{1}\right)  \leq  {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {t}_{1}\right)  + \zeta /4
\]

nodes.proof:
We write \( J \) as a union of disjoint intervals \( {J}_{1},\ldots ,{J}_{k} \) so that \( {J}_{i} < {J}_{i + 1} \) for every \( i \) . Let \( {a}_{i} \) , resp. \( {b}_{i} \) , be the initial, resp. final, point of \( {J}_{i} \) . For each \( i \) let \( {\delta }_{i} \) be the length of the interval between \( {J}_{i} \) and \( {J}_{i + 1} \) . (Also, we set \( {\delta }_{0} = {a}_{1} - {t}_{0} \) , and \( {\delta }_{k} = {t}_{1} - {b}_{k} \) .) Let \( {C}_{6} \geq  0 \) be such that \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  \geq   - 2{C}_{6} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . Let \( V\left( a\right) \) be the maximum value of \( \left| {w}_{a,{t}_{0}}\right| \) on the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) and let \( V = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{a \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\widetilde{A}}\right\rbrack  }}V\left( a\right) \) . Let \( {C}_{7} = {C}_{4} + {2\pi } + {C}_{6}V \) . We shall prove by induction that

\[
f\left( {a}_{i}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {a}_{i}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{{i - 1}}\left( {{C}_{7}{\delta }_{j}\mathop{\prod }\limits_{{\ell  = j + 1}}^{{i - 1}}{e}^{{C}_{6}\left| {J}_{\ell }\right| }}\right)
\]

and

\[
f\left( {b}_{i}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {b}_{i}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{{i - 1}}\left( {{C}_{7}{\delta }_{j}\mathop{\prod }\limits_{{\ell  = j + 1}}^{i}{e}^{{C}_{6}\left| {J}_{\ell }\right| }}\right) .
\]

We begin the induction by establishing the result at \( {a}_{1} \) . By hypothesis we know that

\[
f\left( {a}_{1}\right)  \leq  f\left( {t}_{0}\right)  + {C}_{4}{\delta }_{0}.
\]

On the other hand, from the defining differential equation for \( {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}} \) and the definitions of \( {C}_{6} \) and \( V \) we have

\[
{w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {a}_{1}\right)  \geq  f\left( {t}_{0}\right)  - \left( {{C}_{6}V + {2\pi }}\right) {\delta }_{0}.
\]

Thus,

\[
f\left( {a}_{1}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {a}_{1}\right)  \leq  \left( {{C}_{4} + {2\pi } + {C}_{6}V}\right) {\delta }_{0} = {C}_{7}{\delta }_{0},
\]

which is exactly the formula given in the case of \( {a}_{1} \) .

Now suppose that we know the result for \( {a}_{i} \) and let us establish it for \( {b}_{i} \) . Let \( {\alpha }_{i} = f\left( {a}_{i}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {a}_{i}\right) \) , and let \( {\beta }_{i} = f\left( {b}_{i}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {b}_{i}\right) \) . Then by Claim 18.26 we have

\[
{\beta }_{i} \leq  {e}^{{C}_{6}\left| {J}_{i}\right| }{\alpha }_{i}.
\]

Given the inductive inequality for \( {\alpha }_{i} \) , we immediately get the one for \( {\beta }_{i} \) .

Now suppose that we have the inductive inequality for \( {\beta }_{i} \) . Then

\[
f\left( {a}_{i + 1}\right)  \leq  f\left( {b}_{i}\right)  + {C}_{4}{\delta }_{i}.
\]

On the other hand, by the definition of \( {C}_{6} \) and \( V \) we have

\[
{w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {a}_{i + 1}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {b}_{i}\right)  \geq   - \left( {{C}_{6}V + {2\pi }}\right) {\delta }_{i}.
\]

This yields

\[
f\left( {a}_{i + 1}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {a}_{i + 1}\right)  \leq  {\beta }_{i} + {C}_{7}{\delta }_{i}.
\]

Hence, the inductive result for \( {\beta }_{i} \) implies the result for \( {\alpha }_{i + 1} \) . This completes the induction.

Applying this to \( {a}_{k + 1} = {t}_{1} \) gives

\[
f\left( {t}_{1}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {t}_{1}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{k}\left( {{C}_{7}{\delta }_{j}\mathop{\prod }\limits_{{\ell  = j + 1}}^{k}{e}^{{C}_{6}\left| {J}_{\ell }\right| }}\right)  \leq  {C}_{7}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{k}{\delta }_{j}{e}^{{C}_{6}\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }.
\]

Of course \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{k}{\delta }_{j} = {t}_{1} - {t}_{0} - \ell \left( J\right)  \leq  {\delta }^{\prime } \) , and \( {C}_{7} \) only depends on \( {C}_{6},{C}_{4} \) and \( V \) , while \( V \) only depends on \( \widetilde{A} \) and \( {C}_{6} \) only depends on the sectional curvature bound on the ambient Ricci flow. Thus, given \( {C}_{4},\widetilde{A} \) and \( {t}_{1} - {t}_{0} \) and the bound on the sectional curvature of the ambient Ricci flow, making \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) sufficiently small makes \( f\left( {t}_{1}\right)  - {w}_{f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) arbitrarily small. This completes the proof of the claim.

CLAIM 19.28. After passing to a subsequence of \( \left\{  {\lambda }_{n}\right\} \) , either:

(1) for each \( n \) sufficiently large there is \( {t}_{n} \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) with the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{n}\right)  < {\delta }^{2}{B}^{-1} \) , or

(2) for each component \( {J}_{i} = \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) of \( {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) , after composing \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {x, t}\right) \) by a reparameterization of the domain circle (fixed in \( t \) but a different reparameterization for each \( n \) ) so that the \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) have constant speed, there is a smooth limiting curve-shrinking flow denoted \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}\left( t\right) \) , for \( t \in  {J}_{i} \) for the sequence \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) ,{t}_{i}^{ - } \leq  t \leq  {t}_{i}^{ + } \) . The limiting flow consists of immersions.

After passing to a subsequence of \( \left\{ {\lambda }_{n}\right\} \) , either: (1) for each \( n \) sufficiently large there is \( {t}_{n} \in {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) with the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{n}\right) < {\delta }^{2}{B}^{-1} \) , or (2) for each component \( {J}_{i} = \left\lbrack {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) of \( {J}_{B}\left(...

nodes.proof:
Suppose that the first case does not hold for any subsequence. Fix a component \( {J}_{i} \) of \( {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) . Then, by passing to a subsequence, by the fact that \( {J}_{B}\left( c\right)  \subset  {J}_{B}\left( {c,{\lambda }_{n}}\right) \) for all \( n \) , the curvatures and all the derivatives of the curvatures of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) are uniformly bounded independent of \( n \) for all \( t \in  {J}_{B}\left( c\right) \) . We reparameterize the domain circle so that the \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) have constant speed. By passing to a subsequence we can suppose that the lengths of the \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) converge. The limit is automatically positive since we are assuming that the first case does not hold for any subsequence. Denote by \( {S}_{n} = {S}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) the unit tangent vector to \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) and by \( {u}_{n} \) the inner product \( \left\langle  {{S}_{n}, U}\right\rangle \) . Now we have a family of loops with tangent vectors and all higher derivatives bounded. Since \( {u}_{n} \) is everywhere positive, since \( \int {u}_{n}{ds} = {\lambda }_{n} \) , since the length of the loop \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) is bounded away from 0 independent of \( n \) , and since \( \left| {\left( {u}_{n}\right) }^{\prime }\right|  = \left| \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{{S}_{n}}{S}_{n}, U}\right\rangle  \right| \) is bounded above independent of \( n \) , we see that \( {u}_{n} \) tends uniformly to zero as \( n \) tends to infinity. This means that the \( \left| {{p}_{1}\left( {S}_{n}\right) }\right| \) converge uniformly to 1 as \( n \) goes to infinity. Since the ambient manifold is compact, passing to a further subsequence we have a smooth limit of the \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) \) . The result is an immersed curve in \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{i}^{ - }\right) }\right) \) parameterized at unit speed. Since all the spatial and time derivatives of the \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) are uniformly bounded, by passing to a further subsequence, there is a smooth map \( f : {S}^{1} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) which is a smooth limit of the sequence \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) ,{t}_{i}^{ - } \leq  t \leq  {t}_{i}^{ + } \) . If for some \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) the curve \( {\left. f\right| }_{{S}^{1}\times \{ t\} } \) is immersed, then this limiting map along this curve agrees to first order with the curve-shrinking flow. Thus, for some \( t > {t}_{i}^{ - } \) the restriction of \( f \) to the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - }, t}\right\rbrack \) is a curve-shrinking flow. We claim that \( f \) is a curve-shrinking flow on the entire interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) . Suppose not. Then there is a first \( {t}^{\prime } \leq  {t}_{i}^{ + } \) for which \( {\left. f\right| }_{{S}^{1} \times  \left\{  {t}^{\prime }\right\}  } \) is not an immersion. According to Claim 19.1 the maximum of the norms of the curvature of the curves \( f\left( t\right) \) must tend to infinity as \( t \) approaches \( {t}^{\prime } \) from below. But the curvatures of \( f\left( t\right) \) are the limits of the curvatures of the family \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{{\lambda }_{n}}\left( t\right) \) and hence are uniformly bounded on the entire interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack \) . This contradiction shows that the entire limiting surface

\[
f : {S}^{1} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i}^{ - },{t}_{i}^{ + }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

is a curve-shrinking flow of immersions.

First of all we require that \( \mu  < {e}^{-\left( {{2n} - 1}\right) {C}^{\prime }\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }\zeta /4 \) where \( {C}^{\prime } \) is an upper bound for the norm of the Riemann curvature tensor at any point of the ambient Ricci flow. By Lemma 19.15 the fact that the area of the minimal annulus between the ramps \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) and \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) is less than \( \mu \) implies that the area of the minimal annulus between the ramps \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) and \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) is less than \( \mu {e}^{\left( {{2n} - 1}\right) {C}^{\prime }\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) } = \zeta /4 \) . The same estimate also holds for the image under the projection \( {p}_{1} \) of this minimal annulus. Thus, with this condition on \( \mu \) , and for \( \lambda \) sufficiently small, we have

\[
\left| {A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  - A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right) }\right|  < \zeta /4.
\]

The other condition we impose upon \( \mu \) is that if \( a,\widehat{a} \) are positive numbers at most \( W\left( \Gamma \right)  + \zeta \) and if \( a < \widehat{a} + \mu \) then

\[
{w}_{a,{t}_{0}}\left( {t}_{1}\right)  < {w}_{\widehat{a},{t}_{0}}\left( {t}_{1}\right)  + \zeta /4
\]

Applying this with \( a = A\left( {\widetilde{\Gamma }\left( c\right) }\right) \) and \( \widehat{a} = A\left( {\widetilde{\Gamma }\left( \widehat{c}\right) }\right) \) (both of which are at most \( W\left( \widetilde{\Gamma }\right)  < W\left( \Gamma \right)  + \zeta ) \) , we see that these two conditions on \( \mu \) together imply the result.

nodes.proof:
The proof is by contradiction. Suppose the length of \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) is at least \( \zeta \) and the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) \) is less than \( \zeta /2 \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{2},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . Of course, it follows that the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) is also at least \( \zeta \) . The third condition on \( B \) is equivalent to

\[
{e}^{{C}_{2}{B}^{-1}} < 4/3
\]

It then follows from Corollary 19.10 that for every \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{2},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\lambda }^{c}\left( t\right) \) is at least \( {3\zeta }/4 \) . On the other hand, by hypothesis for every such \( t \) , the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) \) is less than \( \zeta /2 \) . It follows from Equation (19.7) that

\[
{\int }_{{t}_{2}}^{{t}_{1}}\left( {\int {k}^{2}{ds}}\right) {dt} \leq  {C}_{2}\left( {{\int }_{{t}_{2}}^{{t}_{1}}L\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) }\right) {dt}}\right)  - L\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  + L\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{2}\right) }\right) .
\]

(Here \( L \) is the length of the curve.) From this and Corollary 19.10 we see that there is a constant \( {C}_{8} \) depending on the original family \( \Gamma \) and on the curvature of the ambient Ricci flow such that

\[
{\int }_{{t}_{2}}^{{t}_{1}}\left( {{\int }_{{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) }{k}^{2}{ds}}\right) {dt} \leq  {C}_{8}.
\]

Since \( {t}_{1} - {t}_{2} = {B}^{-1} \) , this implies that there is \( {t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{2},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) with

\[
{\int }_{{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }{k}^{2}{ds} \leq  {C}_{8}B.
\]

By Cauchy-Schwarz, for any subinterval \( I \) of length \( \leq  r \) in \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) we have

\[
{\int }_{I}{kds} \leq  \sqrt{{C}_{8}{Br}}
\]

We choose \( 0 < r \leq  \zeta \) sufficiently small so that \( \sqrt{{C}_{8}{Br}} \) is less than or equal to the constant \( \delta \) given in Lemma 19.31. Then we set \( \bar{\mu } \) equal to the constant given by that lemma for this value of \( r \) .

Now suppose that \( \mu \) is sufficiently small so that the solution to the equation

\[
\frac{{d\mu }\left( t\right) }{dt} = \left( {{2n} - 1}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}}_{g\left( t\right) }\right| \mu \left( t\right)
\]

with initial condition \( \mu \left( {t}_{0}\right)  \leq  \mu \) is less than \( \bar{\mu } \) on the entire interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . With this condition on \( \mu \) , Lemma 19.15 implies that for every \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) the ramps \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) \) and \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) \) are connected by an annulus of area at most \( \bar{\mu } \) . In particular, this is true for \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) and \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) . Now we have all the hypotheses of Lemma 19.31 at time \( {t}^{\prime } \) . Applying this lemma we conclude that

\[
L\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{3}{4}L\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right) .
\]

But this is a contradiction since by assumption \( L\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right)  < \zeta /2 \) and the supposition that \( L\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  \geq  \zeta \) led to the conclusion that \( L\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right)  \geq \; {3\zeta }/4 \) . This contradiction shows that our supposition that \( L\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  \geq  \zeta \) is false.

Proof. (of Proposition 18.24.) Fix \( \mu  > 0 \) sufficiently small so that Lemma 19.30 and Claim 19.32 hold. Then we choose a \( \mu /2 \) -net \( X \) for \( \widetilde{\Gamma } \) . We take \( \lambda \) sufficiently small so that Lemma 19.25 holds for every \( \widehat{c} \in  \mathcal{S} \) . We also choose \( \lambda \) sufficiently small so that \( X \) is a \( \mu \) -net for \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}^{\lambda } \) . Let \( c \in  {S}^{2} \) . Then there is \( \widehat{c} \in  \mathcal{S} \) and an arc \( \omega \) connecting \( c \) and \( \widehat{c} \) such that the area of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}^{\lambda }\left( \omega \right)  < \mu \) . Let \( {v}_{\widehat{c}} \) , resp. \( {v}_{c} \) , be the solution to Equation (18.4) with initial condition \( {v}_{\widehat{c}}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = A\left( {\widetilde{\Gamma }\left( \widehat{c}\right) }\right) \) , resp. \( {v}_{c}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = A\left( {\widetilde{\Gamma }\left( c\right) }\right) \) . According to Lemma 19.25 either \( A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  < {v}_{\widehat{c}}\left( {t}_{1}\right)  + \zeta /2 \) or the length of \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\widehat{c}}^{\lambda }\left( t\right) \) is less than \( \zeta /2 \) for every \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{2},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) where \( {t}_{2} = {t}_{1} - {B}^{-1} \) . In the second case, Claim 19.32 implies that the length of \( {p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) is less than \( \zeta \) . In the first case, Lemma 19.30 tells us that \( A\left( {{p}_{1}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{c}^{\lambda }\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  < {v}_{c}\left( {t}_{1}\right)  + \zeta \) . This completes the proof of Proposition 18.24.

Let \( h \) be the induced (possibly singular) metric on \( A \) induced by pulling back \( g \times  d{s}^{2} \) by \( \psi \) , and let \( {C}^{\prime \prime } > 0 \) be an upper bound on the Gaussian curvature of \( h \) (away from the branch points). Then there is a deformation \( \widetilde{h} \) of \( h \) , supported near the interior branch points, to a smooth metric with the property that the area of the deformed smooth metric is at most \( {2\mu } \) and where the upper bound for the curvature of \( \widetilde{h} \) is \( 2{C}^{\prime \prime } \) .

Proof. Fix an interior branch point \( p \) . Since \( \psi \) is smooth and conformal onto its image, there is a disk in \( A \) centered at \( p \) in which \( h = f\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right) {\left| dz\right| }^{2} \) for a smooth function \( f \) on the disk. The function \( f \) vanishes at the origin and is positive on the complement of the origin. Direct computation shows that the Gaussian curvature \( K\left( h\right) \) of \( h \) in this disk is given by

\[
K\left( h\right)  = \frac{-\bigtriangleup f}{2{f}^{2}} + \frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{2{f}^{3}} \leq  C,
\]

where \( \bigtriangleup \) is the usual Euclidean Laplacian on the disk and

\[
{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} = {\left( \partial f/\partial x\right) }^{2} + {\left( \partial f/\partial y\right) }^{2}.
\]

Now consider the metric \( \left( {f + \epsilon }\right) {\left| dz\right| }^{2} \) on the disk. Its Gaussian curvature is

\[
\frac{-\bigtriangleup f}{2{\left( f + \epsilon \right) }^{2}} + \frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{2{\left( f + \epsilon \right) }^{3}}.
\]

nodes.proof:
Proof. We see that \( - \bigtriangleup f \leq  {C}^{\prime \prime }{f}^{2} \) , so that

\[
\frac{-\bigtriangleup f}{{\left( f + \epsilon \right) }^{2}} + \frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{{\left( f + \epsilon \right) }^{3}} = \frac{\left( {f + \epsilon }\right) \left( {-\bigtriangleup f}\right)  + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{{\left( f + \epsilon \right) }^{3}}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{{C}^{\prime \prime }{f}^{3} - \epsilon \bigtriangleup f}{{\left( f + \epsilon \right) }^{3}} \leq  {C}^{\prime \prime } + \frac{\epsilon {f}^{2}{C}^{\prime \prime }}{{\left( f + \epsilon \right) }^{3}} \leq  2{C}^{\prime \prime }.
\]

Now we fix a smooth function \( \rho \left( r\right) \) which is identically 1 on a subdisk \( {D}^{\prime } \) of \( D \) and vanishes near \( \partial D \) and we replace the metric \( h \) on the disk by

\[
{h}_{\epsilon } = \left( {f + {\epsilon \rho }\left( r\right) }\right) {\left| dz\right| }^{2}.
\]

The above computation shows that the Gaussian curvature of \( {h}_{\epsilon } \) on \( {D}^{\prime } \) is bounded above by \( 2{C}^{\prime \prime } \) . As \( \epsilon \) tends to zero the restriction of the metric \( {h}_{\epsilon } \) to \( D \smallsetminus  {D}^{\prime } \) converges uniformly in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) -topology to \( h \) . Thus, for all \( \epsilon  > 0 \) sufficiently small the Gaussian curvature of \( {h}_{\epsilon } \) on \( D \smallsetminus  {D}^{\prime } \) will also be bounded by \( 2{C}^{\prime \prime } \) . Clearly, as \( \epsilon \) tends to zero the area of the metric \( {h}_{\epsilon } \) on \( D \) tends to the area of \( h \) on \( D \) .

Performing this construction near each of the finite number of interior branch points and taking \( \epsilon \) sufficiently small gives the perturbation \( \widetilde{h} \) as required.

LEMMA 19.38. Suppose that we have a focusing triangle \( \mathcal{T} \) with base \( \xi \) bounding a disk \( B \) in \( A \) . Suppose that the length of \( \xi \) is at most 1 . Then

\[
l\left( \xi \right)  \leq  \left( {{\int }_{\xi }{k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds} + \operatorname{Area}\left( B\right) }\right) .
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 19.38. Suppose that we have a focusing triangle \( \mathcal{T} \) with base \( \xi \) bounding a disk \( B \) in \( A \) . Suppose that the length of \( \xi \) is at most 1 . Then \[ l\left( \xi \right) \leq \left( {{\int }_{\xi }{k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds} + \operatorname{Area}\left( B\right) }\right) . \]

nodes.proof:
Proof. We begin with a preliminary computation. We denote by \( a\left( B\right) \) the area of \( B \) . We define

\[
{t}_{\xi } = {\int }_{\xi }{k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds}\;\text{ and }\;{T}_{\xi } = {\int }_{\xi }\left| {k}_{\text{ geod }}\right| {ds}.
\]

Recall that given a piecewise smooth curve, its total turning is the integral of the geodesic curvature over the smooth part of the boundary plus the sum over the break points of \( \pi \) minus the interior angle at the break point. The Gauss-Bonnet theorem tells us that for any compact surface with piecewise smooth boundary the integral of the Gaussian curvature over the interior of the surface plus the total turning around the boundary equals \( {2\pi } \) times the Euler characteristic of the surface.

CLAIM 19.39. The angle \( {\theta }_{B} \) between \( {D}_{x}^{\prime } \) and \( {D}_{y}^{\prime } \) at the vertex \( v \) satisfies

\[
{\theta }_{B} \leq  {t}_{\xi } + a\left( B\right)
\]

and for any measurable subset \( {B}^{\prime } \subset  B \) we have

\[

nodes.proof:
Proof. Since \( {D}_{x}^{\prime } \) and \( {D}_{y}^{\prime } \) meet \( \partial A \) in right angles, the total turning around the boundary of \( B \) is

\[
{t}_{\xi } + {2\pi } - {\theta }_{B}\text{ . }
\]

Thus, by Gauss-Bonnet, we have

\[
{\theta }_{B} = {\int }_{B}{Kda} + {t}_{\xi }.
\]

But \( K \leq  1 \) , giving the first stated inequality. On the other hand \( {\int }_{B}{Kda} = \; {\int }_{B}{K}^{ + }{da} + {\int }_{B}{K}^{ - }{da} \) , where \( {K}^{ + } = \max \left( {K,0}\right) \) and \( {K}^{ - } = K - {K}^{ + } \) . Since \( 0 \leq  {\int }_{B}{K}^{ + }{da} \leq  a\left( B\right) \) and \( {\int }_{B}{K}^{ - } \leq  0 \) , the second string of inequalities follows.

nodes.content: CLAIM 19.40. Let \( a \in  \operatorname{int}\xi \) . There is a shortest path in \( B \) from a to \( v \) . This shortest path is a geodesic meeting \( \partial B \) only in its end points. It has length \( \leq  \left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime } \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: CLAIM 19.40. Let \( a \in \operatorname{int}\xi \) . There is a shortest path in \( B \) from a to \( v \) . This shortest path is a geodesic meeting \( \partial B \) only in its end points. It has length \( \leq \left( {1/2}\right) + {\delta }^{\prime } \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. The length estimate is obvious: Since \( \xi \) has length at most 1, a path along \( \partial A \cap  B \) from \( a \) to the closest of \( x \) and \( y \) has length at most \( 1/2 \) . The corresponding side has length at most \( {\delta }^{\prime } \) . Thus, there is a path from \( a \) to \( v \) in \( B \) of length at most \( \left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime } \) .

Standard convergence arguments show that there is a shortest path in \( B \) from \( a \) to \( v \) . Fix \( a \in  \operatorname{int}\left( {\partial A \cap  B}\right) \) . It is clear that the shortest path cannot meet either of the ’sides’ \( {D}_{x}^{\prime } \) and \( {D}_{y}^{\prime } \) at any point other than \( v \) . If it did, then there would be an angle at this point and a local shortcut, cutting off a small piece of the angle, would provide a shorter path. We must rule out that the shortest path from \( a \) to \( v \) meets \( \partial A \cap  B \) in another point. If it does, let \( {a}^{\prime } \) be the last such point (parameterizing the geodesic starting at \( a) \) . The shortest path from \( a \) then leaves \( \partial A \) at \( {a}^{\prime } \) in the direction tangent at \( {a}^{\prime } \) to \( \partial A \) . (Otherwise, we would have an angle which would allow us to shorten the path just as before.) This means that we have a geodesic \( \gamma \) from \( v \) to \( {a}^{\prime } \) whose interior is contained in the interior of \( B \) and which is tangent to \( \partial A \) at \( {a}^{\prime } \) . We label the endpoints of \( \partial A \cap  B \) so that the union of \( \gamma \) and the interval on \( \partial A \cap  B \) from \( {a}^{\prime } \) to \( y \) gives a \( {C}^{1} \) -curve. Consider the disc \( {B}^{\prime } \) bounded by \( \gamma \) , the arc of \( \partial A \) from \( {a}^{\prime } \) to \( y \) , and \( {D}_{y}^{\prime } \) . The total turning around the boundary is at most \( {3\pi }/2 + \delta \) , and the integral of the Gaussian curvature over \( {B}^{\prime } \) is at most the area of \( B \) , which is less than \( \mu  < 1/{20} < \left( {\pi /4}\right)  - \delta \) . This contradicts the Gauss-Bonnet theorem.

nodes.content: CLAIM 19.41. For any \( a \in  \partial A \cap  B \) there is a unique minimal geodesic in \( B \) from a to \( v \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: CLAIM 19.41. For any \( a \in \partial A \cap B \) there is a unique minimal geodesic in \( B \) from a to \( v \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. Suppose not; suppose there are two \( \gamma \) and \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) from \( v \) to \( a \) . Since they are both minimal in \( B \) , each is embedded, and they must be disjoint except for their endpoints. The upper bound on the curvature and the Gauss-Bonnet theorem imply that the angles that they make at each endpoint are less than \( \mu  < \pi /2 \) . Thus, there is a spray of geodesics (i.e. geodesics determined by an interval \( \beta \) in the circle of directions at \( v \) ) coming out of \( v \) and moving into \( B \) with extremal members of the spray being \( \gamma \) and \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) . The geodesics \( \gamma \) and \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) have length at most \( \left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime } \) , and hence the exponential mapping from \( v \) is a local diffeomorphism on all geodesics of length at most the length of \( \gamma \) . Since the angle they make at \( a \) is less than \( \pi /2 \) and since the exponential mapping is a local diffeomorphism near \( \gamma \) , as we move in from the \( \gamma \) end of the spray we find geodesics from \( v \) of length less than the length of \( \gamma \) ending on points of \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) . The same Gauss-Bonnet argument shows that the angle that each of these shorter geodesics makes with \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) is at most \( \mu \) . Consider the subset \( {\beta }^{\prime } \) of \( \beta \) which are directions of geodesics in \( B \) of length \( < \left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime } \) that end on points of \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) and make an angle less than \( \mu \) with \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) . We have just seen that \( {\beta }^{\prime } \) contains an open neighborhood of the end of \( \beta \) corresponding to \( \gamma \) . Since the Gaussian curvature is bounded above by 1, and these geodesics all have length at most \( 1/2 + \delta \) , it follows that the exponential map is a local diffeomorphism near all such geodesics. Thus, \( {\beta }^{\prime } \) is an open subset of \( \beta \) . On the other, hand if the direction of \( {\gamma }^{\prime \prime } \neq  {\gamma }^{\prime } \) is a point \( {b}^{\prime \prime } \in  \beta \) which is an endpoint of an open interval \( {\beta }^{\prime } \) , and if this interval separates \( {b}^{\prime \prime } \) from the direction of \( \gamma \) , then the length of \( {\gamma }^{\prime \prime } \) is less than the length of each point in the interval. Hence, the length of \( {\gamma }^{\prime \prime } \) is less than \( \left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime } \) . Invoking Gauss-Bonnet again we see that the angle between \( {\gamma }^{\prime \prime } \) and \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) is \( < \mu \) .

This proves that if \( U \) is an open interval in \( {\beta }^{\prime } \) then the endpoint of \( U \) closest to the direction of \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) is also contained in \( {\beta }^{\prime } \) (unless that endpoint is the direction of \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) ). It is now elementary to see that \( {\beta }^{\prime } \) is all of \( \beta \) except the endpoint corresponding to \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) . But this is impossible. Since the exponential mapping is a local diffeomorphism out to distance \( \left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime } \) , and since \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) is embedded, any geodesic from \( v \) whose initial direction is sufficiently close to that of \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) and whose length is at most \( \left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime } \) will not cross \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \) .

nodes.content:
Claim 19.43.

\[
\frac{dl}{dt}\left( t\right)  \leq  \mathop{\max }\limits_{{\psi  \in  E}}h\left( \psi \right) {\int }_{\lambda \left( t\right) }{k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: Claim 19.43. \[ \frac{dl}{dt}\left( t\right) \leq \mathop{\max }\limits_{{\psi \in E}}h\left( \psi \right) {\int }_{\lambda \left( t\right) }{k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds}. \]

nodes.proof:
Proof. First of all notice that, by construction, the curve \( \xi \) , which is defined by \( \{ s = h\left( \psi \right) \} \) , is orthogonal to the radial geodesics to the endpoints. As a consequence, \( {h}^{\prime }\left( \psi \right)  = 0 \) at the endpoints. Thus, each of the curves \( \lambda \left( t\right) \) is orthogonal to the radial geodesics through its end points. Therefore, as we vary the family \( \lambda \left( t\right) \) the formula for the derivative of the length is

\[
{l}^{\prime }\left( t\right)  = {\int }_{\lambda \left( t\right) }{k}_{\text{ geod }}\left( \psi \right) h\left( \psi \right) \left| {\cos \left( {\theta \left( {\psi , t}\right) }\right) }\right| {ds}
\]

where \( \theta \left( {\psi , t}\right) \) is the angle at \( \left( {{th}\left( \psi \right) ,\psi }\right) \) between the curve \( s = {th}\left( \psi \right) \) and the radial geodesic. The result follows immediately.

Next, we must bound the turning of \( \lambda \left( t\right) \) . For this we invoke the Gauss-Bonnet theorem once again. Applying this to the wedge-shaped disk \( W\left( t\right) \) cut out by \( \lambda \left( t\right) \) gives

\[
{\int }_{W\left( t\right) }{Kda} + {\int }_{\lambda \left( t\right) }{k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds} = {\theta }_{B}.
\]

From Claim 19.39 we conclude that

\[
{\int }_{\lambda \left( t\right) }{k}_{\text{ geod }}{ds} \leq  {t}_{\xi } + a\left( B\right) .
\]

Of course, by Claim 19.40 we have \( \mathop{\max }\limits_{{\psi  \in  E}}h\left( \psi \right)  \leq  \left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime } \) . Since \( l\left( 0\right)  = 0 \) , this implies that

\[
l\left( \xi \right)  = l\left( 1\right)  \leq  \left( {a\left( B\right)  + {t}_{B}}\right) \left( {\left( {1/2}\right)  + {\delta }^{\prime }}\right)  < a\left( B\right)  + {t}_{B}.
\]

This completes the proof of Lemma 19.38.

nodes.label: Lemma 19.46
