\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\frac{\partial g}{\partial s} = \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {s}^{2}}\frac{\partial g}{\partial s} - \frac{2}{{g}^{2}}{\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{3}
\]

which shows that the maximum of \( \partial g/\partial s \) decreases. Since \( g \) is bounded above, the maximum principle shows that the maximum value

\[
w = \max \left| \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right|
\]

satisfies an ordinary differential equation

\[
\frac{dw}{dt} \leq   - c{w}^{3}
\]

for some constant \( c > 0 \) , and hence satisfies an estimate

\[
\left| \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right|  \leq  C/\sqrt{t}
\]

for some constant \( C < \infty \) .

Differentiating the equation once more gives

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}} = \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {s}^{2}}\frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}} - \frac{2}{g}{\left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}}\right) }^{2} - \frac{6}{{g}^{2}}{\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2}\frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}} + \frac{4}{{g}^{3}}{\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{4}.
\]

Since \( g \) is bounded above by a constant \( C \) and \( \partial g/\partial s \) is bounded above by \( C/\sqrt{t} \) we find that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}} \leq  \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {s}^{2}}\frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}} - c\left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}}\right)  + \frac{C}{{t}^{2}}
\]

for some constants \( c > 0 \) and \( C < \infty \) . Again the maximum principle shows that the maximum value

\[
z = \max \left| \frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}}\right|
\]

satisfies an ordinary differential equation

\[
\frac{dz}{dt} \leq  \frac{C}{{t}^{2}} - c{z}^{2}
\]

from which we get an estimate

\[
\left| \frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}}\right|  \leq  \frac{C}{t}
\]

for some constant \( C \) .

In terms of the arc length the sectional curvature has components

\[
{K}_{V} =  - \frac{1}{{g}^{2}}{\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2}\;\text{ and }\;{K}_{H} =  - \frac{1}{g}\frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}}
\]

where \( {K}_{H} \) is the sectional curvature of a horizontal plane and \( {K}_{V} \) that of a vertical one. Note that \( {K}_{V} \) must be negative in general but zero somewhere while \( {K}_{H} \) must have both signs. Now the estimate above shows that the curvature remains bounded, so the solution exists for all time \( t < \infty \) .

Moreover since the maximum value \( {g}_{MAX} \) of \( g \) decreases while the minimum value \( {g}_{MIN} \) of \( g \) increases, and since

\[
{g}_{MAX} - {g}_{MIN} \leq  \int \left| \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right| {ds} \leq  C/\sqrt{t}
\]

we see that \( g \) must converge to some constant value \( \bar{g} \) as \( t \rightarrow  \infty \) . Moreover

\[
\left| {K}_{V}\right|  \leq  C/t\text{ and }\left| {K}_{H}\right|  \leq  C/t
\]

so the curvature goes to zero. We can do even better. We can compute

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\int {\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2}{ds} =  - \int \left\{  {2{\left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2} + \frac{5}{{g}^{2}}{\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{4}}\right\}  {ds}
\]

and use Wirtenger's inequality

\[
\int {\left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}g}{\partial {s}^{2}}\right) }^{2}{ds} \geq  {\left( \frac{2\pi }{L}\right) }^{2}\int {\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2}{ds}
\]

and even throw away the term with \( {\left( \partial g/\partial s\right) }^{4} \) and get

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\int {\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2}{ds} \leq   - \frac{8{\pi }^{2}}{{L}^{2}}\int {\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2}{ds}.
\]

Since \( L \) is bounded above, it follows that

\[
\int {\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2}{ds} \leq  C{e}^{-{ct}}
\]

for some constants \( C < \infty \) and \( c > 0 \) . Then

\[
{g}_{MAX} - {g}_{MIN} \leq  \int \left| \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right| {ds} \leq  {L}^{1/2}{\left\{  \int {\left( \frac{\partial g}{\partial s}\right) }^{2}ds\right\}  }^{1/2}
\]

shows that \( g \) approaches the constant \( \bar{g} \) exponentially. A little more work along these lines would show all the derivatives of \( g \) , and hence the curvature and its derivatives, go to zero exponentially as well.

THEOREM 13.1. There exists a constant \( C < \infty \) , depending only on the dimension, with the following property. Suppose we have a smooth solution to the Ricci Flow in an open neighborhood \( U \) of a point \( P \) in a manifold for times \( 0 \leq  t \leq  T \) . Assume that the curvature is bounded

\[
\left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  M
\]

with some constant \( M \) everywhere on \( U \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , and assume that the closed ball of some radius \( r \) at time \( t = 0 \) is a compact set continued in \( U \) . Then at the point \( P \) at time \( T \) we can estimate the covariant derivatives of the curvature by

\[
{\left| \operatorname{DRm}\left( P, T\right) \right| }^{2} \leq  C{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2}} + \frac{1}{T} + M}\right) .
\]

We also have the formula

\[

with the terms in \( {Rc} \) coming from the motion of the frame and the terms in DRc coming from the motion of the connection. This formula gives a bound

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  C\left| {Rm}\right| \left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  + C\left| {DRm}\right| \left| {D\varphi }\right| .

We can use the bound \( \left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  M \) as before, but we get a bound on \( \left| {DRm}\right| \) from \( F \leq  H \) . In particular

\[
b\left( {B{M}^{2} + {\left| Rm\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| DRm\right| }^{2}/{M}^{4} \leq  \frac{\lambda {A}^{2}}{{\phi }^{2}} + \frac{1}{t} + M
\]

gives a bound (for \( t \leq  1/M \) at least)

\[
\left| {DRm}\right|  \leq  {CM}\left( {\frac{1}{\phi } + \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}}\right)
\]

with a constant \( C \) depending on \( b, B, A \) and \( \lambda \) . This yields the estimate

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  {CM}\left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  + {CM}\left( {\frac{1}{\varphi } + \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}}\right) \left| {D\varphi }\right| .
\]

We can estimate \( {\left| D\varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  2{A}^{2} \) from before. Since \( \varphi \) is fixed in time and \( \varphi  \leq  {Ar} \) ,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\varphi \left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  {CM}\left\lbrack  {\varphi \left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  + 1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Now viewing this as an ordinary differential inequality at a fixed point, we see that \( \varphi \left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  2{A}^{2} \) if \( \varphi \left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  {A}^{2} \) at \( t = 0 \) and \( t \leq  c/M \) for a suitably small constant \( c > 0 \) .

To see this, consider the ordinary differential equation

\[
\frac{du}{dt} \leq  {CM}\left( {u + 1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right)
\]

for \( u = \varphi \left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right| \) at a fixed point. Then

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{e}^{-{CMt}}u \leq  {CM}{e}^{-{CMt}}\left( {1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right) .
\]

Since \( {e}^{-{CMt}} \leq  1 \) we get

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{e}^{-{CMt}}u \leq  {CM}\left( {1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right) .
\]

Since \( u \leq  {A}^{2} \) at \( t = 0 \) , we have

\[
u \leq  {e}^{CMt}\left\lbrack  {{A}^{2} + {CM}{\int }_{\theta  = 0}^{t}\left( {1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right) {dt}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

The latter improper integral is finite and gives

\[
u \leq  {e}^{CMt}\left\lbrack  {{A}^{2} + {CM}\left( {t + {2r}\sqrt{t}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

and if \( r \leq  c/\sqrt{M} \) and \( t \leq  c/M \) for a suitably small \( c \) then \( u \leq  2{A}^{2} \) as desired.

COROLLARY 14.3. Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci Flow for \( t > 0 \) which is compact or complete with bounded curvature, and has weakly positive curvature operator or is Kähler with weakly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature. Suppose moreover that at some time \( t > 0 \) we have the scalar curvature \( R \leq  M \) for some constant \( M \) in the ball of radius \( r \) around some point \( P \) . Then the derivatives of the curvature at \( P \) at time \( t \) satisfy a bound

\[
{\left| DRm\left( P, t\right) \right| }^{2} \leq  C{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2}} + \frac{1}{t} + M}\right)
\]

for some constant \( C \) depending only on the dimension.

Suppose now that there is a short loop at \( P \) of length \( L \) with

\[

Then

\[
L \leq  \sqrt{\beta /{M}_{0}}/{B}_{1}

and if \( {B}_{1} \) is large enough we can make

\[
L \leq  \varepsilon /\sqrt{{M}_{0}}
\]

for any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we like. Now as long as

\[
L \leq  c/\sqrt{{M}_{0}}
\]

Thus we get a family of geodesic loops parametrized by \( t \) and varying smoothly, at least for some time backward.

Under the Ricci flow the length of the loop varies by

\[
\frac{dL}{dt} =  - \int {Rc}\left( {V, V}\right) {ds}
\]

where we integrate the Ricci curvature in the tangent direction \( V \) with respect to the arc length over the loop. (Since the loop is kept geodesic, the first variation in \( L \) from the motion of the loop is zero, and we only get the contribution from the change in the metric.) This gives an estimate

\[
\frac{dL}{dt} \geq   - C{M}_{0}L
\]

\[

\]

and hence in time \( 0 \leq  t \leq  \tau \) with \( \tau  = c/{M}_{0} \) for a suitably small \( c \) , if the loop ends with length \( L \leq  \varepsilon /\sqrt{{M}_{0}} \) it is never more than twice as large for as far back in time as we can continue it as a perturbation. But then we can do this all the way to \( t = 0 \) taking \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) small. Hence then must have been a geodesic loop at \( t = 0 \) of length at most \( {2\varepsilon }/\sqrt{{M}_{0}} \) . Now for any \( {g}_{0} \) we can take \( \varepsilon \) so small this is false. Then making \( {B}_{1} \) large compared to \( \varepsilon \) gives us a contradiction if \( W/L \geq  {B}_{1} \) . Thus \( W/L \leq  {B}_{1} \) , and we have established the Lemma.

\]

nodes.content: THEOREM 16.4. For any maximal solution to the Ricci Flow which satisfies an injectivity radius estimate of the type above, of Type I, II, or III, there exists a sequence of dilations of the solution which converges in the limit to a singularity model of the corresponding type.
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 16.4. For any maximal solution to the Ricci Flow which satisfies an injectivity radius estimate of the type above, of Type I, II, or III, there exists a sequence of dilations of the solution which converges in the limit to a singularity model of the corresponding type.

nodes.proof:
\[
\Omega  = \lim \sup \left( {T - t}\right) M\left( t\right)  < \infty .
\]

There is some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) such that we always have \( \Omega  \geq  \varepsilon \) ; for \( M\left( t\right) \) satisfies an ODE

\[
\frac{dM}{dt} \leq  C{M}^{2}
\]

and hence \( M\left( t\right) \) couldn’t go to \( \infty \) at time \( T \) if \( \left( {T - t}\right) M\left( t\right)  < \varepsilon \) at any \( t < T \) when \( \varepsilon \) is small compared to this constant \( C \) . Pick a sequence of points \( {P}_{j} \) and times \( {t}_{j} \) with \( {t}_{j} \rightarrow  T \) and

\[
\lim \left( {T - {t}_{j}}\right) R\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  = \Omega .
\]

For each of these solutions, let \( {P}_{j} \) be the origin 0, translate in time so that \( {t}_{j} \) becomes 0, dilate in space by a factor \( \lambda \) so that \( R\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) becomes 1 at the origin at \( t = 0 \) , and dilate in time by \( {\lambda }^{2} \) so it is still a solution to the Ricci Flow. The dilated solutions exist on a time interval

\[
- {A}_{j} \leq  t < {\Omega }_{j}
\]

where

\[
{\Omega }_{j} = \left( {T - {t}_{j}}\right) M\left( {t}_{j}\right)  \rightarrow  \Omega
\]

and

\[
{A}_{j} = {t}_{j}{\Omega }_{j}/\left( {T - {t}_{j}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty .
\]

Moreover, they satisfy curvature bounds. For any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we can find a time \( \tau  < T \) such that for \( \tau  \leq  t < T \) we have

\[
\left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  \left( {\Omega  + \varepsilon }\right) /\left( {T - t}\right)
\]

by assumption, before dilation. After dilation this becomes a curvature bound

\[
\left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  \left( {\Omega  + \varepsilon }\right) /\left( {{\Omega }_{j} - t}\right)
\]

for times \( - {\theta }_{j} \leq  t < {\Omega }_{j} \) where

\[
{\theta }_{j} = \left( {{t}_{j} - \tau }\right) {\Omega }_{j}/\left( {T - {t}_{j}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty .
\]

Consequently the limit exists on the time interval \( - \infty  < t < \Omega \) and satisfies

\[
\left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  \Omega /\left( {\Omega  - t}\right)
\]

everywhere, while \( \left| {{Rm}\left( {0,0}\right) }\right|  = 1 \) .

For Type II(a), we have to be a little more subtle. We start by picking a sequence \( {T}_{j} < T < \infty \) with \( {T}_{j} \rightarrow  T \) . If the manifold is compact we can pick points \( {P}_{j} \) and \( {t}_{j} \) where

\[
\left( {{T}_{j} - {t}_{j}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{P, t < {T}_{j}}}\left( {{T}_{j} - t}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|
\]

as the latter goes to zero as \( t \nearrow  {T}_{j} \) . If the manifold is not compact, we can take \( {\gamma }_{j} \nearrow  1 \) and find \( {P}_{j} \) and \( {t}_{j} \) so that at least

\[
\left( {{T}_{j} - {t}_{j}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\gamma }_{j}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{P, t \leq  {T}_{j}}}\left( {{T}_{j} - t}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|
\]

Now pick \( {P}_{j} \) to be the origin \( {O}_{j} \) , translate in time so \( {t}_{j} \) becomes zero, dilate in space by a factor \( \lambda \) so \( R\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) becomes 1 at the origin at \( t = 0 \) , and dilate time by \( {\lambda }^{2} \) so that we still have a solution to the Ricci Flow. The dilated solution exists for \( {A}_{j} \leq  t < {\Omega }_{j} \) where

\[
{\Omega }_{j} = \left( {{T}_{j} - {t}_{j}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  \infty
\]

and

\[
{A}_{j} = \frac{{t}_{j}}{{T}_{j} - {t}_{j}}{\Omega }_{j} = {t}_{j}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  \infty
\]

also. To see \( {\Omega }_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \) for Type II(a) where \( T < \infty \) , note that \( {T}_{j} \nearrow  T,{P}_{j} \) and \( {t}_{j} \) are chosen maximally and

\[
\lim \sup \left( {T - t}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  = \infty \text{ . }
\]

To see \( {A}_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \) for Type II(a), use the fact that \( {\Omega }_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \) forces \( {t}_{j} \rightarrow  T \) and \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  \infty \) . We also get a bound on curvature. We have for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  {T}_{j} \)

\[
\left( {{T}_{j} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {\Gamma }_{j}\left( {{T}_{j} - {t}_{j}}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|
\]

where \( {\Gamma }_{j} = 1/{\gamma }_{j} \rightarrow  1 \) also, before dilation. After dilation this becomes for \( - {A}_{j} \leq  t \leq  {\Omega }_{j} \)

\[
\left( {{\Omega }_{j} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {\Gamma }_{j}{\Omega }_{j}.
\]

Write this as

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {\Gamma }_{j}{\Omega }_{j}/\left( {{\Omega }_{j} - t}\right) .
\]

As \( j \rightarrow  \infty ,{\Gamma }_{j} \rightarrow  1 \) and \( {\Omega }_{j}/\left( {{\Omega }_{j} - t}\right)  \rightarrow  1 \) for any fixed \( t \) . Hence the limit exists and satisfies

\[
\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  1
\]

everywhere for \( - \infty  < t <  + \infty \) , while \( \left| {{Rm}\left( {0,0}\right) }\right|  = 1 \) .

For type II(b), we again choose a sequence \( {T}_{j} \nearrow  T = \infty \) , but now we pick \( {P}_{j} \) and \( {t}_{j} \) so that

\[
{t}_{j}\left( {{T}_{j} - {t}_{j}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\gamma }_{j}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{P, t \leq  {T}_{j}}}t\left( {{T}_{j} - t}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|
\]

where again \( {\gamma }_{j} \nearrow  1 \) . Pick \( {P}_{j} \) to be the origin \( {O}_{j} \) , translate in time so \( {t}_{j} \) becomes zero, dilate in space by a factor \( \lambda \) so that \( R\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) becomes 1 at the origin at \( t = 0 \) , and dilate time by \( {\lambda }^{2} \) so it is still a solution of the Ricci Flow. Suppose \( {T}_{j} \) dilates to \( {\Omega }_{j} \) and 0 dilates to \( - {A}_{j} \) . The solution now exists after dilation on a time interval \( - {A}_{j} < t < {\Omega }_{j} \) where by dilation invariance

\[
\frac{{A}_{j}{\Omega }_{j}}{{A}_{j} + {\Omega }_{j}} = \frac{{t}_{j}\left( {{T}_{j} - {t}_{j}}\right) }{{T}_{j}}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  \infty
\]

since by assumption

\[
\lim \sup t\left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  = \infty \text{ . }
\]

This forces \( {A}_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \) and \( {\Omega }_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \) as well since

\[
\frac{xy}{x + y} = \frac{1}{1/x + 1/y}
\]

Before dilation we have an estimate for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  {T}_{j} \)

\[
t\left( {{T}_{j} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {\Gamma }_{j}{t}_{j}\left( {{T}_{j} - {t}_{j}}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|
\]

where again \( {\Gamma }_{j} = 1/{\gamma }_{j} \rightarrow  1 \) . After dilation this becomes for \( - {A}_{j} \leq  t \leq  {\Omega }_{j} \)

\[
\left( {t + {A}_{j}}\right) \left( {{\Omega }_{j} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {\Gamma }_{j}{A}_{j}{\Omega }_{j}.
\]

Write this as

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{{\Gamma }_{j}{A}_{j}{\Omega }_{j}}{\left( {t + {A}_{j}}\right) \left( {{\Omega }_{j} - t}\right) }.
\]

As \( j \rightarrow  \infty ,{\Gamma }_{j} \rightarrow  1 \) and \( {A}_{j}{\Omega }_{j}/\left( {t + {A}_{j}}\right) \left( {{\Omega }_{j} - t}\right)  \rightarrow  1 \) also for any fixed \( t \) . Hence the limit exists and satisfies

\[
\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  1
\]

everywhere for \( - \infty  < t < \infty \) while \( \left| {{Rm}\left( {0,0}\right) }\right|  = 1 \) .

Finally we come to Type III, where \( T = \infty \) and

\[
A = \lim \sup {tM}\left( t\right)  < \infty \text{ . }
\]

First we claim \( A > 0 \) . Indeed if \( t\left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \varepsilon \) for large \( t \) then the diameter \( L \) satisfies an estimate

\[
\frac{dL}{dt} \leq  {C\varepsilon L}
\]

for a constant \( C \) independent of \( \varepsilon \) and \( L \) . This makes \( L \) grow at most like \( {t}^{C\varepsilon } \) while \( \left| {Rm}\right| \) falls off at least like \( 1/t \) . If \( {C\varepsilon } < 1/2 \) we see that \( {L}^{2}M \rightarrow  0 \) , which means that after rescaling the curvature collapses with bounded diameter. By a well-known result of Gromov the manifold is nilpotent; more to the point the injectivity radius bound we assumed would fail. Thus \( A > 0 \) .

Now pick a sequence of points \( {P}_{j} \) and times \( {t}_{j} \) so that \( {t}_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \) and

\[
\lim {t}_{j}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  = A.
\]

Choose \( {P}_{j} \) to be the origin \( {O}_{j} \) , translate in time so \( {t}_{j} \) becomes \( {O}_{j} \) , dilate in space by a factor \( \lambda \) so that \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right| \) becomes 1 at the origin at time \( t = 0 \) , and dilate in time by a factor \( {\lambda }^{2} \) so we still have a solution of the Ricci Flow. After dilation the solution will exist for times \( - {A}_{j} \leq  t < \infty \) where time 0 dilates to

\[
{A}_{j} = {t}_{j}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{P}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  A.
\]

Moreover for any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we can find a time \( \tau  < \infty \) such that for \( t \geq  \tau \)

\[
t\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  A + \varepsilon
\]

by hypothesis, before dilation. After dilation this becomes a bound

\[
\left( {t + A}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  A + \varepsilon
\]

for time \( t \geq   - {\theta }_{j} \) where

\[
{\theta }_{j} = \left( {{t}_{j} - \tau }\right) {A}_{j}/{t}_{j} \rightarrow  A
\]

since \( {t}_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \) and \( {A}_{j} \rightarrow  A > 0 \) while \( \tau \) is fixed. Hence we get a limit which satisfies

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {P, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  A/\left( {t + A}\right)
\]

on \( - A < t < \infty \) while \( \left| {{Rm}\left( {0,0}\right) }\right|  = 1 \) . This completes the proof of the Theorem.

nodes.label: Theorem 16.5
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - The Formation of Singularities in the Ricci Flow
nodes.section_title: 1. The Formation of Singularities in the Ricci Flow
nodes.content: THEOREM 16.5. For any maximal solution to the Ricci Flow with strictly positive sectional curvature on a compact manifold, or with a metric which is complete with bounded curvature at each time with strictly positive sectional curvature, or on a compact Kähler manifold with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature, there exists a sequence of dilations which converges to a singularity model. For Type I solutions the limit exists for \( - \infty  < t < \Omega \) and has \( R\left( {P, t}\right)  \leq  \Omega /\left( {\Omega  - t}\right) \) with \( R\left( {0,0}\right)  = 1 \) , for Type II the limit exists for \( - \infty  < t < \infty \) with \( R \leq  1 \) and \( R\left( {0,0}\right)  = 1 \) , and for Type III the limit exists for \( - A < t < \infty \) with \( R \leq  A/\left( {t + A}\right) \) and \( R\left( {0,0}\right)  = 1 \) . These limits will have weakly positive curvature operator, or weakly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature.

In the real case such a Type III singularity must be a homothetically expanding Ricci soliton with \( {Rc} = {D}^{2}f + {\rho g} \) for some constant \( \rho  > 0 \) . In the Kähler case such a Type III singularity must also be an expanding Ricci-Kähler soliton with \( {Rc} = \partial \bar{\partial }f + {\rho g} \) and \( \partial \partial f = 0 \) .

THEOREM 17.1. There exists a constant \( C \) depending only on the dimension, such that if the curvature \( {Rm} \) is bounded by a constant \( M \)

\[
\left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  M
\]

then

\[
{e}^{-{CM}\left( {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right) }d\left( {P, Q,{t}_{1}}\right)  \leq  d\left( {P, Q,{t}_{2}}\right)  \leq  {e}^{{CM}\left( {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right) }d\left( {P, Q,{t}_{1}}\right)
\]

for any points \( P \) and \( Q \) and any times \( {t}_{1} \) and \( {t}_{2} \) .

nodes.label: Theorem 17.2
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - The Formation of Singularities in the Ricci Flow
nodes.section_title: 1. The Formation of Singularities in the Ricci Flow
nodes.content:
THEOREM 17.2. There exists a constant \( C \) depending only on the dimension such that if

\[
\left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  M
\]

then

\[
d\left( {P, Q,{t}_{2}}\right)  \geq  d\left( {P, Q,{t}_{1}}\right)  - C\sqrt{M}\left( {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right)
\]

for any points \( P \) and \( Q \) and any times \( {t}_{1} \leq  {t}_{2} \) .

The second estimate says that the rate at which a distance shrinks can be bounded independently of how large it is. It is due to the fact that on a long minimal geodesic there cannot be too much positive curvature along its middle or it would be unstable.

Both theorems are proved by the following observation. For any path \( \gamma \) its length \( L \) changes at a rate

\[
\frac{dL}{dt} =  - {\int }_{\gamma }{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds}
\]

where \( T \) is the unit tangent vector to the path \( \gamma \) and we integrate along the path with respect to the arc length \( s \) . The function \( d\left( {P, Q, t}\right) \) is the least length \( L \) of all paths. In general it will not be smooth in \( t \) for fixed \( P \) and \( Q \) , but at least it will be Lipschitz continuous. Hence we can estimate its derivative above and below, in the sense of giving an upper bound on the lim sup of all forward difference quotients and a lower bound on the lim inf of all forward difference quotients.

nodes.label: Theorem 17.4

nodes.section_title: 1. The Formation of Singularities in the Ricci Flow
nodes.content:
THEOREM 17.4. On a Riemannian manifold suppose we have a geodesic from \( P \) to \( Q \) of length \( L \) with arc length \( s \) and unit tangent vector \( T \) . For \( 0 < \sigma  \leq  L/2 \)

(a) if \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right)  \geq  0 \) along \( \gamma \) then

\[
{\int }_{\sigma }^{L - \sigma }\operatorname{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} \leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) }{\sigma };
\]

(b) if \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right)  \geq  \left( {n - 1}\right) {\rho }^{2} \) then

\[
{\int }_{\sigma }^{L - \sigma }{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} \leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \rho }{\tan {\rho \sigma }};
\]

(c) if \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right)  \geq   - \left( {n - 1}\right) {\rho }^{2} \) then

\[
{\int }_{\sigma }^{L - \sigma }\operatorname{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} \leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \rho }{\tan {h\rho \sigma }}.
\]

We give the proof shortly for convenience, but first we finish the proof of Theorem 17.2. We can bound the integral over the whole path \( \gamma \) in three pieces

\[
{\int }_{0}^{L}{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} \leq  {\int }_{0}^{\sigma }{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} + {\int }_{\sigma }^{L - \sigma }{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{L - \sigma }^{L}{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds}
\]

We bound the first and third piece using the maximum of the curvature

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\sigma }\operatorname{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} \leq  {CM\sigma }\;\text{ and }\;{\int }_{L - \sigma }^{L}\operatorname{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} \leq  {CM\sigma }.
\]

We bound the middle piece using Theorem 17.4

\[
{\int }_{L - \sigma }^{L}\operatorname{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} \leq  \frac{C\sqrt{M}}{\tanh \left( {\sqrt{M}\sigma }\right) }.
\]

If we take \( \sigma  = 1/\sqrt{M} \) both bounds are the same and we get

\[
{\int }_{0}^{L}{Rc}\left( {T, T}\right) {ds} \leq  C\sqrt{M}.
\]

Using this bound in Lemma 17.3 gives the result in Theorem 17.2. Now we prove Theorem 17.4.

nodes.proof:
. In time \( {\Delta t} \geq  0 \) the distance between two points shrinks but not by more than \( C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t} \) . Let \( \alpha \) be the aperture at time \( t \) . For any \( \widetilde{\alpha } < \alpha \) and any \( \sigma  < \infty \) we can find \( s \geq  \sigma \) and two points \( P \) and \( Q \) such that

\[
d\left( {0, P, t}\right)  = s\;d\left( {0, Q, t}\right)  = s\;\text{ and }\;d\left( {P, Q, t}\right)  \geq  \widetilde{\alpha }s.
\]

Then

\[
s - C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t} \leq  d\left( {0, P, t \pm  {\Delta t}}\right)  \leq  s + C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t}
\]

\[
s - C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t} \leq  d\left( {0, Q, t \pm  {\Delta t}}\right)  \leq  s + C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t}
\]

and

\[
\widetilde{\alpha }s - C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t} \leq  d\left( {P, Q, t + {\Delta t}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{\alpha }s + C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t}.
\]

Now depending on which is further from 0, we can more \( P \) or \( Q \) back toward 0 by no more than \( C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t} \) and make the distances of \( P \) and \( Q \) from 0 equal again, without reducing the distance between \( P \) and \( Q \) by more than \( C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t} \) . Since

\[
\frac{\widetilde{\alpha }s - C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t}}{s + C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t}} \rightarrow  \widetilde{\alpha }\;\text{ as }\;s \rightarrow  \infty
\]

we see that the aperture at time \( t \pm  {\Delta t} \) is at least \( \alpha \) also. Hence the aperture is constant.

nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 18.2. Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci Flow on a complete manifold with bounded curvature. If \( \left| {Rm}\right| \rightarrow 0 \) as \( s \rightarrow \infty \) at \( t = 0 \) , this remains true for \( t \geq 0 \) .

nodes.proof:
. For every \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we can find \( \sigma  < \infty \) such that \( \left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  \varepsilon \) for \( s \geq  \sigma \) . The curvature tensor evolves by a formula

\[
{D}_{t}{Rm} = {\Delta Rm} + {Rm} * {Rm}
\]

which gives a formula

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| Rm\right| }^{2} = \Delta {\left| Rm\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| DRm\right| }^{2} + {Rm} * {Rm} * {Rm}
\]

and an estimate

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| Rm\right| }^{2} + C{\left| Rm\right| }^{3}
\]

for some constant \( C \) depending only on the dimension. For any \( \delta  > 0 \) choose

\[
\rho  = \sigma  + \left( {{M}^{2} - {\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) /\delta
\]

and choose the continuous function

\[
\psi  = \left\{  \begin{array}{lll} {M}^{2} & \text{ if } & s \leq  \sigma , \\  {M}^{2} - \delta \left( {s - \sigma }\right)  = {\varepsilon }^{2} + \delta \left( {\rho  - s}\right) & \text{ if } & \sigma  \leq  s \leq  \rho , \\  {\varepsilon }^{2} & \text{ if } & s \geq  \rho . \end{array}\right.
\]

where \( s \) is the distance from some origin at \( t = 0 \) . Then \( \psi \) is Lipschitz continuous since \( s \) is, and since \( \left| {Ds}\right|  \leq  1 \) almost everywhere we also have \( \left| {D\psi }\right|  \leq  \delta \) almost everywhere.

Now we can smooth \( \psi \) locally and patch together with a partition of unity to get a function \( \widetilde{\psi } \) which is smooth and has

\[
- {\varepsilon }^{2} \leq  \widetilde{\psi } \leq  {M}^{2} + {\varepsilon }^{2}\;\text{ and }\;\left| {D\widetilde{\psi }}\right|  \leq  {2\delta }\;\text{ everywhere }
\]

and

\[
\widetilde{\psi } \geq  {M}^{2} - {\varepsilon }^{2}\;\text{ for }\;s \leq  \sigma \;\text{ and }\;\widetilde{\psi } \leq  {\varepsilon }^{2}\;\text{ if }\;s \geq  \rho .
\]

Lastly take \( \varphi  = \psi  + 2{\varepsilon }^{2} \) . Then

\[
{\varepsilon }^{2} \leq  \varphi  \leq  {M}^{2} + 3{\varepsilon }^{2}\;\text{ and }\;\left| {D\varphi }\right|  \leq  {2\delta }\;\text{ everywhere }
\]

and

\[
\varphi  \geq  {M}^{2}\text{ if }s \leq  \sigma \text{ and }\varphi  \leq  3{\varepsilon }^{2}\text{ if }s \geq  \rho .
\]

Now define \( \varphi \) for \( t \geq  0 \) by solving the scalar heat equation

\[
\frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial t} = {\Delta \varphi }
\]

in the Laplacian of the metric evolving by the Ricci Flow. By the maximum principle we still have \( {\varepsilon }^{2} \leq  \varphi  \leq  {M}^{2} \) everywhere for \( t \geq  0 \) . The derivative \( {D}_{a}\varphi \) evolves in an evolving orthonormal frame by the formula

\[
{D}_{t}{D}_{a}\varphi  = \Delta {D}_{a}\varphi
\]

and hence

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| D\varphi \right| }^{2} = \Delta {\left| D\varphi \right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2}.
\]

Note this formula does not involve the curvature. Hence \( \left| {D\varphi }\right|  \leq  {2\delta } \) everywhere for \( t \geq  0 \) by the maximum principle.

The second derivative \( {D}_{a}{D}_{b}\varphi \) evolves by the formula

\[
{D}_{t}{D}_{a}{D}_{b}\varphi  = \Delta {D}_{a}{D}_{b}\varphi  + 2{R}_{acbd}{D}_{c}{D}_{d}\varphi
\]

and hence

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} = \Delta {\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {D}^{3}\varphi \right| }^{2} + 4{R}_{acbd}{D}_{a}{D}_{b}\varphi {D}_{c}{D}_{d}\varphi
\]

which gives an estimate

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} + {CM}{\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2}
\]

for some constant \( C \) depending only on the dimension. Let us put

\[
F = t{\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} + {\left| D\varphi \right| }^{2}
\]

and compute

\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial t} \leq  {\Delta F} - \left( {1 - {CMt}}\right) {\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2}.
\]

Then if \( t \leq  c/M \) where \( c = 1/C \) depends only on the dimension, we have

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} \leq  {\Delta F}
\]

and the maximum of \( F \) decreases. But

\[
F \leq  4{\delta }^{2}
\]

at \( t = 0 \) , and hence for \( t \geq  0 \) also. Thus

\[
\left| {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  {2\delta }/\sqrt{t}\;\text{ for }\;0 < t \leq  c/M.
\]

Since \( {\left| \Delta \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  n{\left| {D}^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} \) and \( \varphi \) solves the heat equation,

\[
\left| \frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial t}\right|  \leq  {C\delta }\sqrt{t}\text{ for }0 < t \leq  c/M
\]

where this constant \( C = 2\sqrt{n} \) depends only on the dimension \( n \) . Now \( 1/\sqrt{t} \) has an improper integral which is \( 2\sqrt{t} \) which is finite, so for all \( P \)

\[
\left| {\varphi \left( {P, t}\right)  - \varphi \left( {P,0}\right) }\right|  \leq  {2C\delta }\sqrt{t}\text{ for }0 < t \leq  c/M.
\]

Since \( \delta  > 0 \) is arbitrarily small, we can take

\[
\delta  \leq  {\varepsilon }^{2}\sqrt{M}/{2C}\sqrt{c}
\]

so that \( {2C\delta }\sqrt{t} \leq  {\varepsilon }^{2} \) for \( t \leq  c/M \) . Then \( \varphi  \leq  4{\varepsilon }^{2} \) at times \( t \leq  c/M \) on the set where \( s \geq  \rho \) at \( t = 0 \) . Now distances can expand, but only at an exponential rate governed by \( M \) . In particular if \( s = s\left( {P,0, t}\right) \) is the distance between a point \( P \) and the origin 0 at time \( t \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial s}{\partial t} \leq  {CMs}
\]

and

\[
s\left( t\right)  \leq  s\left( 0\right) {e}^{CMt}.
\]

This gives us a constant \( C \) depending only on the dimension such that if \( s \geq  {C\rho } \) at \( P \) at time \( t \leq  c/M \) then \( s \geq  \rho \) at \( P \) at \( t = 0 \) , and \( \varphi  \leq  4{\epsilon }^{2} \) at \( P \) at time \( t \) .

Now at \( t = 0 \) we have

\[
{\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  {M}^{2} \leq  \varphi \text{ if }s \leq  \sigma
\]

and

\[
{\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  {\varepsilon }^{2} \leq  \varphi \text{ if }s \geq  \sigma
\]

so \( {\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \varphi \) everywhere at \( t = 0 \) . Since

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| Rm\right| }^{2} + C{\left| Rm\right| }^{3}
\]

we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| Rm\right| }^{2} + {CM}{\left| Rm\right| }^{2}
\]

while

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{e}^{CMt}\varphi }\right)  = \Delta \left( {{e}^{CMt}\varphi }\right)  + {CM}\left( {{e}^{CMt}\varphi }\right)
\]

so \( {\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  {e}^{CMt}\varphi \) by the maximum principle. For \( t \leq  c/M \) this gives \( {\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq \; {C\varphi } \) for some other constant \( C \) depending only on the dimension. Hence at time \( t \) we have

\[
{\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  C{\varepsilon }^{2}\text{ for }s \geq  {C\rho }
\]

where these constants \( C \) depend only on the dimension and are independent of \( \varepsilon \) . Thus \( \left| {Rm}\right|  \rightarrow  0 \) for \( t \leq  c/M \) also as \( s \rightarrow  \infty \) . Since the time interval can always be advanced by \( c/M \) as long as \( \left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  M \) , we get the result until \( \left| {Rm}\right| \) becomes unbounded or \( t \rightarrow  \infty \) .

Suppose we have a complete solution to the Ricci Flow with bounded curvature and weakly positive Ricci curvature, where \( \left| {Rm}\right| \rightarrow 0 \) as \( s \rightarrow \infty \) (a condition preserved by the flow). Then the asymptotic volume ratio \( \nu \) is constant.

nodes.proof:
we shall choose soon, and consider the annulus

\[
{N}_{\sigma } = \{ {\gamma \sigma } \leq  s \leq  \sigma \} .
\]

Since

\[
{N}_{\sigma } = {B}_{\sigma } - {B}_{\gamma \sigma }
\]

we have

\[
V\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right)  = V\left( {B}_{\sigma }\right)  - V\left( {B}_{\gamma \sigma }\right) .
\]

If the asymptotic curvature ratio is at least \( \nu \) , then

\[
V\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  \left( {\nu  - {\gamma }^{n}\bar{\nu }}\right) {\sigma }^{n}.
\]

When \( \gamma \) is small, \( \nu  - {\gamma }^{n}\bar{\nu } \) is nearly \( \nu \) and most of the volume of the ball is in the annulus.

The volume of the annulus changes at a rate

\[
\frac{d}{dt}V\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right)  =  - {\int }_{{N}_{\sigma }}{Rdv}
\]

For every \( \varepsilon \) and every \( \gamma \) we can find \( {\sigma }_{0} \) so that if \( \sigma  \geq  {\sigma }_{0} \) then \( \left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  \varepsilon \) on \( {N}_{\sigma } \) . This makes

\[
\left| {\frac{d}{dt}V\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right) }\right|  \leq  {\varepsilon V}\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right) .
\]

If \( {V}_{1}\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right) \) is the volume at time \( {t}_{1} \) and \( {V}_{2}\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right) \) is the volume at time \( {t}_{2} \) we have

\[
{V}_{2}\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  {e}^{-\varepsilon \left| {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right| }{V}_{1}\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right) .
\]

Let \( {\nu }_{1} \) be the asymptotic volume ratio at time \( {t}_{1} \) and \( {\nu }_{2} \) the ratio at time \( {t}_{2} \) . Then

\[
{V}_{1}\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  \left( {{\nu }_{1} - {\gamma }^{n}\bar{\nu }}\right) {\sigma }^{n}
\]

for all \( \sigma \) and all \( \gamma  > 0 \) . If \( {V}_{2}\left( {B}_{\sigma }\right) \) is the volume of \( {B}_{\sigma } \) at time \( {t}_{2} \) then

\[
{V}_{2}\left( {B}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  {V}_{2}\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right)
\]

Together these make

\[
{V}_{2}\left( {B}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  {e}^{-\varepsilon \left| {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right| }\left( {{V}_{1} - {\gamma }^{n}\bar{\nu }}\right) {\sigma }^{n}.
\]

Fix \( \gamma  > 0 \) and let \( \sigma  \rightarrow  0 \) . Then \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) and

\[
{\nu }_{2} = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\sigma  \rightarrow  \infty }}{V}_{2}\left( {B}_{\sigma }\right) /{\sigma }^{2} \geq  {\nu }_{1} - {\gamma }^{n}\bar{\nu }
\]

Since this is true for all \( \gamma  > 0,{\nu }_{2} \geq  {\nu }_{1} \) . But we can switch \( {t}_{1} \) and \( {t}_{2} \) , so \( {\nu }_{1} = {\nu }_{2} \) and \( \nu \) is constant.

nodes.proof:
, and we conclude that the scalar curvature \( R \) is pointwise increasing. If the asymptotic curvature ratio is \( A \) at time \( t \) then for any finite \( \widetilde{A} < A \) and any \( \widetilde{s} \) we can find a point \( P \) at distance \( s \geq  \widetilde{s} \) from 0 at time \( t \) where \( R{s}^{2} \geq  \widetilde{A} \) . At a later time \( t + {\Delta t} \) with \( {\Delta t} \geq  0 \) the scalar curvature \( R \) at \( P \) is at least as big, while if \( M \) is a bound on the curvature everywhere the distance \( s \) of \( P \) from 0 will not have shrunk by more than \( C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t} \) . Since

\[
\frac{s - C\sqrt{M}{\Delta t}}{s} \rightarrow  1\text{ as }s \rightarrow  \infty
\]

we see that the asymptotic scalar curvature ratio is at least \( A \) still at time \( t + {\Delta t} \) . Hence \( A \) does not decrease.

To see \( A \) does not increase either, first suppose at some time \( t \) that \( A \) is finite. Then for any \( \widehat{A} > A \) we can find \( \widetilde{s} \geq  1/\sqrt{M} \) so that \( R{s}^{2} \leq  \widehat{A} \) for \( s \geq  \widetilde{s} \)

at time \( t \) . Moreover for any \( \widetilde{s} \) and any \( \widetilde{A} < A \) we can again pick a point \( P \) at time \( t \) with \( R{s}^{2} \geq  \widetilde{A} \) and \( s \geq  2\widetilde{s} \) . Consider any point \( Q \) at distance

\[
d\left( {P, Q,\tau }\right)  \leq  s/2
\]

for any \( \tau  \leq  t \) . Since \( {Rc} \geq  0 \) , distances shrink and

\[
d\left( {P, Q, t}\right)  \leq  s/2
\]

also. Then

\[
d\left( {Q,0, t}\right)  \geq  s/2 \geq  \widetilde{s}
\]

and by our choice of \( \widetilde{s} \)

\[
R\left( {Q, t}\right)  \leq  4\widehat{A}/{s}^{2}
\]

and since \( R \) increases pointwise

\[
R\left( {Q,\tau }\right)  \leq  4\widehat{A}/{s}^{2}
\]

also. Our interior derivative estimates allow us to bound \( {DR} \) and also \( {D}^{2}R \) , and hence \( \partial R/\partial t \) . Recall from section 13 that if \( \left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  M \) at all points at distance at most \( r \) from \( P \) for all times between \( \tau  - {r}^{2} \) and \( \tau \) with \( M{r}^{2} \leq  1 \) then

\[
\left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {CM}/{r}^{2}
\]

with a constant \( C \) depending only on the dimension. We can bound \( \left| {Rm}\right| \) by \( R \) and take

\[
M = C\widehat{A}/{s}^{2}.
\]

When \( \widehat{A} \leq  1/C \) we can take \( r = s/2 \) ; when \( \widehat{A} \geq  1/C \) we can take \( r = 1/2\sqrt{M} \leq \; s/2 \) . In the first case we find that

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t}\left( {P,\tau }\right)  \leq  C\widehat{A}/{s}^{4}
\]

and in the second case we find

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t}\left( {P,\tau }\right)  \leq  C{\widehat{A}}^{2}/{s}^{4}
\]

for some constant \( C \) depending only on \( n \) , at all \( \tau  \leq  t \) . Use \( \widehat{A} + {\widehat{A}}^{2} \) for either case.

Pick \( {\Delta t} \geq  0 \) . Then

\[
R\left( {P, t - {\Delta t}}\right)  \geq  R\left( {P, t}\right)  - C\left( {\widehat{A} + {\widehat{A}}^{2}}\right) {\Delta t}/{s}^{4}.
\]

Also

\[
d\left( {P,0, t - {\Delta t}}\right)  \geq  d\left( {P,0, t}\right)  = s.
\]

Taking \( s \) very big compared to \( {\Delta t} \) and \( \widetilde{A} \) and \( \widehat{A} \) so that

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right)  \geq  \widetilde{A}/{s}^{2} \geq  C\left( {\widehat{A} + {\widehat{A}}^{2}}\right) {\Delta t}/{s}^{4}
\]

we have

\[
R\left( {P, t - {\Delta t}}\right) s{\left( P,0, t - \Delta t\right) }^{2} \geq  {s}^{2}\left\lbrack  {\frac{\widetilde{A}}{{s}^{2}} - \frac{C\left( {\widehat{A} + {\widehat{A}}^{2}}\right) {\Delta t}}{{s}^{4}}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \widetilde{A}
\]

as \( s \rightarrow  \infty \) . Hence lim sup \( R{s}^{2} \geq  A \) at time \( t - {\Delta t} \) as well.

In the case where \( A = \infty \) at time \( t \) , so that

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}R\left( {Q, t}\right) d{\left( Q,0, t\right) }^{2} = \infty
\]

we have to be more careful. For any \( \widetilde{A} < \infty \) choose the largest \( \widetilde{s} \) so that

\[
\sup \left\{  {R\left( {Q, t}\right) d{\left( Q,0, t\right) }^{2} : d\left( {Q,0, t}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{s}}\right\}   \leq  \widetilde{A}.
\]

That a largest \( \widetilde{s} \) exists is clear since if \( Q \) is any point at distance \( \widetilde{s} \) we can find \( {Q}_{j} \) at distance \( {\widetilde{s}}_{j} \) with \( {\widetilde{s}}_{j} \nearrow  \widetilde{s} \) and \( {Q}_{j} \rightarrow  Q \) . Moreover since the sphere of radius \( \widetilde{s} \) is compact, there must exist a \( \widetilde{Q} \) with

\[
d\left( {\widetilde{Q},0, t}\right)  = \widetilde{s}
\]

and

\[
R\left( {\widetilde{Q}, t}\right) d{\left( \widetilde{Q},0, t\right) }^{2} = \widetilde{A}
\]

or else \( \widetilde{s} \) would not be maximal. Now choose \( P \) so that

\[
d\left( {P,0, t}\right)  \geq  \widetilde{s}
\]

and

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}\sup \{ R\left( {Q, t}\right)  : d\left( {Q,0, t}\right)  \geq  \widetilde{s}\}
\]

which is possible since \( R \) is bounded. Since \( \widetilde{Q} \) is a possible choice

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}R\left( {\widetilde{Q}, t}\right)
\]

and then

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right) d{\left( P,0, t\right) }^{2} \geq  \frac{1}{2}\widetilde{A}.
\]

If \( Q \) is any point with

\[
d\left( {P, Q,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}d\left( {P,0, t}\right)
\]

at some time \( \tau  \leq  t \) , then since distances shrink

\[
d\left( {P, Q, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}d\left( {P,0, t}\right)
\]

as well, and

\[
\frac{1}{2}d\left( {P,0, t}\right)  \leq  d\left( {Q,0, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2}d\left( {P,0, t}\right) .
\]

Either

\[
d\left( {Q,0, t}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{s}
\]

in which case

\[
R\left( {Q, t}\right) d{\left( Q,0, t\right) }^{2} \leq  \widetilde{A}
\]

by our choice of \( \widetilde{s} \) , and

\[
R\left( {Q, t}\right)  \leq  2\widetilde{A}/d{\left( P,0, t\right) }^{2} \leq  {4R}\left( {P, t}\right) ;
\]

or else

\[
d\left( {Q,0, t}\right)  \geq  \widetilde{s}
\]

in which case

\[
R\left( {Q, t}\right)  \leq  {2R}\left( {P, t}\right)
\]

by our choice of \( P \) ; and so in either case

\[
R\left( {Q, t}\right)  \leq  {4R}\left( {P, t}\right) .
\]

Since \( R \) increases pointwise,

\[
R\left( {Q,\tau }\right)  \leq  {4R}\left( {P, t}\right)
\]

for \( \tau  \leq  t \) whenever

\[
d\left( {P, Q,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}d\left( {P,0, t}\right) .
\]

Now we can use the interior derivative estimate again, for \( \widetilde{A} \geq  1 \) we get

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t}\left( {P,\tau }\right)  \leq  C{\widetilde{A}}^{2}/d{\left( P,0, t\right) }^{4}
\]

and as before

\[
R\left( {P,0, t - {\Delta t}}\right) d{\left( P,0, t - \Delta t\right) }^{2} \geq  \frac{1}{2}\widetilde{A} - C{\widetilde{A}}^{2}{\Delta t}/d{\left( P,0, t\right) }^{2}
\]

where \( d\left( {P,0, t}\right) \) is large compared to \( {\Delta t} \) and \( \widetilde{A} \) . As \( d\left( {P,0, t}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) we see that

\[
\lim \sup R{s}^{2} = \infty
\]

a time \( t - {\Delta t} \) as well. This finishes the proof of the Theorem.

THEOREM 19.2. Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci Flow on an ancient time interval \( - \infty  < t < T \) , complete with bounded curvature and strictly positive curvature operator. Assume

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow   - \infty }}\left( {T - t}\right) R < \infty
\]

(as happens in Type I) and assume the asymptotic scalar curvature ratio (which we saw is constant in time) is finite

\[
A = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}R{s}^{2} < \infty
\]

Then we get the following results:

(a) The asymptotic volume ratio (which we saw is constant in time) is strictly positive

\[
\nu  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}V\left( {B}_{s}\right) /{s}^{n} > 0\text{ ; and }
\]

(b) for any origin 0 and any time \( t \) there exists a constant \( \phi \left( {0, t}\right)  > 0 \) such that at all points at the time \( t \)

\[
R{s}^{2} \geq  \phi \left( {0, t}\right) \text{ . }
\]

giving an upper bound on the curvature at all pairs of points and all time.

LEMMA. There exists a constant \( \bar{C} \) such that for all points \( P \) and \( Q \) at all times \( t \leq  0 \) we have

\[
\min \left\lbrack  {R\left( {P, t}\right) , R\left( {Q, t}\right) }\right\rbrack  d{\left( P, Q, t\right) }^{2} \leq  \bar{C}
\]

where \( d\left( {P, Q, t}\right) \) is the distance from \( P \) to \( Q \) at time \( t \) .

Proof. Since \( A < \infty \) , some constant \( {C}_{0} \) works at \( t = 0 \) , so

\[
\min \left\lbrack  {R\left( {P,0}\right) , R\left( {Q,0}\right) }\right\rbrack  d{\left( P, Q,0\right) }^{2} \leq  {C}_{0}
\]

for all \( P \) and \( Q \) . Since \( R \) increases pointwise,

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right)  \leq  R\left( {P,0}\right) \text{ and }R\left( {Q, t}\right)  \leq  R\left( {Q,0}\right)
\]

for \( t \leq  0 \) . Since \( R \leq  C/\left( {T - t}\right) \) , we can use Theorem 1.72 to get

\[
d\left( {P, Q, t}\right)  \leq  d\left( {P, Q,0}\right)  + C\sqrt{T - t}.
\]

This makes

\[
d{\left( P, Q, t\right) }^{2} \leq  {2d}{\left( P, Q,0\right) }^{2} + C\left( {T - t}\right) .
\]

Thus

\[
\min \left\lbrack  {R\left( {P, t}\right) , R\left( {Q, t}\right) }\right\rbrack  d{\left( P, Q, t\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  2\min \left\lbrack  {R\left( {P,0}\right) , R\left( {Q,0}\right) }\right\rbrack  d{\left( P, Q,0\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C\min \left\lbrack  {R\left( {P, t}\right) , R\left( {Q, t}\right) }\right\rbrack  \left( {T - t}\right)  \leq  \bar{C}
\]

for some constant \( \bar{C} \) using the bound on the first term at \( t = 0 \) and the bound \( R \leq  C/\left( {T - t}\right) \) everywhere.

LEMMA. There exists a constant \( c > 0 \) such that for every \( t \leq  0 \) we can find a point \( {P}_{t} \) where

\[
R\left( {{P}_{t}, t}\right)  \geq  c/\left( {T - t}\right) .
\]

Proof. The maximum \( {R}_{\max } \) of \( R \) satisfies the ordinary differential inequality

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{R}_{\max } \leq  C{R}_{\max }^{2}
\]

for some constant \( C \) , by applying the maximum principle to the evolution of \( R \) . If \( {R}_{\max }\left( t\right) \) were even smaller than \( c/\left( {T - t}\right) \) for \( c \) small, it could not make it up to \( {R}_{\max }\left( 0\right) \) in time.

Now fix an origin 0 and let \( s = d\left( {P, t}\right)  = d\left( {P,0, t}\right) \) be the distance of \( P \) to the origin at time \( t \) .

LEMMA. There exists a constant \( {C}^{ * } \) so that \( R{s}^{2} \leq  {C}^{ * } \) for all \( t \leq  0 \) .

Proof. Since

\[
R\left( {{P}_{t},0}\right)  \geq  R\left( {{P}_{t}, t}\right)  \geq  c/\left( {T - t}\right)
\]

while

\[
\min \left\lbrack  {R\left( {{P}_{t},0}\right) , R\left( {0,0}\right) }\right\rbrack  d{\left( {P}_{t},0,0\right) }^{2} \leq  {C}_{0}
\]

we get an estimate

\[
d\left( {{P}_{t},0,0}\right)  \leq  C\sqrt{T - t}
\]

(where the case \( R\left( {{P}_{t},0}\right)  \geq  R\left( {0,0}\right) \) can be handled separately because \( R\left( {0,0}\right)  \leq \; C/T \) anyway while \( T - t \geq  T \) ). Then using our distance shrinking bound

\[
d\left( {{P}_{t},0, t}\right)  \leq  C\sqrt{T - t}
\]

for a larger constant \( C \) . For any \( P \)

\[
d\left( {P,0, t}\right)  \leq  d\left( {P,{P}_{t}, t}\right)  + d\left( {{P}_{t},0, t}\right)
\]

by the triangle inequality. We already have

\[
\min \left\lbrack  {R\left( {P, t}\right) , R\left( {{P}_{t}, t}\right) }\right\rbrack  d{\left( P,{P}_{t}, t\right) }^{2} \leq  \bar{C}
\]

for some constant \( \bar{C} \) independent of \( t \) . If

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right)  \geq  R\left( {{P}_{t}, t}\right)  \geq  c/\left( {T - t}\right)
\]

then the same argument that worked for \( {P}_{t} \) proves that

\[
d\left( {P,0, t}\right)  \leq  C\sqrt{T - t}
\]

and since \( R \leq  C/\left( {T - t}\right) , R{s}^{2} \leq  {C}^{ * } \) for some \( {C}^{ * } \) . The other case when

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right)  \leq  R\left( {{P}_{t}, t}\right)
\]

gives

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right) d{\left( P,{P}_{t}, t\right) }^{2} \leq  \bar{C}
\]

in the estimate above, and since

\[
d\left( {P,0, t}\right)  \leq  d\left( {P,{P}_{t}, t}\right)  + c\sqrt{T - t}
\]

and \( R\left( {P, t}\right)  \leq  C/\sqrt{T - t} \) , we get

\[
R\left( {P, t}\right) d{\left( P,0, t\right) }^{2} \leq  {C}^{ * }
\]

also for some \( {C}^{ * } \) . This proves this Lemma.

Now we turn to the volume estimate. It is useful first to look at annuli.

LEMMA. There exists a constant \( c > 0 \) such that the annulus at \( t = 0 \)

\[
{N}_{\sigma } = \{ \sigma  \leq  s \leq  {3\sigma }\}
\]

has volume

\[
V\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  c{\sigma }^{n}.
\]

Proof. Let \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) be a small constant we can choose later. Look at time

\[
\tau  =  - \varepsilon {\sigma }^{2}
\]

at the annulus

\[
{\widehat{N}}_{\sigma } = \{ {2\sigma } \leq  s \leq  {3\sigma }\} .
\]

Since distances shrink as \( t \) increases from \( \tau \) to 0, the outer sphere of \( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma } \) surely lies inside the outer sphere of \( {N}_{\sigma } \) . But we have seen

\[
d\left( {P,0,\tau }\right)  \geq  d\left( {P,0,0}\right)  - C\sqrt{T - \tau }
\]

and so if \( \sigma \) is large (which is our only concern), in particular \( \sigma  \geq  \sqrt{T/\varepsilon } \) , then \( T - \tau  \leq  2\left| \tau \right|  \leq  {2\varepsilon }{\sigma }^{2} \) and

\[
d\left( {P,0,\tau }\right)  \geq  d\left( {P,0,0}\right)  - C\sqrt{2\varepsilon }\sigma .
\]

Choose \( \varepsilon \) so small that \( C\sqrt{2\varepsilon } \leq  1 \) . Then

\[
d\left( {P,0,\tau }\right)  \geq  d\left( {P,0,0}\right)  - \sigma
\]

so no distance from the origin shrinks by more than \( \sigma \) . Hence the inner sphere of \( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma } \) lies outside the inner sphere of \( {N}_{\sigma } \) , and \( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma } \subseteq  {N}_{\sigma } \) . (Of course we don’t need these to be topological annuli, we only estimate distances.)

Next we claim we can find \( \delta  > 0 \) (depending on the \( \varepsilon \) we choose) so that \( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma } \) has volume

\[
V\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  \delta {\sigma }^{n}
\]

at time \( \tau  =  - \varepsilon {\sigma }^{2} \) . Since the curvature (for \( \sigma  \geq  \sqrt{T/\varepsilon } \) again) satisfies a bound

\[
R \leq  C/\left| \tau \right|  \leq  C/\varepsilon {\sigma }^{2},
\]

this remark follows from the following result by dilation, with \( \delta  = \zeta {\left( \varepsilon /C\right) }^{n/2} \) .

LEMMA. For every \( \rho  > 0 \) there exists a \( \zeta  > 0 \) so that if a complete manifold with positive sectional curvature has \( 0 < R \leq  1 \) , then the annulus

\[
{\widehat{N}}_{\rho } = \{ {2\rho } \leq  s \leq  {3\rho }\}
\]

has volume

\[
V\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\rho }\right)  \geq  \zeta
\]

Proof. Since the manifold is complete with positive curvature but not compact, we can bound the injectivity radius by some apriori constant \( c > 0 \) below. The annulus contains a minimal geodesic of length \( \rho \) , as we see by intersecting it with a ray to infinity. If \( \rho  \leq  c/2 \) the result is easy using geodesic coordinates at the origin, while if \( \rho  > c/2 \) we can put a ball of radius \( c/2 \) inside the annulus. (In fact for large \( \rho \) we see the area is at least a constant times \( \rho \) . This is the best we can do if the manifold opens like a cylinder.)

Now we want to see that \( V\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }\right) \) still has a large area at \( t = 0 \) . At each time \( \tau  \leq  t \leq  0 \) we still have all of \( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma } \) outside the ball of radius \( \sigma \) , where \( R \leq  {C}^{ * }/{\sigma }^{2} \) . Therefore we can estimate the rate at which the volume shrinks by

\[
\frac{d}{dt}V\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }\right)  =  - {\int }_{{\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }}{Rda} \geq   - \frac{{C}^{ * }}{{\sigma }^{2}}V\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right) .
\]

This makes

\[
{\left. V\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }\right) \right| }_{t = 0} \geq  {\left. {e}^{-{C}^{ * }\tau /{\sigma }^{2}}V\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }\right) \right| }_{t = \tau }.
\]

Since \( \tau  = \varepsilon {\sigma }^{2} \) we get

\[
{\left. V\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }\right) \right| }_{t = 0} \geq  {\left. cV\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }\right) \right| }_{t = \tau } \geq  {c\delta }{\sigma }^{n}.
\]

But at \( t = 0, V\left( {B}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  V\left( {N}_{\sigma }\right)  \geq  V\left( {\widehat{N}}_{\sigma }\right) \) so 19.2(a) is done. Next we look at 19.2(b). Given a point \( P \) at distance \( \sigma  = d\left( {P,0,0}\right) \) from the origin at time \( t = 0 \) , we let \( \tau  =  - \varepsilon {\sigma }^{2} \) as before and find \( {P}_{\tau } \) where

\[
R\left( {{P}_{\tau },\tau }\right)  \geq  c/\left( {T - \tau }\right) \text{ and }d\left( {{P}_{\tau },0,\tau }\right)  \leq  c\sqrt{T - \tau }.
\]

The Harnack inequality on a manifold with positive curvature operator in its integrated form (see [29]) gives

\[
R\left( {P,0}\right)  \geq  R\left( {{P}_{\tau },\tau }\right) {e}^{-{Cd}{\left( {P}_{\tau }, P,\tau \right) }^{2}/\left| \tau \right| }
\]

for some constant \( C \) . The triangle inequality gives

\[
d\left( {{P}_{\tau }, P,\tau }\right)  \leq  d\left( {{P}_{\tau },0,\tau }\right)  + d\left( {P,0,\tau }\right)
\]

and

\[
d\left( {P,0,\tau }\right)  \leq  d\left( {P,0,0}\right)  = \sigma .
\]

Then

\[
d\left( {{P}_{\tau }, P,\tau }\right)  \leq  \sigma  + C\sqrt{T - \tau }.
\]

Again if \( \sigma  \geq  \sqrt{T/\varepsilon } \) we have \( T - \tau  \leq  2\left| \tau \right| \) and

\[
d\left( {{P}_{\tau }, P,\tau }\right)  \leq  {C\sigma }
\]

for some constant \( C \) , making

\[
d\left( {{P}_{\tau }, P,\tau }\right) /\left| \tau \right|  \leq  C
\]

for some other constant \( C \) depending on \( \varepsilon \) . This yields \( R\left( {P,0}\right)  \geq  c/{\sigma }^{2} \) as desired. For \( \sigma  \leq  \sqrt{T/\varepsilon } \) some constant \( c > 0 \) works because \( R > 0 \) . Hence the Lemma is proved. A similar bound can be derived at any time.

THEOREM 20.1. Suppose we have a complete Ricci soliton with bounded curvature, so that

\[
{D}^{2}f = {Rc}
\]

for some function \( f \) . Assume the Ricci curvature is weakly positive

\[
{Rc} \geq  0
\]

and assume the scalar curvature attains its maximum \( M \) at an origin. Then the function \( f \) is weakly convex and attains its minimum at the origin, and furthermore

\[
{\left| Df\right| }^{2} + R = M
\]

everywhere on the soliton. The soliton is not compact unless \( {Rc} = 0 \) .

nodes.proof:
Since

\[
{D}_{i}{D}_{j}f = {R}_{ij}
\]

we have

\[
{D}_{i}{D}_{j}{D}_{k}f = {D}_{i}{R}_{jk}
\]

and

\[
{D}_{i}{D}_{j}{D}_{k}f - {D}_{j}{D}_{i}{D}_{k}f = {D}_{i}{R}_{jk} - {D}_{j}{R}_{ik}
\]

and

\[
{D}_{i}{D}_{j}{D}_{k}f - {D}_{j}{D}_{i}{D}_{k}f = {R}_{{ijk}\ell }{D}_{\ell }f
\]

so

\[
{D}_{i}{R}_{jk} - {D}_{j}{R}_{ik} = {R}_{{ijk}\ell }{D}_{\ell }f.
\]

Taking a trace on \( j \) and \( k \) , and using the contracted second Bianchi identity

\[
{D}_{j}{R}_{ij} = \frac{1}{2}{D}_{i}R
\]

we get that

\[
{D}_{i}R + 2{R}_{ij}{D}_{j}f = 0.
\]

Then

\[
{D}_{i}\left( {{\left| Df\right| }^{2} + R}\right)  = 2{D}_{j}f\left( {{D}_{i}{D}_{j}f - {R}_{ij}}\right)  = 0
\]

so \( {\left| Df\right| }^{2} + R \) is constant. Call it \( {M}^{ * } \) .

If \( {M}^{ * } = M \) , then \( {Df} = 0 \) at the origin. Since \( {D}_{i}{D}_{j}f = {R}_{ij} \geq  0 \) , along any geodesic through the origin \( {x}^{i} = {x}^{i}\left( s\right) \) parameterized by arc length \( s \) we have

\[
\frac{df}{ds} = {D}_{i}f \cdot  \frac{d{x}^{i}}{ds}
\]

and

\[
\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{s}^{2}} = {D}_{i}{D}_{j}f \cdot  \frac{d{x}^{i}}{ds}\frac{d{x}^{j}}{ds} \geq  0
\]

so \( f \) is convex and hence least at the origin. Since any point can be joined to the origin by a geodesic, we are done in this case.

If \( {M}^{ * } > M \) , consider a gradient path of \( f \) through the origin \( {x}^{i} = {x}^{i}\left( n\right) \) parametrized by the parameter \( u \) with \( {x}^{i} \) at the origin at \( u = 0 \) and

\[
\frac{d{x}^{i}}{du} = {g}^{ij}{D}_{j}f.
\]

Now \( {\left| Df\right| }^{2} = {M}^{ * } - R \) so \( {\left| Df\right| }^{2} \geq  {M}^{ * } - M > 0 \) everywhere, while \( {\left| Df\right| }^{2} \) is smallest at the origin. But we compute

\[
\frac{d}{du}{\left| Df\right| }^{2} = 2{g}^{ik}{g}^{j\ell }{R}_{ij}{D}_{k}f{D}_{\ell }f \geq  0
\]

since \( {R}_{ij} \geq  0 \) and \( {\left| Df\right| }^{2} \geq  0 \) . Then \( {\left| Df\right| }^{2} \) isn’t smaller at the origin, and we have a contradiction.

If the solution is compact then

\[
{\Delta f} = R \geq  0
\]

implies \( f \) is constant, so \( {Rc} = {D}^{2}f = 0 \) .

nodes.content:
THEOREM 20.2. For a complete Ricci soliton with bounded curvature and strictly positive sectional curvature of dimension \( n \geq  3 \) where the scalar curvature assumes its maximum at an origin, the asymtotic scalar curvature ratio is infinite;

\[
A = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}R{s}^{2} = \infty
\]

where \( s \) is the distance to the origin.
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 20.2. For a complete Ricci soliton with bounded curvature and strictly positive sectional curvature of dimension \( n \geq 3 \) where the scalar curvature assumes its maximum at an origin, the asymtotic scalar curvature ratio is infinite; \[ A = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{s \rightarrow \infty }}R{s}^{2} = \infty \] where \( s \) is the distance to the origin.

nodes.proof:
The solution to the Ricci Flow corresponding to the soliton exists for \( - \infty  < t < \infty \) and is obtained by flowing along the gradient of \( f \) . We will show that the limit

\[
{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( x\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow   - \infty }}{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right)
\]

exists for \( x \neq  0 \) on the manifold \( \mathcal{X} \) and is a flat metric on \( \mathcal{X} - \{ 0\} \) which is complete. Since \( \mathcal{X} \) has positive curvature operator it is diffeomorphic to \( {R}^{n} \) , and \( \mathcal{X} - \{ 0\} \) to \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  {R}^{1} \) . For \( n \geq  3 \) there is no flat metric on this space, and this will finish the proof.

To see the limit metric exists, note that unless \( R{s}^{2} \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( s \rightarrow  \infty \) , surely \( R \rightarrow  0 \) as \( X \rightarrow  \infty \) so \( {\left| Df\right| }^{2} \rightarrow  M \) as \( X \rightarrow  \infty \) , at least at \( t = 0 \) . The function \( f \) itself can be taken to evolve with time, using the definition

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} =  - {\left| Df\right| }^{2} = {\Delta f} - M
\]

which pulls \( f \) back by the flow along the gradient of \( f \) . Then we continue to have \( {D}_{i}{D}_{j}f = {R}_{ij} \) for all time, and \( {\left| Df\right| }^{2} \rightarrow  M \) as \( s \rightarrow  \infty \) for each time.

When we go backwards in time, this is equivalent to flowing outwards along the gradient of \( f \) , and our speed approaches \( \sqrt{M} \) . If \( s \) is the distance from 0, then \( s/\left| t\right|  \rightarrow  \sqrt{M} \) . Since \( R{s}^{2} \leq  C \) for some constant \( C, R \leq  C/{s}^{2} \) , and starting outside of any neighborhood of 0 we have \( R \leq  C/M{\left| t\right| }^{2} \) and hence

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{R}_{ij} \geq   - {2R}{g}_{ij}
\]

gives

\[
0 \geq  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} \geq   - \frac{2C}{M{\left| t\right| }^{2}}{g}_{ij}.
\]

If \( V \) is a tangent vector and \( {\left| V\right| }_{t} \) denotes its length at time \( t \) , so

\[
{\left| V\right| }_{t}^{2} = {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) {V}^{i}{V}^{j}
\]

then

\[
0 \geq  \frac{d}{dt}{\left| V\right| }_{t}^{2} \geq   - \frac{2C}{M{\left| t\right| }^{2}}{\left| V\right| }_{t}^{2}
\]

so

\[
0 \leq  \frac{d}{d\left| t\right| }\log {\left| V\right| }_{t}^{2} \leq  \frac{2C}{M{\left| t\right| }^{2}}
\]

with \( t < 0 \) decreasing and \( \left| t\right| \) increasing. This makes \( {\left| V\right| }_{t}^{2} \) increasing in \( \left| t\right| \) with

\[
\frac{d}{d\left| t\right| }\left( {\log {\left| V\right| }_{t}^{2} + \frac{2C}{M\left| t\right| }}\right)  \leq  0
\]

so that

\[
\log {\left| V\right| }_{t}^{2} + \frac{2C}{M\left| t\right| }
\]

is actually decreasing. This shows \( {\left| V\right| }_{t} \) has a limit as \( t \rightarrow   - \infty \) .

Since the metrics are all essentially the same, it always takes an infinite length to get out to \( \infty \) . On the other hand, any point \( X \) other than 0 will eventually be arbitrarily far from 0 , so the metric in the limit is also complete away from 0 in \( \mathcal{X} - \{ 0\} \) . Using the derivative estimates of W.-X. Shi [43] on the curvature it is straightforward to see that the \( {g}_{ij}\left( {X, t}\right) \) converge in \( {C}^{\infty } \) to a smooth limit metric \( {\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( X\right) \) as \( t \rightarrow   - \infty \) . Since \( R \leq  C/{s}^{2} \) and \( s \approx  \sqrt{M}t \) we have the result that the limit metric is flat. This proves the theorem.

at distance \( r \) from \( P \) , and choose a minimal geodesic from \( {P}^{\prime } \) to \( {Q}^{\prime } \) .

![019eb0e3-717c-7df6-9b24-435b86f7860f_81_485_1663_642_364_0.jpg](images/019eb0e3-717c-7df6-9b24-435b86f7860f_81_485_1663_642_364_0.jpg)

Let \( h = \left| {{P}^{\prime }{Q}^{\prime }}\right| , u = \left| {{P}^{\prime }Q}\right| \) and \( v = \left| {Q{Q}^{\prime }}\right| \) and let \( \alpha  = \angle {P}^{\prime }{PQ} \) and \( \beta  = \; \angle P{Q}^{\prime }{P}^{\prime } \) and \( {\beta }^{\prime } = \pi  - \beta \) . We make three applications of Toponogov’s Theorems.

(1) First note for every \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we can find \( \delta  > 0 \) and \( \eta  > 0 \) such that if \( \alpha  \leq  \frac{\pi }{2} + \delta \) then \( h \leq  \left( {\sqrt{2} - \eta }\right) r \) . This is because \( K \geq  \varepsilon /{r}^{2} \) in \( {B}_{2r}\left( P\right) \) and we can compare the triangle \( {P}^{\prime }P{Q}^{\prime } \) to the triangle with two sides equal to \( r \) and angle \( \alpha \) in the sphere of curvature \( H = \varepsilon /{r}^{2} \) using \( {T2} \) . All the sides are minimal, and we only need to check that

\[
h \leq  {2r} \leq  \pi /\sqrt{H}
\]

if \( \varepsilon  < 1 < {\left( \pi /2\right) }^{2} \) . Hence the comparison can be made.

Now on the sphere of radius 1, take an isosceles triangle of equal sides \( \ell  \leq  1 \) with angle \( \alpha  \leq  \frac{\pi }{2} + \delta \) between them and call the length of the third side \( k \) . In an isosceles right triangle \( k \) is strictly less than the Euclidean value of \( \sqrt{2}\ell \) , and hence depending on \( \ell \) we can find \( \delta  > 0 \) and \( \eta  > 0 \) such that if \( \alpha  \leq  \frac{\pi }{2} + \delta \) then still \( k \leq  \left( {\sqrt{2} - \eta }\right) \ell \) . If we scale the result to a sphere of radius \( r/\sqrt{\varepsilon } \) with curvature \( H = \varepsilon /{r}^{2} \) , then taking \( \ell  = \sqrt{\varepsilon } \) gives the desired result.

(2) Now we just use \( K \geq  0 \) . We compare the triangle \( {P}^{\prime }{Q}^{\prime }P \) with two sides equal to \( r \) and one equal to \( h \leq  \left( {\sqrt{2} - \eta }\right) r \) to the Euclidean triangle with the same three sides using \( {T1} \) . again all the sides are minimal, and we can do the comparison. We find that there exists a \( \theta  > 0 \) depending on \( \eta \) only so that \( \beta  \geq  \frac{\pi }{4} + \theta \) . By scaling it suffices to observe that an isosceles Euclidean triangle with two equal sides 1 and the third side less than \( \sqrt{2} - \eta \) has the equal angles at least \( \frac{\pi }{4} + \theta \) .

(3) Finally we use \( {T2} \) again to compare the triangle \( {P}^{\prime }{Q}^{\prime }Q \) to the Euclidean triangle with sides \( h \) and \( v \) and angle \( {\beta }^{\prime } \leq  \frac{3\pi }{4} - \theta \) . Again all the sides are minimal, and we find

\[
{u}^{2} \leq  {h}^{2} + {v}^{2} - {2hv}\cos {\beta }^{\prime }.
\]

Now \( h \leq  \sqrt{2}r \) while

\[
\cos {\beta }^{\prime } \geq   - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \zeta
\]

for some \( \zeta  > 0 \) depending only on \( \theta  > 0 \) .

Therefore

\[
{u}^{2} \leq  {\left( v + r\right) }^{2} + r\left\lbrack  {r - 2\sqrt{2}{\zeta v}}\right\rbrack
\]

and for every \( \zeta  > 0 \) we can choose \( \lambda  < \infty \) so that if

\[
v + r = \left| {PQ}\right|  \geq  {\lambda r}
\]

then \( v \geq  \left( {\lambda  - 1}\right) r \) and \( 2\sqrt{2}{\zeta v} > r \) . Thus \( \left| {{P}^{\prime }Q}\right|  = u < v + r = \left| {PQ}\right| \) as desired.

nodes.proof:
to \( P \) . Draw a minimal geodesic from \( X \) to \( P \) and let its length be \( \sigma \) . Extend the geodesic \( {XP} \) an equal length \( \sigma \) beyond \( P \) , ending at a point \( Y \) . Draw minimal geodesics \( {Q}_{1}Y \) and \( {Q}_{2}Y \) . We claim

\[
\left| {{Q}_{1}Y}\right|  < \left| {{Q}_{1}X}\right| \text{ and }\left| {{Q}_{2}Y}\right|  < \left| {{Q}_{2}X}\right|
\]

which will show \( {Q}_{1}{Q}_{2} \) is not minimal, provided \( \sigma  \leq  s \) .

![019eb0e3-717c-7df6-9b24-435b86f7860f_83_347_490_955_256_0.jpg](images/019eb0e3-717c-7df6-9b24-435b86f7860f_83_347_490_955_256_0.jpg)

Since both halves of the argument are the same, we drop the subscripts 1 and 2.

Consider the geodesic triangle \( {QXY} \) with \( P \) the midpoint of \( {XY} \) , where \( {QX} \) and \( {QY} \) and \( {PX} \) are minimal and \( \angle {QXP} = \pi /2 \) .

![019eb0e3-717c-7df6-9b24-435b86f7860f_83_510_931_547_339_0.jpg](images/019eb0e3-717c-7df6-9b24-435b86f7860f_83_510_931_547_339_0.jpg)

Choose the point \( Z \) at distance \( r \) from \( P \) towards \( X \) , and draw minimal geodesics \( {QP} \) and \( {QZ} \) . Let \( \alpha  = \angle {QZX} \) and \( {\alpha }^{\prime } = \pi  - \alpha \) , while \( \gamma  = \angle {QPY} \) and \( {\gamma }^{\prime } = \pi  - \gamma \) . Again we make several applications of Toponogov's Theorems.

First note that

\[
\left| {QP}\right|  \geq  {\lambda s}\text{ and }\left| {PX}\right|  \leq  s
\]

so

\[
\left| {QZ}\right|  \geq  \left| {QP}\right|  - \left| {PZ}\right|  \geq  \left( {\lambda  - 1}\right) s
\]

and

\[
\left| {QX}\right|  \leq  \left| {QP}\right|  + \left| {PX}\right|  \leq  \left( {\lambda  + 1}\right) s.
\]

Therefore comparing the triangle \( {QZX} \) to the Euclidean one with the same three sides, we find by \( {T2} \) that for every \( \delta  > 0 \) there exists a \( \lambda  < \infty \) such that \( \alpha  \geq  \frac{\pi }{2} - \delta \) , as is easily seen by first comparing the Euclidean triangle to one of sides proportional to \( \lambda  + 1,\lambda  - 1 \) , and 1 with a more extreme angle \( \alpha \) , and observing \( \alpha  \rightarrow  \pi /2 \) as \( \lambda  \rightarrow  \infty \) . Consequently \( {\alpha }^{\prime } \leq  \frac{\pi }{2} + \delta \) .

Now choosing \( \delta \) small and \( \lambda \) large compared to \( \varepsilon \) , and noting that if \( K \geq  \varepsilon /{r}^{2} \) in \( {B}_{3r}\left( P\right) \) then

\[
{B}_{3r}\left( P\right)  \supseteq  {B}_{2r}\left( Z\right)
\]

we see that Lemma 1 implies \( \left| {QP}\right|  < \left| {QZ}\right| \) . Now if we also had \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \leq  \frac{\pi }{2} + \delta \) we would also have \( {QZ} < {QP} \) by Lemma 3, and we cannot have both. Hence \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \geq  \frac{\pi }{2} + \delta \) and this gives \( {\gamma }^{\prime } \leq  \frac{\pi }{2} - \delta \) .

Now we apply Toponogov’s Theorem 21.2 to the triangle \( {QPY} \) to compare it to the Euclidean triangle of sides \( \left| {QP}\right| \) and \( \left| {PY}\right| \) and angle \( \gamma \) . We do not know if \( {PY} \) is minimal, but \( {QP} \) and \( {QY} \) are by construction, and

\[
\left| {PY}\right|  = \sigma  \leq  s\text{ while }\left| {QP}\right|  \geq  {\lambda s}
\]

and hence \( \left| {PY}\right|  \leq  \left| {QP}\right|  + \left| {QY}\right| \) , which is all we need. Then by the law of cosines

\[
{\left| QY\right| }^{2} \leq  {\left| QP\right| }^{2} + {\left| PY\right| }^{2} - 2\left| {QP}\right|  \cdot  \left| {PY}\right|  \cdot  \cos \gamma .
\]

But we also have

\[
{\left| QP\right| }^{2} \leq  {\left| QX\right| }^{2} + {\left| PX\right| }^{2}
\]

by \( {T1} \) on the triangle of sides \( {QX} \) and \( {PX} \) and angle \( \pi /2 \) . Then

\[
{\left| QY\right| }^{2} \leq  {\left| QX\right| }^{2} + {\left| PX\right| }^{2} + {\left| PY\right| }^{2} - 2\left| {QP}\right|  \cdot  \left| {PY}\right|  \cdot  \cos \gamma .
\]

Use \( \left| {PX}\right|  = \left| {PY}\right|  = \sigma  \leq  s \) and \( \left| {QP}\right|  \geq  {\lambda s} \) and \( \gamma  \leq  \frac{\pi }{2} - \delta \) to get

\[
{\left| QY\right| }^{2} \leq  {\left| QX\right| }^{2} + 2{\sigma }^{2}\left\lbrack  {1 - \lambda \cos \left( {\frac{\pi }{2} - \delta }\right) }\right\rbrack  .
\]

Picking \( \lambda \) large compared to \( \delta \) , we get

\[
\lambda \cos \left( {\frac{\pi }{2} - \delta }\right)  = \lambda \sin \delta  > 1
\]

and \( \left| {QY}\right|  < \left| {QX}\right| \) as desired. This proves the theorem.

nodes.content:
THEOREM 21.6. For every \( \beta  > 0 \) there exists \( \lambda  < \infty \) such that in any complete manifold of positive curvature there are at most a finite number of disjoint balls which are \( \lambda \) -remote curvature \( \beta \) -bumps.

Proof. If the ball \( {B}_{r}\left( P\right) \) is a \( \lambda \) -remote curvature \( \beta \) -bump, and if \( Q \) is any point such that

\[
d\left( {0, Q}\right)  \geq  {2d}\left( {0, P}\right)
\]

then if we take minimal geodesics \( {0P} \) and \( {OQ} \) , we claim that for any \( \beta  > 0 \) we can find \( \lambda  < \infty \) and \( \theta  > 0 \) such that

\[
\angle {POQ} \geq  \theta \text{ . }
\]

To see this, let \( X \) be the point on \( {OQ} \) with \( {OX} = {OP} \) . Since \( K \geq  0 \) everywhere and \( {\Delta OPQ} \) has minimal sides, if the angle \( \angle {POQ} \) is \( < \theta \) , then for every \( \lambda  < \infty \) we can find \( \theta  > 0 \) such that \( {PX} < {OP}/\lambda \) . But this contradicts the repulsion theorem.

![019eb0e3-717c-7df6-9b24-435b86f7860f_85_529_380_546_359_0.jpg](images/019eb0e3-717c-7df6-9b24-435b86f7860f_85_529_380_546_359_0.jpg)

Note there is a curvature \( \beta \) -bump at \( P,{OP} > {\lambda PX} \) and

\[
{PQ} \geq  {OQ} - {OP} \geq  {OP}
\]

so the theorem applies (with \( \varepsilon  = \beta /9 \) to get \( K \geq  \varepsilon /{\rho }^{2} \) on the ball of radius \( \rho  = r/3) \) .

Now pick any sequence \( {P}_{j} \) of curvature \( \beta \) -bumps with

\[
d\left( {O,{P}_{j + 1}}\right)  \geq  {2d}\left( {O,{P}_{j}}\right)
\]

and we find for \( j < k \) the angle

\[
\angle {P}_{j}O{P}_{k} \geq  \theta
\]

for a fixed \( \theta  > 0 \) . This is impossible. Hence there cannot be an infinite sequence of \( \lambda \) -remote disjoint curvature \( \beta \) -bumps; for since \( K \) is bounded on any compact set and \( r \geq  \sqrt{\varepsilon /K} \) on each bump, we can only get a finite number of disjoint bumps into any compact set, and this lets us find \( {P}_{j + 1} \) with \( d\left( {{P}_{j + 1},0}\right)  \geq  {2d}\left( {{P}_{j},0}\right) \) . Thus the theorem is proved.

nodes.content:
THEOREM 22.1. Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci Flow on a compact manifold \( {M}^{m} \) of dimension \( m \) with weakly positive curvature operator for a maximal time interval \( 0 \leq  t < T \) . Then we can find a sequence of dilations which converge to a complete solution of the Ricci Flow with curvature bounded at each time on an ancient time interval \( - \infty  < t < \Omega \) with scalar curvature \( R \) bounded by

\[
R \leq  \Omega /\left( {\Omega  - t}\right)
\]

everywhere and \( R = 1 \) at some origin \( O \) at time \( t = 0 \) , which again has weakly positive curvature operator. Moreover the limit splits as a quotient of a product \( {N}^{n} \times  {R}^{k} \) with \( m = n + k \) flat in the directions \( {R}^{k} \) with \( k \geq  0 \) , and where the interesting factor \( {N}^{n} \) either is compact or has finite asymptotic curvature ratio

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}R{s}^{2} = A < \infty
\]

Moreover the limit factor \( {N}^{n} \) will still satisfy a local injectivity radius estimate.

Of course we conjecture the only possible limit is the round sphere \( {S}^{n} \) or a quotient of it shrinking to a point. In dimension 3 or 4 we have pinching estimates that keep the curvature operator strictly positive if it starts strictly positive, that prevent limits \( {N}^{n} \times  {R}^{k} \) with \( k > 0 \) . We do not know any examples of complete non compact ancient solutions of positive curvature operator with \( R{s}^{2} < \infty \) and \( R\left| t\right|  < \infty \) , and we conjecture none exist, since the curvature has had plenty of space and time to dissipate.

LEMMA 22.2. Given a complete noncompact solution to the Ricci Flow on an ancient time interval \( - \infty  < t < T \) with \( T > 0 \) with curvature bounded at each time and with asymptotic scalar curvature ratio

\[
A = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}R{s}^{2} = \infty
\]

we can find a sequence of points \( {P}_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \) at time \( t = 0 \) , a sequence of radii \( {r}_{j} \) and a sequence of numbers \( {\delta }_{j} \rightarrow  0 \) such that

(a) \( R\left( {P,0}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {\delta }_{j}}\right) R\left( {{P}_{j},0}\right) \) for all \( P \) in the ball \( {B}_{r}\left( {{P}_{j},0}\right) \)

of radius \( {r}_{j} \) around \( {P}_{j} \) at time \( t = 0 \)

(b) \( {r}_{j}^{2}R\left( {{P}_{j},0}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \)

(c) if \( {s}_{j} = d\left( {{P}_{j}, O,0}\right) \) is the distance of \( {P}_{j} \) from some origin \( O \) at time \( t = 0 \) , then \( {\lambda }_{j} = {s}_{j}/{r}_{j} \rightarrow  \infty \)

(d) the balls \( {\operatorname{Br}}_{j}\left( {{P}_{j},0}\right) \) are disjoint.
