This holds for \( n = 0 \) . We proceed by induction. Suppose the estimate above holds up to some \( n \) . Differentiating through the equation, we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\partial }_{v}f = P{\partial }_{v}f + L{\partial }_{v}g + \left( {{\partial }_{v}P}\right) f + \left( {{\partial }_{v}L}\right) g + {\partial }_{v}h,
\]

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\partial }_{v}g = M{\partial }_{v}f + N{\partial }_{v}g + \left( {{\partial }_{v}M}\right) f + \left( {{\partial }_{v}N}\right) g + {\partial }_{v}k.
\]

For simplicity we write

\[
{A}_{n} = {\left| f\right| }_{n + 2} + {\left| g\right| }_{n + 1}
\]

\[
{B}_{n} = {\left\lbrack  P\right\rbrack  }_{n} + {\left\lbrack  L\right\rbrack  }_{n} + {\left\lbrack  M\right\rbrack  }_{n + 1} + {\left\lbrack  N\right\rbrack  }_{n + 1},
\]

\[
{E}_{n} = {\left| h\right| }_{n} + {\left| k\right| }_{n + 1} + {\left| {f}_{0}\right| }_{n + 1} + {\left| {g}_{0}\right| }_{n + 1},
\]

in terms of which the induction hypothesis is \( {A}_{n} \leq  C\left( {{E}_{n} + {B}_{n}{E}_{0}}\right) \) , and \( {B}_{0} \leq  \delta \; \leq  C \) . Applying the induction hypothesis to the derived equation, we have

\[
{\left| {\partial }_{v}f\right| }_{n + 2} + {\left| {\partial }_{v}g\right| }_{n + 1} \leq  C\left( {{E}_{n + 1} + {B}_{1}{A}_{n} + {B}_{n + 1}{A}_{0}}\right) .
\]

Now \( {A}_{0} \leq  C{E}_{0} \) and \( {A}_{n} \leq  C\left( {{E}_{n} + {B}_{n}{E}_{0}}\right) \) . Moreover by interpolation we have

\[
{B}_{1}{B}_{n} \leq  C{B}_{0}{B}_{n + 1} \leq  C{B}_{n + 1}
\]

\[
{B}_{1}{E}_{n} \leq  C\left( {{B}_{0}{E}_{n + 1} + {B}_{n + 1}{E}_{0}}\right) ,
\]

and hence

\[
{A}_{n + 1} = {\left| f\right| }_{n + 3} + {\left| g\right| }_{n + 2} \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{v}{\left| {\partial }_{v}f\right| }_{n + 2} + {\left| {\partial }_{v}g\right| }_{n + 1} + {A}_{n}
\]

\[
\leq  C\left( {{E}_{n + 1} + {B}_{n + 1}{E}_{0}}\right) ,
\]

which completes the induction.

nodes.proof:
We must estimate the terms

\[
{\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j}f\right| }_{n - {2j} + 2} + {\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j}g\right| }_{n - {2j} + 1}
\]

for \( {2j} \leq  n \) . We can do this for \( j = 0 \) as before. We proceed by induction on \( j \) . Suppose we have estimates up to some value of \( j \) . Then for the \( j + 1 \) terms we have

\[
{\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j + 1}f\right| }_{n - {2j}} = {\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j}\left( Pf + Lg + h\right) \right| }_{n - {2j}},
\]

\[
{\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j + 1}g\right| }_{n - {2j} - 1} = {\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j}\left( Mf + Ng + k\right) \right| }_{n - {2j} - 1},
\]

and by interpolation we need only consider the extreme cases where all the derivatives in both space and time fall entirely on \( P, L, M, N \) or entirely on \( f, g, h, k \) .

For the first terms we get

\[
{\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j}f\right| }_{n - {2j} + 2} + {\left| \left\lbrack  P\right\rbrack  \right| }_{n}{\left| f\right| }_{2} + {\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j}g\right| }_{n - {2j} + 1} + {\left| \left\lbrack  L\right\rbrack  \right| }_{n}{\left| g\right| }_{1} + \parallel h{\parallel }_{n}
\]

and for the second terms we get

\[
{\left| {\left( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\right) }^{j}f\right| }_{n - {2j}} + {\left| \left\lbrack  M\right\rbrack  \right| }_{n - 1}{\left| f\right| }_{1} + {\left| {\left( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\right) }^{j}g\right| }_{n - {2j} - 1} + {\left| \left\lbrack  N\right\rbrack  \right| }_{n - 1}{\left| g\right| }_{0} + \parallel k{\parallel }_{n - 1},
\]

which is even better than we need. The above can be bounded by terms

\[
{\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j}f\right| }_{n - {2j} + 2} + {\left| {\left( \partial /\partial t\right) }^{j}g\right| }_{n - {2j} + 1} + \parallel h{\parallel }_{n} + \parallel k{\parallel }_{n + 1}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\left| \left\lbrack  P\right\rbrack  \right| }_{n} + {\left| \left\lbrack  L\right\rbrack  \right| }_{n} + {\left| \left\lbrack  M\right\rbrack  \right| }_{n + 1} + {\left| \left\lbrack  N\right\rbrack  \right| }_{n + 1}}\right) \left( {{\left| f\right| }_{2} + {\left| g\right| }_{1}}\right) .
\]

We apply the induction hypothesis to the first part and our previous estimate to \( {\left| f\right| }_{2} + {\left| g\right| }_{1} \) . This proves the lemma.

Recall we define

\[
\Delta {R}_{ijkl} = {g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{q}{R}_{ijkl}.
\]

Various second order derivatives of the curvature tensor are likely to differ by terms quadratic in the curvature tensor. To this end we introduce the tensors

\[
{B}_{ijkl} = {g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{piqj}{R}_{rksl}.
\]

Note we have the obvious symmetries

\[
{B}_{ijkl} = {B}_{jilk} = {B}_{klij}
\]

but the other symmetries of the curvature tensor \( {R}_{ijkl} \) may fail to hold for \( {B}_{ijkl} \) .

\[

\]

\[
- {g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi} + {R}_{ipkl}{R}_{qj} + {R}_{ijpl}{R}_{qk} + {R}_{ijkp}{R}_{ql}}\right) .
\]

Letting a prime denote differentiation with respect to time \( t \) , we see by considering the formulas for \( {\Gamma }_{jk}^{i} \) and \( {R}_{ijkl} \) in normal coordinates that for any evolution of a metric \( {g}_{ij} \) we have

\[
{\Gamma }_{jl}^{\prime h} = \frac{1}{2}{g}^{hm}\left( {{\partial }_{j}{g}_{lm}^{\prime } + {\partial }_{l}{g}_{jm}^{\prime } - {\partial }_{m}{g}_{jl}^{\prime }}\right) ,
\]

\[
{R}_{ijl}^{\prime h} = {\partial }_{i}{\Gamma }_{jl}^{\prime h} - {\partial }_{j}{\Gamma }_{il}^{\prime h},
\]

\[
{R}_{ijkl}^{\prime } = {g}_{hk}{R}_{ijl}^{h} + {g}_{hk}^{\prime }{R}_{ijl}^{h}.
\]

Combining these results and the identity

\[
{\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{j}{g}_{kl}^{\prime } - {\partial }_{j}{\partial }_{i}{g}_{kl}^{\prime } = {g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{ijkp}{g}_{ql}^{\prime } + {R}_{ijlp}{g}_{qk}^{\prime }}\right) ,
\]

we get the identity

\[
{R}_{ijkl}^{\prime } =  - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{k}{g}_{jl}^{\prime } - {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{l}{g}_{jk}^{\prime } - {\partial }_{j}{\partial }_{k}{g}_{il}^{\prime } + {\partial }_{j}{\partial }_{l}{g}_{ik}^{\prime }}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{2}{g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{ijkp}{g}_{ql}^{\prime } + {R}_{ijpl}{g}_{qk}^{\prime }}\right) ,
\]

which holds for any evolution of a metric. In our case \( {g}_{ij}^{\prime } =  - 2{R}_{ij} \) , and substituting this gives

\[
{R}_{ijkl}^{\prime } = {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{l}{R}_{jk} - {\partial }_{j}{\partial }_{k}{R}_{il} + {\partial }_{j}{\partial }_{l}{R}_{ik}
\]

\[
- {g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{ijkp}{R}_{ql} + {R}_{ijpl}{R}_{qk}}\right) .
\]

Then Theorem 7.1 is an immediate consequence of the following identity, which is independent of any evolution equation.

\[
\Delta {R}_{ijkl} + 2\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{iljk} + {B}_{ikjl}}\right)
\]

\[
= {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{l}{R}_{jk} - {\partial }_{j}{\partial }_{k}{R}_{il} + {\partial }_{j}{\partial }_{l}{R}_{ik}
\]

\[
+ {g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi} + {R}_{ipkl}{R}_{qj}}\right) .
\]

nodes.proof:
This formula is obtained from the second Bianchi identity

\[
{\partial }_{i}{R}_{jklm} + {\partial }_{j}{R}_{kilm} + {\partial }_{k}{R}_{ijlm} = 0
\]

by differentiating, exchanging derivatives, permuting indices and contracting. To begin we have

\[
\Delta {R}_{ijkl} = {g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{q}{R}_{ijkl} = {g}^{pq}\left( {{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} - {\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{j}{R}_{qikl}}\right)
\]

by differentiating the second Bianchi identity and contracting. We examine the first term, since the second is symmetric in \( i \) and \( j \) . Interchanging the order of derivatives we have

\[
{g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} - {g}^{pq}{\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{p}{R}_{qjkl}
\]

\[
= {g}^{pq}{g}^{mn}\left( {{R}_{piqm}{R}_{njkl} + {R}_{pijm}{R}_{qnkl} + {R}_{pikm}{R}_{qjnl} + {R}_{pilm}{R}_{qjkn}}\right) .
\]

The first of these terms contracts to \( {g}^{pq}{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi} \) . On the second term we can use the first Bianchi identity to write it in terms of the tensor \( {B}_{ijkl} \) ; thus

\[
{g}^{pq}{g}^{mn}{R}_{pijm}{R}_{qnkl} =  - {B}_{ijkl} + {B}_{ijlk},
\]

and the last two terms are \( - {B}_{ikjl} + {B}_{iljk} \) . Moreover we have the contracted second Bianchi identity

\[
{g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{R}_{qjkl} = {\partial }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\partial }_{l}{R}_{jk},
\]

to which we apply the derivative \( {\partial }_{i} \) . Then

\[
{g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{i}{R}_{qjkl} = {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{k}{R}_{jl} - {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{l}{R}_{jk}
\]

\[
- \left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk} - {B}_{iljk} + {B}_{ikjl}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {g}^{pq}{R}_{pjkl}{R}_{qi}.
\]

Replacing this in our formula for \( \Delta {R}_{ijkl} \) and doing the same for the term with \( i \) and \( j \) interchanged yields the formula in the lemma.

nodes.label: Corollary 7.3
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content:
7.3 Corollary. The Ricci curvature satisfies the evolution equation

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ik} = \Delta {R}_{ik} + 2{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{piqk}{R}_{rs} - 2{g}^{pq}{R}_{pi}{R}_{qk}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: 7.3 Corollary. The Ricci curvature satisfies the evolution equation \[ \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ik} = \Delta {R}_{ik} + 2{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{piqk}{R}_{rs} - 2{g}^{pq}{R}_{pi}{R}_{qk}. \]

nodes.proof:
Recall \( \Delta {R}_{ik} = {g}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}{\partial }_{q}{R}_{ik} \) . We use the relation \( {R}_{ik} = {g}^{jl}{R}_{ijkl} \) to contract the previous equation. Now

\[
{\left( {g}^{jl}\right) }^{\prime } =  - {g}^{jp}{g}^{lq}{g}_{pq}^{\prime }
\]

by the usual formula for the derivative of the inverse of a matrix, and therefore

\[
{R}_{ik}^{\prime } = {g}^{jl}{R}_{ijkl}^{\prime } + 2{g}^{jp}{g}^{lq}{R}_{ijkl}{R}_{pq}.
\]

Substituting for \( {R}_{ijkl}^{\prime } \) and making the obvious contractions yields

\[
{R}_{ik}^{\prime } = \Delta {R}_{ik} + 2{g}^{jl}\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - 2{B}_{ijlk}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{piqk}{R}_{rs} - 2{g}^{pq}{R}_{pi}{R}_{qk}.
\]

Then the corollary follows from the following lemma.

nodes.label: Lemma 7.4
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content:
7.4 Lemma. For any metric \( {g}_{ij} \) the tensor \( {B}_{ijkl} \) satisfies the identity

\[
{g}^{jl}\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - 2{B}_{ijlk}}\right)  = 0.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: 7.4 Lemma. For any metric \( {g}_{ij} \) the tensor \( {B}_{ijkl} \) satisfies the identity \[ {g}^{jl}\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - 2{B}_{ijlk}}\right) = 0. \]

nodes.proof:
Using the Bianchi identity

\[
{g}^{jl}{B}_{ijkl} = {g}^{jl}{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{piqj}{R}_{rksl}
\]

\[
= {g}^{jl}{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{pqij}{R}_{rskl}
\]

\[
= {g}^{jl}{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}\left( {{R}_{piqj} - {R}_{pjqi}}\right) \left( {{R}_{rksl} - {R}_{rlsk}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{g}^{jl}\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk}}\right)
\]

and the result follows.
nodes.proof_excerpt: Using the Bianchi identity \[ {g}^{jl}{B}_{ijkl} = {g}^{jl}{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{piqj}{R}_{rksl} \] \[ = {g}^{jl}{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{pqij}{R}_{rskl} \] \[ = {g}^{jl}{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}\left( {{R}_{piqj} - {R}_{pjqi}}\right) \left( {{R}_{rksl} - {R}_{rlsk}}\right) \] \[ = 2{g}^{jl}\left( {{B}_{ijkl} - {B}_{ijlk}}\right) \] and the result follows.

nodes.label: Corollary 7.5
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content:
7.5 Corollary. The scalar curvature \( R \) satisfies the evolution equation

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}R = {\Delta R} + 2{g}^{ij}{g}^{kl}{R}_{ik}{R}_{jl}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: 7.5 Corollary. The scalar curvature \( R \) satisfies the evolution equation \[ \frac{\partial }{\partial t}R = {\Delta R} + 2{g}^{ij}{g}^{kl}{R}_{ik}{R}_{jl}. \]

nodes.proof:
Again we contract the previous equation. Since \( R = {g}^{ik}{R}_{ik} \) we have

\[
{R}^{\prime } = {g}^{ik}{R}_{ik}^{\prime } + 2{g}^{ij}{g}^{kl}{R}_{ik}{R}_{jl},
\]

where the second term comes from \( {\left( {g}^{ik}\right) }^{\prime } \) . Then the equation for \( {R}_{ik}^{\prime } \) immediately gives \( {g}^{ik}{R}_{ik}^{\prime } = {\Delta R} \) .
nodes.proof_excerpt: Again we contract the previous equation. Since \( R = {g}^{ik}{R}_{ik} \) we have \[ {R}^{\prime } = {g}^{ik}{R}_{ik}^{\prime } + 2{g}^{ij}{g}^{kl}{R}_{ik}{R}_{jl}, \] where the second term comes from \( {\left( {g}^{ik}\right) }^{\prime } \) . Then the equation for \( {R}_{ik}^{\prime } \) immediately gives \( {g}^{ik}{R}_{ik}^{\prime } = {\Delta R} \) .

nodes.label: Corollary 7.6
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content: 7.6 Corollary. If the scalar curvature \( R > 0 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then it remains so.
nodes.content_excerpt: 7.6 Corollary. If the scalar curvature \( R > 0 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then it remains so.

nodes.proof: The term \( {g}^{ij}{g}^{kl}{R}_{ik}{R}_{jl} \) is just the norm squared of the Ricci curvature, and hence is always positive. The result now follows from the maximum principle for the heat equation. This simple example is a model for our subsequent a priori estimates. It also shows why the evolution equation "prefers" positive curvature.

The Weyl conformal curvature tensor is defined as

\[
{W}_{ijkl} = {R}_{ijkl} - \frac{1}{n - 2}\left( {{g}_{ik}{R}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{R}_{jk} - {g}_{jk}{R}_{il} + {g}_{jl}{R}_{ik}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) }R\left( {{g}_{ik}{g}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{g}_{jk}}\right) .
\]

nodes.label: Theorem 8.1
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content:
8.1 Theorem. In dimension three we have

\[
{R}_{ijkl} = {g}_{ik}{R}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{R}_{jk} - {g}_{jk}{R}_{il} + {g}_{jl}{R}_{ik} - \frac{1}{2}R\left( {{g}_{ik}{g}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{g}_{jk}}\right) .
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: 8.1 Theorem. In dimension three we have \[ {R}_{ijkl} = {g}_{ik}{R}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{R}_{jk} - {g}_{jk}{R}_{il} + {g}_{jl}{R}_{ik} - \frac{1}{2}R\left( {{g}_{ik}{g}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{g}_{jk}}\right) . \]

nodes.label: Corollary 8.2
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content: 8.2 Corollary. In dimension three a metric has positive sectional curvature if and only if \( {R}_{ij} < \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ij} \) . This shows that the condition of positive Ricci curvature is much weaker than that of positive sectional curvature.
nodes.content_excerpt: 8.2 Corollary. In dimension three a metric has positive sectional curvature if and only if \( {R}_{ij} < \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ij} \) . This shows that the condition of positive Ricci curvature is much weaker than that of positive sectional curvature.

nodes.label: Theorem 8.3
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content: 8.3 Theorem. The tensor \( {Q}_{ij} \) vanishes identically on any three dimensional symmetric Riemannian manifold. Any symmetric tensor \( {T}_{ij} \) which is quadratic in the Ricci curvature and has this property must be a scalar multiple of \( {Q}_{ij} \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: 8.3 Theorem. The tensor \( {Q}_{ij} \) vanishes identically on any three dimensional symmetric Riemannian manifold. Any symmetric tensor \( {T}_{ij} \) which is quadratic in the Ricci curvature and has this property must be a scalar multiple of \( {Q}_{ij} \) .

nodes.proof: The Ricci curvature on a three dimensional symmetric space either (a) has all its eigenvalues equal, as for \( {S}^{3} \) , or else (b) has two equal eigenvalues and the third is zero, as for \( {S}^{2} \times  {S}^{1} \) . In either case it is easy to check that \( {Q}_{ij} = 0 \) . Conversely any tensor of the given type which is quadratic in the Ricci tensor must be a linear combination of \( {S}_{ij}, S{g}_{ij}, R{R}_{ij} \) , and \( {R}^{2}{g}_{ij} \) . Then considering the cases (a) and (b) gives enough conditions to show the tensor is a multiple of \( {Q}_{ij} \) .

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ij} = \Delta {R}_{ij} - {Q}_{ij}.
\]

nodes.proof:
This follows directly from substituting the formula in Theorem 8.1 for the Riemannian curvature into the formula in Corollary 7.3 for the evolution of the Ricci curvature. The reader can check for himself that

\[
{g}^{pr}{g}^{qs}{R}_{piqk}{R}_{rs} = \frac{3}{2}R{R}_{ik} - 2{S}_{ik} + \left( {S - \frac{1}{2}{R}^{2}}\right) {g}_{ik},
\]

and since \( {g}^{pq}{R}_{pi}{R}_{qk} = {S}_{ik} \) the result holds.

nodes.label: Theorem 9.1
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content:
9.1 Theorem. Suppose that on \( 0 \leq  t \leq  T \)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{M}_{ij} = \Delta {M}_{ij} + {u}^{k}{\partial }_{k}{M}_{ij} + {N}_{ij},
\]

where \( {N}_{ij} = p\left( {{M}_{ij},{g}_{ij}}\right) \) satisfies the null-eigenvector condition above. If \( {M}_{ij} \geq  0 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then it remains so on \( 0 \leq  t \leq  T \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: 9.1 Theorem. Suppose that on \( 0 \leq t \leq T \) \[ \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{M}_{ij} = \Delta {M}_{ij} + {u}^{k}{\partial }_{k}{M}_{ij} + {N}_{ij}, \] where \( {N}_{ij} = p\left( {{M}_{ij},{g}_{ij}}\right) \) satisfies the null-eigenvector condition above. If \( {M}_{ij} \geq 0 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then it remains so on \( 0 \leq t \leq T \) .

nodes.proof:
We will show \( {M}_{ij} \geq  0 \) on \( 0 \leq  t \leq  \delta \) where \( \delta  > 0 \) is small compared to a constant \( C \) depending only on max \( \left| {M}_{ij}\right| \) . Then repeated application of this result will cover the entire interval in a finite number of steps. To this end, we let

\[
{\widetilde{M}}_{ij} = {M}_{ij} + \varepsilon \left( {\delta  + t}\right) {g}_{ij},
\]

and we claim \( {\widetilde{M}}_{ij} > 0 \) on \( 0 \leq  t \leq  \delta \) for every \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) . Then letting \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) will finish the proof.

If not, there will be a first time \( \theta \) with \( 0 < \theta  \leq  \delta \) where \( {\widetilde{M}}_{ij} \) acquires a null eigenvector \( {v}^{i} \) of unit length at some point \( x \in  X \) . If \( {\widetilde{N}}_{ij} = p\left( {{\widetilde{M}}_{ij},{g}_{ij}}\right) \) , then by our null-eigenvector condition \( {\widetilde{N}}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j} \geq  0 \) at \( \left( {x,\theta }\right) \) . Moreover

\[
\left| {{\widetilde{N}}_{ij} - {N}_{ij}}\right|  \leq  C\left| {{\widetilde{M}}_{ij} - {M}_{ij}}\right| ,
\]

where the constant \( C \) depends only on \( \max \left( {\left| {\widetilde{M}}_{ij}\right|  + \left| {M}_{ij}\right| }\right) \) since \( p \) is a polynomial. If we keep \( \varepsilon ,\delta  \leq  1 \) , then \( \max \left| {\widetilde{M}}_{ij}\right| \) depends only on \( \max \left| {M}_{ij}\right| \) . Therefore

\[
{N}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j} \geq   - {C\varepsilon \delta }
\]

where \( C \) depends only on \( \max \left| {M}_{ij}\right| \) and not on \( \varepsilon \) or \( \delta \) .

We can extend \( {v}^{i} \) to a vector field in a neighborhood of \( x \) with \( {\partial }_{j}{v}^{i} = 0 \) at \( x \) , with \( {v}^{i} \) independent of \( t \) . Let

\[
f = {\widetilde{M}}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j}.
\]

Then \( f \geq  0 \) on \( 0 \leq  t \leq  \theta \) and all of \( X \) , so \( \partial f/\partial t < 0 \) and \( {\partial }_{k}f = 0 \) and \( {\Delta f} \geq  0 \) at \( \left( {x,\theta }\right) \) , where \( f = 0 \) . But

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{M}_{ij}}\right) {v}^{i}{v}^{j} + \varepsilon ,
\]

and at \( \left( {x,\theta }\right) \) where \( {\partial }_{j}{v}^{i} = 0 \) and \( {\widetilde{M}}_{ij}{v}^{i} = 0 \) ,

\[
{\partial }_{k}f = {\partial }_{k}{M}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j},{\Delta f} = \Delta {M}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j}.
\]

From the evolution equation

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{M}_{ij}}\right) {v}^{i}{v}^{j} = \Delta {M}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j} + {u}^{k}{\partial }_{k}{M}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j} + {N}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j},
\]

which shows that \( {N}_{ij}{v}^{i}{v}^{j} \leq   - \varepsilon \) . Combining this with the previous estimate, we have \( \varepsilon  \leq  {C\delta \varepsilon } \) . This gives a contradiction when \( {C\delta } < 1 \) .

\]

nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content: 9.4 Theorem. If \( R \geq  0 \) and \( {R}_{ij} \geq  {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) for some constant \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then both conditions continue to hold on \( 0 \leq  t < T \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: 9.4 Theorem. If \( R \geq 0 \) and \( {R}_{ij} \geq {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) for some constant \( \varepsilon > 0 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then both conditions continue to hold on \( 0 \leq t < T \) .

nodes.proof:
We saw that \( R > 0 \) continues to hold in Corollary 7.6. We apply Theorem 9.1 with

\[
{M}_{ij} = \frac{{R}_{ij}}{R} - \varepsilon {g}_{ij},\;{u}^{k} = \frac{2}{R}{g}^{kl}{\partial }_{l}R,
\]

\[
{N}_{ij} = {2\varepsilon }{R}_{ij} - \left( \frac{R{Q}_{ij} + {2S}{R}_{ij}}{{R}^{2}}\right) .
\]

It is an immediate consequence of Lemma 9.3 that the equation in Theorem 9.1 is satisfied. Let us consider what happens to \( {N}_{ij} \) when \( {M}_{ij} \) acquires a null eigenvector. The analysis is easy since when \( {R}_{ij} \) is diagonal so are \( {M}_{ij} \) and \( {N}_{ij} \) . Suppose the null eigenvalue of \( {M}_{ij} \) occurs in the top position, corresponding to the eigenvalue \( \lambda \) of \( {R}_{ij} \) . Then \( \lambda  = \varepsilon \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \) . The corresponding entry in \( {R}^{2}{N}_{ij} \) is

\[
{2\varepsilon \lambda }{\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \right) }^{2} - \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \left( {2{\lambda }^{2} - {\mu }^{2} - {\mu }^{2} - {\lambda \mu } - {\lambda \nu } + {2\mu \nu }}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda }\left( {{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2}}\right)
\]

Using the previous identity to eliminate \( \varepsilon \) , and multiplying out and gathering terms, this entry becomes

\[
\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \left\lbrack  {\lambda \left( {\mu  + \nu }\right)  + {\left( \mu  - \nu \right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack   - {2\lambda }\left( {{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2}}\right) ,
\]

which further simplifies to

\[
{\lambda }^{2}\left( {\mu  + \nu  - {2\lambda }}\right)  + \left( {\mu  + \nu }\right) {\left( \mu  - \nu \right) }^{2}.
\]

Now if \( {R}_{ij} \geq  {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) then \( R \geq  {3\varepsilon R} \) , and if \( R > 0 \) then \( \varepsilon  \leq  \frac{1}{3} \) . But then \( \mu  + \nu  = \; \left( {1/\varepsilon  - 1}\right) \lambda  \geq  {2\lambda } \) , so \( \mu  + \nu  - {2\lambda } \geq  0 \) . Therefore at any null eigenvector of \( {M}_{ij} \) the matrix \( {N}_{ij} \) is positive. The theorem follows.

nodes.label: Theorem 9.6
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content: 9.6 Theorem. If \( {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \leq  {R}_{ij} \leq  {\beta R}{g}_{ij} \) for some constants \( \varepsilon \) and \( \beta \) with \( 0 < \varepsilon  \leq  \frac{1}{3} < \beta  < 1 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then both conditions continue to hold on \( 0 \leq  t < T \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: 9.6 Theorem. If \( {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \leq {R}_{ij} \leq {\beta R}{g}_{ij} \) for some constants \( \varepsilon \) and \( \beta \) with \( 0 < \varepsilon \leq \frac{1}{3} < \beta < 1 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then both conditions continue to hold on \( 0 \leq t < T \) .

nodes.proof:
Note that if \( \varepsilon  = \frac{1}{3} \) or \( \beta  = \frac{1}{3} \) then the manifold has constant curvature and the result is trivial, while \( \beta  = 1 \) always holds. We apply Theorem 9.1 with

\[
{M}_{ij} = \beta {g}_{ij} - \frac{{R}_{ij}}{R},\;{u}^{k} = \frac{2}{R}{g}^{kl}{\partial }_{l}R,
\]

\[
{N}_{ij} = \left( \frac{R{Q}_{ij} + {2S}{R}_{ij}}{{R}^{2}}\right)  - {2\beta }{R}_{ij}.
\]

It follows immediately from Lemma 9.3 that the equation in Theorem 9.1 is satisfied. Again we consider what happens to \( {N}_{ij} \) when \( {M}_{ij} \) acquires a null eigenvector in the top position where \( {R}_{ij} \) has eigenvalue \( \lambda \) . In this case \( \lambda  = \beta \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \) . The top entry in \( {R}^{2}{N}_{ij} \) is

\[
\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \left( {2{\lambda }^{2} - {\mu }^{2} - {\nu }^{2} - {\lambda \mu } - {\lambda \nu } + {2\mu \nu }}\right)
\]

\[
+ {2\lambda }\left( {{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2}}\right)  - {2\beta \lambda }{\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \right) }^{2}.
\]

Eliminating \( \beta \) with the above identity and gathering terms, this reduces to

\[
{\lambda }^{2}\left( {{2\lambda } - \mu  - \nu }\right)  - \left( {\mu  + \nu }\right) {\left( \mu  - \nu \right) }^{2}
\]

which we can rearrange as

\[
2{\lambda }^{2}\left( {\lambda  - \mu }\right)  + \left( {{\lambda }^{2} - {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2}}\right) \left( {\mu  - \nu }\right) ,
\]

which is clearly positive if \( \lambda  \geq  \mu  \geq  \nu  \geq  0 \) . To handle the possibility that \( \lambda \) is not the largest eigenvalue we use a continuity argument. Let \( \theta \) be the largest time on which \( {R}_{ij} \leq  \left( {\beta  + \delta }\right) R{g}_{ij} \) , where \( \delta \) will be chosen small compared to \( \beta \) and \( \varepsilon \) . If we can show \( {R}_{ij} \leq  {\beta R}{g}_{ij} \) up to time \( \theta \) , then we must have \( \theta  = T \) . Now since \( \lambda  = \beta \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \) and \( \beta  \geq  \frac{1}{3} \) we see \( \lambda \) cannot be the smallest eigenvalue. Assume \( \mu  \geq  \lambda  \geq  \nu \) . Up to time \( \theta \) we have \( \mu  \leq  \left( {\beta  + \delta }\right) \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \) , and by Theorem 9.4 we have \( \nu  \geq  \varepsilon \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \) . Since \( \mu  \geq  \lambda  = \beta \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \) and \( \nu  \leq  \frac{1}{3}\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \) we have \( \mu  - \nu  \geq  \left( {\beta  - \frac{1}{3}}\right) \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \) . If \( \beta  = \frac{1}{3} \) the manifold has constant curvature, and this case is easy to handle. Assume \( \beta  > \frac{1}{3} \) . The entry of \( {N}_{ij} \) in question by algebraic rearrangement becomes

\[
{\nu }^{2}\left( {\mu  - \nu }\right)  - \left( {\mu  - \lambda }\right) \left\lbrack  {2{\lambda }^{2} + \left( {\lambda  + \mu }\right) \left( {\mu  - \nu }\right) }\right\rbrack  ,
\]

which is at least

\[
{\varepsilon }^{2}\left( {\beta  - \frac{1}{3}}\right)  - \delta \left\lbrack  {2{\beta }^{2} + \left( {{2\beta } + \delta }\right) \left( {\beta  + \delta }\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

times \( {\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \right) }^{2} \) . This expression will be positive if \( \delta \) is small enough compared to \( \beta \) and \( \varepsilon \) . This completes the proof.

nodes.label: Theorem 10.1
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content:
10.1 Theorem. We can find a \( \delta  > 0 \) and a constant \( C < \infty \) depending only on the initial metric such that on \( 0 \leq  t < T \) we have

\[
S - \frac{1}{3}{R}^{2} \leq  C{R}^{2 - \delta }.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: 10.1 Theorem. We can find a \( \delta > 0 \) and a constant \( C < \infty \) depending only on the initial metric such that on \( 0 \leq t < T \) we have \[ S - \frac{1}{3}{R}^{2} \leq C{R}^{2 - \delta }. \]

nodes.proof:
Now we can finish the proof of Theorem 10.1. Let \( \delta  > 0 \) be as above and choose \( C \) so that

\[
\frac{S}{{R}^{\gamma }} - \frac{1}{3}{R}^{2 - \gamma } \leq  C
\]

at \( t = 0 \) . Then \( f \leq  C \) at \( t = 0 \) , and by the maximum principle we have \( f \leq  C \) on \( 0 \leq  t < T \) for the same \( C \) . Thus we have \( S - \frac{1}{3}{R}^{2} \leq  C{R}^{2 - \delta } \) as desired.

10.2 Lemma. The expression \( S \) satisfies the evolution equation

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}S = {\Delta S} - 2{\left| {\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk}\right| }^{2} + 4\left( {T - C}\right) .
\]

nodes.proof:
From the evolution equations for \( {g}_{ij} \) and \( {R}_{ij} \) we have

\[

\]

while we also have

\[
{\Delta S} = 2{g}^{ik}{g}^{jl}\Delta {R}_{ij} \cdot  {R}_{kl} + 2{\left| {\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk}\right| }^{2}.
\]

\]

\]

\[
- \frac{\left( {2 - \gamma }\right) \left( {\gamma  - 1}\right) }{{R}^{\gamma  + 2}}S{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2} + \frac{{4R}\left( {T - C}\right)  - {2\gamma }{S}^{2}}{{R}^{\gamma  + 1}}.
\]

We have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( \frac{S}{{R}^{\gamma }}\right)  = \frac{R\frac{\partial S}{\partial t} - {\gamma S}\frac{\partial R}{\partial t}}{{R}^{\gamma  + 1}},\;{\partial }_{j}\left( \frac{S}{{R}^{\gamma }}\right)  = \frac{R{\partial }_{j}S - {\gamma S}{\partial }_{j}R}{{R}^{\gamma  + 1}},
\]

\[
\Delta \left( \frac{S}{{R}^{\gamma }}\right)  = \frac{{R\Delta S} - {\gamma S\Delta R}}{{R}^{\gamma  + 1}} - \frac{2\gamma }{{R}^{\gamma  + 1}}{g}^{ij}{\partial }_{i}R \cdot  {\partial }_{j}S + \frac{\gamma \left( {\gamma  + 1}\right) }{{R}^{\gamma  + 2}}S{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2}.
\]

Introducing the obvious inner product of two tensors

\[
\left\langle  {{T}_{ijk},{U}_{ijk}}\right\rangle   = {g}^{il}{g}^{jm}{g}^{kn}{T}_{ijk}{U}_{lmn},
\]

we have

\[
\left\langle  {{\partial }_{i}R,{\partial }_{i}S}\right\rangle   = 2\left\langle  {{\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk},{\partial }_{i}R \cdot  {R}_{jk}}\right\rangle  ,
\]

\[
\left\langle  {{\partial }_{i}R,{\partial }_{i}\left( \frac{S}{{R}^{\gamma }}\right) }\right\rangle   = \frac{1}{{R}^{\gamma }}\left\langle  {{\partial }_{i}R,{\partial }_{i}S}\right\rangle   - \frac{\gamma }{{R}^{\gamma  + 1}}S{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2},
\]

and we also have

\[
S{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2} = {\left| {\partial }_{i}R \cdot  {R}_{jk}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Thus the terms in the evolution equation for \( S/{R}^{\gamma } \) which are quadratic in the first derivatives of the curvature are equal to \( 1/{R}^{\gamma  + 2} \) times

\[
- 2{R}^{2}{\left| {\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk}\right| }^{2} + {2\gamma R}\left\langle  {{\partial }_{i}R,{\partial }_{i}S}\right\rangle   - \gamma \left( {\gamma  + 1}\right) S{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
=  - 2{\left| R{\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk} - {\partial }_{i}R \cdot  {R}_{jk}\right| }^{2} + 2\left( {\gamma  - 1}\right) \left( {R\left\langle  {{\partial }_{i}R, S}\right\rangle   - {\gamma S}{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {\gamma  - 2}\right) \left( {\gamma  - 1}\right) S{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2},
\]

and now the result follows directly.

nodes.proof:
Using our formulas for \( R, S, T \) , and \( C \) (given just before Lemma 10.2) we can multiply out to get

\[
P = \left( {{\lambda }^{4} + {\mu }^{4} + {\nu }^{4}}\right)  - \left( {{\lambda }^{3}\mu  + \lambda {\mu }^{3} + {\lambda }^{3}\nu  + \lambda {\nu }^{3} + {\mu }^{3}\nu  + \mu {\nu }^{3}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\lambda }^{2}{\mu \nu } + \lambda {\mu }^{2}\nu  + {\lambda \mu }{\nu }^{2}}\right) \text{ . }
\]

And if we multiply out the polynomial above we get the same thing. Note that the polynomial \( P \) vanishes for any symmetric metric, since it vanishes when \( \lambda  = \mu  = \nu \) or when \( \lambda  = \mu \) and \( \nu  = 0 \) .

nodes.label: Lemma 10.7
nodes.document_title: Richard S. Hamilton - Three-Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature
nodes.content: 10.7 Lemma. If \( R > 0 \) and \( {R}_{ij} \geq  {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) then \( P \geq  {\varepsilon }^{2}S\left( {S - \frac{1}{3}{R}^{2}}\right) \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: 10.7 Lemma. If \( R > 0 \) and \( {R}_{ij} \geq {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) then \( P \geq {\varepsilon }^{2}S\left( {S - \frac{1}{3}{R}^{2}}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
Since both sides are homogeneous of degree 4 in \( \lambda ,\mu ,\nu \) , it suffices to check the result on \( S = {\lambda }^{2} + {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2} = 1 \) . Assume \( \lambda  \geq  \mu  \geq  \nu  > 0 \) . Since

\( {\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \right) }^{2} \geq  {\lambda }^{2} + {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2} = 1 \) , we have \( \nu  \geq  \varepsilon \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right)  \geq  \varepsilon \) by the bound \( {R}_{ij} \geq  {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) . Now we can rewrite \( P \) as

\[
P = {\left( \lambda  - \mu \right) }^{2}\left\lbrack  {{\lambda }^{2} + \left( {\lambda  + \mu }\right) \left( {\mu  - \nu }\right) }\right\rbrack   + {\nu }^{2}\left( {\lambda  - \nu }\right) \left( {\mu  - \nu }\right) ,
\]

which makes it clear that

\[
P \geq  {\lambda }^{2}{\left( \lambda  - \mu \right) }^{2} + {\nu }^{2}{\left( \mu  - \nu \right) }^{2},
\]

and since \( \lambda  \geq  \nu  \geq  \varepsilon \) we have

\[
P \geq  {\varepsilon }^{2}\left\lbrack  {{\left( \lambda  - \mu \right) }^{2} + {\left( \mu  - \nu \right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

On the other hand, since

\[
{\left( \lambda  - \nu \right) }^{2} = {\left\lbrack  \left( \lambda  - \mu \right)  + \left( \mu  - \nu \right) \right\rbrack  }^{2} \leq  2\left\lbrack  {{\left( \lambda  - \mu \right) }^{2} + {\left( \mu  - \nu \right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

we see that

\[
S - \frac{1}{3}{R}^{2} = \frac{1}{3}\left\lbrack  {{\left( \lambda  - \mu \right) }^{2} + {\left( \lambda  - \nu \right) }^{2} + {\left( \mu  - \nu \right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack   \leq  {\left( \lambda  - \mu \right) }^{2} + {\left( \mu  - \nu \right) }^{2},
\]

and this proves the lemma.

nodes.content: 11.6 Lemma. \( {\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{20}{7}{\left| {\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk}\right| }^{2} \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: 11.6 Lemma. \( {\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2} \leq \frac{20}{7}{\left| {\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk}\right| }^{2} \) .

nodes.proof:
This is a consequence of the contracted second Bianchi identity, which says,

\[
{g}^{ij}{\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk} = \frac{1}{2}{\partial }_{k}R
\]

It is always a good idea to try writing a tensor as a sum of irreducible components. Write

\[
{\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk} = {E}_{ijk} + {F}_{ijk},
\]

where

\[
{E}_{ijk} = \frac{1}{20}\left( {{g}_{ij}{\partial }_{k}R + {g}_{ik}{\partial }_{j}R}\right)  + \frac{3}{10}{g}_{jk}{\partial }_{i}R.
\]

Then it is easy to compute

\[
{\left| {E}_{ijk}\right| }^{2} = \frac{7}{20}{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2}.
\]

On the other hand, we can check that the tensor \( {F}_{ijk} = {\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk} - {E}_{ijk} \) is trace-free, so that

\[
{g}^{ij}{F}_{ijk} = 0,\;{g}^{ik}{F}_{ijk} = 0,\;{g}^{jk}{F}_{ijk} = 0.
\]

Indeed that was how we figured out what \( {E}_{ijk} \) should be. It follows that \( \left\langle  {{E}_{ijk},{F}_{ijk}}\right\rangle   = 0 \) and the tensors \( {E}_{ijk} \) and \( {F}_{ijk} \) are perpendicular. Then

\[
{\left| {\partial }_{i}{R}_{jk}\right| }^{2} = {\left| {E}_{ijk}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {F}_{ijk}\right| }^{2} \geq  \frac{7}{20}{\left| {\partial }_{i}R\right| }^{2},
\]

and this proves the lemma.

nodes.content: 11.11 Lemma. If \( R \geq  {\rho att} = 0 \) for some constant \( \rho  > 0 \) then \( T \leq  3/\left( {2\rho }\right) \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: 11.11 Lemma. If \( R \geq {\rho att} = 0 \) for some constant \( \rho > 0 \) then \( T \leq 3/\left( {2\rho }\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
The solution of the ordinary differential equation

\[
\frac{df}{dt} = \frac{2}{3}{f}^{2}\;\text{ with }f = \rho \text{ at }t = 0
\]

is given by

\[
f = \frac{3\rho }{3 - {2\rho t}}.
\]

Taking \( f \) as a function on \( X \times  t \) constant in \( X \) we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {R - f}\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {R - f}\right)  + \frac{2}{3}\left( {R + f}\right) \left( {R - f}\right) ,
\]

and the maximum principle implies \( R - f \geq  0 \) on \( 0 \leq  t < T \) . Since \( f \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( t \rightarrow  3/\rho \) , we must have \( T \leq  3/\rho \) .

nodes.content:
## 12. Interpolation inequalities for tensors

Let \( T = \left\{  {T}_{j\cdots k}\right\} \) denote a tensor covariant in any number of indices. We adopt the extended summation convention that if a pair of indices is repeated on the bottom, we should sum over that index in an orthonormal basis with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij} \) . We let \( \partial T = \left\{  {{\partial }_{i}{T}_{j\cdots k}}\right\} \) be the covariant derivative with respect to the Levi-Civita connection \( {\Gamma }_{ij}^{p} \) associated to \( {g}_{ij} \) , and we let \( {\partial }^{2}T = {\partial }_{h}{\partial }_{i}{T}_{j\cdots k} \) be the second (iterated) covariant derivative. We also let \( {d\mu } = \mu \left( x\right) {dx} \) be the volume form associated to the metric. The tensor \( T = {T}_{j\cdots k} \) has length \( \left| T\right| \) given by

12.1 Theorem. Let \( X \) be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension \( m \) and let \( T = {T}_{j\cdots k} \) be any tensor on \( X \) . Suppose

\[
\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = \frac{1}{r}\;\text{ with }r \geq  1.
\]

Then

\[
{\left\{  \int {\left| \partial T\right| }^{2r}d\mu \right\}  }^{1/r} \leq  \left( {{2r} - 2 + m}\right) {\left\{  \int {\left| {\partial }^{2}T\right| }^{p}d\mu \right\}  }^{1/p}{\left\{  \int {\left| T\right| }^{q}d\mu \right\}  }^{1/q}.
\]

nodes.proof:
For simplicity we take \( T = \left\{  {T}_{j}\right\} \) , since the more general case involves nothing extra but is more cumbersome to write. Integrating by parts

\[
\int {\left| \partial T\right| }^{2r}{d\mu } = \int {\partial }_{i}{T}_{j} \cdot  {\partial }_{i}{T}_{j} \cdot  {\left( {\partial }_{k}{T}_{l} \cdot  {\partial }_{k}{T}_{l}\right) }^{r - 1}{d\mu }
\]

\[
=  - \int {T}_{j} \cdot  {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{i}{T}_{j} \cdot  {\left| \partial T\right| }^{{2r} - 2}{d\mu }
\]

\[
- 2\left( {r - 1}\right) \int \left\langle  {{T}_{j}{\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{k}{T}_{l},{\partial }_{i}{T}_{j} \cdot  {\partial }_{k}{T}_{l}}\right\rangle  {\left| \partial T\right| }^{{2r} - 4}{d\mu }.
\]

Now

\[
\left| {{T}_{j} \cdot  {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{i}{T}_{j}}\right|  \leq  m\left| T\right| \left| {{\partial }^{2}T}\right|
\]

\[
\left\langle  {{T}_{j}{\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{k}{T}_{l},{\partial }_{i}{T}_{j} \cdot  {\partial }_{k}{T}_{l}}\right\rangle   \leq  \left| T\right| \left| {{\partial }^{2}T}\right| {\left| \partial T\right| }^{2},
\]

and therefore

\[
\int {\left| \partial T\right| }^{2r}{d\mu } \leq  \left( {{2r} - 2 + m}\right) \int \left| T\right| \left| {{\partial }^{2}T}\right| {\left| \partial T\right| }^{{2r} - 2}{d\mu }.
\]

We can estimate the last integral using Hölder's inequality with

\[
\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} + \frac{r - 1}{r} = 1
\]

and we get

\[
\int {\left| \partial T\right| }^{2r}{d\mu }
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{2r} - 2 + m}\right) {\left\{  \int {\left| {\partial }^{2}T\right| }^{p}d\mu \right\}  }^{1/p}{\left\{  \int {\left| T\right| }^{q}d\mu \right\}  }^{1/q}{\left\{  \int {\left| \partial T\right| }^{2r}d\mu \right\}  }^{1 - 1/r},
\]

and hence

\[
{\left\{  \int {\left| \partial T\right| }^{2r}d\mu \right\}  }^{1/r} \leq  \left( {{2r} - 2 + m}\right) {\left\{  \int {\left| {\partial }^{2}T\right| }^{p}d\mu \right\}  }^{1/p}{\left\{  \int {\left| T\right| }^{q}d\mu \right\}  }^{1/q}.
\]

12.3 Lemma. Let \( f\left( k\right) \) be a real valued function of the integer \( k \) for \( 0 \leq  k \leq  n \) . If

\[
f\left( k\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}\left\lbrack  {f\left( {k - 1}\right)  + f\left( {k + 1}\right) }\right\rbrack  ,
\]

then

\[
f\left( k\right)  \leq  \left( {1 - \frac{k}{n}}\right) f\left( 0\right)  + \frac{k}{n}f\left( n\right) .
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: 12.3 Lemma. Let \( f\left( k\right) \) be a real valued function of the integer \( k \) for \( 0 \leq k \leq n \) . If \[ f\left( k\right) \leq \frac{1}{2}\left\lbrack {f\left( {k - 1}\right) + f\left( {k + 1}\right) }\right\rbrack , \] then \[ f\left( k\right) \leq \left( {1 - \frac{k}{n}}\right) f\left( 0\right) + \frac{k}{n}f\left( n\right) . \]

nodes.proof:
If we replace \( f\left( k\right) \) by

\[
\widetilde{f}\left( k\right)  = f\left( k\right)  - \left( {1 - \frac{k}{n}}\right) f\left( 0\right)  - \frac{k}{n}f\left( n\right) ,
\]

the same hypothesis holds. Thus we may assume \( f\left( 0\right)  = 0 \) and \( f\left( n\right)  = 0 \) . Let \( g\left( k\right)  = f\left( k\right)  - f\left( {k - 1}\right) \) for \( 1 \leq  k \leq  n \) . Then our hypothesis states that \( g\left( k\right)  \leq \; g\left( {k + 1}\right) \) . Choose the integer \( m \) so that

\[
g\left( 1\right)  \leq  \cdots  \leq  g\left( m\right)  \leq  0 \leq  g\left( {m + 1}\right)  \leq  \cdots g\left( n\right) .
\]

For any \( k \)

\[
f\left( k\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{k}g\left( i\right)  =  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = k + 1}}^{n}g\left( i\right) .
\]

When \( k \leq  m \) the first representation is negative, and when \( k \geq  m \) the second is. This proves \( f\left( k\right)  \leq  0 \) for \( 0 \leq  k \leq  n \) , which is the desired conclusion for \( f\left( 0\right)  = 0 \) and \( f\left( n\right)  = 0 \) .

## 13. Higher derivatives of the curvature

If \( A \) and \( B \) are two tensors we write \( A * B \) for any linear combination of tensors formed by contraction on \( {A}_{i\cdots j}{B}_{k\cdots l} \) using the \( {g}^{ik} \) . To avoid confusion between the Riemannian, Ricci and scalar curvatures we let

\[
{Rm} = \left\{  {R}_{ijkl}\right\}  \;\text{ and }{Rc} = \left\{  {R}_{ij}\right\}  .
\]

As before \( {\partial }^{n}T \) is the \( n \) th iterated covariant derivative of a tensor \( T \) .

We want to derive the evolution equation for the \( n \) th covariant derivative \( {\partial }^{n}{Rm} \) of the Riemannian curvature. To that end the following lemma is useful.

13.1 Lemma. If \( A \) and \( B \) are tensors satisfying the evolution equation

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}A = {\Delta A} + B,
\]

then the covariant derivative \( \partial A \) satisfies an equation of the form

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\partial A = \Delta \partial A + {Rm} * \partial A + A * \partial {Rm} + \partial B.
\]

(In dimension 3 we may substitute Rc.)

The covariant derivative \( \partial \) involves the Christöffel symbols \( {\Gamma }_{jk}^{i} \) , and their time derivative is

\]

which may be expressed in terms of \( \partial {Rc} \) since \( {g}_{ij}^{\prime } =  - 2{R}_{ij} \) . Then

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\partial A = \partial \frac{\partial A}{\partial t} + \partial {Rm} * A.
\]

Now by interchanging derivatives

\[
\partial {\Delta A} = \Delta \partial A + \partial {Rm} * A + {Rm} * \partial A,
\]

and this completes the proof.

\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{R}_{ij}

We could then use the short time existence result to continue the solution past \( T \) , showing \( T \) is not maximal.

\frac{d}{dt}{\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2} = {g}_{ij}^{\prime }{v}^{i}{v}^{j}

Then for \( 0 \leq  \tau  \leq  \theta  < T \) we have

\]

If the improper integral is finite, we see that all the metrics are equivalent. Moreover \( {\left| {v}_{t}\right| }^{2} \) converges uniformly to a continuous function \( {\left| v\right| }_{T}^{2} \) as \( t \rightarrow  T \) and \( {\left| v\right| }_{T} \neq  0 \) if \( v \neq  0 \) . \]

continues to hold in the limit, the limiting norm comes from an inner product \( {g}_{ij}\left( T\right) \) , using the rule

\[
g\left( {v, w}\right)  = \frac{1}{4}\left( {{\left| v + w\right| }^{2} - {\left| v - w\right| }^{2}}\right) .
\]

This completes the proof.

Choose a function \( f\left( t\right) \) equal to \( {R}_{\max } \) at \( t = 0 \) and solving the ordinary differential equation

\[
\frac{df}{dt} = 2{R}_{\max }f
\]

which is possible since \( {R}_{\max } \) is a continuous function of \( t \) . Since \( S \leq  {R}^{2} \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {R - f}\right)  \leq  \Delta \left( {R - f}\right)  + 2{R}_{\max }\left( {R - f}\right) ,
\]

and hence \( R \leq  f \) on \( 0 \leq  t < T \) by the maximum principle. Since \( {R}_{\max } \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( t \rightarrow  T \) , we have \( f \rightarrow  \infty \) also. But

\[
\log f\left( t\right) /f\left( 0\right)  = 2{\int }_{0}^{t}{R}_{\max }\left( \theta \right) {d\theta },
\]

and hence the integral diverges as \( t \rightarrow  T \) .

## 17. Exponential convergence

We start with a principle for converting from the unnormalized to the normalized evolution equation. Let \( P \) and \( Q \) be two expressions formed from the metric and curvature tensors, and let \( \widetilde{P} \) and \( \widetilde{Q} \) be the corresponding expressions for the normalized equation. Since they differ by dilations, they differ by a power of \( \psi \) . We say \( P \) has degree \( n \) if \( \widetilde{P} = {\psi }^{n}P \) . Thus \( {g}_{ij} \) has degree \( 1,{R}_{ij} \) has degree \( 0, R \) has degree -1, and \( S \) has degree -2 .

17.1 Lemma. Suppose \( P \) satisfies

\[
\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} = {\Delta P} + Q
\]

for the unnormalized equation, and \( P \) has degree \( n \) . Then \( Q \) has degree \( n - 1 \) , and for the normalized equation

\[
\frac{\partial \widetilde{P}}{\partial \widetilde{t}} = \widetilde{\Delta }\widetilde{P} + \widetilde{Q} + \frac{2}{3}n\widetilde{r}\widetilde{P}.
\]

\[

\]

But from \( §3 \) we know \( d\log \psi /{dt} = \frac{2}{3}r \) , so \( d\log \psi /d\widetilde{t} = \frac{2}{3}\widetilde{r} \) . This prove the lemma.

We let \( \widetilde{f} = \widetilde{S}/{\widetilde{R}}^{2} - \frac{1}{3} \) . Note \( \widetilde{f} \) has degree 0 . Then by Lemma 10.5 with \( \gamma  = 2 \) we have

\[

\]

\[
\widetilde{P} \geq  {\varepsilon }^{2}\widetilde{S}\left( {\widetilde{S} - \frac{1}{3}{\widetilde{R}}^{2}}\right) .

This makes

\[
\frac{\partial \widetilde{f}}{\partial \widetilde{t}} \leq  \Delta \widetilde{f} + {\widetilde{u}}^{k}{\partial }_{k}\widetilde{f} - \delta \widetilde{f}
\]

with \( {\widetilde{u}}^{q} = 2{\widetilde{g}}^{pq}{\partial }_{p}\widetilde{R}/\widetilde{R} \) and \( \delta  = 4{\varepsilon }^{2}/{3C} \) since

\[
4\widetilde{P}/{\widetilde{R}}^{3} \geq  4{\varepsilon }^{2}\widetilde{S}\widetilde{f}/{\widetilde{R}}^{3} \geq  4{\varepsilon }^{2}\widetilde{f}/3\widetilde{R} \geq  \delta \widetilde{f}
\]

with \( \widetilde{S} \geq  \frac{1}{3}{\widetilde{R}}^{2} \) and \( \widetilde{R} \leq  C \) . But then

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \widetilde{t}}\left( {{e}^{\delta \widetilde{t}}\widetilde{f}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{\Delta }\left( {{e}^{\delta \widetilde{t}}\widetilde{f}}\right)  + {\widetilde{u}}^{k}{\partial }_{k}\left( {{e}^{\delta \widetilde{t}}\widetilde{f}}\right) ,
\]

and by the maximum principle \( {e}^{\delta t}\widetilde{f} \leq  C \) . Thus \( \widetilde{f} \leq  C{e}^{-{\delta t}} \) . Since \( \widetilde{R} \) is bounded above and below, this is equivalent to the theorem.

nodes.section_title: 10.1. Weak maximum principles for scalars and symmetric 2-tensors
nodes.content:
1.1. Scalar maximum principle. Let \( {\mathcal{M}}^{n} \) be a closed manifold and let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a family of metrics on \( \mathcal{M} \) . The Laplacian is defined by \( {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) } \Doteq  g{\left( t\right) }^{ij}\nabla {\left( t\right) }_{i}\nabla {\left( t\right) }_{j} \) , where \( \nabla \left( t\right) \) denotes the covariant derivative associated to \( g\left( t\right) \) . Given a \( {C}^{\infty } \) function \( u : \mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) , we define the semilinear second-order parabolic operator:

(10.1)

\[
{Lu} \Doteq  \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }u - \langle X\left( t\right) ,\nabla u\rangle  - F\left( {u, t}\right) ,
\]

where \( X\left( t\right) \) is a time-dependent vector field and the function \( F : \mathbb{R} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow \; \mathbb{R} \) is locally Lipschitz in the \( \mathbb{R} \) factor and continuous in the \( \lbrack 0, T) \) factor. The essence of the scalar maximum principle is contained in the following comparison result.

THEOREM 10.1 (Comparison principle). Suppose that \( u \) and \( v \) satisfy \( {Lu} \leq  {Lv} \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) and \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  v\left( {x,0}\right) \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Then

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  v\left( {x, t}\right) \;\text{ on }\mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T).
\]

EXERCISE 10.5 (A common ODE). Suppose a continuous function \( x\left( t\right)  \geq \) 0 satisfies the ordinary differential inequality

\[
\frac{dx}{dt} \leq   - {C}_{1}{x}^{1 + \alpha }
\]

on \( \lbrack 0, T) \) whenever \( x \geq  {C}_{2} \) , where \( {C}_{1} > 0 \) and \( \alpha  > 0 \) . Show that

\[
x\left( t\right)  \leq  \max \left\{  {{\left( {C}_{1}\alpha t\right) }^{-1/\alpha },{C}_{2}}\right\}   = \left\{  \begin{matrix} {\left( {C}_{1}\alpha t\right) }^{-1/\alpha } & \text{ if }t < \frac{{C}_{2}^{-\alpha }}{{C}_{1}\alpha }, \\  {C}_{2} & \text{ if }t \geq  \frac{{C}_{2}^{-\alpha }}{{C}_{1}\alpha }. \end{matrix}\right.
\]

nodes.proof:
We compute

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {x}^{-\alpha }\right)  =  - \alpha {x}^{-1 - \alpha }\frac{dx}{dt} \geq  {C}_{1}\alpha
\]

whenever \( {x}^{-\alpha } \leq  {C}_{2}^{-\alpha } \) . Hence

\[
x{\left( t\right) }^{-\alpha } \geq  \min \left\{  {{C}_{1}{\alpha t},{C}_{2}^{-\alpha }}\right\}  .
\]

nodes.content:
THEOREM 10.7 (Maximum principle for 2-tensors). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in \; \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a closed manifold with a family of Riemannian metrics smoothly depending on time and let \( \alpha \left( t\right)  \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( {T{\mathcal{M}}^{ * }{ \otimes  }_{S}T{\mathcal{M}}^{ * }}\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a symmetric 2-tensor satisfying

(10.16)

\[
\frac{\partial \alpha }{\partial t} \geq  {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }\alpha  + \langle X\left( t\right) ,\nabla \alpha \rangle  + \beta ,
\]

where \( X\left( t\right) \) is a time-dependent vector field and \( \beta  = \beta \left( {\alpha , t}\right) \) is a symmetric 2-tensor, which is a locally Lipschitz function of \( \alpha \) and is continuous in \( t \) . Suppose that \( \beta \) satisfies the null-eigenvector assumption. If \( \alpha \left( 0\right)  \geq  0 \) , then \( \alpha \left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

nodes.content: REMARK 10.8. Böhm and Wilking [44] proved that, in general, neither the condition of nonnegative Ricci curvature nor the condition of nonnegative sectional curvature is preserved under the Ricci flow on closed manifolds (see Theorem 13.17 in this book for a statement of their result). Earlier it was shown that there exist complete solutions to the Ricci flow on noncom-pact manifolds which neither preserve nonnegative sectional curvature [309] nor nonnegative Ricci curvature [379].

nodes.content:
EXERCISE 10.9 (Curvature pinching estimates). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in \; \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on a closed 3-manifold.

(1) Prove that for any \( \varepsilon  \leq  1/3 \) , the inequality \( {R}_{ij} \geq  {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) is preserved.

(2) Prove that the inequality \( {R}_{ij} \leq  \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ij} \) is preserved.
nodes.content_excerpt: EXERCISE 10.9 (Curvature pinching estimates). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in \; \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on a closed 3-manifold. (1) Prove that for any \( \varepsilon \leq 1/3 \) , the inequality \( {R}_{ij} \geq {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) is preserved. (2) Prove that the inequality \( {R}_{ij} \leq \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ij} \) is preserved.

nodes.proof:
(1) If \( \varepsilon  = 1/3 \) , then \( g\left( 0\right) \) is an Einstein metric (in fact, \( g\left( 0\right) \) has constant sectional curvature) and \( g\left( t\right) \) remains Einstein under the Ricci flow. Now assume \( \varepsilon  < 1/3 \) ; then the assumption \( {R}_{ij} \geq  {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) at \( t = 0 \) implies that \( R \geq  0 \) at \( t = 0 \) (since then \( \left( {1 - {3\varepsilon }}\right) R \geq  0 \) ), and hence \( R \geq  0 \) for \( t \geq  0 \) . We compute from the evolution equation for \( {\alpha }_{ij} = {R}_{ij} - {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij} \) that

\[
{\beta }_{ij} = {3R}\left( {{R}_{ij} - {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij}}\right)  - 6{g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{ip} - {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ip}}\right) \left( {{R}_{qj} - {\varepsilon R}{g}_{qj}}\right)
\]

\[
- {10\varepsilon R}\left( {{R}_{ij} - {\varepsilon R}{g}_{ij}}\right)  + \left( {2\left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) {\left| \operatorname{Rc}\right| }^{2} - \left( {1 - {3\varepsilon } + 4{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) {R}^{2}}\right) {g}_{ij}.
\]

---

\( {}^{3} \) In Lemma 6.28 on p. 189 of Volume One, a proof of the qualitatively equivalent estimate

\[
\lambda \left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right)  \leq  C\left( {\nu \left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right)  + \mu \left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) }\right)
\]

is given using the maximum principle for systems instead of the maximum principle for 2-tensors (following [245]). Here \( \lambda \left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right)  \geq  \mu \left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right)  \geq  \nu \left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) \) denote the eigenvalues of \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \) and \( C < \infty \) is a constant.

---

If at some point \( {\alpha }_{ij}{V}^{j} = 0 \) for some \( V \) with \( \left| V\right|  = 1 \) , then at that point the eigenvalues of Rc are \( {\varepsilon R},{\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2} \) , where \( {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} = \left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) R \) . Hence

\[
{\beta }_{ij}{V}^{i}{V}^{j} = 2\left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) {\left| \mathrm{{Rc}}\right| }^{2} - \left( {1 - {3\varepsilon } + 4{\varepsilon }^{2}}\right) {R}^{2}
\]

\[
= 2\left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{1}^{2} + {\lambda }_{2}^{2}}\right)  - \left( {1 - {3\varepsilon } + 2{\varepsilon }^{2} + 2{\varepsilon }^{3}}\right) {R}^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {{\left( 1 - \varepsilon \right) }^{3} - \left( {1 - {3\varepsilon } + 2{\varepsilon }^{2} + 2{\varepsilon }^{3}}\right) }\right) {R}^{2}
\]

\[
= {\varepsilon }^{2}\left( {1 - {3\varepsilon }}\right) {R}^{2} \geq  0
\]

since \( \varepsilon  < 1/3 \) . Thus \( {\beta }_{ij} \) satisfies the null-eigenvector assumption.

(2) Let \( {\alpha }_{ij} = \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ij} - {R}_{ij} \) . Then

\[
{\beta }_{ij} =  - {3R}\left( {{R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ij}}\right)  + 6{g}^{pq}\left( {{R}_{ip} - \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ip}}\right) \left( {{R}_{qj} - \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{qj}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {5R}\left( {{R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ij}}\right)  - \left( {{\left| \mathrm{{Rc}}\right| }^{2} - \frac{1}{2}{R}^{2}}\right) {g}_{ij}.
\]

If at some point \( {\alpha }_{ij} \geq  0 \) and \( {\alpha }_{ij}{V}^{j} = 0 \) for some \( V \) with \( \left| V\right|  = 1 \) , then at that point the eigenvalues of Rc are \( \frac{1}{2}R,{\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2} \) , where \( {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} = \frac{1}{2}R \) . Hence

\[
{\beta }_{ij}{V}^{i}{V}^{j} =  - \left( {{\left| \mathrm{{Rc}}\right| }^{2} - \frac{1}{2}{R}^{2}}\right)  = 2{\lambda }_{1}{\lambda }_{2}.
\]

Since \( {\lambda }_{a} \leq  \frac{1}{2}R = {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} \) for \( a = 1,2 \) , we have \( {\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2} \geq  0 \) , so that \( {\beta }_{ij}{V}^{i}{V}^{j} \geq  0 \) and the null-eigenvector assumption holds.

nodes.content:
THEOREM 10.13 (Weinberger-Hamilton maximum principle for systems). Let \( \mathcal{K} \subset  \mathcal{V} \) be a closed subset which is invariant under parallel translation with respect to \( \nabla \left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , and convex in the fibers, i.e., \( {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) is convex for each \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Assume \( F\left( {u, t}\right) \) is continuous in \( \left( {u, t}\right) \) and is locally Lipschitz in \( u \) . Suppose that \( \mathcal{K} \) has the property that for any \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) and \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) , the solution \( U\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{T}^{\prime }}\right) \) , to the ODE (10.25),

\[
\frac{dU}{dt} = {F}_{x}\left( {U, t}\right) ,
\]

remains in \( {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) , where \( {T}^{\prime } \) is the maximal time for which the solution exists. \( {}^{5} \) Then any solution \( u\left( {x, t}\right) \) , defined for \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , to the PDE (10.24),

\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = {\Delta u} + {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }u + F\left( {u, t}\right) ,
\]

which starts in \( \mathcal{K} \) at \( t = 0 \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) ) also stays in \( \mathcal{K} \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) for all \( x \) and \( t \) ).

---

\( {}^{5}{T}^{\prime } \) may be strictly less than \( T \) .

---

nodes.content:
THEOREM 10.14 (Rm \( \geq  0 \) is preserved).

(I) If \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq  0 \) at \( t = 0 \) , then \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq  0 \) for \( t > 0 \) .

(II) If at \( t = 0 \) we have \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq  0 \) everywhere and \( \mathrm{{Rm}} > 0 \) at some point, then for \( t > 0 \) we have \( \mathrm{{Rm}} > 0 \) everywhere.

Recall the ODE associated to the PDE for \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \) is (10.31): \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbb{M} = {\mathbb{M}}^{2} + {\mathbb{M}}^{\# } \) , where \( {\mathbb{M}}_{\alpha \beta }^{\# } \Doteq  {C}_{\alpha }^{\gamma \delta }{C}_{\beta }^{\varepsilon \zeta }{\mathbb{M}}_{\gamma \varepsilon }{\mathbb{M}}_{\delta \zeta } \) . Let \( {\left\{  {\varphi }^{\alpha }\right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1}^{n\left( {n - 1}\right) /2} \) be a basis of eigenvectors of \( \mathbb{M} \) . Given any \( U = {U}^{\alpha }{\varphi }_{\alpha }^{ * } \in  {\Lambda }^{2}{T}_{x}^{ * }{\mathcal{M}}^{n} \) , we have

(10.39)

\[
{\mathbb{M}}^{\# }\left( {U, U}\right)  = {\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{\alpha }{U}^{\alpha }{C}_{\alpha }^{\gamma \delta }\right) }^{2}{\mathbb{M}}_{\gamma \gamma }{\mathbb{M}}_{\delta \delta }
\]

Hence, if \( \mathbb{M} \geq  0 \) , then \( {\mathbb{M}}^{\# } \geq  0 \) . On the other hand, for any \( \mathbb{M} \) we have \( {\mathbb{M}}^{2} \geq  0 \) . Therefore, by Proposition 10.54, if \( \mathbb{M}\left( 0\right)  \geq  0 \) , then \( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) for \( t > 0 \) . That is, the inequality \( \mathbb{M} \geq  0 \) is preserved under the ODE. By Theorem 10.13, \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq  0 \) is preserved under the Ricci flow.

Part (II) follows from the strong maximum principle for systems applied to Rm (see Theorem 12.53 ahead).

THEOREM 10.16 (Maximum principle for systems: time-dependent sets). Let \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \subset  \mathcal{V} \) be subsets which are invariant under parallel translation \( \nabla \left( t\right) \) for each \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . We require that \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \Doteq  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \cap  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) be closed and convex and that the space-time track

\[
\mathcal{T} \Doteq  \{ \left( {v, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{V} \times  \mathbb{R} : v \in  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t < T\}
\]

also be closed in \( \mathcal{V} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Assume that \( F\left( {u, t}\right) \) is continuous in \( \left( {u, t}\right) \) and is locally Lipschitz in u. Suppose that, for any \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , any solution \( U\left( t\right) \) of the ODE (10.25), which starts in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{x} \) , will remain in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all later times as long as the solution exists. Then the solution \( u\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , of the PDE (10.24) will remain in \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) if \( u\left( 0\right) \) starts in \( \mathcal{K}\left( 0\right) \) .

THEOREM 10.17 (Hamilton-Ivey estimate). If the initial metric of a solution to the Ricci flow \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , on a closed 3-manifold satisfies the normalizing assumption, \( \mathop{\min }\limits_{{x \in  \mathcal{M}}}\nu \left( {x,0}\right)  \geq   - 1 \) , then, at any point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) in space-time where \( \nu  < 0 \) , we have at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) ,

(10.40)

\[
R \geq  \left| \nu \right| \left( {\log \left| \nu \right|  + \log \left( {1 + t}\right)  - 3}\right) .
\]

To see the estimate, let \( \mathcal{V} = {\operatorname{Sym}}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}\mathcal{M}}\right) \) and let

(10.41)

\[
\mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} \mathbb{P} \in  \mathcal{V} & \begin{array}{l} \operatorname{tr}\mathbb{P} \geq   - 3/\left( {1 + t}\right) , \\  \text{ and if }\nu \left( \mathbb{P}\right)  \leq   - 1/\left( {1 + t}\right) ,\text{ then } \\  \operatorname{tr}\mathbb{P} \geq  \left| {\nu \left( \mathbb{P}\right) }\right| \left( {\log \left| {\nu \left( \mathbb{P}\right) }\right|  + \log \left( {1 + t}\right)  - 3}\right)  \end{array} \end{array}\right\}  .
\]

It suffices to show that \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \) preserves \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) . One can show that \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) is closed, invariant under parallel translation, and fiberwise convex (see Lemma 9.5 on p. 258 of Volume One). From (10.34) and the trivial inequality \( \frac{2}{3}{\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \right) }^{2} \geq  \frac{1}{3}{\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \right) }^{2} \) we see that the first inequality \( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu  \geq   - 3/\left( {1 + t}\right) \) in (10.41) is preserved. Note that if \( \nu  =  - 1/\left( {1 + t}\right) \) , then

\[
\lambda  + \mu  + \nu  \geq   - 3\left| \nu \right|  = \left| \nu \right| \left( {\log \left| \nu \right|  + \log \left( {1 + t}\right)  - 3}\right) .
\]

One computes that

\[
\begin{aligned} \frac{d}{dt}\left( {\frac{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }{-\nu } - \log \left( {-\nu }\right) }\right) &  = \frac{1}{{\nu }^{2}}\left( {-{\nu }^{3} - \nu \left( {{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu }^{2} + {\lambda \mu }}\right)  + \left( {\lambda  + \mu }\right) {\lambda \mu }}\right) \\   &  \geq   - \nu  \end{aligned}
\]

whenever \( \nu  < 0 \) . This implies that if \( \nu  \leq   - 1/\left( {1 + t}\right) \) , then

(10.42)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\frac{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }{-\nu } - \log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - \log \left( {1 + t}\right) }\right)  \geq  0.
\]

We now show that \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} = \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \cap  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) is preserved by the ODE (10.32).

Let \( \left( {\lambda \left( t\right) ,\mu \left( t\right) ,\nu \left( t\right) }\right) \) be a solution of (10.32) with \( \left( {\lambda \left( 0\right) ,\mu \left( 0\right) ,\nu \left( 0\right) }\right)  \in \; \mathcal{K}{\left( 0\right) }_{x} \) . Suppose \( \nu \left( {t}_{1}\right)  <  - 1/\left( {1 + {t}_{1}}\right) \) for some \( {t}_{1} > 0 \) . Then there exists \( {t}_{0} < \; {t}_{1} \) such that \( \nu \left( t\right)  <  - 1/\left( {1 + t}\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right) \) and \( \nu \left( {t}_{0}\right)  =  - 1/\left( {1 + {t}_{0}}\right) \) . This in turn implies that (10.42) holds for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . Let

\[
\Phi \left( t\right)  \Doteq  \frac{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }{-\nu } - \log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - \log \left( {1 + t}\right) .
\]

By our choice of \( {t}_{0} \) , we have \( \Phi \left( {t}_{0}\right)  = \frac{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }{-\nu }\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \geq   - 3 \) . Since \( \frac{d\Phi }{dt}\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) , we conclude \( \Phi \left( {t}_{1}\right)  \geq   - 3 \) . That is, \( \left( {\lambda \left( {t}_{1}\right) ,\mu \left( {t}_{1}\right) ,\nu \left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  \in \; \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{1}\right) }_{x} \) . This completes the proof that \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) is preserved by the ODE. The theorem follows.

By scaling, we have the following.

\[

\[

\]

nodes.proof:
Given \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) and \( C < \infty \) , constants to be chosen later, define

(10.46)

\[
{\tau }_{\varepsilon } \Doteq  \max \left\{  {\tau , T - \frac{\varepsilon }{{12}\left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) {e}^{9}}}\right\}
\]

and

(10.47)

\[
{\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }\left( t\right)  \Doteq  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbb{P} \in  \mathcal{V} : \frac{{\left( T - t\right) }^{\varepsilon }\left( {\lambda \left( \mathbb{P}\right)  - \nu \left( \mathbb{P}\right) }\right) }{{\left( \operatorname{tr}\mathbb{P} + 6\right) }^{1 - {2\varepsilon }}} \leq  C}\right\}  ,
\]

where

\[
\mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll}  & \operatorname{tr}\mathbb{P} \geq   - 3/\left( {1 + t}\right) , \\  \mathbb{P} \in  \mathcal{V} & \operatorname{and}\text{ if }\nu \left( \mathbb{P}\right)  \leq   - 1/\left( {1 + t}\right) ,\text{ then } \\   & \operatorname{tr}\mathbb{P} \geq  \left| {\nu \left( \mathbb{P}\right) }\right| \left( {\log \left| {\nu \left( \mathbb{P}\right) }\right|  + \log \left( {1 + t}\right)  - 3}\right)  \end{array}\right\}
\]

is given by (10.41). For each \( t,{\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }\left( t\right) \) is closed, invariant under parallel translation, and fiberwise convex (we leave it as an exercise to check the convexity of \( {\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }\left( t\right) ) \) . Given \( \delta  > 0 \) , define the avoidance set to be

\[
{\mathcal{A}}_{\delta }\left( t\right)  \Doteq  \left\{  {\mathbb{P} \in  \mathcal{V} : \mu {\left( \mathbb{P}\right) }^{2} + \nu {\left( \mathbb{P}\right) }^{2} \leq  \delta  \cdot  \lambda {\left( \mathbb{P}\right) }^{2}\;\text{ and }\;\lambda \left( \mathbb{P}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{4\left( {T - t}\right) }}\right\}  .
\]

Now we make a claim concerning the ODE and the avoidance set.

Claim. Let \( \tau  \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) and \( \delta  > 0 \) . There exists \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) depending only on \( \delta \) such that for any \( C < \infty \) , if \( \mathbb{M}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{x} \) for some \( {t}_{0} \geq  {\tau }_{\varepsilon } \) and \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , then either

(i) \( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all \( t \geq  {t}_{0} \) , as long as the solution exists or

(ii) there exists \( {t}_{1} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) such that \( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }{\left( t\right) }_{x} - {\mathcal{A}}_{\delta }{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all \( {t}_{0} \leq  t < {t}_{1} \) and \( \mathbb{M}\left( {t}_{1}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{A}}_{\delta }{\left( {t}_{1}\right) }_{x} \) .

We first show that the claim implies the theorem. By the Hamilton-Ivey estimate,

\[
\operatorname{Rm}\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \;\text{ for all }t \in  \lbrack 0, T).
\]

Hence, by choosing \( C \) in (10.47) large enough, we have \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {\tau }_{\varepsilon }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }\left( {\tau }_{\varepsilon }\right) \) and, by the claim and Theorem 10.20 applied on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{\varepsilon }, T}\right) \) , we have either

(a) there exist \( \bar{x} \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{\varepsilon }, T}\right) \) such that \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{A}}_{\delta }{\left( \bar{t}\right) }_{\bar{x}} \) or

(b) \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( t\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \geq  {\tau }_{\varepsilon } \) .

This says that either there exist \( \bar{x} \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{\varepsilon }, T}\right) \) such that

\[
\mu {\left( \operatorname{Rm}\left( \bar{x},\bar{t}\right) \right) }^{2} + \nu {\left( \operatorname{Rm}\left( \bar{x},\bar{t}\right) \right) }^{2} \leq  \delta  \cdot  \lambda {\left( \operatorname{Rm}\left( \bar{x},\bar{t}\right) \right) }^{2}
\]

and

\[
\lambda \left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{4\left( {T - \bar{t}}\right) }
\]

or

(10.48)

\[
\frac{{\left( T - t\right) }^{\varepsilon }\left( {\lambda \left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right)  - \nu \left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) }\right) }{{\left( \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right)  + 6\right) }^{1 - {2\varepsilon }}} \leq  C
\]

on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{\varepsilon }, T}\right) \) . In case (a) we are done since \( {\tau }_{\varepsilon } \geq  \tau \) . In case (b),(10.48) implies there exists a constant \( {C}^{\prime } < \infty \) such that

(10.49)

\[
\frac{\left| \mathrm{{Rm}} - \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) \right| }{\operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right)  + 6} \leq  {C}^{\prime }{\left( T - t\right) }^{-\varepsilon }{\left( \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right)  + 6\right) }^{-{2\varepsilon }}.
\]

Now take a sequence \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow  T \) and such that \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| \) is as large as it ever has been (see Remark 8.12 on p. 238 in Volume One). By Perelman's no local collapsing theorem (Theorem 6.58 on p. 256 in Part I of this volume) and Hamilton's compactness theorem (Theorem 3.10 on p. 131 in Part I of this volume) for solutions of the Ricci flow, there exists a subsequence of dilated solutions

\[
\left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3},{g}_{k}\left( t\right) ,{x}_{k}}\right) ,\;{g}_{k}\left( t\right)  \Doteq  \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| g\left( {{t}_{k} + {\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) \right| }^{-1}t}\right) ,
\]

which converges to a complete limit solution \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3},{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) with bounded curvature. Without much difficulty it can be shown that from (10.49) we have \( {\mathrm{{Rm}}}_{\infty } \equiv  \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\left( {\mathrm{{Rm}}}_{\infty }\right) \) and \( {R}_{\infty } > 0 \) on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3} \) (see pp. 268-269 in Volume One). We conclude that \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty },{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a spherical space form and \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\infty } \) is diffeomorphic to \( \mathcal{M} \) . This contradicts the assumption of the theorem, so only case (a) can occur. The theorem is proved.

Proof of the claim. Let \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) be a constant to be chosen later. Suppose that \( \mathbb{M}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{\varepsilon , C}^{\prime }{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{x} \) for some \( {t}_{0} \geq  {\tau }_{\varepsilon } \) and \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right)  \notin \; {\mathcal{A}}_{\delta }{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) , i.e.,

(10.50)

\[
\mu {\left( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right) \right) }^{2} + \nu {\left( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right) \right) }^{2} > \delta  \cdot  \lambda {\left( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right) \right) }^{2}\;\text{ or }\;\lambda \left( {\mathbb{M}\left( t\right) }\right)  < \frac{1}{4\left( {T - t}\right) }.
\]

By the proof of the Hamilton-Ivey estimate, if \( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right) , t \geq  {t}_{0} \) , where \( {t}_{0} \in \; \lbrack 0, T) \) , is a solution to the ODE with \( \mathbb{M}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) , then \( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \geq  {t}_{0} \) . We need to show that there exist \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) depending only on \( \delta \) such that the inequality in (10.47) with any \( C < \infty \) is preserved by the ODE for \( t \geq  {t}_{0}. \)

Step 1. We have

(10.51)

\[
\frac{\lambda }{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu  + 6} \leq  {e}^{9}.
\]

If \( \lambda  \leq  3{e}^{9} \) , then \( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu  + 6 \geq  3 \) , which implies (10.51). On the other hand, if \( \lambda  > 3{e}^{9} \) , then we have either

(i) \( \nu  \geq   - {e}^{9} \) , which implies \( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu  \geq  \lambda  + {2\nu } > \lambda /3 \) and (10.51) or

(ii) \( \nu  <  - {e}^{9} \) . In this case, since \( \mathbb{M}\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) , we have

\[
{2\lambda } > \lambda  + \mu  + \nu  \geq  \left| \nu \right| \left( {\log \left| \nu \right|  - 3}\right)  > 6\left| \nu \right| ,
\]

which again implies \( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu  \geq  \lambda  + {2\nu } > \lambda /3 \) and (10.51). Hence (10.51) is proved.

Step 2. Given \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) to be chosen later, define

\[
\Phi \left( t\right)  \Doteq  {\left( T - t\right) }^{\varepsilon }\frac{\lambda  - \nu }{{\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu  + 6\right) }^{1 - {2\varepsilon }}}.
\]

We compute (see p. 269 in Volume One)

\[
\frac{d\Phi }{dt} = \left( {{\varepsilon \lambda } - \frac{\varepsilon }{T - t} - \left( {\mu  - \nu }\right)  + \left( {1 - {2\varepsilon }}\right) \frac{{6\lambda } - \left( {{\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2} + {\mu \nu }}\right) }{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu  + 6}}\right) \Phi .
\]

By (10.46), \( {\tau }_{\varepsilon } \geq  T - \frac{\varepsilon }{{12}\left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) {e}^{9}} \) , so that

\[
\left( {1 - {2\varepsilon }}\right) 6{e}^{9} \leq  \frac{\varepsilon }{2\left( {T - t}\right) }
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{\varepsilon }, T}\right) \) . Thus, since \( {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2} + {\mu \nu } \geq  \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2}}\right) \) ,

\[
\frac{d\Phi }{dt} \leq  \left( {{\varepsilon \lambda } - \frac{\varepsilon }{2\left( {T - t}\right) } - \frac{1 - {2\varepsilon }}{2}\frac{{\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2}}{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu  + 6}}\right) \Phi
\]

for all \( t \geq  {t}_{0} \) .

By (10.50), either \( {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2} > \delta {\lambda }^{2} \) or \( \lambda  < \frac{1}{4\left( {T - t}\right) } \) . If \( \lambda  < \frac{1}{4\left( {T - t}\right) } \) , then

\[
\frac{d\Phi }{dt} \leq  \varepsilon \left( {{2\lambda } - \frac{1}{2\left( {T - t}\right) }}\right) \Phi  \leq  0.
\]

On the other hand, if \( \lambda  \geq  \frac{1}{4\left( {T - t}\right) } \) , then \( {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2} > \delta {\lambda }^{2} \) , and we have

\[
\frac{d\Phi }{dt} \leq  \left( {{\varepsilon \lambda } - \frac{\varepsilon }{2\left( {T - t}\right) } - \frac{1 - {2\varepsilon }}{2}\frac{\delta {\lambda }^{2}}{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu  + 6}}\right) \Phi
\]

\[
\leq  \lambda \left( {\varepsilon  - \frac{\left( {1 - {2\varepsilon }}\right) \delta }{2}\frac{3\left( {1 - {2\varepsilon }}\right) {e}^{9}}{9\left( {1 - {2\varepsilon }}\right) {e}^{9} + {6\varepsilon }}}\right) \Phi
\]

where we used

\[

DEFINITION 10.22 (Dini derivatives). Let \( f\left( t\right) \) be a function on \( \left( {a, b}\right) \) . The upper Dini derivative is the lim sup of forward difference quotients:

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }f}{dt} \Doteq  \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{f\left( {t + h}\right)  - f\left( t\right) }{h},
\]

the lower Dini derivative is the liminf of forward difference quotients:

\[
\frac{{d}^{ - }f}{dt} \Doteq  \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{f\left( {t + h}\right)  - f\left( t\right) }{h},
\]

the upper converse Dini derivative is the lim sup of backward difference quotients:

\[
\frac{{d}_{ + }f}{dt} \Doteq  \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{f\left( t\right)  - f\left( {t - h}\right) }{h},
\]

and the lower converse Dini derivative is the lim inf of backward difference quotients:

\[
\frac{{d}_{ - }f}{dt} \Doteq  \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{f\left( t\right)  - f\left( {t - h}\right) }{h}.
\]

Since we do not make any assumption on the continuity of \( f \) , it is possible that any one of the Dini derivatives of \( f \) takes the value \( - \infty \) or the value \( + \infty \) . We say that a function of one variable \( f\left( t\right) \) is right upper semicontinuous at \( \tau \) if \( \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {\tau }^{ + }}}f\left( t\right)  \leq  f\left( \tau \right) \) . Similarly, we say that \( f \) is left lower semi-continuous at \( \tau \) if \( \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {\tau }^{ - }}}f\left( t\right)  \geq  f\left( \tau \right) \) . If, for example, \( \frac{{d}^{ + }f}{dt} < \infty \) , then \( f \) is right upper semi-continuous. We have the following elementary fact concerning monotonicity.

LEMMA 10.23 (A criterion for bounding \( f \) from above). If \( f : \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is right upper semi-continuous and left lower semi-continuous, \( {}^{6} \) with \( f\left( 0\right)  \leq \; c \) , and if \( \frac{{d}^{ + }f}{dt}\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) such that \( f\left( t\right)  > c \) , then \( f\left( t\right)  \leq  c \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0,\widetilde{T}) \) .

---

\( {}^{6} \) These semi-continuity assumptions hold when, for example, \( f \) is continuous.

Given \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , let \( {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( t\right)  \Doteq  f\left( t\right)  - \varepsilon  - {\varepsilon t} \) . We shall show that \( {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( t\right)  \leq  c \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) and \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) ; the lemma follows from taking \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) . Define \( {\tau }_{0} \in  (0, T\rbrack \) depending on \( \varepsilon \) by

(10.52)

\[
{\tau }_{0} \Doteq  \sup \left\{  {\tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   : {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( t\right)  \leq  c\text{ for all }t \in  \lbrack 0,\tau )}\right\}  .
\]

Since \( {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( 0\right)  \leq  c - \varepsilon \) and \( {f}_{\varepsilon } \) is right upper semi-continuous, we have \( {\tau }_{0} > 0 \) . If for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , we have \( {\tau }_{0} < T \) , then there exists a sequence of times \( \left\{  {\tau }_{j}\right\}   \searrow  {\tau }_{0} \) such that \( {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( {\tau }_{j}\right)  > c = {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) \) (the last equality follows from the right upper and left lower semi-continuities of \( {f}_{\varepsilon } \) and \( {\tau }_{0} < T \) ). Then

\[
0 \leq  \frac{{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( {\tau }_{j}\right)  - {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) }{{\tau }_{j} - {\tau }_{0}} = \frac{f\left( {\tau }_{j}\right)  - f\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) }{{\tau }_{j} - {\tau }_{0}} - \varepsilon ,
\]

which implies

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }f}{dt}\left( {\tau }_{0}\right)  \geq  \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{f\left( {\tau }_{j}\right)  - f\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) }{{\tau }_{j} - {\tau }_{0}} \geq  \varepsilon  > 0;
\]

this is a contradiction since \( f\left( {\tau }_{0}\right)  = c + \varepsilon  + \varepsilon {\tau }_{0} > c \) implies \( \frac{{d}^{ + }f}{dt}\left( {\tau }_{0}\right)  \leq  0 \) . Hence for all \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , we have \( {\tau }_{0} = T \) , which implies \( {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( t\right)  \leq  c \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .
