\( \left(  \leq  \right) \) Since for any \( \varepsilon  > 0, g \) is uniformly Lipschitz in the time variable on \( \mathcal{S} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T - \varepsilon }\right\rbrack \) , we have \( f \) is locally Lipschitz. Choose a sequence \( {t}_{j} \searrow  t \) such that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{f\left( {t}_{j}\right)  - f\left( t\right) }{{t}_{j} - t} = \frac{{d}^{ + }f}{dt}\left( t\right) .
\]

Since \( \mathcal{S} \) is compact and \( g\left( {s,{t}_{j}}\right) \) is continuous in \( s \) , for each \( j \) , there exists a point \( {s}_{j} \in  \mathcal{S} \) where \( g\left( {{s}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  = f\left( {t}_{j}\right) \) ; furthermore, there exists a subsequence such that \( {s}_{j} \rightarrow  {s}_{\infty } \in  \mathcal{S} \) . By the continuity of \( g \) and \( f \) , we have

\[
g\left( {{s}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}g\left( {{s}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}f\left( {t}_{j}\right)  = f\left( t\right) ;
\]

that is, at time \( t, g \) attains its maximum at the point \( {s}_{\infty } \) . Hence

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }f}{dt}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{g\left( {{s}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  - g\left( {{s}_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{t}_{j} - t}
\]

\[
\leq  \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{g\left( {{s}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  - g\left( {{s}_{j}, t}\right) }{{t}_{j} - t} = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{\partial g}{\partial t}\left( {{s}_{j},{\tau }_{j}}\right)
\]

for some \( {\tau }_{j} \in  \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{j}}\right\rbrack \) , where the last equality follows from the mean value theorem. Since \( {s}_{j} \rightarrow  {s}_{\infty } \) and \( {\tau }_{j} \rightarrow  t \) , by the continuity of \( \frac{\partial g}{\partial t}\left( {s, t}\right) \) in \( s \) and \( t \) , we have

\[

\]

\[

\]

\]

THEOREM 10.33 (MPS: continuously varying time-dependent sets). Let \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \subset  \mathcal{V} \) be subsets depending continuously on \( t \) such that \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) is invariant under parallel translation \( \nabla \left( t\right) \) for each \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) and \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \Doteq  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \cap  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) is closed and convex. Assume that \( F\left( u\right) \) is locally Lipschitz in u. Suppose that, for any \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , any solution \( U\left( t\right) \) of the ODE

\[
\frac{dU}{dt} = F\left( U\right)
\]

which starts in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{x} \) will remain in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all later times as long as the solution exists. Then the solution \( u\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , of the PDE

\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = {\Delta u} + F\left( u\right)
\]

will remain in \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) if \( u\left( 0\right) \) starts in \( \mathcal{K}\left( 0\right) \) .

LEMMA 10.34 (Why Laplacian term is good for MPS). Let \( \widetilde{\mathcal{K}} \subset  \mathcal{V} \) be a subset which is invariant under parallel translation with respect to a connection \( \widetilde{\nabla } \) which is compatible with the metric \( h \) on \( \mathcal{V} \) . Assume that \( {\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}}_{x} \Doteq  \widetilde{\mathcal{K}} \cap  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) is closed and convex for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . If \( \widetilde{u} \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( \mathcal{V}\right) \) is a smooth section satisfying \( \widetilde{u}\left( x\right)  \in  {\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}}_{x} \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , then

\[
\widetilde{\Delta }\widetilde{u}\left( x\right)  \in  {C}_{\widetilde{u}\left( x\right) }{\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}}_{x}
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Here \( \widetilde{\Delta } \) is the Laplacian acting on sections of \( \mathcal{V} \) defined using the connection \( \widetilde{\nabla } \) on \( \mathcal{V} \) and the Levi-Civita connection on \( \mathcal{M} \) and \( {C}_{\widetilde{u}\left( x\right) }{\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}}_{x} \) is the tangent cone of the convex set \( {\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}}_{x} \) at \( \widetilde{u}\left( x\right) \) . (See Section 4 for the definitions of tangent cones and support functions of convex sets used in the proof below.)

LEMMA 10.35 (Existence of a nearest point on a closed convex set).

(i) For any \( W \notin  \mathcal{J} \) there exists a unique point \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) such that

\[
d\left( {W, V}\right)  = d\left( {W,\mathcal{J}}\right)  \Doteq  \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{X \in  \mathcal{J}}}d\left( {W, X}\right) .
\]

Moreover, \( V \) is a continuous function of \( W \) .

(ii) Let \( \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a continuous family of convex sets. Given \( W \notin  \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) , let \( V\left( {W, t}\right) \) be the point defined by \( W \) and \( \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) as in part (i). Then \( V \) is a continuous function of \( \left( {W, t}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. Since \( \mathcal{J} \) is closed, there exists \( V \in  \mathcal{J} \) such that \( d\left( {W,\mathcal{J}}\right)  = \; d\left( {W, V}\right) \) . Clearly \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) and \( V \) is the unique such point since if there were another such point \( {V}^{\prime } \neq  V \) , then \( \frac{V + {V}^{\prime }}{2} \in  \mathcal{J} \) and \( d\left( {W,\frac{V + {V}^{\prime }}{2}}\right)  < d\left( {W, V}\right)  = \; d\left( {W,{V}^{\prime }}\right) \) , a contradiction. This proves the first part of statement (i).

As we shall now see, uniqueness implies continuity. In particular, we shall prove (ii), which implies the second part of statement (i). If \( V \) is not a continuous function of \( \left( {W, t}\right) \) , then there exist sequences \( {t}_{i} \rightarrow  {t}_{\infty } \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) and \( {W}_{i} \rightarrow  {W}_{\infty } \notin  \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{\infty }\right) \) and a vector \( {V}_{\infty } \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{\infty }\right) \) such that

\[
\mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{i}\right)  \ni  V\left( {{W}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right)  \rightarrow  {V}_{\infty } \neq  V\left( {{W}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty }}\right)
\]

and

\[
d\left( {{W}_{\infty },{V}_{\infty }}\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}d\left( {{W}_{i}, V\left( {{W}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right) }\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}d\left( {{W}_{i},\mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{i}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= d\left( {{W}_{\infty },\mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{\infty }\right) }\right)  = d\left( {{W}_{\infty }, V\left( {{W}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty }}\right) }\right) ,
\]

where we used the assumption that \( \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) is continuous. However, this contradicts the uniqueness of the closest point proved in part (i). Hence \( V \) is a continuous function of \( \left( {W, t}\right) \) .

LEMMA 10.36 (Half-space separating a closed convex set and a point). Given \( W \notin  \mathcal{J} \) and the nearest point \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) as in the above lemma, the half-space

\[
H \Doteq  \left\{  {X \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} : \langle X - V, W - V\rangle  \leq  0}\right\}
\]

contains \( \mathcal{J} \) and \( W \notin  H \) . Hence any convex set is equal to the intersection of a family of half-spaces.

nodes.proof:
Proof. Suppose that there exists \( Y \in  \mathcal{J} - H \) . Then for some \( t \in  (0,1\rbrack \) near 0 ,

\[
d\left( {\left( {1 - t}\right) V + {tY}, W}\right)  < d\left( {V, W}\right)  = d\left( {W,\mathcal{J}}\right) .
\]

Since \( \left( {1 - t}\right) V + {tY} \in  \mathcal{J} \) , this is a contradiction. Finally, that \( W \notin  H \) is obvious.

Proof. The lemma follows from showing that for every point \( W \notin  \Gamma \) , there exists a half-space \( H \) containing \( \Gamma \) with \( U \in  \partial H \) and \( W \notin  H \) . From the previous lemma there is a (unique) point \( V \in  \partial \Gamma \) closest to \( W \) . Define

\[
H \Doteq  \left\{  {X \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} : \langle X - V, W - V\rangle  \leq  0}\right\}  .
\]

Then \( H \) is a closed half-space with \( \Gamma  \subset  H \) and \( W \notin  H \) . Note also that \( V \in  \partial H \) . The ray \( R = \{ U + t\left( {V - U}\right)  : t \geq  0\} \) is contained in \( \Gamma \) . If \( U \notin  \partial H \) , then for some \( t \) near 1, the point \( U + t\left( {V - U}\right)  \in  \Gamma \) is closer to \( W \) than \( V \) , a contradiction. Hence \( U \in  \partial H \) .

nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 10.39 (Characterization of the tangent cone). The tangent cone \( {C}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) is the smallest closed convex cone with vertex \( V \) containing \( \mathcal{J} \) .

nodes.proof: Proof. Let \( \Gamma \) be any closed convex cone with vertex \( V \) containing \( \mathcal{J} \) . By Lemma 10.37 we have \( \Gamma  = \mathop{\bigcap }\limits_{{\alpha  \in  A}}{H}_{\alpha } \) where for each \( \alpha  \in  A,{H}_{\alpha } \) is a closed half-space with \( V \in  \partial {H}_{\alpha } \) and \( {H}_{\alpha } \supset  \mathcal{J} \) . Hence \( \Gamma  \supset  {C}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) .

nodes.content: REMARK 10.43. Note that, in general, the tangent cone at a point in the intersection of a collection of closed convex sets in Euclidean space is contained in (but not necessarily equal to) the intersection of the tangent cones at that point of the convex sets in the collection. An illustrative example is the countable collection \( {\left\{  \left( x, y\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} : y \geq  k{x}^{2}\right\}  }_{k \in  \mathbb{N}} \) and the point \( \left( {0,0}\right) \) . Here the tangent cone of the intersection is the half-line \( \{ \left( {0, y}\right)  : y \geq  0\} \) whereas the intersection of the tangent cones is the half-space \( \{ \left( {x, y}\right)  : x \in  \mathbb{R}, y \geq  0\} . \)

DEFINITION 10.44 (Support function of a closed convex set). A linear function \( \ell  : {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a support function for \( \mathcal{J} \) at \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) if

(1) \( \left| \ell \right|  \doteq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left| X\right|  = 1}}\ell \left( X\right)  = 1 \)

(2) \( \ell \left( W\right)  \leq  \ell \left( V\right) \) for all \( W \in  \mathcal{J} \) .

DEFINITION 10.46 (Half-space associated to a support function). Given a support function \( \ell \) for \( \mathcal{J} \) at \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) , define the associated closed half-space \( {H}_{\ell } \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) by

\[
{H}_{\ell } \Doteq  \left\{  {W \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} : \ell \left( W\right)  \leq  \ell \left( V\right) }\right\}  .
\]

Note that \( {H}_{\ell } \) is the closed half-space with boundary equal to the hyperplane passing through \( V \) and perpendicular to \( {N}_{\ell } \) and where \( {H}_{\ell } \) is on the \( - {N}_{\ell } \) side of \( V \) . Condition (2) in the definition of support function says that \( \mathcal{J} \subset  {H}_{\ell }. \)

nodes.content: LEMMA 10.50 (Criterion for being in the tangent cone). We have \( X \in \; {C}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) if and only if \( \ell \left( X\right)  \leq  \ell \left( V\right) \) for all \( \ell  \in  {S}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. In fact it is not hard to see that the condition \( X \in  {C}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) is equivalent to each of the following:

(1) \( X \in  H \) for all \( H \in  {H}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) ,

(2) \( {\ell }_{H}\left( X\right)  \leq  {\ell }_{H}\left( V\right) \) for all \( H \in  {H}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) ,

(3) \( \ell \left( X\right)  \leq  \ell \left( V\right) \) for all \( \ell  \in  {S}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) .

s\left( W\right)  = \sigma \left( W\right)  \Doteq  \sup \{ \ell \left( {W - V}\right)  : V \in  \partial \mathcal{J}\text{ and }\ell  \in  {S}_{V}\mathcal{J}\} .

Moreover, the supremum is attained and \( s\left( W\right) \) is a continuous function of \( W \) .

Proof. By Corollary 10.51, there exists \( {V}_{0} \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) and \( {H}_{0} \in  {H}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) such that

\[
s\left( W\right)  = {\ell }_{{H}_{0}}\left( {W - {V}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \sigma \left( W\right) .
\]

On the other hand, for any \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) and \( H \in  {H}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) , we have \( \mathcal{J} \subset  H \) , which implies

\[
{\ell }_{H}\left( {W - V}\right)  = d\left( {W, H}\right)  \leq  d\left( {W,\mathcal{J}}\right)  = s\left( W\right) .
\]

Hence \( \sigma \left( W\right)  \leq  s\left( W\right) \) and equality follows. The convexity of the distance function follows from the fact that the supremum function of a family of convex functions is convex.

LEMMA 10.53. Let \( \mathcal{J} \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) be a closed convex set.

(i) The function \( s \) is \( {C}^{1} \) on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{k} - \mathcal{J} \) . For \( W \notin  \mathcal{J} \) let \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) be the unique point such that \( s\left( W\right)  = d\left( {W, V}\right) \) . The gradient \( \nabla s\left( W\right) \) is equal to the unit vector pointing in the direction \( \overrightarrow{VW} \) .

(ii) For \( W \notin  \mathcal{J} \) , define the closed convex set \( \widetilde{\mathcal{J}} \Doteq  {s}^{-1}\left( \left\lbrack  {0, s\left( W\right) }\right\rbrack  \right) \) . Then the boundary of \( \widetilde{\mathcal{J}} \) is \( {C}^{1} \) and the gradient \( \nabla s\left( W\right) \) is equal to the unit outward normal to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{J}} \) at \( W \) .

(iii) Let \( \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a continuous family of convex sets. Given \( W \notin  \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) , let \( s\left( {W, t}\right)  \Doteq  d\left( {W,\mathcal{J}\left( t\right) }\right) \) be the distance function. Then the gradient \( \nabla s\left( {W, t}\right) \) is a continuous function of \( \left( {W, t}\right) \) .

PROPOSITION 10.54 (Characterization of when an ODE preserves a convex set). Let \( \mathcal{J} \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) be a closed convex set and let \( F : {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) be a continuous function which is locally Lipschitz in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) . The ODE

(10.63)

\[
\frac{dU}{dt} = F\left( {U, t}\right)
\]

has the property that for every initial value \( {U}_{0} \in  \mathcal{J} \) and initial time \( {t}_{0} \in \; \lbrack 0, T) \) , the solution \( U\left( t\right) \) to (10.63) with \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = {U}_{0} \) has \( U\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{J} \) for all \( {}^{10} \; t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) if and only if

\[
V + F\left( {V, t}\right)  \in  {C}_{V}\mathcal{J}\;\text{ for all }V \in  \partial \mathcal{J}\text{ and }t \in  \lbrack 0, T),
\]

that is, if and only if

(10.64)

\[
\ell \left\lbrack  {F\left( {V, t}\right) }\right\rbrack   \leq  0
\]

for every \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J}, t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) and every \( \ell  \in  {S}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. Part 1. (Only if case.) Suppose \( {\ell }_{0}\left( {F\left( {{V}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  > 0 \) for some \( {V}_{0} \in  \partial \mathcal{J},{t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , and support function \( {\ell }_{0} \) for \( \mathcal{J} \) at \( {V}_{0} \) . Consider the solution \( U\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) , to (10.63) with \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = {V}_{0} \) . We have

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{dt}\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}}{\ell }_{0}\left( {U\left( t\right) }\right)  = {\ell }_{0}\left( {\frac{dU}{dt}\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right)  = {\ell }_{0}\left( {F\left( {{V}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  > 0.
\]

Hence for \( t > {t}_{0} \) small enough, we have \( {\ell }_{0}\left( {U\left( t\right) }\right)  > {\ell }_{0}\left( {V}_{0}\right) \) . That is, for such \( t, U\left( t\right)  \notin  {H}_{{\ell }_{0}} \) , and in particular, \( U\left( t\right)  \notin  \mathcal{J} \) .

Part 2. (If case.) For any \( {U}_{0} \in  \mathcal{J},{t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , and \( \tau  \in  \left( {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) , there exists \( R \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) such that the solution \( U\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) , to (10.63) with \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = {U}_{0} \) satisfies \( U\left( t\right)  \in  {B}_{R}\left( \overrightarrow{0}\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},\tau }\right\rbrack \) . Let \( {\mathcal{J}}_{R} \doteq  \mathcal{J} \cap  {B}_{3R}\left( \overrightarrow{0}\right) , \) which is both compact and convex. To prove \( U\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{J} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},\tau }\right\rbrack \) , it suffices to prove \( U\left( t\right)  \in  {\mathcal{J}}_{R} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},\tau }\right\rbrack \) . By Lemma 10.52, if \( W \in \; {B}_{R}\left( \overrightarrow{0}\right)  - \mathcal{J} \) , since \( {U}_{0} \in  \mathcal{J} \cap  {B}_{R}\left( \overrightarrow{0}\right) \) , we then have

\[
d\left( {W,\mathcal{J}}\right)  = d\left( {W,{\mathcal{J}}_{R}}\right)  = \sup \left\{  {\ell \left( {W - V}\right)  : V \in  \partial {\mathcal{J}}_{R}\text{ and }\ell  \in  {S}_{V}{\mathcal{J}}_{R}}\right\}  .
\]

In regards to Lemma 10.29, we make the following definition.

DEFINITION 10.56 (Space of support functions of a closed convex set). The space \( \mathcal{S} \) of support functions for \( \mathcal{J} \) is

(10.65)

\[
\mathcal{S} \Doteq  \mathcal{S}\left( \mathcal{J}\right)  \Doteq  \{ \left( {V,\ell }\right)  : V \in  \partial \mathcal{J}\text{ and }\ell  \in  {S}_{V}\mathcal{J}\} .
\]

CLAIM 10.57. If \( \mathcal{J} \) is compact, then \( \mathcal{S} \) is compact. In particular \( {\mathcal{S}}_{R} \Doteq \; \mathcal{S}\left( {\mathcal{J}}_{R}\right) \) is compact.

Proof of claim. Let \( \left\{  \left( {{V}_{i},{\ell }_{i}}\right) \right\}   \in  \mathcal{S} \) be any sequence. Since \( \partial \mathcal{J} \) is compact, there exists a subsequence such that \( {V}_{i} \rightarrow  {V}_{\infty } \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) . Since the unit sphere \( {S}^{k - 1}\left( 1\right) \) is compact, there exists a further subsequence such that \( {N}_{{\ell }_{i}} \rightarrow  {N}_{\infty } \) . We then have \( {\ell }_{i} \rightarrow  {\ell }_{\infty } \) , where \( {\ell }_{\infty }\left( W\right)  \doteq  \left\langle  {W,{N}_{\infty }}\right\rangle \) for all \( W \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) . Clearly \( \left| {\ell }_{\infty }\right|  = 1 \) . Since \( {H}_{{\ell }_{i}} \supset  \mathcal{J} \) for all \( i \) and \( {H}_{{\ell }_{\infty }} = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}{H}_{{\ell }_{i}} \) , we have \( {H}_{{\ell }_{\infty }} \supset  \mathcal{J} \) . Hence \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) is a linear support function for \( \mathcal{J} \) at \( {V}_{\infty } \) and \( \left( {{V}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty }}\right)  \in  \mathcal{S} \) . Therefore \( \mathcal{S} \) is compact, and the claim is proven.

---

\( {}^{10} \) Here and elsewhere in this book we actually mean that the statement holds as long as \( U\left( t\right) \) exists.

---

Define \( g : {\mathcal{S}}_{R} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},\tau }\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) by

\[
g\left( {\left( {V,\ell }\right) , t}\right)  \Doteq  \ell \left( {U\left( t\right)  - V}\right) .
\]

Let \( s\left( t\right)  \Doteq  d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,\mathcal{J}}\right) \) . Then whenever \( s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) , we have by the choice of \( R \)

\[
s\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {V,\ell }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{S}}_{R}}}g\left( {\left( {V,\ell }\right) , t}\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {V,\ell }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{S}}_{R}}}\ell \left( {U\left( t\right)  - V}\right) .
\]

We also have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left\lbrack  {\ell \left( {U\left( t\right)  - V}\right) }\right\rbrack   = \ell \left( {\frac{dU}{dt}\left( t\right) }\right)  = \ell \left\lbrack  {F\left( {U\left( t\right) , t}\right) }\right\rbrack  .
\]

Hence, from Lemma 10.29, whenever \( s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) , we obtain

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }}{dt}s\left( t\right)  = \sup \{ \ell \left\lbrack  {F\left( {U\left( t\right) , t}\right) }\right\rbrack   : \left( {V,\ell }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{S}}_{R}\text{ with }\ell \left( {U\left( t\right)  - V}\right)  = s\left( t\right) \} .
\]

For the \( \left( {V,\ell }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{S}}_{R} \) with respect to which the above supremum is taken, we have

\[
\ell \left( {U\left( t\right)  - V}\right)  = d\left( {U\left( t\right) , V}\right)  = s\left( t\right) ,
\]

\( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) , and \( \ell  \in  {S}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) .

For \( V \in  \partial \mathcal{J} \) and \( \ell  \in  {S}_{V}\mathcal{J} \) as above, by assumption (10.64) we have \( \ell \left\lbrack  {F\left( {V, t}\right) }\right\rbrack   \leq  0 \) . This, together with \( \left| \ell \right|  = 1 \) , implies that for \( \left( {V,\ell }\right)  \in  \mathcal{S} \) as above,

\[
\ell \left\lbrack  {F\left( {U\left( t\right) , t}\right) }\right\rbrack   = \ell \left\lbrack  {F\left( {U\left( t\right) , t}\right)  - F\left( {V, t}\right) }\right\rbrack   + \ell \left\lbrack  {F\left( {V, t}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\leq  \left| {F\left( {U\left( t\right) , t}\right)  - F\left( {V, t}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  C \cdot  d\left( {U\left( t\right) , V}\right)  = C \cdot  s\left( t\right)
\]

provided \( U\left( t\right)  \notin  \mathcal{J} \) (that is, provided \( s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) ). The inequality on the third line follows from \( F \) being locally Lipschitz. Summarizing, we have

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }}{dt}s\left( t\right)  \leq  C \cdot  s\left( t\right)
\]

whenever \( s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) in the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},\tau }\right\rbrack \) . Since \( s\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = 0 \) , by Lemma 10.23 we conclude that \( s\left( t\right)  \equiv  0 \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},\tau }\right\rbrack \) . That is, \( U\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{J} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},\tau }\right\rbrack \) . Since \( \tau  \in  \left( {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) is arbitrary, we obtain \( U\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{J} \) for all \( t \geq  {t}_{0} \) . This completes the proof of Proposition 10.54.

nodes.content:
Proposition 10.61 (ODE preserving a convex set: time-dependent sets). Let \( \mathcal{J}\left( t\right)  \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{k},0 \leq  t < T \) , be a family of nonempty closed convex subsets such that the space-time track \( \mathcal{L} \) is closed in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Consider the ODE (10.63), where \( F : {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) is continuous in \( \left( {U, t}\right) \) and locally Lipschitz in \( U \) . Then the following two conditions are equivalent.

(i) For any initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , any solution of the ODE (10.63) which starts in \( \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) at time \( {t}_{0} \) will remain in \( \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) for all later times.

(ii) \( F\left( {V, t}\right)  \in  {D}_{\left( V, t\right) }\mathcal{L} \) for all \( \left( {V, t}\right)  \in  \partial \mathcal{L} \) and \( t < T \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. (i) \( \Rightarrow \) (ii). Given any \( \left( {{V}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  \partial \mathcal{L} \) , we consider the solution to (10.63) with initial condition \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = {V}_{0} \) . Then (i) implies that \( U\left( {{t}_{0} + s}\right)  \in \; \mathcal{J}\left( {{t}_{0} + s}\right) \) for any \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T - {t}_{0}}\right) \) . Hence for every sequence \( {h}_{i} \searrow  0 \) ,

\[
{F}_{i} \Doteq  \frac{U\left( {{t}_{0} + {h}_{i}}\right)  - U\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{{h}_{i}} \rightarrow  \frac{dU}{dt}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = F\left( {{V}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

and

\[
{V}_{0} + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} = U\left( {{t}_{0} + {h}_{i}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {{t}_{0} + {h}_{i}}\right) .
\]

We conclude that \( F\left( {{V}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {D}_{\left( {V}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }\mathcal{L} \) .

(ii) \( \Rightarrow \) (i). Proof by contradiction. Suppose there exist \( {t}_{0} \) and \( {t}_{2} \) with \( {t}_{0} < {t}_{2} \) and a solution \( U\left( t\right) \) with \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) and \( U\left( {t}_{2}\right)  \notin  \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{2}\right) \) . Since \( \mathcal{L} \) is closed, there exists \( {t}_{1} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{2}}\right) \) such that \( U\left( {t}_{1}\right)  \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) and \( U\left( t\right)  \notin  \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Let

\[
s\left( t\right)  \Doteq  d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,\mathcal{J}\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Then \( s\left( {t}_{1}\right)  = 0 \) and \( s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) for \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . The function \( s\left( t\right) \) is right continuous and left lower semi-continuous on the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) (see Lemma 10.63 below). As before we will derive the inequality \( \frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  \leq  {Cs}\left( t\right) \) for \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , which yields \( s\left( t\right)  = 0 \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , a contradiction.

Given \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , there exists a sequence \( {h}_{i} \searrow  0 \) such that

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s\left( t\right) }{dt} = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - s\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}}.
\]

Let

\[
\mathcal{S}\left( t\right)  \Doteq  \{ \left( {V,\ell }\right)  : V \in  \partial \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \text{ and }\ell  \in  {S}_{V}\mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \}
\]

and recall that \( s\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {V,\ell }\right)  \in  \mathcal{S}\left( t\right) }}g\left( {V,\ell , t}\right) \) , where \( g\left( {V,\ell , t}\right)  \Doteq  \ell \left( {U\left( t\right)  - V}\right) \) . Thus there exist \( {V}_{i} \in  \partial \mathcal{J}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) \) and \( {\ell }_{i} \in  {S}_{{V}_{i}}\mathcal{J}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) \) such that

\[
g\left( {{V}_{i},{\ell }_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  = s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  = \left| {U\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {V}_{i}}\right| .
\]

There also exist \( {V}_{\infty } \in  \partial \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) and \( {\ell }_{\infty } \in  {S}_{{V}_{\infty }}\mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) such that \( g\left( {{V}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty }, t}\right)  = \; s\left( t\right)  = \left| {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{\infty }}\right| \) . The proof below does not require a subsequence of \( {V}_{i} \) to converge to \( {V}_{\infty } \) or a subsequence of \( {\ell }_{i} \) to converge to \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) .

We compute

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s\left( t\right) }{dt} = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{g\left( {{V}_{i},{\ell }_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - g\left( {{V}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {U\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {V}_{i}}\right)  - {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{\infty }}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {U\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - U\left( t\right) }\right)  + {\ell }_{i}\left( {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{i}}\right)  - {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{\infty }}\right) }{{h}_{i}}.
\]

Since by our hypothesis (ii), \( F\left( {{V}_{\infty }, t}\right)  \in  {D}_{\left( {V}_{\infty }, t\right) }\mathcal{L} \) , there exists a subsequence \( {h}_{i} \) and vectors \( {F}_{i} \rightarrow  F\left( {{V}_{\infty }, t}\right) \) such that \( {V}_{\infty } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) \) , so that

\[
{\ell }_{i}\left( {{V}_{\infty } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} - {V}_{i}}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s\left( t\right) }{dt} \leq  \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}{\ell }_{i}\left( {\frac{U\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - U\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}} - {F}_{i}}\right)  + \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {{V}_{\infty } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} - {V}_{i}}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{1}{{h}_{i}}\left( {{\ell }_{i} - {\ell }_{\infty }}\right) \left( {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{\infty }}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\left| {\frac{U\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - U\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}} - {F}_{i}}\right|  = \left| {F\left( {U\left( t\right) , t}\right)  - F\left( {{V}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{\infty }}\right|  = {Cs}\left( t\right)
\]

where we also used \( \left| {\ell }_{i}\right|  = 1 \) and

\[
\left( {{\ell }_{i} - {\ell }_{\infty }}\right) \left( {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{\infty }}\right)  = {\ell }_{i}\left( {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{\infty }}\right)  - \left| {U\left( t\right)  - {V}_{\infty }}\right|  \leq  0
\]

to get the second inequality.

Recall that \( {t}_{1} \) and \( {t}_{2} \) are such that \( U\left( {t}_{1}\right)  \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) and \( U\left( t\right)  \notin  \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. (Lower semi-continuity) Suppose \( {t}_{ * } \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) . Let \( {\widetilde{t}}_{i} \) be a sequence of times approaching \( {t}_{ * } \) . For each \( i \) , since \( \mathcal{J}\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{i}\right) \) is closed, there exists \( {V}_{i} \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{i}\right) \) such that \( d\left( {U\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{i}\right) ,{V}_{i}}\right)  = s\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{i}\right) \) . Consider a subsequence \( {i}_{j} \) such that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}s\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{{i}_{j}}\right)  = \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}s\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{i}\right) .
\]

Since the space time track \( \mathcal{L} \) is closed, there exists a subsequence \( \left\{  {i}_{j}\right\} \) such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{V}_{{i}_{j}} \doteq  {V}_{\infty } \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{ * }\right) \) . We then have

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}s\left( {t}_{i}\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}s\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{{i}_{j}}\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}d\left( {U\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{{i}_{j}}\right) ,{V}_{{i}_{j}}}\right)  = d\left( {U\left( {t}_{ * }\right) ,{V}_{\infty }}\right)  \geq  s\left( {t}_{ * }\right) .
\]

(Right continuity) It suffices to prove the right upper semi-continuity of \( s\left( t\right) \) on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) . Since \( \left( {U\left( t\right) , t}\right)  \notin  \mathcal{L} \) for \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \left( {U\left( {t}_{1}\right) ,{t}_{1}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{L} \) , we have \( \left( {U\left( {t}_{1}\right) ,{t}_{1}}\right)  \in  \partial \mathcal{L} \) . Let \( {V}_{{t}_{1}} = U\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) . For any \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , it follows from \( U\left( t\right)  \notin  \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) that there exists \( {V}_{t} \in  \partial \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) such that \( s\left( t\right)  = d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,{V}_{t}}\right) \) . Hence, for any \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) we can find \( {V}_{t} \in  \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) such that \( s\left( t\right)  = d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,{V}_{t}}\right) \) and \( \left( {{V}_{t}, t}\right)  \in  \partial \mathcal{L} \) . By condition (ii) in Proposition 10.61, \( F\left( {{V}_{t}, t}\right)  \in  {D}_{\left( {V}_{t}, t\right) }\mathcal{L} \) . Given \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , let \( {h}_{i} \searrow  0 \) be a sequence such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  = \; \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \searrow  t}}s\left( \tau \right) \) . By the definition of \( F\left( {{V}_{t}, t}\right)  \in  {D}_{\left( {V}_{t}, t\right) }\mathcal{L} \) , there exists a subsequence such that \( {V}_{t} + {h}_{i}{W}_{i} \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) \) and \( {W}_{i} \rightarrow  F\left( {{V}_{t}, t}\right) \) . So

\[
s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  \leq  d\left( {U\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) ,{V}_{t} + {h}_{i}{W}_{i}}\right) .
\]

Letting \( i \rightarrow  \infty \) , we get

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \searrow  t}}s\left( \tau \right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  \leq  d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,{V}_{t}}\right)  = s\left( t\right) .
\]

nodes.content:
Proposition 10.64 (ODE preserving a convex set: avoidance sets). Let \( \mathcal{J}\left( t\right)  \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{k}, t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a family of nonempty closed convex subsets and let \( \mathcal{B}\left( t\right) \) be avoidance sets such that the space-time track \( \mathcal{L} \) and the avoidance space-time track \( \mathcal{B}\mathcal{L} \Doteq  \left\{  {\left( {V, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \times  \mathbb{R} : V \in  \mathcal{B}\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T)}\right\} \) are closed. Consider the ODE (10.63), where \( F : {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) is continuous in \( \left( {U, t}\right) \) and locally Lipschitz in \( U \) . Then the following two statements are equivalent.

(i) For any \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) and any solution \( U\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) , of the ODE (10.63) with initial condition \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  \mathcal{J}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \smallsetminus  \mathcal{B}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) , either \( U\left( t\right)  \in \; \mathcal{J}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \geq  {t}_{0} \) or there is a time \( {t}_{1} > {t}_{0} \) such that \( U\left( t\right)  \in \; \mathcal{J}\left( t\right)  \smallsetminus  \mathcal{B}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right) \) and \( U\left( {t}_{1}\right)  \in  \mathcal{B}\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) .

(ii) \( F\left( {V, t}\right)  \in  {D}_{\left( V, t\right) }\mathcal{L} \) for all \( \left( {V, t}\right)  \in  \left( {\partial \mathcal{L}}\right)  \smallsetminus  \left( {\mathcal{B}\mathcal{L}}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. This proposition can be proved in the same way as Proposition 10.61 except for the following issue, which arises in proving (ii) \( \Rightarrow \) (i). In the proof of Proposition 10.61 we have used the property \( F\left( {V, t}\right)  \in  {D}_{\left( V, t\right) }\mathcal{L} \) for all \( \left( {V, t}\right)  \in  \partial \mathcal{L} \) ; however here this property holds only for \( \left( {V, t}\right)  \in  \left( {\partial \mathcal{L}}\right)  \smallsetminus  \left( {\mathcal{B}\mathcal{L}}\right) \) . We need to ensure that \( \left( {V, t}\right) \) can be chosen in \( \left( {\partial \mathcal{L}}\right)  \smallsetminus  \left( {\mathcal{B}\mathcal{L}}\right) \) when we use this property in the proof of Proposition 10.61; we adopt the notation used there and resolve the above issue. Since \( \mathcal{B}\mathcal{L} \) is closed and the solution \( U\left( t\right) \) , \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) , in the proof of Proposition 10.61 does not enter in \( \mathcal{B}\mathcal{L} \) , there is a constant \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) such that

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack  }}d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,\mathcal{B}\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq  {3\varepsilon }.
\]

Let \( {V}_{t} \in  \partial \mathcal{L} \) be such that \( d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,{V}_{t}}\right)  = d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,\mathcal{J}\left( t\right) }\right) \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( \left( {{V}_{{t}_{1}},{t}_{1}}\right)  = \left( {U\left( {t}_{1}\right) ,{t}_{1}}\right)  \in  \left( {\partial \mathcal{L}}\right)  \smallsetminus  \left( {\mathcal{B}\mathcal{L}}\right) \) , we have \( s\left( t\right) \) is right continuous at \( {t}_{1} \) by the proof of Lemma 10.63. Hence there exists \( {t}_{3} \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) such that \( s\left( t\right)  \leq  \varepsilon \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{3}}\right) \) . For any \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{3}}\right) \)

\[
d\left( {{V}_{t},\mathcal{B}\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq  d\left( {U\left( t\right) ,\mathcal{B}\left( t\right) }\right)  - d\left( {{V}_{t}, U\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq  {2\varepsilon }.
\]

Hence \( \left( {{V}_{t}, t}\right)  \in  \left( {\partial \mathcal{L}}\right)  \smallsetminus  \left( {\mathcal{B}\mathcal{L}}\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{3}}\right) \) and again \( s\left( t\right) \) can be shown to be left lower semi-continuous and right continuous on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{3}}\right\rbrack \) . For any \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{3}}\right) \) , choose the points \( \left( {{V}_{\infty }, t}\right) \) in \( \partial \mathcal{L} \) as in the proof of Proposition 10.61. These points are at least \( {2\varepsilon } \) away from \( \mathcal{B}\mathcal{L} \) , so by statement (ii) we still have the property \( F\left( {{V}_{\infty }, t}\right)  \in  {D}_{\left( {V}_{\infty }, t\right) }\mathcal{L} \) , which was used in the proof of Proposition 10.61. We may now repeat the rest of the proof of Proposition 10.61 to conclude that there is a constant \( C < \infty \) such that \( \frac{{d}^{ + }s\left( t\right) }{dt} \leq  C \cdot  s\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{3}}\right) \) . By Corollary 10.26 we get \( s\left( t\right)  \equiv  0 \) on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{3}}\right\rbrack \) , which is the required contradiction.

nodes.content: Claim. The function \( s\left( t\right) \) grows at most exponentially: \( \frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  \leq  {Cs}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) and for some constant \( C < \infty \) .

nodes.proof:
As in (10.61) and (10.65), let \( {S}_{v}\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \subset \; {\mathcal{V}}_{x}^{ * } \) be the set of support functions of \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) at \( v \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) and let

\[
\mathcal{S}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \Doteq  \left\{  {\left( {v,\ell }\right)  : v \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}\text{ and }\ell  \in  {S}_{v}\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right\}
\]

be the set of all support functions of \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) . Let

(10.66)

\[
\mathcal{R}\left( t\right)  \Doteq  \bigcup {}_{x \in  \mathcal{M}}\mathcal{S}{\left( t\right) }_{x},
\]

which is a subset of the vector bundle \( \mathcal{V} \oplus  {\mathcal{V}}^{ * } \) . Define \( {}^{11} \)

\[
g\left( {v,\ell , x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \ell \left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - v}\right) \;\text{ for }\left( {v,\ell , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

For \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) the maximum distance of \( u\left( {x, t}\right) \) to \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) may be written as

\[
s\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  \mathcal{M}}}\left\{  {\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {v,\ell }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{S}}_{x}\left( t\right) }}\ell \left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - v}\right) }\right\}   = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {v,\ell , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) }}g\left( {v,\ell , x, t}\right) .
\]

Given \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , let \( {h}_{i} \searrow  0 \) be such that

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - s\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}}.
\]

There exist sequences \( {x}_{i} \in  \mathcal{M},{v}_{i} \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) , and \( {\ell }_{i} \in  {S}_{{v}_{i}}\mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) , such that

\[
g\left( {{v}_{i},{\ell }_{i},{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  = s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) .
\]

By the compactness of \( \mathcal{M} \) and the closedness of the space-time track \( \mathcal{T} \) , there exists a subsequence such that \( {x}_{i} \rightarrow  {x}_{\infty } \in  \mathcal{M},{v}_{i} \rightarrow  {v}_{\infty } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) , and \( {\ell }_{i} \rightarrow  {\ell }_{\infty } \in  {S}_{{v}_{\infty }}\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \subset  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{\infty }}^{ * } \) . Since \( g \) is continuous and \( s \) is right continuous, by Lemma 10.65, we have

(10.67)

\[
s\left( t\right)  = g\left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) .
\]

---

\( {}^{11} \) In our notation we keep track of the projection \( x \) of \( \left( {v,\ell }\right) \) .

---

We compute

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{g\left( {{v}_{i},{\ell }_{i},{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - g\left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

(10.68)

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {v}_{i}}\right)  - {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) }{{h}_{i}}.
\]

Choose \( {v}_{i}^{ * } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) and \( {\ell }_{i}^{ * } \in  {S}_{{v}_{i}^{ * }}\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) such that

(10.69)

\[
d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}}}\right)  = {\ell }_{i}^{ * }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  = {\left| u\left( {x}_{i}, t\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }\right| }_{h}.
\]

Let \( {U}_{i}\left( \tau \right) ,\tau  \in  \lbrack t, t + \varepsilon ) \) , for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) independent of \( i \) , be the solution to the ODE (10.63) in \( {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{i}} \) :

(10.70)

\[
\frac{d{U}_{i}}{d\tau } = F\left( {{U}_{i},\tau }\right) ,
\]

with \( {U}_{i}\left( t\right)  = {v}_{i}^{ * } \) . Define \( {F}_{i} \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{i}} \) by

(10.71)

\[
{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} = {U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) .
\]

By our assumption, \( {U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) . Hence

(10.72)

\[
{\ell }_{i}\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} - {v}_{i}}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Note that (10.70) and (10.71) imply that as \( i \rightarrow  \infty \)

\[
\left| {{F}_{i} - F\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * }, t}\right) }\right|  = \left| {\frac{{U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {U}_{i}\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}} - \frac{d{U}_{i}}{dt}\left( t\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  0.
\]

By passing to a subsequence, we have \( {v}_{i}^{ * } \rightarrow  {v}_{\infty }^{ * } \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) and \( {\ell }_{i}^{ * } \rightarrow  {\ell }_{\infty }^{ * } \) . We claim that \( {v}_{\infty }^{ * } = {v}_{\infty } \) . Taking the limit of (10.69), we have

\[
\left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }^{ * }}\right|  = {\ell }_{\infty }^{ * }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }^{ * }}\right)
\]

\[
= d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right| ,
\]

where the last equality follows from (10.67). Since \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) is convex, we conclude that \( {v}_{\infty }^{ * } = {v}_{\infty } \) . (The point \( {v}_{\infty } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) is the unique point in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) closest to \( u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) \) .)

From (10.68) we have

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\left\lbrack  {{\ell }_{i}\left( {\frac{u\left( {{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}} - {F}_{i}}\right)  + \frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} - {v}_{i}}\right) }{{h}_{i}}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  - {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) }{{h}_{i}}.
\]

Note that for each \( i \) ,

\[
{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  \leq  \left| {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right|  = d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  s\left( t\right)  = d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }}}\right)  = {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) .
\]

From (10.67) we also have that \( \left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) \) satisfies

\[
{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  = s\left( t\right) ,
\]

so that by parallel translating \( {v}_{\infty } \) and \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) along geodesics (with respect to the metric \( g\left( t\right) ) \) emanating from \( {x}_{\infty } \) , so that \( \left( {{v}_{\infty }\left( x\right) ,{\ell }_{\infty }\left( x\right) , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) \) for \( x \) in a neighborhood of \( {x}_{\infty } \) , we have

(10.73)

\[
0 = \nabla \left( {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( t\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) }\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {\nabla u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right) ,
\]

(10.74)

\[
0 \geq  \Delta \left( {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( t\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) }\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = \Delta \left( {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( u\right) }\right) \left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right)
\]

since \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) is linear (note that \( {\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{\infty }} \) and that \( {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) \) is a real-valued function in a neighborhood of \( {x}_{\infty } \) which achieves a local maximum at \( {x}_{\infty } \) ). From (10.73)-(10.74) and (10.72), we have

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  \leq  {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - F\left( {{v}_{\infty }^{ * }, t}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  + {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  + F\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) , t}\right)  - F\left( {{v}_{\infty }^{ * }, t}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right|  = {Cs}\left( t\right)
\]

since \( F \) is locally Lipschitz and \( {v}_{\infty }^{ * } = {v}_{\infty } \) (we also used \( \left. {\left| {\ell }_{\infty }\right|  = 1}\right) \) . This proves the claim.

nodes.content:
REMARK 10.66 (Details of the extension of \( {v}_{\infty } \) and \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) ). If we extend a vector \( s \) in the bundle \( \mathcal{V} \) from the point \( {x}_{\infty } \) by parallel translation along geodesics emanating radially out of \( {x}_{\infty } \) , then we get a smooth section of the bundle on some small neighborhood of \( {x}_{\infty } \) such that \( \left( {\nabla \left( t\right) s}\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = 0 \) and the diagonal part of the second covariant derivatives of the section at \( {x}_{\infty } \) is zero: \( \left( {\nabla {\left( t\right) }_{X, X}^{2}s}\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = 0 \) (see (10.22)). We extend \( {v}_{\infty } \in  \partial {\mathcal{K}}_{{x}_{\infty }}\left( t\right) \) and \( {\ell }_{\infty } \in  {S}_{{v}_{\infty }}{\mathcal{K}}_{{x}_{\infty }}\left( t\right) \) in this manner using the connection \( \nabla \left( t\right) \) to get \( {v}_{\infty }\left( x\right) \) and \( {\ell }_{\infty }\left( x\right) \) defined for all \( x \) in some small neighborhood \( {\mathcal{U}}_{{x}_{\infty }} \) of \( {x}_{\infty } \) . Since the connection \( \nabla \left( t\right) \) is compatible with the metric \( h \) on \( \mathcal{V} \) , we have \( \left| {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( x\right) }\right|  = 1 \) . Since \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) is invariant under parallel translation, we have \( {v}_{\infty }\left( x\right)  \in  \partial {\mathcal{K}}_{x}\left( t\right) \) and \( {\ell }_{\infty }\left( x\right)  \in  {S}_{{v}_{\infty }\left( x\right) }{\mathcal{K}}_{x}\left( t\right) \) . Therefore

\[
\left( {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( x\right) }\right) \left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }\left( x\right) }\right)  \leq  s\left( t\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  {\mathcal{U}}_{{x}_{\infty }} \) . It follows that the function \( \left( {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( x\right) }\right) \left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }\left( x\right) }\right) \) of \( x \in  {\mathcal{U}}_{{x}_{\infty }} \) has a local maximum at \( x = {x}_{\infty } \) , so that

\[
\Delta \left\lbrack  {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( t\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) }\right\rbrack  \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  \leq  0.
\]

By (10.22), we have

\[
\left( {\nabla \left( t\right) {\ell }_{\infty }}\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = 0,\;\left( {\nabla \left( t\right) {v}_{\infty }}\right) \left( x\right)  = 0,
\]

and

\[
\left( {\nabla {\left( t\right) }_{X, X}^{2}{\ell }_{\infty }}\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = 0,\;\left( {\nabla {\left( t\right) }_{X, X}^{2}{v}_{\infty }}\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = 0,
\]

so that \( \left( {\Delta {\ell }_{\infty }}\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = 0 \) and \( \left( {\Delta {v}_{\infty }}\right) \left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = 0 \) . Hence \( {\ell }_{\infty }\left\lbrack  {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right\rbrack   \leq  0 \) .

Proposition 10.68 (Weighted \( {L}^{2} \) -monotonicity). Suppose that a compact evolving Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\Omega }^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies (10.75) and a \( {C}^{\infty } \) function \( u : \Omega  \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) satisfies

\[
u\left( {\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }u}\right)  \leq  0\;\text{ on }\Omega  \times  \lbrack 0, T)
\]

\[
u\frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu } \leq  0\;\text{ on }\partial \Omega  \times  \lbrack 0, T),
\]

where \( \nu \) is the unit outward normal vector to \( \partial \Omega \) . If \( \xi  : \Omega  \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a Lipschitz (weight) function satisfying

(10.76)

\[
\frac{\partial \xi }{\partial t} + \frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla \xi \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2} \leq  0\;\text{ a.e., }
\]

then the quantity

\[
{I}_{u}\left( t\right)  \Doteq  {e}^{-{K}_{1}t}{\int }_{\Omega }{u}^{2}\left( {x, t}\right) {e}^{\xi \left( {x, t}\right) }d{\mu }_{t}\left( x\right)
\]

is monotone nonincreasing in \( t \) .

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{I}_{u}\left( t\right)  = {e}^{-{K}_{1}t}{\int }_{\Omega }\left( {{2u}\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} + {u}^{2}\frac{\partial \xi }{\partial t} - \left( {\mathcal{H} + {K}_{1}}\right) {u}^{2}}\right) {e}^{\xi }d{\mu }_{t}
\]

\[
\leq  {e}^{-{K}_{1}t}{\int }_{\Omega }\left( {{2u\Delta u} - \frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla \xi \right| }^{2}{u}^{2}}\right) {e}^{\xi }d{\mu }_{t}
\]

\[
\leq  {e}^{-{K}_{1}t}{\int }_{\Omega }\left( {-2{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2} - 2\langle \nabla u,\nabla \xi \rangle u - \frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla \xi \right| }^{2}{u}^{2}}\right) {e}^{\xi }d{\mu }_{t}
\]

\[
=  - 2{e}^{-{K}_{1}t}{\int }_{\Omega }{\left| \nabla \left( u{e}^{\xi /2}\right) \right| }^{2}d{\mu }_{t} \leq  0,
\]

where we integrated by parts and used \( {\int }_{\partial \Omega }u\frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu }{e}^{\xi }d{\sigma }_{t} \leq  0 \) to get the inequality in the third line.

\[
v\left( {-\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }v + \mathcal{H}v}\right)  \leq  0\;\text{ on }\Omega  \times  \lbrack 0, T),
\]

\]

(10.79)

DEFINITION 10.75 (Weak solution of heat equation). We say that \( u \in \; {V}_{2,\text{ loc }}\left( {\mathcal{U}}_{T}\right) \) is a weak subsolution of the heat equation \( {Lu} \Doteq  \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - \; {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }u = f \) if for every nonnegative \( {C}^{\infty } \) test function \( \phi  : {\mathcal{U}}_{T} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) such that \( \phi \left( {\cdot ,0}\right)  = 0 \) and \( \phi \left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) is compactly supported in int \( \left( \mathcal{U}\right) \) for each \( t \) , we have

(10.80)

\[

THEOREM 10.79 (ABP maximum principle). Let \( \Omega  \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) be an open and bounded domain with smooth boundary and consider a \( {C}^{2} \) solution \( u \) : \( \Omega  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) , continuous up to the boundary, to the uniformly elliptic PDE with continuous coefficients:

(10.83)

\[
{Lu} \Doteq  {a}^{ij}\frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}} = f\;\text{ in }\Omega ,
\]

(10.84)

where \( {a}^{ij} \in  {C}^{0}\left( \Omega \right) \) satisfies \( {a}^{ij}{V}_{i}{V}_{j} \geq  \lambda {\left| V\right| }^{2} \) for some constant \( \lambda  > 0 \) . Then

\[
\parallel u{\parallel }_{{C}^{0}\left( \Omega \right) } \leq  \parallel \varphi {\parallel }_{{C}^{0}\left( {\partial \Omega }\right) } + \frac{\operatorname{diam}\left( \Omega \right) }{n{\omega }_{n}^{1/n}\lambda }\parallel f{\parallel }_{{L}^{n}\left( \Omega \right) },
\]

where \( {\omega }_{n} \) is the volume of the unit Euclidean n-ball.

nodes.proof:
We sketch the proof, which uses some beautiful geometric arguments, only in the case where \( \varphi  = {0.}^{14} \) More precisely, assuming that \( \varphi  \leq  0 \) , we shall prove the estimate

(10.85)

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{\Omega }u \leq  \frac{\operatorname{diam}\left( \Omega \right) }{n{\omega }_{n}^{1/n}\lambda }\parallel f{\parallel }_{{L}^{n}\left( \Omega \right) }.
\]

On the other hand, if \( \varphi  \geq  0 \) , then the lower bound

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{\Omega }u \geq   - \frac{\operatorname{diam}\left( \Omega \right) }{n{\omega }_{n}^{1/n}\lambda }\parallel f{\parallel }_{{L}^{n}\left( \Omega \right) }
\]

follows from considering \( L\left( {-u}\right)  =  - f \) . These two inequalities imply the estimate for \( \parallel u{\parallel }_{{C}^{0}\left( \Omega \right) } \) when \( \varphi  = 0 \) . We leave it as an exercise to show that the general case follows from the arguments below by considering \( \widetilde{u} \doteq  u \mp  c \) , where \( c \Doteq  \parallel \varphi {\parallel }_{{C}^{0}\left( {\partial \Omega }\right) } \) .

Suppose \( \varphi  \leq  0 \) . Since we may assume the maximum of \( u \) is not attained on the boundary of \( \Omega \) , there exists \( {x}_{0} \in  \Omega \) such that \( u\left( {x}_{0}\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{\Omega }u \) . Let \( R \Doteq  \operatorname{diam}\left( \Omega \right) \) so that \( \Omega  \subset  {B}_{R} \Doteq  B\left( {{x}_{0}, R}\right) \) . One of the key ideas of the proof is to consider the upper concave envelope of \( u \) :

\[
\widehat{u} \Doteq  \inf \left\{  {v : {B}_{R} \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) : v\text{ is concave in }{B}_{R}\text{ and }v \geq  u\text{ in }\Omega }\right\}  .
\]

---

\( {}^{13} \) We would like express our gratitude to Andrejs Treibergs for showing us the proof of the ABP maximum principle.

\( {}^{14} \) For basics about convex analysis used in this proof we refer the reader to Rockafellar [421] and Hiriart-Urruty and Lemaréchal [270].

---

(In the definition above we can equivalently replace the condition that \( v \) is concave by the condition that \( v \) is affine.) The function \( \widehat{u} \) is concave and in particular it is locally Lipschitz continuous and its second derivative exists almost everywhere (see §§6.3-6.4 of [187]). Note that \( \widehat{u}\left( {x}_{0}\right)  = u\left( {x}_{0}\right) \) and \( {\left. \widehat{u}\right| }_{\partial {B}_{R}} = 0 \) . The contact set of \( u \) is defined by

\[
\widehat{\Omega } \Doteq  \left\{  {x \in  {B}_{R} : u\left( x\right)  = \widehat{u}\left( x\right) }\right\}  .
\]

This is a closed set. Elements of the contact set are called contact points of \( u \) . If \( {x}^{\prime } \in  \widehat{\Omega } \) , then since \( \widehat{u} \geq  u,\widehat{u} \) is concave, and \( u\left( {x}^{\prime }\right)  = \widehat{u}\left( {x}^{\prime }\right) \) , we have \( \left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{k}\partial {x}^{\ell }}\right) \left( {x}^{\prime }\right)  \leq  0 \)

The tangential map of a \( {C}^{1} \) function \( f : {B}_{R} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \)

\[
{T}_{f} : {B}_{R} \rightarrow  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}
\]

is defined by

\[
{T}_{f}\left( x\right)  \Doteq  \nabla f\left( x\right) .
\]

More generally, given a function \( f : {B}_{R} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) , we can define the tangent map as a set-valued function by

\[
{T}_{f}\left( x\right)  \Doteq  \left\{  {\nabla \ell  \mid  \ell  : {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}\text{ is affine, }\ell  \geq  f\text{ in }{B}_{R}\text{ , and }\ell \left( x\right)  = f\left( x\right) }\right\}  .
\]

Note that in general \( {T}_{f}\left( x\right) \) may be empty. However, if \( f \) is concave, then \( {T}_{f}\left( x\right) \) is nonempty for all \( x \in  {B}_{R} \) (see Section 4 of this chapter). The image of a set \( S \subset  {B}_{R} \) under the tangent map is defined by

\[
{T}_{f}\left( S\right)  \Doteq  \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{x \in  S}}{T}_{f}\left( x\right) .
\]

If \( \xi  \in  {T}_{f}\left( {B}_{R}\right) \) , then there is a corresponding support function \( \ell \) so that \( \nabla \ell  = \xi \) and we call the graph of \( \ell \) a support plane. Note that the upper concave envelope of \( u \) satisfies

(10.86)

\[
{T}_{\widehat{u}}\left( {B}_{R}\right)  = {T}_{\widehat{u}}\left( \widehat{\Omega }\right)  = {T}_{u}\left( \widehat{\Omega }\right)
\]

(since \( {\left. u\right| }_{\partial \Omega } = \varphi  \leq  0 \) , it is not important that \( u \) is defined only on \( \Omega  \subset  {B}_{R} \) ).

Let \( c : {B}_{R} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be the Lipschitz function whose graph is the cone with vertex \( \left( {{x}_{0}, u\left( {x}_{0}\right) }\right) \) and containing the \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -sphere \( \partial {B}_{R} \times  \{ 0\}  \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 1} \) . We claim that

(10.87)

\[
\operatorname{meas}\left( {{T}_{\widehat{u}}\left( {B}_{R}\right) }\right)  \geq  \operatorname{meas}\left( {{T}_{c}\left( {B}_{R}\right) }\right)  = {\omega }_{n}\frac{u{\left( {x}_{0}\right) }^{n}}{{R}^{n}},
\]

where \( {\omega }_{n} \) is the volume of the unit \( n \) -ball.

1. We first establish the equality in (10.87). By considering the inverted cone as the rotation by \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 1} \) of a right triangle with height \( u\left( {x}_{0}\right) \) and base \( R \) , since we see that if \( \ell  : {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a linear function whose graph is tangent to the cone (intersecting the cone in a line segment from \( \left( {{x}_{0}, u\left( {x}_{0}\right) }\right) \) to \( \left. {\partial {B}_{R}\times \{ 0\} }\right) \) , then \( \left| {\nabla \ell }\right|  = \frac{u\left( {x}_{0}\right) }{R} \) . Thus \( {T}_{c}\left( {B}_{R}\right) \) is an \( n \) -ball of radius \( \frac{u\left( {x}_{0}\right) }{R} \) and the equality follows.

2. Next we establish the inequality in (10.87). Indeed, we can see this geometrically by considering a support plane \( \Pi \) to the cone. We consider planes parallel to \( \Pi \) but above the graph of \( \widehat{u} \) and we continuously lower these planes until they contact \( \widehat{u} \) . Since \( \widehat{u}\left( {x}_{0}\right)  = u\left( {x}_{0}\right) \) and \( {\left. \widehat{u}\right| }_{\partial {B}_{R}} = 0 \) , we have that \( \Pi \) is above the \( n \) -ball \( {B}_{R} \times  \{ 0\} \) . This shows that \( \Pi \) is also a support plane for \( \widehat{u} \) , so that \( {T}_{c}\left( {B}_{R}\right)  \subset  {T}_{\widehat{u}}\left( {B}_{R}\right) \) .

Finally, we complete the proof of the theorem. By (10.86) we have

\[
\operatorname{meas}\left( {{T}_{\widehat{u}}\left( {B}_{R}\right) }\right)  = \operatorname{meas}\left( {{T}_{u}\left( \widehat{\Omega }\right) }\right)  = {\int }_{\widehat{\Omega }}\left| {\det \left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\right) }\right| {dx}
\]

since \( \left| {\det \left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\right) }\right| \) is the Jacobian of the map \( {T}_{u} = \nabla u \) (we assumed \( u \in \; {C}^{2}\left( \Omega \right) ) \) . On the other hand, by the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality, for any nonnegative symmetric matrix \( {B}_{ij} \) we have \( {\left( \frac{\operatorname{trace}B}{n}\right) }^{n} \geq  \det B \) , so that by the elliptic equation (10.83) satisfied by \( f \) and by taking \( {B}_{ij} = \; - {\sqrt{a}}^{ik}\frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{k}\partial {x}^{\ell }}{\sqrt{a}}^{\ell j}\left( {\operatorname{recall}\left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\right)  \leq  0\text{ in }\widehat{\Omega }}\right) ,{}^{15} \) we have

\[
{\left| f\right| }^{n} = {\left| {a}^{ij}\frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\right| }^{n} = {\left| {\sqrt{a}}^{ik}\frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{k}\partial {x}^{\ell }}{\sqrt{a}}^{\ell j}\right| }^{n}
\]

\[
\geq  {n}^{n}\det \left( {a}^{ij}\right) \left| {\det \left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\geq  {\left( n\lambda \right) }^{n}\left| {\det \left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\right) }\right|
\]

since \( \left( {a}^{ij}\right)  \geq  \left( {\lambda {\delta }_{ij}}\right) \) . Hence

\[
{\omega }_{n}\frac{u{\left( {x}_{0}\right) }^{n}}{{R}^{n}} \leq  \operatorname{meas}\left( {{T}_{\widehat{u}}\left( {B}_{R}\right) }\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{{\left( n\lambda \right) }^{n}}{\int }_{\widehat{\Omega }}{\left| f\right| }^{n}{dx}.
\]

Thus

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{\Omega }u \leq  \frac{\operatorname{diam}\left( \Omega \right) }{{n\lambda }{\omega }_{n}^{1/n}}\parallel f{\parallel }_{{L}^{n}\left( \Omega \right) }
\]

and both (10.85) and the theorem are proved.

PROPOSITION 10.81 (Elementary variant of the WMP). Suppose that \( \Omega \) is a compact manifold with possibly nonempty boundary. Let \( T > 0 \) and let \( u : {\Omega }_{T} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a \( {C}^{2} \) function satisfying

\[

\]

where \( F\left( {z, x, t}\right) \) is a smooth function on \( \mathbb{R} \times  \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . If \( u \leq  k \) on \( {\partial }_{\mathrm{{par}}}{\Omega }_{T} \) for some \( k > 0 \) and if for some \( K > k \) , the function \( F \) satisfies the property

\[

Proposition 10.82 \( \left( {C}^{0}\right. \) estimate for Ricci-DeTurck flow). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n},\widetilde{g}}\right) \) be a complete Riemannian manifold with curvature \( \left| \widetilde{\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \) uniformly bounded on \( \mathcal{M} \) . If \( \left( {\Omega , g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a solution to the Ricci-DeTurck flow on a bounded domain \( \Omega  \subset  \mathcal{M} \) , i.e.,

(10.90)

\[
\begin{array}{ll} \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{W}_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}{W}_{i} & \text{ in }{\Omega }_{T}, \\  g\left( {x, t}\right)  = \widetilde{g}\left( x\right) & \text{ on }{\partial }_{\text{ par }}{\Omega }_{T}, \end{array}
\]

where

\[
{W}_{j} \Doteq  {g}_{jk}{g}^{pq}\left( {{\Gamma }_{pq}^{k} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{pq}^{k}}\right) ,
\]

then for any \( \delta  > 0 \) there exists a constant \( T = T\left( {\delta , n,\mathop{\sup }\limits_{\mathcal{M}}\left| \widetilde{\operatorname{Rm}}\right| }\right)  > 0 \) , independent of \( \Omega \) , such that for any \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\Omega }_{T} \) ,

\[
\left( {1 - \delta }\right) \widetilde{g}\left( x\right)  \leq  g\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + \delta }\right) \widetilde{g}\left( x\right) .
\]

Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n},\widetilde{g}}\right) \) be a complete Riemannian manifold with curvature \( \left| \widetilde{\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \) uniformly bounded on \( \mathcal{M} \) . If \( \left( {\Omega , g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a solution to the Ricci-DeTurck flow on a bounded domain \( \Omega \subset \mathcal{...

nodes.proof:
From Lemma 7.50 on p. 280 of [146], in particular, using

\[
- {R}_{ij} =  - {\widetilde{R}}_{ij} + \frac{1}{2}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}\left( {{g}^{kp}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j}{g}_{pk}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{k}\left( {{g}^{kp}\left( {{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{pj} + {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j}{g}_{ip} - {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ij}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\Gamma }_{ip}^{k}{\Gamma }_{kj}^{p} - {\Gamma }_{kp}^{k}{\Gamma }_{ij}^{p}}\right)
\]

and

\[
{W}_{i} = \frac{1}{2}{g}^{pq}\left( {{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{iq} + {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}{g}_{ip} - {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{pq}}\right) ,
\]

we see that the Ricci-DeTurck flow (10.90) may be rewritten as

(10.91)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} = {g}^{pq}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}{g}_{ij} - {g}^{pq}{g}_{ik}{\widetilde{g}}^{k\ell }{\widetilde{R}}_{{jp}\ell q} - {g}^{pq}{g}_{jk}{\widetilde{g}}^{k\ell }{\widetilde{R}}_{{ip}\ell q}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{2}{g}^{pq}{g}^{k\ell }\left( \begin{array}{l} {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j}{g}_{\ell q} + 2{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{jk}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{\ell }{g}_{iq} - 2{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{jk}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}{g}_{i\ell } \\   - 2{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j}{g}_{kp}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}{g}_{i\ell } - 2{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}{g}_{j\ell } \end{array}\right) ,
\]

where \( \widetilde{\nabla } \) is the Levi-Civita connection with respect to \( \widetilde{g} \) . On p. 285, after equation (7.47), of [146] it has been shown that for any \( {\delta }_{0} \in  (0,\delta \rbrack \) there exists \( {T}_{0} = {T}_{0}\left( {{\delta }_{0},{k}_{0}}\right)  > 0 \) , where \( {k}_{0} \Doteq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{\Omega }{\left| {\widetilde{R}}_{{ijk}\ell }\right| }^{2} \) , such that

(10.92)

\[
g\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - {\delta }_{0}}\right) \widetilde{g}\left( x\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - \delta }\right) \widetilde{g}\left( x\right) \;\text{ on }{\Omega }_{{T}_{0}}.
\]

So we just need to prove the upper bound for \( g \) .

Let \( {\lambda }_{i} \) denote the eigenvalues of \( g \) with respect to \( \widetilde{g} \) and choose normal coordinates \( \left\{  {x}^{i}\right\} \) with respect to \( \widetilde{g} \) centered at a point \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) so that \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( x\right)  = {\delta }_{ij} \) and \( g\left( {x, t}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{i}{\lambda }_{i}d{x}^{i} \otimes  d{x}^{i} \) . Let

\[
\psi \left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{n}{\lambda }_{i}^{m} = {g}_{{\alpha }_{1}{\beta }_{1}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{1}{\alpha }_{2}}{g}_{{\alpha }_{2}{\beta }_{2}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{2}{\alpha }_{3}}\cdots {g}_{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{m}{\alpha }_{1}}.
\]

Abbreviating (10.91) as

(10.93)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} = {g}^{pq}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}{g}_{ij} + {A}_{ij}
\]

(this defines the symmetric 2-tensor \( \left. {A}_{ij}\right) \) , we compute at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\psi  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{m}{g}_{{\alpha }_{1}{\beta }_{1}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{1}{\alpha }_{2}}\cdots \left( {{g}^{pq}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}{g}_{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} + {A}_{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}}\right) \cdots {g}_{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{m}{\alpha }_{1}}
\]

(10.94)

\[
= {g}^{pq}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}\psi  + m\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{n}{\lambda }_{i}^{m - 1}{A}_{ii}
\]

\[
- {g}^{pq}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  k}}{g}_{{\alpha }_{1}{\beta }_{1}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{1}{\alpha }_{2}}\cdots {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{{\alpha }_{j}{\beta }_{j}}\cdots {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}{g}_{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}\cdots {g}_{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{m}{\alpha }_{1}}
\]

In regards to the second line in (10.94), from (10.91) and (10.93) we compute

\[
{A}_{ii} =  - 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{p}\frac{{\lambda }_{i}}{{\lambda }_{p}}{\widetilde{R}}_{ipip}
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, p}}\frac{1}{2{\lambda }_{p}{\lambda }_{k}}\left( \begin{array}{l} {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp} + 2{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{k}{g}_{ip} - 2{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik} \\   - 2{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik} - 2{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik} \end{array}\right) ,
\]

so that

\[
m\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{n}{\lambda }_{i}^{m - 1}{A}_{ii}
\]

\[
=  - {2m}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, p}}\frac{{\lambda }_{i}^{m}}{{\lambda }_{p}}{\widetilde{R}}_{ipip}
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, k, p}}\frac{m{\lambda }_{i}^{m - 1}}{2{\lambda }_{p}{\lambda }_{k}}\left( {{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}\right) }^{2} - 4{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik} - {\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik} - {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{k}{g}_{ip}\right) }^{2}}\right) .
\]

The third line in (10.94) is equal \( {\mathrm{{to}}}^{16} \)

\[
- \frac{1}{{\lambda }_{p}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  k}}{g}_{{\alpha }_{1}{\beta }_{1}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{1}{\alpha }_{2}}\cdots {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{{\alpha }_{j}{\beta }_{j}}\cdots {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}\cdots {g}_{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}{\widetilde{g}}^{{\beta }_{m}{\alpha }_{1}}
\]

\[
=  - \frac{2}{{\lambda }_{p}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j < k}}{\lambda }_{q}^{j - 1}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}{\lambda }_{r}^{k - j - 1}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{rs}{\lambda }_{s}^{m - k}{\widetilde{g}}^{sq}
\]

\[
=  - \frac{2}{{\lambda }_{p}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j < k}}{\lambda }_{q}^{m - k + j - 1}{\lambda }_{r}^{k - j - 1}{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
=  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q, r}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\sigma  = 0}}^{{m - 2}}\frac{2\left( {m - \sigma  - 1}\right) }{{\lambda }_{p}}{\lambda }_{q}^{m - \sigma  - 2}{\lambda }_{r}^{\sigma }{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
=  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q, r}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\sigma  = 0}}^{{m - 2}}\frac{m}{{\lambda }_{p}}{\lambda }_{q}^{m - \sigma  - 2}{\lambda }_{r}^{\sigma }{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}\right) }^{2}
\]

(by taking \( k - j - 1 \Doteq  \sigma \) ). \( {}^{17} \)

---

\( {}^{16} \) The reader may wish to ponder a more direct way to derive this fomula.

\( {}^{17} \) Here we also used that \( {g}_{qr} \) is symmetric in \( q \) and \( r \) and that we can replace \( \sigma \) by \( m - \sigma  - 2 \) in the summation.

---

By combining the above formulas, we obtain the following (which does not quite agree with the statement on p. 286 of [146]):

(10.95)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\psi  \leq  {g}^{pq}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}\psi  - {2m}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, p}}\frac{{\lambda }_{i}^{m}}{{\lambda }_{p}}{\widetilde{R}}_{ipip}
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, k, p}}\frac{m{\lambda }_{i}^{m - 1}}{2{\lambda }_{p}{\lambda }_{k}}\left( {{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}\right) }^{2} + 4\left| {{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}}\right| \left| {{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik}}\right| }\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q, r}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\sigma  = 0}}^{{m - 2}}\frac{m}{{\lambda }_{p}}{\lambda }_{q}^{m - \sigma  - 2}{\lambda }_{r}^{\sigma }{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}\right) }^{2}
\]

Thus

(10.96)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\psi  \leq  {g}^{pq}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}\psi  - {2m}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, p}}\frac{{\lambda }_{i}^{m}}{{\lambda }_{p}}{\widetilde{R}}_{ipip}
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, k, p}}\frac{m{\lambda }_{i}^{m - 1}}{2{\lambda }_{p}{\lambda }_{k}}\left( {3{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}\right) }^{2} + 2{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik}\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q, r}}\frac{m}{{\lambda }_{p}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\sigma  = 0}}^{{m - 2}}{\lambda }_{q}^{m - \sigma  - 2}{\lambda }_{r}^{\sigma }{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}\right) }^{2}
\]

We shall show that we can make the negative term on the third line of the RHS of (10.96) dominate the terms on the second line of the RHS by choosing \( {\delta }_{0} \) and \( m \) suitably. First we choose \( m \) large enough so that \( {\left( 2n\right) }^{1/m} \leq  1 + \delta \) . Then we choose \( {\delta }_{0} \in  (0,\delta \rbrack \) in (10.92) small enough so that

(10.97)

\[
{5n} \leq  \left( {m - 1}\right) {\left( 1 - {\delta }_{0}\right) }^{m}.
\]

Then as long as \( \psi  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{i}{\lambda }_{i}^{m} \leq  K = {2n} \) in \( {\Omega }_{{T}_{0}} \) , which implies \( {\lambda }_{i} \leq  {\left( 2n\right) }^{1/m} \) , we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, k, p}}\frac{m{\lambda }_{i}^{m - 1}}{2{\lambda }_{p}{\lambda }_{k}}\left( {3{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}\right) }^{2} + 2{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{ik}\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q, r}}\frac{m}{{\lambda }_{p}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\sigma  = 0}}^{{m - 2}}{\lambda }_{q}^{m - \sigma  - 2}{\lambda }_{r}^{\sigma }{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{{5m}{\left( 2n\right) }^{\frac{m - 1}{m}}}{2{\left( 1 - {\delta }_{0}\right) }^{2}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, k, p}}{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{g}_{kp}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
- \frac{m\left( {m - 1}\right) {\left( 1 - {\delta }_{0}\right) }^{m - 2}}{{\left( 2n\right) }^{1/m}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q, r}}{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {\frac{{5m}{\left( 2n\right) }^{\frac{m - 1}{m}}}{2{\left( 1 - {\delta }_{0}\right) }^{2}} - \frac{m\left( {m - 1}\right) {\left( 1 - {\delta }_{0}\right) }^{m - 2}}{{\left( 2n\right) }^{1/m}}}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q, r}}{\left( {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{g}_{qr}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  0
\]

since \( {\lambda }_{p},{\lambda }_{q} \geq  1 - {\delta }_{0} \) (the last inequality follows from (10.97)). On the other hand, we also have

\[
- {2m}\frac{{\lambda }_{i}^{m}}{{\lambda }_{q}}{\widetilde{R}}_{iqiq} \leq  {A\psi }
\]

where \( A \Doteq  \frac{{2m}{n}^{2}\sqrt{{k}_{0}}}{1 - {\delta }_{0}} \) . Hence, as long as \( \psi  \leq  {2n} \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\psi  \leq  {g}^{pq}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{p}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{q}\psi  + {A\psi }
\]

Applying Proposition 10.81 with \( k = n \) and \( K = {2n} \) , we conclude that there exists \( {T}_{1} \in  \left( {0,{T}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) depending on \( \delta \) and \( {k}_{0} \) such that \( \psi  \leq  K = {2n} \) on \( {\Omega }_{{T}_{1}} \) . This completes the proof of the proposition.

1.2.1. The sharp operator. Given \( A \in  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) \) , let \( {A}_{\alpha \beta } \Doteq  A\left( {{\sigma }_{\alpha },{\sigma }_{\beta }}\right) \) , where \( {\left\{  {\sigma }_{\alpha }\right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1}^{N} \) is the dual (orthonormal) basis for \( {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) introduced above. Given \( A, B \in  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) \) , using the notation in (11.10), we define the sharp product by

(11.12)

\[
{\left( A\# B\right) }_{\alpha \beta } = \left( {A\# B}\right) \left( {{\sigma }_{\alpha },{\sigma }_{\beta }}\right)  \Doteq  \frac{1}{2}{c}_{\alpha }^{\gamma \eta }{c}_{\beta }^{\delta \theta }{A}_{\gamma \delta }{B}_{\eta \theta }.
\]

We denote \( A\# A \doteq  {A}^{\# } \) . It is easy to see that \( {\left( A\# B\right) }_{\alpha \beta } \) is symmetric in \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) . Hence

\[
A\# B \in  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) .
\]

We call the bilinear operator

\[
\#  : {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right)  \times  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right)  \rightarrow  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right)
\]

the sharp operator.

From the anti-symmetry of \( {c}_{\gamma }^{\alpha \beta } \) ,

\[
A\# B = B\# A\text{ . }
\]

Let \( \mathbf{I} \) and0be the identity and zero element in \( {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) \) , respectively. Note that \( A\# \mathbf{0} = \mathbf{0} \) ; however \( A\# \mathbf{I} \) is not necessary \( A \) .

---

\( {}^{4} \) The first Bianchi identity says that \( {R}_{{ijk}\ell } + {R}_{{jki}\ell } + {R}_{{kij}\ell } = 0 \) .

---

A computation also shows that for \( \phi ,\psi  \in  {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) ,

(11.13)

\[
\langle \left( {A\# B}\right) \left( \phi \right) ,\psi \rangle  = \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta }}\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {A\left( {\omega }_{\alpha }\right) , B\left( {\omega }_{\beta }\right) }\right\rbrack  ,\phi }\right\rangle   \cdot  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{\omega }_{\alpha },{\omega }_{\beta }}\right\rbrack  ,\psi }\right\rangle
\]

for any orthonormal basis \( {\left\{  {\omega }_{\alpha }\right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1}^{N} \) of \( {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) .
