1.2.2. Operator \( Q\left( A\right) \) and a trilinear form. Motivated by the consideration of the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) (see Section 2 below), we define the operator

\[
Q : {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right)  \rightarrow  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) ,
\]

(11.14)

\[
Q\left( A\right)  = A \circ  A + A\# A = {A}^{2} + {A}^{\# }.
\]

Related to this operator is the bilinear operator defined by

(11.15)

\[
Q\left( {A, B}\right)  \Doteq  \frac{1}{2}\left( {{AB} + {BA}}\right)  + A\# B,
\]

for \( A, B \in  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) \) . It is clear that \( Q\left( {A, A}\right)  = Q\left( A\right) \) and that \( Q\left( {A,\mathbf{I}}\right)  = \; A + A\# \mathbf{I} \) .

There is a trilinear form tri on \( {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) \) introduced by Huisken and defined by

(11.16)

\[
\operatorname{tri}\left( {A, B, C}\right)  \Doteq  \operatorname{tr}\left( {\left( {{AB} + {BA} + {2A}\# B}\right)  \circ  C}\right) .
\]

Note that (11.13) implies that \( \operatorname{tr}\left( {\left( {A\# B}\right)  \cdot  C}\right) \) is symmetric in \( A, B, C \) since

\[
\operatorname{tr}\left( {\left( {A\# B}\right)  \cdot  C}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{\gamma }\left\langle  {\left( {A\# B}\right)  \cdot  C\left( {\omega }_{\gamma }\right) ,{\omega }_{\gamma }}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma }}\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {A\left( {\omega }_{\alpha }\right) , B\left( {\omega }_{\beta }\right) }\right\rbrack  , C\left( {\omega }_{\gamma }\right) }\right\rangle  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{\omega }_{\alpha },{\omega }_{\beta }}\right\rbrack  ,{\omega }_{\gamma }}\right\rangle  .
\]

Hence tri is symmetric in all three variables. We also observe that

\[
\operatorname{tri}\left( {A, B, C}\right)  = 2\langle Q\left( {A, B}\right) , C\rangle ,
\]

where \( Q\left( {A, B}\right) \) is defined by (11.15) and \( \langle A, B\rangle  \Doteq  \operatorname{tr}\left( {AB}\right) \) .

The ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}A = {A}^{2} + {A}^{\# } \) on \( {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) \) (compare with (11.31) below) is the gradient flow for the functional

(11.17)

\[
P\left( A\right)  \Doteq  \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\left( {{A}^{3} + {A}^{\# } \circ  A}\right)  = \frac{1}{6}\operatorname{tri}\left( {A, A, A}\right) .
\]

To see this, we take a variation \( \frac{\partial }{\partial s}A = B \) and compute

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial s}P\left( A\right)  = \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\left( {B{A}^{2} + {ABA} + {A}^{2}B + \left( {A\# B + B\# A}\right)  \circ  A + {A}^{\# } \circ  B}\right)
\]

\[
= \operatorname{tr}\left( {\left( {{A}^{2} + {A}^{\# }}\right)  \cdot  B}\right)  = \left\langle  {{A}^{2} + {A}^{\# }, B}\right\rangle  ,
\]

using the fact that \( \operatorname{tr}\left( {\left( {A\# B}\right)  \cdot  C}\right) \) is totally symmetric and using the standard inner product on \( {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) \) .

Proposition 11.7 (Irreducible decomposition of \( { \otimes  }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) ).

(11.20)

\[
{\bigotimes }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} = {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \oplus  {S}_{0}^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \oplus  \mathbb{R}{g}_{\text{ can }}
\]

is an \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant irreducible orthogonal decomposition of the space of 2- tensors. Here \( {S}_{0}^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) denotes the space of trace-free symmetric 2-tensors and \( {g}_{\text{ can }} = \mathrm{{id}} \) is the Euclidean metric on \( {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) .

Using the identification of \( { \otimes  }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) with \( \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) , one can also write this

\[
{\bigotimes }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} = {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \oplus  {S}_{0}^{2}\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right)  \oplus  \mathbb{R}\text{ id }.
\]

Here \( {S}_{0}^{2}\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) \) is the space of trace-free symmetric transformations of \( {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) . The nontrivial aspect of the proposition is the irreducibility of the decomposition. In particular, it is easy to see that each of the factors \( {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n},{S}_{0}^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) , and \( \mathbb{R}{g}_{\text{ can }} \) is \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant. For example,

\[
A\left( {v \otimes  w - w \otimes  v}\right)  = {Av} \otimes  {Aw} - {Aw} \otimes  {Av} \in  {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}
\]

for \( A \in  \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) and \( v, w \in  {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) . We leave it as an exercise to show that \( A \in  \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) if and only if \( A\left( {g}_{\text{ can }}\right)  = {g}_{\text{ can }} \) .

We also have the following \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant irreducible decomposition of the tensor space \( {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) }^{ * }}\right) \) , where the notation shall be defined below (in particular, see (11.45)). The following proposition is discussed further in subsection 2.2 below.

LEMMA 11.11. The Bianchi map has the following properties.

(i) The subspace \( {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}\right)  \subset  {\bigotimes }^{4}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) is invariant under the action of b, i.e.,

(11.33)

\[
b\left( {{S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}\right) }\right)  \subset  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}\right) .
\]

(ii) For \( R \in  {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}\right) \) ,

(11.34)

\[
b\left( R\right) \left( {x, z, y, t}\right)  =  - b\left( R\right) \left( {x, y, z, t}\right) .
\]

Hence \( b\left( R\right)  \in  {\Lambda }^{4}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) , i.e.,

\[
{\left. b\right| }_{{S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}\right) } : {S}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}\right)  \rightarrow  {\Lambda }^{4}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}.
\]

For any \( R \in  {\Lambda }^{4}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) , we have \( b\left( R\right)  = R \) , so that the above map is onto.

(iii) The map \( b \) is self-adjoint, i.e., for any \( R, S \in  {\bigotimes }^{4}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) ,

(11.35)

\[
\langle b\left( R\right) , S\rangle  = \langle R, b\left( S\right) \rangle .
\]

---

\[

We may define the Ricci tensor \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \in  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) \) corresponding to an algebraic curvature operator \( \mathbf{R} \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n}}\right) {\text{ by }}^{15} \)

(11.38)

\[
\left\langle  {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \left( {e}_{i}\right) ,{e}_{j}}\right\rangle   = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left\langle  {\mathbf{R}\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{k}}\right) ,{e}_{j} \land  {e}_{k}}\right\rangle   = {\mathbf{R}}_{ikjk}.
\]

That is, the Ricci tensor corresponding to an algebraic curvature operator is the same trace as is used to obtain the usual Ricci tensor from the Riemann curvature operator:

\[
\left\langle  {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) \left( {e}_{i}\right) ,{e}_{j}}\right\rangle   = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left\langle  {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{k}}\right) ,{e}_{j} \land  {e}_{k}}\right\rangle   = 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}R\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{k},{e}_{k},{e}_{j}}\right)  = 2{R}_{ij}.
\]

CAVEAT. Note that for a Riemannian metric the Ricci tensor of its curvature operator \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \) is twice the Ricci curvature tensor of the metric.

We define the scalar curvature associated to an algebraic curvature operator \( \mathbf{R} \) by \( {}^{16} \)

(11.39)

\[
\operatorname{Scal}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \Doteq  \operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right)  = {\mathbf{R}}_{ikik}.
\]

Hence, for a Riemannian metric, the scalar curvature of the curvature operator, i.e., Scal(Rm), is equal to twice the scalar curvature of the metric.

\]

DEFINITION 11.22. Given \( a, b \in  \mathbb{R} \) , define the \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant linear transformation

\[
{\ell }_{a, b} : {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)  \rightarrow  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)
\]

by

(11.58)

\[
{\ell }_{a, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \Doteq  \mathbf{R} + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a{\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{I}} + \left( {n - 2}\right) b{\mathbf{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}}.
\]

Using the decomposition (11.48), we can rewrite this as

\[
{\ell }_{a, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \mathbf{R} + {2a}\bar{\lambda }\mathbf{I} + {2b}\operatorname{id} \land  {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) {\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{I}} + \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) {\mathbf{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}} + {\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{W}}.
\]

It is easy to see that \( {\ell }_{0,0}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \mathbf{R},{\ell }_{a, b}\left( {{S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) }\right)  \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) and \( {\ell }_{a, b} \) is invertible provided both \( a \neq   - \frac{1}{2\left( {n - 1}\right) } \) and \( b \neq   - \frac{1}{n - 2} \) ; we shall always make these assumptions on \( a \) and \( b \) . Each transformation \( {\ell }_{a, b} \) preserves the Weyl part and is a multiple of the identity on each of the other two irreducible components. (In particular, \( {\ell }_{a, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \mathbf{R} \) if \( \mathbf{R} \in  \langle \mathbf{W}\rangle \) .) Hence the 2-parameter family \( \left\{  {\ell }_{a, b}\right\} \) consists of all \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant linear transformations of \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) which preserve the Weyl parts of algebraic curvature operators.

\[
{\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}^{2} \land  \mathrm{{id}} = \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i < j}}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right) \left( {{e}_{i} \otimes  {e}_{i}}\right)  \land  \left( {{e}_{j} \otimes  {e}_{j}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i < j}}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right) {\omega }_{\alpha } \otimes  {\omega }_{\alpha }
\]

Since \( \mathrm{{Rc}} = {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0} + \bar{\lambda }\mathrm{{id}} \) , we have

\[
\mathrm{{Rc}} \land  \mathrm{{Rc}} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j}}\left( {{\operatorname{Rc}}_{ii}{e}_{i} \otimes  {e}_{i}}\right)  \land  \left( {{\operatorname{Rc}}_{jj}{e}_{j} \otimes  {e}_{j}}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i < j}}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{ii}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{jj}{\omega }_{\alpha } \otimes  {\omega }_{\alpha }

\]

\[
{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} \land  {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i < j}}{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j}{\omega }_{\alpha } \otimes  {\omega }_{\alpha }
\]

Note also that \( \mathbf{I} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i < j}}{\omega }_{\alpha } \otimes  {\omega }_{\alpha } \) .

Hence, by (11.62) we have, for \( i < j \) , that \( {\omega }_{\alpha } = {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j} \) is an eigenvector of \( {D}_{a, b}\left( \mathbf{D}\right) \) with eigenvalue \( {d}_{ij} \) given by (11.67).

From (11.63) we have

\[
{r}_{i} =  - {2b}{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) a\bar{\lambda }{\lambda }_{i} + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) b + {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\sigma ,
\]

which simplifies to (11.68).

PROPOSITION 11.31. The algebraic curvature operator \( D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is independent of the Weyl part \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{W}} \) of \( \mathbf{R} \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) . Equivalently,

\[
D\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{S}}\right)  = D\left( \mathbf{R}\right)
\]

for all \( \mathbf{R} \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) and \( \mathbf{S} \in  \langle \mathbf{W}\rangle \) .

Note that by replacing \( \mathbf{R} \) by \( \mathbf{R} - \mathbf{S} \) and \( \mathbf{S} \) by \( 2\mathbf{S} \) , proving the proposition is equivalent to showing that

(11.69)

\[
B\left( {\mathbf{R},\mathbf{S}}\right)  \Doteq  \frac{1}{4}\left( {D\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{S}}\right)  - D\left( {\mathbf{R} - \mathbf{S}}\right) }\right)
\]

vanishes for all \( \mathbf{R} \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) and \( \mathbf{S} \in  \langle \mathbf{W}\rangle \) .

The following exercise, which gives a formula for \( D\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{S}}\right)  - D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) , will be used in the proof of the proposition.

Equivalently, \[ D\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{S}}\right) = D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \] for all \( \mathbf{R} \in {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) and \(...

nodes.proof:
Suppose \( \mathbf{S} \in  \langle \mathbf{W}\rangle \) ; it suffices to show that \( B\left( {\mathbf{R},\mathbf{S}}\right)  = 0 \) for each \( \mathbf{R} \) in any one of the \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -irreducible components of \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) .

(1) \( B\left( {\mathbf{R},\mathbf{S}}\right)  = 0 \) if \( \mathbf{R} \in  \langle \mathbf{W}\rangle \) . Since \( \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{S},\mathbf{R} - \mathbf{S} \in  \langle \mathbf{W}\rangle \) , it follows from (11.61) that

\[
B\left( {\mathbf{R},\mathbf{S}}\right)  = \frac{1}{4}\left( {D\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{S}}\right)  - D\left( {\mathbf{R} - \mathbf{S}}\right) }\right)  = 0.
\]

(2) \( B\left( {\mathbf{I},\mathbf{S}}\right)  = 0 \) . By definition (11.58),

\[
\ell \left( \mathbf{I}\right)  = \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \mathbf{I} \Doteq  \left( {1 + {a}^{\prime }}\right) \mathbf{I}
\]

and by (11.78) and \( \mathbf{S} \in  \langle \mathbf{W}\rangle \) ,

(11.71)

\[
\mathbf{S} + \mathbf{S}\# \mathbf{I} = \left( {n - 1}\right) {\mathbf{S}}_{\mathbf{I}} + \frac{n - 2}{2}{\mathbf{S}}_{{\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}} = 0,
\]

so that

\[
B\left( {\mathbf{I},\mathbf{S}}\right)  = {\ell }^{-1}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {\ell \left( \mathbf{I}\right) \mathbf{S} + \mathbf{S}\ell \left( \mathbf{I}\right) }\right)  + \ell \left( \mathbf{I}\right) \# \mathbf{S}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\mathbf{{IS}} + \mathbf{{SI}}}\right)  - \mathbf{I}\# \mathbf{S}
\]

\[
= {\ell }^{-1}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {\left( {1 + {a}^{\prime }}\right) \mathbf{{IS}} + \mathbf{S}\left( {1 + {a}^{\prime }}\right) \mathbf{I}}\right)  + \left( {1 + {a}^{\prime }}\right) \mathbf{I}\# \mathbf{S}}\right)  - \mathbf{S} - \mathbf{I}\# \mathbf{S}
\]

\[
= \left( {1 + {a}^{\prime }}\right) {\ell }^{-1}\left( {\mathbf{S} + \mathbf{S}\# \mathbf{I}}\right)  - \left( {\mathbf{S} + \mathbf{S}\# \mathbf{I}}\right)  = 0.
\]

(3) \( B\left( {\mathbf{R},\mathbf{S}}\right)  = 0 \) for \( \mathbf{R} \in  \left\langle  {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}\right\rangle \) . Since

\[
B\left( {\mathbf{R},\mathbf{S}}\right)  = {\ell }^{-1}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {\ell \left( \mathbf{R}\right) \mathbf{S} + \mathbf{S}\ell \left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right)  + \ell \left( \mathbf{R}\right) \# \mathbf{S}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\mathbf{{RS}} + \mathbf{{SR}}}\right)  - \mathbf{R}\# \mathbf{S},
\]

it suffices to show that

(11.72)

\[
\ell \left( {\mathbf{{RS}} + \mathbf{{SR}} + 2\mathbf{R}\# \mathbf{S}}\right)  = \ell \left( \mathbf{R}\right) \mathbf{S} + \mathbf{S}\ell \left( \mathbf{R}\right)  + 2\ell \left( \mathbf{R}\right) \# \mathbf{S}
\]

for all \( \mathbf{R} \in  \left\langle  {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}\right\rangle \) . This follows from (11.57) \( {}^{18} \) and the fact that

\[
\ell \left( \widetilde{\mathbf{R}}\right)  = \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) \widetilde{\mathbf{R}} \Doteq  \left( {1 + {b}^{\prime }}\right) \widetilde{\mathbf{R}}
\]

for any \( \widetilde{\mathbf{R}} \in  \left\langle  {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}\right\rangle \) . The proposition is proved.

For the sake of simplicity, we shall denote \( \operatorname{Rc} \Doteq  \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) and \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} \Doteq  {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) . By the identities \( \operatorname{Rc} \land  \mathrm{{id}} = \left( {{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} + \bar{\lambda }\mathrm{{id}}}\right)  \land  \mathrm{{id}},{\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{I}} = \frac{\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}\mathbf{I} \) , and \( {\mathbf{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}} = \frac{2}{n - 2}\mathrm{{id}} \land  {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0} \) , the second stated identity in the lemma follows from the first one. Given an orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {e}_{a}\right\} \) , denote \( {r}_{ab} \Doteq  \operatorname{Rc}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }_{ab} = \; \operatorname{Rc}\left( {{e}_{a},{e}_{b}}\right) \) . We have by (11.18),

\[
{\left( \operatorname{Rc} \land  \mathrm{{id}}\right) }_{abcd} = \left\langle  {\left( {\operatorname{Rc} \land  \mathrm{{id}}}\right) \left( {{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right) ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\left\langle  {\operatorname{Rc}\left( {e}_{a}\right)  \land  {e}_{b} + {e}_{a} \land  \operatorname{Rc}\left( {e}_{b}\right) ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

(11.79)

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\left( {{r}_{ac}{\delta }_{bd} - {r}_{ad}{\delta }_{bc} + {r}_{bd}{\delta }_{ac} - {r}_{bc}{\delta }_{ad}}\right) .
\]

On the other hand, by (11.13) we have

\[
{\left( \mathbf{R}\# \mathbf{I}\right) }_{abcd} = \left\langle  {\left( {\mathbf{R}\# \mathbf{I}}\right) \left( {{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right) ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta }}\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {\mathbf{R}\left( {\omega }_{\alpha }\right) ,{\omega }_{\beta }}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right\rangle  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{\omega }_{\alpha },{\omega }_{\beta }}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{8}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j, s, t}}\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {\mathbf{R}\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right) ,{e}_{s} \land  {e}_{t}}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right\rangle  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j},{e}_{s} \land  {e}_{t}}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{16}\sum {\mathbf{R}}_{{ijk}\ell }\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{e}_{k} \land  {e}_{\ell },{e}_{s} \land  {e}_{t}}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right\rangle  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j},{e}_{s} \land  {e}_{t}}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

(11.80)

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\left( {{r}_{ac}{\delta }_{bd} - {r}_{ad}{\delta }_{ac} + {r}_{bd}{\delta }_{ac} - {r}_{bc}{\delta }_{ad}}\right)  - {\mathbf{R}}_{abcd}.
\]

We now justify the last equality. From (11.8), we have

\[
{\mathbf{R}}_{{ijk}\ell }\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{e}_{k} \land  {e}_{\ell },{e}_{s} \land  {e}_{t}}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right\rangle  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j},{e}_{s} \land  {e}_{t}}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= 4{\mathbf{R}}_{{ijk}\ell }\left( {{\delta }_{\ell s}\left( {{\delta }_{ka}{\delta }_{tb} - {\delta }_{kb}{\delta }_{ta}}\right)  + {\delta }_{kt}\left( {{\delta }_{\ell a}{\delta }_{sb} - {\delta }_{\ell b}{\delta }_{sa}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\times  \left( {-{\delta }_{jt}\left( {{\delta }_{ic}{\delta }_{sd} - {\delta }_{id}{\delta }_{sc}}\right)  + {\delta }_{js}\left( {{\delta }_{ic}{\delta }_{td} - {\delta }_{id}{\delta }_{tc}}\right) )}\right.

\[

\]

\[
= 8{\mathbf{R}}_{{ijk}\ell }\left( \begin{array}{l} {\delta }_{\ell j}\left( {{\delta }_{ka}{\delta }_{db} - {\delta }_{kb}{\delta }_{da}}\right) {\delta }_{ic} - {\delta }_{\ell d}\left( {{\delta }_{ka}{\delta }_{jb} - {\delta }_{kb}{\delta }_{ja}}\right) {\delta }_{ic} \\   - {\delta }_{\ell j}\left( {{\delta }_{ka}{\delta }_{cb} - {\delta }_{kb}{\delta }_{ca}}\right) {\delta }_{id} + {\delta }_{\ell c}\left( {{\delta }_{ka}{\delta }_{jb} - {\delta }_{kb}{\delta }_{ja}}\right) {\delta }_{id} \end{array}\right)
\]

\[
= 8\left( \begin{array}{l} {\delta }_{db}{r}_{ca} - {\delta }_{da}{r}_{cb} - \left( {{\mathbf{R}}_{cbad} - {\mathbf{R}}_{cabd}}\right) \\   - {\delta }_{cb}{r}_{da} + {\delta }_{ca}{r}_{db} + \left( {{\mathbf{R}}_{dbac} - {\mathbf{R}}_{dabc}}\right)  \end{array}\right)
\]

\[
= 8\left( {{\delta }_{db}{r}_{ca} - {\delta }_{da}{r}_{cb} - {\delta }_{cb}{r}_{da} + {\delta }_{ca}{r}_{db} + 2{\mathbf{R}}_{\text{ bacd }}}\right) ,
\]

where we used the first Bianchi identity to obtain the last equality. From this we obtain (11.80). The lemma follows from combining formulas (11.79) and (11.80).

LEMMA 11.35 \( \left( {{\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\text{ when }{\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{W}} = 0}\right) \) . Let \( \mathbf{R} \) be an algebraic curvature operator such that \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{W}} = 0 \) . Then

(11.81)

\[
{\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } = \frac{1}{n - 2}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} \land  {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} + \frac{2\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} \land  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
- \frac{2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{\left( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0} \land  \mathrm{{id}} + \left( {\frac{{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}}{n - 1} + \frac{\sigma }{n - 2}}\right) \mathbf{I}
\]

where \( \bar{\lambda } = \frac{1}{n}\operatorname{Scal}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) and \( \sigma  = \frac{1}{n}{\left| {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}\right| }^{2} \) .

As a consequence, we have the following.

nodes.proof:
Let \( {\mathbf{R}}_{0} \doteq  {\mathbf{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}} = \frac{2}{n - 2}\operatorname{id} \land  {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0} \) . Since \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{W}} = \) 0 , we then have

(11.84)

\[
\mathbf{R} = \frac{\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}\mathbf{I} + {\mathbf{R}}_{0}
\]

and

\[
{\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }
\]

\[
= {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{2} + \frac{2\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}{\mathbf{R}}_{0} + {\left( \frac{\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}\right) }^{2}\mathbf{I} + {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{\# } + \frac{2\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}{\mathbf{R}}_{0}\# \mathbf{I} + {\left( \frac{\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}\right) }^{2}\mathbf{I}\# \mathbf{I}
\]

\[
= {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{\# } + \frac{2\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}\left( {{\mathbf{R}}_{0} + {\mathbf{R}}_{0}\# \mathbf{I}}\right)  + {\left( \frac{\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}\right) }^{2}\left( {\mathbf{I} + \mathbf{I}\# \mathbf{I}}\right) .
\]

Observe that by (11.42),

\[
\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\mathbf{R}}_{0}\right)  = \frac{2}{n - 2}\operatorname{Rc}\left( {{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} \land  \mathrm{{id}}}\right)  = {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}
\]

and

\[
\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{I}\right)  = \left( {n - 1}\right) \mathrm{{id}},
\]

so that by (11.77) we have

\[
{\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } = {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{\# } + \frac{2\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} \land  \operatorname{id} + \frac{{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}}{n - 1}\operatorname{id} \land  \operatorname{id}.
\]

Comparing this with (11.81), we see that to prove the lemma it suffices to show that

(11.85)

\[
{\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{\# } = \frac{1}{n - 2}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} \land  {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} - \frac{2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{\left( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0} \land  \operatorname{id} + \frac{\sigma }{n - 2}\mathbf{I}.
\]

The rest of the proof is devoted to establishing this equation by a direct calculation.

Choose an orthonormal basis \( {\left\{  {e}_{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{n} \) of eigenvectors of \( {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0} \) with corresponding eigenvalues \( {\left\{  {\lambda }_{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{n} \) . It is easy to see that

\[
\left( {\frac{1}{n - 2}{\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0} \land  {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}}\right) \left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)  = \frac{{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}
\]

and

\[
\left( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2}\right) \left( {e}_{i}\right)  = {\lambda }_{i}^{2}{e}_{i}
\]

\[
{\left( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0}\left( {e}_{i}\right)  = \left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} - \sigma }\right) {e}_{i}
\]

so that

\[
- \frac{2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}\left( {{\left( {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0} \land  \mathrm{{id}}}\right) \left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)  =  - \frac{{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2} - {2\sigma }}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}.
\]

Combining these formulas, we have

\[
\left( {\frac{1}{n - 2}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} \land  {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} - \frac{2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{\left( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0} \land  \mathrm{{id}} + \frac{\sigma }{n - 2}\mathbf{I}}\right) \left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\frac{{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2} + \frac{{n\sigma } - {\lambda }_{i}^{2} - {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}}\right) {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}.
\]

Thus, to prove (11.85), we need to show that

(11.86)

\[
\left( {{\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{\# }}\right) \left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)  = \left( {\frac{{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2} + \frac{{n\sigma } - {\lambda }_{i}^{2} - {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}}\right) {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}.
\]

First,

\[
{\mathbf{R}}_{0}\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)  = \frac{2}{n - 2}\left( {\operatorname{id} \land  {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}}\right) \left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)  = \frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j},
\]

so that

(11.87)

\[
{\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{2}\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)  = {\left( \frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}\right) }^{2}{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}.
\]

As in the proof of Lemma 11.33, using equations (11.13), (11.7), and (11.8), we compute

\[
\left\langle  {\left( {{\mathbf{R}}_{0}\# {\mathbf{R}}_{0}}\right) \left( {{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right) ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta }}\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{\mathbf{R}}_{0}\left( {\omega }_{\alpha }\right) ,{\mathbf{R}}_{0}\left( {\omega }_{\beta }\right) }\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right\rangle  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{\omega }_{\alpha },{\omega }_{\beta }}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{8}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i \neq  j, p \neq  q}}\frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}\frac{{\lambda }_{p} + {\lambda }_{q}}{n - 2}\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j},{e}_{p} \land  {e}_{q}}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
\times  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j},{e}_{p} \land  {e}_{q}}\right\rbrack  ,{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  a, b}}\frac{{\lambda }_{a} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}\frac{{\lambda }_{j} + {\lambda }_{b}}{n - 2}\left\langle  {{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b},{e}_{c} \land  {e}_{d}}\right\rangle  .
\]

We then have

(11.88)

\[
\left( {{\mathbf{R}}_{0}\# {\mathbf{R}}_{0}}\right) \left( {{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  a, b}}\frac{{\lambda }_{a} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}\frac{{\lambda }_{j} + {\lambda }_{b}}{n - 2}{e}_{a} \land  {e}_{b}.
\]

Combining (11.87) and (11.88), we have

\[
\left( {{\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}_{0}^{\# }}\right) \left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)  = \left( {{\left( \frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}\right) }^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i, j}}\frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{k}}{n - 2}\frac{{\lambda }_{k} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}}\right) {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}
\]

\[
= \left( {\frac{{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2} + \frac{{n\sigma } - {\lambda }_{i}^{2} - {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}}\right) {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j},
\]

which proves (11.86) and the equivalent (11.85); to obtain the second equality above, we used the fact that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i, j}}{\lambda }_{k} =  - {\lambda }_{i} - {\lambda }_{j}\;\text{ and }\;\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i, j}}{\lambda }_{k}^{2} = {n\sigma } - {\lambda }_{i}^{2} - {\lambda }_{j}^{2}
\]

(since \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}{\lambda }_{k} = 0 \) ) implies

\[
{\left( \frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}\right) }^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i, j}}\frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{k}}{n - 2}\frac{{\lambda }_{k} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2}
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}\left( {{\left( {\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}\right) }^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + {\lambda }_{k}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}\right)  + {\lambda }_{k}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}\left( {\left( {n - 2}\right) {\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + {n\sigma } - {\lambda }_{i}^{2} - {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right) .
\]

The lemma is proved.

Since \( \langle \mathbf{W}\rangle \) is orthogonal to \( {\operatorname{id}}_{ \land  }{S}^{2}\left( {\mathbb{E}}^{n}\right) \) (see (11.44)), the first formula follows directly from (11.81).

For the second formula, from (11.81) we can compute \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( {{\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }}\right) \) using (11.41) and (11.42) as follows:

\[
\operatorname{Rc}\left( {{\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }}\right)
\]

\]

\[
=  - \frac{1}{n - 2}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2} + \frac{n - 2}{n - 1}\bar{\lambda }{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} - \frac{1}{n - 2}{\left( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0} + \left( {{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{n - 1}{n - 2}\sigma }\right) \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
=  - \frac{2}{n - 2}{\left( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0} - \frac{\sigma }{n - 2}\mathrm{{id}} + \frac{\left( n - 2\right) }{n - 1}\bar{\lambda }{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} + \left( {{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{n - 1}{n - 2}\sigma }\right) \mathrm{{id}}
\]

since \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2} = {\left( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0} + \sigma \) id, which implies (11.83).

DEFINITION 11.37 (2-nonnegative curvature operator). We say that an algebraic curvature operator \( \mathbf{R} \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) is 2-nonnegative if

\[
{\mu }_{\alpha } + {\mu }_{\beta } \geq  0
\]

for any \( \alpha  \neq  \beta \) , where \( {\left\{  {\mu }_{\gamma }\right\}  }_{\gamma  = 1}^{N}, N \Doteq  \frac{n\left( {n - 1}\right) }{2} \) , denote the eigenvalues of \( \mathbf{R} \) . We say that \( \mathbf{R} \) is 2-positive if the inequality above is strict.

Clearly this condition only makes sense when \( n \geq  3 \) . When \( n = 3 \) , the condition of 2-nonnegativity is equivalent to the Ricci curvature \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) being nonnegative. The cone \( \mathfrak{C} \) of 2-nonnegative algebraic curvature operators is an \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant convex cone.

DEFINITION 11.38. We say that an algebraic curvature operator \( \mathbf{R} \) is a nonnegative curvature operator of rank 1 if \( \mathbf{R} = \omega  \otimes  \omega \) for some \( \omega  \in  {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) . An algebraic curvature operator is called geometrically nonnegative if it can be written as the linear combination, with positive coefficients, of nonnegative curvature operators of rank 1.

If \( \mathbf{R} \) is geometrically nonnegative, then \( \mathbf{R} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{\alpha }{c}_{\alpha }{\eta }_{\alpha } \otimes  {\eta }_{\alpha } \) , where \( {c}_{\alpha } > 0 \) . Thus, for any 2-form \( \xi \) we have

\[
\mathbf{R}\left( {\xi ,\xi }\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{\alpha }{c}_{\alpha }{\left( {\eta }_{\alpha }\left( \xi \right) \right) }^{2} \geq  0,
\]

so that \( \mathbf{R} \) is a nonnegative curvature operator.

Note that if \( \omega  \otimes  \omega \) is an algebraic curvature operator, then the first Bianchi identity implies \( \omega  \land  \omega  = 0 \) and hence there exist \( v, w \in  {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) such that \( {}^{19} \)

\[
\omega  = v \land  w
\]

---

\( {}^{19} \) Indeed, the first Bianchi identity applied to \( \omega  \land  \omega \) implies

\[
{\left( \omega  \land  \omega \right) }_{{ijk}\ell } = \frac{1}{3}\left( {{\omega }_{ij}{\omega }_{k\ell } + {\omega }_{ki}{\omega }_{j\ell } + {\omega }_{jk}{\omega }_{i\ell }}\right)  = 0.
\]

We may prove, by induction on \( n \) , that \( \omega  \land  \omega  = 0 \) implies there exist \( v, w \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that \( \omega  = v \land  w \) . The result is clearly true for \( n = 1,2 \) . Now suppose the result is true for dimension \( n - 1 \) , where \( n \geq  4 \) . Let \( {\left\{  {e}_{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{n} \) be a basis for \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . We may write

\[
\omega  = {e}_{1} \land  x + \eta
\]

where \( x = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i \geq  2}}{x}^{i}{e}_{i} \) and \( \eta  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j \geq  2}}{\eta }^{ij}{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j} \) . From \( \omega  \land  \omega  = 0 \) we find that

\[
{e}_{1} \land  x \land  \eta  = 0\;\text{ and }\;\eta  \land  \eta  = 0.
\]

By our induction assumption, \( \eta  = y \land  z \) , where \( y = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i > 2}}{y}^{i}{e}_{i} \) and \( z = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i > 2}}{z}^{i}{e}_{i} \) . Now since \( n \geq  3,{e}_{1} \land  x \land  \eta  = 0 \) implies \( x \land  y \land  z = 0 \) , so that the vectors \( x, y, z \) are linearly dependent. Without loss of generality, we may assume that \( x = {c}_{1}y + {c}_{2}z \) for some

---

Note also that the Riemann curvature operator of \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{n - 2} \) is a nonnegative curvature operator of rank 1.

nodes.content:
LEMMA 11.39. If an algebraic curvature operator \( \mathbf{R} \) is 2-nonnegative, then we have the following.

(i) If we order the eigenvalues of \( \mathbf{R} \) so that \( {\mu }_{1} \leq  \cdots  \leq  {\mu }_{N} \) , then the eigenvalues \( {\mu }_{\beta } \) are nonnegative for \( \beta  \geq  2 \) and

(11.91)

\[
{\mu }_{1} \geq   - {\mu }_{2} \geq   - \frac{\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }{N - 2} =  - \frac{2\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4}.
\]

(ii) The scalar curvature \( \operatorname{Scal}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is nonnegative, with equality if and only if \( \mathbf{R} = 0 \) .

(iii) The Ricci curvature \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is nonnegative.

Moreover, the cone \( \mathfrak{C} \) of 2-nonnegative curvature operators contains the cone of geometrically nonnegative operators.

nodes.proof:
(i) Let \( {\left\{  {\widetilde{\omega }}_{\alpha }\right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1}^{N} \) be an orthonormal basis for \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) which satisfies \( \mathbf{R}\left( {\widetilde{\omega }}_{\alpha }\right)  = {\mu }_{\alpha }{\widetilde{\omega }}_{\alpha } \) . Since \( \mathbf{R} \) is 2-nonnegative, \( {\mu }_{\alpha } + {\mu }_{\beta } \geq  0 \) for any \( \alpha  \neq  \beta \) . Hence \( {\mu }_{\alpha } \geq  0 \) for \( \alpha  \geq  2 \) and the only possible negative eigenvalue is \( {\mu }_{1} \) . Since

\[
\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  = 1}}^{N}{\mu }_{\alpha } \geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  \geq  3}}{\mu }_{\alpha } \geq  \left( {N - 2}\right) {\mu }_{3},
\]

formula (11.91) follows.

(ii) Let \( {\left\{  {\omega }_{\alpha }\right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1}^{N} \Doteq  {\left\{  {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}\right\}  }_{i < j} \) be an orthonormal basis for \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) , where each \( \alpha \) corresponds to a pair \( \left( {i, j}\right) \) with \( i < j \) . From definition (11.39) we have

\[
\operatorname{Scal}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j}}{\mathbf{R}}_{ijij} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{\alpha }{\mathbf{R}}_{\alpha \alpha }.
\]

On the other hand, since \( \mathbf{R} \) is 2-nonnegative,

\[
0 \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  \neq  \beta }}\left( {{\mathbf{R}}_{\alpha \alpha } + {\mathbf{R}}_{\beta \beta }}\right)  = \left( {N - 1}\right) \operatorname{Scal}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) .
\]

Hence, if \( \operatorname{Scal}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = 0 \) , then \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\alpha \alpha } + {\mathbf{R}}_{\beta \beta } = 0 \) for all pairs \( \left( {\alpha ,\beta }\right) \) with \( \alpha  \neq  \beta \) , which implies that \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\alpha \alpha } = 0 \) for all \( \alpha \) , i.e., \( \mathbf{R} = 0 \) .

(iii) From definition (11.38) we have

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }_{ii} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i}}\left\langle  {\mathbf{R}\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{k}}\right) ,{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{k}}\right\rangle   = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\beta  \in  \mathcal{B}}}\left\langle  {\mathbf{R}\left( {\omega }_{\beta }\right) ,{\omega }_{\beta }}\right\rangle  ,
\]

where

\[
\mathcal{B} \Doteq  \{ \left( {1, i}\right) ,\left( {2, i}\right) ,\ldots ,\left( {i - 1, i}\right) ,\left( {i, i + 1}\right) ,\left( {i, i + 2}\right) ,\ldots ,\left( {i, n}\right) \} .
\]

---

\( {c}_{1},{c}_{2} \in  \mathbb{R} \) . We conclude

\[
\omega  = \left( {y + {c}_{2}{e}_{1}}\right)  \land  \left( {z - {c}_{1}{e}_{1}}\right)  \Doteq  v \land  w.
\]

---

Since \( \mathbf{R} \) is 2-nonnegative, \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\alpha \alpha } + {\mathbf{R}}_{\beta \beta } \geq  0 \) for any \( \alpha  \neq  \beta \) and \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\gamma \gamma } < 0 \) for at most one \( \gamma  \in  \{ 1,\ldots , N\} \) . This is enough to conclude that \( \operatorname{Rc}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }_{ii} \geq  0 \) for any orthonormal basis \( {\left\{  {e}_{j}\right\}  }_{j = 1}^{n} \) . In fact,

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }_{ii} \geq  \mathop{\inf }\limits_{\left\{  {\eta }_{k}\right\}  }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{{n - 1}}\left\langle  {\mathbf{R}\left( {\eta }_{k}\right) ,{\eta }_{k}}\right\rangle   \geq  {\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2} + \cdots  + {\mu }_{n - 1},
\]

where the infimum on the right-hand side is taken over all orthonormal bases \( {\left\{  {\eta }_{k}\right\}  }_{k = 1}^{n - 1} \) for \( \operatorname{span}\left\{  {{\omega }_{\beta } : \beta  \in  \mathcal{B}}\right\} \) and where \( {\mu }_{1} \leq  {\mu }_{2} \leq  \cdots  \leq  {\mu }_{N} \) are the ordered eigenvalues of \( \mathbf{R} \) . Hence we have

(11.92)

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }_{ii} \geq  \left( {n - 3}\right) {\mu }_{3} \geq  \left( {n - 3}\right) \left| {\mu }_{1}\right| ,
\]

which completes the proof of (iii).

Finally, the last statement in the lemma is clear since the cone of nonnegative curvature operators contains the cone of geometrically nonnegative operators.

nodes.proof:
We only need to show that \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) lies inside the tangent cone of the convex cone \( \mathfrak{C} \) for \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial \mathfrak{C} \) . Let \( {\left\{  {\omega }_{\alpha }\right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1}^{N} \) be an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of \( \mathbf{R} \) in \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) with corresponding eigenvalues \( {\mu }_{1} \leq  {\mu }_{2} \leq  \cdots  \leq \; {\mu }_{N} \) . Given \( \mathbf{S} \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) , let \( {\mathbf{S}}_{\alpha \beta } \doteq  \mathbf{S}\left( {{\omega }_{\alpha },{\omega }_{\beta }}\right) \) . If \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial \mathfrak{C} \) , then a vector \( \mathbf{S} \) at the point \( \mathbf{R} \) lies in the tangent cone of \( \mathfrak{C} \) if \( {\mathbf{S}}_{\alpha \alpha } + {\mathbf{S}}_{\beta \beta } \geq  0 \) for all \( \alpha ,\beta \) with \( \alpha  < \beta \) such that \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\alpha \alpha } + {\mathbf{R}}_{\beta \beta } = 0 \) .

---

\( {}^{20} \) By the proof it is clear that the same result holds on \( {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) (i.e., if we do not assume that \( \mathbf{R} \) satisfies the Bianchi identity).

---

If \( \mathbf{R} \) has nonnegative curvature operator, then \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) has nonnegative curvature operator and we are done. Otherwise, since the eigenvalues of \( \mathbf{R} \) are ordered, the set of all pairs \( \left( {\alpha ,\beta }\right) \) with \( \alpha  < \beta \) and \( {\mathbf{R}}_{\alpha \alpha } + {\mathbf{R}}_{\beta \beta } = 0 \) is equal to \( \{ \left( {1,2}\right) ,\ldots ,\left( {1, k}\right) \} \) for some \( k \geq  2 \) and we have \( - {\mathbf{R}}_{11} = {\mathbf{R}}_{22} = \; \cdots  = {\mathbf{R}}_{kk} > 0 \) . We then have for \( 2 \leq  \alpha  \leq  k \) ,

(11.95)

\[
{\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{11} + {\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{\alpha \alpha } = {\mu }_{1}^{2} + {\mu }_{\alpha }^{2} + 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\beta  < \gamma }}\left( {{\left( {c}_{1}^{\beta \gamma }\right) }^{2} + {\left( {c}_{\alpha }^{\beta \gamma }\right) }^{2}}\right) {\mu }_{\beta }{\mu }_{\gamma }.
\]

Since \( {\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2} \geq  0 \) , we have \( {\mu }_{\gamma } > 0 \) for all \( \gamma  \geq  2 \) . Hence for \( 2 \leq  \alpha  \leq  k \) ,

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\beta  < \gamma }}\left( {{\left( {c}_{1}^{\beta \gamma }\right) }^{2} + {\left( {c}_{\alpha }^{\beta \gamma }\right) }^{2}}\right) {\mu }_{\beta }{\mu }_{\gamma }
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{2 \leq  \beta  < \gamma }}{\left( {c}_{1}^{\beta \gamma }\right) }^{2}{\mu }_{\beta }{\mu }_{\gamma } + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{1 \leq  \beta  < \gamma }}{\left( {c}_{\alpha }^{\beta \gamma }\right) }^{2}{\mu }_{\beta }{\mu }_{\gamma }
\]

\[
\geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\gamma  > \alpha }}{\left( {c}_{1}^{\alpha \gamma }\right) }^{2}{\mu }_{\alpha }{\mu }_{\gamma } + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{2 \leq  \beta  < \alpha }}{\left( {c}_{1}^{\beta \alpha }\right) }^{2}{\mu }_{\beta }{\mu }_{\alpha } + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\gamma  \geq  2}}{\left( {c}_{\alpha }^{1\gamma }\right) }^{2}{\mu }_{1}{\mu }_{\gamma }
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\gamma  \geq  2}}{\left( {c}_{1}^{\alpha \gamma }\right) }^{2}\left( {{\mu }_{\alpha } + {\mu }_{1}}\right) {\mu }_{\gamma }
\]

(11.96)

\[
\geq  0\text{ , }
\]

where we used \( {c}_{1}^{1\gamma } = {c}_{1}^{\alpha \alpha } = 0 \) . Therefore \( {\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{11} + {\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{\alpha \alpha } \geq  0 \) for \( 2 \leq  \alpha  \leq  k \) , i.e., \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) lies in the tangent cone of \( \mathfrak{C} \) ; the proposition follows. \( {}^{21} \)

(11.97)

\[

\]

By Proposition 11.42 the convex cone \( \mathfrak{C} \) of 2-nonnegative operators \( \mathbf{R} \in \; {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) is preserved by the ODE corresponding to the PDE (11.97). Let \( \mathcal{K} \subset \; \mathcal{V} = {\operatorname{Sym}}^{2}\left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{T}^{ * }\mathcal{M}}\right) \) be the corresponding set of 2-nonnegative operators on \( \mathcal{M} \) (which is invariant under parallel translation and independent of time). By the weak maximum principle for systems, i.e., Theorem 10.13 when \( \mathcal{M} \) is closed and Theorem 12.34 in the next chapter when \( \mathcal{M} \) is noncompact, we conclude that if \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( 0\right) }\right)  \subset  \mathcal{K} \) , then \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \subset  \mathcal{K} \) , i.e., \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is 2-nonnegative for \( t \geq  0 \) .

(2) If in addition \( g\left( 0\right) \) has 2-positive curvature operator at some point in \( \mathcal{M} \) , then \( g\left( t\right) \) has 2-positive curvature operator everywhere for \( t > 0 \) .

nodes.proof:
First recall that by Proposition 11.44 we have

\[
{\mu }_{1}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right)  + {\mu }_{2}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right)  \geq  0
\]

for all \( t \geq  0 \) . We prove the parts of the proposition in reverse order.

(2) Let \( {x}_{0} \in  \mathcal{M} \) be a point such that \( \left( {{\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2}}\right) \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{0},0}\right)  > 0 \) . Given any point \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) , let \( \Omega  \subset  \mathcal{M} \) be a connected open set such that \( \bar{\Omega } \) is a compact manifold with smooth boundary and \( \Omega \) contains both \( {x}_{0} \) and \( y \) . Let \( {\varphi }_{1} \) to be a smooth nonnegative function satisfying

\[
{\varphi }_{1}\left( x\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2}}\right) \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,0}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  \bar{\Omega },{\varphi }_{1}\left( {x}_{0}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{4}\left( {{\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2}}\right) \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{0},0}\right)  > 0 \) , and \( {\varphi }_{1} = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega \) . Given a large constant \( A > 0 \) to be chosen later, there exists a solution \( f : \bar{\Omega } \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) of

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} = {\Delta f} - {Af}
\]

---

\( {}^{22} \) The reader may wish to first read the proof of Proposition 12.47.

---

with \( f\left( {x,0}\right)  = {\varphi }_{1}\left( x\right) \) and \( {\left. f\right| }_{\partial \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  } = 0 \) . By the strong maximum principle for scalars (Theorem 12.40), we have \( f\left( {x, t}\right)  > 0 \) on \( \Omega  \times  (0, T\rbrack \) . By the weak maximum principle we have

\[
f\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  \bar{\Omega }}}\left( {{\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2}}\right) \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,0}\right) \text{ on }\bar{\Omega } \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Define

\[
\overline{\operatorname{Rm}}\left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right)  + \left( {\varepsilon {e}^{At} - f\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) {\operatorname{id}}_{{\Lambda }^{2}}\left( x\right) ,
\]

where \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) . For \( A \) sufficiently large we have that for \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,{e}^{-{AT}}}\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\overline{\mathrm{{Rm}}} > \Delta \overline{\mathrm{{Rm}}} + {\overline{\mathrm{{Rm}}}}^{2} + {\overline{\mathrm{{Rm}}}}^{\# }.
\]

This implies that \( \overline{\operatorname{Rm}} \) is 2-positive on \( \bar{\Omega } \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for any \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,{e}^{-{AT}}}\right\rbrack \) (we leave this as an exercise for the reader). Taking the limit as \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) , we conclude that \( \operatorname{Rm} - f{\operatorname{id}}_{{\Lambda }^{2}} \) is 2-nonnegative on \( \bar{\Omega } \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( f\left( {y, t}\right)  > 0 \) , this implies that \( \operatorname{Rm} \) is 2-positive at \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) . This completes the proof of part (2).

(1) By part (2), if \( g\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) is 2-nonnegative everywhere in \( \mathcal{M} \) and 2-positive at a point in \( \mathcal{M} \) , then \( g\left( t\right) \) is 2-positive everywhere for \( t > {t}_{1} \) . Hence, if for some \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) we have \( {\mu }_{1}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) }\right)  + {\mu }_{2}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) }\right)  = 0 \) at some point (i.e., if \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) is not 2 -positive for some \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) ), then

\[
{\mu }_{1}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right)  + {\mu }_{2}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right)  = 0
\]

everywhere for \( t < {t}_{0} \) (which by continuity implies the same for \( t = {t}_{0} \) ). We claim that

\[
{\mu }_{1}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right)  = {\mu }_{2}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right)  = 0
\]

everywhere for \( t \leq  {t}_{0} \) . (The theorem then follows since this implies that \( \operatorname{Rm} \geq  0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , which in turn implies \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq  0 \) for all \( t \geq  0 \) since \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq  0 \) is preserved under the Ricci flow.)

To prove the claim, consider any \( \left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and let \( {\omega }_{1} \) and \( {\omega }_{2} \) be unit 2-forms at \( \left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) \) which are eigenvectors for \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) }\right) \) corresponding to \( {\mu }_{1}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) \) and \( {\mu }_{2}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) \) , respectively. Parallel translate \( {\omega }_{1} \) and \( {\omega }_{2} \) along geodesics emanating from \( {x}_{2} \) with respect to \( g\left( {t}_{2}\right) \) to define \( {\omega }_{1} \) and \( {\omega }_{2} \) in a space-time neighborhood of \( \left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , where \( {\omega }_{1} \) and \( {\omega }_{2} \) are independent of time. We have at \( \left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) \)

\[
0 \geq  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\omega }_{1},{\omega }_{1}}\right)  + \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\omega }_{2},{\omega }_{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right) \left( {{\omega }_{1},{\omega }_{1}}\right)  + \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right) \left( {{\omega }_{2},{\omega }_{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\Delta \mathrm{{Rm}} + {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{2} + {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{\# }}\right) \left( {{\omega }_{1},{\omega }_{1}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {\Delta \mathrm{{Rm}} + {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{2} + {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{\# }}\right) \left( {{\omega }_{2},{\omega }_{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \Delta \left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\omega }_{1},{\omega }_{1}}\right)  + \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\omega }_{2},{\omega }_{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }_{1}{\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) }^{2} + {\mu }_{2}{\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{\# }\right) \left( {{\omega }_{1},{\omega }_{1}}\right)  + \left( {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{\# }\right) \left( {{\omega }_{2},{\omega }_{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {\mu }_{1}{\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) }^{2} + {\mu }_{2}{\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) }^{2},
\]

where to obtain the last inequality we used (11.96) with \( \mathbf{R} \) replaced by \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \) and we used the fact that \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\omega }_{1},{\omega }_{1}}\right)  + \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\omega }_{2},{\omega }_{2}}\right)  \geq  0 \) while at \( \left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) \) we have \( = 0 \) . Hence

\[
{\mu }_{1}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) }\right) }\right)  = {\mu }_{2}\left( {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) }\right) }\right)  = 0.
\]

nodes.proof:
We again adopt the convention of omitting the subscripts \( a, b \) of \( {\ell }_{a, b},{D}_{a, b} \) , and \( {X}_{a, b} \) .

(i) By Lemma 11.26, in order to show that \( \ell \left( \mathfrak{C}\right) \) is preserved by the ODE, we need to show that for any \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial \mathfrak{C} \) the vector

\[
X\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {\ell }^{-1}\left( {\ell {\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }^{2} + \ell {\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }^{\# }}\right)  = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } + D\left( \mathbf{R}\right)
\]

is contained in the tangent cone of \( \mathfrak{C} \) . Since, by Proposition 11.42, \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) lies inside the tangent cone of \( \mathfrak{C} \) , it suffices to show that \( D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) also lies inside the tangent cone of \( \mathfrak{C} \) . However this is true for the following reasons. It follows from Lemma 11.40(ii) that \( D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the cone of geometrically nonnegative operators. \( {}^{23} \) By Exercise 11.43, \( D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is contained in the tangent cone of \( \mathfrak{C} \) .

(ii) First observe that \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) being transverse to the boundary of \( \ell \left( \mathfrak{C}\right) \) is equivalent to

\[
X\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } + D\left( \mathbf{R}\right)
\]

being transverse to \( \partial \mathfrak{C} \) . We have \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) is contained in the tangent cone of \( \mathfrak{C} \) . Thus, to show that \( X\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is transverse to \( \partial \mathfrak{C} \) , it suffices to show that \( D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is a positive curvature operator.

Recall that by (11.66),

\[
D\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {2a}\operatorname{Rc} \land  \operatorname{Rc} + 2{b}^{2}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2} \land  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{\sigma {b}^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\left( {-n\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {4b} + 2}\right) \mathbf{I},
\]

where \( \sigma  = \frac{1}{n}{\begin{Vmatrix}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \end{Vmatrix}}^{2} \cdot  {}^{24} \) We first assume that \( 0 < b < \bar{b} \) so that

\[
- n\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {4b} + 2 > 0.
\]

Case 1. \( \sigma  > 0 \) . Then \( D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is a positive curvature operator since \( {2a}\operatorname{Rc} \land  \operatorname{Rc} \) and \( 2{b}^{2}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{0}^{2} \land \) id are nonnegative and the coefficient in front of \( \mathbf{I} \) is positive. This implies \( X\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is transverse to \( \partial \mathfrak{C} \) .

Case 2. \( \sigma  = 0 \) . Then \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{0} = 0 \) , so that \( \operatorname{Rc} = \frac{1}{n}\operatorname{Scal} \cdot  \mathrm{{id}} > 0 \) since \( \mathbf{R} \neq  0 \) implies Scal \( > 0 \) . Hence

\[
D\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {2a}\operatorname{Rc} \land  \operatorname{Rc} = \frac{2a}{{n}^{2}}{\left( \operatorname{Scal}\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \land  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

is a positive curvature operator.

Hence \( X\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is transverse to \( \partial \mathfrak{C} \) when \( b < \bar{b} \) .

---

\( {}^{23} \) Hence \( D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the cone of nonnegative curvature operators.

\( {}^{24} \) Note that \( D\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is geometrically nonnegative.

---

Now we consider the case where \( b = \bar{b} \) . In this case, by part (iii) of the present proposition (whose proof is independent of part (ii)), we have \( {\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is a positive curvature operator since \( \mathbf{R} \neq  0 \) . This implies

\[
{X}_{a,\bar{b}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}^{-1}\left( {{\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }^{2} + {\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }^{\# }}\right)
\]

is a positive curvature operator and hence transverse to \( \partial \mathfrak{C} \) .

(iii) Finally we show that \( {\ell }_{a, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is a positive algebraic curvature operator when \( \mathbf{R} ≢ 0 \) and \( b \) takes the end value \( \bar{b} \) . We divide the proof of this statement into two cases. Let \( {\mu }_{1} \) be the smallest eigenvalue of \( \mathbf{R} \) . Recall

\[
{\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \mathbf{R} + 2\left( {a - \bar{b}}\right) \bar{\lambda }\mathbf{I} + 2\bar{b}\operatorname{Rc} \land  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

Case (iii-a). Suppose \( {\mu }_{1} \geq  0 \) . Then

\[
{\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > 0
\]

since \( a > \bar{b},\bar{b} > 0 \) , and \( \operatorname{Rc} \land \) id is nonnegative.

Case (iii-b). Suppose \( {\mu }_{1} < 0 \) . Let \( {\mu }_{1}\left( \widetilde{\mathbf{R}}\right) \) denote the smallest eigenvalue of the algebraic curvature operator \( \widetilde{\mathbf{R}} \) . From formula (11.92) we have \( \mathrm{{Rc}} \geq \; \left( {n - 3}\right) \left| {\mu }_{1}\right| \) . Hence from (11.94) we have \( {\mu }_{1}\left( {\mathrm{{Rc}} \land  \mathrm{{id}}}\right)  \geq  \left( {n - 3}\right) \left| {\mu }_{1}\right| \) . Now we have

\[
{\mu }_{1}\left( {{\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right)  > {\mu }_{1} + 2\left( {a - \bar{b}}\right) \bar{\lambda } + 2\bar{b}\left( {n - 3}\right) \left| {\mu }_{1}\right|
\]

\[
\geq  {\mu }_{1} + 2\bar{b}\left| {\mu }_{1}\right|  + 2\left( {a - \bar{b}}\right) \bar{\lambda }
\]

\[
= \left( {2\bar{b} - 1}\right) \left| {\mu }_{1}\right|  + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\bar{b}}^{2}\frac{2\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }{n},
\]

where here we have used that \( n \geq  4 \) and \( \bar{\lambda } = \frac{\operatorname{Scal}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }{n} = \frac{2\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }{n} \) . By elementary computations we have \( \bar{b} < \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{n\left( {n - 2}\right) }} \leq  \frac{1}{2} \) . We may further estimate using (11.91) that

\[
{\mu }_{1}\left( {{\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right)  >  - \left( {1 - 2\bar{b}}\right) \frac{2\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\bar{b}}^{2}\frac{2\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }{n}
\]

\[
= \left( {\frac{2}{{n}^{2}} - \frac{1}{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4}}\right) \left( {1 - 2\bar{b}}\right) 2\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)
\]

since \( {\left( n\left( n - 2\right) \bar{b} + 2\right) }^{2} = {2n}\left( {n - 2}\right)  + 4 \) , so that \( 2\left( {1 - 2\bar{b}}\right)  = n\left( {n - 2}\right) {\bar{b}}^{2} \) . That \( {\ell }_{a,\bar{b}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is a positive algebraic curvature operator now follows from the fact that \( \frac{2}{{n}^{2}} - \frac{1}{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4} \geq  0 \) if \( n \geq  4 \) .

\[

\[
= \frac{1}{{a}_{2}\left( \bar{s}\right) }{\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{W}} + \left( {\frac{1}{{a}_{2}\left( \bar{s}\right) } + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) }\right) {\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{I}} + \frac{1 + \frac{1}{2}\left( {n - 2}\right) }{{a}_{2}\left( \bar{s}\right) }{\mathbf{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0}}

\rightarrow  2\left( {n - 1}\right) {\mathbf{R}}_{\mathbf{I}}

as \( \bar{s} \rightarrow  \infty \) , we see that \( {\ell }_{{a}_{2}\left( \bar{s}\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\left( {C}_{\bar{s}}^{\prime }\right) \) converges to \( {\mathbb{R}}_{ + }\mathbf{I} \) as \( \bar{s} \rightarrow  \infty \) . LEMMA 11.53 (Preserved cones in dimension 3). The following closed convex cones are preserved by the ODE:

(1) \( {\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2} \geq  0 \) , (2) \( {\mu }_{2} + {\mu }_{3} \leq  C\left( {{\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2}}\right) \; \) for any given \( C > 0 \) , (3) \( {\mu }_{3} - {\mu }_{1} \leq  {K}_{1}\left( {{\mu }_{1} + {\mu }_{2} + {\mu }_{3}}\right) \; \) for any given \( {K}_{1} > 0 \) .

Proposition 11.55 (The cone \( {\ell }_{{a}_{1}\left( s\right) , s}\left( {C}_{s}\right) \) is preserved by the ODE). Suppose \( n \geq  4 \) . For \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack \) the sets

\[
{\ell }_{{a}_{1}\left( s\right) , s}\left( {C}_{s}\right) \text{ are preserved by the ODE }\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\text{ . }
\]

Moreover, for \( s \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack \) , the vector field \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) is transverse to the boundary of \( {\ell }_{{a}_{1}\left( s\right) , s}\left( {C}_{s}\right) \) , provided \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {\ell }_{{a}_{1}\left( s\right) , s}\left( {C}_{s}\right)  - \{ 0\} \) .

nodes.proof:
We now prove Proposition 11.55. For simplicity, let \( {a}_{1} = {a}_{1}\left( b\right) \) and \( {p}_{1} = {p}_{1}\left( b\right) \) . Clearly the sets \( {C}_{b} \) defined in (11.101) are \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant closed convex cones. For each \( b,{C}_{b} \) is the intersection of two \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant closed convex cones: \( \{ \mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} \geq  0\} \) and \( \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) }{n}}\right\} \) . By Lemma 11.26, it suffices to show that for any \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{b} \) , the vector

\[
{X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {\ell }_{{a}_{1}, b}^{-1}\left( {{\ell }_{{a}_{1}, b}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }^{2} + {\ell }_{{a}_{1}, b}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }^{\# }}\right)
\]

defined by (11.59) lies in the tangent cone of \( {C}_{b} \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) . The boundary \( \partial {C}_{b} \) consists of those \( \mathbf{R} \in  {C}_{b} \) such that

(1) there exists \( \phi  \in  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) such that \( \mathbf{R}\left( \phi \right)  = 0 \) or

(2) there exists \( V \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) with \( \left| V\right|  = 1 \) such that

\[
\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \left( V\right)  = {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) }{n}.
\]

For \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{b} \) , the tangent cone of \( {C}_{b} \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) is the set of \( \mathbf{S} \) such that

\[
\mathbf{S} \geq  \mathbf{0}\;\text{ and }\;\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{S}\right) \left( V\right)  \geq  {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{S}\right) }\right) }{n}
\]

for all \( V \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) with \( \left| V\right|  = 1 \) and \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \left( V\right)  = {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) }{n} \) .

We shall show, using Corollary 11.29, that for \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{b} - \{ 0\} \) we have (11.106)

\[
\text{ (I) }{X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > 0\text{ and (II) }\operatorname{Rc}\left( {{X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) \left( V\right)  > {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( {{X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) }\right) }{n}
\]

for all \( V \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) with \( \left| V\right|  = 1 \) and \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \left( V\right)  = {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) }{n} \) . Hence \( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{b} \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) .

Proof of (I). \( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > 0 \) . Noticing that \( \mathbf{R} \geq  0 \) implies \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \geq  0 \) , it suffices to show that \( {D}_{{a}_{1}, b} > 0 \) . By (11.67), the eigenvalues of \( {D}_{{a}_{1}, b} \) are given by

\[
{d}_{ij} = {\mathrm{I}}_{ij} + {\mathrm{{II}}}_{ij},
\]

where

(11.107)

\[
{\mathrm{I}}_{ij} \doteq  \left( {\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - 2\left( {{a}_{1} - b}\right) }\right) {\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + \bar{\lambda }}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{j} + \bar{\lambda }}\right)  + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} + {2b}}\right) {\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + 2{a}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}\right) \bar{\lambda } + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

and

(11.108)

\[
{\mathrm{{II}}}_{ij} \Doteq  \frac{\sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\left( {n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {{a}_{1} - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }\right) .
\]

We shall show that \( {\mathrm{I}}_{ij} > 0 \) and \( {\mathrm{{II}}}_{ij} \geq  0 \) for all \( i \neq  j \) . By (11.102),

\[
2\left( {{a}_{1} - b}\right)  = \frac{1 - {2b}}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2},
\]

so that (11.108) implies

\[
{\mathrm{{II}}}_{ij} = \frac{\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\left( {n{b}^{2} - \frac{1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) {b}^{2}\sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\frac{2 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}} \geq  0.
\]

Now we show the positivity of \( {\mathrm{I}}_{ij} \) . Note that from the definition (11.100) of \( {p}_{1} \) ,

\[
1 - {p}_{1} = \frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}} = \frac{2{a}_{1}}{\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} + {2b}}
\]

(or, equivalently, \( \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} + {2b} = \frac{2{a}_{1}}{1 - {p}_{1}} \) ). Note also that \( b > 0 \) implies \( {a}_{1} > 0 \) and \( {p}_{1} > 0 \) . Hence if \( \mathbf{R} \neq  0 \) (which implies \( \bar{\lambda } > 0 \) ), then (11.107) implies

\[
{\mathrm{I}}_{ij} = \frac{2{a}_{1}}{1 - {p}_{1}}{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + 2{a}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}\right) \bar{\lambda } + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{a}_{1}\left( {\frac{1}{1 - {p}_{1}}{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + \left( {1 - {p}_{1}}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}\right) \bar{\lambda }}\right)  + 2{a}_{1}{p}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
> \frac{2{a}_{1}}{1 - {p}_{1}}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + \left( {1 - {p}_{1}}\right) \bar{\lambda }}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{j} + \left( {1 - {p}_{1}}\right) \bar{\lambda }}\right)  \geq  0
\]

since \( \operatorname{Rc} \geq  {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( \operatorname{Rc}\right) }{n} \) implies \( {\lambda }_{i} + \bar{\lambda } \geq  {p}_{1}\bar{\lambda } \) for all \( i \) .

Proof of (II). Now we prove that the Rc pinching condition in (11.106) holds. Suppose that

(11.109)

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }_{ii} = {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) }{n},\;\text{ i.e., }{\lambda }_{i} =  - \left( {1 - {p}_{1}}\right) \bar{\lambda }
\]

for some \( i \) . (Otherwise there is nothing to prove. For convenience of notation we have arbitrarily chosen \( i \) such that the \( i \) -th basis vector is a vector \( V \) as in (11.106).) We need to show that

(11.110)

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }_{ii} - {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{Scal}\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }{n} > 0.
\]

By (11.108) and

\[
{\mathrm{I}}_{ij} \geq  2{a}_{1}{p}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right) ,
\]

we have

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( {D}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }_{ii} = {r}_{i} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  i}}{d}_{ij} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  i}}\left( {{\mathrm{I}}_{ij} + {\mathrm{{II}}}_{ij}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  2{a}_{1}\left( {n - 1}\right) {p}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + n{b}^{2}\sigma
\]

\[
+ \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) \sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\left( {n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {{a}_{1} - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }\right) .
\]

Also, since \( \mathbf{R} \geq  0 \) (actually we only need \( \mathbf{R} \) to have nonnegative sectional curvature) and \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{kk} \geq  {p}_{1}\bar{\lambda } \) ,

(11.111)

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{ii} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{kk}{\mathbf{R}}_{ikik} \geq  {p}_{1}\bar{\lambda }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\mathbf{R}}_{ikik} \geq  {p}_{1}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}.
\]

Since \( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b} = {D}_{{a}_{1}, b}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  + {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) , by combining the above formulas, we have

(11.112)

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }_{ii} \geq  {p}_{1}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {n - 1}\right) {p}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + n{b}^{2}\sigma
\]

\[
+ \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) \sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\left( {n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {{a}_{1} - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

(11.113)

\[
= {p}_{1}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {n - 1}\right) {p}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\lambda }_{i}^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{2} + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {2{a}_{1}b - {a}_{1} + b}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\sigma
\]

(11.114)

\[
= {p}_{1}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {n - 1}\right) {p}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\lambda }_{i}^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {\frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}} + {2b} - 1}\right) \sigma .
\]

We next compute the scalar curvature of the algebraic curvature operator \( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b} \) . By (11.55), i.e., \( \operatorname{Rc}{\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{ii} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{kk}{\mathbf{R}}_{ikik} \) , we have that

\[
\operatorname{Scal}\left( {{\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\left| {\operatorname{Rc}}_{kk}\right| }^{2} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\left( {\lambda }_{k} + \bar{\lambda }\right) }^{2}
\]

(11.115)

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\lambda }_{k}^{2} + n{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} = {n\sigma } + n{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}.
\]

Using (11.68), we compute

\[
\operatorname{Scal}\left( {D}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{i}{r}_{i}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{i}\left( {-{2b}{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {n - 2}\right) \bar{\lambda }{\lambda }_{i} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {n - 1}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{n\sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\left( {{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {{a}_{1} - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }\right)
\]

(11.116)

\[
=  - {2bn\sigma } + 2{a}_{1}n\left( {n - 1}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{n\sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\left( {{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {{a}_{1} - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }\right)
\]

(11.117)

\[
= 2{a}_{1}n\left( {n - 1}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} - {n\sigma } + \frac{n{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\sigma .
\]

Combining this with (11.115), we have

(11.118)

\[
\frac{\operatorname{Scal}\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }{n} = \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\sigma .
\]

Note that both formulas (11.116) and (11.118) hold for any \( {a}_{1} \neq   - \frac{1}{2\left( {n - 1}\right) } \) and do not use the relation (11.102).

Combining (11.114) and (11.118), we have

\[
\mathrm{{Rc}}{\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }_{ii} - {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{Scal}\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }{n}
\]

\[
\geq  {p}_{1}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + 2{a}_{1}\left( {n - 1}\right) {p}_{1}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + \left( {\frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}} + {2b} - 1}\right) \sigma
\]

\[
- {p}_{1}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} - {p}_{1}\frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}}\sigma
\]

\[
= {p}_{1}\left( {{p}_{1} - 1}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + \left( {\left( {1 - {p}_{1}}\right) \frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}} + {2b} - 1}\right) \sigma .
\]

By the definition (11.100) of \( {p}_{1} \) ,

\[
{p}_{1}\left( {{p}_{1} - 1}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\lambda }_{i}^{2} = \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}\left( {-{\left( 1 - {p}_{1}\right) }^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + {\lambda }_{i}^{2}}\right) .
\]

On the other hand, by (11.102) and (11.100), we have

\[
\left( {1 - {p}_{1}}\right) \frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{1}} + {2b} - 1
\]

\[
= \frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{\left( {{nb} + 1}\right) \left( {\left( {n - 2}\right) b + 1}\right) } + {2b} - 1
\]

\[
= \frac{{2n}{b}^{2}}{{nb} + 1}\text{ . }
\]

Hence

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }_{ii} - {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{Scal}\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }{n}
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}\left( {-{\left( 1 - {p}_{1}\right) }^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + {\lambda }_{i}^{2}}\right)  + \frac{{2n}{b}^{2}}{{nb} + 1}\sigma .
\]

By (11.109) we have \( {\lambda }_{i} =  - \left( {1 - {p}_{1}}\right) \bar{\lambda } \) and hence

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }_{ii} - {p}_{1}\frac{\operatorname{Scal}\left( {X}_{{a}_{1}, b}\right) }{n} \geq  \frac{{2n}{b}^{2}}{{nb} + 1}\sigma  > 0.
\]

This proves (11.110) and therefore completes the proof of Proposition 11.55.

Proposition 11.56. For each \( \bar{s} \in  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) , the set

\[
{\ell }_{{a}_{2}\left( \bar{s}\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\left( {C}_{\bar{s}}^{\prime }\right) \text{ is preserved by the ODE }\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\text{ . }
\]

Moreover, \( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) is transverse to the boundary of \( {\ell }_{{a}_{2}\left( \bar{s}\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\left( {C}_{\bar{s}}\right) \) at all points on the boundary with \( \mathbf{R} \neq  0 \) .
