nodes.proof:
We now prove Proposition 11.56. That is, we prove \( {\ell }_{{a}_{2}\left( \bar{s}\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\left( {C}_{\bar{s}}^{\prime }\right) \) is preserved by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) for \( \bar{s} \in  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) . By the same reasoning as in Proposition 11.55 it suffices to show that for \( s \geq  0 \) and \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{s}^{\prime } - \{ 0\} \) , we have

(I) \( {D}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > 0 \) and

(II) if \( i \) is such that \( \operatorname{Rc}{\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }_{ii} = {p}_{2}\left( s\right) \frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) }{n} \) , we have

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( {X}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \right) }_{ii} > {p}_{2}\left( s\right) \frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( {{X}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) }\right) }{n}.
\]

Proof of (I). \( {D}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}} > 0 \) . Using Corollary 11.29 with \( a = \frac{1 + s}{2} \) and \( b = \frac{1}{2} \) (so that \( 2\left( {a - b}\right)  = s \) and \( 1 - {2b} = 0 \) ), we have that the eigenvalues of \( {D}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}} \) are given by

\[
{d}_{ij} = \left( {\frac{n - 2}{4} - s}\right) {\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + \left( {1 + s}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{i} + \bar{\lambda }}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{j} + \bar{\lambda }}\right)  + \frac{1}{4}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
- \frac{ns}{{4n} + 4\left( {n - 1}\right) s}\sigma
\]

(11.119)

\[
= \frac{n + 2}{4}{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + \left( {1 + s}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {1 + s}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}\right) \bar{\lambda } + \frac{1}{4}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
- \frac{ns}{{4n} + 4\left( {n - 1}\right) s}\sigma
\]

Since \( {\lambda }_{j} + \bar{\lambda } \geq  {p}_{2}\bar{\lambda } \) for all \( j \) , we can estimate \( \sigma  = \frac{1}{n}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{j}{\lambda }_{j}^{2} \) from above in terms of \( {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} \) . In particular, consider the optimization problem for \( \sigma  = \; \sigma \left( {{\lambda }_{1},\ldots ,{\lambda }_{n}}\right) \) under the constraint \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{j}{\lambda }_{j} = 0 \) . Since the functional \( \sigma \) has strictly positive Hessian, it achieves its maximum on the boundary of the set

\[
\left\{  {\left( {{\lambda }_{1},\ldots ,{\lambda }_{n}}\right)  : {\lambda }_{j} + \bar{\lambda } \geq  {p}_{2}\bar{\lambda }\text{ for all }j\text{ and }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{j}{\lambda }_{j} = 0}\right\}
\]

and furthermore at the vertices. Therefore the extremal points of \( \sigma \) are \( \left( {-\left( {1 - {p}_{2}}\right) \bar{\lambda },\ldots , - \left( {1 - {p}_{2}}\right) \bar{\lambda },\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 - {p}_{2}}\right) \bar{\lambda }}\right) \) and its permutations. Hence

(11.120)

\[
\sigma  \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( 1 - {p}_{2}\left( s\right) \right) }^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} = \frac{{16}\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{\left( n + 2 + 4s\right) }^{2}}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}.
\]

Now also recall that \( 1 - {p}_{2}\left( s\right)  = \frac{4}{n + 2 + {4s}} \) , so that

(11.121)

\[
{\lambda }_{i} + \frac{4\bar{\lambda }}{n + 2} \geq  {\lambda }_{i} + \frac{4\bar{\lambda }}{n + 2 + {4s}} \geq  0,
\]

where the second inequality follows from \( {D}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > 0 \) . Motivated by this, we have by (11.119) and (11.120),

\[
{d}_{ij} \geq  \frac{n + 2}{4}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + \frac{4\bar{\lambda }}{n + 2}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{j} + \frac{4\bar{\lambda }}{n + 2}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {\frac{n - 2}{n + 2} + s}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + s\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}\right) \bar{\lambda }
\]

\[
- \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) {ns}}{\left( {n + \left( {n - 1}\right) s}\right) {\left( n + 2 + 4s\right) }^{2}}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}.
\]

Therefore, throwing away the first two terms on the RHS above and using (11.121), we have

(11.122)

\[
{d}_{ij} \geq  \left( {\frac{n - 2}{n + 2} + s - \frac{8s}{n + 2 + {4s}} - \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) {ns}}{\left( {n + \left( {n - 1}\right) s}\right) {\left( n + 2 + 4s\right) }^{2}}}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2}
\]

\[
\doteq  C\left( {n, s}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2}
\]

Since \( n \geq  3 \geq  1 \) and \( s \geq  0 \) ,

\[
C\left( {n, s}\right)  \geq  \frac{n - 2}{n + 2} + s - \frac{8s}{n + 2 + {4s}} - \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) s}{\left( {n + 2}\right) \left( {n + 2 + {4s}}\right) }
\]

\[
= \frac{4{s}^{2} + \left( {n - 6 - \frac{4}{n + 2}}\right) s + n - 2}{n + 2 + {4s}}.
\]

In particular, if \( n = 3 \) , then \( 4{s}^{2} + \left( {n - 6 - \frac{4}{n + 2}}\right) s + n - 2 = 4{s}^{2} - \frac{19}{5}s + 1 > 0 \) so that \( C\left( {3, s}\right)  > 0 \) . Now, given \( s \geq  0 \) , the function \( 4{s}^{2} + \left( {n - 6 - \frac{4}{n + 2}}\right) s + \; n - 2 \) is monotone increasing in \( n \) . Hence \( C\left( {n, s}\right)  > 0 \) for all \( n \geq  3 \) and \( s \geq  0 \) . Therefore \( {d}_{ij} > 0 \) ; this completes the proof of (I).

Proof of (II). By formula (11.118) in the proof of Proposition 11.55 with \( {a}_{1} \) replaced by \( {a}_{2}\left( s\right) \) and \( b = \frac{1}{2} \) (see the comment after formula (11.118)), we have

\[
\frac{\operatorname{Scal}\left( {X}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\right) }{n} = \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{2}\left( s\right) }\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) \frac{1}{2}\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {a}_{2}\left( s\right) }\sigma
\]

\[
= \left( {n + \left( {n - 1}\right) s}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{{n}^{2}\sigma }{{4n} + 4\left( {n - 1}\right) s}.
\]

Using Corollary 11.29 with \( a = {a}_{2}\left( s\right)  = 1 + \frac{s}{2} \) and \( b = \frac{1}{2} \) , we have

\[
{r}_{i} =  - {\lambda }_{i}^{2} + \left( {1 + s}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) \bar{\lambda }{\lambda }_{i} + \left( {1 + s}\right) \left( {n - 1}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{{n}^{2}\sigma }{{4n} + 4\left( {n - 1}\right) s}.
\]

Using the estimate (note that \( \mathbf{R} \) has nonnegative sectional curvature and \( \left. {{\operatorname{Rc}}_{kk} \geq  {p}_{2}\left( s\right) \bar{\lambda }}\right) \)

(11.123)

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{ii} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\operatorname{Rc}}_{kk}{\mathbf{R}}_{ikik} \geq  {p}_{2}\left( s\right) \bar{\lambda }{\operatorname{Rc}}_{ii} \geq  {p}_{2}^{2}\left( s\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2},
\]

to prove the Rc pinching condition

\[
\mathrm{{Rc}}{\left( {D}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\right) }_{ii} + \mathrm{{Rc}}{\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{ii}
\]

\[
= \operatorname{Rc}{\left( {X}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\right) }_{ii} > {p}_{2}\frac{\operatorname{Scal}\left( {X}_{{a}_{2}\left( s\right) ,\frac{1}{2}}\right) }{n},
\]

where \( i \) is such that \( {\lambda }_{i} =  - \left( {1 - {p}_{2}}\right) \bar{\lambda } \) , it is suffices to show that

\[
- {\lambda }_{i}^{2} + \left( {1 + s}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) \bar{\lambda }{\lambda }_{i} + \left( {1 + s}\right) \left( {n - 1}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{{n}^{2}\sigma }{{4n} + 4\left( {n - 1}\right) s} + {p}_{2}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}
\]

\[
> {p}_{2}\left( {\left( {n + \left( {n - 1}\right) s}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{{n}^{2}\sigma }{{4n} + 4\left( {n - 1}\right) s}}\right) \text{ . }
\]

We leave it to the reader to carry out this easy verification. This completes the proof of Proposition 11.56.

DEFINITION 11.59 (Pinching set). We say that a subset \( Z \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) is a pinching set if

(1) \( Z \) is closed and convex,

(2) \( Z \) is \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant,

(3) \( Z \) is preserved by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) ,

(4) there exist \( \delta  > 0 \) and \( K < \infty \) such that

\[
\left| \widetilde{\mathbf{R}}\right|  \leq  K{\left| \mathbf{R}\right| }^{1 - \delta }
\]

for all \( \mathbf{R} \in  Z \) , where \( \widetilde{\mathbf{R}} \doteq  \mathbf{R} - \frac{1}{N}\operatorname{trace}\mathbf{R} \cdot  \mathbf{I} \) is the trace-free part of R.

REMARK 11.60. In this regard we note that given a solution \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) , \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , to the Ricci flow, one way to consider Uhlenbeck’s trick (see Section 2 of Chapter 6 in Volume One) is to define time-dependent bundle isometries

\[
\iota \left( t\right)  : \left( {T\mathcal{M}, g\left( 0\right) }\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {T\mathcal{M}, g\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

by

(11.124)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\iota \left( t\right)  = {\operatorname{Rc}}_{g\left( t\right) } \circ  \iota \left( t\right) \;\text{ and }\;\iota \left( 0\right)  = {\operatorname{id}}_{T\mathcal{M}},
\]

where we raise an index on the Ricci tensor so that \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{g\left( t\right) } : T\mathcal{M} \rightarrow  T\mathcal{M} \) .

By the Weinberger-Hamilton maximum principle for systems, if we have \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( {g}_{0}\right)  \subset  \bar{Z} \) , then the solution of the Ricci flow \( g\left( t\right) \) , with \( g\left( 0\right)  = {g}_{0} \) , satisfies

\[
\iota {\left( t\right) }^{ * }\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  \subset  \bar{Z}
\]

for \( t \geq  0 \) , where the \( \iota \left( t\right) \) are defined by (11.124). In particular, we then have the pinching estimate

(11.125)

\[
\left| \widetilde{\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  \leq  K{\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{1 - \delta }.
\]

This estimate is sufficient (but, as we shall see below, not necessary) to prove convergence of the normalized Ricci flow to a constant positive sectional curvature metric.

THEOREM 11.64 (Existence of a generalized pinching set). Let

\[
{C}_{\clubsuit }{\left( s\right) }_{s \in  \lbrack 0,1)} \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)
\]

be a continuous family of closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant cones of maximum dimension, such that \( {C}_{4}\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) is contained in the half-space of curvature operators with positive scalar curvature for all \( s \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) . Suppose that for \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) the vector field \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) for all \( s \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) . Then for any \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) and \( {h}_{0} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) there exists a closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subset \( F \subset \; {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) with the following properties:

(1) \( F \) is preserved by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = {\mathbf{R}}^{2} + {\mathbf{R}}^{\# } \) ;

(2) \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( \varepsilon \right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \leq  {h}_{0}}\right\}   \subset  F \subset  {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( \varepsilon \right) \) ;

(3) \( \overline{F \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right) } \) is compact (i.e., bounded) for all \( s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) .

nodes.proof:
Fix any \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) and \( {h}_{0} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) . Define the set \( F \) to be the intersection of all closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subsets of \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) satisfying properties (1) and (2) in the statement of Theorem 11.64. We want to show that \( F \) is the desired generalized pinching set. Since \( {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( \varepsilon \right) \) is such a set, \( F \) is a well-defined closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subset contained in \( {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( \varepsilon \right) \) .

(I) Suppose \( {\mathbf{R}}_{0} \in  F \) and \( \mathbf{R}\left( t\right) \) is a solution of the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) with \( \mathbf{R}\left( 0\right)  = {\mathbf{R}}_{0} \) . Then for any closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subset \( G \) of \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) satisfying properties (1) and (2), \( {}^{29} \) we have \( \mathbf{R}\left( t\right)  \in  G \) . Hence, by definition, \( \mathbf{R}\left( t\right)  \in  F \) . Thus property (1) holds for \( F \) .

(II) It is also clear that property (2) holds for \( F \) , i.e.,

\[
{C}_{\text{ ♣ }}\left( \varepsilon \right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \leq  {h}_{0}}\right\}   \subset  F.
\]

(III) It remains to prove property (3). Suppose, with the goal of obtaining a contradiction, that property (3) is false for \( F \) for some \( s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) . Let \( {s}_{0} \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) be the infimum of all \( s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) for which property (3) is false for \( F \) , i.e.,

\[
{s}_{0} \Doteq  \inf \{ s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) : F \smallsetminus  {C}_{ \clubsuit  }\left( s\right) \text{ is unbounded }\} .
\]

Then there exists a sequence \( {\left\{  {s}_{i}\right\}  }_{i \in  \mathbb{N}} \) with \( {s}_{i} \rightarrow  {s}_{0} \) such that \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( {s}_{i}\right) \) is unbounded for all \( i \) . We shall obtain the contradiction from showing that \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{4}\left( s\right) \) is bounded for any \( s \) sufficiently close to \( {s}_{0} \) .

For \( s \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) and \( \delta  > 0 \) define

\[
{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  \Doteq  \text{ the cone over the set }
\]

\[
\left\{  {\mathbf{R} \in  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right)  : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = 1,\operatorname{dist}\left( {\mathbf{R},\partial {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right) }\right)  \geq  \delta }\right\}  ,
\]

which is a slightly smaller cone contained in \( {C}_{4}\left( s\right) \) (with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\delta  \rightarrow  0}}{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  = \; \left. {{C}_{4}\left( s\right) }\right) \) . For \( \delta , h > 0 \) define

\[
{T}_{h}{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  \Doteq  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) ,\operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  h}\right\}  ,
\]

which is, as noted in [43], a 'truncated shifted cone'. We leave it to the reader to show that both \( {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) and \( {T}_{h}{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) are closed, convex, and \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant (convexity is the main issue). \( {}^{30} \)

(1) When \( \delta \) is sufficiently small, the cones \( {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) are preserved by the ODE. For any \( s \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) there exists \( {\delta }_{0} = {\delta }_{0}\left( s\right)  > 0 \) such that for all \( \delta  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\delta }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  - \{ 0\} \) the vector \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) .

This fact follows from

(i) \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\delta  \rightarrow  0}}\partial {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right)  = \partial {C}_{\Phi }\left( s\right) \) ,

(ii) the continuity of \( Q \) ,

(iii) our assumption that for \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} , Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of tangent cone of \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) , and

(iv) the fact that \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) is homogeneous of degree 2, i.e., \( Q\left( {c\mathbf{R}}\right)  = \; {c}^{2}Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) for all \( c \geq  0 \) (which addresses the issue of the noncompactness of the cones).

---

\( {}^{29} \) Note that we do not use property (2) here.

\( {}^{30} \) Note that the set \( \sum  \doteq  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} \in  {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right)  : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = 1}\right\} \) is convex. To prove the convexity of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) , one just needs to show that

\[
\{ \mathbf{R} \in  \sum  : \operatorname{dist}\left( {\mathbf{R},\partial \sum }\right)  \geq  \delta \}
\]

is convex. The convexity of \( {T}_{h}{C}_{\delta }\left( s\right) \) also follows easily.

---

(2) Truncated shifted cones are preserved by the ODE. There exists \( \bar{h} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) (in particular, for \( \bar{h} \) sufficiently large) such that the set

\[
{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  = \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}   \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  \bar{h}\}
\]

is preserved by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) for all \( \delta  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\delta }_{0}\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\rbrack \) .

First note that

\[
\partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \subset  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}   \cup  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\} .
\]

We have

\[
\operatorname{trace}Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = {\left| \operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \right| }^{2} \geq  \frac{4}{n}{\left( \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \right) }^{2} \geq  \frac{4}{n}{\bar{h}}^{2} > 0
\]

for \( \mathbf{R} \in  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) (note that \( \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}\left( {\operatorname{Rc}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right) \) ).

Case (a). Hence for \( \mathbf{R} \) with \( \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h} \) the vector \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  \bar{h}\} \) . This implies that for

\[
\mathbf{R} \in  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \smallsetminus  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}   \subset  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\} ,
\]

the vector \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) , which is the half-space \( \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  0\} \) .

Case (b). Now assume

\[
\mathbf{R} \in  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\}
\]

\[
\subset  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}
\]

so that in particular trace \( \left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > \bar{h} \) . In this case the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) is the same as the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \) (after shifting the vertex by \( \mathbf{I} \) ).

Let \( {\eta }_{0} \) be the infimum of the distance from \( Q\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right) \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) among \( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime } \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) with \( \operatorname{trace}\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right)  = 1 \) . Since by part (1), \( {\eta }_{0} > 0 \) , we have that the distance from \( Q\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right) \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) grows quadratically; in particular, it is at least

(11.128)

\[
{\eta }_{0}{\left( \operatorname{trace}\left( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right) \right) }^{2} \geq  c{\eta }_{0}{\left| {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime }\right| }^{2}
\]

for all \( {\mathbf{R}}^{\prime } \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) , where \( c > 0 \) . For \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in \; \left. {\partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\} \)

(i) let \( {d}_{1}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) be the distance of \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) and

(ii) let \( {d}_{2}\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) be the distance of \( Q\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I}}\right) \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \) , so that by (11.128)

\[
{d}_{2}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  c{\eta }_{0}{\left| \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I}\right| }^{2} \geq  \frac{1}{2}c{\eta }_{0}{\left| \mathbf{R}\right| }^{2}
\]

(with the last inequality holding for \( \bar{h} \) large enough). Next observe that

\[
\left| {Q\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I}}\right)  - Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) }\right|  = \left| {2\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} + 2\mathbf{R}\# \mathbf{I} + \mathbf{I}\# \mathbf{I}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {A}_{1}\left| \mathbf{R}\right|
\]

for some constant \( {A}_{1} < \infty \) . Hence, by the triangle inequality and the above estimates,

\[
{d}_{1}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \geq  {d}_{2}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  - \left| {Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  - Q\left( {\mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I}}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}c{\eta }_{0}{\left| \mathbf{R}\right| }^{2} - {A}_{1}\left| \mathbf{R}\right|
\]

so that \( {d}_{1}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  > 0 \) provided that \( \left| \mathbf{R}\right| \) is sufficiently large. Thus \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) .

Case (c). Finally, if

\[
\mathbf{R} \in  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{I} \in  \partial {C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right\}   \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\}  \subset  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right) ,
\]

then by the arguments in proving Cases (a) and (b), it follows that \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) at \( \mathbf{R} \) .

By Cases (a),(b), and (c), we have shown that for all \( \mathbf{R} \in  \partial \left( {{T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right) \) , the vector \( Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) .

(3) Given any \( \bar{h} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) , there exists \( \delta  > 0 \) (in particular, for \( \delta \) sufficiently small) such that the set \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}}\right\} \) is contained in the interior of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}}\right\} \) as subsets of the hyperplane \( \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}}\right\} \) . This is geometrically clear from considering the limit as \( \delta  \rightarrow  0 \) .

(4) By part (3), for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small and for \( s \) close enough to \( {s}_{0} \) , \( {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( s\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\} \) is contained in the interior of \( {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \; \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\} \) . We claim that by the definition of \( {s}_{0} \) , for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small there exists \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {\varepsilon ,{s}_{0}}\right) \) (except when \( {s}_{0} = \varepsilon \) , where we let \( \bar{s} = {s}_{0} \) ) and \( k \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) large enough such that

(11.129)

\( F \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = k\bar{h}\}  \subset  {C}_{\Phi }\left( \bar{s}\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = k\bar{h}\}  \subset  k \cdot  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) , \) that is,

\[
\frac{1}{k}F \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\}  \subset  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( \bar{s}\right)  \cap  \{ \mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  = \bar{h}\}  \subset  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) .
\]

(a) If \( {s}_{0} = \varepsilon  = \bar{s} \) , then the claim is clear since \( F \subset  {C}_{\Phi }\left( \varepsilon \right) \) .

(b) If \( {s}_{0} > \varepsilon \) , then \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{\Phi }\left( \bar{s}\right) \) is compact for all \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {\varepsilon ,{s}_{0}}\right) \) . Therefore, for each \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {\varepsilon ,{s}_{0}}\right) \) , there exists \( {k}_{0} \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) such that the first inclusion in (11.129) holds for all \( k \geq  {k}_{0} \) .

(5) By part (4), for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small and \( k \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) large enough, the set

\[
{F}^{\prime } \Doteq  \left( {F \cap  \left\{  {\mathbf{R} : \operatorname{trace}\left( \mathbf{R}\right)  \leq  k\bar{h}}\right\}  }\right)  \cup  \left( {F \cap  k \cdot  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right) }\right)
\]

is closed, convex, \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant, and preserved by the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{R} = Q\left( \mathbf{R}\right) \) . In particular, the convexity of \( {F}^{\prime } \) follows from the inclusion (11.129). Now clearly \( {F}^{\prime } \subset  F \) . On the other hand, by the definition of \( F \) (in particular, its minimality), we have \( F \subset  {F}^{\prime } \) . Hence for \( \delta  > 0 \) sufficiently small and \( k \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) large enough,

\[
F = {F}^{\prime }\text{ . }
\]

(6) Since the set \( k \cdot  {T}_{\bar{h}}{C}_{\delta }\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \smallsetminus  {C}_{\delta /2}\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) is bounded, we have that the set \( {F}^{\prime } \smallsetminus  {C}_{\delta /2}\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) is bounded. On the other hand, clearly

\[
{F}^{\prime } \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right)  \subset  {F}^{\prime } \smallsetminus  {C}_{\delta /2}\left( {s}_{0}\right)
\]

for any \( s \) close enough to \( {s}_{0} \) . Hence the set \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right)  = {F}^{\prime } \smallsetminus  {C}_{\clubsuit }\left( s\right) \) is bounded for any \( s \) close enough to \( {s}_{0} \) . This contradicts the definition of \( {s}_{0} \) since there exists a sequence \( {\left\{  {s}_{i}\right\}  }_{i \in  \mathbb{N}} \) with \( {s}_{i} \rightarrow  {s}_{0} \) such that \( F \smallsetminus  {C}_{ \bullet  }\left( {s}_{i}\right) \) is not bounded for all \( i \) .

THEOREM 12.1 (WMP on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) under exponential quadratic growth). If \( u : {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) , where \( u \in  {C}^{2,1}\left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  (0, T\rbrack }\right)  \cap  {C}^{0}\left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) , is a solution to the heat equation on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) such that

(12.2)

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  A{e}^{B{\left| x\right| }^{2}}\;\text{ on }{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack
\]

for some constants \( A, B < \infty \) , then

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }}u\left( {x, t}\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}}}u\left( {x,0}\right) .
\]

nodes.proof:
Proof. If \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}}}u\left( {x,0}\right)  = \infty \) , then there is nothing to prove. Below we assume that \( D \Doteq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}}}u\left( {x,0}\right)  < \infty \) . The idea is to use the standard exponential quadratically growing solution to the heat equation, which is dual to the fundamental solution, as a barrier function so that we can apply the second derivative test to a modification of \( u \) which attains its maximum on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) .

Consider the function \( {}^{3} \)

(12.3)

\[
v\left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  u\left( {x, t}\right)  - \frac{\delta }{{\left( {T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon  - t\right) }^{n/2}}{e}^{\frac{{\left| x\right| }^{2}}{4\left( {{T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon  - t}\right) }},
\]

where \( \delta ,\varepsilon  > 0 \) , which is a solution to the heat equation on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left( {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right) \) . Choose \( {T}^{\prime } \leq  T \) small enough so that \( {4B}{T}^{\prime } < 1 \) , which implies that the coefficient in the exponential on the RHS of (12.3) satisfies

\[
\frac{1}{4\left( {{T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon  - t}\right) } \geq  \frac{1}{4\left( {{T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon }\right) } > B
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) sufficiently small. By (12.2) this implies that \( v\left( {x, t}\right)  \rightarrow   - \infty \) as \( \left| x\right|  \rightarrow  \infty \) uniformly for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right) {.}^{4} \) Let

\[
H\left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  v\left( {x, t}\right)  - D - {\delta t}
\]

We claim that \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}}}H\left( {x, t}\right)  < 0 \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) and \( \delta ,\varepsilon  > 0 \) . Assuming the claim, we have

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack  }}v\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}}}u\left( {x,0}\right)  + \delta {T}^{\prime }.
\]

Taking the limit as \( \delta  \rightarrow  0 \) , we have

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack  }}u\left( {x, t}\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}}}u\left( {x,0}\right) .
\]

Repeating this argument on the time intervals \( \left\lbrack  {{T}^{\prime },\min \left\{  {2{T}^{\prime }, T}\right\}  }\right\rbrack \) , etc., we obtain the theorem assuming the claim.

Now we turn to proving the claim (compare to the proof of Theorem 4.2 on p. 94 of Volume One). Suppose that the claim is false. Then, since

---

\( {}^{3} \) Qualitatively, the solution \( {\left( {T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon  - t\right) }^{-n/2}\exp \left( \frac{{\left| x\right| }^{2}}{4\left( {{T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon  - t}\right) }\right) \) grows as \( x \) tends to spatial infinity and the 'heat at spatial infinity' diffuses to the finite region; as such, the time-derivative of this solution is positive. Note also that this solution is ancient, e.g., it exists on the time interval \( \left( {-\infty ,{T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon }\right) \) .

\( {}^{4} \) Note that \( v\left( {x, t}\right)  < 0 \) if \( {\left| x\right| }^{2} > {\left( \frac{1}{4\left( {{T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon }\right) } - B\right) }^{-1}\log \left( {\frac{A}{\delta }{\left( {T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon \right) }^{n/2}}\right) \) .

---

\( v \) tends to \( - \infty \) at spatial infinity and since \( H\left( {x,0}\right)  < 0 \) , there exists a first time \( {t}_{0} \in  \left( {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) and a point \( {x}_{0} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that

\[
H\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  }}H\left( {x, t}\right)  = 0.
\]

The second derivative test implies

\[
\frac{\partial H}{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  0,\;\nabla H\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0,\;{\Delta H}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Hence

\[
0 \leq  \frac{\partial H}{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = \frac{\partial v}{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - \delta
\]

\[
= {\Delta v}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - \delta  = {\Delta H}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - \delta
\]

\[
< 0\text{ . }
\]

This is a contradiction and the claim is proved.

Proof. Let \( h\left( x\right) \) be the barrier function constructed in Lemma 12.30 below using the initial metric \( g\left( 0\right) \) . Recall that \( h\left( x\right) \) satisfies (12.34), i.e.,

(12.6)

\[
{C}^{-1}\left( {d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right)  \leq  h\left( x\right)  \leq  C\left( {d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , and (12.35), i.e.,

(12.7)

\[
\left| {\nabla h}\right|  \leq  C,\;\nabla \nabla h \leq  C\;\text{ on }\mathcal{M}
\]

for some constant \( C \) .

(i) By (3.3) in Lemma 3.11 on p. 132 in Part I of this volume, we have

\[
{C}^{-1}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  \leq  {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  \leq  C{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {O, x}\right) .
\]

Hence (12.4) follows from (12.6).

(ii) We compute

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| \nabla h\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2} = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}^{ij}}\right) {\nabla }_{i}h{\nabla }_{j}h
\]

\[
= 2\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla h,\nabla h}\right)  \leq  2\left( {n - 1}\right) {k}_{0}{\left| \nabla h\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2},
\]

so that, by integrating in time, we have

\[
{\left| \nabla h\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2} \leq  {e}^{2\left( {n - 1}\right) {k}_{0}T}{\left| \nabla h\right| }_{g\left( 0\right) }^{2}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Hence \( {\left| \nabla h\right| }_{g\left( t\right) } \leq  C \) follows from (12.7).

(iii) We compute \( {}^{5} \) that at time \( t \) ,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\nabla }_{g\left( t\right) }{\nabla }_{g\left( t\right) }h}\right)  \leq  3\left| {{\nabla }_{g\left( t\right) }\operatorname{Rc}}\right| {\left| \nabla h\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }g\left( t\right) .
\]

Hence, by Shi’s local derivative estimate \( {}^{6} \) and part (ii), we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\nabla }_{g\left( t\right) }{\nabla }_{g\left( t\right) }h}\right)  \leq  \frac{C}{\sqrt{t}}{\left| \nabla h\right| }_{g\left( t\right) }g\left( t\right)  \leq  \frac{{C}^{\prime }}{\sqrt{t}}g\left( t\right) .
\]

Integrating the above inequality in time, we obtain for any \( {t}_{0} \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) and vector \( V \in  {T}_{p}\mathcal{M} \) with \( {\left| V\right| }_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) } = 1 \) ,

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }{\nabla }_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }h}\right) \left( {V, V}\right)  \leq  \left( {{\nabla }_{g\left( 0\right) }{\nabla }_{g\left( 0\right) }h}\right) \left( {V, V}\right)  + {\int }_{0}^{{t}_{0}}\frac{C}{\sqrt{t}}g\left( t\right) \left( {V, V}\right) {dt}
\]

\[
\leq  C
\]

since \( {\left| V\right| }_{g\left( t\right) } \leq  C \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) .

SOLUTION TO EXERCISE 12.8. We compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {g}^{ij}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j} - {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) \phi
\]

\[
\geq  {B\phi } - {\delta }^{-1}\phi {\widetilde{g}}^{ij}\left( {\gamma {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j}h + {\gamma }^{2}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}h{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j}h}\right)  - {\left| X\left( t\right) \right| }_{\widetilde{g}}{\left| \widetilde{\nabla }\phi \right| }_{\widetilde{g}}
\]

\[
\geq  \phi \left( {B - {\delta }^{-1}\left( {\gamma \widetilde{\Delta }h + {\gamma }^{2}{\left| \widetilde{\nabla }h\right| }_{\widetilde{g}}^{2}}\right)  - {b}_{1}\gamma {\left| \widetilde{\nabla }h\right| }_{\widetilde{g}}}\right) .
\]

By (12.34) and (12.35) we have \( {\left| \widetilde{\nabla }h\right| }_{\widetilde{g}} \leq  C \) and \( \widetilde{\Delta }h \leq  {nC} \) . Hence

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {g}^{ij}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j} - {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) \phi  \geq  \phi \left( {B - {\delta }^{-1}\left( {{\gamma nC} + {\gamma }^{2}{C}^{2}}\right)  - {b}_{1}{\gamma C}}\right)
\]

and by choosing \( B \geq  {2\beta } \) and \( \gamma \) sufficiently small so that

\[
{\delta }^{-1}\left( {{n\gamma C} + {\left( \gamma C\right) }^{2}}\right)  + {b}_{1}{\gamma C} \leq  B/2,
\]

we obtain the lemma.

Proof of Theorem 12.10. Let

\[

\]

It suffices to show that \( \widetilde{u} \leq  0 \) . From (12.12) we have

\[

\]

Let \( \phi \) be the barrier supersolution given by Lemma 12.7 with \( \beta  = 1 \) and \( \alpha  = {2b} \) , where \( b \) is as in (12.13).

Claim. For any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we have \( \widetilde{u} \leq  {\varepsilon \phi } \) , which by taking \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) implies \( \widetilde{u} \leq  0 \) , as desired. \( {}^{8} \)

If the claim is false, then there exists \( \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) \) such that

\[
\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  > 0.
\]

By the assumption (12.13) on the growth of \( u \) and the lower bound (12.9) of \( \phi \) we know that \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  < 0 \) for \( \widetilde{d}\left( {O, x}\right) \) sufficiently large independent of \( t \) ; in fact

\[
\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  \rightarrow   - \infty \;\text{ as }\widetilde{d}\left( {O, x}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty
\]

uniformly in \( t \) . Note also that \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x,0}\right)  < 0 \) . Hence \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  < 0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \) sufficiently small. Moreover, there exist \( {t}_{0} \in  \left( {0,{t}_{1}}\right) \) and \( {x}_{0} \in  \mathcal{M} \) such that \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0 \) . At \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  \geq  0
\]

and

\[
\nabla \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  = 0,\;{g}^{ij}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j}\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

This yields a contradiction since at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we then have

\[
0 \leq  \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {g}^{ij}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{i}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j} - {\widetilde{\nabla }}_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  \leq   - {\varepsilon \phi } < 0
\]

(recall \( \beta  = 1 \) ).

---

\( {}^{8} \) Considering \( \widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi } \) is analogous to considering \( v \) in (12.3).

---

nodes.content:
PROPOSITION 12.12 (Uniqueness for Ricci-DeTurck flow). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n},\widetilde{g}}\right) \) is a complete Riemannian manifold with \( \left| \widetilde{\operatorname{Rm}}\right|  \leq  A \) for some \( A < \infty \) , then the solution \( g\left( t\right) \) to the Ricci-DeTurck flow

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{W}_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}{W}_{i}
\]

\[
g\left( 0\right)  = {g}_{0}
\]

where

\[
{W}_{j} \Doteq  {g}_{jk}{g}^{pq}\left( {{\Gamma }_{pq}^{k} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{pq}^{k}}\right) ,
\]

is unique in the class of solutions satisfying

(12.14)

\[
{A}^{-1}\widetilde{g} \leq  g\left( t\right)  \leq  A\widetilde{g},
\]

(12.15)

\[
\left| {\widetilde{\nabla }g\left( t\right) }\right|  + \sqrt{t}\left| {{\widetilde{\nabla }}^{2}g\left( t\right) }\right|  \leq  A.
\]

Suppose that \( g\left( t\right) \) and \( \bar{g}\left( t\right) \) are two solutions of the Ricci-DeTurck flow satisfying \( g\left( 0\right)  = \bar{g}\left( 0\right) \) and (12.14)-(12.15). Under these assumptions, in the proof of Proposition 12.12, we derived on p. 284 of [146] the following evolution inequality:

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {g}^{j\ell }{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{j}{\widetilde{\nabla }}_{\ell }}\right) {\left| g - \bar{g}\right| }^{2} \leq  \left( {\frac{{C}_{1}A}{\sqrt{t}} + {\left( \frac{{C}_{1}A}{2}\right) }^{2}}\right) {\left| g - \bar{g}\right| }^{2}.
\]

We may now apply Theorem 12.10 to conclude that since \( {\left| g\left( t\right)  - \bar{g}\left( t\right) \right| }^{2} = 0 \) at \( t = 0 \) , we have \( {\left| g\left( t\right)  - \bar{g}\left( t\right) \right| }^{2} = 0 \) for all \( t \geq  0 \) . Thus

\[
g\left( t\right)  = \bar{g}\left( t\right)
\]

for \( t \geq  0 \) and the proof of Proposition 12.12 is now complete.

THEOREM 12.14. Suppose that \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , is a complete solution to the Ricci flow on a noncompact manifold \( {\mathcal{M}}^{n} \) with \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right|  \leq  {k}_{0} \) for some \( {k}_{0} > 0 \) . Let \( L \) be defined by (10.1), i.e.,

\[
{Lu} \Doteq  \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }u - \langle X\left( t\right) ,\nabla u\rangle  - F\left( {u, t}\right) ,
\]

where \( X\left( t\right) \) is a smooth family of bounded vector fields and the function \( F : \mathbb{R} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is locally Lipschitz in the \( \mathbb{R} \) factor and continuous in the \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) factor. Suppose that \( u \in  {C}^{2,1} \) satisfies

(12.16)

\[
{Lu} \leq  0\;\text{ and }\;\left| {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \exp \left( {\widetilde{b}\left( {{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right)
\]

for some constant \( \widetilde{b} \) . For any constant \( c \in  \mathbb{R} \) , let \( U\left( t\right) \) be the solution to the corresponding ordinary differential equation:

(12.17)

\[
\frac{dU}{dt} = F\left( {U, t}\right) ,
\]

(12.18)

\[
U\left( 0\right)  = c.
\]

If \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  c \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , then we have

(12.19)

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  U\left( t\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) as long as the solution to the ODE exists.

Let \( L \) be defined by (10.1), i.e., \[ {Lu} \Doteq \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\righ...

nodes.proof:
Proof. Consider the difference between the subsolution to the PDE and the solution to the ODE:

\[
v \Doteq  u - U
\]

By \( {Lu} \leq  0,\left( {12.17}\right) \) , and our initial assumptions on \( u \) and \( U \) , we have

(12.20)

\[
{L}_{0}v \Doteq  \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) } - {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) v \leq  F\left( {u, t}\right)  - F\left( {U, t}\right)
\]

and \( v\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Let

\[
\widetilde{u} \Doteq  {e}^{-{A}_{1}t}v
\]

where the constant \( {A}_{1} \) is to be chosen sufficiently large below. Let \( \phi \) be the barrier supersolution given by Lemma 12.9, where \( A = 0 \) in (12.10), where \( a = 2\widetilde{b} \) in (12.11), and where \( \widetilde{b} \) is as in (12.16).

Claim. For any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we have

\[
\widetilde{u} \leq  {\varepsilon \phi }\;\text{ on }\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack
\]

By taking \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) , we then have \( \widetilde{u} \leq  0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) and the lemma follows directly. \( {}^{9} \)

Now we prove the claim by contradiction. If the claim is false, then there exists \( \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) \) such that

\[
\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  > 0.
\]

On the other hand, by the assumption (12.16) on the growth of \( u \) and the lower bound (12.9) for \( \phi \) we have \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  < 0 \) for \( {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {O, x}\right) \) sufficiently large independent of \( t \) ; in fact \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  \rightarrow   - \infty \) as \( {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  \rightarrow \; \infty \) uniformly in \( t \) . Note also that \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x,0}\right)  < 0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Hence there exists \( {t}_{0} \in  \left( {0,{t}_{1}}\right) \) and \( {x}_{0} \in  \mathcal{M} \) such that

\[
\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  < 0\;\text{ for all }\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

---

\( {}^{9} \) Note that considering \( \widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi } \) is analogous to considering \( v \) in (12.3).

---

and

(12.21)

\[
\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0.
\]

By the locally Lipschitz property of \( F \) there exists a constant \( {K}_{0} \) independent of \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) with (12.21) and \( {A}_{1} \geq  0 \) (but depending on \( \varepsilon \) ) such that \( {}^{10} \)

\[
\left| {F\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\right)  - F\left( {U\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right|  \leq  {K}_{0}\left| {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - U\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right| .
\]

Therefore (12.20) implies at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,{}^{11} \)

\[
{L}_{0}\widetilde{u} = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) } - {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) \widetilde{u}
\]

\[
\leq  {e}^{-{A}_{1}t}\left( {F\left( {u, t}\right)  - F\left( {U, t}\right) }\right)  - {A}_{1}\widetilde{u}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{K}_{0} - {A}_{1}}\right) \widetilde{u}.
\]

By the first and second derivative tests, at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  \geq  0
\]

and

\[
{\nabla }_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  = 0,\;{\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Hence, using (12.10), at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
0 \leq  \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) } - {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)
\]

\[
= {L}_{0}\widetilde{u} - \varepsilon {L}_{0}\phi  \leq  \left( {{K}_{0} - {A}_{1}}\right) \widetilde{u}
\]

\[
= \left( {{K}_{0} - {A}_{1}}\right) {\varepsilon \phi }
\]

since \( {L}_{0}\phi  \geq  0 \) . Choosing \( {A}_{1} > {K}_{0} \) , we obtain a contradiction and the theorem is proved.

DEFINITION 12.15. Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a Riemannian manifold and let \( \Omega  \subset \; \mathcal{M} \) be an open set.

(i) A \( {C}^{0} \) function \( u \) on \( \Omega \) is subharmonic (superharmonic) if for every domain \( D \subset   \subset  \Omega \) and for every harmonic function \( h \) on \( D \) with \( u \leq  h \; \left( {u \geq  h}\right) \) on \( \partial D \) , we have \( u \leq  h\left( {u \geq  h}\right) \) in \( D \) .

(ii) A \( {C}^{0} \) function \( u \) on \( \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) is a subsolution (supersolution) of the heat equation \( \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta u} = 0 \) if for every domain \( D \subset   \subset  \Omega \) and for every solution \( h \) on \( D \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) with \( u \leq  h\left( {u \geq  h}\right) \) on the parabolic boundary \( \partial {D}_{T} \) , we have \( u \leq  h\left( {u \geq  h}\right) \) in \( D \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

nodes.content: LEMMA 12.16 (Absolute value of a solution is a subsolution). If \( u \) is a \( {C}^{0} \) harmonic function on a Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) , then \( {u}_{ + },{u}_{ - } \) , and \( \left| u\right| \) are all nonnegative \( {C}^{0} \) subharmonic functions.
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 12.16 (Absolute value of a solution is a subsolution). If \( u \) is a \( {C}^{0} \) harmonic function on a Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) , then \( {u}_{ + },{u}_{ - } \) , and \( \left| u\right| \) are all nonnegative \( {C}^{0} \) subharmonic functions.

nodes.proof:
Proof. First note that \( \left| u\right|  = \max \{ u, - u\}  = {u}_{ + } + {u}_{ - } \) . The lemma follows from showing that if \( {u}_{1} \) and \( {u}_{2} \) are \( {C}^{0} \) subharmonic functions, then \( \max \left\{  {{u}_{1},{u}_{2}}\right\} \) is a \( {C}^{0} \) subharmonic function. Let \( D \) be a bounded domain and let \( h \) be a harmonic function on \( D \) with \( \max \left\{  {{u}_{1},{u}_{2}}\right\}   \leq  h \) on \( \partial D \) . Then \( {u}_{i} \leq  h \) on \( \partial D \) for \( i = 1,2 \) . Since \( {u}_{1} \) and \( {u}_{2} \) are \( {C}^{0} \) subharmonic functions, this implies \( {u}_{i} \leq  h \) in \( D \) for \( i = 1,2 \) . Hence

\[
\max \left\{  {{u}_{1},{u}_{2}}\right\}   \leq  h
\]

in \( D \) . We conclude that \( \max \left\{  {{u}_{1},{u}_{2}}\right\} \) is a \( {C}^{0} \) subharmonic function.

THEOREM 12.18 (WMP for weak subsolutions on noncompact manifolds). Suppose \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is a complete manifold. If \( u \in  {V}_{2,\text{ loc }}\left( {\mathcal{M}}_{T}\right) \) is a weak subsolution of the heat equation \( \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta u} = 0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) with \( u\left( {\cdot ,0}\right)  \leq  0 \) and if

\]

\[

\]

COROLLARY 12.20 (WMP for bounded weak subsolutions). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is a complete, noncompact Riemannian manifold having Ricci curvature with a negative quadratic lower bound and if \( u\left( {x, t}\right) \) is a bounded weak subsolution of the heat equation with \( u\left( {\cdot ,0}\right)  \leq  0 \) , then

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  0\;\text{ for all }x \in  \mathcal{M}\text{ and }t > 0.
\]

In particular, bounded weak solutions of the heat equation are unique.

\]

< \infty

nodes.content: REMARK 12.21. In [335], Li and Yau proved the uniqueness of solutions which are bounded from below on any complete Riemannian manifold with \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( x\right)  \geq   - C\left( {{d}^{2}\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) \) . THEOREM 12.22 (WMP on noncompact manifolds). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in \; \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a family of complete metrics evolving by \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{h}_{ij} \) and let

\( \mathcal{H} \Doteq  {g}^{ij}{h}_{ij} \) . Assume that \( g\left( t\right)  \geq  {g}_{ * } \) , where \( {g}_{ * } \) is a complete metric, and that \( {\mathcal{H}}_{ * }\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\inf }\limits_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{H}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) is integrable on \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Let \( u \in  {V}_{2,\text{ loc }}\left( {\mathcal{M}}_{{T}_{1}}\right) \) be a weak subsolution to the heat equation \( \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }u = 0 \) such that there exists a constant \( b > 0 \) and \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) where

(12.26)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{T}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{e}^{-b{d}_{ * }^{2}\left( {O, x}\right) }{u}_{ + }^{2}\left( {x, t}\right) d{\mu }_{t}\left( x\right) {dt} < \infty
\]

where \( {d}_{ * } \) is the distance with respect to \( {g}_{ * } \) . If \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  0 \) , then

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  0\;\text{ on }\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack
\]

Proof. Without loss of generality we may assume that \( u \) is contained in the slightly smaller space \( {W}_{2,\text{ loc }}^{1,1}\left( {\mathcal{M}}_{T}\right)  \subset  {V}_{2,\text{ loc }}\left( {\mathcal{M}}_{T}\right) \) . We are able to do this because of a standard trick using the so-called Steklov mean (see [120]). Without loss of generality we may assume that \( T \leq  \frac{1}{8b} \) since we can split \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) into smaller intervals (each with length less than \( \frac{1}{8b} \) ) and apply induction. The proof of the theorem relies on an integration by parts and a good choice of the test function \( \phi \) .

For any \( {T}_{1} \in  (0, T\rbrack \) , let

\[
\eta \left( {x, t}\right)  \doteq   - \frac{{d}_{ * }^{2}\left( {x, O}\right) }{4\left( {2{T}_{1} - t}\right) }.
\]

Therefore, by (12.26) and \( \frac{1}{4\left( {2{T}_{1} - t}\right) } \geq  b \) , we have

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{u}_{ + }^{2}{e}^{\eta }d{\mu }_{t}{dt} < \infty .
\]

Since \( g\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  {g}_{ * }\left( x\right) \) , we also have

(12.27)

\[
\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial t} + {\left| \nabla \eta \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2} \leq  0
\]

Let \( \psi \left( s\right)  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) be a cutoff function where \( \psi \left( s\right)  = 0 \) for \( s \geq  1 \) , \( \psi \left( s\right)  = 1 \) for \( s \leq  \frac{1}{2} \) , and \( \left| {{\psi }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right|  \leq  3 \) . Let \( \varphi \left( x\right)  \Doteq  \psi \left( \frac{{d}_{ * }\left( {O, x}\right) }{r}\right) \) for some \( r > 0 \) , so that \( {\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2} \leq  \frac{9}{{r}^{2}} \) , again using the assumption that \( g\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  {g}_{ * }\left( x\right) \) (later we shall let \( r \rightarrow  \infty \) ). Now define

(12.28)

\[
\phi \left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\left( t\right) \varphi {\left( x\right) }^{2}{e}^{\eta \left( {x, t}\right) }{u}_{ + }\left( {x, t}\right) ,
\]

where \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\left( t\right)  \Doteq  \exp \left( {{\int }_{0}^{t}{\mathcal{H}}_{ * }\left( s\right) {ds}}\right) \) . By our assumption \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  0 \) , we have \( \phi \left( {x,0}\right)  = 0 \) . Furthermore we also have

(12.29)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\left( t\right) {e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}{dt} < \infty .
\]

Substituting (12.28) into the definition of weak subsolution (10.82) with \( f = 0 \) , we have

\[
0 \geq  \left( {{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}}\right) \left( {T}_{1}\right)  + {\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{H}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

\[
- {\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\mathcal{H}}_{ * }\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2} + \frac{1}{2}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {u}_{ + }^{2}\right)  + \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial t}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}}\right) d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\left( {{\varphi }^{2}{\left| \nabla {u}_{ + }\right| }^{2} + 2\langle \nabla u,\nabla \varphi \rangle \varphi {u}_{ + } + {u}_{ + }\left\langle  {\nabla {u}_{ + },\nabla \eta }\right\rangle  {\varphi }^{2}}\right) {e}^{\eta }d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

since \( \frac{d}{dt}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}} = {\mathcal{H}}_{ * }\widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) . Using \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}d{\mu }_{t}}\right)  = \left( {{\mathcal{H}}_{ * } - \mathcal{H}}\right) \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}d{\mu }_{t} \) , we have

\[
- \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {u}_{ + }^{2}\right) d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

\[
=  - \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}}\right) {dt}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial t}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\mathcal{H}}_{ * } - \mathcal{H}}\right) \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

Integrating by parts in time and applying the fundamental theorem of calculus yield

\[
0 \geq  \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}}\right) \left( {T}_{1}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\mathcal{H} - {\mathcal{H}}_{ * }}\right) \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

\[
- \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}\left( {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial t} + {\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2}{u}_{ + }^{2} + {u}_{ + }\left\langle  {\nabla {u}_{ + },\nabla \eta }\right\rangle   + \frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla {u}_{ + }\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{\eta }d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\left( {\frac{1}{2}{\varphi }^{2}{\left| \nabla {u}_{ + }\right| }^{2} + 2\left\langle  {\nabla {u}_{ + },\nabla \varphi }\right\rangle  \varphi {u}_{ + } + 2{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2}{u}_{ + }^{2}}\right) {e}^{\eta }d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

\[
- 2{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}{dt}
\]

Completing the squares, using (12.27), and \( \mathcal{H} - {\mathcal{H}}_{ * } \geq  0 \) imply

\[
\frac{1}{2}\left( {{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\varphi }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}}\right) \left( {T}_{1}\right)  - 2{\int }_{0}^{{T}_{1}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}{dt} \leq  0.
\]

Since (12.29), \( {\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  9{r}^{-2} \) , and \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}\left( {T}_{1}\right)  > 0 \) , by taking \( r \rightarrow  \infty \) , we have

\[
\left( {{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{e}^{\eta }{u}_{ + }^{2}d{\mu }_{t}}\right) \left( {T}_{1}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

This implies \( u\left( {x,{T}_{1}}\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Since \( {T}_{1} \in  (0, T\rbrack \) is arbitrary, the theorem follows.

SKETCH OF THE PROOF. (This is from pp. 448-449 of [327]; see [327] for more details.) Let \( \psi  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) be a smooth cutoff function where \( \psi \left( s\right)  = 1 \) for \( s \leq  1,\psi \left( s\right)  = 0 \) for \( s \geq  2 \) , and \( \left| {{\psi }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right|  \leq  \sqrt{3} \) . Choose \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) and define the radial cutoff function \( {\varphi }_{r} : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) by

\[
{\varphi }_{r}\left( x\right)  \Doteq  \psi \left( \frac{d\left( {x, O}\right) }{r}\right)
\]

for \( r > 0 \) . We have that \( {\varphi }_{r} \) has compact support in \( \bar{B}\left( {O,{2r}}\right) \) and \( {\left| \nabla {\varphi }_{r}\right| }^{2} \leq \; \frac{3}{{r}^{2}} \)

By applying the time-derivative to the \( {L}^{p} \) -norm of \( u \) weighted by \( {\varphi }_{r}^{2} \) , one obtains, for any \( {T}^{\prime } \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) ,

(12.30)

\[

\]

\[
\leq  \frac{6p}{\left( {p - 1}\right) {r}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{T}^{\prime }}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{u}^{p}{d\mu dt}
\]

Taking \( r \rightarrow  \infty \) , we have

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{u}^{p}\left( {x,{T}^{\prime }}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = 0
\]

(and \( {\int }_{0}^{{T}^{\prime }}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\left| \nabla \left( {u}^{p/2}\right) \right| }^{2}{d\mu dt} = 0 \) ), which implies \( u \equiv  0 \) .

nodes.content:
2.1. Mollifying functions in general. To prove maximum principles on complete noncompact manifolds using the second derivative test, for both the Laplace equation and heat-type equations, we need barrier functions. \( {}^{13} \) These barrier functions are often constructed by mollifying the distance function. \( {}^{14} \) First we review how to smooth locally integrable functions on manifolds via convolution with mollifiers. As in subsection 9.2 of Chapter 7 in Part I of this volume, we define the standard mollifier \( \eta  : {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) by

\[
\eta \left( v\right)  \Doteq  \left\{  \begin{matrix} a{e}^{1/\left( {{\left| v\right| }^{2} - 1}\right) } & \text{ if }\left| v\right|  < 1, \\  0 & \text{ if }\left| v\right|  \geq  1, \end{matrix}\right.
\]

where \( a > 0 \) is chosen so that \( {\int }_{\left| v\right|  < 1}{\eta d}{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }} = 1 \) and where \( d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }} \) denotes the Euclidean measure on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . This function is \( {C}^{\infty } \) with compact support and all derivatives vanishing for \( \left| x\right|  \geq  1 \) (including \( \left| x\right|  = 1 \) ).

Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a complete manifold with sectional curvature bounded from above by \( {k}_{0} \) . Define

\[
{\rho }_{0} = \frac{\pi }{\sqrt{{k}_{0}}}
\]

For any \( p \in  \mathcal{M} \) , let \( {}^{15} \)

\[
{\widehat{B}}_{r}\left( 0\right)  \Doteq  \left\{  {v \in  {T}_{p}\mathcal{M} : {\left| v\right| }_{g\left( p\right) } < r}\right\}  .
\]

The exponential map \( {\exp }_{p} : {\widehat{B}}_{{\rho }_{0}}\left( 0\right)  \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) is a local diffeomorphism. Choose an orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) of \( {T}_{p}\mathcal{M} \) . This basis defines an isometry

\[
{\iota }_{p} : {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \rightarrow  \left( {{T}_{p}\mathcal{M}, g\left( p\right) }\right)
\]

and a local diffeomorphism \( {\exp }_{p} \circ  {\iota }_{p} : B\left( {\rho }_{0}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) , where \( B\left( r\right)  \Doteq  \left\{  {v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}}\right. \) : \( \left| v\right|  < r\} \) . By parallel translating the orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) along minimal geodesics emanating from \( p \) , we obtain an isometry

\[
{\iota }_{q} : {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \rightarrow  \left( {{T}_{q}\mathcal{M}, g\left( q\right) }\right)
\]

for each \( q \in  B\left( {p,{\rho }_{0}}\right) \) . Given \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) , recall that \( B\left( {O,{r}_{0}}\right) \) denotes a geodesic ball in \( \mathcal{M} \) (where we allow \( {r}_{0} = \infty \) ).

Let \( f : B\left( {O,{r}_{0}}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a locally integrable function. For positive numbers \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,\min \left\{  {{r}_{0},\frac{1}{2}{\rho }_{0}}\right\}  }\right) \) we define the mollified function (see p. 57 of [217])

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon } : B\left( {O,{r}_{0} - \varepsilon }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}
\]

by

(12.31)

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( p\right)  \Doteq  \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) f\left( {{\exp }_{p} \circ  {\iota }_{p}\left( v\right) }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( v\right) .
\]

---

\( {}^{13} \) An example of a barrier function is \( w\left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \delta {\left( {T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon  - t\right) }^{-n/2}\exp \left( \frac{{\left| x\right| }^{2}}{4\left( {{T}^{\prime } + \varepsilon  - t}\right) }\right) \) used in (12.3) for the heat equation on \( {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) .

\( {}^{14}\mathrm{{On}}{\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) the square of the distance function is smooth, but in general on Riemannian manifolds it is only Lipschitz continuous.

\( {}^{15} \) In the following discussion we often suppress the dependence on \( p \) in our notation.

---

Since \( \eta \left( v\right) \) is a rotationally symmetric function, the definition above is independent of the choice of isometry \( {\iota }_{p} \) . When \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is Euclidean space \( {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) , definition (12.31) agrees with (7.142) in subsection 9.2 of Chapter 7 in Part I of this volume (where \( {\exp }_{p} \circ  {\iota }_{p}\left( v\right)  = p + v \) ). Here, because \( {\exp }_{p} \circ  {\iota }_{p}\left( v\right) \) is in general nonlinear, we need to discuss the smoothness of \( {f}_{\varepsilon } \) and the estimates of its derivatives with some care. We will define an associated function \( {\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon } \) on \( {T}_{p}\mathcal{M} \) and use it to show in the next lemma that \( {f}_{\varepsilon } \) is smooth.

Given a fixed \( p \in  B\left( {O,{r}_{0}}\right) \) , define

\[
{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right)  \Doteq  \sup \left\{  {r \leq  {\rho }_{0} : B\left( {p, r}\right)  \subset  B\left( {O,{r}_{0}}\right) }\right\}
\]

and

\[
\widehat{g} \Doteq  {\exp }_{p}^{ * }g
\]

note that for \( p \in  B\left( {O,{r}_{0} - \varepsilon }\right) \) , where \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,\min \left\{  {{r}_{0},\frac{1}{2}{\rho }_{0}}\right\}  }\right) \) , we have \( {\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right)  \geq  \varepsilon \) .

Consider the Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\widehat{B}}_{{\rho }_{0}}\left( 0\right) ,\widehat{g}}\right) \) . We define

\[
\widehat{f} : {\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}
\]

by

\[
\widehat{f}\left( \widehat{q}\right)  = f\left( {{\exp }_{p}\left( \widehat{q}\right) }\right) .
\]

When \( p \in  B\left( {O,{r}_{0} - \varepsilon }\right) \) , the mollified function

\[
{\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon } : {\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right)  - \varepsilon }\left( 0\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}
\]

of \( \widehat{f} \) on \( \left( {{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right) ,\widehat{g}}\right) \) can be described as follows. Given \( \widehat{q} \in  {\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right)  - \varepsilon }\left( 0\right) \) , using the natural identification \( {}^{16}{T}_{\widehat{q}}{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right)  = {T}_{p}\mathcal{M} \) and the isometry \( {\iota }_{p} \) : \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  \left( {{T}_{p}\mathcal{M}, g\left( p\right) }\right) \) , we can define the isometry \( {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}} : {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  {T}_{\widehat{q}}{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right) \) . Let

\[
{\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} : {T}_{\widehat{q}}{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right)  \rightarrow  {\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right)
\]

be the exponential map with respect to the metric \( \widehat{g} \) , which is well defined on a subset of \( {T}_{\widehat{q}}{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right) \) . Then we have

\[
{\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon }\left( \widehat{q}\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) \widehat{f}\left( {{\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\left( v\right) }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( v\right) .
\]

Let \( {\widetilde{B}}_{r}\left( 0\right) \) be the ball with center 0 and radius \( r \) in \( \left( {{T}_{\widehat{q}}{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right) ,\widehat{g}\left( \widehat{q}\right) }\right) \) and let \( {B}_{\widehat{q}}\left( {\widehat{q},\varepsilon }\right) \) be the ball with center \( \widehat{q} \) and radius \( \varepsilon \) in the manifold \( \left( {{\widehat{B}}_{{\rho }_{0}}\left( 0\right) ,\widehat{g}}\right) \) . Note that for \( \widehat{q} \in  {\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0} - \varepsilon }\left( 0\right) \) , the map

\[
{\exp }_{p} : \left( {{B}_{\widehat{g}}\left( {\widehat{q},\varepsilon }\right) ,\widehat{g}}\right)  \rightarrow  B\left( {p,{\rho }_{0}}\right)  \subset  \mathcal{M}
\]

is a local isometry (this map may not be onto). On the other hand, using the parallel translated orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) , we may identify \( {B}_{\widehat{g}}\left( {\widehat{q},\varepsilon }\right) \) with the ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\varepsilon }^{\prime }\left( 0\right)  \subset  {T}_{q}\mathcal{M} \) via the map \( {\iota }_{q} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}^{-1} \) , where \( q = {\exp }_{p}\left( \widehat{q}\right)  \cdot  {}^{17} \) Since the map \( {\exp }_{q} : {\widetilde{B}}_{\varepsilon }^{\prime }\left( 0\right)  \rightarrow  B\left( {p,{\rho }_{0}}\right)  \subset  \mathcal{M} \) is a local isometry and since both \( {B}_{\widehat{g}}\left( {\widehat{q},\varepsilon }\right) \) and \( {\widetilde{B}}_{\varepsilon }^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \) are simply connected, elementary covering space theory tells us that there exists an onto isometry

\[
\Phi  \Doteq  {\iota }_{q} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}^{-1} : \left( {{B}_{\widehat{g}}\left( {\widehat{q},\varepsilon }\right) ,\widehat{g}}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {{\widetilde{B}}_{\varepsilon }^{\prime }\left( 0\right) ,{\exp }_{q}^{ * }g}\right)
\]

---

\( {}^{16} \) This identification will be used implicitly in this section.

---

and that \( \widehat{f}\left( {{\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}}\left( \widehat{w}\right) }\right)  = f\left( {{\exp }_{q}\left( {\Phi \left( \widehat{w}\right) }\right) }\right) \) for \( \widehat{w} \in  {B}_{\widehat{g}}\left( {\widehat{q},\varepsilon }\right) \) .

Now we are ready to prove the following lemma (which is trivial when \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is Euclidean space).

LEMMA 12.28. Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a smooth complete Riemannian manifold with sectional curvature bounded from above by \( {k}_{0} \geq  0 \) . Let \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) and let \( f : B\left( {O,{r}_{0}}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a locally integrable function for some \( {r}_{0} \in  (0,\infty \rbrack \) . Define \( {\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right)  \Doteq  \sup \left\{  {r \leq  \frac{\pi }{\sqrt{{k}_{0}}} : B\left( {p, r}\right)  \subset  B\left( {O,{r}_{0}}\right) }\right\} \) . For \( p \in  B\left( {O,{r}_{0} - \varepsilon }\right) \) and \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,\frac{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }{10}}\right) \) , we have

(i) for \( \widehat{q} \in  {\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right)  - \varepsilon }\left( 0\right) \) ,

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( {{\exp }_{p}\widehat{q}}\right)  = {\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon }\left( \widehat{q}\right) ;
\]

(ii) \( {\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon }\left( \widehat{q}\right) \) is a smooth function of \( \widehat{q} \in  {\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right)  - \varepsilon }\left( 0\right) \) ;

(iii) \( {f}_{\varepsilon }\left( q\right) \) is a smooth function of \( q \in  B\left( {O,{r}_{0}\left( p\right)  - \varepsilon }\right) \) .

(i) Note that

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( q\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) f\left( {{\exp }_{q} \circ  {\iota }_{q}\left( v\right) }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( v\right) ,
\]

where \( {\iota }_{q} : {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \rightarrow  \left( {{T}_{q}\mathcal{M}, g\left( q\right) }\right) \) is the isometry defined by parallel translating the orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) . From

\[
\widehat{f}\left( {{\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}}\left( \widehat{w}\right) }\right)  = f\left( {{\exp }_{q}\left( {{\iota }_{q} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}^{-1}\left( \widehat{w}\right) }\right) }\right)
\]

we have \( f\left( {{\exp }_{q} \circ  {\iota }_{q}\left( v\right) }\right)  = \widehat{f}\left( {{\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}}\left( {{\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\left( v\right) }\right) }\right) \) for some \( \widehat{q} \in  {B}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0} - \varepsilon }\left( 0\right) \) with \( {\exp }_{p}\widehat{q} = q \) . Hence

(12.32)

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( q\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) \widehat{f}\left( {{\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}}\left( {{\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\left( v\right) }\right) }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( v\right)  = {\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon }\left( \widehat{q}\right) .
\]

(ii) From the second equality in (12.32) and the fact that

\[
{\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}} : B\left( \varepsilon \right)  \rightarrow  {\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\left( 0\right)
\]

is a diffeomorphism (into), we have that

\[
{\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1} : \left( {{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\left( 0\right) ,\widehat{g}}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n},{g}_{\operatorname{can}}}\right)
\]

is a diffeomorphism. Let \( {J}_{{\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) \) be the Jacobian of \( {\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1} \) at \( y \) . Then

\[
{\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon }\left( \widehat{q}\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\left( 0\right) }\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) \widehat{f}\left( y\right) {J}_{{\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}}{\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1}}d{\mu }_{\widehat{g}}\left( y\right) .
\]

---

\( {}^{17} \) We use the notation ’ to emphasize that the ball is in \( {T}_{q}\mathcal{M} \) as opposed to \( {T}_{\widehat{q}}{\widehat{B}}_{{\widehat{r}}_{0}\left( p\right) }\left( 0\right) \) .

---

Since the metric \( \widehat{g} \) is smooth, by Proposition 4.48 on p. 179 of Part I of this volume, it follows that both \( {\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) \) and \( {J}_{{\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) \) are smooth functions of \( \widehat{q} \) and \( y \) . In the above convolution formula for \( {\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon }\left( \widehat{q}\right) \) the kernel \( \eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) {J}_{{\left( {\widehat{\exp }}_{\widehat{q}} \circ  {\widehat{\iota }}_{\widehat{q}}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) \) is smooth in \( \widehat{q} \) ; hence \( {\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon }\left( \widehat{q}\right) \) is smooth in \( \widehat{q} \) .

(iii) \( {\operatorname{Since}}^{18}{\exp }_{p} : {\widehat{B}}_{\min \{ \operatorname{inj}\left( p\right) ,{r}_{0}\left( p\right)  - \varepsilon \} }\left( 0\right)  \rightarrow  B\left( {p,\min \left\{  {\operatorname{inj}\left( p\right) ,{r}_{0}\left( p\right)  - \varepsilon }\right\}  }\right) \) is a smooth diffeomorphism and since we have the equality

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( q\right)  = {\widehat{f}}_{\varepsilon }\left( {{\exp }_{p}^{-1}q}\right)
\]

for \( q \in  B\left( {p,\min \{ \operatorname{inj}\left( p\right) ,{r}_{0}\left( p\right)  - \varepsilon \} }\right) \) , part (iii) follows from (i) and (ii). The lemma is proved.

LEMMA 12.29 (Mollifiers and derivatives). Make the same assumptions as in Lemma 12.28. Let \( {\left\{  {x}^{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{n} \) be normal coordinates defined by an orthonormal frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) at \( p \in  B\left( {O,{r}_{0} - \varepsilon }\right) \) (so that \( {x}^{i}\left( p\right)  = 0 \) ). \( {}^{19} \) Let \( \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}} \) and \( \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}} \) denote the partial derivatives with respect to \( \left\{  {x}^{i}\right\} \) .

(i) If a function \( f : B\left( {O,{r}_{0}}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is continuous at \( p \) , then

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( 0\right)  = f\left( 0\right)
\]

Let \( \Omega  \subset  B\left( {O,{r}_{0}}\right) \) be a compact subset. If \( f \) is a continuous function on

\[
\overline{\Omega \left( {\varepsilon }_{0}\right) } \Doteq  \left\{  {x : d\left( {x,\Omega }\right)  \leq  {\varepsilon }_{0}}\right\}
\]

for some \( {\varepsilon }_{0} > 0 \) , then

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( q\right)  = f\left( q\right)
\]

uniformly for \( q \in  \Omega \) .

---

\( {}^{18} \) Here inj \( \left( p\right) \) denotes the injectivity radius of \( p \) .

\( {}^{19} \) In the notation below we identify \( p \) with 0 .

---

(ii) If the first derivatives \( {\left( \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right) \right) }_{i = 1}^{n} \) exist at \( p \) in the sense of Aleksandrov, \( {}^{20} \) then

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\left( \frac{\partial {f}_{\varepsilon }}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right) \right) }_{i = 1}^{n} = {\left( \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right) \right) }_{i = 1}^{n}.
\]

(iii) If \( f \) has second derivatives \( {\left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) \right) }_{i, j = 1}^{n} \) at \( p \) in the sense of Aleksandrov, then

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\left( \frac{{\partial }^{2}{f}_{\varepsilon }}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) \right) }_{i, j = 1}^{n} = \frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) .
\]

(iv) If \( f \in  {L}_{\text{ loc }}^{p} \) , where \( p \in  \lbrack 1,\infty ) \) , then \( {f}_{\varepsilon } \) converges to \( f \) in \( {L}_{\text{ loc }}^{p} \) .
