nodes.proof:
(i) By composing with the inverse map of a normal coordinate system \( \left\{  {x}^{i}\right\} \) , we treat \( f \) as a function of \( x \in  {\widehat{B}}_{{r}_{0} - \varepsilon }\left( 0\right) \) and we write \( f\left( {{\exp }_{p} \circ  {\iota }_{p}\left( v\right) }\right) \) as \( f\left( v\right) \) . The continuity of \( f \) at 0 implies

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left| v\right|  \leq  \varepsilon }}\left| {f\left( v\right)  - f\left( 0\right) }\right|  = 0.
\]

Note that

\[
\left| {\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) \left( {f\left( v\right)  - f\left( 0\right) }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( v\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left| v\right|  \leq  \varepsilon }}\left| {f\left( v\right)  - f\left( 0\right) }\right|  \cdot  \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( v\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left| v\right|  \leq  \varepsilon }}\left| {f\left( v\right)  - f\left( 0\right) }\right| .
\]

We compute

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( 0\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) \left( {f\left( v\right)  - f\left( 0\right) }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( v\right)
\]

\[
+ f\left( 0\right) \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( v\right)
\]

\[
= f\left( 0\right) \text{ . }
\]

This proves the first part of (i).

The second part of (i) follows from a similar proof using the uniform continuity of \( f \) on \( \overline{\Omega \left( {\varepsilon }_{0}\right) } \)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{q \in  \Omega }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left| v\right|  \leq  \varepsilon }}\left| {f\left( {{\exp }_{q} \circ  {\iota }_{q}\left( v\right) }\right)  - f\left( q\right) }\right|  = 0.
\]

---

\( {}^{20} \) For first- and second-order derivatives in the sense of Aleksandrov on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , see Definition 7.115 on p. 366-367 in Part I of this volume.

---

(ii) By the definition of the first-order Aleksandrov derivative of \( f \) at 0 we have the expansion

\[
f\left( y\right)  \Doteq  f\left( 0\right)  + \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right)  \cdot  {y}^{i} + \widetilde{f}\left( y\right) ,
\]

where \( \widetilde{f}\left( 0\right)  = {\left( \frac{\partial \widetilde{f}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right) \right) }_{i = 1}^{n} = 0 \) . When \( \varepsilon  < \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{inj}\left( p\right) \) and \( x \) is sufficiently close to 0 , we have

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( x\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) f\left( y\right) {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right) .
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{\partial {f}_{\varepsilon }}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\left( \begin{array}{l} \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( \mathop{\exp }\limits_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) {J}_{{\left( \mathop{\exp }\limits_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) }\right) \\   \cdot  \left( {f\left( 0\right)  + \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right)  \cdot  {y}^{j} + \widetilde{f}\left( y\right) }\right)  \end{array}\right) d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right) .
\]

We now evaluate the limit as \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) of the above expression as the sum of three limits corresponding to the three terms on the last line of the RHS.

First we show that the limit corresponding to the last term \( \widetilde{f}\left( y\right) \) is zero. Since \( {\left( \frac{\partial \widetilde{f}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right) \right) }_{i = 1}^{n} = 0 \) , given any \( {\varepsilon }_{1} > 0 \) , there exists \( \delta  > 0 \) such that

\[
\left| {\widetilde{f}\left( y\right) }\right|  \leq  {\varepsilon }_{1}\left| y\right|  \leq  {\varepsilon }_{1}
\]

whenever \( \left| y\right|  \leq  \delta \) . Let \( z \doteq  {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) \) and \( w \doteq  \frac{z}{\varepsilon } \) . Using \( {\exp }_{p} \circ  {\iota }_{p}\left( v\right)  = \; v \) , we have \( \left| y\right|  = \left| z\right| \) at \( p \) . Hence, if \( \varepsilon  \leq  \delta \) , then we compute at the point \( p \)

\[
\left| {\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) }\right) \widetilde{f}\left( y\right) }\right| d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }{\varepsilon }_{1}\left| z\right| \left( \begin{array}{l} \frac{1}{\varepsilon }\left| {\frac{\partial {z}^{j}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( z\right) }\right| \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{j}}\left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) }\right| {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( z\right) \\   + \eta \left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) \left| {\frac{\partial {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( z\right) }\right|  \end{array}\right)
\]

\[
\cdot  {J}_{{\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}}\left( z\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( z\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\varepsilon }_{1}{\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\left( \begin{array}{l} \left| w\right| \left| {\frac{\partial {z}^{j}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\varepsilon w}\right) }\right| \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{i}}\left( w\right) }\right| {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( {\varepsilon w}\right) \\   + \varepsilon \left| w\right| \left| {\frac{\partial {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\varepsilon w}\right) }\right|  \end{array}\right)
\]

\[
\cdot  \left| {{J}_{{\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}}\left( {\varepsilon w}\right) }\right| d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( w\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{1}{\varepsilon }_{1}
\]

Note that \( \left| {\frac{\partial {z}^{j}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\varepsilon w}\right) }\right| \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{i}}\left( w\right) }\right| \) are bounded for \( w \in  B\left( 1\right) \) by a constant independent of \( \varepsilon \) . By Proposition 4.48 in Part I of this volume, \( {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( {\varepsilon w}\right) \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\varepsilon w}\right) }\right| \) are also bounded for \( w \in  B\left( 1\right) \) by a constant independent of \( \varepsilon \) . These facts yield the last inequality in the displayed equation above.

Next we consider the limit corresponding to the first term \( f\left( 0\right) \) :

\[
\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right)  \cdot  {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}\right)  \cdot  f\left( 0\right) d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right)
\]

\[
= f\left( 0\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) d{\mu }_{\mathrm{{Euc}}}}\right)
\]

\[
= 0\text{ . }
\]

For the limit corresponding to the second term \( \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right)  \cdot  {y}^{j} \) we compute(12.33)

\[
\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right)  \cdot  {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}\right)  \cdot  \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) {y}^{j}d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right)  \cdot  {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( z\right) \right) }^{j}d{\mu }_{\mathrm{{Euc}}}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {{\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\eta \left( w\right)  \cdot  {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{j}d{\mu }_{\mathrm{{Euc}}}}\right) .
\]

By Proposition 4.48 in Part I of this volume, we have that at \( x = 0 \) ,

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{j}\right)  = {\delta }_{i}^{j}.
\]

We conclude that the expression in the last line of (12.33) limits to \( \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right) \) . Hence (ii) is proved.

(iii) By the definition of the second-order Aleksandrov derivative of \( f \) at 0 we have

\[
f\left( y\right)  \Doteq  f\left( 0\right)  + \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right)  \cdot  {y}^{i} + \frac{1}{2}\frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) {y}^{i}{y}^{j} + \breve{f}\left( y\right) ,
\]

where \( \breve{f} \) has the property that given any \( {\varepsilon }_{1} > 0 \) there exists \( \delta  > 0 \) such that \( \left| {\breve{f}\left( y\right) }\right|  \leq  {\varepsilon }_{1}{\left| y\right| }^{2} \leq  {\varepsilon }_{1} \) whenever \( \left| y\right|  \leq  \delta \) (see Definition 7.115 in Part I of this volume). We have

\[
\frac{{\partial }^{2}{f}_{\varepsilon }}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\left( \begin{array}{l} \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) }\right) \\   \cdot  \left( {f\left( 0\right)  + \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right)  \cdot  {y}^{i} + \frac{1}{2}\frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) {y}^{i}{y}^{j} + \breve{f}\left( y\right) }\right)  \end{array}\right) d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right) .
\]

Similarly to the proof of (ii), we evaluate \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  0}}\frac{{\partial }^{2}{f}_{\varepsilon }}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) \) in four parts. Let \( z \doteq  {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) \) and let \( w \doteq  \frac{z}{\varepsilon } \) . Using \( {\exp }_{p} \circ  {\iota }_{p}\left( v\right)  = v \) , we have \( \left| y\right|  = \left| z\right| \) at \( p \) .

(a) The limit of the \( f\left( y\right) \) term is zero. If \( \varepsilon  \leq  \delta \) , then by a change of variables we compute at the point \( p \)

\[
\left| {\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) }\right) \breve{f}\left( y\right) d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }{\varepsilon }_{1}{\left| z\right| }^{2}\left( \begin{matrix} \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{2}}\left| \frac{\partial {z}^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\right| \left| \frac{\partial {z}^{\ell }}{\partial {x}^{j}}\right| \left| {\frac{{\partial }^{2}\eta }{\partial {w}^{k}\partial {w}^{\ell }}\left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) }\right| {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}} \\   + \frac{1}{\varepsilon }\left| \frac{{\partial }^{2}{z}^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\right| \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{k}}\left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) }\right| {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}} \\   + \frac{1}{\varepsilon }\left| \frac{\partial {z}^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\right| \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{k}}\left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) }\right| \left| \frac{\partial {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}{\partial {x}^{j}}\right| \\   + \frac{1}{\varepsilon }\left| \frac{\partial {z}^{k}}{\partial {x}^{j}}\right| \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{k}}\left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) }\right| \left| {\frac{\partial i}{\partial {x}^{i}}{J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}\right| \\   + \eta \left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) \left| {\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}{J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}\right|  \end{matrix}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\varepsilon }_{1}\left| {{\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }{\left| w\right| }^{2}\left( \begin{matrix} \left| \frac{\partial {z}^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\right| \left| \frac{\partial {z}^{\ell }}{\partial {x}^{j}}\right| \left| {\frac{{\partial }^{2}\eta }{\partial {w}^{k}\partial {w}^{\ell }}\left( w\right) }\right| {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}} \\   + \varepsilon \left| \frac{{\partial }^{2}{z}^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\right| \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{k}}\left( w\right) }\right| {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}} \\   + \varepsilon \left| \frac{\partial {z}^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\right| \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{k}}\left( w\right) }\right| \left| \frac{\partial {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}{\partial {x}^{j}}\right| \\   + \varepsilon \left| \frac{\partial {z}^{k}}{\partial {x}^{j}}\right| \left| {\frac{\partial \eta }{\partial {w}^{k}}\left( w\right) }\right| \left| \frac{\partial {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\right|  \end{matrix}\right) \left| \frac{{J}_{{\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}}\left( {\varepsilon w}\right) }{d{\mu }_{{}_{Euc}}\left( w\right) }\right| }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{2}{\varepsilon }_{1}
\]

(b) The \( f\left( 0\right) \) term is zero. We compute

\[
\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}\left( y\right) }\right) f\left( 0\right) d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right)
\]

\[
= f\left( 0\right) \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}\left( z\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= 0\text{ . }
\]

(c) The limit of the \( \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( 0\right)  \cdot  {y}^{i} \) term is zero. We have

\[
\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}\right) \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{k}}\left( 0\right) {y}^{k}d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{k}}\left( 0\right) \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}\eta \left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( z\right) \right) }^{k}d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{k}}\left( 0\right) {\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\eta \left( w\right) \frac{{\partial }^{2}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}.
\]

By the proof of Proposition 4.48 in Part I of this volume, we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  0}}\frac{{\partial }^{2}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}} = 0
\]

at \( p \) . Hence the last line of the displayed equation limits to zero.

(d) The limit of the \( \frac{1}{2}\frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) {y}^{i}{y}^{j} \) term is equal to \( \frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) \) . We compute at \( x = 0 \)

\[
\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( {p,{\widehat{r}}_{0}}\right) }\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\eta \left( {\frac{1}{\varepsilon }{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}\left( y\right) }\right) {J}_{{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\right) }^{-1}}}\right) \frac{1}{2}\frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( 0\right) {y}^{i}{y}^{j}d{\mu }_{g}\left( y\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{k}\partial {x}^{\ell }}\left( 0\right) \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{z}{\varepsilon }\right) {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( z\right) \right) }^{k}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( z\right) \right) }^{\ell }d{\mu }_{\mathrm{{Euc}}}\left( z\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{k}\partial {x}^{\ell }}\left( 0\right) \frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {{\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\eta \left( w\right) {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{\ell }d{\mu }_{\mathrm{{Euc}}}\left( w\right) }\right) .
\]

We further compute

\[
\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {{\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\eta \left( w\right) {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{\ell }d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}}\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\eta \left( w\right) \frac{{\partial }^{2}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{\ell }d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\eta \left( w\right) {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}\frac{{\partial }^{2}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{\ell }}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}}d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\eta \left( w\right) \frac{\partial {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\frac{\partial {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{\ell }}{\partial {x}^{j}}d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{B\left( 1\right) }\eta \left( w\right) \frac{\partial {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}}{\partial {x}^{j}}\frac{\partial {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{\ell }}{\partial {x}^{i}}d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}.
\]

From \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  0}}\frac{{\partial }^{2}{\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{k}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}} = 0 \) at \( p \) we see that the first two terms above are zero. Since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  0}}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\left( {\exp }_{x} \circ  {\iota }_{x}\left( \varepsilon w\right) \right) }^{j}\right)  = {\delta }_{i}^{j} \) , we have that the last two terms are equal to \( {\delta }_{i}^{k}{\delta }_{j}^{\ell } + {\delta }_{i}^{\ell }{\delta }_{j}^{k} \) . Hence (iii) follows.

(iv) The proof of Theorem 6(iv) on p. 630 of [185] can be easily adapted from Euclidean space to Riemannian manifolds.

nodes.section_title: 12.2. Mollifying distance functions on Riemannian manifolds
nodes.content:
LEMMA 12.30 (Distance-like function with control on first and second derivatives, I). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {k}_{0} \) for some \( {k}_{0} \geq  0 \) . Then there exists \( C = C\left( {n,{k}_{0}}\right)  > 0 \) such that for any \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) there exists a \( {C}^{\infty } \) function \( h : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) satisfying

(12.34)

\[
{C}^{-1}\left( {d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right)  \leq  h\left( x\right)  \leq  C\left( {d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and

(12.35)

\[
\left| {\nabla h}\right|  \leq  C,\;\nabla \nabla h \leq  C\;\text{ on }\mathcal{M}.
\]

nodes.proof:
Consider the (shifted) distance function

\[
f\left( x\right)  \Doteq  d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 2
\]

defined on \( \mathcal{M} \) . We shall show that for any \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{10}\min \left\{  {\frac{\pi }{\sqrt{{k}_{0}}},1}\right\}  }\right) \) , the mollified function \( {f}_{\varepsilon } \) is the function \( h \) with the desired properties.

(i) By (12.31) we have

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( x\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) \left( {d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 3}\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}
\]

\[
= d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 3 \leq  3\left( {d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) .
\]

We also have

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( x\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{B\left( \varepsilon \right) }\eta \left( \frac{v}{\varepsilon }\right) \left( {d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) d{\mu }_{\text{ Euc }}
\]

\[
= d\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1\text{ , }
\]

so that (12.34) holds with \( C = 3 \) .

(ii) Given a vector \( V \in  {T}_{x}\mathcal{M} \) , we proceed to compute the directional derivative \( V{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( x\right) \) . For \( z \in  B\left( {x,1}\right) \) let

\[
{\pi }_{x, z} : {T}_{x}\mathcal{M} \rightarrow  {T}_{z}\mathcal{M}
\]

denote parallel translation along the unique minimal geodesic joining \( x \) to \( z \) . If \( z \in  B\left( {x,\varepsilon }\right) \) , then

\[
{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( z\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\rho \left( {{\exp }_{z}\left( {{\pi }_{x, z}\left( v\right) }\right) }\right) \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right)
\]

since \( {\pi }_{x, z} : \left( {{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}, g\left( x\right) }\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {{T}_{z}\mathcal{M}, g\left( z\right) }\right) \) is an isometry. Hence

\[
V{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( x\right)
\]

\[
= {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( {{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\left. \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}\frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\rho \left( {{\exp }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( {{\pi }_{x,{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( v\right) }\right) }\right) \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\left\langle  {{\left( \nabla \rho \right) }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( v\right) },{\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}{\exp }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( {{\pi }_{x,{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( v\right) }\right) }\right\rangle
\]

\[
\cdot  \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\left\langle  {{\left( \nabla \rho \right) }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( v\right) }, J}\right\rangle  \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right) ,
\]

where \( J = {J}_{x, v, V} \in  {T}_{{\exp }_{x}\left( v\right) }\mathcal{M} \) is the end vector \( J\left( 1\right) \) of the Jacobi field \( J\left( r\right) \) along the path \( r \mapsto  {\exp }_{x}\left( {rv}\right) \) with \( J\left( 0\right)  = V \) and \( {J}^{\prime }\left( 0\right)  = 0 \) and where we used

(12.36)

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}{\exp }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( {{\pi }_{x,{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( v\right) }\right)  = J.
\]

That is,

\[
V{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( x\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\left\langle  {{\left( \nabla \rho \right) }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( v\right) },{J}_{x, v, V}}\right\rangle  \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right) .
\]

Since the sectional curvatures of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) are bounded from below, by the Rauch comparison theorem, we have \( \left| J\right|  \leq  C \) . Hence

\[
\left| {V{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( x\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\left| J\right| \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{C}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right)
\]

\[
= C\text{ . }
\]

This proves the gradient bound part of (12.35).

(iii) Now we compute the Hessian of \( {f}_{\varepsilon } \) . If \( z \in  B\left( {x,1}\right) \) and \( V \in  {T}_{z}\mathcal{M} \) , then

\[
V{f}_{\varepsilon }\left( z\right)  = \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\left\langle  {{\left( \nabla \rho \right) }_{{\exp }_{z}\left( {{\pi }_{x, z}\left( v\right) }\right) },{J}_{z,{\pi }_{x, z}\left( v\right) , V}}\right\rangle  \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right) .
\]

Given \( V \in  {T}_{x}\mathcal{M} \) , let \( \gamma  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) be the constant speed geodesic with \( \dot{\gamma }\left( 0\right)  = V \) . Define \( V = \dot{\gamma } \) along \( \gamma \) so that \( {\nabla }_{V}V = 0 \) along \( \gamma \) . We have

\[
\text{ (Hess }{f}_{\varepsilon })\left( {V, V}\right)
\]

\[
= V\left( {V{f}_{\varepsilon }}\right)  = {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\left( {V{f}_{\varepsilon }}\right) \left( {{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\left\langle  {{\left( \nabla \rho \right) }_{{\exp }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( {{\pi }_{x,{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( v\right) }\right) },{J}_{{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) ,{\pi }_{x,{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( v\right) , V}}\right\rangle  }\right)
\]

\[
\cdot  \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right) .
\]

Note that in general, for a function \( \widetilde{f} \) , vector fields \( \widetilde{J} \) and \( W \) , and a path \( \beta \left( s\right) \) with \( \dot{\beta }\left( 0\right)  = \widetilde{J} \) , we have

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\left\langle  {{\left( \nabla \widetilde{f}\right) }_{\beta \left( s\right) },{W}_{\beta \left( s\right) }}\right\rangle   = \langle \nabla \nabla \widetilde{f},\widetilde{J} \otimes  W\rangle  + \left\langle  {\nabla \widetilde{f},{\nabla }_{\widetilde{J}}W}\right\rangle  .
\]

Hence, using (12.36), we compute

(12.37)

\[
\text{ (Hess }{f}_{\varepsilon })\left( {V, V}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\left\langle  {{\left( \nabla \rho \right) }_{{\exp }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( {{\pi }_{x,{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( v\right) }\right) },{J}_{{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) ,{\pi }_{x,{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( v\right) , V}}\right\rangle  }\right)
\]

\[
\cdot  \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\varepsilon }^{n}}{\int }_{{T}_{x}\mathcal{M}}\left( {\langle \nabla \nabla \rho , J \otimes  J\rangle +\langle \nabla \rho ,{\nabla }_{J}J\rangle }\right) \eta \left( \frac{\left| v\right| }{\varepsilon }\right) d{m}_{g\left( x\right) }\left( v\right) .
\]

From equation (12.37), a uniform upper bound for the Hessian of \( {f}_{\varepsilon } \) follows from bounding \( \langle \nabla \nabla \rho , J \otimes  J\rangle \) and \( \left\langle  {\nabla \rho ,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle \) independent of \( \varepsilon \) .

By our assumption that the curvature is bounded, we have

(1) an estimate from above for \( \nabla \nabla \rho \) by the Hessian comparison theorem and

(2) \( \left| J\right| \) is bounded.

We may also bound \( \left\langle  {\nabla \rho ,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle \) as follows.

Let \( \gamma \left( t\right)  \Doteq  {\exp }_{x}\left( {tv}\right) \) . Define \( \Gamma \left( {t, s}\right)  \Doteq  {\exp }_{{\exp }_{x}\left( {sV}\right) }\left( {tv}\right) \) so that \( \Gamma \left( {t,0}\right)  = \; \gamma \left( t\right) \) . We have \( J\left( {t, s}\right)  = \frac{\partial \Gamma }{\partial s}\left( {t, s}\right) \) and define \( T\left( {t, s}\right)  = \frac{\partial \Gamma }{\partial t}\left( {t, s}\right) \) so that \( T\left( {t,0}\right)  = \frac{\partial \gamma }{\partial t}\left( t\right) \) . Note that \( \left| {T\left( {t, s}\right) }\right|  = \left| v\right|  \equiv \) const and

\[
{\nabla }_{J}T - {\nabla }_{T}J = \left\lbrack  {J, T}\right\rbrack   = {\Gamma }_{ * }\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial s},\frac{\partial }{\partial t}}\right)  = 0.
\]

We have

\[
\left\langle  {\nabla \rho ,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle
\]

by the Gauss lemma. Now

\[
T\left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{T}\left( {{\nabla }_{J}J}\right) }\right\rangle   = \langle T, R\left( {T, J}\right) J\rangle  + \left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}\left( {{\nabla }_{T}J}\right) }\right\rangle
\]

so that

\[
\left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle   = {\int }_{0}^{\rho }T\left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle  {dt} = {\int }_{0}^{\rho }\left( {\langle T, R\left( {T, J}\right) J\rangle  + \left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}\left( {{\nabla }_{T}J}\right) }\right\rangle  }\right) {dt}.
\]

On the other hand,

\[
\left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{T}J}\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}T}\right\rangle   = \frac{1}{2}J{\left| T\right| }^{2} \equiv  0
\]

so that

\[
0 = J\left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{T}J}\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{J}T,{\nabla }_{T}J}\right\rangle   + \left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}\left( {{\nabla }_{T}J}\right) }\right\rangle  .
\]

Hence

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\rho }\left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}\left( {{\nabla }_{T}J}\right) }\right\rangle  {dt} =  - {\int }_{0}^{\rho }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{J}T,{\nabla }_{T}J}\right\rangle  {dt} =  - {\int }_{0}^{\rho }{\left| {\nabla }_{T}J\right| }^{2}{dt}.
\]

We conclude that

\[
\left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle   = {\int }_{0}^{\rho }\langle T, R\left( {T, J}\right) J\rangle {dt} - {\int }_{0}^{\rho }{\left| {\nabla }_{T}J\right| }^{2}{dt}.
\]

Hence, since the curvature is bounded, to bound \( \left\langle  {\nabla \rho ,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {T,{\nabla }_{J}J}\right\rangle \) , it suffices to bound \( {\left| {\nabla }_{T}J\right| }^{2} \) . This latter bound follows from \( \left| {\left( {{\nabla }_{T}J}\right) \left( 0\right) }\right|  = 0 \) and the integral equation

\[
{\left| {\nabla }_{T}J\right| }^{2} = {\int }_{0}^{\rho }T{\left| {\nabla }_{T}J\right| }^{2}{dt} = 2{\int }_{0}^{\rho }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{T}\left( {{\nabla }_{T}J}\right) ,{\nabla }_{T}J}\right\rangle  {dt}
\]

\[
=  - 2{\int }_{0}^{\rho }\left\langle  {R\left( {J, T}\right) T,{\nabla }_{T}J}\right\rangle  {dt}
\]

\[
\leq  C{\int }_{0}^{\rho }\left| {{\nabla }_{T}J}\right| {dt}
\]

since \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \) and \( \left| J\right| \) are bounded. This completes the proof of the Hessian upper bound part of (12.35).

PROPOSITION 12.31 (WMP for systems-preserving nonnegativity). Under the setting above, suppose that the symmetric bilinear form \( \beta \left( {u, t}\right) \) is locally Lipschitz in \( u \) and continuous in \( t \) and suppose that \( \beta \) satisfies the null-eigenvector assumption, i.e., if \( \omega  \in  {\left( \mathcal{W}{ \otimes  }_{S}\mathcal{W}\right) }_{x} \) with \( \omega  \geq  0 \) for some point \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( V \in  {\mathcal{W}}_{x}^{ * } \) are such that \( \omega \left( V\right)  = 0 \) , then

(12.39)

\[
\beta \left( {\omega , t}\right) \left( {V, V}\right)  \geq  0\;\text{ for any }t \in  \lbrack 0, T).
\]

---

\( {}^{21} \) Note that \( h \) is a section of \( {\mathcal{W}}^{ * }{ \otimes  }_{S}{\mathcal{W}}^{ * } \) .

---

Let \( u \) be a smooth supersolution of (12.38) with \( u\left( 0\right)  \geq  0 \) . If there exists a constant \( \widehat{a} > 0 \) such that for some fixed \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) we have

\[
\left| {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \exp \left( {\widehat{a}\left( {{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right)
\]

on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , then

\[
u\left( t\right)  \geq  0\;\text{ for all }t \geq  0.
\]

nodes.proof:
Let the barrier supersolution \( \phi  : \mathcal{M} \times \; \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be as in Lemma 12.9 so that (12.10) and (12.11) hold for \( a \doteq  \widehat{a} + 1 \) and \( A \) to be chosen later. We identify \( \mathcal{W} \) with its dual \( {\mathcal{W}}^{ * } \) using the metric \( h \) so that the dual of a vector \( X \) in \( \mathcal{W} \) is given by \( {X}^{ * }\left( Y\right)  \Doteq  h\left( {X, Y}\right) \) . We then define the section \( \widetilde{h} \) of \( \mathcal{V} = \mathcal{W}{ \otimes  }_{S}\mathcal{W} \) by

(12.41)

\[
\widetilde{h}\left( {X, Y}\right)  = h\left( {{X}^{ * },{Y}^{ * }}\right) .
\]

Note that \( \widetilde{h}\left( x\right)  > 0 \) and we have \( \nabla \left( t\right) \widetilde{h} = 0 \) and \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\widetilde{h} = 0 \) . We modify the supersolution \( u \) by defining

\[
\widetilde{u}\left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  u\left( {x, t}\right)  + {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) \widetilde{h}\left( x\right)
\]

for \( \varepsilon  > {0.}^{22} \) Since \( \phi \left( {x, t}\right)  > 0 \) , we have \( \widetilde{u}\left( {x,0}\right)  > 0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . We claim that for all \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we have \( \widetilde{u}\left( {x, t}\right)  > 0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \geq  0 \) . Assuming the claim and taking the limit as \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) , we obtain the proposition.

---

\( {}^{22} \) This is analogous to considering \( \widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi } \) as in the proof of Theorem 12.10.

---

We prove the claim by contradiction. From the growth assumption of \( u \) and

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {x, O}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty }}\phi \left( {x, t}\right)  = \infty
\]

(uniformly in \( t \) ), it is easy to see that for some \( {C}_{1} \) sufficiently large independent of \( t,\widetilde{u}\left( {x, t}\right)  > 0 \) when \( {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {x, O}\right)  \geq  {C}_{1} \) . Now suppose that the claim is false. Then there exists a first time \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) , a point \( {x}_{0} \in  \mathcal{M} \) , and a unit vector \( {V}_{0} \in  {\mathcal{W}}_{{x}_{0}}^{ * } \) such that

\[
\widetilde{u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  = 0
\]

and \( \widetilde{u}\left( {x, t}\right)  > 0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t < {t}_{0} \) . As in Section 2 of Chapter 10, we extend \( {V}_{0} \) in space to a section \( V \) defined in a neighborhood \( {\mathcal{U}}_{{x}_{0}} \) of \( {x}_{0} \) by parallel translation along geodesics emanating from \( {x}_{0} \) and then we further extend \( V \) in time to a neighborhood \( {\mathcal{U}}_{{x}_{0}} \times  \left( {{t}_{0} - {\varepsilon }_{1},{t}_{0} + {\varepsilon }_{1}}\right) \) by taking \( V \) to be constant in time. We then have \( \nabla V\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0 \) and \( {\Delta V}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0 \) . The choice of \( {x}_{0},{t}_{0} \) , and \( {V}_{0} \) implies that at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right) \)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\widetilde{u}\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  \leq  0
\]

\[
\nabla \left( {\widetilde{u}\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  = 0,\;\text{ i.e., }\left( {\nabla u + \varepsilon \nabla \phi \widetilde{h}}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
\Delta \left( {\widetilde{u}\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  \geq  0
\]

From (12.38) and (12.10) we compute at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) ,

\[
0 \geq  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\widetilde{u}\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  = \left( \frac{\partial \widetilde{u}}{\partial t}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {\Delta \widetilde{u}+\langle X,\nabla u\rangle  + \beta \left( {u, t}\right)  + {\varepsilon A\phi }\widetilde{h}}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \Delta \left( {\widetilde{u}\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  - \varepsilon \langle X,\nabla \phi \rangle {\left| {V}_{0}\right| }^{2} + \beta \left( {u, t}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  + {\varepsilon A\phi }{\left| {V}_{0}\right| }^{2}
\]

(12.42)

\[
\geq   - \varepsilon \langle X,\nabla \phi \rangle {\left| {V}_{0}\right| }^{2} + \beta \left( {\widetilde{u}, t}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)
\]

\[
- \left( {\beta \left( {u + {\varepsilon \phi }\widetilde{h}, t}\right)  - \beta \left( {u, t}\right) }\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  + {\varepsilon A\phi }{\left| {V}_{0}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Since \( \widetilde{u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  = 0,{d}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0}, O}\right)  \leq  {C}_{1} \) , and \( \left| {V}_{0}\right|  = 1 \) , we have

\[
\left| {{\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right|  = \left| {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right) }\right|  \leq  {e}^{\widehat{a}\left( {{C}_{1} + 1}\right) }.
\]

Thus, since \( \beta \) is locally Lipschitz on \( \mathcal{V} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , on the compact set

\[
\left\{  {\left( {x, v}\right)  : {d}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {x, O}\right)  \leq  {C}_{1},\left| {v\left( {\widetilde{V},\widetilde{V}}\right) }\right|  \leq  2{e}^{\widehat{a}\left( {{C}_{1} + 1}\right) }\text{ for }{\left| \widetilde{V}\right| }_{h} = 1}\right\}   \subset  \mathcal{V},
\]

there exists a constant \( {K}_{0} \) such that

\[
{\left| \beta \left( {v}_{1},{t}_{0}\right)  - \beta \left( {v}_{2},{t}_{0}\right) \right| }_{\widetilde{h}} \leq  \frac{1}{\sqrt{r}}{K}_{0}{\left| {v}_{1} - {v}_{2}\right| }_{\widetilde{h}},
\]

where \( r = \operatorname{rank}\left( \mathcal{W}\right) \) . Hence at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have \( {}^{23} \)

\[
\left( {\beta \left( {u + {\varepsilon \phi }\widetilde{h}, t}\right)  - \beta \left( {u, t}\right) }\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{\sqrt{r}}{K}_{0}{\varepsilon \phi }{\left| \widetilde{h}\right| }_{\widetilde{h}} = {K}_{0}{\varepsilon \phi }{\left| {V}_{0}\right| }^{2}.
\]

By the choice of \( \phi \) there exists a constant \( {C}_{2} \) such that

\[
\left| {\langle X,\nabla \phi \rangle }\right| \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {C}_{2}\phi .
\]

By assumption, \( \beta \left( {\widetilde{u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  \geq  0 \) ; hence from (12.42) we have

\[
0 \geq  \left( {A - {K}_{0} - {C}_{2}}\right) {\varepsilon \phi }{\left| {V}_{0}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Taking \( A = {K}_{0} + {C}_{2} + 1 \) , we obtain a contradiction.

REMARK 12.32. From the proof below we shall see that the above proposition holds on closed manifolds. On closed manifolds this result is a generalization of Theorem 10.7.

The main example we have in mind is where \( u\left( t\right) \) is the Riemann curvature operator \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( t\right) \) of a metric \( g\left( t\right) \) evolving by the Ricci flow, where \( \mathcal{W} = {\Lambda }^{2}{T}^{ * }\mathcal{M} \) . The proposition will be used to prove that nonnegative curvature operator is preserved, as well as Hamilton's matrix differential Harnack estimate, for complete solutions of the Ricci flow on noncompact manifolds with bounded curvature. For such applications, a direct consequence of Proposition 12.31 (which is the version of Theorem 10.7 for noncompact manifolds) may be stated as follows.

THEOREM 12.33 (Maximum principle for 2-tensors). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in \; \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a smooth family of complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds with bounded curvature \( {\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( g\left( t\right) \right) \right| }^{2} \leq  {k}_{0} \) . Let \( \alpha \left( t\right)  \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( {T{\mathcal{M}}^{ * }{ \otimes  }_{S}T{\mathcal{M}}^{ * }}\right) \) , \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a symmetric 2-tensor satisfying

(12.40)

\[
\frac{\partial \alpha }{\partial t} \geq  {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }\alpha  + {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }\alpha  + \beta ,
\]

where \( X\left( t\right) \) is a time-dependent vector field and \( \beta  = \beta \left( {\alpha , t}\right) \) is a symmetric 2-tensor, which is locally Lipschitz in \( \alpha \) and continuous in t. Suppose that \( \left| {\alpha \left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \exp \left( {\widehat{a}\left( {{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right) \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for some \( \widehat{a} \) and \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) , and suppose that \( \beta \) satisfies the null-eigenvector assumption (10.15). If \( \alpha \left( 0\right)  \geq  0 \) , then \( \alpha \left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

THEOREM 12.34 (Weinberger-Hamilton maximum principle for systems). Let \( \mathcal{K} \subset  \mathcal{V} \) be a closed subset which is invariant under parallel translation with respect to \( \nabla \left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , and convex in the fibers, i.e., \( {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) is convex for each \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Assume \( F\left( {u, t}\right) \) is continuous in \( \left( {u, t}\right) \) and is locally Lipschitz in \( u \) . Suppose that \( \mathcal{K} \) has the property that for any \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) and \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) , the solution \( U\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{T}^{\prime }}\right) \) , to the ODE (10.25), i.e.,

\[
\frac{dU}{dt} = {F}_{x}\left( {U, t}\right) ,
\]

where \( {T}^{\prime } \) is the maximal time for which the solution exists, remains in \( {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) . Let \( u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a solution to the PDE (10.24), i.e.,

\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = {\Delta u} + {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }u + F\left( {u, t}\right) ,
\]

satisfying \( d\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) ,{\mathcal{K}}_{x}}\right)  \leq  \exp \left( {\widehat{a}\left( {{d}_{q\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right) \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for some \( \widehat{a} \) and \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) . If \( u \) starts in \( \mathcal{K} \) at \( t = 0 \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) ), then \( u \) stays in \( \mathcal{K} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) for all \( x \) and \( t \) ).

THEOREM 12.35 (Maximum principle for systems: time-dependent sets). Let \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \subset  \mathcal{V} \) be subsets which are invariant under parallel translation by \( \nabla \left( t\right) \) for each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . We require that \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \doteq  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \cap  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) be closed and convex and that the space-time track

\[
\mathcal{T} \Doteq  \{ \left( {v, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{V} \times  \mathbb{R} : v \in  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t \leq  T\}
\]

---

\( {}^{23} \) Note that for any \( \widetilde{V} \) with \( \left| \widetilde{V}\right|  = 1 \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we have \( \left| {\left( {u + {\varepsilon \phi }\widetilde{h}}\right) \left( {\widetilde{V},\widetilde{V}}\right) }\right|  \leq \; 2{e}^{\widehat{a}\left( {{C}_{1} + 1}\right) } \) .

---

also be closed in \( \mathcal{V} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Assume that \( F\left( {u, t}\right) \) is continuous in \( \left( {u, t}\right) \) and locally Lipschitz in u. Suppose that, for any \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , any solution \( U\left( t\right) \) of the ODE (10.63) which starts in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{x} \) will remain in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all later times as long as the solution exists. Let \( u\left( t\right) \) , \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution of the PDE (10.24) which satisfies

\[
d\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right)  \leq  \exp \left( {\widehat{a}\left( {{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right)
\]

on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for some \( \widehat{a} \) and \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) . If \( u \) starts in \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) at \( t = 0 \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( 0\right) }_{x} \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) ), then \( u \) stays in \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all \( x \) and \( t \) ).

nodes.proof:
For any \( v \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) , define

\[
{\rho }_{t}\left( v\right)  \Doteq  d\left( {v,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right) .
\]

Fixing \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , the function \( {\rho }_{t}\left( \cdot \right) \) is Lipschitz on \( {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) . Consider the function

\[
{\rho }_{t}\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right)
\]

on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , where \( \phi \) is given in Lemma 12.9 so that (12.10) and (12.11) hold for \( a \Doteq  \widehat{a} + 1 \) and \( A \) to be chosen later. Taking the spatial supremum of the above function, we define \( s : \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) by

\[
s\left( t\right)  \Doteq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  \mathcal{M}}}\left( {d\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) .
\]

Claim. For all \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we have \( s\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( t \geq  0 \) .

Assuming the claim and taking the limit as \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) , we obtain the proposition.

We now prove the claim. Suppose the claim is false; then there exists a solution \( u\left( {x, t}\right) \) of the PDE (10.24) on \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) such that \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}\left( 0\right) \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( s\left( {t}_{2}\right)  > 0 \) for some \( {t}_{2} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . Since the space-time track \( \mathcal{T} \) is closed, by a proof similar to that of Lemma 10.65, \( s \) is lower semicontinuous and right continuous at any \( t \) with \( s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) . Hence there exists a time \( {t}_{1} \geq  0 \) such that \( s\left( {t}_{1}\right)  = 0, s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) for any \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) , and \( s\left( t\right) \) is lower semi-continuous and right continuous on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . By Corollary 10.26 the claim follows from showing \( \frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt} \leq  {Cs} \) on \( \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

Now we turn to proving \( \frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt} \leq  {Cs} \) on \( \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . For \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) , since \( d\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right)  > 0 \) for some \( x \in  \mathcal{M}, s\left( t\right) \) may be written as

\[
s\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  \mathcal{M}}}\left\{  {\left( {\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {v,\ell }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{S}}_{x}\left( t\right) }}\ell \left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - v}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right\}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {v,\ell , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) }}\left( {g\left( {v,\ell , x, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) ,
\]

where \( \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) \) is defined as in (10.66), and as in Chapter 10,

\[
g\left( {v,\ell , x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \ell \left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - v}\right) ,\;\text{ for }\left( {v,\ell , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Given \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , let \( {h}_{i} \searrow  0 \) be such that

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - s\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}}.
\]

From the growth assumption on \( u \) and (12.11), it is easy to see that

\[
{\rho }_{t}\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right)  < 0
\]

when \( {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {x, O}\right)  \geq  {C}_{1} \) , where \( {C}_{1} \) is sufficiently large independent of \( t \) . Hence there exist sequences \( {x}_{i} \in  \mathcal{M},{v}_{i} \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) , and \( {\ell }_{i} \in  {S}_{{v}_{i}}\mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) such that

\[
g\left( {{v}_{i},{\ell }_{i},{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  = s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) .
\]

For the same reason as above, there exists a subsequence such that \( {x}_{i} \rightarrow \; {x}_{\infty } \in  \mathcal{M},{v}_{i} \rightarrow  {v}_{\infty } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) , and \( {\ell }_{i} \rightarrow  {\ell }_{\infty } \in  {S}_{{v}_{\infty }}\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \subset  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{\infty }}^{ * } \) . Since \( g \) is continuous and \( s \) is right continuous, we have

(12.43)

\[
s\left( t\right)  = g\left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) .
\]

We compute(12.44)

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{g\left( {{v}_{i},{\ell }_{i},{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - g\left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  + {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
- \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {v}_{i}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  + {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
- \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) .
\]

Choose \( {v}_{i}^{ * } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) and \( {\ell }_{i}^{ * } \in  {S}_{{v}_{i}^{ * }}\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) such that

(12.45)

\[
d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}}}\right)  = {\ell }_{i}^{ * }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  = {\left| u\left( {x}_{i}, t\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }\right| }_{h}.
\]

Let \( {U}_{i}\left( \tau \right) ,\tau  \in  \lbrack t, t + \varepsilon ) \) , for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) independent of \( i \) , be the solution to the ODE (10.63) in \( {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{i}} \) :

(12.46)

\[
\frac{d{U}_{i}}{d\tau } = F\left( {{U}_{i},\tau }\right)
\]

with \( {U}_{i}\left( t\right)  = {v}_{i}^{ * } \) . Define \( {F}_{i} \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{i}} \) by

(12.47)

\[
{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} = {U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) .
\]

By our assumption, we have \( {U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) . Hence

(12.48)

\[
{\ell }_{i}\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} - {v}_{i}}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Note that (12.46) and (12.47) imply that as \( i \rightarrow  \infty \) ,

\[
\left| {{F}_{i} - F\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * }, t}\right) }\right|  = \left| {\frac{{U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {U}_{i}\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}} - \frac{d{U}_{i}}{dt}\left( t\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  0.
\]

By passing to a subsequence, we have \( {v}_{i}^{ * } \rightarrow  {v}_{\infty }^{ * } \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) and \( {\ell }_{i}^{ * } \rightarrow  {\ell }_{\infty }^{ * } \) . We claim that \( {v}_{\infty }^{ * } = {v}_{\infty } \) . Taking the limit of (12.45), we have

\[
\left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }^{ * }}\right|  = {\ell }_{\infty }^{ * }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }^{ * }}\right)
\]

\[
= d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right| ,
\]

where the last equality follows from (12.43). Since \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) is convex, we conclude that \( {v}_{\infty }^{ * } = {v}_{\infty } \) . (The point \( {v}_{\infty } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) is the unique point in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) closest to \( u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) \) .)

From (10.68) we have

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\left\lbrack  {{\ell }_{i}\left( {\frac{u\left( {{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}} - {F}_{i}}\right)  + \frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} - {v}_{i}}\right) }{{h}_{i}}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  + {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
- \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) .
\]

Note that for each \( i \) ,

\[
{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left| {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right|  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)
\]

\[
= d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)
\]

\[
= {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) .
\]

From (12.43) we also have that \( \left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) \) satisfies

\[
{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = s\left( t\right) ,
\]

so that by parallel translating \( {v}_{\infty } \) and \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) along geodesics (with respect to \( g\left( t\right) ) \) emanating from \( {x}_{\infty } \) , so that \( \left( {{v}_{\infty }\left( x\right) ,{\ell }_{\infty }\left( x\right) , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) \) for \( x \) in a neighborhood of \( {x}_{\infty } \) , we have

\[
\nabla \left( {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right)  = 0
\]

\[
\Delta \left\lbrack  {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right\rbrack  \left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = {\ell }_{\infty }\left\lbrack  {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right\rbrack   - {\varepsilon \Delta \phi } \leq  0
\]

since \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) is linear (note that \( {\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{\infty }} \) and that \( {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) \) is a real-valued function in a neighborhood of \( {x}_{\infty } \) which achieves a local maximum at \( {x}_{\infty } \) ). From this, (12.48), (12.10), and 12.11, we have

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  \leq  {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - F\left( {{v}_{\infty }^{ * }, t}\right) }\right)  - \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)
\]

\[
= {\ell }_{\infty }\left\lbrack  {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  + {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  + F\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) , t}\right)  - F\left( {{v}_{\infty }^{ * }, t}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
- {\varepsilon \Delta \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon A\phi }
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right|  + \varepsilon {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }\phi \left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon A\phi }
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right|  + {C}_{2}\phi \left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon A\phi } \leq  {Cs}\left( t\right) ,
\]

where we choose \( A \geq  C + \frac{{C}_{2}}{\varepsilon } \) . This completes the proof of the theorem.

nodes.content: EXERCISE 12.37. Use the method in subsection 3.4 of Chapter 10 to give another proof of Theorem 12.34 assuming \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) changes continuously in \( t \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: EXERCISE 12.37. Use the method in subsection 3.4 of Chapter 10 to give another proof of Theorem 12.34 assuming \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) changes continuously in \( t \) .

nodes.proof:
Let \( s\left( t\right) \) be the function defined in the proof of Theorem 12.35. Since \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) changes continuously in \( t, s\left( t\right) \) is a continuous function. We shall show that for some constant \( C < \infty ,\frac{{d}_{ + }s}{dt} \leq  {Cs} \) whenever \( s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) ; the theorem then follows from Exercise 10.28 since \( s\left( 0\right)  = 0 \) .

We shall compute \( \frac{{d}_{ \pm  }s}{dt} \) at \( {t}_{0} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) where \( s\left( {t}_{0}\right)  > 0 \) . From the growth assumption on \( u \) and (12.11), there exists \( {x}_{0} \in  \mathcal{M} \) such that

\[
s\left( {t}_{0}\right)  = {\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  = d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{{x}_{0}}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) .
\]

For \( h > 0 \) , since \( s\left( {{t}_{0} - h}\right)  \geq  {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0} - h}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0} - h}\right) \) , we have

\[
\frac{{d}_{ + }s}{dt} \leq  \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0} - h}\right) }\right) }{h} - \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) .
\]

From the PDE \( \left( {10.24}\right) \) (we are using \( X\left( t\right)  = 0 \) and \( F\left( {u, t}\right)  = F\left( u\right) \) ),

\[
u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0} - h}\right)  = u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {h\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  + o\left( h\right) .
\]

Since \( {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( \cdot \right) \) is a Lipschitz function on \( {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) (with Lipschitz constant 1), we have

\[
\frac{\left| {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0} - h\right) \right)  - {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right)  - h\Delta u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right)  - hF\left( u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) \right) \right) \right| }{h}
\]

\[
\leq  o\left( 1\right) \text{ . }
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{{d}_{ + }s}{dt} \leq   - \varepsilon \left( {{\Delta \phi } + {A\phi }}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {h\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right) }{h}.
\]

Next we claim that for any \( {\varepsilon }_{1} > 0 \) , when \( h \) is small enough, we have

(12.50)

\[
{\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {h\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - {\varepsilon }_{1}h - {\varepsilon \Delta \phi }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  + {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right) .
\]

To see the claim, from the convexity of the distance function \( {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h} \) we have for \( h > 0 \)

\[
{\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {h\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right)  - \left\langle  {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,\nabla {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u}_{1}\right) }\right\rangle   \cdot  h,
\]

where \( {u}_{1} \Doteq  u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) \) and \( \langle \) , \( \rangle {istheinnerproductonV} \) . We shall show that

(12.51)

\[
\left\langle  {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,\nabla {\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right\rangle   \leq  {\varepsilon \Delta \phi }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) .
\]

Since \( \nabla {\rho }_{t}\left( w\right) \) is a continuous function of \( \left( {w, t}\right) \) (see Lemma 10.53(iii)), given \( {\varepsilon }_{1} > 0 \) , we can choose \( h \) small enough so that

\[
\left\langle  {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,\nabla {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u}_{1}\right) }\right\rangle   \leq  {\varepsilon }_{1} + {\varepsilon \Delta \phi }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,
\]

which will imply the claim.

Now inequality (12.50) implies that we can drop the Laplacian term in (12.49):(12.52)

\[
\frac{{d}_{ + }s}{dt} \leq  \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right) }{h} - {\varepsilon A\phi }.
\]

Given \( h > 0 \) small enough, we choose \( {v}_{h} \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0} - h\right) }_{{x}_{0}} \) (the closest point) so that

(12.53)

\[
{\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right)  = {\left| u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right)  - hF\left( u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) \right)  - {v}_{h}\right| }_{{\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}},
\]

where \( {\left| \cdot \right| }_{{\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}} \) denotes the norm on \( {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}} \) . This implies that

\[
{\left| u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right)  - {v}_{h}\right| }_{{\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}} = {\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  + o\left( 1\right) .
\]

By (12.53) and the fact that \( {\rho }_{{t}_{0}} \) has Lipschitz constant 1, we may bound the numerator of the RHS of (12.52) as follows:

\[
{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\left| u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right)  - hF\left( {v}_{h}\right)  - {v}_{h}\right| }_{{\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}}
\]

\[
+ {\left| hF\left( {v}_{h}\right)  - hF\left( u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) \right) \right| }_{{\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}}
\]

\[
\leq  {\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{hF}\left( {v}_{h}\right)  + {v}_{h}}\right)  + {\left. h\left| F\left( {v}_{h}\right)  - F\left( u\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) \right) \right| \right| }_{{\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}}
\]

(12.54)

\[
\leq  {\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{hF}\left( {v}_{h}\right)  + {v}_{h}}\right)  + {hC}{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  + o\left( h\right) ,
\]

where to obtain the last inequality we have used the locally Lipschitz property of \( F \) .

Let \( {U}_{{v}_{h}} \) be the solution of the ODE (10.63) with initial value

\[
{U}_{{v}_{h}}\left( {{t}_{0} - h}\right)  = {v}_{h} \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0} - h\right) }_{{x}_{0}}.
\]

Then

\[
{\left| {U}_{{v}_{h}}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  - \left( {v}_{h} + hF\left( {v}_{h}\right) \right) \right| }_{{\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}} \leq  o\left( h\right) .
\]

Since the sets \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{0}} \) are preserved under the ODE, we have \( {U}_{{v}_{h}}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in \; \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{{x}_{0}} \) , and hence

(12.55)

\[
\text{ 55) }{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{v}_{h} + {hF}\left( {v}_{h}\right) }\right)  \leq  {\left| {U}_{{v}_{h}}\left( {t}_{0}\right)  - \left( {v}_{h} + hF\left( {v}_{h}\right) \right) \right| }_{{\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}} \leq  o\left( h\right) \text{ . }
\]

Hence, by (12.54) and (12.55), we have

\[
{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\rho }_{{t}_{0} - h}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {hF}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) }\right)  \leq  {hC}{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  + o\left( h\right) .
\]

Combining this with (10.57), we have proved

\[
\frac{{d}_{ + }s}{dt} \leq  C{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon A\phi } = {Cs}\left( {t}_{0}\right)
\]

when we choose \( A \geq  C \) (while \( s\left( 0\right)  = 0 \) ). The version of Theorem 10.16 where \( X\left( t\right)  = 0, F\left( {u, t}\right)  = F\left( u\right) \) , and the fiberwise convex sets depend continuously on time has been proved.

Finally we give a proof of (12.51). Note that the function \( {\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - \; {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) \) attains its maximum at \( x = {x}_{0} \) . Hence if \( {\rho }_{{t}_{0}} \) is \( {C}^{2} \) at \( u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , then at \( {x}_{0} \) we have

\[
0 \geq  \Delta \left( {{\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\left( {u\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \operatorname{Hess}\left( {\rho }_{{t}_{0}}\right) \left( {\nabla u,\nabla u}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  + \left\langle  {\nabla {\rho }_{{t}_{0}},{\Delta u}}\right\rangle  \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \Delta \phi }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left\langle  {\nabla {\rho }_{{t}_{0}},{\Delta u}}\right\rangle  \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \Delta \phi }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

since \( {\rho }_{{t}_{0}} \) is a convex function. Note that when \( {\rho }_{{t}_{0}} \) is not \( {C}^{2} \) , then the support function argument in Section 9 of Chapter 7 of Part I of this volume will apply, still giving the above inequality since \( {\rho }_{{t}_{0}} \) is \( {C}^{1} \) .

THEOREM 12.38 (Maximum principle for systems: avoidance sets). Make the same assumptions as in Theorem 12.35 regarding \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) and \( F \) . Suppose for any \( x \in  \mathcal{M},{t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , and any solution \( U\left( t\right) \) of the ODE (10.25) with initial condition \( U\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{x} \) that either

(i) (the solution to the ODE stays in \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) ) \( U\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all \( t \geq  {t}_{0} \) or

(ii) (the solution to the ODE hits some \( \mathcal{A}\left( t\right) \) ) there is a time \( {t}_{1} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) such that \( U\left( t\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} - \mathcal{A}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all \( {t}_{0} \leq  t < {t}_{1} \) and \( U\left( {t}_{1}\right)  \in \; \mathcal{A}{\left( {t}_{1}\right) }_{x} \)

Let \( u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution of the PDE (10.24) satisfying

\[
d\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right)  \leq  \exp \left( {\widehat{a}\left( {{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right)
\]

on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for some \( \widehat{a} \) and \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) . If \( u \) starts in \( \mathcal{K} \) at \( t = 0 \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M}) \) and satisfies \( u\left( {x, t}\right)  \notin  \mathcal{A}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and all \( t \geq  0 \) , then \( u \) will remain in \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) for all later times \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{K}}_{x} \) for all \( x \) and \( t \) ).

nodes.content: REMARK 12.39. Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a smooth family of complete Riemannian manifolds (where \( \mathcal{M} \) is not necessarily compact and \( g\left( t\right) \) is not necessarily evolving by the Ricci flow). Assume that \( g\left( t\right) \) has bounded curvature \( {\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( g\left( t\right) \right) \right| }^{2} \leq  {k}_{0} \) . Let \( \pi  : {\mathcal{W}}^{r} \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) be a vector bundle with a smooth family of bundle metrics \( h\left( t\right) \) on \( \mathcal{W} \) and time-dependent connections \( \nabla \left( t\right) \) on \( \mathcal{W} \) compatible with \( h\left( t\right) \) . Assume that \( \frac{\partial h}{\partial t} \geq   - {c}_{1}h \) for some constant \( {c}_{1} \) . Then, after appropriate modifications of the proofs, Theorem 12.33, Theorem 12.34, Theorem 12.35, and Theorem 12.38 still hold (see Chapter 15 for an example of such a result). When applied to the curvature operator under the Ricci flow, since \( h\left( t\right) \) may depend on \( t \) , such maximum principles enable us to avoid the use of Uhlenbeck's trick.

COROLLARY 12.44 (Euclidean mean value property). Let \( \Omega  \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) be a connected domain and let \( T \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) . If \( u\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {C}^{2,1} \) is a solution to the heat equation \( \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{0}u = 0 \) on \( {\Omega }_{T} \doteq  \Omega  \times  (0, T\rbrack \) , then for any \( {E}_{r}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \subset  {\Omega }_{T} \) we have

(12.57)

\[
u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = \frac{1}{4{r}^{n}}{\iint }_{{E}_{r}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) }u\left( {y, t}\right) \frac{{\left| {x}_{0} - y\right| }^{2}}{{\left( {t}_{0} - t\right) }^{2}}{dydt},
\]

where

\[
{E}_{r}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = \left\{  {\left( {y, t}\right)  : {\left| y - {x}_{0}\right| }^{2} < {2n}\left( {{t}_{0} - t}\right) \log \frac{{r}^{2}}{{4\pi }\left( {{t}_{0} - t}\right) }}\right\}
\]

\[
\subset  B\left( {{x}_{0},\sqrt{\frac{n}{2e\pi }}r}\right)  \times  \left( {{t}_{0} - \frac{{r}^{2}}{4\pi },{t}_{0}}\right) .
\]
