(14.11)

\]

where \( \beta \) depends only on \( \max \{ \alpha ,1\} \) and \( n \) , and deriving the following inequality

\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial t} \leq  {\Delta F} + C\left( n\right) \beta {K}^{3},
\]

By the maximum principle, \( F \leq  C\left( {n,\alpha }\right) {K}^{2} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\alpha /K}\right\rbrack \) , where \( C\left( {n,\alpha }\right) \) depends only on \( \max \{ \alpha ,1\} \) and \( n \) , and the first derivative estimate is then an easy consequence. nodes.content:
REMARK 14.8 (Derivatives and scaling).

(1) (Riemannian manifolds) Given a Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) , we say that a scalar geometric quantity \( a\left( g\right) \) depending on \( g \) scales like \( {g}^{k} \) , where \( k \in  \mathbb{R} \) , if

\[
a\left( {cg}\right)  = {c}^{k}a\left( g\right) \;\text{ for all }c > 0.
\]

We write \( a\left( g\right)  \sim  {g}^{k} \) . If \( k = 0 \) , then we say that \( a\left( g\right) \) is scale-invariant. If two quantities \( a\left( g\right) \) and \( b\left( g\right) \) scale like the same power of \( g \) , we say that they scale the same and denote this by \( a\left( g\right)  \sim  b\left( g\right) \) . For example,

\[
R \sim  \left| \mathrm{{Rc}}\right|  \sim  \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \sim  {g}^{-1} \sim  {s}^{-2}
\]

all scale the same, where \( s \) denotes the distance function. We also have \( \left| {{\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  \sim  {s}^{-m - 2} \) for all \( m \in  \mathbb{N} \) .

(2) (Ricci flow) Given a solution \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) to the Ricci flow and \( c > 0 \) , the family of metrics \( \widetilde{g}\left( \widetilde{t}\right)  = {cg}\left( t\right) \) , where \( \widetilde{t} = {ct} \) , is also a solution to the Ricci flow. For this reason we say that \( t \) scales like \( g \) . For example,

\[
\widetilde{t}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left\lbrack  {\widetilde{g}\left( \widetilde{t}\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right|  = t\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left\lbrack  {g\left( t\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right| ,
\]

and we say that the quantity \( t\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left\lbrack  {g\left( t\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right| \) is scale-invariant. For \( m \in  \mathbb{N} \) , we have

\[
{\widetilde{t}}^{m/2}\left| {{\widetilde{\nabla }}^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\left\lbrack  {\widetilde{g}\left( \widetilde{t}\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right|  = {c}^{-1}{t}^{m/2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\left\lbrack  {g\left( t\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right| ,
\]

so that \( {t}^{m/2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\left\lbrack  {g\left( t\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right| \) scales like \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left\lbrack  {g\left( t\right) }\right\rbrack  }\right| \) , which is bounded by \( K \) . For these reasons and since \( C\left( {m, n,\alpha }\right) \) is scale-invariant, we see that inequality (14.11) has the right scaling properties. Note that as \( t \) approaches 0, the estimate gets worse, as expected since at \( t = 0 \) no bound on the derivatives of curvature is assumed. For short time, as \( t \) increases, it is the smoothing nature of the Ricci flow which enables bounds on the derivatives to be proved.

THEOREM 14.10 (Local first derivative estimate-Shi). For any \( \alpha  > 0 \) there exists a constant \( C\left( {\alpha , K, r, n}\right) \) depending only on \( \alpha , K, r \) , and \( n \) such that if \( {\mathcal{M}}^{n} \) is a manifold, \( p \in  \mathcal{M} \) , and \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack  ,0 < \tau  \leq  \alpha /K \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow on an open neighborhood \( \mathcal{U} \) of \( p \) containing \( {\bar{B}}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r}\right) \) as a compact subset and if

\[
\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  K\text{ for all }x \in  \mathcal{U}\text{ and }t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack  \text{ , }
\]

then

(14.15)

\[
\left| {\nabla \operatorname{Rm}\left( {y, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{C\left( {\alpha , K, r, n}\right) }{\sqrt{t}} = \frac{C\left( {\alpha ,\sqrt{K}r, n}\right) K}{\sqrt{t}}
\]

for all \( \left( {y, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack \) . Given in addition \( \beta  > 0 \) and \( \gamma  > 0 \) , if also \( \gamma /\sqrt{K} \leq  r \leq  \beta /\sqrt{K} \) , then there exists \( C\left( {n,\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma }\right) \) such that under the above assumptions

\[
\left| {\nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  \leq  C\left( {\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma , n}\right) \frac{K}{\sqrt{t}}
\]

in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack \) .

nodes.proof:
This involves considering a good first derivative quantity and multiplying it by a cutoff function to localize it. Using the above evolution equations for \( {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \) and \( {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \) , we compute that

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left\lbrack  {\left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
= {\left| \nabla \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + \left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {\left| \nabla \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- 2\nabla {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \cdot  \nabla {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq   - 2{\left| \nabla \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{4} + {16}{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{3}{\left| \nabla \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} - 2\left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| {\nabla }^{2}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C\left( n\right) \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + 8\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }^{2}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq   - 2{\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4} + {16}{K}^{3}{\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} - {32}{K}^{2}{\left| {\nabla }^{2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ {17C}\left( n\right) {K}^{3}{\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + {8K}{\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }^{2}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| .
\]

Since

\[
- \frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4} + {8K}{\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }^{2}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  - {32}{K}^{2}{\left| {\nabla }^{2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  0
\]

and

\[
- \frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4} + \left\lbrack  {{16} + {17C}\left( n\right) }\right\rbrack  {K}^{3}{\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  {C}^{\prime }\left( n\right) {K}^{6},
\]

we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left\lbrack  {\left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack   \leq   - {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4} + C\left( n\right) {K}^{6}.
\]

Recall \( F = \left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \) . Using \( {16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  {17}{K}^{2} \) , we find

(14.19)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) F \leq   - \frac{1}{{289}{K}^{4}}{F}^{2} + C\left( n\right) {K}^{6},
\]

where \( C\left( n\right) \) depends only on \( n \) .

Because of the negative quadratic term on the RHS, we are in good shape. We can make things better by making our function tend to 0 as \( t \) tends to 0. In particular, let

\[
G \Doteq  {tF} = t\left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Then

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) G \leq  \frac{1}{t}\left( {-\frac{1}{{289}{K}^{4}}{G}^{2} + G + C\left( n\right) {K}^{6}{t}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{t}\left( {-\frac{c}{{K}^{4}}{G}^{2} + C\left( n\right) {\alpha }^{2}{K}^{4}}\right) ,
\]

where \( c \) is a universal constant and \( C\left( n\right) \) depends only on \( n \) (here we used \( t \leq  \alpha /K) \) .

To make local use of the above nice evolution equation for \( G \) , we multiply by a cutoff function. Let \( \eta  : \mathcal{U} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a Lipschitz cutoff function as defined in Lemma 14.3. We compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\eta G}\right)  \leq  \frac{\eta }{t}\left( {-\frac{c}{{K}^{4}}{G}^{2} + C\left( {n,\alpha }\right) {K}^{4}}\right)  - {\Delta \eta } \cdot  G - 2\nabla \eta  \cdot  \nabla G.
\]

At a point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) where \( {\eta G} \) attains its maximum in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) , we have \( {t}_{0} > 0\left( {G\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right. \) vanishes when \( t = 0) \) and

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\eta G}\right)  \geq  0,\;\Delta \left( {\eta G}\right)  \leq  0,\;0 = \nabla \left( {\eta G}\right)  = \eta \nabla G + G\nabla \eta .
\]

See subsection 1.13 of Appendix A on pp. 453-456 of Part I of this volume for Calabi's trick, which explains why we can for the purpose of applying the maximum principle treat \( \eta \) as a smooth function. Hence, at the maximum point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
0 \leq   - \frac{c}{{K}^{4}}{\left( \eta G\right) }^{2} + C\left( {n,\alpha }\right) {\eta }^{2}{K}^{4} - {t\Delta \eta }\left( {\eta G}\right)  + {2tG}{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2}.
\]

Let

\[
H \Doteq  {\eta G} = {\eta t}\left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Using the bounds (14.1) and (14.2) for \( {\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2} \) and \( - {\Delta \eta } \) ,

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  }}{\left( \eta \Theta \right) }^{1/2}\left( {{x}_{0}, t}\right)  \leq  {\eta G}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,
\]

\[
- {\Delta }_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\eta \left( {x}_{0}\right)  \leq  \frac{C\left( {\alpha ,\sqrt{K}r, n}\right) }{{r}^{2}} + \frac{{16C}\left( {\alpha , n}\right) }{{K}^{3/2}r}{\eta G}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,
\]

and the facts that \( \eta  \leq  1 \) and \( t \leq  \tau  \leq  \alpha /K \) , we have at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) ,

(14.20)

\[
0 \leq   - \frac{c}{{K}^{4}}{H}^{2} + \frac{C\left( {\alpha , n}\right) }{{K}^{5/2}r}{H}^{3/2} + \frac{C\left( {\alpha ,\sqrt{K}r, n}\right) }{{r}^{2}K}H + C\left( {\alpha , n}\right) {K}^{4}
\]

\[
= {K}^{4}\left( {-c{\left( \frac{H}{{K}^{4}}\right) }^{2} + C\left( {\alpha ,\sqrt{K}r, n}\right) {\left( \frac{H}{{K}^{4}}\right) }^{3/2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {K}^{4}\left( {C\left( {\alpha ,\sqrt{K}r, n}\right) \frac{H}{{K}^{4}} + C\left( {\alpha , n}\right) }\right) .
\]

(Note that if \( r \) scales like \( 1/\sqrt{K} \) , ignoring the dependence on \( n,\alpha \) , and \( \sqrt{K}r \) , then since \( H \) scales like \( {K}^{4} \) , all of the terms scale like \( {K}^{4} \) .) Now (14.20) implies

\[
H \leq  C\left( {\alpha , K, r, n}\right)  = C\left( {\alpha ,\sqrt{K}r, n}\right) {K}^{4},
\]

where \( C\left( {n,\sqrt{K}r,\alpha }\right) \) depends only on \( n,\sqrt{K}r \) , and \( \alpha \) . Hence

\[
{17}{K}^{2}t{\left| \nabla \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} \leq  t\left( {{16}{K}^{2} + {\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  C\left( {\alpha , K, r, n}\right)  = C\left( {\alpha ,\sqrt{K}r, n}\right) {K}^{4}
\]

in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) , which implies

\[
\left| {\nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  \leq  \frac{C\left( {n, K, r,\alpha }\right) }{\sqrt{t}} = \frac{C\left( {n,\sqrt{K}r,\alpha }\right) K}{\sqrt{t}}
\]

in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack \) . This completes the proof of the theorem modulo the next lemma.

\[
0 \leq   - \frac{c}{{K}^{4}}{H}^{2} + \frac{C\left( {\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma , n}\right) }{{K}^{2}}{H}^{3/2} + C\left( {\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma , n}\right) H + C\left( {\alpha , n}\right) {K}^{4}
\]

nodes.proof:
The case where \( m = 1 \) is Theorem 14.10. We shall assume by induction that given \( m \in  \mathbb{N} \) ,

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{j}\operatorname{Rm}}\right|  \leq  \frac{C\left( {\alpha , K, r, j, n}\right) }{{t}^{j/2}}\text{ in }{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{j}}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack
\]

for \( j = 1,\ldots , m \) , and we shall prove

(14.21)

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}}\right|  \leq  \frac{C\left( {\alpha , K, r, m + 1, n}\right) }{{t}^{\left( {m + 1}\right) /2}}\text{ in }{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m + 1}}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack .
\]

Clearly, there really is nothing special about the radius \( r/{2}^{m + 1} \) and essentially the same argument gives the estimate in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right) \) , from which the theorem follows.

In the discussion below the constant \( C \) may change from line to line and depends on some or all of \( \alpha , K, r, m \) , and \( n \) . Let

(14.22)

\[
{F}_{m} \Doteq  \left( {C + {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2},
\]

where \( C \) is to be chosen. The main calculation is given by

LEMMA 14.15 (Nice evolution equation for derivative quantity). If

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{j}\operatorname{Rm}}\right|  \leq  \frac{C\left( {\alpha , K, r, j, n}\right) }{{t}^{j/2}}
\]

in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack \) for \( j = 1,\ldots , m \) , then

(14.23)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m} \leq   - \frac{c}{t}{\left( {F}_{m}\right) }^{2} + \frac{C}{t}\;\text{ in }{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack .
\]

We may now obtain the theorem from Lemma 14.15. In particular, we choose \( \eta \) to be a nice cutoff function with \( \eta  = 1 \) in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m + 1}}\right) \) and support in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right) \) as in Lemma 14.4. We shall compute the evolution inequality for \( \eta {F}_{m} \) and conclude that \( \eta {F}_{m} \) is bounded. Since, by now we already have a local first derivative of curvature estimate, assumption (14.8) in Lemma 14.4 holds and consequently the bound on the Laplacian of the cutoff function holds at all points. In this sense the local derivative estimates of orders greater than 1 are easier to obtain.

Using (14.23), we compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\eta {F}_{m}}\right)  \leq  \frac{\eta }{t}\left( {-c{F}_{m}^{2} + C}\right)  - {\Delta \eta } \cdot  {F}_{m} - 2\nabla \eta  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m},
\]

where \( c \) and \( C \) are as in Lemma 14.15. At a point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) where \( \eta {F}_{m} \) attains its maximum in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\eta {F}_{m}}\right)  \geq  0,\;\Delta \left( {\eta {F}_{m}}\right)  \leq  0,\;0 = \nabla \left( {\eta {F}_{m}}\right)  = \eta \nabla {F}_{m} + {F}_{m}\nabla \eta .
\]

Hence, at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
0 \leq  \frac{1}{t}\left( {-c{\left( \eta {F}_{m}\right) }^{2} + {C\eta }}\right)  - {\Delta \eta }\left( {\eta {F}_{m}}\right)  + 2{F}_{m}{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2}.
\]

Let \( {G}_{m} \Doteq  \eta {F}_{m} \) . Using the above bounds (14.9) and (14.10) for \( {\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2} \) and \( {\Delta \eta } \) and the facts that \( \eta  \leq  1 \) and \( t \leq  \tau  \leq  \alpha /K \) , we have at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \)

\[
0 \leq   - c{G}_{m}^{2} + C + C\left( {\alpha , K, r, m, n}\right) {G}_{m}
\]

which implies for \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \)

\[
{G}_{m}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {G}_{m}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  C\left( {\alpha , K, r, m, n}\right) ,
\]

where \( C\left( {\alpha , K, r, m, n}\right) \) depends only on \( \alpha , K, r, m \) , and \( n \) . Hence

\[
C{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;R}\mathrm{m}\right| }^{2} \leq  \left( {C + {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;R}\mathrm{m}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;R}\mathrm{m}\right| }^{2}
\]

(14.24)

\[
\leq  C\left( {\alpha , K, r, m, n}\right)
\]

in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m + 1}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) , which implies

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  \leq  \frac{C\left( {\alpha , K, r, m + 1, n}\right) }{{t}^{\left( {m + 1}\right) /2}}
\]

in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m + 1}}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack \) . This proves (14.21) and hence the theorem.

nodes.proof:
Recall from (7.4) on p. 229 of Volume One that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} = \Delta {\left| {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\ell  = 0}}^{k}{\nabla }^{\ell }\mathrm{{Rm}} * {\nabla }^{k - \ell }\mathrm{{Rm}} * {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{{Rm}}
\]

(14.25)

\[
\leq  \Delta {\left| {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\ell  = 0}}^{k}\left| {{\nabla }^{\ell }\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{k - \ell }\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| ,
\]

where for tensors \( A \) and \( B, A * B \) denotes a linear combination of contractions of the tensor product of \( A \) and \( B \) . Hence

(14.26)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{k}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right)  \leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{k}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{k}{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C{t}^{k}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\ell  = 0}}^{k}\left| {{\nabla }^{\ell }\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{k - \ell }\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  + k{t}^{k - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}.
\]

In particular, by our assumption that for \( j = 1,\ldots , m \) , there exist constants \( {C}_{j} \) depending only on \( j, K, r,\alpha \) , and \( n \) such that

\[
{t}^{j/2}\left| {{\nabla }^{j}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{j}\;\text{ in }{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack  ,
\]

we have in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right)  \leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C{t}^{m + 1}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\ell  = 0}}^{{m + 1}}\left| {{\nabla }^{\ell }\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1 - \ell }\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}}\right|
\]

\[
+ \left( {m + 1}\right) {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C{t}^{\left( {m + 1}\right) /2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|
\]

\[
+ \left( {{2Ct}\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  + m + 1}\right) {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C{t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + {Ct}
\]

where we used \( {2Ct}\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  + m + 1 \leq  \frac{1}{2}C \) .

From (14.26) and the local bounds on the first \( m \) derivatives of Rm, we have in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + m{t}^{m - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + C,
\]

since

\[
{t}^{m}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\ell  = 0}}^{m}\left| {{\nabla }^{\ell }\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m - \ell }\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}}\right|  \leq  C.
\]

Hence if \( C \) is chosen so that \( 4{t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  C \) , then in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times \; \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left\lbrack  {\left( {C + {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
= \left( {C + {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left\lbrack  {\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {C + {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) }\right\rbrack  {t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- 2{t}^{{2m} + 1}\nabla {\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \cdot  \nabla {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {C + {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {-2{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + C{t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + {Ct}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {-2{t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + m{t}^{m - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + C}\right) {t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- 2{t}^{{2m} + 1}\nabla {\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} \cdot  \nabla {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq   - {10}{t}^{{2m} + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 8{t}^{{2m} + 1}\left| {{\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|
\]

\[
- 2{t}^{{2m} + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4} + \left( {C + {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {C{t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + {Ct}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {m{t}^{m - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + C}\right) \left( {{t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{2}{5t}{\left( {t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2} + C\left( {1 + t}\right) {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + {Ct} + \frac{C}{t}
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{c}{t}{\left\lbrack  \left( C + {t}^{m}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;R}\mathrm{\;m}\right| }^{2}\right) {t}^{m + 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;R}\mathrm{\;m}\right| }^{2}\right\rbrack  }^{2} + \frac{C}{t},
\]

where the term with the coefficient \( - \frac{2}{5} \) arose from applying the inequality \( - {10}{x}^{2} + {8xy} - 2{y}^{2} \leq   - \frac{2}{5}{y}^{2} \) , and we used

\[
m{t}^{m - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + C \leq  C + \frac{C}{t} \leq  \frac{{C}^{\prime }}{t}.
\]

The lemma follows from the definition of \( {F}_{m} \) .

THEOREM 14.16 (Shi's estimates with some initial derivative bounds). For any integers \( \ell  \geq  0, n \geq  2 \) , and \( m \geq  1 \) and any positive numbers \( \alpha \) , \( K,{K}_{\ell } \) , and \( r \) , there exists \( C < \infty \) depending only on \( \alpha , K,{K}_{\ell }, r,\ell , m \) , and \( n \) such that if \( {\mathcal{M}}^{n} \) is a manifold and \( p \in  \mathcal{M} \) , if \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) , where \( 0 < \tau  \leq  \alpha /K \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow on an open neighborhood \( \mathcal{U} \) of p containing \( {\bar{B}}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r}\right) \) as a compact subset, and if

\[
\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  K\;\text{ for all }x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r}\right) \text{ and }t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack  ,
\]

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{\beta }\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,0}\right) }\right|  \leq  {K}_{\ell }\;\text{ for all }x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r}\right) \text{ and }\beta  \leq  \ell ,
\]

then

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {y, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{C}{{t}^{{\left( m - \ell \right) }_{ + }/2}}
\]

for all \( y \in  {\bar{B}}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right) \) and \( t \in  (0,\tau \rbrack \) . In particular if \( m \leq  \ell \) , then we have the uniform bound

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {y, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  C
\]

on \( {\bar{B}}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) .

Let \( \eta  : \mathcal{U} \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) be a cutoff function with \( \eta  = 1 \) on \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m + 1}}\right) \) , with support in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right) \) , and satisfying \( {\eta }^{-1}{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }\eta  \leq  \bar{C} \) for some \( \bar{C} < \infty \) (as in Lemma 14.4).

(1) When \( m - \ell  + 1 \leq  0 \) , i.e., \( \operatorname{sign}\left( {\left( m - \ell  + 1\right) }_{ + }\right)  = 0 \) , we have \( {F}_{m,\ell } = \; \left( {\widetilde{C} + {\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \) and inequality (14.29) says that

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {F}_{m,\ell } \leq   - c{\left( {F}_{m,\ell }\right) }^{2} + C.
\]

\[
\operatorname{sign}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} 1 & \text{ if }s > 0 \\  0 & \text{ if }s = 0 \\   - 1 & \text{ if }s < 0 \end{array}\right.
\]

From this we compute

(14.30)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\eta {F}_{m,\ell }}\right)  \leq  \eta \left( {-c{\left( {F}_{m,\ell }\right) }^{2} + C}\right)  - {\Delta \eta } \cdot  {F}_{m,\ell } - 2\nabla \eta  \cdot  \nabla {F}_{m,\ell }.
\]

---

---

Let \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) be a point where \( \eta {F}_{m,\ell } \) attains its maximum in \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times \; \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) . The maximum is attained and is finite by the assumptions on the derivatives of curvature of the initial metric in the theorem.

(i) If \( {t}_{0} = 0 \) , then the estimate follows by hypothesis.

(ii) If \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) , then the maximum principle implies that \( \eta {F}_{m,\ell } \) is bounded, in particular, using \( {F}_{m,\ell }\nabla \eta  + \eta \nabla {F}_{m,\ell } = 0 \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) and multiplying (14.30) by \( \eta \) , we have

\[
0 \leq   - c{\left( \eta {F}_{m,\ell }\right) }^{2} + C{\eta }^{2} + \left( {-{\Delta \eta } + 2{\eta }^{-1}{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2}}\right) \eta {F}_{m,\ell }.
\]

Since \( - {\Delta \eta } + 2{\eta }^{-1}{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2} \) is bounded, we obtain a bound for \( \eta {F}_{m,\ell } \) .

(2) When \( m - \ell  + 1 > 0 \) , i.e., \( \operatorname{sign}\left( {\left( m - \ell  + 1\right) }_{ + }\right)  = 1 \) , using (14.29), we see that \( \eta {F}_{m,\ell } \) satisfies the evolution inequality:

\[
\eta \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\eta {F}_{m,\ell }}\right)  \leq   - 2\nabla \eta  \cdot  \nabla \left( {\eta {F}_{m,\ell }}\right)  - \frac{c}{t}{\left( \eta {F}_{m,\ell }\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {-{\Delta \eta } + 2{\eta }^{-1}{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2}}\right) \eta {F}_{m,\ell } + \frac{C{\eta }^{2}}{t}.
\]

Again let \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) be a point where \( \eta {F}_{m,\ell } \) attains its maximum. If \( {t}_{0} = 0 \) , we are done, whereas if \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) , then at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
0 \leq   - c{\left( \eta {F}_{m,\ell }\right) }^{2} + t\left( {-{\Delta \eta } + 2{\eta }^{-1}{\left| \nabla \eta \right| }^{2}}\right) \eta {F}_{m,\ell } + C{\eta }^{2}.
\]

We conclude that

\[
\eta {F}_{m,\ell } = \eta \left( {\widetilde{C} + {t}^{\left( m - \ell \right) } + {\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{\left( m - \ell  + 1\right) } + {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

is bounded. Hence \( \eta {t}^{{\left( m - \ell  + 1\right) }_{ + }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  C \) on \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) for some \( C < \infty \) . Since \( \eta  = 1 \) on \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m + 1}}\right) \) , we conclude that

(14.31)

\[
{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{C}{{t}^{{\left( m - \ell  + 1\right) }_{ + }}}
\]

on \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m + 1}}\right)  \times  (0,\tau \rbrack \) .

nodes.proof:
By hypothesis we fix \( \ell \) and assume by induction that for \( j = 1,\ldots , m \) there exist constants \( {C}_{j} \) depending only on \( \alpha , K \) , \( {K}_{\ell }, r, n,\ell \) , and \( m \) such that for \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{j}}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
{t}^{{\left( j - \ell \right) }_{ + }/2}\left| {{\nabla }^{j}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{j}.
\]

Recall from (14.25) that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{k}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{k - i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| .
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{{\left( k - \ell \right) }_{ + }}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{\left( k - \ell \right) }_{ + }}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

(14.32)

\[
- 2{t}^{{\left( k - \ell \right) }_{ + }}{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C{t}^{{\left( k - \ell \right) }_{ + }}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{k}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{k - i}\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{k}\operatorname{Rm}}\right|
\]

\[
+ {\left( k - \ell \right) }_{ + }{t}^{{\left( k - \ell \right) }_{ + } - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Using our induction hypothesis that

\[
{t}^{{\left( j - \ell \right) }_{ + }/2}\left| {{\nabla }^{j}\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{j}\;\text{ on }{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/{2}^{m}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack
\]

for \( j = 1,\ldots , m \) , we have with

\[
{m}_{\ell } \Doteq  {\left( m - \ell  + 1\right) }_{ + }\;\text{ and }\;{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } \Doteq  {\left( m - \ell \right) }_{ + }
\]

that (by taking \( k = m + 1 \) in (14.32); note also that \( {m}_{\ell } - 1 = {\widehat{m}}_{\ell } \) if \( {m}_{\ell } \neq  0 \) )

(14.33)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{{m + 1}}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1 - i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  + {m}_{\ell }{t}^{{m}_{\ell } - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C{t}^{{m}_{\ell }/2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|  + \left( {{2C}\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| {t}^{{m}_{\ell }} + {m}_{\ell }{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}}\right) {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;R}\mathrm{m}\right| }^{2} + C{t}^{{m}_{\ell } - {\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}
\]

using \( {t}^{{m}_{\ell }} \leq  C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }} \) for \( t \leq  \tau \) to obtain the last inequality and since

\[
{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{m}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m + 1 - i}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  C{t}^{{\left( m + 1 - \ell \right) }_{ + }}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{m}{t}^{-{\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + }/2 - {\left( m + 1 - i - \ell \right) }_{ + }/2}
\]

\[
\leq  C{t}^{{\left( m + 1 - \ell \right) }_{ + }/2}
\]

where we used \( {\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + } + {\left( m + 1 - i - \ell \right) }_{ + } \leq  {\left( m + 1 - \ell \right) }_{ + } \) ,6 which can be seen as follows:

(i) If \( i \in  \left\lbrack  {1,\ell }\right\rbrack \) , then \( {\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + } = 0 \) so that

\[
{\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + } + {\left( m + 1 - i - \ell \right) }_{ + } = {\left( m + 1 - i - \ell \right) }_{ + } \leq  {\left( m + 1 - \ell \right) }_{ + }.
\]

(ii) If \( i \in  \left\lbrack  {m + 1 - \ell , m}\right\rbrack \) , then \( {\left( m + 1 - i - \ell \right) }_{ + } = 0 \) so that

\[
{\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + } + {\left( m + 1 - i - \ell \right) }_{ + } = {\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + } \leq  {\left( m + 1 - \ell \right) }_{ + }.
\]

(iii) If \( i \in  \left\lbrack  {\ell  + 1, m - \ell }\right\rbrack \) and \( 2\ell  < m \) , then

\[
{\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + } + {\left( m + 1 - i - \ell \right) }_{ + } = m + 1 - 2\ell  \leq  {\left( m + 1 - \ell \right) }_{ + }.
\]

From taking \( k = m \) in (14.32) and the induction hypothesis, we have

(14.34)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  \leq  \Delta \left( {{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}}\right)  - 2{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ {\widehat{m}}_{\ell }{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + C
\]

since

\[
C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}\left| {{\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{m}\left| {{\nabla }^{i}\operatorname{Rm}}\right| \left| {{\nabla }^{m - i}\operatorname{Rm}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }/2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{m}{t}^{-{\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + }/2 - {\left( m - i - \ell \right) }_{ + }/2} \leq  C.
\]

---

\( {}^{6} \) Exercise: Show that if \( \ell  > 0 \) , then \( {\left( i - \ell \right) }_{ + } + {\left( m + 1 - i - \ell \right) }_{ + } \leq  {\left( m - \ell \right) }_{ + } \) .

---

Hence if \( \widetilde{C} \) is chosen so that \( 4{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  \widetilde{C} \) , then by (14.33) and (14.34) we have (note that \( {t}^{{m}_{\ell } - {\widehat{m}}_{\ell }} \leq  C \) for \( t \leq  \tau \) )

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\left( {\widetilde{C} + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {\widetilde{C} + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {-2{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + C}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {-2{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + {\widehat{m}}_{\ell }{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + C}\right) {t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- 2{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } + {m}_{\ell }}\nabla {\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} \cdot  \nabla {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq   - {10}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } + {m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 2}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {\widetilde{C} + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + C}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } + {m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4} + \left( {{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } - 1}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} + C}\right) {t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 8{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } + {m}_{\ell }}\left| {{\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right| {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}\left| {{\nabla }^{m + 2}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right|
\]

using \( \widetilde{C} + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \geq  5{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \) to obtain the second inequality. Hence (note that \( {m}_{\ell } - 1 = {\widehat{m}}_{\ell } \) if \( {\widehat{m}}_{\ell } \neq  0 \) )

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\left( {\widetilde{C} + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2})}\right.
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{2}{5}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } + {m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{4} + \frac{5}{4}\widetilde{C}\left( {C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + C}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {\frac{1}{4}\widetilde{C}{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }{t}^{{m}_{\ell } - 1} + C{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}}\right) {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{\;{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
=  - \frac{2}{5}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } + {m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{4} + \frac{5}{4}\widetilde{C}C
\]

\[
+ \left( {\left( {\frac{5}{4}\widetilde{C}C + \frac{1}{4}\widetilde{C}{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}\right) {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }} + C{t}^{{m}_{\ell }}}\right) {\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2}
\]

since \( {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\mathrm{{Rm}}\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{1}{4}\widetilde{C} \) . From this we obtain

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\left( {\widetilde{C} + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{2}{5}{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } + {m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{4} + C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2} + \frac{5}{4}\widetilde{C}C
\]

\[

\]

(again using \( {t}^{{m}_{\ell }} \leq  C{t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }} \) for \( t \leq  \tau \) ). Since \( \operatorname{sign}\left( {m}_{\ell }\right)  = {m}_{\ell } - {\widehat{m}}_{\ell } \) , we conclude

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\left( {\widetilde{C} + {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right) {t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{c}{5{t}^{\operatorname{sign}\left( {m}_{\ell }\right) }}{\left( {t}^{{m}_{\ell }}{\left| {\nabla }^{m + 1}\operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}\right) }^{2} + C{t}^{-\operatorname{sign}\left( {m}_{\ell }\right) }
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{c}{{t}^{\operatorname{sign}\left( {m}_{\ell }\right) }}{F}_{m,\ell }^{2} + \frac{C}{{t}^{\operatorname{sign}\left( {m}_{\ell }\right) }},
\]

using \( {t}^{{\widehat{m}}_{\ell } + {m}_{\ell }} = {t}^{2{m}_{\ell }} \cdot  {t}^{-\operatorname{sign}\left( {m}_{\ell }\right) } \) . The lemma follows.

nodes.content:
THEOREM 14.19 (Modified Cheeger-Gromov-type compactness theorem). Let \( {\left\{  \left( {\mathcal{M}}_{k}^{n},{g}_{k}\left( t\right) ,{p}_{k}\right) \right\}  }_{k \in  \mathbb{N}}, t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a sequence of pointed complete solutions of the Ricci flow which satisfy the following assumptions:

(i) (derivative bounds for initial metric) for some \( {m}_{0} \in  \mathbb{N} \cup  \{ \infty \} \) we have

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{k \in  \mathbb{N}}}\left( {\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{k}}}\left| {{\nabla }^{m}{\operatorname{Rm}}_{{g}_{k}\left( 0\right) }\left( x\right) }\right| }\right)  < \infty
\]

for \( 0 \leq  m \leq  {m}_{0} + 1 \) ,

(ii) (space-time curvature bound)

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{k \in  \mathbb{N}}}\left( {\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{k} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}_{0}}\right\rbrack  }}\left| {{\operatorname{Rm}}_{{g}_{k}\left( t\right) }\left( x\right) }\right| }\right)  < \infty
\]

for any \( {T}_{0} < T \) ,

(iii) (injectivity radius lower bound) inj \( {}_{{g}_{k}\left( 0\right) }\left( {p}_{k}\right)  \geq  \delta \) for some \( \delta  > 0 \) .

Part (1). Without loss of generality, we may assume \( \tau  \leq \; \alpha \left( n\right) /K \) , where \( \alpha \left( n\right) \) is a constant to be chosen later. By the local derivative estimate, for all \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right) \) , we have \( \left| {\nabla \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,\tau }\right) }\right|  \leq  C\left( {n, K, r,\tau }\right) \) . Now

\[

\]

where \( \beta \) is a minimal geodesic joining \( p \) and \( x \) and \( {ds} \) denotes the arc length element of \( \beta \) with respect to \( g\left( \tau \right) \) . Choosing \( \alpha \left( n\right)  > 0 \) small enough, we have \( g\left( \tau \right)  \leq  {2g}\left( 0\right) \) , so that by choosing \( \eta \left( {n, K, r,\tau , c}\right)  > 0 \) small enough, we conclude \( {\lambda }_{1}\left( \operatorname{Rm}\right) \left( {x,\tau }\right)  \geq  \frac{c}{2}K \) for all \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p,\eta }\right) \) .

\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r/2}\right) \) . Hence, taking \( \beta \) to be the same as above, we have

\[
{\lambda }_{1}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) \left( {x,\tau }\right)  \geq  {\lambda }_{1}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) \left( {p,\tau }\right)  - {\int }_{\beta }\left| {\nabla \mathrm{{Rm}}\left( {\beta \left( s\right) ,\tau }\right) }\right| {ds}
\]

\[

\]

nodes.content: Proposition 14.25 (Short time existence for the local RF). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n},{g}_{0}}\right) \) is a complete Riemannian manifold, then there exists \( \delta  > 0 \) depending only on \( {g}_{0} \) restricted to the support of \( \chi \) such that there exists a solution \( g\left( t\right) \) , \( t \in  \lbrack 0,\delta ) \) , to the local Ricci flow with \( g\left( 0\right)  = {g}_{0} \) .

If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n},{g}_{0}}\right) \) is a complete Riemannian manifold, then there exists \( \delta > 0 \) depending only on \( {g}_{0} \) restricted to the support of \( \chi \) such that there exists a solution \( g\left( t\right) \) , \( t \in \lbrack 0,\delta ) \) , to the local Ricci flow with \( g\left( 0\right) = {g}_{0} \) .

nodes.proof:
As on pp. 90-91 of [505] we use DeTurck's trick. In particular, consider the local Ricci-DeTurck flow defined by (analogous to (3.33a) in Volume One7)

(14.38)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{\chi }^{2}{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\left( {\chi }^{2}W\right) }_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}{\left( {\chi }^{2}W\right) }_{i},
\]

where (as in (3.34) in Volume One)

\[
{W}_{j} \Doteq  {g}_{jk}{g}^{pq}\left( {{\Gamma }_{pq}^{k} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{pq}^{k}}\right)
\]

and \( \widetilde{\Gamma } \) is a fixed background connection. Define the 1-parameter family of diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{t} : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) by

(14.39)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\varphi }_{t}\left( p\right)  =  - \left( {{\chi }^{2}W}\right) \left( {{\varphi }_{t}\left( p\right) , t}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\varphi }_{0} = {\operatorname{id}}_{\mathcal{M}}
\]

(Note that \( {\varphi }_{t}\left( x\right)  = x \) for \( x \in  \mathcal{M} - \operatorname{supp}\left( \chi \right) \) .) As on p. 81 of Volume One, we compute that

(14.40)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\varphi }_{t}^{ * }g\left( t\right) }\right)  =  - 2{\chi }^{2}\operatorname{Rc}\left( {{\varphi }_{t}^{ * }g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

Hence, if we can solve (14.38) with \( g\left( 0\right)  = {g}_{0} \) , then since (14.39) is an ODE and solvable, we obtain a solution \( \bar{g}\left( t\right)  \doteq  {\varphi }_{t}^{ * }g\left( t\right) \) to the local Ricci flow (14.40).

Now we show that we can solve (14.38) for a short time. First, (14.38) may be expressed as

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{\chi }^{2}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{W}_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}{W}_{i}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {2\chi }\left( {{\nabla }_{i}\chi {W}_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}\chi {W}_{i}}\right) ,
\]

where the second line is first-order in the metric \( g \) . By the displayed equation between (3.30) and (3.31) on p. 80 of Volume One, we have that if \( \frac{\partial }{\partial s}{g}_{ij} = \; - 2{h}_{ij} \) , then

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial s}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{W}_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}{W}_{i}}\right)  = \Delta {h}_{ij} + {U}_{ij},
\]

---

\( {}^{7} \) The only difference between (14.38) here and (3.33a) in Volume One is that on the RHS of (14.38) both Rc and \( W \) are multiplied by the cutoff function \( {\chi }^{2} \) .

---

where \( {U}_{ij} \) is a linear first-order expression in \( h \) . Hence the linearization of the local Ricci-DeTurck flow is given by

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{h}_{ij} = {\chi }^{2}\Delta {h}_{ij} + {V}_{ij},
\]

where \( {V}_{ij} \) is first-order in \( h \) . Short time existence can be established from this fact; see the remarks on p. 91 of [505].

Henceforth, \( \triangleq \) will denote an equality that holds for expanding gradient Ricci solitons with \( c\left( t\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\log t \) . An expanding gradient Ricci soliton flowing along the vector field \( \nabla f\left( t\right) \) with \( c\left( t\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\log t \) satisfies

(15.2)

\[
{R}_{ij} + \frac{1}{2t}{g}_{ij}\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = } - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f.
\]

More generally, for a gradient Ricci soliton, we have

(15.3)

\[
{R}_{ij} + \dot{c}\left( t\right) {g}_{ij}\overset{\mathrm{G}}{ = } - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f,
\]

where \( \overset{\mathrm{G}}{ = } \) denotes an equality which holds for all gradient Ricci solitons.

Defining

(15.9)

\[
{M}_{ij} \Doteq  \bigtriangleup {R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}R + 2{R}_{\ell {ij}}^{p}{R}_{p}^{\ell } - {R}_{i}^{p}{R}_{pj} + \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ij},
\]

we may rewrite (15.8) as

(15.10)

\[
{M}_{ij} - {P}_{pji}{\nabla }^{p}f\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = }0.
\]

Note that contracting (15.7) with \( {\nabla }^{k}f \) shows that the second term in (15.10) is symmetric in \( i \) and \( j \) . Adding this contraction to (15.10), we have

(15.11)

\[
{M}_{ij} - \left( {{P}_{pji} + {P}_{pij}}\right) {\nabla }^{p}f + {R}_{pij}^{q}{\nabla }_{q}f{\nabla }^{p}f\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = }0.
\]

Thus, for any vector \( W \) we have

\[
{M}_{ij}{W}^{i}{W}^{j} - \left( {{P}_{pji} + {P}_{pij}}\right) {\nabla }^{p}f{W}^{i}{W}^{j} + {R}_{pij}^{q}{\nabla }_{q}f{\nabla }^{p}f{W}^{i}{W}^{j}\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = }0.
\]

Setting \( U = W \land  \nabla f \) , that is, \( {U}_{ij} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{W}_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - {W}_{j}{\nabla }_{i}f}\right) \) , this becomes

\[
{M}_{ij}{W}^{i}{W}^{j} + 2{P}_{pij}{U}^{pi}{W}^{j} + {R}_{pijq}{U}^{qj}{U}^{pi}\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = }0.
\]

Proposition 15.14 (Maximum principle for bilinear forms). Let \( {F}_{t} \) : \( {\mathcal{V}}^{ * } \otimes  {\mathcal{V}}^{ * } \rightarrow  {\mathcal{V}}^{ * } \otimes  {\mathcal{V}}^{ * }, t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a fiber-preserving map with the following properties.

---

(1) \( \left( {{F}_{t}\text{ is locally Lipschitz })}\right. \) For any \( C < \infty \) there exists \( {C}_{0} < \infty \) such

	that

---

(15.27)

\[
\left| {{F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{1}\right)  - {F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{2}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{0}\left| {{Q}_{1} - {Q}_{2}}\right|
\]

\[
\text{ for all }{Q}_{1},{Q}_{2} \in  {\mathcal{V}}^{ * } \otimes  {\mathcal{V}}^{ * }\text{ with }\left| {Q}_{1}\right| ,\left| {Q}_{2}\right|  \leq  C\text{ . }
\]

(2) (Null-eigenvector property) If \( {Q}_{0} \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}^{ * } \otimes  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}}^{ * } \) and \( {V}_{0} \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{0}} \) , where \( {x}_{0} \in  \mathcal{M} \) , are such that \( {Q}_{0} \geq  0 \) and \( {Q}_{0}\left( {V}_{0}\right)  = 0 \) , then for any \( {t}_{0} \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) we have at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \)

(15.28)

\[
{F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{0}\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

Further suppose that \( Q\left( t\right)  \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( {{\mathcal{V}}^{ * } \otimes  {\mathcal{V}}^{ * }}\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , satisfies the following properties. There exist constants \( {C}_{1},{C}_{2},{C}_{3} < \infty \) such that at any point \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) and any \( V \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}^{\prime }} \) there exists an extension of \( V \) to a space-time neighborhood of \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) such that at \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) we have

(15.29)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {Q\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {Q\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  + {F}_{t}\left( Q\right) \left( {V, V}\right) ,
\]

(15.30)

\[
\frac{\partial h}{\partial t} \geq   - {C}_{1}h
\]

(15.31)

\[
\left| {\nabla V}\right|  \leq  {C}_{2}\left| V\right|
\]

(15.32)

\[
\left| {\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) V}\right|  \leq  {C}_{3}\left| V\right|
\]

If \( Q\left( 0\right)  \geq  0 \) , then \( Q\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

nodes.proof:
Define for any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \)

\[
{Q}_{\varepsilon } \Doteq  Q + \varepsilon \left( {\delta  + t - {t}_{0}}\right) h\left( t\right) ,
\]

where \( \delta  > 0 \) will be chosen below, so that for any \( V \in  \mathcal{V} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \)

\[
{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right)  = Q\left( {V, V}\right)  + \varepsilon \left( {\delta  + t - {t}_{0}}\right) {\left| V\right| }_{h\left( t\right) }^{2}.
\]

At any point \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) and for any \( V \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) , provided (15.29) holds at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) , we compute

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {Q\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  + {F}_{t}\left( Q\right) \left( {V, V}\right)  + {2\varepsilon }\left( {\delta  + t - {t}_{0}}\right) \left\langle  {\frac{\partial V}{\partial t}, V}\right\rangle
\]

\[
+ \varepsilon \left( {\delta  + t - {t}_{0}}\right) \frac{\partial h}{\partial t}\left( {V, V}\right)  + \varepsilon {\left| V\right| }_{h\left( t\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
= \Delta \left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  + {2\varepsilon }\left( {\delta  + t - {t}_{0}}\right) \left\langle  {\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) V, V}\right\rangle
\]

\[
- {2\varepsilon }\left( {\delta  + t - {t}_{0}}\right) {\left| \nabla V\right| }^{2} + {F}_{t}\left( Q\right) \left( {V, V}\right)
\]

\[
+ \varepsilon \left( {\delta  + t - {t}_{0}}\right) \frac{\partial h}{\partial t}\left( {V, V}\right)  + \varepsilon {\left| V\right| }_{h\left( t\right) }^{2},
\]

where we used

\[
\Delta {\left| V\right| }_{h\left( t\right) }^{2} = 2\langle {\Delta V}, V\rangle  + 2{\left| \nabla V\right| }^{2}.
\]

Provided (15.30)-(15.32) hold at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) , where \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{0} + \delta }\right\rbrack \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  + \left( {1 - \left( {4{C}_{3} + 4{C}_{2} + 2{C}_{1}}\right) \delta }\right) \varepsilon {\left| V\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ {F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\right) \left( {V, V}\right)  + \left( {{F}_{t}\left( Q\right)  - {F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\right) }\right) \left( {V, V}\right) .
\]

On the other hand, by (15.27) we have

\[
\left( {{F}_{t}\left( Q\right)  - {F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\right) }\right) \left( {V, V}\right)  \geq   - \left| {{F}_{t}\left( Q\right)  - {F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\right) }\right| {\left| V\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq   - {C}_{0}\left| {Q - {Q}_{\varepsilon }}\right| {\left| V\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
=  - {C}_{0}\varepsilon \left( {\delta  + t - {t}_{0}}\right) \sqrt{k}{\left| V\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq   - 2\sqrt{k}{C}_{0}{\varepsilon \delta }{\left| V\right| }^{2}
\]

since \( \left| {h\left( t\right) }\right|  = \sqrt{k} \) . Hence

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  + {F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\right) \left( {V, V}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {1 - \left( {4{C}_{3} + 4{C}_{2} + 2{C}_{1} + 2\sqrt{k}{C}_{0}}\right) \delta }\right) \varepsilon {\left| V\right| }^{2}.
\]

Therefore choosing \( \delta  = \min \left\{  {\frac{1}{2}{\left( 4{C}_{3} + 4{C}_{2} + 2{C}_{1} + 2\sqrt{k}{C}_{0}\right) }^{-1}, T}\right\} \) , we have, provided (15.29)-(15.32) hold at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) ,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V, V}\right) }\right)  + {F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\right) \left( {V, V}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon {\left| V\right| }^{2}.
\]

Suppose that \( Q\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \geq  0 \) , where \( {t}_{0} \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T - \delta }\right\rbrack \) . We shall show that \( Q\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{0} + \delta }\right\rbrack \) . The proposition follows easily from this assertion.

Since \( Q\left( {t}_{0}\right)  \geq  0 \) and \( \varepsilon ,\delta  > 0 \) , we have \( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {t}_{0}\right)  > 0 \) . We claim that for any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we have \( {Q}_{\varepsilon } > 0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{0} + \delta }\right\rbrack \) . This claim implies \( Q\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{0} + \delta }\right\rbrack \) by taking the limit as \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) . To prove the claim, we assume it is false and derive a contradiction. That is, suppose that \( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {V}_{0}\right)  = 0 \) at \( \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) \) and \( {Q}_{\varepsilon } \geq  0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) for some nonzero \( {V}_{0},{t}_{1} \in  \left( {{t}_{0},{t}_{0} + \delta }\right\rbrack \) , and \( {x}_{1} \in  \mathcal{M} \) . In a neighborhood of \( \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) \) we extend \( {V}_{0} \) so that \( \left( {15.29}\right)  - \left( {15.32}\right) \) hold at \( \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) \) . Using the null-eigenvector property, we then have at \( \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) \)

\[
0 \geq  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {{Q}_{\varepsilon }\left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right) }\right)  + {F}_{t}\left( {Q}_{\varepsilon }\right) \left( {{V}_{0},{V}_{0}}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon {\left| {V}_{0}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon {\left| {V}_{0}\right| }^{2}
\]

which is a contradiction. Hence \( {Q}_{\varepsilon } > 0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{0} + \delta }\right\rbrack \) for all \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) as claimed.

nodes.content:
THEOREM 15.16 (Matrix Harnack evolution equation). Let \( U \in  {\Lambda }^{2}\mathcal{M} \) , \( W \in  {\Lambda }^{1}\mathcal{M} \) , and let \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) be a point at which the heat operators and covariant derivatives of \( W \) and \( U \) are prescribed as

(15.39)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{a} = \frac{1}{t}{W}_{a}
\]

(15.40)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {U}_{ab} = 0,
\]

(15.41)

\[
{\nabla }_{a}{W}_{b} = 0,
\]

(15.42)

\[
{\nabla }_{a}{U}_{bc} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ab}{W}_{c} - {R}_{ac}{W}_{b}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ab}{W}_{c} - {g}_{ac}{W}_{b}}\right) .
\]

Then at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) the evolution of Hamilton’s matrix Harnack quadratic is given \( b{y}^{14} \)

(15.43)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q = 2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 8{R}_{adec}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + 4{R}_{aefc}{R}_{befd}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {R}_{abdc}{U}_{cd}}\right) \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + {R}_{abfe}{U}_{ef}}\right) .
\]

nodes.proof:
At a point where \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {U}_{ab} = 0 \) and \( {\nabla }_{a}{W}_{b} = 0 \) , by simply applying the heat operator to \( Q \) , we have that

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q = \left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {M}_{ab}}\right) {W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 2{M}_{ab}\left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{a}}\right) {W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 2\left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {P}_{abc}}\right) {U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + 2{P}_{abc}{U}_{ab}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{c}
\]

\[
- 4{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{abc}{\nabla }_{e}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + \left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{abdc}}\right) {U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
- 4{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{abdc}{\nabla }_{e}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd} - 2{R}_{abdc}{\nabla }_{e}{U}_{ab}{\nabla }_{e}{U}_{cd}
\]

If we substitute the expressions for the evolution equations (15.37), (15.45), and (15.46) of \( {M}_{ab},{P}_{abc} \) , and \( {R}_{abcd} \) , respectively, and use the hypotheses (15.39) and (15.42) on \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{a} \) and \( {\nabla }_{a}{U}_{bc} \) and equations (15.47) and identity (15.50), we get

(15.56)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q = \left( {2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right) }\right) {W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}}\right) {W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 2{M}_{ab}\frac{1}{t}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 2{P}_{abc}{U}_{ab}\frac{1}{t}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
+ 2\left( {2{R}_{adeb}{P}_{dec} + 2{R}_{adec}{P}_{dbe} + 2{R}_{bdec}{P}_{ade} - 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{abec}}\right) {U}_{ab}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
- 4{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{abc}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {R}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {g}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right) }\right) {W}_{c}
\]

\[
+ 2\left( {{B}_{abdc} - {B}_{abcd} + {B}_{adbc} - {B}_{acbd}}\right) {U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
- 4{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{abdc}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {R}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {g}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right) }\right) {U}_{cd}
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{abdc}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {R}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {g}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\times  \left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ec}{W}_{d} - {R}_{ed}{W}_{c}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ec}{W}_{d} - {g}_{ed}{W}_{c}}\right) }\right) .
\]

Now the term on the last two lines of (15.56) is equal to

\[
- 2{R}_{abdc}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {R}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {g}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\times  \left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ec}{W}_{d} - {R}_{ed}{W}_{c}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ec}{W}_{d} - {g}_{ed}{W}_{c}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
=  - 2{R}_{abdc}\left( {{R}_{ea}{W}_{b} + \frac{1}{2t}{g}_{ea}{W}_{b}}\right) \left( {{R}_{ec}{W}_{d} + \frac{1}{2t}{g}_{ec}{W}_{d}}\right)
\]

\[
=  - 2{R}_{abdc}{R}_{ea}{R}_{ec}{W}_{b}{W}_{d} - \frac{2}{t}{R}_{abdc}{R}_{ac}{W}_{b}{W}_{d} - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{bd}{W}_{b}{W}_{d},
\]

the term on the third line from the bottom of (15.56) is

\[
- 4{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{abdc}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {R}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {g}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right) }\right) {U}_{cd}
\]

\[
=  - 4{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{abdc}{R}_{ea}{W}_{b}{U}_{cd} - \frac{2}{t}{P}_{cdb}{W}_{b}{U}_{cd},
\]

and the term on the fifth line of (15.56) is

\[
- 4{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{abc}\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {R}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4\dot{t}}\left( {{g}_{ea}{W}_{b} - {g}_{eb}{W}_{a}}\right) }\right) {W}_{c}
\]

\[
=  - 4{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{abc}{R}_{ea}{W}_{b}{W}_{c} - \frac{2}{t}{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ebc}{W}_{b}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
=  - 4{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{abc}{R}_{ea}{W}_{b}{W}_{c} - \frac{2}{t}\left( {{M}_{bc} - {R}_{bdec}{R}_{de} - \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{bc}}\right) {W}_{b}{W}_{c},
\]

where we used (15.47).

Hence, by applying the above three identities and canceling terms in (15.56), we have

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q = 2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}}\right) {W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 2\left( {2{R}_{adeb}{P}_{dec} + 2{R}_{adec}{P}_{dbe} + 2{R}_{bdec}{P}_{ade}}\right) {U}_{ab}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
+ 2\left( {{B}_{abdc} - {B}_{abcd} + {B}_{adbc} - {B}_{acbd}}\right) {U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}.
\]

Since one infers from (6.14) on p. 179 of Volume One that

\[
2\left( {{B}_{abdc} - {B}_{abcd} + {B}_{adbc} - {B}_{acbd}}\right)
\]

\[
= {R}_{abef}{R}_{dcfe} - 2{R}_{eadf}{R}_{befc} + 2{R}_{eafc}{R}_{bedf},
\]

we may rewrite (15.57) as

(15.58)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q = 2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 8{R}_{adec}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + 4{R}_{eafc}{R}_{bedf}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ {P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 4{R}_{adeb}{P}_{dec}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + {R}_{abef}{R}_{dcfe}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}.
\]

Since

\[
2{R}_{adeb}{P}_{dec}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} = \left( {{R}_{adeb} + {R}_{eadb}}\right) {P}_{dec}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
=  - {R}_{deab}{P}_{dec}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c}
\]

equation (15.43) now follows from completing the square on the last line of (15.58).

nodes.content:
REMARK 15.17. The equation for \( {\nabla }_{a}{U}_{bc} \) in (15.42) is motivated by considering the special case of expanding gradient solitons. Namely, suppose \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g, f}\right) \) is an expanding gradient soliton, so that \( {\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}f\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = }{R}_{ab} + \frac{1}{2t}{g}_{ab} \) .

---

\( {}^{13} \) Due to the difference in sign convention, our definition of \( B \) is the negative of that of Hamilton’s in \( §7 \) of [244].

\( {}^{14} \) Note that since \( Q \) is a scalar, we have \( {\nabla }_{t}Q = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}Q \) .

---

Given a 1-form \( {W}_{a} \) , chosen so that (15.41), i.e., \( {\nabla }_{a}{W}_{b} = 0 \) , holds at a point, if we let

(15.44)

\[
{U}_{ab} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}f{W}_{b} - {W}_{a}{\nabla }_{b}f}\right) ,
\]

then we obtain equation (15.42):

\[
{\nabla }_{a}{U}_{bc}\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = }\frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ab}{W}_{c} - {R}_{ac}{W}_{b}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ab}{W}_{c} - {g}_{ac}{W}_{b}}\right) .
\]

Furthermore, using \( {}^{15} \)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) f\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = } - \frac{1}{t}f + C\left( t\right) \;\text{ and }\;\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{a}f = {\nabla }_{a}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) f
\]

and assuming (15.39) and (15.41), we compute that \( {U}_{ab} \) defined by (15.44) also satisfies

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {U}_{ab}\overset{\mathrm{E}}{ = }\frac{1}{2}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) f{W}_{b} - {W}_{a}{\nabla }_{b}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) f}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}f\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{b} - \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{a}{\nabla }_{b}f}\right)
\]

\[
= 0\text{ . }
\]

To calculate the evolution equation for \( Q \) , we need the evolution equations of \( {M}_{ab} \) and \( {P}_{abc} \) .

nodes.label: Lemma 15.18
nodes.document_title: Bennett Chow et al. - The Ricci Flow Techniques and Applications Part II Analytic Aspects

nodes.content:
LEMMA 15.18 ( \( {P}_{abc} \) evolution). The evolution equation of \( {P}_{abc} \) is given by

(15.45)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {P}_{abc} = 2{R}_{adeb}{P}_{dec} + 2{R}_{adec}{P}_{dbe}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{bdec}{P}_{ade} - 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{abec}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 15.18 ( \( {P}_{abc} \) evolution). The evolution equation of \( {P}_{abc} \) is given by (15.45) \[ \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {P}_{abc} = 2{R}_{adeb}{P}_{dec} + 2{R}_{adec}{P}_{dbe} \] \[ + 2{R}_{bdec}{P}_{ade} - 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{abec}. \]

nodes.proof:
Recall from (15.5) that \( {P}_{abc} = {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bc} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac} \) , and so

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {P}_{abc} = \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bc} - \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}.
\]

To calculate \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bc} \) , we use the commutator formula (15.34) and the evolution equation (15.36) for the Ricci tensor to find that

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bc} = {\nabla }_{a}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{bc} + 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ec} + 2{R}_{adec}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{{be}.}
\]

\[
= 2{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bdec}{R}_{de} + 2{R}_{bdec}{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{de}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ec} + 2{R}_{adec}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{be}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {P}_{abc} = 2{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bdec}{R}_{de} + 2{R}_{bdec}{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{de} + 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ec} + 2{R}_{adec}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{be}
\]

\[
- 2{\nabla }_{b}{R}_{adec}{R}_{de} - 2{R}_{adec}{\nabla }_{b}{R}_{de} - 2{R}_{beda}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{dc} - 2{R}_{bdec}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ae}
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{de}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bdec} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{adec}}\right)  + 2{R}_{bdec}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{de} - {\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ae}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{adeb}\left( {{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ec} - {\nabla }_{e}{R}_{dc}}\right)  + 2{R}_{adec}\left( {{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{be} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{de}}\right) .
\]

---

\( {}^{15} \) The equation \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) f =  - \frac{1}{t}f + C\left( t\right) \) may be derived from the formulas in \( §1 \) of Chapter 4 of [146].

---

The lemma now follows from the second Bianchi identity, i.e.,

\[
{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bdec} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{adec} =  - {\nabla }_{d}{R}_{abec},
\]

and the definition of \( {P}_{abc} \) .

nodes.label: Lemma 15.19
nodes.document_title: Bennett Chow et al. - The Ricci Flow Techniques and Applications Part II Analytic Aspects
nodes.section_title: 15.4. Proof of the matrix Harnack estimate
nodes.content:
LEMMA 15.19 \( \left( {M}_{ab}\right. \) evolution). The evolution equation of \( {M}_{ab} \) is given by

(15.46)

\[
\text{ 5) }\;\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {M}_{ab} = 2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}.
\]

nodes.proof:
Since, by definition,

\[
{M}_{ab} = \Delta {R}_{ab} - \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}R + 2{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd} - {R}_{ac}{R}_{bc} + \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ab}
\]

and we compute

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = {\nabla }_{c}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{ab} - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{cb}}\right)
\]

\[
= \Delta {R}_{ab} - {\nabla }_{c}{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{cb}
\]

\[
= \Delta {R}_{ab} - \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}R - {R}_{ad}{R}_{db} + {R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd},
\]

where we used the contracted second Bianchi identity, we may write \( {M}_{ab} \) in the form

(15.47)

\[
{M}_{ab} = {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} + {R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd} + \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ab}.
\]

This enables us to compute the evolution of \( {M}_{ab} \) using the evolution of \( {P}_{cab} \) previously derived. In particular, we may compute the evolution equation

of \( {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} \) as follows. By formulas (15.35) and (15.45), we have

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = {\nabla }_{c}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {P}_{cab} + 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}
\]

(15.48)

\[
= 2{\nabla }_{c}\left( {{R}_{cdea}{P}_{deb} + {R}_{cdeb}{P}_{dae} + {R}_{adeb}{P}_{cde} - {R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab} + 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}
\]

(15.49)

\[
= 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{cdea}{P}_{deb} + 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{cdeb}{P}_{dae} + 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{deb}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae} + 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{adeb}{P}_{cde} - 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cde} - 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{c}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb} + 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}.
\]

To rewrite expression (15.49) in a better form, we apply a couple of formulas. First,

(15.50)

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{cdab} = {P}_{bad}
\]

by the second Bianchi identity. \( {}^{16} \) Second, ha regards to the term

\[
- 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{c}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{\text{ caeb }}
\]

on the RHS of (15.49), we have

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb} = {\nabla }_{d}{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{caeb} - {R}_{cdcf}{R}_{faeb} - {R}_{cdaf}{R}_{cfeb}
\]

\[
- {R}_{cdef}{R}_{cafb} - {R}_{cdbf}{R}_{caef}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{bea} + {R}_{df}{R}_{faeb} - {R}_{dcaf}\left( {{R}_{cebf} + {R}_{cbfe}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{dcef}{R}_{acbf} - {R}_{dcbf}{R}_{acef}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{bea} + {R}_{df}{R}_{faeb} - {B}_{daeb} + {B}_{dabe} - {B}_{deab} + {B}_{dbae},
\]

which follows from commuting \( {\nabla }_{c} \) and \( {\nabla }_{d} \) and then using equation (15.50) and the definition (15.38) of \( {B}_{abcd} \) . Applying these two identities to (15.48) and then grouping like terms, we have

(15.51)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cde} + 2{P}_{aed}{P}_{deb} + 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{dae}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{deb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} + 2{R}_{cdeb}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}
\]

\[
+ 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{adeb}{P}_{cde} - 2{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb}
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{de}\left( {-{B}_{daeb} + {B}_{dabe} - {B}_{deab} + {B}_{dbae}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{de}{R}_{df}{R}_{faeb} + 2{R}_{de}\left( {{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab} - {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{bea}}\right) .
\]

Next,

\[
{R}_{cdea}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{deb} + {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb}}\right)  = \left( {{R}_{cdea} + {R}_{dcea}}\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{deb} = 0,
\]

\[
{R}_{cdeb}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae} + {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{cae}}\right)  = \left( {{R}_{cdeb} + {R}_{dceb}}\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae} = 0,
\]

---

\( {}^{16} \) Indeed,

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{cdab} =  - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{cdbc} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{cdca} =  - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{db} + {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{da} = {P}_{bad}.
\]

---

which we obtained by relabeling \( c \) and \( d \) in the terms \( {R}_{cdea}{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{ceb} \) and \( {R}_{dceb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dae} \) . This and

\[
{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{adeb}{P}_{cde} - {\nabla }_{c}{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{caeb} = {\nabla }_{d}{R}_{aceb}\left( {{P}_{dce} + {\nabla }_{c}{R}_{de}}\right)
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{d}{R}_{aceb}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ce}
\]

imply that we may rewrite (15.51) as

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = 2{R}_{adeb}{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cde} + 2{R}_{de}\left( {{\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eab} + {\nabla }_{d}{P}_{eba}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{P}_{aed}{P}_{deb} + 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{dae} + 2{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{aceb}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ce}
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{de}\left( {-{B}_{daeb} + {B}_{dabe} - {B}_{deab} + {B}_{dbae}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{de}{R}_{df}{R}_{afeb}
\]

Using the Bianchi-type identity (15.6), we have

\[
2{P}_{aed}{P}_{deb} + 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{dae}
\]

\[
= \left( {{P}_{aed} + {P}_{dae}}\right) {P}_{deb} + 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{dae}
\]

\[
= {P}_{dea}{P}_{deb} - 2{P}_{bed}{P}_{ade}.
\]

This, relabeling indices, and the symmetry relations

(15.52)

\[
{B}_{abcd} = {B}_{cdab} = {B}_{badc} = {B}_{dcba}
\]

now imply that(15.53)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{cab} = 2{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ecd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)  + {P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb}
\]

\[
- 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} + 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{B}_{abcd} + {B}_{acbd} - {B}_{acdb} - {B}_{adcb}}\right) .
\]

The evolution equations of the other terms of \( {M}_{ab} \) are straightforward, namely

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd}}\right)  = \left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{acdb}}\right) {R}_{cd} + {R}_{acdb}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{cd}
\]

\[
- 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

(15.54)

\[
= 2{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cefd}{R}_{ef} - 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{B}_{acdb} - {B}_{acbd} + {B}_{adcb} - {B}_{abcd}}\right)
\]

and

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ab}}\right)  = 2{R}_{acdb}\left( {\frac{1}{2t}{R}_{cd}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}
\]

(15.55)

\[
= 2{R}_{acdb}\left( {{M}_{cd} - {\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ecd} + {R}_{cefd}{R}_{ef}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}.
\]

Thus, from (15.47) and the evolution equations (15.53), (15.54), and (15.55), we calculate

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {M}_{ab} = 2{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ecd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)  + {P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb}
\]

\[
- 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} + 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{B}_{abcd} + {B}_{acbd} - {B}_{acdb} - {B}_{adcb}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cefd}{R}_{ef} - 2{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{acdb}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{B}_{acdb} - {B}_{acbd} + {B}_{adcb} - {B}_{abcd}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{acdb}\left( {{M}_{cd} - {\nabla }_{e}{P}_{ecd} - {R}_{cefd}{R}_{ef}}\right)  - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab},
\]

where to obtain the last equality we canceled three pairs of terms.

nodes.content:
REMARK 15.20. Note that

\[
{P}_{cda}{P}_{cdb} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} = 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bcd} - 4{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc},
\]

which yields the way Lemma 4.4 is stated in [247]. Namely,

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {M}_{ab} = 2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bcd} - 4{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adeb} - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}.
\]

LEMMA 15.22 (Existence of nice exhaustion function). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) , \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , where \( T < \infty \) , be a complete solution of the Ricci flow on a noncompact manifold with \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right|  \leq  {k}_{0} \) and \( \left| {\nabla \operatorname{Rc}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right|  \leq  {k}_{0} \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times \; \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for some \( {k}_{0} \geq  0 \) . Then there exists \( C = C\left( {n,{k}_{0}, T}\right)  \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) such that for any \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) there exists a \( {C}^{\infty } \) function \( h : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) satisfying

(15.69)

\[
{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1 \leq  h\left( x\right)  \leq  C\left( {{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right)
\]

for all \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) and

(15.70)

\[
{\left| \nabla h\right| }_{g\left( t\right) } \leq  C,\;{\nabla }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}h \leq  C\;\text{ on }\mathcal{M}.
\]

In particular, \( h \geq  1, h\left( y\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {y, O}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) , and \( {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }h \leq  C \) .

LEMMA 15.23. For any constants \( C > 0 \) and \( \eta  > 0 \) and compact set \( \Omega  \subset  \mathcal{M} \) , there exist smooth functions \( \phi \left( {x, t}\right) \) and \( \psi \left( t\right) \) such that for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) ,

(1) \( \delta  \leq  \psi  \leq  \eta \) for some \( \delta  > 0 \) ,

(2) \( \phi  \geq  \varepsilon \) for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) and

\[
\phi \left( {x, t}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty
\]

as \( x \rightarrow  \infty \) (meaning that the sets \( \phi  \leq  K \) are compact in space-time for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  T \) ); moreover,

\[
\phi  \leq  \eta \;\text{ in }\Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack
\]

(3) \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \phi  > {C\phi } \)

(4) \( {\nabla }_{t}\psi  > {C\psi } \) ,

(5) \( \phi  \geq  {C\psi } \) .
