nodes.proof:
We define

\[
\phi \left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \varepsilon {e}^{At}h\left( x\right) ,
\]

where \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) and \( A > 0 \) will be chosen shortly and \( h \) is as in Lemma 15.22. Since \( h \geq  1 \) , we have \( \phi \left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \varepsilon \) . We also have that \( h\left( x\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( x \rightarrow  \infty \) implies \( \phi \left( {x, t}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( x \rightarrow  \infty \) . Taking \( \varepsilon  \leq  \eta {e}^{-{AT}}{\left( \mathop{\max }\limits_{\Omega }h\right) }^{-1} \) implies \( \phi  \leq  \eta \) in \( \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Hence (2) holds.

Since \( {\Delta h} \leq  C \) and \( h \geq  1 \) , we have

\[
{\Delta \phi } = \varepsilon {e}^{At}{\Delta h} \leq  {C\varepsilon }{e}^{At} \leq  {C\phi }.
\]

Therefore inequality (3) holds provided \( A > C \) .

Next, define

\[
\psi \left( t\right)  \Doteq  \delta {e}^{Bt}
\]

where \( \delta , B > 0 \) are to be chosen. Then (4) is satisfied provided \( B > C \) .

Clearly \( \psi  \geq  \delta \) . Given any \( \eta  > 0 \) , choose \( \delta \) so that \( \delta  \leq  \eta {e}^{-{BT}} \) , which implies (1).

Finally, if we choose \( \delta  \leq  \varepsilon {e}^{-{BT}}/C \) , then

\[
\phi  = \varepsilon {e}^{At}h\left( x\right)  \geq  \varepsilon  \geq  {C\delta }{e}^{BT} \geq  {C\delta }{e}^{Bt} = {C\psi }
\]

since \( {e}^{At} \geq  1 \) and \( h \geq  1 \) . This proves (5).

LEMMA 15.24. Let \( \phi \) and \( \psi \) be defined as in Lemma 15.23. Let \( {U}_{ab} \) be a 2-form and let \( {W}_{a} \) be a 1-form that satisfy equations (15.39)-(15.42) at a point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) :

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{a} = \frac{1}{t}{W}_{a},\;\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {U}_{ab} = 0,\;{\nabla }_{a}{W}_{b} = 0,
\]

---

in time yields a bound for \( \left| {{\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}\left( t\right)  - {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}\left( 0\right) }\right| \) .

---

and

\[
{\nabla }_{a}{U}_{bc} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ab}{W}_{c} - {R}_{ac}{W}_{b}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ab}{W}_{c} - {g}_{ac}{W}_{b}}\right) .
\]

Define \( \widehat{Q},{\widehat{M}}_{ab} \) , and \( {\widehat{R}}_{abcd} \) by (15.66),(15.67), and (15.68). Then at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) we have

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \widehat{Q} \geq  2{\widehat{R}}_{acdb}{\widehat{M}}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 8{\widehat{R}}_{adec}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + 4{\widehat{R}}_{aefc}{\widehat{R}}_{befd}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {\widehat{R}}_{abdc}{U}_{cd}}\right) \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + {\widehat{R}}_{abfe}{U}_{ef}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{t}\left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \phi  + \frac{1}{t}\phi  - \frac{C}{t}\psi  - {C\phi }}\right) {\left| W\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\nabla }_{t}\psi  - {C\psi }}\right) {\left| U\right| }^{2}.
\]

nodes.proof:
We rewrite

\[
\widehat{Q} = \left( {{M}_{ab} + \frac{1}{t}\phi {g}_{ab}}\right) {W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 2{P}_{abc}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{R}_{abdc} + \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{ac}{g}_{bd} - {g}_{ad}{g}_{bc}}\right) }\right) {U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
= Q + \frac{1}{t}\phi {\left| W\right| }^{2} + \psi {\left| U\right| }^{2},
\]

and so

(15.71)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \widehat{Q} = \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q + \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\frac{1}{t}\phi {\left| W\right| }^{2} + \psi {\left| U\right| }^{2}}\right) .
\]

We first estimate the last term on the RHS of (15.71). By hypothesis, the formulas (15.39)-(15.42) on the derivatives of \( {W}_{a} \) and \( {U}_{bc} \) hold at a point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) . Since (15.41), i.e., \( \nabla W = 0 \) and (15.40), i.e., \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) U \) , we have at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \)

(15.72)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\frac{1}{t}\phi {\left| W\right| }^{2} + \psi {\left| U\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\phi  + \frac{1}{t}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \phi }\right) {\left| W\right| }^{2} + \frac{2}{t}\phi \left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{a}}\right) {W}_{a}
\]

\[
+ {\nabla }_{t}\psi {\left| U\right| }^{2} - {2\psi }{\left| \nabla U\right| }^{2}.
\]

Furthermore, by (15.39) we have \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) W = \frac{1}{t}W \) and since \( t \leq  C \) and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  C \) for some \( C < \infty \) , by (15.42) we have

\[
{\left| \nabla U\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{C}{4}\left( {{\left| \mathrm{{Rc}}\right| }^{2} + \frac{1}{{t}^{2}}}\right) {\left| W\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{C}{2{t}^{2}}{\left| W\right| }^{2}
\]

for some \( C < \infty \) . Hence (15.72) implies

(15.73)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\frac{1}{t}\phi {\left| W\right| }^{2} + \psi {\left| U\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\phi  + \frac{1}{t}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \phi  - \frac{C}{{t}^{2}}\psi }\right) {\left| W\right| }^{2} + {\nabla }_{t}\psi {\left| U\right| }^{2}.
\]

We next estimate the first term on the RHS of (15.71), which is \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q \) . In (15.43), rewrite \( {M}_{ab} \) and \( {R}_{abcd} \) in terms of (15.67) and (15.68):

\[
{M}_{ab} = {\widehat{M}}_{ab} - \frac{1}{t}\phi {g}_{ab}\;\text{ and }\;{R}_{abcd} = {\widehat{R}}_{abcd} - \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{ad}{g}_{bc} - {g}_{ac}{g}_{bd}}\right) .
\]

Moreover, \( {P}_{abc} \) is bounded since the derivatives of Rm are bounded and \( {M}_{ab} \) consists of bounded terms plus \( 1/t \) times a (bounded) nonnegative term. Therefore we have

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{acdb}{M}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 8{R}_{adec}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
+ 4{R}_{aefc}{R}_{befd}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd} + \left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {R}_{abdc}{U}_{cd}}\right) \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + {R}_{abfe}{U}_{ef}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{acdb} - \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{ab}{g}_{cd} - {g}_{ad}{g}_{cb}}\right) }\right) \left( {{\widehat{M}}_{cd} - \frac{1}{t}\phi {g}_{cd}}\right) {W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
- 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 8\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{adec} - \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{ac}{g}_{de} - {g}_{ae}{g}_{dc}}\right) }\right) {P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
+ 4\left( {{\widehat{R}}_{aefc} - \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{ac}{g}_{ef} - {g}_{af}{g}_{ec}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\times  \left( {{\widehat{R}}_{befd} - \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{bd}{g}_{ef} - {g}_{bf}{g}_{ed}}\right) }\right) {U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + \left( {{\widehat{R}}_{abdc} - \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{ac}{g}_{bd} - {g}_{ad}{g}_{bc}}\right) }\right) {U}_{cd}}\right)
\]

\[
\times  \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + \left( {{\widehat{R}}_{abfe} - \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{ae}{g}_{bf} - {g}_{af}{g}_{be}}\right) }\right) {U}_{ef}}\right) .
\]

We simplify this as

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q = 2{\widehat{R}}_{acdb}{\widehat{M}}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 8{\widehat{R}}_{adec}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + 4{\widehat{R}}_{aefc}{\widehat{R}}_{befd}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {\widehat{R}}_{abdc}{U}_{cd}}\right) \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + {\widehat{R}}_{abfe}{U}_{ef}}\right)
\]

\[
+ E
\]

where

\[
E \Doteq  \psi \left( {-{g}_{cd}{M}_{cd}{\left| W\right| }^{2} + {M}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}}\right)
\]

\[
- \frac{2}{t}\phi {R}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - \frac{1}{t}{\phi \psi }\left( {n - 1}\right) {\left| W\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- {4\psi }\left( {{g}_{de}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{a} - {P}_{cba}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c}}\right)  + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\psi }^{2}{\left| U\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ {4\psi }\left( {-{g}_{ef}{\widehat{R}}_{aefc}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cb} + {\widehat{R}}_{adbc}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\psi }\left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {\widehat{R}}_{abdc}{U}_{cd}}\right) {U}_{ab} + {\psi }^{2}{\left| U\right| }^{2}.
\]

Since \( \left| {\widehat{R}}_{\text{ aefc }}\right|  \leq  C \) , we may estimate this as

\[
E \geq   - {C\psi }{\left| W\right| }^{2} - \frac{C}{t}\phi {\left| W\right| }^{2} - \frac{n - 1}{t}{\phi \psi }{\left| W\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- {C\psi }\left| U\right| \left| W\right|  + \left( {n - 1}\right) {\psi }^{2}{\left| U\right| }^{2} - {C\psi }{\left| U\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq   - \frac{C}{t}\left( {\phi  + \psi  + {\phi \psi }}\right) {\left| W\right| }^{2} - {C\psi }\left| U\right| \left| W\right|  - {C\psi }{\left| U\right| }^{2}.
\]

By the inequalities \( \psi \left| U\right| \left| W\right|  \leq  \psi {\left| W\right| }^{2} + \psi {\left| U\right| }^{2},\psi  \leq  \phi \) , and \( \psi  \leq  C \) , we have

\[
E \geq   - \frac{C}{t}\phi {\left| W\right| }^{2} - {C\psi }{\left| U\right| }^{2}.
\]

That is,

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) Q \geq  2{\widehat{R}}_{acdb}{\widehat{M}}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 8{\widehat{R}}_{adec}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + 4{\widehat{R}}_{aefc}{\widehat{R}}_{befd}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {\widehat{R}}_{abdc}{U}_{cd}}\right) \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + {\widehat{R}}_{abfe}{U}_{ef}}\right)
\]

\[
- \frac{C}{t}\phi {\left| W\right| }^{2} - {C\psi }{\left| U\right| }^{2}.
\]

If we combine this with (15.73), then (15.71) implies that

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \widehat{Q} \geq  2{\widehat{R}}_{acdb}{\widehat{M}}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 8{\widehat{R}}_{adec}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + 4{\widehat{R}}_{aefc}{\widehat{R}}_{befd}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {\widehat{R}}_{abdc}{U}_{cd}}\right) \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + {\widehat{R}}_{abfe}{U}_{ef}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{t}\left( {\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \phi  + \frac{1}{t}\phi  - \frac{C}{t}\psi  - {C\phi }}\right) {\left| W\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\nabla }_{t}\psi  - {C\psi }}\right) {\left| U\right| }^{2}.
\]

This completes the proof of the lemma.

nodes.content:
THEOREM 15.25 (Matrix Harnack 2-tensor evolution when \( {Z}_{ab} \geq  0 \) ). If \( \mathrm{{Rm}} > 0 \) , then as long as \( {Z}_{ab} \geq  0 \) , the quantity \( {Z}_{ab} \) satisfies the evolution equation:

(15.78)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {Z}_{ab} = 2{S}_{mntu}{K}_{avut}{K}_{bvmn} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{N, M}}{L}_{a}^{NM}{L}_{b}^{NM} - \frac{2}{t}{Z}_{ab},
\]

---

\( {}^{18} \) The reader may easily check that if \( {R}_{abcd} = {I}_{abcd} \) , then \( {S}_{abcd} = {I}_{abcd} \) .

---

where

\[
{K}_{\text{ avtu }} \Doteq  {\nabla }_{v}{P}_{\text{ tua }} - {S}_{\text{ ijrs }}{P}_{\text{ ija }}{\nabla }_{v}{R}_{\text{ rstu }} + {R}_{\text{ tuaw }}{R}_{vw} + \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{\text{ tuav }}
\]

and

\[
{L}_{a}^{NM} \Doteq  2{Y}_{id}^{N}{Y}_{jd}^{M}{S}_{{ijk}\ell }{P}_{k\ell a} + {Y}_{ah}^{N}{X}_{h}^{M} - {Y}_{ah}^{M}{X}_{h}^{N}.
\]

nodes.content:
REMARK 15.26. Note that by (15.47) and (15.50), we have

\[
{g}^{vt}{K}_{avtu} \Doteq  {\nabla }_{v}{P}_{vua} - {S}_{ijrs}{P}_{ija}{\nabla }_{v}{R}_{rsvu} + {R}_{vuaw}{R}_{vw} + \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ua}
\]

\[
= {M}_{ua} - {S}_{ijrs}{P}_{ija}{P}_{sru}
\]

(15.79)

\[
= {Z}_{ua}\text{ . }
\]

Note also that \( {K}_{\text{ avtu }} =  - {K}_{\text{ avut }} \) .

The proof of this requires long but straightforward calculations (see [132] or [139] for details). One point we would like to reiterate is that as long as \( {Z}_{ab} \geq  0 \) , we have \( Q\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  \geq  0 \) for any \( U \) and \( W \) , and consequently the sum of squares decomposition (15.77) is valid.

Concerning the RHS of formula (15.78) we observe the following. Clearly \( {L}_{a}^{NM}{L}_{b}^{NM} \geq  0 \) . Note also that we may write \( {S}_{mntu} \) as a sum of squares, i.e., \( {S}_{\text{ mntu }} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{N}{A}_{mn}^{N}{A}_{ut}^{N} \) , where \( {\left\{  {A}^{N}\right\}  }_{N = 1}^{n\left( {n - 1}\right) /2} \) is an orthogonal set of vectors in \( {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathcal{M}}_{x} \) . We then have

\[
{S}_{\text{ mntu }}{K}_{\text{ avut }}{K}_{\text{ bvmn }} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{N,\nu }}\left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{t, u}}{K}_{\text{ avut }}{A}_{ut}^{N}}\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{m, n}}{K}_{\text{ bvmn }}{A}_{mn}^{N}}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{N, v}}{E}_{av}^{N}{E}_{bv}^{N}
\]

where \( {E}_{av}^{N} \Doteq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{t, u}}{K}_{avut}{A}_{ut}^{N} \) . Hence \( {S}_{mntu}{K}_{avut}{K}_{bvmn} \geq  0 \) (is a nonnegative 2-tensor).

nodes.content: CAVEAT. The reader should note that a direct application of the maximum principle to (15.78) does not immediately yield a proof of the matrix Harnack estimate. nodes.content:
EXERCISE 15.29. Assuming \( \mathrm{{Rm}} > 0 \) , show that

\[
{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {R}_{abdc}{U}_{cd} = 0
\]

if and only if

\[
{U}_{ab} = {S}_{abij}{P}_{ijp}{W}_{p}.
\]

Note that if \( \nabla W = 0 \) and \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) W = \frac{1}{t}W \) , then

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{Z}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}}\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {{Z}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}}\right)  + {\widetilde{J}}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}.
\]

Furthermore, note that if \( {U}_{ab} = {S}_{abij}{P}_{ijp}{W}_{p} \) and (15.39)-(15.42) are satisfied at a point, then

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {Q\left( {U \oplus  W}\right) }\right)  = J\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  = {\widetilde{J}}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}.
\]

By (15.76) we have for any 2 -form \( U \) ,

\[
Q\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  \geq  {Z}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

with equality if and only if \( {U}_{ab} = {S}_{abij}{P}_{ijp}{W}_{p} \) . Hence, if \( {Z}_{ab} \geq   - \varepsilon {g}_{ab} \) , then

(15.83)

\[
Q\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  \geq   - \varepsilon {\left| W\right| }^{2} \geq   - \varepsilon {\left| U \oplus  W\right| }^{2}
\]

for all \( U \) . Now (15.83) implies that there exists \( C < \infty \) such that

\[
\left( {{Q}^{2} + {Q}^{\# }}\right) \left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  \geq   - {C\varepsilon }{\left| U \oplus  W\right| }^{2}
\]

for all \( U \) , where the square and sharp operations are defined using the degenerate metric and the affine Lie algebra bracket on \( {\Lambda }^{1}\mathcal{M} \oplus  {\Lambda }^{2}\mathcal{M} \cdot  {}^{20} \) On the other hand,

\[
{\widetilde{J}}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} = \left( {{Q}^{2} + {Q}^{\# }}\right) \left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  \geq   - {C\varepsilon }{\left| U \oplus  W\right| }^{2} \geq   - {C}^{\prime }\varepsilon {\left| W\right| }^{2}
\]

for some \( {C}^{\prime } < \infty \) , where \( {U}_{ab} = {S}_{abij}{P}_{ijp}{W}_{p} \) (in particular, \( \left| U\right|  \leq  C\left| W\right| \) , where \( C < \infty \) depends only on \( {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{-1} \) and \( \left. \left| {\nabla \mathrm{{Rc}}}\right| \right) \) .

We also have the following observation of Hamilton.

REMARK 15.30. Suppose that \( \dim \mathcal{M} = 3 \) . Let

\[
{A}_{ab} \Doteq  {S}_{mntu}{K}_{avut}{K}_{bvmn}.
\]

If \( \left\{  {x}^{i}\right\} \) are coordinates where both Rc is diagonal and \( {g}_{ij} = {\delta }_{ij} \) at a point, then \( {R}_{{ijk}\ell } = 0 \) if at least three of the indices are distinct. By the definition of \( S \) , given \( i \neq  j \) , we have \( \frac{1}{2} = {I}_{ijji} = 2{R}_{ijji}{S}_{ijji} \) , so that \( 4{S}_{ijji} = \frac{1}{{R}_{ijji}} \) . Using \( {K}_{\text{ avtu }} =  - {K}_{\text{ avut }} \) we now see that

\[
{A}_{11} = {S}_{mntu}{K}_{1vut}{K}_{1vmn}
\]

\[
= 4{S}_{1221}{\left( {K}_{1v21}\right) }^{2} + 4{S}_{1331}{\left( {K}_{1v31}\right) }^{2} + 4{S}_{2332}{\left( {K}_{1v32}\right) }^{2}
\]

\geq  \frac{1}{{R}_{1221}}{\left( {K}_{1221}\right) }^{2} + \frac{1}{{R}_{1331}}{\left( {K}_{1331}\right) }^{2}
\]

\]

\]

\]

= \frac{1}{{R}_{11}}{\left( {Z}_{11}\right) }^{2} + \frac{1}{{R}_{22}}{\left( {Z}_{12}\right) }^{2} + \frac{1}{{R}_{33}}{\left( {Z}_{13}\right) }^{2}
\]

\]

since \( {K}_{1111} = {K}_{1222} = {K}_{1333} = 0 \) and where we used (15.79). Here we also used the inequality

\[
\frac{{x}^{2}}{a} + \frac{{y}^{2}}{b} \geq  \frac{{\left( x + y\right) }^{2}}{a + b}

nodes.content: THEOREM 15.33 (Ancient solutions with \( \mathrm{{Rm}} > 0 \) and attaining \( {R}_{\max } \) ). On a simply-connected manifold, a complete ancient solution with strictly positive curvature operator and curvature bounded uniformly in time, such that the scalar curvature \( R \) attains its maximum in space and time, is necessarily a steady gradient soliton.

LEMMA 15.37 (Null space of \( \bar{Q} \) ). Suppose that, at \( t = 0 \) , the null space of \( \bar{Q} \) has dimension less than \( n \) at some point. Then the null space has dimension less than \( n \) at every point at subsequent times.

In other words, if the null space has dimension \( n \) at some point and time, then the dimension of the null space is \( n \) at all points at all earlier times.
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 15.37 (Null space of \( \bar{Q} \) ). Suppose that, at \( t = 0 \) , the null space of \( \bar{Q} \) has dimension less than \( n \) at some point. Then the null space has dimension less than \( n \) at every point at subsequent times. In other words, if the null space has dimension \( n \) at some point and time, then the dimension of the null space is \( n \) at all points at all earlier times.

nodes.proof:
Let \( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }} \) denote the null space of \( \bar{Q} \) . By hypothesis and since \( \dim \left( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }}\right) \) is upper semi-continuous, at time \( t = 0 \) there exists a point \( {x}_{0} \in  \mathcal{M} \) such that \( \dim \left( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }}\right)  < n \) is constant in a neighborhood \( \mathcal{U} \) of \( {x}_{0} \) . From this it is easy to see that there exists a smooth vector field \( Y \) , with \( Y\left( {x}_{0}\right)  \neq  \overrightarrow{0} \) and support in \( \mathcal{U} \) , such that \( Y \oplus  0 \) is orthogonal to the null space, i.e.,

\[
\langle Y, W\rangle  = 0
\]

for all \( W \) such that there exists \( U \) such that \( \bar{Q}\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  = 0 \) . By taking the metric dual of \( Y \) , we may define a quadratic form

\[
{F}_{0} \Doteq  {Y}^{ * } \otimes  {Y}^{ * }
\]

on \( {\Lambda }^{1}T\mathcal{M} \) (i.e., \( {\left( {F}_{0}\right) }_{ij} = {Y}_{i}^{ * }{Y}_{j}^{ * } \) , where \( {Y}_{i}^{ * } \Doteq  {g}_{ik}{Y}^{k} \) ) that, when extended trivially in the \( {\Lambda }^{2}T\mathcal{M} \) factor to \( {\Lambda }^{1}T\mathcal{M} \oplus  {\Lambda }^{2}T\mathcal{M} \) , vanishes on the null space of \( \bar{Q} \) . Note that \( {F}_{0} \) has support in \( \mathcal{U} \) . By choosing \( Y \) with \( \left| Y\right| \) sufficiently small, we obtain

\[
\bar{Q}\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  \geq  {\left( {F}_{0}\right) }_{ij}{W}^{i}{W}^{j}
\]

for all \( U \) and \( W \) at time zero.

Let \( F\left( t\right) \) be a solution of the heat equation with initial data \( {F}_{0} : {}^{24} \)

(15.86)

\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial t} = {\Delta F}
\]

\[
F\left( 0\right)  = {F}_{0}
\]

---

\( {}^{24} \) Alternatively, we may choose \( F \) to satisfy \( \frac{\partial F}{\partial t} = {\Delta }_{L}F \) , where \( {\Delta }_{L} \) is the Lichnerowicz Laplacian, i.e.,

(15.87)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{F}_{ij} = \Delta {F}_{ij} + 2{R}_{{kij}\ell }{F}_{k\ell },
\]

where the formula is with respect to an evolving local orthonormal frame. Since \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  C \) , a solution to (15.87) exists.

---

By the maximum principle for symmetric 2-tensors (Theorem 10.7), the condition \( F \geq  0 \) is preserved (in particular, \( \operatorname{tr}F \geq  0 \) for \( t \geq  0 \) ). Furthermore, since we have the heat equation \( {}^{25}\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{tr}F = \Delta \left( {\operatorname{tr}F}\right) \) and \( \operatorname{tr}F\left( {{x}_{0},0}\right)  = \; {\left| Y\right| }^{2} > 0 \) , by the strong maximum principle we have \( \operatorname{tr}F > 0 \) for \( t > 0 \) . Thus the null space of \( F \) is of dimension at most \( n - 1 \) at all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t > 0 \) .

Claim. \( \bar{Q}\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  - {F}_{ij}{W}^{i}{W}^{j} \) remains nonnegative.

We refer the reader to Theorem 4.2 in [248] for details of the proof of the claim. The proof uses the same idea as the proof of the Harnack estimate in the complete, noncompact case, expounded in subsection 4.5 of this chapter. One considers a modification \( \widehat{Q} \) of \( \bar{Q} \) ,

\[
\widehat{Q} = {\widehat{M}}_{ij}{W}^{i}{W}^{j} + 2{P}_{pij}{U}^{pi}{W}^{j} + {\widehat{R}}_{pijq}{U}^{pi}{U}^{qj},
\]

where

\[
{\widehat{M}}_{ij} = {\bar{M}}_{ij} + \phi {g}_{ij}
\]

\[
{\widehat{R}}_{pijq} = {R}_{pijq} + \frac{1}{2}\psi \left( {{g}_{pj}{g}_{iq} - {g}_{pq}{g}_{ij}}\right) ,
\]

and \( \phi ,\psi \) are suitable barrier functions to be determined (which we let go to zero in the end). One applies the heat operator to

\[
\widehat{Q} - {F}_{ij}{W}^{i}{W}^{j},
\]

extends \( U \) and \( W \) as in (15.89) and (15.90), and constructs functions \( \phi \) and \( \psi \) which allow an application of the maximum principle (see, e.g., Lemmas 15.22 and 15.23).

To see that the lemma follows, note that if \( {U}_{1} \oplus  W \) and \( {U}_{2} \oplus  W \) are both in the null space of \( \bar{Q} \) , then

\[
0 = \bar{Q}\left( {\left( {{U}_{1} - {U}_{2}}\right)  \oplus  0}\right)  = \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{U}_{1} - {U}_{2},{U}_{1} - {U}_{2}}\right)
\]

so that \( {U}_{1} = {U}_{2} \) since \( \mathrm{{Rm}} > {0.}^{26} \) That is, each element of \( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }} \) is uniquely determined by its projection onto \( T\mathcal{M} \) . Thus

\[
\dim \left( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }}\right)  = \dim \left\{  {W : U \oplus  W \in  {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }}\text{ for some }U}\right\}  .
\]

The claim implies

\[
\dim \left\{  {W : U \oplus  W \in  {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }}\text{ for some }U}\right\}   \leq  \dim \left( {\operatorname{null}\left( F\right) }\right) ,
\]

where null \( \left( F\right) \) denotes the null space of \( F \) . We conclude that \( \dim \left( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }}\right)  \leq \; n - 1 \) for \( t > 0 \) . This completes the proof of the lemma.

LEMMA 15.38 ( \( L \) is obtained from wedging with \( V \) ). We have

(15.94)

\[
{L}_{ijk} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{V}_{i}{g}_{jk} - {V}_{j}{g}_{ik}}\right) .
\]

That is,

\[
{U}^{ij} = {L}_{k}^{ij}{W}^{k} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{V}^{i}{W}^{j} - {V}^{j}{W}^{i}}\right)  = {\left( V \land  W\right) }_{ij},
\]

so that \( U = V \land  W \) whenever \( U \oplus  W \) lies in \( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }} \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 15.38 ( \( L \) is obtained from wedging with \( V \) ). We have (15.94) \[ {L}_{ijk} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{V}_{i}{g}_{jk} - {V}_{j}{g}_{ik}}\right) . \] That is, \[ {U}^{ij} = {L}_{k}^{ij}{W}^{k} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{V}^{i}{W}^{j} - {V}^{j}{W}^{i}}\right) = {\left( V \land W\right) }_{ij}, \] so that \( U = V \land W \) whenever \( U \oplus W \) lies in \( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }} \) .

nodes.proof:
Suppose \( U \oplus  W \) lies in \( {\bar{Q}}_{\text{ nul }} \) . Substituting (15.88) in each term of (15.92) gives

\[
{X}_{k}^{\alpha } =  - {Y}_{ij}^{\alpha }{L}_{k}^{ij}.
\]

Since \( \bar{J}\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  = 0 \) , then substituting this and (15.88) into each term of (15.93) gives

(15.95)

\[
{Y}_{ik}^{\alpha }{Y}_{j\ell }^{\beta }{L}_{k}^{j\ell } - {Y}_{ik}^{\beta }{Y}_{j\ell }^{\alpha }{L}_{k}^{j\ell } + 2{Y}_{j\ell }^{\alpha }{Y}_{k\ell }^{\beta }{L}_{i}^{jk} = 0
\]

for all \( \alpha ,\beta \) , and \( i \) . When choosing the \( {X}^{\alpha } \) and \( {Y}^{\alpha } \) to diagonalize \( \bar{Q} \) at a point, we may simultaneously diagonalize the standard positive definite quadratic form \( G \) on \( {\Lambda }^{1}{T}_{x}\mathcal{M} \oplus  {\Lambda }^{2}{T}_{x}\mathcal{M} \) defined by

\[
G\left( {U \oplus  W}\right)  \Doteq  \frac{1}{2}\left( {{g}_{ik}{g}_{j\ell } - {g}_{i\ell }{g}_{jk}}\right) {U}^{ij}{U}^{k\ell } + {g}_{ij}{W}^{i}{W}^{j}
\]

\[
= {\left| U\right| }^{2} + {\left| W\right| }^{2}.
\]

(If we raise indices on \( \bar{Q} \) and \( G \) , then they commute as linear transformations.) In particular, we may assume that there exists a basis \( \left\{  {E}^{\alpha }\right\} \) for \( {\Lambda }^{2}{T}_{x}^{ * }\mathcal{M} \) such that \( {Y}_{ij}^{\alpha } = {\lambda }^{\alpha }{E}_{ij}^{\alpha } \) for positive constants \( {\lambda }^{\alpha } \) and such that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{\alpha }{E}_{ij}^{\alpha }{E}_{k\ell }^{\alpha } = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{g}_{ik}{g}_{j\ell } - {g}_{i\ell }{g}_{jk}}\right) ;
\]

that is, \( \left\{  {E}^{\alpha }\right\} \) is orthonormal. Dividing (15.95) by \( {\lambda }^{\alpha }{\lambda }^{\beta } \) , multiplying by \( {E}_{pq}^{\alpha }{E}_{rs}^{\beta } \) , and summing on \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) give

\[
{g}_{ip}{L}_{rsq} - {g}_{iq}{L}_{rsp} - {g}_{ir}{L}_{pqs} + {g}_{is}{L}_{pqr} + {g}_{qs}{L}_{pri} - {g}_{qr}{L}_{pse} - {g}_{ps}{L}_{qri} + {g}_{pr}{L}_{qsi} = 0.
\]

Contracting with \( {g}^{ip} \) gives the required identity (15.94) for \( L \) .

As mentioned earlier, the variations of \( \bar{Q}\left( {U \oplus  W}\right) \) with respect to \( U \) and \( W \) must vanish when \( U \oplus  W \in  {Q}_{\text{ nul }} \) . This gives

\[
{\left( \frac{\delta \bar{Q}}{\delta U}\right) }_{ij} = {P}_{ijk}{W}^{k} - {R}_{{ijk}\ell }{U}^{k\ell } = 0
\]

\[
{\left( \frac{\delta \bar{Q}}{\delta W}\right) }_{k} = {\bar{M}}_{ik}{W}^{i} + {P}_{ijk}{U}^{ij} = 0
\]

for all \( i, j \) and for all \( k \) , respectively. Substituting \( U = V \land  W \) gives

(15.96)

\[
{P}_{ijk} + {R}_{{ijk}\ell }{V}^{\ell } = 0,
\]

(15.97)

\[
{\bar{M}}_{ik} - {V}^{j}{P}_{ijk} = 0,
\]

respectively. Applying the divergence operator \( {\nabla }^{i} \) to (15.96) and using the facts that

\[
{\nabla }^{i}{R}_{{ijk}\ell } = {P}_{\ell {jk}},\;{\nabla }^{i}{P}_{ijk} = {\bar{M}}_{jk} - {R}_{p}^{\ell }{R}_{\ell {jk}}^{p},
\]

we obtain

(15.98)

\[
{R}_{{ijk}\ell }\left( {{\nabla }_{j}{V}_{\ell } - {R}_{j\ell }}\right)  = 0.
\]

Let \( {T}_{ij} = {R}_{ij} - {\nabla }_{i}{V}_{j} \) . Decomposing (15.98) into symmetric and skew-symmetric parts with respect to the indices \( i \) and \( k \) and using the positivity of the curvature show that \( T \) is symmetric. Thus, \( {\nabla }_{j}{V}_{\ell } = {\nabla }_{\ell }{V}_{j} \) and \( V \) is a gradient since \( \mathcal{M} \) is simply connected.

Intuitively, the positivity of the curvature operator in (15.98) ought to imply that the tensor \( T \) vanishes, and hence \( g \) is a steady gradient soliton. This works easily in dimension 3: if we choose an orthonormal frame that diagonalizes \( T \) , then (15.98) gives the following linear equations for the eigenvalues of \( T \) , which we write in matrix form:

\[
\left( \begin{matrix} 0 & {R}_{1221} & {R}_{1331} \\  {R}_{1221} & 0 & {R}_{2332} \\  {R}_{1331} & {R}_{2332} & 0 \end{matrix}\right) \left( \begin{array}{l} {T}_{11} \\  {T}_{22} \\  {T}_{33} \end{array}\right)  = \left( \begin{array}{l} 0 \\  0 \\  0 \end{array}\right) .
\]

This system has determinant \( 2{R}_{1221}{R}_{1331}{R}_{2332} > 0 \) (since \( \mathrm{{Rm}} > 0 \) ), so that

\[
{T}_{11} = {T}_{22} = {T}_{33} = 0.
\]

In general, i.e., in dimensions \( n \geq  4 \) , to obtain the condition

\[
{R}_{{ijk}\ell }{T}_{im}{T}_{m\ell } = 0,
\]

one applies the heat operator to (15.97) and substitutes the evolution equations of \( {\bar{M}}_{ab} \) and \( {P}_{abc} \) obtained from Lemmas 15.19 and 15.18 (see [248] for details). Then diagonalizing \( T \) shows that its eigenvalues vanish at each point. This proves Theorem 15.33.

nodes.content: THEOREM 15.40 (A 3-dimensional noncompact manifold with \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq  0 \) and pinched Ricci is flat). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3},{g}_{0}}\right) \) is a 3-dimensional complete noncom-pact Riemannian manifold with bounded nonnegative sectional curvature and \( {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0} \geq  \varepsilon {R}_{0}{g}_{0} \) for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , then \( {g}_{0} \) is flat.
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 15.40 (A 3-dimensional noncompact manifold with \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq 0 \) and pinched Ricci is flat). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3},{g}_{0}}\right) \) is a 3-dimensional complete noncom-pact Riemannian manifold with bounded nonnegative sectional curvature and \( {\mathrm{{Rc}}}_{0} \geq \varepsilon {R}_{0}{g}_{0} \) for some \( \varepsilon > 0 \) , then \( {g}_{0} \) is flat.

nodes.proof:
The idea of the proof is to use the metric \( {g}_{0} \) as the initial metric for a solution \( g\left( t\right) \) to the Ricci flow and then to analyze the possible forming singularities to obtain a contradiction to the assumption that \( {g}_{0} \) is not flat. By the work of W.-X. Shi, in particular, the short time existence Theorem

D. 2 and the curvature estimates (3) and (4) in subsection 5.1 of Chapter 12, there exists a solution \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , to the Ricci flow defined on a maximal time interval with \( g\left( 0\right)  = {g}_{0} \) , bounded \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) , and

(15.99)

\[
\operatorname{Rc}\left( t\right)  \geq  {\varepsilon R}\left( t\right) g\left( t\right)
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , where \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) ; see (3) in subsection 5.1 of Chapter 12 for a justification of (15.99).

Suppose that the metric \( {g}_{0} \) is not flat; then \( R\left( {g}_{0}\right)  > 0 \) at some point in \( \mathcal{M} \) and by the strong maximum principle, \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  > 0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . Directly analogous to the ’pinching improves’ estimate (see (6.37) on p. 190 of Volume One), there exist \( C < \infty \) and \( \delta  > 0 \) such that

(15.100)

\[
\left| {\operatorname{Rc} - \frac{1}{3}{Rg}}\right|  \leq  C{R}^{1 - \delta }
\]

on \( {\mathcal{M}}^{3} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Here one needs to justify that estimate (15.100) holds for complete solutions with bounded nonnegative sectional curvature on noncompact manifolds. This was accomplished in [445] and Lemma 6.1 of [106]. In particular, recall from pp. 191-194 of Volume One (see the proof of Lemma 6.34 there) that the quantity \( f \Doteq  {\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{2}/{R}^{2 - \eta } \) , where \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \doteq  \mathrm{{Rm}} - \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{{Rm}}\right) \) id, satisfies for \( \eta  > 0 \) sufficiently small

(15.101)

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} \leq  {\Delta f} + 2\left( {1 - \eta }\right) \langle \nabla \log R,\nabla f\rangle  - \eta \left( {1 - \eta }\right) f{\left| \nabla \log R\right| }^{2}.
\]

Note that since \( \operatorname{Rc} \geq  {\varepsilon Rg} \) , we have \( {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Rm}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}/{R}^{2} \leq  C \) for some constant \( C < \infty \) . Since \( \eta  > 0 \) , we first have \( f \leq  C \) , where \( C \) may depend on time. From (15.101) we obtain

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} \leq  {\Delta f} + \frac{1 - \eta }{\eta }\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{f}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {f}^{1/\eta }\right)  \leq  \Delta \left( {f}^{1/\eta }\right) .
\]

By the maximum principle on noncompact manifolds, we conclude that

\[
{f}^{1/\eta }\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{y \in  \mathcal{M}}}{f}^{1/\eta }\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

for all \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

CLAIM 1. \( \operatorname{Rm}\left( t\right)  > 0 \) for \( t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) .

Proof of CLAIM 1. By the strong maximum principle for systems (i.e., Theorem 12.53), if the claim is false, then the universal cover \( \left( {{\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}}^{3},\widetilde{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) splits as the product of a surface solution with \( \mathbb{R} \) for \( t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . However this contradicts the estimate \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{\widetilde{g}\left( t\right) } \geq  \varepsilon {R}_{\widetilde{g}\left( t\right) }\widetilde{g}\left( t\right) \) , where \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , which follows from \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{g\left( t\right) } \geq  \varepsilon {R}_{g\left( t\right) }g\left( t\right) \) .

Now since \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is complete and noncompact and has bounded positive sectional curvature for \( t > 0 \) , by the Gromoll-Meyer theorem, we have the injectivity radius estimate

\[
\operatorname{inj}\left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{\pi }{\sqrt{{K}_{\text{ sup }}\left( t\right) }},
\]

where \( {K}_{\text{ sup }}\left( t\right) \) is the supremum of the sectional curvatures of \( g\left( t\right) \) . This will allow us to take a limit in the discussion below.

CLAIM 2. The solution \( g\left( t\right) \) exists for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) .

Proof of CLAIM 2. If \( T < \infty \) , then by Theorem D. 2 we have

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T)}}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}}_{g\left( t\right) }\right|  = \infty .
\]

In fact,

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  \mathcal{M}}}{R}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( x\right)  = \infty .
\]

Hence we can apply an elementary point picking method (see \( §2 \) of Chapter 8 in [146]) and the compactness theorem for solutions of the Ricci flow, i.e., Theorem 3.10 on p. 131 of Part I of this volume, to obtain a sequence \( \left( {{x}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{i} \rightarrow  T \) such that the rescaled solutions \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{i}^{3},{g}_{i}\left( t\right) ,{x}_{i}}\right) \) with

\[
{g}_{i}\left( t\right)  \Doteq  {R}_{i}g\left( {{t}_{i} + {R}_{i}^{-1}t}\right) ,
\]

where \( {R}_{i} \Doteq  R\left( {{x}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) as \( i \rightarrow  \infty \) , converge in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) Cheeger-Gromov sense on compact sets to a complete limit solution \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3},{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) , t \in \; \left( {-\infty ,\omega }\right) \) . By the ’pinching improves’ estimate (15.100) and \( {R}_{i} \rightarrow  \infty \) , we have

\[
{\operatorname{Rc}}_{\infty }\left( t\right)  \equiv  \frac{1}{3}{R}_{\infty }\left( t\right) {g}_{\infty }\left( t\right)
\]

and \( {R}_{\infty }\left( t\right) \) is constant in space by Schur’s lemma. Since \( {g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) \) is complete, this implies \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3} \) is closed (and diffeomorphic to a spherical space form). This contradicts the fact that the sequence \( {g}_{i}\left( t\right) \) is defined on \( {\mathcal{M}}^{3} \) , which is noncompact.

Now that we know that the solution \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is immortal, i.e., defined on \( \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) , we divide its analysis into two cases.

Case 1. \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is Type IIb, i.e., \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\mathcal{M}\times \lbrack 0,\infty )}}t\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( t\right) }\right|  = \infty \) . In this case, by a point picking method (again see §2 of Chapter 8 in [146]) and the compactness theorem, there exists \( \left( {{x}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{i} \rightarrow  \infty \) such that the rescaled solutions \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3},{g}_{i}\left( t\right) ,{x}_{i}}\right) \) converge in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) Cheeger-Gromov sense to a nonflat complete limit eternal solution \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3},{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) , t \in  \left( {-\infty ,\infty }\right) \) , with nonnegative sectional curvature and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\mathcal{M} \times  \left( {-\infty ,\infty }\right) }}{R}_{\infty } = {R}_{\infty }\left( {{x}_{\infty },0}\right) .
\]

Since the pinching estimate (15.99) is preserved under \( {C}^{\infty } \) Cheeger-Gromov convergence, we have

\[
\operatorname{Rc}{}_{\infty } \geq  \varepsilon {R}_{\infty }{g}_{\infty }\text{ . }
\]

By Theorem 15.33 (see also Section 4 of Chapter 20 of Part III of this volume for a weakening of the assumption \( \mathrm{{Rm}} > 0 \) to \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq  0 \) ) we conclude that \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3},{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a steady gradient Ricci soliton with \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{\infty } \geq  \varepsilon {R}_{\infty }{g}_{\infty } \) , where \( \varepsilon  > 0,{R}_{\infty } > 0 \) and \( \dim \mathcal{M} > 2 \) . By Corollary 9.61 on p. 364 of [146] this is impossible. Thus Case 1 cannot occur.

Case 2. \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is Type III, i.e., \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\mathcal{M}\times \lbrack 0,\infty )}}t\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( t\right) }\right|  < \infty \) . In this case, by a point picking method and the compactness theorem, there exists \( \left( {{x}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right) ,{t}_{i} \rightarrow  \infty \) , such that \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{3},{g}_{i}\left( t\right) ,{x}_{i}}\right) \) converges to a nonflat complete limit immortal solution \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3},{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) , t \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) , with nonnegative sectional curvature and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty } \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right) }}t{R}_{\infty }\left( t\right)  = {R}_{\infty }\left( {{x}_{\infty },1}\right) .
\]

We have \( {\operatorname{Rc}}_{\infty }\left( t\right)  \geq  \varepsilon {R}_{\infty }\left( t\right) {g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) \) and by Theorem D. 49 we also have \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3},{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is an expanding gradient Ricci soliton. Note also that from the same reasoning as in Claim 1, \( {\operatorname{Rm}}_{\infty }\left( t\right)  > 0 \) . Thus the curvature of \( {g}_{\infty } \) decays exponentially in the distance to a fixed point (see Theorem 9.56 on p. 362 of [146]). By the gap theorem, i.e., Theorem 15.41, this contradicts the assumption that \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{3} \) is nonflat and has positive sectional curvature.

THEOREM 16.1 (Li-Yau estimate). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) has nonnegative Ricci curvature, then

(16.7)

\[
{\Delta f} - \frac{n}{2\tau } = \frac{\partial f}{\partial \tau } + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} \leq  0.
\]

In terms of \( u \) this says

(16.8)

\[
\Delta \log u + \frac{n}{2\tau } = \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\log u - {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + \frac{n}{2\tau } \geq  0.
\]

1.2. Linear entropy monotonicity. Now let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold. Again motivated by (16.3), given a function \( f : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) and a positive number \( \tau \) , we define the linear entropy by \( {}^{5} \) (16.20)

\[
{\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f,\tau }\right)  \Doteq  {\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {g, f,\tau }\right)  \Doteq  {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\tau \left( {{2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n}\right) \frac{{e}^{-f}}{{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{n/2}}{d\mu },
\]

where the pair \( \left( {f,\tau }\right) \) is constrained to satisfy

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\frac{{e}^{-f}}{{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{n/2}}{d\mu } = 1.
\]

---

\( {}^{5} \) Usually we shall use the notation \( {\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f,\tau }\right) \) , where we drop the dependence on \( g \) in the notation.

---

By the integration by parts identity \( {}^{6} \)

\[
{\int }_{{\mathcal{M}}^{n}}{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}{e}^{-f}{d\mu } = {\int }_{{\mathcal{M}}^{n}}\left( {\Delta f}\right) {e}^{-f}{d\mu },
\]

we may rewrite (16.20) as

(16.21)

\[
{\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f,\tau }\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\tau {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + f - n}\right) \frac{{e}^{-f}}{{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{n/2}}{d\mu }.
\]

Letting \( w \Doteq  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/4}{e}^{-f/2} \) , we have under the constraint \( {\int }_{{\mathcal{M}}^{n}}{w}^{2}{d\mu } = 1 \)

\[
{\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f,\tau }\right)  = {\mathcal{V}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {w,\tau }\right)  \Doteq  {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{4\tau }{\left| \nabla w\right| }^{2} - {w}^{2}\log \left( {w}^{2}\right) }\right) {d\mu } - \frac{n}{2}\log \left( {4\pi \tau }\right)  - n.
\]

The term \( {4\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\left| \nabla w\right| }^{2}{d\mu } \) is the ’Dirichlet energy’ part while \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{w}^{2}\log \left( {w}^{2}\right) {d\mu } \) is the 'classical entropy' part.

Suppose \( \sigma \left( \tau \right)  > 0 \) satisfies \( \frac{d\sigma }{d\tau } = 1 \) and define the function \( f \) by

(16.23)

\[
u \Doteq  {\left( 4\pi \sigma \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-f}.

Then \( {\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( \tau \right)  \Doteq  {\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f\left( \tau \right) ,\sigma \left( \tau \right) }\right) \) satisfies

THEOREM 16.12 (Parametrix for heat operator). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a complete manifold and let \( H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \) be the minimal positive fundamental solution to the heat equation. Then as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) we have

(16.38)

\[
H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  \sim  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{\infty }{\tau }^{j}{u}_{j}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) .
\]

More specifically, by (16.38) we mean that for any compact subset \( K \) of \( \mathcal{M} \) , there exist \( T > 0 \) and a sequence of functions \( {u}_{j} \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( {K \times  K \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) , defined for \( j \in  \mathbb{N} \cup  \{ 0\} \) , such that for each \( k \in  \mathbb{N} \cup  \{ 0\} \) ,

\[
{w}_{k}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  \Doteq  H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  - {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{k}{\tau }^{j}{u}_{j}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)
\]

satisfies

\[
{w}_{k}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  = O\left( {{\tau }^{k + 1 - \frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-\frac{\delta {d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }}\right) }\right)
\]

as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) , uniformly for all \( x, y \in  K \) , where \( \delta  > 0 \) is a number depending only on \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) . The function \( {u}_{0}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \) can be chosen so that \( {u}_{0}\left( {x, x,0}\right)  = 1 \) .

H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{C\left( \delta \right) }{{\omega }_{n}\operatorname{AVR}\left( g\right) {\tau }^{n/2}}\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{\left( {4 + \delta }\right) \tau }}\right) .
\]

(This is because \( \operatorname{AVR}\left( g\right)  \leq  \frac{\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {p,\sqrt{\tau }}\right) }{{\omega }_{n}{\tau }^{n/2}} \) by the Bishop-Gromov volume comparison theorem.)

(16.45)

\[

\]

Under the same hypotheses as in Theorem 16.13 there exists \( C\left( n\right) < \infty \) such that (16.45) \[ {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}f\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) {d\mu }\left( y\right) \leq C\left( n\right) \] for any \( x \in \mathcal{M} \) and \( \tau > 0 \) .

nodes.proof:
By applying (16.41) together with the upper bound (16.42), we obtain for the heat kernel \( H \) an upper bound for the classical entropy-type quantity \( - {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}H\log {Hd\mu } - \frac{n}{2}\log \left( {4\pi \tau }\right) \) :

(16.46)

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{fHd\mu } \leq  \frac{C}{\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right) }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{5\tau }}\right) {d\mu }\left( y\right)  < \infty
\]

for any \( \tau  > 0 \) (taking \( \delta  = 1 \) and where \( C \) depends only on \( n \) ). By estimating the RHS of (16.46), we shall prove (16.45). In particular, we shall split the region of integration \( \mathcal{M} \) into \( B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right) \) and \( \mathcal{M} - B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right) \) . In the complement of the ball, we then compare the integral to the corresponding Euclidean value.

We have

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{5\tau }}\right) {d\mu }
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right) }\frac{1}{4}{d\mu } + {\int }_{\mathcal{M} - B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right) }\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{5\tau }}\right) {d\mu }
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right)  + {\int }_{\sqrt{\tau }}^{\infty }\frac{{r}^{2}}{4\tau }\exp \left( {-\frac{{r}^{2}}{5\tau }}\right) \operatorname{Area}\partial B\left( {x, r}\right) {dr}.
\]

Now recall

\[
\text{ Area }\partial B\left( {x, r}\right)  \leq  \frac{n{r}^{n - 1}}{{\tau }^{n/2}}\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right)
\]

for \( r \geq  \sqrt{\tau } \) (see (1.155) of [146] for example). It follows that

\[
{\int }_{\sqrt{\tau }}^{\infty }\frac{{r}^{2}}{4\tau }\exp \left( {-\frac{{r}^{2}}{5\tau }}\right) \operatorname{Area}\partial B\left( {x, r}\right) {dr}
\]

\[
\leq  \operatorname{Vol}B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right) {\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{n}{4}{s}^{n + 1}\exp \left( {-\frac{1}{5}{s}^{2}}\right) {ds}
\]

\[
\Doteq  C\left( n\right) \operatorname{Vol}B\left( {x,\sqrt{\tau }}\right) .
\]

The estimate (16.45) now follows from applying the above inequalities to (16.46).

nodes.content:
THEOREM 16.18 (Gradient and Laplacian bound for positive solutions). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a complete Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature. Suppose \( u \) is a positive solution to the heat equation with \( u \leq  A \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for some constant \( A < \infty \) . Then

(1)

(16.48)

\[
\tau \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} \leq  \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)
\]

and

(2)

(16.49)

\[
\tau \left( {\frac{\Delta u}{u} + \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}}}\right)  \leq  n + 4\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) .
\]

Suppose \( u \) is a positive solution to the heat equation with \( u \leq A \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times \left\lbrack {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for some constant \( A < \infty \) . Then (1) (16.48) \[ \tau \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right|...

nodes.proof:
We prove the theorem in the case where \( \mathcal{M} \) is closed and after the proof we indicate the modifications necessary to handle the complete case.

Let \( L \doteq  \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla \) . The idea of the proof is simply to take the difference of the LHS and the RHS of each inequality above, apply the heat-type operator \( L \) , and then apply the maximum principle.

(1) Since \( \frac{\partial u}{\partial \tau } = {\Delta u} \) , we have \( \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\log u = \Delta \log u + {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \) . Using this and (16.26), we compute

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} = 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla \left( {\Delta \log u + {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

(16.50)

\[
= \Delta {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- 2{\left| \nabla \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - 2\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log u}\right) ,
\]

which yields

(16.51)

\[
L\left( {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}\right)  =  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - 2\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log u}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

We also compute

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  =  - \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\log u =  - \Delta \log u - {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}
\]

(16.52)

\[
= \Delta \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2},
\]

which is the same as

(16.53)

\[
L\left( {\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)  = {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}.
\]

Hence

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( {\tau {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Since \( u \leq  A \) at \( \tau  = 0 \) , we have \( \tau {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  \leq  0 \) at \( \tau  = 0 \) . When \( \mathcal{M} \) is a closed manifold, inequality (16.48) now follows from the maximum principle.

(2) Let

\[
F \Doteq  \tau \left( {\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)  - n - 4\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) .
\]

Using

\[
L\left( {\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)  =  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - 2\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log u}\right) ,
\]

we shall show that \( {LF} \leq  0 \) wherever \( F \geq  0 \) .

First note that \( \frac{\Delta u}{u} + \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} = \Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \) . We compute

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\left( {\Delta \log u}\right)  = \Delta \left( {\Delta \log u + {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \Delta \left( {\Delta \log u}\right)  + 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla \left( {\Delta \log u}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{\left| \nabla \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + 2\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log u}\right) .
\]

Hence, combining this with (16.50), we have

\[
L\left( {\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)  =  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - 2\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log u}\right)
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{2}{n}{\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2}.
\]

Combining this with (16.52), we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) F \leq   - \frac{2\tau }{n}{\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} + \Delta \log u - 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \Doteq  G.
\]

If \( F \geq  0 \) , then

\[
\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \geq  \frac{1}{\tau }\left( {n + 4\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{n}{\tau },
\]

so that

\[
- 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta \log u - \frac{n}{\tau }.
\]

This implies

\[
G \leq   - \frac{2\tau }{n}{\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} + {2\Delta }\log u - \frac{n}{\tau } \leq   - \frac{n}{2\tau } < 0.
\]

That is, wherever \( F \geq  0 \) , the function \( F \) is a subsolution to the heat equation with a gradient term. Since \( F \leq   - n < 0 \) at \( \tau  = 0 \) , by the maximum principle we conclude \( F \leq  0 \) for all \( \tau  \geq  0 \) , and hence inequality (16.49), when \( \mathcal{M} \) is a closed manifold.

See the following remarks for an indication of the proof of the theorem in the case where \( \mathcal{M} \) is noncompact.

With a little work, one can generalize the above result of Hamilton to complete noncompact manifolds. The point is that one can first assume that \( u \geq  \varepsilon \) by replacing \( u \) by \( {u}_{\varepsilon } \Doteq  u + \varepsilon \) and then let \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) once one has proven the result for \( {u}_{\varepsilon } \) . One can then apply Bernstein’s derivative estimate for the heat equation (compare with the Bernstein-Bando-Shi estimates in Chapter 7 of Volume One and Shi's local estimates in Chapter 14 of this book) to obtain bounds on (growth estimates) \( {\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2} \) and \( {\Delta u} \) (and then an integral estimate for \( {\left| \nabla \nabla u\right| }^{2} \) via integration by parts), so that one can still apply the maximum principle on noncompact manifolds to obtain the desired estimate (see Kotschwar [316] for details).

EXERCISE 16.20. Find a solution \( u \) to the heat equation on the line \( \mathbb{R} \) with

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  0}}u\left( {x, t}\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} 1 & \text{ if }x > 0, \\  0 & \text{ if }x < 0. \end{array}\right.
\]

(The function on the RHS is called the Heaviside function.)

HINT: Look for a solution of the form

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  = h\left( \frac{x}{\sqrt{t}}\right)
\]

and derive an ODE for \( h \) . What are the boundary values at infinity for \( h \) ?

nodes.content:
SOLUTION TO EXERCISE 16.20. We compute

\[
- \frac{1}{2}\frac{x}{{t}^{3/2}}{h}^{\prime }\left( \frac{x}{\sqrt{t}}\right)  = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \frac{{\partial }^{2}u}{\partial {x}^{2}} = \frac{1}{t}{h}^{\prime \prime }\left( \frac{x}{\sqrt{t}}\right) ,
\]

so that by taking \( y = \frac{x}{\sqrt{t}} \) we have

\[
{h}^{\prime \prime }\left( y\right)  =  - \frac{1}{2}y{h}^{\prime }\left( y\right) .
\]

The solution to this ODE satisfies

\[
{h}^{\prime }\left( y\right)  = C{e}^{-\frac{1}{4}{y}^{2}}
\]

for some \( C \in  \mathbb{R} \) . We wish to find a solution of this ODE with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{y \rightarrow  \infty }}h\left( y\right)  = 1 \) and \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{y \rightarrow   - \infty }}h\left( y\right)  = 0 \) . Thus we define

\[
h\left( y\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi }}{\int }_{-\infty }^{y}{e}^{-\frac{1}{4}{\bar{y}}^{2}}d\bar{y}.
\]

We leave it to the reader to check that the solution

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi }}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x/\sqrt{t}}{e}^{-\frac{1}{4}{\bar{y}}^{2}}d\bar{y}
\]

has the desired properties. Note that

\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\left( {x, t}\right)  = \frac{1}{{\left( 4\pi t\right) }^{1/2}}{e}^{-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4t}},
\]

which is the positive fundamental solution of the heat equation. This corresponds to the fact that the derivative of the Heaviside function is the \( \delta \) -function.

nodes.content:
THEOREM 16.26. Suppose there exists \( A > 2 \) such that

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{H}^{2}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \exp \left( \frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{A\tau }\right) {d\mu } \leq  \frac{1}{f\left( \tau \right) }
\]

for a positive integrable function \( f \) on \( \left( {0, T}\right) \) . Then there exist constants \( {C}_{i}\left( \tau \right)  < \infty \) depending on \( \tau \) , for \( i = 1,2,3 \) , such that

\[

3.1. The differential Harnack estimate for the heat equation.

Given a positive solution \( u \) of the heat equation, define \( f \) by \( u \Doteq  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-f} \) . Recall from (16.27) that

\[

\]

Hereafter, we denote

\[

\]

We now restate and prove Theorem 16.4 in the more general case of a complete Riemannian manifold with \( \mathrm{{Rc}} \geq  0 \) .

THEOREM 16.28 (Li-Yau-Perelman-type estimate for the heat kernel). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a complete Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature. If \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) is a fixed point and \( H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \) is the (minimal) positive fundamental solution of the heat equation based at \( x \) :

\[
\frac{\partial H}{\partial \tau } = {\Delta }_{y}H
\]

\[

\]

then

(16.63)

\]

where \( f \) is defined by \( H \Doteq  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-f} \) .

nodes.proof:
From (16.28),

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( {Wu}\right)  = u\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) W - 2\nabla u \cdot  \nabla W
\]

( \( u \) is a solution to the heat equation), and \( u\nabla f =  - \nabla u \) , we have

(16.66)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) v =  - {2\tau }\left( {{\left| \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2\tau }g\right| }^{2} + \operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla f,\nabla f}\right) }\right) u.
\]

Let \( h\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \geq  0 \) be a compactly supported function at \( \tau  = {\tau }_{0} \) . One can solve the backward heat equation

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } + \Delta }\right) h = 0
\]

and obtain a bounded solution \( h\left( {y,\tau }\right) \) for all \( 0 \leq  \tau  \leq  {\tau }_{0} \) . Such a solution can be given via the above representation formula (16.62), now using the heat kernel to the backward heat equation. By the maximum principle we have

\[
h\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  \max h\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)
\]

and

\[
\left| {\nabla h}\right| \left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  \max \left| {\nabla h}\right| \left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)
\]

(the integral bound for \( \left| {\nabla h}\right| \left( {y,\tau }\right) \) can be shown via integration by parts such as in [76]). We also have

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{vhd\mu } = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {h\frac{\partial v}{\partial \tau } + v\frac{\partial h}{\partial \tau }}\right) {d\mu }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) v}\right) {d\mu }
\]

\[
=  - {2\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {{\left| \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2\tau }g\right| }^{2} + \operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla f,\nabla f}\right) }\right) {ud\mu }
\]

(16.67)

\[
\leq  0,
\]

where we used the \( \mathrm{{Rc}} \geq  0 \) assumption and (16.66). (Notice that we still have the desired final inequality even if \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla f,\nabla f}\right) {d\mu } \) is not finite.) In view of the above estimate for \( h\left( {y,\tau }\right) \) and \( \left| {\nabla h}\right| \left( {y,\tau }\right) \) , we can also integrate by parts:

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{v}_{H}{\Delta h} - {h\Delta }{v}_{H}}\right) {d\mu } = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\operatorname{div}\left( {{v}_{H}\nabla h - h\nabla {v}_{H}}\right) {d\mu } = 0.
\]

To justify the last equality when \( \mathcal{M} \) is noncompact, we may apply standard estimates for the decay of the heat kernel at spatial infinity. In particular, (16.68)

\[
{\int }_{B\left( {x, R}\right) }\left( {{v}_{H}{\Delta h} - {h\Delta }{v}_{H}}\right) {d\mu } = {\int }_{\partial B\left( {x, R}\right) }\left( {{v}_{H}\langle \nabla h,\nu \rangle  - h\left\langle  {\nabla {v}_{H},\nu }\right\rangle  }\right) {d\sigma },
\]

where \( \nu \) is the unit outward normal to \( \partial B\left( {x, R}\right) \) . In fact

\[
{v}_{H} =  - {2\tau \Delta H} + \tau \frac{{\left| \nabla H\right| }^{2}}{H} - H\left( {\log H + \frac{n}{2}\log \left( {4\pi \tau }\right)  + n}\right) ,
\]

whose absolute value has a pointwise upper bound in terms of \( H \) , which tends to 0 as \( y \rightarrow  \infty \) . This takes care of the first term on the RHS of (16.68). Thus for the integration by parts we only need to show the claim that \( {\int }_{\partial B\left( {x,{R}_{i}}\right) }h\left\langle  {\nabla {v}_{H},\nu }\right\rangle  {d\sigma } \rightarrow  0 \) for some sequence \( {R}_{i} \rightarrow  \infty \) . A direct computation shows that

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{v}_{H} = \tau \left( {2{\nabla }_{i}\left( {\Delta fH}\right)  - 4{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f{\nabla }_{j}{fH} - 2{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}{\nabla }_{i}H}\right)  + {\nabla }_{i}\left( {fH}\right) .
\]

Our discussion, from the previous section, on verifying the linear entropy formula, shows that (we leave this as an exercise) for every \( \tau  > 0 \)

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left| {\nabla v}\right| \left( {y,\tau }\right) {d\mu } < \infty .
\]

This is enough for our claim.

In order to prove that \( {v}_{H} \leq  0 \) , we shall show that for any \( {\tau }_{0} > 0 \) and any compactly supported nonnegative smooth function \( h\left( y\right) \) ,

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) h\left( y\right) {d\mu } \leq  0.
\]

Clearly this implies \( {v}_{H}\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \leq  0 \) for any \( y \) . In order to achieve this, we solve the adjoint heat equation \( \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } + \Delta }\right) h\left( {y,\tau }\right)  = 0 \) with \( h\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  = h\left( y\right) \) backward in time. By the above monotonicity (16.67) of \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{vhd\mu } \) , it suffices to prove the following.

LEMMA 16.30 \( \left( {{v}_{H} \rightarrow  0}\right. \) as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0) \) . For the above bounded function \( h \geq  0 \) solving

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } + \Delta }\right) h = 0,
\]

we have

(16.69)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{hd\mu } = 0
\]

PROOF OF LEMMA. The proof of the lemma will be divided into several steps.

(1) We first show that there exists \( C > 0 \) , independent of \( \tau \) , such that

\[
\left( {{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{hd\mu }}\right) \left( \tau \right)  \leq  C.
\]

Since the function \( h\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) \) is compactly supported and smooth, we have \( h\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) ,\left| {\nabla h}\right| \left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) \) , and \( \left| {\Delta h}\right| \left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) \) are bounded on \( \mathcal{M} \) . By the above discussion, this implies that there exists a bounded solution (the solution given by the representation formula through the heat kernel to the backward heat equation is such a solution) \( h\left( {y,\tau }\right) \) with \( \left| {\nabla h}\right| \left( {y,\tau }\right) \) and \( \left| {\Delta h}\right| \left( {y,\tau }\right) \) uniformly bounded (in terms of \( \tau \) ) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) ; for the result on \( \left| {\Delta h}\right| \) , notice that \( {\Delta h} \) also solves the backward heat equation. Integration by parts shows that

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau \left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {Hhd\mu } =  - {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau \langle \nabla f,\nabla h\rangle {Hd\mu }
\]

\[
= \tau {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\langle \nabla H,\nabla h\rangle {d\mu } =  - \tau {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{H\Delta hd\mu } \rightarrow  0
\]

as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) . Therefore

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{hd\mu } = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\tau {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + f - n}\right) {Hhd\mu }.
\]

By the lower bound for the heat kernel of Cheeger and Yau, i.e., (16.11), we know that

\[
f\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau },
\]

which implies

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {Hhd\mu } \leq  0.
\]

On the other hand, the gradient estimate (16.57) implies

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}{Hhd\mu } \leq  {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}2\left( {C\left( \delta \right)  + \frac{{d}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{\left( {4 - \delta }\right) \tau }}\right) {Hhd\mu },
\]

which can be seen to be bounded from above as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) by consideration of the heat kernel parametrix (Theorem 16.12).

(2) We next show that there exists a sequence \( {\tau }_{k} \rightarrow  0 \) such that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\tau }_{k}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\Delta f} - \frac{n}{2{\tau }_{k}}}\right) {Hhd\mu } = 0.
\]

Notice that by (1) and the monotonicity of \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{vhd\mu } \) , we know that there exists a finite number \( \alpha \) such that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{hd\mu } = \alpha
\]

By the strong maximum principle, we have \( h\left( {x,0}\right)  > 0 \) and

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{Hhd\mu } = {\left. {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}Hhd\mu \right| }_{\tau  = 0} = h\left( {x,0}\right) .
\]

Therefore, by scaling, we may assume that \( h\left( {x,0}\right)  = 1 \) . By the linear entropy formula

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{vhd\mu } \leq   - {2\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\left| \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2\tau }g\right| }^{2}{uhd\mu },
\]

we have

\[
{\int }_{\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}^{\bar{\tau }}\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{vhd\mu }}\right) {d\tau } \leq   - 2{\int }_{\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}^{\bar{\tau }}\tau {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\left| \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2\tau }g\right| }^{2}{uhd\mu d\tau }.
\]

Therefore we have

\[
2{\int }_{\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}^{\bar{\tau }}\tau \int {\left| \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2\tau }g\right| }^{2}{Hhd\mu d\tau }
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{\left. {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}hd\mu \right| }_{\tau  = \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}} - {\left. {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}hd\mu \right| }_{\tau  = \bar{\tau }}}\right)  \rightarrow  0
\]

as \( \bar{\tau } \rightarrow  0 \) . By the mean value theorem, we can find \( {\tau }_{k} \rightarrow  0 \) so that

\[
{\tau }_{k}^{2}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\left| \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2{\tau }_{k}}g\right| }^{2}{Hhd\mu } \rightarrow  0.
\]

By Hölder's inequality we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\tau }_{k}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\Delta f} - \frac{n}{2{\tau }_{k}}}\right) {Hhd\mu } = 0.
\]

(3) Now we write

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{vh}\;{d\mu } = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau \left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {uh}\;{d\mu } + {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau \left( {{\Delta f} - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {uh}\;{d\mu }
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {uh}\;{d\mu }
\]

By the above discussion we know that when \( u = H \) , the first two of three terms on the right-hand side of the above equation tend to zero. Therefore by (1) we know that \( \alpha  \leq  0 \) .

{\tau }_{k}^{2}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\left| \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2{\tau }_{k}}g\right| }^{2}{Hhd\mu } \rightarrow  0.
\]

By Hölder's inequality we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\tau }_{k}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\Delta f} - \frac{n}{2{\tau }_{k}}}\right) {Hhd\mu } = 0.
\]

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{vh}\;{d\mu } = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau \left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {uh}\;{d\mu } + {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau \left( {{\Delta f} - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {uh}\;{d\mu }
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {uh}\;{d\mu }
\]

By the above discussion we know that when \( u = H \) , the first two of three terms on the right-hand side of the above equation tend to zero. Therefore by (1) we know that \( \alpha  \leq  0 \) .

Recall from (16.65) that \( {\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f\left( \tau \right) ,\tau }\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{d\mu } \leq  0 \) for all \( \tau  > 0 \) . From (16.24) we also have

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }{\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f\left( \tau \right) ,\tau }\right)  =  - {2\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\left| \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2\tau }g\right| }^{2} + \operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla f,\nabla f}\right) }\right) {Hd\mu } \leq  0.
\]

Therefore, from \( {\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) ,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \geq  0 \) we conclude that \( {\mathcal{W}}_{\text{ lin }}\left( {f\left( \tau \right) ,\tau }\right)  \equiv  0 \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . This implies

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f\left( \tau \right)  = \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}
\]

for all \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . That is, for any such \( \tau ,\phi  \doteq  {4\tau f} \) satisfies

(16.70)

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\phi  = 2{g}_{ij}.
\]

From (16.70) we see that \( \phi \) attains its minimum at some point \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) . We claim

\[
\phi \left( x\right)  - \phi \left( O\right)  = {d}^{2}\left( {x, O}\right) .
\]

To see this, let \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) be any point and consider a unit speed minimal geodesic \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0, d\left( {x, O}\right) }\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) joining \( O \) to \( x \) . We have

\[
\frac{{d}^{2}}{d{s}^{2}}f\left( {\gamma \left( s\right) }\right)  = \left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {\dot{\gamma }}^{i}{\dot{\gamma }}^{j} = 2.
\]

Since \( \nabla \phi \left( O\right)  = \overrightarrow{0} \) , we have \( \phi \left( {\gamma \left( s\right) }\right)  = \phi \left( O\right)  + {d}^{2}\left( {O,\gamma \left( s\right) }\right) \) for all \( s \in \; \left\lbrack  {0, d\left( {x, O}\right) }\right\rbrack \) ; the claim follows. This also tells us that \( {d}^{2} \) is smooth on all of \( \mathcal{M} \) . Hence, taking the trace of (16.70), we have

\[
\Delta \left( {d}^{2}\right)  \equiv  {2n}
\]

This, together with our assumption that \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( g\right)  \geq  0 \) , implies \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is isometric to Euclidean space (see the following exercise).

Prove that if \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is a complete Riemannian manifold, \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) , and \( {d}^{2}\left( {\cdot , O}\right) \) is a smooth function with \( \Delta \left( {d}^{2}\right)  \equiv  {2n} \) , then \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) is isometric to Euclidean space.

HINT: Show that

\[
\frac{r\operatorname{Area}\left( {\partial B\left( {O, r}\right) }\right) }{\operatorname{Vol}\left( {B\left( {O, r}\right) }\right) } \equiv  n.
\]

This implies

\[
\frac{d}{dr}\log \left\lbrack  {\operatorname{Vol}\left( {B\left( {O, r}\right) }\right) }\right\rbrack   = \frac{\operatorname{Area}\left( {\partial B\left( {O, r}\right) }\right) }{\operatorname{Vol}\left( {B\left( {O, r}\right) }\right) } = \frac{n}{r}
\]

so that \( \operatorname{Vol}\left( {B\left( {O, r}\right) }\right)  = {\omega }_{n}{r}^{n} \) since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{r \rightarrow  0}}\frac{\operatorname{Vol}\left( {B\left( {O, r}\right) }\right) }{{\omega }_{n}{r}^{n}} = 1 \) . The result now follows from the equality case of the Bishop-Gromov volume comparison theorem.

Using a similar reduction as in step (2) of the proof of Lemma 16.30 (the main lemma for proving the differential Harnack estimate (16.63)), \( {}^{10} \) one can reduce proving (16.76) to proving

(16.77)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  \infty }}\left( {{\int }_{\mathcal{M}} - H\log {Hd\mu } - \frac{n}{2}\log \left( {4\pi \tau }\right)  - \frac{n}{2}}\right)  = \log \left( {\operatorname{AVR}\left( g\right) }\right) .
\]

The reader may consult [377] for the details. It is in the proof of (16.77) that we use Theorem 16.38 on precise upper and lower bounds for the heat kernel. The rest of the proof involves some straightforward computations, noticing that \( \operatorname{AVR}\left( g\right)  = \frac{\theta }{{\omega }_{n}} \) .

Another way to interpret (16.76) is that for the linear heat equation, the large time asymptotic limit of the linear entropy is equal to the logarithm of the large time asymptotic limit of the static reduced volume (see (16.73)). It seems to be unknown whether the corresponding relation holds for the Ricci flow case. (See [377] for more explanations regarding this problem.)

---

(16.80)

\[
{\square }_{y}^{ * }H = 0\;\text{ and }\;\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  = {\delta }_{x}\left( y\right)
\]

for any \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: DEFINITION 16.43. We say that \( H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) \) is a fundamental solution for the adjoint heat equation centered at \( \left( {x,0}\right) \) if (16.80) \[ {\square }_{y}^{ * }H = 0\;\text{ and }\;\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau \rightarrow 0}}H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) = {\delta }_{x}\left( y\right) \] for any \( x \in \mathcal{M} \) .

THEOREM 16.44 (Perelman's differential Harnack estimate). Suppose that \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow on a closed manifold. Let \( H,\tau  = T - t \) , and \( {v}_{H} \) be as above. Then

(16.82)

\[
{v}_{H} \leq  0,
\]

or, equivalently,

(16.83)

\[
\tau \left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n \leq  0.
\]
