Let \( H,\tau = T - t \) , and \( {v}_{H} \) be as above. Then (16.82) \[ {v}_{H} \leq 0, \] or, equivalently, (16.83) \[ \tau \left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)...

nodes.proof:
The proof follows the same line of argument as in the previous linear case. Recall from Lemma 6.8 on p. 227 of Part I of this volume the pointwise differential equality:

(16.84)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta  + R}\right) {v}_{u} =  - {2\tau }{\left| \operatorname{Rc} + \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2\tau }g\right| }^{2}u
\]

for any positive solution \( u \) to the adjoint heat equation. Here \( {v}_{u} \) is defined by (6.20) on p. 227 of Part I of this volume, which is the same as (16.81) with \( H \) replaced by \( u \) . Note that one of the ways in which Perelman obtained his entropy monotonicity formula is essentially by integrating the above equality (see subsection 1.2.2 of Chapter 6 in Part I of this volume).

In §9.3 of [402] Perelman describes the proof of the claim

\[
{v}_{H} \leq  0
\]

by demonstrating in a clever way that for any \( {\tau }_{ * } \) with \( T \geq  {\tau }_{ * } > 0 \) ,

(16.85)

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}\left( {y,{\tau }_{ * }}\right) h\left( y\right) d{\mu }_{{\tau }_{ * }}\left( y\right)  \leq  0
\]

for any function \( h\left( y\right)  \geq  0 \) with compact support. \( {}^{11} \)

In order to achieve this, in [402] the heat equation

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) h\left( {y, t}\right)  = 0
\]

is solved with the 'initial data'

\[
h\left( {y, T - {\tau }_{ * }}\right)  = h\left( y\right)
\]

\( \left( {t = T - {\tau }_{ * }}\right. \) corresponds to \( \left. {\tau  = {\tau }_{ * }}\right) \) being the given compactly supported nonnegative function. Applying (16.84) to \( u\left( {y,\tau }\right)  = H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) \) , one derives, via integration by parts, that

(16.86)

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{hd}{\mu }_{\tau } = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } + R}\right) {v}_{H}d{\mu }_{\tau } + {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}\frac{\partial h}{\partial \tau }d{\mu }_{\tau }
\]

\[
=  - 2{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau {\left| \operatorname{Rc} + \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2\tau }g\right| }^{2}{Hhd}{\mu }_{\tau } \leq  0,
\]

---

\( {}^{11} \) Given any \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , we may then take \( h \) limiting to the \( \delta \) -function centered at \( x \) to obtain \( {v}_{H}\left( {x,{\tau }_{ * }}\right)  \leq  0 \) .

---

where we used

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h\Delta }{v}_{H}d{\mu }_{\tau } - {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{\Delta h}\;d{\mu }_{\tau } = 0.
\]

The Li-Yau-type inequality \( {v}_{H} \leq  0 \) , i.e., Theorem 16.44, then follows from the above monotonicity, provided we can establish the following.

Claim.

(16.87)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{hd}{\mu }_{\tau } \leq  0
\]

The rest of this subsection is devoted to proving the above claim (16.87) following [384]. We shall need the heat kernel parametrix as well as some results on the reduced distance. With respect to the metric \( g\left( \tau \right) \) , let \( {d}_{\tau }\left( {x, y}\right) \) denote the distance function, let \( {B}_{\tau }\left( {x, r}\right) \) denote the ball of radius \( r \) centered at \( x \) , and let \( {\operatorname{Vol}}_{\tau } \) denote the volume.

Analogously to Theorem 16.12 we have the following.

THEOREM 16.46 (Ricci flow adjoint heat kernel parametrix). Suppose \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow on a closed manifold. Let \( H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) \) (we also denote this by \( H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \) ) be the fundamental solution to the (backward in t) adjoint heat equation (16.80). Then as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) we have

\[
H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \sim  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{\infty }{\tau }^{j}{u}_{j}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) .
\]

That is, there exist \( \bar{\tau } > 0 \) and a sequence \( {u}_{j} \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( {\mathcal{M} \times  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) such that

\[
H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  - {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{k}{\tau }^{j}{u}_{j}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  = {w}_{k}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) ,
\]

where

\[
{w}_{k}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  = O\left( {\tau }^{k + 1 - \frac{n}{2}}\right)
\]

as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) , uniformly for all \( x, y \in  \mathcal{M} \) . The function \( {u}_{0}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \) may be chosen so that \( {u}_{0}\left( {x, x,0}\right)  = 1 \) .

This result was proved by Garofalo and Lanconelli [204] for fundamental solutions of heat-type equations in divergence form. In comparison, for the adjoint heat equation \( \frac{\partial u}{\partial \tau } - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }u + {Ru} = 0 \) there is a zeroth-order term \( {Ru} \) and the Laplacian is with respect to a time-dependent metric \( g\left( t\right) \) . However, one can verify that the argument in [204] carries over to the case of the adjoint heat equation provided \( g\left( t\right) \) is \( {C}^{\infty } \) on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . We leave this verification as a (somewhat nontrivial) exercise for the reader.

Define the entropy-like quantity

(16.88)

\[
{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right)  \Doteq  {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{hd}{\mu }_{\tau },
\]

where \( h \) is the previously described solution to the heat equation. It is clear that for any \( \tau \) with \( T \geq  \tau  > 0,{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right) \) is a well-defined quantity. A priori it may blow up as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) .

It turns out that in our course of proving \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right)  \leq  0 \) , we need to show first that there exists \( C > 0 \) , which may depend on the geometry of the Ricci flow solution \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) defined on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) but which is independent of \( \tau \) (as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) ), such that

(16.89)

\[
{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right)  \leq  C
\]

for all \( T \geq  \tau  > 0 \) .

The following lemma supplies the key estimates for this purpose.

LEMMA 16.47 (Gradient estimates for the adjoint heat equation). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) ,\tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a smooth solution to the backward Ricci flow on a closed manifold. Suppose there exist positive constants \( {k}_{1} \) and \( {k}_{2} \) such that on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
{R}_{ij}\left( {g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \geq   - {k}_{1}{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) \;\text{ and }\;\max \left\{  {R\left( {y,\tau }\right) ,{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}\left( {y,\tau }\right) }\right\}   \leq  {k}_{2}.
\]

(i) (Gradient estimate for uniformly bounded positive solutions) If \( u \leq \; A \) is a positive solution to the adjoint heat equation on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , then there exist constants \( {C}_{1},{C}_{2} < \infty \) depending only on \( {k}_{1},{k}_{2} \) , and \( n \) such that for \( 0 < \tau  \leq  \min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\} \) ,

(16.90)

\[
\tau \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} \leq  \left( {1 + {C}_{1}\tau }\right) \left( {\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + {C}_{2}\tau }\right) .
\]

(ii) (Gradient estimate for positive solutions) If \( u \) is a positive solution to the adjoint heat equation on \( \mathcal{M} \times  (0, T\rbrack \) , then there exists a constant \( B < \infty \) , depending on the solution \( \{ g\left( \tau \right) {\} }_{t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  } \) , such that for

\[
0 < \tau  \leq  \min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  ,
\]

(16.91)

\[
\tau \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} \leq  \left( {2 + {C}_{1}\tau }\right) \left( {\log \left( {\frac{B}{{\tau }^{n/2}u}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud}{\mu }_{\tau }}\right)  + {C}_{2}\tau }\right) .
\]

Here and henceforth we shall use the same notation \( {C}_{i} \) (or \( B \) ) on different lines if the constants differ at most by a multiplicative factor depending only on \( n \) . Note that \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud}{\mu }_{\tau } \) is independent of \( \tau \) and equals 1 if \( u \) is the fundamental solution. The proof of the lemma given below is a modification of some arguments in Hamilton [249]. See Appendix E of this volume for an exposition of some of the estimates in [249].

Proof. (i) If \( u \) is a solution of \( {\square }^{ * }u = 0 \) , then we compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( {{g}^{ij}{\nabla }_{i}u{\nabla }_{j}u}\right)  =  - 4\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla u,\nabla u}\right)  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla u\right| }^{2} - 2\nabla \left( {Ru}\right)  \cdot  \nabla u,
\]

where we used \( \nabla \left( {{\square }^{ * }u}\right)  \cdot  \nabla u = 0 \) and where the Rc term on the RHS is from both differentiating \( {g}^{ij} \) in time and commuting \( \Delta \) and \( \nabla \) . Hence

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}\right)  = \frac{-4\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla u,\nabla u}\right)  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla u\right| }^{2} - 2\nabla \left( {Ru}\right)  \cdot  \nabla u}{u}
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\nabla u \cdot  \nabla {\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} - \frac{2{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{4}}{{u}^{3}} - \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) u
\]

\[
=  - \frac{4\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla u,\nabla u}\right) }{u} - 2\nabla R \cdot  \nabla u - \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}R
\]

\[
- \frac{2}{u}{\left| \nabla \nabla u - \frac{\nabla u \otimes  \nabla u}{u}\right| }^{2}
\]

Applying the assumed bounds for \( \operatorname{Rc}, R \) , and \( \left| {\nabla R}\right| \) , we obtain

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}\right)  \leq  \left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1}\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + 2\left| {\nabla R}\right| \left| {\nabla u}\right|
\]

(16.92)

\[
\leq  \left( {\left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1} + 1}\right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + {k}_{2}u
\]

where in the last line we used \( 2\left| {\nabla R}\right| \left| {\nabla u}\right|  \leq  \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + u{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2} \) and \( {\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2} \leq  {k}_{2} \) .

We also compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( {u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) u + u\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + 2\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}
\]

\[
= \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + {Ru} - {Ru}\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)
\]

(16.93)

\[
\geq  \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} - n{k}_{1}u - {k}_{2}u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) ,
\]

where we used

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \log u = \frac{\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) u}{u} + \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} =  - R + \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}},
\]

\( {\square }^{ * }u = 0, u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  \geq  0 \) , and the upper and lower bounds for \( R \) .

Consider the quantity

\[
\Phi  \Doteq  \varphi \left( \tau \right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} - {e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  - {C\tau u},
\]

where below we shall choose \( C \) and the function \( \varphi \left( \tau \right) \) of \( \tau  \geq  0 \) . By combining the above two equations (16.92) and (16.93), we obtain

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \Phi  = \frac{d\varphi }{d\tau }\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + \varphi \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}
\]

\[
- {k}_{2}{e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  - {e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( {u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
- C\left( {u + \tau \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) u}\right)
\]

(16.94)

\[
\leq  \left( {\frac{d\varphi }{d\tau } + \left( {\left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1} + 1}\right) \varphi  - {e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }}\right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{k}_{2}\varphi  + n{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }}\right) u - C\left( {u - {\tau Ru}}\right) .
\]

Now let \( \varphi \left( \tau \right)  \Doteq  \frac{\tau }{1 + \left( {\left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1} + 1}\right) \tau } \) (note that \( \frac{\tau }{2 + \left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1}} \leq  \varphi \left( \tau \right)  \leq  \tau  \leq  1 \) for \( 0 \leq  \tau  \leq  1) \) . Since in general, for \( c \geq  0 \) ,

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( \frac{\tau }{1 + {c\tau }}\right)  = \frac{1}{{\left( 1 + c\tau \right) }^{2}} \leq  \frac{1}{1 + {c\tau }} = 1 - \frac{c\tau }{1 + {c\tau }},
\]

we have that the function \( \varphi \left( \tau \right) \) satisfies

\[
\frac{d\varphi }{d\tau } + \left( {\left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1} + 1}\right) \varphi  - 1 \leq  0.
\]

From this and \( {\tau R} \leq  \frac{1}{2} \) (since \( \left. {\tau  \leq  \frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right) \) , we see that (16.94) implies

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \Phi  \leq  \left( {{k}_{2}\varphi  + n{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }}\right) u - \frac{1}{2}{Cu} \leq  0,
\]

provided we choose \( C \doteq  2\left( {{k}_{2} + n{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{2}}}\right) \) (since \( \tau ,\varphi  \leq  1 \) ). By the maximum principle, since \( \Phi \left( 0\right)  =  - u\left( 0\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u\left( 0\right) }\right)  \leq  0 \) , we have

\[
\Phi \left( {x,\tau }\right)  \leq  0
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( 0 \leq  \tau  \leq  \min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\} \) . That is, on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\} \) ,

\[
\varphi \left( \tau \right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} \leq  {e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + 2\left( {{k}_{2} + n{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{2}}}\right) {\tau u}.
\]

From this one can easily derive (16.90). This completes the proof of part (i) of Lemma 16.47.

(ii) To prove the second part, we first claim that for a positive solution \( u \) to the adjoint heat equation, there exists a constant \( C < \infty \) depending on \( \{ g\left( \tau \right) {\} }_{\tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  } \) such that

(16.95)

\[
u\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{C}{{\tau }^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {z,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( z\right)  = \frac{\text{ const }}{{\tau }^{n/2}}.
\]

Assuming (16.95), we have for \( \widetilde{\tau } \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{\tau }{2},\tau }\right\rbrack \) that

\[
u\left( {y,\widetilde{\tau }}\right)  \leq  \frac{C}{{\left( \tau /2\right) }^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud\mu }
\]

since \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud\mu } \) is constant. Let \( A \Doteq  \frac{C}{{\left( \tau /2\right) }^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud\mu },\widetilde{u}\left( \widetilde{\tau }\right)  \Doteq  u\left( {\widetilde{\tau } + \frac{\tau }{2}}\right) \) , and \( \widetilde{g}\left( \widetilde{\tau }\right)  \Doteq  g\left( {\widetilde{\tau } + \frac{\tau }{2}}\right) \) . Since \( \widetilde{u} \leq  A \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau /2}\right\rbrack \) , we may apply estimate (16.90) using the above quantities to obtain

\[
\frac{\tau }{2}\frac{{\left| \nabla \widetilde{u}\right| }^{2}}{{\widetilde{u}}^{2}}\left( \frac{\tau }{2}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {C}_{1}\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) \left( {\log \left( \frac{A}{\widetilde{u}\left( \frac{\tau }{2}\right) }\right)  + {C}_{2}\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) .
\]

That is,

\[
\frac{\tau }{2}\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}}\left( \tau \right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {C}_{1}\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) \left( {\log \left( \frac{\frac{C}{{\left( \tau /2\right) }^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud\mu }}{u\left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {C}_{2}\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) .
\]

Estimate (16.91) now follows.

Now we prove the claim. Inequality (16.95) is a mean value-type inequality, which can be proved via Moser iteration for example; we shall instead follow [249]. Note that in the proof we may assume without loss of generality that

\[
{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  }\right\rbrack  }{\tau }^{n/2}u
\]

is finite; the reason for this is that we shall establish estimate (16.95) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {\varepsilon ,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  \rbrack }\right. \) with \( \tau \) replaced by \( {\tau }_{\varepsilon } \Doteq  \tau  - \varepsilon \) and \( C \) independent of \( \varepsilon \) and then take \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) . For simplicity, below we do not change the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  }\right\rbrack \) and we leave it to the reader to check that this does not affect the argument.

Let \( \left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  }\right\rbrack \) be a space-time point such that

\[
{\tau }_{0}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  }\right\rbrack  }}{\tau }^{n/2}u\left( {y,\tau }\right) .
\]

We then have

\[
\mathop{\max }\limits_{{\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2},{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack  }}u\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  {\left( \frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2}\right) }^{-n/2}{\tau }_{0}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  = {2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \Doteq  A.
\]

With this upper bound, we apply inequality (16.90) to \( u \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2},{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and conclude \( {}^{12} \)

\[
\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2}\left( \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}}\right) \left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + \frac{{C}_{1}}{2}{\tau }_{0}}\right) \left( {\log \left( \frac{{2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) }{u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) }\right)  + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}{\tau }_{0}}\right)
\]

---

\( {}^{12} \) In (16.90), \( \tau \) is replaced by \( \tau  - \frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2} \) so that \( {\tau }_{0} \) is replaced by \( \frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2} \) .

---

for all \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Let \( U\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \Doteq  \log \left( \frac{{2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) }{u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) }\right)  + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}{\tau }_{0} \) so that \( \nabla U =  - \frac{\nabla u}{u} \) . The above inequality can be rewritten as

\[
\left| {\nabla \sqrt{U}}\right|  \leq  \sqrt{\frac{1 + \frac{1}{2}{C}_{1}{\tau }_{0}}{2{\tau }_{0}}}.
\]

Integrating this along geodesics with respect to \( g\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) \) emanating from \( {y}_{0} \) implies

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{B}_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( {{y}_{0},\sqrt{\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{1 + \frac{1}{2}{C}_{1}{\tau }_{0}}}}\right) }}\sqrt{U}\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \leq  \sqrt{U}\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.
\]

Rewriting the above in terms of \( u \) , we have

\[
u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \geq  {2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) \exp \left\{  {-{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}\log 2 + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) }^{2} + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}}\right\}
\]

\[
\geq  {2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) {e}^{-\left( {\frac{1}{2} + \frac{n}{2}\log 2 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{\frac{n}{2}\log 2 + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}}}\right) } \doteq  {c}_{3}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)
\]

for all \( y \in  {B}_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( {{y}_{0},\sqrt{\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{1 + \frac{1}{2}{C}_{1}{\tau }_{0}}}}\right) \) ; here we have also used \( {\tau }_{0} \leq  1 \) .

Notice that

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( {{y}_{0},\sqrt{\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{1 + \frac{1}{2}{C}_{1}{\tau }_{0}}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {c}_{4}{\tau }_{0}^{n/2}
\]

for some \( {c}_{4} > 0 \) depending on the geometry of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) }\right) \) . Therefore we have

\[
\frac{{C}_{5}}{{\tau }_{0}^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) d{\mu }_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( y\right)  \geq  u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) ,
\]

where \( {C}_{5} = \frac{1}{{c}_{3}{c}_{4}} \) . By our choice of \( \left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) \) , we have

\[
{\tau }^{n/2}u\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  {\tau }_{0}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \leq  {C}_{5}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) d{\mu }_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( y\right)  = {C}_{5}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right) .
\]

This proves (16.95) and hence completes the proof of part (ii) of Lemma 16.47.

We now return to considering the quantity \( {\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right) \) . We shall first show that this quantity is bounded and then show that it has a nonpositive limit as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) . Integrating by parts, we can rewrite the entropy-like quantity in (16.88)

\[
{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, u,\tau }\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\tau \left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n}\right) {uhd}{\mu }_{\tau }
\]

as

\[
{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, u,\tau }\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}{uh}{d}_{\mu } - {2\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\langle \nabla f,\nabla h\rangle {ud}{\mu }_{\tau }
\]

\[
+ \tau {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\operatorname{Ruh}d{\mu }_{\tau } + {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {f - n}\right) {uh}{d}^{ * }
\]

\[
\Doteq  \mathrm{I} + \mathrm{{II}} + \mathrm{{III}} + \mathrm{{IV}},
\]

where the terms on the RHS are defined as ordered.

Now if \( u = {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-f} \) is the fundamental solution to the adjoint heat equation, we have \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud}{\mu }_{\tau } \equiv  1 \) . Therefore, by (16.91),

\[
\tau {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} \leq  \left( {2 + {C}_{1}\tau }\right) \left( {\log B + \frac{n}{2}\log \left( {4\pi }\right)  + f + {C}_{2}\tau }\right) ,
\]

so that

(16.96)

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\tau {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}{uhd}{\mu }_{\tau } \leq  \left( {2 + {C}_{1}\tau }\right) {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\log B + f + {C}_{2}\tau }\right) {uhd}{\mu }_{\tau },
\]

where the constant \( B \) changed in the two inequalities above.

The term I is bounded above by the RHS of (16.96), which contains only one ’bad’ term (recall that \( h \) is bounded and \( \int {ud}{\mu }_{\tau } \equiv  1 \) ),

(16.97)

\[
\mathrm{V} \Doteq  {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{fuhd}{\mu }_{\tau }
\]

in the sense that it could possibly blow up (later we shall bound this term). The second term

\[
\mathrm{{II}} = {2\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\langle \nabla u,\nabla h\rangle {d\mu } =  - {2\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{u\Delta hd}{\mu }_{\tau }
\]

is clearly bounded as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) . It is also clear that II \( \rightarrow  0 \) as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) since \( \left| {\Delta h}\right| \) is bounded. The same conclusion holds for III since \( R \) and \( h \) are bounded. Finally, note that

\[
\mathrm{{IV}} = \mathrm{V} - n{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{uhd}{\mu }_{\tau }
\]

Summarizing the above discussion, we have reduced the problem of bounding from above the quantity \( {\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, u,\tau }\right) \) , i.e., the problem of showing (16.89), to bounding the single term \( \mathrm{V} \) from above (as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) ). In the discussion below we shall show that

(16.98)

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\left( {\mathrm{\;V} - \frac{n}{2}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{Hhd}{\mu }_{\tau }}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

To do this, we need to use some facts about the reduced distance function.

Let \( x \) be a fixed point in \( \mathcal{M} \) . Let \( \ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) \) denote the reduced distance based at the point \( \left( {x,0}\right) \) as defined in Chapter 7 of Part I of this volume. We also need the following properties of \( \ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) \) . Let \( \bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \Doteq  {4\tau }\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) \) . The following is essentially Lemma 7.13 on pp.294-295 of Part I of this volume.

LEMMA 16.48 (Bounds for \( \bar{L} \) and \( \ell \) ).

(i) If there exists a constant \( {k}_{1} \) such that \( {R}_{ij}\left( {g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \geq   - {k}_{1}{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) \) , then \( \bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right) \) is a locally Lipschitz function on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

(ii) Suppose there exist constants \( {k}_{1} \) and \( {k}_{2} \) so that

\[
- {k}_{1}{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right)  \leq  {R}_{ij}\left( {g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \leq  {k}_{2}{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) .
\]

Then

(a)

(16.99)

\[
\bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  {e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau }{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right)  + \frac{{4n}{k}_{2}}{3}{\tau }^{2},
\]

or, equivalently,

(16.100)

\[
\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \leq  {e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau }\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau } + \frac{n{k}_{2}}{3}\tau ,
\]

and

(b)

(16.101)

\[
\bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \geq  {e}^{-2{k}_{1}\tau }{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right)  - \frac{{4n}{k}_{1}}{3}{\tau }^{2},
\]

or, equivalently,

(16.102)

\[
\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \geq  {e}^{-2{k}_{1}\tau }\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau } - \frac{n{k}_{1}}{3}\tau .
\]

(iii) Furthermore,

(16.103)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta  + R}\right) \left\lbrack  {{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell }}\right\rbrack   \leq  0
\]

in the weak sense.

Proof. (i) This is equivalent to Lemma 7.30 on p. 308 of Part I of this volume.

(ii) (a) Equation (16.99) follows from Lemma 7.13(iii) on pp. 294-295 of Part I of this volume, where we only need the upper bound for Rc and in Lemma 7.13(iii) \( {C}_{0},\bar{\tau } \) are replaced by \( {k}_{2},\tau \) , respectively. \( {}^{13} \) (b) Equation (16.101) follows from Lemma 7.13(i), where \( {C}_{0} \) is replaced by \( {k}_{1} \) .

(iii) Recall that (7.91) on p. 327 of Part I of this volume says

\[
\frac{\partial \ell }{\partial \tau } - \Delta \ell  + {\left| \nabla \ell \right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau } \geq  0.
\]

Hence

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta  + R}\right) \left( {{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell }}\right)
\]

\[
= {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell }\left( {-\frac{n}{2\tau } - \frac{\partial \ell }{\partial \tau } + \Delta \ell  - {\left| \nabla \ell \right| }^{2} + R}\right)  \leq  0,
\]

which holds in the weak sense (see Lemma 7.129 on pp. 377-378 of Part I of this volume).

---

\( {}^{13} \) Note that from its proof, in Lemma 7.13(iii) of Part I of this volume we may replace \( {d}_{g\left( 0\right) } \) by \( {d}_{g\left( \bar{\tau }\right) } \) in the inequality.

---

We have

(16.104)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) } = {\delta }_{x}\left( y\right)
\]

in the sense of distributions. Indeed, by (16.100) and (16.102), one sees that for any smooth function \( \phi  : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) , we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) }\phi \left( y\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right)  = \phi \left( x\right) .
\]

Here the key to establishing this is that in the upper and lower estimates (16.100) and (16.102) for \( \ell \) , the factors \( {e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau } \) and \( {e}^{-2{k}_{1}\tau } \) both tend to 1 as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) , whereas the terms \( \frac{n{k}_{2}}{3}\tau \) and \( - \frac{n{k}_{1}}{3}\tau \) both tend to 0 as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) .

We can conclude from equation (16.104) together with (16.103) the following. \( {}^{14} \)

LEMMA 16.49. The fundamental solution to the adjoint heat equation \( H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) \) is bounded from below by

(16.105)

\[
{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-f\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) } = H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \geq  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) }.
\]

Here we have included in our notation for \( f \) its dependence on the basepoint \( \left( {x,0}\right) \) . Equivalently,

(16.106)

\[
f\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \leq  \ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) .
\]

Proof. Let \( U\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \Doteq  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) } \) so that (16.105) is equivalent to

(16.107)

\[
F\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \Doteq  H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  - U\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

By (16.80), (16.103), and (16.104) we have

(16.108)

\[
{\square }^{ * }F \geq  0
\]

and

\[
F\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right)  \rightarrow  0\text{ as }\tau  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }
\]

in the sense of distributions. \( {}^{15} \) We claim that this yields the desired estimate (16.107).

Given any \( \bar{\tau } > 0 \) , we shall show that \( F\left( {\cdot ,\bar{\tau }}\right)  \geq  0 \) . Let \( \phi  : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be an arbitrary nonnegative \( {C}^{2} \) function and let \( \Phi  : \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be the solution to the initial-value problem

(16.109)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } + {\Delta }_{g\left( \tau \right) }}\right) \Phi  = 0
\]

\[
\Phi \left( {\cdot ,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = \phi
\]

which always exists. By the weak maximum principle we have \( \Phi  \geq  0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . By (16.108), we have for \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,\bar{\tau }}\right) \)

\[
0 \leq  {\int }_{\varepsilon }^{\bar{\tau }}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\Phi \left( {y,\tau }\right) \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - {\Delta }_{g\left( \tau \right) } + R}\right) F\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\varepsilon }^{\bar{\tau }}\left( {\frac{d}{d\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Phi Fd}{\mu }_{\tau }}\right) {d\tau } - {\int }_{\varepsilon }^{\bar{\tau }}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}F\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } + {\Delta }_{g\left( \tau \right) }}\right) {\Phi d}{\mu }_{\tau }{d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Phi Fd}{\mu }_{\bar{\tau }} - {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Phi Fd}{\mu }_{\varepsilon }
\]

---

\( {}^{14} \) This proof was shown to us by Brett Kotschwar.

\( {}^{15} \) The limit is the difference of two \( \delta \) -functions centered at \( x \) .

---

where we used \( \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }d{\mu }_{\tau } = {Rd}{\mu }_{\tau } \) , integration by parts, and (16.109). Since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Phi Fd}{\mu }_{\varepsilon } = 0 \) and \( \Phi \left( {\cdot ,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = \phi \) , we have

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\phi Fd}{\mu }_{\bar{\tau }} \geq  0
\]

Since \( \phi \) is an arbitrary nonnegative \( {C}^{2} \) function, we conclude that \( F\left( {\cdot ,\bar{\tau }}\right)  \geq \) 0.

REMARK 16.50. Note that, in [402], the estimate (16.106) is proved by integrating the claimed differential Harnack inequality \( {v}_{H} \leq  {0.}^{16} \) In this section we have first proved (16.106) in a different manner and, using this, we shall then prove \( {v}_{H} \leq  0 \) below. Namely, in this book we have reversed part of the logic in the proof of \( {v}_{H} \leq  0 \) and (16.106) given in \( §9 \) of [402].

Now we assemble the results above to prove the claim that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\mathcal{W}}_{h} = 0
\]

As the first step we show that \( {\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right) \) is bounded, i.e.,(16.89), where \( H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \) is the fundamental solution to the adjoint heat equation with \( H\left( {x, y,0}\right)  = {\delta }_{x}\left( y\right) \) . Because of the monotonicity formula (16.86), it suffices to bound \( {\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right) \) from above as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) . Moreover, by the above reduction, we only need to show that \( \mathrm{V} = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{fHhd}{\mu }_{\tau } \) is bounded from above as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) .

By (16.106) we have

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{fHhd}{\mu }_{\tau }
\]

\[
\leq  \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\ell \left( {y,\tau }\right) H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) h\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right)
\]

(16.110)

\[
\leq  \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) h\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right)
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\frac{{e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau } - 1}{4\tau }{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right)  + \frac{{k}_{2}n}{3}\tau }\right) H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) h\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right) .
\]

---

\( {}^{16} \) See also subsection 4.3 below.

---

Here we have used (16.100) in the last inequality. By the asymptotics of the heat kernel parametrix, Theorem 16.46, some elementary computations giver \( {}^{17} \)

(16.111)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) h\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right)  = \frac{n}{2}h\left( {x,0}\right) .
\]

Since \( \frac{{e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau } - 1}{4\tau }{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right)  + \frac{{k}_{2}n}{3}\tau \) is a uniformly bounded continuous function near \( \tau  = 0 \) and since it can be continuously extended to \( \tau  = 0 \) , we have

(16.112)

\[
\text{ (16.112) }\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\frac{{e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau } - 1}{4\tau }{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right)  + \frac{{k}_{2}n}{3}\tau }\right) H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) h\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right)  = 0\text{ , }
\]

where we used \( \frac{{k}_{2}n}{3}\tau  \rightarrow  0 \) and \( \frac{{e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau } - 1}{4\tau }{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right)  \rightarrow  0 \) as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) and \( y \rightarrow  x \) .

This finishes our proof of the finiteness of lim \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{M}{fHhd}{\mu }_{\tau } \) . In fact, by (16.110), (16.111), and (16.112), we have proved (16.98), i.e.,

(16.113)

\[
\text{ (16.113) }\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\left( {\mathrm{\;V} - \frac{n}{2}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{Hhd}{\mu }_{\tau }}\right)  = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {Hhd}{\mu }_{\tau } \leq  0\text{ . }
\]

This completes the proof of (16.89).

By the finiteness of \( {\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right) \) as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) , which we have just proved above, and the (entropy) monotonicity formula (16.86), we know that the limit \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right) \) exists. Let

(16.114)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{v}_{H}{hd}{\mu }_{\tau } \Doteq  \alpha ,
\]

where \( \alpha  < \infty \) . This implies

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\left( {{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right)  - {\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) }\right)  = 0.
\]

By the entropy monotonicity formula (16.86) and the mean value theorem we can find \( {\tau }_{k} \rightarrow  0 \) such that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{\tau }_{k} \rightarrow  0}}{\tau }_{k}^{2}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\left| \operatorname{Rc} + \nabla \nabla f - \frac{1}{2{\tau }_{k}}g\right| }^{2}{Hhd}{\mu }_{{\tau }_{k}} = 0.
\]

---

\( {}^{17} \) The basic idea is that on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}\frac{{\left| x - y\right| }^{2}}{4\tau }{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\frac{{\left| x - y\right| }^{2}}{4\tau }}h\left( {y,\tau }\right) {dy} = \frac{n}{2}h\left( {x,0}\right) .
\]

The heat kernel parametrix enables the analogue of this formula to carry over to manifolds.

---

By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the Hölder inequality we have \( {}^{18} \)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{\tau }_{k} \rightarrow  0}}{\tau }_{k}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {R + {\Delta f} - \frac{n}{2{\tau }_{k}}}\right) {Hhd}{\mu }_{{\tau }_{k}} = 0.
\]

This implies

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{\tau }_{k} \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\tau }_{k}\left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n}\right) {Hhd}{\mu }_{{\tau }_{k}}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{\tau }_{k} \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\tau }_{k}\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {Hhd}{\mu }_{{\tau }_{k}}.
\]

Again, integration by parts shows

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\tau }_{k}\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {Hhd}{\mu }_{{\tau }_{k}} = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\tau }_{k}\langle \nabla H,\nabla h\rangle d{\mu }_{{\tau }_{k}}
\]

\[
=  - {\tau }_{k}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{H\Delta hd}{\mu }_{{\tau }_{k}} \rightarrow  0.
\]

Hence, by (16.113)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\mathcal{W}}_{h}\left( {g, H,\tau }\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{\tau }_{k} \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {Hhd}{\mu }_{{\tau }_{k}} \leq  0.
\]

This proves in (16.114) that we have \( \alpha  \leq  0 \) . The proofs of both (16.87) and Theorem 16.44 are complete.

THEOREM 16.46 (Ricci flow adjoint heat kernel parametrix). Suppose \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow on a closed manifold. Let \( H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) \) (we also denote this by \( H\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \) ) be the fundamental solution to the (backward in t) adjoint heat equation (16.80). Then as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) we have

\[
H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \sim  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{\infty }{\tau }^{j}{u}_{j}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) .
\]

That is, there exist \( \bar{\tau } > 0 \) and a sequence \( {u}_{j} \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( {\mathcal{M} \times  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) such that

\[
H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  - {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}\exp \left( {-\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau }}\right) \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 0}}^{k}{\tau }^{j}{u}_{j}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  = {w}_{k}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) ,
\]

where

\[
{w}_{k}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right)  = O\left( {\tau }^{k + 1 - \frac{n}{2}}\right)
\]

as \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) , uniformly for all \( x, y \in  \mathcal{M} \) . The function \( {u}_{0}\left( {x, y,\tau }\right) \) may be chosen so that \( {u}_{0}\left( {x, x,0}\right)  = 1 \) .

LEMMA 16.47 (Gradient estimates for the adjoint heat equation). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) ,\tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a smooth solution to the backward Ricci flow on a closed manifold. Suppose there exist positive constants \( {k}_{1} \) and \( {k}_{2} \) such that on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
{R}_{ij}\left( {g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \geq   - {k}_{1}{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) \;\text{ and }\;\max \left\{  {R\left( {y,\tau }\right) ,{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}\left( {y,\tau }\right) }\right\}   \leq  {k}_{2}.
\]

(i) (Gradient estimate for uniformly bounded positive solutions) If \( u \leq \; A \) is a positive solution to the adjoint heat equation on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , then there exist constants \( {C}_{1},{C}_{2} < \infty \) depending only on \( {k}_{1},{k}_{2} \) , and \( n \) such that for \( 0 < \tau  \leq  \min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\} \) ,

(16.90)

\[
\tau \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} \leq  \left( {1 + {C}_{1}\tau }\right) \left( {\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + {C}_{2}\tau }\right) .
\]

(ii) (Gradient estimate for positive solutions) If \( u \) is a positive solution to the adjoint heat equation on \( \mathcal{M} \times  (0, T\rbrack \) , then there exists a constant \( B < \infty \) , depending on the solution \( \{ g\left( \tau \right) {\} }_{t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  } \) , such that for

\[
0 < \tau  \leq  \min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  ,
\]

(16.91)

\[
\tau \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} \leq  \left( {2 + {C}_{1}\tau }\right) \left( {\log \left( {\frac{B}{{\tau }^{n/2}u}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud}{\mu }_{\tau }}\right)  + {C}_{2}\tau }\right) .
\]

Here and henceforth we shall use the same notation \( {C}_{i} \) (or \( B \) ) on different lines if the constants differ at most by a multiplicative factor depending only on \( n \) . Note that \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud}{\mu }_{\tau } \) is independent of \( \tau \) and equals 1 if \( u \) is the fundamental solution. The proof of the lemma given below is a modification of some arguments in Hamilton [249]. See Appendix E of this volume for an exposition of some of the estimates in [249].

nodes.proof:
(i) If \( u \) is a solution of \( {\square }^{ * }u = 0 \) , then we compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( {{g}^{ij}{\nabla }_{i}u{\nabla }_{j}u}\right)  =  - 4\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla u,\nabla u}\right)  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla u\right| }^{2} - 2\nabla \left( {Ru}\right)  \cdot  \nabla u,
\]

where we used \( \nabla \left( {{\square }^{ * }u}\right)  \cdot  \nabla u = 0 \) and where the Rc term on the RHS is from both differentiating \( {g}^{ij} \) in time and commuting \( \Delta \) and \( \nabla \) . Hence

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}\right)  = \frac{-4\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla u,\nabla u}\right)  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla u\right| }^{2} - 2\nabla \left( {Ru}\right)  \cdot  \nabla u}{u}
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\nabla u \cdot  \nabla {\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} - \frac{2{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{4}}{{u}^{3}} - \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) u
\]

\[
=  - \frac{4\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla u,\nabla u}\right) }{u} - 2\nabla R \cdot  \nabla u - \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}R
\]

\[
- \frac{2}{u}{\left| \nabla \nabla u - \frac{\nabla u \otimes  \nabla u}{u}\right| }^{2}
\]

Applying the assumed bounds for \( \operatorname{Rc}, R \) , and \( \left| {\nabla R}\right| \) , we obtain

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}\right)  \leq  \left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1}\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + 2\left| {\nabla R}\right| \left| {\nabla u}\right|
\]

(16.92)

\[
\leq  \left( {\left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1} + 1}\right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + {k}_{2}u
\]

where in the last line we used \( 2\left| {\nabla R}\right| \left| {\nabla u}\right|  \leq  \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + u{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2} \) and \( {\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2} \leq  {k}_{2} \) .

We also compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( {u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) u + u\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + 2\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}
\]

\[
= \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + {Ru} - {Ru}\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)
\]

(16.93)

\[
\geq  \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} - n{k}_{1}u - {k}_{2}u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) ,
\]

where we used

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \log u = \frac{\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) u}{u} + \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} =  - R + \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}},
\]

\( {\square }^{ * }u = 0, u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  \geq  0 \) , and the upper and lower bounds for \( R \) .

Consider the quantity

\[
\Phi  \Doteq  \varphi \left( \tau \right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} - {e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  - {C\tau u},
\]

where below we shall choose \( C \) and the function \( \varphi \left( \tau \right) \) of \( \tau  \geq  0 \) . By combining the above two equations (16.92) and (16.93), we obtain

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \Phi  = \frac{d\varphi }{d\tau }\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + \varphi \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}
\]

\[
- {k}_{2}{e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  - {e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \left( {u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
- C\left( {u + \tau \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) u}\right)
\]

(16.94)

\[
\leq  \left( {\frac{d\varphi }{d\tau } + \left( {\left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1} + 1}\right) \varphi  - {e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }}\right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{k}_{2}\varphi  + n{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }}\right) u - C\left( {u - {\tau Ru}}\right) .
\]

Now let \( \varphi \left( \tau \right)  \Doteq  \frac{\tau }{1 + \left( {\left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1} + 1}\right) \tau } \) (note that \( \frac{\tau }{2 + \left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1}} \leq  \varphi \left( \tau \right)  \leq  \tau  \leq  1 \) for \( 0 \leq  \tau  \leq  1) \) . Since in general, for \( c \geq  0 \) ,

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( \frac{\tau }{1 + {c\tau }}\right)  = \frac{1}{{\left( 1 + c\tau \right) }^{2}} \leq  \frac{1}{1 + {c\tau }} = 1 - \frac{c\tau }{1 + {c\tau }},
\]

we have that the function \( \varphi \left( \tau \right) \) satisfies

\[
\frac{d\varphi }{d\tau } + \left( {\left( {4 + n}\right) {k}_{1} + 1}\right) \varphi  - 1 \leq  0.
\]

From this and \( {\tau R} \leq  \frac{1}{2} \) (since \( \left. {\tau  \leq  \frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right) \) , we see that (16.94) implies

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \Phi  \leq  \left( {{k}_{2}\varphi  + n{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }}\right) u - \frac{1}{2}{Cu} \leq  0,
\]

provided we choose \( C \doteq  2\left( {{k}_{2} + n{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{2}}}\right) \) (since \( \tau ,\varphi  \leq  1 \) ). By the maximum principle, since \( \Phi \left( 0\right)  =  - u\left( 0\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u\left( 0\right) }\right)  \leq  0 \) , we have

\[
\Phi \left( {x,\tau }\right)  \leq  0
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( 0 \leq  \tau  \leq  \min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\} \) . That is, on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\} \) ,

\[
\varphi \left( \tau \right) \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} \leq  {e}^{{k}_{2}\tau }u\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + 2\left( {{k}_{2} + n{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{2}}}\right) {\tau u}.
\]

From this one can easily derive (16.90). This completes the proof of part (i) of Lemma 16.47.

(ii) To prove the second part, we first claim that for a positive solution \( u \) to the adjoint heat equation, there exists a constant \( C < \infty \) depending on \( \{ g\left( \tau \right) {\} }_{\tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  } \) such that

(16.95)

\[
u\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{C}{{\tau }^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {z,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( z\right)  = \frac{\text{ const }}{{\tau }^{n/2}}.
\]

Assuming (16.95), we have for \( \widetilde{\tau } \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{\tau }{2},\tau }\right\rbrack \) that

\[
u\left( {y,\widetilde{\tau }}\right)  \leq  \frac{C}{{\left( \tau /2\right) }^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud\mu }
\]

since \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud\mu } \) is constant. Let \( A \Doteq  \frac{C}{{\left( \tau /2\right) }^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud\mu },\widetilde{u}\left( \widetilde{\tau }\right)  \Doteq  u\left( {\widetilde{\tau } + \frac{\tau }{2}}\right) \) , and \( \widetilde{g}\left( \widetilde{\tau }\right)  \Doteq  g\left( {\widetilde{\tau } + \frac{\tau }{2}}\right) \) . Since \( \widetilde{u} \leq  A \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau /2}\right\rbrack \) , we may apply estimate (16.90) using the above quantities to obtain

\[
\frac{\tau }{2}\frac{{\left| \nabla \widetilde{u}\right| }^{2}}{{\widetilde{u}}^{2}}\left( \frac{\tau }{2}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {C}_{1}\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) \left( {\log \left( \frac{A}{\widetilde{u}\left( \frac{\tau }{2}\right) }\right)  + {C}_{2}\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) .
\]

That is,

\[
\frac{\tau }{2}\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}}\left( \tau \right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {C}_{1}\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) \left( {\log \left( \frac{\frac{C}{{\left( \tau /2\right) }^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{ud\mu }}{u\left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {C}_{2}\frac{\tau }{2}}\right) .
\]

Estimate (16.91) now follows.

Now we prove the claim. Inequality (16.95) is a mean value-type inequality, which can be proved via Moser iteration for example; we shall instead follow [249]. Note that in the proof we may assume without loss of generality that

\[
{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  }\right\rbrack  }{\tau }^{n/2}u
\]

is finite; the reason for this is that we shall establish estimate (16.95) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {\varepsilon ,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  \rbrack }\right. \) with \( \tau \) replaced by \( {\tau }_{\varepsilon } \Doteq  \tau  - \varepsilon \) and \( C \) independent of \( \varepsilon \) and then take \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) . For simplicity, below we do not change the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  }\right\rbrack \) and we leave it to the reader to check that this does not affect the argument.

Let \( \left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  }\right\rbrack \) be a space-time point such that

\[
{\tau }_{0}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\min \left\{  {1, T,\frac{1}{2{k}_{2}}}\right\}  }\right\rbrack  }}{\tau }^{n/2}u\left( {y,\tau }\right) .
\]

We then have

\[
\mathop{\max }\limits_{{\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2},{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack  }}u\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  {\left( \frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2}\right) }^{-n/2}{\tau }_{0}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  = {2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \Doteq  A.
\]

With this upper bound, we apply inequality (16.90) to \( u \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2},{\tau }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and conclude \( {}^{12} \)

\[
\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2}\left( \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}}\right) \left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + \frac{{C}_{1}}{2}{\tau }_{0}}\right) \left( {\log \left( \frac{{2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) }{u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) }\right)  + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}{\tau }_{0}}\right)
\]

---

\( {}^{12} \) In (16.90), \( \tau \) is replaced by \( \tau  - \frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2} \) so that \( {\tau }_{0} \) is replaced by \( \frac{{\tau }_{0}}{2} \) .

---

for all \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Let \( U\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \Doteq  \log \left( \frac{{2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) }{u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) }\right)  + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}{\tau }_{0} \) so that \( \nabla U =  - \frac{\nabla u}{u} \) . The above inequality can be rewritten as

\[
\left| {\nabla \sqrt{U}}\right|  \leq  \sqrt{\frac{1 + \frac{1}{2}{C}_{1}{\tau }_{0}}{2{\tau }_{0}}}.
\]

Integrating this along geodesics with respect to \( g\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) \) emanating from \( {y}_{0} \) implies

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{B}_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( {{y}_{0},\sqrt{\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{1 + \frac{1}{2}{C}_{1}{\tau }_{0}}}}\right) }}\sqrt{U}\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \leq  \sqrt{U}\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.
\]

Rewriting the above in terms of \( u \) , we have

\[
u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \geq  {2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) \exp \left\{  {-{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}\log 2 + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) }^{2} + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}}\right\}
\]

\[
\geq  {2}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) {e}^{-\left( {\frac{1}{2} + \frac{n}{2}\log 2 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{\frac{n}{2}\log 2 + \frac{{C}_{2}}{2}}}\right) } \doteq  {c}_{3}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)
\]

for all \( y \in  {B}_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( {{y}_{0},\sqrt{\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{1 + \frac{1}{2}{C}_{1}{\tau }_{0}}}}\right) \) ; here we have also used \( {\tau }_{0} \leq  1 \) .

Notice that

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( {{y}_{0},\sqrt{\frac{{\tau }_{0}}{1 + \frac{1}{2}{C}_{1}{\tau }_{0}}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {c}_{4}{\tau }_{0}^{n/2}
\]

for some \( {c}_{4} > 0 \) depending on the geometry of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g\left( {\tau }_{0}\right) }\right) \) . Therefore we have

\[
\frac{{C}_{5}}{{\tau }_{0}^{n/2}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) d{\mu }_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( y\right)  \geq  u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) ,
\]

where \( {C}_{5} = \frac{1}{{c}_{3}{c}_{4}} \) . By our choice of \( \left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) \) , we have

\[
{\tau }^{n/2}u\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  {\tau }_{0}^{n/2}u\left( {{y}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right)  \leq  {C}_{5}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {y,{\tau }_{0}}\right) d{\mu }_{{\tau }_{0}}\left( y\right)  = {C}_{5}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right) .
\]

This proves (16.95) and hence completes the proof of part (ii) of Lemma 16.47.

LEMMA 16.48 (Bounds for \( \bar{L} \) and \( \ell \) ).

(i) If there exists a constant \( {k}_{1} \) such that \( {R}_{ij}\left( {g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \geq   - {k}_{1}{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) \) , then \( \bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right) \) is a locally Lipschitz function on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

(ii) Suppose there exist constants \( {k}_{1} \) and \( {k}_{2} \) so that

\[
- {k}_{1}{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right)  \leq  {R}_{ij}\left( {g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \leq  {k}_{2}{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) .
\]

Then

(a)

(16.99)

\[
\bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \leq  {e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau }{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right)  + \frac{{4n}{k}_{2}}{3}{\tau }^{2},
\]

or, equivalently,

(16.100)

\[
\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \leq  {e}^{2{k}_{2}\tau }\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau } + \frac{n{k}_{2}}{3}\tau ,
\]

and

(b)

(16.101)

\[
\bar{L}\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \geq  {e}^{-2{k}_{1}\tau }{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right)  - \frac{{4n}{k}_{1}}{3}{\tau }^{2},
\]

or, equivalently,

(16.102)

\[
\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \geq  {e}^{-2{k}_{1}\tau }\frac{{d}_{0}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }{4\tau } - \frac{n{k}_{1}}{3}\tau .
\]

(iii) Furthermore,

(16.103)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta  + R}\right) \left\lbrack  {{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell }}\right\rbrack   \leq  0
\]

in the weak sense.

Let \( U\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \Doteq  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\ell \left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right) } \) so that (16.105) is equivalent to

(16.107)

\[
F\left( {y,\tau }\right)  \Doteq  H\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  - U\left( {y,\tau ;x,0}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

By (16.80), (16.103), and (16.104) we have

(16.108)

\[
{\square }^{ * }F \geq  0
\]

and

\[
F\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right)  \rightarrow  0\text{ as }\tau  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }
\]

in the sense of distributions. \( {}^{15} \) We claim that this yields the desired estimate (16.107).

Given any \( \bar{\tau } > 0 \) , we shall show that \( F\left( {\cdot ,\bar{\tau }}\right)  \geq  0 \) . Let \( \phi  : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be an arbitrary nonnegative \( {C}^{2} \) function and let \( \Phi  : \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be the solution to the initial-value problem

(16.109)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } + {\Delta }_{g\left( \tau \right) }}\right) \Phi  = 0
\]

\[
\Phi \left( {\cdot ,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = \phi
\]

which always exists. By the weak maximum principle we have \( \Phi  \geq  0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . By (16.108), we have for \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,\bar{\tau }}\right) \)

\[
0 \leq  {\int }_{\varepsilon }^{\bar{\tau }}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\Phi \left( {y,\tau }\right) \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - {\Delta }_{g\left( \tau \right) } + R}\right) F\left( {y,\tau }\right) d{\mu }_{\tau }\left( y\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\varepsilon }^{\bar{\tau }}\left( {\frac{d}{d\tau }{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Phi Fd}{\mu }_{\tau }}\right) {d\tau } - {\int }_{\varepsilon }^{\bar{\tau }}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}F\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } + {\Delta }_{g\left( \tau \right) }}\right) {\Phi d}{\mu }_{\tau }{d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Phi Fd}{\mu }_{\bar{\tau }} - {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Phi Fd}{\mu }_{\varepsilon }
\]

---

\( {}^{15} \) The limit is the difference of two \( \delta \) -functions centered at \( x \) .

---

where we used \( \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }d{\mu }_{\tau } = {Rd}{\mu }_{\tau } \) , integration by parts, and (16.109). Since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  0}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Phi Fd}{\mu }_{\varepsilon } = 0 \) and \( \Phi \left( {\cdot ,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = \phi \) , we have

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\phi Fd}{\mu }_{\bar{\tau }} \geq  0
\]

Since \( \phi \) is an arbitrary nonnegative \( {C}^{2} \) function, we conclude that \( F\left( {\cdot ,\bar{\tau }}\right)  \geq \) 0.

nodes.proof:
By scaling, we may assume that \( A = 1 \) . Let \( f = \log u \) and \( w = {\left| \nabla \log \left( 1 - f\right) \right| }^{2} \) . (This was used in [455] for the linear heat equation case in their localization of Hamilton's work [249]. A similar expression was also used by Yau in [507].) Direct calculations give the following equations: \( {}^{19} \)

(16.118)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) f =  - \mathcal{H} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2},
\]

(16.119)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} =  - 2{h}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} - 2{R}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} - 2{f}_{ij}^{2} + \left\langle  {\nabla \left( {-\mathcal{H} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) ,\nabla f}\right\rangle  ,
\]

and

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) w = \frac{1}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{2}}\left( {-2{h}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} - 2{R}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} + 2{\mathcal{H}}_{i}{f}_{i}}\right)  - 2\mathcal{H}\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{3}}
\]

\[
+ 2\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{4}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{3}} - 4\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{4}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{4}} + 4\frac{{f}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{2}} - 4\frac{{f}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{3}}
\]

\[
- 2\frac{1}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{2}}\left( {{f}_{ij}^{2} + 2\frac{{f}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j}}{\left( 1 - f\right) } + \frac{{f}_{i}^{2}{f}_{j}^{2}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{2}}}\right) ,
\]

where we have computed with respect to a local orthonormal frame and \( {\mathcal{H}}_{i} \Doteq  {\nabla }_{i}\mathcal{H} \) . Rewriting \( {f}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} \) in terms of \( {w}_{i}{f}_{i} \) in the above equation, we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) w = \frac{1}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{2}}\left( {-2{h}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} - 2{R}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} + 2{\mathcal{H}}_{i}{f}_{i}}\right)  - 2\mathcal{H}\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{3}}
\]

\[
- 2\frac{1}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{2}}\left( {{f}_{ij}^{2} + 2\frac{{f}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j}}{\left( 1 - f\right) } + \frac{{f}_{i}^{2}{f}_{j}^{2}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{2}}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2\frac{-f}{1 - f}\langle \nabla w,\nabla f\rangle  - 2\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{4}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{3}}.
\]

---

\( {}^{19} \) We use the notation \( {f}_{i} = {\nabla }_{i}f \) and \( {f}_{ij} = {\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }_{i}f \) .

---

Now let \( \eta \left( s\right) \) be a cutoff function such that \( \eta  = 1 \) when \( s \leq  1 \) and \( \eta  = 0 \) when \( s \geq  2 \) with \( {\eta }^{\prime } \leq  0,\frac{{\left| {\eta }^{\prime }\right| }^{2}}{\eta } \leq  {C}_{2} \) , and \( {\eta }^{\prime \prime } \geq   - {C}_{2} \) . Let \( \varphi  = \eta \left( \frac{{d}_{\tau }\left( {O, x}\right) }{R}\right) \) . We then have

\[
\frac{{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2}}{\varphi } \leq  \frac{{C}_{2}}{{R}^{2}}
\]

\[
\frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial \tau } \leq  {C}_{2}{k}_{1}
\]

and

\[
- {\Delta \varphi } \leq  \frac{1}{{R}^{2}}\left( {{C}_{1}\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R\coth \left( {\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R}\right)  + {C}_{2}}\right) .
\]

Now we let \( G = {w\varphi } \) and compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) {\tau G} = G + {\tau \varphi }\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) w + {\tau w}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) \varphi  - {2\tau }\langle \nabla w,\nabla \varphi \rangle .
\]

At a maximum point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) \) of \( {\tau G} \) we have

\[
0 \leq  \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \Delta }\right) {\tau G} \leq  G + {\tau \varphi }\left( {\frac{1}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{2}}\left( {-2{h}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} - 2{R}_{ij}{f}_{i}{f}_{j} + 2{\mathcal{H}}_{i}{f}_{i}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ {\tau \varphi }\left( {-2\mathcal{H}\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{3}} + 2\frac{-f}{1 - f}\langle \nabla w,\nabla f\rangle  - 2\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{4}}{{\left( 1 - f\right) }^{3}}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\tau w}\left( {{C}_{2}{k}_{1} + \frac{1}{{R}^{2}}\left( {{C}_{1}\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R\coth \left( {\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R}\right)  + {C}_{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
- {2\tau }\langle \nabla w,\nabla \varphi \rangle
\]

Using the equation \( \nabla G = 0 \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{\tau }_{0}}\right) \) , we can replace \( \varphi \nabla w \) in the above inequality by \( - w\nabla \varphi \) . Also, multiplying \( \varphi \) on the both sides of the above inequality, we have

\[
0 \leq  G + \tau \left( {2{k}_{1}\left( {1 + n}\right) G + 2{k}_{2}G + 2{k}_{3}^{\frac{3}{2}}{G}^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {2\tau G}\left| {\nabla \varphi }\right| \left| {\nabla f}\right| \frac{-f}{1 - f} - {2\tau }\left( {1 - f}\right) {G}^{2}
\]

\[
+ {\tau G}\left( {{C}_{2}{k}_{1} + \frac{1}{{R}^{2}}\left( {{C}_{1}\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R\coth \left( {\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R}\right)  + {C}_{2}}\right) }\right) .
\]

Here we have used that \( 0 \leq  \varphi  \leq  1 \) and \( \frac{1}{1 - f} \leq  1 \) . Noticing

\[
2{k}_{3}^{\frac{3}{2}}{G}^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq  {k}_{3}G + {k}_{3}^{2}
\]

and

\[
{2\tau G}\left| {\nabla \varphi }\right| \left| {\nabla f}\right| \frac{-f}{1 - f} \leq  {\tau G}\left( {\frac{{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}{1 - f}\varphi  + \frac{{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2}}{\varphi }\frac{{f}^{2}}{1 - f}}\right)
\]

\[
= \tau \left( {1 - f}\right) {G}^{2} + {\tau G}\frac{{C}_{2}}{{R}^{2}}\frac{{f}^{2}}{1 - f},
\]

we have that at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) ,

\[
0 \leq  \tau {k}_{3}^{2} + G\left( {1 + \tau \left( {{C}_{2}{k}_{1} + 2{k}_{2} + {k}_{3} + \frac{1}{{R}^{2}}\left( {{C}_{1}\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R\coth \left( {\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R}\right)  + {C}_{2}}\right) }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ {\tau G}\frac{{C}_{2}}{{R}^{2}}\frac{{f}^{2}}{1 - f} - \tau \left( {1 - f}\right) {G}^{2}.
\]

Dividing \( \tau \left( {1 - f}\right) \) on both sides, noticing that \( \frac{1}{1 - f} \leq  1 \) and \( \frac{-f}{1 - f} \leq  1 \) , we have

\[
0 \leq  {k}_{3}^{2} + G\left( {\frac{1}{\tau } + \left( {{C}_{2}{k}_{1} + 2{k}_{2} + {k}_{3} + \frac{1}{{R}^{2}}\left( {{C}_{1}\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R\coth \left( {\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R}\right)  + {C}_{2}}\right) }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
- {G}^{2}
\]

from which we can conclude

\[
G \leq  \frac{1}{\tau } + \left( {{C}_{2}{k}_{1} + 2{k}_{2} + {k}_{3} + \frac{1}{{R}^{2}}\left( {{C}_{1}\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R\coth \left( {\sqrt{{k}_{2}}R}\right)  + {C}_{2}}\right) }\right)  + {k}_{3}.
\]

This completes the proof.

For the case of the Ricci flow, when \( u \) is globally defined and \( g\left( \tau \right) \) has nonnegative Ricci curvature, we have the following clean form.

1.3. Evolution of the Riemann curvature tensor. With respect to Uhlenbeck's trick, the evolution of the Riemann curvature tensor is given by

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{abcd} = \Delta {R}_{abcd} + 2\left( {{B}_{abcd} - {B}_{abdc} + {B}_{acbd} - {B}_{adbc}}\right) ,
\]

where \( {B}_{abcd} =  - {R}_{aebf}{R}_{cedf} \) (see Section 2 of Chapter 6 of Volume One). The evolution of the Ricci tensor is

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ab} = \Delta {R}_{ab} + 2{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd}.
\]

---

\( {}^{1} \) See [48] for these references.

---

The facts in this paragraph are derived on pp. 185-186 of Volume One. Consider the Lie algebra \( \mathfrak{g} \doteq  \left( {{\Lambda }^{2}{T}_{x}^{ * }{\mathcal{M}}^{n},\left\lbrack  {\cdot , \cdot  }\right\rbrack  }\right) \) , where the bracket is defined by

(D.1)

\[
{\left\lbrack  U, V\right\rbrack  }_{ij} \Doteq  {g}^{k\ell }\left( {{U}_{ik}{V}_{\ell j} - {V}_{ik}{U}_{\ell j}}\right) ,
\]

which is isomorphic to \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) . Given local coordinates \( \left\{  {x}^{i}\right\} \) , define the basis \( \left\{  {{\varphi }^{\left( ij\right) } : 1 \leq  i < j \leq  n}\right\} \) for \( \mathfrak{g} \) by

\[
{\varphi }^{\left( ij\right) } \Doteq  d{x}^{i} \land  d{x}^{j}.
\]

The structure constants \( {C}_{\left( ij\right) }^{\left( {pq}\right) ,\left( {rs}\right) } \) of \( \mathfrak{g} \) are defined by

(D.2)

\[
\left\lbrack  {d{x}^{p} \land  d{x}^{q}, d{x}^{r} \land  d{x}^{s}}\right\rbrack   = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{\left( ij\right) }{C}_{\left( ij\right) }^{\left( {pq}\right) ,\left( {rs}\right) }d{x}^{i} \land  d{x}^{j}.
\]

We have

\[
{C}_{\left( ij\right) }^{\left( {pq}\right) ,\left( {rs}\right) } = {\left\lbrack  d{x}^{p} \land  d{x}^{q}, d{x}^{r} \land  d{x}^{s}\right\rbrack  }_{ij}
\]

(D.3)

\[
= \frac{1}{4}\left\{  \begin{array}{l} {g}^{qr}\left( {{\delta }_{i}^{p}{\delta }_{j}^{s} - {\delta }_{i}^{s}{\delta }_{j}^{p}}\right)  + {g}^{qs}\left( {{\delta }_{i}^{r}{\delta }_{j}^{p} - {\delta }_{i}^{p}{\delta }_{j}^{r}}\right) \\   + {g}^{pr}\left( {{\delta }_{i}^{s}{\delta }_{j}^{q} - {\delta }_{i}^{q}{\delta }_{j}^{s}}\right)  + {g}^{ps}\left( {{\delta }_{i}^{q}{\delta }_{j}^{r} - {\delta }_{i}^{r}{\delta }_{j}^{q}}\right)  \end{array}\right\}  .
\]

The components of \( {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{\# } \) are given by

(D.4)

\[
{\left( {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{\# }\right) }_{{ijk}\ell } = {R}_{pquv}{R}_{rswx}{C}_{\left( ij\right) }^{\left( {pq}\right) ,\left( {rs}\right) }{C}_{\left( \ell k\right) }^{\left( {uv}\right) ,\left( {wx}\right) }
\]

(D.5)

\[
= 2\left( {{B}_{{ikj}\ell } - {B}_{i\ell {jk}}}\right) .
\]

Using the first Bianchi identity, we have

\[
{\left( {\mathrm{{Rm}}}^{2}\right) }_{{ijk}\ell } = 2\left( {{B}_{{ijk}\ell } - {B}_{{ij}\ell k}}\right) .
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{Rm} = \Delta \operatorname{Rm} + {\operatorname{Rm}}^{2} + {\operatorname{Rm}}^{\# }.
\]

nodes.content:
We now describe a set of initial data that will pinch in finite time. We call local minima of \( f \) necks and local maxima bumps. We call the region between either pole and its closest bump a polar cap. Consider the following assumptions.

(1) The metric has at least one neck that is 'sufficiently pinched'. To wit, the value of \( f \) at the smallest neck is sufficiently small relative to its value at either adjacent bump.

(2) The scalar curvature \( R = 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {K}_{\text{ rad }} + \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {K}_{\text{ sph }} \) is positive everywhere.

(3) The sectional curvature \( {K}_{\text{ sph }} \) tangential to each sphere \( \{ r\}  \times  {\mathcal{S}}^{n - 1} \) is positive.

(4) The Ricci curvature is positive on each polar cap.

THEOREM D.11 (Existence of rotationally symmetric neckpinch). Assumptions (1)-(4) above define an open set of initial data \( {g}_{0} \) in the space of rotationally symmetric metrics on \( {\mathcal{S}}^{n} \) such that for each metric \( {g}_{0} \) in this open set, there exists a unique rotationally symmetric solution \( g\left( t\right) \) of Ricci flow on \( {\mathcal{S}}^{n} \) with \( g\left( 0\right)  = {g}_{0} \) . This solution forms a Type I singularity at a finite time \( T = T\left( {g}_{0}\right) \) . Let \( \bar{s}\left( t\right) \) denote the location of the smallest neck at time \( t \) . Then there exist \( C < \infty \) and \( \delta  > 0 \) such that the following estimates hold for the cylindrical radius function \( f \) .

(1) (Interior cylinder estimate) In the innermost region

(D.9)

\[
\left| {s - \bar{s}}\right|  \leq  2\sqrt{\left( {T - t}\right) \log \left( \frac{1}{T - t}\right) },
\]

we have

(D.10)

\[
1 + o\left( 1\right)  \leq  \frac{f\left( {r, t}\right) }{\sqrt{2\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {T - t}\right) }} \leq  1 + C\frac{{\left( s\left( r, t\right)  - \bar{s}\left( t\right) \right) }^{2}}{\left( {T - t}\right) \log \left( \frac{1}{T - t}\right) }
\]

uniformly as \( t \nearrow  T \) .

In particular, for \( s - \bar{s} = o\left( \sqrt{\left( {T - t}\right) \log \left( \frac{1}{T - t}\right) }\right) \) , we have

(D.11)

\[
\frac{f\left( {r, t}\right) }{\sqrt{2\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {T - t}\right) }} = 1 + o\left( 1\right) \;\text{ as }t \nearrow  T.
\]

(2) (Intermediate cylinder estimate) In the intermediate annular regions

(D.12)

\[
2\sqrt{\left( {T - t}\right) \log \left( \frac{1}{T - t}\right) } \leq  \left| {s - \bar{s}}\right|  \leq  {\left( T - t\right) }^{\frac{1 - \delta }{2}},
\]

we have

(D.13)

\[
\frac{f\left( {r, t}\right) }{\sqrt{T - t}} \leq  C\frac{s\left( {r, t}\right)  - \bar{s}\left( t\right) }{\sqrt{\left( {T - t}\right) \log \left( \frac{1}{T - t}\right) }}\sqrt{\log \left( \frac{s\left( {r, t}\right)  - \bar{s}\left( t\right) }{\sqrt{\left( {T - t}\right) \log \left( \frac{1}{T - t}\right) }}\right) }.
\]

THEOREM D. 12 (Asymptotics of rotationally symmetric neckpinch). Under assumptions (1)-(5), the singularity time \( T \) is a continuous function of the initial datum \( {g}_{0} \) . The diameter remains bounded for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , and the singularity occurs only on the hypersurface \( \{ 0\}  \times  {S}^{n - 1} \) . As the singularity develops, the solution exhibits the following asymptotic profile.

Inner region: on any interval \( \left| \sigma \right|  \leq  A \) , one has

(D.14)

\[
u\left( {\sigma ,\tau }\right)  = 1 + \frac{{\sigma }^{2} - 2}{8\tau } + o\left( \frac{1}{\tau }\right) \;\text{ uniformly as }\tau  \rightarrow  \infty .
\]

Intermediate region: on any interval \( A \leq  \left| \sigma \right|  \leq  B\sqrt{\tau } \) , one has

(D.15)

\[
u\left( {\sigma ,\tau }\right)  = \sqrt{1 + \left( {1 + o\left( 1\right) }\right) \frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{4\tau }}\;\text{ uniformly as }\tau  \rightarrow  \infty .
\]

Outer region: for any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exist \( C > 1 \) and \( \bar{t} < T \) such that(D.16)

\[
\left( {\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{n - 2} - \varepsilon }\right) \frac{s}{\sqrt{\log \left( {1/s}\right) }} \leq  f\left( {r, t}\right)  \leq  \left( {\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{n - 2} + \varepsilon }\right) \frac{s}{\sqrt{\log \left( {1/s}\right) }}
\]

for all points near the neck such that \( \left| \sigma \right|  \geq  C\sqrt{\tau } \) and \( t \in  \left( {\bar{t}, T}\right) \) .

nodes.content:
PROPOSITION D. 16 (Estimates for neckpinches). Let \( g\left( t\right) \) be a solution to Ricci flow of the form (D.6). If \( g\left( 0\right)  = {g}_{0} \) satisfies assumptions (1)-(4), then the following hold for as long as the solution exists.

---

\( {}^{2} \) See Hamilton [255] or Part III of this volume for the definition of \( {}^{\varepsilon }\varepsilon \) -neck’.

---

(1) The gradient bound

(D.17)

\[
\left| {f}^{\prime }\right|  \leq  1
\]

is preserved.

(2) The scale-invariant difference of the sectional curvatures

\[
a = {f}^{2}\left( {{K}_{\text{ sph }} - {K}_{\text{ rad }}}\right)
\]

is uniformly bounded:

(D.18)

\[
\sup \left| {a\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right|  \leq  A \Doteq  \sup \left| {a\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\right| .
\]

(3) The full curvature is controlled by the radius of the \( {\mathcal{S}}^{n - 1} \) factor; that is, there exists \( C = C\left( {n,{g}_{0}}\right) \) such that

(D.19)

\[
\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right|  \leq  \frac{C}{{f}^{2}}.
\]

(4) The radius \( f \) is strictly decreasing pointwise, and \( {f}^{2} \) is uniformly Lipschitz in time, satisfying

(D.20)

\[
\left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {f}^{2}\right) }\right|  \leq  2\left( {A + n - 1}\right) .
\]

(5) The radius \( {f}_{\min }\left( t\right) \) of the smallest neck satisfies

(D.21)

\[
\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {T - t}\right)  \leq  {f}_{\min }{\left( t\right) }^{2} \leq  2\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {T - t}\right) .
\]

(6) The singularity is of Type I. That is, there exists \( C = C\left( {n,{g}_{0}}\right) \) such that

(D.22)

\[
\left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  \frac{C}{T - t}
\]

(7) The solution has the Sturmian property. That is, the number of zeroes of \( {f}^{\prime } \) is finite and nonincreasing in time. If \( f \) ever has a degenerate critical point, i.e., a point such that \( {f}^{\prime } = {f}^{\prime \prime } = 0 \) , then the number of zeroes of \( {f}^{\prime } \) decreases.

(8) The solution remains concave on the polar caps, i.e., \( {K}_{\text{ rad }} > 0 \) there. If \( \widehat{r}\left( t\right) \) denotes the location of the right-most (left-most) bump, then the limit \( D = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \nearrow  T}}f\left( {\widehat{r}\left( t\right) , t}\right) \) exists. Also, if \( D > 0 \) , then no singularity occurs on the polar cap.

(9) Let \( c = 2 - \log \left( {\inf \left( {{K}_{\mathrm{{sph}}}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\right) }\right) \) . The quantity

(D.23)

\[
\widehat{F} =  - \frac{{K}_{\text{ rad }}}{{K}_{\text{ sph }}}\log \left( {{K}_{\text{ sph }} + c}\right)
\]

is bounded from above by \( \max \{ n - 2,\sup \widehat{F}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) \} \) .

\]

\]

\]

for any vector field \( V \) and \( t > 0 \) . In particular, taking \( V = 0 \) , one obtains

(D.29)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {tR}\right)  = t\left( {\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} + \frac{R}{t}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Hence, for any \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( 0 < {t}_{1} \leq  {t}_{2} \) , we have

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{2}}\right)  \geq  \frac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{2}}R\left( {x,{t}_{1}}\right) .
\]

THEOREM D. 28 (Linear trace Harnack estimate). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) , h\left( t\right) }\right) \) , \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution to the linearized Ricci flow system

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{R}_{ij}
\]

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{h}_{ij} = {\left( {\Delta }_{L}h\right) }_{ij} \Doteq  \Delta {h}_{ij} + 2{R}_{{kij}\ell }{h}_{k\ell } - {R}_{ik}{h}_{kj} - {R}_{jk}{h}_{ki}
\]

(D.31)

\[

\]

(D.32)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{T}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{e}^{-B{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }^{2}\left( {x, O}\right) }{\left| h\left( x, t\right) \right| }^{2}d{\mu }_{g\left( t\right) }{dt} < \infty
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , where \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Then \( h\left( t\right)  \geq  0 \) for \( t \in  \lbrack 0, t) \) and for any vector \( V \) we have

(D.33)

\[
\text{ (D.33) }\;Z \Doteq  \operatorname{div}\left( {\operatorname{div}\left( h\right) }\right)  + \langle \mathrm{{Rc}}, h\rangle  + 2\langle \operatorname{div}\left( h\right) , V\rangle  + h\left( {V, V}\right)  + \frac{H}{2t} \geq  0\text{ , }
\]

where \( H = {g}^{ij}{h}_{ij} \) .

LEMMA D. 42 (Behavior of \( \mu \left( {g,\tau }\right) \) for \( \tau \) small). Suppose \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is a closed Riemannian manifold.

(i) There exists \( \bar{\tau } > 0 \) such that

\[
\mu \left( {g,\tau }\right)  < 0\;\text{ for all }\tau  \in  \left( {0,\bar{\tau }}\right) .
\]

(ii)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}\mu \left( {g,\tau }\right)  = 0.
\]

LEMMA D. 43 ( \( \nu \) -invariant monotonicity). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on a closed manifold.

(1) The invariant \( \nu \left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is nondecreasing on \( \lbrack 0, T) \) , as long as \( \nu \left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is well defined and finite.

(2) Furthermore, if \( \lambda \left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  > 0 \) and if \( \nu \left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is not strictly increasing on some interval, then \( g\left( t\right) \) is a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton.

(3) If \( \nu \left( {g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right)  =  - \infty \) for some \( {t}_{0} \) , then \( \nu \left( {g\left( t\right) }\right)  =  - \infty \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) .

Proposition D. 44 \( \left( \mu \right. \) controls volume ratios). Let \( \rho  \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) . There exists a constant \( {C}_{2} = {C}_{2}\left( {n,\rho }\right)  < \infty \) such that if \( \left( {{\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}^{n},\widehat{g}}\right) \) is a closed Riemannian manifold, \( p \in  \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \) and \( r \in  (0,\rho \rbrack \) are such that \( \operatorname{Rc} \geq   - {c}_{1}\left( n\right) {r}^{-2} \) and \( R \leq  {c}_{1}\left( n\right) {r}^{-2} \) in \( B\left( {p, r}\right) \) , then

(D.55)

\[
\mu \left( {\widehat{g},{r}^{2}}\right)  \leq  \log \frac{\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {p, r}\right) }{{r}^{n}} + {C}_{2}\left( {n,\rho }\right) .
\]

That is,

\[
\frac{\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {p, r}\right) }{{r}^{n}} \geq  {e}^{-{C}_{2}\left( {n,\rho }\right) }{e}^{\mu \left( {\widehat{g},{r}^{2}}\right) }.
\]

\[
\mu \left( {\widehat{g},{r}^{2}}\right)  \leq  \log \kappa  + {C}_{2}\left( {n,\rho }\right) .
\]
