COROLLARY D. 47 (Obtaining singularity models). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in \; \lbrack 0, T), T < \infty \) , be a singular solution to the Ricci flow on a closed manifold. If \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right) \right\} \) is a sequence of points and times with \( {t}_{i} \rightarrow  T \) and if for some \( C < \infty \) and \( \beta  > 0 \)

(D.57)

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{\mathcal{M}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{i} - \beta {K}_{i}^{-1},{t}_{i}}\right\rbrack  }}\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right|  \leq  C{K}_{i}
\]

where \( {K}_{i} \Doteq  \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  \infty \) , then there exists a subsequence such that the dilated solutions \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n},{g}_{i}\left( t\right) ,{x}_{i}}\right) \) , where

\[
{g}_{i}\left( t\right)  \Doteq  {K}_{i}g\left( {{t}_{i} + {K}_{i}^{-1}t}\right) ,
\]

converge to a complete limit solution \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{n},{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) of the Ricci flow defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-\beta ,0}\right\rbrack \) on a possibly noncompact and topologically distinct manifold \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{n} \) with \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}}_{\infty }\right|  \leq  C \) . Moreover, there exists \( \kappa  > 0 \) , independent of \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{i},{t}_{i}}\right) \right\} \) , such that \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{n},{g}_{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales.

Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on a closed manifold with \( T < \infty \) . The Euclidean Green’s function on \( {\mathbb{E}}^{n} \) , where \( n \geq  3 \) , is defined by

(E.1)

\[
\Gamma \left( {x, y}\right)  \Doteq  \frac{1}{\left( {n - 2}\right) n{\omega }_{n}}{\left| x - y\right| }^{2 - n}.
\]

Here \( {\omega }_{n} \) denotes the volume of the unit \( n \) -ball \( {B}^{n} \) , so that \( n{\omega }_{n} \) is the area of the unit \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -sphere \( {\mathcal{S}}^{n - 1} \) . When \( n = 2 \) , we define \( \Gamma \left( {x, y}\right)  \Doteq \; - \frac{1}{2\pi }\log \left| {x - y}\right| \) . Henceforth we consider the case \( n \geq  3 \) and leave the remaining case of \( n = 2 \) to the reader.

LEMMA E.1. \[

\]

nodes.proof:
We may assume that \( \frac{3}{2}d\left( {x, y}\right)  < \iota \) , since otherwise \( \Phi \left( {x, y}\right) \) is bounded by a constant. Let \( d \Doteq  d\left( {x, y}\right) /2 \) . In order to avoid singularities in one of the functions, we split \( \Phi \left( {x, y}\right) \) into

(E.12)

\[
\Phi \left( {x, y}\right)  = {\int }_{B\left( {x, d}\right) }\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) \Theta \left( {z, y}\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{B\left( {y,{3d}}\right)  \smallsetminus  B\left( {x, d}\right) }\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) \Theta \left( {z, y}\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{\mathcal{M} \smallsetminus  B\left( {y,{3d}}\right) }\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) \Theta \left( {z, y}\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right) .
\]

There is no singularity for \( \Theta \) in the first integral in (E.12), so

\[
\left| {{\int }_{B\left( {x, d}\right) }\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) \Theta \left( {z, y}\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right) }\right|  \leq  {\int }_{B\left( {x, d}\right) }\left| {\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) \Theta \left( {z, y}\right) }\right| {d\mu }\left( z\right)
\]

\[
\leq  C{d}^{b - n}{\int }_{B\left( {x, d}\right) }\left| {\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) }\right| {d\mu }\left( z\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {C}^{2}{d}^{b - n}{\int }_{B\left( {x, d}\right) }d{\left( x, z\right) }^{a - n}{d\mu }\left( z\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {C}^{\prime }{d}^{a + b - n}.
\]

The second integral in (E.12) has no singularity in \( \Psi \) , so

\[
\left| {{\int }_{B\left( {y,{3d}}\right)  \smallsetminus  B\left( {x, d}\right) }\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) \Theta \left( {z, y}\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  C{d}^{a - n}{\int }_{B\left( {y,{3d}}\right) }\left| {\Theta \left( {z, y}\right) }\right| {d\mu }\left( z\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {C}^{2}{d}^{a - n}{\int }_{B\left( {y,{3d}}\right) }d{\left( y, z\right) }^{b - n}{d\mu }\left( z\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {C}^{\prime }{d}^{a + b - n}\text{ . }
\]

Finally, we compute the third integral in (E.12):

\[
\left| {{\int }_{\mathcal{M} \smallsetminus  B\left( {y,{3d}}\right) }\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) \Theta \left( {z, y}\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{1} + {C}^{2}\left| {{\int }_{B\left( {y,\iota }\right)  \smallsetminus  B\left( {y,{3d}}\right) }d{\left( x, z\right) }^{a - n}d{\left( z, y\right) }^{b - n}{d\mu }\left( z\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{1} + {C}^{2}\left| {{\int }_{B\left( {y,\iota }\right)  \smallsetminus  B\left( {y,{3d}}\right) }{\left( d\left( y, z\right)  - 2d\right) }^{a - n}d{\left( y, z\right) }^{b - n}{d\mu }\left( z\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{2}\left( {1 + \left| {{\int }_{{S}^{n - 1}}{\int }_{3d}^{\iota }{\left( \frac{1}{3}r\right) }^{a - n}{r}^{b - 1}{drd\sigma }}\right| }\right)
\]

since \( d\left( {y, z}\right)  \leq  d\left( {x, z}\right)  + {2d} \) and \( \frac{2}{3}r \geq  {2d} \) on the domain. Hence

\[
\left| {{\int }_{\mathcal{M} \smallsetminus  B\left( {y,{3d}}\right) }\Psi \left( {x, z}\right) \Theta \left( {z, y}\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right) }\right|  \leq  \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} {C}^{\prime }\left( {1 + {d}^{a + b - n}}\right) & \text{ if }a + b \neq  n, \\  {C}^{\prime }\left( {1 + \left| {\log d}\right| }\right) & \text{ if }a + b = n. \end{array}\right.
\]

If \( u : \Omega  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a function with \( u \in  {C}^{2}\left( {\operatorname{int}\left( \Omega \right) }\right) \) satisfying

\[
{\Delta u} + \langle X,\nabla u\rangle  \geq  0,
\]

where \( X \) is a bounded vector field, \( {x}_{0} \in  \partial \Omega \) is a point where

\[
u\left( x\right)  < u\left( {x}_{0}\right) \;\text{ for all }x \in  \Omega ,
\]

\( u \) is continuous at \( {x}_{0} \) , and \( \Omega \) satisfies the interior sphere condition at \( {x}_{0} \) , then

\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu }\left( {x}_{0}\right)  > 0
\]

if this unit outward normal derivative exists.

nodes.content:
DEFINITION E. 7 (Fundamental solution to heat equation). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a complete Riemannian manifold. We say a function \( h : \mathcal{M} \times  \mathcal{M} \times \; \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a fundamental solution to the heat equation if

(1) (regularity) \( h \) is continuous, \( {C}^{2} \) in the first variable, and \( {C}^{1} \) in the third variable,

(2) (solution to the heat equation)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{x}}\right) h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = 0,
\]

(3) (tends to the delta function)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}h\left( {\cdot , y, t}\right)  = {\delta }_{y}
\]

for any \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) , i.e., for any continuous function \( f \) on \( \mathcal{M} \) with compact support we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) f\left( x\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = f\left( y\right) .
\]

As we shall see below, there exists a \( {C}^{\infty } \) fundamental solution \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) which is symmetric in \( x \) and \( y \) , and, in the case where \( \mathcal{M} \) is closed, which is unique and positive. When \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) is complete and noncompact, the minimal positive fundamental solution (i.e., heat kernel) is unique and symmetric in \( x \) and \( y \) ; see subsection 2.2 below.

First note that if \( u \) is a solution of the heat equation on a closed manifold, then

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)
\]

(E.14)

\[
= {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Delta u}\left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = 0.
\]

We also have that if \( u > 0 \) , then

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {x, t}\right) \log u\left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {{\Delta u} \cdot  \log u + {\Delta u}}\right) \left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)
\]

(E.15)

\[
=  - {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u}\left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  \leq  0.
\]

In particular, for the fundamental solution \( h \) we have

(E.16)

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  \equiv  1
\]

for all \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) (since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = 1 \) ).

LEMMA E. 8 (Duhamel’s principle, I). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold. If \( A \) and \( B \) are functions on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0, t}\right) \) which are both \( {C}^{2} \) in space and \( {C}^{1} \) in time, then for any \( 0 < {t}_{1} < {t}_{2} < t \) we have(E.17)

\[

\]

\[
= {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}A\left( {w, t - {t}_{2}}\right) B\left( {w,{t}_{2}}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)  - {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}A\left( {w, t - {t}_{1}}\right) B\left( {w,{t}_{1}}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right) ,
\]

and(E.18)

\[
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {-\left( {\square A}\right) \left( {w, t - s}\right) B\left( {w, s}\right)  + A\left( {w, t - s}\right) \left( {\square B}\right) \left( {w, s}\right) }\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {A\left( {w, t - {t}_{2}}\right) B\left( {w,{t}_{2}}\right)  - A\left( {w, t - {t}_{1}}\right) B\left( {w,{t}_{1}}\right) }\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right) .
\]

THEOREM E. 9 (Uniqueness and symmetry of fundamental solution). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold. The fundamental solution \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) to the heat equation is unique and symmetric, i.e., \( h\left( {y, x, t}\right)  = \; h\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) .

---

\( {}^{1} \) This statement applies to (E.18); equation (E.17) follows simply from the fundamental theorem of calculus.

\( {}^{2} \) We used \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\left( {\Delta A}\right) B - A\left( {\Delta B}\right) }\right) {d\mu } = 0 \) to obtain the first equality.

\( {}^{3} \) Compare with the symmetry of the Green’s function: \( G\left( {y, x}\right)  = G\left( {x, y}\right) \) .

---

Proof. Suppose that \( {h}_{1}\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) and \( {h}_{2}\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) are fundamental solutions of the heat equation. Taking \( {t}_{1} \rightarrow  {0}_{ + },{t}_{2} \rightarrow  {t}_{ - }, A\left( {w,\tau }\right)  = {h}_{1}\left( {w, x,\tau }\right) \) , and \( B\left( {w, s}\right)  = {h}_{2}\left( {w, y, s}\right) \) in (E.18), we have

\[
0 = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{t}_{2} \rightarrow  {t}_{ - }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h}_{1}\left( {w, x, t - {t}_{2}}\right) {h}_{2}\left( {w, y,{t}_{2}}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{t}_{1} \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h}_{1}\left( {w, x, t - {t}_{1}}\right) {h}_{2}\left( {w, y,{t}_{1}}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
= {h}_{2}\left( {x, y, t}\right)  - {h}_{1}\left( {y, x, t}\right) .
\]

In particular, if \( h \) is a fundamental solution, then by taking \( {h}_{1} = {h}_{2} = h \) we have

\[
h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = h\left( {y, x, t}\right) .
\]

Thus, for any fundamental solutions \( {h}_{1} \) and \( {h}_{2} \) ,

\[
{h}_{1}\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = {h}_{2}\left( {x, y, t}\right) .
\]

THEOREM E.10 (Representation for solution to IVP). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold. If \( f : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a continuous function and \( F : \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a bounded continuous function, then the solution \( u : \mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) to the initial-value problem

(E.19a)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) u = F\;\text{ on }\mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right) ,
\]

(E.19b)

\[
u\left( {\cdot ,0}\right)  = f\left( \cdot \right) \;\text{ on }\mathcal{M},
\]

if it exists, is given by

(E.20)

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) f\left( y\right) {d\mu }\left( y\right)  + {\int }_{0}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t - s}\right) F\left( {y, s}\right) {d\mu }\left( y\right) .
\]

If \( F \equiv  0 \) , then the solution does exist and is given by

(E.21)

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) f\left( y\right) {d\mu }\left( y\right) .
\]

Proof. By taking \( {t}_{1} \rightarrow  {0}_{ + },{t}_{2} \rightarrow  {t}_{ - } \) ,

\[
A\left( {w,\tau }\right)  = h\left( {x, w,\tau }\right) ,\;\text{ and }\;B\left( {w, s}\right)  = u\left( {w, s}\right)
\]

all in (E.18), we have

\[
{\int }_{0}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, w, t - s}\right) F\left( {w, s}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\varepsilon  \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {h\left( {x, w,\varepsilon }\right) u\left( {w, t}\right)  - h\left( {x, w, t}\right) u\left( {w,\varepsilon }\right) }\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
= u\left( {x, t}\right)  - {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, w, t}\right) f\left( w\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right) .
\]

This shows that if the solution to the IVP (E.19) exists, then it is of the form (E.20).

Now if \( F \equiv  0 \) , then we can differentiate (E.21) under the integral sign:

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta u}}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\frac{\partial h}{\partial t} - {\Delta h}}\right) \left( {x, y, t}\right) f\left( y\right) {d\mu }\left( y\right)  = 0.
\]

On the other hand, for each \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) f\left( y\right) {d\mu }\left( y\right)  = f\left( x\right)
\]

so that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}u\left( {x, t}\right)  = f\left( x\right) \) .

nodes.content: LEMMA E.11 (Strict positivity of the heat kernel). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold. The heat kernel is positive, i.e., \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  > 0 \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA E.11 (Strict positivity of the heat kernel). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold. The heat kernel is positive, i.e., \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right) > 0 \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. We first show that \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  \geq  0 \) . Given a nonnegative function \( f : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) , let \( u : \mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be the solution to the heat equation with \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  = f\left( x\right) \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . By the maximum principle we have \( u \geq  0 \) . On the other hand, by (E.21) we have

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, z, t}\right) f\left( z\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right) .
\]

Now given \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) , take \( {f}_{k} \) to be a sequence of nonnegative functions limiting to \( {\delta }_{y} \) . Since \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, z, t}\right) {f}_{k}\left( z\right) {d\mu }\left( z\right)  \geq  0 \) , we conclude \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  \geq \) 0.

The strict positivity \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  > 0 \) follows from the strong maximum principle and the simple fact that \( h \) is not identically zero; note that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\left( 4\pi t\right) }^{n/2}h\left( {x, x, t}\right)  = 1.
\]

COROLLARY E. 12 (Heat kernel has largest sup norm). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold. We have

(E.25)

\[
\left| {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \mathop{\max }\limits_{{y \in  \mathcal{M}}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left| {f\left( y\right) }\right| {d\mu }\left( y\right) .
\]

Thus, at any positive time (a multiple of) the fundamental solution has the largest \( {L}^{\infty } \) -norm among all solutions of the heat equation with fixed initial \( {L}^{1} \) -norm.

DEFINITION E. 14 (Dirichlet heat kernel). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold with interior int \( \left( \mathcal{M}\right) \) and nonempty boundary \( \partial \mathcal{M} \) . We say that \( {h}_{\mathrm{D}} : \mathcal{M} \times  \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a Dirichlet heat kernel of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) if \( {h}_{\mathrm{D}} \) is continuous and \( {\left. {h}_{\mathrm{D}}\right| }_{\operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right)  \times  \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right)  \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right) } \) is a fundamental solution \( {}^{4} \) and satisfies the Dirichlet boundary condition:

\[
{h}_{\mathrm{D}}\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = 0
\]

for all \( x \in  \partial \mathcal{M}, y \in  \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right) \) , and \( t \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) .

Clearly

(E.26)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h}_{\mathrm{D}}\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = 1.
\]

Note that in comparison to (E.16) we have

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h}_{\mathrm{D}}\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\Delta {h}_{\mathrm{D}}\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\partial \mathcal{M}}\frac{\partial {h}_{\mathrm{D}}}{\partial \nu }\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  < 0,
\]

where we used the Hopf boundary point lemma (Theorem E.4). Hence

(E.27)

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h}_{\mathrm{D}}\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  < 1
\]

for all \( y \in  \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) .

Proof. (Sketch.) There exists an extension of \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) to a smooth closed Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}^{n},\widehat{g}}\right) \) . Let

\[
\widehat{h} : \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \times  \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}
\]

be the heat kernel of \( \left( {\widehat{\mathcal{M}},\widehat{g}}\right) \) , which exists by Theorem E.13. There exists a solution

\[
u : \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right)  \times  \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right)  \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}
\]

---

\( {}^{4} \) That is, \( \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{x}}\right) h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = 0 \) and for any continuous function \( f \) on int \( \left( \mathcal{M}\right) \) with compact support we have \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right) }h\left( {x, y, t}\right) f\left( x\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = f\left( y\right) \) .

---

to \( \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{x}}\right) u\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = 0 \) with \( u\left( {x, y,0}\right)  = 0 \) for \( x, y \in  \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right) \) and with

\[
u\left( {x, y, t}\right)  =  - \widehat{h}\left( {x, y, t}\right)
\]

for \( x \in  \partial \mathcal{M}, y \in  \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right) \) , and \( t \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) (see pp. 161-164 of [92]). Define

\[
{h}_{\mathrm{D}} : \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right)  \times  \operatorname{int}\left( \mathcal{M}\right)  \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}
\]

by

\[
{h}_{\mathrm{D}}\left( {x, y, t}\right)  \Doteq  \widehat{h}\left( {x, y, t}\right)  + u\left( {x, y, t}\right) .
\]

We leave it as an exercise for the reader to check that \( {h}_{\mathrm{D}} \) is a Dirichlet heat kernel of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) .

LEMMA E. 16 (Duhamel’s principle, II). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold with boundary \( \partial \mathcal{M} \) and let \( \square  = \frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta \) . If \( A \) and \( B \) are functions on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0, t}\right) \) which are both \( {C}^{2} \) in space and \( {C}^{1} \) in time, then for any \( 0 < {t}_{1} < {t}_{2} < t \) we have

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {A\left( {w, t - {t}_{2}}\right) B\left( {w,{t}_{2}}\right)  - A\left( {w, t - {t}_{1}}\right) B\left( {w,{t}_{1}}\right) }\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {-\left( {\square A}\right) \left( {w, t - s}\right) B\left( {w, s}\right)  + A\left( {w, t - s}\right) \left( {\square B}\right) \left( {w, s}\right) }\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}{ds}{\int }_{\partial \mathcal{M}}\left( {-\left( \frac{\partial A}{\partial \nu }\right) \left( {w, t - s}\right) B\left( {w, s}\right)  + A\left( {w, t - s}\right) \left( \frac{\partial B}{\partial \nu }\right) \left( {w, s}\right) }\right) {d\sigma }\left( w\right) ,
\]

where \( \frac{\partial }{\partial \nu } \) and \( {d\sigma } \) are the unit outward normal derivative and volume form on \( \partial \mathcal{M} \) , respectively.

The proof of this lemma is the same as for Lemma E. 8 except that now Green's formula says that

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {\left( {\Delta A}\right) B - A\left( {\Delta B}\right) }\right) {d\mu } = {\int }_{\partial \mathcal{M}}\left( {B\frac{\partial A}{\partial \nu } - A\frac{\partial B}{\partial \nu }}\right) {d\sigma }.
\]

nodes.content: DEFINITION E. 17 (Minimal positive fundamental solution). We say that a positive fundamental solution \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) is the minimal positive fundamental solution if for every positive fundamental solution \( \widetilde{h}\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) we have \( \widetilde{h}\left( {x, y, t}\right)  \geq  h\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) . Clearly, if \( h \) exists, then it is unique.

Clearly, if \( h \) exists, then it is unique.

nodes.content:
THEOREM E.19 (Existence of minimal positive fundamental solution). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold, then there exists a minimal positive fundamental solution of \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) .

The main tool we use is the following (see Lemma 3 on p. 187 of [92]).
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM E.19 (Existence of minimal positive fundamental solution). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold, then there exists a minimal positive fundamental solution of \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) . The main tool we use is the following (see Lemma 3 on p. 187 of [92]).

nodes.proof:
Proof of THEOREM E.19. Let \( h : \mathcal{M} \times  \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be the function defined by (E.28) as the limit of increasing Dirichlet heat kernels associated to an exhaustion \( {\left\{  {\mathcal{U}}_{i}\right\}  }_{i \in  \mathbb{N}} \) of \( \mathcal{M} \) by compact regular domains. By Lemma E.20, for any compact subset \( K \subset  \mathcal{M} \) and \( {t}_{0} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) we have

\[
\left| {{h}_{i}\left( {x, y, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{0}
\]

for all \( x, y \in  K \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) , where \( {C}_{0} < \infty \) is independent of \( i \) . Hence

(E.32)

\[
h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  \Doteq  \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}{h}_{i}\left( {x, y, t}\right)
\]

is finite on \( K \times  K \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) . By Lemma E.20, for all \( k \in  \mathbb{N} \) we have \( \left| {{\nabla }^{k}{h}_{i}\left( {x, y, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{k} < \infty \) independent of \( i \in  \mathbb{N} \) in \( K \times  K \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) . Hence the limit function \( h \) is \( {C}^{\infty } \) and after passing to a subsequence the convergence of \( \left\{  {h}_{i}\right\} \) to \( h \) in (E.32) is uniform in any \( {C}^{\ell } \) on compact subsets of \( \mathcal{M} \) . Thus \( h \) is a solution of the heat equation, i.e.,

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{x}}\right) h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = 0.
\]

Since \( {h}_{i}\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = {h}_{i}\left( {y, x, t}\right) \) , we have that \( h \) is symmetric, i.e.,

\[
h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = h\left( {y, x, t}\right) .
\]

Since \( {h}_{i} > 0 \) in int \( \left( {\mathcal{U}}_{i}\right) \) and \( h \geq  {h}_{i} \) , we have \( h > 0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) .

Now we show that \( h \) is a fundamental solution of the heat equation. By (E.27) we have

(E.33)

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  \leq  1
\]

for all \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) . If \( \mathcal{U} \subset  \mathcal{M} \) is a compact regular domain with nonempty interior, then by (E.33) and (E.26) and since \( h \geq  {h}_{\mathcal{U}} \) , where \( {h}_{\mathcal{U}} \) is the Dirichlet heat kernel of \( \left( {\mathcal{U},{\left. g\right| }_{\mathcal{U}}}\right) \) , we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{U}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = 1
\]

for any \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Finally, if \( \varphi \) is continuous, then

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}h\left( {x, y, t}\right) \varphi \left( y\right) {d\mu }\left( y\right)  = \varphi \left( x\right) .
\]

(See p. 190 of [92] for a proof of this.)

nodes.content:
LEMMA E.20 (Local bound for solutions of the heat equation). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a complete Riemannian manifold and suppose \( u : \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0, T}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a solution to the heat equation with

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left| {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right| {d\mu }\left( x\right)  \leq  C
\]

for all \( t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . Then for any compact subset \( K \subset  \mathcal{M} \) and \( {t}_{0} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) ,

\[
\left| {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  C
\]

for all \( x \in  K \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) , where \( C < \infty \) depends only on \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) , K \) , \( T \) , and \( {t}_{0} \) . Moreover, for each \( k \in  \mathbb{N} \) we have

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{k}u}\right|  \leq  {C}_{k}\;\text{ on }K \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) ,
\]

where \( {C}_{k} < \infty \) depends only on \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) , k, K, T \) , and \( {t}_{0} \) .

Then for an...

nodes.proof:
Proof. The idea of the proof is similar to that for obtaining inequality (E.25). In the present case we localize the application of Duhamel's principle as follows. Given any compact subset \( K \subset  \mathcal{M} \) , let \( \varphi  : \mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) be a smooth function with compact support and with \( \varphi  \equiv  1 \) on \( K \) . Let \( u \) : \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0, T}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a solution to the heat equation with

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left| {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right| {d\mu }\left( x\right)  \leq  C
\]

for all \( t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . Let \( \Omega \) be a compact regular domain with \( K \subset  \operatorname{supp}\left( \varphi \right)  \subset \; \Omega  \subset  \mathcal{M} \) and let \( {h}_{\Omega } \) denote the Dirichlet heat kernel of \( \left( {\Omega ,{\left. g\right| }_{\Omega }}\right) \) , which exists by Proposition E.15. Given any \( {t}_{0} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , if \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \left( {\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}, T}\right) \) , then by taking \( {t}_{1} = \frac{{t}_{0}}{2},{t}_{2} \nearrow  t, A\left( {w,\tau }\right)  = {h}_{\Omega }\left( {w, x,\tau }\right) \) , and \( B\left( {w, s}\right)  = \; \varphi \left( w\right) u\left( {w, s}\right) \) all in (E.18), we have

\[
\varphi \left( x\right) u\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h}_{\Omega }\left( {w, x, t - \frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right) \varphi \left( w\right) u\left( {w,\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
- {\int }_{\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h}_{\Omega }\left( {\cdot , x, t - s}\right) \left( {u\left( s\right) {\Delta \varphi } + 2\langle \nabla u\left( s\right) ,\nabla \varphi \rangle }\right) {d\mu }
\]

since

\[
\square \left( {\varphi \left( \cdot \right) u\left( {\cdot , s}\right) }\right)  =  - u\left( s\right) {\Delta \varphi } - 2\langle \nabla u\left( s\right) ,\nabla \varphi \rangle .
\]

Integrating by parts, we have

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{h}_{\Omega }\left( {\cdot , x, t - s}\right) \left( {u\left( s\right) {\Delta \varphi } + 2\langle \nabla u\left( s\right) ,\nabla \varphi \rangle }\right) {d\mu }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( {-{h}_{\Omega }\left( {\cdot , x, t - s}\right) u\left( s\right) {\Delta \varphi } - {2u}\left( s\right) \langle \nabla {h}_{\Omega }\left( {\cdot , x, t - s}\right) ,\nabla \varphi \rangle }\right) {d\mu }.
\]

Hence, if \( x \in  K \) and \( t \in  \left( {\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}, T}\right) \) , then(E.29)

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\int }_{\Omega }{h}_{\Omega }\left( {w, x, t - \frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right) \varphi \left( w\right) u\left( {w,\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\Omega  - K}u\left( s\right) \left( {{h}_{\Omega }\left( {\cdot , x, t - s}\right) {\Delta \varphi } + 2\left\langle  {\nabla {h}_{\Omega }\left( {\cdot , x, t - s}\right) ,\nabla \varphi }\right\rangle  }\right) {d\mu },
\]

where we could change the domains of integration from \( \mathcal{M} \) to \( \Omega \) and \( \Omega  - K \) since \( \operatorname{supp}\left( \varphi \right)  \subset  \Omega \) and \( \varphi  \equiv  1 \) on \( K \) , respectively.

We have

\[
0 \leq  {h}_{\Omega }\left( {w, x, t - \frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right)  \leq  C
\]

for all \( x \in  K, w \in  \Omega \) , and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) . Hence

\[
\left| {{\int }_{\Omega }{h}_{\Omega }\left( {w, x, t - \frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right) \varphi \left( w\right) u\left( {w,\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right) }\right|
\]

(E.30)

\[
\leq  C{\int }_{\Omega }\left| {u\left( {w,\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right) }\right| {d\mu }\left( w\right)  \leq  C{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left| {u\left( {w,\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}\right) }\right| {d\mu }\left( w\right)  \leq  C.
\]

Moreover,

\[
\left| {{h}_{\Omega }\left( {w, x, t - s}\right) {\Delta \varphi }\left( w\right)  + 2\left\langle  {\nabla {h}_{\Omega }\left( {w, x, t - s}\right) ,\nabla \varphi \left( w\right) }\right\rangle  }\right|  \leq  C
\]

for \( x \in  K, w \in  \Omega  - K, t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) , and \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}, t}\right\rbrack \) . Hence(E.31)

\[
\left| {{\int }_{\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\Omega  - K}u\left( s\right) \left( {{h}_{\Omega }\left( {\cdot , x, t - s}\right) {\Delta \varphi } + 2\left\langle  {\nabla {h}_{\Omega }\left( {\cdot , x, t - s}\right) ,\nabla \varphi }\right\rangle  }\right) {d\mu }}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {{\int }_{\frac{{t}_{0}}{2}}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\Omega  - K}u\left( s\right) {d\mu }}\right|  \leq  {CT}.
\]

We conclude from (E.29),(E.30), and (E.31) that for \( x \in  K,{t}_{0} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) ,

\[
\left| {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  C\text{ . }
\]

Taking covariant derivatives of (E.29), we obtain bounds of all spatial derivatives of \( u \) in \( K \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) .

nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM E. 22 (Cheeger and Yau). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is a complete Riemannian manifold with \( \mathrm{{Rc}} \geq \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) for some \( K \in \mathbb{R} \) , then the positive fundamental solution \( h\left( {x, y, t}\right) \) of the heat equation has the lower bound (E.34) \[ h\left( {x, y, t}\right) \geq {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}\left( {d\left( {x, y}\right) , t}\right) . \]

nodes.proof:
Proof. (Sketch.) The idea of the proof is to apply Duhamel's principle and the Laplacian comparison theorem. By Duhamel's principle, in particular, taking \( {t}_{1} \rightarrow  {0}_{ + },{t}_{2} \rightarrow  {t}_{ - }, A\left( {w,\tau }\right)  = {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) ,\tau }\right) \) , and \( B\left( {w, s}\right)  = h\left( {w, y, s}\right) \) all in (E.17), we have

\[
h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  - {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}\left( {d\left( {x, y}\right) , t}\right)
\]

(E. 35)

\[
=  - {\int }_{0}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\left( \frac{\partial {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}}{\partial t}\right) \left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right)  \cdot  h\left( {w, y, s}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right)  \cdot  \left( \frac{\partial h}{\partial t}\right) \left( {w, y, s}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right) .
\]

Now \( \frac{\partial h}{\partial t} = {\Delta }_{g}h \) , whereas we have

\[
- \left( \frac{\partial {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}}{\partial t}\right) \left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right)
\]

\[
=  - \left( {\widetilde{\Delta }{\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}}\right) \left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right)
\]

\[
=  - \left( {\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {r}^{2}} + {H}_{K}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) }\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial r}}\right) {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right) ,
\]

where \( \left( {\widetilde{\Delta }{\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}}\right) \left( {{d}_{\widetilde{g}}\left( {\widetilde{x},\widetilde{y}}\right) , t}\right)  \Doteq  \left( {\widetilde{\Delta }{h}_{n, K}}\right) \left( {\widetilde{x},\widetilde{y}, t}\right) \) is well-defined since the latter is a radial function and where \( {H}_{K}\left( r\right) \) denotes the mean curvature of the sphere of radius \( r \) in the simply-connected space form of constant sectional curvature \( K \) .

Given a point \( p \in  \mathcal{M} \) , let \( \operatorname{Cut}\left( p\right) \) denote the cut locus of \( p \) . Recall that the Laplacian on \( \mathcal{M} \) may be written in geodesic spherical coordinates centered at \( p \) as

(E.36)

\[
\left( {\Delta f}\right) \left( w\right)  = \frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {r}^{2}}\left( w\right)  + H\left( {w, p}\right) \frac{\partial f}{\partial r}\left( w\right)  + \left( {{\Delta }_{S\left( {p, r}\right) }f}\right) \left( w\right)
\]

for \( w \in  \mathcal{M} - \left( {\{ p\}  \cup  \operatorname{Cut}\left( p\right) }\right) \) , where \( H\left( {w, p}\right) \) denotes the mean curvature at \( w \) of the geodesic sphere \( S\left( {p, r}\right)  \Doteq  \{ y \in  \mathcal{M} : d\left( {y, p}\right)  = r\} \) , where \( r = d\left( {w, p}\right) \) , and where \( {\Delta }_{S\left( {p, r}\right) } \) denotes the intrinsic Laplacian of \( S\left( {p, r}\right) \) .

By the Laplacian comparison theorem (i.e., by the comparisons for the mean curvatures of geodesic spheres) we have

\[
H\left( {w, x}\right)  \leq  {H}_{K}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) }\right) .
\]

This inequality and (see Lemma 2.3 of [105])

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial r}{\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}}\right) \left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right)  < 0
\]

imply

\[
- \left( {\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {r}^{2}} + {H}_{K}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) }\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial r}}\right) {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - \left( {\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {r}^{2}} + H\left( {w, x}\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial r}}\right) \widetilde{h}\left( {x, w, t - s}\right) ,
\]

where \( \widetilde{h}\left( {x, w, t - s}\right)  \Doteq  {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right) \) . Hence

\[
- \frac{\partial {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}}{\partial t}\left( {d\left( {x, w}\right) , t - s}\right)  \geq   - \left( {{\Delta }_{g, w}\widetilde{h}}\right) \left( {x, w, t - s}\right) ,
\]

where \( {\Delta }_{g, w} \) denotes the Laplacian with respect to the metric \( g \) and the variable \( w \) . Applying this to (E.35), we conclude that

\[
h\left( {x, y, t}\right)  - {\mathrm{H}}_{n, K}\left( {d\left( {x, y}\right) , t}\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - {\int }_{0}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}{\Delta }_{g, w}\widetilde{h}\left( {x, w, t - s}\right)  \cdot  h\left( {w, y, s}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{t}{ds}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}\widetilde{h}\left( {x, w, t - s}\right)  \cdot  {\Delta }_{g, w}h\left( {w, y, s}\right) {d\mu }\left( w\right)
\]

\[
= 0\text{ . }
\]

nodes.content:
EXAMPLE E. 25 (Flat plane bundles over \( {\mathcal{S}}^{1} \) ). Given \( A \in  \mathrm{O}\left( 2\right) \) , consider the flat rank 2 real vector bundle \( \mathcal{V} \) over the circle \( {\mathcal{S}}^{1} \Doteq  \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} = \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack  /\widetilde{} \) , where \( 0 \sim  1 \) , defined by

\[
\mathcal{V} = \left( {\left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2}}\right) / \approx
\]

where \( \left( {0, A\left( x\right) }\right)  \approx  \left( {1, x}\right) \) for \( x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) . Note that \( \mathcal{V} \) is orientable if \( A \in  \mathrm{{SO}}\left( 2\right) \) and \( \mathcal{V} \) is nonorientable if \( A \in  \mathrm{O}\left( 2\right)  - \mathrm{{SO}}\left( 2\right) \) . The standard flat metric on \( \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) induces a flat Riemannian metric on \( \mathcal{V} \) .

Generalizing the above example, consider the following situation. Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a complete Riemannian manifold and suppose that \( \pi  : \mathcal{V} \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) is a flat rank \( k \) real vector bundle over \( \mathcal{M} \) , where locally \( \left( {\mathcal{V},{g}_{\mathcal{V}}}\right) \) is isometric to the product \( \mathcal{M} \times  {\mathbb{E}}^{k} \) and parallel translation defines local isometries from \( \left( {{\pi }^{-1}\left( \mathcal{U}\right) ,{g}_{\mathcal{V}}}\right) \) to \( \left( {\mathcal{U}, g}\right)  \times  {\mathbb{E}}^{k} \) for sufficiently small neighborhoods \( \mathcal{U} \) in \( \mathcal{M} \) . Note that if \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) is flat, then \( \left( {\mathcal{V},{g}_{\mathcal{V}}}\right) \) is also flat (as a Riemannian manifold).

Let \( h : \mathcal{M} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a fundamental solution to the heat equation:

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g}}\right) h = 0
\]

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}h = {\delta }_{y}
\]

where \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) . The fundamental solution on Euclidean space \( {\mathbb{E}}^{k} = \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{k},{g}_{{\mathbb{R}}^{k}}}\right) \) , centered at the origin, is given by

\[
{h}_{{\mathbb{R}}^{k}}\left( w\right)  = {\left( 4\pi t\right) }^{-k/2}{e}^{-{\left| w\right| }^{2}/{4t}},
\]

where \( w = \left( {{w}^{1},\ldots ,{w}^{k}}\right) \) and \( {\left| w\right| }^{2} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{k}{\left( {w}^{i}\right) }^{2} \) . Given \( z \in  \mathcal{V} \) , let \( \left| z\right| \) be the norm of \( z \) considered as a vector in the fiber \( {\mathcal{V}}_{\pi \left( z\right) } \) (this is the same as the distance of \( z \) to the 0-section of \( \mathcal{V} \) ). Given \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) , let \( {0}_{y} \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{y} \) denote the zero vector in the fiber over \( y \) . We define the function

\[
{h}_{\mathcal{V}}\left( {z, t}\right)  \Doteq  h\left( {\pi \left( z\right) , t}\right)  \cdot  {\left( 4\pi t\right) }^{-k/2}{e}^{-{\left| z\right| }^{2}/{4t}}.
\]

Then \( {h}_{\mathcal{V}} : \mathcal{V} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a fundamental solution centered at \( {0}_{y} \in  \mathcal{V} \) . That is, a fundamental solution of \( \mathcal{V} \) , when centered at a point on the 0 - section, can be well-defined as a ’product’ of fundamental solutions of \( \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) and Euclidean space.

Consider the circle of length 1, i.e., \( {\mathcal{S}}^{1} \Doteq  \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}{.}^{5} \) Its universal cover is \( \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \rightarrow  {\mathcal{S}}^{1} \) with the deck transformations given by the translations by the integers. The fundamental solution on \( \mathbb{R} \) centered at 0 is

\[
{h}_{\mathbb{R}}\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\left( 4\pi t\right) }^{-1/2}{e}^{-{x}^{2}/{4t}}.
\]

This induces the fundamental solution on \( {\mathcal{S}}^{1} \) , which as a \( \mathbb{Z} \) -invariant function on \( \mathbb{R} \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) , is defined by

\[
{h}_{{\mathcal{S}}^{1}}\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\left( 4\pi t\right) }^{-1/2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{m \in  \mathbb{N}}}{e}^{-{\left( x + m\right) }^{2}/{4t}}.
\]

By \( \mathbb{Z} \) -invariant we mean \( {h}_{{\mathcal{S}}^{1}}\left( {x + \ell , t}\right)  = {h}_{{\mathcal{S}}^{1}}\left( {x, t}\right) \) for all \( \ell  \in  \mathbb{N}, x \in  \mathbb{R} \) , and \( t > 0 \) .

where the \( {C}^{\infty } \) function \( \psi  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) is defined so that

(1) \( \psi  = 1 \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) and \( \psi  = 0 \) for \( t \geq  2 \) ,

(2) \( {\psi }^{\prime } \leq  0,\frac{{\left| {\psi }^{\prime }\right| }^{2}}{\psi } \leq  C \) , and \( \left| {\psi }^{\prime \prime }\right|  \leq  C \) .

\]

where \( \varepsilon  \geq  0 \) is to be chosen below (when \( k = 0 \) , it is optimal to take \( \varepsilon  = 0 \) ). \( {}^{7} \) One may compute that

THEOREM E.28 (Path-integrated Harnack estimate for Rc ≥ -k). If \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) is a complete Riemannian manifold with \( \operatorname{Rc} \geq   - k \) and if \( u \) is a positive solution to the heat equation, then for any \( \alpha  > 1 \) we have

(E.41)

\[
\frac{u\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) }{u\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) } \geq  {\left( \frac{{t}_{2}}{{t}_{1}}\right) }^{-\alpha \frac{n}{2}}\exp \left\{  {-\frac{\alpha }{4}\frac{d{\left( {x}_{1},{x}_{2}\right) }^{2}}{{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}} - \frac{n\alpha k}{2\left( {\alpha  - 1}\right) }\left( {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right) }\right\}
\]

for any \( {x}_{1},{x}_{2} \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( 0 \leq  {t}_{1} < {t}_{2} \) .

Note that, taking \( k = 0 \) and \( \alpha  \rightarrow  1 \) , we obtain (16.10):

(E.42)

\[
\frac{u\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) }{u\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) } \geq  {\left( \frac{{t}_{2}}{{t}_{1}}\right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\frac{d{\left( {x}_{1},{x}_{2}\right) }^{2}}{4\left( {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right) }}.
\]

In the case of a fundamental solution for \( k = 0 \) we have

\[
H\left( {x, y, t}\right)  \geq  H\left( {x, x,{t}_{1}}\right) {\left( \frac{t}{{t}_{1}}\right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\frac{d{\left( x, y\right) }^{2}}{4\left( {t - {t}_{1}}\right) }}.
\]

Since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{t}_{1} \rightarrow  {0}_{ + }}}{\left( 4\pi {t}_{1}\right) }^{n/2}H\left( {x, x,{t}_{1}}\right)  = 1 \) , we obtain (16.12):

\[
H\left( {x, y, t}\right)  \geq  {\left( 4\pi t\right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-\frac{d{\left( x, y\right) }^{2}}{4t}}.
\]

Suppose that \( \left\{  \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{i}^{n},{g}_{i},{x}_{i}}\right) \right\} \) is a sequence of pointed complete Riemannian manifolds with \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( {g}_{i}\right)  \geq  0 \) which converges in the pointed \( {C}^{\infty } \) Cheeger-Gromov sense to a complete Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty }^{n},{g}_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) (note that this limit has \( \operatorname{Rc}\left( {g}_{\infty }\right)  \geq  0 \) but may not have bounded curvature even if each manifold in the sequence does). That is, there exist an exhaustion \( \left\{  {U}_{i}\right\} \) of \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\infty } \) by open sets with \( {x}_{\infty } \in  {U}_{i} \) and a sequence of diffeomorphisms \( {\Phi }_{i} : {U}_{i} \rightarrow \; {V}_{i} \Doteq  {\Phi }_{i}\left( {U}_{i}\right)  \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{i} \) with \( {\Phi }_{i}\left( {x}_{\infty }\right)  = {x}_{i} \) such that \( \left( {{U}_{i},{\Phi }_{i}^{ * }\left\lbrack  {\left. {g}_{i}\right| }_{{V}_{i}}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) converges in \( {C}^{\infty } \) to \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{\infty },{g}_{\infty }}\right) \) uniformly on compact sets in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\infty } \) . Under what conditions does a sequence \( \left\{  {{u}_{i} : {\mathcal{M}}_{i} \times  \left( {0, T}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {0,\infty }\right) }\right\} \) of positive solutions of the heat equation admit a subsequence for which the functions \( {u}_{i} \circ  {\Phi }_{i} : {U}_{i} \rightarrow  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) converge to a positive solution \( {u}_{\infty } : {\mathcal{M}}_{\infty } \rightarrow  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) of the heat equation? One may ask the same question assuming a uniform lower bound for the Ricci curvatures.

nodes.content:
THEOREM E.30 (Gradient estimate for bounded solutions). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold with \( \mathrm{{Rc}} \geq   - {k}_{1} \) , where \( {k}_{1} \geq  0 \) . If \( u \) is a positive solution to the heat equation with \( u \leq  A \) , then

(E.43)

\[
t\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} \leq  \left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) .
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM E.30 (Gradient estimate for bounded solutions). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold with \( \mathrm{{Rc}} \geq - {k}_{1} \) , where \( {k}_{1} \geq 0 \) . If \( u \) is a positive solution to the heat equation with \( u \leq A \) , then (E.43) \[ t\frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{{u}^{2}} \leq \left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) . \]

nodes.proof:
Since \( \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = {\Delta u} \) , we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \log u = {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}
\]

and

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
=  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - 2\operatorname{Rc}\left( {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log u}\right)  + 2\left\langle  {\nabla \log u,\nabla {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right\rangle  .
\]

Hence, using \( \operatorname{Rc} \geq   - {k}_{1} \) , we obtain

(E.44)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + 2\left\langle  {\nabla \log u,\nabla \left( {t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right) }\right\rangle  .
\]

On the other hand,

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  =  - {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
= 2\left\langle  {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right\rangle   + {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2},
\]

where we rewrote the equation so as to match the gradient term in (E.44), and then

(E.45)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)  = 2\left\langle  {\nabla \log u,\nabla \left( {\left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right) }\right\rangle
\]

\[
+ \left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + 2{k}_{1}\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) .
\]

Since \( \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  \geq  0 \) and \( {k}_{1} \geq  0 \) , we conclude from (E.44) and (E.45) that

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( {t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - \left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Now \( t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - \left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  \leq  0 \) at \( t = 0 \) . Hence the weak maximum principle implies

\[
t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - \left( {1 + 2{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  \leq  0
\]

for all \( t \geq  0 \) .

EXERCISE E. 31 (An extension of the gradient estimate). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold evolving by

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{h}_{ij}
\]

with \( {R}_{ij} \geq   - {k}_{1}{g}_{ij},{h}_{ij} \leq  {k}_{1}{g}_{ij}, V \leq  {k}_{1} \) , and \( {\left| \nabla V\right| }^{2} \leq  {k}_{1} \) , where \( {k}_{1} \geq  0 \) . Show that if \( u \) is a positive solution to the heat-type equation

\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = {\Delta u} + {Vu}
\]

with \( u \leq  A \) , then

(E.46)

\[
t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \leq  2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + \left( {\frac{T}{4} + 2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) {k}_{1}}\right) t
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

nodes.proof:
Since \( \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = {\Delta u} + {Vu} \) ,

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \log u = {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + V
\]

and, using \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} =  - 2{h}_{ij} \) , we compute

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} =  - 2{\left| \nabla \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - 2\left( {\operatorname{Rc} - h}\right) \left( {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log u}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2\left\langle  {\nabla \log u,{\left. \nabla \left| \nabla \log u\right| \right| }^{2}}\right\rangle   + 2\langle \nabla \log u,\nabla V\rangle
\]

Since \( {R}_{ij} \geq   - {k}_{1}{g}_{ij} \) and \( {h}_{ij} \leq  {k}_{1}{g}_{ij} \) , this implies

(E.47)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 2\left\langle  {\nabla \log u,\nabla \left( {t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right) }\right\rangle
\]

\[
+ {2t}\langle \nabla \log u,\nabla V\rangle
\]

Hence, using \( {\left| \nabla V\right| }^{2} \leq  {k}_{1} \) , we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( {t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + \frac{{t}^{2}}{1 + 4{k}_{1}t}{\left| \nabla V\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}T}\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + \frac{T}{4}
\]

provided \( t \leq  T \) . On the other hand,

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  =  - {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - V
\]

\[
\geq  2\left\langle  {\nabla \log u,\nabla \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right\rangle   + {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - {k}_{1},
\]

where we used \( V \leq  {k}_{1} \) , and then

(E.48)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( {2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - 2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) {k}_{1}.
\]

Combining (E.47) and (E.48), we obtain

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( {t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} - 2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{T}{4} + 2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) {k}_{1} \doteq  {C}_{1}
\]

The weak maximum principle implies

\[
t{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \leq  2\left( {1 + 4{k}_{1}t}\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  + {C}_{1}t
\]

for all \( t \geq  0 \) .

nodes.content:
COROLLARY E.32. Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold. There exists a constant \( C < \infty \) depending only on \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) and \( T < \infty \) such that if \( u \) is a positive solution to the heat equation, then

\[
u\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  C{t}^{-n/2}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)
\]

for all \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

nodes.proof:
Let \( {k}_{1} = \max \left\{  {0, - \mathop{\min }\limits_{\mathcal{M}}\mathrm{{Rc}}}\right\} \) so that \( \operatorname{Rc} \geq   - {k}_{1} \) and \( {k}_{1} \geq  0 \) . Since \( \mathcal{M} \) is compact, there exists \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) such that

\[
{\bar{t}}^{n/2}u\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }}{t}^{n/2}u\left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  J.
\]

For \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t}/2,\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) , we have

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {t}^{-n/2}J \leq  {\left( \frac{\bar{t}}{2}\right) }^{-n/2}J \Doteq  A.
\]

Note that

(E.49)

\[
u\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  = {\bar{t}}^{-n/2}J = {2}^{-n/2}A.
\]

Let \( L\left( {x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \log \left( \frac{A}{u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) . We may apply Theorem E. 30 to the solution \( u\left( {t + \frac{\bar{t}}{2}}\right) \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{t}/2}\right\rbrack \) to obtain

\[
\frac{\bar{t}}{2}{\left| \nabla L\left( x,\bar{t}\right) \right| }^{2} \leq  \left( {1 + {k}_{1}\bar{t}}\right) L\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . In other words,

\[
\left| {\nabla \sqrt{L}\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right) }\right|  \leq  \sqrt{\frac{1 + {k}_{1}\bar{t}}{2\bar{t}}} \leq  \frac{{C}_{1}}{\sqrt{\bar{t}}},
\]

where \( {C}_{1} \Doteq  \frac{\sqrt{1 + {k}_{1}T}}{2} \) . By integrating this estimate along minimal geodesics, we obtain for any \( x,\bar{x} \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( \bar{t} \in  (0, T\rbrack \)

\[
\sqrt{L}\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right)  - \sqrt{L}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \leq  \frac{{C}_{1}}{\sqrt{\bar{t}}}d\left( {x,\bar{x}}\right) .
\]

Hence, if \( d\left( {x,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  \sqrt{\bar{t}} \) , then

\[
\sqrt{L}\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right)  \leq  \sqrt{L}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  + {C}_{1} = \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}\log 2} + {C}_{1} \Doteq  {C}_{2},
\]

where we used (E.49).

In terms of the original solution \( u \) , this says that if \( d\left( {x,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  \sqrt{\bar{t}} \) , then

\[
u\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right)  = A{e}^{-L\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right) } \geq  A{e}^{-{C}_{2}^{2}} \Doteq  {c}_{3}A,
\]

where \( {c}_{3} > 0 \) depends only on \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) and \( T \) . Since \( \bar{t} \leq  T \) , we have

\[
\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {\bar{x},\sqrt{\bar{t}}}\right)  \geq  {c}_{4}{\bar{t}}^{n/2}
\]

where \( {c}_{4} > 0 \) depends only on \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) and \( T \) . From all of this we conclude that

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  \geq  {\int }_{B\left( {\bar{x},\sqrt{\bar{t}}}\right) }u\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {c}_{3}A\operatorname{Vol}B\left( {\bar{x},\sqrt{\bar{t}}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {c}_{3}{c}_{4}A{\bar{t}}^{n/2}
\]

that is,

\[
{t}^{n/2}u\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  {\bar{t}}^{n/2}u\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \leq  {2}^{-n/2}A{\bar{t}}^{n/2}
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{5}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {x,\bar{t}}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)
\]

\[
= {C}_{5}{\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)
\]

for all \( y \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , where we used \( {\int }_{\mathcal{M}}u\left( {x, t}\right) {d\mu }\left( x\right)  = \) const. This completes the proof of the corollary.

THEOREM E.36 (Laplacian estimate for bounded solutions). Let \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) be a closed Riemannian manifold with \( \mathrm{{Rc}} \geq   - {k}_{1} \) , where \( {k}_{1} \geq  0 \) . If \( u \) is a positive solution to the heat equation with \( u \leq  A \) , then

\[
\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{1}t}}{{e}^{{k}_{1}t} - 1}\left( {n + 4\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right) .
\]

By the exercise we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( \frac{\Delta u}{u}\right)  = 0
\]

and

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \leq   - \frac{2}{n}{\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} + 2{k}_{1}{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2},
\]

where we used \( {\left| \nabla \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \geq  \frac{1}{n}{\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} \) . Hence for any function \( \phi \left( t\right) \) we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( {\phi \left( t\right) \left( {\frac{\Delta u}{u} + {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{2}{n}\phi \left( t\right) {\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} + 2{k}_{1}\phi \left( t\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} + {\phi }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \left( {\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
=  - \frac{2}{n}\phi \left( t\right) {\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} + {\phi }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \Delta \log u + 2\left( {{\phi }^{\prime }\left( t\right)  + {k}_{1}\phi \left( t\right) }\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2},
\]

where we used \( \frac{\Delta u}{u} + {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} = \Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \) . On the other hand,

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right)  = {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}.
\]

Hence

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( {\phi \left( {\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)  - B - 4\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{2}{n}\phi {\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} + {\phi }^{\prime }\Delta \log u + 2\left( {{\phi }^{\prime } + {k}_{1}\phi  - 2}\right) {\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}.
\]

Now choose \( \phi \left( t\right)  = \frac{{e}^{{k}_{1}t} - 1}{{k}_{1}{e}^{{k}_{1}t}} \) so that \( {\phi }^{\prime }\left( t\right)  = \frac{1}{{e}^{{k}_{1}t}} \) and \( {\phi }^{\prime } + {k}_{1}\phi  = 1 \) ; note also that \( \phi \left( t\right)  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1/{k}_{1}}\right) \) . Then

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \left( {\phi \left( {\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)  - n - 4\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq   - \frac{2}{n}\phi {\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} + {\phi }^{\prime }\Delta \log u - 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \doteq  J.
\]

At any point where

\[
\phi \left( {\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)  \geq  n + 4\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) ,
\]

we have either \( {\phi \Delta }\log u \geq  n/2 \) or \( {2\phi }{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \geq  n/2 \) . If \( {\phi \Delta }\log u \geq  n/2 \) , then

\[
J \leq  \left( {{\phi }^{\prime } - 1}\right) \Delta \log u - 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \leq  0.
\]

On the other hand, if \( {2\phi }{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2} \geq  n/2 \) , then

\[
J \leq   - \frac{2}{n}\phi {\left( \Delta \log u\right) }^{2} + {\phi }^{\prime }\Delta \log u - \frac{n}{2\phi }
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{n}{2\phi }\left( {\frac{{\left( {\phi }^{\prime }\right) }^{2}}{4} - 1}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Let \( \Phi  \Doteq  \phi \left( {\Delta \log u + 2{\left| \nabla \log u\right| }^{2}}\right)  - n - 4\log \left( \frac{A}{u}\right) \) . We have shown that at any point where \( \Phi  \geq  0 \) we have

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta  - 2\nabla \log u \cdot  \nabla }\right) \Phi  \leq  0.
\]

On the other hand, \( \Phi  \leq  0 \) at \( t = 0 \) . Hence by the maximum principle we conclude that \( \Phi  \leq  0 \) for \( t \geq  0 \) .

## 1. Introduction

In this appendix we describe a formalism for performing tensor calculations on both fixed and evolving (by Ricci flow) Riemannian manifolds. We use this formalism in computing the evolution equation satisfied by the differential Harnack quadratic for the Ricci flow in Chapter 15.

In particular we shall view tensors on a differentiable manifold \( {\mathcal{M}}^{n} \) as vector-valued \( \left( {\mathbb{R}}^{k}\right) \) functions on the frame bundle by evaluating the tensors on the vectors in the frames. We define natural, globally defined frame fields on the frame bundle \( F\mathcal{M} \) of a Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) consisting of vertical and horizontal vector fields. These frame fields are orthonormal when restricted/projected to the orthonormal frame bundle \( O\mathcal{M}{.}^{1} \) Via the correspondence between tensors and vector-valued functions, the covariant derivatives of tensors on \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g}\right) \) become the directional derivatives of the corresponding functions on \( F\mathcal{M} \) with respect to the horizontal vectors in the globally defined frame fields. \( {}^{2} \)

The directional derivatives with respect to the vertical vectors act algebraically on the functions on \( F\mathcal{M} \) corresponding to tensors on \( \mathcal{M} \) because the functions are invariant under the action of \( \operatorname{GL}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) .

We find it convenient to confirm these formulas by using local coordinates \( \left\{  {x}^{i}\right\} \) on \( \mathcal{M} \) , which induce local coordinates on \( F\mathcal{M} \) . The brackets of the horizontal vector fields in the frame fields on \( F\mathcal{M} \) are curvatures contracted with the vertical vector fields; this corresponds to commuting covariant derivatives. The brackets of the vertical vector fields are again vertical, and the bracket of a horizontal and a vertical vector field is horizontal; in both of these cases the bracket operation is algebraic.

The above considerations also apply to the subbundle of orthonormal frames \( O\mathcal{M} \) . Since we are most interested in a time-dependent metric \( g\left( t\right) \) , which is a solution to Ricci flow on some interval \( \mathcal{I} \) , we consider the corresponding time-dependent bundles \( O\mathcal{M}\left( t\right) \) . In general, for solutions to the

---

\( {}^{1} \) See Lemma F.12 below.

\( {}^{2} \) See Lemma F.14 below.

---

Ricci flow, we consider the time-derivatives of various tensors, usually tensors in the curvature and its covariant derivatives. These time derivatives correspond to directional derivatives with respect to a 'time' vector field defined on \( F\mathcal{M} \times  \mathcal{I} \) . This time vector field is tangent to the submanifold

\[
O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \Doteq  \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{t \in  \mathcal{I}}}O\mathcal{M}\left( t\right)  \times  \{ t\}  \subset  F\mathcal{M} \times  \mathcal{I}.
\]

With this setup, we can compute the commutator formulas for the heat operator and the covariant derivatives, which we use to carry out the calculations for the proof of the Harnack estimate in Section 4 of Chapter 15 of this volume. Calculations in these frames on \( O\mathcal{M} \) are equivalent to those with respect to a moving orthonormal frame (or more generally, using Uhlenbeck's trick), as described in Section 2 of Chapter 6 in Volume One.

The interested reader may wish to keep the following in mind while reading this appendix.

DEFINITION F.2. Every tensor \( U \) of type \( \left( {p, q}\right) \) has a corresponding vector-valued function \( {U}^{ \dagger  } \) on the frame bundle

\[
{U}^{ \dagger  } : F\mathcal{M} \rightarrow  {\mathbb{R}}^{{n}^{p + q}}
\]

defined by

\[
{U}^{ \dagger  }\left( Y\right)  \Doteq  {\left( {U}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}}^{{a}_{1}\cdots {a}_{q}}\left( Y\right) \right) }_{{a}_{1},\ldots ,{a}_{q},{b}_{1},\ldots ,{b}_{p} = 1}^{n}.
\]

We shall often abuse notation and write \( {U}^{ \dagger  } \) as \( U \) .

Note that if \( Y = {\left\{  {Y}_{a}\right\}  }_{a = 1}^{n} \) is a frame, then

\[
U\left( {{Y}_{{b}_{1}},\ldots ,{Y}_{{b}_{p}}}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{{a}_{1},\ldots ,{a}_{q} = 1}}^{n}{U}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}}^{{a}_{1}\cdots {a}_{q}}\left( Y\right)  \cdot  {Y}_{{a}_{1}} \otimes  \cdots  \otimes  {Y}_{{a}_{q}}.
\]

(Here we are not abusing notation since we are considering \( U \) as a tensor on \( \mathcal{M} \) .) For example, if \( V \) is a \( \left( {p,0}\right) \) -tensor, the components \( {V}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}} : F\mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) satisfy

\[
{V}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}}\left( Y\right)  \Doteq  {\left\lbrack  {V}^{ \dagger  }\left( Y\right) \right\rbrack  }_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}} = V\left( {{Y}_{{b}_{1}},\ldots ,{Y}_{{b}_{p}}}\right) .
\]

We emphasize that \( {V}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}} \) is a real-valued function on \( F\mathcal{M} \) (we have one for each choice of \( {b}_{1},\ldots ,{b}_{p} \) ) while \( V \) is a tensor on \( \mathcal{M} \) .

The effect of a change of frame on the components of a tensor \( U \) is given by the following:

## 3. Local coordinates on the frame bundle

In carrying out the various computations, we shall find it convenient to use local coordinates. Let \( {\left\{  {x}^{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{n} \) be a local coordinate system defined on an open set \( \mathcal{O} \subset  \mathcal{M} \) . Then \( {\left\{  \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{n} \) is a frame field on \( \mathcal{O} \) , so it is a section of \( {\left. {\pi }_{\mathcal{O}} : F\mathcal{M}\right| }_{\mathcal{O}} \rightarrow  \mathcal{O} \) , where \( {\pi }_{\mathcal{O}} \) is the restriction of the natural projection \( \pi  : F\mathcal{M} \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) . We define functions

\[
{y}_{a}^{i} : {\left. F\mathcal{M}\right| }_{\mathcal{O}} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}
\]

by

\[
{Y}_{a} \Doteq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{n}{y}_{a}^{i}\left( Y\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}.
\]

The function \( {y}_{a}^{i} \) assigns to a frame \( Y \) the \( i \) -th component of the \( a \) -th vector. The vector- (or matrix-) valued function

\[
y \Doteq  {\left( {y}_{a}^{i}\right) }_{i, a = 1}^{n} : {\left. F\mathcal{M}\right| }_{\mathcal{O}} \rightarrow  \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right)  \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{{n}^{2}}
\]

describes the transition of the frame \( {\left\{  \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{n} \) to the frame \( Y = {\left\{  {Y}_{a}\right\}  }_{a = 1}^{n} \) . That is, \( \left\{  {y}_{a}^{i}\right\} \) are the components of the frame \( \left\{  \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\right\} \) with respect to the frame \( \left\{  {Y}_{a}\right\} \) .

### 4.The metric on the frame bundle

Now let \( g \) be a Riemannian metric on \( {\mathcal{M}}^{n} \) . We proceed to define the induced Riemannian metric on the principal \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) -bundle \( F\mathcal{M} \) . Let \( \rho \) : \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right)  \times  F\mathcal{M} \rightarrow  F\mathcal{M} \) denote the left action. Given \( Y \in  F\mathcal{M} \) , define

\[
{\rho }_{Y} : \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right)  \rightarrow  F\mathcal{M}
\]

by

\[
{\rho }_{Y}\left( G\right)  \Doteq  \rho \left( {G, Y}\right) \;\text{ for }G \in  \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) .
\]

We have

\[
{\rho }_{Y}{\left( G\right) }_{a} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{b = 1}}^{n}{G}_{a}^{b}{Y}_{b}
\]

The derivative

\[
{\left( {\rho }_{Y}\right) }_{ * } : \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right)  \rightarrow  {T}_{Y}\left( {F{\mathcal{M}}_{x}}\right)
\]

is a vector space isomorphism, where \( x = \pi \left( Y\right) \) . Given \( G \in  \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) , left multiplication \( {L}_{G} : F\mathcal{M} \rightarrow  F\mathcal{M} \) is defined by \( {L}_{G}\left( Y\right)  \Doteq  \rho \left( {G, Y}\right) \) . The vertical spaces are the tangent spaces to the fibers:

\[
{V}_{Y} \Doteq  {T}_{Y}\left( {F{\mathcal{M}}_{x}}\right)  = \text{ image }\left\lbrack  {\left( {\rho }_{Y}\right) }_{ * }\right\rbrack  ,
\]

where \( x = \pi \left( Y\right) \) .

The Levi-Civita connection \( \nabla \) on the associated tangent bundle \( T\mathcal{M} \) induces a connection on the principal \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) -bundle \( F\mathcal{M} \) , which is a \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) -invariant 1-form \( \omega \) on \( F\mathcal{M} \) with values in \( \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) , called the connection 1-form. Defining \( \omega \) is equivalent to defining \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) -invariant horizontal subspaces of the tangent spaces of \( F\mathcal{M} \) (the null spaces of \( \omega \) ). The horizontal spaces in \( F\mathcal{M} \) have the following property. Given a path \( \gamma \left( t\right) \) in \( \mathcal{M} \) , a parallel frame \( Y\left( t\right) \) along \( \gamma \left( t\right) \) is tangent to the horizontal spaces. The horizontal spaces \( {H}_{Y} = \ker \omega \) are the kernels of \( \omega  : {T}_{Y}\left( {F{\mathcal{M}}_{x}}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) , which are \( \operatorname{GL}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) -invariant:

\[
{\left( {L}_{G}\right) }_{ * }\left( {H}_{Y}\right)  = {H}_{{L}_{G}\left( Y\right) }
\]

for all \( G \in  \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) and \( Y \in  F\mathcal{M} \) .

Given an inner product \( h \) on the Lie algebra \( \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) , the frame bundle has an induced Riemannian metric \( {g}^{F} \) defined uniquely by the following conditions:

(1) \( {\left( {\rho }_{Y}\right) }_{ * } : \left( {\mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) , h}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {{T}_{Y}\left( {F{\mathcal{M}}_{x}}\right) ,{g}^{F}}\right) \) is an isometry, i.e.,

\[
{\left( {\left. {\rho }_{Y}\right| }^{ * }\left( {\left. {g}^{F}\right| }_{{T}_{Y}\left( {F{\mathcal{M}}_{x}}\right) }\right)  = h\right) }^{ * }
\]

for all \( Y \in  F{\mathcal{M}}_{x} \) and \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) ;

(2) the horizontal subspaces induced by the Levi-Civita connection are the orthogonal complements of the tangent spaces to the fibers with respect to the metric \( {g}^{F} \) ; and

(3) \( \pi  : \left( {F\mathcal{M},{g}^{F}}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {\mathcal{M}, g}\right) \) is a Riemannian submersion, i.e.,

\[
\left( {{\pi }^{ * }g}\right) \left( {V, W}\right)  = {g}^{F}\left( {V, W}\right)
\]

for all horizontal vectors \( V, W \in  {H}_{Y} \subset  {T}_{Y}F\mathcal{M} \) .

Consider the standard basis \( \{ e\left( {a, b}\right) {\} }_{a, b = 1}^{n} \) of \( \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) defined by

\[
e{\left( a, b\right) }_{c}^{d} \Doteq  {\delta }_{c}^{a}{\delta }_{b}^{d}.
\]

We choose the metric \( h \) on \( \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) by taking this basis to be orthonormal with respect to \( h = \langle \) , \( \rangle n \) , namely

\[
\langle e\left( {a, b}\right) , e\left( {c, d}\right) \rangle  = {\delta }_{f}^{a}{\delta }_{b}^{e}{\delta }_{e}^{c}{\delta }_{d}^{f} = {\delta }_{d}^{a}{\delta }_{b}^{c}.
\]

The Lie brackets of these basis elements are given by

\[
\left\lbrack  {e\left( {a, b}\right) , e\left( {c, d}\right) }\right\rbrack   = {\delta }_{b}^{c}e\left( {a, d}\right)  - {\delta }_{d}^{a}e\left( {c, b}\right) .
\]

\[

\]

The \( {\left\{  {\Lambda }_{b}^{a}\right\}  }_{a, b = 1}^{n} \) are orthonormal since they are the push forwards of \( \{ e\left( {a, b}\right) {\} }_{a, b = 1}^{n} \) by the isometry \( {\rho }_{Y} \) and \( \{ e\left( {a, b}\right) {\} }_{a, b = 1}^{n} \) are orthonormal with respect to \( h \) on \( \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) . \[

\]

\[
\left\lbrack  {{\left( {\rho }_{Y}\right) }_{ * }\left( {e\left( {a, b}\right) }\right) }\right\rbrack   = \left( {{\left. \frac{d}{dt}\right| }_{t = 0}{y}_{d}^{i}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) Y}\right) }\right) {\left. \frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{d}^{i}}\right| }_{Y}
\]

\[
+ {\left. \left( {\left. \frac{d}{dt}\right| }_{t = 0}{\widetilde{x}}^{j}\left( \gamma \left( t\right) Y\right) \right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {\widetilde{x}}^{j}}\right| }_{Y}
\]

\[
= {\delta }_{d}^{a}{\delta }_{b}^{e}{y}_{e}^{i}\left( Y\right) {\left. \frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{d}^{i}}\right| }_{Y}
\]

\[
= {y}_{b}^{i}\left( Y\right) {\left. \frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{a}^{i}}\right| }_{Y}.
\]

LEMMA F.16. On \( F\mathcal{M} \) ,

(F.9)

\[
\left\lbrack  {{\nabla }_{a},{\nabla }_{b}}\right\rbrack   =  - {R}_{abc}^{d}{\Lambda }_{d}^{c},
\]

where

\[
R\left( {{Y}_{a},{Y}_{b}}\right) {Y}_{c} \Doteq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{d = 1}}^{n}{R}_{abc}^{d}\left( Y\right)  \cdot  {Y}_{d}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA F.16. On \( F\mathcal{M} \) , (F.9) \[ \left\lbrack {{\nabla }_{a},{\nabla }_{b}}\right\rbrack = - {R}_{abc}^{d}{\Lambda }_{d}^{c}, \] where \[ R\left( {{Y}_{a},{Y}_{b}}\right) {Y}_{c} \Doteq \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{d = 1}}^{n}{R}_{abc}^{d}\left( Y\right) \cdot {Y}_{d}. \]

nodes.proof:
We have

\[
{\nabla }_{a} = {y}_{a}^{i}\left\{  {\frac{\partial }{\partial {\widetilde{x}}^{i}} - {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}{y}_{c}^{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{c}^{k}}}\right\}
\]

and

\[
{y}_{d}^{q}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{d}^{k}} = {y}_{d}^{q}{\left( {y}^{-1}\right) }_{k}^{c}{\Lambda }_{c}^{d},
\]

(where in the sequel we shall use \( \{ p, q, r\} \) in the same manner as \( \{ i, j, k\} \) ) which follows from

\[
{\left( {y}^{-1}\right) }_{k}^{c}{\Lambda }_{c}^{d} = \frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{d}^{k}}.
\]

Using

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial {\widetilde{x}}^{i}}{y}_{j}^{b} = 0\;\text{ for all }i, j, b,
\]

we compute

\[
{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b} - {\nabla }_{b}{\nabla }_{a} = {y}_{a}^{i}\left\{  {\frac{\partial }{\partial {\widetilde{x}}^{i}} - {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}{y}_{c}^{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{c}^{k}}}\right\}  \left( {{y}_{b}^{p}\left\{  {\frac{\partial }{\partial {\widetilde{x}}^{p}} - {\Gamma }_{pq}^{r}{y}_{d}^{q}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{d}^{r}}}\right\}  }\right)
\]

\[
- {y}_{b}^{p}\left\{  {\frac{\partial }{\partial {\widetilde{x}}^{p}} - {\Gamma }_{pq}^{r}{y}_{d}^{q}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{d}^{r}}}\right\}  \left( {{y}_{a}^{i}\left\{  {\frac{\partial }{\partial {\widetilde{x}}^{i}} - {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}{y}_{c}^{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{c}^{k}}}\right\}  }\right)
\]

\[
= {y}_{a}^{i}{y}_{b}^{p}\left( {-\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}{\Gamma }_{pq}^{k} + \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{p}}{\Gamma }_{iq}^{k} + {\Gamma }_{iq}^{j}{\Gamma }_{pj}^{k} - {\Gamma }_{pq}^{j}{\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}}\right) {y}_{d}^{q}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{d}^{k}}
\]

\[
= {y}_{a}^{i}{y}_{b}^{p}{y}_{d}^{q}{\left( {y}^{-1}\right) }_{k}^{c}\left( {-\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}{\Gamma }_{pq}^{k} + \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{p}}{\Gamma }_{iq}^{k} + {\Gamma }_{iq}^{j}{\Gamma }_{pj}^{k} - {\Gamma }_{pq}^{j}{\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}}\right) {\Lambda }_{c}^{d}
\]

\[
=  - {y}_{a}^{i}{y}_{b}^{p}{y}_{d}^{q}{\left( {y}^{-1}\right) }_{k}^{c}{R}_{ipq}^{k}{\Lambda }_{c}^{d}
\]

\[
=  - {R}_{abd}^{c}{\Lambda }_{c}^{d}
\]

## 8. Reduction to the orthonormal frame bundle

It will simplify our calculations considerably to work on the orthonormal frame bundle \( O\mathcal{M} \) , which is the subbundle of \( F\mathcal{M} \) with \( {g}_{ab} = {\delta }_{ab} \) ; i.e.,

\[
O\mathcal{M} \Doteq  \left\{  {Y \in  F\mathcal{M} : {g}_{ab}\left( Y\right)  = {\delta }_{ab}\text{ for all }a, b}\right\}  .
\]

The metric \( g \) may be considered as a function

\[
g = {\left( {g}_{ab}\right) }_{a, b = 1}^{n} : F\mathcal{M} \rightarrow  {\mathbb{S}}_{ + }^{n \times  n} \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n\left( {n + 1}\right) /2},
\]

where \( {\mathbb{S}}_{ + }^{n \times  n} \) denotes the set of symmetric, positive-definite \( n \times  n \) matrices. In particular, \( O\mathcal{M} = {g}^{-1}\left( I\right) \) , where \( I \in  {\mathbb{S}}_{ + }^{n \times  n} \) is the identity matrix. Note that given a point \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , a tensor \( U \) at \( x \) , as a function on \( F{\mathcal{M}}_{x} \) , is determined by its value \( U\left( Y\right) \) at one frame \( Y \in  F{\mathcal{M}}_{x} \) because \( {GL}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) acts transitively on the frames. In particular, tensors, as functions on \( F\mathcal{M} \) , are determined by their restrictions to \( O\mathcal{M} \) .

REMARK F.21. As a vector field on \( O\mathcal{M},{\rho }_{ab} \) represents an infinitesimal counterclockwise rotation of the \( {ab} \) -plane. In particular, consider the path

\[
\gamma \left( t\right)  \Doteq  \left( {x,{Y}_{1},\ldots ,{Y}_{a - 1},\cos t{Y}_{a} + \sin t{Y}_{b},{Y}_{a + 1},\ldots ,{Y}_{b - 1}, - \sin t{Y}_{a} + \cos t{Y}_{b},{Y}_{b + 1},\ldots ,{Y}_{n}}\right)
\]

in \( {OM} \) . We have

\[
\frac{d\gamma }{dt}\left( 0\right)  = {\left. {\rho }_{ab}\right| }_{Y}.
\]

Rotating counterclockwise in the \( {ab} \) -plane skews the \( a \) -axis into the \( b \) -axis and the \( b \) -axis into the negative \( a \) -axis.

nodes.proof:
Since \( \nabla g = 0 \) , we have

\[
{\nabla }_{a}\left( {g}_{bc}\right)  = 0.
\]

Thus \( {\nabla }_{a} \) restricts to a vector field on \( O\mathcal{M} \) . We also calculate

\[
\left\langle  {{\rho }_{ab},{\rho }_{cd}}\right\rangle   = \left\langle  {{\Lambda }_{b}^{a} - {\Lambda }_{a}^{b},{\Lambda }_{d}^{c} - {\Lambda }_{c}^{d}}\right\rangle   = 2{\delta }_{ac}{\delta }_{bd}
\]

for \( a < b \) and \( c < d \) .

LEMMA F.27. On \( F\mathcal{M} \) , we have

\[
\left\lbrack  {{\rho }_{ab},{\nabla }_{c}}\right\rbrack   = {\rho }_{ab}{\nabla }_{c} - {\nabla }_{c}{\rho }_{ab} = {g}_{ac}{\nabla }_{b} - {g}_{bc}{\nabla }_{a}
\]

and

\[
\left\lbrack  {{\rho }_{ab},{\rho }_{cd}}\right\rbrack   = {\rho }_{ab}{\rho }_{cd} - {\rho }_{cd}{\rho }_{ab}
\]

\[
= {g}_{ac}{\rho }_{bd} + {g}_{bd}{\rho }_{ac} - {g}_{ad}{\rho }_{bc} - {g}_{bc}{\rho }_{ad}.
\]

nodes.proof: These equations follow from the commutators \( \left\lbrack  {{\Lambda }_{b}^{d},{\nabla }_{c}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \left\lbrack  {{\Lambda }_{b}^{e},{\Lambda }_{d}^{f}}\right\rbrack \) (equations (F.13) and (F.14)) and the definition of \( {\rho }_{ab} \) .
