nodes.content:
## 9. Time dependent orthonormal frame bundle for solutions to the Ricci flow

Now we consider a solution to the Ricci flow \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Let \( {\mathcal{M}}^{n} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) be the space-time manifold. We have the principal \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{R}}\right) \) - bundle

\[
\widetilde{\pi } : F\mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T)
\]

defined by \( \widetilde{\pi } \Doteq  \pi  \times  {\operatorname{id}}_{\lbrack 0, T)} \) . Recall that the time-dependent metric \( g\left( t\right) \) may be considered as a function

\[
g : F\mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  {\mathbb{S}}^{n \times  n}
\]

( \( {\mathbb{S}}^{n \times  n} \) are the symmetric \( n \times  n \) matrices). Consider the degenerate metric \( {\widetilde{g}}^{F} \) on \( F\mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) given by \( {\left. {\widetilde{g}}^{F}\right| }_{F\mathcal{M}\times \{ t\} } = {g}^{F}\left( t\right) \) , the metric on \( F\mathcal{M} \) induced by \( g\left( t\right) \) . That is,

\[
{\left. {\widetilde{g}}^{F}\right| }_{F\mathcal{M}\times \{ t\} }\left( {\left( {X, u}\right) ,\left( {Y, v}\right) }\right)  = {g}^{F}\left( t\right) \left( {X, Y}\right)
\]

for \( X, Y \in  T\left( {F\mathcal{M}}\right) \) and \( u, v \in  \mathbb{R} \) . We have the vector fields \( \left\{  {\nabla }_{a}\right\}  ,\left\{  {\Lambda }_{a}^{b}\right\} \) , and \( \left\{  {\rho }_{ab}\right\} \) , which are all tangent to \( F\mathcal{M} \times  \{ t\} \) for each \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

Consider the subbundle

\[
O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \Doteq  \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{t \in  \lbrack 0, T)}}O{\mathcal{M}}_{g\left( t\right) } \times  \{ t\}  = {g}^{-1}\left( I\right)  \subset  F\mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T).
\]

The time-like vector field \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t} \) is not always tangent to \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) , unless \( g\left( t\right) \) is independent of time; however, there is a canonical way to modify it so that it becomes tangent to \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) .

The vector field \( {\nabla }_{t} \) restricted to \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \subset  F\mathcal{M} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) is the unique vector field that is tangent to the subbundle \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) and such that \( {\nabla }_{t} - \frac{\partial }{\partial t} \) is space-like (tangent to \( F\mathcal{M} \times  \{ t\} \) ), vertical, and perpendicular to each \( O{\mathcal{M}}_{g\left( t\right) } \subset  F\mathcal{M} \) .

nodes.proof:
On \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) we have \( {g}_{ab} = {\delta }_{ab} \) , which we shall use a few times below. Now let's look carefully at the conditions.

(1) Since \( {\nabla }_{t} - \frac{\partial }{\partial t} \) is space-like and vertical, it is of the form

\[
{\nabla }_{t} - \frac{\partial }{\partial t} = {\alpha }_{c}^{d}{\Lambda }_{d}^{c}
\]

where \( {\alpha }_{c}^{d} \) are functions on \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) .

(2) Since \( {\nabla }_{t} - \frac{\partial }{\partial t} \) is perpendicular to the subbundles \( O{\mathcal{M}}_{g\left( t\right) } \) , we need

\[
0 = \left\langle  {{\rho }_{ab},{\alpha }_{c}^{d}{\Lambda }_{d}^{c}}\right\rangle   = {\alpha }_{a}^{b} - {\alpha }_{b}^{a}
\]

and hence \( \alpha \) is symmetric.

(3) Now since \( {\nabla }_{t} \) is tangent to \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) , we have \( {\nabla }_{t}{g}_{ab} = 0 \) . Thus

\[
0 = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ab} + {\alpha }_{a}^{d}{g}_{bd} + {\alpha }_{b}^{c}{g}_{ac}
\]

\[
=  - 2{R}_{ab} + {\alpha }_{a}^{b} + {\alpha }_{b}^{a}.
\]

Hence \( {\alpha }_{a}^{b} = {R}_{ab} \) since \( \alpha \) is symmetric.

Thus we must have that \( {\nabla }_{t} - \frac{\partial }{\partial t} = {R}_{ab}{\Lambda }_{b}^{a} \) . Conversely, if \( {\nabla }_{t} \) is defined this way, then it satisfies all of the above properties.

and if \( V \) is a 2-tensor, then

\[
{\nabla }_{t}{V}_{ab} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{V}_{ab} + {R}_{ac}{g}^{cd}{V}_{db} + {R}_{bc}{g}^{cd}{V}_{ad}.
\]

In general, if \( U \) is a time-dependent \( \left( {p, q}\right) \) -tensor, then

\[
{\nabla }_{t}{U}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}}^{{a}_{1}\cdots {a}_{q}} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{U}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}}^{{a}_{1}\cdots {a}_{q}} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{p}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{c, d = 1}}^{n}{R}_{{b}_{j}c}{g}^{cd}{U}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{j - 1}d{b}_{j + 1}\cdots {b}_{p}}^{{a}_{1}\cdots {a}_{q}}
\]

(F.20)

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{q}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{c, d = 1}}^{n}{g}^{{a}_{i}c}{R}_{d}^{c}{U}_{{b}_{1}\cdots {b}_{p}}^{{a}_{1}\cdots {a}_{i - 1}d{a}_{i + 1}\cdots {a}_{q}}.
\]

nodes.proof:
By Lemma F. 8,

\[
{\Lambda }_{c}^{d}{V}_{a} = {y}_{c}^{i}{\delta }_{a}^{d}{V}_{i} = {\delta }_{a}^{d}{V}_{c}
\]

and so the first equation follows immediately:

\[
{\nabla }_{t}{V}_{a} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{V}_{a} + {R}_{db}{g}^{bc}{\Lambda }_{c}^{d}{V}_{a} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{V}_{a} + {R}_{ab}{g}^{bc}{V}_{c}.
\]

Again by Lemma F. 8 we have

\[
{\Lambda }_{c}^{d}{V}_{ab} = {\delta }_{a}^{d}{V}_{cb} + {\delta }_{b}^{d}{V}_{ac},
\]

and so

\[
{\nabla }_{t}{V}_{ab} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{V}_{ab} + {R}_{de}{g}^{ec}{\Lambda }_{c}^{d}{V}_{ab} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{V}_{ab} + {R}_{ae}{g}^{ec}{V}_{cb} + {R}_{be}{g}^{ec}{V}_{ac}.
\]

The equation for general tensors follows similarly.

In particular,

(F.21)

\[
{\nabla }_{t}{g}_{ab} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ab} + {R}_{ac}{g}^{cd}{g}_{db} + {R}_{bc}{g}^{cd}{g}_{ad} = 0.
\]

This agrees with the fact that \( {\nabla }_{t} \) is tangent to \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) .

We now define the Laplacian (or Laplace operator)

(F.22)

\[
\Delta  \Doteq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{e = 1}}^{n}{\nabla }_{e}{\nabla }_{e}
\]

acting on vector-valued functions on \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) . This corresponds to the rough Laplacian \( \Delta  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j = 1}}^{n}{g}^{ij}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j} \) acting on tensors on \( \mathcal{M} \) . Using (see Lemma 6.15 on p. 179 in Volume One)

(F.23)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{{ijk}\ell } = \Delta {R}_{{ijk}\ell } + 2\left( {{B}_{{ijk}\ell } - {B}_{{ij}\ell k} + {B}_{{ikj}\ell } - {B}_{i\ell {jk}}}\right)
\]

\[
- \left( {{R}_{i}^{p}{R}_{{pjk}\ell } + {R}_{j}^{p}{R}_{{ipk}\ell } + {R}_{k}^{p}{R}_{{ijp}\ell } + {R}_{\ell }^{p}{R}_{ijkp}}\right) ,
\]

(F.20), and (F.19), we can calculate the evolution equations of \( {R}_{abcd} \) and \( {R}_{ab} \) , obtaining

(F.24)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{abcd} = 2\left( {{B}_{abcd} - {B}_{abdc} + {B}_{acbd} - {B}_{adbc}}\right) ,
\]

where \( {B}_{abcd} =  - {R}_{aebf}{R}_{cedf} \) , and

(F.25)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{ab} = 2{R}_{acdb}{R}_{cd}.
\]

REMARK F.34. Note that equation (F.24) matches with equation (6.21) of Volume One, which was obtained by Uhlenbeck's trick. In Uhlenbeck's trick one evolves a frame by (equation (6.18a) of Volume One)

(F.26)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{Y}_{a} = \operatorname{Rc}\left( {Y}_{a}\right)  = {R}_{ab}{g}^{bc}{Y}_{c}.
\]

Note that in coordinates on the frame bundle, this says

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{y}_{a}^{k}\left( Y\right)  = {R}_{ab}{g}^{bc}{y}_{c}^{k}\left( Y\right) .
\]

This is equivalent to equation (6.19a) of Volume One: \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\iota  = \operatorname{Rc} \circ  \iota \) for a bundle isomorphism \( \iota  : V \rightarrow  {TM} \) . One computes that under the Ricci flow \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left\lbrack  {g\left( {{Y}_{a},{Y}_{b}}\right) }\right\rbrack   = 0 \) . In particular, if a frame is initially orthonormal, then it remains so. The path \( \gamma \left( t\right)  \Doteq  \left( {Y\left( t\right) , t}\right) \) lies in \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) so that \( \frac{d}{dt}\gamma \left( t\right)  \in \; T\left( {O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}}\right) \) . We claim \( \frac{d}{dt}\gamma \left( t\right)  = {\nabla }_{t} \) . To see this, we first note that

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\gamma \left( t\right)  = \operatorname{Rc}\left( Y\right)  + \frac{\partial }{\partial t}.
\]

In coordinates this is

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\gamma \left( t\right)  = {R}_{ab}{g}^{bc}{y}_{c}^{k}\left( Y\right) {\left. \frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{a}^{k}}\right| }_{\gamma \left( t\right) } + {\left. \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\right| }_{\gamma \left( t\right) }
\]

\[
= {R}_{ab}{g}^{bc}{\left. {\Lambda }_{c}^{a}\right| }_{\gamma \left( t\right) } + {\left. \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\right| }_{\gamma \left( t\right) }
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{t}\text{ . }
\]

Thus the time-derivative \( {\nabla }_{t} \) defined by (F.19) corresponds to taking the time-derivative \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left\lbrack  {U\left( {{Y}_{{a}_{1}},\ldots ,{Y}_{{a}_{p}}}\right) }\right\rbrack \) of a tensor where \( {Y}_{{a}_{i}} \) satisfy (F.26). For example, the terms in \( \left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \frac{\partial }{\partial t}}\right) \mathrm{{Rm}} \) match with those in \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\iota }^{ * }\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right)  - \; {\iota }^{ * }\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\mathrm{{Rm}}}\right) \) as in the proof of Lemma 6.22 of Volume One.

nodes.content:
LEMMA F.35. On \( O\widetilde{\mathcal{M}} \) we have the commutators

\[
\left\lbrack  {{\nabla }_{t},{\nabla }_{a}}\right\rbrack   = {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}{\rho }_{bc} + {R}_{ac}{\nabla }_{c}
\]

and

\[
\left\lbrack  {\Delta ,{\nabla }_{a}}\right\rbrack   = {R}_{eadc}{\nabla }_{e}{\rho }_{cd} + {R}_{ad}{\nabla }_{d} + {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}{\rho }_{bc},
\]

which imply

(F.27)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{a} - {\nabla }_{a}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right)  = {R}_{abcd}{\nabla }_{b}{\rho }_{cd}.
\]

nodes.proof:
Since

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\Gamma }_{ij}^{k} = {g}^{k\ell }\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{j\ell } + {\nabla }_{j}{R}_{i\ell } - {\nabla }_{\ell }{R}_{ij}}\right)
\]

for Ricci flow, we first calculate

\[
\left\lbrack  {\frac{\partial }{\partial t},{\nabla }_{a}}\right\rbrack   =  - \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}}\right) {y}_{a}^{i}{y}_{b}^{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{b}^{k}}
\]

\[
= {g}^{k\ell }\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{j\ell } - {\nabla }_{j}{R}_{i\ell } - {\nabla }_{\ell }{R}_{ij}}\right) {y}_{a}^{i}{y}_{b}^{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{b}^{k}}
\]

\[
= {y}_{c}^{\ell }{y}_{d}^{k}{g}^{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{j\ell } + {\nabla }_{j}{R}_{i\ell } - {\nabla }_{\ell }{R}_{ij}}\right) {y}_{a}^{i}{y}_{b}^{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial {y}_{b}^{k}}
\]

\[
= {g}^{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bc} + {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac} - {\nabla }_{c}{R}_{ab}}\right) {\Lambda }_{d}^{b}.
\]

Together with the commutator for \( {\nabla }_{a} \) and \( {\Lambda }_{b}^{c} \) (equation (F.13)), this implies that

\[
\left\lbrack  {{\nabla }_{t},{\nabla }_{a}}\right\rbrack   = {g}^{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac} - {\nabla }_{c}{R}_{ab}}\right) {\Lambda }_{d}^{b} + {R}_{bc}{g}^{cd}{\delta }_{a}^{b}{\nabla }_{d}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}\left( {{g}^{cd}{\Lambda }_{d}^{b} - {g}^{bd}{\Lambda }_{d}^{c}}\right)  + {R}_{ac}{g}^{cd}{\nabla }_{d}
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}{\rho }_{bc} + {R}_{ac}{\nabla }_{c}.
\]

We next compute \( \left\lbrack  {\Delta ,{\nabla }_{a}}\right\rbrack \) . Using

\[
{\nabla }_{e}{\nabla }_{e}{\nabla }_{a} = {\nabla }_{e}\left( {\frac{1}{2}{R}_{eadc}{\rho }_{cd} + {\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{e}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{eadc}{\rho }_{cd} + \frac{1}{2}{R}_{eadc}{\nabla }_{e}{\rho }_{cd} + \left( {\frac{1}{2}{R}_{eadc}{\rho }_{cd} + {\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{e}}\right) {\nabla }_{e},
\]

we obtain

\[
\left\lbrack  {\Delta ,{\nabla }_{a}}\right\rbrack   = \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{eadc}{\rho }_{cd} + \frac{1}{2}{R}_{eadc}{\nabla }_{e}{\rho }_{cd} + \frac{1}{2}{R}_{eadc}{\rho }_{cd}
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}{R}_{eadc}{\nabla }_{e}{\rho }_{cd} + \frac{1}{2}{R}_{eadc}\left( {{g}_{ce}{\nabla }_{d} - {g}_{de}{\nabla }_{c}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{eadc}{\rho }_{cd} + \frac{1}{2}{R}_{eadc}{\nabla }_{e}{\rho }_{cd}
\]

\[
= {R}_{eadc}{\nabla }_{e}{\rho }_{cd} + {R}_{ad}{\nabla }_{d} + \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{eadc}{\rho }_{cd}.
\]

By the second Bianchi identity,

\[
{\nabla }_{e}{R}_{eadc} = {\nabla }_{e}{R}_{dcea} = {\nabla }_{c}{R}_{da} - {\nabla }_{d}{R}_{ca}.
\]

Since \( {\rho }_{cd} =  - {\rho }_{dc} \) , this implies

(F.28)

\[
\Delta {\nabla }_{a} - {\nabla }_{a}\Delta  = {R}_{eadc}{\nabla }_{e}{\rho }_{cd} + {R}_{ad}{\nabla }_{d} + {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}{\rho }_{bc};
\]

hence,

(F.29)

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right) {\nabla }_{a} - {\nabla }_{a}\left( {{\nabla }_{t} - \Delta }\right)  = {R}_{abdc}{\nabla }_{b}{\rho }_{cd}.
\]

nodes.content:
Claim. If \( R \in  C\left( {S, h}\right) \) and \( v \in  S \) with \( R\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right)  = h \) , then \( {R}^{2}\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right)  \geq  0 \) .

Clearly, \( {R}^{2}\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right)  \geq  0 \) . We plan to establish the inequality by showing that the second summand is nonnegative as well:

\[
2{R}^{\# }\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right)  =  - \operatorname{tr}\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{v}R{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{v}}R}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Using that \( S \) is invariant under \( {\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{{\mathrm{G}}_{\mathbb{C}}} \) we deduce that

\[
h \leq  R\left( {{\operatorname{Ad}}_{\exp \left( {tx}\right) }v,{\operatorname{Ad}}_{\exp \left( {t\bar{x}}\right) }\bar{v}}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathfrak{g}{ \otimes  }_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C} \) and for all \( t \) and with equality at \( t = 0 \) . Recall that \( {\operatorname{Ad}}_{\exp \left( {tx}\right) } = \; \exp \left( {t{\operatorname{ad}}_{x}}\right) \) . Thus differentiating twice with respect to \( t \) and evaluating at 0 gives

\[
0 \leq  {2R}\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{x}v,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{x}}\bar{v}}\right)  + R\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{x}{\operatorname{ad}}_{x}v,\bar{v}}\right)  + R\left( {v,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{x}}{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{x}}\bar{v}}\right)
\]

If we replace \( x \) by \( {ix} \) , it is easy to see that the first summand in the above inequality remains unchanged while the other two summands change their sign. Therefore

(1)

\[
0 \leq  R\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{x}v,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{x}}\bar{v}}\right)  = R\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{v}x,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{v}}\bar{x}}\right) \text{ for all }x \in  \mathfrak{g}{ \otimes  }_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C}\text{ . }
\]

In other words the hermitian operator \( - {\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{v}}R{\operatorname{ad}}_{v} \) and its conjugate \( - {\operatorname{ad}}_{v}R{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{v}} \) on the unitary vectorspace \( \mathfrak{g}{ \otimes  }_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C} \) are nonnegative. Recall that we plan to show \( \operatorname{tr}\left( {-{\operatorname{ad}}_{v}R{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{v}}R}\right)  \geq  0 \) . It is an elementray well known lemma that the scalar product of two nonnegative hermitian matrices is nonnegative. By a slight extension of this lemma it suffices to show that the operator \( R \) induces a nonnegative sesquilinear form on the image of the first operator \( - {\operatorname{ad}}_{v}R{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{v}} \) . Clearly the image is contained in the image of \( {\operatorname{ad}}_{v} \) and by [1] \( R \) is indeed nonnegative on it which completes the proof of the claim.

Theorem 2.1. Suppose \( C\left( t\right)  \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( \mathfrak{g}\right) \) is a family of closed convex sets which is invariant under the above representation of \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) . We assume that \( C \) is invariant under the ODE

\[
{\mathrm{{Hk}}}^{\prime } = 2\left( {\mathrm{{Hk}}\operatorname{pr}\mathrm{{Hk}} + {\mathrm{{Hk}}}^{\# }}\right)
\]

where \( \operatorname{pr} : \mathfrak{{iso}}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)  \rightarrow  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) is the orthogonal projection, \( \mathrm{H}\mathrm{k}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{r}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{k} \) is the composition of the three endomorphisms and

\[
\left\langle  {{\mathrm{{Hk}}}^{\# }A, B}\right\rangle   =  - \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{ \cdot  }^{tr}A\mathrm{{Hk}}{\operatorname{ad}}_{ \cdot  }^{tr}B\mathrm{{Hk}}}\right) .
\]

Then \( C\left( t\right) \) defines a Ricci flow invariant condition, that is, if \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \left( {t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) }\right) \) is a compact solution to the Ricci flow and \( \operatorname{Hk}\left( {p,0}\right)  \in  C\left( 0\right) \) for all \( p \in  M \) then \( \mathrm{{Hk}}\left( {p, t}\right)  \in  C\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \) .

We assume that \( C \) is invariant under the ODE \[ {\mathrm{{Hk}}}^{\prime } = 2\left( {\mathrm{{Hk}}\operatorname{pr}\mathrm{{Hk}} + {\mathrm{{Hk}}}^{\# }}\right) \] where \( \oper...

nodes.proof:
Since \( C\left( s\right)  \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( \mathfrak{g}\right) \) is invariant under \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) we can identify it naturally with a subset of \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{iso}}\left( {{T}_{p}M, g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right. \) for all \( \left( {p, t}\right)  \in  N \) .

It suffices to prove that \( {S}_{k}\left( {p, t}\right)  \in  C\left( t\right) \left( {t \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{k}, T - \frac{1}{k}}\right\rbrack  }\right) \) for a sequence \( {S}_{k} \) as in the lemma. We assume, on the contrary, that for some minimal \( {t}_{0} > \frac{1}{k} \) we can find some \( p \in  M \) such that \( {S}_{k}\left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right) \) is contained in the boundary of \( C\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) .

Because of the minimal choice of \( {t}_{0} \) we know that \( {S}_{k}\left( {q, t}\right)  \in  C\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \leq  {t}_{0} \) and \( q \in  M \) . To get a contradiction we will show that \( {S}_{k}\left( {p,{t}_{0} - h}\right)  \notin  C\left( {{t}_{0} - h}\right) \) for small positive \( h \) .

For small \( h \geq  0 \) and \( q \in  M \) we define \( H\left( s\right)  \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{iso}}\left( {{T}_{q}, g\left( {{t}_{0} - h}\right) }\right) }\right) \) as the solution of the ODE \( {H}^{\prime } = 2\left( {H\operatorname{pr}H + {H}^{\# }}\right) \) with \( H\left( 0\right)  = {S}_{k}\left( {{t}_{0} - h}\right) \) . Since the family \( C\left( t\right) \) is invariant under the ODE we know that \( {P}_{k}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - h}\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} H\left( h\right)  \in  C\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) . By construction

\[
{\nabla }_{\frac{\partial }{\partial t}}{P}_{k}\left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right)  = \Delta {P}_{k}\left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right)  + {\varepsilon }_{k}\left( {T - {P}_{k}}\right) \left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

Using that \( {P}_{k}\left( {q,{t}_{0}}\right)  = {S}_{k}\left( {q,{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  C\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) and that \( C\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) is invariant under the representation of \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) it is immediate that \( \Delta {P}_{k}\left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right)  = {T}_{{P}_{k}\left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right) }C\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) . Furthermore we know by construction that \( {\varepsilon }_{k}\left( {T - {P}_{k}}\right) \left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right) \) is contained in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{{P}_{k}\left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right) }C\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) . We deduce that \( {P}_{k}\left( {p,{t}_{0} - h}\right)  \notin  C\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) for small positive \( h \) - a contradiction.

Lemma 2.3. Any tensor Hk on \( N \) satisfying

\[
{\nabla }_{\frac{\partial }{\partial t}}\mathrm{{Hk}} = \Delta \mathrm{{Hk}} + 2\left( {\mathrm{{Hk}}\operatorname{pr}\mathrm{{Hk}} + {\mathrm{{Hk}}}^{\# }}\right)
\]

can be approximated by a sequence \( {S}_{k} \) of tensors on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{k}, T - \frac{1}{k}}\right\rbrack \) satisfying

\[
{\nabla }_{\frac{\partial }{\partial t}}{S}_{k} = \Delta {S}_{k} + 2\left( {{S}_{k}\operatorname{pr}{S}_{k} + {S}_{k}^{\# }}\right)  + {\varepsilon }_{k}\left( {T - {S}_{k}}\right)
\]

and \( S\left( {p,\frac{1}{k}}\right) \) represents an interior point of \( C\left( \frac{1}{k}\right) \) and \( {\varepsilon }_{k} > 0 \) converges to 0 .

Clearly one can find an initial value \( S\left( {p,\frac{1}{k}}\right)  \in  \operatorname{Int}\left( {C{\delta }_{k}}\right) \) such that \( S\left( {p,\frac{1}{k}}\right)  - \; \operatorname{Hk}\left( {p,\frac{1}{k}}\right) \left( {p \in  M}\right) \) converges to 0 in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology. Moreover, \( S\left( {p,\frac{1}{k}}\right) \) is a solution if and only if \( {S}_{k} - \mathrm{{Hk}} \) is a solution of an equation with the obvious modifications. Since one can prove similarly to Shi a priori estimates for the corresponding linearized equation, it follows that a solution of the initial value problem exists.

nodes.content:
Remark 2.4. a) If one carries out everything in this section in the special case that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a Kähler manifold, then the holonomy group of the connection \( \nabla \) is isomorphic to a subgroup of \( \mathrm{U}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right)  \rtimes  {T}_{p}M \subset  \mathrm{{SO}}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right)  \rtimes  {T}_{p}M \) and the image of the Harnack operator is contained in the Lie subalgebra \( {\mathfrak{g}}^{\prime } \) of this group. One can then formulate and prove an analogous statement for Harnack operators of Kähler manifolds.

b) Let \( \mathrm{{Hk}} \) be a Harnack operator and \( R = {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{\mid {so}\left( n\right) } \) . A simple computation shows that the trace Harnack inequality is equivalent to

\[
\inf \left\{  {\operatorname{tr}\left( {{\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{v}{\mathrm{{HkAd}}}_{v}^{tr}}\right)  \mid  v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \subset  \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) }\right\}   - \operatorname{tr}\left( R\right)  \geq  0.
\]

If \( R \) has positive Ricci curvature, then there is a unique \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that \( {\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{v}\mathrm{{Hk}}{\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{v}^{tr} \) has minimal trace.

c) The reason for the somewhat complicated approach toward the maximum principle is that it is in general not true that a convex set \( C\left( t\right) \) is contained in the interior of another slightly larger convex set \( C \) which is also invariant under the action of \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) , cf. next subsection. This is of course related to the fact that the connection is not compatible with a metric on the space of curvature tensors.

Suppose, on the contrary, we can find \( {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i} \in  C \) and \( {v}_{i} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that the Ricci curvature \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{i} \) of \( {\operatorname{Hk}}_{i \mid  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right)  \times  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) } \) satisfies the following \( \left( {i = 1,2}\right)  : {\operatorname{Ric}}_{1}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{1}}\right)  > \) 0 and \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{2}}\right)  < 0 \) . Put \( {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i}\left( t\right)  = {\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{t{v}_{i}}{\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i}{\mathrm{{Ad}}}_{t{v}_{i}}^{tr} \) . It is straightforward to check that the trace \( \operatorname{tr}\left( {{\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i}\left( t\right) }\right) \) converges quadratically in \( t \) to \( {\left( -1\right) }^{i + 1}\infty \) as \( t \rightarrow  \infty \; \left( {i = 1,2}\right) \) . The element \( {X}_{i} = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{i}\left( t\right) }{{t}^{2}} \) is an element in the cone at infinity

\[
{\partial }_{\infty }C \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\lambda  \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{C}{\lambda }
\]

of \( C \) . We know \( \operatorname{tr}\left( {X}_{1}\right)  > 0,\operatorname{tr}\left( {X}_{2}\right)  < 0 \) and it is straightforward to check \( {X}_{i} \in  W \) . Moreover the operator \( {X}_{i} \) has \( {v}_{i} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) in its kernel.

Clearly the cone \( {\partial }_{\infty }C \) is invariant under the the representation of \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) . The barry center of the \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) -orbit of \( {X}_{1} \) (resp. \( {X}_{2} \) ) is a positive (resp. negative) multiple of the orthogonal projection of \( \mathfrak{g} \) to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) .

Under \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) the vectorspace \( W \) decomposes into a one dimensional trivial and an irreducible representation. Since \( {X}_{i} \in  W \) itself is not a multiple of the orthogonal projection we can also find a traceless operator \( X \in  {\partial }_{\infty }C \cap  W \) . Clearly this implies \( W \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) .

The quotient space \( V/W \) decomposes under \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) in two inequivalent irreducible nontrivial subrepresentations.

Using that \( C \) has maximal dimension we can find \( \mathrm{{Hk}} \in  C \) such that for some \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n},\left( {{\operatorname{Ad}}_{v}{\mathrm{{HkAd}}}_{v}^{tr} - \mathrm{{Hk}}}\right)  \in  V \) projects to an element in \( V/W \) which is not contained in a nontrivial invariant subspace.

For each \( t \) we choose \( Y\left( t\right)  \in  W \) such that \( L\left( t\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\operatorname{Ad}}_{t}v\operatorname{Hk}{\operatorname{Ad}}_{t}{v}^{tr} - Y\left( t\right) \) has minimal norm. It then follows that the norm of \( L \) increases linearly and \( {L}_{\infty } \mathrel{\text{ := }} \; \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{L\left( t\right) }{t} \in  V \cap  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) corresponds in \( V/W \) to an element that does not lie in a nontrivial invariant subspace.

This in turn shows \( V \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) and hence \( C \) is of the form \( {C}^{\prime } + V \) .

Lemma 2.6. Let \( C \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( \mathfrak{g}\right) \) be a convex subset of maximal dimension which is invariant under the representation of \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) . Suppose there is an element \( \mathrm{{Hk}} \in \; C \) such that \( R \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{\mid \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right)  \times  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) } \) satisfies for some \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} : \operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  = 0 \) and \( R\left( {\cdot , v, v, \cdot  }\right)  \neq  0 \) . Then for any family of convex sets \( C\left( t\right) \) which is invariant under the ODE, invariant under \( \operatorname{Iso}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) with \( C\left( 0\right)  = C \) we have \( C\left( t\right)  = C\left( t\right)  + V \) for all \( t > 0 \) .

The lemma shows for example that one can not prove a Harnack inequality in the class of 3-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature evolving under the Ricci flow by means of the maximum principle of Theorem 2.1

It is straightforward to check that \( X \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\operatorname{Ad}}_{tv}{\operatorname{HkAd}}_{vt}^{tr}}{{t}^{2}} \) is a traceless operator in \( W \) . Clearly \( X \in  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) .

Since the traceless operators \( {W}^{\prime } \subset  W \) form an irreducible subspace we deduce that \( {W}^{\prime } \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C \) . Let \( C\left( t\right) \) be as in the lemma.

Consider the element \( - \mathrm{{id}} \in  O\left( n\right) \) and let \( \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right)  \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( \mathfrak{g}\right) \) denote the fixed point set of - id. Notice that \( \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right) \) is still invariant under \( \operatorname{SO}\left( n\right) \) . It is easy to see that \( \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-{id}}\right)  \cap  C \) has maximal dimension in \( \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right) \) . Moreover the set \( \widetilde{C}\left( t\right)  = C\left( t\right)  \cap  \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right) \) is invariant under the ODE.

Notice that \( \widetilde{C}\left( 0\right) \) contains a subset of the form \( {\lambda I} + {W}^{\prime } \) where \( I \) is the orthogonal projection of \( \mathfrak{g} \) to \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) for some \( \lambda \) . If we evolve this set under the ODE we see that \( {W}^{\prime } \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \) .

Thus \( \widetilde{C}\left( t\right)  = \widetilde{C}{\left( t\right) }^{\prime } + {W}^{\prime } \) where \( \widetilde{C}{\left( t\right) }^{\prime } \subset  {W}^{\prime  \bot  } \cap  \operatorname{Fix}\left( {-\mathrm{{id}}}\right) \) is convex.

We may assume that the norm of \( {\mathrm{{Hk}}}_{\mid \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right)  \times  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) } \) is bounded by some a priori constant for all \( \mathrm{{Hk}} \in  C\left( t\right) \) . This in turn implies that a sequence in \( \widetilde{C}{\left( t\right) }^{\prime } \) tends to \( \infty \) if and only if its trace is unbounded.

Using that \( \widetilde{C}\left( t\right) \) is invariant under the ODE and that \( {C}^{\prime }\left( t\right) \) has full dimension it is easy to see that for all positive \( t \) there are endomorphisms with arbitrary small as well as endomorphisms with arbitrary large trace in \( \widetilde{C}\left( t\right) \) and hence in \( \widetilde{C}{\left( t\right) }^{\prime } \) . Therefore \( W \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }\widetilde{C}\left( t\right) \) . This implies as before \( V \subset  {\partial }_{\infty }C\left( t\right) \) for all positive \( t \) as claimed.

We extend the maps \( \mathfrak{g} \times  \mathfrak{g} \rightarrow  \mathfrak{g},\left( {x, v}\right)  \mapsto  {\operatorname{ad}}_{x}^{tr}v \) to a complex bilinear map \( {\mathfrak{g}}_{\mathbb{C}} \times  {\mathfrak{g}}_{\mathbb{C}} \rightarrow  {\mathfrak{g}}_{\mathbb{C}} \) which we also denote by \( \left( {x, v}\right)  \mapsto  {\operatorname{ad}}_{x}^{tr}v \) .

Using that \( S \) is invariant under \( {\operatorname{Ad}}_{{\mathrm{G}}_{\mathbb{C}}}^{tr} \) we deduce that for any \( x \in  \mathfrak{g}{ \otimes  }_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C} \) we have for all \( t \in  \mathbb{R} \)

\[
h \leq  R\left( {{\operatorname{Ad}}_{\exp \left( {tx}\right) }^{tr}v,{\operatorname{Ad}}_{\exp \left( {t\bar{x}}\right) }^{tr}\bar{v}}\right)

\[

Therefore

Remark 3.2. a) Using Remark 2.4 and the proposition in the case that \( \mathfrak{g} \) is given by the Lie algebra of \( \mathrm{U}\left( n\right)  \rtimes  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) one can derive Harnack inequalities for Kähler manifolds. The complexification of \( \mathrm{U}\left( n\right)  \rtimes  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) is given by \( \operatorname{GL}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right)  \rtimes \; \left( {{\mathbb{C}}^{n} \oplus  {\mathbb{C}}^{n}}\right) \) , where \( \mathrm{{GL}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) acts in the standard way on the first summand and by \( \left( {A, v}\right)  \mapsto  {\left( {\bar{A}}^{tr}\right) }^{-1}v \) on the second \( {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \) -summand. Thus the set

\[
S \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left\{  {\left( {A, v,0}\right)  \in  \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right)  \times  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \times  {\mathbb{C}}^{n} \mid  \operatorname{rank}\left( A\right)  = 1, v \in  A\left( {\mathbb{C}}^{n}\right) }\right\}  ,
\]

is invariant under the coadjoint representation. This gives a Harnack inequality for Kähler manifolds with positive bisectional curvature whose trace form is similar to Cao's [1992] Harnack inequality.

b) Let \( \left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) \) be as in the proposition and let \( G : \mathfrak{g} \rightarrow  \mathfrak{g} \) denote a selfadjoint positive endomorphism. Put \( g\left( {v, w}\right)  = \langle  \cdot  , G \cdot  \rangle \) . The ODE \( {R}^{\prime } = {R}^{{\# }_{g}} \) corresponding to the metric Lie algebra \( \left( {\mathfrak{g}, g}\right) \) is obtained by pulling back the corresponding ODE for the metric Lie algebra \( \left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) \) under the linear map \( {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{g}, g}\right)  \rightarrow  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{g},\langle \cdot , \cdot  \rangle }\right) , R \mapsto  R{G}^{-1} \) . Thus \( {R}^{{\# }_{g}} = {\left( R{G}^{-1}\right) }^{\# } \cdot  G \) .

nodes.section_title: 5. KÄHLER MANIFOLDS WITH POSITIVE ORTHOGONAL BISECTIONAL CURVATURE
nodes.content: Lemma 5.1. Let \( M \) be a compact Kähler manifold with nonnegative orthogonal bisectional curvature. Then the Bochner operator on two forms is nonnegative. In particular any harmonic two form is parallel. If \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has positive orthogonal bisectional curvature, then \( {H}^{2}\left( {M,\mathbb{R}}\right)  \cong  \mathbb{R} \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: Lemma 5.1. Let \( M \) be a compact Kähler manifold with nonnegative orthogonal bisectional curvature. Then the Bochner operator on two forms is nonnegative. In particular any harmonic two form is parallel. If \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has positive orthogonal bisectional curvature, then \( {H}^{2}\left( {M,\mathbb{R}}\right) \cong \mathbb{R} \) .

nodes.proof:
For a Riemannian manifold the Bochner operator on two forms is given by \( \mathcal{R} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \operatorname{Ric} \land  \mathrm{{id}} - R \) where \( R \) is the curvature operator \( \operatorname{Ric} \) is the Ricci curvature and \( \operatorname{Ric} \land  \operatorname{id}\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}\left( {e}_{i}\right)  \land  {e}_{j} + {e}_{i} \land  \operatorname{Ric}\left( {e}_{j}\right) }\right) \) . Compare for example [Ni and Wilking,2009]. If \( R \) is the curvature operator of a Kähler manifold, then it is easy to see that Ric \( \land \) id leaves the Lie algebra \( \mathfrak{u}\left( n\right)  \subset  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( {2n}\right) \) invariant. Since the orthogonal complement of \( \mathfrak{u}{\left( n\right) }^{ \bot  } \) is contained in kernel of \( R \) , we can show \( {\mathcal{R}}_{\mid \mathfrak{u}{\left( n\right) }^{ \bot  }} \geq  0 \) by establishing

Claim 1. For a Kähler manifold with nonnegative orthogonal bisectional curvature the following holds: If \( {v}_{1},{v}_{2} \in  {T}_{p}M \) are unit vectors with \( \mathbb{C}{v}_{1} \bot  \mathbb{C}{v}_{2} \) , then \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{1}}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{2}}\right)  \geq  0. \)

We extend \( {v}_{1},{v}_{2} \) to a complex orthonormal basis \( {v}_{1},\ldots ,{v}_{n} \) of \( {T}_{p}M \) . Then

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{1}}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{2}}\right)  = K\left( {{v}_{1}, i{v}_{1}}\right)  + {2K}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}\right)  + {2K}\left( {{v}_{1}, i{v}_{2}}\right)  + K\left( {{v}_{2}, i{v}_{2}}\right)  +
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 3}}^{n}K\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{j}}\right)  + K\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{j}}\right)  + K\left( {{v}_{1}, i{v}_{j}}\right)  + K\left( {{v}_{2}, i{v}_{j}}\right)
\]

Since \( R \) has nonnegative orthogonal bisectional curvature we know \( K\left( {{v}_{j},{v}_{k}}\right)  + \; K\left( {{v}_{j}, i{v}_{k}}\right)  \geq  0 \) for \( k \neq  l \) . In other words it suffices to show that the first four summands add up to a nonnegative number. This in turn is equivalent to establishing the claim for complex surfaces. But if \( n = 2 \) , then \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{1}}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{2}}\right)  = \; \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{scal} \geq  0. \)

We can finish the proof of the first part of Lemma by establishing

Claim 2. \( {\mathcal{R}}_{\mid \mathfrak{u}\left( n\right) } \geq  0 \) .

Suppose \( \omega  \in  \mathfrak{u}\left( n\right) \) is an eigenvector of \( \mathcal{R} \) . We can find an orthonormal basis \( {v}_{1},\cdots ,{v}_{n} \) with \( \mathbb{C}{v}_{j} \bot  \mathbb{C}{v}_{k} \) for \( j \neq  k \) and real numbers \( {\lambda }_{i} \) such that \( \omega \) is given by \( \omega  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{\lambda }_{j}{v}_{j} \land  i{v}_{j} \) . One now checks by straightforward computation

\[
2\langle \mathcal{R}\omega ,\omega \rangle  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  k}}^{n}\left( {{\lambda }_{j}^{2} + {\lambda }_{k}^{2}}\right) \left( {K\left( {{v}_{j},{v}_{k}}\right)  + K\left( {{v}_{j}, i{v}_{k}}\right) }\right)  - 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  k}}{\lambda }_{j} \cdot  {\lambda }_{k}R\left( {{v}_{j}, i{v}_{j},{v}_{k}, i{v}_{k}}\right)
\]

Since \( {v}_{j} \land  {v}_{k} + i{v}_{k} \land  i{v}_{j} \) and \( {v}_{j} \land  i{v}_{k} + i{v}_{j} \land  {v}_{k} \) are in the kernel of \( R \) it follows from the first Bianchi identity that \( R\left( {{v}_{j}, i{v}_{j},{v}_{k}, i{v}_{k}}\right)  = K\left( {{v}_{j}, i{v}_{k}}\right)  + K\left( {{v}_{j},{v}_{k}}\right) \) . Hence

\[
2\langle \mathcal{R}\omega ,\omega \rangle  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  k}}^{n}{\left( {\lambda }_{j} - {\lambda }_{k}\right) }^{2}\left( {K\left( {{v}_{j},{v}_{k}}\right)  + K\left( {{v}_{j}, i{v}_{k}}\right) }\right)
\]

which is nonnegative as each summand is nonnegative.

This shows that \( \mathcal{R} \) is nonnegative. Therefore any harmonic two form is parallel. If the orthogonal bisectional curvature is positive, it is easy to deduce that the kernel of \( \mathcal{R} \) is given by multiples of the Kähler form and thus any harmonic two form is a multiple of the Kähler form.

We let \( \langle W\rangle  \subset  {S}_{K}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{u}\left( n\right) }\right) \) denote the kernel of \( R \mapsto  \operatorname{Ric}\left( R\right) \) . For \( R \in  {S}_{K}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{u}\left( n\right) }\right) \) the orthogonal projection \( {R}_{W} \) of \( R \) to \( \langle W\rangle \) is called the (Kähler)-Weyl part of \( R \) . As in the real case \( \langle W\rangle \) is an irreducible module and analogously to [Böhm and Wilking,2008] one can show that \( D\left( t\right) \left( R\right) \) is independent of \( {R}_{W} \) . We let

\[
B\left( s\right) \left( {{R}_{1},{R}_{2}}\right)  = \frac{1}{4}\left( {D\left( s\right) \left( {{R}_{1} + {R}_{2}}\right)  - D\left( s\right) \left( {{R}_{1} - {R}_{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

denote the corresponding bilinear form. Since any Ricci tensor is the sum of commuting rank one tensors it suffices to prove the corresponding statement for \( B \) in the special case that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {R}_{1}\right) \) and \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {R}_{2}\right) \) are commuting rank 1 matrices. Clearly we may assume that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {R}_{1}\right) \) have 1 as an eigenvalue. Using the polarization

\[
B\left( s\right) \left( {{R}_{1},{R}_{2}}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\left( {D\left( s\right) \left( {{R}_{1} + {R}_{2}}\right)  - D\left( t\right) \left( {R}_{1}\right)  - D\left( s\right) \left( {R}_{2}\right) }\right) .
\]

we deduce that it suffices to prove the original statement for the following two special cases: The statement holds for one curvature operator for which \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( R\right) \) has rank 1 and the statement holds for one curvature operator for which \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( R\right) \) has rank 2 with 2 equal nonzero eigenvalues. In particular, it suffices to check that the statement holds in the case that \( R \) is the curvature operator \( {R}_{k} \) of \( {\mathbb{{CP}}}^{k} \times  {\mathbb{C}}^{n - k} \) , \( k = 1,\ldots , n \) .

It is straightforward to check that \( {D}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \left( R\right) \) and \( 2\operatorname{Ric} \star  \operatorname{Ric} \) have the same trace. Clearly this proves the formula for \( {R}_{k} \) in the case \( k = n \) .

Notice that \( {R}_{k}^{2} + {R}_{k}^{\# } = \left( {k + 1}\right) {R}_{k} \) . It is easy to see that \( {D}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) {\left( {R}_{k}\right) }_{\mid \mathfrak{u}\left( k\right) } \) is independent of \( n \) . Using that we know the formula in the case \( k = n \) we deduce \( {\left. {D}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) {\left( {R}_{k}\right) }_{\mid \mathfrak{u}\left( k\right) } = 2\operatorname{Ric} \star  {\operatorname{Ric}}_{\mid \mathfrak{u}\left( k\right) }\text{ . Moreover it is easy to see that both operators }\right| }_{v = 0} \) contain the subalgebra \( \mathfrak{u}\left( {n - k}\right) \) in their kernel. It remains to check that \( {D}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \left( {R}_{k}\right) \) restricted to \( {\left( \mathfrak{u}\left( n - k\right)  \oplus  \mathfrak{u}\left( k\right) \right) }^{ \bot  } \) vanishes. For symmetry reasons this restriction is given by a multiple of the identity. Combining this with the facts that \( {D}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \left( {R}_{k}\right) \) and \( 2\operatorname{Ric} \star  \operatorname{Ric} \) coincide on \( \mathfrak{u}\left( {n - k}\right)  \oplus  \mathfrak{u}\left( k\right) \) and have the same trace the lemma follows.

Claim. For some \( \varepsilon , p > 0 \) we have that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies \( {C}_{2}\left( p\right) \) (see Corollary 5.5 for a definition) for all \( t \in  \lbrack T - \varepsilon , T) \) .

By Lemma 4.1 we can find some small \( h \) such that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies \( C\left( {S, h}\right) \) , where \( S \subset  \mathfrak{{gl}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) is the set of rank 1 matrices which have 1 as an eigenvalue.

We argue by contradiction and assume that we can find \( {p}_{i} \rightarrow  0 \) and \( {t}_{i} \rightarrow  T \) such that \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{i}\right) }\right) \) does not satisfy \( {C}_{2}\left( {p}_{i}\right) \) . We rescale the manifold to have maximal curvature one. By an argument of Perelman which was written up by Sesum and Tian [2006] \( \left( {M,{\lambda }_{i}g\left( {t}_{i}\right) }\right) \) subconverges to a compact limit manifold \( \left( {M,{g}_{\infty }}\right) \) .

\( \left( {M,{g}_{\infty }}\right) \) is a Kähler manifold satisfying the curvature condition \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{1}{{\lambda }_{i}}C\left( {S, h}\right)  = \; C\left( {S,0}\right) \) . Recall that \( C\left( {S,0}\right) \) is the cone of curvature operators with nonnegative bisectional curvature. Thus \( \left( {M,{g}_{\infty }}\right) \) has nonnegative bisectional curvature and in particular nonnegative Ricci curvature. By compactness we can assume that \( {g}_{\infty } \) has a backward solution to the Ricci flow with nonnegative bisectional curvature. Since \( \left( {M,{g}_{\infty }}\right) \) is diffeomorphic to \( M \) we know from Lemma 5.1 that its second homology is isomorphic to \( \mathbb{R} \) . Thus \( \left( {M,{g}_{\infty }}\right) \) does not have any flat factors. Combining with the strong maximum principle we deduce that \( \left( {M,{g}_{\infty }}\right) \) has positive Ricci curvature. But this contradicts our choice of \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{i}\right) }\right) \) .

Theorem 5.6. Let \( S \subset  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) be an \( {\operatorname{Ad}}_{\mathrm{{SO}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) } \) -invariant subset and consider a solution to the Ricci flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , satisfying \( C\left( S\right) \) for all \( t \) . By choosing a linear isometry between \( \left( {{T}_{p}M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) and \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) we obtain a subset \( S\left( {p, t}\right)  \subset \; \mathfrak{{so}}\left( \left( {{T}_{p}M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \right) { \otimes  }_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C} \) corresponding to \( S \) for each \( \left( {p, t}\right) \) . Put

\[
N\left( {p, t}\right)  = \left\{  {X \in  S\left( {p, t}\right)  \mid  {R}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {X,\bar{X}}\right)  = 0}\right\}
\]

Then \( N\left( {p, t}\right) \) is invariant under parallel transport for \( t > 0 \) .

As usual with strong maximum principles we do not require that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is compact or complete. The methods used to derive the above theorem from Theorem 1 (and its proof) are due to Brendle and Schoen [2008]. In fact, Proposition 8 in that paper is the special case of the above theorem where \( S \) is given by the totally isotropic rank 2 matrices. The analogue of the above theorem for Kähler manifolds holds as well with the same proof.

A delicate part of Brendle and Schoen's proof of the strong maximum principle for isotropic curvature is that it does not just use the invariance of positive isotropic curvature but also the proof of the invariance by means of first and second variation formulas. This is here true as well.

In the following we can assume that \( S \) is invariant under scaling with positive numbers. Moreover we may assume that for \( X, Y \in  S \) there is some \( g \in  \mathrm{{SO}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) and \( \lambda  > 0 \) with \( {\operatorname{Ad}}_{g}X = {\lambda Y} \) . In fact otherwise we decompose \( S \) into subsets with this property and prove the theorem for each subset separately. Notice that these assumptions imply in particular that \( S \) is a submanifold with a transitive smooth action of \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right)  \times  {\mathbb{R}}_{ + } \) . Therefore \( S\left( {p, t}\right) \) defines a bundle over \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) whose totalspace we denote by \( T \) . We consider on \( T \) the function

\[
u : T \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}, u\left( v\right)  = {R}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right) .
\]

We lift the vectorfield \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t} \) horizontally to a vectorfield on \( T \) using the connection induced on \( T \) by the connection \( \nabla \) on \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) from section 2 . We denote this horizontal lift again by \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t} \) . Then

\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right)  = {\Delta }_{h}u + 2\left( {{R}^{2}\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right) }\right) ,
\]

where \( {\Delta }_{h}u \) is the horizontal Laplacian which is defined as follows. Choose in a neighborhood of \( \left( {p, t}\right) \) vectorfields \( {X}_{1},\ldots ,{X}_{n} \) tangential to \( M \) with \( g\left( t\right) \left( {{X}_{i},{X}_{j}}\right)  = \; {\delta }_{ij} \) and put \( {Y}_{j} = {\nabla }_{{X}_{i}}^{g\left( t\right) }{X}_{i} \) . Let \( {\widehat{X}}_{i} \) and \( {\widehat{Y}}_{i} \) denote the horizontal lifts of \( {X}_{i} \) and \( {Y}_{i} \) to \( T \) . Then \( {\Delta }_{h}u = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{n}{\widehat{X}}_{i}{\widehat{X}}_{i}u - {\widehat{Y}}_{i}u \) .

From the proof of the invariance in section 1 we can derive

\[
{R}_{g\left( t\right) }^{\# }\left( {v,\bar{v}}\right)  \geq  C\parallel R\parallel \inf \left\{  {\left. {\frac{{d}^{2}}{d{t}^{2}}u\left( {A{d}_{\exp \left( {tx}\right) }v}\right) }\right| \;x \in  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( {\left( {{T}_{p}M, g\left( t\right) }\right) ,\mathbb{C}}\right) ,\parallel x\parallel  \leq  1}\right\}
\]

for all \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) where \( C = C\left( n\right) \) is a constant. We now introduce coordinates on some relative compact subset \( U \subset  T \) , which have an extension to a neighborhood of \( \bar{U} \) . Then the corresponding function \( \widetilde{u} \) in local coordinates, which is defined on some open subset \( V \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) , satisfies

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{n}{\widetilde{X}}_{i}{\widetilde{X}}_{i}\widetilde{u} \leq   - K\inf \left\{  {\operatorname{Hess}\left( \widetilde{u}\right) \left( {a, a}\right)  \mid  a \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n},\parallel a\parallel  \leq  1}\right\}   + K\parallel \operatorname{grad}\left( \widetilde{u}\right) \parallel
\]

for some large constant \( K \) , where \( {\widetilde{X}}_{i} \) denote the corresponding vectorfields in coordinates. We can now apply Proposition 4 from [Brendle and Schoen, 2008], to see that the level set \( {\widetilde{u}}^{-1}\left( 0\right) \) is invariant under the (local) flows of the vectorfields \( {X}_{i} \) . Translating this back we obtain that the level set \( {u}^{-1}\left( 0\right) \) in \( T \) is invariant under spacial parallel translation.

## 1. Algebraic preliminaries

For a Euclidean vector space \( V \) we let \( {\Lambda }^{2}V \) denote the exterior product of \( V \) . We endow \( {\Lambda }^{2}V \) with its natural scalar product; if \( {e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n} \) is an orthonormal basis of \( V \) then \( {e}_{1} \land  {e}_{2},\ldots ,{e}_{n - 1} \land  {e}_{n} \) is an orthonormal basis of \( {\Lambda }^{2}V \) . Notice that two linear endomorphisms \( A, B \) of \( V \) induce a linear map

\[
A \land  B : {\Lambda }^{2}V \rightarrow  {\Lambda }^{2}V;v \land  w \mapsto  \frac{1}{2}\left( {A\left( v\right)  \land  B\left( w\right)  + B\left( v\right)  \land  A\left( w\right) }\right) .
\]

We will identify \( {\Lambda }^{2}{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) with the Lie algebra \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) by mapping the unit vector \( {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j} \) onto the linear map \( L\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}}\right) \) of rank two which is a rotation with angle \( \pi /2 \) in the plane spanned by \( {e}_{i} \) and \( {e}_{j} \) . Notice that under this identification the scalar product on \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) corresponds to \( \langle A, B\rangle  =  - 1/2\operatorname{tr}\left( {AB}\right) \) .

For \( n \geq  4 \) there is a natural decomposition of

\[
{S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)  = \langle I\rangle  \oplus  \left\langle  {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}\right\rangle   \oplus  \langle \mathrm{W}\rangle  \oplus  {\Lambda }^{4}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)
\]

into \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant, irreducible and pairwise inequivalent subspaces. An endomorphism \( \mathrm{R} \in  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) satisfies the first Bianchi identity if and only if \( \mathrm{R} \) is an element in \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)  = \langle I\rangle  \oplus  \left\langle  {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}\right\rangle   \oplus  \langle \mathrm{W}\rangle \) . Given a curvature operator \( \mathrm{R} \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) we let \( {\mathrm{R}}_{I},{\mathrm{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}} \) and \( {\mathrm{R}}_{\mathrm{W}} \) , denote the projections onto \( \langle I\rangle \) , \( \left\langle  {\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}\right\rangle \) and \( \langle \mathrm{W}\rangle \) , respectively. Moreover, let

\[
\text{ Ric : }{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \rightarrow  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}
\]

denote the Ricci tensor of \( \mathrm{R},{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0} \) the traceless Ricci tensor and

(2)

\[
\bar{\lambda } \mathrel{\text{ := }} \operatorname{tr}\left( \operatorname{Ric}\right) /n\;\text{ and }\;\sigma  \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\begin{Vmatrix}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}\end{Vmatrix}}^{2}/n.
\]

Then

(3)

\[
{\mathrm{R}}_{I} = \frac{\bar{\lambda }}{n - 1}\mathrm{{id}} \land  \mathrm{{id}}\;\text{ and }\;{\mathrm{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}} = \frac{2}{n - 2}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \land  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

Hamilton observed in [H2] that next to the map \( \left( {\mathrm{R},\mathrm{S}}\right)  \mapsto  \frac{1}{2}\left( {\mathrm{{RS}} + \mathrm{{SR}}}\right) \) there is a second natural \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -equivariant bilinear map

\[
\#  : {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)  \times  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)  \rightarrow  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) ;\left( {\mathrm{R},\mathrm{S}}\right)  \mapsto  \mathrm{R}\# \mathrm{S}
\]

given by

(4)

\[
\langle \left( {\mathrm{R}\# \mathrm{S}}\right) \left( h\right) , h\rangle  = \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta  = 1}}^{N}\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {\mathrm{R}\left( {b}_{\alpha }\right) ,\mathrm{S}\left( {b}_{\beta }\right) }\right\rbrack  , h}\right\rangle   \cdot  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{b}_{\alpha },{b}_{\beta }}\right\rbrack  , h}\right\rangle
\]

for \( h \in  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) and an orthonormal basis \( {b}_{1},\ldots ,{b}_{N} \) of \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) . The factor \( 1/2 \) stems from that fact that we are using the scalar product \( - 1/2\operatorname{tr}\left( {AB}\right) \) instead of \( - \operatorname{tr}\left( {AB}\right) \) as in [H2]. We would like to mention that \( \mathrm{R}\# \mathrm{\;S} = \mathrm{S}\# \mathrm{R} \) can be described invariantly

\[
\mathrm{R}\# S = \mathrm{{ad}} \circ  \left( {\mathrm{R} \land  \mathrm{S}}\right)  \circ  {\mathrm{{ad}}}^{ * }\text{ , }
\]

where ad: \( {\Lambda }^{2}\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right)  \rightarrow  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) , u \land  v \mapsto  \left\lbrack  {u, v}\right\rbrack \) denotes the adjoint representation and ad* is its dual. Following Hamilton we set

\[
{\mathrm{R}}^{\# } = \mathrm{R}\# \mathrm{R}
\]

We will also consider the trilinear form

(5)

\[
\operatorname{tri}\left( {{\mathrm{R}}_{1},{\mathrm{R}}_{2},{\mathrm{R}}_{3}}\right)  = \operatorname{tr}\left( {\left( {{\mathrm{R}}_{1}{\mathrm{R}}_{2} + {\mathrm{R}}_{2}{\mathrm{R}}_{1} + 2{\mathrm{R}}_{1}\# {\mathrm{R}}_{2}}\right)  \cdot  {\mathrm{R}}_{3}}\right) .
\]

The authors learned from Huisken that tri is symmetric in all three components. In fact by (4) it is straightforward to check that

\[
\operatorname{tr}\left( {2\left( {{\mathrm{R}}_{1}\# {\mathrm{R}}_{2}}\right)  \cdot  {\mathrm{R}}_{3}}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma  = 1}}^{N}\left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{\mathrm{R}}_{1}\left( {b}_{\alpha }\right) ,{\mathrm{R}}_{2}\left( {b}_{\beta }\right) }\right\rbrack  ,{\mathrm{R}}_{3}\left( {b}_{\gamma }\right) }\right\rangle   \cdot  \left\langle  {\left\lbrack  {{b}_{\alpha },{b}_{\beta }}\right\rbrack  ,{b}_{\gamma }}\right\rangle  .
\]

Since the right-hand side is clearly symmetric in all three components this gives the desired result. Huisken also observed that the ordinary differential equation (1) is the gradient flow of the function

\[
P\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  = \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\left( {{\mathrm{R}}^{3} + {\mathrm{{RR}}}^{\# }}\right)  = \frac{1}{6}\operatorname{tri}\left( {\mathrm{R},\mathrm{R},\mathrm{R}}\right) .
\]

Finally we recall that if \( {e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n} \) denotes an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of Ric, then

(6)

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( {\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{ij} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{kk}{\mathrm{R}}_{kijk}
\]

where \( {\mathrm{R}}_{kijk} = \left\langle  {\mathrm{R}\left( {{e}_{i} \land  {e}_{k}}\right) ,{e}_{j} \land  {e}_{k}}\right\rangle \) ; see [H1],[H2].

Since there is a natural embedding of the Weyl curvature operators in \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( 4\right) }\right) \) to the Weyl curvature operators in \( {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) this implies the same result for \( n \geq  5 \) .

{\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# } = \frac{1}{n - 2}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \land  {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} + \frac{2\bar{\lambda }}{\left( n - 1\right) }{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \land  \operatorname{id} - \frac{2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{\left( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}^{2}\right) }_{0} \land  \operatorname{id}
\]

Moreover

nodes.proof:
By equation (3)

\[
\mathrm{R} = {\mathrm{R}}_{I} + {\mathrm{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}} = \frac{\bar{\lambda }}{\left( n - 1\right) }I + \frac{2}{\left( n - 2\right) }{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \land  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

Using the abbreviation \( {\mathrm{R}}_{0} = {\mathrm{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}} \) we have

\[
{\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# } = {\mathrm{R}}_{0}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}_{0}^{\# } + \frac{2\bar{\lambda }}{\left( n - 1\right) }\left( {{\mathrm{R}}_{0} + {\mathrm{R}}_{0}\# I}\right)  + \frac{{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}}{{\left( n - 1\right) }^{2}}\left( {I + {I}^{\# }}\right) .
\]

Since the last two summands are known by Lemma 2.1, we may assume that \( \mathrm{R} = {\mathrm{R}}_{{\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0}} \) . Let \( {\lambda }_{1},\ldots ,{\lambda }_{n} \) denote the eigenvalues of \( {\mathrm{{Ric}}}_{0} \) corresponding to an orthonormal basis \( {e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n} \) of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . The curvature operator \( \mathrm{R} \) is diagonal with respect to \( {e}_{1} \land  {e}_{2},\ldots ,{e}_{n - 1} \land  {e}_{n} \) and we denote by \( {\mathrm{R}}_{ij} = \frac{{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}}{n - 2} \) the corresponding eigenvalues for \( 1 \leq  i < j \leq  n \) . Inspection of (4) shows that also \( {\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# } \) is diagonal with respect to this basis. We have

\[
{\left( {\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{ij} = {\mathrm{R}}_{ij}^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i, j}}{\mathrm{R}}_{ik}{\mathrm{R}}_{jk}
\]

\[
= \frac{{\left( {\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j}\right) }^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}} + \frac{1}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i, j}}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{k}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{j} + {\lambda }_{k}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{{\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j}}{\left( n - 2\right) } + \frac{{n\sigma } - {\lambda }_{i}^{2} - {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}
\]

as claimed.

The second identity follows immediately from the first. To show the last identity notice that the Ricci tensor of \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \land  {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \) is given by \( - {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}^{2} \) . A computation shows the claim.

nodes.content:
COROLLARY 2.3. We keep the notation of Theorem 2, and let \( \sigma ,\bar{\lambda } \) be as in (2). Suppose that \( {e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n} \) is an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalues \( {\lambda }_{1},\ldots ,{\lambda }_{n} \) of \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \) . Then \( {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j}\left( {i < j}\right) \) is an eigenvector of \( {D}_{a, b} \) corresponding to the eigenvalue

\[
{d}_{ij} = \left( {\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - 2\left( {a - b}\right) }\right) {\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + {2a}\left( {\bar{\lambda } + {\lambda }_{i}}\right) \left( {\bar{\lambda } + {\lambda }_{j}}\right)  + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{\sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\left( {n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }\right) .
\]

Furthermore, \( {e}_{i} \) is an eigenvector of the Ricci tensor of \( {D}_{a, b} \) with respect to the eigenvalue

\[
{r}_{i} =  - {2b}{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {2a}\bar{\lambda }\left( {n - 2}\right) {\lambda }_{i} + {2a}\left( {n - 1}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{\sigma }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\left( {{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }\right) .
\]

Notice that \( {\lambda }_{i} + \bar{\lambda } \) are the eigenvalues of the Ricci tensor Ric. The first formula follows immediately from Theorem 2, the second from (8).

### 3.New invariant sets

We call a continuous family \( C{\left( s\right) }_{s \in  \lbrack 0,1)} \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) of closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) - invariant cones of full dimension a pinching family, if

(1) each \( \mathrm{R} \in  C\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) has positive scalar curvature,

(2) \( {\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# } \) is contained in the interior of the tangent cone of \( C\left( s\right) \) at \( \mathrm{R} \) for all \( \mathrm{R} \in  C\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) and all \( s \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) ,

(3) \( C\left( s\right) \) converges in the pointed Hausdorff topology to the one-dimensional cone \( {\mathbb{R}}^{ + }I \) as \( s \rightarrow  1 \) .

nodes.content:
Example. A straightforward computation shows that

\[
C\left( s\right)  = \left\{  {\mathrm{R} \in  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( 3\right) }\right) \left| {\;\operatorname{Ric} \geq  s \cdot  \frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( \operatorname{Ric}\right) }{3}\mathrm{{id}}}\right. }\right\}  , s \in  \lbrack 0,1)
\]

defines a pinching family, with \( C\left( 0\right) \) being the cone of 3-dimensional curvature operators with nonnegative Ricci curvature.

The main aim of this section is to prove the following analogue of this result in higher dimensions.

Proposition 3.2. Let \( C \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) be a closed convex \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant subset which is invariant under the ordinary differential equation (1). Suppose that \( C \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) is contained in the half space of curvature operators with positive scalar curvature, that each \( \mathrm{R} \in  C \) has nonnegative Ricci curvature and that \( C \) contains all nonnegative curvature operators of rank 1 . Then for \( n \geq  3 \) and

\[
b \in  \left( {0,\frac{\sqrt{{2n}\left( {n - 2}\right)  + 4} - 2}{n\left( {n - 2}\right) }}\right\rbrack  \;\text{ and }\;{2a} = {2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}
\]

the set \( {\mathrm{l}}_{a, b}\left( C\right) \) is invariant under the vector field corresponding to (1) as well. In fact, it is transverse to the boundary of the set at all boundary points \( \mathrm{R} \neq  0 \) .

Using the Bianchi identity it is straightforward to check that a nonnegative curvature operator of rank 1 corresponds up to a positive factor and a change of basis in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) to the curvature operator of \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{n - 2} \) . The condition that \( C \) contains all these operators is equivalent to saying that \( C \) contains the cone of geometrically nonnegative curvature operators. A curvature operator is geometrically nonnegative if it can be written as the sum of nonnegative curvature operators of rank 1. In dimensions above 4 this cone is strictly smaller than the cone of nonnegative curvature operators. Although we will not need it, we remark that the cone of geometrically nonnegative curvature operators is invariant under (1) as well.

Suppose \( n \geq  4 \) . Notice that the cone \( C \) of 2-nonnegative curvature operators satisfies the assumptions of Proposition 3.2. We plan to show that the family of closed invariant cones from Proposition 3.2 can be extended to a pinching family. By the above remark it suffices to show that \( {\mathrm{l}}_{a\left( b\right) , b}\left( C\right) \) is contained in the cone of nonnegative curvature operators where \( b \) is the maximal allowed value from Proposition 3.2. In fact then we can extend the family from Proposition 3.2 to a pinching family by defining it on the second part of the interval as a reparametrization of the pinching family \( {\left( C\left( s\right)  \cap  {C}^{\prime }\right) }_{s \in  \lbrack 0,1)} \) where \( {C}^{\prime } \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\mathrm{l}}_{a\left( b\right) , b}\left( C\right) \) .

Let \( \mathrm{R} \in  C \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) . Recall that by (7) we have \( {\mathrm{l}}_{a, b}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  = \mathrm{R} + {2b}\operatorname{Ric} \land  \mathrm{{id}} + h{\mathrm{R}}_{I} \) for \( h \mathrel{\text{ := }} 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \) . The smallest eigenvalue of \( \mathrm{R} \) is by a standard estimate larger than or equal to \( - \frac{2\operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right) }{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4} \) . Moreover, since the sum of the two smallest eigenvalues of \( \mathrm{R} \) is nonnegative the smallest eigenvalue of Ric is bounded from below by \( \left( {n - 3}\right) \) times the absolute value of the smallest eigenvalue of \( \mathrm{R} \) . Thus in order to show that \( {\mathrm{l}}_{a, b}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  \geq  0 \) it is sufficient to prove \( h \geq  \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \frac{n\left( {n - 1}\right) }{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4} \) . This is equivalent to

\[
\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} \geq  \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \frac{n}{n\left( {n - 1}\right)  - 4}.
\]

By the definition of \( b \) we have \( \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} = \frac{2}{n}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \) . This shows the claim for \( n \geq  4 \) . For \( n = 3 \) , Theorem 3.1 is well known.

nodes.proof:
Put

\[
C\left( p\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left\{  {\mathrm{R} \in  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right)  \mid  \mathrm{R} \geq  0,\operatorname{Ric} \geq  p\left( b\right) \frac{\operatorname{tr}\left( \operatorname{Ric}\right) }{n}}\right\}  .
\]

It suffices to check that for \( \mathrm{R} \in  C\left( p\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) the pulled back vector field \( {X}_{a, b} \) defined in (9) is in the interior of the tangent cone of \( C\left( p\right) \) at \( \mathrm{R} \) .

In the first step we verify that \( {X}_{a, b} \) is positive definite for \( b \in  (0,1/2\rbrack \) . Since \( {\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# } \) is positive semi-definite, we can establish \( {X}_{a, b} > 0 \) by showing \( {D}_{a, b} > 0 \) . Since by assumption \( \mathrm{R} \in  C\left( p\right) \) we have the following estimate for the eigenvalues of \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0} \) :

\[
{\lambda }_{i} \geq   - \left( {1 - p}\right) \bar{\lambda }.
\]

Next, observe that

\[
2\left( {a - b}\right)  = \frac{1 - {2b}}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}.
\]

We use the notation of Theorem 2 and Corollary 2.3. Rewriting \( {d}_{ij} \) gives

(10)

\[
{d}_{ij} = \frac{2a}{1 - p}\left( {\left( {1 - p}\right) \bar{\lambda } + {\lambda }_{i}}\right) \left( {\left( {1 - p}\right) \bar{\lambda } + {\lambda }_{j}}\right)  + {2ap}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{n\left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right)  - \left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }{\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) }\sigma {b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)
\]

\[
> \frac{2 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}{\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) }\sigma {b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  0\text{ . }
\]

In the second step we must show that the above Ricci pinching is preserved by the ordinary differential equation (1). Let \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X}_{a, b}\right) \) denote the Ricci tensor of \( {X}_{a, b} \) . Assume that \( {\lambda }_{i} =  - \left( {1 - p}\right) \bar{\lambda } \) . We have to show that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( {X}_{a, b}\right) }_{ii} > p\frac{\operatorname{scal}\left( {X}_{a, b}\right) }{n} = p\left( {\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\sigma }\right)
\]

holds for \( b \in  (0,1/2\rbrack \) . We first observe that by (6)

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( {\mathrm{R}}^{2} + {\mathrm{R}}^{\# }\right) }_{ii} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i}}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{kk}{\mathrm{R}}_{kiik} \geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k \neq  i}}p\bar{\lambda }{\mathrm{R}}_{kiik} = {p}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2}.
\]

Using formula (10) for \( {d}_{ij} \) and \( {\lambda }_{i} =  - \left( {1 - p}\right) \bar{\lambda } \) we see that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( {X}_{a, b}\right) }_{ii} \geq  {p}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j \neq  i}}{d}_{ij}
\]

\[
= {p}^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {ap}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\left( 1 - p\right) }^{2}{\bar{\lambda }}^{2} + n{b}^{2}\sigma
\]

\[
+ \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) \sigma {b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) }\left( {2 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) .
\]

By our choice for \( b \) and \( p \) it is straightforward to check that

\[
{p}^{2} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}{\left( 1 - p\right) }^{2} = p.
\]

This shows that in the asserted inequality the \( {\bar{\lambda }}^{2} \) -terms cancel each other. Since \( \sigma  > 0 \) it remains to verify

\[
n{b}^{2} + \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) {b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) }\left( {2 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right)  > p\frac{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}.
\]

The identity

\[
\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right)  = \frac{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) b + n\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}
\]

shows that this is equivalent to

\[
0 < n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) b + n\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right)  - \left( {n - 2}\right) {\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \left( {2 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right)
\]

\[
= {2n} + {2n}\left( {n - 2}\right) b\text{ . }
\]

This shows the claim.

We remark that the above sets remain in fact invariant for all \( b > 0 \) . For \( b \rightarrow   + \infty \) they converge to an invariant set of Einstein curvature operators.

Let \( C{\left( s\right) }_{s \in  \lbrack 0,1)} \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) be a continuous family of closed convex \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) -invariant cones of full dimension, such that \( C\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) is contained in the half space of curvature operators with positive scalar curvature. (3) \( F \smallsetminus  C\left( s\right) \) is relatively compact for all \( s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) .

Let \( F \) denote the minimal closed convex \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) - invariant subset which is invariant under the flow of \( X \) and which contains the set

\[
C\left( \varepsilon \right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  \leq  {h}_{0}}\right\}  .
\]

Notice that \( F \) is the intersection of all subsets which satisfy the above properties. In particular \( F \) is well defined and \( F \subset  C\left( \varepsilon \right) \) . We have to prove that for all \( s \in  \lbrack \varepsilon ,1) \) the set \( F \smallsetminus  C\left( s\right) \) is bounded.

Suppose on the contrary that \( F \smallsetminus  C\left( s\right) \) is not bounded for some \( s \) . Let \( {s}_{0} \geq  \varepsilon \) denote the infimum among all \( s \) with this property. By the choice of \( {s}_{0} \) it follows that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\lambda  \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{1}{\lambda }F \subset  C\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) . We consider the set \( H = H\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) from Lemma 4.2. Notice that the interior of \( {T}_{0}H = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\lambda  \rightarrow  \infty }}{\lambda H} \) contains \( C\left( {s}_{0}\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) . Thus we can find large numbers \( \lambda , r \geq  {h}_{0} \) such that \( F \cap  \{ \mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  = r\} \) is contained in the interior of \( {\lambda H} \) .

We now define \( {F}^{\prime } \) as the union of \( F \cap  \{ \mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  \leq  r\} \) and \( F \cap  \{ \mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\mathrm{R} \geq  r\} \; \cap  {\lambda H} \) . By construction \( {F}^{\prime } \) is convex, invariant under the vector field \( X \) and contains the set \( C\left( \varepsilon \right)  \cap  \left\{  {\mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  \leq  {h}_{0}}\right\} \) . By the definition of \( F \) this implies \( {F}^{\prime } \subset  F \) . By the definition of \( {F}^{\prime } \) we have \( F \subset  {F}^{\prime } \) and equality does not occur - a contradiction.

LEMMA 4.2. Let \( C = C\left( s\right) \) for some \( s \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) . Then there exists a closed convex \( \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) -invariant set \( H = H\left( s\right) \) such that

(1) \( H \) is invariant under the vector field \( X \) .

(2) \( \{ \mathrm{R} \in  C \smallsetminus  \{ 0\}  \mid  \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  \leq  1\} \) is contained in the interior of \( H \) .

(3) \( \{ \mathrm{R} \in  H \mid  \operatorname{tr}\mathrm{R} \geq  l\} \) is contained in the interior of \( C \) for some large \( l \) .

nodes.proof:
Since the vector field \( X \) is transverse to the boundary of \( C \) it is clear that for some \( {\delta }_{0} > 0 \) and all \( \delta  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\delta }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) the cone \( {C}_{\delta } \) over the convex set

\[
\{ \mathrm{R} \in  C \mid  \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  = 1, d\left( {\mathrm{R},\partial C}\right)  \geq  \delta \}
\]

is invariant under \( X \) . We also may assume that for all \( \delta  \in  \left\lbrack  {-{\delta }_{0},0}\right\rbrack \) the cone \( {C}_{\delta } \) over the convex set

\[
\{ \mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  = 1, d\left( {\mathrm{R}, C}\right)  \leq   - \delta \}
\]

is invariant under \( X \) . Notice that the size of the cones \( {C}_{\delta } \) is decreasing in \( \delta \) . After possibly decreasing \( {\delta }_{0} \) , we may assume that there is some constant \( \eta \) such that for each \( \mathrm{R} \in  {C}_{\delta } \) the vector field \( X \) has distance at least \( \eta \parallel \mathrm{R}{\parallel }^{2} \) to the boundary of the tangent cone of \( {C}_{\delta } \) at \( \mathrm{R} \) for all \( \delta  \in  \left\lbrack  {-{\delta }_{0},{\delta }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . We note that \( X \) is locally Lipschitz continuous with a Lipschitz constant that growths linearly in \( \parallel \mathrm{R}\parallel \) . Combining both facts we see that there is some constant \( c > 0 \) such that the truncated shifted cone

\[
T{C}_{\delta } \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left\{  {\mathrm{R} \mid  \mathrm{R} + {cI} \in  {C}_{\delta },\operatorname{tr}\left( \mathrm{R}\right)  \geq  1}\right\}
\]

is invariant under the flow of \( X \) for all \( \delta  \in  \left\lbrack  {-{\delta }_{0},{\delta }_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . For a suitable small \( \delta  > 0 \) the interior of \( T{C}_{\delta } \) contains the set

\[
{C}_{-\delta } \cap  \{ \mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\mathrm{R} = 1\} .
\]

Therefore the union of \( T{C}_{\delta } \cap  {C}_{-\delta } \) and \( {C}_{-\delta } \cap  \{ \mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\mathrm{R} \leq  1\} \) defines a convex set \( H \) . Clearly \( H \) is invariant under the vector field \( X \) . By construction the interior of \( H \) contains \( C \cap  \{ \mathrm{R} \mid  \operatorname{tr}\mathrm{R} \leq  1,\mathrm{R} \neq  0\} \) . Furthermore the cone at infinity of \( H \) is given by \( {C}_{\delta } \) . Thus for some large \( l \) the interior of \( C \) contains \( \{ \mathrm{R} \in  H \mid  \operatorname{tr}\mathrm{R} \geq  l\} . \)

nodes.label: Theorem 5.1
nodes.document_title: Christoph Boehm and Burkhard Wilking - Manifolds with Positive Curvature Operators Are Space Forms
nodes.content: THEOREM 5.1. Let \( C{\left( s\right) }_{s \in  \lbrack 0,1)} \subset  {S}_{B}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) be a pinching family of closed convex cones, \( n \geq  3 \) . Suppose that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is a compact Riemannian manifold such that the curvature operator of \( M \) at each point is contained in the interior of \( C\left( 0\right) \) . Then the normalized Ricci flow evolves \( g \) to a constant curvature limit metric.
