nodes.proof:
By Proposition 4.10, we can find a real number \( \eta  \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) such that \( \left( {1 - t}\right) \operatorname{scal} \geq  \alpha \) on \( {S}^{2} \times  \lbrack 1 - \eta ,1) \) . Using Lemma 4.11, we obtain

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\left| M\right| }^{2}\right)  = \Delta \left( {\left| M\right| }^{2}\right)  - 2{\left| DM\right| }^{2} + \frac{2}{1 - t}{\left| M\right| }^{2} - 2\operatorname{scal}{\left| M\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta \left( {\left| M\right| }^{2}\right)  - 2{\left| DM\right| }^{2} + \frac{2 - {2\alpha }}{1 - t}{\left| M\right| }^{2}
\]

on \( {S}^{2} \times  \lbrack 1 - \eta ,1) \) . By the maximum principle, the function \( {\left( 1 - t\right) }^{2 - {2\alpha }}{\left| M\right| }^{2} \) is uniformly bounded from above.

nodes.content:
Proposition 4.13. Fix a real number \( \alpha  \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) . There exists a positive constant \( C \) such that

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{S}^{2}}{\left( {\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{1 - t}\right) }^{2} \leq  C{\left( 1 - t\right) }^{{2\alpha } - 2}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 4.13. Fix a real number \( \alpha \in \left( {0,1}\right) \) . There exists a positive constant \( C \) such that \[ \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{S}^{2}}{\left( {\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{1 - t}\right) }^{2} \leq C{\left( 1 - t\right) }^{{2\alpha } - 2}. \]

nodes.proof:
We compute

\[
2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j = 1}}^{2}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}^{2}M}\right) \left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right)  = {\Delta \Delta f} + \operatorname{scal}{\Delta f} + \langle d\operatorname{scal},{df}\rangle
\]

\[
=  - \Delta {\operatorname{scal}}^{2} - {\operatorname{scal}}^{2} + \frac{1}{1 - t}\operatorname{scal} + \langle d\operatorname{scal},{df}\rangle
\]

\[
=  - \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal} + \frac{1}{1 - t}\operatorname{scal} + \langle d\operatorname{scal},{df}\rangle .
\]

For abbreviation, let \( H = \left( {1 - t}\right) M \) and \( h = \left( {1 - t}\right) \) scal -1 . Then

\[
2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j = 1}}^{2}\left( {{D}_{{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}^{2}H}\right) \left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right)  =  - \frac{\partial }{\partial t}h + \langle {dh},{df}\rangle .
\]

By Lemma 4.12, we can find a positive constant \( {C}_{1} \) such that

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{S}^{2}}\left| H\right|  \leq  {C}_{1}{\left( 1 - t\right) }^{\alpha }
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) . Moreover, it follows from Lemma 4.11 that

\[
{D}_{\frac{\partial }{\partial t}}H = {\Delta H} - \operatorname{scal}H.
\]

By Corollary 3.6, we can find a positive constant \( {C}_{2} \) such that

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{S}^{2}}{\left| {D}^{2}H\right| }^{2} \leq  {C}_{2}{\left( 1 - t\right) }^{{2\alpha } - 2}
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) . This implies

\[
\left| {-\frac{\partial }{\partial t}h+\langle {dh},{df}\rangle }\right|  \leq  {C}_{3}{\left( 1 - t\right) }^{\alpha  - 1}
\]

for some positive constant \( {C}_{3} \) . If we integrate this inequality, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{p \in  {S}^{2}}}\left| {h\left( {p, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{q \in  {S}^{2}}}\left| {h\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right|  + \frac{{C}_{3}}{\alpha }\left\lbrack  {{\left( 1 - t\right) }^{\alpha } - {\left( 1 - \tau \right) }^{\alpha }}\right\rbrack
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) and all \( \tau  \in  \lbrack t,1) \) .

We now pass to the limit as \( \tau  \rightarrow  1 \) . It follows from Proposition 4.10 that \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{q \in  {S}^{2}}}\left| {h\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  0 \) as \( \tau  \rightarrow  1 \) . Consequently, we have

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{p \in  {S}^{2}}}\left| {h\left( {p, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{{C}_{3}}{\alpha }{\left( 1 - t\right) }^{\alpha }
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) . This completes the proof.

nodes.label: Definition 5.1
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.section_title: 5.2. The tangent and normal cone to a convex set
nodes.content:
Definition 5.1. Let \( F \) be a closed, convex subset of \( X \) . For each point \( y \in  F \) , we define

\[
{N}_{y}F = \{ z \in  X : \langle x - y, z\rangle  \geq  0\text{ for all }x \in  F\}
\]

and

\[
{T}_{y}F = \left\{  {x \in  X : \langle x, z\rangle  \geq  0\text{ for all }z \in  {N}_{y}F}\right\}  .
\]

We refer to the cone \( {N}_{y}F \) as the normal cone to \( F \) at \( y \) . Moreover, the cone \( {T}_{y}F \) is called the tangent cone to \( F \) at the point \( y \) .

Note that \( {N}_{y}F \) and \( {T}_{y}F \) are closed and convex. Moreover, if \( y \) lies in the interior of \( F \) , then \( {N}_{y}F = \{ 0\} \) and \( {T}_{y}F = X \) .

nodes.content:
Lemma 5.2. Let \( F \) be a closed, convex subset of \( X \) . Moreover, we consider two points \( y \in  F \) and \( z \in  X \) . Then the following statements are equivalent:

(i) \( d\left( {z, F}\right)  = \left| {y - z}\right| \) .

(ii) \( y - z \in  {N}_{y}F \) .

nodes.proof:
(i) \( \Rightarrow \) (ii): Consider an arbitrary point \( x \in  F \) . Since \( F \) is convex, we have \( {sx} + \left( {1 - s}\right) y \in  F \) for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . This implies

\[
\left| {{sx} + \left( {1 - s}\right) y - z}\right|  \geq  d\left( {z, F}\right)  = \left| {y - z}\right|
\]

for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . Consequently, we have

\[
\langle x - y, y - z\rangle  = {\left. \frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{ds}{\left| sx + \left( 1 - s\right) y - z\right| }^{2}\right| }_{s = 0} \geq  0
\]

for all \( x \in  F \) . Thus, we conclude that \( y - z \in  {N}_{y}F \) .

(ii) \( \Rightarrow \) (i): Since \( y - z \in  {N}_{y}F \) , we have \( \langle x - y, y - z\rangle  \geq  0 \) for all \( x \in  F \) . This implies

\[
{\left| x - z\right| }^{2} = {\left| x - y\right| }^{2} + 2\langle x - y, y - z\rangle  + {\left| y - z\right| }^{2} \geq  {\left| y - z\right| }^{2}
\]

for all \( x \in  F \) . Taking the infimum over all points \( x \in  F \) , we obtain \( d\left( {z, F}\right)  \geq \; \left| {y - z}\right| \) . Since \( y \in  F \) , we conclude that \( d\left( {z, F}\right)  = \left| {y - z}\right| \) , as claimed.

Proposition 5.4. Let \( F \) be a closed, convex subset of \( X \) and let \( x\left( t\right) , t \in \; \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a smooth path in \( X \) such that \( x\left( 0\right)  \in  F \) . Then the following holds:

(i) If \( x\left( t\right)  \in  F \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , then \( {x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right)  \in  {T}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) .

(ii) If \( {x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) , then there exists a real number \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) such that \( x\left( t\right)  \in  F \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\varepsilon }\right\rbrack \) .

Then the following holds: (i) If \( x\left( t\right) \in F \) for all \( t \in \lbrack 0, T) \) , then \( {x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \in {T}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) . (ii) If \( {x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \) lies in the...

nodes.proof:
(i) Suppose that \( x\left( t\right)  \in  F \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Then \( \langle x\left( t\right)  - x\left( 0\right) , z\rangle  \geq  0 \) for all \( z \in  {N}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) and all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . This implies

\[
\left\langle  {{x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) , z}\right\rangle   = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \searrow  0}}\frac{1}{t}\langle x\left( t\right)  - x\left( 0\right) , z\rangle  \geq  0
\]

for all \( z \in  {N}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) . Therefore, \( {x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right)  \in  {T}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) .

(ii) We argue by contradiction. Suppose that \( {x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) . Moreover, we assume that there exists a sequence of real numbers \( {t}_{k} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{t}_{k} = 0 \) and \( x\left( {t}_{k}\right)  \notin  F \) for all \( k \) . For each \( k \) , we can find a point \( {y}_{k} \in  F \) such that \( d\left( {x\left( {t}_{k}\right) , F}\right)  = \left| {{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right|  > 0 \) . We next define

\[
{z}_{k} = \frac{{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }{\left| {y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) \right| }.
\]

By Lemma 5.2, we have \( {z}_{k} \in  {N}_{{y}_{k}}F \) for all \( k \) . Since \( x\left( 0\right)  \in  F \) , it follows that \( \left\langle  {x\left( 0\right)  - {y}_{k},{z}_{k}}\right\rangle   \geq  0 \) for all \( k \) . Moreover, we have \( \left\langle  {{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) ,{z}_{k}}\right\rangle   \geq  0 \) by definition of \( {z}_{k} \) . Putting these facts together, we obtain \( \left\langle  {x\left( {t}_{k}\right)  - x\left( 0\right) ,{z}_{k}}\right\rangle   \leq  0 \) for all \( k \) .

Since \( x\left( 0\right)  \in  F \) , we have \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{y}_{k} = x\left( 0\right) \) . After passing to a subsequence if necessary, we may assume that the sequence \( {z}_{k} \) converges to some unit vector \( z \in  X \) . Since \( {z}_{k} \in  {N}_{{y}_{k}}F \) for each \( k \) , it follows that \( z \in  {N}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) . Since \( {x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{x\left( 0\right) }F \) , we conclude that \( \left\langle  {{x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) , z}\right\rangle   > 0 \) . On the other hand, we have \( \left\langle  {x\left( {t}_{k}\right)  - x\left( 0\right) ,{z}_{k}}\right\rangle   \leq  0 \) for all \( k \) . This implies

\[
\left\langle  {{x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) , z}\right\rangle   = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{1}{{t}_{k}}\left\langle  {x\left( {t}_{k}\right)  - x\left( 0\right) ,{z}_{k}}\right\rangle   \leq  0.
\]

This is a contradiction.

Proposition 5.5. Let \( F \) be a closed subset of \( X \) . Then the following statements are equivalent:

(i) The set \( F \) is invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}x\left( t\right)  = \Phi \left( {x\left( t\right) }\right) \) .

(ii) We have \( \langle \Phi \left( y\right) , y - z\rangle  \geq  0 \) for all points \( y \in  F \) and \( z \in  X \) satisfying \( d\left( {z, F}\right)  = \left| {y - z}\right| . \)
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 5.5. Let \( F \) be a closed subset of \( X \) . Then the following statements are equivalent: (i) The set \( F \) is invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}x\left( t\right) = \Phi \left( {x\left( t\right) }\right) \) . (ii) We have \( \langle \Phi \left( y\right) , y - z\rangle \geq 0 \) for all points \( y \in F \) and \( z \in X \) satisfying \( d\left( {z, F}\right) = \left| {y - z}\right| . \)

nodes.proof:
(i) \( \Rightarrow \) (ii): Consider two points \( y \in  F \) and \( z \in  X \) satisfying \( d\left( {z, F}\right)  = \left| {y - z}\right| \) . Let \( x\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) be the unique solution of the ODE \( {x}^{\prime }\left( t\right)  = \Phi \left( {x\left( t\right) }\right) \) with initial condition \( x\left( 0\right)  = y \) . Since \( F \) is an invariant set, we have \( x\left( t\right)  \in  F \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . This implies

\[
\left| {x\left( t\right)  - z}\right|  \geq  d\left( {z, F}\right)  = \left| {y - z}\right|  = \left| {x\left( 0\right)  - z}\right|
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Consequently, we have

\[
\langle \Phi \left( y\right) , y - z\rangle  = \left\langle  {{x}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) , x\left( 0\right)  - z}\right\rangle   = {\left. \frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}{\left| x\left( t\right)  - z\right| }^{2}\right| }_{t = 0} \geq  0.
\]

(ii) \( \Rightarrow \) (i): Let \( x\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution to the ODE \( {x}^{\prime }\left( t\right)  = \Phi \left( {x\left( t\right) }\right) \) such that \( x\left( 0\right)  \in  F \) . We claim that \( x\left( t\right)  \in  F \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . To prove this, we argue by contradiction. Suppose that \( x\left( \tau \right)  \notin  F \) for some real number \( \tau  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . We define a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \) by

\[
{t}_{k} = \sup \left\{  {t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack   : d\left( {x\left( t\right) , F}\right)  \leq  {e}^{{kt} - {k}^{2}}}\right\}
\]

for \( k \) sufficiently large. It is easy to see that \( {t}_{k} \in  \left( {0,\tau }\right) \) and \( d\left( {x\left( {t}_{k}\right) , F}\right)  = \; {e}^{k{t}_{k} - {k}^{2}} > 0 \) if \( k \) is sufficiently large. Since \( F \) is closed, we can find a point \( {y}_{k} \in  F \) such that \( d\left( {x\left( {t}_{k}\right) , F}\right)  = \left| {{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right|  > 0 \) .

By definition of \( {t}_{k} \) , we have

\[
{e}^{k\left( {{t}_{k} - t}\right) }\left| {{y}_{k} - x\left( t\right) }\right|  \geq  {e}^{k\left( {{t}_{k} - t}\right) }d\left( {x\left( t\right) , F}\right)  \geq  d\left( {x\left( {t}_{k}\right) , F}\right)  = \left| {{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right|
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k},\tau }\right\rbrack \) . Consequently, we have

\[
k{\left| {y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) \right| }^{2} + \left\langle  {{x}^{\prime }\left( {t}_{k}\right) ,{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - {\left. \frac{1}{2}\frac{d}{dt}\left( {e}^{{2k}\left( {{t}_{k} - t}\right) }{\left| {y}_{k} - x\left( t\right) \right| }^{2}\right) \right| }_{t = {t}_{k}} \leq  0.
\]

This implies

\[
\left\langle  {\Phi \left( {x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right) ,{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right\rangle   \leq   - k{\left| {y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) \right| }^{2}.
\]

By assumption, we have

\[
\left\langle  {\Phi \left( {y}_{k}\right) ,{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right\rangle   \geq  0.
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
\left\langle  {\Phi \left( {y}_{k}\right)  - \Phi \left( {x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right) ,{y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right\rangle   \geq  k{\left| {y}_{k} - x\left( {t}_{k}\right) \right| }^{2}.
\]

This contradicts the Lipschitz continuity of \( \Phi \) .

nodes.content:
### 5.3. Hamilton's maximum principle for the Ricci flow

Let \( V \) be a finite-dimensional vector space equipped with an inner product. We denote by \( \mathcal{C}\left( V\right) \) the space of all multilinear forms \( R : V \times  V \times  V \times  V \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) such that

\[
R\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  =  - R\left( {Y, X, Z, W}\right)  = R\left( {Z, W, X, Y}\right)
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  V \) . Moreover, we denote by \( {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) the space of all multilinear forms \( R \in  \mathcal{C}\left( V\right) \) satisfying

\[
R\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + R\left( {Y, Z, X, W}\right)  + R\left( {Z, X, Y, W}\right)  = 0
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  V \) . In other words, \( {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) is the space of algebraic curvature tensors on \( V \) (cf. [13], Definition 1.108).

Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal basis of \( V \) . Given any algebraic curvature tensor \( R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) , we define

\[
{R}^{2}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X, Y,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {Z, W,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

and

\[
{R}^{\# }\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  V \) . Moreover, we write

\[
Q\left( R\right)  = {R}^{2} + {R}^{\# }.
\]

Note that \( {R}^{2} \) and \( {R}^{\# } \) lie in the space \( \mathcal{C}\left( V\right) \) , but not necessarily in \( {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) . However, the sum \( Q\left( R\right)  = {R}^{2} + {R}^{\# } \) lies in the space \( {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) :

Proposition 5.7. Let \( R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) be an algebraic curvature tensor on \( V \) . Then

\[
Q\left( R\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + Q\left( R\right) \left( {Y, Z, X, W}\right)  + Q\left( R\right) \left( {Z, X, Y, W}\right)  = 0
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  V \) . Consequently, \( Q\left( R\right)  \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 5.7. Let \( R \in {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) be an algebraic curvature tensor on \( V \) . Then \[ Q\left( R\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right) + Q\left( R\right) \left( {Y, Z, X, W}\right) + Q\left( R\right) \left( {Z, X, Y, W}\right) = 0 \] for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in V \) . Consequently, \( Q\left( R\right) \in {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
By definition of \( {R}^{\# } \) , we have

\[
{R}^{\# }\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {Y, Z, X, W}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {Z, X, Y, W}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}\left\lbrack  {R\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, Y,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack  R\left( {Z,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}\left\lbrack  {R\left( {Z,{e}_{p}, Y,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack  R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}\left\lbrack  {R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {Z,{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack  R\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right) .
\]

This implies

\[
{R}^{\# }\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {Y, Z, X, W}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {Z, X, Y, W}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}\left\lbrack  {R\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, Y,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack  \left\lbrack  {R\left( {Z,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {W,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}\left\lbrack  {R\left( {Z,{e}_{p}, Y,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack  \left\lbrack  {R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {W,{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}\left\lbrack  {R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {Z,{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack  \left\lbrack  {R\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right)  - R\left( {W,{e}_{p}, Y,{e}_{q}}\right) }\right\rbrack  .
\]

Since \( R \) satisfies the first Bianchi identity, it follows that

\[
{R}^{\# }\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {Y, Z, X, W}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {Z, X, Y, W}\right)
\]

\[
=  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}R\left( {X, Y,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {Z, W,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}R\left( {Y, Z,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {X, W,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
- \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}R\left( {Z, X,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {Y, W,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right) .
\]

Thus, we conclude that

\[
{R}^{\# }\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {Y, Z, X, W}\right)  + {R}^{\# }\left( {Z, X, Y, W}\right)

\[

\]

This completes the proof.

Proposition 5.9. Assume that \( F \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) is closed, convex, and \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) - invariant. Moreover, let \( M \) be a compact manifold of dimension \( n \) , and let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on \( M \) . Suppose that \( \left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) is a point in \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) with the property that

\[
{e}^{\mu \left( {{t}_{0} - t}\right) }d\left( {{R}_{\left( p, t\right) },{F}_{\left( p, t\right) }}\right)  \leq  d\left( {{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) },{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right)
\]

for all points \( \left( {p, t}\right)  \in  M \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Finally, let \( S \in  {F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) } \) be an algebraic curvature tensor satisfying \( d\left( {{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) },{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right)  = \left| {S - {R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right| \) . Then the following holds:

(i) \( \left\langle  {{D}_{\frac{\partial }{\partial t}}{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }, S - {R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right\rangle   \leq   - \mu {\left| S - {R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }\right| }^{2} \) . (ii) \( \left\langle  {{D}_{v, v}^{2}{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }, S - {R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right\rangle   \geq  0 \) for all \( v \in  {T}_{{p}_{0}}M \) .

(i) Let \( D \) be the connection defined in (6). For each \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we denote by \( P\left( s\right)  : {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {E}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }\right)  \rightarrow  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {E}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0} - s\right) }\right) \) the parallel transport with respect to the connection \( D \) . Moreover, we define an algebraic curvature tensor \( H\left( s\right)  \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {E}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) by

\[
P\left( s\right) H\left( s\right)  = {R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0} - s\right) } \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {E}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0} - s\right) }\right)
\]

for each \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Clearly, \( H\left( 0\right)  = {R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) } \) . Since \( F \) is \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant, we have \( P\left( s\right) {F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) } = {F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0} - s\right) } \) for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) . This implies

\[
{e}^{\mu s}d\left( {H\left( s\right) ,{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right)  = {e}^{\mu s}d\left( {{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0} - s\right) },{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0} - s\right) }}\right)
\]

(30)

\[
\leq  d\left( {{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) },{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right)
\]

\[
= \left| {S - H\left( 0\right) }\right|
\]

for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Moreover, it follows from Lemma 5.3 that

(31)

\[
0 \leq  d\left( {H\left( s\right) ,{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right) \left| {S - H\left( 0\right) }\right|  + \langle H\left( s\right)  - S, S - H\left( 0\right) \rangle
\]

for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Combining (30) and (31), we obtain

\[
0 \leq  {e}^{-{\mu s}}{\left| S - H\left( 0\right) \right| }^{2} + \langle H\left( s\right)  - S, S - H\left( 0\right) \rangle
\]

for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) , with equality for \( s = 0 \) . This implies

\[
- \mu {\left| S - H\left( 0\right) \right| }^{2} + \left\langle  {{H}^{\prime }\left( 0\right) , S - H\left( 0\right) }\right\rangle
\]

\[
= {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\left( {e}^{-{\mu s}}{\left| S - H\left( 0\right) \right| }^{2}+\langle H\left( s\right)  - S, S - H\left( 0\right) \rangle \right) \right| }_{s = 0} \geq  0.
\]

We next observe that \( {H}^{\prime }\left( 0\right)  =  - {D}_{\frac{\partial }{\partial t}}{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) } \) . Putting these facts together, the assertion follows.

(ii) Fix a vector \( v \in  {T}_{{p}_{0}}M \) . We define a path \( \gamma  : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow  M \) by \( \gamma \left( s\right)  = \; {\exp }_{{p}_{0}}\left( {sv}\right) \) , where \( {\exp }_{{p}_{0}} \) denotes the exponential map with respect to the metric \( g\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) . For each \( s \in  \mathbb{R} \) , we denote by \( P\left( s\right)  : {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {E}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }\right)  \rightarrow  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {E}_{\left( \gamma \left( s\right) ,{t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) the parallel transport along \( \gamma \) . Moreover, we define an algebraic curvature tensor \( H\left( s\right)  \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {E}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) by

\[
P\left( s\right) H\left( s\right)  = {R}_{\left( \gamma \left( s\right) ,{t}_{0}\right) } \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {E}_{\left( \gamma \left( s\right) ,{t}_{0}\right) }\right)
\]

for each \( s \in  \mathbb{R} \) . Clearly, \( H\left( 0\right)  = {R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) } \) . Since \( F \) is \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant, we have \( P\left( s\right) {F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) } = {F}_{\left( \gamma \left( s\right) ,{t}_{0}\right) } \) . This implies

\[
d\left( {H\left( s\right) ,{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right)  = d\left( {{R}_{\left( \gamma \left( s\right) ,{t}_{0}\right) },{F}_{\left( \gamma \left( s\right) ,{t}_{0}\right) }}\right)
\]

(32)

\[
\leq  d\left( {{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) },{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right)
\]

\[
= \left| {S - H\left( 0\right) }\right|
\]

for all \( s \in  \mathbb{R} \) . Moreover, it follows from Lemma 5.3 that

(33)

\[
0 \leq  d\left( {H\left( s\right) ,{F}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }}\right) \left| {S - H\left( 0\right) }\right|  + \langle H\left( s\right)  - S, S - H\left( 0\right) \rangle
\]

for all \( s \in  \mathbb{R} \) . Combining (32) and (33), we obtain

\[
0 \leq  {\left| S - H\left( 0\right) \right| }^{2} + \langle H\left( s\right)  - S, S - H\left( 0\right) \rangle
\]

for all \( s \in  \mathbb{R} \) , with equality for \( s = 0 \) . Thus, we conclude that

\[
\left\langle  {{H}^{\prime \prime }\left( 0\right) , S - H\left( 0\right) }\right\rangle   = {\left. \frac{{d}^{2}}{d{s}^{2}}\langle H\left( s\right)  - S, S - H\left( 0\right) \rangle \right| }_{s = 0} \geq  0.
\]

Finally, we have \( {H}^{\prime \prime }\left( 0\right)  = {D}_{v, v}^{2}{R}_{\left( {p}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) } \) . This completes the proof of (ii).

nodes.content: Theorem 5.10 (R. Hamilton [45]). Assume that \( F \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) is closed, convex, O(n)-invariant, and invariant under the Hamilton ODE. Moreover, suppose that \( M \) is a compact manifold of dimension \( n \) , and \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow on \( M \) with the property that \( {R}_{\left( p,0\right) } \in  {F}_{\left( p,0\right) } \) for all points \( p \in  M \) . Then \( {R}_{\left( p, t\right) } \in  {F}_{\left( p, t\right) } \) for all points \( p \in  M \) and all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

nodes.proof:
We define a function \( u : \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) by

\[
u\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{p \in  M}}d\left( {{R}_{\left( p, t\right) },{F}_{\left( p, t\right) }}\right)
\]

for \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . By assumption, we have \( u\left( 0\right)  = 0 \) . We claim that \( u\left( t\right)  = 0 \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . To prove this, we argue by contradiction. Suppose that \( u\left( \tau \right)  > 0 \) for some real number \( \tau  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . We define a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \) by

\[
{t}_{k} = \inf \left\{  {t \in  \lbrack 0, T) : u\left( t\right)  \geq  {e}^{{kt} - {k}^{2}}}\right\}
\]

for \( k \) sufficiently large. It is easy to see that \( {t}_{k} \in  \left( {0,\tau }\right) \) and \( u\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = {e}^{k{t}_{k} - {k}^{2}} > \) 0 if \( k \) is sufficiently large. Since \( M \) is compact, there exists a point \( {p}_{k} \in  M \) such that \( u\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = d\left( {{R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) },{F}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right) \) . Since \( F \) is closed, we can find an algebraic curvature tensor \( {S}_{k} \in  {F}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) } \) such that

\[
u\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = d\left( {{R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) },{F}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right)  = \left| {{S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right|  > 0.
\]

By definition of \( \left( {{p}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , we have

\[
{e}^{k\left( {{t}_{k} - t}\right) }d\left( {{R}_{\left( p, t\right) },{F}_{\left( p, t\right) }}\right)  \leq  {e}^{k\left( {{t}_{k} - t}\right) }u\left( t\right)  \leq  u\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = d\left( {{R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) },{F}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right)
\]

for all points \( \left( {p, t}\right)  \in  M \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) . Hence, it follows from Proposition 5.9 that

(34)

\[
\left\langle  {{D}_{\frac{\partial }{\partial t}}{R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) },{S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right\rangle   \leq   - k{\left| {S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }\right| }^{2}
\]

and

(35)

\[
\left\langle  {\Delta {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) },{S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right\rangle   \geq  0.
\]

Subtracting (35) from (34) yields

(36)

\[
\left\langle  {Q\left( {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }\right) ,{S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right\rangle   \leq   - k{\left| {S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }\right| }^{2}.
\]

By assumption, the set \( F \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE. Consequently, we have

(37)

\[
\left\langle  {Q\left( {S}_{k}\right) ,{S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right\rangle   \geq  0
\]

by Proposition 5.5. If we subtract (36) from (37), we obtain

\[
\left\langle  {Q\left( {S}_{k}\right)  - Q\left( {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }\right) ,{S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }}\right\rangle   \geq  k{\left| {S}_{k} - {R}_{\left( {p}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }\right| }^{2}.
\]

This contradicts the Lipschitz continuity of \( Q \) . Thus, we conclude that \( u\left( t\right)  = 0 \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

Definition 5.12. A set \( F \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) is called a pinching set if the following conditions are met:

- \( F \) is closed, convex, and \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant.

- \( F \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) \) .

- For each \( \delta  \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) , the set \( \{ R \in  F : R \) is not weakly \( \delta \) -pinched \( \} \) is bounded.

\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}\left| {\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }}_{g\left( t\right) }\right|  \leq  \varepsilon {K}_{\max }\left( t\right)  + {C}_{1}
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . This implies

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}\left| {\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }}_{g\left( t\right) }\right|  \leq  {2\varepsilon }{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  + {C}_{1}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) . By Corollary 2.17, the trace-free Ricci tensor satisfies an evolution equation of the form

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  } = \Delta \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  } + R * \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }
\]

Hence, by Corollary 3.6, there exists a positive constant \( {C}_{2} \) such that

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\left| D{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2} \leq  {C}_{2}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right) {\left( 2\varepsilon {K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  + {C}_{1}\right) }^{2}.
\]

Using Proposition 1.5, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\left| d{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right| }^{2} \leq  {C}_{3}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right) {\left( 2\varepsilon {K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  + {C}_{1}\right) }^{2}
\]

for some positive constant \( {C}_{3} \) . This implies

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  {\Omega }_{k}}}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\left( x\right)  \geq  {\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\left( {p}_{k}\right)  - {2\pi }\sqrt{{C}_{3}}\left( {{2\varepsilon }{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  + {C}_{1}}\right) ,
\]

hence

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  {\Omega }_{k}}}{K}_{\max }\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right)  \geq  {K}_{\min }\left( {{p}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  - \frac{2\pi }{n\left( {n - 1}\right) }\sqrt{{C}_{3}}\left( {{2\varepsilon }{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  + {C}_{1}}\right) .
\]

By Lemma 5.13, we can find a positive constant \( {C}_{4} \) such that

\[
{K}_{\min }\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) {K}_{\max }\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right)  - {C}_{4}
\]

for all points \( x \in  M \) . In particular, we have

\[
{K}_{\min }\left( {{p}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) {K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  - {C}_{4}.
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  {\Omega }_{k}}}{K}_{\min }\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right)  \geq  {\left( 1 - \varepsilon \right) }^{2}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  - \left( {2 - \varepsilon }\right) {C}_{4}
\]

\[
- \frac{2\pi }{n\left( {n - 1}\right) }\sqrt{{C}_{3}}\left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) \left( {{2\varepsilon }{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  + {C}_{1}}\right) .
\]

Finally, we observe that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = \infty \) by Lemma 5.14. Thus, we conclude that

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  {\Omega }_{k}}}{K}_{\min }\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right) }{{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right) } \geq  {\left( 1 - \varepsilon \right) }^{2} - \frac{4\pi }{n\left( {n - 1}\right) }\sqrt{{C}_{3}}\left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) \varepsilon .
\]

Since \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) is arbitrary, the assertion follows.

Suppose the assertion is false. After passing to a subsequence if necessary, we may assume that

(38)

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{K}_{\min }\left( {t}_{k}\right) }{{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right) } < 1.
\]

For each \( k \) , we choose a point \( {p}_{k} \in  M \) such that \( {K}_{\max }\left( {{p}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  = {K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right) \) . As above, we define

\[
{\Omega }_{k} = \left\{  {x \in  M : {d}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\left( {{p}_{k}, x}\right)  \leq  {2\pi }{K}_{\max }{\left( {t}_{k}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  .
\]

By Lemma 5.15, we have

(39)

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  {\Omega }_{k}}}{K}_{\min }\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right) }{{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right) } \geq  1.
\]

It follows from (38) and (39) that \( {\Omega }_{k} \neq  M \) if \( k \) is sufficiently large. Hence, if \( k \) is sufficiently large, there exists a point \( {x}_{k} \in  M \) such that \( {d}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\left( {{p}_{k},{x}_{k}}\right)  = \; {2\pi }{K}_{\max }{\left( {t}_{k}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) . Moreover, we can find a geodesic \( {\gamma }_{k} : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\right) \) such that \( {\gamma }_{k}\left( 0\right)  = {p}_{k},{\gamma }_{k}\left( 1\right)  = {x}_{k} \) , and

\[
{L}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\left( {\gamma }_{k}\right)  = {d}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\left( {{p}_{k},{x}_{k}}\right)  = {2\pi }{K}_{\max }{\left( {t}_{k}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}.
\]

Since \( {\gamma }_{k} \) is free of conjugate points, we have

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack  }}{K}_{\min }\left( {{\gamma }_{k}\left( s\right) ,{t}_{k}}\right)  \leq  {\pi }^{2}{L}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }{\left( {\gamma }_{k}\right) }^{-2} = \frac{1}{4}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)
\]

if \( k \) is sufficiently large. Moreover, we have \( {\gamma }_{k}\left( s\right)  \in  {\Omega }_{k} \) for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . This implies

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  {\Omega }_{k}}}{K}_{\min }\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack  }}{K}_{\min }\left( {{\gamma }_{k}\left( s\right) ,{t}_{k}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)
\]

if \( k \) is sufficiently large. This contradicts (39).

nodes.proof:
Suppose the assertion is false. Then there exists a sequence of times \( {\tau }_{k} \) such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\tau }_{k} = T \) and

(40)

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{K}_{\min }\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) }{{K}_{\max }\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) } < 1.
\]

For each \( k \) , there exists a real number \( {t}_{k} \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }_{k}}\right\rbrack \) such that

\[
{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }_{k}}\right\rbrack  }}{K}_{\max }\left( t\right) .
\]

It follows from Lemma 5.14 that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = \infty \) . From this, we deduce that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{t}_{k} = T \) . Using Lemma 5.16, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{K}_{\min }\left( {t}_{k}\right) }{{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right) } \geq  1
\]

In particular, we have \( {K}_{\min }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right) \) if \( k \) is sufficiently large. Since the minimum of the scalar curvature is monotone increasing in time, we have

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  M}}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) }\left( x\right)  \geq  \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  M}}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( {t}_{k}\right) }\left( x\right) ,
\]

hence,

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  M}}{K}_{\max }\left( {x,{\tau }_{k}}\right)  \geq  \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  M}}{K}_{\min }\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right) .
\]

Putting these facts together, we conclude that

\[
{K}_{\max }\left( {\tau }_{k}\right)  \geq  {K}_{\min }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}{K}_{\max }\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\tau }_{k}}\right\rbrack  }}{K}_{\max }\left( t\right)
\]

if \( k \) is sufficiently large. Consequently, we have

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{K}_{\min }\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) }{{K}_{\max }\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) } \geq  1
\]

by Lemma 5.16. This contradicts (40).

Lemma 5.18. We have

\[
\left( {T - t}\right) \mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) } \rightarrow  \frac{n}{2}
\]

and

\[
\left( {T - t}\right) \mathop{\inf }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) } \rightarrow  \frac{n}{2}
\]

as \( t \rightarrow  T \) .

We have \[ \left( {T - t}\right) \mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) } \rightarrow \frac{n}{2} \] and \[ \left( {T - t}\right) \mathop{\inf }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) } \rightarrow \frac{n}{2} \] as \( t \rightarrow T \) .

nodes.proof:
Fix a real number \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) . By Proposition 5.17, there exists a real number \( \eta  > 0 \) such that \( {\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{\varepsilon }{n}{\operatorname{scal}}^{2} \) on \( M \times  \lbrack T - \eta , T) \) . Using Corollary 2.16, we obtain

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal} = \Delta \operatorname{scal} + 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta \operatorname{scal} + \frac{2\left( {1 + \varepsilon }\right) }{n}{\operatorname{scal}}^{2}
\]

on \( M \times  \lbrack T - \eta , T) \) . Hence, it follows from the maximum principle that

\[
\frac{n}{2\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }} + \left( {1 + \varepsilon }\right) \left( {\tau  - t}\right)  \geq  \frac{n}{2\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) }}
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack T - \eta , T) \) and all \( \tau  \in  \lbrack t, T) \) . We now pass to the limit as \( \tau  \rightarrow  T \) . By Lemma 5.14, we have \( \lim \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  T}}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( \tau \right) } = \infty \) . This implies

\[
\left( {1 + \varepsilon }\right) \left( {T - t}\right)  \geq  \frac{n}{2\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) }}
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack T - \eta , T) \) . Since \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) is arbitrary, we conclude that

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {T - t}\right) \mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) }}\right\rbrack   \geq  \frac{n}{2}.
\]

Using Proposition 5.17, we obtain

(41)

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {T - t}\right) \mathop{\inf }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) }}\right\rbrack   \geq  \frac{n}{2}.
\]

On the other hand, it follows from Proposition 2.19 that

\[
T - t \leq  \frac{n}{2\mathop{\inf }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) }}
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . This implies

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {T - t}\right) \mathop{\inf }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) }}\right\rbrack   \leq  \frac{n}{2}.
\]

Using Proposition 5.17, we conclude that

(42)

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\left\lbrack  {\left( {T - t}\right) \mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) }}\right\rbrack   \leq  \frac{n}{2}.
\]

Putting (41) and (42) together, the assertion follows.

\[

nodes.content: Theorem 5.23 (R. Hamilton [45]). Let \( M \) be a compact manifold of dimension \( n \geq  3 \) , and let \( {g}_{0} \) be a Riemannian metric on \( M \) with positive scalar curvature. Suppose that there exists a pinching set \( F \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) such that the curvature tensor of \( {g}_{0} \) lies in \( F \) for all points \( p \in  M \) . Finally, let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be the unique maximal solution to the Ricci flow with initial metric \( {g}_{0} \) . Then, as \( t \rightarrow  T \) , the metrics \( \frac{1}{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {T - t}\right) }g\left( t\right) \) converge in \( {C}^{\infty } \) to a metric of constant sectional curvature 1.

Let us consider the rescaled metrics \( \widetilde{g}\left( t\right)  = \frac{1}{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {T - t}\right) }g\left( t\right) \) . Then \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\widetilde{g}\left( t\right)  = \omega \left( t\right) \) , where

\[
\omega \left( t\right)  =  - \frac{1}{\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {T - t}\right) }\left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{2\left( {T - t}\right) }g\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

We now fix a real number \( \alpha  \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{n - 1}}\right) \) . By Proposition 5.22, we have

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \lbrack 0, T)}}\left\lbrack  {{\left( T - t\right) }^{1 - \alpha }\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\left| \omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widetilde{g}\left( t\right) }}\right\rbrack   < \infty .
\]

Moreover, it follows from Lemma 5.21 that

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \lbrack 0, T)}}\left\lbrack  {{\left( T - t\right) }^{1 - \alpha }\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\left| {D}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widetilde{g}\left( t\right) }}\right\rbrack   < \infty
\]

for \( m = 1,2,\ldots \) By Proposition A.5, the metrics \( \widetilde{g}\left( t\right) \) converge in \( {C}^{\infty } \) to a limit metric \( \bar{g} \) on \( M \) . By Lemma 5.18, the scalar curvature of \( \bar{g} \) is equal to \( n\left( {n - 1}\right) \) . Moreover, it follows from Proposition 5.17 that \( \bar{g} \) has constant sectional curvature. This completes the proof.

\[
K \subset  \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{3}\right)  : {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} \geq  {2\delta }{\lambda }_{3}\text{ and }{\left( {\lambda }_{3} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{1 + \delta } \leq  N\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2}}\right) }\right\}  .
\]

We now define

\[
F = \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{3}\right)  : {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} \geq  {2\delta }{\lambda }_{3}\text{ and }{\left( {\lambda }_{3} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{1 + \delta } \leq  N\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2}}\right) }\right\}  .

Consequently, the set \( F \) is convex. Moreover, the set \( F \) is invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) \) by Proposition 6.6. Therefore, \( F \) is a pinching set.

nodes.proof:
Note that the sum \( {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3} \) is monotone increasing along the Hamilton ODE; hence, the condition \( {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3} \geq   - \frac{1}{2} \) is preserved. We next show that the condition \( {\lambda }_{1} + {f}^{-1}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right)  \geq  0 \) is preserved by the ODE. To that end, we assume that \( {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3} \geq   - \frac{1}{2} \) and

\[
{\lambda }_{1} + {f}^{-1}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Then \( {\lambda }_{1} <  - 1 \) and

\[
{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3} = f\left( {-{\lambda }_{1}}\right)  =  - {\lambda }_{1}\log \left( {-{\lambda }_{1}}\right)  + {\lambda }_{1}.
\]

This implies

\[
{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3} =  - {\lambda }_{1}\log \left( {-{\lambda }_{1}}\right)  > 0.
\]

In particular, we have \( {\lambda }_{3} > 0 \) . Using the chain rule, we obtain

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{f}^{-1}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right)  = \frac{1}{\log \left( {{f}^{-1}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right) }\right) }\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{\log \left( {-{\lambda }_{1}}\right) }\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right)
\]

\[
=  - \frac{{\lambda }_{1}}{{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right) .
\]

Hence, it follows from Corollary 6.4 that

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {f}^{-1}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\lambda }_{1}^{2} + {\lambda }_{2}{\lambda }_{3} - \frac{{\lambda }_{1}\left( {{\lambda }_{1}^{2} + {\lambda }_{2}^{2} + {\lambda }_{3}^{2} + {\lambda }_{1}{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{2}{\lambda }_{3} + {\lambda }_{3}{\lambda }_{1}}\right) }{{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}
\]

\[
= \left( {{\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}}\right) {\lambda }_{3} - \frac{{\lambda }_{1}\left( {{\lambda }_{1}^{2} + {\lambda }_{2}^{2}}\right) }{{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}
\]

\[
\geq  0\text{ . }
\]

This completes the proof.

(i) \( R \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(ii) We have \( R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  \geq  0 \) for all vectors \( \zeta ,\eta  \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) satisfying \( g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = 0. \)

nodes.proof:
(i) \( \Rightarrow \) (ii): Suppose that \( R \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Let \( \zeta ,\eta  \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) be two linearly independent vectors satisfying \( g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = \; g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = 0 \) , and let \( \sigma  \subset  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) denote the complex two-plane spanned by \( \zeta ,\eta \) . By Corollary B.5, there exists an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  V \) such that \( {e}_{1} + i{e}_{2} \in  \sigma \) and \( {e}_{3} + i{e}_{4} \in  \sigma \) . For abbreviation, let \( z = {e}_{1} + i{e}_{2} \) and \( w = {e}_{3} + i{e}_{4} \) . Since \( z, w \in  \sigma \) , we can find complex numbers \( a, b, c, d \) such that \( \zeta  = {az} + {bw} \) and \( \eta  = {cz} + {dw} \) . This implies

\[
R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  = {\left| ad - bc\right| }^{2}R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right) .
\]

Using the first Bianchi identity, we obtain

\[
R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)  = R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Thus, we conclude that \( R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  \geq  0 \) .

(ii) \( \Rightarrow \) (i): We now assume that (ii) holds. We claim that \( R \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \) . We define \( \zeta  = {e}_{1} + i{e}_{2} \) and \( \eta  = {e}_{3} + i{e}_{4} \) . Then \( g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = \; g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = 0 \) . Hence, it follows from the first Bianchi identity that

\[
0 \leq  R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  = R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right) .
\]

Consequently, \( R \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

nodes.content: Proposition 7.3 (M. Micallef, M. Wang [61]). Let \( V \) be a vector space of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) equipped with an inner product. Moreover, let \( R \) be an algebraic curvature tensor on \( V \) with nonnegative isotropic curvature. Then the scalar curvature of \( R \) is nonnegative. Moreover, if the Ricci tensor of \( R \) is equal to zero, then \( R = 0 \) .

Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) be an arbitrary orthonormal basis of \( V \) . Since \( R \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, we have

\[
R\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{k},{e}_{i},{e}_{k}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{l},{e}_{i},{e}_{l}}\right)
\]

(45)

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{j},{e}_{k},{e}_{j},{e}_{k}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{j},{e}_{l},{e}_{j},{e}_{l}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

whenever \( i, j, k, l \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\} \) are mutually distinct. Summation over \( l \in \; \{ 1,\ldots , n\}  \smallsetminus  \{ i, j, k\} \) yields

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{i}}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{j},{e}_{j}}\right)  - {2R}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j},{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {n - 4}\right) \left( {R\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{k},{e}_{i},{e}_{k}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{j},{e}_{k},{e}_{j},{e}_{k}}\right) }\right)  \geq  0
\]

if \( i, j, k \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\} \) are mutually distinct. In the next step, we take the sum over \( k \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\}  \smallsetminus  \{ i, j\} \) . This implies

(46)

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{i}}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{j},{e}_{j}}\right)  - {2R}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j},{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

if \( i, j \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\} \) are distinct. Summation over \( j \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\}  \smallsetminus  \{ i\} \) yields

\[
\left( {n - 4}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{i}}\right)  + \operatorname{scal} \geq  0
\]

for all \( i \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\} \) . This implies scal \( \geq  0 \) . From this, the first statement follows.

In order to prove the second statement, we assume that \( \operatorname{Ric} = 0 \) . Using (46), we conclude that \( R \) has nonpositive sectional curvature. From this, we deduce that \( R = 0 \) .

nodes.content: Theorem 7.7 (S. Brendle, R. Schoen [20]; H. Nguyen [64]). Let \( M \) be a compact manifold, and let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on M. If \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, then \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

\]

\]

\[
\left\langle  {E{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right\rangle   = {R}_{12pq},\;\left\langle  {F{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right\rangle   = {R}_{34pq}
\]

for \( p, q \in  \{ 5,\ldots , n\} \) . Note that \( A \) and \( B \) are symmetric, while \( E \) and \( F \) are antisymmetric. Using Lemma 7.12, we obtain

\]

\]

\[
- 2\left\langle  {F{w}_{1},{w}_{2}}\right\rangle   - 2\left\langle  {E{w}_{3},{w}_{4}}\right\rangle   \geq  0
\]

for all vectors \( {w}_{1},{w}_{2},{w}_{3},{w}_{4} \in  W \) . We next define

\[
\mathbb{M} = \left\lbrack  \begin{matrix} B & F &  - {C}^{ * } &  - {D}^{ * } \\   - F & B & {D}^{ * } &  - {C}^{ * } \\   - C & D & A & E \\   - D &  - C &  - E & A \end{matrix}\right\rbrack

\]

\[

\]

\]

as claimed.

(i) \( \widetilde{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(ii) We have

nodes.proof:
(i) \( \Rightarrow \) (ii): Suppose that \( \widetilde{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \) , and let \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . We define

\[
{\widetilde{e}}_{1} = \left( {{e}_{1},0}\right) ,\;{\widetilde{e}}_{2} = \left( {{e}_{2},0}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{e}}_{3} = \left( {{e}_{3},0}\right) ,\;{\widetilde{e}}_{4} = \left( {\lambda {e}_{4},\sqrt{1 - {\lambda }^{2}}}\right) .
\]

Since \( \widetilde{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, we have

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{3}}\right)  + \widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{4},{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3}}\right)  + \widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{4},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

This implies

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

as claimed.

(ii) \( \Rightarrow \) (iii): We next assume that (ii) holds. Let \( \zeta ,\eta  \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) be two linearly independent vectors satisfying \( g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right) g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  - g{\left( \zeta ,\eta \right) }^{2} = 0 \) , and let \( \sigma  \subset  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) be the complex two-plane spanned by \( \zeta ,\eta \) . By Corollary B.4, we can find an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  V \) and a real number \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) such that \( {e}_{1} + i{e}_{2} \in  \sigma \) and \( {e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4} \in  \sigma \) . For abbreviation, let \( z = {e}_{1} + i{e}_{2} \) and \( w = {e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4} \) . Since \( z, w \in  \sigma \) , we can find complex numbers \( a, b, c, d \) such that \( \zeta  = {az} + {bw} \) and \( \eta  = {cz} + {dw} \) . This implies

\[
R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  = {\left| ad - bc\right| }^{2}R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right) .
\]

Moreover, it follows from the first Bianchi identity that

\[
R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)  = R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Putting these facts together, we conclude that \( R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  \geq  0 \) .

(iii) \( \Rightarrow \) (i): We now assume that (iii) holds. We claim that \( \widetilde{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Let \( \left\{  {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \times  \mathbb{R} \) . We write \( {\widetilde{e}}_{j} = \left( {{v}_{j},{y}_{j}}\right) \) , where \( {v}_{j} \in  V \) and \( {y}_{j} \in  \mathbb{R} \) . Moreover, we define \( \zeta  = {v}_{1} + i{v}_{2} \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) and \( \eta  = {v}_{3} + i{v}_{4} \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) . Since \( \left\{  {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal four-frame, we have \( \left\langle  {{v}_{k},{v}_{l}}\right\rangle   = {\delta }_{kl} - {y}_{k}{y}_{l} \) for all \( k, l \in  \{ 1,2,3,4\} \) . This implies

\[
g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = {\left| {v}_{1}\right| }^{2} - {\left| {v}_{2}\right| }^{2} + {2i}\left\langle  {{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - {y}_{1}^{2} + {y}_{2}^{2} - {2i}{y}_{1}{y}_{2}
\]

\[
=  - {\left( {y}_{1} + i{y}_{2}\right) }^{2},
\]

\[
g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = {\left| {v}_{3}\right| }^{2} - {\left| {v}_{4}\right| }^{2} + {2i}\left\langle  {{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - {y}_{3}^{2} + {y}_{4}^{2} - {2i}{y}_{3}{y}_{4}
\]

\[
=  - {\left( {y}_{3} + i{y}_{4}\right) }^{2},
\]

and

\[
g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = \left\langle  {{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right\rangle   - \left\langle  {{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right\rangle   + i\left\langle  {{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right\rangle   + i\left\langle  {{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - {y}_{1}{y}_{3} + {y}_{2}{y}_{4} - i{y}_{1}{y}_{4} - i{y}_{2}{y}_{3}
\]

\[
=  - \left( {{y}_{1} + i{y}_{2}}\right) \left( {{y}_{3} + i{y}_{4}}\right) \text{ . }
\]

Therefore, we have

\[
g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right) g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  - g{\left( \zeta ,\eta \right) }^{2} = 0.
\]

Using the first Bianchi identity, we obtain

\[
0 \leq  R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  = R\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

This implies

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{3}}\right)  + \widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{4},{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3}}\right)  + \widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{4},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Consequently, \( \widetilde{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

nodes.proof:
(i) \( \Rightarrow \) (ii): Suppose that \( \widehat{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \) , and let \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . We define

\[
{\widehat{e}}_{1} = \left( {{e}_{1},\left( {0,0}\right) }\right) ,\;{\widehat{e}}_{2} = \left( {\mu {e}_{2},\left( {0,\sqrt{1 - {\mu }^{2}}}\right) }\right) ,
\]

\[
{\widehat{e}}_{3} = \left( {{e}_{3},\left( {0,0}\right) }\right) ,\;{\widehat{e}}_{4} = \left( {\lambda {e}_{4},\left( {\sqrt{1 - {\lambda }^{2}},0}\right) }\right) .
\]

Clearly, the vectors \( \left\{  {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right\} \) form an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) . Since \( \widehat{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, we have

\[
\widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{3}}\right)  + \widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{4},{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3}}\right)  + \widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{4},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

This implies

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

(ii) \( \Rightarrow \) (iii): We next assume that (ii) holds. Let \( \zeta ,\eta  \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) be two linearly independent vectors. Moreover, let \( \sigma  \subset  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) denote the complex two-plane spanned by \( \zeta ,\eta \) . By Proposition B.3, we can find an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  V \) and real numbers \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) such that \( {e}_{1} + {i\mu }{e}_{2} \in \; \sigma \) and \( {e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4} \in  \sigma \) . Let \( z = {e}_{1} + {i\mu }{e}_{2} \) and \( w = {e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4} \) . Since \( \zeta ,\eta  \in  \sigma \) , we can find complex numbers \( a, b, c, d \) such that \( \zeta  = {az} + {bw} \) and \( \eta  = {cz} + {dw} \) . This implies

\[
R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  = {\left| ad - bc\right| }^{2}R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right) .
\]

Using the first Bianchi identity, we obtain

\[
R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)  = R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Putting these facts together, we conclude that \( R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  \geq  0 \) .

(iii) \( \Rightarrow \) (i): We now assume that (iii) holds. We claim that \( \widehat{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Let \( \left\{  {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) . We write \( {\widehat{e}}_{j} = \left( {{v}_{j},{y}_{j}}\right) \) , where \( {v}_{j} \in  V \) and \( {y}_{j} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) . Moreover, we define \( \zeta  = {v}_{1} + i{v}_{2} \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) and \( \eta  = {v}_{3} + i{v}_{4} \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) . It follows from the first Bianchi identity that

\[
0 \leq  R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  = R\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

This implies

\[
\widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{3}}\right)  + \widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{4},{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3}}\right)  + \widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{4},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\widehat{R}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Therefore, \( \widehat{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

nodes.content:
Proposition 7.22. Let \( R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) be an algebraic curvature tensor on \( V \) , and let \( S \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {V \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2}}\right) \) be defined by (56). Then the following statements are equivalent:

(i) \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(ii) We have

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  + \left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  V \) and all \( \lambda ,\mu  \in \; \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

(iii) We have

\[
R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  + \left| {g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right) g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  - g{\left( \zeta ,\eta \right) }^{2}}\right|  \geq  0
\]

for all vectors \( \zeta ,\eta  \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) .

Then the following statements are equivalent: (i) \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. nodes.proof:
(i) \( \Rightarrow \) (ii): Suppose that \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \) , and let \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . We define

\[
{\widehat{e}}_{1} = \left( {{e}_{1},\left( {0,0}\right) }\right) ,\;{\widehat{e}}_{2} = \left( {\mu {e}_{2},\left( {0,\sqrt{1 - {\mu }^{2}}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
{\widehat{e}}_{3} = \left( {{e}_{3},\left( {0,0}\right) }\right) ,\;{\widehat{e}}_{4} = \left( {\lambda {e}_{4},\left( {\sqrt{1 - {\lambda }^{2}},0}\right) }\right) .
\]

Clearly, the vectors \( \left\{  {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right\} \) form an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) . Since \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, we have

\[
S\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{3}}\right)  + S\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{4},{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ S\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3}}\right)  + S\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{4},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2S}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Using (56), we obtain

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  + \left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

(ii) \( \Rightarrow \) (iii): We next assume that (ii) holds. Let \( \zeta ,\eta  \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) be two linearly independent vectors. Moreover, we denote by \( \sigma  \subset  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) the complex two-plane spanned by \( \zeta ,\eta \) . By Proposition B.3, we can find an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  V \) and real numbers \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) such that \( {e}_{1} + \; {i\mu }{e}_{2} \in  \sigma \) and \( {e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4} \in  \sigma \) . For abbreviation, let \( z = {e}_{1} + {i\mu }{e}_{2} \) and \( w = {e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4} \) . Since \( z, w \in  \sigma \) , we can find complex numbers \( a, b, c, d \) such that \( \zeta  = {az} + {bw} \) and \( \eta  = {cz} + {dw} \) . This implies

\[
R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  = {\left| ad - bc\right| }^{2}R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)
\]

and

\[
g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right) g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  - g{\left( \zeta ,\eta \right) }^{2} = {\left( ad - bc\right) }^{2}\left( {g\left( {z, z}\right) g\left( {w, w}\right)  - g{\left( z, w\right) }^{2}}\right) .
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  + \left| {g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right) g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  - g{\left( \zeta ,\eta \right) }^{2}}\right|
\]

\[
= {\left| ad - bc\right| }^{2}\left\lbrack  {R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)  + \left| {g\left( {z, z}\right) g\left( {w, w}\right)  - g{\left( z, w\right) }^{2}}\right| }\right\rbrack  .
\]

Moreover, it follows from the first Bianchi identity that

\[
R\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)  + \left| {g\left( {z, z}\right) g\left( {w, w}\right)  - g{\left( z, w\right) }^{2}}\right|
\]

\[
= R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  + \left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Thus, we conclude that

\[
R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  + \left| {g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right) g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  - g{\left( \zeta ,\eta \right) }^{2}}\right|  \geq  0,
\]

as claimed.

(iii) \( \Rightarrow \) (i): We now assume that (iii) holds. We claim that \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Let \( \left\{  {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) . We write \( {\widehat{e}}_{j} = \left( {{v}_{j},{y}_{j}}\right) \) , where \( {v}_{j} \in  V \) and \( {y}_{j} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) . Moreover, we define \( \zeta  = {v}_{1} + i{v}_{2} \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) and \( \eta  = {v}_{3} + i{v}_{4} \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) . Note that

\[
R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  = R\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

by the first Bianchi identity. Since \( \left\{  {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal four-frame, we have \( \left\langle  {{v}_{k},{v}_{l}}\right\rangle   = {\delta }_{kl} - \left\langle  {{y}_{k},{y}_{l}}\right\rangle \) for all \( k, l \in  \{ 1,2,3,4\} \) . This implies

\[
g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = {\left| {v}_{1}\right| }^{2} - {\left| {v}_{2}\right| }^{2} + {2i}\left\langle  {{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - {\left| {y}_{1}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {y}_{2}\right| }^{2} - {2i}\left\langle  {{y}_{1},{y}_{2}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - g\left( {{y}_{1} + i{y}_{2},{y}_{1} + i{y}_{2}}\right) ,
\]

\[
g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = {\left| {v}_{3}\right| }^{2} - {\left| {v}_{4}\right| }^{2} + {2i}\left\langle  {{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - {\left| {y}_{3}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {y}_{4}\right| }^{2} - {2i}\left\langle  {{y}_{3},{y}_{4}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - g\left( {{y}_{3} + i{y}_{4},{y}_{3} + i{y}_{4}}\right) ,
\]

and

\[
g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = \left\langle  {{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right\rangle   - \left\langle  {{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right\rangle   + i\left\langle  {{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right\rangle   + i\left\langle  {{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - \left\langle  {{y}_{1},{y}_{3}}\right\rangle   + \left\langle  {{y}_{2},{y}_{4}}\right\rangle   - i\left\langle  {{y}_{1},{y}_{4}}\right\rangle   - i\left\langle  {{y}_{2},{y}_{3}}\right\rangle
\]

\[
=  - g\left( {{y}_{1} + i{y}_{2},{y}_{3} + i{y}_{4}}\right) .
\]

Using Proposition B.1, we obtain

\[
\left| {g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right) g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  - g{\left( \zeta ,\eta \right) }^{2}}\right|
\]

\[
= \left| {g\left( {{y}_{1} + i{y}_{2},{y}_{1} + i{y}_{2}}\right) g\left( {{y}_{3} + i{y}_{4},{y}_{3} + i{y}_{4}}\right)  - g{\left( {y}_{1} + i{y}_{2},{y}_{3} + i{y}_{4}\right) }^{2}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  g\left( {{y}_{1} + i{y}_{2},{y}_{1} - i{y}_{2}}\right) g\left( {{y}_{3} + i{y}_{4},{y}_{3} - i{y}_{4}}\right)  - {\left| g\left( {y}_{1} + i{y}_{2},{y}_{3} - i{y}_{4}\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
= \left( {{\left| {y}_{1}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {y}_{2}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {{\left| {y}_{3}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {y}_{4}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
- {\left( \left\langle  {y}_{1},{y}_{3}\right\rangle   + \left\langle  {y}_{2},{y}_{4}\right\rangle  \right) }^{2} - {\left( \left\langle  {y}_{1},{y}_{4}\right\rangle   - \left\langle  {y}_{2},{y}_{3}\right\rangle  \right) }^{2}.
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
0 \leq  R\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  + \left| {g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right) g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  - g{\left( \zeta ,\eta \right) }^{2}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  R\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  + \left( {{\left| {y}_{1}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {y}_{2}\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {{\left| {y}_{3}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {y}_{4}\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
- {\left( \left\langle  {y}_{1},{y}_{3}\right\rangle   + \left\langle  {y}_{2},{y}_{4}\right\rangle  \right) }^{2} - {\left( \left\langle  {y}_{1},{y}_{4}\right\rangle   - \left\langle  {y}_{2},{y}_{3}\right\rangle  \right) }^{2}.
\]

Using (56), we conclude that

\[
S\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{3}}\right)  + S\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{4},{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ S\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3}}\right)  + S\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{4},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2S}\left( {{\widehat{e}}_{1},{\widehat{e}}_{2},{\widehat{e}}_{3},{\widehat{e}}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Therefore, \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, as claimed.

Let \( G \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) denote the set of all algebraic curvature tensors on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) with the property that \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature:

\[
G = \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)  : S\text{ has nonnegative isotropic curvature }}\right\}  .
\]

Clearly, \( G \) is closed, convex, and \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant.

Proposition 7.26. Let \( R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( V\right) \) be an algebraic curvature tensor on \( V \) , and let \( S \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {V \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2}}\right) \) be defined by (56). We assume that \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Moreover, suppose that \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal four-frame in \( V \) satisfying

\[

#### 7.7.An overview of various curvature conditions

We conclude this chapter with a diagram showing the logical implications among various curvature conditions. Given a Riemannian manifold \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) , we consider the following curvature conditions:

(C1) \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is weakly \( 1/4 \) -pinched in the pointwise sense.

(C2) \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative sectional curvature.

(C3) \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative Ricci curvature.

(C4) \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative scalar curvature.

(C5) \( \left( {M, g}\right)  \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(C6) \( \left( {M, g}\right)  \times  {S}^{2}\left( 1\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(C7) \( \left( {M, g}\right)  \times  \mathbb{R} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(C8) \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(C9) \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative curvature operator.

(C10) \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has two-nonnegative curvature operator.

The curvature conditions (C4)-(C10) are preserved by the Ricci flow. The following diagram shows the logical implications among the curvature conditions (C1)-(C10). Most of these implications have been established in the preceeding sections (see also Proposition 8.13 below).

Definition 8.1. Let \( A \) and \( B \) be symmetric bilinear forms on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . The Kulkarni-Nomizu product of \( A \) and \( B \) is defined by

\[
{\left( A \oslash  B\right) }_{ijkl} = {A}_{ik}{B}_{jl} - {A}_{il}{B}_{jk} - {A}_{jk}{B}_{il} + {A}_{jl}{B}_{ik}.
\]

It is straightforward to verify that \( A \oslash  B \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) .

nodes.content:
Given any algebraic curvature tensor \( R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) , we define

\[
{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right)  = \left( {\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - 2\left( {a - b}\right) }\right) \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  } \oslash  \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }
\]

(65)

\[
+ {2a}\operatorname{Ric} \oslash  \operatorname{Ric} + 2{b}^{2}{\operatorname{Ric}}^{2} \oslash  \operatorname{id}
\]

\[
+ \frac{n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}\text{ id } \oslash  \text{ id. }
\]

Clearly, \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right)  \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) . The Ricci and scalar curvature of \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) are given by

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)  =  - {4b}{\operatorname{Ric}}^{2} + \frac{4}{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \text{ scal }\operatorname{Ric}
\]

(66)

\[
+ 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}\mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{4}{{n}^{2}}\left( {a - b}\right) {\operatorname{scal}}^{2}\text{ id }
\]

and

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)  = \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) }{n}a{\operatorname{scal}}^{2} - {4b}{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}
\]

(67)

\[
+ 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]
