nodes.label: Proposition 8.5
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.section_title: 8.1. An algebraic identity for curvature tensors
nodes.content:
Proposition 8.5 (C. Böhm, B. Wilking [14]). For every algebraic curvature tensor \( R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) , we have

\[
{\ell }_{a, b}^{-1}\left( {Q\left( {{\ell }_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) }\right)  = Q\left( R\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) .
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 8.5 (C. Böhm, B. Wilking [14]). For every algebraic curvature tensor \( R \in {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) , we have \[ {\ell }_{a, b}^{-1}\left( {Q\left( {{\ell }_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) }\right) = Q\left( R\right) + {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) . \]

nodes.proof:
Note that

\[
{\ell }_{a, b}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)  = {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right)  + b\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \varnothing \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{n}\left( {a - b}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \text{ id } \oslash  \text{ id. }
\]

It follows from (65) that

\[
{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right)  = \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) \operatorname{Ric} \oslash  \operatorname{Ric} + 2{b}^{2}{\operatorname{Ric}}^{2} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
- \frac{2}{n}\left( {n{b}^{2} - 2\left( {a - b}\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\operatorname{Ric} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{{n}^{2}}\left( {n{b}^{2} - 2\left( {a - b}\right) }\right) {\operatorname{scal}}^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

Using (66) and (67), we obtain

\[
{\ell }_{a, b}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)  = \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) \operatorname{Ric} \oslash  \operatorname{Ric} - 2{b}^{2}{\operatorname{Ric}}^{2} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \left( {2{b}^{2} + \frac{4}{n}\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\operatorname{Ric} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{n}\left( {n{b}^{2} - 2\left( {a - b}\right) }\right) {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{{n}^{2}}\left( {n{b}^{2} - 2\left( {a - b}\right) }\right) {\operatorname{scal}}^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{4}{{n}^{2}}\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {b + \left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) {\operatorname{scal}}^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

Using Lemma 8.4 and the identity \( {\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} = {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2} + \frac{1}{n}{\operatorname{scal}}^{2} \) , we conclude that

\[
Q\left( {{\ell }_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)  = {\ell }_{a, b}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  + {\ell }_{a, b}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) .
\]

This completes the proof.

nodes.label: Definition 8.2-extra-1
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.section_title: 8.2. Constructing a family of invariant cones
nodes.content:
Let us consider a cone \( C \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) , where \( n \geq  4 \) . We say that \( C \) satisfies condition \( \left( \star \right) \) if the following conditions are met:

- \( C \) is closed, convex, and \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant.

- \( C \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) \) .

- Every algebraic curvature tensor \( R \in  C \) has nonnegative sectional curvature.

- If \( R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) has nonnegative curvature operator, then \( R \in  C \) .

nodes.content:
Proposition 8.6. Assume that \( C \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) is a cone satisfying \( \left( \star \right) \) . Fix a real number \( b \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack \) , and let

\[
{2a} = \frac{{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}},\;\delta  = 1 - \frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}.
\]

Then the cone

\[
\left\{  {{\ell }_{a, b}\left( R\right)  : R \in  C\text{ and }\operatorname{Ric} \geq  \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\mathrm{{id}}}\right\}
\]

is transversally invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
The proof is analogous to the proof of Lemma 3.4 in [14]. In view of Proposition 8.5, it suffices to show that the cone

\[
\left\{  {R \in  C : \operatorname{Ric} \geq  \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\mathrm{{id}}}\right\}
\]

is transversally invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) . In order to verify this, we consider an algebraic curvature tensor \( R \in  C \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) satisfying \( \operatorname{Ric} \geq  \frac{\delta }{n} \) scal id. We will show:

(i) The sum \( Q\left( R\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R}C \) .

(ii) If \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) is a unit vector satisfying \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  = \frac{\delta }{n} \) scal, then

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)
\]

\[
> \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  + \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) .
\]

Proof of (i). By scaling, we may assume that scal \( = n \) . We can find an orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right)  = 0 \) for \( i \neq  j \) . For abbreviation, we write \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{k},{e}_{k}}\right)  = 1 + {\lambda }_{k} \) , where \( {\lambda }_{k} \geq  \delta  - 1 \) and \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}{\lambda }_{k} = 0. \)

Fix a pair of indices \( i \neq  j \) . It is easy to see that \( {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j} \) is an eigenvector of \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) with eigenvalue \( {\sigma }_{ij} = {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j},{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right) \) . Using the definition of \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) , we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\sigma }_{ij} = \left( {\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - 2\left( {a - b}\right) }\right) {\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j}
\]

\[
+ {2a}\left( {1 + {\lambda }_{i}}\right) \left( {1 + {\lambda }_{j}}\right)  + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2}.
\]

This implies

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\sigma }_{ij} = \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{i} + \frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{j} + \frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {2a}\frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}} + {b}^{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2};
\]

hence,

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\sigma }_{ij} > \frac{n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

Moreover, we have

\[
n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}} \geq  0
\]

by our choice of \( a, b \) . Thus, we conclude that \( {\sigma }_{ij} > 0 \) . Therefore, \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) has positive curvature operator.

By assumption, \( C \) is a convex cone that contains all nonnegative curvature operators. Hence, \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R}C \) . Moreover, we have \( Q\left( R\right)  \in  {T}_{R}C \) since \( C \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE. Consequently, the sum \( Q\left( R\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R}C \) .

Proof of (ii). Suppose that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  = \frac{\delta }{n} \) scal for some unit vector \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . By scaling, we may assume that \( \operatorname{scal} = n \) . Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal basis of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right)  = 0 \) for \( i \neq  j \) . Then

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  = 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}R\left( {v,{e}_{k}, v,{e}_{k}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{k},{e}_{k}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {2\delta }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}R\left( {v,{e}_{k}, v,{e}_{k}}\right)  = {2\delta }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  = 2{\delta }^{2}
\]

and

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  = 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} = {2n} + 2{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

From this, we deduce that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  =  - {2\delta }\left( {1 - \delta }\right)  - \frac{2}{n}\delta {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

Using (66) and (67), we obtain

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  =  - {4b}{\delta }^{2} + 4\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) \delta  + 4\left( {a - b}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}
\]

and

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)  = {4n}\left( {n - 1}\right) a - {4b}{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

This implies

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {4a}\left( {1 - \delta }\right)  - {4b}{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{4b}{n}\delta {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2} + 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }\left( {1 - \delta }\right) {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - {2\delta }\left( {1 - \delta }\right)  + {4a}\left( {1 - \delta }\right)  - {4b}{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{2}
\]

\[
- \frac{2\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n}\delta {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2} + 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }\left( {1 - \delta }\right) {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

Note that \( {2a} - {2b}\left( {1 - \delta }\right)  = \delta \) by our choice of \( a, b \) , and \( \delta \) . From this, we deduce that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - \frac{2\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n}\delta {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2} + 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }\left( {1 - \delta }\right) {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

We claim that the right-hand side is positive. Since \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  = \delta  - 1 < 0 \) , we have \( {\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} > 0 \) . Hence, it suffices to show that

(68)

\[
\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\left( {1 - \delta }\right)  > \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) \delta .
\]

By our choice of \( a, b \) , we have

\[
{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right)
\]

\[
- \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)
\]

\[
= {2n}{b}^{2}\left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right)  + \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a\left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right)
\]

\[
= {2n}{b}^{2}\left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right)  > 0.
\]

This implies

\[
\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} > \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) .
\]

Since \( \delta  = \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2}\left( {1 - \delta }\right) \) , the inequality (68) follows.

nodes.proof:
The proof is analogous to the proof of Lemma 3.5 in [14]. As above, it suffices to show that the cone

\[
\left\{  {R \in  C : \operatorname{Ric} \geq  \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\mathrm{{id}}}\right\}
\]

is transversally invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) . Consider an algebraic curvature tensor \( R \in  C \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) satisfying Ric \( \geq  \frac{\delta }{n} \) scal id. We claim:

(i) The sum \( Q\left( R\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R}C \) .

(ii) If \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) is a unit vector satisfying \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  = \frac{\delta }{n} \) scal, then

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)
\]

\[
> \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  + \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) .
\]

Proof of (i). By scaling, we may assume that \( \operatorname{scal} = n \) . There exists an orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right)  = 0 \) for \( i \neq  j \) . For abbreviation, we write \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{k},{e}_{k}}\right)  = 1 + {\lambda }_{k} \) , where \( {\lambda }_{k} \geq  \delta  - 1 \) and \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}{\lambda }_{k} = 0 \)

Fix a pair of indices \( i \neq  j \) . It is easy to see that \( {e}_{i} \land  {e}_{j} \) is an eigenvector of \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) with eigenvalue \( {\sigma }_{ij} = {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j},{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right) \) . Using the definition of \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) , we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\sigma }_{ij} = \left( {\frac{n + 2}{4} - {2a}}\right) {\lambda }_{i}{\lambda }_{j} + {2a}\left( {1 + {\lambda }_{i}}\right) \left( {1 + {\lambda }_{j}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
- \frac{1}{4}\frac{{2a} - 1}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

This implies

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\sigma }_{ij} = \frac{n + 2}{4}\left( {{\lambda }_{i} + \frac{4}{n + 2}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{j} + \frac{4}{n + 2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {{2a} - 1}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{i} + {\lambda }_{j} + \frac{8}{n - 2 + {8a}}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4}\left( {{\lambda }_{i}^{2} + {\lambda }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{n - 2}{n + 2} + \left( {{2a} - 1}\right) \frac{n - {10} + {8a}}{n - 2 + {8a}} - \frac{1}{4}\frac{{2a} - 1}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2};
\]

hence,

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\sigma }_{ij} \geq  \frac{n - 2}{n + 2} + \left( {{2a} - 1}\right) \frac{n - {10} + {8a}}{n - 2 + {8a}} - \frac{1}{4}\frac{{2a} - 1}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

By assumption, we have \( {\lambda }_{k} \geq  \delta  - 1 \) for \( k = 1,\ldots , n \) . Since \( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}{\lambda }_{k} = 0 \) , it follows that \( {\lambda }_{k} \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 - \delta }\right) \) for \( k = 1,\ldots , n \) . Consequently, we have

\[
n\left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{2} - {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{n}\left( {{\lambda }_{k} + 1 - \delta }\right) \left( {\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 - \delta }\right)  - {\lambda }_{k}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\sigma }_{ij} \geq  \frac{n - 2}{n + 2} + \left( {{2a} - 1}\right) \frac{n - {10} + {8a}}{n - 2 + {8a}} - \frac{{2a} - 1}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\frac{{4n}\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{\left( n - 2 + 8a\right) }^{2}}.
\]

Since \( a > \frac{1}{2} \) , we conclude that

\[
\frac{1}{2}\left( {n - 2 + {8a}}\right) {\sigma }_{ij}
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{n - 2}{n + 2}\left( {n - 2 + {8a}}\right)  + \left( {{2a} - 1}\right) \left( {n - {10} + {8a}}\right)  - \frac{{2a} - 1}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\frac{{4n}\left( {n - 1}\right) }{n - 2 + {8a}}
\]

\[
> \frac{n - 2}{n + 2}\left( {n - 2 + {8a}}\right)  + \left( {{2a} - 1}\right) \left( {n - {10} + {8a}}\right)  - \left( {{2a} - 1}\right) \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) }{n + 2}
\]

\[
= \left( {n - 3}\right)  + \left( {{2a} - 1}\right) \left( {n - 2 - \frac{4}{n + 2}}\right)  + {\left( 4a - 3\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
> 0\text{ . }
\]

Hence, \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) has positive curvature operator.

Therefore, \( {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R}C \) . Moreover, we have \( Q\left( R\right)  \in  {T}_{R}C \) since \( C \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE. Consequently, the sum \( Q\left( R\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R}C \) .

Proof of (ii). Suppose that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  = \frac{\delta }{n} \) scal for some unit vector \( v \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . By scaling, we may assume that \( \operatorname{scal} = n \) . Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal basis of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) such that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{i},{e}_{j}}\right)  = 0 \) for \( i \neq  j \) . Arguing as in the proof of Proposition 8.6, we obtain

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - {2\delta }\left( {1 - \delta }\right)  + {4a}\left( {1 - \delta }\right)  - {4b}{\left( 1 - \delta \right) }^{2}
\]

\[
- \frac{2\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n}\delta {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2} + 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }\left( {1 - \delta }\right) {\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\right| }^{2}.
\]

Since \( b = \frac{1}{2} \) , it follows that

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right) \left( {v, v}\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {Q\left( R\right) }\right)  - \frac{\delta }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{D}_{a, b}\left( R\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {{4a} - 2}\right) \left( {1 - \delta }\right)  + \frac{1}{2}\frac{n}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\left( {1 - \delta }\right) {\left| {\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }}^{2}\right| }^{2} > 0.
\]

This completes the proof of Proposition 8.7.

### 8.3. Proof of the Differentiable Sphere Theorem

Throughout this section, we fix an integer \( n \geq  4 \) . Moreover, let \( \widehat{C} \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) be the cone introduced in Section 7.5. For each \( s > 0 \) , we define a cone \( \widehat{C}\left( s\right)  \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) by

\[
\widehat{C}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  {{\ell }_{a\left( s\right) , b\left( s\right) }\left( R\right)  : R \in  \widehat{C}\text{ and }\operatorname{Ric} \geq  \frac{\delta \left( s\right) }{n}\text{ scal id }}\right\}  ,
\]

where

\[
{2a}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} \frac{{2s} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {s}^{2}}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {s}^{2}} & \text{ for }0 < s \leq  \frac{1}{2}, \\  {2s} & \text{ for }s > \frac{1}{2}, \end{array}\right.
\]

\[
{2b}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} {2s} & \text{ for }0 < s \leq  \frac{1}{2}, \\  1 & \text{ for }s > \frac{1}{2}, \end{array}\right.
\]

\[
\delta \left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} 1 - \frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {s}^{2}} & \text{ for }0 < s \leq  \frac{1}{2} \\  1 - \frac{4}{n - 2 + {8s}} & \text{ for }s > \frac{1}{2} \end{array}\right.
\]

Note that \( a\left( s\right) , b\left( s\right) \) , and \( \delta \left( s\right) \) are continuous functions of \( s \) .

For each \( s > 0 \) , the cone \( \widehat{C}\left( s\right) \) is closed, convex, and \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant. Moreover, the point \( I \) lies in the interior of \( \widehat{C}\left( s\right) \) for each \( s > 0 \) .

The first statement is a consequence of Proposition 8.6 and Proposition 8.7. In order to prove the second statement, we fix a real number \( s > \frac{1}{2} \) . Every algebraic curvature tensor in \( \widehat{C}\left( s\right) \) can be written in the form \( {\ell }_{s,\frac{1}{2}}\left( R\right) \) for some curvature tensor \( R \in  \widehat{C} \) . Since \( R \) has nonnegative sectional curvature, we have

\[
0 \leq  R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{1}}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

for each orthonormal two-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\}   \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Using (62), we obtain

\[
{\ell }_{s,\frac{1}{2}}\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right)  \geq  \frac{{2s} - 1}{n}\text{ scal }
\]

and

\[
{\ell }_{s,\frac{1}{2}}\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{1}}\right)  + \operatorname{Ric}\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{2}}\right)  + \frac{{2s} - 1}{n}\text{ scal }
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{{2s} + n - 1}{n}\text{ scal }
\]

for each orthonormal two-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\}   \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Therefore, the curvature tensor \( {\ell }_{s,\frac{1}{2}}\left( R\right) \) is weakly \( \frac{{2s} - 1}{{2s} + n - 1} \) -pinched.

Lemma 8.9. Fix a compact interval \( \left\lbrack  {\alpha ,\beta }\right\rbrack   \subset  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) . Then there exists a real number \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , depending only on \( \alpha ,\beta \) , and \( n \) , with the following property.

If \( F \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) is a closed set which is invariant under the Hamilton ODE and satisfies

\]

\[

\]

is also invariant under the Hamilton ODE. Moreover, we have

\[
\{ R \in  F : \operatorname{scal}\left( R\right)  \leq  h\}  \subset  \widehat{F}.
\]

The proof is similar to the proof of Theorem 4.1 in [14] (see also [20], Proposition 16). If \( R \in  \widehat{C}\left( s\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) for some \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {\alpha ,\beta  + 1}\right\rbrack \) , then \( Q\left( R\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R}\widehat{C}\left( s\right) \) by Proposition 8.8. Hence, there exists a constant \( N \geq  1 \) , depending only on \( \alpha ,\beta \) , and \( n \) , with the following property: if \( \operatorname{scal}\left( R\right)  \geq  N \) and \( R \in  \widehat{C}\left( s\right) \) for some \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {\alpha ,\beta  + 1}\right\rbrack \) , then \( Q\left( {R - {2I}}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R}\widehat{C}\left( s\right) \) .

Since the cones \( \widehat{C}\left( s\right) \) vary continuously in \( s \) , we can find a real number \( \varepsilon  \in  (0,1\rbrack \) , depending only on \( \alpha ,\beta \) , and \( n \) , such that

\[
\left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)  : R + I \in  \widehat{C}\left( s\right) \text{ and }\operatorname{scal}\left( R\right)  \leq  N}\right\}
\]

(69)

\[
\subset  \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)  : R + {2I} \in  \widehat{C}\left( {s + \varepsilon }\right) }\right\}
\]

for each \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {\alpha ,\beta }\right\rbrack \) .

We claim that \( \varepsilon \) has the desired property. It suffices to verify this in the special case when \( h = 1 \) . (The general case follows by scaling.) Therefore, let us assume that \( F \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) is a closed set which is invariant under the Hamilton ODE and satisfies

(70)

\[
F \subset  \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)  : R + I \in  \widehat{C}\left( s\right) }\right\}
\]

for some \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {\alpha ,\beta }\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, we define a set \( \widehat{F} \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) by

\[
\widehat{F} = \{ R \in  F : R + {2I} \in  \widehat{C}\left( {s + \varepsilon }\right) \} .
\]

Using (69) and (70), we obtain

(71)

\[
\{ R \in  F : \operatorname{scal}\left( R\right)  \leq  N\}  \subset  \widehat{F}.
\]

It remains to show that the set \( \widehat{F} \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE. Suppose that \( R\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , is a solution of the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R\left( t\right)  = Q\left( {R\left( t\right) }\right) \) such that \( R\left( 0\right)  \in  \widehat{F} \) . Since \( F \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE, we have \( R\left( t\right)  \in  F \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Hence, it suffices to prove that \( R\left( t\right)  + {2I} \in  \widehat{C}\left( {s + \varepsilon }\right) \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Suppose this is false. We define

\[
{t}_{0} = \inf \{ t \in  \lbrack 0, T) : R\left( t\right)  + {2I} \notin  \widehat{C}\left( {s + \varepsilon }\right) \} .
\]

Clearly, \( R\left( {t}_{0}\right)  + {2I} \in  \widehat{C}\left( {s + \varepsilon }\right) \) . There are two possibilities now:

Case 1. Suppose that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {R\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right)  \geq  N \) . It follows from our choice of \( N \) that \( Q\left( {R\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{R\left( {t}_{0}\right)  + {2I}}\widehat{C}\left( {s + \varepsilon }\right) \) . By Proposition 5.4, there exists a real number \( {t}_{1} \in  \left( {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) such that \( R\left( t\right)  + {2I} \in \; \widehat{C}\left( {s + \varepsilon }\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . This contradicts the definition of \( {t}_{0} \) .

Case 2. Suppose that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {R\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right)  < N \) . By continuity, there exists a real number \( {t}_{1} \in  \left( {{t}_{0}, T}\right) \) such that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {R\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  N \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . Using (71), we conclude that \( R\left( t\right)  + {2I} \in  \widehat{C}\left( {s + \varepsilon }\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0},{t}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . Again, this contradicts the definition of \( {t}_{0} \) .

nodes.proof:
Let \( \mathcal{S} \) be the set of all real numbers \( s > 0 \) with the property that

\[
F \subset  \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)  : R + {hI} \in  \widehat{C}\left( s\right) }\right\}
\]

for some real number \( h > 0 \) . By assumption, \( {s}_{0} \in  \mathcal{S} \) . In particular, the set \( \mathcal{S} \) is nonempty.

Let \( \sigma \) denote the supremum of \( \mathcal{S} \) . Moreover, we choose a sequence of real numbers \( {s}_{j} \in  \mathcal{S} \) such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{s}_{j} = \sigma \) . For each \( j \) , there exists a real number \( {h}_{j} > 0 \) such that

\[
F \subset  \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)  : R + {h}_{j}I \in  \widehat{C}\left( {s}_{j}\right) }\right\}  .
\]

By increasing \( {h}_{j} \) if necessary, we can arrange that

(72)

\[
{h}_{j} \geq  \sup \{ \operatorname{scal}\left( R\right)  : R \in  K\}
\]

for all \( j \) .

We claim that \( \sigma  = \infty \) . Suppose this is false. Then the sequence \( \left\{  {{s}_{j} : j = 1,2,\ldots }\right\} \) is contained in a compact subinterval of \( \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) . By Lemma 8.9, there exists a real number \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) with the following property. For each \( j \) , the set

\[
{\widehat{F}}_{j} = \left\{  {R \in  F : R + 2{h}_{j}I \in  \widehat{C}\left( {{s}_{j} + \varepsilon }\right) }\right\}
\]

is invariant under the Hamilton ODE, and

(73)

\[
\left\{  {R \in  F : \operatorname{scal}\left( R\right)  \leq  {h}_{j}}\right\}   \subset  {\widehat{F}}_{j}.
\]

It follows from (72) and (73) that \( K \subset  {\widehat{F}}_{j} \) for each \( j \) . Moreover, the set \( {\widehat{F}}_{j} \) is closed, convex, \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant, and invariant under the Hamilton ODE. Consequently, we have \( F \subset  {\widehat{F}}_{j} \) for each \( j \) . This implies \( {s}_{j} + \varepsilon  \in  \mathcal{S} \) for all \( j \) . On the other hand, the number \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) is independent of \( j \) . Therefore, we have \( {s}_{j} + \varepsilon  > \sigma \) if \( j \) is sufficiently large. This contradicts the definition of \( \sigma \) .

Thus, we conclude that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{s}_{j} = \sigma  = \infty \) . Hence, it follows from Proposition 8.8 that \( F \) is a pinching set.

\[

nodes.proof:
Let \( F \subset  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right) \) be the smallest set containing \( K \) which is closed, convex, O(n)-invariant, and invariant under the Hamilton ODE. By assumption, the set \( K \) is contained in the interior of the cone \( \widetilde{C} \) . Using Proposition 7.14, we obtain

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all \( R \in  K \) , all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , and all pairs \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) satisfying \( \left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right)  = 0 \) . Consequently, we can find a positive real number \( N \) such that

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  + N\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all \( R \in  K \) , all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , and all \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

Without loss of generality, we may assume that \( N = 1 \) . By Proposition 7.22, \( K \) is contained in the interior of the set \( G \) . We next consider a pair of real numbers \( a, b \) such that \( {2a} = {2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} \) and \( b \in  \left( {0,\frac{\sqrt{{2n}\left( {n - 2}\right)  + 4} - 2}{n\left( {n - 2}\right) }}\right\rbrack \) . By continuity, we can choose \( b \) sufficiently small so that \( K \subset  {\ell }_{a, b}\left( G\right) \) . The set \( {\ell }_{a, b}\left( G\right) \) is closed, convex, and \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -invariant. Moreover, the set \( {\ell }_{a, b}\left( G\right) \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE by Proposition 8.15. Thus, we conclude that \( F \subset  {\ell }_{a, b}\left( G\right) \) .

We now consider the cones \( \widehat{C}\left( s\right) , s > 0 \) , defined in Section 8.3. We can find a real number \( {s}_{0} > 0 \) such that \( {\ell }_{a, b}\left( \widehat{C}\right)  \subset  \widehat{C}\left( {s}_{0}\right) \) . Using Proposition 7.24, we obtain

\[
{\ell }_{a, b}\left( R\right)  + \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) I = {\ell }_{a, b}\left( {R + I}\right)  \in  {\ell }_{a, b}\left( \widehat{C}\right)  \subset  \widehat{C}\left( {s}_{0}\right)
\]

for all \( R \in  G \) . Thus, we conclude that

\[

nodes.label: Definition 9.2-extra-1
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.content:
Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a complete Riemannian manifold, and let \( p \) be a point on \( M \) . A loop based at \( p \) is a piecewise smooth path \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) satisfying \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = \gamma \left( 1\right)  = p \) . The holonomy group of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) at \( p \) consists of all parallel transport maps \( {P}_{\gamma } \) , where \( \gamma \) is a loop based at \( p \) :

\[
{\operatorname{Hol}}_{p}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \left\{  {{P}_{\gamma } : {T}_{p}M \rightarrow  {T}_{p}M : \gamma \text{ is a loop based at }p}\right\}  .
\]

The restricted holonomy group of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) at \( p \) is defined by

\[
{\operatorname{Hol}}_{p}^{0}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \left\{  {{P}_{\gamma } : {T}_{p}M \rightarrow  {T}_{p}M : \gamma \text{ is a contractible loop based at }p}\right\}  .
\]

The isomorphism type of \( {\operatorname{Hol}}_{p}\left( {M, g}\right) \) is independent of the choice of the base point. More precisely, for any pair of points \( p, q \in  M \) , the holonomy group \( {\operatorname{Hol}}_{p}\left( {M, g}\right) \) is conjugate to \( {\operatorname{Hol}}_{q}\left( {M, g}\right) \) .

Definition 9.1. We say that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is locally reducible if there exists a nontrivial subspace of \( {T}_{p}M \) which is invariant under the action of \( {\operatorname{Hol}}_{p}^{0}\left( {M, g}\right) \) .

By a theorem of de Rham, a complete manifold \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is locally reducible if and only if the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is isometric to a product of two Riemannian manifolds of lower dimension (see [13], Theorem 10.43).

Definition 9.2. We say that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is locally symmetric if the Riemann curvature tensor of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is parallel.

By a theorem of Cartan, a complete manifold \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is locally symmetric if and only if the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space (see [13], Theorem 10.72).

nodes.content:
Theorem 9.3 (M. Berger [7]). Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a complete, simply connected Riemannian manifold which is irreducible and not isometric to a symmetric space. Then one of the following statements holds:

(i) \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) .

(ii) \( n = {2m} \geq  4 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \mathrm{U}\left( m\right) \) .

(iii) \( n = {4m} \geq  8 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \operatorname{Sp}\left( m\right)  \cdot  \operatorname{Sp}\left( 1\right) \) .

(iv) \( n = {2m} \geq  4 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \mathrm{{SU}}\left( m\right) \) .

(v) \( n = {4m} \geq  8 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \operatorname{Sp}\left( m\right) \) .

(vi) \( n = 7 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = {\mathrm{G}}_{2} \) .

(vii) \( n = 8 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \operatorname{Spin}\left( 7\right) \) .

Berger’s original list also included the possibility that \( n = {16} \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \operatorname{Spin}\left( 9\right) \) . However, in this case, a theorem of D. Alekseevskii implies that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space (see [1], Corollary 1, or [23], Theorem 8.1).

Proposition 9.5. Let \( \Omega \) be an open subset of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , and let \( {X}_{1},\ldots ,{X}_{m} \) be smooth vector fields on \( \Omega \) . Assume that \( \varphi  : \Omega  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is a nonnegative smooth function satisfying

(74)

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}\left( {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right) \left( {{X}_{j},{X}_{j}}\right)  \leq   - L\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{\left| \xi \right|  \leq  1}}\left( {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right) \left( {\xi ,\xi }\right)  + L\left| {d\varphi }\right|  + {L\varphi },
\]

where \( L \) is a positive constant. Let \( F = \left\{  {x \in  \Omega  : \varphi \left( x\right)  = 0}\right\} \) denote the zero set of the function \( \varphi \) . Then \( \left\langle  {{X}_{j}\left( y\right) , y - z}\right\rangle   = 0 \) for all points \( y \in  F \) and \( z \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) satisfying \( d\left( {z, F}\right)  = \left| {y - z}\right| \) .

nodes.proof:
The proof is by contradiction. Suppose that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left\langle  {X}_{j}\left( y\right) , y - z\right\rangle  }^{2} > 0
\]

for some point \( y \in  F \) and some point \( z \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) satisfying \( d\left( {z, F}\right)  = \left| {y - z}\right| \) . Without loss of generality, we may assume that \( \left| {x - z}\right|  > \left| {y - z}\right| \) for all points \( x \in  F \smallsetminus  \{ y\} \) . (Otherwise, we replace \( z \) by \( \frac{1}{2}\left( {y + z}\right) \) .) We can find a real number \( \alpha  > 0 \) such that

\[
4{\alpha }^{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left\langle  {X}_{j}\left( y\right) , y - z\right\rangle  }^{2} - {2\alpha }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left| {X}_{j}\left( y\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
> {2L\alpha } + {2L\alpha }\left| {y - z}\right|  + L\text{ . }
\]

By continuity, there exists a bounded open set \( U \) such that \( y \in  U,\bar{U} \subset  \Omega \) , and

\[
4{\alpha }^{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left\langle  {X}_{j}\left( x\right) , x - z\right\rangle  }^{2} - {2\alpha }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left| {X}_{j}\left( x\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

(75)

\[
> {2L\alpha } + {2L\alpha }\left| {x - z}\right|  + L
\]

for all \( x \in  U \) . We define a function \( \psi \) by

\[
\psi \left( x\right)  = {e}^{-\alpha {\left| x - z\right| }^{2}} - {e}^{-\alpha {\left| y - z\right| }^{2}}.
\]

Moreover, we denote by \( B \) the closed ball of radius \( \left| {y - z}\right| \) centered at \( z \) . By assumption, we have \( F \cap  B = \{ y\} \) . This implies \( \varphi \left( x\right)  > 0 \) for all \( x \in  B \smallsetminus  \{ y\} \) . In particular, we have \( \varphi \left( x\right)  > 0 \) for all \( x \in  \partial U \cap  B \) . Hence, there exists a real number \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) such that \( \varphi \left( x\right)  - {\varepsilon \psi }\left( x\right)  > 0 \) for all \( x \in  \partial U \cap  B \) . We next observe that \( \varphi \left( x\right)  - {\varepsilon \psi }\left( x\right)  > \varphi \left( x\right)  \geq  0 \) for all \( x \in  \partial U \smallsetminus  B \) . Putting these facts together, we conclude that \( \varphi \left( x\right)  - {\varepsilon \psi }\left( x\right)  > 0 \) for all \( x \in  \partial U \) .

By compactness, there exists a point \( {x}_{0} \in  \bar{U} \) such that \( \varphi \left( {x}_{0}\right)  - {\varepsilon \psi }\left( {x}_{0}\right)  \leq \; \varphi \left( x\right)  - {\varepsilon \psi }\left( x\right) \) for all \( x \in  U \) . In particular, we have \( \varphi \left( {x}_{0}\right)  - {\varepsilon \psi }\left( {x}_{0}\right)  \leq \; \varphi \left( y\right)  - {\varepsilon \psi }\left( y\right)  = 0 \) . Consequently, we have \( {x}_{0} \in  U \) and

\[
\varphi \left( {x}_{0}\right)  \leq  {\varepsilon \psi }\left( {x}_{0}\right)  \leq  \varepsilon {e}^{-\alpha {\left| {x}_{0} - z\right| }^{2}}.
\]

The function \( \varphi  - {\varepsilon \psi } \) attains a local minimum at the point \( {x}_{0} \) . This implies

\[
\left| {d\varphi }\right|  = \varepsilon \left| {d\psi }\right|  = {2\varepsilon \alpha }\left| {{x}_{0} - z}\right| {e}^{-\alpha {\left| {x}_{0} - z\right| }^{2}}
\]

at the point \( {x}_{0} \) . Moreover, we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}\left( {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right) \left( {{X}_{j},{X}_{j}}\right)  \geq  \varepsilon \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}\left( {{D}^{2}\psi }\right) \left( {{X}_{j},{X}_{j}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {{4\varepsilon }{\alpha }^{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left\langle  {X}_{j}\left( {x}_{0}\right) ,{x}_{0} - z\right\rangle  }^{2} - {2\varepsilon \alpha }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left| {X}_{j}\left( {x}_{0}\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-\alpha {\left| {x}_{0} - z\right| }^{2}}
\]

and

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{\left| \xi \right|  \leq  1}}\left( {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right) \left( {\xi ,\xi }\right)  \geq  \varepsilon \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{\left| \xi \right|  \leq  1}}\left( {{D}^{2}\psi }\right) \left( {\xi ,\xi }\right)  \geq   - {2\varepsilon \alpha }{e}^{-\alpha {\left| {x}_{0} - z\right| }^{2}}
\]

at the point \( {x}_{0} \) . Substituting this into (74), we obtain

\[
4{\alpha }^{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left\langle  {X}_{j}\left( {x}_{0}\right) ,{x}_{0} - z\right\rangle  }^{2} - {2\alpha }\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{\left| {X}_{j}\left( {x}_{0}\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  {{2L\alpha } + {2L\alpha }}\left| {{x}_{0} - z}\right|  + L.
\]

This contradicts (75).

Suppose that \( \gamma \left( \sigma \right)  \notin  F \) for some real number \( \sigma  \in  (0,1\rbrack \) . We define a sequence of real numbers \( {s}_{k} \) by

\[
{s}_{k} = \sup \left\{  {s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\sigma }\right\rbrack   : d\left( {\gamma \left( s\right) , F}\right)  \leq  {e}^{{ks} - {k}^{2}}}\right\}
\]

for \( k \) sufficiently large. It is easy to see that \( {s}_{k} \in  \left( {0,\sigma }\right) \) and \( d\left( {\gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) , F}\right)  = \; {e}^{k{s}_{k} - {k}^{2}} > 0 \) if \( k \) is sufficiently large. For each \( k \) , we can find a point \( {y}_{k} \in  \bar{F} \) such that \( d\left( {\gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) , F}\right)  = \left| {{y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right|  > 0 \) . Then

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\left| {{y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right|  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{e}^{k{s}_{k} - {k}^{2}} = 0.
\]

Consequently, we have \( {y}_{k} \in  \bar{F} \cap  \Omega \) if \( k \) is sufficiently large. Since \( F \) is relatively closed, it follows that \( {y}_{k} \in  F \) if \( k \) is sufficiently large.

By definition of \( {s}_{k} \) , we have

\[
{e}^{k\left( {{s}_{k} - s}\right) }\left| {{y}_{k} - \gamma \left( s\right) }\right|  \geq  {e}^{k\left( {{s}_{k} - s}\right) }d\left( {\gamma \left( s\right) , F}\right)  \geq  d\left( {\gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) , F}\right)  = \left| {{y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right|
\]

for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {{s}_{k},\sigma }\right\rbrack \) . Consequently, we have

\[
k{\left| {y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) \right| }^{2} + \left\langle  {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( {s}_{k}\right) ,{y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right\rangle
\]

\[

\]

This implies

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{f}_{j}\left( {s}_{k}\right) \left\langle  {{X}_{j}\left( {\gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right) ,{y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right\rangle   \leq   - k{\left| {y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) \right| }^{2}.
\]

By assumption, we have \( \left\langle  {{X}_{j}\left( {y}_{k}\right) ,{y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right\rangle   = 0 \) for \( j = 1,\ldots , m \) . Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{m}{f}_{j}\left( {s}_{k}\right) \left\langle  {{X}_{j}\left( {y}_{k}\right)  - {X}_{j}\left( {\gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right) ,{y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) }\right\rangle   \geq  k{\left| {y}_{k} - \gamma \left( {s}_{k}\right) \right| }^{2}.
\]

This is impossible since the functions \( {f}_{1},\ldots ,{f}_{m} \) are bounded and the vector fields \( {X}_{1},\ldots ,{X}_{m} \) are Lipschitz continuous.

nodes.content:
We first introduce some notation. These definitions make sense in arbitrary dimension, though we will later specialize to the three-dimensional case. Let \( M \) be a compact manifold of dimension \( n \) , and let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a family of metrics on \( M \) evolving under the Ricci flow. Let us consider the \( \left( {n + 1}\right) \) -dimensional manifold \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . As in Section 2.3, we denote by \( E \) the pull-back of the tangent bundle of \( M \) under the map \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right)  \rightarrow  M,\left( {p, t}\right)  \mapsto  p \) . The bundle \( E \) is equipped with a natural bundle metric. Moreover, there is a natural connection \( D \) on \( E \) , which is given by (6). By Proposition 2.13, the connection \( D \) is compatible with the bundle metric on \( E \) .

Let \( \mathcal{O} \) be the orthonormal frame bundle of \( E \) , and let \( \pi  : \mathcal{O} \rightarrow  M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) denote the associated bundle projection. By definition, the fiber of \( \mathcal{O} \) over a point \( \left( {p, t}\right)  \in  M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) consists of all \( n \) -frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\}   \subset  {E}_{\left( p, t\right) } \) that are orthonormal with respect to the metric \( g\left( t\right) \) . Note that \( \mathcal{O} \) is a principal \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -bundle over \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) .

For each point \( \underline{e} \in  \mathcal{O} \) , we denote by \( {\mathcal{V}}_{e} \subset  {T}_{e}\mathcal{O} \) the vertical subspace at \( \underline{e} \) . In other words, \( {\mathcal{V}}_{\underline{e}} \) is the tangent space to the fiber \( {\pi }^{-1}\left( {\{ \pi \left( \underline{e}\right) \} }\right) \) at the point e. Since \( \mathcal{O} \) is a principal \( \mathrm{O}\left( n\right) \) -bundle, there is a canonical isomorphism from the Lie algebra \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) to the vertical subspace \( {\mathcal{V}}_{\underline{e}} \) . By transplanting the standard inner product on \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) \) , we obtain a natural inner product on \( {\mathcal{V}}_{\underline{e}} \) .

For each point \( \underline{e} \in  \mathcal{O} \) we denote by

\[
{\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{e}} : {T}_{\pi \left( \underline{e}\right) }\left( {M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) }\right)  \rightarrow  {T}_{\underline{e}}\mathcal{O}
\]

the horizontal lift induced by the connection \( D \) . We next define a collection of smooth horizontal vector fields \( {\mathcal{X}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{X}}_{n},\mathcal{Y} \) on \( \mathcal{O} \) . For each \( j \in  \{ 1,\ldots , n\} \) , the value of \( {\mathcal{X}}_{j} \) at a point \( \underline{e} = \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\}   \in  \mathcal{O} \) is given by the horizontal lift of the vector \( {e}_{j} \) :

\[
{\left. {\mathcal{X}}_{j}\right| }_{\underline{e}} = {\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{e}}\left( {e}_{j}\right)  \in  {T}_{\underline{e}}\mathcal{O}.
\]

Moreover, the value of \( \mathcal{Y} \) at a point \( \underline{e} = \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\}   \in  \mathcal{O} \) is defined as the horizontal lift of the vector \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t} \) :

\[
{\left. \mathcal{Y}\right| }_{\underline{e}} = {\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{e}}\left( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\right)  \in  {T}_{\underline{e}}\mathcal{O}.
\]

It is easy to see that \( {T}_{\underline{e}}\mathcal{O} = {\mathcal{V}}_{\underline{e}} \oplus  \operatorname{span}\left\{  {{\mathcal{X}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{X}}_{n},\mathcal{Y}}\right\} \) .

For the remainder of this section, we shall restrict our attention to the case \( n = 3 \) . For each orthonormal frame \( \underline{e} = \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right\}   \subset  {E}_{\left( p, t\right) } \) , we define

(76)

\[
\varphi \left( \underline{e}\right)  = {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{1}}\right) .
\]

This defines a smooth function \( \varphi  : \mathcal{O} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) . The function \( \varphi \) satisfies the following differential equation.

Let \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) be a smooth path, and let \( \left\{  {{v}_{1}\left( s\right) ,{v}_{2}\left( s\right) ,{v}_{3}\left( s\right) }\right\}   \subset \; {E}_{\left( \gamma \left( s\right) ,\tau \right) } \) be a parallel orthonormal frame along \( \gamma \) with respect to the metric \( g\left( \tau \right) \) . We define a smooth path \( \underline{v} : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{O} \) by

\[
\underline{v}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  {{v}_{1}\left( s\right) ,{v}_{2}\left( s\right) ,{v}_{3}\left( s\right) }\right\}  .
\]

Clearly, \( \pi \left( {\underline{v}\left( s\right) }\right)  = \left( {\gamma \left( s\right) ,\tau }\right) \) and \( {\underline{v}}^{\prime }\left( s\right)  = {\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{v}\left( s\right) }\left( {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right) \) for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, we can find smooth functions \( {f}_{1},{f}_{2},{f}_{3} : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) such that \( {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{3}{f}_{j}\left( s\right) {v}_{j}\left( s\right) \) for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . This implies

\[
{\underline{v}}^{\prime }\left( s\right)  = {\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{v}\left( s\right) }\left( {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{3}{f}_{j}\left( s\right) {\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{v}\left( s\right) }\left( {{v}_{j}\left( s\right) }\right)  = {\left. \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{3}{f}_{j}\left( s\right) {\mathcal{X}}_{j}\right| }_{\underline{v}\left( s\right) }
\]

for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

We next consider the function \( \varphi  : \mathcal{O} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) defined in (76). Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has nonnegative Ricci curvature for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , the function \( \varphi \) is nonnegative. For abbreviation, we denote by \( \mathcal{F} = \{ \underline{e} \in  \mathcal{O} : \varphi \left( \underline{e}\right)  = 0\} \) the zero set of the function \( \varphi \) . Using Lemma 9.8, we obtain

\[
\mathcal{Y}\left( \varphi \right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{3}{\mathcal{X}}_{j}\left( {{\mathcal{X}}_{j}\left( \varphi \right) }\right)  \geq  0
\]

at each point \( \underline{e} \in  \mathcal{O} \) .

nodes.proof:
By assumption, the manifold \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is locally irreducible. Hence, we can find a real number \( \tau  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) such that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible. For each point \( p \in  M \) , we consider the set

\[
\left\{  {v \in  {T}_{p}M : {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {v, v}\right)  = 0}\right\}  .
\]

By Proposition 9.9, this defines a subbundle of \( {TM} \) which is invariant under parallel transport. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irrreducible, this subbundle must have rank 0 or 3 . Hence, there are two cases:

Case 1. Suppose that

\[
\left\{  {v \in  {T}_{p}M : {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {v, v}\right)  = 0}\right\}   = \{ 0\}
\]

for all points \( p \in  M \) . In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) has positive Ricci curvature. By Theorem 6.8, the metrics \( \frac{1}{4\left( {T - t}\right) }g\left( t\right) \) converge in \( {C}^{\infty } \) to a metric of constant sectional curvature 1.

Case 2. Suppose that

\[
\left\{  {v \in  {T}_{p}M : {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {v, v}\right)  = 0}\right\}   = {T}_{p}M
\]

for all points \( p \in  M \) . In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is Ricci flat. Since \( M \) is three-dimensional, it follows that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is flat. This contradicts our assumption that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible.

Let \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) be a smooth path, and let \( \left\{  {{v}_{1}\left( s\right) ,\ldots ,{v}_{n}\left( s\right) }\right\}   \subset \; {E}_{\left( \gamma \left( s\right) ,\tau \right) } \) be a parallel orthonormal frame along \( \gamma \) with respect to the metric \( g\left( \tau \right) \) . We define a smooth path \( \underline{v} : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{O} \) by

\[
\underline{v}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  {{v}_{1}\left( s\right) ,\ldots ,{v}_{n}\left( s\right) }\right\}  .
\]

Clearly, \( \pi \left( {\underline{v}\left( s\right) }\right)  = \left( {\gamma \left( s\right) ,\tau }\right) \) and \( {\underline{v}}^{\prime }\left( s\right)  = {\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{v}\left( s\right) }\left( {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right) \) for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, we can find smooth functions \( {f}_{1},\ldots ,{f}_{n} : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) such that \( {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{f}_{j}\left( s\right) {v}_{j}\left( s\right) \) for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . This implies

\[
{\underline{v}}^{\prime }\left( s\right)  = {\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{v}\left( s\right) }\left( {{\gamma }^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{f}_{j}\left( s\right) {\mathcal{H}}_{\underline{v}\left( s\right) }\left( {{v}_{j}\left( s\right) }\right)  = {\left. \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{f}_{j}\left( s\right) {\mathcal{X}}_{j}\right| }_{\underline{v}\left( s\right) }
\]

for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

We next consider the function \( \varphi  : \mathcal{O} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) defined in (77). Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , the function \( \varphi \) is nonnegative. For abbreviation, we denote by \( \mathcal{F} = \{ \underline{e} \in  \mathcal{O} : \varphi \left( \underline{e}\right)  = 0\} \) the zero set of the function \( \varphi \) . By Lemmas 9.11 and 9.12, there exists a positive constant \( L \) such that

\[
\mathcal{Y}\left( \varphi \right)  - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{\mathcal{X}}_{j}\left( {{\mathcal{X}}_{j}\left( \varphi \right) }\right)
\]

\geq  L\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{\xi  \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{\underline{e}},\left| \xi \right|  \leq  1}}\left( {{D}^{2}\varphi }\right) \left( {\xi ,\xi }\right)  - L\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\xi  \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{\underline{e}},\left| \xi \right|  \leq  1}}{d\varphi }\left( \xi \right)  - {L\varphi }
\]

at each point \( \underline{e} \in  \mathcal{O} \) .

We now assume that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1}\left( 0\right) ,{v}_{3}\left( 0\right) ,{v}_{1}\left( 0\right) ,{v}_{3}\left( 0\right) }\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1}\left( 0\right) ,{v}_{4}\left( 0\right) ,{v}_{1}\left( 0\right) ,{v}_{4}\left( 0\right) }\right)
\]

\[

\]

Corollary 9.14. Let \( M \) be a compact, simply connected manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) , and let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on \( M \) with nonnegative isotropic curvature. Moreover, suppose that \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \; \mathrm{{SO}}\left( n\right) \) for some \( \tau  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . Then

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\]

\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) .

nodes.proof:
We argue by contradiction. Suppose that there exist a point \( p \in  M \) and an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {T}_{p}M \) such that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  = 0.
\]

We claim that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

(80)

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  = 0
\]

for each point \( q \in  M \) and each orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right\}   \subset \; {T}_{q}M \) .

Since \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{SO}\left( n\right) \) , there exists a piecewise smooth path \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) such that \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = p,\gamma \left( 1\right)  = q \) , and

\[
{v}_{1} = {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{1},\;{v}_{2} = {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{2},\;{v}_{3} = {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{3},\;{v}_{4} =  \pm  {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{4}.
\]

Here, \( {P}_{\gamma } \) denotes the parallel transport along \( \gamma \) with respect to the metric \( g\left( \tau \right) \) . If \( {v}_{4} = {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{4} \) , then the identity (80) follows directly from Theorem 9.13. Hence, it suffices to consider the case \( {v}_{4} =  - {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{4} \) . Using Theorem 9.13, we obtain

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

(81)

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Furthermore, Theorem 9.13 implies that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}\right)
\]

(82)

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{3},{v}_{4},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{4},{v}_{2}}\right)  = 0
\]

and

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)
\]

(83)

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{4},{v}_{2}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{4},{v}_{3},{v}_{4},{v}_{3}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Using the relations (81)-(83), we deduce that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  \leq  0
\]

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{4},{v}_{2}}\right)  \leq  0
\]

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Using the first Bianchi identity, we conclude that \( {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  = 0 \) . Hence, the identity (80) is a consequence of (81). This completes the proof of (80).

By Proposition 7.3, the manifold \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has nonnegative scalar curvature for each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, the relation (80) implies that the scalar curvature of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) vanishes identically. (To prove this, we apply Proposition 7.3 to \( - {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) } \) .) Using Proposition 2.18, we conclude that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is Ricci flat. Hence, it follows from Proposition 7.3 that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is flat. This is a contradiction.

Then \[ Q\left( R\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) \leq - {2R}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2} \] \[ + 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{2m}}R{\left( X, JX,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}\right) }^{2} \] for all unit vectors \( X \in {T}_{p}M \) .

nodes.proof:
By definition of \( Q\left( R\right) \) , we have

\[
Q\left( R\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{2m}}R{\left( X, JX,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{2m}}R\left( {X,{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {{JX},{e}_{p},{JX},{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{2m}}R\left( {X,{e}_{p},{JX},{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {{JX},{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right) .
\]

This implies

\[
Q\left( R\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{2m}}R{\left( X, JX,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
- 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{2m}}R\left( {X,{e}_{p},{JX},{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {{JX},{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right) .
\]

The expression on the right-hand side is independent of the choice of the orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{2m}}\right\} \) . Hence, we may assume without loss of generality that \( {e}_{1} = X \) and \( {e}_{2} = {JX} \) . This implies

\[
- 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{2m}}R\left( {X,{e}_{p},{JX},{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {{JX},{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
=  - 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 3}}^{{2m}}R\left( {X,{e}_{p},{JX},{e}_{q}}\right) R\left( {{JX},{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 3}}^{{2m}}{\left( R\left( X,{e}_{p}, JX,{e}_{q}\right)  - R\left( JX,{e}_{p}, X,{e}_{q}\right) \right) }^{2}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 3}}^{{2m}}R{\left( X, JX,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq   - {2R}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{2m}}R{\left( X, JX,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}\right) }^{2}.
\]

Putting these facts together, the assertion follows.

\[

Consider the unit vector \( \cos \left( s\right) X + \sin \left( s\right) Y \) . Since \( R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) \) is maximal, we have

\[
{\cos }^{4}\left( s\right) R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  + {\sin }^{4}\left( s\right) R\left( {Y,{JY}, Y,{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 4{\cos }^{3}\left( s\right) \sin \left( s\right) R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JY}}\right)  + 4\cos \left( s\right) {\sin }^{3}\left( s\right) R\left( {X,{JY}, Y,{JY}}\right)
\]

\]

\[
\leq  R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)
\]

for all \( s \in  \mathbb{R} \) with equality for \( s = 0 \) . This implies

\[
R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JY}}\right)  = 0
\]

and

(85)

\[

\]

Replacing \( Y \) by \( {JY} \) yields

\[
R\left( {X,{JX}, X, Y}\right)  = 0
\]

and

(86)

\[
{2R}\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  \leq  R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  - R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right) .
\]

Taking the arithmetic mean of (85) and (86), we obtain

\[
R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)  = R\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  + R\left( {X,{JY}, X,{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  - R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right) .
\]

From this, the assertion follows.

Theorem 9.17 (S. Goldberg, S. Kobayashi [37]). Assume that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is a Kähler-Einstein manifold. Moreover, suppose that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has positive orthogonal bisectional curvature; that is,

\[
R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all points \( p \in  M \) and all unit vectors \( X, Y \in  {T}_{p}M \) satisfying \( g\left( {X, Y}\right)  = \; g\left( {{JX}, Y}\right)  = 0 \) . Then \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant holomorphic sectional curvature.

nodes.proof:
By assumption, we have \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {m + 1}\right) {\kappa g} \) for some constant \( \kappa \) . Using Proposition 2.11, we obtain

\[
{\Delta R} + Q\left( R\right)  = \left( {m + 1}\right) {\kappa R}.
\]

In the next step, we choose a point \( p \in  M \) and a unit vector \( X \in  {T}_{p}M \) such that \( R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) \) is maximal. This implies

\[
\left( {{D}_{v, v}^{2}R}\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq  0
\]

for all vectors \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Taking the trace over \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) yields

\[
\left( {\Delta R}\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

(87)

\[
Q\left( R\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \geq  \left( {m + 1}\right) {\kappa R}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) .
\]

We now analyze the term \( Q\left( R\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) \) . For abbreviation, let \( {w}_{1} = X \) . We can find vectors \( {w}_{2},\ldots ,{w}_{m} \in  {T}_{p}M \) with the property that \( \left\{  {{w}_{1}, J{w}_{1},{w}_{2}, J{w}_{2},\ldots ,{w}_{m}, J{w}_{m}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal basis of \( {T}_{p}M \) and

\[
R\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha },{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = R\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = 0
\]

for \( 2 \leq  \alpha  < \beta  \leq  m \) . It follows from Lemma 9.16 that

\[
R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = R\left( {X,{JX}, X, J{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = 0
\]

for \( 2 \leq  \beta  \leq  m \) . Putting these facts together, we conclude that

(88)

\[
R\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha },{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = R\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = 0
\]

for \( 1 \leq  \alpha  < \beta  \leq  m \) .

By Proposition 9.15, we have

\[
Q\left( R\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq   - {2R}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta  = 1}}^{m}R{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha },{w}_{\beta }\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta  = 1}}^{m}R{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\beta }\right) }^{2}
\]

Using (88), this inequality can be rewritten as

\[
Q\left( R\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq   - {2R}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}
\]

(89)

\[
+ 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  = 1}}^{m}R{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }\right) }^{2}.
\]

Combining (87) and (89), we obtain

\[
2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  = 2}}^{m}R\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }}\right) R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  - {2R}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}
\]

(90)

\[
= \left( {m + 1}\right) {\kappa R}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  - {2R}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  Q\left( R\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  - {2R}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  = 2}}^{m}R{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }\right) }^{2}.
\]

Since \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has positive orthogonal bisectional curvature, we have

\[
R\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }}\right)  > 0
\]

for \( 2 \leq  \alpha  \leq  m \) . Moreover, it follows from Lemma 9.16 that

\[
{2R}\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }}\right)  \leq  R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)
\]

for \( 2 \leq  \alpha  \leq  m \) . Using (90), we conclude that

\[
{2R}\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }}\right)  = R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)
\]

for \( 2 \leq  \alpha  \leq  m \) . This implies

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  = 1}}^{m}R\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\left( {m + 1}\right) R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) .
\]

Using the identity \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {m + 1}\right) {\kappa g} \) , we obtain \( R\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  = \kappa \) . Therefore, the holomorphic sectional curvatures of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) are bounded from above by \( \kappa \) . Since \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {m + 1}\right) {\kappa g} \) , we conclude that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant holomorphic sectional curvature \( \kappa \) .

nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 9.18. Assume that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is a Kähler-Einstein manifold. If \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, then \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has positive orthogonal bisectional curvature.

nodes.proof:
Consider two unit vectors \( X, Y \in  {T}_{p}M \) satisfying \( g\left( {X, Y}\right)  = \; g\left( {{JX}, Y}\right)  = 0 \) . Then

\[
R\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  + R\left( {X,{JY}, X,{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{JX}, Y,{JX}, Y}\right)  + R\left( {{JX},{JY},{JX},{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
= {2R}\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right) \text{ . }
\]

Since \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, it follows that

\[
R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

It remains to show that \( R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)  \neq  0 \) . To prove this, we argue by contradiction. Suppose that \( R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)  = 0 \) . This implies that the four-frame \( \{ X,{JX}, Y, - {JY}\} \) has zero isotropic curvature. Let us fix a point \( q \in  M \) and two unit vectors \( Z, W \in  {T}_{q}M \) satisfying \( g\left( {Z, W}\right)  = g\left( {{JZ}, W}\right)  = \) 0. We claim that

(91)

\[
R\left( {Z,{JZ}, W,{JW}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Since \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \mathrm{U}\left( m\right) \) , we can find a piecewise smooth path \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) such that \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = p,\gamma \left( 1\right)  = q,{P}_{\gamma }X = Z \) , and \( {P}_{\gamma }Y = W \) . By Theorem 9.13, the four-frame \( \left\{  {{P}_{\gamma }X,{P}_{\gamma }{JX},{P}_{\gamma }Y, - {P}_{\gamma }{JY}}\right\} \) has zero isotropic curvature. Consequently, the four-frame \( \{ Z,{JZ}, W, - {JW}\} \) has zero isotropic curvature. Thus, we conclude that \( R\left( {Z,{JZ}, W,{JW}}\right)  = 0 \) , as claimed.

In the next step, we apply the identity (91) to the vectors \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left( {Z + W}\right) \) and \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left( {Z - W}\right) \) . This yields

\[
0 = R\left( {Z + W,{JZ} + {JW}, Z - W,{JZ} - {JW}}\right)
\]

(92)

\[
= R\left( {Z,{JZ}, Z,{JZ}}\right)  + R\left( {W,{JW}, W,{JW}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {2R}\left( {Z,{JZ}, W,{JW}}\right)  - {4R}\left( {Z,{JW}, Z,{JW}}\right) .
\]

Similarly, if we apply the identity (91) to the vectors \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left( {Z + {JW}}\right) \) and \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left( {Z - {JW}}\right) \) , then we obtain

\[
0 = R\left( {Z + {JW},{JZ} - W, Z - {JW},{JZ} + W}\right)
\]

(93)

\[
= R\left( {Z,{JZ}, Z,{JZ}}\right)  + R\left( {W,{JW}, W,{JW}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {2R}\left( {Z,{JZ}, W,{JW}}\right)  - {4R}\left( {Z, W, Z, W}\right) .
\]

We now take the arithmetic mean of (92) and (93). This implies

(94)

\[
R\left( {Z,{JZ}, Z,{JZ}}\right)  + R\left( {W,{JW}, W,{JW}}\right)  = 0
\]

for all unit vectors \( Z, W \in  {T}_{q}M \) satisfying \( g\left( {Z, W}\right)  = g\left( {{JZ}, W}\right)  = 0 \) .

It follows from (91) and (94) that the scalar curvature of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is equal to zero. Consequently, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is Ricci flat. Since \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, Proposition 7.3 implies that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is flat. This is a contradiction.

Lemma 9.21. Fix a point \( p \in  M \) . Let us define an algebraic curvature tensor \( S \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right) \) by

\[
S\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = g\left( {X, Z}\right) g\left( {Y, W}\right)  - g\left( {X, W}\right) g\left( {Y, Z}\right)
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Then \( B\left( {{R}_{1}, S}\right)  = 0 \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: Lemma 9.21. Fix a point \( p \in M \) . Let us define an algebraic curvature tensor \( S \in {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right) \) by \[ S\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right) = g\left( {X, Z}\right) g\left( {Y, W}\right) - g\left( {X, W}\right) g\left( {Y, Z}\right) \] for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in {T}_{p}M \) . Then \( B\left( {{R}_{1}, S}\right) = 0 \) .

nodes.proof:
Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{4m}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal basis of \( {T}_{p}M \) . It follows from (95) that the Ricci tensor of \( {R}_{1} \) is equal to zero. Therefore, we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{4m}}{R}_{1}\left( {X, Y,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right) S\left( {Z, W,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right)  = 2{R}_{1}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)
\]

and

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{4m}}{R}_{1}\left( {X,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right) S\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right)  =  - {R}_{1}\left( {X, W, Z, Y}\right)
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Using the first Bianchi identity, we obtain

\[
B\left( {{R}_{1}, S}\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = {R}_{1}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + {R}_{1}\left( {Z, W, X, Y}\right)
\]

\[
- {R}_{1}\left( {X, W, Z, Y}\right)  - {R}_{1}\left( {Y, Z, W, X}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{1}\left( {X, Z, W, Y}\right)  + {R}_{1}\left( {Y, W, Z, X}\right)
\]

\[
= 0
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  {T}_{p}M \) .

Lemma 9.22. Fix a point \( p \in  M \) and an almost complex structure \( J \in  {\mathcal{J}}_{p} \) . Let us define an algebraic curvature tensor \( S \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right) \) by

\[
S\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = {2g}\left( {{JX}, Y}\right) g\left( {{JZ}, W}\right)
\]

\[
+ g\left( {{JX}, Z}\right) g\left( {{JY}, W}\right)  - g\left( {{JX}, W}\right) g\left( {{JY}, Z}\right)
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Then \( B\left( {{R}_{1}, S}\right)  = 0 \) .

Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{4m}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal basis of \( {T}_{p}M \) . Using (95), we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{4m}}{R}_{1}\left( {X, Y,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right) S\left( {Z, W,{e}_{p},{e}_{q}}\right)  = 2{R}_{1}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)
\]

and

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{{4m}}{R}_{1}\left( {X,{e}_{p}, Z,{e}_{q}}\right) S\left( {Y,{e}_{p}, W,{e}_{q}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JY}, Z,{JW}}\right)  + {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JW}, Z,{JY}}\right)
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  {T}_{p}M \) . This implies

\[
B\left( {{R}_{1}, S}\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = {R}_{1}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + {R}_{1}\left( {Z, W, X, Y}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JY}, Z,{JW}}\right)  + {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JW}, Z,{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{R}_{1}\left( {Y,{JX}, W,{JZ}}\right)  + {R}_{1}\left( {Y,{JZ}, W,{JX}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JY}, W,{JZ}}\right)  - {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JZ}, W,{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{1}\left( {Y,{JX}, Z,{JW}}\right)  - {R}_{1}\left( {Y,{JW}, Z,{JX}}\right)
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Using the first Bianchi identity, we obtain

\[
B\left( {{R}_{1}, S}\right) \left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{1}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  + 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JW}, Y,{JZ}}\right)  - 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JZ}, Y,{JW}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{1}\left( {X, Y,{JZ},{JW}}\right)  + 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JW}, Y,{JZ}}\right)  - 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JZ}, Y,{JW}}\right)
\]

\[
= 0
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  {T}_{p}M \) .

nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.content: Proposition 9.23. We have \( Q\left( R\right)  = Q\left( {R}_{1}\right)  + {\kappa }^{2}Q\left( {R}_{0}\right) \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 9.23. We have \( Q\left( R\right) = Q\left( {R}_{1}\right) + {\kappa }^{2}Q\left( {R}_{0}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
Let us fix a point \( p \in  M \) . Moreover, suppose that \( I, J, K \in  {\mathcal{J}}_{p} \) are three almost complex structures satisfying \( {IJK} =  - \mathrm{{id}} \) . We define algebraic curvature tensors \( {S}_{0},{S}_{1},{S}_{2},{S}_{3} \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right) \) by

\[
{S}_{0}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = g\left( {X, Z}\right) g\left( {Y, W}\right)  - g\left( {X, W}\right) g\left( {Y, Z}\right) ,
\]

\[
{S}_{1}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = {2g}\left( {{IX}, Y}\right) g\left( {{IZ}, W}\right)
\]

\[
+ g\left( {{IX}, Z}\right) g\left( {{IY}, W}\right)  - g\left( {{IX}, W}\right) g\left( {{IY}, Z}\right) ,
\]

\[
{S}_{2}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = {2g}\left( {{JX}, Y}\right) g\left( {{JZ}, W}\right)
\]

\[
+ g\left( {{JX}, Z}\right) g\left( {{JY}, W}\right)  - g\left( {{JX}, W}\right) g\left( {{JY}, Z}\right) ,
\]

\[
{S}_{3}\left( {X, Y, Z, W}\right)  = {2g}\left( {{KX}, Y}\right) g\left( {{KZ}, W}\right)
\]

\[
+ g\left( {{KX}, Z}\right) g\left( {{KY}, W}\right)  - g\left( {{KX}, W}\right) g\left( {{KY}, Z}\right)
\]

for all vectors \( X, Y, Z, W \in  {T}_{p}M \) . It follows from Lemmas 9.21 and 9.22 that

\[
B\left( {{R}_{1},{S}_{0}}\right)  = B\left( {{R}_{1},{S}_{1}}\right)  = B\left( {{R}_{1},{S}_{2}}\right)  = B\left( {{R}_{1},{S}_{3}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Since \( {S}_{0} + {S}_{1} + {S}_{2} + {S}_{3} = 4{R}_{0} \) , we conclude that \( B\left( {{R}_{1},{R}_{0}}\right)  = 0 \) . This implies

\[
Q\left( R\right)  = Q\left( {R}_{1}\right)  + {2\kappa B}\left( {{R}_{1},{R}_{0}}\right)  + {\kappa }^{2}Q\left( {R}_{0}\right)  = Q\left( {R}_{1}\right)  + {\kappa }^{2}Q\left( {R}_{0}\right) ,
\]

as claimed.
