nodes.label: Theorem 9.24
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.content: Theorem 9.24. Assume that \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  < \kappa \) for each point \( p \in  M \) , each unit vector \( X \in  {T}_{p}M \) , and every almost complex structure \( J \in  {\mathcal{J}}_{p} \) . Then \( {R}_{1} \) vanishes identically.
nodes.content_excerpt: Theorem 9.24. Assume that \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) < \kappa \) for each point \( p \in M \) , each unit vector \( X \in {T}_{p}M \) , and every almost complex structure \( J \in {\mathcal{J}}_{p} \) . Then \( {R}_{1} \) vanishes identically.

nodes.proof:
It follows from (95) that the Ricci tensor of \( {R}_{1} \) is equal to zero. Therefore, we have \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} = \left( {m + 2}\right) {\kappa g} \) . Hence, Proposition 2.11 implies that

\[
{\Delta R} + Q\left( R\right)  = \left( {{2m} + 4}\right) {\kappa R}.
\]

We next observe that \( Q\left( {R}_{0}\right)  = \left( {{2m} + 4}\right) {R}_{0} \) . Using Proposition 9.23, we obtain \( Q\left( R\right)  = Q\left( {R}_{1}\right)  + \left( {{2m} + 4}\right) {\kappa }^{2}{R}_{0} \) . Moreover, we have \( {\Delta R} = \Delta {R}_{1} \) since \( {R}_{0} \) is parallel. Thus, we conclude that

\[
\Delta {R}_{1} + Q\left( {R}_{1}\right)  = \left( {{2m} + 4}\right) \kappa {R}_{1}.
\]

In the next step, we choose a point \( p \in  M \) , a unit vector \( X \in  {T}_{p}M \) , and an almost complex structure \( J \in  {\mathcal{J}}_{p} \) such that \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) \) is maximal. This implies

\[
\left( {{D}_{v, v}^{2}{R}_{1}}\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq  0
\]

for all vectors \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Taking the trace over \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) yields

\[
\left( {\Delta {R}_{1}}\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Putting these facts together, we conclude that

(96)

\[
Q\left( {R}_{1}\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \geq  \left( {{2m} + 4}\right) \kappa {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) .
\]

We now analyze the term \( Q\left( {R}_{1}\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) \) . For abbreviation, let \( {w}_{1} = X \) and \( {w}_{2} = {IX} \) . We can find vectors \( {w}_{3},\ldots ,{w}_{2m} \in  {T}_{p}M \) such that \( \left\{  {{w}_{1}, J{w}_{1},{w}_{2}, J{w}_{2},\ldots ,{w}_{2m}, J{w}_{2m}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal basis of \( {T}_{p}M \) and

\[
{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha },{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = 0
\]

for \( 3 \leq  \alpha  < \beta  \leq  {2m} \) . It follows from Lemma 9.16 that

\[
{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X, J{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = 0
\]

for \( 2 \leq  \beta  \leq  {2m} \) . Moreover, we have

\[
{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X, I{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JI}{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = 0
\]

for \( 3 \leq  \beta  \leq  {2m} \) . Using (95), we deduce that

\[
{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX},{IX},{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX},{IX}, J{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = 0
\]

for \( 3 \leq  \beta  \leq  {2m} \) . Putting these facts together, we conclude that

(97)

\[
{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha },{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\beta }}\right)  = 0
\]

for \( 1 \leq  \alpha  < \beta  \leq  {2m} \) .

Using Lemma 9.16, we obtain

\[
2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }}\right)  \leq  {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)
\]

and

\[
2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, I{w}_{\alpha },{JI}{w}_{\alpha }}\right)  \leq  {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)
\]

for \( 3 \leq  \alpha  \leq  {2m} \) . In view of (95), the latter inequality can be rewritten as

\[
- 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX},{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }}\right)  \leq  {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)
\]

for \( 3 \leq  \alpha  \leq  {2m} \) . Thus, we conclude that

(98)

\[
4{R}_{1}{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }\right) }^{2} \leq  {R}_{1}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}
\]

for \( 3 \leq  \alpha  \leq  {2m} \) .

By Proposition 9.15, we have

\[
Q\left( {R}_{1}\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq   - 2{R}_{1}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta  = 1}}^{{2m}}{R}_{1}{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha },{w}_{\beta }\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha ,\beta  = 1}}^{{2m}}{R}_{1}{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\beta }\right) }^{2}
\]

Using (97) and (98), we obtain

\[
Q\left( {R}_{1}\right) \left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq   - 2{R}_{1}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2} + 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  = 1}}^{{2m}}{R}_{1}{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }\right) }^{2}
\]

(99)

\[
= 6{R}_{1}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2} + 4\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{\alpha  = 3}}^{{2m}}{R}_{1}{\left( X, JX,{w}_{\alpha }, J{w}_{\alpha }\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{2m} + 4}\right) {R}_{1}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}.
\]

Combining (96) and (99), we conclude that

\[
\kappa {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq  {R}_{1}{\left( X, JX, X, JX\right) }^{2}.
\]

Since \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  < \kappa \) , it follows that \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq  0 \) . Therefore, \( {R}_{1} \) has nonpositive holomorphic sectional curvature. Since the Ricci tensor of \( {R}_{1} \) is equal to zero, we conclude that \( {R}_{1} \) vanishes identically.

nodes.content: Proposition 9.25. Assume that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Then \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  < \kappa \) for each point \( p \in  M \) , each unit vector \( X \in  {T}_{p}M \) , and every almost complex structure \( J \in  {\mathcal{J}}_{p} \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 9.25. Assume that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Then \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) < \kappa \) for each point \( p \in M \) , each unit vector \( X \in {T}_{p}M \) , and every almost complex structure \( J \in {\mathcal{J}}_{p} \) .

nodes.proof:
Let us fix a point \( p \in  M \) and a unit vector \( X \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Moreover, suppose that \( I, J, K \in  {\mathcal{J}}_{p} \) are three almost complex structures satisfying \( {IJK} =  - \mathrm{{id}} \) . For abbreviation, we put \( Y = {IX} \) . Then

\[
{R}_{1}\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  + {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JY}, X,{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{1}\left( {{JX}, Y,{JX}, Y}\right)  + {R}_{1}\left( {{JX},{JY},{JX},{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right) .
\]

Moreover, we have

\[
{R}_{0}\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  = {R}_{0}\left( {X,{JY}, X,{JY}}\right)  = 1,
\]

\[
{R}_{0}\left( {{JX}, Y,{JX}, Y}\right)  = {R}_{0}\left( {{JX},{JY},{JX},{JY}}\right)  = 1,
\]

\[
{R}_{0}\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)  = 0
\]

by definition of \( {R}_{0} \) . Using the identity \( R = {R}_{1} + \kappa {R}_{0} \) and (95), we obtain

\[
R\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  + R\left( {X,{JY}, X,{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{JX}, Y,{JX}, Y}\right)  + R\left( {{JX},{JY},{JX},{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {2R}\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)
\]

\[
= 4\left( {\kappa  + {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= 4\left( {\kappa  - {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right) }\right) .
\]

Since \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature, it follows that

\[
{R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \leq  \kappa .
\]

It remains to show that \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  \neq  \kappa \) . To prove this, we argue by contradiction. Suppose that \( {R}_{1}\left( {X,{JX}, X,{JX}}\right)  = \kappa \) . This implies that the four-frame \( \{ X,{JX}, Y, - {JY}\} \) has zero isotropic curvature. Given any unit vector \( Z \in  {T}_{p}M \) , we can find a linear isometry \( L : {T}_{p}M \rightarrow  {T}_{p}M \) which commutes with \( I, J, K \) and satisfies \( {LX} = Z \) . Since \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \; \mathrm{{Sp}}\left( m\right)  \cdot  \mathrm{{Sp}}\left( 1\right) \) , there exists a piecewise smooth path \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) such that \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = \gamma \left( 1\right)  = p \) and \( {P}_{\gamma } = L \) . By Theorem 9.13, the four-frame \( \left\{  {{P}_{\gamma }X,{P}_{\gamma }{JX},{P}_{\gamma }Y, - {P}_{\gamma }{JY}}\right\} \) has zero isotropic curvature. Hence, if we put \( W = {IZ} \) , then the four-frame \( \{ Z,{JZ}, W, - {JW}\} \) has zero isotropic curvature. Consequently, we have

\[
{R}_{1}\left( {Z,{JZ}, Z,{JZ}}\right)  = \kappa
\]

for each unit vector \( Z \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Since the Ricci tensor of \( {R}_{1} \) is equal to zero, we conclude that \( \kappa  = 0 \) . Hence, Proposition 7.3 implies that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is flat. This is a contradiction.

Theorem 9.27 (S. Brendle [19]). Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a compact Einstein manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) . Suppose that

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all points \( p \in  M \) and all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {T}_{p}M \) . Then \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant sectional curvature.

Suppose that \[ R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right) + R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right) \] \[ + R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right) + R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right) \] \[ - {2R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right) > 0 \] fo...

nodes.proof:
After rescaling the metric if necessary, we may assume that \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} = \; \left( {n - 1}\right) g \) . Using Proposition 2.11, we obtain

\[
{\Delta R} + Q\left( R\right)  = 2\left( {n - 1}\right) R.
\]

We now define

\[
{S}_{ijkl} = {R}_{ijkl} - \kappa \left( {{g}_{ik}{g}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{g}_{jk}}\right) ,
\]

where \( \kappa \) is a positive constant. Note that \( S \) is an algebraic curvature tensor. Let \( \kappa \) be the largest constant with the property that \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Then there exist a point \( p \in  M \) and a four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {T}_{p}M \) such that

\[
S\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + S\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ S\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + S\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2S}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Hence, it follows from Proposition 7.5 that

\[
Q\left( S\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + Q\left( S\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

(100)

\[
+ Q\left( S\right) \left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + Q\left( S\right) \left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2Q}\left( S\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

We next observe that

\[
Q{\left( S\right) }_{ijkl} = Q{\left( R\right) }_{ijkl} + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) {\kappa }^{2}\left( {{g}_{ik}{g}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{g}_{jk}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\kappa }\left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{ik}{g}_{jl} - {\operatorname{Ric}}_{il}{g}_{jk} - {\operatorname{Ric}}_{jk}{g}_{il} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{jl}{g}_{ik}}\right) ,
\]

hence

\[
Q{\left( S\right) }_{ijkl} = Q{\left( R\right) }_{ijkl} + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \kappa \left( {\kappa  - 2}\right) \left( {{g}_{ik}{g}_{jl} - {g}_{il}{g}_{jk}}\right) .
\]

Substituting this into (100), we obtain

\[
Q\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + Q\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

(101)

\[
+ Q\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + Q\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2Q}\left( R\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  + 8\left( {n - 1}\right) \kappa \left( {\kappa  - 2}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Since \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) realizes the minimum isotropic curvature of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) , we have

\[
\left( {{D}_{v, v}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + \left( {{D}_{v, v}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \left( {{D}_{v, v}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + \left( {{D}_{v, v}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\left( {{D}_{v, v}^{2}R}\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

for all vectors \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) . Taking the trace over \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) yields

\[
\left( {\Delta R}\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + \left( {\Delta R}\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

(102)

\[
+ \left( {\Delta R}\right) \left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + \left( {\Delta R}\right) \left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\left( {\Delta R}\right) \left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

We now add (101) and (102), and divide the result by \( 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \) . This implies

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  + {4\kappa }\left( {\kappa  - 2}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

On the other hand, we have

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  - {4\kappa } = 0.
\]

Since \( \kappa \) is positive, it follows that \( \kappa  \geq  1 \) . Therefore, \( S \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature and nonpositive Ricci curvature. Consequently, we have \( S = 0 \) by Proposition 7.3. This completes the proof.

nodes.content: Proposition 9.28. Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a compact, simply connected Einstein manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) which is irreducible and has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Then \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space.
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 9.28. Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a compact, simply connected Einstein manifold of dimension \( n \geq 4 \) which is irreducible and has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Then \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space.

nodes.proof:
Suppose the assertion is false. By Corollary 9.4, there are three possibilities:

Case 1. Suppose that \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \operatorname{SO}\left( n\right) \) . In this case, Corollary 9.14 implies that

\[
R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + R\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2R}\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) . By Theorem 9.27, the manifold \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant sectional curvature. In particular, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is symmetric, contrary to our assumption.

Case 2. Suppose that \( n = {2m} \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \mathrm{U}\left( m\right) \) . In this case, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is a Kähler manifold. By Corollary 9.19, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant holomorphic sectional curvature. Consequently, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is isometric to \( {\mathbb{{CP}}}^{m} \) up to scaling. This contradicts our assumption that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is nonsymmetric.

Case 3. Suppose that \( n = {4m} \geq  8 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g}\right)  = \operatorname{Sp}\left( m\right)  \cdot  \operatorname{Sp}\left( 1\right) \) . In this case, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is a quaternionic-Kähler manifold. Moreover, it follows from Corollary 9.26 that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space. This is a contradiction.

If \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is Ricci flat, then Proposition 7.3 implies that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is flat. Hence, it suffices to consider the case that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has positive Einstein constant. By a theorem of de Rham (cf. [13], Theorem 10.43), the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is isometric to a Riemannian product of the form \( {N}_{1} \times  \cdots  \times  {N}_{j} \) , where \( {N}_{1},\ldots ,{N}_{j} \) are simply connected and irreducible. Since \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is an Einstein manifold, we conclude that the factors \( {N}_{1},\ldots ,{N}_{j} \) are

Einstein manifolds. Since \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has positive Einstein constant, the manifolds \( {N}_{1},\ldots ,{N}_{j} \) are compact by Myers’ theorem. By Proposition 9.28, each of the factors \( {N}_{1},\ldots ,{N}_{j} \) is isometric to a symmetric space. Consequently, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is locally symmetric.

nodes.content:
Theorem 9.30 (S. Brendle [19]). Let \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) be a compact, simply connected Riemannian manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) which is irreducible and has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Then one of the following statements holds:

(i) \( M \) is homeomorphic to \( {S}^{n} \) .

(ii) \( n = {2m} \) and \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is a Kähler manifold.

(iii) \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space.

(iii) \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) i...

nodes.proof:
Suppose that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is not isometric to a symmetric space. Let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be the unique solution of the Ricci flow with initial metric \( {g}_{0} \) . By continuity, there exists a real number \( \delta  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) such that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is irreducible and nonsymmetric for all \( t \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . According to Corollary 9.4, there are three possibilities:

Case 1. Suppose that \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{SO}\left( n\right) \) for some real number \( \tau  \in \; \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . Using Corollary 9.14, we obtain

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) . Consequently, \( M \) is homeomorphic to \( {S}^{n} \) by Theorem 1.20.

Case 2. Suppose that \( n = {2m} \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right)  = \mathrm{U}\left( m\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a Kähler manifold for each \( t \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . Since \( g\left( t\right)  \rightarrow  {g}_{0} \) in \( {C}^{\infty } \) , it follows that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is a Kähler manifold.

Case 3. Suppose that \( n = {4m} \geq  8 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{Sp}\left( m\right)  \cdot  \operatorname{Sp}\left( 1\right) \) for some real number \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a quaternionic-Kähler manifold. By Corollary 9.26, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space. This is a contradiction.

Theorem 9.31. Let \( M \) be a compact manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) , and let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on \( M \) . We assume that the curvature tensor of \( g\left( t\right) \) lies in the cone \( \widetilde{C} \) for all points \( p \in  M \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, let us fix real numbers \( \tau  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) and \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . Then the set of all four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) that are orthonormal with respect to \( g\left( \tau \right) \) and satisfy

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  = 0
\]

is invariant under parallel transport.

By assumption, the curvature tensor of \( g\left( t\right) \) lies in the cone \( \widetilde{C} \) for all points \( p \in  M \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Consequently, the product \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right)  \times  {S}^{1} \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Hence, we may apply Theorem 9.13 to the manifolds \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right)  \times  {S}^{1}, t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

We now assume that \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {T}_{p}M \) is an orthonormal four-frame satisfying

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

(103)

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  = 0.
\]

We define an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {T}_{p}M \times  \mathbb{R} \) by

\[
{\widetilde{e}}_{1} = \left( {{e}_{1},0}\right) ,\;{\widetilde{e}}_{2} = \left( {{e}_{2},0}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{e}}_{3} = \left( {{e}_{3},0}\right) ,\;{\widetilde{e}}_{4} = \left( {\lambda {e}_{4},\sqrt{1 - {\lambda }^{2}}}\right) .
\]

The relation (103) implies

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{3}}\right)  + {\widetilde{R}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{4},{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

(104)

\[
+ {\widetilde{R}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3}}\right)  + {\widetilde{R}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{4},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{\widetilde{R}}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right)  = 0,
\]

where \( {\widetilde{R}}_{g\left( \tau \right) } \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {{T}_{p}M \times  \mathbb{R}}\right) \) denotes the trivial extension of the curvature tensor \( {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) } \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {{T}_{p}M}\right) \) . By Theorem 9.13, the set of all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},{\widetilde{e}}_{2},{\widetilde{e}}_{3},{\widetilde{e}}_{4}}\right\} \) satisfying (104) is invariant under parallel transport. From this, the assertion follows.

Corollary 9.32. Let \( M \) be a compact, simply connected manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) , and let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on \( M \) . We assume that the curvature tensor of \( g\left( t\right) \) lies in the cone \( \widetilde{C} \) for all points \( p \in  M \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, suppose that \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{SO}\left( n\right) \) for some \( \tau  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . Then

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and all \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

We assume that the curvature tensor of \( g\left( t\right) \) lies in the cone \( \widetilde{C} \) for all points \( p \in M \) and all \( t \in \left\lbrack {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . nodes.proof:
We argue by contradiction. Suppose that there exist a point \( p \in  M \) , an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {T}_{p}M \) , and a real number \( \lambda  \in \; \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) such that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  = 0.
\]

We claim that

(105)

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  = 0
\]

for each point \( q \in  M \) and each orthonormal three-frame \( \left\{  {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right\}   \subset  {T}_{q}M \) .

Since \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{SO}\left( n\right) \) , there exists a piecewise smooth path \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) such that \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = p,\gamma \left( 1\right)  = q \) , and

\[
{v}_{1} = {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{1},\;{v}_{2} = {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{2},\;{v}_{3} = {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{3}.
\]

Here, \( {P}_{\gamma } \) denotes the parallel transport along \( \gamma \) with respect to the metric \( g\left( \tau \right) \) . For abbreviation, let \( {v}_{4} = {P}_{\gamma }{e}_{4} \) . It follows from Theorem 9.31 that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{1},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

(106)

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Furthermore, Theorem 9.31 implies that

\[

\]

- {2\lambda }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{4},{v}_{2}}\right)  = 0
\]

and

\lambda {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{4},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Using the first Bianchi identity, we conclude that \( \lambda {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  = 0 \) . Substituting this into (106) gives

\[
0 \leq  {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{3},{v}_{1},{v}_{3}}\right)  + {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}}\right)

\[

\]

This proves (105). Consequently, the manifold \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is flat. This is a contradiction.

nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.content:
Theorem 9.33. Let \( M \) be a compact, simply connected manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) , and let \( {g}_{0} \) be a Riemannian metric on \( M \) . We assume that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is irreducible. Moreover, we assume that the curvature tensor of \( {g}_{0} \) lies in the cone \( \widetilde{C} \) for all points \( p \in  M \) . Let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be the unique maximal solution to the Ricci flow with initial metric \( {g}_{0} \) . Then one of the following statements holds:

(i) As \( t \rightarrow  T \) , the metrics \( \frac{1}{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {T - t}\right) }g\left( t\right) \) converge in \( {C}^{\infty } \) to a metric of constant sectional curvature 1.

(ii) \( n = {2m} \) and \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is a Kähler manifold.

(iii) \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space.

Suppose that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is not isometric to a symmetric space. By continuity, there exists a real number \( \delta  \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) such that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is irreducible and nonsymmetric for all \( t \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . In view of Corollary 9.4, there are three possibilities:

Case 1. Suppose that \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{SO}\left( n\right) \) for some real number \( \tau  \in \; \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . Using Corollary 9.32, we obtain

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and all \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . By Theorem 8.17, the metrics \( \frac{1}{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {T - t}\right) }g\left( t\right) \) converge in \( {C}^{\infty } \) to a metric of constant sectional curvature 1.

Case 2. Suppose that \( n = {2m} \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right)  = \mathrm{U}\left( m\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a Kähler manifold for each \( t \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . Since \( g\left( t\right)  \rightarrow  {g}_{0} \) in \( {C}^{\infty } \) , it follows that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is a Kähler manifold.

Case 3. Suppose that \( n = {4m} \geq  8 \) and \( \operatorname{Hol}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{Sp}\left( m\right)  \cdot  \operatorname{Sp}\left( 1\right) \) for some real number \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) . In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a quaternionic-Kähler manifold. By Corollary 9.26, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is isometric to a symmetric space. This is a contradiction.

nodes.content: Proposition 9.34. Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a Kähler manifold of real dimension \( {2m} \geq \) 4. If \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is weakly \( 1/4 \) -pinched in the pointwise sense, then \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant holomorphic sectional curvature.
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 9.34. Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a Kähler manifold of real dimension \( {2m} \geq \) 4. If \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is weakly \( 1/4 \) -pinched in the pointwise sense, then \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant holomorphic sectional curvature.

nodes.proof:
For each point \( p \in  M \) , we denote by \( {K}_{\max }\left( p\right) \) the maximum sectional curvature at the point \( p \) . Similarly, we denote by \( {K}_{\min }\left( p\right) \) the minimum sectional curvature at the point \( p \) . Since \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is weakly \( 1/4 \) -pinched, we have \( 0 \leq  {K}_{\max }\left( p\right)  \leq  4{K}_{\min }\left( p\right) \) for all points \( p \in  M \) .

We next consider a two-dimensional plane \( \pi  \subset  {T}_{p}M \) which is invariant under \( J \) . We claim that \( K\left( \pi \right)  = 4{K}_{\min }\left( p\right) \) . Since \( m \geq  2 \) , we can find unit vectors \( X, Y \in  {T}_{p}M \) such that \( g\left( {X, Y}\right)  = g\left( {{JX}, Y}\right)  = 0 \) and \( X + Y \in  \pi \) . Using the first Bianchi identity, we obtain

\[
R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)  = R\left( {X, Y, X, Y}\right)  + R\left( {X,{JY}, X,{JY}}\right)  \geq  2{K}_{\min }\left( p\right) .
\]

On the other hand, it follows from Proposition 1.9 that

\[
R\left( {X,{JX}, Y,{JY}}\right)  \leq  \frac{2}{3}\left( {{K}_{\max }\left( p\right)  - {K}_{\min }\left( p\right) }\right)  \leq  2{K}_{\min }\left( p\right) .
\]

Analyzing the case of equality in Proposition 1.9 yields

\[
R\left( {X + Y,{JX} + {JY}, X + Y,{JX} + {JY}}\right)  = {16}{K}_{\min }\left( p\right) .
\]

Thus, we conclude that \( K\left( \pi \right)  = 4{K}_{\min }\left( p\right) \) , as claimed.

Therefore, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has pointwise constant holomorphic sectional curvature. In particular, the trace-free Ricci tensor of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) vanishes. By Corollary 1.6, the scalar curvature of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) is constant. Consequently, \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant holomorphic sectional curvature.

Suppose first that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is locally reducible. Since \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is weakly \( 1/4 \) -pinched in the pointwise sense, it follows that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is flat. This contradicts our assumption that \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is not locally symmetric.

Therefore, \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is locally irreducible. By the splitting theorem of Cheeger and Gromoll [27], the universal cover of \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is isometric to a Riemannian product of the form \( N \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{k} \) , where \( N \) is compact (cf. [13], Corollary 6.67). Since \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) is locally irreducible, we conclude that \( k = 0 \) . Hence, the universal cover of \( M \) is compact. If we apply Proposition 9.35 to the universal cover of \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) , the assertion follows.

= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 0}}^{{m - 2}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{{i}_{1} + \cdots  + {i}_{q} = m - l - 1}}{\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{1}}g\left( t\right)  * \cdots  * {\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{q}}g\left( t\right)  * {\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right) .
\]

This implies

\[
D{D}^{m - 1}\omega \left( t\right)  - D{\widehat{D}}^{m - 1}\omega \left( t\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 0}}^{{m - 2}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{{i}_{1} + \cdots  + {i}_{q} = m - l - 1}}{\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{1}}g\left( t\right)  * \cdots  * {\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{q}}g\left( t\right)  * D{\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right)
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 0}}^{{m - 2}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{{i}_{1} + \cdots  + {i}_{q} = m - l - 1}}{\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{1}}g\left( t\right)  * \cdots  * {\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{q - 1}}g\left( t\right)  * D{\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{q}}g\left( t\right)  * {\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right) .
\]

Moreover, it follows from Lemma A. 2 that

\[
D{\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right)  = \widehat{D}{\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right)  + \widehat{D}g\left( t\right)  * {\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right)
\]

and

\[
D{\widehat{D}}^{j}g\left( t\right)  = \widehat{D}{\widehat{D}}^{j}g\left( t\right)  + \widehat{D}g\left( t\right)  * {\widehat{D}}^{j}g\left( t\right) .
\]

Putting these facts together, we conclude that

\[
{D}^{m}\omega \left( t\right)  - {\widehat{D}}^{m}\omega \left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 0}}^{{m - 1}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{{i}_{1} + \cdots  + {i}_{q} = m - l}}{\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{1}}g\left( t\right)  * \cdots  * {\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{q}}g\left( t\right)  * {\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right) ,
\]

as claimed.

nodes.content:
For simplicity, let \( \widehat{D} \) be the Levi-Civita connection associated with the metric \( \widehat{g} = g\left( 0\right) \) . For each integer \( m \geq  1 \) , we define continuous functions \( {u}_{m} : \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) and \( {\widehat{u}}_{m} : \lbrack 0, T) \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) by

\[
{u}_{m}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\left| {D}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }
\]

and

\[
{\widehat{u}}_{m}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}
\]

for each \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Using the identity

\[
g\left( t\right)  = \widehat{g} + {\int }_{0}^{t}\omega \left( \tau \right) {d\tau },
\]

we obtain

(109)

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{m}g\left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}} \leq  {\int }_{0}^{t}{\widehat{u}}_{m}\left( \tau \right) {d\tau }
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

nodes.label: Lemma A.4
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.content: Lemma A.4. Assume that \( {\int }_{0}^{T}{u}_{m}\left( t\right) {dt} < \infty \) for \( m = 0,1,2,\ldots \) Then \( {\int }_{0}^{T}{\widehat{u}}_{m}\left( t\right) {dt} < \infty \) for \( m = 1,2,\ldots \)
nodes.content_excerpt: Lemma A.4. Assume that \( {\int }_{0}^{T}{u}_{m}\left( t\right) {dt} < \infty \) for \( m = 0,1,2,\ldots \) Then \( {\int }_{0}^{T}{\widehat{u}}_{m}\left( t\right) {dt} < \infty \) for \( m = 1,2,\ldots \)

nodes.proof:
The proof is by induction on \( m \) . Fix an integer \( m \geq  1 \) , and suppose that \( {\int }_{0}^{T}{\widehat{u}}_{l}\left( t\right) {dt} < \infty \) for \( l = 1,2,\ldots , m - 1 \) . It follows from (109) that

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \lbrack 0, T)}}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{M}{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{l}g\left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}} < \infty
\]

for \( l = 1,2,\ldots , m - 1 \) . Moreover, the metrics \( g\left( t\right) \) are uniformly equivalent by Lemma A.1. Using Lemma A.3, we obtain

\[
{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}} - {\left| {D}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{1}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 0}}^{{m - 1}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{{i}_{1} + \cdots  + {i}_{q} = m - l}}{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{1}}g\left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}\cdots {\left| {\widehat{D}}^{{i}_{q}}g\left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}
\]

for some positive constant \( {C}_{1} \) . This implies

\[
{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}} \leq  {\left| {D}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}} + {C}_{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 1}}^{{m - 1}}{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}
\]

\[
+ {C}_{2}\left( {1 + {\left| {\widehat{D}}^{m}g\left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}}\right) {\left| \omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}},
\]

hence

\[
{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}} \leq  {C}_{3}{\left| {D}^{m}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) } + {C}_{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 1}}^{{m - 1}}{\left| {\widehat{D}}^{l}\omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}
\]

\[
+ {C}_{2}{C}_{3}\left( {1 + {\left| {\widehat{D}}^{m}g\left( t\right) \right| }_{\widehat{g}}}\right) {\left| \omega \left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }.
\]

Using (109), we obtain

\[
{\widehat{u}}_{m}\left( t\right)  \leq  {C}_{3}{u}_{m}\left( t\right)  + {C}_{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 1}}^{{m - 1}}{\widehat{u}}_{l}\left( t\right)
\]

\[
+ {C}_{2}{C}_{3}{u}_{0}\left( t\right) \left( {1 + {\int }_{0}^{t}{\widehat{u}}_{m}\left( \tau \right) {d\tau }}\right)
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . This implies

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\log \left( {1 + {\int }_{0}^{t}{\widehat{u}}_{m}\left( \tau \right) {d\tau }}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{3}{u}_{m}\left( t\right)  + {C}_{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{l = 1}}^{{m - 1}}{\widehat{u}}_{l}\left( t\right)  + {C}_{2}{C}_{3}{u}_{0}\left( t\right)
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . By assumption, we have \( {\int }_{0}^{T}{u}_{0}\left( t\right) {dt} < \infty \) and \( {\int }_{0}^{T}{u}_{m}\left( t\right) {dt} < \; \infty \) . Moreover, the induction hypothesis implies that \( {\int }_{0}^{T}{\widehat{u}}_{l}\left( t\right) {dt} < \infty \) for \( l = 1,2,\ldots , m - 1 \) . Putting these facts together, we conclude that

\[
{\int }_{0}^{T}{\widehat{u}}_{m}\left( \tau \right) {d\tau } < \infty .
\]

This completes the proof.

nodes.content:
Proposition B.1. We have

\[
\left| {g\left( {z, z}\right) g\left( {w, w}\right)  - g{\left( z, w\right) }^{2}}\right|  \leq  g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right) g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  - {\left| g\left( z,\bar{w}\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

for all vectors \( z, w \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition B.1. We have \[ \left| {g\left( {z, z}\right) g\left( {w, w}\right) - g{\left( z, w\right) }^{2}}\right| \leq g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right) g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right) - {\left| g\left( z,\bar{w}\right) \right| }^{2} \] for all vectors \( z, w \in {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) .

nodes.proof:
Let us write \( z \land  w = \varphi  + {i\psi } \) , where \( \varphi ,\psi  \in  { \land  }^{2}V \) . Then

\[
g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right) g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  - {\left| g\left( z,\bar{w}\right) \right| }^{2} = g\left( {z \land  w,\bar{z} \land  \bar{w}}\right)
\]

\[
= g\left( {\varphi  + {i\psi },\varphi  - {i\psi }}\right)
\]

\[
= {\left| \varphi \right| }^{2} + {\left| \psi \right| }^{2}.
\]

On the other hand, we have

\[
g\left( {z, z}\right) g\left( {w, w}\right)  - g{\left( z, w\right) }^{2} = g\left( {z \land  w, z \land  w}\right)
\]

\[
= g\left( {\varphi  + {i\psi },\varphi  + {i\psi }}\right)
\]

\[
= {\left| \varphi \right| }^{2} - {\left| \psi \right| }^{2} + {2i}\langle \varphi ,\psi \rangle .
\]

Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we obtain

\[
{\left| g\left( z, z\right) g\left( w, w\right)  - g{\left( z, w\right) }^{2}\right| }^{2} = {\left( {\left| \varphi \right| }^{2} - {\left| \psi \right| }^{2}\right) }^{2} + 4\langle \varphi ,\psi {\rangle }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  {\left( {\left| \varphi \right| }^{2} - {\left| \psi \right| }^{2}\right) }^{2} + 4{\left| \varphi \right| }^{2}{\left| \psi \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
= {\left( {\left| \varphi \right| }^{2} + {\left| \psi \right| }^{2}\right) }^{2}
\]

hence,

\[
\left| {g\left( {z, z}\right) g\left( {w, w}\right)  - g{\left( z, w\right) }^{2}}\right|  \leq  {\left| \varphi \right| }^{2} + {\left| \psi \right| }^{2}.
\]

Putting these facts together, the assertion follows.

nodes.label: Lemma B.2
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow and the Sphere Theorem
nodes.section_title: B. Results from complex linear algebra
nodes.content: Lemma B.2. Let \( \sigma \) be a complex two-plane in \( {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) . Then there exist vectors \( z, w \in  \sigma \) such that \( g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right)  = g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  = 1 \) and \( g\left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = g\left( {z, w}\right)  = 0 \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: Lemma B.2. Let \( \sigma \) be a complex two-plane in \( {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) . Then there exist vectors \( z, w \in \sigma \) such that \( g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right) = g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right) = 1 \) and \( g\left( {z,\bar{w}}\right) = g\left( {z, w}\right) = 0 \) .

nodes.proof:
Let \( \{ \zeta ,\eta \} \) be an orthonormal basis of \( \sigma \) . Then \( g\left( {\zeta ,\bar{\zeta }}\right)  = g\left( {\eta ,\bar{\eta }}\right)  = 1 \) and \( g\left( {\zeta ,\bar{\eta }}\right)  = 0 \) . If \( g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = 0 \) , we are done. Hence, it suffices to consider the case \( g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  \neq  0 \) . By the intermediate value theorem, we can find a real number \( \delta \) such that

\[
\operatorname{Im}\left( \frac{{e}^{2i\delta }g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  - {e}^{-{2i\delta }}g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right) }{g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right) }\right)  = 0.
\]

Moreover, we can find a real number \( \theta \) such that

\[
\frac{1}{2}\sin \left( {2\theta }\right) \operatorname{Re}\left( \frac{{e}^{2i\delta }g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  - {e}^{-{2i\delta }}g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right) }{g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right) }\right)  = \cos \left( {2\theta }\right) .
\]

We now define

\[
z = \cos \left( \theta \right) {e}^{i\delta }\zeta  + \sin \left( \theta \right) {e}^{-{i\delta }}\eta
\]

and

\[
w =  - \sin \left( \theta \right) {e}^{i\delta }\zeta  + \cos \left( \theta \right) {e}^{-{i\delta }}\eta .
\]

It is straightforward to verify that \( g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right)  = g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  = 1 \) and \( g\left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = 0 \) . Moreover, we have

\[
g\left( {z, w}\right)  = \cos \left( {2\theta }\right) g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  - \frac{1}{2}\sin \left( {2\theta }\right) \left( {{e}^{2i\delta }g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  - {e}^{-{2i\delta }}g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right) }\right)  = 0.
\]

This completes the proof.

Then there exist an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  V \) and real numbers \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) such that \( {e}_{1} + {i\mu }{e}_{2} \in  \sigma \) and \( {e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4} \in  \sigma \) .

nodes.proof:
By Lemma B.2, we can find vectors \( z, w \in  \sigma \) such that \( g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right)  = \; g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  = 1 \) and \( g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right)  = g\left( {z, w}\right)  = 0 \) . Moreover, there exists a real number \( a \) such that \( \operatorname{Im}\left( {{e}^{2ia}g\left( {z, z}\right) }\right)  = 0 \) and \( \operatorname{Re}\left( {{e}^{2ia}g\left( {z, z}\right) }\right)  \geq  0 \) . Similarly, we can find a real number \( b \) such that \( \operatorname{Im}\left( {{e}^{2ib}g\left( {w, w}\right) }\right)  = 0 \) and \( \operatorname{Re}\left( {{e}^{2ib}g\left( {w, w}\right) }\right)  \geq  0 \) .

In the next step, we write \( {e}^{ia}z = {v}_{1} + i{v}_{2} \) and \( {e}^{ib}w = {v}_{3} + i{v}_{4} \) for suitable vectors \( {v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4} \in  V \) . Then

\[
g\left( {{v}_{1} + i{v}_{2},{v}_{3} - i{v}_{4}}\right)  = {e}^{i\left( {a - b}\right) }g\left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
g\left( {{v}_{1} + i{v}_{2},{v}_{3} + i{v}_{4}}\right)  = {e}^{i\left( {a + b}\right) }g\left( {z, w}\right)  = 0
\]

and

\[
g\left( {{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{Im}\left( {{e}^{2ia}g\left( {z, z}\right) }\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
g\left( {{v}_{3},{v}_{4}}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{Im}\left( {{e}^{2ib}g\left( {w, w}\right) }\right)  = 0.
\]

Therefore, the vectors \( {v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3},{v}_{4} \) are mutually orthogonal. Moreover, we have

\[
{\left| {v}_{1}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {v}_{2}\right| }^{2} = g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right)  = 1,
\]

\[
{\left| {v}_{3}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {v}_{4}\right| }^{2} = g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  = 1
\]

and

\[
{\left| {v}_{1}\right| }^{2} - {\left| {v}_{2}\right| }^{2} = \operatorname{Re}\left( {{e}^{2ia}g\left( {z, z}\right) }\right)  \geq  0
\]

\[
{\left| {v}_{3}\right| }^{2} - {\left| {v}_{4}\right| }^{2} = \operatorname{Re}\left( {{e}^{2ib}g\left( {w, w}\right) }\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Hence, there exist an orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  V \) and real numbers \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) such that

\[
{v}_{1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + {\mu }^{2}}}{e}_{1},\;{v}_{2} = \frac{\mu }{\sqrt{1 + {\mu }^{2}}}{e}_{2},
\]

\[
{v}_{3} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + {\lambda }^{2}}}{e}_{3},\;{v}_{4} = \frac{\lambda }{\sqrt{1 + {\lambda }^{2}}}{e}_{4}.
\]

This implies

\[
{e}_{1} + {i\mu }{e}_{2} = \sqrt{1 + {\mu }^{2}}\left( {{v}_{1} + i{v}_{2}}\right)  = \sqrt{1 + {\mu }^{2}}{e}^{ia}\zeta  \in  \sigma ,
\]

\[
{e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4} = \sqrt{1 + {\lambda }^{2}}\left( {{v}_{3} + i{v}_{4}}\right)  = \sqrt{1 + {\lambda }^{2}}{e}^{ib}\eta  \in  \sigma .
\]

This completes the proof.

Problem 1. This problem is concerned with the Bochner formula for harmonic two-forms (cf. [61]; see also [59]). Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension \( n \geq  4 \) , and let \( \psi \) be a harmonic two-form on \( M \) .

(i) Show that

\[
\Delta {\psi }_{ik} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{i}^{j}{\psi }_{jk} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j = 1}}^{n}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{k}^{j}{\psi }_{ij} - 2\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{j, l = 1}}^{n}{R}_{ijkl}{\psi }^{jl}.
\]

(ii) Suppose that \( n \) is even and \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature. Show that \( \psi \) is parallel.

(iii) Suppose that \( n \) is odd and the curvature tensor of \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) lies in the cone \( \widetilde{C} \) for all points \( p \in  M \) . Show that \( \psi \) is parallel.

nodes.content:
Problem 5. This problem is concerned with the Ricci flow on compact surfaces of higher genus (cf. [46]). Let \( M \) be a compact surface with \( \chi \left( M\right)  < \) 0, and let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) be a maximal solution to the Ricci flow on \( M \) . By scaling, we may assume that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right)  =  - {4\pi \chi }\left( M\right) \) .

(i) Show that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right)  =  - {4\pi \chi }\left( M\right) \left( {1 + t}\right) \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

(ii) Please show: there exists a smooth function \( f \) such that

\[
\operatorname{scal} + {\Delta f} =  - \frac{1}{1 + t}
\]

for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Moreover, the function \( f \) satisfies

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}f = {\Delta f} - \frac{1}{1 + t}f + \text{ constant. }
\]

(iii) We next consider the function \( h =  - {\Delta f} + {\left| df\right| }^{2} \) . Prove that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}h \leq  {\Delta h} - \frac{2}{1 + t}h
\]

(iv) Show that

\[
\frac{\alpha }{1 - {\alpha t}} \leq  \operatorname{scal} \leq  \frac{\beta }{{\left( 1 + t\right) }^{2}} - \frac{1}{1 + t},
\]

where \( \alpha  \leq   - 1 \) denotes the infimum of the scalar curvature of \( g\left( 0\right) \) and \( \beta \) denotes the supremum of the function \( h\left( 0\right) \) . Deduce from this that \( T = \infty \) .

(v) Show that the rescaled metrics \( \frac{1}{t}g\left( t\right) \) converge in \( {C}^{\infty } \) to a metric of constant scalar curvature -1 .

\]

Problem 7. The goal of this problem is to show that nonnegative curvature operator is preserved by the Ricci flow in all dimensions. This was first proved by R. Hamilton (cf. [49], Section 5).

(i) Let \( R \) be an algebraic curvature tensor on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) with nonnegative curvature operator. Show that \( {R}^{\# }\left( {\varphi ,\varphi }\right)  \geq  0 \) for all \( \varphi  \in  { \land  }^{2}{\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) .

(ii) Show that the cone

\[
\left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{C}}_{B}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\right)  : R\text{ has nonnegative curvature operator }}\right\}
\]

is invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) \) .

Problem 10. Let \( V \) be an oriented vector space of dimension 4 equipped with an inner product. Moreover, let \( R \) be an algebraic curvature tensor on

\( V \) . We may view \( R \) as a symmetric bilinear form on the space of two-forms. The space of two-forms splits as a direct sum \( { \land  }^{2}V = { \land  }_{ + }^{2}V \oplus  { \land  }_{ - }^{2}V \) , where \( { \land  }_{ + }^{2}V \) denotes the space of self-dual two-forms and \( { \land  }_{ - }^{2}V \) denotes the space of anti-self-dual two-forms. Let

\[
{\kappa }_{ + } = \inf \left\{  {R\left( {\varphi ,\varphi }\right)  + R\left( {\psi ,\psi }\right)  : \varphi ,\psi  \in  { \land  }_{ + }^{2}V,{\left| \varphi \right| }^{2} = {\left| \psi \right| }^{2} = 1,\langle \varphi ,\psi \rangle  = 0}\right\}
\]

and

\[
{\kappa }_{ - } = \inf \left\{  {R\left( {\varphi ,\varphi }\right)  + R\left( {\psi ,\psi }\right)  : \varphi ,\psi  \in  { \land  }_{ - }^{2}V,{\left| \varphi \right| }^{2} = {\left| \psi \right| }^{2} = 1,\langle \varphi ,\psi \rangle  = 0}\right\}  .
\]

Show that \( R \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature if and only if \( {\kappa }_{ + } \) and \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) are nonnegative.

Problem 11. This problem is concerned with two-convex hypersurfaces in manifolds of nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(i) Let \( V \) be a finite-dimensional vector space equipped with an inner product. Moreover, let \( A \) be a symmetric bilinear form on \( V \) . Suppose that \( A \) is two-nonnegative; that is, the sum of any two eigenvalues of \( h \) is nonnegative. Show that \( A\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right)  \geq  0 \) for all vectors \( z \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) satisfying \( g\left( {z, z}\right)  = 0. \)

(ii) Let \( V \) be a finite-dimensional vector space equipped with an inner product. Moreover, let \( A \) be a symmetric bilinear form on \( V \) which is two-nonnegative. Show that \( A\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right) A\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  - {\left| A\left( z,\bar{w}\right) \right| }^{2} \geq  0 \) for all vectors \( z, w \in  {V}^{\mathbb{C}} \) satisfying \( g\left( {z, z}\right)  = g\left( {z, w}\right)  = g\left( {w, w}\right)  = 0 \) .

(iii) Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a Riemannian manifold with nonnegative isotropic curvature, and let \( \sum \) be a two-convex hypersurface in \( M \) . Show that \( \sum \) has nonnegative isotropic curvature.

(ii) Show that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has nonnegative sectional curvature. (Hint: Use Corollary 6.11.)

(iii) Show that \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) has constant sectional curvature.

Problem 14. Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a compact manifold Riemannian manifold of dimension \( n \geq  3 \) , and let \( \rho \) be a positive real number. Moreover, we consider a sequence of real numbers \( {\varepsilon }_{k} \in  (0,1\rbrack \) such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\varepsilon }_{k} = 0 \) . For each \( k \) , we define a functional \( {\mathcal{F}}_{k} \) by

\[
{\mathcal{F}}_{k}\left( \psi \right)  = {\int }_{M}\left( {{\left| d\psi \right| }_{g}^{2} + \frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g}{\psi }^{2} - \frac{1}{2}\rho {\psi }^{2}\log \left( {{\varepsilon }_{k}^{2} + {\psi }^{2}}\right) }\right) d{\operatorname{vol}}_{g}.
\]

(i) Show that there exists a constant \( N \) , depending only on \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) and \( \rho \) , such that

\[
{\mathcal{F}}_{k}\left( \psi \right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{M}{\left| d\psi \right| }_{g}^{2}d{\operatorname{vol}}_{g} - N
\]

for all functions \( \psi  \in  {H}^{1}\left( M\right) \) satisfying \( {\int }_{M}{\psi }^{2}d{\operatorname{vol}}_{g} = 1 \) .

(ii) For each \( k \) , there exists a nonnegative function \( {\varphi }_{k} \in  {H}^{1}\left( M\right) \) such that \( {\int }_{M}{\varphi }_{k}^{2}d{\operatorname{vol}}_{g} = 1 \) and

\[
{\mathcal{F}}_{k}\left( {\varphi }_{k}\right)  = \inf \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{k}\left( \psi \right)  : \psi  \in  {H}^{1}\left( M\right) ,{\int }_{M}{\psi }^{2}d{\operatorname{vol}}_{g} = 1}\right\}  .
\]

(iii) Let

\[

Show that \( {\varphi }_{k} \) is a smooth solution of the equation

\[
{\Delta }_{g}{\varphi }_{k} = \left( {\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g} - \frac{1}{2}\rho \log \left( {{\varepsilon }_{k}^{2} + {\varphi }_{k}^{2}}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}\rho \frac{{\varepsilon }_{k}^{2}}{{\varepsilon }_{k}^{2} + {\varphi }_{k}^{2}} - {\mu }_{k}}\right) {\varphi }_{k}.

\[

\[

\]

if \( r > 0 \) is sufficiently small.

\[
u\left( r\right)  \leq  C{\int }_{0}^{r}\left| {\log u\left( s\right) }\right| u\left( s\right) {ds}
\]

if \( r > 0 \) is sufficiently small. Deduce from this that \( u\left( r\right)  = 0 \) for \( r \) sufficiently small.

(vii) Show that the function \( \varphi \) is a strictly positive. Deduce from this that the functions \( {\varphi }_{k} \) converge to \( \varphi \) in \( {C}^{\infty }\left( M\right) \) .

nodes.content:
Problem 15. The goal of this problem is to show that every compact Ricci soliton is a gradient Ricci soliton. This was first proved by G. Perelman [68]. Let \( \left( {M, g}\right) \) be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension \( n \geq  3 \) , and let \( \rho \) be a positive real number. By the previous problem, we can find a real number \( \mu \) and a positive function \( \varphi  \in  {C}^{\infty }\left( M\right) \) such that

\[
{\Delta }_{g}\varphi  = \left( {\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{scal}}_{g} - \rho \log \varphi  - \mu }\right) \varphi .
\]

(i) Consider the tensor \( H = {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} + {D}^{2}f - {\rho g} \) , where \( f =  - 2\log \varphi \) . Show that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j = 1}}^{n}{g}^{ij}{D}_{j}\left( {{e}^{-f}{H}_{ik}}\right)  = 0.
\]

(ii) Suppose that \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g} + \frac{1}{2}{\mathcal{L}}_{\xi }g = {\rho g} \) for some vector field \( \xi \) . Show that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i, j, k = 1}}^{n}{g}^{ij}{D}_{j}\left( {{e}^{-f}{H}_{ik}\left( {{\partial }^{k}f - {\xi }^{k}}\right) }\right)  = {e}^{-f}{\left| H\right| }^{2}.
\]

Deduce from this that \( H = 0 \) .

Definition 1.1. (i) We denote by PIC the set of all algebraic curvature tensors that have nonnegative isotropic curvature in the sense that \( R\left( {\varphi ,\bar{\varphi }}\right)  \geq  0 \) for all complex two-forms of the form \( \varphi  = \left( {{e}_{1} + i{e}_{2}}\right)  \land  \left( {{e}_{3} + i{e}_{4}}\right) \) , where \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal four-frame.

(ii) We denote by PIC1 the set of all algebraic curvature tensors satisfying \( R\left( {\varphi ,\bar{\varphi }}\right)  \geq  0 \) for all complex two-forms of the form \( \varphi  = \left( {{e}_{1} + i{e}_{2}}\right)  \land  \left( {{e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4}}\right) \) , where \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal four-frame and \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

(iii) We denote by PIC2 the set of all algebraic curvature tensors satisfying \( R\left( {\varphi ,\bar{\varphi }}\right)  \geq  0 \) for all complex two-forms of the form \( \varphi  = \left( {{e}_{1} + {i\mu }{e}_{2}}\right)  \land  \left( {{e}_{3} + {i\lambda }{e}_{4}}\right) \) , where \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal four-frame and \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

THEOREM 1.2. Assume that \( n \geq  {12} \) . Let \( \mathcal{K} \) be a compact set of algebraic curvature tensors in dimension \( n \) that is contained in the interior of the PIC cone, and let \( T > 0 \) be given. Then there exist a small positive real number \( \theta \) , a large positive real number \( N \) , an increasing concave function \( f > 0 \) satisfying \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{f\left( s\right) }{s} = 0 \) , and a continuous family of closed, convex, \( O\left( n\right) \) -invariant sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) such that the family \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) ;\mathcal{K} \subset  {\mathcal{F}}_{0} \) ; and

\[
{\mathcal{F}}_{t} \subset  \{ R : R - \theta \text{ scalid } \oslash  \text{ id } \in  \text{ PIC }\}
\]

\[

\]

Suppose that \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal four-frame satisfying

\[

\]

We need to show that

\[
\widehat{b}\left( {{U}_{1313} + {U}_{1414} + {U}_{2323} + {U}_{2424} - 2{U}_{1234}}\right)
\]

\[
- \widehat{a}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{44}}\right)  - 4\widehat{a} + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2} \geq  0
\]

for this particular orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) .

Using condition (iii), we obtain \( \widehat{R} - 4\widehat{b}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC. Therefore,

\[
{32}\widehat{b} \leq  {\widehat{R}}_{1313} + {\widehat{R}}_{1414} + {\widehat{R}}_{2323} + {\widehat{R}}_{2424} - 2{\widehat{R}}_{1234}
\]

\[
= {\widehat{S}}_{1313} + {\widehat{S}}_{1414} + {\widehat{S}}_{2323} + {\widehat{S}}_{2424} - 2{\widehat{S}}_{1234}
\]

+ 2\widehat{b}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{44}}\right)  + \frac{4\left( {n - 2}\right) {\widehat{b}}^{2}}{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {16}\widehat{b} + \frac{4\left( {n - 2}\right) {\widehat{b}}^{2}}{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) ,
\]

hence \( \widehat{b}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \geq  \frac{4n}{n - 2} \) . Since \( U \in  {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC by Lemma 2.5, we conclude that

\[
\widehat{b}\left( {{U}_{1313} + {U}_{1414} + {U}_{2323} + {U}_{2424} - 2{U}_{1234}}\right)
\]

- \widehat{a}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{44}}\right)  - 4\widehat{a} + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}
\]

\]

\geq   - {12}\widehat{a} + \frac{{16}{n}^{2}}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{1}{8}}
\]

\[
> 0
\]

if \( \widehat{b} > 0 \) is sufficiently small.

Case 2: Suppose finally that \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{44} \geq  8 \) . By definition of \( U \) , we obtain

\[
\widehat{b}\left( {{U}_{1313} + {U}_{1414} + {U}_{2323} + {U}_{2424} - 2{U}_{1234}}\right)

- \widehat{a}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{22} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }_{44}}\right)  - 4\widehat{a} + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}

\]

- \frac{8\widehat{b}}{n}\left( {\frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \widehat{b}} - \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \widehat{b}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \widehat{a}}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right)
\]

\[

\]

\[
> 0
\]

if \( \widehat{b} > 0 \) is sufficiently small.

nodes.content: LEMMA 2.7. Let \( \widehat{a},\widehat{b} \) be real numbers such that \( 0 \leq  \widehat{b} \leq  \delta {e}^{-8\widehat{t}},2\widehat{a} = \; 2\widehat{b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\widehat{b}}^{2} \) , and let \( \widehat{S} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\ell }_{a, b}^{-1}\left( \widehat{R}\right) \) . Then \( \widehat{S} \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone.
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 2.7. Let \( \widehat{a},\widehat{b} \) be real numbers such that \( 0 \leq \widehat{b} \leq \delta {e}^{-8\widehat{t}},2\widehat{a} = \; 2\widehat{b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\widehat{b}}^{2} \) , and let \( \widehat{S} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\ell }_{a, b}^{-1}\left( \widehat{R}\right) \) . Then \( \widehat{S} \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone.

nodes.proof:
In view of condition (iii), \( \widehat{R} \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Therefore, the assertion is true for \( \widehat{b} = 0 \) . Hence, it suffices to consider the case \( 0 < \widehat{b} \leq  \delta {e}^{-8\widehat{t}} \) . Let us define functions \( a\left( t\right) , b\left( t\right) \) by \( b\left( t\right)  = {e}^{8\left( {\widehat{t} - t}\right) }\widehat{b} \) and \( a\left( t\right)  = {2b}\left( t\right)  + \left( {n - 2}\right) b{\left( t\right) }^{2} \) . Moreover, let \( S\left( t\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\ell }_{a\left( t\right) , b\left( t\right) }^{-1}\left( {R\left( t\right) }\right) \) . Since condition (i) holds up to time \( \widehat{t} \) , we know that \( S\left( t\right)  \in \) PIC for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\widehat{t}}\right\rbrack \) . The evolution of \( S\left( t\right) \) is given by

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{dt}S\left( t\right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}} = Q\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  - {b}^{\prime }\left( \widehat{t}\right) U = Q\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U,
\]

where

\[
U = \frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \widehat{b}}\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
- \frac{1}{n}\left( {\frac{1}{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \widehat{b}} - \frac{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \widehat{b}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \widehat{a}}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \text{ id } \oslash  \text{ id. }
\]

We claim that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC. To verify this, we distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) is strictly two-positive. By Lemma A.2, \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Since \( 2\widehat{a} = 2\widehat{b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\widehat{b}}^{2} \) , this implies that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Since \( U \in  {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC by Lemma 2.5, it follows that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC, as claimed.

Case 2: Suppose next that \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) is not strictly two-positive. In this case, \( \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) \left| {\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right| \) . Since \( 2\widehat{a} = 2\widehat{b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {\widehat{b}}^{2} \) , it follows that

\[
{D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  - 2\widehat{a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  - 2{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in  \mathrm{{PIC}}
\]

if \( \widehat{b} > 0 \) is sufficiently small. Condition (ii) implies \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + \left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \) id is weakly two-positive. Using Lemma A.2, we obtain

\[
2\widehat{a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)
\]

\[
+ 4\widehat{a}\left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} + 4\widehat{a}\left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}}\right) \mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
= 2\widehat{a}\left\lbrack  {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + \left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \mathrm{{id}}}\right\rbrack   \oslash  \left\lbrack  {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + \left( {1 + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right) \mathrm{{id}}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ 2\widehat{a}{\left( 1 - {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in  \text{ PIC. }
\]

On the other hand, Lemma 2.6 gives

\[
8\widehat{b}U - 4\widehat{a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} - 4\widehat{a}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} + {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in  {T}_{\widehat{S}}\mathrm{{PIC}}\text{ . }
\]

Moreover, if \( \widehat{b} > 0 \) is sufficiently small, then \( \widehat{a}{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}} \) is much smaller than \( {\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}} \) . Since \( \left| {\operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right) }\right|  \leq  C\left( n\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \) , it follows that

\[
{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{17}{8}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} - 4\widehat{a}{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{4}}\operatorname{scal}\left( \widehat{S}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} - 4\widehat{a}{\widehat{b}}^{\frac{5}{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \widehat{S}\right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

lies in the interior of the PIC cone. Adding all four formulae, we conclude that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC.

To summarize, we have shown that \( {D}_{\widehat{a},\widehat{b}}\left( \widehat{S}\right)  + 8\widehat{b}U \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC. Since \( Q\left( \widehat{S}\right)  \in  {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC by Proposition 7.5 in [5], we conclude that \( {\left. \frac{d}{dt}S\left( t\right) \right| }_{t = \widehat{t}} \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{\widehat{S}} \) PIC. Hence, if \( \widehat{S} \) lies on the boundary of the PIC cone, then \( S\left( t\right) \) lies outside the PIC cone if \( t \in  \lbrack 0,\widehat{t}) \) is sufficiently close to \( \widehat{t} \) . This is a contradiction. This completes the proof of Lemma 2.7.
