nodes.proof:
It suffices to show that \( \widetilde{\mathcal{E}}\left( b\right) \) is transversally invariant under the ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}S = Q\left( S\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( S\right) \) . Suppose that \( S \in  \widetilde{\mathcal{E}}\left( b\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) . Then

\[
Z \mathrel{\text{ := }} {S}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{S}_{1414} + {S}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{S}_{2424} - {2\lambda }{S}_{1234}
\]

\[
+ \sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right)  \geq  0
\]

for every orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and every \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, we assume that \( Z = 0 \) for some orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and some \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . We will show that \( \frac{d}{dt}Z > 0 \) for this particular four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and this particular \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose that \( \lambda  \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) . Using the formula for \( {D}_{a, b}\left( S\right) \) , we obtain

\[
\frac{d}{dt}S = Q\left( S\right)  + {2a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  + 2{b}^{2}\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

and

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  = {2S} * \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  - {4b}\mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{4\left( {n - 2}\right) a}{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  + \frac{4a}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\text{ id }
\]

\[
+ 2\frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}\mathrm{{id}},
\]

where \( {\left( S * H\right) }_{ik} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}{S}_{ipkq}{H}_{pq} \) . This implies

\[
\frac{d}{dt}Z \geq  Q{\left( S\right) }_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}Q{\left( S\right) }_{1414} + Q{\left( S\right) }_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}Q{\left( S\right) }_{2424} - {2\lambda Q}{\left( S\right) }_{1234}
\]

\[
+ {2a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1313} + {2a}{\lambda }^{2}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1414}
\]

\[
+ {2a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{2323} + {2a}{\lambda }^{2}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{2424}
\]

\[
- {4a\lambda }{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1234}
\]

\[
+ 2\sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {{\left( S * \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{11} + {\left( S * \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{4\left( {n - 2}\right) a}{n}\sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
- {4b}\sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {{\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{11} + {\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{8a}{{n}^{2}}\sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}.
\]

Applying Proposition A. 8 with \( H = \sqrt{2a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) , we obtain

\[
Q{\left( S\right) }_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}Q{\left( S\right) }_{1414} + Q{\left( S\right) }_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}Q{\left( S\right) }_{2424} - {2\lambda Q}{\left( S\right) }_{1234}
\]

\[
+ {2a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1313} + {2a}{\lambda }^{2}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1414}
\]

\[
+ {2a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{2323} + {2a}{\lambda }^{2}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{2424}
\]

\[
- {4a\lambda }{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1234}
\]

\[
+ 2\sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {{\left( S * \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{11} + {\left( S * \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{22}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Since \( S \in  \widetilde{\mathcal{E}}\left( b\right)  \subset \) PIC, Lemma A. 3 implies that the largest eigenvalue of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) is bounded from above by \( \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \) . Moreover, by Lemma 4.5, the sum of the two smallest eigenvalues of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) is bounded from below by \( \frac{2\left( {1 - \zeta }\right) }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \) . Applying Lemma A. 1 with \( H = \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) and \( \rho  = \frac{b}{a} \) gives

\[
\frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) a}{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right)  - b\left( {{\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{11} + {\left( \mathop{\operatorname{Ric}}\limits^{ \circ  }{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{22}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{2}{{n}^{2}}\left( {a\left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {1 - \zeta }\right)  - {2b}{\zeta }^{2}\frac{{n}^{2} - {2n} + 2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}}\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}.
\]

Putting these facts together, we conclude that

\[
\frac{d}{dt}Z \geq  \frac{8}{{n}^{2}}\left( {a\left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {1 - \zeta }\right) }\right)  - {2b}{\zeta }^{2}\frac{{n}^{2} - {2n} + 2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}}\right) \sqrt{2a}\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( S\right) }^{2}.
\]

On the other hand, Lemma 4.4 implies

\[
a\left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {1 - \zeta }\right) }\right)  \geq  {2a}{\zeta }^{2}\frac{{n}^{2} - {2n} + 2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}} > {2b}{\zeta }^{2}\frac{{n}^{2} - {2n} + 2}{{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}.
\]

Since \( \lambda  \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) , it follows that \( \frac{d}{dt}Z > 0 \) .

Case 2: Finally, suppose that \( \lambda  = 1 \) . In this case,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}Z = Q{\left( S\right) }_{1313} + Q{\left( S\right) }_{1414} + Q{\left( S\right) }_{2323} + Q{\left( S\right) }_{2424} - {2Q}{\left( S\right) }_{1234}
\]

\[
+ {2a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1313} + {2a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1414}
\]

\[
+ {2a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{2323} + {2a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{2424}
\]

\[
- {4a}{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1234}.
\]

Since \( S \in \) PIC and \( Z = {S}_{1313} + {S}_{1414} + {S}_{2323} + {S}_{2424} - 2{S}_{1234} = 0 \) , we obtain

\[
Q{\left( S\right) }_{1313} + Q{\left( S\right) }_{1414} + Q{\left( S\right) }_{2323} + Q{\left( S\right) }_{2424} - {2Q}{\left( S\right) }_{1234} \geq  0
\]

for this particular four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) . By Lemma 4.5, the sum of the two smallest eigenvalues of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) is strictly positive. This implies

\[
{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1313} + {\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1414}
\]

\[
+ {\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{2323} + {\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{2424}
\]

\[
- 2{\left( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right) }_{1234} > 0
\]

by Lemma A.2. Putting these facts together, we conclude that \( \frac{d}{dt}Z > 0 \) . This completes the proof of Theorem 4.6.

\]

\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

By Proposition 4.3, we have \( \widetilde{\mathcal{C}}\left( {\widetilde{b}}_{\max }\right)  = \mathcal{C}\left( {b}_{\max }\right) \) . For each \( b \in \; \left( {0,{b}_{\max } + {\widetilde{b}}_{\max }}\right) \) , we define

\[
\widehat{\mathcal{C}}\left( b\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} \mathcal{C}\left( b\right) & \text{ for }b \in  \left( {0,{b}_{\max }}\right\rbrack  , \\  \widetilde{\mathcal{C}}\left( {{b}_{\max } + {\widetilde{b}}_{\max } - b}\right) & \text{ for }b \in  \left( {{b}_{\max },{b}_{\max } + {\widetilde{b}}_{\max }}\right) . \end{array}\right.
\]

Therefore, \( \widehat{\mathcal{C}}\left( b\right) \) is a family of closed, convex, \( O\left( n\right) \) -invariant cones that depends continuously on the parameter \( b \in  \left( {0,{b}_{\max } + {\widetilde{b}}_{\max }}\right) \) . Moreover, for each \( b \in \; \left( {0,{b}_{\max } + {\widetilde{b}}_{\max }}\right) \) , the cone \( \widehat{\mathcal{C}}\left( b\right) \) is transversally invariant under the Hamilton ODE.

By Theorem 2.1, there exists a family of closed, convex, \( O\left( n\right) \) -invariant sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( 0\right) } : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) such that the family \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( 0\right) } : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) \) . Furthermore, \( \mathcal{K} \subset  {\mathcal{G}}_{0}^{\left( 0\right) } \) and

\[
{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( 0\right) } \subset  \{ R : R - \theta \text{ scalid } \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in  \mathrm{{PIC}}\}
\]

\[
\cap  \{ R : {\operatorname{Ric}}_{11} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{22} - \theta \operatorname{scal} + N \geq  0\}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Consequently, we can find a small positive number \( {\beta }_{0} \) (depending on \( \theta \) ) such that

\[
{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( 0\right) } \subset  \left\{  {R : R + N\text{ id } \otimes  \text{ id } \in  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}\left( {\beta }_{0}\right) }\right\}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

Arguing as in Theorem 4.1 in [1] (see also Proposition 16 in [8]), we can construct an increasing sequence \( {\beta }_{0} < {\beta }_{1} < {\beta }_{2} < \cdots \) with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{\beta }_{j} = \; {b}_{\max } + {\widetilde{b}}_{\max } \) and a sequence of families of sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( j\right) } : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) with the following properties:

- For \( j = 0 \) , the family of sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( 0\right) } : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) coincides with the one constructed in Theorem 2.1.

- For each \( j \geq  1 \) , the family of sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( j\right) } : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is defined by

\[
{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( j\right) } = \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( j - 1\right) } : R + {2}^{j}N\text{ id }@\text{ id } \in  \widehat{\mathcal{C}}\left( {\beta }_{j}\right) }\right\}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

- For each \( j \geq  1 \) , the family \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( j\right) } : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE.

- For each \( j \geq  1 \) , we have \( \mathcal{K} \subset  {\mathcal{G}}_{0}^{\left( j\right) } \) .

Since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{\beta }_{j} = {b}_{\max } + {\widetilde{b}}_{\max } \) , we can find a sequence of positive numbers \( {\varepsilon }_{j} \) such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{\varepsilon }_{j} = 0 \) and \( \widehat{\mathcal{C}}\left( {\beta }_{j}\right)  \subset  \left\{  {R : R + {\varepsilon }_{j}}\right. \) scalid \( \left. {\varnothing \text{ id } \in  \text{ PIC }1}\right\} \) . This implies

\[
{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( j\right) } \subset  \left\{  {R : R + {\varepsilon }_{j}\text{ scal id }\varnothing \mathrm{{id}} + {2}^{j}N\left( {1 + {2n}\left( {n - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }_{j}}\right) \mathrm{{id}}\varnothing \mathrm{{id}} \in  \mathrm{{PIC}}1}\right\}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

We now define \( {\mathcal{G}}_{t} = \mathop{\bigcap }\limits_{{j \in  \mathbb{N}}}{\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( j\right) } \) for each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Then \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{G}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is a family of closed, convex, \( O\left( n\right) \) -invariant sets satisfying \( \mathcal{K} \subset  {\mathcal{G}}_{0} \) . Moreover, the family of sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{G}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE. Furthermore,

\[
{\mathcal{G}}_{t} \subset  \left\{  {R \in  {\mathcal{G}}_{t}^{\left( 0\right) } : R + h\left( \text{ scal }\right) \text{ id } \oslash  \text{ id } \in  \mathrm{{PIC}}1}\right\}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , where \( h\left( s\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{j \in  \mathbb{N}}}\left( {{\varepsilon }_{j}s + {2}^{j}N\left( {1 + {2n}\left( {n - 1}\right) {\varepsilon }_{j}}\right) }\right) \) . Clearly, \( h \) is an increasing concave function satisfying \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{h\left( s\right) }{s} = 0 \) . Finally, we put \( g\left( s\right)  \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\int }_{0}^{1}\chi \left( r\right) h\left( {s + r}\right) {dr} \) , where \( \chi \) is a nonnegative smooth function that is supported in \( \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) and satisfies \( {\int }_{0}^{1}\chi \left( r\right) {dr} = 1 \) . Clearly, \( g\left( s\right)  \geq  h\left( s\right) \) . It is easy to see that \( g \) has all the required properties.

nodes.proof:
We first show that the family of sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is preserved by the Hamilton ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) \) . To prove this, we assume that \( R \in  {\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) , \( S = R + {2g} \) (scal) id \( \oslash \) id, and

\[
{S}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{S}_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}{S}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{S}_{2424} - {2\lambda \mu }{S}_{1234}
\]

\[
+ \left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right) f\left( \text{ scal }\right)  = 0
\]

for one particular orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and one particular pair \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( S \) lies in the interior of the PIC1 cone, it follows that \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) . Moreover,

\[
{R}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}{R}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{R}_{2424} - {2\lambda \mu }{R}_{1234}
\]

\[
< {S}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{S}_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}{S}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{S}_{2424} - {2\lambda \mu }{S}_{1234} \leq  0.
\]

Hence, Proposition 5.2 implies that

\[
{\lambda }^{2}{\left( 1 - {\mu }^{2}\right) }^{2} + {\mu }^{2}{\left( 1 - {\lambda }^{2}\right) }^{2} + {\left( 1 - {\lambda }^{2}\right) }^{2}{\left( 1 - {\mu }^{2}\right) }^{2} > \kappa .
\]

Since \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \lbrack 0,1) \) , the first order conditions corresponding to variations of \( \lambda \) and \( \mu \) give

\[
\lambda \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right) f\left( \mathrm{{scal}}\right)  = \lambda {S}_{1414} + \lambda {\mu }^{2}{S}_{2424} - \mu {S}_{1234}
\]

\[
= \left( {\lambda {S}_{1414} + \mu {S}_{1423}}\right)  - \mu \left( {{S}_{1324} - {\lambda \mu }{S}_{2424}}\right)
\]

and

\[
\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) {\mu f}\left( \text{ scal }\right)  = \mu {S}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}\mu {S}_{2424} - \lambda {S}_{1234}
\]

\[
= \left( {\lambda {S}_{1423} + \mu {S}_{2323}}\right)  - \lambda \left( {{S}_{1324} - {\lambda \mu }{S}_{2424}}\right) .
\]

Moreover,

\[
\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right) f\left( \text{ scal }\right)  =  - \left( {{S}_{1313} - {\lambda \mu }{S}_{1324}}\right)  - \lambda \left( {\lambda {S}_{1414} + \mu {S}_{1423}}\right)
\]

\[
- \mu \left( {\lambda {S}_{1423} + \mu {S}_{2323}}\right)  + {\lambda \mu }\left( {{S}_{1324} - {\lambda \mu }{S}_{2424}}\right) .
\]

Consequently,

\[
\left\lbrack  {{\lambda }^{2}{\left( 1 - {\mu }^{2}\right) }^{2} + {\mu }^{2}{\left( 1 - {\lambda }^{2}\right) }^{2} + {\left( 1 - {\lambda }^{2}\right) }^{2}{\left( 1 - {\mu }^{2}\right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack  f{\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  2{\left( \lambda {S}_{1414} + \mu {S}_{1423}\right) }^{2} + 2{\mu }^{2}{\left( {S}_{1324} - \lambda \mu {S}_{2424}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 2{\left( \lambda {S}_{1423} + \mu {S}_{2323}\right) }^{2} + 2{\lambda }^{2}{\left( {S}_{1324} - \lambda \mu {S}_{2424}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 4{\left( {S}_{1313} - \lambda \mu {S}_{1324}\right) }^{2} + 4{\lambda }^{2}{\left( \lambda {S}_{1414} + \mu {S}_{1423}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
+ 4{\mu }^{2}{\left( \lambda {S}_{1423} + \mu {S}_{2323}\right) }^{2} + 4{\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{\left( {S}_{1324} - \lambda \mu {S}_{2424}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  {16}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{13pq} - \lambda \mu {S}_{24pq}\right) }^{2} + {16}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}{\left( \lambda {S}_{14pq} + \mu {S}_{23pq}\right) }^{2}.
\]

Putting these facts together, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}{\left( {S}_{13pq} - \lambda \mu {S}_{24pq}\right) }^{2} + \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}{\left( \lambda {S}_{14pq} + \mu {S}_{23pq}\right) }^{2} \geq  \frac{\kappa }{16}f{\left( \mathrm{{scal}}\right) }^{2}.
\]

On the other hand, Proposition 7.26 in [5] implies

\[
{\left( {S}^{\# }\right) }_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{\left( {S}^{\# }\right) }_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}{\left( {S}^{\# }\right) }_{2323}
\]

\[
+ {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{\left( {S}^{\# }\right) }_{2424} + {2\lambda \mu }{\left( {S}^{\# }\right) }_{1342} + {2\lambda \mu }{\left( {S}^{\# }\right) }_{1423} \geq  0.
\]

Adding these inequalities gives

\[
Q{\left( S\right) }_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}Q{\left( S\right) }_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}Q{\left( S\right) }_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}Q{\left( S\right) }_{2424}
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu Q}{\left( S\right) }_{1234} \geq  \frac{\kappa }{16}f{\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) }^{2}.
\]

Since \( Q\left( R\right)  - Q\left( S\right)  + L\left( n\right) \left( {\operatorname{scal} + g\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) }\right) g\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) \) id \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC2, it follows that

\[
Q{\left( R\right) }_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}Q{\left( R\right) }_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}Q{\left( R\right) }_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}Q{\left( R\right) }_{2424} - {2\lambda \mu Q}{\left( R\right) }_{1234}
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{\kappa }{16}f{\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) }^{2} - {8L}\left( n\right) \left( {\operatorname{scal} + g\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) }\right) g\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) .
\]

Since \( f \) and \( g \) are monotone increasing, we conclude that

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{S}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{S}_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}{S}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{S}_{2424} - {2\lambda \mu }{S}_{1234}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+\left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right) f\left( \text{ scal }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{\kappa }{16}f{\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) }^{2} - {8L}\left( n\right) \left( {\operatorname{scal} + g\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) }\right) g\left( \operatorname{scal}\right) ,
\]

and the right-hand side is positive in view of our choice of \( f \) . This shows that the family of sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE.

If \( R \in  {\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) and \( S = R + {2g} \) (scal) id \( \oslash \) id, then \( S + {2f} \) (scal) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2 (cf. Proposition 7.18 in [5]), and consequently \( R + 2\left( {f\left( \text{ scal }\right)  + g\left( \text{ scal }\right) }\right) \) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2.

Finally, if we choose \( \Lambda \) sufficiently large, we can arrange that the following holds: if \( R \in  \mathcal{K} \) and \( S = R + {2g}\left( \text{ scal }\right) \) id \( \mathcal{O} \) id, then

\[
{S}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{S}_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}{S}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{S}_{2424} - {2\lambda \mu }{S}_{1234}
\]

\[
+ \left( {1 - {\lambda }^{2}}\right) \left( {1 - {\mu }^{2}}\right) f\left( \text{ scal }\right)  \geq  0
\]

for \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . This ensures that \( \mathcal{K} \subset  {\mathcal{F}}_{0} \) .

THEOREM 6.1 (cf. R. Hamilton [19]). Assume that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow that is complete with bounded curvature and is weakly PIC2. Then

\[

\]

for every tangent vector \( v \) . In particular, the product \( t \) scal is monotone increasing at each point in space.

nodes.proof:
Suppose that the assertion is false. Then there exists a time \( \tau  \in \; \left( {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) with the property that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) does not locally split as a product of an \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional manifold with an interval. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, we conclude that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible.

The Ricci tensor of \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the evolution equation

\[
{D}_{t}\operatorname{Ric} = \Delta \operatorname{Ric} + {2R} * \operatorname{Ric},
\]

where \( {\left( R * \operatorname{Ric}\right) }_{ik} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p, q = 1}}^{n}{R}_{ipkq}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{pq} \) . Since \( R \) is weakly PIC2, the term \( R * \operatorname{Ric} \) is weakly positive definite. Using the strict maximum principle (see \( \left\lbrack  {5,§9}\right\rbrack \) or [18]), we conclude that the null space of \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( \tau \right) } \) defines a parallel subbundle of the tangent bundle of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) . Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible, this subbundle must have rank 0 . Consequently, the Ricci curvature of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly positive.

Let \( \Omega \) be a bounded open neighborhood of the point \( {p}_{0} \) with smooth boundary. Let us choose a smooth function \( f : \bar{\Omega } \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) with the property that \( f > 0 \) in \( \Omega , f = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega \) , and \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( \tau \right) } - f \) id is weakly positive definite. Let \( F : \bar{\Omega } \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) denote the solution of the linear heat equation with respect to the evolving metric \( g\left( t\right) \) with initial data \( F\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right)  = f \) and Dirichlet boundary condition \( F = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Using the maximum principle, we conclude that \( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{g\left( t\right) } - F\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) id is weakly positive definite at each point in \( \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( F\left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  > 0 \) , the Ricci curvature at \( \left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) is strictly positive, contrary to our assumption.

Moreover, we assume that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is weakly PIC2 and strictly PIC. nodes.proof:
Suppose that the assertion is false. Then there exists a time \( \tau  \in \; \left( {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) with the property that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) does not split off a line. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, we conclude that \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible. In view of Berger's holonomy classification theorem, there are four possible cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = {SO}\left( n\right) \) . If we fix an arbitrary pair of real numbers \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) , then Theorem 9.13 in [5] implies that the set of all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) satisfying

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  = 0
\]

is invariant under parallel transport. Since \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = {SO}\left( n\right) \) , we conclude that

\[
{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{3},{e}_{1},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{4},{e}_{1},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{2},{e}_{3}}\right)  + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{2},{e}_{4},{e}_{2},{e}_{4}}\right)
\]

\[
- {2\lambda \mu }{R}_{g\left( \tau \right) }\left( {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right)  > 0
\]

for all orthonormal four-frames \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and all \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) . In other words, the curvature tensor of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC2 cone.

Let \( \Omega \) be a bounded open neighborhood of the point \( {p}_{0} \) with smooth boundary. Let us choose a smooth function \( f : \bar{\Omega } \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) with the property that \( f > 0 \) in \( \Omega , f = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega \) , and \( {R}_{g\left( \tau \right) } - \frac{1}{2}f \) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2. Let \( F \) : \( \bar{\Omega } \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) denote the solution of the linear heat equation with respect to the evolving metric \( g\left( t\right) \) with initial data \( F\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right)  = f \) and Dirichlet boundary condition \( F = 0 \) on \( \partial \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Let \( S \mathrel{\text{ := }} {R}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{2}F\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) id \( \oslash \) id. Then \( {D}_{t}S = {\Delta S} + Q\left( S\right)  + {2F}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \oslash  \operatorname{id} + \left( {n - 1}\right) {F}^{2}\operatorname{id} \oslash  \operatorname{id} \) . Using the maximum principle, we conclude that \( {R}_{g\left( t\right) } - \frac{1}{2}F\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) id \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC2 at each point in \( \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {\tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( F\left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  > 0 \) , the curvature tensor at \( \left( {{p}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) lies in the interior of the PIC2 cone, contrary to our assumption.

Case 2: Suppose that \( n = {2m} \) and \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = U\left( m\right) \) . In this case, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a Kähler manifold. This is impossible since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC.

Case 3: Suppose next that \( n = {4m} \geq  8 \) and \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  = \operatorname{Sp}\left( m\right) \) . \( \mathrm{{Sp}}\left( 1\right) \) . In this case, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a quaternionic Kähler manifold. In particular, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is an Einstein manifold. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, we conclude that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a round sphere (cf. [4]). This is impossible.

Case 4: Suppose finally that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \neq  {SO}\left( n\right) \) and \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally symmetric. In this case, \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is an Einstein manifold, for otherwise the eigenspaces of the Ricci tensor give a splitting of the tangent bundle into parallel subbundles, which is impossible since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is locally irreducible. Since \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC, it follows that the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right) \) is a round sphere (cf. [4]). This contradicts the fact that \( {\operatorname{Hol}}^{0}\left( {M, g\left( \tau \right) }\right)  \neq  {SO}\left( n\right) \) . This completes the proof of Theorem 6.6.

Proposition 6.11. Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , is a complete ancient solution to the Ricci flow that is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, is weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC for some uniform constant \( \theta  > 0 \) . Moreover, suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal} + 2\langle \nabla \operatorname{scal}, v\rangle  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  \geq  0
\]

for every tangent vector \( v \) . Then \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature.
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 6.11. Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , is a complete ancient solution to the Ricci flow that is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, is weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC for some uniform constant \( \theta > 0 \) . Moreover, suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the...

nodes.proof:
Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality, it suffices to show that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature. The proof is by contradiction. Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has unbounded curvature.

By the strict maximum principle, we can find a real number \( \delta  > 0 \) with the property that the scalar curvature \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly positive for \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) .

Consequently, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC for \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) . We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2. In this case, \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) by the soul theorem (cf. [10]). By a standard point-picking argument, there exists a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  M \) such that \( {Q}_{j} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \; \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  {j}^{4} \) and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-4{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack  }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

Using Shi's interior derivative estimate, we obtain bounds for all the derivatives of curvature on \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, j{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . We now dilate the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) . Using the noncollapsing assumption and the curvature derivative estimates, we conclude that, after passing to a subsequence, the rescaled flows converge in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to a smooth nonflat ancient solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . The limit \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is complete, has bounded curvature, is weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC. By Proposition 6.8, the manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) splits off a line. By Corollary 6.7, universal cover of \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a family of shrinking cylinders \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Therefore, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a quotient \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1}/\Gamma }\right)  \times  \mathbb{R} \) . If \( \Gamma \) is nontrivial, then a result of Hamilton implies that \( M \) contains a nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space form \( {S}^{n - 1}/\Gamma \) (cf. [6, Th. A.2]), but this is impossible since \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Thus, \( \Gamma \) is trivial, and \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a standard cylinder \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Consequently, \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) contains a sequence of necks with radii converging to 0 . This contradicts Proposition 6.9.

Case 2: Suppose finally that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is not strictly PIC2. By Proposition 6.6, the universal cover of \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a product \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( t\right) }\right)  \times  \mathbb{R} \) for each \( t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) . Clearly, \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  ( - \delta ,0\rbrack \) , is a complete solution to the Ricci flow of dimension \( n - 1 \) , which is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, weakly PIC2, and uniformly PIC1. By assumption, \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has unbounded curvature. Using a point-picking lemma, we can construct a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  X \) such that \( {Q}_{j} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  {j}^{4} \) and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{2j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4{Q}_{j}.
\]

As in Case 1, the Harnack inequality and Shi's interior derivative estimate give bounds for all the derivatives of curvature on \( {B}_{{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, j{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{j}^{2}{Q}_{j}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . We now dilate the manifold \( \left( {X,{g}_{X}\left( 0\right) }\right) \) around the point \( {x}_{j} \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) . Passing to the limit as \( j \rightarrow  \infty \) , we obtain a smooth nonflat limit that is uniformly PIC1 and that must split off a line by Proposition 6.8. This is a contradiction.

THEOREM 6.13 (cf. G. Perelman [33,§11.7]). Given \( \kappa  > 0 \) , we can find a positive function \( \omega  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) (depending on \( n \) and \( \kappa \) ) with the following property: Let \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) be a an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. Then

\]

for all points \( x, y \in  M \) and all \( t \) .

nodes.proof:
The proof is essentially the same as in Section 11.7 in Perelman's paper [33] (see also [12]). We sketch the argument for the convenience of the reader. Let us fix a point \( y \in  M \) . By rescaling, we can arrange that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)  = 1 \) . For abbreviation, let \( A = \left\{  {x \in  M : \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right) {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, x\right) }^{2} \geq  1}\right\} \) . We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose that \( A = \varnothing \) . In this case, we can find a point \( z \in  M \) such that \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  = \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right) \) . Using the Harnack inequality, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right)
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . By Shi’s derivative estimates, \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{2} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, \( {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) since \( A = \varnothing \) . Hence, we can find a small positive constant \( \beta \) , depending only on \( n \) , such that for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\beta \operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right) \;\text{ and }\;{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {y, z}\right)  \leq  2\operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}.
\]

If we apply the Harnack inequality (cf. Corollary 6.3) with \( t =  - \beta \operatorname{scal}{\left( z,0\right) }^{-1} \) , then we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \exp \left( \frac{{d}_{g\left( t\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2}}{\left( -2t\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \exp \left( \frac{2}{\left( {-t}\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

\[
= \exp \left( \frac{2}{\beta }\right) \text{ . }
\]

Putting these facts together, we conclude that \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  2\exp \left( \frac{2}{\beta }\right) \) .

Case 2: Suppose now that \( A \neq  \varnothing \) . In this case, we choose a point \( z \in  A \) that has minimal distance from \( y \) with respect to the metric \( g\left( 0\right) \) . Note that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right)  = {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2} \) since \( z \) lies on the boundary of \( A \) . Let \( p \) be the mid-point of the minimizing geodesic in \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) joining \( y \) and \( z \) . Clearly, \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p,\frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right)  \cap  A = \varnothing \) . This implies

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p,\frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  {16}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}.
\]

By the Harnack inequality,

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {p,\frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {16}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . The noncollapsing assumption gives

\[
{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {p,\frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{4}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( y, z\right) \right) }^{n}
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . This implies

\[
{\left( 4r\right) }^{-n}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {p,{4r}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{16}{r}^{-1}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( y, z\right) \right) }^{n}
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) and all \( r \geq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) \) . Applying Theorem 6.12 with \( {x}_{0} \mathrel{\text{ := }} p \) , \( {r}_{0} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {4r} \) , and \( w \mathrel{\text{ := }} \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{16}{r}^{-1}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( y, z\right) \right) }^{n} \) , we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}\omega \left( {{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-1}r}\right)
\]

for all \( r \geq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) \) , where \( \omega  : \lbrack 1,\infty ) \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) is a positive and increasing function that may depend on \( n \) and \( \kappa \) . In particular, if we put \( r = {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) \) and apply the Harnack inequality, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p,{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}\omega \left( 1\right) ,
\]

for all \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) . By Shi’s derivative estimates,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( {n,\kappa }\right) {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-4}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2},0}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {z,0}\right)  = {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2} \) by our choice of \( z \) . Therefore, we can find a small positive constant \( \beta \) , depending only on \( n \) and \( \kappa \) , such that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2} \) and \( {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {y, z}\right)  \leq  2{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\beta {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2},0}\right\rbrack \) . If we apply the Harnack inequality (cf. Corollary 6.3) with \( t =  - \beta {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2} \) , then we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{2}{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2} \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {z, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \exp \left( \frac{{d}_{g\left( t\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2}}{\left( -2t\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \exp \left( \frac{2{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{2}}{\left( -t\right) }\right) \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

\[
= \exp \left( \frac{2}{\beta }\right) \text{ . }
\]

This finally implies

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, r}\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {p, r + {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y, z}\right) }\right) }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-2}\omega \left( {{d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( y, z\right) }^{-1}r + 1}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  2{e}^{\frac{2}{\beta }}\omega \left( {\sqrt{2}{e}^{\frac{1}{\beta }}r + 1}\right)
\]

for all \( r \geq  0 \) . This completes the proof of Theorem 6.13.

It follows from the noncollapsing assumption and the long-range curvature estimate in Theorem 6.13 that, after passing to a subsequence if necessary, the sequence \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) ,{x}_{j}}\right) \) converges in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to a smooth nonflat ancient solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) . Clearly, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, is weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC. It remains to show that \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature. Since \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature, the flow \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Harnack inequality

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal} + 2\langle \nabla \operatorname{scal}, v\rangle  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  \geq  0
\]

(cf. Corollary 6.2). Passing to the limit as \( j \rightarrow  \infty \) , we conclude that the Harnack inequality holds on the limit \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) . Consequently, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature by Proposition 6.11.

nodes.proof: By the soul theorem (cf. [10]), \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . By the solution of the Schoenflies conjecture in dimension \( n \geq  5,\sum \) bounds a compact domain \( \Omega \) that is diffeomorphic to \( {B}^{n} \) . Let us choose a diffeomorphism \( F : \Omega  \rightarrow \; {B}^{n} \) , and let \( f : \partial \Omega  \rightarrow  {S}^{n - 1} \) be an \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \) -isometry. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the map \( {\left. F\right| }_{\partial \Omega } \circ  {f}^{-1} : {S}^{n - 1} \rightarrow  {S}^{n - 1} \) is orientation-preserving. We claim that the map \( {\left. F\right| }_{\partial \Omega } \circ  {f}^{-1} : {S}^{n - 1} \rightarrow  {S}^{n - 1} \) is isotopic to the identity. To prove this, let \( z \) denote the height function on the neck \( N \) , so that \( \{ z = 0\}  = \sum \) and \( \{ z \in  \lbrack  - {10},0)\}  \subset  \Omega \) . Moreover, let \( \varphi \left( z\right)  = {e}^{-\frac{1}{z}} \) for \( z \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . Let us define a modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) as follows. The metric \( \widetilde{g} \) agrees with \( g \) inside \( \Omega \) . In the region \( \left\{  {z \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{20}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , we change the metric conformally by \( \widetilde{g} = {e}^{-{2\varphi }}g \) . In the region \( \left\{  {z \in  \left( {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , we define \( \widetilde{g} = {e}^{-{2\varphi }}\left( {\chi \left( z\right) g + \left( {1 - \chi \left( z\right) }\right) \bar{g}}\right) \) , where \( \bar{g} \) denotes the standard metric on the cylinder and \( \chi  : \left( {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) is a smooth cutoff function satisfying \( \chi \left( z\right)  = 1 \) for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{18}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \chi \left( z\right)  = 0 \) for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{12},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . Since the original metric \( g \) is strictly PIC2, the modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) will be strictly PIC2 in the region \( \left\{  {z \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) . Moreover, the surgically modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) is rotationally symmetric for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{12},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . Consequently, we can extend \( \widetilde{g} \) by gluing in a rotationally symmetric cap. This can be done in such a way that the glued metric is strictly PIC2. To summarize, we obtain a closed manifold that is obtained by gluing two balls, and that admits a metric that is strictly PIC2. If the map \( {\left. F\right| }_{\partial \Omega } \circ  {f}^{-1} \) is not isotopic to the identity, then this glued manifold is an exotic sphere, that contradicts the fact that exotic spheres do not admit metrics that are strictly PIC2 (cf. [8]).

nodes.content:
THEOREM 6.18 (cf. G. Perelman [33, Cor. 11.8], Chen-Zhu [12, Prop. 3.4]). Given \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) and \( \theta  > 0 \) , we can find large positive constants \( {C}_{1} = {C}_{1}\left( {n,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) and \( {C}_{2} = {C}_{2}\left( {n,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) with the following property: Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a noncompact ancient \( \kappa \) -solution satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC that is not locally isometric to a family of shrinking cylinders. Then, for each point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) in space-time, we can find a neighborhood \( B \) of \( {x}_{0} \) satisfying

\[
{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{C}_{1}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{C}_{1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)
\]

and

\[
{C}_{2}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {C}_{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  B \) . Moreover, \( B \) satisfies one of the following conditions:

- \( B \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -neck with center at \( {x}_{0} \) .

- \( B \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -cap in the sense of Definition 6.16.

In particular, \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) is \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -noncollapsed for some universal constant \( {\kappa }_{0} = \; {\kappa }_{0}\left( {n,\theta }\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
It suffices to prove the assertion for \( {t}_{0} = 0 \) . Suppose that \( {x}_{0} \) does not lie at the center of an \( \varepsilon \) -neck in \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) . Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is not locally isometric to a family of shrinking cylinders, Corollary 6.7 implies that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2. By the soul theorem (cf. [10]), \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . We denote by \( {M}_{\varepsilon } \) the set of all points that do not lie at the center of an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{4} \) -neck in \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) . Note that \( {x}_{0} \) lies in the interior of \( {M}_{\varepsilon } \) .

Step 1: We claim that the closure of \( {M}_{\varepsilon } \) is compact. If this is false, we can find a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  {M}_{\varepsilon } \) such that \( {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{j}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) . The long-range curvature estimate in Theorem 6.13 implies \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( {x}_{0},{x}_{j}\right) }^{2} \; = \infty \) . We now dilate the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) \) by the factor \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) \) . By Corollary 6.15, the rescaled flows converge in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \mathcal{O} \) id \( \in \) PIC. By Proposition 6.8, the manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) splits off a line. Since the limit \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature, Corollary 6.7 implies that the universal cover of \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a family of shrinking cylinders \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Therefore, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a quotient \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1}/\Gamma }\right)  \times  \mathbb{R} \) . If \( \Gamma \) is nontrival, then Theorem A. 2 in [6] implies that \( M \) contains a nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space form \( {S}^{n - 1}/\Gamma \) , but this is impossible since \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Thus, \( \Gamma \) is trivial, and \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a standard cylinder \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Consequently, \( {x}_{j} \) lies at the center of an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{8} \) -neck if \( j \) is sufficiently large. This contradicts the assumption that \( {x}_{j} \in  {M}_{\varepsilon } \) .

Step 2: We now consider an arbitrary point \( y \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon } \) . By definition of \( {M}_{\varepsilon } \) , \( y \) lies at the center of an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{2} \) -neck in \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) . The Harnack inequality gives \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  2\operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) \) for all \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\operatorname{scal}{\left( y,0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) and all \( t \leq  0 \) . Using Shi’s derivative estimates, we obtain \( \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal}\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) \operatorname{scal}{\left( y,0\right) }^{2} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\operatorname{scal}{\left( y,0\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . Hence, we can find a small constant \( \beta  = \beta \left( n\right)  > 0 \) such that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {y, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) \) and

\[
{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {y,\operatorname{scal}{\left( y,0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \beta \operatorname{scal}{\left( y,0\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\beta \operatorname{scal}{\left( y,0\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . Applying Theorem 6.12, we obtain

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) \omega \left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( x, y\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  M \) , where \( \omega  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) denotes a positive function that does not depend on \( \kappa \) . Using the Harnack inequality, we conclude that

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) \omega \left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( x, y\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  M \) and all \( t \leq  0 \) .

Step 3: We again consider an arbitrary point \( y \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon } \) . Recall that \( y \) lies at the center of an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{2} \) -neck in \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) . By work of Hamilton [21], a neck admits a unique foliation by constant mean curvature (CMC) spheres. Let \( {\sum }_{y} \) denote the leaf of the CMC foliation of \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) that passes through \( y \) . By Proposition 6.17, \( {\sum }_{y} \) bounds an \( \varepsilon \) -cap, which we denote by \( {\Omega }_{y} \) .

We next show that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) {\operatorname{diam}}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( {\Omega }_{y}\right) }^{2} \leq  C \) , where \( C \) depends on \( n,\theta \) , and \( \varepsilon \) , but not on \( \kappa \) . The proof is by contradiction. Suppose that \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a sequence of noncompact ancient \( {\kappa }_{j} \) -solutions that satisfy \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC and that are not locally isometric to a family of shrinking cylinders. Suppose further that \( {y}_{j} \in  {M}^{\left( j\right) } \) is a sequence of points such that \( {y}_{j} \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon }^{\left( j\right) } \) and \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{y}_{j},0}\right) {\operatorname{diam}}_{{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }{\left( {\Omega }_{{y}_{j}}\right) }^{2} \rightarrow  \infty \) , where \( {\Omega }_{{y}_{j}} \) denotes the region in \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) that is bounded by the CMC sphere passing through \( {y}_{j} \) . We dilate the flow \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{y}_{j},0}\right) \) by the factor \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{y}_{j},0}\right) \) . Using the long-range curvature estimate established in Step 2, we conclude that, after passing to a subsequence if necessary, the rescaled manifolds converge to a complete, smooth, nonflat ancient solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) that is weakly PIC2 and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC. Since \( {y}_{j} \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon }^{\left( j\right) } \) for each \( j \) , the limit \( {y}_{\infty } \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{y}_{j} \) lies at the center of an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{2} \) -neck in \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) . Since \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{y}_{j},0}\right) {\operatorname{diam}}_{{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }{\left( {\Omega }_{{y}_{j}}\right) }^{2} \rightarrow  \infty \) , the manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) contains a minimizing geodesic line. By the Cheeger-Gromoll splitting theorem (cf. [9]), the manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a product \( X \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Since \( {y}_{\infty } \) lies at the center of an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{2} \) -neck, the cross-section \( X \) is compact and is nearly isometric to \( {S}^{n - 1} \) . In particular, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature. By Corollary 6.7, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to family of shrinking cylinders \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Therefore, if \( j \) is sufficiently large, then \( {y}_{j} \) lies at the center of an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{8} \) -neck. This contradicts the fact that \( {y}_{j} \) lies on the boundary of \( {M}_{\varepsilon }^{\left( j\right) } \) .

Step 4: By Step 3, we have \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }{\left( x, y\right) }^{2} \leq  C \) for all \( y \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon } \) and all \( x \in  {\Omega }_{y} \) , where \( C \) is a positive constant that depends only on \( n,\theta \) , and \( \varepsilon \) , but not on \( \kappa \) . Combining this estimate with the long-range curvature estimate in Step 2, we conclude that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) \) and \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right) {d}_{g\left( t\right) }{\left( x, y\right) }^{2} \leq  C \) for all \( y \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon } \) , all \( x \in  {\Omega }_{y} \) , and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\beta \operatorname{scal}{\left( y,0\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . Here, \( C \) is a positive constant that depends only on \( n,\theta \) , and \( \varepsilon \) , but not on \( \kappa \) . Using the Harnack inequality (cf. Corollary 6.3), we obtain

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{C}\operatorname{scal}\left( {y, - \beta \operatorname{scal}{\left( y,0\right) }^{-1}}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2C}\operatorname{scal}\left( {y,0}\right)
\]

for all \( y \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon } \) and all \( x \in  {\Omega }_{y} \) , where \( C \) depends only on \( n,\theta \) , and \( \varepsilon \) , but not on \( \kappa \) .

Step 5: Finally, we claim that we can find a point \( y \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon } \) such that \( {x}_{0} \in  {\Omega }_{y} \) . To prove this, let \( \gamma  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) be a minimizing unit-speed geodesic with \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = {x}_{0} \) . We define \( \bar{s} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \sup \left\{  {s \in  \lbrack 0,\infty ) : \gamma \left( s\right)  \in  {M}_{\varepsilon }}\right\} \) . Note that \( \bar{s} > 0 \) since \( {x}_{0} \) lies in the interior of \( {M}_{\varepsilon } \) , and \( \bar{s} < \infty \) since the closure of \( {M}_{\varepsilon } \) is compact. Let \( \bar{y} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \gamma \left( \bar{s}\right) \) . Clearly, \( \bar{y} \in  \partial {M}_{\varepsilon } \) . In particular, \( \bar{y} \) lies at the center of an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{2} \) -neck. Since \( {x}_{0} \) does not lie at the center of an \( \varepsilon \) -neck, we must have \( {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},\bar{y}}\right)  > {100n}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \bar{y},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) . We claim that \( {x}_{0} \in  {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \) . Suppose this is false. Then the curve \( \gamma \) must enter and exit the cap \( {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \) . More precisely, we have \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  \notin  {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \cup  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {\bar{y},{100n}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \bar{y},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,\gamma \left( \bar{s}\right)  \in  {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \) , and \( \gamma \left( s\right)  \notin  {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \cup  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {\bar{y},{100n}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \bar{y},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) when \( s \) is sufficiently large. This is impossible since \( \gamma \) minimizes length. Consequently, \( {x}_{0} \in  {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \) . The inequality \( {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},\bar{y}}\right)  > {100n}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \bar{y},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) implies \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{C}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( \bar{y},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \) . Moreover, the diameter estimate in Step 3 gives \( {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \subset  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{0}, C\operatorname{scal}{\left( \bar{y},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) . Here, \( C \) is a positive constant that depends only on \( n,\theta \) , and \( \varepsilon \) , but not on \( \kappa \) . Finally, by Step 4, we can estimate \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},0}\right) \) from above and below in terms of \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {\bar{y},0}\right) \) . Putting these facts together, we conclude that \( {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{C}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \) and \( {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \subset  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{0}, C\operatorname{scal}{\left( \bar{y},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) , where \( C \) is a positive constant that depends only on \( n,\theta \) , and \( \varepsilon \) , but not on \( \kappa \) . To summarize, the set \( B \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\Omega }_{\bar{y}} \) has all the required properties.

nodes.proof:
If \( M \) is noncompact, the assertion follows from Theorem 6.18. Hence, we may assume that \( M \) is compact. Moreover, we may assume that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is not a metric quotient of the round sphere \( {S}^{n} \) . The noncollapsing assumption implies that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) cannot be a compact quotient of a standard cylinder. By Corollary 6.7, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2.

Consider a sequence of times \( {t}_{j} \rightarrow   - \infty \) and a sequence of points \( {q}_{j} \in  M \) such that \( \ell \left( {{q}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  \leq  n \) , where \( \ell \) denotes the reduced distance. By Perelman’s work, \( \ell \left( {x,{t}_{j}}\right)  + \left( {-{t}_{j}}\right) R\left( {x,{t}_{j}}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) \) for all \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{q}_{j},{\left( -{t}_{j}\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) . If we dilate the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{q}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) by the factor \( {\left( -{t}_{j}\right) }^{-1} \) , then the rescaled flows converge to a complete ancient solution \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) (cf. [33, §11.2]). Perelman proved that the limit \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a nonflat shrinking gradient Ricci soliton. Clearly, \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed, weakly PIC2, and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC. Moreover, since the Harnack inequality holds on \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) , it holds on the limit \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) . By Proposition 6.11, \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature. We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: We first consider the case that \( \bar{M} \) is compact. A shrinking soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) cannot be isometric to a compact quotient of a standard cylinder. By

Corollary 6.7, \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2. Since \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a shrinking soliton, results in [8] imply that \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) must be isometric to a metric quotient of the round sphere \( {S}^{n} \) . Consequently, the original ancient solution \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a metric quotient of \( {S}^{n} \) , contrary to our assumption.

Case 2: Suppose next that \( \bar{M} \) is noncompact. In view of Theorem 6.18, there are two possibilities: either \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -noncollapsed for some universal constant \( {\kappa }_{0} = {\kappa }_{0}\left( {n,\theta }\right) \) , or else \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a noncompact quotient of the standard cylinder. The second case can be divided into two subcases:

- If the dimension \( n \) is odd and \( \bar{M} \) is a noncompact quotient \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R}}\right) /\Gamma \) , then there are only finitely many possibilities for the group \( \Gamma \) , and the resulting quotients are all noncollapsed with a universal constant.

- If the dimension \( n \) is even and \( \bar{M} \) is a noncompact quotient \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R}}\right) /\Gamma \) , then the center slice \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1}\times \{ 0\} }\right) /\Gamma \) is incompressible in \( M \) by Theorem A. 1 in [6]. Moreover, since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2, the fundamental group of \( M \) has order at most 2 by Synge’s theorem. Hence, there are only finitely many possibilities for the group \( \Gamma \) , and the resulting quotients \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R}}\right) /\Gamma \) are noncollapsed with a universal constant.

To summarize, we have shown that the asymptotic shrinking soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{g}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is noncollapsed with a universal constant that depends only on \( n \) and \( \theta \) . This implies \( \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{\left( -{t}_{j}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{q}_{j},{\left( -{t}_{j}\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{C\left( {n,\theta }\right) } \) . Hence, if \( V\left( t\right)  = \; {\int }_{M}{\left( -t\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {\cdot , t}\right) }d{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) } \) denotes the reduced volume, then \( \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}V\left( {t}_{j}\right)  \geq \; \frac{1}{C\left( {n,\theta }\right) } \) . Perelman’s monotonicity formula gives \( V\left( t\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{C\left( {n,\theta }\right) } \) . Thus, \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is noncollapsed with a universal constant that depends only on \( n \) and \( \theta \) .

nodes.content:
Theorem 6.21 (cf. G. Perelman [35,§1.5]). Given \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) and \( \theta  > 0 \) , there exist positive constants \( {C}_{1} = {C}_{1}\left( {n,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) and \( {C}_{2} = {C}_{2}\left( {n,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) such that the following holds: Assume that \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC. Then, for each point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) in space-time, there exists a neighborhood \( B \) of \( {x}_{0} \) such that \( {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{C}_{1}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  B \subset \; {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{C}_{1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) and \( {C}_{2}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {C}_{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) for all \( x \in  B \) . Finally, \( B \) satisfies one of the following conditions:

- \( B \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -neck with center at \( {x}_{0} \) .

- \( B \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -cap.

- \( B \) is a closed manifold diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{n}/\Gamma \) .

- \( B \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -quotient neck of the form \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1} \times  \left\lbrack  {-L, L}\right\rbrack  }\right) /\Gamma \) .

nodes.proof:
If \( M \) is noncompact, the assertion follows from Theorem 6.18. Hence, it suffices to consider the case when \( M \) is compact. As usual, it is enough to consider the case \( {t}_{0} = 0 \) . Suppose that the assertion is false. Then we can find a sequence of compact ancient \( {\kappa }_{j} \) -solutions \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC and a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  {M}^{\left( j\right) } \) with the following property: There does not exist a neighborhood \( B \) of \( {x}_{j} \) with the property that \( {B}_{{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{j}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{j},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, j\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{j},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) , \( {j}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  j\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) \) for all \( x \in  B \) , and such that \( B \) is either an \( \varepsilon \) -neck with center at \( {x}_{j} \) ; or an \( \varepsilon \) -cap; or a closed manifold diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{n}/\Gamma \) ; or an \( \varepsilon \) -quotient neck. By scaling, we may assume \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  = 1 \) for each \( j \) .

The noncollapsing assumption implies that \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) cannot be isometric to a compact quotient of the standard cylinder. By Corollary 6.7, \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2. Clearly, \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) cannot be isometric to a quotient of a round sphere. By Theorem 6.19, \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -noncollapsed for some uniform constant \( {\kappa }_{0} \) that is independent of \( j \) .

We now apply the compactness theorem for ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solutions (cf. Corollary 6.15) to the sequence \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) ,{x}_{j}}\right) \) . Consequently, after passing to a subsequence if necessary, the sequence \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) ,{x}_{j}}\right) \) will converge in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to an ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solution satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC. Let us denote this limiting ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solution by \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) , and let \( {x}_{\infty } \) denote the limit of the sequence \( {x}_{j} \) . There are two possibilities:

Case 1: We first consider the case that \( {M}^{\infty } \) is compact. In this case, the diameter of \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) has a uniform upper bound independent of \( j \) . Therefore, if \( j \) is sufficiently large, then \( {B}^{\left( j\right) } \mathrel{\text{ := }} {M}^{\left( j\right) } \) is a neighborhood of the point \( {x}_{j} \) satisfying \( {B}_{{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{j}^{-1}}\right)  \subset  {B}^{\left( j\right) } \subset  {B}_{{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, j}\right) \) and \( {j}^{-1} \leq \; \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  j \) for all \( x \in  {B}^{\left( j\right) } \) . Since \( \left( {{M}^{\left( j\right) },{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is strictly PIC2, results in [8] imply that \( {B}^{\left( j\right) } = {M}^{\left( j\right) } \) is diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{n}/\Gamma \) . This contradicts our choice of \( {x}_{j} \) .

Case 2: We now consider the case that \( {M}^{\infty } \) is noncompact. If \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a noncompact quotient of the standard cylinder, then, for \( j \) large enough, the point \( {x}_{j} \) lies at the center of an \( \varepsilon \) -neck or it lies on an \( \varepsilon \) -quotient neck. This contradicts our choice of \( {x}_{j} \) . Consequently, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is not isometric to a quotient of the standard cylinder. At this point, we apply Theorem 6.18 to \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) (and with \( \varepsilon \) replaced by \( \frac{\varepsilon }{2} \) ). Therefore, we can find a neighborhood \( {B}^{\infty } \subset  {M}^{\infty } \) of the point \( {x}_{\infty } \) satisfying \( {B}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{\infty },{C}_{1}^{-1}}\right)  \subset \; {B}^{\infty } \subset  {B}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{\infty },{C}_{1}}\right) \) and \( {C}_{2}^{-1} \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  {C}_{2} \) for all \( x \in  {B}^{\infty } \) . Furthermore, \( {B}^{\infty } \) is either an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{2} \) -neck with center at \( {x}_{\infty } \) or an \( \frac{\varepsilon }{2} \) -cap. Hence, if we choose \( j \) sufficiently large, then we can find a neighborhood \( {B}^{\left( j\right) } \subset  {M}^{\left( j\right) } \) of the point \( {x}_{j} \) satisfying \( {B}_{{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{\left( 2{C}_{1}\right) }^{-1}}\right)  \subset  {B}^{\left( j\right) } \subset  {B}_{{g}^{\left( j\right) }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},2{C}_{1}}\right) \) and \( {\left( 2{C}_{2}\right) }^{-1} \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  2{C}_{2} \) for all \( x \in  {B}^{\left( j\right) } \) . Furthermore, \( {B}^{\left( j\right) } \) is either an \( \varepsilon \) -neck with center at \( {x}_{j} \) or an \( \varepsilon \) -cap. This contradicts our choice of \( {x}_{j} \) .
