nodes.proof:
The proof of Theorem 7.2 is an adaptation of Perelman's work [33]. (See also [12], where the four-dimensional case is treated.) By Corollary 1.3, the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has \( \left( {f,\theta }\right) \) -pinched curvature for some function \( f \) satisfying \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{f\left( s\right) }{s} \; = 0 \) and some constant \( \theta  > 0 \) . Let us fix a small number \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , and let \( {C}_{1} = {C}_{1}\left( {n,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) and \( {C}_{2} = {C}_{2}\left( {n,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) denote the constants in Corollary 6.22. It suffices to prove the assertion when \( {A}_{0} \geq  8{C}_{1} \) and \( \widetilde{\varepsilon } \) is much smaller than \( \varepsilon \) . To do that, we argue by contradiction. If the assertion is false, then we can find a sequence of points \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) in space-time with the following properties:

(i) \( {Q}_{j} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  \geq  {j}^{2} \) .

(ii) After dilating by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) , the parabolic neighborhood

\[
{B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{A}_{0}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{j} - {A}_{0}{Q}_{j}^{-1},{t}_{j}}\right\rbrack
\]

is not \( \widetilde{\varepsilon } \) -close to the corresponding subset of any ancient \( \kappa \) -solution satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC.

By a point-picking argument, we can arrange that \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) satisfies the following condition:

(iii) If \( \left( {\widetilde{x},\widetilde{t}}\right) \) is a point in space-time such that \( \widetilde{t} \leq  {t}_{j} \) and \( \widetilde{Q} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \operatorname{scal}\left( {\widetilde{x},\widetilde{t}}\right)  \geq  4{Q}_{j} \) , then the parabolic neighborhood \( {B}_{g\left( \widetilde{t}\right) }\left( {\widetilde{x},{A}_{0}{\widetilde{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - {A}_{0}{\widetilde{Q}}^{-1},\widetilde{t}}\right\rbrack \) is, after dilating by the factor \( \widetilde{Q},\widetilde{\varepsilon } \) -close to the corresponding subset of an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC.

Our strategy is to rescale the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) . We will show that the rescaled flows converge to an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC. To that end, we proceed in several steps:

Step 1: We first establish a pointwise curvature derivative estimate. By Corollary 6.20, we can find a large constant \( \eta \) , depending only on \( n \) and \( \theta \) , such that \( \left| {D\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq  \eta {\operatorname{scal}}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq  \eta {\operatorname{scal}}^{2} \) on every ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. Using property (iii) above, we conclude that \( \left| {D\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq  {2\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq  {2\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{2} \) for each point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) in space-time satisfying \( t \leq  {t}_{j} \) and \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  4{Q}_{j} \) .

Step 2: We next prove bounds for the higher order covariant derivatives of the curvature tensor. Suppose that \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is a point in space-time satisfying \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  + {Q}_{j} \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) . The pointwise curvature derivative estimate in Step 1 implies that \( \operatorname{scal} \leq  8{r}_{0}^{-2} \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{100\eta }, - \frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{100\eta }}\right) \) . Using Shi’s interior derivative estimates, we conclude \( \left| {{D}^{m}R}\right|  \leq  C\left( {n, m,\eta }\right) {r}_{0}^{-m - 2} \) at the point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) .

Step 3: We next prove a long-range curvature estimate. Given any \( \rho  > 0 \) , we define

\[
\mathbb{M}\left( \rho \right)  = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},\rho {Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }}{Q}_{j}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,{t}_{j}}\right) .
\]

Here, we allow the possibility that \( \mathbb{M}\left( \rho \right)  = \infty \) . The pointwise curvature derivative estimate in Step 1 implies that \( \mathbb{M}\left( \rho \right)  \leq  8 \) for \( 0 < \rho  < \frac{1}{100\eta } \) .

We claim that \( \mathbb{M}\left( \rho \right)  < \infty \) for all \( \rho  > 0 \) . Suppose this is false. Let

\[
{\rho }^{ * } = \sup \{ \rho  \geq  0 : \mathbb{M}\left( \rho \right)  < \infty \}  < \infty .
\]

Clearly, \( {\rho }^{ * } \geq  \frac{1}{100\eta } \) . By definition of \( {\rho }^{ * } \) , we have an upper bound for the curvature in the geodesic ball \( {B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},\rho {Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) for each \( \rho  < {\rho }^{ * } \) . By Step 2, we obtain bounds for the covariant derivatives of the curvature tensor in the geodesic ball \( {B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},\rho {Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) for each \( \rho  < {\rho }^{ * } \) . Moreover, Perelman’s noncollapsing estimate gives a lower bound for the volume. We rescale around \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) and pass to the limit as \( j \rightarrow  \infty \) . In the limit, we obtain an incomplete manifold \( \left( {{B}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) that is weakly PIC2 (cf. [31, Th. 5.6]).

By definition of \( {\rho }^{ * } \) , we can find a sequence of points \( {y}_{j} \) such that

\[
{\rho }_{j} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {Q}_{j}^{\frac{1}{2}}{d}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{x}_{j},{y}_{j}}\right)  \rightarrow  {\rho }^{ * }\;\text{ and }\;{Q}_{j}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{y}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty .
\]

For each \( j \) , we can find a unit speed geodesic \( {\gamma }_{j} : \left\lbrack  {0,{\rho }_{j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\right) \) such that \( {\gamma }_{j}\left( 0\right)  = {x}_{j} \) and \( {\gamma }_{j}\left( {{\rho }_{j}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  = {y}_{j} \) . Let \( {\gamma }_{\infty } : \left\lbrack  {0,{\rho }^{ * }}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {{B}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) denote the limit of \( {\gamma }_{j} \) . Using the pointwise curvature derivative estimate in Step 1, we obtain

\[
{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }}\left( {{\gamma }_{\infty }\left( s\right) }\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}{Q}_{j}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {s{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right)  \geq  {\left( \eta \left( {\rho }^{ * } - s\right) \right) }^{-2} \geq  {100}
\]

if \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {{\rho }^{ * } - \frac{1}{100\eta },{\rho }^{ * }}\right) \) .

Let us consider a real number \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {{\rho }^{ * } - \frac{1}{100\eta },{\rho }^{ * }}\right) \) such that \( 8{C}_{1}\eta \left( {{\rho }^{ * } - \bar{s}}\right)  \leq  \bar{s} \) . We claim that \( {\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) lies at the center of a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck if \( j \) is sufficiently large (depending on \( \bar{s} \) ). Indeed, if \( j \) is sufficiently large, it follows from property (iii) and Corollary 6.22 that the point \( \left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) has a Canonical Neighborhood that is either a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck; or a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap; or a closed manifold diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{n}/\Gamma \) ; or a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -quotient neck. Furthermore, the Canonical Neighborhood is contained in a geodesic ball around \( {\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) of radius \( 2{C}_{1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {\gamma }_{j}\left( \bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) ,{t}_{j}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , and the scalar curvature is at most \( 2{C}_{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) at each point in the Canonical Neighborhood. Since \( \mathbb{M}\left( \bar{s}\right)  < \infty \) , we obtain

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {\gamma }_{j}\left( \bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) ,{t}_{j}\right) }^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{y}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  = \infty ;
\]

consequently, \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{y}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  \geq  4{C}_{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) if \( j \) is sufficiently large. Hence, if \( j \) is sufficiently large, then the Canonical Neighborhood does not contain the point \( {y}_{j} \) . We next observe that

\[
8{C}_{1}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }}{\left( {\gamma }_{\infty }\left( \bar{s}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \leq  8{C}_{1}\eta \left( {{\rho }^{ * } - \bar{s}}\right)  \leq  \bar{s}.
\]

This implies \( 4{C}_{1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {\gamma }_{j}\left( \bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) ,{t}_{j}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \leq  \bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) if \( j \) is sufficiently large. Hence, if \( j \) is sufficiently large, then the Canonical Neighborhood does not contain the point \( {x}_{j} \) . In particular, if \( j \) is sufficiently large, then the Canonical Neighborhood of \( \left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) cannot be a closed manifold diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{n}/\Gamma \) . Moreover, if the Canonical Neighborhood of \( \left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) is a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap, then the geodesic \( {\gamma }_{j} \) must enter and exit this \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap, but this is impossible since \( {\gamma }_{j} \) minimizes length. Finally, if the Canonical Neighborhood of \( \left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) is a quotient neck, then Theorem A. 1 in [6] implies that \( M \) contains a nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space form, contrary to our assumption. To summarize, if \( j \) is sufficiently large (depending on \( \bar{s} \) ), then the point \( \left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) has a Canonical Neighborhood that is a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck. In particular, if \( j \) is sufficiently large (depending on \( \bar{s} \) ), then we have \( \left| {D\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq  C\left( n\right) \varepsilon {\operatorname{scal}}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) at the point \( \left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) .

Passing to the limit as \( j \rightarrow  \infty \) , we conclude that \( \left| {D{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }}}\right|  \leq  C\left( n\right) \varepsilon {\operatorname{scal}}_{{q}^{\infty }}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) at the point \( {\gamma }_{\infty }\left( \bar{s}\right) \) . Integrating this estimate along \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) gives \( {\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }}\left( {{\gamma }_{\infty }\left( \bar{s}\right) }\right)  \geq \; {\left( C\left( n\right) \varepsilon \left( {\rho }^{ * } - \bar{s}\right) \right) }^{-2} \) . Moreover, since \( \left( {{\gamma }_{j}\left( {\bar{s}{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) ,{t}_{j}}\right) \) lies at the center of a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck for \( j \) sufficiently large, the point \( {\gamma }_{\infty }\left( \bar{s}\right) \) must lie on a \( C\left( n\right) \varepsilon \) -neck in \( \left( {{B}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) .

As in [33, §12.1], there is a sequence of rescalings that converges to a piece of a nonflat metric cone in the limit. Using the pointwise curvature derivative estimate established in Step 1, we can extend the metric backwards in time. This gives a locally defined solution to the Ricci flow that is weakly PIC2 and that, at the final time, is a piece of nonflat metric cone. This contradicts Proposition 6.5.

Step 4: We now rescale the manifold \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\right) \) around the point \( {x}_{j} \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) . By Step 3, we have uniform bounds for the curvature at bounded distance. Using the curvature derivative estimate in Step 1 together with Shi's interior derivative estimates, we conclude that the covariant derivatives of the curvature tensor are bounded at bounded distance. Combining this with Perelman's noncollapsing estimate, we conclude that (after passing to a subsequence) the rescaled manifolds converge in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to a complete smooth limit manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) . Since \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\right) \) has \( \left( {f,\theta }\right) \) -pinched curvature, the curvature tensor of \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) is weakly PIC2 and satisfies \( R - \; \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC. Using property (iii) and Corollary 6.22, we conclude that every point in \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) with scalar curvature greater than 4 has a Canonical Neighborhood that is either a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck; or a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap; or a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -quotient neck. Note that the last possibility cannot occur; indeed, if \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) contains a quotient neck, then \( \left( {M, g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\right) \) contains a quotient neck for \( j \) sufficiently large, and Theorem A.1 in [6] then implies that \( M \) contains a nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space form, contrary to our assumption.

We claim that the limit manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) has bounded curvature. Indeed, if there is a sequence of points in \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) with curvature going to infinity, then \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) contains a sequence of necks with radii converging to 0, contradicting Proposition 6.9. Thus, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) has bounded curvature.

Step 5: We now extend the limit \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) backwards in time. By Step 4, the scalar curvature of \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) is bounded from above by a constant \( \Lambda  > 4 \) . Using the pointwise curvature derivative estimate in Step 1, we conclude that

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{j}\right) }\left( {{x}_{j}, A{Q}_{j}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{j} - \frac{1}{100\eta \Lambda }{Q}_{j}^{-1},{t}_{j}}\right\rbrack  }}{Q}_{j}^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {2\Lambda }
\]

for each \( A > 1 \) . Hence, if we put \( {\tau }_{1} \mathrel{\text{ := }}  - \frac{1}{200\eta \Lambda } \) , then we can extend \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) \) backwards in time to a complete solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) of the Ricci flow that is defined for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},0}\right\rbrack \) and satisfies \( {\Lambda }_{1} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},0}\right\rbrack  }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{M}^{\infty }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) } \leq  {2\Lambda } \) . In the next step, we put \( {\tau }_{2} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\tau }_{1} - \frac{1}{{200n}{\Lambda }_{1}} \) . Using the pointwise curvature derivative estimate in Step 1, we can extend the solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }}\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},0}\right\rbrack \) , backwards in time to a solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{2},0}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, \( {\Lambda }_{2} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \; \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{2},0}\right\rbrack  }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{M}^{\infty }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) } \leq  2{\Lambda }_{1} \) . Continuing this process, we can extend the solution backwards in time to the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{m},0}\right\rbrack \) , where \( {\tau }_{m + 1} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\tau }_{m} - \frac{1}{{200\eta }{\Lambda }_{m}} \) and \( {\Lambda }_{m + 1} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{m + 1},0}\right\rbrack  }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{M}^{\infty }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) } \leq  2{\Lambda }_{m} \) .

Let \( {\tau }^{ * } = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{m \rightarrow  \infty }}{\tau }_{m} \leq   - \frac{1}{200\eta \Lambda } \) . Using a standard diagonal sequence argument, we obtain a complete, smooth limit flow \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) that is defined on the interval \( \left( {{\tau }^{ * },0}\right\rbrack \) and that has bounded curvature for each \( t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },0}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has \( \left( {f,\theta }\right) \) -pinched curvature, the curvature tensor of the limit flow \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is weakly PIC2 and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC.

Step 6: We claim that \( {\tau }^{ * } =  - \infty \) . To prove this, we argue by contradiction. Suppose \( {\tau }^{ * } >  - \infty \) . Clearly, \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{m \rightarrow  \infty }}\left( {{\tau }_{m} - {\tau }_{m + 1}}\right)  = 0 \) , hence \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{m \rightarrow  \infty }}{\Lambda }_{m} = \infty \) .

By the Harnack inequality (cf. Theorem 6.1 above), the function \( t \mapsto \; \left( {t - {\tau }^{ * }}\right) {\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\left( x\right) \) is monotone increasing at each point \( x \in  {M}^{\infty } \) . Since \( {\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\left( x\right)  \leq  \Lambda \) for all \( x \in  {M}^{\infty } \) , we obtain

\[
{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\left( x\right)  \leq  \frac{-{\tau }^{ * }}{t - {\tau }^{ * }}\Lambda
\]

for all \( x \in  {M}^{\infty } \) and all \( t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },0}\right\rbrack \) . Using Lemma 8.3(b) in [33], we conclude that

\[
0 \leq   - \frac{d}{dt}{d}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\left( {x, y}\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) \sqrt{\frac{-{\tau }^{ * }}{t - {\tau }^{ * }}\Lambda }
\]

for all \( x, y \in  {M}^{\infty } \) and all \( t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },0}\right\rbrack \) . Integrating over \( t \) gives

\[
{d}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\left( {x, y}\right)  \leq  {d}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\left( {x, y}\right)  \leq  {d}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\left( {x, y}\right)  + C\left( n\right) \left( {-{\tau }^{ * }}\right) \sqrt{\Lambda }
\]

for all \( x, y \in  {M}^{\infty } \) and all \( t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },0}\right\rbrack \) .

By the maximum principle,

\[
\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{M}^{\infty }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) } \leq  \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{M}^{\infty }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) } \leq  1
\]

for all \( t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },0}\right\rbrack \) . Hence, we can find a point \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {M}^{\infty } \) such that \( {\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\left( {y}_{\infty }\right) \; \leq  4 \) for \( t = {\tau }^{ * } + \frac{1}{1000\eta \Lambda } \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },0}\right\rbrack \) . Using the pointwise curvature derivative estimate in Step 1, we obtain \( {\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\left( {y}_{\infty }\right)  \leq  8 \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },{\tau }^{ * } + \frac{1}{1000\eta \Lambda }}\right\rbrack \) . In particular, \( {\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) }\left( {y}_{\infty }\right)  \leq  8 \) if \( m \) is sufficiently large. Arguing as in Step 3, we can show that

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{m \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{B}_{{g}^{\infty }}\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) \left( {{y}_{\infty }, A}\right) }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) } < \infty
\]

for every \( A > 1 \) .

Consequently, a subsequence of the manifolds \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) ,{y}_{\infty }}\right) \) converges in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to a complete, smooth limit. If this limit manifold has unbounded curvature, then (by property (iii) above) it contains a sequence of necks with radii converging to 0 , contradicting Proposition 6.9. Therefore, a subsequence of the manifolds \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) ,{y}_{\infty }}\right) \) converges in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to a complete, smooth limit with bounded curvature. Consequently, we can find a constant \( {\Lambda }^{ * } > \Lambda \) (independent of \( A \) ) such that

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{m \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{B}_{{g}^{\infty }}\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) }{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) } \leq  {\Lambda }^{ * }
\]

for every \( A > 1 \) . Using the distance estimate, we obtain \( {B}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( 0\right) }\left( {{y}_{\infty }, A}\right)  \subset \; {B}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) }\left( {{y}_{\infty }, A + C\left( n\right) \left( {-{\tau }^{ * }}\right) \sqrt{\Lambda }}\right) \) . Putting these facts together, we conclude that

\[
\mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{m \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{B}_{{g}^{\infty }}\left( 0\right) }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) }{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) } \leq  {\Lambda }^{ * }
\]

for every \( A > 1 \) . Hence, for each \( A > 1 \) , we can find a large integer \( m \) (depending on \( A \) ) such that \( {\tau }_{m} \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },{\tau }^{ * } + \frac{1}{{1000\eta }{\Lambda }^{ * }}}\right\rbrack \) and

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{B}_{g}\infty \left( 0\right) }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {{\tau }_{m}, A}\right) }{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( {\tau }_{m}\right) } \leq  2{\Lambda }^{ * }.
\]

Using the pointwise derivative estimate in Step 1, we obtain

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },{\tau }^{ * } + \frac{1}{{1000\eta }{\Lambda }^{ * }}}\right\rbrack  }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{B}_{{g}^{\infty }}\left( 0\right) }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) } \leq  4{\Lambda }^{ * }
\]

for every \( A > 1 \) . Since \( {\Lambda }^{ * } \) is independent of \( A \) , we conclude that

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },{\tau }^{ * } + \frac{1}{{1000\eta }{\Lambda }^{ * }}}\right\rbrack  }}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{M}^{\infty }}{\operatorname{scal}}_{{g}^{\infty }}\left( t\right)  \leq  4{\Lambda }^{ * }.
\]

Therefore, the flow \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \left( {{\tau }^{ * },0}\right\rbrack \) , has bounded curvature. This contradicts the fact that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{m \rightarrow  \infty }}{\Lambda }_{m} = \infty \) . Thus, \( {\tau }^{ * } =  - \infty \) .

To summarize, if we dilate the flow \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) around the point \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) by the factor \( {Q}_{j} \) , then (after passing to a subsequence), the rescaled flows converge in the Cheeger-Gromov sense to an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) , \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC. Here, \( \kappa \) depends only on the initial data. This contradicts statement (ii). This completes the proof of Theorem 7.2.

nodes.content:
COROLLARY 7.3 (cf. G. Perelman [33, Th. 12.1]). Let \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) be a compact manifold with positive isotropic curvature of dimension \( n \geq  {12} \) , which does not contain any nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space forms. Let \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , denote the solution to the Ricci flow with initial metric \( {g}_{0} \) . Given any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exists a positive number \( \widehat{r} \) with the following property: If \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) is a point in space-time with \( Q \mathrel{\text{ := }} \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {\widehat{r}}^{-2} \) , then we can find a neighborhood \( B \) of \( {x}_{0} \) such that

\[
{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{\left( 2{C}_{1}\right) }^{-1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},2{C}_{1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)
\]

and

\[
{\left( 2{C}_{2}\right) }^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  2{C}_{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  B \) . Furthermore, \( B \) satisfies one of the following conditions:

- \( B \) is a strong \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck (in the sense of [35]) with center at \( {x}_{0} \) .

- \( B \) is a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap in the sense of Definition 6.16.

- \( B \) is a closed manifold diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{n}/\Gamma \) .

Here, \( {C}_{1} = {C}_{1}\left( {n,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) and \( {C}_{2} = {C}_{2}\left( {n,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) are the constants appearing in Corollary 6.22. Finally, we have \( \left| {D\mathrm{{scal}}}\right|  \leq  {2\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\mathrm{{scal}}}\right|  \leq  {2\eta }{\mathrm{{scal}}}^{2} \) at the point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , where \( \eta \) is a constant that depends only on \( n \) and \( \theta \) .

nodes.content:
Throughout this section, we fix a compact initial manifold \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) of dimension \( n \geq  {12} \) that has positive isotropic curvature and does not contain any nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space forms. Let \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) be the solution of the Ricci flow with initial metric \( {g}_{0} \) , and let \( \lbrack 0, T) \) denote the maximal time interval on which the solution is defined. Note that \( T \leq  \frac{n}{2\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right) } \) . By Theorem 1.2, we can find a continuous family of closed, convex, \( O\left( n\right) \) -invariant sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) such that the family \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is invariant under the Hamilton ODE \( \frac{d}{dt}R = Q\left( R\right) \) ; the curvature tensor of \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) lies in the set \( {\mathcal{F}}_{0} \) ; and

\[
{\mathcal{F}}_{t} \subset  \{ R : R - \theta \text{ scalid }\varnothing \text{ id } \in  \mathrm{{PIC}}\}
\]

\[
\cap  \{ R : R + f\left( \text{ scal }\right) \text{ id } \oslash  \text{ id } \in  \text{ PIC2 }\}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Here, \( f \) is a concave and increasing function satisfying \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{f\left( s\right) }{s} = 0 \) , and \( \theta \) and \( N \) are positive numbers. Note that \( f,\theta \) , and \( N \) depend only on the initial data. By Hamilton's PDE-ODE principle (cf. [14, Th. 3], or [13, Th. 10.16]), the curvature tensor of \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) lies in the set \( {\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) for each \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

Let \( \rho \) be a small positive number with the property that every point with scal \( \geq  \frac{1}{4}{\rho }^{-2} \) satisfies the conclusion of the Canonical Neighborhood Theorem. In particular, we have \( \left| {D\mathrm{{scal}}}\right|  \leq  {2\eta }{\mathrm{{scal}}}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\mathrm{{scal}}}\right|  \leq  {2\eta }{\mathrm{{scal}}}^{2} \) whenever \( \mathrm{{scal}} \geq  \frac{1}{4}{\rho }^{-2} \) . We define

\[
\Omega  \mathrel{\text{ := }} \{ x \in  M : \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  < \infty \} .
\]

The pointwise curvature derivative estimate implies that \( \Omega \) is an open subset of \( M \) . Using the pointwise curvature derivative estimate together with Shi’s interior estimates, we conclude the metrics \( g\left( t\right) \) converge to a smooth metric \( g\left( T\right) \) on \( \Omega \) . Following [33], we consider the set

\[
{\Omega }_{\rho } \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left\{  {x \in  M : \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {\rho }^{-2}}\right\}   = \left\{  {x \in  \Omega  : \operatorname{scal}\left( {x, T}\right)  \leq  {\rho }^{-2}}\right\}  .
\]

nodes.content: Proposition 8.1. The pre-surgery manifold \( M \) is diffeomorphic to a connected sum of the post-surgery manifold with a finite collection of standard spaces, each of which is a quotient of \( {S}^{n} \) or \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) by standard isometries.
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 8.1. The pre-surgery manifold \( M \) is diffeomorphic to a connected sum of the post-surgery manifold with a finite collection of standard spaces, each of which is a quotient of \( {S}^{n} \) or \( {S}^{n - 1} \times \mathbb{R} \) by standard isometries.

nodes.proof:
Suppose first that \( {\Omega }_{\rho } = \varnothing \) . In this case, \( M \) is diffeomorphic to either a quotient of \( {S}^{n} \) by standard isometries; or a tube with caps attached on both sides; or an \( {S}^{n - 1} \) -bundle over \( {S}^{1} \) with a fiberwise round metric. In the second case, Definition 6.16 ensures that \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{n} \) . To handle the third case, we note that that there are two \( {S}^{n - 1} \) -bundles over \( {S}^{1} \) with a fiberwise round metric. One of them is orientable, the other one is not. Both are diffeomorphic to quotients of \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) by standard isometries. To summarize, \( M \) is diffeomorphic to a quotient of \( {S}^{n} \) or a quotient of \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) by standard isometries.

Suppose next that \( {\Omega }_{\rho } \neq  \varnothing \) . In this case, we can recover the pre-surgery manifold \( M \) from the post-surgery manifold as follows. We first reinstate the components that were discarded after surgery. More precisely, we form a disjoint union of the post-surgery manifold and a finite collection of standard spaces, each of which is a quotient of \( {S}^{n} \) or \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) by standard isometries. In the next step, we reverse the surgery by gluing in finitely many handles of the form \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  I \) . Note that, as we glue in these handles, the attaching maps are nearly isometric. Thus, the pre-surgery manifold is diffeomorphic to a connected sum of the post-surgery manifold with finitely many quotients of \( {S}^{n} \) and \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . This completes the proof of Proposition 8.1.

nodes.content: PROPOSITION 8.2. Suppose that the curvature tensor of a \( \delta \) -neck lies in the set \( {\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) prior to surgery. If \( \delta \) is sufficiently small and the curvature of the neck is sufficiently large, then the curvature tensor of the surgically modified manifold lies in the set \( {\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) . Moreover, the scalar curvature is pointwise increasing under surgery.
nodes.content_excerpt: PROPOSITION 8.2. Suppose that the curvature tensor of a \( \delta \) -neck lies in the set \( {\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) prior to surgery. If \( \delta \) is sufficiently small and the curvature of the neck is sufficiently large, then the curvature tensor of the surgically modified manifold lies in the set \( {\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) . Moreover, the scalar curvature is pointwise increasing under surgery.

nodes.proof:
Suppose that the scalar curvature of the neck is close to \( {h}^{-2} \) , where \( h \) is small. Let us rescale by the factor \( {h}^{-1} \) so that the scalar curvature of the neck is close to 1 after rescaling. Let us, therefore, assume that \( g \) is a Riemannian metric on \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \left\lbrack  {-{10},{10}}\right\rbrack \) that is close to the round metric with scalar curvature 1, and that has curvature in the set \( {h}^{2}{\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) . We first recall the definition of the surgically modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) (cf. [21,§4.1]). To that end, let \( z \) denote the height function on \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \left\lbrack  {-{10},{10}}\right\rbrack \) , and let \( \varphi \left( z\right)  = {e}^{-\frac{1}{z}} \) for \( z \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . In the region \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \left\lbrack  {-{10},0}\right\rbrack \) , the metric is unchanged under surgery, i.e., \( \widetilde{g} = g \) . In the region \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \left( {0,\frac{1}{20}}\right\rbrack \) , we change the metric conformally by \( \widetilde{g} = \; {e}^{-{2\varphi }}g \) . In the region \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \left( {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) , we define \( \widetilde{g} = {e}^{-{2\varphi }}\left( {\chi \left( z\right) g + \left( {1 - \chi \left( z\right) }\right) \bar{g}}\right) \) , where \( \bar{g} \) denotes the standard metric on the cylinder and \( \chi  : \left( {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) is a smooth cutoff function satisfying \( \chi \left( z\right)  = 1 \) for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{18}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \chi \left( z\right)  = 0 \) for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{12},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . In particular, the surgically modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) is rotationally symmetric for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{12},\frac{1}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . Hence, we may extend \( \widetilde{g} \) by gluing in a rotationally symmetric cap.

We now analyze the curvature of the surgically modified metric \( \widetilde{g} \) . It suffices to consider the case when \( z > 0 \) is small. In this region, \( \widetilde{g} = {e}^{-{2\varphi }}g \) . Let \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) denote a local orthonormal frame with respect to the metric \( g \) . If we put \( {\widetilde{e}}_{i} = {e}^{\varphi }{e}_{i} \) , then \( \left\{  {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},\ldots ,{\widetilde{e}}_{n}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal frame with respect to the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) . We will express geometric quantities associated with the metric \( g \) relative to the frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) , while geometric quantities associated with \( \widetilde{g} \) will be expressed in terms of \( \left\{  {{\widetilde{e}}_{1},\ldots ,{\widetilde{e}}_{n}}\right\} \) . With this understood, the curvature tensor after surgery is related to the curvature tensor before surgery by the formula

\[
\widetilde{R} = {e}^{2\varphi }R + {e}^{2\varphi }\left( {{D}^{2}\varphi  + {d\varphi } \otimes  {d\varphi } - \frac{1}{2}{\left| d\varphi \right| }^{2}\mathrm{{id}}}\right)  \otimes  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

This implies

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R} - R - {z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}\left( {{dz} \otimes  {dz}}\right)  \otimes  \mathrm{{id}}}\right|  \ll  {z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}
\]

for \( z > 0 \) sufficiently small. Consequently, \( \operatorname{scal}\left( \widetilde{R}\right)  > \operatorname{scal}\left( R\right) \) if \( z > 0 \) is sufficiently small. Since the metric \( g \) is close to the cylindrical metric, we obtain

\[
\left| {R - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\mathrm{{id}} - {2z} \otimes  z}\right)  \otimes  \mathrm{{id}}}\right|  \ll  1,
\]

hence

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R} - \left( {1 - {z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}}\right) R - \frac{1}{2}{z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  \left| {\widetilde{R} - R - {z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}\left( {{dz} \otimes  {dz}}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}}\right|  + {z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}\left| {R - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\mathrm{{id}} - {2z} \otimes  z}\right)  \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}}\right|
\]

\[
\ll  {z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}
\]

for \( z > 0 \) sufficiently small. Therefore, we may write

\[
\widetilde{R} = \left( {1 - {z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}}\right) R + {z}^{-4}{e}^{-\frac{1}{z}}S,
\]

where \( \left| {S - \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{{id}} \oslash  \mathrm{{id}}}\right|  \ll  1 \) for \( z > 0 \) sufficiently small. Consequently, \( S \in  {h}^{2}{\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) if \( z > 0 \) is sufficiently small. Moreover, \( R \in  {h}^{2}{\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) in view of our assumption. Since \( {\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) is a convex set, we conclude that \( \widetilde{R} \in  {h}^{2}{\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) if \( z > 0 \) is sufficiently small. This easily implies that \( \widetilde{R} \in  {h}^{2}{\mathcal{F}}_{t} \) for all \( z \in  \left( {0,{10}}\right) \) .

nodes.content:
### 9.The standard solution

In this section, we recall some basic facts concerning the so-called standard solution. The standard solution is used to model the evolution of a cap that is glued in during a surgery procedure. More precisely, suppose that \( \left( {{S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R}}\right. \) , \( g\left( t\right) ), t < 0 \) , is a family of shrinking cylinders, normalized so that \( {\operatorname{scal}}_{g\left( t\right) } = \; \frac{1}{1 - \frac{2t}{n - 1}} \) for \( t < 0 \) . Suppose that we perform surgery at time \( t = 0 \) ; that is, we remove a half-cylinder and glue in a cap that is rotationally symmetric and has positive curvature. This gives a rotationally symmetric metric \( g\left( 0\right) \) on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . The standard solution is obtained by evolving the manifold \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) under the Ricci flow.

THEOREM 9.1 (G. Perelman [35, §2]; B.L. Chen, X.P. Zhu [12, Th. A.1]). There exists a complete solution \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , to the Ricci flow with the following properties:

(i) The initial manifold \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to a standard cylinder with scalar curvature 1 outside of a compact set, and this compact set is isometric to the cap used in the surgery procedure.

(ii) For each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , the manifold \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is rotationally symmetric.

(iii) For each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , the manifold \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is asymptotic to a cylinder with scalar curvature \( \frac{1}{1 - \frac{2t}{n - 1}} \) at infinity.

(iv) The scalar curvature is bounded from below by \( \frac{1}{{K}_{\text{ stnd }}\left( {1 - \frac{2t}{n - 1}}\right) } \) , where \( {K}_{\text{ stnd }} \) is a positive constant that depends only on \( n \) .

(v) For each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , the manifold \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is weakly PIC2 and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash  \mathrm{{id}} \in \) PIC for some constant \( \theta  > 0 \) that depends only on \( n \) .

(vi) The flow \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed for some constant \( \kappa  > 0 \) that depends only on \( n \) .

(vii) There exists a function \( \omega  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \left( {0,\infty }\right) \) such that

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {y, t}\right) \omega \left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( {y, t}\right) {d}_{g\left( t\right) }{\left( x, y\right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

for all points \( x, y \) and all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
The statements (i), (ii), (iii), (iv), (vi) and (vii) are established in [12, App. A]. Moreover, it is shown in [12] that \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) has nonnegative curvature operator. Hence, it remains to show that \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC.

To see this, we observe that the initial manifold \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is uniformly PIC. Moreover, on the initial manifold \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) , the sum of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Ricci tensor is bounded from below by a small multiple of the scalar curvature. Hence, we can find a small constant \( b \in  \left( {0,{b}_{\max }}\right) \) such that the curvature tensor of \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) lies in the cone \( \mathcal{C}\left( b\right) \) . By Hamilton’s PDE-ODE principle (see [13, Th. 12.34]), the curvature tensor of \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) lies in \( \mathcal{C}\left( b\right) \) for each \( t \geq  0 \) . Consequently, the curvature tensor of \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \oslash \) id \( \in \) PIC for each \( t \geq  0 \) .

nodes.proof:
Suppose that the assertion is false. Then we can find a sequence of points \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) on the standard solution such that \( {t}_{j} \rightarrow  \frac{n - 1}{2} \) and the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j},{A}_{0}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{j},{t}_{j}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - {A}_{0}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{j},{t}_{j}\right) }^{-1}}\right) \) is not \( \widetilde{\varepsilon } \) -close to the corresponding subset of a noncompact ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solution satisfying \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC. We dilate the solution around the point \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) by the factor \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) . Using statement (vii) in Theorem 9.1 together with the Harnack inequality (cf. Theorem 6.1), we conclude that the rescaled flows converge to a complete, noncompact ancient solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) . The limiting ancient solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is weakly PIC2 and satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \varnothing \) id \( \in \) PIC. Moreover, the limiting ancient solution is \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -noncollapsed.

By Theorem 6.1, the standard solution satisfies the Harnack inequality

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal} + 2\langle \nabla \operatorname{scal}, v\rangle  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  + \frac{1}{t}\operatorname{scal} \geq  0
\]

for \( t \in  \left( {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) . Consequently, the limiting ancient solution \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\operatorname{scal} + 2\langle \nabla \operatorname{scal}, v\rangle  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {v, v}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Using Proposition 6.11, we conclude that \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) has bounded curvature. Thus, \( \left( {{M}^{\infty },{g}^{\infty }\left( t\right) }\right) \) is a noncompact ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solution satisfying \( R - \theta \) scal id (b) i ∈ PIC. This is a contradiction.

Corollary 9.3 (cf. G. Perelman [35]; B.L. Chen, X.P. Zhu [12, Cor. A.2]). Given \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exist positive constants \( {C}_{1} = {C}_{1}\left( {n,\varepsilon }\right) \) and \( {C}_{2} = {C}_{2}\left( {n,\varepsilon }\right) \) such that the following holds: For each point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) on the standard solution, there exists a neighborhood \( B \) of \( {x}_{0} \) such that

\[

\]

\[

\]

- \( B \) is a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck (in the sense of [35]) with center at \( {x}_{0} \) . In particular, if \( {t}_{0} - R{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-1} \leq  0 \) , then \( B \) is disjoint from the surgical cap that was glued in at time 0 .

nodes.title: 10. A priori estimates for Ricci flow with surgery
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow with Surgery on Manifolds with Positive Isotropic Curvature

nodes.label: Definition 10.1
nodes.document_title: Simon Brendle - Ricci Flow with Surgery on Manifolds with Positive Isotropic Curvature
nodes.section_title: 10. A priori estimates for Ricci flow with surgery
nodes.content:
Definition 10.1. A Ricci flow with surgery on the interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) consists of the following data:

- A decomposition of \( \lbrack 0, T) \) into a disjoint union of finitely many subintervals \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k}^{ - },{t}_{k}^{ + }}\right) , k \in  \{ 0,1,\ldots , l\} \) . In other words, \( {t}_{0}^{ - } = 0,{t}_{l}^{ + } = T \) , and \( {t}_{k}^{ - } = {t}_{k - 1}^{ + } \) for \( k \in  \{ 1,\ldots , l\} \) .

- A collection of smooth Ricci flows \( \left( {{M}^{\left( k\right) },{g}^{\left( k\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) , defined for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k}^{ - },{t}_{k}^{ + }}\right) \) and going singular as \( t \rightarrow  {t}_{k}^{ + } \) for \( k \in  \{ 0,1,\ldots , l - 1\} \) .

- Positive numbers \( \varepsilon , r,\delta , h \) , where \( \delta  \leq  \varepsilon \) and \( h \leq  {\delta r} \) . These are referred to as the surgery parameters.

For each \( k \in  \{ 0,1,\ldots , l - 1\} \) , we put \( {\Omega }^{\left( k\right) } = \left\{  {x \in  {M}^{\left( k\right) } : \lim \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {t}_{k}^{ + }}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right. \; < \infty \} \) . We assume that the following conditions are satisfied:

- The manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\left( 0\right) },{g}^{\left( 0\right) }\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is isometric to the given initial manifold \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) .

- The manifold \( \left( {{M}^{\left( k\right) },{g}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {t}_{k}^{ - }\right) }\right) \) is obtained from \( \left( {{\Omega }^{\left( k - 1\right) },{g}^{\left( k - 1\right) }\left( {t}_{k - 1}^{ + }\right) }\right) \) by performing surgery on finitely many necks. For each neck on which we perform surgery, we can find a point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) at the center of that neck such that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = {h}^{-2} \) ; moreover, the parabolic neighborhood

\[
P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{\delta }^{-1}h, - {\delta }^{-1}{h}^{2}}\right)
\]

is free of surgeries and is a \( \delta \) -neck.

- After each surgery, we discard all double \( {4\varepsilon } \) -horns and all capped \( {4\varepsilon } \) -horns. Moreover, we remove all connected components that are diffeomorphic to \( {S}^{n}/\Gamma \) .

- Each flow \( \left( {{M}^{\left( k\right) },{g}^{\left( k\right) }\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies the Canonical Neighborhood Property with accuracy \( {4\varepsilon } \) on all scales less than \( r \) . That is to say, if \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) is an arbitrary point in space-time satisfying \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {r}^{-2} \) , then there exists a neighborhood \( B \) of \( {x}_{0} \) with the property that

\[
{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{\left( 8{C}_{1}\right) }^{-1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},8{C}_{1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)
\]

and

\[
{\left( 8{C}_{2}\right) }^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  8{C}_{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  B \) . Moreover, \( B \) is either a strong \( {4\varepsilon } \) -neck (in the sense of [35]) with center at \( {x}_{0} \) or a \( {4\varepsilon } \) -cap (in the sense of Definition 6.16).

- If \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) is an arbitrary point in space-time satisfying \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {r}^{-2} \) , then \( \left| {D\mathrm{{scal}}}\right|  \leq  {4\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\mathrm{{scal}}}\right|  \leq  {4\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{2} \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) .

nodes.content: PROPOSITION 10.2. Suppose that we have a Ricci flow with surgery starting from \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) that is defined on \( \lbrack 0, T) \) . Then \( T \leq  \frac{n}{2\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right) } \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: PROPOSITION 10.2. Suppose that we have a Ricci flow with surgery starting from \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) that is defined on \( \lbrack 0, T) \) . Then \( T \leq \frac{n}{2\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x,0}\right) } \) .

nodes.proof:
By the maximum principle, the function

\[
t \mapsto  \frac{n}{2\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right) } + t
\]

is monotone decreasing under smooth Ricci flow. By Proposition 8.2, this function is monotone decreasing across surgery times. From this, the assertion follows.

Proposition 10.5 (cf. G. Perelman [35, Lemma 4.5]). Fix \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) small, \( \alpha  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , and \( A > 1 \) . Then there exists \( \bar{\delta } > 0 \) (depending on \( \alpha \) and \( A \) ) with the following property: Suppose that we have a Ricci flow with surgery with parameters \( \varepsilon , r,\delta , h \) , where \( \delta  \leq  \bar{\delta } \) . Suppose that \( {T}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) is a surgery time, and let \( {x}_{0} \) be a point that lies on a gluing cap at time \( {T}_{0} \) . Let \( {T}_{1} = \; \min \left\{  {T,{T}_{0} + \alpha {h}^{2}}\right\} \) . Then one of the following statements holds:

(i) The flow is defined on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{T}_{0},{Ah},{T}_{1} - {T}_{0}}\right) \) . Moreover, after dilating the flow by \( {h}^{-2} \) and shifting time \( {T}_{0} \) to 0, the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{T}_{0},{Ah},{T}_{1} - {T}_{0}}\right) \) is \( {A}^{-1} \) -close to the corresponding subset of the standard solution.

(ii) There exists a surgery time \( {t}^{ + } \in  \left( {{T}_{0},{T}_{1}}\right) \) such that the flow is defined on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{T}_{0},{Ah},{t}^{ + } - {T}_{0}}\right) \) . Moreover, the parabolic neighborhood

\[
P\left( {{x}_{0},{T}_{0},{Ah},{t}^{ + } - {T}_{0}}\right)
\]

is, after dilation by the factor \( {h}^{-2},{A}^{-1} \) -close to the corresponding subset of the standard solution. Finally, for each point \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( {T}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{Ah}}\right) \) , the flow exists exactly until time \( {t}^{ + } \) .

The proof is the same as the proof of Lemma 4.5 in Perelman's paper [35]. We omit the details.

nodes.content: Definition 10.7. Suppose we are given a Ricci flow with surgery. A curve in space-time is said to be admissible if it stays in the region unaffected by surgery. A curve in space-time is called barely admissible if it is on the boundary of the set of admissible curves.

LEMMA 10.8 (cf. G. Perelman [35, Lemma 5.3]). Fix \( \varepsilon , r, L \) . Then we can find a real number \( \bar{\delta } > 0 \) (depending on \( r \) and \( L \) ) with the following property: Suppose that we have a Ricci flow with surgery with parameters \( \varepsilon , r,\delta , h \) , where \( \delta  \leq  \bar{\delta } \) . Let \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) be a point in space-time such that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) , and let \( {T}_{0} < {t}_{0} \) be a surgery time. Finally, let \( \gamma \) be a barely admissible curve (parametrized by the interval \( \left. \left\lbrack  {{T}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  \right) \) such that \( \gamma \left( {T}_{0}\right) \) lies on the boundary of a surgical cap at time \( {T}_{0} \) , and \( \gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right)  = {x}_{0} \) . Then

\[
{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{t}_{0}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}\left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  + {\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}}\right) {dt} \geq  L.
\]

Let \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) be a point in space-time such that \( \o...

nodes.proof:
By Definition 10.1, we have \( \left| {D\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq  {4\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq \; {4\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{2} \) whenever scal \( \geq  {r}^{-2} \) . Since \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) , it follows that \( \operatorname{scal} \leq \; 4{r}^{-2} \) in \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{r}{100\eta }, - \frac{{r}^{2}}{100\eta }}\right) \) . Let \( \gamma \) be a barely admissible curve in space-time satisfying the assumptions of Lemma 10.8, and suppose that

\[
{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{t}_{0}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}\left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  + {\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}}\right) {dt} < L.
\]

Using Hölder's inequality and the positivity of the scalar curvature, we obtain \( {\int }_{{t}_{0} - \tau }^{{t}_{0}}{\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }{dt} < {\left( 2L\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\tau }^{\frac{1}{4}} \) for \( \tau  > 0 \) . Hence, we can find a real number \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,\frac{{r}^{2}}{100\eta }}\right) \) , depending only on \( r \) and \( L \) , such that \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {t}_{0} - \tau ,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  } \) is contained in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{r}{100\eta }, - \frac{{r}^{2}}{100\eta }}\right) \) . This implies

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  \leq  4{r}^{-2}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) .

Having chosen \( \tau \) , we define real numbers \( \alpha  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) and \( l > 0 \) by the relations

\[
\frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) \sqrt{\tau }}{4{K}_{\text{ stnd }}}\left| {\log \left( {1 - \frac{2\alpha }{n - 1}}\right) }\right|  = L
\]

and

\[
\frac{l}{2}\sqrt{\tau } = L
\]

Having fixed \( \alpha \) and \( l \) , we choose a large constant \( A \) so that the conclusion of Lemma 9.4 holds. Having chosen \( \alpha \) and \( A \) , we choose \( \bar{\delta } \) so that the conclusion of Proposition 10.5 holds. Moreover, by choosing \( \bar{\delta } \) small enough, we can arrange that \( {K}_{\text{ stnd }}{\bar{\delta }}^{2} \leq  \frac{1}{16} \) .

In the following, we assume that \( \delta  \leq  \bar{\delta } \) . Let \( {T}_{1} \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{0},{T}_{0} + \alpha {h}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) denote the largest number with the property that \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {T}_{0},{T}_{1}\right\rbrack  } \) is contained in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\gamma \left( {T}_{0}\right) ,{T}_{0},{Ah},\alpha {h}^{2}}\right) \) . By Proposition 10.5, the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\gamma \left( {T}_{0}\right) ,{T}_{0},{Ah},{T}_{1} - {T}_{0}}\right) \) is close to the corresponding subset of the standard solution. Since \( h \leq  {\delta r} \) , it follows that

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2{K}_{\text{ stnd }}\left( {{h}^{2} - \frac{2\left( {t - {T}_{0}}\right) }{n - 1}}\right) } \geq  \frac{1}{2{K}_{\text{ stnd }}{\delta }^{2}{r}^{2}} \geq  8{r}^{-2}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{0},{T}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  \leq  4{r}^{-2} \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , the intervals \( \left\lbrack  {{T}_{0},{T}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) and \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \tau ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) are disjoint. In other words, \( {T}_{1} \leq  {t}_{0} - \tau \) . We distinguish two cases:

Case 1: Suppose that \( {T}_{1} < {T}_{0} + \alpha {h}^{2} \) . In this case, the curve \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {T}_{0},{T}_{1}\right\rbrack  } \) exits the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\gamma \left( {T}_{0}\right) ,{T}_{0},{Ah},\alpha {h}^{2}}\right) \) at time \( {T}_{1} \) . Since the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\gamma \left( {T}_{0}\right) ,{T}_{0},{Ah},{T}_{1} - {T}_{0}}\right) \) is close to the corresponding subset of the standard solution, Lemma 9.4 implies that \( {\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{1}}{\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}{dt} \geq  \frac{l}{2} \) . (Here, we have used the fact that \( \int {\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}{dt} \) is invariant under scaling.) Consequently,

\[
L > {\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{1}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}\left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  + {\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}}\right) {dt}
\]

\[
\geq  \sqrt{\tau }{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{1}}{\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}{dt}
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{l}{2}\sqrt{\tau }
\]

which contradicts our choice of \( l \) .

Case 2: Suppose that \( {T}_{1} = {T}_{0} + \alpha {h}^{2} \) . In this case,

\[
L > {\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{1}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}\left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  + {\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}}\right) {dt}
\]

\[
\geq  \sqrt{\tau }{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{1}}\operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right) {dt}
\]

\[
\geq  \sqrt{\tau }{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{1}}\frac{1}{2{K}_{\text{ stnd }}\left( {{h}^{2} - \frac{2\left( {t - {T}_{0}}\right) }{n - 1}}\right) }{dt}
\]

\[
= \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) \sqrt{\tau }}{4{K}_{\text{ stnd }}}\left| {\log \left( {1 - \frac{2\alpha }{n - 1}}\right) }\right| ,
\]

which contradicts our choice of \( \alpha \) .

nodes.content:
Proposition 10.9 (cf. G. Perelman [35, Lemma 5.2]). Fix a small number \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) . Then we can find a positive number \( \kappa \) and a positive function \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( \cdot \right) \) with the following property: Suppose that we have a Ricci flow with surgery with parameters \( \varepsilon , r,\delta , h \) , where \( \delta  \leq  \widetilde{\delta }\left( r\right) \) . Then the flow is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales less than \( \varepsilon \) .

Note that the constant \( \kappa \) in the noncollapsing estimate may depend on the initial data, but it is independent of the surgery parameters \( \varepsilon , r,\delta , h \) .

nodes.proof:
Consider a point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) in space-time and a positive number \( {r}_{0} \leq  \varepsilon \) such that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) for all points \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) for which the flow is defined. We need to show that \( {\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}_{0}^{n} \) for some uniform constant \( \kappa  > 0 \) . We distinguish three cases:

Case 1: Suppose first that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {r}^{-2} \) . In this case, the Canonical Neighborhood Assumption implies that \( {\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}_{0}^{n} \) for some uniform constant \( \kappa  > 0 \) .

Case 2: Suppose next that the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{2}, - \frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{4}}\right) \) contains points modified by surgery. Let \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) be a point in \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{2}, - \frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{4}}\right) \) that lies on a surgical cap. Clearly, \( \frac{1}{4}{h}^{-2} \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) , hence \( {r}_{0} \leq  {2h} \) . This implies \( {\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {x,\frac{{r}_{0}}{100}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}_{0}^{n} \) for some uniform constant \( \kappa  > 0 \) . Since \( {B}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {x,\frac{{r}_{0}}{100}}\right)  \subset  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {x,\frac{{r}_{0}}{4}}\right) \) , we deduce that \( {\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq \; {\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {x,\frac{{r}_{0}}{4}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}_{0}^{n}. \)

Case 3: Suppose finally that \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) and the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{2}, - \frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{4}}\right) \) is free of surgeries. Note that \( {t}_{0} \) is bounded from above by Proposition 10.2. By Lemma 10.8, we can find a positive function \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( \cdot \right) \) such that the following holds: Suppose that the surgery parameters satisfy \( \delta  \leq  \widetilde{\delta }\left( r\right) \) , and suppose further that \( {T}_{0} < {t}_{0} \) is a surgery time and \( \gamma \) is a barely admissible curve (parametrized by the interval \( \left. \left\lbrack  {{T}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  \right) \) such that \( \gamma \left( {T}_{0}\right) \) lies on the boundary of a surgical cap at time \( {T}_{0} \) and \( \gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right)  = {x}_{0} \) . Then

\[
{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{t}_{0}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}\left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  + {\left| {\gamma }^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) }^{2}}\right) {dt} \geq  {8n}\sqrt{{t}_{0}}.
\]

Thus, if \( \delta  \leq  \widetilde{\delta }\left( r\right) \) , then every barely admissible curve has reduced length greater than \( {2n} \) .

In the following, we assume that \( \delta  \leq  \widetilde{\delta }\left( r\right) \) . For \( t < {t}_{0} \) , we denote by \( \ell \left( {x, t}\right) \) the reduced distance from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , i.e., the infimum of the reduced length over all admissible curves joining \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) and \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . We claim that \( \mathop{\inf }\limits_{x}\ell \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{n}{2} \) for all \( t < {t}_{0} \) . This is clearly true if \( t \) is sufficiently close to \( {t}_{0} \) . Now, if \( \ell \left( {x, t}\right) \; < {2n} \) for some point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) in space-time, then the reduced length is attained by a strictly admissible curve. Hence, we may apply results of Perelman (cf. [33, §7]) to conclude that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\ell  \geq  \Delta \ell  + \frac{1}{{t}_{0} - t}\left( {\ell  - \frac{n}{2}}\right)
\]

whenever \( \ell  < {2n} \) . Using the maximum principle, we deduce that \( \mathop{\inf }\limits_{x}\ell \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq \; \frac{n}{2} \) for all \( t < {t}_{0} \) .

In particular, there exists a point \( y \in  M \) such that \( \ell \left( {y,\varepsilon }\right)  \leq  \frac{n}{2} \) . Hence, we can find a radius \( \rho  > 0 \) such that \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) }}\ell \left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  n \) . Note that \( \rho \) depends only on \( \varepsilon \) and the initial data \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) , but not on the surgery parameters. Hence, for each point \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) \) , the reduced distance is attained by a strictly admissible curve, and this curve must be an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic.

Given a tangent vector \( v \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we denote by \( {\gamma }_{v}\left( t\right)  = {\mathcal{L}}_{t,{t}_{0}}{\exp }_{{x}_{0}}\left( v\right) \) the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic satisfying \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {t}_{0}}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}{\gamma }_{v}^{\prime }\left( t\right)  = v \) . Note that, due to the presence of surgeries, \( {\gamma }_{v}\left( t\right) \) may not be defined on the entire interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) .

Let \( \mathcal{V} \) denote the set of all tangent vectors \( v \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) with the property that \( {\gamma }_{v} \) is defined on \( \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) ;{\gamma }_{v} \) has minimal \( \mathcal{L} \) -length; and \( {\gamma }_{v}\left( 0\right)  \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) \) . In view of the discussion above, the map \( {\mathcal{L}}_{0,{t}_{0}}{\exp }_{{x}_{0}} : \mathcal{V} \rightarrow  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) \) is onto. For each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we define

\[
V\left( t\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{V}}{\left( {t}_{0} - t\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {{\gamma }_{v}\left( t\right) , t}\right) }{J}_{v}\left( t\right) ,
\]

where \( {J}_{v}\left( t\right)  = \det {\left( D{\mathcal{L}}_{t,{t}_{0}}{\exp }_{{x}_{0}}\right) }_{v} \) denotes the Jacobian determinant of the \( \mathcal{L} \) - exponential map, and the integration is with respect to the standard Lebesgue measure on the tangent space \( \left( {{T}_{{x}_{0}}M, g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right) \) . For each tangent vector \( v \in \; \mathcal{V} \) , Perelman’s Jacobian comparison theorem (cf. [33,§7]) implies that the function \( t \mapsto  {\left( {t}_{0} - t\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {{\gamma }_{v}\left( t\right) , t}\right) }{J}_{v}\left( t\right) \) is monotone increasing. Moreover, \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {t}_{0}}}{\left( {t}_{0} - t\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {{\gamma }_{v}\left( t\right) , t}\right) }{J}_{v}\left( t\right)  = {2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| v\right| }^{2}} \) for each \( v \in  \mathcal{V} \) . The monotonicity property for the Jacobian determinant implies that the function \( t \mapsto  V\left( t\right) \) is monotone increasing.

We first estimate the reduced volume from below in terms of the initial data. Since \( \ell \left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  n \) for all points \( x \in  {B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) \) , we obtain a uniform lower bound for \( V\left( 0\right) \) :

\[
V\left( 0\right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{V}}{t}_{0}^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {{\gamma }_{v}\left( 0\right) ,0}\right) }{J}_{v}\left( 0\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {\int }_{{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) }{t}_{0}^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {x,0}\right) }d{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( x\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {t}_{0}^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-n}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) }\right) .
\]

We next estimate the reduced volume from above. By assumption, the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{2}, - \frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{4}}\right) \) is free of surgeries, and we have scal \( \leq \; {r}_{0}^{-2} \) in \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{2}, - \frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{4}}\right) \) . Using Shi’s interior derivative estimates, we conclude that the covariant derivatives of the Riemann curvature tensor are bounded by \( C\left( n\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \) and the second covariant derivatives of the Riemann curvature tensor are bounded by \( C\left( n\right) {r}_{0}^{-4} \) in \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{4}, - \frac{{r}_{0}^{2}}{16}}\right) \) . Using the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation, we conclude that there exists a small positive constant \( \mu \left( n\right) \) (depending only on \( n \) ) with the following property: if \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \mu \left( n\right) {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right) \) and \( \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{32}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - \bar{t}}} \) , then \( \sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}{\left| {\gamma }_{v}^{\prime }\left( t\right) \right| }_{g\left( t\right) } \leq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{16}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - \bar{t}}} \) and \( {\gamma }_{v}\left( t\right)  \in  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}}{4\sqrt{{t}_{0} - \bar{t}}}}\right)  \subset  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{4}}\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . This implies

\[
V\left( 0\right)  \leq  V\left( \bar{t}\right)  \leq  {\int }_{\left\{  v \in  \mathcal{V} : \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{32}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - \bar{t}}}\right\}  }{\left( {t}_{0} - \bar{t}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {{\gamma }_{v}\left( \bar{t}\right) ,\bar{t}}\right) }{J}_{v}\left( \bar{t}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{\left\{  v \in  \mathcal{V} : \left| v\right|  \geq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{32}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}}{\left. \right\}  }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\ell \left( {{\gamma }_{v}\left( \bar{t}\right) ,\bar{t}}\right) }{J}_{v}\left( \bar{t}\right) \right\}  }
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{\left\{  v \in  \mathcal{V} : \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{32}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - \bar{t}}}\right\}  }{\left( {t}_{0} - \bar{t}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{J}_{v}\left( \bar{t}\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  \geq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{32}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - \bar{t}}}\right\}  }{2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}
\]

\[
\leq  {\left( {t}_{0} - \bar{t}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( \bar{t}\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{4}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  \geq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{32}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - \bar{t}}}\right\}  }{2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}
\]

for all \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \mu \left( n\right) {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Putting these facts together gives

\[
{\left( {t}_{0} - \bar{t}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( \bar{t}\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{4}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {t}_{0}^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-n}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) }\right)  - {\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  \geq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{32}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}}\right\}  }{2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}
\]

for all \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \mu \left( n\right) {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Finally, we choose \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \mu \left( n\right) {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right) \) so that \( {t}_{0} - \bar{t} \) is a small, but fixed, multiple of \( {r}_{0}^{2} \) , and the quantity

\[
{t}_{0}^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-n}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {y,\rho }\right) }\right)  - {\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  \geq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{{32}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}}\right\}  }{2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}
\]

is bounded from below by a positive constant. This gives a lower bound for \( {r}_{0}^{-n}{\operatorname{vol}}_{g\left( \bar{t}\right) }\left( {{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{{r}_{0}}{4}}\right) }\right) \) , as desired.

nodes.content:
THEOREM 10.10 (cf. G. Perelman [35,§5]). Fix a small number \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) . Then we can find positive numbers \( \widehat{r} \) and \( \widehat{\delta } \) with the following property: Suppose that we have a Ricci flow with surgery with parameters \( \varepsilon ,\widehat{r},\widehat{\delta }, h \) that is defined on some interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) . Moreover, suppose that \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) is an arbitrary point in space-time satisfying \( \operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {\left( 2\widehat{r}\right) }^{-2} \) . Then there exists a neighborhood \( B \) of \( {x}_{0} \) such that

\[
{B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},{\left( 2{C}_{1}\right) }^{-1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{g\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\left( {{x}_{0},2{C}_{1}\operatorname{scal}{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)
\]

and

\[
{\left( 2{C}_{2}\right) }^{-1}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \operatorname{scal}\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  2{C}_{2}\operatorname{scal}\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  B \) . Moreover, \( B \) is either a strong \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck (in the sense of [35]) with center at \( {x}_{0} \) or a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap. Finally, we have \( \left| {D\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq  {2\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{\frac{3}{2}} \) and \( \left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\text{ scal }}\right|  \leq \; {2\eta }{\operatorname{scal}}^{2} \) at the point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) .
