nodes.content:
Remark 13.15. We caution the reader that this definition differs slightly from the definition of noncollapsing that is used from section I.7 onwards.

Note that except for the overall scale \( \rho \) , the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed condition is scale-invariant. From the proof of Theorem 13.3 we extract the following statement. Given a Ricci flow defined on an interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) , with \( T < \infty \) , and a scale \( \rho \) , there is some number \( \kappa  = \; \kappa \left( {g\left( 0\right) , T,\rho }\right) \) so that the solution is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on the scale \( \rho \) for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . We note that the estimate on \( \kappa \) deteriorates as \( T \rightarrow  \infty \) , as there are Ricci flow solutions that collapse at long time.

##### 14.I.5.The \( \mathcal{W} \) -FUNCTIONAL AS A TIME DERIVATIVE

We will only discuss one formula from I.5, showing that along a Ricci flow, \( \mathcal{W} \) is itself the time-derivative of an integral expression.

Again, we put \( \tau  =  - t \) . Consider the evolution equations (12.9), with \( {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-f}{dV} = \; {dm} \) . Then

(14.1)

\[
\text{ (14.1) }\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {\tau {\int }_{M}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {dm}}\right)  = {\int }_{M}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {dm} + \tau {\int }_{M}\left( {{\Delta f} + R - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {dm}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {dm} + \tau {\int }_{M}\left( {{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {dm}
\]

\[
= \mathcal{W}\left( {g\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) ,\tau }\right) .
\]

With respect to the evolution equations (12.12) obtained by performing diffeomorphisms, we get

(14.2)

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {\tau {\int }_{M}\left( {f - \frac{n}{2}}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-f}{dV}}\right)  = \mathcal{W}\left( {g\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) ,\tau }\right) .
\]

Similarly, with respect to (5.21),

(14.3)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {-{\int }_{M}f{e}^{-f}{dV}}\right)  = \mathcal{F}\left( {g\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

nodes.content:
#### 15.I.7. Overview of REDUCED LENGTH AND REDUCED VOLUME

We first give a brief summary of I.7. In I.7, the variable \( \tau  = {t}_{0} - t \) is used and so the corresponding Ricci flow equation is \( {\left( {g}_{ij}\right) }_{\tau } = 2{R}_{ij} \) . The goal is to prove a no local collapsing theorem by means of the \( \mathcal{L} \) -lengths of curves \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {{\tau }_{1},{\tau }_{2}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) , defined by

(15.1)

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{{\tau }_{1}}^{{\tau }_{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau },
\]

where the scalar curvature \( R\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right) \) and the norm \( \left| {\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\right| \) are evaluated using the metric at time \( {t}_{0} - \tau \) . Here \( {\tau }_{1} \geq  0 \) . With \( X = \frac{d\gamma }{d\tau } \) , the corresponding \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation is

(15.2)

\[
{\nabla }_{X}X - \frac{1}{2}\nabla R + \frac{1}{2\tau }X + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, \cdot  }\right)  = 0,
\]

where again the connection and curvature are taken at the corresponding time, and the 1-form \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, \cdot  }\right) \) has been identified with the corresponding dual vector field.

Fix \( p \in  M \) . Taking \( {\tau }_{1} = 0 \) and \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = p \) , the vector \( v = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\sqrt{\tau }X\left( \tau \right) \) is well-defined in \( {T}_{p}M \) and is called the initial vector of the geodesic. The \( \mathcal{L} \) -exponential map \( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\tau } : {T}_{p}M \rightarrow  M \) sends \( v \) to \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) .

The function \( L\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) \) is the infimal \( \mathcal{L} \) -length of curves \( \gamma \) with \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = p \) and \( \gamma \left( \bar{\tau }\right)  = q \) . Defining the reduced length by

(15.3)

\[
l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  = \frac{L\left( {q,\tau }\right) }{2\sqrt{\tau }}
\]

and the reduced volume by

(15.4)

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = {\int }_{M}{\tau }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-l\left( {q,\tau }\right) }{dq},
\]

the goal is to show that \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) is nonincreasing in \( \tau \) , i.e. nondecreasing in \( t \) . To do this, one uses the \( \mathcal{L} \) -exponential map to write \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) as an integral over \( {T}_{p}M \) :

(15.5)

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = {\int }_{{T}_{p}M}{\tau }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-l\left( {\mathcal{L}\operatorname{ex}{p}_{\tau }\left( v\right) ,\tau }\right) }\mathcal{J}\left( {v,\tau }\right) {\chi }_{\tau }\left( v\right) {dv}
\]

where \( \mathcal{J}\left( {v,\tau }\right)  = \det d{\left( \mathcal{L}\exp {\tau }_{v}\right) }_{v} \) is the Jacobian factor in the change of variable and \( {\chi }_{\tau } \) is a cutoff function related to the \( \mathcal{L} \) -cut locus of \( p \) . To show that \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) is nonincreasing in \( \tau \) it suffices to show that \( {\tau }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-l\left( {\mathcal{L}\exp {\tau }_{v}\left( v\right) ,\tau }\right) }\mathcal{J}\left( {v,\tau }\right) \) is nonincreasing in \( \tau \) or, equivalently, that \( - \frac{n}{2}\ln \left( \tau \right)  - l\left( {\mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\tau }\left( v\right) ,\tau }\right)  + \ln \mathcal{J}\left( {v,\tau }\right) \) is nonincreasing in \( \tau \) . Hence it is necessary to compute \( \frac{{dl}\left( {\mathcal{L}{ex}{p}_{\tau }\left( v\right) ,\tau }\right) }{d\tau } \) and \( \frac{d\mathcal{J}\left( {v,\tau }\right) }{d\tau } \) . The computation of the latter will involve the \( \mathcal{L} \) -Jacobi fields.

The fact that \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) is nonincreasing in \( \tau \) is then used to show that the Ricci flow solution cannot be collapsed near \( p \) .

## 16. BASIC EXAMPLE FOR I.7

In this section we say what the various expressions of I. 7 become in the model case of a flat Euclidean Ricci solution.

If \( M \) is flat \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) and \( p = \overrightarrow{0} \) then the unique \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) with \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = \overrightarrow{0} \) and \( \gamma \left( \bar{\tau }\right)  = \overrightarrow{q} \) is

(16.1)

\[
\gamma \left( \tau \right)  = {\left( \frac{\tau }{\bar{\tau }}\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}\overrightarrow{q} = 2{\tau }^{\frac{1}{2}}\overrightarrow{v}
\]

The function \( L \) is given by

(16.2)

\[
L\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = \frac{1}{2}{\bar{\tau }}^{-\frac{1}{2}}{\left| q\right| }^{2}
\]

and the reduced length (15.3) is given by

(16.3)

\[

The function \( \bar{L}\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = 2{\bar{\tau }}^{\frac{1}{2}}L\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) \) is

(16.4)

\[
\bar{L}\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = {\left| q\right| }^{2}.
\]

Then

(16.5)

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = {\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}{\tau }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\frac{{\left| q\right| }^{2}}{4\tau }}{d}^{n}q = {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{\frac{n}{2}}
\]

is constant in \( \tau \) .

nodes.content: The first sense is that of a barrier differential inequality. Given \( f \in  C\left( M\right) \) and a function \( g \) on \( M \) , one says that \( \bigtriangleup f \leq  g \) in the sense of barriers if for all \( q \in  M \) and \( \epsilon  > 0 \) , there is a neighborhood \( V \) of \( q \) and some \( {u}_{\epsilon } \in  {C}^{2}\left( V\right) \) so that \( {u}_{\epsilon }\left( q\right)  = f\left( q\right) ,{u}_{\epsilon } \geq  f \) on \( V \) and \( \bigtriangleup {u}_{\epsilon } \leq  g + \epsilon \) on \( V \) [13]. There is a similar spacetime definition for \( \bigtriangleup f - \frac{\partial f}{\partial t} \leq  g \) [26]. The point of barrier differential inequalities is that they allow one to apply the maximum principle just as with smooth solutions.

We now say that a Ricci flow solution \( g\left( \cdot \right) \) defined on a time interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on the scale \( \rho \) if for each \( r < \rho \) and all \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  M \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( {t}_{0} \geq  {r}^{2} \) , whenever it is true that \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {r}^{-2} \) for every \( x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , then we also have \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}^{n} \) .

nodes.content: Theorem 26.2. Given numbers \( n \in  {\mathbb{Z}}^{ + }, T < \infty \) and \( \rho , K, c > 0 \) , there is a number \( \kappa  = \kappa \left( {n, K, c,\rho , T}\right)  > 0 \) with the following property. Let \( \left( {{M}^{n}, g\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) be a Ricci flow solution defined on a time interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T < \infty \) , such that the curvature \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \) is bounded on every compact subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack   \subset  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Suppose that \( \left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right) \) is a complete Riemannian manifold with \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  K \) and \( \operatorname{inj}\left( {M, g\left( 0\right) }\right)  \geq  c > 0 \) . Then the Ricci flow solution is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on the scale \( \rho \) , in the sense of Definition 26.1. Furthermore, with the other constants fixed, we can take \( \kappa \) to be nonincreasing in \( T \) .

nodes.proof:
We first observe that the existence of \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics and the monotonicity of the reduced volume are valid in this setting; see Section 17.

Suppose that the theorem were false. Then for given \( T < \infty \) and \( \rho , K, c > 0 \) , there are : 1. A sequence \( {\left\{  \left( {M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( \cdot \right) \right) \right\}  }_{k = 1}^{\infty } \) of Ricci flow solutions, each defined on the time interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) , with \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  K \) on \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( 0\right) }\right) \) and \( \operatorname{inj}\left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( 0\right) }\right)  \geq  c \) ,

2. Spacetime points \( \left( {{p}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \in  {M}_{k} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) and

3. Numbers \( {r}_{k} \in  \left( {0,\rho }\right) \)

having the following property : \( {t}_{k} \geq  {r}_{k}^{2} \) and if we put \( {B}_{k} = {B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{p}_{k},{r}_{k}}\right)  \subset  {M}_{k} \) then \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {r}_{k}^{-2} \) whenever \( x \in  {B}_{k} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - {r}_{k}^{2},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) , but \( {\epsilon }_{k} = {r}_{k}^{-1}\operatorname{vol}{\left( {B}_{k}\right) }^{\frac{1}{n}} \rightarrow  0 \) as \( k \rightarrow  \infty \) . From short-time curvature estimates along with the assumed bounded geometry at time zero, there is some \( \bar{t} > 0 \) so that we have uniformly bounded geometry on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . In particular, we may assume that each \( {t}_{k} \) is greater than \( \bar{t} \) .

We define \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k} \) using curves going backward in real time from the basepoint \( \left( {{p}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , i.e. forward in \( \tau \) -time from \( \tau  = 0 \) . The first step is to show that \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) \) is small. Note that \( \tau  = {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2} \) corresponds to a real time of \( {t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2} \) , which is very close to \( {t}_{k} \) .

Given an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) with \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = {p}_{k} \) and velocity vector \( X\left( \tau \right)  = \frac{d\gamma }{d\tau } \) , its initial vector is \( v = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\sqrt{\tau }X\left( \tau \right)  \in  {T}_{{p}_{k}}{M}_{k} \) . We first want to show that if \( \left| v\right|  \leq  {.1}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-1/2} \) then \( \gamma \) does not escape from \( {B}_{k} \) in time \( {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2} \) .

We have

(26.3)

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\langle X\left( \tau \right) , X\left( \tau \right) \rangle  = 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  + 2\left\langle  {X,{\nabla }_{X}X}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  + \langle X,\nabla R - \frac{1}{\tau }X - 4\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, \cdot  }\right) \rangle
\]

\[
=  - \frac{{\left| X\right| }^{2}}{\tau } - 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  + \langle X,\nabla R\rangle ,
\]

SO

(26.4)

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {\tau {\left| X\right| }^{2}}\right)  =  - {2\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  + \tau \langle X,\nabla R\rangle .
\]

Letting \( C \) denote a generic \( n \) -dependent constant, for \( x \in  B\left( {{p}_{k},{r}_{k}/2}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - {r}_{k}^{2}/2,{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) , the fact that \( {g}_{k} \) satisfies the Ricci flow gives an estimate \( \left| {\nabla R}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C{r}_{k}^{-3} \) , as follows from the case \( l = 0, m = 1 \) of Appendix D. Then in terms of dimensionless variables,

(26.5)

\[
\left| {\frac{d}{d\left( {\tau /{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\left( {\tau {\left| X\right| }^{2}}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C\tau }{\left| X\right| }^{2} + C{\left( \tau /{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{1/2}{\left( \tau {\left| X\right| }^{2}\right) }^{1/2}.
\]

Equivalently,

(26.6)

\[
\left| {\frac{d}{d\left( {\tau /{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\left| X\right| }\right) }\right|  \leq  C\sqrt{\tau }\left| X\right|  + C{\left( \tau /{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{1/2}.
\]

Let us rewrite this as

(26.7)

\[
\left| {\frac{d}{d\left( \frac{\tau }{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left| X\right| }\right) }\right|  \leq  C{\epsilon }_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left| X\right| }\right)  + C{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}{\left( \frac{\tau }{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }^{1/2}.
\]

We are interested in the time range when \( \frac{\tau }{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}} \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) and the initial condition satisfies \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}{\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left| X\right| \left( \tau \right)  \leq  {.1} \) . Then because of the \( {\epsilon }_{k} \) -factors on the right-hand side, it follows

from (26.7) that for large \( k \) , we will have \( {\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left| X\right| \left( \tau \right)  \leq  {.11} \) for all \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Next,

(26.8)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\left| {X\left( \tau \right) }\right| {d\tau } = {\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}{\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left| X\right| \left( \tau \right) \frac{d\tau }{\sqrt{\tau }} \leq  {.11}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\frac{d\tau }{\sqrt{\tau }} = {.22}{r}_{k}.
\]

From the Ricci flow equation \( {g}_{\tau } = 2 \) Ric, it follows that the metrics \( g\left( \tau \right) \) between \( \tau  = 0 \) and \( \bar{\tau } = {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2} \) are \( {e}^{C{\epsilon }_{k}} \) -biLipschitz close to each other. Then for \( {\epsilon }_{k} \) small, the length of \( \gamma \) , as measured with the metric at time \( {t}_{k} \) , will be at most \( {.3}{r}_{k} \) . This shows that \( \gamma \) does not leave \( {B}_{k} \) within time \( {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2} \) .

Hence the contribution to \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) \) coming from vectors \( v \in  {T}_{{p}_{k}}{M}_{k} \) with \( \left| v\right|  \leq  {.1}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) is at most \( {\int }_{{B}_{k}}{\left( {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }{dq} \) . We now want to give a lower bound on \( l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) \) for \( q \in  {B}_{k} \) . Given the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {M}_{k} \) with \( \gamma \left( 0\right)  = {p}_{k} \) and \( \gamma \left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  = q \) , we have

(26.9)

\[
\text{ 26.9) }\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  \geq  {\int }_{0}^{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\sqrt{\tau }R\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right) {d\tau } \geq   - {\int }_{0}^{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\sqrt{\tau }n\left( {n - 1}\right) {r}_{k}^{-2}{d\tau } =  - \frac{2}{3}n\left( {n - 1}\right) {\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{3}{2}}{r}_{k}\text{ . }
\]

Then

(26.10)

\[
l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  \geq   - \frac{1}{3}n\left( {n - 1}\right) {\epsilon }_{k}.
\]

Thus the contribution to \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) \) coming from vectors \( v \in  {T}_{{p}_{k}}{M}_{k} \) with \( \left| v\right|  \leq  {.1}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) is at most

(26.11)

\[
{e}^{\frac{1}{3}n\left( {n - 1}\right) {\epsilon }_{k}}{\left( {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\operatorname{vol}}_{{t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\left( {B}_{k}\right)  \leq  {e}^{\frac{1}{3}n\left( {n - 1}\right) {\epsilon }_{k}}{e}^{\text{ const. }\frac{1}{{r}_{k}^{2}}{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}{\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{n}{2}},
\]

which is less than \( 2{\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{n}{2}} \) for large \( k \) .

To estimate the contribution to \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) \) coming from vectors \( v \in  {T}_{{p}_{k}}{M}_{k} \) with \( \left| v\right|  > {.1}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , we can use the previously-shown monotonicity of the integrand in \( \tau \) . As \( \tau  \rightarrow  0 \) , the Euclidean calculation of Section 16 shows that \( {\tau }^{-n/2}{e}^{-l\left( {\mathcal{L}{ex}{p}_{\tau }\left( v\right) ,\tau }\right) }\mathcal{J}\left( {v,\tau }\right)  \rightarrow  {2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| v\right| }^{2}} \) . Then for all \( \tau  > 0 \) and all \( v \in  {\Omega }_{\tau } \) ,

(26.12)

\[
{\tau }^{-n/2}{e}^{-l\left( {{\mathcal{L}}_{\tau }\left( v\right) ,\tau }\right) }\mathcal{J}\left( {v,\tau }\right)  \leq  {2}^{n}{e}^{-{\left| v\right| }^{2}},
\]

giving

(26.13)

\[
{\int }_{{T}_{{p}_{k}}{M}_{k} - B\left( {0,1{\epsilon }_{k}^{-1/2}}\right) }{\tau }^{-n/2}{e}^{-l\left( {{\mathcal{L}}_{\tau }\left( v\right) ,\tau }\right) }J\left( {v,\tau }\right) {\chi }_{\tau }{d}^{n}v \leq  {2}^{n}{\int }_{{T}_{{p}_{k}}{M}_{k} - B\left( {0,1{\epsilon }_{k}^{-1/2}}\right) }{e}^{-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}{d}^{n}v \leq  {e}^{-\frac{1}{{10}{\epsilon }_{k}}}
\]

for \( k \) large.

The conclusion is that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  = 0 \) . We now claim that there is a uniform positive lower bound on \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {t}_{k}\right) \) .

To estimate \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {t}_{k}\right) \) (where \( \tau  = {t}_{k} \) corresponds to \( t = 0 \) ), we choose a point \( {q}_{k} \) at time \( t = \frac{\bar{t}}{2} \) , i.e. at \( \tau  = {t}_{k} - \frac{\bar{t}}{2} \) , for which \( l\left( {{q}_{k},{t}_{k} - \bar{t}/2}\right)  \leq  \frac{n}{2} \) ; see Section 24. Then we consider the concatenation of a fixed curve \( {\gamma }_{1}^{\left( k\right) } : \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{k} - \bar{t}/2}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {M}_{k} \) , having \( {\gamma }_{1}^{\left( k\right) }\left( 0\right)  = {p}_{k} \) and \( {\gamma }_{1}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {{t}_{k} - \bar{t}/2}\right)  = {q}_{k} \) , with a fan of curves \( {\gamma }_{2}^{\left( k\right) } : \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - \bar{t}/2,{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {M}_{k} \) having \( {\gamma }_{2}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {{t}_{k} - \bar{t}/2}\right)  = {q}_{k} \) . Because of the uniformly bounded geometry in the spacetime region with \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{t}/2}\right\rbrack \) , we can get an upper bound in this way for \( l\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k}}\right) \) in a region around \( {q}_{k} \) . Integrating \( {e}^{-l\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k}}\right) } \) , we get a positive lower bound on \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {t}_{k}\right) \) that is uniform in \( k \) .

As \( {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2} \rightarrow  0 \) , the monotonicity of \( \widetilde{V} \) implies that \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {t}_{k}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) \) for large \( k \) , which is a contradiction.

Lemma 27.1. If \( \operatorname{Ric} \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) then for \( {t}_{1} > {t}_{0} \) ,

(27.2)

\[
\frac{{\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{1}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }{{\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) } \geq  {e}^{-\left( {n - 1}\right) K\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }.
\]

nodes.proof:
For any curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0, a}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) , we have(27.3)

\[
\text{ (27.3) }\frac{d}{dt}L\left( \gamma \right)  = \frac{d}{dt}{\int }_{0}^{a}\sqrt{\left\langle  \frac{d\gamma }{ds},\frac{d\gamma }{ds}\right\rangle  }{ds} =  - {\int }_{0}^{a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\frac{d\gamma }{ds},\frac{d\gamma }{ds}}\right) \frac{ds}{\left| \frac{d\gamma }{ds}\right| } \geq   - \left( {n - 1}\right) {KL}\left( \gamma \right) \text{ . }
\]

Integrating gives

(27.4)

\[
\frac{{\left. L\left( \gamma \right) \right| }_{{t}_{1}}}{{\left. L\left( \gamma \right) \right| }_{{t}_{0}}} \geq  {e}^{-\left( {n - 1}\right) K\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }.
\]

The lemma follows by taking \( \gamma \) to be a minimal geodesic at time \( {t}_{1} \) between \( {x}_{0} \) and \( {x}_{1} \) .

Remark 27.5. By a similar argument, if Ric \( \geq   - \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) then for \( {t}_{1} > {t}_{0} \) ,

(27.6)

\[
\frac{{\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{1}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }{{\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) } \leq  {e}^{\left( {n - 1}\right) K\left( {{t}_{1} - {t}_{0}}\right) }.
\]

We can write the conclusion of Lemma 27.1 as

(27.7)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  \geq   - \left( {n - 1}\right) K{\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) ,
\]

where the derivative is interpreted in the sense of forward difference quotients.

The estimate in Lemma 27.1 is multiplicative. We now give an estimate that is additive in the distance.

Lemma I.8.3(b)) Suppose \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  \geq  2{r}_{0} \) , and \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) for all \( x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right)  \cup  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{1},{r}_{0}}\right) \) . Then

nodes.proof:
If \( \gamma \) is a normalized minimal geodesic from \( {x}_{0} \) to \( {x}_{1} \) with velocity field \( X\left( s\right)  = \frac{d\gamma }{ds} \) then for any piecewise-smooth normal vector field \( V \) along \( \gamma \) that vanishes at the endpoints, the second variation formula gives

(27.10)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\left( {{\left| {\nabla }_{X}V\right| }^{2}+\langle R\left( {V, X}\right) V, X\rangle }\right) {ds} \geq  0.
\]

Let \( {\left\{  {e}_{i}\left( s\right) \right\}  }_{i = 1}^{n - 1} \) be a parallel orthonormal frame along \( \gamma \) that is perpendicular to \( X \) . Put \( {V}_{i}\left( s\right)  = f\left( s\right) {e}_{i}\left( s\right) \) , where

(27.11)

\[
f\left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} \frac{s}{{r}_{0}} & \text{ if }0 \leq  s \leq  {r}_{0}, \\  1 & \text{ if }{r}_{0} \leq  s \leq  d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - {r}_{0}, \\  \frac{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - s}{{r}_{0}} & \text{ if }d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - {r}_{0} \leq  s \leq  d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) . \end{array}\right.
\]

Then \( \left| {{\nabla }_{X}{V}_{i}}\right|  = \left| {{f}^{\prime }\left( s\right) }\right| \) and

(27.12)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }{\left| {\nabla }_{X}{V}_{i}\right| }^{2}{ds} = 2{\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\frac{1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}{ds} = \frac{2}{{r}_{0}}.
\]

Next,

(27.13)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\left\langle  {R\left( {{V}_{i}, X}\right) {V}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  {ds} = {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left\langle  {R\left( {{e}_{i}, X}\right) {e}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  {ds} +
\]

\[
{\int }_{{r}_{0}}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - {r}_{0}}\left\langle  {R\left( {{e}_{i}, X}\right) {e}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  {ds} +
\]

\[
{\int }_{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - {r}_{0}}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\frac{{\left( d\left( {x}_{0},{x}_{1}\right)  - s\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left\langle  {R\left( {{e}_{i}, X}\right) {e}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  {ds}.
\]

Then

(27.14)

\[
0 \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\left( {{\left| {\nabla }_{X}{V}_{i}\right| }^{2} + \left\langle  {R\left( {{V}_{i}, X}\right) {V}_{i}, X}\right\rangle  }\right) {ds}
\]

\[
= \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{r}_{0}} - {\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} + {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left( {1 - \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} +
\]

\[
{\int }_{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - {r}_{0}}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\left( {1 - \frac{{\left( d\left( {x}_{0},{x}_{1}\right)  - s\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds}.
\]

This gives

(27.15)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  =  - {\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds}
\]

\[
\geq   - \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{r}_{0}} - {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left( {1 - \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds}
\]

\[
- {\int }_{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - {r}_{0}}^{d\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\left( {1 - \frac{{\left( d\left( {x}_{0},{x}_{1}\right)  - s\right) }^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds}
\]

\[
\geq   - \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{r}_{0}} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) K \cdot  \frac{2}{3}{r}_{0},
\]

which proves the lemma.

nodes.content: Theorem 28.2. (cf. Theorem I.8.2) For any \( 0 < A < \infty \) , there is some \( \kappa  = \kappa \left( A\right)  > 0 \) with the following property. Let \( g\left( \cdot \right) \) be a Ricci flow solution defined for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{r}_{0}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) , having complete time slices and uniformly bounded sectional curvature. Suppose that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {{B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {A}^{-1}{r}_{0}^{n} \) and that \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{n{r}_{0}^{2}} \) for all \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{r}_{0}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Then the solution cannot be \( \kappa \) -collapsed on a scale less than \( {r}_{0} \) at any point \( \left( {x,{r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) with \( x \in  {B}_{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left( {{x}_{0}, A{r}_{0}}\right) \) .

Suppose that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {{B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0...

nodes.proof:
We follow the lines of the proof of Theorem 26.2. By scaling, we can take \( {r}_{0} = 1 \) . Choose \( x \in  M \) with \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{1}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  < A \) . Define the reduced volume \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) by means of curves starting at \( \left( {x,1}\right) \) . An effective lower bound on \( \widetilde{V}\left( 1\right) \) would imply that the solution is not \( \kappa \) -collapsed at \( \left( {x,1}\right) \) , on a scale less than 1, for an appropriate \( \kappa  > 0 \) .

We first note that the geometry of the region \( \left\{  {\left( {y, t}\right)  : {\operatorname{dist}}_{\frac{1}{2}}\left( {y,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{10}, t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is uniformly bounded. To see this, the upper sectional curvature bound implies that Ric \( \leq  1 \) , so the distance distortion estimate of Section 27 implies that \( {B}_{\frac{1}{2}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{1}{10}}\right)  \subset  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},1}\right) \) . In particular, \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{n} \) on the region. By Remark 27.5, if \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{\frac{1}{2}}\left( {y,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{10} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack \) then \( {B}_{0}\left( {y,\frac{1}{1000}}\right)  \subset  {B}_{t}\left( {y,\frac{1}{100}}\right) \) . The Bishop-Gromov inequality gives a lower bound for the time-zero volume of \( {B}_{0}\left( {y,\frac{1}{1000}}\right) \) , of the form \( {\operatorname{vol}}_{0}\left( {{B}_{0}\left( {y,\frac{1}{1000}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {C}_{1}\left( {n, A}\right) \) . The Ricci flow equation then gives a lower bound for the time- \( t \) volume of \( {B}_{0}\left( {y,\frac{1}{1000}}\right) \) , of the form \( {\operatorname{vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{0}\left( {y,\frac{1}{1000}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {C}_{2}\left( {n, A}\right) \) . Thus the time- \( t \) volume of \( {B}_{t}\left( {y,\frac{1}{100}}\right) \) satisfies \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {y,\frac{1}{100}}\right) }\right)  \geq \; {C}_{2}\left( {n, A}\right) \) . This, along with the uniform sectional curvature bound, implies that the region has uniformly bounded geometry.

If we have an effective upper bound on \( \mathop{\min }\limits_{y}l\left( {y,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \) , where \( y \) ranges over points that satisfy \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{\frac{1}{2}}\left( {y,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{10} \) , then we obtain a lower bound on \( \widetilde{V}\left( 1\right) \) . Thus it suffices to obtain an effective upper bound on \( \mathop{\min }\limits_{y}l\left( {y,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \) or, equivalently, on \( \mathop{\min }\limits_{y}\bar{L}\left( {y,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \) (as defined using \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics from \( \left( {x,1}\right) ) \) for \( y \) satisfying \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{\frac{1}{2}}\left( {y,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{10} \) . Applying the maximum principle to (24.1) gave an upper bound on \( \mathop{\inf }\limits_{M}\bar{L} \) . The idea is to spatially localize this estimate near \( {x}_{0} \) , by means of a radial function \( \phi \) .

Let \( \phi  = \phi \left( u\right) \) be a smooth function that equals 1 on \( \left( {-\infty ,\frac{1}{20}}\right) \) , equals infinity on \( \left( {\frac{1}{10},\infty }\right) \) and is increasing on \( \left( {\frac{1}{20},\frac{1}{10}}\right) \) , with

(28.4)

\[
2{\left( {\phi }^{\prime }\right) }^{2}/\phi  - {\phi }^{\prime \prime } \geq  \left( {{2A} + {100n}}\right) {\phi }^{\prime } - C\left( A\right) \phi
\]

for some constant \( C\left( A\right)  < \infty \) . To satisfy (28.4), it suffices to take \( \phi \left( u\right)  = \frac{1}{{e}^{\left( {{2A} + {100n}}\right) \left( {\frac{1}{10} - u}\right) } - 1} \) for \( u \) near \( \frac{1}{10} \) .

We claim that \( \bar{L} + {2n} + 1 \geq  1 \) for \( t \geq  \frac{1}{2} \) . To see this, from the end of Section 24,

(28.5)

\[
R\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right)  \geq   - \frac{n}{2\left( {1 - \tau }\right) }.
\]

Then for \( \bar{\tau } \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack \) ,

(28.6)

\[
L\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right)  \geq   - {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\frac{n}{2\left( {1 - \tau }\right) }{d\tau } \geq   - n{\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }{d\tau } =  - \frac{2n}{3}{\bar{\tau }}^{3/2}.
\]

Hence

(28.7)

\[
\bar{L}\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}L\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right)  \geq   - \frac{4n}{3}{\bar{\tau }}^{2} \geq   - \frac{n}{3},
\]

which proves the claim.

Now put

(28.8)

\[
h\left( {y, t}\right)  = \phi \left( {d\left( {y, t}\right)  - A\left( {{2t} - 1}\right) }\right) \left( {\bar{L}\left( {y,1 - t}\right)  + {2n} + 1}\right) ,
\]

where \( d\left( {y, t}\right)  = {\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {y,{x}_{0}}\right) \) . It follows from the above claim that \( h\left( {y, t}\right)  \geq  0 \) if \( t \geq  \frac{1}{2} \) . Also,

(28.9)

\[
\mathop{\min }\limits_{y}h\left( {y,1}\right)  \leq  h\left( {x,1}\right)  = \phi \left( {{\operatorname{dist}}_{1}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  - A}\right)  \cdot  \left( {{2n} + 1}\right)  = {2n} + 1.
\]

As \( \phi \) is infinite on \( \left( {\frac{1}{10},\infty }\right) \) and \( \bar{L}\left( {\cdot ,\frac{1}{2}}\right)  + {2n} + 1 \geq  1 \) , the minimum of \( h\left( {\cdot ,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \) is achieved at some \( y \) satisfying \( d\left( {y,\frac{1}{2}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{10} \) .

The calculations in I. 8 give

(28.10)

\[
\square h \geq   - \left( {{2n} + C\left( A\right) }\right) h
\]

at a minimum point of \( h \) , where \( \square  = {\partial }_{t} - \bigtriangleup \) . Then \( \frac{d}{dt}{h}_{\min }\left( t\right)  \geq   - \left( {{2n} + C\left( A\right) }\right) {h}_{\min }\left( t\right) \) , so

(28.11)

\[
{h}_{\min }\left( \frac{1}{2}\right)  \leq  {e}^{n + \frac{C\left( A\right) }{2}}{h}_{\min }\left( 1\right)  \leq  \left( {{2n} + 1}\right) {e}^{n + \frac{C\left( A\right) }{2}}.
\]

It follows that

(28.12)

\[
\mathop{\min }\limits_{{y : d\left( {y,\frac{1}{2}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{10}}}\bar{L}\left( {y,\frac{1}{2}}\right)  + {2n} + 1 \leq  \left( {{2n} + 1}\right) {e}^{n + \frac{C\left( A\right) }{2}}.
\]

This implies the theorem.

#### 29.I.9. Perelman's DIFFERENTIAL HARNACK INEQUALITY

This section is concerned with a localized version of the \( \mathcal{W} \) -functional. It is mainly used in I.10.

Let \( g\left( \cdot \right) \) be a Ricci flow solution on a manifold \( M \) , defined for \( t \in  \left( {a, b}\right) \) . Put \( \square  = {\partial }_{t} - \bigtriangleup \) . For \( {f}_{1},{f}_{2} \in  {C}_{c}^{\infty }\left( {\left( {a, b}\right)  \times  M}\right) \) , we have

(29.1)

\[
0 = {\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{d}{dt}{\int }_{M}{f}_{1}\left( {t, x}\right) {f}_{2}\left( {t, x}\right) {dVdt}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{M}\left( {\left( {{\partial }_{t} - \bigtriangleup }\right) {f}_{1}}\right) {f}_{2}{dV} + {\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{M}{f}_{1}\left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup  - R}\right) {f}_{2}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{M}\left( {\square {f}_{1}}\right) {f}_{2}{dV} - {\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{M}{f}_{1}{\square }^{ * }{f}_{2}{dV},
\]

where \( {\square }^{ * } =  - {\partial }_{t} - \bigtriangleup  + R \) . In this sense, \( {\square }^{ * } \) is the formal adjoint to \( \square \) .

Now suppose that the Ricci flow is defined for \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Suppose that

(29.2)

\[
u = {\left( 4\pi \left( T - t\right) \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}
\]

satisfies \( {\square }^{ * }u = 0 \) . Put

(29.3)

\[
v = \left\lbrack  {\left( {T - t}\right) \left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right)  + f - n}\right\rbrack  u.
\]

If \( M \) is compact then using (5.10),

(29.4)

\[
\mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}, f, T - t}\right)  = {\int }_{M}{vdV}.
\]

nodes.proof:
We note that the right-hand side of I.(9.1) should be multiplied by \( u \) .

To prove the proposition, we first claim that

(29.7)

\[
\frac{d\bigtriangleup }{dt} = 2{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}
\]

To see this, for \( {f}_{1},{f}_{2} \in  {C}_{c}^{\infty }\left( M\right) \) , we have

(29.8)

\[
{\int }_{M}{f}_{1}\bigtriangleup {f}_{2}{dV} =  - {\int }_{M}\left\langle  {d{f}_{1}, d{f}_{2}}\right\rangle  {dV}.
\]

Differentiating with respect to \( t \) gives

(29.9)

\[
\text{ 9.9) }{\int }_{M}{f}_{1}\frac{d\bigtriangleup }{dt}{f}_{2}{dV} - {\int }_{M}{f}_{1}\bigtriangleup {f}_{2}{RdV} =  - 2{\int }_{M}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {d{f}_{1}, d{f}_{2}}\right) {dV} + {\int }_{M}\left\langle  {d{f}_{1}, d{f}_{2}}\right\rangle  {RdV}\text{ , }
\]

so

(29.10)

\[
\frac{d\bigtriangleup }{dt}{f}_{2} - R\bigtriangleup {f}_{2} = 2{\nabla }_{i}\left( {{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{j}{f}_{2}}\right)  - {\nabla }_{i}\left( {R{\nabla }_{i}{f}_{2}}\right) .
\]

Then (29.7) follows from the traced second Bianchi identity.

Next, one can check that \( {\square }^{ * }u = 0 \) is equivalent to

(29.11)

\[
\left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup }\right) f = \frac{n}{2}\frac{1}{T - t} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R.
\]

Then one obtains

(29.12)

\[
\text{ (29.12) }{u}^{-1}{\square }^{ * }v =  - \left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup }\right) \left\lbrack  {\left( {T - t}\right) \left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right)  + f}\right\rbrack   -
\]

\[
2\left\langle  {\nabla \left\lbrack  {\left( {T - t}\right) \left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right)  + f}\right\rbrack  ,{u}^{-1}\nabla u}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= 2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R - \left( {T - t}\right) \left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup }\right) \left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right)
\]

\[
- \left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup }\right) f + 2\left( {T - t}\right) \left\langle  {\nabla \left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right) ,\nabla f}\right\rangle   + 2{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}.
\]

Now

(29.13)

\[
\left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup }\right) \left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right)  = 2\left( {{\partial }_{t}\bigtriangleup }\right) f + 2\bigtriangleup \left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup }\right) f
\]

\[
- \left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup }\right) {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + \left( {{\partial }_{t} + \bigtriangleup }\right) R
\]

\[
= 4{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f + 2\bigtriangleup \left( {{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R}\right)  - 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{df},{df}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\left\langle  {\nabla {f}_{t},\nabla f}\right\rangle   - \bigtriangleup {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + \bigtriangleup R + 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} + \bigtriangleup R
\]

\[
= 4{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f + 2\bigtriangleup {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{df},{df}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\langle \nabla \left( {-\bigtriangleup f + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R}\right) ,\nabla f\rangle  - \bigtriangleup {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Hence the term in \( {u}^{-1}{\square }^{ * }v \) proportionate to \( {\left( T - t\right) }^{-1} \) is

(29.14)

\[
- \frac{n}{2}\frac{1}{T - t}
\]

The term proportionate to \( {\left( T - t\right) }^{0} \) is

(29.15)

\[
2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R + 2{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} = 2\left( {\bigtriangleup f + R}\right) .
\]

The term proportionate to \( \left( {T - t}\right) \) is \( \left( {T - t}\right) \) times

(29.16)

\[
- 4{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - 2\bigtriangleup {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{df},{df}}\right)  +
\]

\[
2\left\langle  {\nabla \left( {-\bigtriangleup f + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R}\right) ,\nabla f}\right\rangle   + \bigtriangleup {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} +
\]

\[
2\left\langle  {\nabla \left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right) ,\nabla f}\right\rangle   =
\]

\[
- 4{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \bigtriangleup {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{df},{df}}\right)  + 2\langle \nabla \bigtriangleup f,\nabla f\rangle  - 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2} =
\]

\[
- 4{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - 2{\left| \operatorname{Hess}\left( f\right) \right| }^{2} - 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2}.
\]

Putting this together gives

(29.17)

\[
{\square }^{ * }v =  - 2\left( {T - t}\right) {\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\left( {T - t}\right) }{g}_{ij}\right| }^{2}u.
\]

This proves the proposition.

nodes.content: Theorem 30.1. (cf. Theorem I.10.1) For every \( \alpha  > 0 \) there exist \( \delta ,\epsilon  > 0 \) with the following property. Suppose that we have a smooth pointed Ricci flow solution \( \left( {M,\left( {{x}_{0},0}\right) , g\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) defined for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\left( \epsilon {r}_{0}\right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) , such that each time slice is complete. Lemma 31.1. (cf. Claim 1 of I.10.1) For any \( A > 0 \) , if \( g\left( \cdot \right) \) is a Ricci flow solution for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\epsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) , with \( {A\epsilon } < \frac{1}{100n} \) , and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \alpha {t}^{-1} + {\epsilon }^{-2} \) for some \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) satisfying \( t \in  \left( {0,{\epsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) and \( d\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \epsilon \) , then one can find \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \in  {M}_{\alpha } \) with \( \bar{t} \in  \left( {0,{\epsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) and \( d\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  < \left( {{2A} + 1}\right) \epsilon \) , such that

(31.2)

\[
\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right) }\right|  \leq  4\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) }\right|
\]

whenever

(31.3)

\[
\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \in  {M}_{\alpha },\;{t}^{\prime } \in  (0,\bar{t}\rbrack ,\;d\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  d\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  + A{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) .
\]

nodes.proof:
The proof is by a point selection argument as in Appendix H. By assumption, there is a point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) satisfying \( t \in  \left( {0,{\epsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack  , d\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \epsilon \) and \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \geq  \alpha {t}^{-1} + {\epsilon }^{-2} \) . Clearly \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {M}_{\alpha } \) . Define points \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) inductively as follows. First, \( \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  = \left( {x, t}\right) \) . Next, suppose that \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) is constructed but cannot be taken for \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) . Then there is some point \( \left( {{x}_{k + 1},{t}_{k + 1}}\right)  \in  {M}_{\alpha } \) such that \( 0 < {t}_{k + 1} \leq  {t}_{k}, d\left( {{x}_{k + 1},{t}_{k + 1}}\right)  \leq  d\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  + A{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) and \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {{x}_{k + 1},{t}_{k + 1}}\right)  > 4\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) . Continuing in this way, the point \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) constructed has \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \geq  {4}^{k - 1}\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  \geq  {4}^{k - 1}{\epsilon }^{-2} \) . Then

(31.4)

\[
d\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \leq  d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  + A{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  + \ldots  + A{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {{x}_{k - 1},{t}_{k - 1}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \epsilon  + {2A}{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  \leq  \left( {{2A} + 1}\right) \epsilon .
\]

As the solution is smooth, the induction process must terminate after a finite number of steps and the last value \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) can be taken for \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
We first claim that if \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) satisfies \( \bar{t} - \frac{1}{2}\alpha {Q}^{-1} \leq  {t}^{\prime } \leq  \bar{t} \) and \( d\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  d\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  + A{Q}^{-1/2} \) then \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  {4Q} \) . To see this, if \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \in  {M}_{\alpha } \) then it is true by Lemma 31.1. If \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \notin  {M}_{\alpha } \) then \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  < \alpha {\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }^{-1} \) . As \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \in  {M}_{\alpha } \) , we know that \( Q \geq  \alpha {\bar{t}}^{-1} \) . Then \( {t}^{\prime } \geq  \bar{t} - \frac{1}{2}\alpha {Q}^{-1} \geq  \frac{1}{2}\bar{t} \) and so \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  < {2\alpha }{\bar{t}}^{-1} \leq  {2Q} \) .

Thus we have a uniform curvature bound on the time- \( {t}^{\prime } \) distance ball \( B\left( {{x}_{0}, d\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  + }\right. \; \left. {A{Q}^{-1/2}}\right) \) , provided that \( \bar{t} = \frac{1}{2}\alpha {Q}^{-1} \leq  {t}^{\prime } \leq  \bar{t} \) . We now claim that the time- \( \bar{t} \) ball \( B\left( {{x}_{0}, d\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  + \frac{1}{10}A{Q}^{-1/2}}\right) \) lies in the time- \( {t}^{\prime } \) distance ball \( B\left( {{x}_{0}, d\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  + A{Q}^{-1/2}}\right) \) . To see this, applying Lemma 27.8 with \( {r}_{0} = \frac{1}{100}A{Q}^{-1/2} \) and the above curvature bound, if \( {x}^{\prime } \) is in the time- \( \bar{t} \) ball \( B\left( {{x}_{0}, d\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  + \frac{1}{10}A{Q}^{-1/2}}\right) \) then

(32.4)

\[
{\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}^{\prime }}\right)  - {\operatorname{dist}}_{\bar{t}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}\alpha {Q}^{-1} \cdot  2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3} \cdot  {4Q}\left( {\frac{1}{100}A{Q}^{-1/2}}\right)  + {100}{A}^{-1}{Q}^{1/2}}\right) .
\]

Assuming that \( A \) is sufficiently large (we’ll take \( A \rightarrow  \infty \) later) and using the fact that \( \alpha  < \frac{1}{100n} \) , it follows that \( d\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  d\left( {{x}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}A{Q}^{-1/2} \leq  d\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  + A{Q}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , which is what we want to show. We note that the argument also shows that is indeed self-consistent to use the curvature bounds in the application of Lemma 27.8.

Now suppose that \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) satisfies (32.3). ## 33. CLAIM 3 OF I.10.1. An upper BOUND ON THE INTEGRAL OF \( v \)

We first make some remarks about the fundamental solution to the backward heat equation. Let \( \left( {M,\left( {\bar{x}, b}\right) , g\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) be a smooth one-parameter family of complete pointed Riemannian manifolds, parametrized by \( t \in  (a, b\rbrack \) . The fundamental solution \( u \) of the backward heat equation is a positive solution of \( {\square }^{ * }u = 0 \) on \( M \times  \left( {a, b}\right) \) such that \( u\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) converges to \( {\delta }_{\bar{x}} \) in the distributional sense, as \( t \rightarrow  {b}^{ - } \) . It is constructed as follows (cf. [26, Section 3]). Let \( {\left\{  {D}_{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{\infty } \) be an exhaustion of \( M \) by an increasing sequence of smooth compact codimension-zero submanifolds-with-boundary containing \( \bar{x} \) in the interior. Let \( {u}^{\left( i\right) } \) be the unique solution of \( {\square }^{ * }{u}^{\left( i\right) } = 0 \) on \( {D}_{i} \times  \left( {a, b}\right) \) with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {b}^{ - }}}{u}^{\left( i\right) }\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\delta }_{\bar{x}}\left( x\right) \) , as constructed using Dirichlet boundary conditions on \( {D}_{i} \) . If \( {D}_{i} \subset  {D}_{j} \) then \( {u}^{\left( i\right) } \leq  {u}^{\left( j\right) } \) on \( {D}_{i} \) , using the maximum principle as in [26, Lemma 3.1]. Then the fundamental solution is defined to be the limit \( u = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}{u}^{\left( i\right) } \) , with smooth convergence on compact subsets of \( M \times  \left( {a, b}\right) \) . The function \( u \) is independent of the choice of exhaustion sequence \( {\left\{  {D}_{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{\infty } \) . For any \( t \in  \left( {a, b}\right) \) , we have \( {\int }_{M}u\left( {x, t}\right) {dV}\left( x\right)  \leq  1 \) . If \( {\int }_{M}u\left( {x, t}\right) {dV}\left( x\right)  = 1 \) for all \( t \) then we say that \( \left( {M,\left( {\bar{x}, b}\right) , g\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) is stochastically complete for \( {\square }^{ * } \) . This will be the case if one has bounded curvature on compact time intervals, but need not be the case in general.

nodes.proof:
Suppose that the claim is not true. After passing to a subsequence, we can assume that for any choice of \( {\widetilde{t}}_{k} \) , \( \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\int }_{{B}_{k}}{v}_{k}d{V}_{k} \geq  0 \) .

Consider the pointed solution \( \left( {{M}_{k},\left( {{\bar{x}}_{k},{\bar{t}}_{k}}\right) ,{g}_{k}\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) parabolically rescaled by \( {Q}_{k} \) . Suppose first that there is a subsequence so that the injectivity radii of the scaled metrics at \( \left( {{\bar{x}}_{k},{\bar{t}}_{k}}\right) \) are bounded away from zero. Since \( {A}_{k} \rightarrow  \infty \) , we can use Lemma 32.1 and Appendix E to take a subsequence that converges to a complete Ricci flow solution \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) ,{g}_{\infty }\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) on a time interval \( \left( {{\bar{t}}_{\infty } - \frac{1}{2}\alpha ,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) , with \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  4 \) and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right)  = 1 \) . Consider the fundamental solution \( {u}_{\infty } \) of \( {\square }^{ * } \) on \( {M}_{\infty } \) with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {\bar{t}}_{\infty }^{ - }}}{u}_{\infty }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = {\delta }_{{\bar{x}}_{\infty }}\left( {x}_{\infty }\right) \) . As before, let \( {u}_{k} \) be the fundamental solution of \( {\square }^{ * } \) on \( {M}_{k} \) with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {\bar{t}}_{k}^{ - }}}{u}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k}, t}\right)  = {\delta }_{{\bar{x}}_{k}}\left( {x}_{k}\right) \) . In view of the pointed convergence of the rescalings of \( \left( {{M}_{k},\left( {{\bar{x}}_{k},{\bar{t}}_{k}}\right) ,{g}_{k}\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) to \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) ,{g}_{\infty }\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) , Lemma 33.1 implies that after passing to a further subsequence we can ensure that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{u}_{k} = {u}_{\infty } \) , with smooth convergence on compact subsets of \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left( {{\bar{t}}_{\infty } - \frac{1}{2}\alpha ,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) . (The curvature bounds on \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) ,{g}_{\infty }\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) ensure that it is stochastically complete for \( {\square }^{ * } \) .) From Corollary 29.21, \( {v}_{\infty } \leq  0 \) . Note that we are applying Corollary 29.21 on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left( {{\bar{t}}_{\infty } - \frac{1}{2}\alpha ,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) , where we have the curvature bounds needed to use the maximum principle.

Given \( {\widetilde{t}}_{\infty } \in  \left( {{\bar{t}}_{\infty } - \frac{1}{2}\alpha ,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) , let \( {B}_{\infty } \) be the time- \( {\widetilde{t}}_{\infty } \) ball of radius \( \sqrt{{\bar{t}}_{\infty } - {\widetilde{t}}_{\infty }} \) centered at \( {\bar{x}}_{\infty } \) . In view of the smooth convergence \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{u}_{k} = {u}_{\infty } \) on compact subsets of \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left( {{\bar{t}}_{\infty } - }\right. \; \left. {\frac{1}{2}\alpha ,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) , it follows that \( {\int }_{{B}_{\infty }}{v}_{\infty }d{V}_{\infty } = 0 \) at time \( {\widetilde{t}}_{\infty } \) , so \( {v}_{\infty } \) vanishes on \( {B}_{\infty } \) at time \( {\widetilde{t}}_{\infty } \) . Let \( h \) be a solution to \( \square h = 0 \) on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {{\widetilde{t}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) with \( h\left( {\cdot ,{\widetilde{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) a nonnegative nonzero function supported in \( {B}_{\infty } \) . As in the proof of Corollary 29.21, \( {\int }_{{M}_{\infty }}h{v}_{\infty }d{V}_{\infty } \) is nondecreasing in \( t \) and vanishes for \( t = {\widetilde{t}}_{\infty } \) and \( t \rightarrow  {\bar{t}}_{\infty } \) . Thus \( {\int }_{{M}_{\infty }}h{v}_{\infty }d{V}_{\infty } \) vanishes for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\widetilde{t}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) . However, for \( t \in  \left( {{\widetilde{t}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) , h \) is strictly positive and \( {v}_{\infty } \) is nonpositive. Thus \( {v}_{\infty } \) vanishes on \( {M}_{\infty } \) for all \( t \in  \left( {{\widetilde{t}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) , and so

(33.5)

\[
\operatorname{Ric}\left( {g}_{\infty }\right)  + \text{ Hess }{f}_{\infty } - \frac{1}{2\left( {\bar{t} - t}\right) }{g}_{\infty } = 0.
\]

on this interval. We know that \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  4 \) on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left( {{\bar{t}}_{\infty } - \frac{1}{2}\alpha ,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) . From the evolution equation,

(33.6)

\[
\frac{d{g}_{\infty }}{dt} =  - 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {g}_{\infty }\right)  = 2\operatorname{Hess}{f}_{\infty } - \frac{1}{\bar{t} - t}{g}_{\infty }.
\]

It follows that the supremal and infimal sectional curvatures of \( {g}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) go like \( {\left( {\bar{t}}_{\infty } - t\right) }^{-1} \) . Hence \( {g}_{\infty } \) is flat, which contradicts the fact that \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right)  = 1 \) .

Suppose now that there is a subsequence so that the injectivity radii of the scaled metrics at \( \left( {{\bar{x}}_{k},{\bar{t}}_{k}}\right) \) tend to zero. Parabolically rescale \( \left( {{M}_{k},\left( {{\bar{x}}_{k},{\bar{t}}_{k}}\right) ,{g}_{k}\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) further so that the injectivity radius becomes one. After passing to a subsequence we will have convergence to a flat Ricci flow solution \( ( - \infty ,0\rbrack  \times  L \) . The complete flat manifold \( L \) can be described as the total space of a flat orthogonal \( {\mathbb{R}}^{m} \) -bundle over a flat compact manifold \( C \) . After separating variables, the fundamental solution \( {u}_{\infty } \) on \( L \) will be Gaussian in the fiber directions and will decay exponentially fast to a constant in the base directions, i.e. \( u\left( {x,\tau }\right)  \sim  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-m/2}{e}^{-\frac{{\left| x\right| }^{2}}{4\tau }}\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}\left( C\right) } \) , where \( \left| x\right| \) is the fiber norm. With this for \( {u}_{\infty } \) , one finds that \( {v}_{\infty } = \left( {m - n}\right) \left( {1 + \frac{1}{2}\ln \left( {4\pi \tau }\right) }\right) {u}_{\infty } \) . With \( {B}_{\tau } \) the ball around a basepoint of radius \( \sqrt{\tau } \) , the integral of \( u \) over \( {B}_{\tau } \) has a positive limit as \( \tau  \rightarrow  \infty \) , and so \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  \infty }}{\int }_{{B}_{\tau }}{v}_{\infty }d{V}_{\infty } =  - \infty \) . Then there are times \( {\widetilde{t}}_{k} \in  \left\lbrack  {{\bar{t}}_{k} - \frac{1}{2}\alpha {Q}_{k}^{-1},{\bar{t}}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) so that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\int }_{{B}_{k}}{v}_{k}d{V}_{k} =  - \infty \) , which is a contradiction.

## 34. THEOREM I.10.1. Proof of the PSEUDOLOCALITY THEOREM

Continuing with the proof of Theorem 30.1, we now use Lemma 33.4 to get a contradiction to a log Sobolev inequality. For simplicity of notation, we drop the subscript \( k \) and deal with a particular \( \left( {{M}_{k},\left( {{\bar{x}}_{k},{\bar{t}}_{k}}\right) ,{g}_{k}\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) for \( k \) large. Define a smooth function \( \phi \) on \( \mathbb{R} \) which is one on \( ( - \infty ,1\rbrack \) , decreasing on \( \left\lbrack  {1,2}\right\rbrack \) and zero on \( \left\lbrack  {2,\infty }\right\rbrack \) , with \( {\phi }^{\prime \prime } \geq   - {10}{\phi }^{\prime } \) and \( {\left( {\phi }^{\prime }\right) }^{2} \leq  {10\phi } \) . To construct \( \phi \) we can take the function which is 1 on \( ( - \infty ,1\rbrack ,1 - 2{\left( x - 1\right) }^{2} \) on \( \left\lbrack  {1,3/2}\right\rbrack \) , \( 2{\left( x - 2\right) }^{2} \) on \( \left\lbrack  {3/2,2}\right\rbrack \) and 0 on \( \lbrack 2,\infty ) \) , and smooth it slightly.

Put \( \widetilde{d}\left( {y, t}\right)  = d\left( {y, t}\right)  + {200n}\sqrt{t} \) . We claim that if \( {10A\epsilon } \leq  \widetilde{d}\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  {20A\epsilon } \) then \( {d}_{t}\left( {y, t}\right)  - \; \bigtriangleup d\left( {y, t}\right)  + \frac{100n}{\sqrt{t}} \geq  0 \) . To see this, recalling that \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\epsilon }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) , if \( {10A\epsilon } \leq  \widetilde{d}\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  {20A\epsilon } \) and \( A \) is sufficiently large then \( {9A\epsilon } \leq  d\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  {21A\epsilon } \) . We apply Lemma 27.18 with the parameter \( {r}_{0} \) of Lemma 27.18 equal to \( \sqrt{t} \) . As \( {r}_{0} \leq  \epsilon \) , we have \( y \notin  B\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) . From (33.3), on \( B\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) we have \( \left| \operatorname{Rm}\right| \left( {\cdot , t}\right)  \leq  \alpha {t}^{-1} + 2{\epsilon }^{-2} \) . Then from Lemma 27.18, at \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) we have

(34.1)

\[
{d}_{t} - \bigtriangleup d \geq   - \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}\left( {\alpha {t}^{-1} + 2{\epsilon }^{-2}}\right) {t}^{1/2} + {t}^{-1/2}}\right)
\]

\[
=  - \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + \frac{2}{3}\alpha  + \frac{4}{3}{\epsilon }^{-2}t}\right) {t}^{-1/2}.
\]

It follows that \( {d}_{t} - \bigtriangleup d + \frac{100n}{\sqrt{t}} \geq  0 \) .

Now put \( h\left( {y, t}\right)  = \phi \left( \frac{\widetilde{d}\left( {y, t}\right) }{10A\epsilon }\right) \) . Then \( \square h = \frac{1}{10A\epsilon }\left( {{d}_{t} - \bigtriangleup d + \frac{100n}{\sqrt{t}}}\right) {\phi }^{\prime } - \frac{1}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}{\phi }^{\prime \prime } \) , where the arguments of \( {\phi }^{\prime } \) and \( {\phi }^{\prime \prime } \) are \( \frac{\widetilde{d}\left( {y, t}\right) }{10A\epsilon } \) . Where \( {\phi }^{\prime } \neq  0 \) , we have \( {d}_{t} - \bigtriangleup d + \frac{100n}{\sqrt{t}} \geq  0 \) . The fundamental solution \( u\left( {x, t}\right)  = {\left( 4\pi \left( \bar{t} - t\right) \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f\left( {x, t}\right) } \) of \( {\square }^{ * } \) is positive for \( t \in  \lbrack 0,\bar{t}) \) and we have \( {\int }_{M}{udV} \leq  1 \) for all \( t \) . (Recall that we are not assuming stochastic completeness.)

Then(34.2)

\[
{\left( {\int }_{M}hudV\right) }_{t} = {\int }_{M}\left( {\left( {\square h}\right) u - h{\square }^{ * }u}\right) {dV} = {\int }_{M}\left( {\square h}\right) {udV} \leq   - \frac{1}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}{\int }_{M}{\phi }^{\prime \prime }{udV}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{10}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}{\int }_{M}{\phi udV} \leq  \frac{10}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}{\int }_{M}{udV} \leq  \frac{10}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}.
\]

Hence

(34.3)

\[
{\left. {\int }_{M}hudV\right| }_{t = 0} \geq  {\left. {\int }_{M}hudV\right| }_{t = \bar{t}} - \frac{\bar{t}}{{\left( A\epsilon \right) }^{2}} \geq  1 - {A}^{-2}.
\]

Similarly, using Proposition 29.5 and Corollary 29.21,(34.4)

\[
{\left( -{\int }_{M}hvdV\right) }_{t} =  - {\int }_{M}\left( {\left( {\square h}\right) v - h{\square }^{ * }v}\right) {dV} \leq   - {\int }_{M}\left( {\square h}\right) {vdV}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}{\int }_{M}{\phi }^{\prime \prime }{vdV} \leq   - \frac{10}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}{\int }_{M}{\phi vdV} =  - \frac{10}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}{\int }_{M}{hvdV}.
\]

Consider the time \( \widetilde{t} \) of Lemma 33.4. As \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \in  {M}_{\alpha },\widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t}/2,\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . Then \( \sqrt{\bar{t} - \widetilde{t}} \leq  {2}^{-1/2}\epsilon \) and so for large \( A, h \) will be one on the ball \( B \) at time \( \widetilde{t} \) of radius \( \sqrt{\bar{t} - \widetilde{t}} \) centered at \( \bar{x} \) , using (32.4). Then at time \( \widetilde{t} \) ,

(34.5)

\[
- {\int }_{M}{hvdV} \geq   - {\int }_{B}{vdV} \geq  \beta
\]

Thus

(34.6)

\[
- {\left. {\int }_{M}hvdV\right| }_{t = 0} \geq  \beta {e}^{-\frac{\bar{t}}{{\left( A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}} \geq  \beta {e}^{-\frac{\bar{t}}{{\left( A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}} \geq  \beta \left( {1 - \frac{\bar{t}}{{\left( A\epsilon \right) }^{2}}}\right)  \geq  \beta \left( {1 - {A}^{-2}}\right) .
\]

Working at time 0, put \( \widetilde{u} = {hu} \) and \( \widetilde{f} = f - \log h \) . In what follows we implicitly integrate over \( \operatorname{supp}\left( h\right) \) . We have

(34.7)

\[
\beta \left( {1 - {A}^{-2}}\right)  \leq   - {\int }_{M}{hvdV} = {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\left( {-2\bigtriangleup f + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R}\right) \bar{t} - f + n}\right\rbrack  {hudV}.
\]

We claim that

(34.8)

\[
{\int }_{M}\left( {-{2\Delta f} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) h{e}^{-f}{dV} = {\int }_{M}\left( {-{\left| \nabla \widetilde{f}\right| }^{2} + \frac{{\left| \nabla h\right| }^{2}}{{h}^{2}}}\right) h{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

This follows from

(34.9)

\[
{\int }_{M}\left( {-{2\Delta f} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) h{e}^{-f}{dV} = {\int }_{M}\left( {2\left\langle  {\nabla f,\nabla \left( {h{e}^{-f}}\right) }\right\rangle   + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}h{e}^{-f}}\right) {dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left( {2\left\langle  {\nabla f,\frac{\nabla h}{h} - \nabla f}\right\rangle   + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) h{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\langle  {\nabla f,2\frac{\nabla h}{h} - \nabla f}\right\rangle  h{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\langle  {\nabla \widetilde{f} + \frac{\nabla h}{h},\frac{\nabla h}{h} - \nabla \widetilde{f}}\right\rangle  h{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left( {-{\left| \nabla \widetilde{f}\right| }^{2} + \frac{{\left| \nabla h\right| }^{2}}{{h}^{2}}}\right) h{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

Then

(34.10)

\[
{\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\left( {-{2\Delta f} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R}\right) \bar{t} - f + n}\right\rbrack  {hudV} =
\]

\[
{\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-\bar{t}{\left| \nabla \widetilde{f}\right| }^{2} - \widetilde{f} + n}\right\rbrack  \widetilde{u}{dV} + {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\bar{t}\left( {{\left| \nabla h\right| }^{2}/h - {Rh}}\right)  - h\log h}\right\rbrack  {udV}.
\]

Next, \( \frac{{\left| \nabla h\right| }^{2}}{h} \leq  \frac{10}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}} \) and \( - {Rh} \leq  1 \) (from the assumed lower bound on \( R \) at time zero). Then

(34.11)

\[
{\int }_{M}\bar{t}\left( {\frac{{\left| \nabla h\right| }^{2}}{h} - {Rh}}\right) {udV} \leq  {\epsilon }^{2}\left( {\frac{10}{{\left( {10}A\epsilon \right) }^{2}} + 1}\right)  \leq  {A}^{-2} + {\epsilon }^{2}.
\]

Also,

(34.12)

\[
- {\int }_{M}{uh}\log {hdV} =  - {\int }_{B\left( {{x}_{0},{20A\epsilon }}\right)  - B\left( {{x}_{0},{10A\epsilon }}\right) }{uh}\log {hdV} \leq  {\int }_{M - B\left( {{x}_{0},{10A\epsilon }}\right) }{udV}
\]

\[
\leq  1 - {\int }_{B\left( {{x}_{0},{10A\epsilon }}\right) }{udV}
\]

Putting \( \bar{h}\left( y\right)  = \phi \left( \frac{d\left( y\right) }{5A\epsilon }\right) \) , a result similar to (34.3) shows that

(34.13)

\[
{\int }_{B\left( {{x}_{0},{10A\epsilon }}\right) }{udV} \geq  {\int }_{M}\bar{h}{udV} \geq  1 - c{A}^{-2}
\]

for an appropriate constant \( c \) . Putting this together gives

(34.14)

\[
\beta \left( {1 - {A}^{-2}}\right)  \leq  {\int }_{M}\left( {-\bar{t}{\left| \nabla \widetilde{f}\right| }^{2} - \widetilde{f} + n}\right) \widetilde{u}{dV} + \left( {1 + c}\right) {A}^{-2} + {\epsilon }^{2}.
\]

Put \( \widehat{g} = \frac{1}{2\bar{t}}g,\widehat{u} = {\left( 2\bar{t}\right) }^{\frac{n}{2}}\widetilde{u} \) and define \( \widehat{f} \) by \( \widehat{u} = {\left( 2\pi \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\widehat{f}} \) . From (34.3) and (34.14), if we restore the subscript \( k \) then \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\int }_{M}{\widehat{u}}_{k}d{\widehat{V}}_{k} = 1 \) and for large \( k \) ,

(34.15)

\[
\frac{1}{2}\beta  \leq  {\int }_{{M}_{k}}\left( {-\frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla {\widehat{f}}_{k}\right| }^{2} - {\widehat{f}}_{k} + n}\right) {\widehat{u}}_{k}d{\widehat{V}}_{k}.
\]

If we normalize \( {\widehat{u}}_{k} \) by putting \( {U}_{k} = \frac{{\widehat{u}}_{k}}{{\int }_{{M}_{k}}{\widehat{u}}_{k}d{\widehat{V}}_{k}} \) , and define \( {F}_{k} \) by \( {U}_{k} = {\left( 2\pi \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-{F}_{k}} \) , then for large \( k \) , we also have

(34.16)

\[
\frac{1}{2}\beta  \leq  {\int }_{{M}_{k}}\left( {-\frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla {F}_{k}\right| }^{2} - {F}_{k} + n}\right) {U}_{k}d{\widehat{V}}_{k}.
\]

On the other hand, the logarithmic Sobolev inequality for \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\left\lbrack  {8,\mathrm{I}.\left( 8\right) }\right\rbrack \) says that

(34.17)

\[
{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}\left( {-\frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} - F + n}\right) {UdV} \leq  0,
\]

provided that the compactly-supported function \( U = {\left( 2\pi \right) }^{-n/2}{e}^{-F} \) satisfies \( {\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}{UdV} = 1 \) . As was mentioned to us by Peter Topping, one can get a sharper inequality by applying (34.17) to the rescaled function \( {U}_{c}\left( x\right)  = {c}^{n}U\left( {cx}\right) \) and optimizing with respect to \( c \) . The result is

(34.18)

\[
{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}{\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2}{UdV} \geq  n{e}^{1 - \frac{2}{n}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}{FUdV}}
\]

Given this inequality on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , one can use a symmetrization argument to prove the same inequality for a compactly-supported function on any complete Riemannian manifold, provided that the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality holds for domains in the support of \( U \) . See, for example,[48, Proposition 4.1] which gives the symmetrization argument for (34.17), attributing it to Perelman. Again using the inequality for \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , if instead we have \( \operatorname{vol}{\left( \partial \Omega \right) }^{n} \geq  \left( {1 - {\delta }_{k}}\right) {c}_{n}\operatorname{vol}{\left( \Omega \right) }^{n - 1} \) for domains \( \Omega  \subset  \operatorname{supp}\left( {U}_{k}\right) \) then the symmetrization argument gives

(34.19)

\[
{\int }_{{M}_{k}}{\left| \nabla {F}_{k}\right| }^{2}{U}_{k}d{\widehat{V}}_{k} \geq  {\left( 1 - {\delta }_{k}\right) }^{\frac{2}{n}}n{e}^{1 - \frac{2}{n}{\int }_{{M}_{k}}{F}_{k}{U}_{k}d{\widehat{V}}_{k}}.
\]

Equations (34.16) and (34.19) imply that

(34.20)

\[
\frac{n}{2}\left( {{\left( 1 - {\delta }_{k}\right) }^{\frac{2}{n}}{e}^{1 - \frac{2}{n}{\int }_{{M}_{k}}{F}_{k}{U}_{k}d{\widehat{V}}_{k}} - 1 - \left( {1 - \frac{2}{n}{\int }_{{M}_{k}}{F}_{k}{U}_{k}d{\widehat{V}}_{k}}\right) }\right)  \leq   - \frac{\beta }{2}.
\]

However,

(34.21)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathop{\inf }\limits_{{x \in  \mathbb{R}}}\left( {{\left( 1 - {\delta }_{k}\right) }^{\frac{2}{n}}{e}^{x} - 1 - x}\right)  = 0.
\]

This is a contradiction.

nodes.proof:
Choose \( \alpha  > 0 \) . Let \( \delta \) and \( \epsilon \) be the parameters of Theorem 30.1. Consider Ricci flow \( g\left( \cdot \right) \) starting from \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) . Let \( T > 0 \) be the maximal number so that a smooth flow exists for \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . If \( T < \infty \) then \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  {T}^{ - }}}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  = \infty \) . It follows from Theorem 30.1 that \( T > {\left( \epsilon {r}_{0}\right) }^{2} \) . Put \( \widehat{g} = g\left( {\left( \epsilon {r}_{0}\right) }^{2}\right) \) . Theorem 30.1 gives a uniform double-sided sectional curvature bound on \( \left( {M,\widehat{g}}\right) \) . Corollary 35.1 gives a uniform lower bound on the volumes of \( \left( {\epsilon {r}_{0}}\right) \) -balls in \( \left( {M,\widehat{g}}\right) \) . Let \( {\left\{  {x}_{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{N} \) be a maximal \( \left( {{2\epsilon }{r}_{0}}\right) \) -separated net in \( \left( {M,\widehat{g}}\right) \) .

From the lower bound \( R \geq   - {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) and the maximum principle, we have \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq   - {r}_{0}^{-2} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\left( \epsilon {r}_{0}\right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Then the Ricci flow equation gives a uniform upper bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {M,\widehat{g}}\right) \) . This implies a uniform upper bound on \( N \) or, equivalently, a uniform upper bound on \( \operatorname{diam}\left( {M,\widehat{g}}\right) \) . The theorem now follows from the diffeomorphism finiteness of \( n \) -dimensional Riemannian manifolds with double-sided sectional curvature bounds, upper bounds on diameter and lower bounds on volume.

Definition 38.1. Given \( \kappa  > 0 \) , a \( \kappa \) -solution is a Ricci flow solution \( \left( {M, g\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) that is defined on a time interval of the form \( \left( {-\infty , C}\right) \) (or \( \left( {-\infty , C\rbrack }\right) \) such that

- The curvature \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right| \) is bounded on each compact time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack   \subset  \left( {-\infty , C}\right) \) (or \( \left( {-\infty , C\rbrack }\right) \) , and each time slice \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) is complete.

- The curvature operator is nonnegative and the scalar curvature is everywhere positive.

- The Ricci flow is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed at all scales.

By abuse of terminology, we may sometimes write that " \( \left( {M, g\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) is a \( \kappa \) -solution" if it is a \( \kappa \) -solution for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) .

From Appendix F, \( {R}_{t} \geq  0 \) for an ancient solution. This implies the essential equivalence of the notions of \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing in Definitions 13.14 and 26.1, when restricted to ancient solutions. Namely, if a solution is \( \kappa \) -collapsed in the sense of Definition 26.1 then it is automatically \( \kappa \) -collapsed in the sense of Definition 13.14. Conversely, if a time- \( {t}_{0} \) slice of an ancient solution is collapsed in the sense of Definition 13.14 then the fact that \( {R}_{t} \geq  0 \) , together with bounds on distance distortion, implies that it is collapsed in the sense of Definition 26.1 (possibly for a different value of \( \kappa \) ).

##### 39.I.11.2. Asymptotic solitons

This section shows that every \( \kappa \) -solution has a gradient shrinking soliton buried inside of it, in an asymptotic sense as \( t \rightarrow   - \infty \) . Such a soliton will be called an asymptotic soliton.

nodes.proof:
Equation (25.5) implies that \( {\left| \nabla {l}^{1/2}\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{C}{4\tau } \) , and so

(39.2)

\[
\left| {{l}^{1/2}\left( {q,\tau }\right)  - {l}^{1/2}\left( {q\left( \tau \right) ,\tau }\right) }\right|  \leq  \sqrt{\frac{C}{4\tau }}{\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }\left( {q, q\left( \tau \right) }\right) .
\]

We apply this estimate initially at some fixed time \( \tau  = \bar{\tau } \) , to obtain

(39.3)

\[
l\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right)  \leq  {\left( \sqrt{\frac{C}{4\bar{\tau }}}{\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0} - \bar{\tau }}\left( q, q\left( \bar{\tau }\right) \right)  + \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}}\right) }^{2}.
\]

From (18.13), (18.14) and (25.5),

(39.4)

\[
{\partial }_{\tau }l = \frac{R}{2} - \frac{{\left| \nabla l\right| }^{2}}{2} - \frac{l}{2\tau } \geq   - \frac{\left( {1 + C}\right) l}{2\tau }.
\]

This implies that for \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{2}\bar{\tau },\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) ,

(39.5)

\[
l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  \leq  {\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{\tau }\right) }^{\frac{1 + C}{2}}{\left( \sqrt{\frac{C}{4\bar{\tau }}}{\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0} - \bar{\tau }}\left( q, q\left( \bar{\tau }\right) \right)  + \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}}\right) }^{2}.
\]

Also from (25.5), we have \( {\tau R} \leq  {Cl} \) . Then we can plug in the previous bound on \( l \) to get an upper bound on \( {\tau R} \) for \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{2}\bar{\tau },\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . The upshot is that for any \( \epsilon  > 0 \) , one can find \( \delta  > 0 \) so that both \( l\left( {q,\tau }\right) \) and \( {\tau R}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) do not exceed \( {\delta }^{-1} \) whenever \( \frac{1}{2}\bar{\tau } \leq  \tau  \leq  \bar{\tau } \) and \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0} - \bar{\tau }}^{2}\left( {q, q\left( \bar{\tau }\right) }\right)  \leq  {\epsilon }^{-1}\bar{\tau }. \)

Varying \( \bar{\tau } \) , as the rescaled solutions (with basepoints at \( \left( {q\left( \bar{\tau }\right) ,{t}_{0} - \bar{\tau }}\right) \) ) are uniformly noncollapsing and have uniform curvature bounds on balls, Appendix E implies that we can take a sequence \( {\bar{\tau }}_{i} \rightarrow  \infty \) to get a pointed limit \( \left( {\bar{M},\bar{q},\bar{g}\left( \cdot \right) }\right) \) that is a complete Ricci flow solution (in the backward parameter \( \tau \) ) for \( \frac{1}{2} < \tau  < 1 \) . We may assume that we have locally Lipschitz convergence of \( l \) to a limit function \( \bar{l} \) .

We define the reduced volume \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) for the limit solution using the limit function \( \bar{l} \) . We claim that for any \( \tau  \in  \left( {\frac{1}{2},1}\right) \) , if we put \( {\tau }_{i} = \tau {\bar{\tau }}_{i} \) then the number \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) for the limit solution is the limit of numbers \( \widetilde{V}\left( {\tau }_{i}\right) \) for the original solution. One wishes to apply dominated convergence to the integrals \( {\int }_{M}{e}^{-l\left( {q,{\tau }_{i}}\right) }{\tau }_{i}^{-n/2}\operatorname{dvol}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{i}}\right) \) . (Note that \( {\tau }_{i}^{-n/2}\operatorname{dvol}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{i}}\right)  = \; {\tau }^{-n/2}{\bar{\tau }}_{i}^{-n/2}\operatorname{dvol}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{i}}\right) \) and \( {\bar{\tau }}_{i}^{-n/2}\operatorname{dvol}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{i}}\right) \) is the volume form for the rescaled metric \( {\bar{\tau }}_{i}^{-1}g\left( {{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{i}}\right) \) .) However, to do so one needs uniform lower bounds on \( l\left( {q,{\tau }^{\prime }}\right) \) for the original solution in terms of \( {d}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }^{\prime }}\left( {q, q\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right) \) , for \( {\tau }^{\prime } \in  \left( {-\infty ,0}\right) \) . By an argument of Perelman, written in detail in [67], one does indeed have a lower bound of the form

(39.6)

\[
l\left( {q,{\tau }^{\prime }}\right)  \geq   - l\left( {q\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) }\right)  - 1 + C\left( n\right) \frac{{d}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }^{\prime }}{\left( q, q\left( {\tau }^{\prime }\right) \right) }^{2}}{{\tau }^{\prime }}.
\]

The nonnegative curvature gives polynomial volume growth for distance balls, so using (39.6) one can apply dominated convergence to the integrals \( {\int }_{M}{e}^{-l\left( {q,{\tau }_{i}}\right) }{\tau }_{i}^{-n/2}\operatorname{dvol}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{i}}\right) \) . Thus \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\widetilde{V}\left( {\tau }_{i}\right)  = \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) . \)

As (39.5) gives a uniform upper bound on \( l \) on an appropriate ball around \( q\left( {\tau }_{i}\right) \) , and there is a lower volume bound on the ball, it follows that as \( i \rightarrow  \infty ,\widetilde{V}\left( {\tau }_{i}\right) \) is uniformly bounded away from zero. From this argument and the monotonicity of \( \widetilde{V},\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) is a positive constant \( c \) as a function of \( \tau \) , namely the limit of the reduced volume of the original solution as real time goes to \( - \infty \) . As the original solution is nonflat, the constant \( c \) is strictly less than the limit of the reduced volume of the original solution as real time goes to zero, which is \( {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{\frac{n}{2}} \) .

Next, we will apply (24.6) and (24.8). As (24.6) holds distributionally for each rescaled solution, it follows that it holds distributionally for \( \bar{l} \) . In particular, the nonpositivity implies that the left-hand side of (24.6), when computed for the limit solution, is actually a nonpositive measure. If the left-hand side of (24.6) (for the limit solution) were not strictly zero then using (24.7) we would conclude that \( \frac{d\widetilde{V}}{d\tau } \) is somewhere negative, which is a contradiction. (We use the fact that (39.6) passes to the limit to give a similar lower bound on \( \bar{l} \) .) Thus we must have equality in (24.6) for the limit solution. This implies equality in (21.2), which implies equality in (24.8). Writing (24.8) as

(39.7)

\[
\left( {4\bigtriangleup  - R}\right) {e}^{-\frac{l}{2}} = \frac{l - n}{\tau }{e}^{-\frac{l}{2}},
\]

elliptic theory gives smoothness of \( \bar{l} \) .

In I.11.2 it is said that equality in (24.8) implies equality in (23.9), which implies that one has a gradient shrinking soliton. There is a problem with this argument, as the use of (23.9) implicitly assumes that the solution is defined for all \( \tau  \geq  0 \) , which we do not know. (The function \( \bar{l} \) is only defined by a limiting procedure, and not in terms of \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics on some

Ricci flow solution.) However, one can instead use Proposition 29.5, with \( f = \bar{l} \) . Equality in (24.8) implies that \( v = 0 \) , so (29.6) directly gives the gradient shrinking soliton equation. (The problem with the argument using (23.9), and its resolution using (29.6), were pointed out by the UCSB group.)

If the gradient shrinking soliton \( \bar{g}\left( \cdot \right) \) is flat then, as it will be \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed at all scales, it must be \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . From the soliton equation, \( {\partial }_{i}{\partial }_{j}\bar{l} = \frac{{\bar{g}}_{ij}}{2\tau } \) and \( \bigtriangleup \bar{l} = \frac{n}{2\tau } \) . Putting this into the equality (24.8) gives \( {\left| \nabla \bar{l}\right| }^{2} = \frac{\bar{l}}{\tau } \) . It follows that the level sets of \( \bar{l} \) are distance spheres. Then (24.6) implies that with an appropriate choice of origin, \( \bar{l} = \frac{{\left| x\right| }^{2}}{4\tau } \) . The reduced volume \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) for the limit solution is now computed to be \( {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{\frac{n}{2}} \) , which is a contradiction. Therefore the gradient shrinking soliton is not flat.
