nodes.label: Remark 73.3
nodes.document_title: Bruce Kleiner and John Lott - Notes on Perelman's Papers
nodes.section_title: 73. II.4.4. PERFORMING SURGERY AND CONTINUING FLOWS
nodes.content:
Remark 73.3. Our definition of surgery differs slightly from that in [52]. The paper [52] has two extra steps involving throwing away certain components of the postsurgery manifold. We omit these steps in order to simplify the definition of surgery, but there is no real loss either way.

First, in the setup of [52, Section 4.4], any component of \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t}^{ + } \) that is \( \epsilon \) -close to a metric quotient of the round \( {S}^{3} \) is thrown away. The motivation of [52] was to not have to include these in the list of canonical neighborhoods. Such components are topologically standard. We do include such manifolds in the list of canonical neighborhoods and do not throw them away in the surgery procedure.

Second, when considering the long-time behavior of Ricci flow in [52, Section 7], any component of \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t}^{ + } \) which admits a metric of nonnegative scalar curvature is thrown away. The motivation for this extra step is that any such component admits a metric that is either flat or has finite extinction time. In either case one concludes that the component is a graph manifold and, for the purposes of the geometrization conjecture, is standard. (Recall the definition of graph manifolds from Appendix I.) Again, we do not throw away such components.

Note that the definition of Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff also depends on the function \( r\left( t\right) \) through the a priori assumption. We now state how the topology of the time slice changes when going backward through the singular time \( t \) . Recall that for \( {t}^{\prime } < t \) close to \( t \) , the time slices \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) are all diffeomorphic; we refer to this diffeomorphism type as the presurgery manifold, and the forward time slice \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t}^{ + } \) as the postsurgery manifold.

nodes.section_title: 73. II.4.4. PERFORMING SURGERY AND CONTINUING FLOWS
nodes.content:
Remark 73.6. For a Ricci flow with surgery whose original manifold is nonaspherical and irreducible, one wants to know that the Ricci flow goes extinct within a finite time [24, 25, 53]. Consider the effect of a first surgery, say at time \( t \) . Among the connected components of the postsurgery manifold \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t}^{ + } \) , one will be diffeomorphic to the presurgery manifold and the others will be 3-spheres. Let \( {\mathcal{N}}_{t}^{ + } \) be a component of \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t}^{ + } \) that is diffeomorphic to the presurgery manifold. By the nature of the surgery procedure, there is a function \( \xi \) defined on a small interval \( \left( {t - \alpha , t}\right) \) so that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{t}^{\prime } \rightarrow  t}}\xi \left( {t}^{\prime }\right)  = 1 \) and for \( {t}^{\prime } \in  \left( {t - \alpha , t}\right) \) , there is a homotopy-equivalence from \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{{t}^{\prime }}, g\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) }\right) \) to \( {\mathcal{N}}_{t}^{ + } \) that expands distances by at most \( \xi \left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) . Following the subsequent evolution of \( {\mathcal{N}}_{t}^{ + } \) , there is a similar statement for the later singular times. This fact is needed in \( \left\lbrack  {{24},{25},{53}}\right\rbrack \) in order to control the decay of a certain area functional as one goes through a surgery.

We discuss how to continue Ricci flows after surgery. We recall that in Definition 68.1 of a Ricci flow with surgery defined on an interval \( \left\lbrack  {a, c}\right\rbrack \) , the final time slice \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c} \) consists of a single manifold \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ - } = \Omega \) that may or may not be singular.

nodes.content:
Lemma 73.7. (Prolongation of Ricci flows with cutoff) Take the function \( \Phi \) to be the time-dependent pinching function associated to Definition B. 5 in Appendix B. Suppose that \( r \) and \( \delta \) are nonincreasing positive functions defined on \( \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) . Let \( \mathcal{M} \) be a Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff defined on an interval \( \left\lbrack  {a, c}\right\rbrack   \subset  \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) . Provided \( \sup \delta \) is sufficiently small, either

(1) \( \mathcal{M} \) can be prolonged to a Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff defined on \( \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) , or

(2) There is an extension of \( \mathcal{M} \) to a Ricci flow with surgery defined on an interval \( \left\lbrack  {a, T}\right\rbrack \) with \( T \in  (c, b\rbrack \) , where

a. The restriction of the flow to any subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {a,{T}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack  ,{T}^{\prime } < T \) , is a Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff, but

b. The \( r \) -canonical neighborhood assumption fails at some point \( \left( {x, T}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{T}^{ - } \) .

In particular, the only obstacle to prolongation of Ricci flows with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff is the potential breakdown of the r-canonical neighborhood assumption.

nodes.proof:
Consider the time slice of \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c} = {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ - } \) at time \( c \) . If it is singular then we perform steps A-E of Definition 73.1 to produce \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ + } \) ; otherwise we set \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ + } = {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ - } \) . Since the surgery is done using Lemma 72.24, provided \( \delta  > 0 \) is sufficiently small, the forward time slice \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ + } \) will satisfy the \( \Phi \) -pinching assumption.

We claim that the \( r \) -canonical neighborhood assumption holds in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ + } \) . More precisely, if a point \( \left( {x, c}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ + } \) lies within a distance of \( {10}{\epsilon }^{-1}h \) from the added part \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ + } - {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ - } \) then it lies in an \( \epsilon \) -cap, while if \( \left( {x, c}\right) \) lies at distance greater than \( {10}{\epsilon }^{-1}h \) from \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ + } - {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ - } \) and has scalar curvature greater than \( r{\left( c\right) }^{-2} \) then it lies in a canonical neighborhood that was present in the presurgery manifold \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ - } \) . (We are assuming that \( \epsilon  < \frac{1}{100} \) .) In view of Lemma 63.1, the only point to observe is that points at distance roughly \( {10}{\epsilon }^{-1}h \) lie in \( \epsilon \) -necks, as they are unaltered by the surgery and they were in \( \delta \) -necks before the surgery. This gives the \( \epsilon \) -neck needed to define an \( \epsilon \) -cap.

We now prolong \( \mathcal{M} \) by Ricci flow with initial condition \( {\mathcal{M}}_{c}^{ + } \) . If the flow extends smoothly up to time \( b \) then we are done because either the canonical neighborhood assumption holds up to time \( b \) yielding (a), or it fails at some time in the interval \( (c, b\rbrack \) , and we have (b). Otherwise, there is some time \( {t}_{\text{ sing }} \leq  b \) at which it goes singular. We add the singular limit \( \Omega \) at time \( {t}_{\text{ sing }} \) to obtain a Ricci flow with surgery defined on \( \left\lbrack  {a,{t}_{\text{ sing }}}\right\rbrack \) . From Lemma 72.24, \( \mathcal{M} \) satisfies the Hamilton-Ivey pinching condition of Definition B. 5 on \( \left\lbrack  {a,{t}_{\text{ sing }}}\right\rbrack \) . As the function \( r \) is nonincreasing in \( t \) , it follows from Definition 69.1 that the set of times \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {c,{t}_{\text{ sing }}}\right\rbrack \) for which the \( r \) -canonical neighborhood assumption holds is relatively open to the right (i.e. if the \( r \) -canonical neighborhood assumption holds at time \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {c,{t}_{\text{ sing }}}\right) \) then it also holds within some interval \( \left\lbrack  {t,{t}^{\prime })}\right\rbrack \) ). Thus the set of times \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {c,{t}_{\text{ sing }}}\right\rbrack \) for which the \( r \) -canonical neighborhood assumption holds is either an interval \( \lbrack c, T) \) , with \( T \leq  {t}_{\text{ sing }} \) , or \( \left\lbrack  {c,{t}_{\text{ sing }}}\right\rbrack \) . If the set of such times \( t \) is \( \left( {c, T}\right) \) for some \( T \leq  {t}_{\text{ sing }} \) then the lemma holds. Otherwise, the \( r \) -canonical neighborhood assumption holds at \( {t}_{\text{ sing }} \) . In this case we repeat the construction with \( c \) replaced by \( {t}_{\text{ sing }} \) , and iterate if necessary. Either we will reach time \( b \) after a finite number of iterations, or we will reach a time \( T \) satisfying (2), or we will hit an infinite number of singular times before time \( b \) . However, the last possibility cannot occur. A singular time corresponds to a component going extinct or to a surgery. The number of components going extinct before time \( b \) can be bounded in terms of the number of surgeries before time \( b \) , so it suffices to show that the latter is finite. Each surgery removes a volume of at least \( {h}^{3} \) , but the lower bound on the scalar curvature during the flow, coming from the maximum principle, gives a finite upper bound on the total volume growth during the complement of the singular times.

Suppose that there is a surgery time \( {T}_{0} \in  \left( {a, b}\right) \) , with \( \delta \left( {T}_{0}\right)  \leq  \widehat{\delta } \) . Fix \( \theta \) and \( \widehat{r} \) . Suppose that the lemma is not true. Then for some \( A > 0 \) , there is a sequence \( {\left\{  {\mathcal{M}}^{\alpha },\left( {p}^{\alpha },{T}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) \right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1}^{\infty } \) of pointed Ricci flows with \( \left( {{r}^{\alpha },{\delta }^{\alpha }}\right) \) -cutoff that together provide a counterexample. In particular,

1. \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\alpha  \rightarrow  \infty }}{\delta }^{\alpha }\left( {T}_{0}^{\alpha }\right)  = 0 \) .

2. \( {\mathcal{M}}^{\alpha } \) is unscathed on \( P\left( {{p}^{\alpha },{T}_{0}^{\alpha }, A{\widehat{h}}^{\alpha },{T}_{1}^{\alpha } - {T}_{0}^{\alpha }}\right) \) .

3. If \( \left( {{\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}^{\alpha },\left( {{\widehat{p}}^{\alpha },0}\right) }\right) \) is the pointed Ricci flow arising from \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{\alpha },\left( {{p}^{\alpha },{T}_{0}^{\alpha }}\right) }\right) \) by a time shift of \( {T}_{0}^{\alpha } \) and a parabolic rescaling by \( {\widehat{h}}^{\alpha } \) then \( P\left( {{\widehat{p}}^{\alpha },0, A,\left( {{T}_{1}^{\alpha } - {T}_{0}^{\alpha }}\right) {\left( {\widehat{h}}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2}}\right) \) is not \( {A}^{-1} \) -close to a pointed subset of a standard solution.

(We do not exclude that \( {T}_{2} = 0 \) .) Clearly \( {T}_{2} \leq  \theta \) . After passing to a subsequence, we can assume that \( {T}_{2} = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\alpha  \rightarrow  \infty }}\left( {{T}_{1}^{\alpha } - {T}_{0}^{\alpha }}\right) {\left( {\widehat{h}}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} \) . Corollary II.4.6) For any \( l < \infty \) and \( \widehat{r} > 0 \) , we can find \( A = \; A\left( {l,\widehat{r}}\right)  < \infty \) and \( \theta  = \theta \left( {l,\widehat{r}}\right) \) with the following property. For the moment, fix \( A < \infty \) and \( \theta  \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) . Choose \( \widehat{\delta } = \widehat{\delta }\left( {A,\theta ,\widehat{r}}\right) \) so as to satisfy Lemma 74.1. Let \( \mathcal{M},\left( {p,{T}_{0}}\right) \) , etc., be as in the hypotheses of Lemma 74.1. Let \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {{T}_{0},{T}_{\gamma }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow \; \mathcal{M} \) be a curve as in the hypotheses of the Corollary. From Lemma 74.1, we know that there is a standard solution \( \mathcal{S} \) such that the parabolic region \( P\left( {p,{T}_{0}, A\widehat{h},{T}_{\gamma } - {T}_{0}}\right)  \subset  \mathcal{M} \) , with basepoint \( \left( {p,{T}_{0}}\right) \) , is (after parabolic rescaling by \( {\widehat{h}}^{-2} \) ) \( {A}^{-1} \) -close to a pointed flow \( {U}_{0} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}\right\rbrack   \subset  \mathcal{S} \) , the latter having basepoint \( \left( {c,0}\right) \) . Here \( {U}_{0} \subset  {\mathcal{S}}_{0} \) and \( {\widehat{T}}_{\gamma } = \left( {{T}_{\gamma } - {T}_{0}}\right) {\widehat{h}}^{-2} \) . Then the image of \( \gamma \) , under the diffeomorphism implicit in the definition of \( {A}^{-1} \) -closeness, gives rise to a smooth curve \( {\gamma }_{0} : \left\lbrack  {0,{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {U}_{0} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}\right\rbrack \) so that (if \( A \) is sufficiently large) :

(75.3)

\[
{\gamma }_{0}\left( 0\right)  \in  B\left( {c,0,\frac{3}{5}A}\right)
\]

(75.4)

\[
{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{\gamma }}{\left| \dot{\gamma }\right| }^{2}{dt} \geq  \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}{\left| {\dot{\gamma }}_{0}\right| }^{2}{dt}
\]

(75.5)

\[
{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{\gamma }}R\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right) {dt} \geq  \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}R\left( {{\gamma }_{0}\left( t\right) , t}\right) {dt}
\]

and

(a) \( {\widehat{T}}_{\gamma } = \theta \) ,

or

(b) \( {\gamma }_{0}\left( {\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }\right)  \notin  P\left( {c,0,\frac{4}{5}A,{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}\right) \) .

In case (a) we have, by Lemma 63.1,

(75.6)

\[
\text{ 5.6) }{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{\gamma }}R\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right) {dt} \geq  \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\theta }R\left( {{\gamma }_{0}\left( t\right) , t}\right) {dt} \geq  \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\theta }\text{ const. }{\left( 1 - t\right) }^{-1}{dt} = \text{ const. }\log \left( {1 - \theta }\right) \text{ . }
\]

If we choose \( \theta \) sufficiently close to 1 then in this case, we can ensure that

(75.7)

\[
{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{\gamma }}\left( {R\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right)  + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( t\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {dt} \geq  {\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{\gamma }}R\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) , t}\right) {dt} > l.
\]

In case (b), we may use the fact that the Ricci curvature of the standard solution is everywhere nonnegative, and hence the metric tensor is nonincreasing with time. So if \( \pi  : \mathcal{S} = {\mathcal{S}}_{0} \times  \lbrack 0,1) \rightarrow  {\mathcal{S}}_{\theta } \) is projection to the time- \( \theta \) slice and we put \( \eta  = \pi  \circ  {\gamma }_{0} \) then

(75.8)

\[
{\int }_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{\gamma }}{\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( t\right) \right| }^{2}{dt} \geq  \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}{\left| {\dot{\gamma }}_{0}\left( t\right) \right| }^{2}{dt} \geq  \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}{\left| \dot{\eta }\left( t\right) \right| }^{2}{dt} \geq  \frac{1}{2{\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }}{\left( d\left( \eta \left( 0\right) ,\eta \left( {\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }\right) \right) \right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}{\left( d\left( \eta \left( 0\right) ,\eta \left( {\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }\right) \right) \right) }^{2}
\]

With our given value of \( \theta \) , in view of (b), if we take \( A \) large enough then we can ensure that \( \frac{1}{2}{\left( d\left( \eta \left( 0\right) ,\eta \left( {\widehat{T}}_{\gamma }\right) \right) \right) }^{2} > l \) . This proves the lemma.

nodes.content:
Let \( \mathcal{M} \) be a Ricci flow with surgery, and fix a point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \) . One may define the \( \mathcal{L} \) -length of an admissible curve \( \gamma \) from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) to some \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) , for \( t < {t}_{0} \) , using the formula

(78.1)

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  = {\int }_{t}^{{t}_{0}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - \bar{t}}\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\right| }^{2}}\right) d\bar{t},
\]

where \( \dot{\gamma } \) denotes the spatial part of the velocity of \( \gamma \) . One defines the \( L \) -function on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\left( -\infty ,{t}_{0}\right) } \) by setting \( L\left( {x, t}\right) \) to be the infimal \( \mathcal{L} \) -length of the admissible curves from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) to \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) if such an admissible curve exists, and infinity otherwise. We note that if \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is in a surgery time slice \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t}^{ - } \) and is actually removed by the surgery then there will not be an admissible curve from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) to \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) .

If \( \gamma \) is an admissible curve lying in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \) then the first variation formula applies. Hence an admissible curve in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \) from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) to \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) whose \( \mathcal{L} \) -length equals \( L\left( {x, t}\right) \) will satisfy the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation. If \( \gamma \) is a stable \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \) then the proof of the monotonicity along \( \gamma \) of the weighted Jacobian \( {\tau }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( \tau \right) }\right) J\left( \tau \right) \) remains valid. Similarly, if \( U \subset \; {\mathcal{M}}_{\left( -\infty ,{t}_{0}\right) } \) is an open set such that every \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  U \) is accessible from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) by a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic (i.e. an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic of \( \mathcal{L} \) -length \( L\left( {x, t}\right) \) ) contained in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \) , then the arguments of Section 24 imply that the differential inequality

(78.2)

\[
{\bar{L}}_{\tau } + \Delta \bar{L} \leq  6
\]

holds in \( U \) , in the barrier sense, where \( \tau  = {t}_{0} - t,\bar{L} = 2\sqrt{\tau }L \) and \( l = \frac{\bar{L}}{4\tau } \) .

Lemma 78.3 (Existence of \( \mathcal{L} \) -minimizers). Let \( \mathcal{M} \) be a Ricci flow with surgery defined on \( \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) . Suppose that \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \) lies in the backward time slice \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}}^{ - } \) .

(1) For each \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right) } \) with \( L\left( {x, t}\right)  < \infty \) , there exists an \( \mathcal{L} \) -minimizing admissible path \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) from \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) to \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) which satisfies the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation at every time \( \bar{t} \in  \left( {t,{t}_{0}}\right) \) for which \( \gamma \left( \bar{t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \) .

(2) \( L \) is lower semicontinuous on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right) } \) and continuous on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \cap  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right) } \) . (Note that \( \left. {{\mathcal{M}}_{a}^{ + } \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }}.}\right) \)

(3) Every sequence \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right) } \) with \( \lim \mathop{\sup }\limits_{j}L\left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  < \infty \) has a convergent subsequence.

nodes.proof:
(1) Let \( {\left\{  {\gamma }_{j} : \left\lbrack  t,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M}\right\}  }_{j = 1}^{\infty } \) be a sequence of admissible curves from \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) to \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{j}\right)  = L\left( {x, t}\right)  < \infty \) . By restricting the sequence, we may assume that \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{j}\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{j}\right)  < {2L}\left( {x, t}\right) \) . We claim that there is a subsequence of the \( {\gamma }_{j} \) ’s that

(a) converges uniformly to some \( {\gamma }_{\infty } : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) ,

and

(b) converges weakly to \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) in \( {W}^{1,2} \) on any subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack   \subset  \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right) \) such that \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack \) is free of singular times.

To see this, note that on any time interval \( \left\lbrack  {c, d}\right\rbrack   \subset  \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right) \) which is free of singular times, one may apply the Schwarz inequality to the \( \mathcal{L} \) -length, along with the fact that the metrics on the time slices \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t}, t \in  \left\lbrack  {c, d}\right\rbrack \) , are uniformly biLipschitz to each other, to conclude that the \( {\gamma }_{j} \) ’s are uniformly Hölder-continuous on \( \left\lbrack  {c, d}\right\rbrack \) . We know that \( {\gamma }_{j}\left( {t}^{\prime }\right) \) lies in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}^{\prime }}^{ - } \cap  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}^{\prime }}^{ + } \) for each surgery time \( {t}^{\prime } \in  \left( {t,{t}_{0}}\right) \) , and so one can use similar reasoning to get Hölder control on a short time interval of the form \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime \prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) . Using a change of variable as in (17.6), one obtains uniform Hölder control near \( {t}_{0} \) after reparametrizing with \( s \) . It follows that the \( {\gamma }_{j} \) ’s are equicontinuous and map into a compact part of spacetime, so Arzela-Ascoli applies; therefore, by passing to a subsequence we may assume that (a) holds.

To show (b), we apply weak compactness to the sequence

(78.4)

\[
\left\{  {\left. {\gamma }_{j}\right| }_{\left\lbrack  {t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }\right\rbrack  }\right\}  ;
\]

this is justified by the fact that the paths \( {\left. {\gamma }_{j}\right| }_{\left\lbrack  {t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }\right\rbrack  } \) ’s remain in a part of \( \mathcal{M} \) with bounded geometry. Thus we may assume that our sequence \( \left\{  {\gamma }_{j}\right\} \) converges uniformly on \( \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and weakly on every subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack \) as in (b). By weak lower semicontinuity of \( \mathcal{L} \) -length, it follows that the \( {W}^{1,2} \) -path \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) has \( \mathcal{L} \) -length \( \leq  L\left( {x, t}\right) \) . Since any \( {W}^{1,2} \) path may be approximated in \( {W}^{1,2} \) by admissible curves with the same endpoints, it follows that \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) minimizes \( \mathcal{L} \) -length among \( {W}^{1,2} \) paths, and therefore it restricts to a smooth solution of the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation on each time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right\rbrack   \subset  \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) such that \( \left( {{t}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime \prime }}\right) \) is free of singular times. Hence \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) is an \( \mathcal{L} \) -minimizing admissible curve.

(2) Pick \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right) } \) . To verify lower semicontinuity at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) we suppose the sequence \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \right\}   \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right) } \) converges to \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) and \( \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}L\left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  < \infty \) . By (1) there is a sequence \( \left\{  {\gamma }_{j}\right\} \) of \( \mathcal{L} \) -minimizing admissible curves, where \( {\gamma }_{j} \) runs from \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) to \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . By the reasoning above, a subsequence of \( \left\{  {\gamma }_{j}\right\} \) converges uniformly and weakly in \( {W}^{1,2} \) to a \( {W}^{1,2} \) curve \( {\gamma }_{\infty } : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) going from \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) to \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , with

(78.5)

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{\infty }\right)  \leq  \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\mathcal{L}\left( {\gamma }_{j}\right)
\]

Therefore \( L\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}L\left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) , and we have established semicontinuity. If \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in \; {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \) , the opposite inequality obviously holds, so in this case \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is a point of continuity.

(3) Because \( \left\{  {L\left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) }\right\} \) is uniformly bounded, any sequence \( \left\{  {\gamma }_{j}\right\} \) of \( \mathcal{L} \) -minimizing paths with \( {\gamma }_{j}\left( {t}_{j}\right)  = \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) will be equicontinuous, and hence by Arzela-Ascoli a subsequence converges uniformly. Therefore a subsequence of \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \right\} \) converges.

nodes.content: Lemma 78.6. Suppose that \( \mathcal{M} \) is a Ricci flow with surgery defined on \( \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) . Take \( {t}_{0} \in  (a, b\rbrack \) and \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}}^{ - } \) . Suppose that for every \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {a,{t}_{0}}\right) \) , every admissible curve \( \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) ending at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) which does not lie in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \cup  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}}^{ - } \) has reduced length strictly greater than \( \frac{3}{2} \) . Then there is a point \( \left( {x, a}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{a}^{ + } \) where \( l\left( {x, a}\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) .

nodes.proof:
As in the case when there are no surgeries, the proof relies on the maximum principle and a continuity argument.

Let \( \beta  : {\mathcal{M}}_{\lbrack a,{t}_{0})} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \cup  \{ \infty \} \) be the function

(78.8)

\[
\beta  = \bar{L} - {6\tau } = {4\tau }\left( {l - \frac{3}{2}}\right) ,
\]

where as usual, \( \tau \left( {x, t}\right)  = {t}_{0} - t \) . Note that for each \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,{t}_{0} - a}\right\rbrack \) , the function \( \beta \) attains a minimum \( {\beta }_{\min }\left( \tau \right)  < \infty \) on the slice \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau } \) , because by (2) of Lemma 78.3, it is continuous on the compact manifold \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }^{ + } \) (as seen by changing the parameter \( a \) of Lemma 78.3 to \( \left. {{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) , and \( \beta  \equiv  \infty \) on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau } - {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }^{ + } \) . Thus it suffices to show that \( {\beta }_{\min }\left( {{t}_{0} - a}\right)  \leq  0 \) .

From Lemma 24.3, \( {\beta }_{\min }\left( \tau \right)  < 0 \) for \( \tau  > 0 \) small. Let \( {\tau }_{1} \in  \left( {0,{t}_{0} - a}\right\rbrack \) be the supremum of the \( \bar{\tau } \in  \left( {0,{t}_{0} - a}\right\rbrack \) such that \( {\beta }_{\min } < 0 \) on the interval \( \left( {0,\bar{\tau }}\right) \) .

We claim that

(a) \( {\beta }_{\min } \) is continuous on \( \left( {0,{\tau }_{1}}\right) \)

and

(b) The upper right \( \tau \) -derivative of \( {\beta }_{\min } \) is nonpositive on \( \left( {0,{\tau }_{1}}\right) \) .

To see (a), pick \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,{\tau }_{1}}\right) \) , suppose that \( \left\{  {\tau }_{j}\right\}   \subset  \left( {0,{\tau }_{1}}\right) \) is a sequence converging to \( \tau \) and choose \( \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{j}}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{j}}^{ + } \) such that \( \beta \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{j}}\right)  = {\beta }_{\min }\left( {\tau }_{j}\right)  < 0 \) . By Lemma 78.3 part (3), the sequence \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{j}}\right) \right\} \) subconverges to some \( \left( {x,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }^{ + } \) for which \( \beta \left( {x,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right)  \leq  \mathop{\liminf }\limits_{{j \rightarrow  \infty }}\beta \left( {{x}_{j},{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{j}}\right) \) . Thus \( {\beta }_{\min } \) is lower semicontinuous at \( \tau \) . On the other hand, since \( {\beta }_{\min }\left( \tau \right)  < 0 \) , the minimum of \( \beta \) on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau } \) will be attained at a point \( \left( {x,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }^{ + } \) lying in the interior of \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }^{ - } \cap  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }^{ + } \) , as \( \beta  > 0 \) elsewhere on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau } \) (by Lemma 78.3 and the hypothesis on admissible curves). Therefore \( \beta \) is continuous at \( \left( {x,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) , which implies that \( {\beta }_{\min } \) is upper semicontinuous at \( \tau \) . This gives (a).

Part (b) of the claim follows from the fact that if \( \tau  \in  \left( {0,{\tau }_{1}}\right) \) and the minimum of \( \beta \) on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0} - \tau } \) is attained at \( \left( {x,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) then \( l\left( {x,\tau }\right)  < \frac{3}{2} \) , so there is a neighborhood \( U \) of \( \left( {x,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) such that the inequality

(78.9)

\[
\frac{\partial \beta }{\partial \tau } + {\Delta \beta } \leq  0
\]

holds in the barrier sense on \( U \) (by Lemma 78.3 and the hypothesis on admissible curves). Hence the upper right derivative \( {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\beta \left( {x,\tau  + s}\right) \) is nonpositive, so the upper right \( \tau \) - derivative of \( {\beta }_{\min }\left( \tau \right) \) is also nonpositive.

The claim implies that \( {\beta }_{\min } \) is nonincreasing on \( \left( {0,{\tau }_{1}}\right) \) , and so \( \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {\tau }_{1}^{ - }}}\beta \left( \tau \right)  < 0 \) . By parts (2) and (3) of Lemma 78.3, we have \( {\beta }_{\min }\left( {\tau }_{1}\right)  < 0 \) , and the minimum is attained at some \( \left( {x,{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{1}}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \) . (Recall that \( {\mathcal{M}}_{a} \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \) .) This implies that \( {\tau }_{1} = {t}_{0} - a \) , for otherwise \( {\beta }_{\min }\left( \tau \right) \) would be strictly negative for \( \tau  \geq  {\tau }_{1} \) close to \( {\tau }_{1} \) , contradicting the definition of \( {\tau }_{1} \) .

Lemma 79.3. (Forcing \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) to be large, cf. Lemma II.5.3)

For all \( \Lambda  < \infty ,\bar{r} > 0 \) and \( \widehat{r} > 0 \) , there is a constant \( {F}_{0} = {F}_{0}\left( {\Lambda ,\bar{r},\widehat{r}}\right) \) with the following property. Suppose that

- \( \mathcal{M} \) is a Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff defined on an interval containing \( \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , where \( r\left( \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  \right)  \subset  \left\lbrack  {\widehat{r},\epsilon }\right\rbrack  , \)

- \( {r}_{0} \geq  \bar{r}, B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) is a proper ball which is unscathed on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) ,

- \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) is an admissible curve ending at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) whose image is not contained in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \cup  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}} \) , and

- \( \delta  < {F}_{0}\left( {\Lambda ,\bar{r},\widehat{r}}\right) \) on \( \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) .

Then \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  > \Lambda \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. The idea is that the hypotheses on \( \gamma \) imply that it must touch the part of the manifold added during surgery at some time \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Then either \( \gamma \) has to move very fast at times close to \( \bar{t} \) or \( {t}_{0} \) , or it will stay in the surgery region while it develops large scalar curvature. In the first case \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right) \) will be large because of the \( {\left| \dot{\gamma }\right| }^{2} \) term in the formula for \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) , and in the second case it will be large because of the \( R\left( \gamma \right) \) term.

First, we can assume that \( {F}_{0} \) is small enough so that \( {F}_{0} < \sqrt{\frac{\bar{r}}{100\epsilon }} \) . Then since

(79.4)

\[
\mathop{\max }\limits_{\left\lbrack  t,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  }h\left( t\right)  \leq  {\left( \mathop{\max }\limits_{\left\lbrack  t,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  }\delta \right) }^{2}\left( {\mathop{\max }\limits_{\left\lbrack  t,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  }r\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  {F}_{0}^{2}\epsilon
\]

we have \( \mathop{\max }\limits_{\left\lbrack  t,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  }h\left( t\right)  < \frac{\bar{r}}{100} \leq  \frac{{r}_{0}}{100} \) .

Put \( {\Delta t} = {10}^{-{10}}{\bar{r}}^{4}{\Lambda }^{-2} \) . It always suffices to prove the lemma for a larger value of \( \Lambda \) , so without loss of generality we can assume that \( {\Delta t} \leq  {\bar{r}}^{2} \leq  {r}_{0}^{2} \) . Set

(79.5)

\[
A = A\left( {{\left( \Delta t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\Lambda ,\widehat{r}}\right) ,\;\theta  = \theta \left( {{\left( \Delta t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\Lambda ,\widehat{r}}\right)
\]

where \( A\left( {\cdot , \cdot  }\right) \) and \( \theta \left( {\cdot , \cdot  }\right) \) are the functions from Corollary 75.1. That is, we will eventually be applying Corollary 75.1 with \( l = {\left( \Delta t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\Lambda \) . We impose the additional constraint on \( {F}_{0} \) that

(79.6)

\[
{F}_{0} \leq  \widehat{\delta }\left( {A + 2,\theta ,\widehat{r}}\right)
\]

on the interval \( \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , where \( \widehat{\delta } \) is the function from Lemma 74.1.

As \( \gamma \) is admissible but is not contained in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \cup  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}} \) , it must pass through the boundary of a surgery cap at some time in the interval \( \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right) \) or it must start in the interior of a surgery cap at time \( t \) . By dropping an initial segment of \( \gamma \) if necessary, we may assume that \( \gamma \left( t\right) \) lies in a surgery cap.

Let \( x \) denote the tip of the surgery cap. Note that

(79.7)

\[
P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right)  \cap  P\left( {x, t,{Ah}\left( t\right) ,\theta {h}^{2}\left( t\right) }\right)  = \varnothing
\]

since by Lemma 74.1 the scalar curvature on \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah}\left( t\right) ,\theta {h}^{2}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is at least \( \frac{{h}^{-2}}{2} > \frac{{10}^{4}}{2}{r}_{0}^{-2} \) , while \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) . Therefore when going backward in time from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,\gamma \) must leave the parabolic region \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) before it arrives at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) . If it exits at a time \( \widetilde{t} > {t}_{0} - {\Delta t} \) then applying the Schwarz inequality we get

(79.8)

\[
{\int }_{\widetilde{t}}^{{t}_{0}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - s}{\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \right| }^{2}{ds} \geq  {\left( {\int }_{\widetilde{t}}^{{t}_{0}}\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \right| ds\right) }^{2}{\left( {\int }_{\widetilde{t}}^{{t}_{0}}{\left( {t}_{0} - s\right) }^{-1/2}ds\right) }^{-1} \geq  \frac{1}{100}{r}_{0}^{2}{\left( \Delta t\right) }^{-1/2} > \Lambda ,
\]

where the factor of \( \frac{1}{100} \) comes from the length distortion estimate of Section 27, using the fact that \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) . So we can restrict to the case when \( \gamma \) exits \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {\Delta t}}\right) \) through the initial time slice at time \( {t}_{0} - {\Delta t} \) . In particular, by (79.7), \( \gamma \) must exit the parabolic region \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah}\left( t\right) ,\theta {h}^{2}\left( t\right) }\right) \) by time \( {t}_{0} - {\Delta t} \) .

By Lemma 74.1, the parabolic region \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah},\theta {h}^{2}}\right) \) is either unscathed, or it coincides (as a set) with the parabolic region \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah}, s}\right) \) for some \( s \in  \left( {0,\theta {h}^{2}}\right) \) and the entire final time slice \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah}, s}\right)  \cap  {\mathcal{M}}_{t + s} \) of \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah}, s}\right) \) is thrown away by a surgery at time \( t + s \) .

One possibility is that \( \gamma \) exits \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah},\theta {h}^{2}}\right) \) through the final time slice. If this is the case then \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah},\theta {h}^{2}}\right) \) must be unscathed (as otherwise the final face is removed by surgery at time \( t + s < t + \theta {h}^{2} \) and \( \gamma \) would have nowhere to go after this time), so \( \gamma \) lies in \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah},\theta {h}^{2}}\right) \) for the entire time interval \( \left\lbrack  {t, t + \theta {h}^{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

The other possibility is that \( \gamma \) leaves \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah},\theta {h}^{2}}\right) \) before the final time slice of \( P\left( {x, t,{Ah},\theta {h}^{2}}\right) \) , in which case it exits the ball \( B\left( {x, t,{Ah}}\right) \) by time \( t + \theta {h}^{2} \) .

Corollary 75.1 applies to either of these two possibilities. Putting

(79.9)

\[
{T}_{\gamma } = \sup \left\{  {\bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {t, t + \theta {h}^{2}}\right\rbrack   \mid  \gamma \left( \left\lbrack  {t,\bar{t}}\right\rbrack  \right)  \subset  P\left( {x, t,{Ah},\theta {h}^{2}}\right) }\right\}
\]

and using the fact that \( {T}_{\gamma } \leq  {t}_{0} - {\Delta t} \) , we have(79.10)

\[
{\int }_{t}^{{t}_{0}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - s}\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( s\right) , s}\right)  + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {ds} \geq  {\int }_{t}^{{T}_{\gamma }}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - s}\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( s\right) , s}\right)  + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {ds} \geq
\]

\[
{\left( \Delta t\right) }^{1/2}{\int }_{t}^{{T}_{\gamma }}\left( {{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( s\right) , s}\right)  + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {ds} \geq  {\left( \Delta t\right) }^{1/2}l = \Lambda ,
\]

where the last inequality comes from Corollary 75.1 and the choice of \( A,\theta \) , and \( \delta \) in (79.5) and (79.6). This completes the proof.

Lemma 79.12. (Noncollapsing estimate) (cf. Lemma II.5.2)

Suppose \( \epsilon  \geq  {r}_{ - } \geq  {r}_{ + } > 0,{\kappa }_{ - } > 0,{E}_{ - } > 0 \) and \( E < \infty \) . Then there are constants \( \bar{\delta } = \bar{\delta }\left( {{r}_{ - },{r}_{ + },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) and \( {\kappa }_{ + } = {\kappa }_{ + }\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) with the following property. Suppose that

- \( a < b < c,\;b - a \geq  {E}_{ - },\;c - a \leq  E, \)

- \( \mathcal{M} \) is a Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff with normalized initial condition defined on a time interval containing \( \lbrack a, c) \) ,

- \( r \geq  {r}_{ - } \) on \( \lbrack a, b) \) and \( r \geq  {r}_{ + } \) on \( \lbrack b, c) \) ,

- \( r \leq  \epsilon \) ,

- \( \mathcal{M} \) is \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) -noncollapsed at scales below \( \epsilon \) on \( \lbrack a, b) \) and

- \( \delta  \leq  \bar{\delta } \) on \( \lbrack a, c) \) ,

Then \( \mathcal{M} \) is \( {\kappa }_{ + } \) -noncollapsed at scales below \( \epsilon \) on \( \lbrack b, c) \) .

Then there are constants \( \bar{\delta } = \bar{\delta }\left( {{r}_{ - },{r}_{ + },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) and \( {\kappa }_{ + } = {\kappa }_{ + }\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) with the following prop...

nodes.proof:
Proof. In the proof, we can assume that \( \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \leq  \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) . If this were not the case then we could prove the lemma with \( {r}_{ + } \) replaced by \( {100}\sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) . Then the lemma would also hold for the original value of \( {r}_{ + } \) .

First, from Lemma 79.11, \( R \geq   - 6 \) on \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\lbrack a, c)} \) .

Suppose that \( {r}_{0} \in  \left( {0,\epsilon }\right) ,\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{M}}_{\lbrack b, c)}, B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) is a proper ball unscathed on the interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}, - {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) .

We first assume that \( {r}_{0} \leq  \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) and \( {r}_{0} \geq  \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

We will consider \( \mathcal{L} \) -length, \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) -length, etc in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right) } \) with basepoint at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Suppose that \( \widehat{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {a,{t}_{0}}\right) \) . Then for any admissible curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {\widehat{t},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  } \) ending at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we have

(79.14)

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  {\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  \mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  + {\int }_{a}^{c}6\sqrt{c - t}{dt} \leq  \mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}}
\]

\[
\text{ and }l\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{{L}_{ + } - 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}}}{2{E}^{\frac{1}{2}}}\text{ . }
\]

Assume that \( \bar{\delta } \leq  {F}_{0}\left( {4{E}^{\frac{1}{2}} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}},\frac{{r}_{ + }}{100},{r}_{ + }}\right) \) where \( {F}_{0} \) is the function from Lemma 79.3. Then by (79.14) and Lemma 79.3, we conclude that any admissible curve \( \left\lbrack  {\widehat{t},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {\mathcal{M}}_{\left\lbrack  a,{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  } \) ending at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) which does not lie in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \cup  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}} \) has reduced length bounded below by \( 2 = \frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{2} \) . By Lemma 78.6 there is an admissible curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {a,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) ending at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) such that

(79.15)

\[
\mathcal{L}\left( \gamma \right)  = L\left( {\gamma \left( a\right) }\right)  = 2\sqrt{{t}_{0} - a}l\left( {\gamma \left( a\right) }\right)  \leq  3\sqrt{{t}_{0} - a},
\]

so by (79.14) it follows that

(79.16)

\[
{\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  \leq  3\sqrt{{t}_{0} - a} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}} \leq  3\sqrt{E} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

Set

(79.17)

\[
{t}_{1} = a + \frac{b - a}{3},\;{t}_{2} = a + \frac{2\left( {b - a}\right) }{3}
\]

and

(79.18)

\[
\rho  = \left( {3\sqrt{E} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right) {\left( \frac{1}{3}{E}_{ - }\right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

By construction, \( {t}_{2} \leq  {t}_{0} - {r}_{0}^{2} \) . Note that there is a \( \bar{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) such that \( R\left( {\gamma \left( \bar{t}\right) }\right)  \leq  \rho \) . Otherwise we would get

(79.19)

\[
{\mathcal{L}}_{ + }\left( \gamma \right)  > {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{t}_{0} - t}{R}_{ + }\left( {\gamma \left( t\right) }\right) {dt} \geq  \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}{E}_{ - }}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}{\rho dt} \geq  \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}{E}_{ - }}\left( {\frac{1}{3}{E}_{ - }}\right) \rho  = 3\sqrt{E} + 4{E}^{\frac{3}{2}},
\]

contradicting (79.16).

Put \( \bar{x} = \gamma \left( \bar{t}\right) \) . By Lemma 70.1, there is an estimate of the form

(79.20)

\[
R \leq  \text{ const. }{s}^{-2}
\]

on the parabolic ball \( \widehat{P} = P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) with \( {s}^{-2} = \) const. \( \left( {\rho  + {r}_{ - }^{-2}}\right) \) . Appealing to Hamilton-Ivey curvature pinching as usual, we get that \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq \) const. \( {s}^{-2} \) in \( \widehat{P} \) . If \( \bar{t} - {s}^{2} < a \) then we shrink \( s \) (as little as possible) to ensure that \( \widehat{P} \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{\lbrack a, b)} \) . Provided that \( \bar{\delta } \) is less than a small constant \( {c}_{1} = {c}_{1}\left( {{r}_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) , we can guarantee that \( \widehat{P} \) is unscathed, by forcing the curvature in a surgery cap to exceed our bound (79.20) on \( R \) . Put \( U = {\mathcal{M}}_{\bar{t} - \frac{1}{2}{s}^{2}} \cap  \widehat{P} \) . If \( s < \epsilon \) then the \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) -noncollapsing assumption on \( \lbrack a, b) \) gives a lower bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {\widetilde{B}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}, s}\right) }\right) {s}^{-3} \) . If \( s \geq  \epsilon \) then the \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) -noncollapsing assumption gives a lower bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\epsilon /2}\right) }\right) {\left( \epsilon /2\right) }^{-3} \) . In either, case, we get a lower bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}, s}\right) }\right) \) and hence a lower bound \( \operatorname{vol}\left( U\right)  \geq \; v = v\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) . Now every point in \( U \) can be joined to \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) by a curve of \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) - length at most \( {\Lambda }_{ + } = {\Lambda }_{ + }\left( {{r}_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) , by concatenating an admissible curve \( \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} - \frac{1}{2}{s}^{2},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) (of controlled \( {\mathcal{L}}_{ + } \) -length) with \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  \bar{t},{t}_{0}\right\rbrack  } \) . Shrinking \( \bar{\delta } \) again, we can apply Lemmas 78.3 and 79.3 with (79.14) to ensure that every point in \( U \) can be joined to \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) by a minimizing \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic lying in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{\text{ reg }} \cup  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}} \) . Lemma 78.11 then implies that

(79.21)

\[
\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq  {\kappa }_{1} = {\kappa }_{1}\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) .
\]

(We briefly recall the argument. We have a parabolic ball around \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , of small but controlled size, on which we have uniform curvature bounds. The lower volume bound coming from the \( {\kappa }_{ - } \) -noncollapsing assumption on \( \lbrack a, b) \) means that we have bounded geometry on the parabolic ball. As we have a fixed upper bound on \( l\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , we can estimate from below the reduced volume of the accessible points \( Y \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{\bar{t} - \frac{1}{2}{s}^{2}}^{ + } \) . Then we obtain a lower bound on \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \) as in Theorem 26.2.)

This completes the proof of the lemma when \( {r}_{0} \leq  \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) and \( {r}_{0} \geq  \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

(79.22)

Now suppose that \( {r}_{0} > \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) . Applying our noncollapsing estimate (79.21) to the ball of radius \( \sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3} \) gives

\[
\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq  \left( {\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\sqrt{{E}_{ - }/3}}\right) {\left( {E}_{ - }/3\right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}}\right) }\right) \frac{{\left( {E}_{ - }/3\right) }^{\frac{3}{2}}}{{r}_{0}^{3}} \geq  {\kappa }_{1}\frac{{\left( {E}_{ - }/3\right) }^{\frac{3}{2}}}{{\epsilon }^{3}} = {\kappa }_{2},
\]

where \( {\kappa }_{2} = {\kappa }_{2}\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) .

The next sublemma deals with the case when \( {r}_{0} < \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

Sublemma 79.23. If \( {r}_{0} < \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) then \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq  {\kappa }_{3} = {\kappa }_{3}\left( {{r}_{ - },{\kappa }_{ - },{E}_{ - }, E}\right) \) .

Proof. Let \( s \) be the maximum of the numbers \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {{r}_{0},\frac{{r}_{ + }}{100}}\right\rbrack \) such that \( B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\bar{s}}\right) \) is unscathed on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\bar{s}}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {\bar{s}}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\bar{s}, - {\bar{s}}^{-2}}\right) \) . Then either

(a) Some point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) on the frontier of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) lies in a surgery cap

or

(b) Some point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) in the closure of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) has \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  = {s}^{-2} \)

or

(c) \( s = \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

In case (a) the scalar curvature at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) will satisfy \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \left( {\frac{{h}^{-2}}{2},{10}{h}^{-2}}\right) \) , since \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) lies in the cap at the surgery time. Since \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {s}^{-2} \) we conclude that \( s \leq \) const. \( h\left( t\right) \) . If \( \bar{\delta } \) is small then the pointed time slice \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{t},\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) will be close, modulo scaling by \( h\left( t\right) \) , to the initial condition of the standard solution with the basepoint somewhere in the cap. Using the fact that the time slices of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) have comparable metrics, along with the fact that \( {r}_{0} \leq  s \leq \) const. \( h\left( t\right) \) , we get a lower bound vol \( \left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq \) const.

In case (b), we have a static curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) such that \( \gamma \left( t\right)  = \left( {x, t}\right) ,\gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in \; \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \) , and \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  = {s}^{-2} \geq  {10}^{4}{r}_{ + }^{-2} \) . Hence by \( \Phi \) -pinching, \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{100}{s}^{-2} \geq \; {100}{r}_{ + }^{-2} \) (cf. the remark just before the statement of Lemma 79.12). With reference to the constant \( \eta \) of (69.2), put \( \sigma  = {10}^{-6}\min \left( {1,\frac{1}{\eta }}\right) \) . Let \( \alpha  : \left\lbrack  {0,\widehat{\rho }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}}^{ - } \) be a minimizing geodesic from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) to \( \gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \) . We can find a point \( z \) along \( \alpha \) with \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,\gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right)  \leq  {\sigma s} \) and \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 - \sigma }\right) s \) . Let \( \bar{\gamma } : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) be the static curve ending at \( z \) and put \( \left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  = \bar{\gamma }\left( t\right) \) . In brief, we get \( \left( {\bar{x}, t}\right) \) by "pulling \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) slightly inward from the boundary".

From the distance distortion estimate of Section 27, we can say that \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x}, x}\right)  \leq  {10}^{6}{\sigma s} \) . Then applying (69.2) along a minimizing time- \( t \) curve from \( \bar{x} \) to \( x \) , we conclude that

(79.24)

\[
\left| {{R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  - {R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{2}\eta {\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x}, x}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}s,
\]

so \( {R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \leq  {R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {x, t}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}s \leq  {20s} \) and hence \( R\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{400}{s}^{-2} \geq  {25}{r}_{ + }^{-2} \) . In particular, \( \left( {\bar{x}, t}\right) \) has a canonical neighborhood. We also know that \( R\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \leq  6\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  6{s}^{-2} \) . It follows from the definition of canonical neighborhoods (see Definition 69.1) that there is some universal constant so that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {\bar{x}, t,{10}^{-9}s}\right) }\right)  \geq \) const. \( {s}^{3} \) . (We recall that from Lemma 60.3, there is a \( \kappa  > 0 \) such that a standard solution is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed as scales < 1.) The distance distortion estimate ensures that \( B\left( {\bar{x}, t,{10}^{-9}s}\right)  \subset  B\left( {z,{t}_{0},{10}^{-6}s}\right)  \subset \; B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) \) . Then the standard volume distortion estimate implies that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) }\right)  \geq \) const. \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {\bar{x}, t,{10}^{-9}s}\right) }\right)  \geq \) const. \( {s}^{3} \) , again for some universal constant. Finally we use Bishop-Gromov volume comparison to get \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq \) const. \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) }\right) {s}^{-3} \) .

Proof. Let \( s \) be the maximum of the numbers \( \bar{s} \in  \left\lbrack  {{r}_{0},\frac{{r}_{ + }}{100}}\right\rbrack \) such that \( B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\bar{s}}\right) \) is unscathed on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\bar{s}}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , and \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  \leq  {\bar{s}}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},\bar{s}, - {\bar{s}}^{-2}}\right) \) . Then either

(a) Some point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) on the frontier of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) lies in a surgery cap

or

(b) Some point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) in the closure of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) has \( \left| \mathrm{{Rm}}\right|  = {s}^{-2} \)

or

(c) \( s = \frac{{r}_{ + }}{100} \) .

In case (a) the scalar curvature at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) will satisfy \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \left( {\frac{{h}^{-2}}{2},{10}{h}^{-2}}\right) \) , since \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) lies in the cap at the surgery time. Since \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {s}^{-2} \) we conclude that \( s \leq \) const. \( h\left( t\right) \) . If \( \bar{\delta } \) is small then the pointed time slice \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{t},\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) will be close, modulo scaling by \( h\left( t\right) \) , to the initial condition of the standard solution with the basepoint somewhere in the cap. Using the fact that the time slices of \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s, - {s}^{2}}\right) \) have comparable metrics, along with the fact that \( {r}_{0} \leq  s \leq \) const. \( h\left( t\right) \) , we get a lower bound vol \( \left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right) {r}_{0}^{-3} \geq \) const.

In case (b), we have a static curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) such that \( \gamma \left( t\right)  = \left( {x, t}\right) ,\gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in \; \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \) , and \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  = {s}^{-2} \geq  {10}^{4}{r}_{ + }^{-2} \) . Hence by \( \Phi \) -pinching, \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{100}{s}^{-2} \geq \; {100}{r}_{ + }^{-2} \) (cf. the remark just before the statement of Lemma 79.12). With reference to the constant \( \eta \) of (69.2), put \( \sigma  = {10}^{-6}\min \left( {1,\frac{1}{\eta }}\right) \) . Let \( \alpha  : \left\lbrack  {0,\widehat{\rho }}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \subset  {\mathcal{M}}_{{t}_{0}}^{ - } \) be a minimizing geodesic from \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) to \( \gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right)  \in  \overline{B\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}, s}\right) } \) . We can find a point \( z \) along \( \alpha \) with \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,\gamma \left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right)  \leq  {\sigma s} \) and \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {1 - \sigma }\right) s \) . Let \( \bar{\gamma } : \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) be the static curve ending at \( z \) and put \( \left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  = \bar{\gamma }\left( t\right) \) . In brief, we get \( \left( {\bar{x}, t}\right) \) by "pulling \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) slightly inward from the boundary".

From the distance distortion estimate of Section 27, we can say that \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x}, x}\right)  \leq  {10}^{6}{\sigma s} \) . Then applying (69.2) along a minimizing time- \( t \) curve from \( \bar{x} \) to \( x \) , we conclude that

nodes.proof:
Suppose first that \( {T}_{1} < 0 \) . Then the arguments of Theorem 52.7 apply in the time interval \( \left( {{T}_{1},0}\right\rbrack \) , to give the Ricci flow (without surgery) \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}^{\infty },\left( {{\bar{x}}^{\infty },0}\right) }\right) \) . Since \( {r}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) , Hamilton-Ivey pinching implies that \( {\mathcal{M}}^{\infty } \) will have nonnegative curvature. The fact that the canonical neighborhood assumption, with \( \epsilon \) replaced by \( {2\epsilon } \) , holds for each \( {\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}^{\alpha } \) allows us to deduce that the scalar curvature of \( {\mathcal{M}}^{\infty } \) is globally bounded above by some number \( Q < \infty \) ; compare with Section 46 and Step 4 of the proof of Theorem 52.7.

Now suppose that \( {T}_{1} = 0 \) . The argument is similar to Steps 2 and 3 of the proof of Theorem 52.7. As in Step 2, or more precisely as in Lemma 70.2, for each \( \rho  < \infty \) the scalar curvature on \( B\left( {{\bar{x}}^{\alpha },0,\rho }\right)  \subset  {\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}_{0}^{\alpha } \) is uniformly bounded in terms of \( \alpha \) . Given \( \rho  < \infty \) and \( \left( {{x}^{\alpha },0}\right)  \in  B\left( {{\bar{x}}^{\alpha },0,\rho }\right)  \subset  {\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}^{\alpha } \) , if the parabolic region of Lemma 70.1 (centered around \( \left. {\left( {{x}^{\alpha },0}\right)  \in  {\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}^{\alpha }}\right) \) is unscathed then we can apply the \( {2\epsilon } \) -canonical neighborhood assumption on \( {\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}^{\alpha } \) , Lemma 70.1 and Appendix D to derive bounds on the curvature derivatives at \( \left( {{x}^{\alpha },0}\right)  \in  {\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}_{0}^{\alpha } \) that depend on \( \rho \) but are independent of \( \alpha \) . If the parabolic region is scathed then we can apply Lemma 74.1, along with our scalar curvature bound at \( \left( {{x}^{\alpha },0}\right) \) , to again obtain uniform bounds on the curvature derivatives at \( \left( {{x}^{\alpha },0}\right) \) . Hence there is a subsequence of the pointed Riemannian manifolds \( {\left\{  \left( {\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}_{0}^{\alpha },{\bar{x}}^{\alpha }\right) \right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1}^{\infty } \) that converges to a smooth complete pointed Riemannian manifold \( \left( {{\mathcal{M}}_{0}^{\infty },{\bar{x}}^{\infty }}\right) \) . As in the previous case, it will have bounded nonnegative sectional curvature.

This proves the lemma. Alternatively, in the case \( {T}_{1} = 0 \) one can argue directly that if the parabolic region of Lemma 70.1 is scathed then \( \left( {{\bar{x}}^{\alpha },{T}^{\alpha }}\right) \) has a canonical neighborhood; see the rest of the proof of Proposition 77.2.

For terminology, with reference to Section 68, by a time-dependent family \( \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {c, d}\right\rbrack  }}B\left( {x, t, r}\right) \) of metric balls we mean first that there is a static curve \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {c, d}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathcal{M} \) , whose intersection with each \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t} \) will be denoted by \( x \) , and second that there is a subset \( \mathcal{U} \) of \( \mathcal{M} \) so that

(1) If \( t \notin  \left\lbrack  {c, d}\right\rbrack \) then \( \mathcal{U} \cap  {\mathcal{M}}_{t} = \varnothing \) .

(2) If \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {c, d}\right\rbrack \) is not a singularity time then \( \mathcal{U} \cap  {\mathcal{M}}_{t} \) is the \( r \) -ball around \( x \) in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t} \) .

(3) If \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {c, d}\right\rbrack \) is a surgery time \( {t}_{k}^{ + } \) then \( \mathcal{U} \cap  {\mathcal{M}}_{t} \) is the image in \( {\mathcal{M}}_{t} \) of an \( r \) -ball around \( x \) in \( {\Omega }_{k} \) , that lies entirely in \( {X}_{k}^{ + } \subset  {\Omega }_{k} \) .

At the expense of being redundant, if these conditions are satisfied then we will say that we have an unscathed time-dependent family of metric balls, to emphasize that the metric balls do not touch the surgery regions. The restriction of the Ricci-flow-with-surgery to \( \mathcal{U} \) is a smooth Riemannian metric \( g \) on the "horizontal" subbundle of \( T\mathcal{U} \) .

Lemma 82.1. Given \( w > 0 \) , there exist \( {\tau }_{0} = {\tau }_{0}\left( w\right)  > 0 \) and \( {K}_{0}^{\prime } = {K}_{0}^{\prime }\left( w\right)  < \infty \) with the following property. Suppose that we have a Ricci flow with \( \left( {r,\delta }\right) \) -cutoff such that

1. \( \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\tau {r}_{0}^{2},0}\right\rbrack  }}B\left( {{x}_{0}, t,{r}_{0}}\right) \) is an unscathed time-dependent family of metric balls, where \( \tau  \leq  {\tau }_{0} \) .

2. The sectional curvatures are bounded below by \( - {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on the above family of balls.

3. \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{0},0,{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  w{r}_{0}^{3} \) .

Then

(1) \( R \leq  {K}_{0}^{\prime }{\tau }^{-1}{r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\tau {r}_{0}^{2}/2,0}\right\rbrack  }}B\left( {{x}_{0}, t,{r}_{0}/2}\right) \) , and

If \( {\tau }_{0} \) is sufficiently small, then for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\tau {r}_{0}^{2},0}\right\rbrack \) and \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  B\left( {{x}_{0}, t,9{r}_{0}/{10}}\right) \) , the lower curvature bound \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq   - {r}_{0}^{-2} \) on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},0,{r}_{0}, - \tau {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) implies that \( \left( {x,0}\right)  \in  B\left( {{x}_{0},0,{r}_{0}}\right) \) (more precisely, that \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) lies on a static curve with one endpoint in \( B\left( {{x}_{0},0,{r}_{0}}\right) \) , or equivalently, that \( \left. {\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {{x}_{0},0,{r}_{0}, - \tau {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) }\right) \) . Thus \( \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\tau {r}_{0}^{2},0}\right\rbrack  }}B\left( {{x}_{0}, t,9{r}_{0}/{10}}\right)  \subset  P\left( {{x}_{0},0,{r}_{0}, - \tau {r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) and so \( \mathrm{{Rm}} \geq   - {r}_{0}^{-2} \geq   - {\left( 9{r}_{0}/{10}\right) }^{-2} \) on \( \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\tau {\left( 9{r}_{0}/{10}\right) }^{2},0}\right\rbrack  }}B\left( {{x}_{0}, t,9{r}_{0}/{10}}\right) \) .

(82.3)

\[
P\left( {{x}_{0},0,{r}_{0}/4, - \tau {r}_{0}^{2}/2}\right)  \subset  \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\tau {r}_{0}^{2}/2,0}\right\rbrack  }}B\left( {{x}_{0}, t,9{r}_{0}/{20}}\right) .
\]

Suppose that the claim is not true. Then there is a sequence of Riemannian manifolds \( {\left\{  {M}_{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1}^{\infty } \) and balls \( B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right)  \subset  {M}_{i} \) with compact closure so that \( {\left. \operatorname{Rm}\right| }_{B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) } \geq   - 1 \) and \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) }\right)  \geq  w \) , along with a sequence \( {r}_{i}^{\prime } \rightarrow  0 \) so that each subball \( B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime }}\right)  \subset  B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) \) has a subball \( B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime \prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }}\right)  \subset  B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime }}\right) \) with \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime \prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }}\right) }\right)  < (1 - \; \widehat{\epsilon }){\omega }_{3}{\left( {r}^{\prime \prime }\right) }^{n} \) . After taking a subsequence, we can assume that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) ,{x}_{i}}\right)  = \left( {X,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) in the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff topology, where \( \left( {X,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) is a pointed Alexandrov space with curvature bounded below by -1 . From [12, Theorem 10.8], the Riemannian volume forms \( {\operatorname{dvol}}_{{M}_{i}} \) converge weakly to the three-dimensional Hausdorff measure \( \mu \) of \( X \) . If \( {x}_{\infty }^{\prime } \) is a regular point of \( X \) then there is some \( \delta  > 0 \) so that \( B\left( {{x}_{\infty }^{\prime },\delta }\right) \) has compact closure in \( X \) and for all \( r < \delta ,\mu \left( {B\left( {{x}_{\infty }^{\prime }, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - \frac{\widehat{\epsilon }}{10}}\right) {\omega }_{3}{r}^{3} \) . Fixing such an \( r \) for the moment, for large \( i \) there are balls \( B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime }, r}\right)  \subset  B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) \) with \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime }, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - \frac{\widehat{\epsilon }}{5}}\right) {\omega }_{3}{r}^{3} \) . Recalling the sequence \( \left\{  {r}_{i}^{\prime }\right\} \) , by hypothesis there is a subball \( B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime \prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }}\right)  \subset  B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime }}\right) \) with \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime \prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }}\right) }\right)  < \left( {1 - \widehat{\epsilon }}\right) {\omega }_{3}{\left( {r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }\right) }^{3} \) . Clearly \( B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime }, r}\right)  \subset  B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime \prime }, r + {r}_{i}^{\prime }}\right) \) . From the Bishop-Gromov inequality,

(83.2)

\[
\frac{\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime \prime }, r + {r}_{i}^{\prime }}\right) }\right) }{\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime \prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }}\right) }\right) } \leq  \frac{{\int }_{0}^{r + {r}_{i}^{\prime }}{\sinh }^{2}\left( s\right) {ds}}{{\int }_{0}^{{r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }}{\sinh }^{2}\left( s\right) {ds}}.
\]

Then(83.3)

\[
\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime }, r}\right) }\right)  \leq  \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime \prime }, r + {r}_{i}^{\prime }}\right) }\right)  \leq  \left( {1 - \widehat{\epsilon }}\right) {\omega }_{3}\frac{{\left( {r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }\right) }^{3}}{{\int }_{0}^{{r}_{i}^{\prime \prime }}{\sinh }^{2}\left( s\right) {ds}}{\int }_{0}^{r + {r}_{i}^{\prime }}{\sinh }^{2}\left( s\right) {ds}.
\]

For large \( i \) we obtain

(83.4)

\[
\operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime }, r}\right) }\right)  \leq  \left( {1 - \frac{\widehat{\epsilon }}{2}}\right) {\omega }_{3} \cdot  3{\int }_{0}^{r}{\sinh }^{2}\left( s\right) {ds}.
\]

Then if we choose \( r \) to be sufficiently small, we contradict the fact that \( \operatorname{vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime }, r}\right) }\right)  \geq \; \left( {1 - \frac{\widehat{\epsilon }}{5}}\right) {\omega }_{3}{r}^{3} \) for all \( i \) .
