nodes.proof:
Without loss of generality, we may assume \( r \leq  \theta /\sqrt{M} \) and the exponential map at \( p \) at time \( t = 0 \) is injective on the ball of radius \( r \) (by passing to a local cover if necessary, and pulling back the local solution of the Ricci flow to the ball of radius \( r \) in the tangent space at \( p \) at time \( t = 0 \) ).

Recall

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| Rm\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2} + C{\left| Rm\right| }^{3}
\]

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{2}Rm\right| }^{2} + C\left| {Rm}\right|  \cdot  {\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2}.
\]

Define

\[
S = \left( {B{M}^{2} + {\left| Rm\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2}
\]

where \( B \) is a positive constant to be determined. By choosing \( B \geq  {C}^{2}/4 \) and using the Cauchy inequality, we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}S \leq  {\Delta S} - {2B}{M}^{2}{\left| {\nabla }^{2}Rm\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{4}
\]

\[
+ {CM}{\left| \nabla {Rm}\right| }^{2} \cdot  \left| {{\nabla }^{2}{Rm}}\right|  + {CB}{M}^{3}{\left| \nabla {Rm}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  {\Delta S} - {\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{4} + C{B}^{2}{M}^{6}
\]

\[
\leq  {\Delta S} - \frac{{S}^{2}}{{\left( B + 1\right) }^{2}{M}^{4}} + C{B}^{2}{M}^{6}.
\]

If we take

\[
F = b\left( {B{M}^{2} + {\left| Rm\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2}/{M}^{4} = {bS}/{M}^{4},
\]

and \( b \leq  \min \left\{  {1/{\left( B + 1\right) }^{2},1/C{B}^{2}}\right\} \) , we get

(1.4.3)

\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial t} \leq  {\Delta F} - {F}^{2} + {M}^{2}.
\]

We now want to choose a cutoff function \( \varphi \) with the support in the ball \( {B}_{0}\left( {p, r}\right) \) such that at \( t = 0 \) ,

\[
\varphi \left( p\right)  = r,\;0 \leq  \varphi  \leq  {Ar},
\]

and

\[
\left| {\nabla \varphi }\right|  \leq  A,\;\left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  \frac{A}{r}
\]

for some positive constant \( A \) depending only on the dimension. Indeed, let \( g \) : \( \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right)  \rightarrow  \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) be a smooth, nonnegative function satisfying

\[
g\left( u\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} 1, & u \in  \left( {-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}}\right) , \\  0, & \text{ outside }\left( {-1,1}\right) . \end{array}\right.
\]

Set

\[
\varphi  = {rg}\left( \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}\right) ,
\]

where \( s \) is the geodesic distance function from \( p \) with respect to the metric at \( t = 0 \) . Then

\[
\nabla \varphi  = \frac{1}{r}{g}^{\prime }\left( \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}\right)  \cdot  {2s}\nabla s
\]

and hence

\[
\left| {\nabla \varphi }\right|  \leq  2{C}_{1}
\]

Also,

\[
{\nabla }^{2}\varphi  = \frac{1}{r}{g}^{\prime \prime }\left( \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}\right) \frac{1}{{r}^{2}}4{s}^{2}\nabla s \cdot  \nabla s + \frac{1}{r}{g}^{\prime }\left( \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}\right) 2\nabla s \cdot  \nabla s + \frac{1}{r}{g}^{\prime }\left( \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}\right)  \cdot  {2s}{\nabla }^{2}s.
\]

Thus, by using the standard Hessian comparison,

\[
\left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  \frac{{C}_{1}}{r} + \frac{{C}_{1}}{r}\left| {s{\nabla }^{2}s}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{{C}_{1}}{r}\left( {1 + s\left( {\frac{{C}_{2}}{s} + \sqrt{M}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{{C}_{3}}{r}.
\]

Here \( {C}_{1},{C}_{2} \) and \( {C}_{3} \) are positive constants depending only on the dimension.

Now extend \( \varphi \) to \( U \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{\theta }{M}}\right\rbrack \) by letting \( \varphi \) to be zero outside \( {B}_{0}\left( {p, r}\right) \) and independent of time. Introduce the barrier function

(1.4.4)

\[
H = \frac{\left( {{12} + 4\sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{2}}{{\varphi }^{2}} + \frac{1}{t} + M
\]

which is defined and smooth on the set \( \{ \varphi  > 0\}  \times  (0, T\rbrack \) .

As the metric evolves, we will still have \( 0 \leq  \varphi  \leq  {Ar} \) (since \( \varphi \) is independent of time \( t) \) ; but \( {\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \) and \( \varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right| \) may increase. By continuity it will be a while before they double.

CLAIM 1. As long as

\[
{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  2{A}^{2},\;\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  2{A}^{2},
\]

we have

\[
\frac{\partial H}{\partial t} > {\Delta H} - {H}^{2} + {M}^{2}.
\]

Indeed, by the definition of \( H \) , we have

\[
{H}^{2} > \frac{{\left( {12} + 4\sqrt{n}\right) }^{2}{A}^{4}}{{\varphi }^{4}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{2}} + {M}^{2}
\]

\[
\frac{\partial H}{\partial t} =  - \frac{1}{{t}^{2}}
\]

and

\[
{\Delta H} = \left( {{12} + 4\sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{2}\Delta \left( \frac{1}{{\varphi }^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {{12} + 4\sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{2}\left( \frac{6{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} - {2\varphi \Delta \varphi }}{{\varphi }^{4}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{12} + 4\sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{2}\left( \frac{{12}{A}^{2} + 4\sqrt{n}{A}^{2}}{{\varphi }^{4}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{{\left( {12} + 4\sqrt{n}\right) }^{2}{A}^{4}}{{\varphi }^{4}}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
{H}^{2} > {\Delta H} - \frac{\partial H}{\partial t} + {M}^{2}.
\]

CLAIM 2. If the constant \( \theta  > 0 \) is small enough compared to \( b, B \) and \( A \) , then we have the following property: as long as \( r \leq  \theta /\sqrt{M}, t \leq  \theta /M \) and \( F \leq  H \) , we will have

\[
{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  2{A}^{2}\;\text{ and }\;\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  2{A}^{2}.
\]

Indeed, by considering the evolution of \( \nabla \varphi \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\nabla }_{a}\varphi  = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{F}_{a}^{i}{\nabla }_{i}\varphi }\right)
\]

\[
= {F}_{a}^{i}{\nabla }_{i}\left( \frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial t}\right)  + {\nabla }_{i}\varphi {R}_{k}^{i}{F}_{a}^{k}
\]

\[
= {R}_{ab}{\nabla }_{b}\varphi
\]

which implies

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  {CM}{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2},
\]

and then

\[
{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  {A}^{2}{e}^{CMt} \leq  2{A}^{2},
\]

provided \( t \leq  \theta /M \) with \( \theta  \leq  \log 2/C \) .

By considering the evolution of \( {\nabla }^{2}\varphi \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}\varphi }\right)  = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{F}_{a}^{i}{F}_{b}^{j}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\varphi }\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{F}_{a}^{i}{F}_{b}^{j}\left( {\frac{{\partial }^{2}\varphi }{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}} - {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}\frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial {x}^{k}}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}\left( \frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial t}\right)  + {R}_{ac}{\nabla }_{b}{\nabla }_{c}\varphi  + {R}_{bc}{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{c}\varphi
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{ab} - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bc} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}}\right) {\nabla }_{c}\varphi
\]

which implies

(1.4.5)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  C\left| {Rm}\right|  \cdot  \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  + C\left| {\nabla {Rm}}\right|  \cdot  \left| {\nabla \varphi }\right| .
\]

By assumption \( F \leq  H \) , we have

(1.4.6)

\[
{\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{2{M}^{2}}{bB}\left( {\frac{\left( {{12} + 4\sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{2}}{{\varphi }^{2}} + \frac{1}{t}}\right) ,\;\text{ for }t \leq  \theta /M.
\]

Thus by noting \( \varphi \) independent of \( t \) and \( \varphi  \leq  {Ar} \) , we get from (1.4.5) and (1.4.6) that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right| }\right)  \leq  {CM}\left( {\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  + 1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right)
\]

which implies

\[
\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  {e}^{CMt}\left\lbrack  {{\left. \left( \varphi \left| {\nabla }^{2}\varphi \right| \right) \right| }_{t = 0} + {CM}{\int }_{0}^{t}\left( {1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right) {dt}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\leq  {e}^{CMt}\left\lbrack  {{A}^{2} + {CM}\left( {t + {2r}\sqrt{t}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\leq  2{A}^{2}
\]

provided \( r \leq  \theta /\sqrt{M} \) , and \( t \leq  \theta /M \) with \( \theta \) small enough. Therefore we have obtained Claim 2.

The combination of Claim 1 and Claim 2 gives us

\[
\frac{\partial H}{\partial t} > {\Delta H} - {H}^{2} + {M}^{2}
\]

as long as \( r \leq  \theta /\sqrt{M},\;t \leq  \theta /M \) and \( F \leq  H \) . And (1.4.3) tells us

\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial t} \leq  {\Delta F} - {F}^{2} + {M}^{2}.
\]

Then the standard maximum principle immediately gives the estimate

\[
{\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  C{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{\varphi }^{2}} + \frac{1}{t} + M}\right) \;\text{ on }\{ \varphi  > 0\}  \times  \left( {0,\frac{\theta }{M}}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

which implies the first order derivative estimate.

The higher order derivative estimates can be obtained in the same way by induction. Suppose we have the bounds

\[
{\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  {C}_{k}{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right) .
\]

As before, by (1.4.1) and (1.4.2), we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2} + C{M}^{3}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right) ,
\]

and

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \Delta {\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 2}Rm\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ {CM}{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2} + C{M}^{3}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2\left( {k + 1}\right) }} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k + 1}} + {M}^{k + 1}}\right) .
\]

Here and in the following we denote by \( C \) various positive constants depending only on \( {C}_{k} \) and the dimension.

Define

\[
{S}_{k} = \left\lbrack  {{B}_{k}{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right)  + {\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack   \cdot  {\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2}
\]

where \( {B}_{k} \) is a positive constant to be determined. By choosing \( {B}_{k} \) large enough and Cauchy inequality, we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{S}_{k} \leq  \left\lbrack  {-\frac{k}{{t}^{k + 1}} + \Delta {\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+C{M}^{3}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right) }\right\rbrack   \cdot  {\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \left\lbrack  {{B}_{k}{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right)  + {\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\cdot  \left\lbrack  {\Delta {\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 2}Rm\right| }^{2} + {CM}{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+C{M}^{3}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2\left( {k + 1}\right) }} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k + 1}} + {M}^{k + 1}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta {S}_{k} + 8\left| {{\nabla }^{k}{Rm}}\right|  \cdot  {\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2} \cdot  \left| {{\nabla }^{k + 2}{Rm}}\right|  - \frac{k}{{t}^{k + 1}}{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
- 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{4} + C{M}^{3}{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 2}Rm\right| }^{2}\left\lbrack  {{B}_{k}{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right)  + {\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ {CM}{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2}\left\lbrack  {{B}_{k}{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right)  + {\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ C{M}^{3}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2\left( {k + 1}\right) }} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k + 1}} + {M}^{k + 1}}\right)
\]

\[
\cdot  \left\lbrack  {{B}_{k}{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right)  + {\left| {\nabla }^{k}Rm\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta {S}_{k} - {\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{4} + C{B}_{k}^{2}{M}^{6}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{4k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{2k}} + {M}^{2k}}\right)
\]

\[
+ C{B}_{k}{M}^{5}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2\left( {{2k} + 1}\right) }} + \frac{1}{{t}^{{2k} + 1}} + {M}^{{2k} + 1}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta {S}_{k} - {\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{4} + C{B}_{k}^{2}{M}^{5}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2\left( {{2k} + 1}\right) }} + \frac{1}{{t}^{{2k} + 1}} + {M}^{{2k} + 1}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta {S}_{k} - \frac{{S}_{k}}{{\left( B + 1\right) }^{2}{M}^{4}{\left( \frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
+ C{B}_{k}^{2}{M}^{5}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2\left( {{2k} + 1}\right) }} + \frac{1}{{t}^{{2k} + 1}} + {M}^{{2k} + 1}}\right) .
\]

Let \( u = 1/{r}^{2} + 1/t + M \) and set \( {F}_{k} = b{S}_{k}/{u}^{k} \) . Then

\[
\frac{\partial {F}_{k}}{\partial t} \leq  \Delta {F}_{k} - \frac{{F}_{k}^{2}}{b{\left( {B}_{k} + 1\right) }^{2}{M}^{4}{u}^{k}} + {bC}{B}_{k}^{2}{M}^{5}{u}^{k + 1} + k{F}_{k}u
\]

\[
\leq  \Delta {F}_{k} - \frac{{F}_{k}^{2}}{{2b}{\left( {B}_{k} + 1\right) }^{2}{M}^{4}{u}^{k}} + b\left( {C + 2{k}^{2}}\right) {\left( {B}_{k} + 1\right) }^{2}{M}^{4}{u}^{k + 2}.
\]

By choosing \( b \leq  1/\left( {2\left( {C + 2{k}^{2}}\right) {\left( {B}_{k} + 1\right) }^{2}{M}^{4}}\right) \) , we get

\[
\frac{\partial {F}_{k}}{\partial t} \leq  \Delta {F}_{k} - \frac{1}{{u}^{k}}{F}_{k}^{2} + {u}^{k + 2}.
\]

Introduce

\[
{H}_{k} = 5\left( {k + 1}\right) \left( {2\left( {k + 1}\right)  + 1 + \sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{2}{\varphi }^{-2\left( {k + 1}\right) } + L{t}^{-\left( {k + 1}\right) } + {M}^{k + 1},
\]

where \( L \geq  k + 2 \) . Then by using Claim 1 and Claim 2, we have

\[
\frac{\partial {H}_{k}}{\partial t} =  - \left( {k + 1}\right) L{t}^{-\left( {k + 2}\right) },
\]

\[
\Delta {H}_{k} \leq  {20}{\left( k + 1\right) }^{2}\left( {2\left( {k + 1}\right)  + 1 + \sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{4}{\varphi }^{-2\left( {k + 2}\right) }
\]

and

\[
{H}_{k}^{2} > {25}{\left( k + 1\right) }^{2}\left( {2\left( {k + 1}\right)  + 1 + \sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{4}{\varphi }^{-4\left( {k + 1}\right) } + {L}^{2}{t}^{-2\left( {k + 1}\right) } + {M}^{2\left( {k + 1}\right) }.
\]

These imply

\[
\frac{\partial {H}_{k}}{\partial t} > \Delta {H}_{k} - \frac{1}{{u}^{k}}{H}_{k}^{2} + {u}^{k + 2}.
\]

Then the maximum principle immediately gives the estimate

\[
{F}_{k} \leq  {H}_{k}\text{ . }
\]

In particular,

\[
\frac{b}{{u}^{k}}{B}_{k}{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2k}} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k}} + {M}^{k}}\right)  \cdot  {\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  5\left( {k + 1}\right) \left( {2\left( {k + 1}\right)  + 1 + \sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{2}{\varphi }^{-2\left( {k + 1}\right) } + L{t}^{-\left( {k + 1}\right) } + {M}^{k + 1}.
\]

So by the definition of \( u \) and the choosing of \( b \) , we obtain the desired estimate

\[
{\left| {\nabla }^{k + 1}Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  {C}_{k + 1}{M}^{2}\left( {\frac{1}{{r}^{2\left( {k + 1}\right) }} + \frac{1}{{t}^{k + 1}} + {M}^{k + 1}}\right) .
\]

Therefore we have completed the proof of the theorem. [

\[

and

\]

\[
= \frac{{\left( {12} + 4\sqrt{n}\right) }^{2}{A}^{4}}{{\varphi }^{4}}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
{H}^{2} > {\Delta H} - \frac{\partial H}{\partial t} + {M}^{2}.
\]

nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content:
CLAIM 2. If the constant \( \theta  > 0 \) is small enough compared to \( b, B \) and \( A \) , then we have the following property: as long as \( r \leq  \theta /\sqrt{M}, t \leq  \theta /M \) and \( F \leq  H \) , we will have

\[
{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  2{A}^{2}\;\text{ and }\;\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  2{A}^{2}.
\]

Indeed, by considering the evolution of \( \nabla \varphi \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\nabla }_{a}\varphi  = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{F}_{a}^{i}{\nabla }_{i}\varphi }\right)
\]

\[
= {F}_{a}^{i}{\nabla }_{i}\left( \frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial t}\right)  + {\nabla }_{i}\varphi {R}_{k}^{i}{F}_{a}^{k}
\]

\[
= {R}_{ab}{\nabla }_{b}\varphi
\]

which implies

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  {CM}{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2},
\]

and then

\[
{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} \leq  {A}^{2}{e}^{CMt} \leq  2{A}^{2},
\]

provided \( t \leq  \theta /M \) with \( \theta  \leq  \log 2/C \) .

By considering the evolution of \( {\nabla }^{2}\varphi \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}\varphi }\right)  = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{F}_{a}^{i}{F}_{b}^{j}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\varphi }\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{F}_{a}^{i}{F}_{b}^{j}\left( {\frac{{\partial }^{2}\varphi }{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}} - {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}\frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial {x}^{k}}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}\left( \frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial t}\right)  + {R}_{ac}{\nabla }_{b}{\nabla }_{c}\varphi  + {R}_{bc}{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{c}\varphi
\]

\[
+ \left( {{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{ab} - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bc} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}}\right) {\nabla }_{c}\varphi
\]

which implies

(1.4.5)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  C\left| {Rm}\right|  \cdot  \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  + C\left| {\nabla {Rm}}\right|  \cdot  \left| {\nabla \varphi }\right| .
\]

By assumption \( F \leq  H \) , we have

(1.4.6)

\[
{\left| \nabla Rm\right| }^{2} \leq  \frac{2{M}^{2}}{bB}\left( {\frac{\left( {{12} + 4\sqrt{n}}\right) {A}^{2}}{{\varphi }^{2}} + \frac{1}{t}}\right) ,\;\text{ for }t \leq  \theta /M.
\]

Thus by noting \( \varphi \) independent of \( t \) and \( \varphi  \leq  {Ar} \) , we get from (1.4.5) and (1.4.6) that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right| }\right)  \leq  {CM}\left( {\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  + 1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right)
\]

which implies

\[
\varphi \left| {{\nabla }^{2}\varphi }\right|  \leq  {e}^{CMt}\left\lbrack  {{\left. \left( \varphi \left| {\nabla }^{2}\varphi \right| \right) \right| }_{t = 0} + {CM}{\int }_{0}^{t}\left( {1 + \frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}}\right) {dt}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\leq  {e}^{CMt}\left\lbrack  {{A}^{2} + {CM}\left( {t + {2r}\sqrt{t}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\leq  2{A}^{2}
\]

provided \( r \leq  \theta /\sqrt{M} \) , and \( t \leq  \theta /M \) with \( \theta \) small enough. Therefore we have obtained Claim 2.

nodes.label: Definition 1.5.1

nodes.content: DEFINITION 1.5.1. A metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) evolving by the Ricci flow is called a breather if for some \( {t}_{1} < {t}_{2} \) and \( \alpha  > 0 \) the metrics \( \alpha {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) and \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{2}\right) \) differ only by a diffeomorphism; the case \( \alpha  = 1,\alpha  < 1,\alpha  > 1 \) correspond to steady, shrinking and expanding breathers, respectively.

nodes.content:
Lemma 1.5.2 (Perelman [103]). If \( \delta {g}_{ij} = {v}_{ij} \) and \( {\delta f} = h \) are variations of \( {g}_{ij} \) and \( f \) respectively, then the first variation of \( \mathcal{F} \) is given by

\[
\delta \mathcal{F}\left( {{v}_{ij}, h}\right)  = {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-{v}_{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right)  + \left( {\frac{v}{2} - h}\right) \left( {{2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right) }\right\rbrack  {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

where \( v = {g}^{ij}{v}_{ij} \) .

nodes.proof:
In any normal coordinates at a fixed point, we have

\[
\delta {R}_{ijl}^{h} = \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {\delta {\Gamma }_{jl}^{h}}\right)  - \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( {\delta {\Gamma }_{il}^{h}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{2}{g}^{hm}\left( {{\nabla }_{j}{v}_{lm} + {\nabla }_{l}{v}_{jm} - {\nabla }_{m}{v}_{jl}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
- \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{2}{g}^{hm}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{v}_{lm} + {\nabla }_{l}{v}_{im} - {\nabla }_{m}{v}_{il}}\right) }\right\rbrack  ,
\]

\[
\delta {R}_{jl} = \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{2}{g}^{im}\left( {{\nabla }_{j}{v}_{lm} + {\nabla }_{l}{v}_{jm} - {\nabla }_{m}{v}_{jl}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
- \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{2}{g}^{im}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{v}_{lm} + {\nabla }_{l}{v}_{im} - {\nabla }_{m}{v}_{il}}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left\lbrack  {{\nabla }_{j}{v}_{l}^{i} + {\nabla }_{l}{v}_{j}^{i} - {\nabla }^{i}{v}_{jl}}\right\rbrack   - \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\left\lbrack  {{\nabla }_{l}v}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

\[
{\delta R} = \delta \left( {{g}^{jl}{R}_{jl}}\right)
\]

\[
=  - {v}_{jl}{R}_{jl} + {g}^{jl}\delta {R}_{jl}
\]

\[
=  - {v}_{jl}{R}_{jl} + \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}\left\lbrack  {{\nabla }^{l}{v}_{l}^{i} + {\nabla }_{l}{v}^{il} - {\nabla }^{i}v}\right\rbrack   - \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\left\lbrack  {{\nabla }^{j}v}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
=  - {v}_{jl}{R}_{jl} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{l}{v}_{il} - {\Delta v}.
\]

Thus

(1.5.2)

\[
{\delta R}\left( {v}_{ij}\right)  =  - {\Delta v} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}{v}_{ij} - {v}_{ij}{R}_{ij}.
\]

The first variation of the functional \( \mathcal{F}\left( {{g}_{ij}, f}\right) \) is

(1.5.3)

\[
\delta \left( {{\int }_{M}\left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}}\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left( {\left\lbrack  {{\delta R}\left( {v}_{ij}\right)  + \delta \left( {{g}^{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) }\right\rbrack  {e}^{-f}{dV}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+\left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) \left\lbrack  {-h{e}^{-f}{dV} + {e}^{-f}\frac{v}{2}{dV}}\right\rbrack  }\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-{\Delta v} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}{v}_{ij} - {R}_{ij}{v}_{ij} - {v}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+2\langle \nabla f,\nabla h\rangle  + \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {\frac{v}{2} - h}\right) }\right\rbrack  {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

On the other hand,

\[
{\int }_{M}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}{v}_{ij} - {v}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV} = {\int }_{M}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}{v}_{ij} - {v}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{M}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {v}_{ij}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
{\int }_{M}2\langle \nabla f,\nabla h\rangle {e}^{-f}{dV} =  - 2{\int }_{M}{h\Delta f}{e}^{-f}{dV} + 2{\int }_{M}{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}h{e}^{-f}{dV},
\]

and

\[
{\int }_{M}\left( {-{\Delta v}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV} =  - {\int }_{M}\langle \nabla f,\nabla v\rangle {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}{v\Delta f}{e}^{-f}{dV} - {\int }_{M}{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}v{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

Plugging these identities into (1.5.3) the first variation formula follows. [

Proposition 1.5.3 (Perelman [103]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) and \( f\left( t\right) \) evolve according to the coupled flow

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l} \frac{\partial {g}_{ij}}{\partial t} =  - 2{R}_{ij}, \\  \frac{\partial f}{\partial t} =  - {\Delta f} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R. \end{array}\right.
\]

Then

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{F}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) }\right)  = 2{\int }_{M}{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f\right| }^{2}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

and \( {\int }_{M}{e}^{-f}{dV} \) is constant. In particular \( \mathcal{F}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) }\right) \) is nondecreasing in time and the monotonicity is strict unless we are on a steady gradient soliton.

nodes.proof:
Under the coupled flow and using the first variation formula in Lemma 1.5.2, we have

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{F}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-\left( {-2{R}_{ij}}\right) \left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) }\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+\left( {\frac{1}{2}\left( {-{2R}}\right)  - \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}}\right) \left( {{2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right) }\right\rbrack  {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {2{R}_{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right)  + \left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {{2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right) }\right\rbrack  {e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

Now

\[
{\int }_{M}\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {{2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M} - {\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{i}\left( {{2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M} - {\nabla }_{i}f\left( {2{\nabla }_{j}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right)  - 2{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{j}f - 2\left\langle  {\nabla f,{\nabla }_{i}\nabla f}\right\rangle  }\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
=  - 2{\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\left( {{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - {R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f-\langle \nabla f,{\nabla }_{i}\nabla f\rangle {\nabla }_{i}f}\right\rbrack  {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= 2{\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {{\left| {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f\right| }^{2} + {R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f}\right\rbrack  {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

and

\[
{\int }_{M}\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) R{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M} - {\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{i}R{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= 2{\int }_{M}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f{R}_{ij}{e}^{-f}{dV} - 2{\int }_{M}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f{R}_{ij}{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

Here we have used the contracted second Bianchi identity. Therefore we obtain

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{F}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {2{R}_{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right)  + 2\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f + {R}_{ij}}\right) }\right\rbrack  {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= 2{\int }_{M}{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f\right| }^{2}{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

It remains to show \( {\int }_{M}{e}^{-f}{dV} \) is a constant. Note that the volume element \( {dV} = \; \sqrt{\det {g}_{ij}}{dx} \) evolves under the Ricci flow by

(1.5.4)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{dV} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( \sqrt{\det {g}_{ij}}\right) {dx}
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\log \left( {\det {g}_{ij}}\right) }\right) {dV}
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\left( {{g}^{ij}\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij}}\right) {dV}
\]

\[
=  - {RdV}\text{ . }
\]

Hence

(1.5.5)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{e}^{-f}{dV}}\right)  = {e}^{-f}\left( {-\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} - R}\right) {dV}
\]

\[
= \left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
=  - \Delta \left( {e}^{-f}\right) {dV}\text{ . }
\]

It then follows that

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\int }_{M}{e}^{-f}{dV} =  - {\int }_{M}\Delta \left( {e}^{-f}\right) {dV} = 0.
\]

This finishes the proof of the proposition.

nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content_excerpt: COROLLARY 1.5.5. (i) \( \bar{\lambda }\left( {g}_{ij}\right) \) is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow whenever it is nonpositive; moreover, the monotonicity is strict unless we are on a gradient expanding soliton; (ii) An expanding breather is necessarily an expanding gradient soliton.

nodes.proof:
Let \( {f}_{0} \) be a minimizer of \( \lambda \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) at \( t = {t}_{0} \) and solve the backward heat equation

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} =  - {\Delta f} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R
\]

to obtain \( f\left( t\right) , t \leq  {t}_{0} \) , with \( {\int }_{M}{e}^{-f\left( t\right) }{dV} = 1 \) . We compute the derivative (understood in the barrier sense) at \( t = {t}_{0} \) ,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\bar{\lambda }\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{d}{dt}\left( {\mathcal{F}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) }\right)  \cdot  {V}^{\frac{2}{n}}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {V}^{\frac{2}{n}}{\int }_{M}2{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f\right| }^{2}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ \frac{2}{n}{V}^{\frac{2 - n}{n}}{\int }_{M}\left( {-R}\right) {dV} \cdot  {\int }_{M}\left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= 2{V}^{\frac{2}{n}}{\left\lbrack  {\int }_{M}{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{n}\left( R + \Delta f\right) {g}_{ij}\right| }^{2}{e}^{-f}dV\right\rbrack  }^{2}
\]

\[
\left. {+\frac{1}{n}{\int }_{M}{\left( R + \Delta f\right) }^{2}{e}^{-f}{dV} + \frac{1}{n}\left( {-{\int }_{M}\left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}}\right) \left( {\frac{1}{V}{\int }_{M}{RdV}}\right) }\right\rbrack  ,
\]

where we have used the formula (1.5.4) in the computation of \( {dV}/{dt} \) .

Suppose \( \lambda \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right)  \leq  0 \) , then the last term on the RHS is given by,

\[
\frac{1}{n}\left( {-{\int }_{M}\left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}}\right) \left( {\frac{1}{V}{\int }_{M}{RdV}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{n}\left( {-{\int }_{M}\left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}}\right) \left( {{\int }_{M}\left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV}}\right)
\]

\[
=  - \frac{1}{n}{\left( {\int }_{M}\left( R + \Delta f\right) {e}^{-f}dV\right) }^{2}.
\]

Thus at \( t = {t}_{0} \) ,

(1.5.8)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\bar{\lambda }\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  2{V}^{\frac{2}{n}}\left\lbrack  {{\int }_{M}{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{n}\left( R + \Delta f\right) {g}_{ij}\right| }^{2}{e}^{-f}{dV}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+\frac{1}{n}\left( {{\int }_{M}{\left( R + \Delta f\right) }^{2}{e}^{-f}{dV} - {\left( {\int }_{M}\left( R + \Delta f\right) {e}^{-f}dV\right) }^{2}}\right) }\right\rbrack   \geq  0
\]

by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Thus we have proved statement (i).

We note that on an expanding breather on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) with \( \alpha {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) and \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{2}\right) \) differ only by a diffeomorphism for some \( \alpha  > 1 \) , it would necessary have

\[
\frac{dV}{dt} > 0,\;\text{ for some }t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

On the other hand, for every \( t \) ,

\[
- \frac{d}{dt}\log V = \frac{1}{V}{\int }_{M}{RdV} \geq  \lambda \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right)
\]

by the definition of \( \lambda \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) . It follows that on an expanding breather on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
\bar{\lambda }\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right)  = \lambda \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) {V}^{\frac{2}{n}}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right)  < 0
\]

for some \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . Then by using statement (i), it implies

\[
\bar{\lambda }\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  < \bar{\lambda }\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{2}\right) }\right)
\]

unless we are on an expanding gradient soliton. We also note that \( \bar{\lambda }\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is invariant under diffeomorphism and scaling which implies

\[
\bar{\lambda }\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{1}\right) }\right)  = \bar{\lambda }\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{2}\right) }\right) .
\]

Therefore the breather must be an expanding gradient soliton.

LEMMA 1.5.7 (Perelman [103]). If \( {v}_{ij} = \delta {g}_{ij}, h = {\delta f} \) , and \( \eta  = {\delta \tau } \) , then

\[
\delta \mathcal{W}\left( {{v}_{ij}, h,\eta }\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M} - \tau {v}_{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\left( {\frac{v}{2} - h - \frac{n}{2\tau }\eta }\right) \left\lbrack  {\tau \left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n - 1}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\eta \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

Here \( v = {g}^{ij}{v}_{ij} \) as before.

nodes.proof:
Arguing as in the proof of Lemma 1.5.2, the first variation of the functional \( \mathcal{W} \) can be computed as follows,

\[
{\delta W}\left( {{v}_{ij}, h,\eta }\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\eta \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + \tau \left( {-{\Delta v} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}{v}_{ij} - {R}_{ij}{v}_{ij} - {v}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f}\right. }\right.
\]

\[
+ 2\langle \nabla f,\nabla h\rangle ) + h\rbrack {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\left( {\tau \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n}\right) \left( {-\frac{n}{2}\frac{\eta }{\tau } + \frac{v}{2} - h}\right) }\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\eta \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + h}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-\tau {v}_{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right)  + \tau \left( {v - {2h}}\right) \left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) }\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\left( {\tau \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n}\right) \left( {-\frac{n}{2}\frac{\eta }{\tau } + \frac{v}{2} - h}\right) }\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{M}\tau {v}_{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\left( {\frac{v}{2} - h - \frac{n}{2\tau }\eta }\right) \left\lbrack  {\tau \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) }\right.
\]

\[
+ f - n + {2\tau }\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) \rbrack {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\eta \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right)  + \left( {h - \frac{v}{2} + \frac{n}{2\tau }\eta }\right) }\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M} - \tau {v}_{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\left( {\frac{v}{2} - h - \frac{n}{2\tau }\eta }\right) \left\lbrack  {\tau \left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n - 1}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\eta \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

nodes.label: Proposition 1.5.8
nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content:
Proposition 1.5.8. If \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) \) and \( \tau \left( t\right) \) evolve according to the system

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l} \frac{\partial {g}_{ij}}{\partial t} =  - 2{R}_{ij}, \\  \frac{\partial f}{\partial t} =  - {\Delta f} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau }, \\  \frac{\partial \tau }{\partial t} =  - 1, \end{array}\right.
\]

then we have the identity

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) ,\tau \left( t\right) }\right)  = {\int }_{M}{2\tau }{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}\right| }^{2}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

and \( {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV} \) is constant. In particular \( \mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) ,\tau \left( t\right) }\right) \) is nondecreasing in time and the monotonicity is strict unless we are on a shrinking gradient soliton.

nodes.proof:
Using Lemma 1.5.7, we have

(1.5.11)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) ,\tau \left( t\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}{2\tau }{R}_{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M}\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) \left\lbrack  {\tau \left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
- {\int }_{M}\left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

Here we have used the fact that \( {\int }_{M}\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {e}^{-f}{dV} = 0 \) .

The second term on the RHS of (1.5.11) is

\[
{\int }_{M}\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) \left\lbrack  {\tau \left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) \left( {{2\tau \Delta f} - \tau {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
- {\int }_{M}{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV} + \tau {\int }_{M}\left( {-{\nabla }_{i}f}\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}R}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= \tau {\int }_{M}\left( {-{\nabla }_{i}f}\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}\left( {{2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right) }\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
- {\int }_{M}{\Delta f}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV} - {2\tau }{\int }_{M}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}{R}_{ij}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
=  - {2\tau }{\int }_{M}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}f}\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\Delta f}-\langle \nabla f,{\nabla }_{i}\nabla f\rangle }\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {2\tau }{\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {R}_{ij} - {\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f{R}_{ij}}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {2\tau }{\int }_{M}\left( {-\frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
=  - {2\tau }{\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\left( {{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f - {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - {R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {-{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {2\tau }{\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {R}_{ij} - {\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f{R}_{ij}}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
+ {2\tau }{\int }_{M}\left( {-\frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {2\tau }{\int }_{M}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f}\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f + {R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

Also the third term on the RHS of (1.5.11) is

\[
{\int }_{M} - \left( {R + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M} - \left( {R + {\Delta f} - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}
\]

\[
= {2\tau }{\int }_{M}\left( {\frac{-1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) \left( {{R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}}\right) {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

Therefore, by combining the above identities, we obtain

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) ,\tau \left( t\right) }\right)  = {2\tau }{\int }_{M}{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}\right| }^{2}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}.
\]

Finally, by using the computations in (1.5.5) and the evolution equations of \( f \) and \( \tau \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV}}\right)  = {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\left\lbrack  {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{e}^{-f}{dV}}\right)  + \frac{n}{2\tau }{e}^{-f}{dV}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
=  - {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\Delta \left( {e}^{-f}\right) {dV}
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV} =  - {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\int }_{M}\Delta \left( {e}^{-f}\right) {dV} = 0.
\]

nodes.label: Corollary 1.5.9
nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content_excerpt: COROLLARY 1.5.9. (i) \( \mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,\tau - t}\right) \) is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow; moveover, the monotonicity is strict unless we are on a shrinking gradient soliton; (ii) A shrinking breather is necessarily a shrinking gradient soliton.

nodes.proof:
Fix any time \( {t}_{0} \) , let \( {f}_{0} \) be a minimizer of \( \mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,\tau  - {t}_{0}}\right) \) . Note that the backward heat equation

\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} =  - {\Delta f} + {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} - R + \frac{n}{2\tau }
\]

is equivalent to the linear equation

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}}\right)  =  - \Delta \left( {{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}}\right)  + R\left( {{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}}\right) .
\]

Thus we can solve the backward heat equation of \( f \) with \( {\left. f\right| }_{t = {t}_{0}} = {f}_{0} \) to obtain \( f\left( t\right) , t \leq  {t}_{0} \) , with \( {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f\left( t\right) }{dV} = 1 \) . It then follows from Proposition 1.5.8 that

\[
\mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,\tau  - t}\right)  \leq  \mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) , f\left( t\right) ,\tau  - t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) , f\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,\tau  - {t}_{0}}\right)
\]

\[
= \mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,\tau  - {t}_{0}}\right)
\]

for \( t \leq  {t}_{0} \) and the second inequality is strict unless we are on a shrinking gradient soliton. This proves statement (i).

Consider a shrinking breather on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) with \( \alpha {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{1}\right) \) and \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{2}\right) \) differ only by a diffeomorphism for some \( \alpha  < 1 \) . Recall that the functional \( \mathcal{W} \) is invariant under simultaneous scaling of \( \tau \) and \( {g}_{ij} \) and invariant under diffeomorphism. Then for \( \tau  > 0 \) to be determined,

\[
\mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{1}\right) ,\tau  - {t}_{1}}\right)  = \mu \left( {\alpha {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{1}\right) ,\alpha \left( {\tau  - {t}_{1}}\right) }\right)  = \mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{2}\right) ,\alpha \left( {\tau  - {t}_{1}}\right) }\right)
\]

and by the monotonicity of \( \mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,\tau  - t}\right) \) ,

\[
\mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{1}\right) ,\tau  - {t}_{1}}\right)  \leq  \mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{2}\right) ,\tau  - {t}_{2}}\right) .
\]

Now take \( \tau  > 0 \) such that

\[
\alpha \left( {\tau  - {t}_{1}}\right)  = \tau  - {t}_{2},
\]

i.e.,

\[
\tau  = \frac{{t}_{2} - \alpha {t}_{1}}{1 - \alpha }.
\]

This shows the equality holds in the monotonicity of \( \mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,\tau  - t}\right) \) . So the shrinking breather must be a shrinking gradient soliton. [

\]

nodes.proof:
Let \( \varphi \left( v\right) \) be a smooth function on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) which is nonnegative, rotationally symmetric and has compact support in a small ball centered at the origin with \( {\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}\varphi \left( v\right) {dv} = 1. \)

For each \( x \in  M \) , set

\[
f\left( x\right)  = {\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}\varphi \left( v\right) \left( {{d}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{ex}{p}_{x}\left( v\right) }\right)  + 1}\right) {dv},
\]

where the integral is taken over the tangent space \( {T}_{x}M \) at \( x \) which we have identified with \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . If the size of the support of \( \varphi \left( v\right) \) is small compared to the maximum curvature, then it is well known that this defines a smooth function \( f \) on \( M \) with \( f\left( x\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) as \( {d}_{0}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) , while the bounds on the first and second covariant derivatives of \( f \) with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) \) follow from the Hessian comparison theorem. Thus it remains to show these bounds hold with respect to the evolving metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) .

We compute, using the frame \( \left\{  {{F}_{a}^{i}{\nabla }_{i}f}\right\} \) introduced in Section 1.3,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\nabla }_{a}f = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{F}_{a}^{i}{\nabla }_{i}f}\right)  = {R}_{ab}{\nabla }_{b}f.
\]

Hence

\[
\left| {\nabla f}\right|  \leq  {C}_{1} \cdot  {e}^{{C}_{2}t}
\]

where \( {C}_{1},{C}_{2} \) are some positive constants depending only on the dimension. Also

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{b}f}\right)  = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{F}_{a}^{i}{F}_{b}^{j}\left( {\frac{{\partial }^{2}f}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{j}} - {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}\frac{\partial f}{\partial {x}^{k}}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {R}_{ac}{\nabla }_{b}{\nabla }_{c}f + {R}_{bc}{\nabla }_{a}{\nabla }_{c}f + \left( {{\nabla }_{c}{R}_{ab} - {\nabla }_{a}{R}_{bc} - {\nabla }_{b}{R}_{ac}}\right) {\nabla }_{c}f.
\]

Then by Shi's derivative estimate (Theorem 1.4.1), we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left| {{\nabla }^{2}f}\right|  \leq  {C}_{3}\left| {{\nabla }^{2}f}\right|  + \frac{{C}_{3}}{\sqrt{t}},
\]

which implies

\[
{\left| {\nabla }^{2}f\right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) } \leq  {e}^{{C}_{3}t}\left( {{\left| {\nabla }^{2}f\right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( 0\right) } + {\int }_{0}^{t}\frac{{C}_{3}}{\sqrt{\tau }}{e}^{-{C}_{3}\tau }{d\tau }}\right)
\]

for some positive constants \( {C}_{3} \) depending only on the dimension and the curvature bound. \( \square \)

nodes.proof:
Let \( f \) be the function constructed in Lemma 2.1.1 and recall

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} = {\Delta R} + 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\right| }^{2}.
\]

For any small constant \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) and large constant \( A > 0 \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right)  = \frac{\partial R}{\partial t} + {\varepsilon A}{e}^{At}f
\]

\[
= \Delta \left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right)  + 2{\left| Ric\right| }^{2} + \varepsilon {e}^{At}\left( {{Af} - {\Delta f}}\right)
\]

\[
> \Delta \left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right)
\]

by choosing \( A \) large enough.

We claim that

\[
R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f > 0\;\text{ on }\;M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Suppose not, then there exist a first time \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) and a point \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) such that

\[
\left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
\nabla \left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
\Delta \left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  0,
\]

\[
\text{ and }\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  0\text{ . }
\]

Then

\[
0 \geq  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  > \Delta \left( {R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  0,
\]

which is a contradiction. So we have proved that

\[
R + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f > 0\;\text{ on }\;M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Letting \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) , we get

\[
R \geq  0\;\text{ on }\;M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  .
\]

This finishes the proof of the proposition. I

nodes.proof:
Set

\[
{\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta } = {M}_{\alpha \beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f{h}_{\alpha \beta },
\]

where \( A > 0 \) is a suitably large constant (to be chosen later) and \( f \) is the function constructed in Lemma 2.1.1.

We claim that \( {\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta } > 0 \) on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for every \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) . If not, then for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there will be a first time \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) where \( {\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta } \) acquires a null vector \( {v}^{\alpha } \) of unit length at some point \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) . At \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) ,

\[
{N}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta } \geq  {N}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta } - {\widetilde{N}}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }
\]

\[
\geq   - {C\varepsilon }{e}^{A{t}_{0}}f\left( {x}_{0}\right) ,
\]

where \( {\widetilde{N}}_{\alpha \beta } = \mathcal{P}\left( {{\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta },{h}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) \) , and \( C \) is a positive constant (depending on the bound of \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) , but independent of \( A \) ).

Let us extend \( {v}^{\alpha } \) to a local vector field in a neighborhood of \( {x}_{0} \) by parallel translating \( {v}^{\alpha } \) along geodesics (with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) ) emanating radially out of \( {x}_{0} \) , with \( {v}^{\alpha } \) independent of \( t \) . Then, at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }}\right)  \leq  0,
\]

\[
\nabla \left( {{\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }}\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
\text{ and }\Delta \left( {{\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }}\right)  \geq  0\text{ . }
\]

But

\[
0 \geq  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }}\right)  = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right)
\]

\[
= \Delta \left( {{\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }}\right)  - \Delta \left( {\varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right)  + {u}^{i}{\nabla }_{i}\left( {{\widetilde{M}}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }}\right)
\]

\[
- {u}^{i}{\nabla }_{i}\left( {\varepsilon {e}^{At}f}\right)  + {N}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta } + {\varepsilon A}{e}^{A{t}_{0}}f\left( {x}_{0}\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - {C\varepsilon }{e}^{A{t}_{0}}f\left( {x}_{0}\right)  + {\varepsilon A}{e}^{A{t}_{0}}f\left( {x}_{0}\right)  > 0
\]

when \( A \) is chosen sufficiently large. This is a contradiction. [

nodes.content: THEOREM 2.2.1 (Hamilton’s strong maximum principle). Let \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) be a smooth solution of the equation (2.2.1). Suppose \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \geq  0 \) on \( \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Then there exists a positive constant \( 0 < \delta  \leq  T \) such that on \( \Omega  \times  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) , the rank of \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) is constant, and the null space of \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) is invariant under parallel translation and invariant in time and also lies in the null space of \( {N}_{\alpha \beta } \) .

Suppose \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \geq 0 \) on \( \Omega \times \left\lbrack {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Then there exists a positive constant \( 0 < \delta \leq T \) such that on \( \Omega \times \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) , the rank of \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) is constant, and the null sp...

nodes.proof:
Set

\[
l = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  \Omega }}\{ \text{ rank of }{M}_{\alpha \beta }\left( {x,0}\right) \} .
\]

Then we can find a nonnegative smooth function \( \rho \left( x\right) \) , which is positive somewhere and has compact support in \( \Omega \) , so that at every point \( x \in  \Omega \) ,

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}{M}_{\alpha \beta }\left( {x,0}\right) {v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } \geq  \rho \left( x\right)
\]

for any \( \left( {n - l + 1}\right) \) orthogonal unit vectors \( \left\{  {{v}_{1},\ldots ,{v}_{n - l + 1}}\right\} \) at \( x \) .

Let us evolve \( \rho \left( x\right) \) by the heat equation

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\rho  = {\Delta \rho }
\]

with the Dirichlet condition \( {\left. \rho \right| }_{\partial \Omega } = 0 \) to get a smooth function \( \rho \left( {x, t}\right) \) defined on \( \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . By the standard strong maximum principle, we know that \( \rho \left( {x, t}\right) \) is positive everywhere in \( \Omega \) for all \( t \in  (0, T\rbrack \) .

For every \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , we claim that at every point \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \Omega  \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , there holds

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}{M}_{\alpha \beta }\left( {x, t}\right) {v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{t} > \rho \left( {x, t}\right)
\]

for any \( \left( {n - l + 1}\right) \) orthogonal unit vectors \( \left\{  {{v}_{1},\ldots ,{v}_{n - l + 1}}\right\} \) at \( x \) .

We argue by contradiction. Suppose not, then for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there will be a first time \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) and some \( \left( {n - l + 1}\right) \) orthogonal unit vectors \( \left\{  {{v}_{1},\ldots ,{v}_{n - l + 1}}\right\} \) at some point \( {x}_{0} \in  \Omega \) so that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}{M}_{\alpha \beta }\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) {v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{{t}_{0}} = \rho \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

Let us extend each \( {v}_{i}\left( {i = 1,\ldots , n - l + 1}\right) \) to a local vector field, independent of \( t \) , in a neighborhood of \( {x}_{0} \) by parallel translation along geodesics (with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) ) emanating radially out of \( {x}_{0} \) . Clearly \( \left\{  {{v}_{1},\ldots ,{v}_{n - l + 1}}\right\} \) remain orthogonal unit vectors in the neighborhood. Then, at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{t} - \rho }\right)  \leq  0
\]

\[
\text{ and }\Delta \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{t} - \rho }\right)  \geq  0\text{ . }
\]

But, since \( {N}_{\alpha \beta } \geq  0 \) by our assumption, we have

\[
0 \geq  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{t} - \rho }\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}\left( {\Delta {M}_{\alpha \beta } + {N}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{t} - {\Delta \rho }
\]

\[
\geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}\Delta \left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta }}\right)  + \varepsilon {e}^{t} - {\Delta \rho }
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}\Delta \left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } + \varepsilon {e}^{t} - \rho }\right)  + \varepsilon {e}^{t}
\]

\[
\geq  \varepsilon {e}^{t} > 0
\]

This is a contradiction. Thus by letting \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) , we prove that

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - l + 1}}{M}_{\alpha \beta }\left( {x, t}\right) {v}_{i}^{\alpha }{v}_{i}^{\beta } \geq  \rho \left( {x, t}\right)
\]

for any \( \left( {n - l + 1}\right) \) orthogonal unit vectors \( \left\{  {{v}_{1},\ldots ,{v}_{n - l + 1}}\right\} \) at \( x \in  \Omega \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Hence \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) has at least rank \( l \) everywhere in the open set \( \Omega \) for all \( t \in  (0, T\rbrack \) . Therefore we can find a positive constant \( \delta \left( { \leq  T}\right) \) such that the rank \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) is constant over \( \Omega  \times  \left( {0,\delta }\right) \) .

Next we proceed to analyze the null space of \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) . Let \( v \) be any smooth section of \( V \) in the null of \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) on \( 0 < t < \delta \) . Then

\[
0 = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{M}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta } + 2{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }\frac{\partial {v}^{\beta }}{\partial t}
\]

\[
= \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{M}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta },
\]

and

\[
0 = \Delta \left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta }}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\Delta {M}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta } + 4{g}^{kl}{\nabla }_{k}{M}_{\alpha \beta } \cdot  {v}^{\alpha }{\nabla }_{l}{v}^{\beta }
\]

\[
+ 2{M}_{\alpha \beta }{g}^{kl}{\nabla }_{k}{v}^{\alpha } \cdot  {\nabla }_{l}{v}^{\beta } + 2{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }\Delta {v}^{\beta }
\]

\[
= \left( {\Delta {M}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta } + 4{g}^{kl}{\nabla }_{k}{M}_{\alpha \beta } \cdot  {v}^{\alpha }{\nabla }_{l}{v}^{\beta } + 2{M}_{\alpha \beta }{g}^{kl}{\nabla }_{k}{v}^{\alpha } \cdot  {\nabla }_{l}{v}^{\beta }.
\]

By noting that

\[
0 = {\nabla }_{k}\left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\beta }}\right)  = \left( {{\nabla }_{k}{M}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}^{\alpha } + {M}_{\alpha \beta }{\nabla }_{k}{v}^{\alpha }
\]

and using the evolution equation (2.2.1), we get

\[
{N}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }{v}^{\beta } + 2{M}_{\alpha \beta }{g}^{kl}{\nabla }_{k}{v}^{\alpha } \cdot  {\nabla }_{l}{v}^{\beta } = 0.
\]

Since \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \geq  0 \) and \( {N}_{\alpha \beta } \geq  0 \) , we must have

\[
v \in  \operatorname{null}\left( {N}_{\alpha \beta }\right) \text{ and }{\nabla }_{i}v \in  \operatorname{null}\left( {M}_{\alpha \beta }\right) \text{ , for all }i\text{ . }
\]

The first inclusion shows that null \( \left( {M}_{\alpha \beta }\right)  \subset \) null \( \left( {N}_{\alpha \beta }\right) \) , and the second inclusion shows that null \( \left( {M}_{\alpha \beta }\right) \) is invariant under parallel translation.

To see null \( \left( {M}_{\alpha \beta }\right) \) is also invariant in time, we first note that

\[
{\Delta v} = {\nabla }^{i}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}v}\right)  \in  \text{ null }\left( {M}_{\alpha \beta }\right)
\]

and then

\[
{g}^{kl}{\nabla }_{k}{M}_{\alpha \beta } \cdot  {\nabla }_{l}{v}^{\alpha } = {g}^{kl}{\nabla }_{k}\left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{\nabla }_{l}{v}^{\alpha }}\right)  - {M}_{\alpha \beta }\Delta {v}^{\alpha } = 0.
\]

Thus we have

\[
0 = \Delta \left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\Delta {M}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}^{\alpha } + 2{g}^{kl}{\nabla }_{k}{M}_{\alpha \beta } \cdot  {\nabla }_{l}{v}^{\alpha } + {M}_{\alpha \beta }\Delta {v}^{\alpha }
\]

\[
= \left( {\Delta {M}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}^{\alpha },
\]

and hence

\[
0 = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {{M}_{\alpha \beta }{v}^{\alpha }}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\Delta {M}_{\alpha \beta } + {N}_{\alpha \beta }}\right) {v}^{\alpha } + {M}_{\alpha \beta }\frac{\partial {v}^{\alpha }}{\partial t}
\]

\[
= {M}_{\alpha \beta }\frac{\partial {v}^{\alpha }}{\partial t}.
\]

This shows that

\[
\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} \in  \text{ null }\left( {M}_{\alpha \beta }\right)
\]

so the null space of \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) is invariant in time. 0

nodes.content: THEOREM 2.3.1 (Hamilton’s advanced maximum principle [59]). Let \( K \) be a closed subset of \( V \) satisfying the hypothesis (H1) and (H2). Suppose that for any \( x \in  M \) and any initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , any solution \( {\sigma }_{x}\left( t\right) \) of the (ODE) which starts in \( {K}_{x} \) at \( {t}_{0} \) will remain in \( {K}_{x} \) for all later times. Then for any initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) the solution \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) of the (PDE) will remain in \( K \) for all later times provided \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) starts in \( K \) at time \( {t}_{0} \) and \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) is uniformly bounded with respect to the bundle metric \( {h}_{ab} \) on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right\rbrack \) .

nodes.proof:
Since the solution \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) of the (PDE) is uniformly bounded with respect to the bundle metric \( {h}_{ab} \) on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right\rbrack \) by hypothesis, we may assume that \( K \) is contained in a tubular neighborhood \( V\left( r\right) \) of the zero section in \( V \) whose intersection with each fiber \( {V}_{x} \) is a ball of radius \( r \) around the origin measured by the bundle metric \( {h}_{ab} \) for some large \( r > 0 \) .

Recall that \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , is a smooth solution to the Ricci flow with uniformly bounded curvature on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . From Lemma 2.1.1, we have a smooth function \( f \) such that \( f \geq  1 \) everywhere, \( f\left( x\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) as \( {d}_{0}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) for some fixed point \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) , and the first and second covariant derivatives with respect to the metrics \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) are uniformly bounded on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Using the metric \( {h}_{ab} \) in each fiber \( {V}_{x} \) and writing \( \left| {\varphi  - \eta }\right| \) for the distance between \( \varphi  \in  {V}_{x} \) and \( \eta  \in  {V}_{x} \) , we set

\[
s\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left\{  {\inf \left\{  {\left| {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right|  \mid  \eta  \in  {K}_{x} \triangleq  K \cap  {V}_{x}}\right\}   - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right\}
\]

where \( \epsilon \) is an arbitrarily small positive number and \( A \) is a positive constant to be determined. We rewrite the function \( s\left( t\right) \) as

\[
s\left( t\right)  = \sup \left\{  {l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right)  \mid  x \in  M,\eta  \in  \partial {K}_{x}\text{ and }l \in  {S}_{\eta }{K}_{x}}\right\}  .
\]

By the construction of the function \( f \) , we see that the sup is taken in a compact subset of \( M \times  V \times  {V}^{ * } \) for all \( t \) . Then by Lemma 2.3.3,

(2.3.2)

\[
\frac{{ds}\left( t\right) }{dt} \leq  \sup \left\{  {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - {\epsilon A}{e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right\}
\]

where the sup is over all \( x \in  M,\eta  \in  \partial {K}_{x} \) and \( l \in  {S}_{\eta }{K}_{x} \) such that

\[
l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right)  = s\left( t\right) ;
\]

in particular we have \( \left| {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right|  = l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right) \) , where \( \eta \) is the unique closest point in \( {K}_{x} \) to \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) , and \( l \) is the linear function of length one on the fiber \( {V}_{x} \) with gradient in the direction of \( \eta \) to \( \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) \) . We compute at these \( \left( {x,\eta , l}\right) \) ,

(2.3.3)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - {\epsilon A}{e}^{At}f\left( x\right)
\]

\[
= l\left( \frac{\partial \sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }{\partial t}\right)  - {\epsilon A}{e}^{At}f\left( x\right)
\]

\[
= l\left( {{\Delta }_{t}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + l\left( {{u}^{i}\left( {x, t}\right) {\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + l\left( {N\left( {x,\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) , t}\right) }\right)  - {\epsilon A}{e}^{At}f\left( x\right) .
\]

By the assumption and Lemma 2.3.4 we have \( \eta  + N\left( {x,\eta , t}\right)  \in  {T}_{\eta }{K}_{x} \) . Hence, for those \( \left( {x,\eta , l}\right) , l\left( {N\left( {x,\eta , t}\right) }\right)  \leq  0 \) and then

(2.3.4)

\[
l\left( {N\left( {x,\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) , t}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  l\left( {N\left( {x,\eta , t}\right) }\right)  + \left| {N\left( {x,\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) , t}\right)  - N\left( {x,\eta , t}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right|  = C\left( {s\left( t\right)  + \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right)
\]

for some positive constant \( C \) by the assumption that \( N\left( {x,\sigma , t}\right) \) is Lipschitz in \( \sigma \) and the fact that the sup is taken on a compact set. Thus the combination of (2.3.2)-(2.3.4) gives

(2.3.5)

\[
\frac{{ds}\left( t\right) }{dt} \leq  l\left( {{\Delta }_{t}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + l\left( {{u}^{i}\left( {x, t}\right) {\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  + {Cs}\left( t\right)  + \epsilon \left( {C - A}\right) {e}^{At}f\left( x\right)
\]

for those \( x \in  M,\eta  \in  \partial {K}_{x} \) and \( l \in  {S}_{\eta }{K}_{x} \) such that \( l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right)  = s\left( t\right) \) .

Next we estimate the first two terms of (2.3.5). As we extend a vector in a bundle from a point \( x \) by parallel translation along geodesics emanating radially out of \( x \) , we will get a smooth section of the bundle in some small neighborhood of \( x \) such that all the symmetrized covariant derivatives at \( x \) are zero. Now let us extend \( \eta  \in  {V}_{x} \) and \( l \in  {V}_{x}^{ * } \) in this manner. Clearly, we continue to have \( \left| l\right| \left( \cdot \right)  = 1 \) . Since \( K \) is invariant under parallel translations, we continue to have \( \eta \left( \cdot \right)  \in  \partial K \) and \( l\left( \cdot \right) \) as a support function for \( K \) at \( \eta \left( \cdot \right) \) . Therefore

\[
l\left( {\sigma \left( {\cdot , t}\right)  - \eta \left( \cdot \right) }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( \cdot \right)  \leq  s\left( t\right)
\]

in the neighborhood. It follows that the function \( l\left( {\sigma \left( {\cdot , t}\right)  - \eta \left( \cdot \right) }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( \cdot \right) \) has a local maximum at \( x \) , so at \( x \)

\[
{\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}\left( {l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
\text{ and }{\Delta }_{t}\left( {l\left( {\sigma \left( {x, t}\right)  - \eta }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}f\left( x\right) }\right)  \leq  0\text{ . }
\]

Hence at \( x \)

\[
l\left( {{\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}{\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}f\left( x\right)  = 0,
\]

\[
\text{ and }l\left( {{\Delta }_{t}\sigma \left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - \epsilon {e}^{At}{\Delta }_{t}f\left( x\right)  \leq  0\text{ . }
\]

Therefore by combining with (2.3.5), we have

\[
\frac{d}{dt}s\left( t\right)  \leq  {Cs}\left( t\right)  + \epsilon \left( {{\Delta }_{t}f\left( x\right)  + {u}^{i}{\left( {\nabla }_{t}\right) }_{i}f\left( x\right)  + \left( {C - A}\right) f\left( x\right) }\right) {e}^{At}
\]

\[
\leq  {Cs}\left( t\right)
\]

for \( A > 0 \) large enough, since \( f\left( x\right)  \geq  1 \) and the first and second covariant derivatives of \( f \) are uniformly bounded on \( M \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . So by applying Lemma 2.3.2 and the arbitrariness of \( \epsilon \) , we have completed the proof of Theorem 2.3.1. 0

LEMMA 2.3.2. Suppose \( \varphi  : \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is Lipschitz continuous and suppose for some constant \( C <  + \infty \) ,

\[

\]

and \( \;\varphi \left( a\right)  \leq  0 \) .

Then \( \varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) on \( \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) .

nodes.proof:
By replacing \( \varphi \) by \( {e}^{-{Ct}}\varphi \) , we may assume

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  0,\;\text{ whenever }\;\varphi \left( t\right)  \geq  0\text{ on }\lbrack a, b),
\]

\[
\varphi \left( a\right)  \leq  0.
\]

For arbitrary \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , we shall show \( \varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  \varepsilon \left( {t - a}\right) \) on \( \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) . Clearly we may assume \( \varphi \left( a\right)  = 0 \) . Since

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{\varphi \left( {a + h}\right)  - \varphi \left( a\right) }{h} \leq  0,
\]

there must be some interval \( a \leq  t < \delta \) on which \( \varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  \varepsilon \left( {t - a}\right) \) .

Let \( a \leq  t < c \) be the largest interval with \( c \leq  b \) such that \( \varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  \varepsilon \left( {t - a}\right) \) on \( \lbrack a, c) \) . Then by continuity \( \varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  \varepsilon \left( {t - a}\right) \) on the closed interval \( \left\lbrack  {a, c}\right\rbrack \) . We claim that \( c = b \) . Suppose not, then we can find \( \delta  > 0 \) such that \( \varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  \varepsilon \left( {t - a}\right) \) on \( \left\lbrack  {a, c + \delta }\right\rbrack \) since

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{h \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\frac{\varphi \left( {c + h}\right)  - \varphi \left( c\right) }{h} \leq  0.
\]

This contradicts the choice of the largest interval \( \lbrack a, c) \) . Therefore, since \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) can be arbitrary small, we have proved \( \varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) on \( \left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) . \( \square \)

nodes.proof:
Choose a sequence of times \( \left\{  {t}_{j}\right\} \) decreasing to \( t \) for which

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{t}_{j} \rightarrow  t}}\frac{\varphi \left( {t}_{j}\right)  - \varphi \left( t\right) }{{t}_{j} - t} = \frac{{d\varphi }\left( t\right) }{dt}.
\]

Since \( Y \) is compact, we can choose \( {y}_{j} \in  Y \) with \( \varphi \left( {t}_{j}\right)  = \psi \left( {{y}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right) \) . By passing to a subsequence, we can assume \( {y}_{j} \rightarrow  y \) for some \( y \in  Y \) . By continuity, we have \( \varphi \left( t\right)  = \psi \left( {y, t}\right) \) . It follows that \( \psi \left( {{y}_{j}, t}\right)  \leq  \psi \left( {y, t}\right) \) , and then

\[
\varphi \left( {t}_{j}\right)  - \varphi \left( t\right)  \leq  \psi \left( {{y}_{j},{t}_{j}}\right)  - \psi \left( {{y}_{j}, t}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\psi \left( {{y}_{j},{\widetilde{t}}_{j}}\right)  \cdot  \left( {{t}_{j} - t}\right)
\]

for some \( {\widetilde{t}}_{j} \in  \left\lbrack  {t,{t}_{j}}\right\rbrack \) by the mean value theorem. Thus we have

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{t}_{j} \rightarrow  t}}\frac{\varphi \left( {t}_{j}\right)  - \varphi \left( t\right) }{{t}_{j} - t} \leq  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\psi \left( {y, t}\right) .
\]

This proves the result. 0

LEMMA 2.3.4. Let \( U \subset  {R}^{n} \) be an open set and \( Z \subset  U \) be a closed convex subset. Consider the ODE

(2.3.1)

\[
\frac{d\varphi }{dt} = N\left( {\varphi , t}\right)
\]

where \( N : U \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  {R}^{n} \) is continuous and Lipschitz in \( \varphi \) . Then the following two statements are equivalent.

(i) For any initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , any solution of the ODE (2.3.1) which starts in \( Z \) at \( {t}_{0} \) will remain in \( Z \) for all later times;

(ii) \( \varphi  + N\left( {\varphi , t}\right)  \in  {T}_{\varphi }Z \) for all \( \varphi  \in  \partial Z \) and \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

Consider the ODE (2.3.1) \[ \frac{d\varphi }{dt} = N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) \] where \( N : U \times \left\lbrack {0, T}\right\rbrack \rightarrow {R}^{n} \) is continuous and Lipschitz in \( \varphi \) . Then the following two statements are equivalent. (i) For any initial time \( {t}_{0} \in \left\lbrack {...

nodes.proof:
We say that a linear function \( l \) on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) is a support function for \( Z \) at \( \varphi  \in  \partial Z \) and write \( l \in  {S}_{\varphi }Z \) if \( \left| l\right|  = 1 \) and \( l\left( \varphi \right)  \geq  l\left( \eta \right) \) for all \( \eta  \in  Z \) . Then \( \varphi  + N\left( {\varphi , t}\right)  \in  {T}_{\varphi }Z \) if and only if \( l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( l \in  {S}_{\varphi }Z \) . Suppose \( l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  > 0 \) for some \( \varphi  \in  \partial Z \) and some \( l \in  {S}_{\varphi }Z \) . Then

\[
\frac{d}{dt}l\left( \varphi \right)  = l\left( \frac{d\varphi }{dt}\right)  = l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  > 0,
\]

so \( l\left( \varphi \right) \) is strictly increasing and the solution \( \varphi \left( t\right) \) of the ODE (2.3.1) cannot remain in \( Z \) .

To see the converse, first note that we may assume \( Z \) is compact. This is because we can modify the vector field \( N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) \) by multiplying a cutoff function which is everywhere nonnegative, equals one on a large ball and equals zero on the complement of a larger ball. The paths of solutions of the ODE are unchanged inside the first large ball, so we can intersect \( Z \) with the second ball to make \( Z \) convex and compact. If there were a counterexample before the modification there would still be one after as we chose the first ball large enough.

Let \( s\left( \varphi \right) \) be the distance from \( \varphi \) to \( Z \) in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Clearly \( s\left( \varphi \right)  = 0 \) if \( \varphi  \in  Z \) . Then

\[
s\left( \varphi \right)  = \sup \{ l\left( {\varphi  - \eta }\right)  \mid  \eta  \in  \partial Z\text{ and }l \in  {S}_{\eta }Z\} .
\]

The sup is taken over a compact subset of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Hence by Lemma 2.3.3

\[
\frac{d}{dt}s\left( \varphi \right)  \leq  \sup \{ l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  \mid  \eta  \in  \partial Z, l \in  {S}_{\eta }Z\text{ and }s\left( \varphi \right)  = l\left( {\varphi  - \eta }\right) \} .
\]

It is clear that the sup on the RHS of the above inequality can be takeen only when \( \eta \) is the unique closest point in \( Z \) to \( \varphi \) and \( l \) is the linear function of length one with gradient in the direction of \( \varphi  - \eta \) . Since \( N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) \) is Lipschitz in \( \varphi \) and continuous in \( t \) , we have

\[
\left| {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right)  - N\left( {\eta , t}\right) }\right|  \leq  C\left| {\varphi  - \eta }\right|
\]

for some constant \( C \) and all \( \varphi \) and \( \eta \) in the compact set \( Z \) .

By hypothesis (ii),

\[
l\left( {N\left( {\eta , t}\right) }\right)  \leq  0,
\]

and for the unique \( \eta \) , the closest point in \( Z \) to \( \varphi \) ,

\[
\left| {\varphi  - \eta }\right|  = s\left( \varphi \right) .
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{d}{dt}s\left( \varphi \right)  \leq  \sup \left\{  \begin{matrix} l\left( {N\left( {\eta , t}\right) }\right)  + \left| {l\left( {N\left( {\varphi , t}\right) }\right)  - l\left( {N\left( {\eta , t}\right) }\right) }\right| \; \mid  \;\eta  \in  \partial Z, \\  l \in  {S}_{\eta }Z,\;\text{ and }\;s\left( \varphi \right)  = l\left( {\varphi  - \eta }\right)  \end{matrix}\right\}
\]

\[
\leq  {Cs}\left( \varphi \right)
\]

Since \( s\left( \varphi \right)  = 0 \) to start at \( {t}_{0} \) , it follows from Lemma 2.3.2 that \( s\left( \varphi \right)  = 0 \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right\rbrack \) . This proves the lemma. 0

nodes.content:
THEOREM 2.4.1 (Hamilton [63], Ivey [73]). Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci flow on a three-manifold which is complete with bounded curvature for each \( t \geq  0 \) . Assume at \( t = 0 \) the eigenvalues \( \lambda  \geq  \mu  \geq  \nu \) of the curvature operator at each point are bounded below by \( \nu  \geq   - 1 \) . The scalar curvature \( R = \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \) is their sum. Then at all points and all times \( t \geq  0 \) we have the pinching estimate

\[
R \geq  \left( {-\nu }\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - 3}\right\rbrack
\]

whenever \( \nu  < 0 \) .
