nodes.proof:
Consider the function

\[
y = f\left( x\right)  = x\left( {\log x - 3}\right)
\]

defined on \( {e}^{2} \leq  x <  + \infty \) . It is easy to check that \( f \) is increasing and convex with range \( - {e}^{2} \leq  y <  + \infty \) . Let \( {f}^{-1}\left( y\right)  = x \) be the inverse function, which is also increasing but concave and satisfies

(2.4.3)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{y \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{f}^{-1}\left( y\right) }{y} = 0
\]

Consider also the set \( K \) of matrices \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) defined by the inequalities

(2.4.4)

\[
K : \left\{  \begin{array}{l} \lambda  + \mu  + \nu  \geq   - 3, \\  \nu  + {f}^{-1}\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right)  \geq  0. \end{array}\right.
\]

By Theorem 2.3.1 and the assumptions in Theorem 2.4.1 at \( t = 0 \) , we only need to check that the set \( K \) defined above is closed, convex and preserved by the ODE (2.4.2).

Clearly \( K \) is closed because \( {f}^{-1} \) is continuous. \( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \) is just the trace function of \( 3 \times  3 \) matrices which is a linear function. Hence the first inequality in (2.4.4) defines a linear half-space, which is convex. The function \( \nu \) is the least eigenvalue function, which is concave. Also note that \( {f}^{-1} \) is concave. Thus the second inequality in (2.4.4) defines a convex set as well. Therefore we proved \( K \) is closed and convex.

Under the ODE (2.4.2)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right)  = {\lambda }^{2} + {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2} + {\lambda \mu } + {\lambda \nu } + {\mu \nu }
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\left\lbrack  {{\left( \lambda  + \mu \right) }^{2} + {\left( \lambda  + \nu \right) }^{2} + {\left( \mu  + \nu \right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\geq  0\text{ . }
\]

Thus the first inequality in (2.4.4) is preserved by the ODE.

The second inequality in (2.4.4) can be written as

\[
\lambda  + \mu  + \nu  \geq  f\left( {-\nu }\right) ,\;\text{ whenever }\nu  \leq   - {e}^{2},
\]

which becomes

(2.4.5)

\[
\lambda  + \mu  \geq  \left( {-\nu }\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - 2}\right\rbrack  ,\;\text{ whenever }\nu  \leq   - {e}^{2}.
\]

To show the inequality is preserved we only need to look at points on the boundary of the set. If \( \nu  + {f}^{-1}\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right)  = 0 \) then \( \nu  =  - {f}^{-1}\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right)  \leq   - {e}^{2} \) since \( {f}^{-1}\left( y\right)  \geq  {e}^{2} \) . Hence the RHS of (2.4.5) is nonnegative. We thus have \( \lambda  \geq  0 \) because \( \lambda  \geq  \mu \) . But \( \mu \) may have either sign. We split our consideration into two cases:

Case (i): \( \mu  \geq  0 \) .

We need to verify

\[
\frac{d\lambda }{dt} + \frac{d\mu }{dt} \geq  \left( {\log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - 1}\right) \frac{d\left( {-\nu }\right) }{dt}
\]

when \( \lambda  + \mu  = \left( {-\nu }\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - 2}\right\rbrack \) . Solving for

\[
\log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - 2 = \frac{\lambda  + \mu }{\left( -\nu \right) }
\]

and substituting above, we must show

\[
{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu \nu } + {\mu }^{2} + {\lambda \nu } \geq  \left( {\frac{\lambda  + \mu }{\left( -\nu \right) } + 1}\right) \left( {-{\nu }^{2} - {\lambda \mu }}\right)
\]

which is equivalent to

\[
\left( {{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu }^{2}}\right) \left( {-\nu }\right)  + {\lambda \mu }\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \left( {-\nu }\right) }\right)  + {\left( -\nu \right) }^{3} \geq  0.
\]

Since \( \lambda ,\mu \) and \( \left( {-\nu }\right) \) are all nonnegative we are done in the first case.

Case (ii): \( \mu  < 0 \) .

We need to verify

\[
\frac{d\lambda }{dt} \geq  \frac{d\left( {-\mu }\right) }{dt} + \left( {\log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - 1}\right) \frac{d\left( {-\nu }\right) }{dt}
\]

when \( \lambda  = \left( {-\mu }\right)  + \left( {-\nu }\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - 2}\right\rbrack \) . Solving for

\[
\log \left( {-\nu }\right)  - 2 = \frac{\lambda  - \left( {-\mu }\right) }{\left( -\nu \right) }
\]

and substituting above, we need to show

\[
{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu \nu } \geq   - {\mu }^{2} - {\lambda \nu } + \left( {\frac{\lambda  - \left( {-\mu }\right) }{\left( -\nu \right) } + 1}\right) \left( {-{\nu }^{2} - {\lambda \mu }}\right)
\]

or

\[
{\lambda }^{2} + \left( {-\mu }\right) \left( {-\nu }\right)  \geq  \lambda \left( {-\nu }\right)  - {\left( -\mu \right) }^{2} + \left( {\frac{\lambda  - \left( {-\mu }\right) }{\left( -\nu \right) } + 1}\right) \left( {\lambda \left( {-\mu }\right)  - {\left( -\nu \right) }^{2}}\right)
\]

which reduces to

\[
{\lambda }^{2}\left( {-\nu }\right)  + \lambda {\left( -\mu \right) }^{2} + {\left( -\mu \right) }^{2}\left( {-\nu }\right)  + {\left( -\nu \right) }^{3} \geq  {\lambda }^{2}\left( {-\mu }\right)  + \lambda \left( {-\mu }\right) \left( {-\nu }\right)
\]

or equivalently

\[
\left( {{\lambda }^{2} - \lambda \left( {-\mu }\right)  + {\left( -\mu \right) }^{2}}\right) \left( {\left( {-\nu }\right)  - \left( {-\mu }\right) }\right)  + {\left( -\mu \right) }^{3} + {\left( -\nu \right) }^{3} \geq  0.
\]

Since \( {\lambda }^{2} - \lambda \left( {-\mu }\right)  + {\left( -\mu \right) }^{2} \geq  0 \) and \( \left( {-\nu }\right)  - \left( {-\mu }\right)  \geq  0 \) we are also done in the second case.

Therefore the proof is completed. 0

\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - \frac{{\left| \nabla u\right| }^{2}}{u} + \frac{n}{2t}u \geq  0\;\text{ on }\;M \times  \left( {0,\infty }\right) .
\]

Assume the scalar curvature of the initial metric is bounded, nonnegative everywhere and positive somewhere. Then the scalar curvature \( R\left( {x, t}\right) \) satisfies the Li-Yau estimate

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} - \frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} + \frac{R}{t} \geq  0
\]

nodes.proof:
Proof. By the above discussion, we know \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  > 0 \) for \( t > 0 \) . If we set

\[
L = \log R\left( {x, t}\right) \;\text{ for }\;t > 0,
\]

then

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}L = \frac{1}{R}\left( {\bigtriangleup R + {R}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \bigtriangleup L + {\left| \nabla L\right| }^{2} + R
\]

and (2.5.4) is equivalent to

\[
\frac{\partial L}{\partial t} - {\left| \nabla L\right| }^{2} + \frac{1}{t} = \bigtriangleup L + R + \frac{1}{t} \geq  0.
\]

Following Li-Yau [82] in the linear heat equation case, we consider the quantity

(2.5.5)

\[
Q = \frac{\partial L}{\partial t} - {\left| \nabla L\right| }^{2} = {\Delta L} + R.
\]

Then by a direct computation,

\[
\frac{\partial Q}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\bigtriangleup L + R}\right)
\]

\[
= \bigtriangleup \left( \frac{\partial L}{\partial t}\right)  + R\bigtriangleup L + \frac{\partial R}{\partial t}
\]

\[
= \bigtriangleup Q + 2\nabla L \cdot  \nabla Q + 2{\left| {\nabla }^{2}L\right| }^{2} + {2R}\left( {\bigtriangleup L}\right)  + {R}^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  \bigtriangleup Q + 2\nabla L \cdot  \nabla Q + {Q}^{2}.
\]

So we get

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {Q + \frac{1}{t}}\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {Q + \frac{1}{t}}\right)  + 2\nabla L \cdot  \nabla \left( {Q + \frac{1}{t}}\right)  + \left( {Q - \frac{1}{t}}\right) \left( {Q + \frac{1}{t}}\right) .
\]

Hence by a similar maximum principle argument as in the proof of Lemma 2.1.3, we obtain

\[
Q + \frac{1}{t} \geq  0
\]

This proves the theorem. [

\]

Proof. Take the geodesic path \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) ,\tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) , from \( {x}_{1} \) to \( {x}_{2} \) at time \( {t}_{1} \) with constant velocity \( {d}_{{t}_{1}}\left( {{x}_{1},{x}_{2}}\right) /\left( {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right) \) . Consider the space-time path \( \eta \left( \tau \right)  = \left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) ,\tau }\right) \) , \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . We compute

\[
\log \frac{R\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) }{R\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) } = {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\frac{d}{d\tau }L\left( {\gamma \left( \tau \right) ,\tau }\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\frac{1}{R}\left( {\frac{\partial R}{\partial \tau } + \nabla R \cdot  \frac{d\gamma }{d\tau }}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
\geq  {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\left( {\frac{\partial L}{\partial \tau } - {\left| \nabla L\right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) }^{2} - \frac{1}{4}{\left| \frac{d\gamma }{d\tau }\right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }.
\]

Then by Theorem 2.5.2 and the fact that the metric is shrinking (since the scalar curvature is nonnegative), we have

\[
\log \frac{R\left( {{x}_{2},{t}_{2}}\right) }{R\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) } \geq  {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\left( {-\frac{1}{\tau } - {\left. \frac{1}{4}{\left| \frac{d\gamma }{d\tau }\right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) }^{2}\right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= \log \frac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{2}} - \frac{{d}_{{t}_{1}}{\left( {x}_{1},{x}_{2}\right) }^{2}}{4\left( {{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}\right) }
\]

After exponentiating above, we obtain the desired Harnack inequality. 0

THEOREM 2.5.4 (Hamilton [61]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be a complete solution with bounded curvature to the Ricci flow on a manifold \( M \) for \( t \) in some time interval \( \left( {0, T}\right) \) and suppose the curvature operator of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) is nonnegative. Then for any one-form \( {W}_{a} \) and any two-form \( {U}_{ab} \) we have

\[
{M}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 2{P}_{abc}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + {R}_{abcd}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd} \geq  0
\]

on \( M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) .

The proof of this theorem requires some rather intense calculations. Here we only give a sketch of the proof. For more details, we refer the reader to Hamilton's original paper [61].
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 2.5.4 (Hamilton [61]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be a complete solution with bounded curvature to the Ricci flow on a manifold \( M \) for \( t \) in some time interval \( \left( {0, T}\right) \) and suppose the curvature operator of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) is nonnegative. Then for any one-form \( {W}_{a} \) and any two-form \( {U}_{ab} \) we have \[ {M}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 2{P}_{a...

nodes.proof:
Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be the complete solution with bounded and nonnegative curvature operator. Recall that in the orthonormal frame coordinate system, the curvatures evolve by

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l} \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{abcd} = \Delta {R}_{abcd} + 2\left( {{B}_{abcd} - {B}_{abdc} - {B}_{adbc} + {B}_{acbd}}\right) , \\  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{R}_{ab} = \Delta {R}_{ab} + 2{R}_{acbd}{R}_{cd}, \\  \frac{\partial }{\partial t}R = {\Delta R} + 2{\left| Ric\right| }^{2}, \end{array}\right.
\]

where \( {B}_{abcd} = {R}_{aebf}{R}_{cedf} \) .

By a long but straightforward computation from these evolution equations, one can get

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {P}_{abc} = 2{R}_{adbe}{P}_{dec} + 2{R}_{adce}{P}_{dbe} + 2{R}_{bdce}{P}_{ade} - 2{R}_{de}{\nabla }_{d}{R}_{abce}
\]

and

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {M}_{ab} = 2{R}_{acbd}{M}_{cd} + 2{R}_{cd}\left( {{\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dab} + {\nabla }_{c}{P}_{dba}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bcd} - 4{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc} + 2{R}_{cd}{R}_{ce}{R}_{adbe} - \frac{1}{2{t}^{2}}{R}_{ab}.
\]

Now consider

\[
Q \triangleq  {M}_{ab}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 2{P}_{abc}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + {R}_{abcd}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}.
\]

At a point where

(2.5.14)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {W}_{a} = \frac{1}{t}{W}_{a},\;\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {U}_{ab} = 0,
\]

and

(2.5.15)

\[
{\nabla }_{a}{W}_{b} = 0,\;{\nabla }_{a}{U}_{bc} = \frac{1}{2}\left( {{R}_{ab}{W}_{c} - {R}_{ac}{W}_{b}}\right)  + \frac{1}{4t}\left( {{g}_{ab}{W}_{c} - {g}_{ac}{W}_{b}}\right) ,
\]

we have

(2.5.16)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) Q = 2{R}_{acbd}{M}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 8{R}_{adce}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{c} + 4{R}_{aecf}{R}_{bedf}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
+ \left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {R}_{abcd}{U}_{cd}}\right) \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + {R}_{abef}{U}_{ef}}\right) .
\]

For simplicity we assume the manifold is compact and the curvature operator is strictly positive. (For the general case we shall mess the formula up a bit to sneak in the term \( \epsilon {e}^{At}f \) , as done in Lemma 2.1.3). Suppose not; then there will be a first time when the quantity \( Q \) is zero, and a point where this happens, and a choice of \( U \) and \( W \) giving the null eigenvectors. We can extend \( U \) and \( W \) any way we like in space and time and still have \( Q \geq  0 \) , up to the critical time. In particular we can make the first derivatives in space and time to be anything we like, so we can extend first in space to make (2.5.15) hold at that point. And then, knowing \( \Delta {W}_{a} \) and \( \Delta {U}_{ab} \) , we can extend in time to make (2.5.14) hold at that point and that moment. Thus we have (2.5.16) at the point.

In the RHS of (2.5.16) the quadratic term

\[
\left( {{P}_{abc}{W}_{c} + {R}_{abcd}{U}_{cd}}\right) \left( {{P}_{abe}{W}_{e} + {R}_{abef}{U}_{ef}}\right)
\]

is clearly nonnegative. By similar argument as in the proof of Lemma 2.1.3, to get a contradiction we only need to show the remaining part in the RHS of (2.5.16) is also nonnegative.

A nonnegative quadratic form can always be written as a sum of squares of linear forms. This is equivalent to diagonalizing a symmetric matrix and writing each nonnegative eigenvalue as a square. Write

\[
Q = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{\left( {X}_{a}^{k}{W}_{a} + {Y}_{ab}^{k}{U}_{ab}\right) }^{2},\;\left( {1 \leq  k \leq  n + \frac{n\left( {n - 1}\right) }{2}}\right) .
\]

This makes

\[
{M}_{ab} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{X}_{a}^{k}{X}_{b}^{k},\;{P}_{abc} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{Y}_{ab}^{k}{X}_{c}^{k}
\]

and

\[
{R}_{abcd} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{Y}_{ab}^{k}{Y}_{cd}^{k}.
\]

It is then easy to compute

\[
2{R}_{acbd}{M}_{cd}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} - 2{P}_{acd}{P}_{bdc}{W}_{a}{W}_{b} + 8{R}_{adce}{P}_{dbe}{U}_{ab}{W}_{e}
\]

\[
+ 4{R}_{aecf}{R}_{bedf}{U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
= 2\left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{Y}_{ac}^{k}{Y}_{bd}^{k}}\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{l}{X}_{a}^{l}{Y}_{c}^{l}}\right) {W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
- 2\left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{Y}_{ac}^{k}{X}_{d}^{k}}\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{l}{Y}_{bd}^{l}{X}_{c}^{l}}\right) {W}_{a}{W}_{b}
\]

\[
+ 8\left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{Y}_{ad}^{k}{Y}_{ce}^{k}}\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{l}{Y}_{db}^{l}{X}_{e}^{l}}\right) {U}_{ab}{W}_{c}
\]

\[
+ 4\left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{k}{Y}_{ae}^{k}{Y}_{cf}^{k}}\right) \left( {\mathop{\sum }\limits_{l}{Y}_{be}^{l}{Y}_{df}^{l}}\right) {U}_{ab}{U}_{cd}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k, l}}{\left( {Y}_{ac}^{k}{X}_{c}^{l}{W}_{a} - {Y}_{ac}^{l}{X}_{c}^{k}{W}_{a} - 2{Y}_{ac}^{k}{Y}_{bc}^{l}{U}_{ab}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  0\text{ . }
\]

This says that the remaining part in the RHS of (2.5.16) is also nonnegative. Therefore we have completed the sketch of the proof. 0

COROLLARY 2.5.6. Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci flow for \( t > 0 \) which is complete with bounded curvature, and has nonnegative curvature operator. \]

for some constant \( {C}_{k} \) depending only on the dimension and \( k \) .

nodes.content:
LEMMA 2.6.1 (Perelman [103]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) ,0 \leq  t < T \) , be a complete solution to the Ricci flow on an n-dimensional manifold \( M \) and let \( u = {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f} \) be a solution to the conjugate equation (2.6.7) with \( \tau  = T - t \) . Set

\[
H = {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{f - n}{\tau }
\]

and

\[
v = {\tau Hu} = \left( {\tau \left( {R + {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}}\right)  + f - n}\right) u.
\]

Then we have

\[
\frac{\partial H}{\partial \tau } = {\Delta H} - 2\nabla f \cdot  \nabla H - \frac{1}{\tau }H - 2{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}\right| }^{2},
\]

and

\[
\frac{\partial v}{\partial \tau } = {\Delta v} - {Rv} - {2\tau u}{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}\right| }^{2}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 2.6.1 (Perelman [103]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) ,0 \leq t < T \) , be a complete solution to the Ricci flow on an n-dimensional manifold \( M \) and let \( u = {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f} \) be a solution to the conjugate equation (2.6.7) with \( \tau = T - t \) . Set \[ H = {2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{f - n}{\tau } \] and \[ v = {\tau Hu} = \lef...

nodes.proof:
By direct computations, we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }H = \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{f - n}{\tau }}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\bigtriangleup \left( \frac{\partial f}{\partial \tau }\right)  - 2\left\langle  {2{R}_{ij},{f}_{ij}}\right\rangle   - 2\left\langle  {\nabla f,\nabla \left( \frac{\partial f}{\partial \tau }\right) }\right\rangle   + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\nabla f,\nabla f}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }R + \frac{1}{\tau }\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }f - \frac{f - n}{{\tau }^{2}}
\]

\[
= 2\bigtriangleup \left( {\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right)  - 4\left\langle  {{R}_{ij},{f}_{ij}}\right\rangle   + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\nabla f,\nabla f}\right)
\]

\[
- 2\left\langle  {\nabla f,\nabla \left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right) }\right\rangle   - {\Delta R} - 2{\left| {R}_{ij}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \frac{1}{\tau }\left( {{\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R - \frac{n}{2\tau }}\right)  - \frac{f - n}{{\tau }^{2}},
\]

\[
\nabla H = \nabla \left( {{2\Delta f} - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{f - n}{\tau }}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\nabla \left( {\Delta f}\right)  - 2\left\langle  {\nabla {\nabla }_{i}f,{\nabla }_{i}f}\right\rangle   + \nabla R + \frac{1}{\tau }\nabla f,
\]

\[
\bigtriangleup H = \bigtriangleup \left( {2\bigtriangleup f - {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R + \frac{f - n}{\tau }}\right)
\]

\[
= 2\bigtriangleup \left( {\bigtriangleup f}\right)  - \bigtriangleup \left( {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}\right)  + \bigtriangleup R + \frac{1}{\tau }\bigtriangleup f,
\]

and

\[
2\nabla H \cdot  \nabla f = 2\left\langle  {2\nabla \left( {\bigtriangleup f}\right)  - 2\left\langle  {\nabla {\nabla }_{i}f,{\nabla }_{i}f}\right\rangle   + \nabla R + \frac{1}{\tau }\nabla f,\nabla f}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= 2\left\lbrack  {\langle 2\nabla \left( {\bigtriangleup f}\right) ,\nabla f\rangle  - 2\left\langle  {{f}_{ij},{f}_{i}{f}_{j}}\right\rangle  +\langle \nabla R,\nabla f\rangle }\right\rbrack   + \frac{2}{\tau }{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}.
\]

Thus we get

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }H - \bigtriangleup H + 2\nabla f \cdot  \nabla H + \frac{1}{\tau }H
\]

\[
=  - 4\left\langle  {{R}_{ij},{f}_{ij}}\right\rangle   + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\nabla f,\nabla f}\right)  - 2{\left| {R}_{ij}\right| }^{2} - \bigtriangleup \left( {\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2}\right)  + 2\left\langle  {\nabla \left( {\bigtriangleup f}\right) ,\nabla f}\right\rangle
\]

\[
+ \frac{2}{\tau }\bigtriangleup f + \frac{2}{\tau }R - \frac{n}{2{\tau }^{2}}
\]

\[
=  - 2\left\lbrack  {{\left| {R}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {f}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + \frac{n}{4{\tau }^{2}} + 2\left\langle  {{R}_{ij},{f}_{ij}}\right\rangle   - \frac{R}{\tau } - \frac{1}{\tau }\bigtriangleup f}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
=  - 2{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}\right| }^{2},
\]

and

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \bigtriangleup  + R}\right) v = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \bigtriangleup  + R}\right) \left( {\tau Hu}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \bigtriangleup }\right) \left( {\tau H}\right)  \cdot  u - 2\langle \nabla \left( {\tau H}\right) ,\nabla u\rangle
\]

\[
= \left( {\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau } - \bigtriangleup }\right) \left( {\tau H}\right)  - 2\langle \nabla \left( {\tau H}\right) ,\nabla f\rangle }\right) u
\]

\[
= \tau \left( {\frac{\partial H}{\partial \tau } - \bigtriangleup H + 2\nabla f \cdot  \nabla H + \frac{1}{\tau }H}\right) u
\]

\[
=  - {2\tau u}{\left| {R}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2\tau }{g}_{ij}\right| }^{2}.
\]

nodes.content: Proposition 3.1.1. The components of the curvature tensor of the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) coincide (modulo \( {N}^{-1} \) ) with the components of the Li-Yau-Hamilton quadratic.
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 3.1.1. The components of the curvature tensor of the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) coincide (modulo \( {N}^{-1} \) ) with the components of the Li-Yau-Hamilton quadratic.

nodes.proof:
By definition, the Christoffel symbols of the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) are given by the following list:

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{ij}^{k} = {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{i\beta }^{k} = 0\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{ij}^{\gamma } = 0,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\alpha \beta }^{k} = 0\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{i\beta }^{\gamma } = 0,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{k} = {g}^{kl}{R}_{li}\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{ij}^{o} =  - {\widetilde{g}}^{oo}{R}_{ij},
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{oo}^{k} =  - \frac{1}{2}{g}^{kl}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{l}}R\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{o} = \frac{1}{2}{\widetilde{g}}^{oo}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}R,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{i\beta }^{o} = 0,{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{o\beta }^{k} = 0\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{oj}^{\gamma } = 0,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\alpha \beta }^{\gamma } = {\Gamma }_{\alpha \beta }^{\gamma }
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\alpha o}^{\gamma } = \frac{1}{2\tau }{\delta }_{\alpha }^{\gamma }\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\alpha \beta }^{o} =  - \frac{1}{2}{\widetilde{g}}^{oo}{g}_{\alpha \beta },
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{oo}^{\gamma } = 0\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{o\beta }^{o} = 0
\]

\[
{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{oo}^{o} = \frac{1}{2}{\widetilde{g}}^{oo}\left( {-\frac{N}{2{\tau }^{2}} + \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }R}\right) .
\]

Fix a point \( \left( {p, s,\tau }\right)  \in  M \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{N} \times  {\mathbb{R}}^{ + } \) and choose normal coordinates around \( p \in  M \) and normal coordinates around \( s \in  {\mathbb{S}}^{N} \) such that \( {\Gamma }_{ij}^{k}\left( p\right)  = 0 \) and \( {\Gamma }_{\alpha \beta }^{\gamma }\left( s\right)  = 0 \) for all \( i, j, k \) and \( \alpha ,\beta ,\gamma \) . We compute the curvature tensor \( \widetilde{R}m \) of the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) at the point

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{ijkl} = {R}_{ijkl} + {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{jl}^{o} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{jo}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{il}^{o} = {R}_{ijkl} + O\left( \frac{1}{N}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{ijk\delta } = 0
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{ij\gamma \delta } = 0\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{R}}_{i\beta k\delta } = {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\beta \delta }^{o} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\beta o}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{i\delta }^{o} =  - \frac{1}{2}{\widetilde{g}}^{oo}{g}_{\beta \delta }{g}^{kl}{R}_{li} = O\left( \frac{1}{N}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{i\beta \gamma \delta } = 0
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{ijko} = \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}{R}_{jk} - \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}{R}_{ik} + {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{jo}^{o} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{jo}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{o} = {P}_{ijk} + O\left( \frac{1}{N}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{ioko} =  - \frac{1}{2}\frac{{\partial }^{2}}{\partial {x}^{i}\partial {x}^{k}}R - \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\left( {{R}_{il}{g}^{lk}}\right)  + {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{oo}^{o} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{oj}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{j} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{oo}^{k}{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{o}
\]

\[
=  - \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{k}R - \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }{R}_{ik} + 2{R}_{ik}{R}_{lk} - \frac{1}{2\tau }{R}_{ik} - {R}_{ij}{R}_{jk} + O\left( \frac{1}{N}\right)
\]

\[
= {M}_{ik} + O\left( \frac{1}{N}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{ij\gamma o} = 0\;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{R}}_{i\gamma jo} = 0,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{i\beta \gamma o} =  - \tau {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\beta o}^{\gamma }{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{io}^{o} = O\left( \frac{1}{N}\right) \;\text{ and }\;{\widetilde{R}}_{io\gamma \delta } = 0,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{io\gamma o} = 0
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\alpha \beta \gamma o} = 0
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\alpha o\gamma o} = \left( {\frac{1}{2{\tau }^{2}}{\delta }_{\alpha }^{\gamma } + {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\alpha o}^{\gamma }{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{oo}^{o} - {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{o\beta }^{\gamma }{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\alpha o}^{\beta }}\right) \tau  = O\left( \frac{1}{N}\right) ,
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\alpha \beta \gamma \delta } = O\left( \frac{1}{N}\right) .
\]

Thus the components of the curvature tensor of the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) coincide (modulo \( {N}^{-1} \) ) with the components of the Li-Yau-Hamilton quadratic.

nodes.proof:
By direct computations,

\[
{\delta }_{Y}\left( \mathcal{L}\right)  = {\int }_{{\tau }_{1}}^{{\tau }_{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {\langle \nabla R, Y\rangle  + 2\left\langle  {X,{\nabla }_{Y}X}\right\rangle  }\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{{\tau }_{1}}^{{\tau }_{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {\langle \nabla R, Y\rangle  + 2\left\langle  {X,{\nabla }_{X}Y}\right\rangle  }\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{{\tau }_{1}}^{{\tau }_{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {\langle \nabla R, Y\rangle  + 2\frac{d}{d\tau }\langle X, Y\rangle  - 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}X, Y}\right\rangle   - 4\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, Y}\right) }\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\left. 2\sqrt{\tau }\langle X, Y\rangle \right| }_{{\tau }_{1}}^{{\tau }_{2}} + {\int }_{{\tau }_{1}}^{{\tau }_{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left\langle  {Y,\nabla R - 2{\nabla }_{X}X - 4\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\cdot , X}\right)  - \frac{1}{\tau }X}\right\rangle  {d\tau }.
\]

LEMMA 3.2.2 (Second variation formula). For any \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) , we have

\[
{\delta }_{Y}^{2}\left( \mathcal{L}\right)  = {\left. 2\sqrt{\tau }\left\langle  {\nabla }_{Y}Y, X\right\rangle  \right| }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }} + {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {2{\left| {\nabla }_{X}Y\right| }^{2} + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle }\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+{\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}R + 2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, X}\right) }\right\rbrack  {d\tau }.
\]

nodes.proof:
We compute

\[
{\delta }_{Y}^{2}\left( \mathcal{L}\right)  = Y\left( {{\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {Y\left( R\right)  + 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}X, X}\right\rangle  }\right) {d\tau }}\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {Y\left( {Y\left( R\right) }\right)  + 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}X, X}\right\rangle   + 2{\left| {\nabla }_{Y}X\right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {Y\left( {Y\left( R\right) }\right)  + 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{X}Y, X}\right\rangle   + 2{\left| {\nabla }_{X}Y\right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

and

\[
2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{X}Y, X}\right\rangle
\]

\[
= 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle   + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle
\]

\[
= 2\frac{d}{d\tau }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle   - 4\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right)  - 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y,{\nabla }_{X}X}\right\rangle
\]

\[
- \left( {2\left\langle  {\frac{d}{d\tau }{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle   - 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{X}{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle  }\right)  + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle
\]

\[
= 2\frac{d}{d\tau }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle   - 4\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right)  - 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y,{\nabla }_{X}X}\right\rangle
\]

\[
- 2\left\langle  {{Y}^{i}{Y}^{j}\left( {{g}^{kl}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{lj} + {\nabla }_{j}{R}_{li} - {\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ij}}\right) }\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{k}}, X}\right\rangle   + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle
\]

\[
= 2\frac{d}{d\tau }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle   - 4\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right)  - 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y,{\nabla }_{X}X}\right\rangle   - 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, Y}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle
\]

where we have used the computation

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }{\Gamma }_{ij}^{k} = {g}^{kl}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{lj} + {\nabla }_{j}{R}_{li} - {\nabla }_{l}{R}_{ij}}\right) .
\]

Thus by using the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation (3.2.1), we get

\[
{\delta }_{Y}^{2}\left( \mathcal{L}\right)  = {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {Y\left( {Y\left( R\right) }\right)  + 2\frac{d}{d\tau }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle   - 4\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right) }\right.
\]

\[
- 2\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y,{\nabla }_{X}X}\right\rangle   - 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, Y}\right)  + 2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)
\]

\[
\left. {+2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle  + 2{\left| {\nabla }_{X}Y\right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack  {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\left\lbrack  {2\sqrt{\tau }\frac{d}{d\tau }\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle   + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau }}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle  }\right\rbrack  {d\tau }
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {Y\left( {Y\left( R\right) }\right)  - \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y,\nabla R}\right\rangle   - 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, Y}\right) }\right.
\]

\[
+ 2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + 2\left\langle  {R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X}\right\rangle   + 2{\left| {\nabla }_{X}Y\right| }^{2}\rbrack {d\tau }
\]

\[
= 2\sqrt{\tau }{\left. \left\langle  {\nabla }_{Y}Y, X\right\rangle  \right| }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }} + {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {2{\left| {\nabla }_{X}Y\right| }^{2} + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle }\right.
\]

\[
+ {\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}R - 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, Y}\right)  + 2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right) \rbrack {d\tau }.
\]

PROPOSITION 3.2.3. Given any unit vector \( Y \) at any point \( q \in  M \) with \( \tau  = \bar{\tau } \) , consider an \( \mathcal{L} \) -shortest geodesic \( \gamma \) connecting \( p \) to \( q \) and extend \( Y \) along \( \gamma \) by solving

the ODE (3.2.8). Then the Hessian of the \( \mathcal{L} \) -distance function \( L \) on \( M \) with \( \tau  = \bar{\tau } \) satisfies

\[
{\operatorname{Hess}}_{L}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}} - 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }Q\left( {X, Y}\right) {d\tau }
\]

in the sense of distributions, where

\[
Q\left( {X, Y}\right)  =  - {\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}R - 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle  - 4{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, X}\right)
\]

\[
- 2{\operatorname{Ric}}_{\tau }\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( Y, \cdot  \right) \right| }^{2} - \frac{1}{\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)
\]

is the Li-Yau-Hamilton quadratic. Moreover the equality holds if and only if the vector field \( Y\left( \tau \right) ,\tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) , is an \( \mathcal{L} \) -Jacobian field (i.e., \( Y \) is the derivative of a variation of \( \gamma \) by \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics).

nodes.proof:
Proof. As said before, we pretend that the shortest \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics between \( p \) and \( q \) are unique so that \( L\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) \) is smooth. Otherwise, the inequality is still valid, by a standard barrier argument, when understood in the sense of distributions (see, for example, [112]).

Recall that \( \nabla L\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right)  = 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}X \) . Then \( \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y,\nabla L}\right\rangle   = 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle \) . We compute by using Lemma 3.2.2, (3.2.8) and (3.2.9),

\[
{\operatorname{Hess}}_{L}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  = Y\left( {Y\left( L\right) }\right) \left( \bar{\tau }\right)  - \left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y,\nabla L}\right\rangle  \left( \bar{\tau }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\delta }_{Y}^{2}\left( \mathcal{L}\right)  - 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}\left\langle  {{\nabla }_{Y}Y, X}\right\rangle  \left( \bar{\tau }\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {2{\left| {\nabla }_{X}Y\right| }^{2} + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle  + {\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}R}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, X}\right) }\right\rbrack  {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {2{\left| -\operatorname{Ric}\left( Y, \cdot  \right)  + \frac{1}{2\tau }Y\right| }^{2} + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle  + {\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}R}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, X}\right) }\right\rbrack  {d\tau }
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( Y, \cdot  \right) \right| }^{2} - \frac{2}{\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + \frac{1}{{2\tau }\bar{\tau }} + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle }\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+{\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}R + 2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - 4{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, X}\right) }\right\rbrack  {d\tau }.
\]

Since

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  = {\operatorname{Ric}}_{\tau }\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + {\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{\nabla }_{X}Y, Y}\right)
\]

\[
= {\operatorname{Ric}}_{\tau }\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + {\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( Y, \cdot  \right) \right| }^{2} + \frac{1}{\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right) ,
\]

we have

\[
{\operatorname{Hess}}_{L}\left( {Y, Y}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( Y, \cdot  \right) \right| }^{2} - \frac{2}{\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + \frac{1}{{2\tau }\bar{\tau }} + 2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle }\right.
\]

\[
+ {\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}R - 4\left( {{\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}}\right) \left( {X, Y}\right)  - \left( {2\frac{d}{d\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - 2{\operatorname{Ric}}_{\tau }\left( {Y, Y}\right) }\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+4{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( Y, \cdot  \right) \right| }^{2} - \frac{2}{\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right) ) + 4{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right) }\right\rbrack  {d\tau }
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\left\lbrack  {2\sqrt{\tau }\frac{d}{d\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau }}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right) }\right\rbrack  {d\tau } + \frac{1}{2\bar{\tau }}{\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau }}{d\tau }
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {2\langle R\left( {Y, X}\right) Y, X\rangle  + {\nabla }_{Y}{\nabla }_{Y}R + \frac{1}{\tau }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right) }\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+4\left( {{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - {\nabla }_{Y}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, Y}\right) }\right)  + 2{\operatorname{Ric}}_{\tau }\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - 2{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( Y, \cdot  \right) \right| }^{2}}\right\rbrack  {d\tau }
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}} - 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {Y, Y}\right)  - {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }Q\left( {X, Y}\right) {d\tau }.
\]

This proves the inequality.

As usual, the quadratic form

\[
I\left( {V, V}\right)  = {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left\lbrack  {2{\left| {\nabla }_{X}V\right| }^{2} + 2\langle R\left( {V, X}\right) V, X\rangle  + {\nabla }_{V}{\nabla }_{V}R}\right.
\]

\[
+ 2{\nabla }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {V, V}\right)  - 4{\nabla }_{V}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {V, X}\right) \rbrack {d\tau },
\]

for any vector field \( V \) along \( \gamma \) , is called the index form. Since \( \gamma \) is shortest, the standard Dirichlet principle for \( I\left( {V, V}\right) \) implies that the equality holds if and only if the vector field \( Y \) is the derivative of a variation of \( \gamma \) by \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesics. \( \square \)

COROLLARY 3.2.4. We have

\[
{\Delta L} \leq  \frac{n}{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}} - 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}R - \frac{1}{\bar{\tau }}K
\]

in the sense of distribution. Moreover, the equality holds if and only if we are on a gradient shrinking soliton with

\[
{R}_{ij} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}L = \frac{1}{2\bar{\tau }}{g}_{ij}.
\]

Moreover, the equality holds if and only if we are on a gradient shrinking soliton with \[ {R}_{ij} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}L = \frac{1}{2\bar{\tau }}{g}_{ij}. \]

Proof. Choose an orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {{Y}_{1},\ldots ,{Y}_{n}}\right\} \) at \( \tau  = \bar{\tau } \) and extend them along the shortest \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) to get vector fields \( {Y}_{i}\left( \tau \right) , i = 1,\ldots , n \) , by solving the ODE (3.2.8), with \( \left\langle  {{Y}_{i}\left( \tau \right) ,{Y}_{j}\left( \tau \right) }\right\rangle   = \frac{\tau }{\bar{\tau }}{\delta }_{ij} \) on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) . Taking \( Y = {Y}_{i} \) in Proposition 3.2.3 and summing over \( i \) , we get

(3.2.10)

\[
{\Delta L} \leq  \frac{n}{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}} - 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}R - \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{n}{\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }Q\left( {X,{Y}_{i}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= \frac{n}{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}} - 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}R - {\int }_{0}^{\bar{\tau }}\sqrt{\tau }\left( \frac{\tau }{\bar{\tau }}\right) Q\left( X\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
= \frac{n}{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}} - 2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}R - \frac{1}{\bar{\tau }}K.
\]

Moreover, by Proposition 3.2.3, the equality in (3.2.10) holds everywhere if and only if for each \( \left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) \) and any shortest \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \) on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\bar{\tau }}\right\rbrack \) connecting \( p \) and \( q \) , and for any unit vector \( Y \) at \( \tau  = \bar{\tau } \) , the extended vector field \( Y\left( \tau \right) \) along \( \gamma \) by the ODE (3.2.8) must be an \( \mathcal{L} \) -Jacobian field. \[

\]

\[
= 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{Y}_{i},{Y}_{j}}\right)  + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}}{\operatorname{Hess}}_{L}\left( {{Y}_{i},{Y}_{j}}\right)
\]

and then by (3.2.9),

\[
2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {{Y}_{i},{Y}_{j}}\right)  + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}}{\operatorname{Hess}}_{L}\left( {{Y}_{i},{Y}_{j}}\right)  = \frac{1}{\bar{\tau }}{\delta }_{ij},\;\text{ at }\tau  = \bar{\tau }.
\]

Therefore the equality in (3.2.10) holds everywhere if and only if we are on a gradient shrinking soliton with

\[
{R}_{ij} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\bar{\tau }}}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}L = \frac{1}{2\bar{\tau }}{g}_{ij}.
\]

If \( M \) is compact, we define Perelman’s reduced volume by

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right) d{V}_{\tau }\left( q\right) ,
\]

where \( d{V}_{\tau } \) denotes the volume element with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) \) . Note that Perelman's reduced volume resembles the expression in Huisken's monotonicity formula for the mean curvature flow [72]. It follows, from the above computation, that

\[
\frac{d}{d\bar{\tau }}{\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \bar{\tau }\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) }\right) d{V}_{\bar{\tau }}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {\frac{\partial }{\partial \bar{\tau }}\left( {{\left( 4\pi \bar{\tau }\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) }\right) }\right)  + R{\left( 4\pi \bar{\tau }\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) }\right) }\right\rbrack  d{V}_{\bar{\tau }}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{M}\Delta \left( {{\left( 4\pi \bar{\tau }\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) }\right) }\right) d{V}_{\bar{\tau }}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
= 0\text{ . }
\]

This says that if \( M \) is compact, then Perelman’s reduced volume \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) is nonincreasing in \( \tau \) ; moreover, the monotonicity is strict unless we are on a gradient shrinking soliton.

THEOREM 3.2.7 (Perelman’s Jacobian comparison theorem). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) \) be a family of complete solutions to the Ricci flow \( \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }{g}_{ij} = 2{R}_{ij} \) on a manifold \( M \) with bounded curvature. \[

\]

is nonincreasing in \( \tau \) along \( \gamma \) .

THEOREM 3.2.8 (Monotonicity of Perelman's reduced volume). Let \( {g}_{ij} \) be a family of complete metrics evolving by the Ricci flow \( \frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }{g}_{ij} = 2{R}_{ij} \) on a manifold \( M \) with bounded curvature. Fix a point \( p \) in \( M \) and let \( l\left( {q,\tau }\right) \) be the reduced distance from \( \left( {p,0}\right) \) . Then

(i) Perelman's reduced volume

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right) d{V}_{\tau }\left( q\right)
\]

is finite and nonincreasing in \( \tau \) ;

(ii) the monotonicity is strict unless we are on a gradient shrinking soliton.

nodes.proof:
Proof. For any \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) we can find an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) , starting at \( p \) , with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  = v \) . Recall that \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) satisfies the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation

\[
{\nabla }_{\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  - \frac{1}{2}\nabla R + \frac{1}{2\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) , \cdot  }\right)  = 0.
\]

Multiplying this equation by \( \sqrt{\tau } \) , we get

(3.2.16)

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }}\right)  - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\tau }\nabla R + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) , \cdot  }\right)  = 0.
\]

Since the curvature of the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) \) is bounded, it follows from Shi’s derivative estimate (Theorem 1.4.1) that \( \left| {\nabla R}\right| \) is also bounded for small \( \tau  > 0 \) . Thus by integrating (3.2.16), we have

(3.2.17)

\[
\left| {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  - v}\right|  \leq  {C\tau }\left( {\left| v\right|  + 1}\right)
\]

for \( \tau \) small enough and for some positive constant \( C \) depending only the curvature bound.

Let \( {v}_{1},\ldots ,{v}_{n} \) be \( n \) linearly independent vectors in \( {T}_{p}M \) and let

\[
{V}_{i}\left( \tau \right)  = {\left( \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{v}\left( \tau \right) \right) }_{ * }\left( {v}_{i}\right)  = {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\left( v + s{v}_{i}\right) }\left( \tau \right) ,\;i = 1,\ldots , n.
\]

The \( \mathcal{L} \) -Jacobian \( \mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right) \) is given by

\[
\mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right)  = {\left| {V}_{1}\left( \tau \right)  \land  \cdots  \land  {V}_{n}\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right) }/\left| {{v}_{1} \land  \cdots  \land  {v}_{n}}\right|
\]

By (3.2.17), we see that

\[
\left| {\sqrt{\tau }\frac{d}{d\tau }\mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\left( v + s{v}_{i}\right) }\left( \tau \right)  - \left( {v + s{v}_{i}}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C\tau }\left( {\left| v\right|  + \left| {v}_{i}\right|  + 1}\right)
\]

for \( \tau \) small enough and all \( s \in  \left( {-\epsilon ,\epsilon }\right) \) (for some \( \epsilon  > 0 \) small) and \( i = 1,\ldots , n \) . This implies that

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\sqrt{\tau }{\dot{V}}_{i}\left( \tau \right)  = {v}_{i},\;i = 1,\ldots , n,
\]

so we deduce that

(3.2.18)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}{\tau }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right)  = 1
\]

Meanwhile, by using (3.2.17), we have

\[
l\left( \tau \right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\tau }}{\int }_{0}^{\tau }\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
\rightarrow  {\left| v\right| }^{2}\text{ as }\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }\text{ . }
\]

Thus

(3.2.19)

\[
l\left( 0\right)  = {\left| v\right| }^{2}.
\]

Combining (3.2.18) and (3.2.19) with Theorem 3.2.7, we get

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right) d{V}_{\tau }\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{{T}_{p}M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( \tau \right) }\right) \mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right) {\left. \right| }_{\tau  = 0}{dv}
\]

\[
= {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n}}\exp \left( {-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}\right) {dv}
\]

\[
<  + \infty \text{ . }
\]

This proves that Perelman's reduced volume is always finite and hence well defined. Now the monotonicity assertion in (i) follows directly from Theorem 3.2.7.

For the assertion (ii), we note that the equality in (3.2.13) holds everywhere when the monotonicity of Perelman's reduced volume is not strict. Therefore we have completed the proof of the theorem. I

DEFINITION 3.3.1. Let \( \kappa , r \) be two positive constants and let \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t < T \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow on an \( n \) -dimensional manifold \( M \) . We call the solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \kappa \) -noncollapsed at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  M \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) on the scale \( r \) if it satisfies the following property: whenever

\[
\left| {Rm}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {r}^{-2}
\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {r}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}^{n}.
\]

Here \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) \) is the geodesic ball centered at \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) and of radius \( r \) with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
We argue by contradiction. Suppose that there are sequences \( {p}_{k} \in  M \) , \( {t}_{k} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) and \( {r}_{k} \rightarrow  0 \) such that

(3.3.1)

\[
\left| {Rm}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {r}_{k}^{-2}
\]

for \( x \in  {B}_{k} = {B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{p}_{k},{r}_{k}}\right) \) and \( {t}_{k} - {r}_{k}^{2} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{k} \) , but

(3.3.2)

\[
{\epsilon }_{k} = {r}_{k}^{-1}{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{k}}{\left( {B}_{k}\right) }^{\frac{1}{n}} \rightarrow  0\text{ as }k \rightarrow  \infty .
\]

Without loss of generality, we may assume that \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow  T \) as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Let \( \bar{\tau }\left( t\right)  = {t}_{k} - t, p = {p}_{k} \) and

\[
{\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( \bar{\tau }\right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \bar{\tau }\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{k} - \bar{\tau }}\left( q\right) ,
\]

where \( l\left( {q,\bar{\tau }}\right) \) is the Li-Yau-Perelman distance with respect to \( p = {p}_{k} \) .

Step 1. We first want to show that for \( k \) large enough,

\[
{\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  \leq  2{\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{n}{2}}.
\]

For any \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) we can find an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) starting at \( p \) with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \; = v \) . Recall that \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) satisfies the equation (3.2.16). It follows from assumption (3.3.1) and Shi's local derivative estimate (Theorem 1.4.2) that \( \left| {\nabla R}\right| \) has a bound in the order of \( 1/{r}_{k}^{3} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) . Thus by integrating (3.2.16) we see that for \( \tau  \leq  {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2} \) satisfying the property that \( \gamma \left( \sigma \right)  \in  {B}_{k} \) as long as \( \sigma  < \tau \) , there holds

(3.3.3)

\[
\left| {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  - v}\right|  \leq  C{\epsilon }_{k}\left( {\left| v\right|  + 1}\right)
\]

where \( C \) is some positive constant depending only on the dimension. Here we have implicitly used the fact that the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) is equivalent for \( x \in  {B}_{k} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - }\right. \; \left. {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) . In fact since \( \frac{\partial {g}_{ij}}{\partial t} =  - 2{R}_{ij} \) and \( \left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  {r}_{k}^{-2} \) on \( {B}_{k} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - {r}_{k}^{2},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) , we have

(3.3.4)

\[
{e}^{-2{\epsilon }_{k}}{g}_{ij}\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right)  \leq  {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {e}^{2{\epsilon }_{k}}{g}_{ij}\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right) ,
\]

for \( x \in  {B}_{k} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) .

Suppose \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) with \( \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) . Let \( \tau  \leq  {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2} \) such that \( \gamma \left( \sigma \right)  \in  {B}_{k} \) as long as \( \sigma  < \tau \) , where \( \gamma \) is the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic starting at \( p \) with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  0}}\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  = v \) . Then, by (3.3.3) and (3.3.4), for \( k \) large enough,

\[
{d}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{p}_{k},\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  \leq  {\int }_{0}^{\tau }{\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \sigma \right) \right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{k}\right) }{d\sigma }
\]

\[
< \frac{1}{2}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\tau }\frac{d\sigma }{\sqrt{\sigma }}
\]

\[
= {\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\tau }
\]

\[
\leq  {r}_{k}\text{ . }
\]

This shows that for \( k \) large enough,

(3.3.5)

\[
\mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-1/2}\right\}  }\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  \subset  {B}_{k} = {B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{p}_{k},{r}_{k}}\right) .
\]

We now estimate the integral of \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) \) as follows,(3.3.6)

\[
{\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{\mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-1/2}\right\}  }\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }{\left( 4\pi {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\int }\limits_{{M \smallsetminus  \mathcal{L}{\exp }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-1/2}\right\}  }\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }}{\left( 4\pi {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\left( q\right) .
\]

We observe that for each \( q \in  {B}_{k} \) ,

\[
L\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  = {\int }_{0}^{{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } \geq   - C\left( n\right) {r}_{k}^{-2}{\left( {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{\frac{3}{2}} =  - C\left( n\right) {\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{3}{2}}{r}_{k},
\]

hence \( l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  \geq   - C\left( n\right) {\epsilon }_{k} \) . Thus, the first term on the RHS of (3.3.6) can be estimated by

(3.3.7)

\[
\mathop{\int }\limits_{{\mathcal{L}\mathop{\exp }\limits_{{\{ \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-1}/2\} }}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }}{\left( 4\pi {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {e}^{n{\epsilon }_{k}}{\int }_{{B}_{k}}{\left( 4\pi {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{k}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {e}^{n{\epsilon }_{k}}{\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}} \cdot  {e}^{C\left( n\right) {\epsilon }_{k}} \cdot  {\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{n}{2}} \cdot  \left( {{r}_{k}^{-n}{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {B}_{k}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= {e}^{\left( {n + C\left( n\right) }\right) {\epsilon }_{k}}{\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}} \cdot  {\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{n}{2}},
\]

where we have also used (3.3.5) and (3.3.4).

Meanwhile, by using (3.2.18), (3.2.19) and the Jacobian Comparison Theorem

3.2.7, the second term on the RHS of (3.3.6) can be estimated as follows

(3.3.8)

\[
\mathop{\int }\limits_{{M \smallsetminus  \mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  }}{\left( 4\pi {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{k} - {\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\left. {\left. {\left. {\left. {}^{f}{\Phi }^{f}\right| }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( -l\left( \tau \right) \right) \mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{\tau  = 0}dv\right| }_{.}\right| }_{\partial }
\]

\[
\left\{  {\left| v\right|  > \frac{1}{4}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}
\]

\[
= {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  > \frac{1}{4}{\epsilon }_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\}  }\exp \left( {-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}\right) {dv}
\]

\[
\leq  {\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{n}{2}}
\]

for \( k \) sufficiently large. Combining (3.3.6)-(3.3.8), we finish the proof of Step 1.

Step 2. We next want to show

\[
{\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {t}_{k}\right)  = {\left( 4\pi {t}_{k}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\int }_{M}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,{t}_{k}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{0}\left( q\right)  > {C}^{\prime }
\]

for all \( k \) , where \( {C}^{\prime } \) is some positive constant independent of \( k \) .

It suffices to show the Li-Yau-Perelman distance \( l\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k}}\right) \) is uniformly bounded from above on \( M \) . By Corollary 3.2.6 we know that the minimum of \( l\left( {\cdot ,\tau }\right) \) does not exceed \( \frac{n}{2} \) for each \( \tau  > 0 \) . Choose \( {q}_{k} \in  M \) such that the minimum of \( l\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}}\right) \) is attained at \( {q}_{k} \) . We now construct a path \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) connecting \( {p}_{k} \) to any given point \( q \in  M \) as follows: the first half path \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  0,{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}\right\rbrack  } \) connects \( {p}_{k} \) to \( {q}_{k} \) so that

\[
l\left( {{q}_{k},{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}}\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } \leq  \frac{n}{2}
\]

and the second half path \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2},{t}_{k}\right\rbrack  } \) is a shortest geodesic connecting \( {q}_{k} \) to \( q \) with respect to the initial metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( 0\right) \) . Then, for any \( q \in  {M}^{n} \) ,

\[
l\left( {q,{t}_{k}}\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{t}_{k}}}L\left( {q,{t}_{k}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{t}_{k}}}\left( {{\int }_{0}^{{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}} + {\int }_{{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}}^{{t}_{k}}}\right) \sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{t}_{k}}}\left( {n\sqrt{{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}} + {\int }_{{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2}}^{{t}_{k}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  C
\]

for some constant \( C > 0 \) , since all geometric quantities in \( {g}_{ij} \) are uniformly bounded when \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{T}{2}}\right\rbrack \) (or equivalently, \( \tau  \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - \frac{T}{2},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) ).

Combining Step 1 with Step 2, and using the monotonicity of \( {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( \tau \right) \) , we get

\[
{C}^{\prime } < {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {t}_{k}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{V}}_{k}\left( {{\epsilon }_{k}{r}_{k}^{2}}\right)  \leq  2{\epsilon }_{k}^{\frac{n}{2}} \rightarrow  0
\]

as \( k \rightarrow  \infty \) . This gives the desired contradiction. Therefore we have proved the theorem. \( \square \)

THEOREM 3.3.3 (No local collapsing theorem \( {\mathrm{I}}^{\prime } \) ). Suppose \( M \) is a compact Riemannian manifold, and \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t < T <  + \infty \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow. Then there exists a positive constant \( \kappa \) depending only the initial metric and \( T \) such that for any \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  M \times  \left( {0, T}\right) \) if

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {r}^{-2},\;\forall x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right)
\]

with \( 0 < r \leq  \sqrt{T} \) , then we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {r}^{n}.
\]

nodes.proof:
We will prove the assertion

\( {\left( *\right) }_{a} \)

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, a}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {a}^{n}
\]

for all \( 0 < a \leq  r \) . Recall that

\[
\mu \left( {{g}_{ij},\tau }\right)  = \inf \left\{  {\mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}, f,\tau }\right) \left| {\;{\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}{dV} = 1}\right. }\right\}  .
\]

Set

\[
{\mu }_{0} = \mathop{\inf }\limits_{{0 \leq  \tau  \leq  {2T}}}\mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( 0\right) ,\tau }\right)  >  - \infty .
\]

By Corollary 1.5.9, we have

(3.3.9)

\[
\mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) , b}\right)  \geq  \mu \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( 0\right) ,{t}_{0} + b}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {\mu }_{0}
\]

for \( 0 < b \leq  {r}^{2} \) . Let \( 0 < \zeta  \leq  1 \) be a positive smooth function on \( \mathbb{R} \) where \( \zeta \left( s\right)  = 1 \) for \( \left| s\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{2},{\left| {\zeta }^{\prime }\right| }^{2}/\zeta  \leq  {20} \) everywhere, and \( \zeta \left( s\right) \) is very close to zero for \( \left| s\right|  \geq  1 \) . Define a function \( f \) on \( M \) by

\[
{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f\left( x\right) } = {e}^{-c}{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\zeta \left( \frac{{d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right) }{r}\right) ,
\]

where the constant \( c \) is chosen so that \( {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}d{V}_{{t}_{0}} = 1 \) . Then it follows from (3.3.9) that

(3.3.10)

\[
\mathcal{W}\left( {{g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) , f,{r}^{2}}\right)  = {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {{r}^{2}\left( {{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2} + R}\right)  + f - n}\right\rbrack  {\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}d{V}_{{t}_{0}}
\]

\[
\geq  {\mu }_{0}
\]

Note that

\[
1 = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-c}\zeta \left( \frac{{d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right) }{r}\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0}}
\]

\[
\geq  {\int }_{{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{r}{2}}\right) }{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-c}d{V}_{{t}_{0}}
\]

\[
= {\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-c}{\text{ Vol }}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{r}{2}}\right) }\right) .
\]

By combining with (3.3.10) and the scalar curvature bound, we have

\[
c \geq   - {\int }_{M}\left( {\frac{{\left( {\zeta }^{\prime }\right) }^{2}}{\zeta } - \log \zeta  \cdot  \zeta }\right) {e}^{-c}{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}d{V}_{{t}_{0}} + \left( {n - 1}\right)  + {\mu }_{0}
\]

\[
\geq   - 2\left( {{20} + {e}^{-1}}\right) {e}^{-c}{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right)  + \left( {n - 1}\right)  + {\mu }_{0}
\]

\[
\geq   - 2\left( {{20} + {e}^{-1}}\right) \frac{{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right) }{{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{r}{2}}\right) }\right) } + \left( {n - 1}\right)  + {\mu }_{0},
\]

where we used the fact that \( \zeta \left( s\right) \) is very close to zero for \( \left| s\right|  \geq  1 \) . Note also that

\[
2{\int }_{{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }{e}^{-c}{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}d{V}_{{t}_{0}} \geq  {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-f}d{V}_{{t}_{0}} = 1.
\]

Let us set

\[
\kappa  = \min \left\{  {\frac{1}{2}\exp \left( {-2\left( {{20} + {e}^{-1}}\right) {3}^{-n} + \left( {n - 1}\right)  + {\mu }_{0}}\right) ,\frac{1}{2}{\alpha }_{n}}\right\}
\]

where \( {\alpha }_{n} \) is the volume of the unit ball in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Then we obtain

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}{e}^{c}{\left( 4\pi {r}^{2}\right) }^{\frac{n}{2}}
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}{\left( 4\pi \right) }^{\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-2\left( {{20} + {e}^{-1}}\right) {3}^{-n} + \left( {n - 1}\right)  + {\mu }_{0}}\right)  \cdot  {r}^{n}
\]

\[
\geq  \kappa {r}^{n}
\]

provided \( {\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{r}{2}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {3}^{-n}{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) }\right) \) .

Note that the above argument also works for any smaller radius \( a \leq  r \) . Thus we have proved the following assertion:

(3.3.11)

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, a}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {a}^{n}
\]

whenever \( a \in  (0, r\rbrack \) and \( {\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{a}{2}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {3}^{-n}{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, a}\right) }\right) \) .

Now we argue by contradiction to prove the assertion \( {\left( *\right) }_{a} \) for any \( a \in  (0, r\rbrack \) . Suppose \( {\left( *\right) }_{a} \) fails for some \( a \in  (0, r\rbrack \) . Then by (3.3.11) we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{a}{2}}\right) }\right)  < {3}^{-n}{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, a}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
< {3}^{-n}\kappa {a}^{n}
\]

\[
< \kappa {\left( \frac{a}{2}\right) }^{n}\text{ . }
\]

This says that \( {\left( *\right) }_{\frac{a}{2}} \) would also fail. By induction, we deduce that

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{a}{{2}^{k}}}\right) }\right)  < \kappa {\left( \frac{a}{{2}^{k}}\right) }^{n}\;\text{ for all }k \geq  1.
\]

This is a contradiction since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},\frac{a}{{2}^{k}}}\right) }\right) /{\left( \frac{a}{{2}^{k}}\right) }^{n} = {\alpha }_{n} \) .

LEMMA 3.4.1 (Perelman [103]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be a solution to the Ricci flow on an n-dimensional manifold \( M \) and denote by \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right) \) the distance between \( x \) and \( {x}_{0} \) with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) .

(i) Suppose \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) on \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) for some \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) and some positive constants \( K \) and \( {r}_{0} \) . Then the distance function \( d\left( {x, t}\right)  = {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right) \) satisfies, at \( t = {t}_{0} \) and outside \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) , the differential inequality:

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}d - {\Delta d} \geq   - \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{0} + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

(ii) Suppose \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) K \) on \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \bigcup {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{1},{r}_{0}}\right) \) for some \( {x}_{0},{x}_{1} \in \; M \) and some positive constants \( K \) and \( {r}_{0} \) . Then, at \( t = {t}_{0} \) ,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  \geq   - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{0} + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

nodes.proof:
Let \( \gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0, d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) be a shortest normal geodesic from \( {x}_{0} \) to \( x \) with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) . As usual, we may assume that \( x \) and \( {x}_{0} \) are not conjugate to each other in the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) , otherwise we can understand the differential inequality in the barrier sense. Let \( X = \dot{\gamma }\left( 0\right) \) and let \( \left\{  {X,{e}_{1},\ldots ,{e}_{n - 1}}\right\} \) be an orthonormal basis of \( {T}_{{x}_{0}}M \) . Extend this basis parallel along \( \gamma \) to form a parallel orthonormal basis \( \left\{  {X\left( s\right) ,{e}_{1}\left( s\right) ,\ldots ,{e}_{n - 1}\left( s\right) }\right\} \) along \( \gamma \) .

(i) Let \( {X}_{i}\left( s\right) , i = 1,\ldots , n - 1 \) , be the Jacobian fields along \( \gamma \) such that \( {X}_{i}\left( 0\right)  = 0 \) and \( {X}_{i}\left( {d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right)  = {e}_{i}\left( {d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) \) for \( i = 1,\ldots , n - 1 \) . Then it is well-known that (see for example [112])

\[
\Delta {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\left( {{\left| {\dot{X}}_{i}\right| }^{2} - R\left( {X,{X}_{i}, X,{X}_{i}}\right) }\right) {ds}
\]

(in Proposition 3.2.3 we actually did this for the more complicated \( \mathcal{L} \) -distance function).

Define vector fields \( {Y}_{i}, i = 1,\ldots , n - 1 \) , along \( \gamma \) as follows:

\[
{Y}_{i}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} \frac{s}{{r}_{0}}{e}_{i}\left( s\right) , & \text{ if }s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{r}_{0}}\right\rbrack  , \\  {e}_{i}\left( s\right) , & \text{ if }s \in  \left\lbrack  {{r}_{0}, d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right\rbrack  . \end{array}\right.
\]

which have the same value as the corresponding Jacobian fields \( {X}_{i}\left( s\right) \) at the two end points of \( \gamma \) . Then by using the standard index comparison theorem (see for example [22]) we have

\[
\Delta {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\left( {{\left| {\dot{X}}_{i}\right| }^{2} - R\left( {X,{X}_{i}, X,{X}_{i}}\right) }\right) {ds}
\]

\[
\leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\left( {{\left| {\dot{Y}}_{i}\right| }^{2} - R\left( {X,{Y}_{i}, X,{Y}_{i}}\right) }\right) {ds}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\frac{1}{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left( {n - 1 - {s}^{2}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) }\right) {ds} + {\int }_{{r}_{0}}^{d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\left( {-\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) }\right) {ds}
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{\gamma }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  + {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left( {\frac{\left( n - 1\right) }{{r}_{0}^{2}} + \left( {1 - \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) }\right) {ds}
\]

\[
\leq   - {\int }_{\gamma }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right)  + \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{0} + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

On the other hand,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  = \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right) }\sqrt{{g}_{ij}{X}^{i}{X}^{j}}{ds}
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{\gamma }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds}.
\]

Hence we obtain the desired differential inequality.

(ii) The proof is divided into three cases.

Case (1): \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  \geq  2{r}_{0} \) .

Define vector fields \( {Y}_{i}, i = 1,\ldots , n - 1 \) , along \( \gamma \) as follows:

\[
{Y}_{i}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} \frac{s}{{r}_{0}}{e}_{i}\left( s\right) , & \text{ if }s \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{r}_{0}}\right\rbrack  , \\  {e}_{i}\left( s\right) , & \text{ if }s \in  \left\lbrack  {{r}_{0}, d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right\rbrack  , \\  \frac{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right)  - s}{{r}_{0}}{e}_{i}\left( s\right) , & \text{ if }s \in  \left\lbrack  {d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {r}_{0}, d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right) }\right\rbrack  . \end{array}\right.
\]

Then by the second variation formula, we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right) }R\left( {X,{Y}_{i}, X,{Y}_{i}}\right) {ds} \leq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 1}}^{{n - 1}}{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right) }{\left| {\dot{Y}}_{i}\right| }^{2}{ds},
\]

which implies

\[
{\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} + {\int }_{{r}_{0}}^{d\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  - {r}_{0}}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds}
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {r}_{0}}^{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right) }{\left( \frac{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right)  - s}{{r}_{0}}\right) }^{2}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} \leq  \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{r}_{0}}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - {\int }_{0}^{{r}_{0}}\left( {1 - \frac{{s}^{2}}{{r}_{0}^{2}}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds}
\]

\[
- {\int }_{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right)  - {r}_{0}}^{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right) }\left( {1 - {\left( \frac{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right)  - s}{{r}_{0}}\right) }^{2}}\right) \operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} - \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{r}_{0}}
\]

\[
\geq   - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{0} + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

Case (2): \( \frac{2}{\sqrt{\frac{2K}{3}}} \leq  {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  \leq  2{r}_{0} \) .

In this case, letting \( {r}_{1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{2K}{3}}} \) and applying case (1) with \( {r}_{0} \) replaced by \( {r}_{1} \) , we get

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\right)  \geq   - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{1} + {r}_{1}^{-1}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{0} + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right) .
\]

Case (3): \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  \leq  \min \left\{  {\frac{2}{\sqrt{\frac{2K}{3}}},2{r}_{0}}\right\} \) .

In this case,

\[
{\int }_{0}^{d\left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{0}}\right) }\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} \leq  \left( {n - 1}\right) K\frac{2}{\sqrt{\frac{2K}{3}}} = \left( {n - 1}\right) \sqrt{6K},
\]

and

\[
2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {\frac{2}{3}K{r}_{0} + {r}_{0}^{-1}}\right)  \geq  \left( {n - 1}\right) \sqrt{\frac{32}{3}K}.
\]

This proves the lemma. \( \square \)

nodes.content:
THEOREM 3.4.2 (No local collapsing theorem II). For any \( A > 0 \) there exists \( \kappa  = \kappa \left( A\right)  > 0 \) with the following property: if \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) is a complete solution to the Ricci flow on \( 0 \leq  t \leq  {r}_{0}^{2} \) with bounded curvature and satifying

\[
\left| {Rm}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2}\;\text{ on }{B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{r}_{0}^{2}}\right\rbrack
\]

and

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{0}\left( {{B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {A}^{-1}{r}_{0}^{n},
\]

then \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales less than \( {r}_{0} \) at every point \( \left( {x,{r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) with \( {d}_{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  A{r}_{0}. \)
