nodes.proof:
Type I: We consider a maximal solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) on \( M \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T <  + \infty \) and

\[
\Omega \overset{\Delta }{ = }\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\left( {T - t}\right) {K}_{\max }\left( t\right)  <  + \infty .
\]

First we note that \( \Omega  > 0 \) . Indeed by the evolution equation of curvature,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{K}_{\max }\left( t\right)  \leq  \text{ Const } \cdot  {K}_{\max }^{2}\left( t\right) .
\]

This implies that

\[
{K}_{\max }\left( t\right)  \cdot  \left( {T - t}\right)  \geq  \text{ Const } > 0,
\]

because

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}{K}_{\max }\left( t\right)  =  + \infty .
\]

Thus \( \Omega \) must be positive.

Choose a sequence of points \( {x}_{k} \) and times \( {t}_{k} \) such that \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow  T \) and

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}\left( {T - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  = \Omega .
\]

Denote by

\[
{\epsilon }_{k} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) \right| }}.
\]

We translate in time so that \( {t}_{k} \) becomes 0, dilate in space by the factor \( {\epsilon }_{k} \) and dilate in time by \( {\epsilon }_{k}^{2} \) to get

\[
{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right)  = {\epsilon }_{k}^{-2}{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right) ,\;\widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{k}/{\epsilon }_{k}^{2},\left( {T - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}}\right) .
\]

Then

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \widetilde{t}}{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right)  = {\epsilon }_{k}^{-2}\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right)  \cdot  {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}
\]

\[
=  - 2{R}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right)
\]

\[
=  - 2{\widetilde{R}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right) ,
\]

where \( {\widetilde{R}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) } \) is the Ricci curvature of the metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) } \) . So \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right) \) is still a solution to the Ricci flow which exists on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{k}/{\epsilon }_{k}^{2},\left( {T - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}}\right) \) , where

\[
{t}_{k}/{\epsilon }_{k}^{2} = {t}_{k}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow   + \infty
\]

and

\[
\left( {T - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2} = \left( {T - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  \Omega .
\]

For any \( \epsilon  > 0 \) we can find a time \( \tau  < T \) such that for \( t \in  \lbrack \tau , T) \) ,

\[
\left| {Rm}\right|  \leq  \left( {\Omega  + \epsilon }\right) /\left( {T - t}\right)
\]

by the assumption. Then for \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {\left( {\tau  - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2},\left( {T - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}}\right) \) , the curvature of \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right) \) is bounded by

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}^{\left( k\right) }}\right|  = {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\left| {Rm}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {\Omega  + \epsilon }\right) /\left( {\left( {T - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {\Omega  + \epsilon }\right) /\left( {\left( {T - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  + \left( {{t}_{k} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }\right)
\]

\[
\rightarrow  \left( {\Omega  + \epsilon }\right) /\left( {\Omega  - \widetilde{t}}\right) ,\;\text{ as }k \rightarrow   + \infty .
\]

This implies that \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \right\} \) is a sequence of (almost) maximum points. And then by the injectivity radius condition and Hamilton's compactness theorem 4.1.5, there exists a subsequence of the metrics \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) which converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a limit metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( \infty \right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) on a limiting manifold \( \widetilde{M} \) with \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left( {-\infty ,\Omega }\right) \) such that \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( \infty \right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) is a complete solution of the Ricci flow and its curvature satisfies the bound

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}^{\left( \infty \right) }}\right|  \leq  \Omega /\left( {\Omega  - \widetilde{t}}\right)
\]

everywhere on \( \widetilde{M} \times  \left( {-\infty ,\Omega }\right) \) with the equality somewhere at \( \widetilde{t} = 0 \) .

Type II(a): We consider a maximal solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) on \( M \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with

\[
T <  + \infty \text{ and }\;\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}\left( {T - t}\right) {K}_{\max }\left( t\right)  =  + \infty .
\]

Let \( {T}_{k} < T <  + \infty \) with \( {T}_{k} \rightarrow  T \) , and \( {\gamma }_{k} \nearrow  1 \) , as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Pick points \( {x}_{k} \) and times \( {t}_{k} \) such that, as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) ,

\[
\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\gamma }_{k}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M, t \leq  {T}_{k}}}\left( {{T}_{k} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow   + \infty .
\]

Again denote by

\[
{\epsilon }_{k} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) \right| }}
\]

and dilate the solution as before to get

\[
{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right)  = {\epsilon }_{k}^{-2}{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right) ,\;\widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{k}/{\epsilon }_{k}^{2},\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}}\right) ,
\]

which is still a solution to the Ricci flow and satisfies the curvature bound

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}^{\left( k\right) }}\right|  = {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\left| {Rm}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{{\gamma }_{k}} \cdot  \frac{\left( {T}_{k} - {t}_{k}\right) }{\left( {T}_{k} - t\right) }
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\gamma }_{k}}\frac{\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }{\left\lbrack  {\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  - \widetilde{t}}\right\rbrack  }\;\text{ for }\widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-\frac{{t}_{k}}{{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}},\frac{\left( {T}_{k} - {t}_{k}\right) }{{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}}}\right) ,
\]

since \( t = {t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t} \) and \( {\epsilon }_{k} = 1/\sqrt{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) \right| } \) . Hence \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \right\} \) is a sequence of (almost) maximum points. And then as before, by applying Hamilton's compactness theorem 4.1.5, there exists a subsequence of the metrics \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) which converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a limit \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( \infty \right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) on a limiting manifold \( \widetilde{M} \) and \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right) \) such that \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( \infty \right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) is a complete solution of the Ricci flow and its curvature satisfies

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}^{\left( \infty \right) }}\right|  \leq  1
\]

everywhere on \( \widetilde{M} \times  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right) \) and the equality holds somewhere at \( \widetilde{t} = 0 \) .

Type II(b): We consider a maximal solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) on \( M \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with

\[
T =  + \infty \;\text{ and }\;\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}t{K}_{\max }\left( t\right)  =  + \infty .
\]

Again let \( {T}_{k} \rightarrow  T =  + \infty \) , and \( {\gamma }_{k} \nearrow  1 \) , as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Pick \( {x}_{k} \) and \( {t}_{k} \) such that

\[
{t}_{k}\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\gamma }_{k}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M, t \leq  {T}_{k}}}t\left( {{T}_{k} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right| .
\]

Define

\[
{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right)  = {\epsilon }_{k}^{-2}{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right) ,\;\widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{k}/{\epsilon }_{k}^{2},\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}}\right) ,
\]

where \( {\epsilon }_{k} = 1/\sqrt{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) \right| } \) .

Since

\[
{t}_{k}\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\gamma }_{k}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M, t \leq  {T}_{k}}}t\left( {{T}_{k} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\geq  {\gamma }_{k}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M, t \leq  {T}_{k}/2}}t\left( {{T}_{k} - t}\right) \left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{{T}_{k}}{2}{\gamma }_{k}\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M, t \leq  {T}_{k}/2}}t\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|
\]

we have

\[
\frac{{t}_{k}}{{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}} = {t}_{k}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  \geq  \frac{{\gamma }_{k}}{2}\left( \frac{{T}_{k}}{{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M, t \leq  {T}_{k}/2}}t\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow   + \infty ,
\]

and

\[
\frac{\left( {T}_{k} - {t}_{k}\right) }{{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}} = \left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  \geq  \frac{{\gamma }_{k}}{2}\left( \frac{{T}_{k}}{{t}_{k}}\right) \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  M, t \leq  {T}_{k}/2}}t\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \rightarrow   + \infty ,
\]

as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) . As before, we also have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \widetilde{t}}{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right)  =  - 2{\widetilde{R}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right)
\]

and

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}^{\left( k\right) }}\right|
\]

\[
= {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\left| {Rm}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{{\gamma }_{k}} \cdot  \frac{{t}_{k}\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) }{t\left( {{T}_{k} - t}\right) }
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\gamma }_{k}} \cdot  \frac{{t}_{k}\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }{\left( {{t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right) \left\lbrack  {\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right)  - {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right\rbrack   \cdot  \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\gamma }_{k}} \cdot  \frac{{t}_{k}\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }{\left( {{t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right) \left\lbrack  {\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  - \widetilde{t}}\right\rbrack  }
\]

\[
= \frac{{t}_{k}\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }{{\gamma }_{k}\left( {1 + \widetilde{t}/\left( {{t}_{k}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }\right) }\right) \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k}\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| \rbrack \left( {1 - \widetilde{t}/\left( {\left( {{T}_{k} - {t}_{k}}\right) \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right| }\right) }\right) }\right\rbrack  }
\]

\[
\rightarrow  1,\;\text{ as }\;k \rightarrow   + \infty .
\]

Hence \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \right\} \) is again a sequence of (almost) maximum points. As before, there exists a subsequence of the metrics \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) which converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a limit \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( \infty \right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) on a limiting manifold \( \widetilde{M} \) and \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right) \) such that \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( \infty \right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) is a complete solution of the Ricci flow and its curvature satisfies

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}^{\left( \infty \right) }}\right|  \leq  1
\]

everywhere on \( \widetilde{M} \times  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right) \) with the equality somewhere at \( \widetilde{t} = 0 \) .

Type III(a): We consider a maximal solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) on \( M \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T =  + \infty \) and

\[
\mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{t \rightarrow  T}}t{K}_{\max }\left( t\right)  = A \in  \left( {0, + \infty }\right) .
\]

Choose a sequence of \( {x}_{k} \) and \( {t}_{k} \) such that \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) and

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{t}_{k}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  = A.
\]

Set \( {\epsilon }_{k} = 1/\sqrt{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) \right| } \) and dilate the solution as before to get

\[
{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( {\cdot ,\widetilde{t}}\right)  = {\epsilon }_{k}^{-2}{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right) ,\;\widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{k}/{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}, + \infty }\right)
\]

which is still a solution to the Ricci flow. Also, for arbitrarily fixed \( \epsilon  > 0 \) , there exists a sufficiently large positive constant \( \tau \) such that for \( t \in  \lbrack \tau , + \infty ) \) ,

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}^{\left( k\right) }}\right|  = {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\left| {Rm}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\left( \frac{A + \epsilon }{t}\right)
\]

\[
= {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\left( \frac{A + \epsilon }{{t}_{k} + {\epsilon }_{k}^{2}\widetilde{t}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {A + \epsilon }\right) /\left( {{t}_{k}\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  + \widetilde{t}}\right) ,\;\text{ for }\widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {\left( {\tau  - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2}, + \infty }\right) .
\]

Note that

\[
\left( {A + \epsilon }\right) /\left( {{t}_{k}\left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right|  + \widetilde{t}}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {A + \epsilon }\right) /\left( {A + \widetilde{t}}\right) ,\;\text{ as }k \rightarrow   + \infty
\]

and

\[
\left( {\tau  - {t}_{k}}\right) /{\epsilon }_{k}^{2} \rightarrow   - A,\;\text{ as }k \rightarrow   + \infty .
\]

Hence \( \left\{  \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \right\} \) is a sequence of (almost) maximum points. And then as before, there exists a subsequence of the metrics \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) which converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a limit \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( \infty \right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) on a limiting manifold \( \widetilde{M} \) and \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left( {-A, + \infty }\right) \) such that \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( \infty \right) }\left( \widetilde{t}\right) \) is a complete solution of the Ricci flow and its curvature satisfies

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}^{\left( \infty \right) }}\right|  \leq  A/\left( {A + \widetilde{t}}\right)
\]

everywhere on \( \widetilde{M} \times  \left( {-A, + \infty }\right) \) with the equality somewhere at \( \widetilde{t} = 0 \) . C

nodes.label: Corollary 4.3.5
nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content:
COROLLARY 4.3.5. For any complete maximal solution to the Ricci flow with bounded and nonnegative curvature operator on a Riemannian manifold, or on a Kähler manifold with bounded and nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature, there exists a sequence of dilations of the solution along (almost) maximum points which converges to a singular model.

For Type I solutions: the limit model exists for \( t \in  \left( {-\infty ,\Omega }\right) \) with \( 0 < \Omega  <  + \infty \) and has

\[
R \leq  \Omega /\left( {\Omega  - t}\right)
\]

everywhere with equality somewhere at \( t = 0 \) .

For Type II solutions: the limit model exists for \( t \in  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right) \) and has

\[
R \leq  1
\]

everywhere with equality somewhere at \( t = 0 \) .

For Type III solutions: the limit model exists for \( t \in  \left( {-A, + \infty }\right) \) with \( 0 < A <  + \infty \) and has

\[
R \leq  A/\left( {A + t}\right)
\]

everywhere with equality somewhere at \( t = 0 \) .

nodes.label: Theorem 4.3.6
nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content:
Theorem 4.3.6.

(i) (Hamilton [66]) Any Type II singularity model with nonnegative curvature operator and positive Ricci curvature to the Ricci flow on a manifold \( M \) must be a (steady) Ricci soliton.

(ii) (Chen-Zhu [30]) Any Type III singularity model with nonnegative curvature operator and positive Ricci curvature on a manifold \( M \) must be a homotheti-cally expanding Ricci soliton.
nodes.content_excerpt: Theorem 4.3.6. (i) (Hamilton [66]) Any Type II singularity model with nonnegative curvature operator and positive Ricci curvature to the Ricci flow on a manifold \( M \) must be a (steady) Ricci soliton. (ii) (Chen-Zhu [30]) Any Type III singularity model with nonnegative curvature operator and positive Ricci curvature on a manifold \( M \) must be a homotheti-cally expanding Ricci soliton.

nodes.proof:
We only give the proof of (ii), since the proof of (i) is similar and easier.

After a shift of the time variable, we may assume the Type III singularity model is defined on \( 0 < t <  + \infty \) and \( {tR} \) assumes its maximum in space-time.

Recall from the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Theorem 2.5.4) that for any vectors \( {V}^{i} \) and \( {W}^{i} \) ,

(4.3.1)

\[
{M}_{ij}{W}^{i}{W}^{j} + \left( {{P}_{kij} + {P}_{kji}}\right) {V}^{k}{W}^{i}{W}^{j} + {R}_{ikjl}{W}^{i}{W}^{j}{V}^{k}{V}^{l} \geq  0,
\]

where

\[
{M}_{ij} = \Delta {R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}R + 2{R}_{ipjq}{R}^{pq} - {g}^{pq}{R}_{ip}{R}_{jq} + \frac{1}{2t}{R}_{ij}
\]

and

\[
{P}_{ijk} = {\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jk} - {\nabla }_{j}{R}_{ik}.
\]

Take the trace on \( W \) to get

(4.3.2)

\[
Q \triangleq  \frac{\partial R}{\partial t} + \frac{R}{t} + 2{\nabla }_{i}R \cdot  {V}^{i} + 2{R}_{ij}{V}^{i}{V}^{j} \geq  0
\]

for any vector \( {V}^{i} \) . Let us choose \( V \) to be the vector field minimizing \( Q \) , i.e.,

(4.3.3)

\[
{V}^{i} =  - \frac{1}{2}{\left( {\operatorname{Ric}}^{-1}\right) }^{ik}{\nabla }_{k}R,
\]

where \( {\left( Ri{c}^{-1}\right) }^{ik} \) is the inverse of the Ricci tensor \( {R}_{ij} \) . Substitute this vector field \( V \) into \( Q \) to get a smooth function \( \widetilde{Q} \) . By a direct computation from the evolution equations of curvatures (see [61] for details),

(4.3.4)

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\widetilde{Q} \geq  \Delta \widetilde{Q} - \frac{2}{t}\widetilde{Q}
\]

Suppose \( {tR} \) assumes its maximum at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) , then

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} + \frac{R}{t} = 0,\;\text{ at }\;\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) .
\]

This implies that the quantity

\[
Q = \frac{\partial R}{\partial t} + \frac{R}{t} + 2{\nabla }_{i}R \cdot  {V}^{i} + 2{R}_{ij}{V}^{i}{V}^{j}
\]

vanishes in the direction \( V = 0 \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . We claim that for any earlier time \( t < {t}_{0} \) and any point \( x \in  M \) , there is a vector \( V \in  {T}_{x}M \) such that \( Q = 0 \) .

We argue by contradiction. Suppose not, then there is \( \bar{x} \in  M \) and \( 0 < \bar{t} < {t}_{0} \) such that \( \widetilde{Q} \) is positive at \( x = \bar{x} \) and \( t = \bar{t} \) . We can find a nonnegative smooth function \( \rho \) on \( M \) with support in a neighborhood of \( \bar{x} \) so that \( \rho \left( \bar{x}\right)  > 0 \) and

\[
\widetilde{Q} \geq  \frac{\rho }{{\bar{t}}^{2}}
\]

at \( t = \bar{t} \) . Let \( \rho \) evolve by the heat equation

\[
\frac{\partial \rho }{\partial t} = {\Delta \rho }
\]

It then follows from the standard strong maximum principle that \( \rho  > 0 \) everywhere for any \( t > \bar{t} \) . From (4.3.4) we see that

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\widetilde{Q} - \frac{\rho }{{t}^{2}}}\right)  \geq  \Delta \left( {\widetilde{Q} - \frac{\rho }{{t}^{2}}}\right)  - \frac{2}{t}\left( {\widetilde{Q} - \frac{\rho }{{t}^{2}}}\right)
\]

Then by the maximum principle as in Chapter 2, we get

\[
\widetilde{Q} \geq  \frac{\rho }{{t}^{2}} > 0,\;\text{ for all }t \geq  \bar{t}.
\]

This gives a contradiction with the fact \( Q = 0 \) for \( V = 0 \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) . We thus prove the claim.

Consider each time \( t < {t}_{0} \) . The null vector field of \( Q \) satisfies the equation

(4.3.5)

\[
{\nabla }_{i}R + 2{R}_{ij}{V}^{j} = 0,
\]

by the first variation of \( Q \) in \( V \) . Since \( {R}_{ij} \) is positive, we see that such a null vector field is unique and varies smoothly in space-time.

Substituting (4.3.5) into the expression of \( Q \) , we have

(4.3.6)

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} + \frac{R}{t} + {\nabla }_{i}R \cdot  {V}^{i} = 0
\]

Denote by

\[
{Q}_{ij} = {M}_{ij} + \left( {{P}_{kij} + {P}_{kji}}\right) {V}^{k} + {R}_{ikjl}{V}^{k}{V}^{l}.
\]

From (4.3.1) we see that \( {Q}_{ij} \) is nonnegative definite with its trace \( Q = 0 \) for such a null vector \( V \) . It follows that

\[
{Q}_{ij} = {M}_{ij} + \left( {{P}_{kij} + {P}_{kji}}\right) {V}^{k} + {R}_{ikjl}{V}^{k}{V}^{l} = 0.
\]

Again from the first variation of \( {Q}_{ij} \) in \( V \) , we see that

(4.3.7)

\[
\left( {{P}_{kij} + {P}_{kji}}\right)  + \left( {{R}_{ikjl} + {R}_{jkil}}\right) {V}^{l} = 0,
\]

and hence

(4.3.8)

\[
{M}_{ij} - {R}_{ikjl}{V}^{k}{V}^{l} = 0.
\]

Applying the heat operator to (4.3.5) and (4.3.6) we get

(4.3.9)

\[
0 = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}R + 2{R}_{ij}{V}^{j}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{R}_{ij}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {V}^{j} + \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}R}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{V}^{j}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {R}_{ij} - 4{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{ij}{\nabla }^{k}{V}^{j}
\]

and

(4.3.10)

\[
0 = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} + \frac{R}{t} + {\nabla }_{i}R \cdot  {V}^{i}}\right)
\]

\[
= {\nabla }_{i}R\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) {V}^{i} + {V}^{i}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{i}R}\right)  - 2{\nabla }_{k}{\nabla }_{i}R \cdot  {\nabla }^{k}{V}^{i}
\]

\[
+ \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - \Delta }\right) \left( {\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} + \frac{R}{t}}\right) .
\]

Multiplying (4.3.9) by \( {V}^{i} \) , summing over \( i \) and adding (4.3.10), as well as using the evolution equations on curvature, we get

(4.3.11)

\[
0 = 2{V}^{i}\left( {2{\nabla }_{i}\left( {\left| Rc\right| }^{2}\right)  - {R}_{il}{\nabla }^{l}R}\right)  + 2{V}^{i}{V}^{j}\left( {2{R}_{piqj}{R}^{pq} - 2{g}^{pq}{R}_{pi}{R}_{qj}}\right)
\]

\[
- 4{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{ij} \cdot  {\nabla }^{k}{V}^{j} \cdot  {V}^{i} - 2{\nabla }_{k}{\nabla }_{i}R \cdot  {\nabla }^{k}{V}^{i} + 4{R}^{ij}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}R
\]

\[
+ 4{g}^{kl}{g}^{mn}{g}^{pq}{R}_{km}{R}_{np}{R}_{ql} + 4{R}_{ijkl}{R}^{ik}{V}^{j}{V}^{l} - \frac{R}{{t}^{2}}.
\]

From (4.3.5), we have the following equalities

(4.3.12)

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l}  - 2{V}^{i}{R}_{il}{\nabla }^{l}R - 4{V}^{i}{V}^{j}{g}^{pq}{R}_{pi}{R}_{qj} = 0, \\   - 4{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{ij} \cdot  {\nabla }^{k}{V}^{j} \cdot  {V}^{i} - 2{\nabla }_{k}{\nabla }_{i}R \cdot  {\nabla }^{k}{V}^{i} = 4{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{k}{V}^{i} \cdot  {\nabla }^{k}{V}^{j}, \\  {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}R =  - 2{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jl} \cdot  {V}^{l} - 2{R}_{jl}{\nabla }_{i}{V}^{l}. \end{array}\right.
\]

Substituting (4.3.12) into (4.3.11), we obtain

\[
8{R}^{ij}\left( {{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{ij} \cdot  {V}^{k} + {R}_{ikjl}{V}^{k}{V}^{l} - {\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jl} \cdot  {V}^{l} - {R}_{jl}{\nabla }_{i}{V}^{l}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 4{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{k}{V}^{i} \cdot  {\nabla }^{k}{V}^{j} + 4{g}^{kl}{g}^{mn}{g}^{pq}{R}_{km}{R}_{np}{R}_{ql} - \frac{R}{{t}^{2}} = 0.
\]

By using (4.3.7), we know

\[
{R}^{ij}\left( {{\nabla }_{k}{R}_{ij} \cdot  {V}^{k} + {R}_{ikjl}{V}^{k}{V}^{l} - {\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jl} \cdot  {V}^{l}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Then we have

(4.3.13)

\[
- 8{R}^{ij}{R}_{jl}{\nabla }_{i}{V}^{l} + 4{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{k}{V}^{i} \cdot  {\nabla }^{k}{V}^{j} + 4{g}^{kl}{g}^{mn}{g}^{pq}{R}_{km}{R}_{np}{R}_{ql} - \frac{R}{{t}^{2}} = 0.
\]

By taking the trace in the last equality in (4.3.12) and using (4.3.6) and the evolution equation of the scalar curvature, we can get

(4.3.14)

\[
{R}^{ij}\left( {{R}_{ij} + \frac{{g}_{ij}}{2t} - {\nabla }_{i}{V}_{j}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Finally by combining (4.3.13) and (4.3.14), we deduce

\[
4{R}^{ij}{g}^{kl}\left( {{R}_{ik} + \frac{{g}_{ik}}{2t} - {\nabla }_{k}{V}_{i}}\right) \left( {{R}_{jk} + \frac{{g}_{jk}}{2t} - {\nabla }_{k}{V}_{j}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Since \( {R}_{ij} \) is positive definite, we get

(4.3.15)

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{V}_{j} = {R}_{ij} + \frac{{g}_{ij}}{2t},\;\text{ for all }i, j.
\]

This means that \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) is a homothetically expanding Ricci soliton.

nodes.content:
REMARK 4.3.7. Recall from Section 1.5 that any compact steady Ricci soliton or expanding Ricci soliton must be Einstein. If the manifold \( M \) in Theorem 4.3.6 is noncompact and simply connected, then the steady (or expanding) Ricci soliton must be a steady (or expanding) gradient Ricci soliton. For example, we know that \( {\nabla }_{i}{V}_{j} \) is symmetric from (4.3.15). Also, by the simply connectedness of \( M \) there exists a function \( F \) such that

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}F = {\nabla }_{i}{V}_{j},\;\text{ on }M.
\]

So

\[
{R}_{ij} = {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}F - \frac{{g}_{ij}}{2t},\;\text{ on }M
\]

This means that \( {g}_{ij} \) is an expanding gradient Ricci soliton.

In the Kähler case, we have the following results for Type II and Type III singularity models with nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature obtained by the first author in [14].

Theorem 4.3.8 (Cao [14]).

(i) Any Type II singularity model on a Kähler manifold with nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature and positive Ricci curvature must be a steady Kähler-Ricci soliton.

(ii) Any Type III singularity model on a Kähler manifold with nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature and positive Ricci curvature must be an expanding Kähler-Ricci soliton.

nodes.label: Lemma 4.4.1
nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content:
LEMMA 4.4.1. Suppose we have a complete gradient steady Ricci soliton \( {g}_{ij} \) with bounded curvature so that

\[
{R}_{ij} = {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}F
\]

for some function \( F \) on \( M \) . Assume the Ricci curvature is positive and the scalar curvature \( R \) attains its maximum \( {R}_{\max } \) at a point \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) . Then

(4.4.1)

\[
{\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} + R = {R}_{\max }
\]

everywhere on \( M \) , and furthermore \( F \) is convex and attains its minimum at \( {x}_{0} \) .

nodes.proof:
Recall that, from (1.1.15) and noting our \( F \) here is \( - f \) there, the steady gradient Ricci soliton has the property

\[
{\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} + R = {C}_{0}
\]

for some constant \( {C}_{0} \) . Clearly, \( {C}_{0} \geq  {R}_{\max } \) .

If \( {C}_{0} = {R}_{\max } \) , then \( \nabla F = 0 \) at the point \( {x}_{0} \) . Since \( {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}F = {R}_{ij} > 0 \) , we see that \( F \) is convex and \( F \) attains its minimum at \( {x}_{0} \) .

If \( {C}_{0} > {R}_{\max } \) , consider a gradient path of \( F \) in a local coordinate neighborhood through \( {x}_{0} = \left( {{x}_{0}^{1},\ldots ,{x}_{0}^{n}}\right) \) :

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l} {x}^{i} = {x}^{i}\left( u\right) ,\;u \in  \left( {-\varepsilon ,\varepsilon }\right) , i = 1,\ldots , n \\  {x}_{0}^{i} = {x}^{i}\left( 0\right) , \end{array}\right.
\]

and

\[
\frac{d{x}^{i}}{du} = {g}^{ij}{\nabla }_{j}F,\;u \in  \left( {-\varepsilon ,\varepsilon }\right) .
\]

Now \( {\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} = {C}_{0} - R \geq  {C}_{0} - {R}_{\max } > 0 \) everywhere, while \( {\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} \) is smallest at \( x = {x}_{0} \) since \( R \) is largest there. But we compute

\[
\frac{d}{du}{\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} = 2{g}^{jl}\left( {\frac{d}{du}{\nabla }_{j}F}\right) {\nabla }_{l}F
\]

\[
= 2{g}^{ik}{g}^{jl}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}F \cdot  {\nabla }_{k}F{\nabla }_{l}F
\]

\[
= 2{g}^{ik}{g}^{jl}{R}_{ij}{\nabla }_{k}F{\nabla }_{l}F
\]

\[
> 0
\]

since \( {R}_{ij} > 0 \) and \( {\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} > 0 \) . Then \( {\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} \) is not smallest at \( {x}_{0} \) , and we have a contradiction. [

nodes.content:
We remark that when we are considering a complete expanding gradient Ricci soliton on \( M \) with positive Ricci curvature and

\[
{R}_{ij} + \rho {g}_{ij} = {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}F
\]

for some constant \( \rho  > 0 \) and some function \( F \) , the above argument gives

\[
{\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} + R - {2\rho F} = C
\]

for some positive constant \( C \) . Moreover the function \( F \) is an exhausting and convex function. In particular, such an expanding gradient Ricci soliton is diffeomorphic to the Euclidean space \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) .

Let us introduce a geometric invariant as follows. Let \( O \) be a fixed point in a Riemannian manifold \( M, s \) the distance to the fixed point \( O \) , and \( R \) the scalar curvature. We define the asymptotic scalar curvature ratio

\[
A = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{s \rightarrow   + \infty }}R{s}^{2}
\]

Clearly the definition is independent of the choice of the fixed point \( O \) and invariant under dilation.

For a complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton with bounded curvature and positive sectional curvature of dimension \( n \geq \) 3 where the scalar curvature assume its maximum at a point \( O \in  M \) , the asymptotic scalar curvature ratio is infinite, i.e.,

\[
A = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{s \rightarrow   + \infty }}R{s}^{2} =  + \infty
\]

where \( s \) is the distance to the point \( O \) .

nodes.proof:
The solution to the Ricci flow corresponding to the soliton exists for \( - \infty  < t <  + \infty \) and is obtained by flowing along the gradient of a potential function \( F \) of the soliton. We argue by contradiction. Suppose \( R{s}^{2} \leq  C \) . We will show that the limit

\[
{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( x\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow   - \infty }}{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right)
\]

exists for \( x \neq  O \) on the manifold \( M \) and is a complete flat metric on \( M \smallsetminus  \{ O\} \) . Since the sectional curvature of \( M \) is positive everywhere, it follows from Cheeger-Gromoll [23] that \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Thus \( M \smallsetminus  \{ O\} \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{S}}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . But for \( n \geq  3 \) there is no flat metric on \( {\mathbb{S}}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) , and this will finish the proof.

To see the limit metric exists, we note that \( R \rightarrow  0 \) as \( s \rightarrow   + \infty \) , so \( {\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} \rightarrow  {R}_{\max } \) as \( s \rightarrow   + \infty \) by (4.4.1). The function \( F \) itself can be taken to evolve with time, using the definition

\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial t} = {\nabla }_{i}F \cdot  \frac{\partial {x}^{i}}{\partial t} =  - {\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} = {\Delta F} - {R}_{\max }
\]

which pulls \( F \) back by the flow along the gradient of \( F \) . Then we continue to have \( {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}F = {R}_{ij} \) for all time, and \( {\left| \nabla F\right| }^{2} \rightarrow  {R}_{\max } \) as \( s \rightarrow   + \infty \) for each time.

When we go backward in time, this is equivalent to flowing outwards along the gradient of \( F \) , and our speed approaches \( \sqrt{{R}_{\max }} \) . So, starting outside of any neighborhood of \( O \) we have

\[
\frac{s}{\left| t\right| } = \frac{{d}_{t}\left( {\cdot , O}\right) }{\left| t\right| } \rightarrow  \sqrt{{R}_{\max }},\;\text{ as }t \rightarrow   - \infty
\]

and

(4.4.2)

\[
R\left( {\cdot , t}\right)  \leq  \frac{C}{{R}_{\max } \cdot  {\left| t\right| }^{2}},\;\text{ as }\left| t\right| \text{ large enough. }
\]

Hence for \( \left| t\right| \) sufficiently large,

\[
0 \geq   - 2{R}_{ij}
\]

\[
= \frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij}
\]

\[
\geq   - {2R}{g}_{ij}
\]

\[
\geq   - \frac{2C}{{R}_{\max } \cdot  {\left| t\right| }^{2}}{g}_{ij}
\]

which implies that for any tangent vector \( V \) ,

\[
0 \leq  \frac{d}{d\left| t\right| }\left( {\log \left( {{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) {V}^{i}{V}^{j}}\right) }\right)  \leq  \frac{2C}{{R}_{\max } \cdot  {\left| t\right| }^{2}}.
\]

These two inequalities show that \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) {V}^{i}{V}^{j} \) has a limit \( {\bar{g}}_{ij}{V}^{i}{V}^{j} \) as \( t \rightarrow   - \infty \) .

Since the metrics are all essentially the same, it always takes an infinite length to get out to the infinity. This shows the limit \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) is complete at the infinity. One the other hand, any point \( P \) other than \( O \) will eventually be arbitrarily far from \( O \) , so the limit metric \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) is also complete away from \( O \) in \( M \smallsetminus  \{ O\} \) . Using Shi’s derivative estimates in Chapter 1, it follows that \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a complete smooth limit metric \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) as \( t \rightarrow   - \infty \) , and the limit metric is flat by (4.4.2).

nodes.content:
THEOREM 4.4.3 (Hamilton [60]). The only complete steady Ricci soliton on a two-dimensional manifold with bounded curvature which assumes its maximum 1 at an origin is the "cigar" soliton on the plane \( {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) with the metric

\[
d{s}^{2} = \frac{d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2}}{1 + {x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 4.4.3 (Hamilton [60]). The only complete steady Ricci soliton on a two-dimensional manifold with bounded curvature which assumes its maximum 1 at an origin is the "cigar" soliton on the plane \( {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) with the metric \[ d{s}^{2} = \frac{d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2}}{1 + {x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}. \]

nodes.proof:
Recall that the scalar curvature evolves by

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} = {\Delta R} + {R}^{2}
\]

on a two-dimensional manifold \( M \) . Denote by \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  = \inf \{ R\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  x \in  M\} \) . We see from the maximum principle (see for example Chapter 2) that \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right) \) is strictly increasing whenever \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  \neq  0 \) , for \( - \infty  < t <  + \infty \) . This shows that the curvature of a steady Ricci soliton on a two-dimensional manifold \( M \) must be nonnegative and \( {R}_{\min }\left( t\right)  = 0 \) for all \( t \in  \left( {-\infty , + \infty }\right) \) . Further by the strong maximum principle we see that the curvature is actually positive everywhere. In particular, the manifold must be noncompact. So the manifold \( M \) is diffiomorphic to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) and the Ricci soliton must be a gradient soliton. Let \( F \) be a potential function of the gradient Ricci soliton. Then, by definition, we have

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{V}_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}{V}_{i} = R{g}_{ij}
\]

with \( {V}_{i} = {\nabla }_{i}F \) . This says that the vector field \( V \) must be conformal. In complex coordinate a conformal vector field is holomorphic. Hence \( V \) is locally given by \( V\left( z\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial z} \) for a holomorphic function \( V\left( z\right) \) . At a zero of \( V \) there will be a power series expansion

\[
V\left( z\right)  = a{z}^{p} + \cdots ,\left( {a \neq  0}\right)
\]

and if \( p > 1 \) the vector field will have closed orbits in any neighborhood of the zero. Now the vector field is gradient and a gradient flow cannot have a closed orbit. Hence \( V\left( z\right) \) has only simple zeros. By Lemma 4.4.1, we know that \( F \) is strictly convex with the only critical point being the minima, chosen to be the origin of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) . So the holomorphic vector field \( V \) must be

\[
V\left( z\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial z} = {cz}\frac{\partial }{\partial z},\;\text{ for }z \in  C,
\]

for some complex number \( c \) .

We now claim that \( c \) is real. Let us write the metric as

\[
d{s}^{2} = g\left( {x, y}\right) \left( {d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2}}\right)
\]

with \( z = x + \sqrt{-1}y \) . Then \( \nabla F = {cz}\frac{\partial }{\partial z} \) means that if \( c = a + \sqrt{-1}b \) , then

\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial x} = \left( {{ax} - {by}}\right) g,\;\frac{\partial F}{\partial y} = \left( {{bx} + {ay}}\right) g.
\]

Taking the mixed partial derivatives \( \frac{{\partial }^{2}F}{\partial x\partial y} \) and equating them at the origin \( x = y = 0 \) gives \( b = 0 \) , so \( c \) is real.

Let

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{ll} x = {e}^{u}\cos v, &  - \infty  < u <  + \infty , \\  y = {e}^{u}\sin v, & 0 \leq  v \leq  {2\pi }. \end{array}\right.
\]

Write

\[
d{s}^{2} = g\left( {x, y}\right) \left( {d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= g\left( {{e}^{u}\cos v,{e}^{u}\sin v}\right) {e}^{2u}\left( {d{u}^{2} + d{v}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
\overset{\Delta }{ = }g\left( {u, v}\right) \left( {d{u}^{2} + d{v}^{2}}\right) .
\]

Then we get the equations

\[
\frac{\partial F}{\partial u} = {ag},\;\frac{\partial F}{\partial v} = 0
\]

since the gradient of \( F \) is just \( a\frac{\partial }{\partial u} \) for a real constant \( a \) . The second equation shows that \( F = F\left( u\right) \) is a function of \( u \) only, then the first equation shows that \( g = g\left( u\right) \) is also a function of \( u \) only. Then we can write the metric as

(4.4.4)

\[
d{s}^{2} = g\left( u\right) \left( {d{u}^{2} + d{v}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= g\left( u\right) {e}^{-{2u}}\left( {d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2}}\right) .
\]

This implies that \( {e}^{-{2u}}g\left( u\right) \) must be a smooth function of \( {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = {e}^{2u} \) . So as \( u \rightarrow   - \infty , \)

(4.4.5)

\[
g\left( u\right)  = {b}_{1}{e}^{2u} + {b}_{2}{\left( {e}^{2u}\right) }^{2} + \cdots ,
\]

with \( {b}_{1} > 0 \) .

The curvature of the metric is given by

\[
R =  - \frac{1}{g}{\left( \frac{{g}^{\prime }}{g}\right) }^{\prime }
\]

where \( {\left( \cdot \right) }^{\prime } \) is the derivative with respect to \( u \) . Note that the soliton is by translation in \( u \) with velocity \( c \) . Hence \( g = g\left( {u + {ct}}\right) \) satisfies

\[
\frac{\partial g}{\partial t} =  - {Rg}
\]

which becomes

\[
c{g}^{\prime } = {\left( \frac{{g}^{\prime }}{g}\right) }^{\prime }.
\]

Thus by (4.4.5),

\[
\frac{{g}^{\prime }}{g} = {cg} + 2
\]

and then by integrating

\[
{e}^{2u}\left( \frac{1}{g}\right)  =  - \frac{c}{2}{e}^{2u} + {b}_{1}
\]

i.e.,

\[
g\left( u\right)  = \frac{{e}^{2u}}{{b}_{1} - \frac{c}{2}{e}^{2u}}.
\]

In particular, we have \( c < 0 \) since the Ricci soliton is not flat. Therefore

\[
d{s}^{2} = g\left( u\right) {e}^{-{2u}}\left( {d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2}}\right)  = \frac{d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2}}{{\alpha }_{1} + {\alpha }_{2}\left( {{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}\right) }
\]

for some constants \( {\alpha }_{1},{\alpha }_{2} > 0 \) . By the normalization condition that the curvature attains its maximum 1 at the origin, we conclude that

\[
d{s}^{2} = \frac{d{x}^{2} + d{y}^{2}}{1 + \left( {{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}\right) }.
\]

LEMMA 5.1.1. Suppose \( P \) satisfies

\[
\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} = {\Delta P} + Q
\]

for the unnormalized Ricci flow, and \( P \) has degree \( k \) . Then \( Q \) has degree \( k - 1 \) , and for the normalized Ricci flow,

\[
\frac{\partial \widetilde{P}}{\partial \widetilde{t}} = \widetilde{\Delta }\widetilde{P} + \widetilde{Q} + \frac{2}{n}k\widetilde{r}\widetilde{P}.
\]
nodes.content_excerpt: LEMMA 5.1.1. Suppose \( P \) satisfies \[ \frac{\partial P}{\partial t} = {\Delta P} + Q \] for the unnormalized Ricci flow, and \( P \) has degree \( k \) . Then \( Q \) has degree \( k - 1 \) , and for the normalized Ricci flow, \[ \frac{\partial \widetilde{P}}{\partial \widetilde{t}} = \widetilde{\Delta }\widetilde{P} + \widetilde{Q} + \frac{2}{n}k\widetilde{r}\widetilde{P}. \]

nodes.proof:
We first see \( Q \) has degree \( k - 1 \) since \( \partial \widetilde{t}/\partial t = \psi \) and \( \Delta  = \psi \widetilde{\Delta } \) . Then

\[
\psi \frac{\partial }{\partial \widetilde{t}}\left( {{\psi }^{-k}\widetilde{P}}\right)  = \psi \widetilde{\Delta }\left( {{\psi }^{-k}\widetilde{P}}\right)  + {\psi }^{-k + 1}\widetilde{Q}
\]

which implies

\[
\frac{\partial \widetilde{P}}{\partial \widetilde{t}} = \widetilde{\Delta }\widetilde{P} + \widetilde{Q} + \frac{k}{\psi }\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial \widetilde{t}}\widetilde{P}
\]

\[
= \widetilde{\Delta }\widetilde{P} + \widetilde{Q} + \frac{2}{n}k\widetilde{r}\widetilde{P}
\]

since \( \frac{\partial }{\partial \widetilde{t}}\log \psi  = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\log \psi }\right) {\psi }^{-1} = \frac{2}{n}\widetilde{r} \) . \( \square \)

nodes.proof:
Under the normalized Ricci flow,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}^{ij}}\right) {\nabla }_{i}\varphi {\nabla }_{j}\varphi  + 2{g}^{ij}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\nabla }_{i}\varphi }\right) \left( {{\nabla }_{j}\varphi }\right)
\]

\[
= \left( {R - r}\right) {\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} + 2{g}^{ij}{\nabla }_{i}\left( {{\Delta \varphi } + {r\varphi } - b\left( t\right) }\right) {\nabla }_{j}\varphi
\]

\[
= \left( {R + r}\right) {\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} + 2{g}^{ij}\left( {\Delta {\nabla }_{i}\varphi  - {R}_{ik}{\nabla }_{k}\varphi }\right) {\nabla }_{j}\varphi
\]

\[
= \left( {R + r}\right) {\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} + \Delta {\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} - 2{g}^{ij}{R}_{ik}{\nabla }_{k}\varphi {\nabla }_{j}\varphi
\]

\[
= \Delta {\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} + r{\left| \nabla \varphi \right| }^{2},
\]

where \( {R}_{ik} = \frac{1}{2}R{g}_{ik} \) on a surface.

On the other hand we may rewrite the evolution equation (5.1.2) as

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {R - r}\right)  = \Delta \left( {R - r}\right)  + {\left( \Delta \varphi \right) }^{2} + r\left( {R - r}\right) .
\]

Then the combination of above two equations yields

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}h = {\Delta h} - 2\left( {{\left| {\nabla }^{2}\varphi \right| }^{2} - \frac{1}{2}{\left( \Delta \varphi \right) }^{2}}\right)  + {rh}
\]

\[
= {\Delta h} - 2{\left| {M}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + {rh}
\]

as desired. \( \square \)

On a compact surface with \( \chi \left( M\right) < 0 \) , for any initial metric the solution of the normalized Ricci flow (5.1.1) exists for all time and converges in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology to a metric with negative constant curvature.

nodes.proof:
The estimate (5.1.8) shows that the scalar curvature \( R\left( {x, t}\right) \) converges exponentially to the negative constant \( r \) as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) .

Fix a tangent vector \( v \in  {T}_{x}M \) at a point \( x \in  M \) and let \( {\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2} = {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) {v}^{i}{v}^{j} \) . Then we have

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2} = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) {v}^{i}{v}^{j}
\]

\[
= \left( {r - R}\right) {\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2}
\]

which implies

\[
\left| {\frac{d}{dt}\log {\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2}}\right|  \leq  C{e}^{rt},\text{ for all }t > 0
\]

for some positive constant \( C \) depending only on the initial metric (by using (5.1.8)). Thus \( {\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2} \) converges uniformly to a continuous function \( {\left| v\right| }_{\infty }^{2} \) as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) and \( {\left| v\right| }_{\infty }^{2} \neq  0 \) if \( v \neq  0 \) . Since the parallelogram law continues to hold to the limit, the limiting norm \( {\left| v\right| }_{\infty }^{2} \) comes from an inner product \( {g}_{ij}\left( \infty \right) \) . This says, the metrics \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) are all equivalent and as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) , the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) converges uniformly to a positive-definite metric tensor \( {g}_{ij}\left( \infty \right) \) which is continuous and equivalent to the initial metric.

By the virtue of Shi's derivative estimates of the unnormalized Ricci flow in Section 1.4, we see that all derivatives and higher order derivatives of the curvature of the solution \( {g}_{ij} \) of the normalized flow are uniformly bounded on \( M \times  \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) .

This shows that the limiting metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( \infty \right) \) is a smooth metric with negative constant curvature and the solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) converges to the limiting metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( \infty \right) \) in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) . \( \square \)

nodes.proof:
Since \( \frac{\partial \widetilde{\varphi }}{\partial t} = \Delta \widetilde{\varphi } \) , it follows from the maximum principle that

\[
\left| {\widetilde{\varphi }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{6},\;\text{ on }M \times  \lbrack 0, + \infty )
\]

for some positive constant \( {C}_{6} \) depending only on the initial metric. Recall that \( \Delta \widetilde{\varphi } = \; R \) . We thus obtain for any tangent vector \( v \in  {T}_{x}M \) at a point \( x \in  M \) ,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}{\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2} = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) {v}^{i}{v}^{j}
\]

\[
=  - R\left( {x, t}\right) {\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2}
\]

and then

\[
\left| {\log \frac{{\left| v\right| }_{t}^{2}}{{\left| v\right| }_{0}^{2}}}\right|  = \left| {{\int }_{0}^{t}\frac{d}{dt}\log }\right| {v}_{t}{\left. \right| }^{2}{dt} \mid
\]

\[
= \left| {{\int }_{0}^{t}R\left( {x, t}\right) {dt}}\right|
\]

\[
= \left| {\widetilde{\varphi }\left( {x, t}\right)  - \widetilde{\varphi }\left( {x,0}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  2{C}_{6}
\]

for all \( x \in  M \) and \( t \in  \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) . This shows that the solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) of the normalized Ricci flow are all equivalent. This gives us control of the diameter and injectivity radius.

As before, by Shi's derivative estimates of the unnormalized Ricci flow, all derivatives and higher order derivatives of the curvature of the solution \( {g}_{ij} \) of the normalized Ricci flow (5.1.1) are uniformly bounded on \( M \times  \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) . By the virtue of Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5) we see that the solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) subsequentially converges in \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology. The decay estimate (5.1.15) implies that each limit must be a flat metric on \( M \) . Clearly, we will finish the proof if we can show that limit is unique.

Note that the solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) is changing conformally under the Ricci flow (5.1.1) on surfaces. Thus each limit must be conformal to the initial metric, denoted by \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) . Let us denote \( {g}_{ij}\left( \infty \right)  = {e}^{u}{\bar{g}}_{ij} \) to be a limiting metric. Since \( {g}_{ij}\left( \infty \right) \) is flat, it is easy to compute

\[
0 = {e}^{-u}\left( {\bar{R} - \bar{\Delta }u}\right) ,\;\text{ on }M,
\]

where \( \bar{R} \) is the curvature of \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) and \( \bar{\Delta } \) is the Laplacian in the metric \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) . The solution of Poission equation

\[
\bar{\Delta }u = \bar{R},\;\text{ on }M
\]

is unique up to constant. Moreover the constant must be also uniquely determined since the area of the solution of the normalized Ricci flow (5.1.1) is constant in time. So the limit is unique and we complete the proof of Theorem 5.1.5. 0

nodes.content:
Proposition 5.1.7. Let \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) be a solution of the normalized Ricci flow on a compact surface with \( \chi \left( M\right)  > 0 \) . Then there exist a time \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) and a positive constant \( C \) such that the estimate

\[
{C}^{-1} \leq  R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C
\]

holds for all \( x \in  M \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, + \infty }\right) \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 5.1.7. Let \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) be a solution of the normalized Ricci flow on a compact surface with \( \chi \left( M\right) > 0 \) . Then there exist a time \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) and a positive constant \( C \) such that the estimate \[ {C}^{-1} \leq R\left( {x, t}\right) \leq C \] holds for all \( x \in M \) and \( t \in \left\lbrack {{t}_{0}, + \infty }\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
Recall that

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  s\left( t\right)  = \frac{r}{1 - c{e}^{rt}},\;\text{ on }M \times  \lbrack 0, + \infty ).
\]

For any \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0, r}\right) \) , there exists a large enough \( {t}_{0} > 0 \) such that

(5.1.18)

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq   - {\varepsilon }^{2},\;\text{ on }M \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, + \infty }\right) .
\]

Let \( t \) be any fixed time with \( t \geq  {t}_{0} + 1 \) . Obviously there is some point \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) such that \( R\left( {{x}_{0}, t + 1}\right)  = r \) .

Consider the geodesic ball \( {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},1}\right) \) , centered at \( {x}_{0} \) and radius 1 with respect to the metric at the fixed time \( t \) . For any point \( x \in  {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},1}\right) \) , we choose a geodesic \( \gamma \) : \( \left\lbrack  {t, t + 1}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) connecting \( x \) and \( {x}_{0} \) with respect to the metric at the fixed time \( t \) . Since

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij} = \left( {r - R}\right) {g}_{ij} \leq  {2r}{g}_{ij}\;\text{ on }M \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, + \infty }\right) ,
\]

we have

\[
{\int }_{t}^{t + 1}{\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{\tau }^{2}{d\tau } \leq  {e}^{2r}{\int }_{t}^{t + 1}{\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{t}^{2}{d\tau } \leq  {e}^{2r}.
\]

Then by Lemma 5.1.6, we have

(5.1.19)

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  s\left( t\right)  + \exp \left\{  {\frac{1}{4}{e}^{2r} + C}\right\}   \cdot  \left( {R\left( {{x}_{0}, t + 1}\right)  - s\left( {t + 1}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{1},\;\text{ as }x \in  {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},1}\right) ,
\]

for some positive constant \( {C}_{1} \) depending only on the initial metric. Note the the corresponding unnormalized Ricci flow in this case has finite maximal time since its volume decreases at a fixed rate \( - {4\pi \chi }\left( M\right)  < 0 \) . Hence the no local collapsing theorem \( {\mathrm{I}}^{\prime } \) (Theorem 3.3.3) implies that the volume of \( {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},1}\right) \) with respect to the metric at the fixed time \( t \) is bounded from below by

(5.1.20)

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},1}\right) }\right)  \geq  {C}_{2}
\]

for some positive constant \( {C}_{2} \) depending only on the initial metric.

We now want to bound the diameter of \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) from above. The following argument is analogous to Yau in [128] where he got a lower bound for the volume of geodesic balls of a complete Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature. Without loss of generality, we may assume that the diameter of \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is at least 3. Choose a point \( {x}_{1} \in  M \) such that the distance \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) \) between \( {x}_{1} \) and \( {x}_{0} \) with respect to the metric at the fixed time \( t \) is at least a half of the diameter of \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) . By (5.1.18), the standard Laplacian comparison theorem (c.f. [112]) implies

\[
\Delta {\rho }^{2} = {2\rho \Delta \rho } + 2 \leq  2\left( {1 + {\varepsilon \rho }}\right)  + 2
\]

in the sense of distribution, where \( \rho \) is the distance function from \( {x}_{1} \) (with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) ). That is, for any \( \varphi  \in  {C}_{0}^{\infty }\left( M\right) ,\varphi  \geq  0 \) , we have

(5.1.21)

\[
- {\int }_{M}\nabla {\rho }^{2} \cdot  \nabla \varphi  \leq  {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {2\left( {1 + {\varepsilon \rho }}\right)  + 2}\right\rbrack  \varphi .
\]

Since \( {C}_{0}^{\infty }\left( M\right) \) functions can be approximated by Lipschitz functions in the above inequality, we can set \( \varphi \left( x\right)  = \psi \left( {\rho \left( x\right) }\right) , x \in  M \) , where \( \psi \left( s\right) \) is given by

\[
\psi \left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} 1, & 0 \leq  s \leq  {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - 1, \\  {\psi }^{\prime }\left( s\right)  =  - \frac{1}{2}, & {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - 1 \leq  s \leq  {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  + 1, \\  0, & s \geq  {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  + 1. \end{array}\right.
\]

Thus, by using (5.1.20), the left hand side of (5.1.21) is

\[
- {\int }_{M}\nabla {\rho }^{2} \cdot  \nabla \varphi
\]

\[
= {\int }_{{B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{1},{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  + 1}\right)  \smallsetminus  {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{1},{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - 1}\right) }\rho
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - 1}\right) {\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{1},{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  + 1}\right)  \smallsetminus  {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{1},{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - 1}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - 1}\right) {\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},1}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - 1}\right) {C}_{2},
\]

and the right hand side of (5.1.21) is

\[
{\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {2\left( {1 + {\varepsilon \rho }}\right)  + 2}\right\rbrack  \varphi  \leq  {\int }_{{B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{1},{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  + 1}\right) }\left\lbrack  {2\left( {1 + {\varepsilon \rho }}\right)  + 2}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\leq  \left\lbrack  {2\left( {1 + \varepsilon {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\right)  + 4}\right\rbrack  {\text{ Vol }}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{1},{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left\lbrack  {2\left( {1 + \varepsilon {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\right)  + 4}\right\rbrack  A
\]

where \( A \) is the area of \( M \) with respect to the initial metric. Here we have used the fact that the area of solution of the normalized Ricci flow is constant in time. Hence

\[
{C}_{2}\left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  - 1}\right)  \leq  \left\lbrack  {2\left( {1 + \varepsilon {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right) }\right)  + 4}\right\rbrack  A,
\]

which implies, by choosing \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) small enough,

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{1}}\right)  \leq  {C}_{3}
\]

for some positive constant \( {C}_{3} \) depending only on the initial metric. Therefore, the diameter of \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) is uniformly bounded above by

(5.1.22)

\[
\operatorname{diam}\left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right)  \leq  2{C}_{3}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, + \infty }\right) \) .

We then argue, as in deriving (5.1.19), by applying Lemma 5.1.6 again to obtain

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {C}_{4},\;\text{ on }\;M \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, + \infty }\right)
\]

for some positive constant \( {C}_{4} \) depending only on the initial metric.

It remains to prove a positive lower bound estimate of the curvature. First, we note that the function \( s\left( t\right)  \rightarrow  0 \) as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) , and the average scalar curvature of the solution equals to \( r \) , a positive constant. Thus the Harnack inequality in Lemma 5.1.6 and the diameter estimate (5.1.22) imply a positive lower bound for the curvature. Therefore we have completed the proof of Proposition 5.1.7. 0

(5.1.23)

\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\left| {M}_{ij}\right| }^{2} = \Delta {\left| {M}_{ij}\right| }^{2} - 2{\left| {\nabla }_{k}{M}_{ij}\right| }^{2} - {2R}{\left| {M}_{ij}\right| }^{2},\;\text{ on }M \times  \lbrack 0, + \infty ).

First we note the time-derivative of the Levi-Civita connection is

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\Gamma }_{ij}^{k} = \frac{1}{2}{g}^{kl}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{jl} + {\nabla }_{j}\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{il} - {\nabla }_{l}\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{g}_{ij}}\right)

\]

By using this and (5.1.4), we have

\[

\]

\]

\]

= \Delta {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\varphi  - {\nabla }^{k}\left( {{R}_{ikj}^{l}{\nabla }_{l}\varphi }\right)  - {R}_{ikj}^{l}{\nabla }_{l}{\nabla }^{k}\varphi
\]

\[
- {R}_{il}{\nabla }_{j}{\nabla }^{l}\varphi  - {R}_{jl}{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }^{l}\varphi  - {\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jl}{\nabla }^{l}\varphi
\]

\[
= \Delta {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\varphi  - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}R \cdot  {\nabla }_{j}\varphi  + {\nabla }_{j}R \cdot  {\nabla }_{i}\varphi -\langle \nabla R,\nabla \varphi \rangle {g}_{ij}}\right)

- {2R}\left( {{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\varphi  - \frac{1}{2}{\Delta \varphi } \cdot  {g}_{ij}}\right) .

\[

\]

Thus the evolution \( {M}_{ij} \) is given by

(5.1.24)

\[
\frac{\partial {M}_{ij}}{\partial t} = \Delta {M}_{ij} + \left( {r - {2R}}\right) {M}_{ij}.
\]

nodes.content: PROPOSITION 5.1.10. On a compact surface there are no shrinking Ricci solitons other than constant curvature.
nodes.content_excerpt: PROPOSITION 5.1.10. On a compact surface there are no shrinking Ricci solitons other than constant curvature.

nodes.proof:
By definition, a shrinking Ricci soliton on a compact surface \( M \) is given by

(5.1.26)

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{X}_{j} + {\nabla }_{j}{X}_{i} = \left( {R - r}\right) {g}_{ij}
\]

for some vector field \( X = {X}_{j} \) . By contracting the above equation by \( R{g}^{-1} \) , we have

\[
{2R}\left( {R - r}\right)  = {2R}\operatorname{div}X
\]

and hence

\[
{\int }_{M}{\left( R - r\right) }^{2}{dV} = {\int }_{M}R\left( {R - r}\right) {dV} = {\int }_{M}R\operatorname{div}{XdV}.
\]

Since \( X \) is a conformal vector field (by the Ricci soliton equation (5.1.26)), by integrating by parts and applying the Kazdan-Warner identity [77], we obtain

\[
{\int }_{M}{\left( R - r\right) }^{2}{dV} =  - {\int }_{M}\langle \nabla R, X\rangle {dV} = 0.
\]

Hence \( R \equiv  r \) , and the lemma is proved. \( \square \)

nodes.content: THEOREM 5.2.1 (Hamilton [58]). A compact three-manifold with positive Ricci curvature must be diffeomorphic to the three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or a quotient of it by a finite group of fixed point free isometries in the standard metric.
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 5.2.1 (Hamilton [58]). A compact three-manifold with positive Ricci curvature must be diffeomorphic to the three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or a quotient of it by a finite group of fixed point free isometries in the standard metric.

nodes.proof:
Proof of Theorem 5.2.1. Let \( M \) be a compact three-manifold with positive Ricci curvature and let the metric evolve by the Ricci flow. By Lemma 5.2.4 we know that there exists a positive constant \( \beta  > 0 \) such that

\[
{R}_{ij} \geq  {\beta R}{g}_{ij}
\]

for all \( t \geq  0 \) as long as the solution exists. The scalar curvature evolves by

\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial t} = {\Delta R} + 2{\left| {R}_{ij}\right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  {\Delta R} + \frac{2}{3}{R}^{2}
\]

which implies, by the maximum principle, that the scalar curvature remains positive and tends to +0 in finite time.

We now use a blow up argument as in Section 4.3 to get the following gradient estimate.

CLAIM. For any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exists a positive constant \( {C}_{\varepsilon } <  + \infty \) such that for any time \( \tau  \geq  0 \) , we have

\[
\mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  \tau }}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {\nabla {Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \varepsilon \mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  \tau }}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}{\left| Rm\left( x, t\right) \right| }^{\frac{3}{2}} + {C}_{\varepsilon }.
\]

We argue by contradiction. Suppose the above gradient estimate fails for some fixed \( {\varepsilon }_{0} > 0 \) . Pick a sequence \( {C}_{j} \rightarrow   + \infty \) , and pick points \( {x}_{j} \in  M \) and times \( {\tau }_{j} \) such that

\[
\left| {\nabla \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{j},{\tau }_{j}}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\varepsilon }_{0}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  {\tau }_{j}}}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( x, t\right) \right| }^{\frac{3}{2}} + {C}_{j},\;j = 1,2,\ldots
\]

Choose \( {x}_{j} \) to be the origin, and pull the metric back to a small ball on the tangent space \( {T}_{{x}_{j}}M \) of radius \( {r}_{j} \) proportional to the reciprocal of the square root of the maximum curvature up to time \( {\tau }_{j} \) (i.e., \( \mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  {\tau }_{j}}}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right| \) ). Clearly the maximum curvatures go to infinity by Shi's derivative estimate of curvature (Theorem 1.4.1). Dilate the metrics so that the maximum curvature

\[
\mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  {\tau }_{j}}}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|
\]

becomes 1 and translate time so that \( {\tau }_{j} \) becomes the time 0 . By Theorem 4.1.5, we can take a (local) limit. The limit metric satisfies

\[
\left| {\nabla \operatorname{Rm}\left( {0,0}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\varepsilon }_{0} > 0.
\]

However the pinching estimate in Proposition 5.2.5 tells us the limit metric has

\[
{R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{3}R{g}_{ij} \equiv  0.
\]

By using the contracted second Bianchi identity

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{i}R = {\nabla }^{j}{R}_{ij} = {\nabla }^{j}\left( {{R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{3}R{g}_{ij}}\right)  + \frac{1}{3}{\nabla }_{i}R,
\]

we get

\[
{\nabla }_{i}R \equiv  0\;\text{ and then }\;{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jk} \equiv  0.
\]

For a three-manifold, this in turn implies

\[
\nabla {Rm} = 0
\]

which is a contradiction. Hence we have proved the gradient estimate claimed.

We can now show that the solution to the Ricci flow becomes round as the time \( t \) tends to the maximal time \( T \) . We have seen that the scalar curvature goes to infinity in finite time. Pick a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  M \) and times \( {\tau }_{j} \) where the curvature at \( {x}_{j} \) is as large as it has been anywhere for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  {\tau }_{j} \) and \( {\tau }_{j} \) tends to the maximal time. Since \( \left| {\nabla {Rm}}\right| \) is very small compared to \( \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{j},{\tau }_{j}}\right) }\right| \) by the above gradient estimate and \( \left| {{R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{3}R{g}_{ij}}\right| \) is also very small compared to \( \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{j},{\tau }_{j}}\right) }\right| \) by Proposition 5.2.5, the curvature is nearly constant and positive in a large ball around \( {x}_{j} \) at the time \( {\tau }_{j} \) . But then the Bonnet-Myers’ theorem tells us this is the whole manifold. For \( j \) large enough, the sectional curvature of the solution at the time \( {\tau }_{j} \) is sufficiently pinched. Then it follows from the Klingenberg injectivity radius estimate (see Section 4.2) that the injectivity radius of the metric at time \( {\tau }_{j} \) is bounded from below by \( c/\sqrt{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{j},{\tau }_{j}\right) \right| } \) for some positive constant \( c \) independent of \( j \) . Dilate the metrics so that the maximum curvature \( \left| {{Rm}\left( {{x}_{j},{\tau }_{j}}\right) }\right|  = \mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  {\tau }_{j}}}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right| \) becomes 1 and shift the time \( {\tau }_{j} \) to the new time 0 . Then we can apply Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5) to take a limit. By the pinching estimate in Proposition 5.2.5, we know that the limit has positive constant curvature which is either the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or a metric quotient of the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) . Consequently, the compact three-manifold \( M \) is diffeomorphic to the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or a metric quotient of the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) . 0

Again the evolution equation of the scalar curvature tells us that the scalar curvature remains positive and becomes unbounded in finite time. Pick a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \in  M \) and times \( {\tau }_{j} \) where the curvature at \( {x}_{j} \) is as large as it has been anywhere for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  {\tau }_{j} \) . The Klin-genberg injectivity radius estimate in Section 4.2 tells us that the injectivity radii of the rescaled metrics at the origins \( {x}_{j} \) and at the new time 0 are uniformly bounded from below. Then we can apply the Hamilton's compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5) to take a limit. By the pinching estimate in Corollary 5.2.7, we know that the limit metric has positive constant curvature which is either \( {\mathbb{S}}^{4} \) or \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{4} \) . Therefore the compact four-manifold \( M \) is diffeomorphic to the sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{4} \) or the real projective space \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{4} \) . 0

nodes.proof:
Proof of Theorem 5.2.3. In views of Theorem 5.2.1 and Theorem 5.2.2, we may assume the Ricci curvature (in dimension 3) and the curvature operator (in dimension 4) always have nontrivial kernels somewhere along the Ricci flow.

(i) In the case of dimension 3, we consider the evolution equation (1.3.5) of the Ricci curvature

\[
\frac{\partial {R}_{ab}}{\partial t} = \bigtriangleup {R}_{ab} + 2{R}_{acbd}{R}_{cd}
\]

in an orthonormal frame coordinate. At each point, we diagonalize \( {R}_{ab} \) with eigenvectors \( {e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3} \) and eigenvalues \( {\lambda }_{1} \leq  {\lambda }_{2} \leq  {\lambda }_{3} \) . Since

\[
{R}_{1c1d}{R}_{cd} = {R}_{1212}{R}_{22} + {R}_{1313}{R}_{33}
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\left( {\lambda }_{3} - {\lambda }_{2}\right) }^{2} + {\lambda }_{1}\left( {{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{3}}\right) }\right) ,
\]

we know that if \( {R}_{ab} \geq  0 \) , then \( {R}_{acbd}{R}_{cd} \geq  0 \) . By Hamilton’s strong maximum principle (Theorem 2.2.1), there exists an interval \( 0 < t < \delta \) on which the rank of \( {R}_{ab} \) is constant and the null space of \( {R}_{ab} \) is invariant under parallel translation and invariant in time and also lies in the null space of \( {R}_{acbd}{R}_{cd} \) . If the null space of \( {R}_{ab} \) has rank one, then \( {\lambda }_{1} = 0 \) and \( {\lambda }_{2} = {\lambda }_{3} > 0 \) . In this case, by De Rham decomposition theorem, the universal cover \( M \) of the compact \( M \) splits isometrically as \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\sum }^{2} \) and the curvature of \( {\sum }^{2} \) has a positive lower bound. Hence \( {\sum }^{2} \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) . Assume \( M = \mathbb{R} \times  {\sum }^{2}/\Gamma \) , for some isometric subgroup \( \Gamma \) of \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\sum }^{2} \) . Note that \( \Gamma \) remains to be an isometric subgroup of \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\sum }^{2} \) during the Ricci flow by the uniqueness (Theorem 1.2.4). Since the Ricci flow on \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\sum }^{2}/\Gamma \) converges to the standard metric by Theorem 5.1.11, \( \Gamma \) must be an isometric subgroup of \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) in the standard metric. If the null space of \( {R}_{ab} \) has rank greater than one, then \( {R}_{ab} = 0 \) and the manifold is flat. This proves Theorem 5.2.3 part (i).

(ii) In the case of dimension 4, we classify the manifolds according to the (restricted) holonomy algebra \( \mathcal{G} \) . Note that the curvature operator has nontrivial kernel and \( \mathcal{G} \) is the image of the the curvature operator, we see that \( \mathcal{G} \) is a proper subalgebra of \( {so}\left( 4\right) \) . We divide the argument into two cases.

Case 1. \( \mathcal{G} \) is reducible.

In this case the universal cover \( \widetilde{M} \) splits isometrically as \( {\widetilde{M}}_{1} \times  {\widetilde{M}}_{2} \) . By the above results on two and three dimensional Ricci flow, we see that \( M \) is diffeomorphic to a quotient of one of the spaces \( {\mathbb{R}}^{4},\mathbb{R} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{3},{\mathbb{R}}^{2} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{2},{\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) by a group of fixed point free isometries. As before by running the Ricci flow until it converges and using the uniqueness (Theorem 1.2.4), we see that this group is actually a subgroup of the isometries in the standard metrics.

Case 2. \( \mathcal{G} \) is not reducible (i.e., irreducible).

If the manifold is not Einstein, then by Berger's classification theorem for holonomy groups [7], \( \mathcal{G} = {so}\left( 4\right) \) or \( u\left( 2\right) \) . Since the curvature operator is not strictly positive, \( \mathcal{G} = u\left( 2\right) \) , and the universal cover \( \widetilde{M} \) of \( M \) is Kähler and has positive bisectional curvature. In this case \( \widetilde{M} \) is biholomorphic to \( {\mathbb{{CP}}}^{2} \) by the result of Andreotti-Frankel [47] (also the resolution of the Frankel conjecture by Mori [96] and Siu-Yau [120]).

If the manifold is Einstein, then by the block decomposition of the curvature operator matrix in four-manifolds (see the third section of Chapter 1),

\[
\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\Lambda }_{ + }^{2},{\Lambda }_{ - }^{2}}\right)  = 0.
\]

Let \( \varphi  \neq  0 \) , and

\[
\varphi  = {\varphi }_{ + } + {\varphi }_{ - } \in  {\Lambda }_{ + }^{2} \oplus  {\Lambda }_{ - }^{2},
\]

lies in the kernel of the curvature operator, then

\[
0 = {Rm}\left( {{\varphi }_{ + },{\varphi }_{ + }}\right)  + {Rm}\left( {{\varphi }_{ - },{\varphi }_{ - }}\right) .
\]

It follows that

\[
\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\varphi }_{ + },{\varphi }_{ + }}\right)  = 0\text{ , and }\operatorname{Rm}\left( {{\varphi }_{ - },{\varphi }_{ - }}\right)  = 0\text{ . }
\]

We may assume \( {\varphi }_{ + } \neq  0 \) (the argument for the other case is similar). We consider the restriction of \( {Rm} \) to \( {\Lambda }_{ + }^{2} \) , since \( {\Lambda }_{ + }^{2} \) is an invariant subspace of \( {Rm} \) and the intersection of \( {\Lambda }_{ + }^{2} \) with the null space of \( {Rm} \) is nontrivial. By considering the null space of \( {Rm} \) and its orthogonal complement in \( {\Lambda }_{ + }^{2} \) , we obtain a parallel distribution of rank one in \( {\Lambda }_{ + }^{2} \) . This parallel distribution gives a parallel translation invariant two-form \( \omega  \in  {\Lambda }_{ + }^{2} \) on the universal cover \( \widetilde{M} \) of \( M \) . This two-form is nondegenerate, so it induces a Kähler structure of \( \widetilde{M} \) . Since the Kähler metric is parallel with respect to the original metric and the manifold is irreducible, the Kähler metric is proportional to the original metric. Hence the manifold \( \widetilde{M} \) is Kähler-Einstein with nonnegative curvature operator. Taking into account the irreducibility of \( \mathcal{G} \) , it follows that \( \widetilde{M} \) is biholomorphic to \( {\mathbb{{CP}}}^{2} \) . Therefore the proof of Theorem 5.2.3 is completed. D

nodes.proof:
Proof. If we diagonalize the \( 3 \times  3 \) curvature operator matrix \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) with eigenvalues \( \lambda  \geq  \mu  \geq  \nu \) , then nonnegative sectional curvature corresponds to \( \nu  \geq  0 \) and nonnegative Ricci curvature corresponds to the inequality \( \mu  + \nu  \geq  0 \) . Also, the scalar curvature \( R = \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \) . So we need to show

\[
\mu  + \nu  \geq  0\text{ and }\mu  + \nu  \geq  {\delta \lambda },\text{ with }\delta  = {2\varepsilon }/\left( {1 - {2\varepsilon }}\right) ,
\]

are preserved by the Ricci flow. By Hamilton's advanced maximum principle (Theorem 2.3.1), it suffices to show that the closed convex set

\[
K = \left\{  {{M}_{\alpha \beta } \mid  \mu  + \nu  \geq  0\text{ and }\mu  + \nu  \geq  {\delta \lambda }}\right\}
\]

is preserved by the ODE system (5.2.2).

Now suppose we have diagonalized \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) with eigenvalues \( \lambda  \geq  \mu  \geq  \nu \) at \( t = 0 \) , then both \( {M}_{\alpha \beta }^{2} \) and \( {M}_{\alpha \beta }^{\# } \) are diagonal, so the matrix \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) remains diagonal for \( t > 0 \) . Moreover, since

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\mu  - \nu }\right)  = \left( {\mu  - \nu }\right) \left( {\mu  + \nu  - \lambda }\right) ,
\]

it is clear that \( \mu  \geq  \nu \) for \( t > 0 \) also. Similarly, we have \( \lambda  \geq  \mu \) for \( t > 0 \) . Hence the inequalities \( \lambda  \geq  \mu  \geq  \nu \) persist. This says that the solutions of the ODE system (5.2.2) agree with the original choice for the eigenvalues of the curvature operator.

The condition \( \mu  + \nu  \geq  0 \) is clearly preserved by the ODE, because

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\mu  + \nu }\right)  = {\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2} + \lambda \left( {\mu  + \nu }\right)  \geq  0.
\]

It remains to check

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\mu  + \nu }\right)  \geq  \delta \frac{d}{dt}\lambda
\]

or

\[
{\mu }^{2} + {\lambda \nu } + {\nu }^{2} + {\lambda \mu } \geq  \delta \left( {{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu \nu }}\right)
\]

on the boundary where

\[
\mu  + \nu  = {\delta \lambda } \geq  0.
\]

In fact, since

\[
\left( {\lambda  - \nu }\right) {\mu }^{2} + \left( {\lambda  - \mu }\right) {\nu }^{2} \geq  0,
\]

we have

\[
\lambda \left( {{\mu }^{2} + {\nu }^{2}}\right)  \geq  \left( {\mu  + \nu }\right) {\mu \nu }
\]

Hence

\[
{\mu }^{2} + {\mu \lambda } + {\nu }^{2} + {\nu \lambda } \geq  \left( \frac{\mu  + \nu }{\lambda }\right) \left( {{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu \nu }}\right)
\]

\[
= \delta \left( {{\lambda }^{2} + {\mu \nu }}\right) .
\]

So we get the desired pinching estimate.

nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 5.2.5. Suppose that the initial metric of the solution to the Ricci flow on \( {M}^{3} \times \lbrack 0, T) \) has positive Ricci curvature. Then for any \( \varepsilon > 0 \) we can find \( {C}_{\varepsilon } < + \infty \) such that \[ \left| {{R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{3}R{g}_{ij}}\right| \leq {\varepsilon R} + {C}_{\varepsilon } \] for all subsequent \( t \in \lbrack 0, T) \) .

nodes.proof:
Proof. Again we consider the ODE system (5.2.2). Let \( {M}_{\alpha \beta } \) be diagonalized with eigenvalues \( \lambda  \geq  \mu  \geq  \nu \) at \( t = 0 \) . We saw in the proof of Lemma 5.2.4 the inequalities \( \lambda  \geq  \mu  \geq  \nu \) persist for \( t > 0 \) . We only need to show that there are positive constants \( \delta \) and \( C \) such that the closed convex set

\[
K = \left\{  {{M}_{\alpha \beta } \mid  \lambda  - \nu  \leq  C{\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \right) }^{1 - \delta }}\right\}
\]

is preserved by the ODE.

We compute

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\lambda  - \nu }\right)  = \left( {\lambda  - \nu }\right) \left( {\lambda  + \nu  - \mu }\right)
\]

and

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right)  = \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \left( {\lambda  + \nu  - \mu }\right)  + {\mu }^{2}
\]

\[
+ \mu \left( {\mu  + \nu }\right)  + \lambda \left( {\mu  - \nu }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right) \left( {\lambda  + \nu  - \mu }\right)  + {\mu }^{2}.
\]

Thus, without loss of generality, we may assume \( \lambda  - \nu  > 0 \) and get

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\log \left( {\lambda  - \nu }\right)  = \lambda  + \nu  - \mu
\]

and

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\log \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right)  \geq  \lambda  + \nu  - \mu  + \frac{{\mu }^{2}}{\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }.
\]

By Lemma 5.2.4, there exists a positive constant \( C \) depending only on the initial metric such that

\[
\lambda  \leq  \lambda  + \mu  \leq  C\left( {\mu  + \nu }\right)  \leq  {2C\mu }
\]

\[
\lambda  + \nu  - \mu  \leq  \lambda  + \mu  + \nu  \leq  {6C\mu }
\]

and hence with \( \epsilon  = 1/{36}{C}^{2} \) ,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\log \left( {\lambda  + \mu  + \nu }\right)  \geq  \left( {1 + \epsilon }\right) \left( {\lambda  + \nu  - \mu }\right) .
\]

Therefore with \( \left( {1 - \delta }\right)  = 1/\left( {1 + \epsilon }\right) \) ,

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\log \left( {\left( {\lambda  - \nu }\right) /{\left( \lambda  + \mu  + \nu \right) }^{1 - \delta }}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

This proves the proposition.

\[
\mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  \tau }}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {\nabla {Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \varepsilon \mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  \tau }}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}{\left| Rm\left( x, t\right) \right| }^{\frac{3}{2}} + {C}_{\varepsilon }.
\]

nodes.proof:
We argue by contradiction. Suppose the above gradient estimate fails for some fixed \( {\varepsilon }_{0} > 0 \) . Pick a sequence \( {C}_{j} \rightarrow   + \infty \) , and pick points \( {x}_{j} \in  M \) and times \( {\tau }_{j} \) such that

\[
\left| {\nabla \operatorname{Rm}\left( {{x}_{j},{\tau }_{j}}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\varepsilon }_{0}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  {\tau }_{j}}}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( x, t\right) \right| }^{\frac{3}{2}} + {C}_{j},\;j = 1,2,\ldots
\]

Choose \( {x}_{j} \) to be the origin, and pull the metric back to a small ball on the tangent space \( {T}_{{x}_{j}}M \) of radius \( {r}_{j} \) proportional to the reciprocal of the square root of the maximum curvature up to time \( {\tau }_{j} \) (i.e., \( \mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  {\tau }_{j}}}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right| \) ). Clearly the maximum curvatures go to infinity by Shi's derivative estimate of curvature (Theorem 1.4.1). Dilate the metrics so that the maximum curvature

\[
\mathop{\max }\limits_{{t \leq  {\tau }_{j}}}\mathop{\max }\limits_{{x \in  M}}\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|
\]

becomes 1 and translate time so that \( {\tau }_{j} \) becomes the time 0 . By Theorem 4.1.5, we can take a (local) limit. The limit metric satisfies

\[
\left| {\nabla \operatorname{Rm}\left( {0,0}\right) }\right|  \geq  {\varepsilon }_{0} > 0.
\]

However the pinching estimate in Proposition 5.2.5 tells us the limit metric has

\[
{R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{3}R{g}_{ij} \equiv  0.
\]

By using the contracted second Bianchi identity

\[
\frac{1}{2}{\nabla }_{i}R = {\nabla }^{j}{R}_{ij} = {\nabla }^{j}\left( {{R}_{ij} - \frac{1}{3}R{g}_{ij}}\right)  + \frac{1}{3}{\nabla }_{i}R,
\]

we get

\[
{\nabla }_{i}R \equiv  0\;\text{ and then }\;{\nabla }_{i}{R}_{jk} \equiv  0.
\]

For a three-manifold, this in turn implies

\[
\nabla {Rm} = 0
\]

which is a contradiction. Hence we have proved the gradient estimate claimed.
