nodes.proof:
First we claim that \( \mathcal{H} \) is isometric to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) for an appropriate choice of compact set \( \mathcal{K} \) , positive integer \( q \) and positive number \( \delta \) . Let \( l : \mathcal{H} \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) be a function defined at each point by the length of the shortest non-contractible loop starting and ending at this point. Denote the Margulis constant by \( \mu \) . Then by Margulis lemma (see for example [55] or [76]), for any \( 0 < {\varepsilon }_{0} < \frac{1}{2}\mu \) , the set \( {l}^{-1}\left( \left\lbrack  {0,{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right\rbrack  \right)  \subset  \mathcal{H} \) consists of finitely many components and each of these components is isometric to a cusp or to a tube. Topologically, a tube is just a solid torus. Let \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \) be even smaller than one half of the minimum of the lengths of the all closed geodesics on the tubes. Then \( {l}^{-1}\left( \left\lbrack  {0,{\varepsilon }_{0}}\right\rbrack  \right) \) consists of finite number of cusps. Set \( {\mathcal{K}}_{0} = {l}^{-1}\left( \left\lbrack  {{\varepsilon }_{0},\infty }\right) \right) \) . The boundary of \( {\mathcal{K}}_{0} \) consists of flat tori with constant mean curvatures. Note that each embedded torus in a complete hyperbolic three-manifold with finite volume either bounds a solid torus or is isotopic to a standard torus in a cusp. The diffeomorphism \( F \) implies the boundary \( F\left( {\partial {\mathcal{K}}_{0}}\right) \) are embedded tori. If one of components bounds a solid torus, then as \( \delta \) sufficiently small and \( q \) sufficiently large, \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) would have fewer cusps than \( \mathcal{H} \) , which contradicts with our assumption. Consequently, \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) is diffeomorphic to \( F\left( {\mathcal{K}}_{0}\right) \) . Here \( {\mathcal{K}}_{0} \) is the interior of the set \( {\mathcal{K}}_{0} \) . Since \( \mathcal{H} \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathcal{K}}_{0},\mathcal{H} \) is diffeomorphic to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) . Hence by Mostow’s rigidity theorem (see [97] and [107]), \( \mathcal{H} \) is isometric to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) .

So we can assume \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} = \mathcal{H} \) . For \( \mathcal{K} = {\mathcal{K}}_{0} \) , we argue by contradiction. Suppose there is some \( k > 0 \) and \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) so that there exist sequences of integers \( {q}_{j} \rightarrow  \infty ,{\delta }_{j} \rightarrow  {0}^{ + } \) and diffeomorphisms \( {F}_{j} \) mapping \( \mathcal{K} \) into \( \mathcal{H} \) with

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{F}_{j}^{ * }h - h\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{{q}_{j}}\left( \mathcal{K}\right) } < {\delta }_{j}
\]

and

\[
{d}_{{C}^{k}\left( \mathcal{K}\right) }\left( {{F}_{j}, I}\right)  \geq  \varepsilon
\]

for all isometries \( I \) of \( \mathcal{H} \) to itself. We can extract a subsequence of \( {F}_{j} \) convergent to a map \( {F}_{\infty } \) with \( {F}_{\infty }^{ * }h = h \) on \( \mathcal{K} \) .

We need to check that \( {F}_{\infty } \) is still a diffeomorphism on \( \mathcal{K} \) . Since \( {F}_{\infty } \) is a local diffeomorphism and is the limit of diffeomorphisms, we can find an inverse of \( {F}_{\infty } \) on \( {F}_{\infty }\left( \mathcal{K}\right) \) . So \( {F}_{\infty } \) is a diffeomorphism on \( \mathcal{K} \) . We claim the image of the boundary can not touch the image of the interior. Indeed, if \( {F}_{\infty }\left( {x}_{1}\right)  = {F}_{\infty }\left( {x}_{2}\right) \) with \( {x}_{1} \in  \partial \mathcal{K} \) and \( {x}_{2} \in  \overset{o}{\mathcal{K}} \) , then we can find \( {x}_{3} \in  \overset{o}{\mathcal{K}} \) near \( {x}_{1} \) and \( {x}_{4} \in  \overset{o}{\mathcal{K}} \) near \( {x}_{2} \) with \( {F}_{\infty }\left( {x}_{3}\right)  = {F}_{\infty }\left( {x}_{4}\right) \) , since \( {F}_{\infty } \) is a local diffeomorphism. This contradicts with the fact that \( {F}_{\infty } \) is a diffeomorphism on \( \mathcal{K} \) . This proves our claim. Hence, the only possible overlap is at the boundary. But the image \( {F}_{\infty }\left( {\partial \mathcal{K}}\right) \) is strictly concave, this prevents the boundary from touching itself. We conclude that the mapping \( {F}_{\infty } \) is a diffeomorphism on \( \mathcal{K} \) , hence an isometry.

To extend \( {F}_{\infty } \) to a global isometry, we argue as follows. For each truncated cusp end of \( \mathcal{K} \) , the area of constant mean curvature flat torus is strictly decreasing. Since \( {F}_{\infty } \) takes each such torus to another of the same area, we see that \( {F}_{\infty } \) takes the foliation of an end by constant mean curvature flat tori to another such foliation. So \( {F}_{\infty } \) takes cusps to cusps and preserves their foliations. Note that the isometric type of a cusp is just the isometric type of the torus, more precisely, let \( \left( {N, d{r}^{2} + {e}^{-{2r}}{g}_{\mathcal{V}}}\right) \) be a cusp (where \( {g}_{\mathcal{V}} \) is the flat metric on the torus \( \mathcal{V} \) ), \( 0 < a < b \) are two constants, any isometry of \( N \cap  {l}^{-1}\left\lbrack  {a, b}\right\rbrack \) to itself is just an isometry of \( \mathcal{V} \) . Hence the isometry \( {F}_{\infty } \) can be extended to the whole cusps. This gives a global isometry \( I \) contradicting our assumption when \( j \) large enough.

The proof of the Lemma 5.3.7 is completed. [

LEMMA 5.3.8. Let \( \left( {X, g}\right) \) be a compact Riemannian manifold with strictly negative Ricci curvature and with strictly concave boundary. Then there are positive integer \( {l}_{0} \) and small number \( {\varepsilon }_{0} > 0 \) such that for each positive integer \( l \geq  {l}_{0} \) and positive number \( \varepsilon  \leq  {\varepsilon }_{0} \) we can find positive integer \( q \) and positive number \( \delta  > 0 \) such that for every metric \( \widetilde{g} \) on \( X \) with \( {\begin{Vmatrix}\widetilde{g} - g\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( X\right) } \leq  \delta \) we can find a unique diffeomorphism \( F \) of \( X \) to itself so that

(a) \( F : \left( {X, g}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {X,\widetilde{g}}\right) \) is harmonic,

(b) \( F \) takes the boundary \( \partial X \) to itself and satisfies the free boundary condition that the normal derivative \( {\nabla }_{N}F \) of \( F \) at the boundary is normal to the boundary,

(c) \( {d}_{{C}^{l}\left( X\right) }\left( {F,{Id}}\right)  < \varepsilon \) , where \( {Id} \) is the identity map.

nodes.proof:
Let \( \Phi \left( {X,\partial X}\right) \) be the space of maps of \( X \) to itself which take \( \partial X \) to itself. Then \( \Phi \left( {X,\partial X}\right) \) is a Banach manifold and the tangent space to \( \Phi \left( {X,\partial X}\right) \) at the identity is the space of vector fields \( V = {V}^{i}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}} \) tangent to the boundary. Consider the map sending \( F \in  \Phi \left( {X,\partial X}\right) \) to the pair \( \left\{  {{\Delta F},{\left( {\nabla }_{N}F\right) }_{//}}\right\} \) consisting of the harmonic map Laplacian and the tangential component (in the target) of the normal derivative of \( F \) at the boundary. By using the inverse function theorem, we only need to check that the derivative of this map is an isomorphism at the identity with \( \widetilde{g} = g \) .

Let \( {\left\{  {x}^{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1,\ldots , n} \) be a local coordinates of \( \left( {X, g}\right) \) and \( {\left\{  {y}^{\alpha }\right\}  }_{\alpha  = 1,\ldots , n} \) be a local coordinates of \( \left( {X,\widetilde{g}}\right) \) . The harmonic map Laplacian of \( F : \left( {X, g}\right)  \rightarrow  \left( {X,\widetilde{g}}\right) \) is given in local coordinates by

\[
{\left( \Delta F\right) }^{\alpha } = \Delta \left( {F}^{\alpha }\right)  + {g}^{ij}\left( {{\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\beta \gamma }^{\alpha } \circ  F}\right) \frac{\partial {F}^{\beta }}{\partial {x}^{i}}\frac{\partial {F}^{\gamma }}{\partial {x}^{j}}
\]

where \( \Delta \left( {F}^{\alpha }\right) \) is the Laplacian of the function \( {F}^{\alpha } \) on \( X \) and \( {\widetilde{\Gamma }}_{\beta \gamma }^{\alpha } \) is the connection of \( \widetilde{g} \) . Let \( F \) be a one-parameter family with \( {\left. F\right| }_{s = 0} = {Id} \) and \( {\left. \frac{dF}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0} = V \) , a smooth vector field on \( X \) tangent to the boundary (with respect to \( g \) ). At an arbitrary given point \( x \in  X \) , we choose the coordinates \( {\left\{  {x}^{i}\right\}  }_{i = 1,\ldots , n} \) so that \( {\Gamma }_{jk}^{i}\left( x\right)  = 0 \) . We compute at the point \( x \) with \( \widetilde{g} = g \) ,

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}{\left( \Delta F\right) }^{\alpha } = \Delta \left( {V}^{\alpha }\right)  + {g}^{ij}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{k}}{\Gamma }_{ij}^{\alpha }}\right) {V}^{k}.
\]

Since

\[
{\left( {\nabla }_{i}V\right) }^{\alpha } = {\nabla }_{i}{V}^{\alpha } + \left( {{\Gamma }_{i\beta }^{\alpha } \circ  F}\right) {V}^{\beta },
\]

we have, at \( s = 0 \) and the point \( x \) ,

\[
{\left( \Delta V\right) }^{\alpha } = \Delta \left( {V}^{\alpha }\right)  + {g}^{ij}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}{\Gamma }_{jk}^{\alpha }{V}^{k}.
\]

Thus we obtain

(5.3.5)

\[
\frac{d}{ds}{ \mid  }_{s = 0}{\left( \Delta F\right) }^{\alpha } = {\left( \Delta V\right) }^{\alpha } + {g}^{ij}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{k}}{\Gamma }_{ij}^{\alpha } - \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}{\Gamma }_{jk}^{\alpha }}\right) {V}^{k}
\]

\[
= {\left( \Delta V\right) }^{\alpha } + {g}^{\alpha i}{R}_{ik}{V}^{k}.
\]

Since

\[
\left( {{\nabla }_{N}F}\right) \left( {{F}^{-1}\left( x\right) }\right)  = {N}^{i}\left( {{F}^{-1}\left( x\right) }\right) \frac{\partial {F}^{j}}{\partial {x}^{i}}\left( {{F}^{-1}\left( x\right) }\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\left( x\right) \;\text{ on }\partial X,
\]

we have

(5.3.6)

\[
{\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\left\{  {\left( {\nabla }_{N}F\right) }_{//}\right\}   = {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\left( {{\nabla }_{N}F-\langle {\nabla }_{N}F, N\rangle N}\right)
\]

\[
= {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}\left( {{\nabla }_{N}F}\right)  - \left\langle  {{\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}{\nabla }_{N}F, N}\right\rangle  N
\]

\[
- {\left. \left\langle  {\nabla }_{N}F,{\nabla }_{V}N\right\rangle  N\right| }_{s = 0} - {\left. \left\langle  {\nabla }_{N}F, N\right\rangle  {\nabla }_{V}N\right| }_{s = 0}
\]

\[
= {\left( {\left. \frac{d}{ds}\right| }_{s = 0}{\nabla }_{N}F\right) }_{//} - {\nabla }_{V}N
\]

\[
= {\left( -V\left( {N}^{i}\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}} + N\left( {V}^{j}\right) \frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{j}}\right) }_{//} - {II}\left( V\right)
\]

\[
= {\left\lbrack  N, V\right\rbrack  }_{//} - {II}\left( V\right)
\]

\[
= {\left( {\nabla }_{N}V\right) }_{//} - {2II}\left( V\right)
\]

where \( {II} \) is the second fundamental form of the boundary (as an automorphism of \( T\left( {\partial X}\right) ) \) . Thus by (5.3.5) and (5.3.6), the kernel of the map sending \( F \in  \Phi \left( {X,\partial X}\right) \) to the pair \( \left\{  {{\Delta F},{\left( {\nabla }_{N}F\right) }_{//}}\right\} \) is the space of solutions of elliptic boundary value problem

(5.3.7)

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{ll} {\Delta V} + \operatorname{Ric}\left( V\right)  = 0 & \text{ on }X \\  {V}_{ \bot  } = 0, & \text{ at }\partial X, \\  {\left( {\nabla }_{N}V\right) }_{//} - {2II}\left( V\right)  = 0, & \text{ at }\partial X, \end{array}\right.
\]

where \( {V}_{ \bot  } \) is the normal component of \( V \) .

Now using these equations and integrating by parts gives

\[
{\int }_{X}{\left| \nabla V\right| }^{2} = {\iint }_{X}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {V, V}\right)  + 2{\int }_{\partial X}{II}\left( {V, V}\right) .
\]

Since \( {Rc} < 0 \) and \( {II} < 0 \) we conclude that the kernel is trivial. Clearly this elliptic boundary value is self-adjoint because of the free boundary condition. Thus the cokernel is trivial also. This proves the lemma.

nodes.proof:
We argue by contradiction. Suppose there exist a sequence of positive constants \( {\varepsilon }^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) and a sequence of \( n \) -dimensional complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds \( \left( {{M}^{\alpha },{g}_{ij}^{\alpha }}\right) \) such that for each fixed \( \alpha \) , there exists a sequence of \( {\varepsilon }^{\alpha } \) -necks \( {N}_{k} \) of radius at most \( 1/k \) in \( {M}^{\alpha } \) with centers \( {P}_{k} \) divergent to infinity.

Fix a point \( P \) on the manifold \( {M}^{\alpha } \) and connect each \( {P}_{k} \) to \( P \) by a minimizing geodesic \( {\gamma }_{k} \) . By passing to a subsequence we may assume the angle \( {\theta }_{kl} \) between geodesic \( {\gamma }_{k} \) and \( {\gamma }_{l} \) at \( P \) is very small and tends to zero as \( k, l \rightarrow   + \infty \) , and the length of \( {\gamma }_{k + 1} \) is much bigger than the length of \( {\gamma }_{k} \) . Let us connect \( {P}_{k} \) to \( {P}_{l} \) by a minimizing geodesic \( {\eta }_{kl} \) . For each fixed \( l > k \) , let \( {\widetilde{P}}_{k} \) be a point on the geodesic \( {\gamma }_{l} \) such that the geodesic segment from \( P \) to \( {\widetilde{P}}_{k} \) has the same length as \( {\gamma }_{k} \) and consider the triangle \( {\Delta P}{P}_{k}{\widetilde{P}}_{k} \) in \( {M}^{\alpha } \) with vertices \( P,{P}_{k} \) and \( {\widetilde{P}}_{k} \) . By comparing with the corresponding triangle in the Euclidean plane \( {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) whose sides have the same corresponding lengths, Toponogov's comparison theorem implies

\[
d\left( {{P}_{k},{\widetilde{P}}_{k}}\right)  \leq  2\sin \left( {\frac{1}{2}{\theta }_{kl}}\right)  \cdot  d\left( {{P}_{k}, P}\right) .
\]

Since \( {\theta }_{kl} \) is very small, the distance from \( {P}_{k} \) to the geodesic \( {\gamma }_{l} \) can be realized by a geodesic \( {\zeta }_{kl} \) which connects \( {P}_{k} \) to a point \( {P}_{k}^{\prime } \) on the interior of the geodesic \( {\gamma }_{l} \) and has length at most \( 2\sin \left( {\frac{1}{2}{\theta }_{kl}}\right)  \cdot  d\left( {{P}_{k}, P}\right) \) . Clearly the angle between \( {\zeta }_{kl} \) and \( {\gamma }_{l} \) at the intersection point \( {P}_{k}^{\prime } \) is \( \frac{\widetilde{\pi }}{2} \) . Consider \( \alpha \) to be fixed and sufficiently large. We claim that for large enough \( k \) , each minimizing geodesic \( {\gamma }_{l} \) with \( l > k \) , connecting \( P \) to \( {P}_{l} \) , goes through the neck \( {N}_{k} \) .

Suppose not; then the angle between \( {\gamma }_{k} \) and \( {\zeta }_{kl} \) at \( {P}_{k} \) is close to either zero or \( \pi \) since \( {P}_{k} \) is in the center of an \( {\varepsilon }^{\alpha } \) -neck and \( \alpha \) is sufficiently large. If the angle between \( {\gamma }_{k} \) and \( {\zeta }_{kl} \) at \( {P}_{k} \) is close to zero, we consider the triangle \( {\Delta P}{P}_{k}{P}_{k}^{\prime } \) in \( {M}^{\alpha } \) with vertices \( P,{P}_{k} \) , and \( {P}_{k}^{\prime } \) . Note that the length between \( {P}_{k} \) and \( {P}_{k}^{\prime } \) is much smaller than the lengths from \( {P}_{k} \) or \( {P}_{k}^{\prime } \) to \( P \) . By comparing the angles of this triangle with those of the corresponding triangle in the Euclidean plane with the same corresponding lengths and using Toponogov's comparison theorem, we find that it is impossible. Thus the angle between \( {\gamma }_{k} \) and \( {\zeta }_{kl} \) at \( {P}_{k} \) is close to \( \pi \) . We now consider the triangle \( \Delta {P}_{k}{P}_{k}^{\prime }{P}_{l} \) in \( {M}^{\alpha } \) with the three sides \( {\zeta }_{kl},{\eta }_{kl} \) and the geodesic segment from \( {P}_{k}^{\prime } \) to \( {P}_{l} \) on \( {\gamma }_{l} \) . We have seen that the angle of \( \Delta {P}_{k}{P}_{k}^{\prime }{P}_{l} \) at \( {P}_{k} \) is close to zero and the angle at \( {P}_{k}^{\prime } \) is \( \frac{\pi }{2} \) . By comparing with corresponding triangle \( \bar{\Delta }\overline{{P}_{k}}\overline{{P}_{k}^{\prime }}\overline{{P}_{l}} \) in the Euclidean plane \( {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) whose sides have the same corresponding lengths, Toponogov's comparison theorem implies

\[
\angle {\bar{P}}_{l}{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k}^{\prime } + \angle {\bar{P}}_{l}{\bar{P}}_{k}^{\prime }{\bar{P}}_{k} \leq  \angle {P}_{l}{P}_{k}{P}_{k}^{\prime } + \angle {P}_{l}{P}_{k}^{\prime }{P}_{k} < \frac{3}{4}\pi .
\]

This is impossible since the length between \( {\bar{P}}_{k} \) and \( {\bar{P}}_{k}^{\prime } \) is much smaller than the length from \( {\bar{P}}_{l} \) to either \( {\bar{P}}_{k} \) or \( {\bar{P}}_{k}^{\prime } \) . So we have proved each \( {\gamma }_{l} \) with \( l > k \) passes through the neck \( {N}_{k} \) .

Hence by taking a limit, we get a geodesic ray \( \gamma \) emanating from \( P \) which passes through all the necks \( {N}_{k}, k = 1,2,\ldots \) , except a finite number of them. Throwing these finite number of necks away, we may assume \( \gamma \) passes through all necks \( {N}_{k} \) , \( k = 1,2,\ldots \) Denote the center sphere of \( {N}_{k} \) by \( {S}_{k} \) , and their intersection points with \( \gamma \) by \( {p}_{k} \in  {S}_{k} \cap  \gamma , k = 1,2,\ldots \) .

Take a sequence of points \( \gamma \left( m\right) \) with \( m = 1,2,\ldots \) . For each fixed neck \( {N}_{k} \) , arbitrarily choose a point \( {q}_{k} \in  {N}_{k} \) near the center sphere \( {S}_{k} \) and draw a geodesic segment \( {\gamma }^{km} \) from \( {q}_{k} \) to \( \gamma \left( m\right) \) . Now we claim that for any neck \( {N}_{l} \) with \( l > k,{\gamma }^{km} \) will pass through \( {N}_{l} \) for all sufficiently large \( m \) .

We argue by contradiction. Let us place all the necks \( {N}_{i} \) horizontally so that the geodesic \( \gamma \) passes through each \( {N}_{i} \) from the left to the right. We observe that the geodesic segment \( {\gamma }^{km} \) must pass through the right half of \( {N}_{k} \) ; otherwise \( {\gamma }^{km} \) cannot be minimal. Then for large enough \( m \) , the distance from \( {p}_{l} \) to the geodesic segment \( {\gamma }^{km} \) must be achieved by the distance from \( {p}_{l} \) to some interior point \( {p}_{k}{}^{\prime } \) of \( {\gamma }^{km} \) . Let us draw a minimal geodesic \( \eta \) from \( {p}_{l} \) to the interior point \( {p}_{k}{}^{\prime } \) with the angle at the intersection point \( {p}_{k}{}^{\prime } \in  \eta  \cap  {\gamma }^{km} \) to be \( \frac{\pi }{2} \) . Suppose the claim is false. Then the angle between \( \eta \) and \( \gamma \) at \( {p}_{l} \) is close to 0 or \( \pi \) since \( {\varepsilon }^{\alpha } \) is small.

If the angle between \( \eta \) and \( \gamma \) at \( {p}_{l} \) is close to 0, we consider the triangle \( \Delta {p}_{l}{p}_{k}{}^{\prime }\gamma \left( m\right) \) and construct a comparison triangle \( \bar{\Delta }{\bar{p}}_{l}{\overline{{p}_{k}}}^{\prime }\bar{\gamma }\left( m\right) \) in the plane with the same corresponding length. Then by Toponogov's comparison theorem, we see the sum of the inner angles of the comparison triangle \( \bar{\Delta }{\bar{p}}_{l}{\overline{{p}_{k}}}^{\prime }\bar{\gamma }\left( m\right) \) is less than \( {3\pi }/4 \) , which is impossible.

If the angle between \( \eta \) and \( \gamma \) at \( {p}_{l} \) is close to \( \pi \) , by drawing a minimal geodesic \( \xi \) from \( {q}_{k} \) to \( {p}_{l} \) , we see that \( \xi \) must pass through the right half of \( {N}_{k} \) and the left half of \( {N}_{l} \) ; otherwise \( \xi \) cannot be minimal. Thus the three inner angles of the triangle \( \Delta {p}_{l}{p}_{k}{}^{\prime }{q}_{k} \) are almost \( 0,\pi /2 \) , and 0 respectively. This is also impossible by the Toponogov comparison theorem.

Hence we have proved that the geodesic segment \( {\gamma }^{km} \) passes through \( {N}_{l} \) for \( m \) large enough.

Consider the triangle \( \Delta {p}_{k}{q}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) \) with two long sides \( \overline{{p}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) }\left( { \subset  \gamma }\right) \) and \( \overline{{q}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) }( = \; {\gamma }^{km} \) ). For any \( s > 0 \) , choose points \( {\widetilde{p}}_{k} \) on \( \overline{{p}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) } \) and \( {\widetilde{q}}_{k} \) on \( \overline{{q}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) } \) with \( d\left( {{p}_{k},{\widetilde{p}}_{k}}\right)  = \; d\left( {{q}_{k},{\widetilde{q}}_{k}}\right)  = s \) . By Toponogov’s comparison theorem, we have

\[
{\left( \frac{d\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k},{\widetilde{q}}_{k}}\right) }{d\left( {{p}_{k},{q}_{k}}\right) }\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
= \frac{d{\left( {\widetilde{p}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) }^{2} + d{\left( {\widetilde{q}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) }^{2} - {2d}\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) d\left( {{\widetilde{q}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) \cos \bar{\measuredangle }\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) {\widetilde{q}}_{k}}\right) }{d{\left( {p}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) }^{2} + d{\left( {q}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) }^{2} - {2d}\left( {{p}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) d\left( {{q}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) \cos \bar{\measuredangle }\left( {{p}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) {q}_{k}}\right) }
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{d{\left( {\widetilde{p}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) }^{2} + d{\left( {\widetilde{q}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) }^{2} - {2d}\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) d\left( {{\widetilde{q}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) \cos \bar{\measuredangle }\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) {\widetilde{q}}_{k}}\right) }{d{\left( {p}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) }^{2} + d{\left( {q}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) }^{2} - {2d}\left( {{p}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) d\left( {{q}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) \cos \bar{\measuredangle }\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) {\widetilde{q}}_{k}}\right) }
\]

\[
= \frac{{\left( d\left( {\widetilde{p}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right)  - d\left( {\widetilde{q}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) \right) }^{2} + {2d}\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) d\left( {{\widetilde{q}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) \left( {1 - \cos \bar{\measuredangle }\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) {\widetilde{q}}_{k}}\right) }\right) }{{\left( d\left( {\widetilde{p}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right)  - d\left( {\widetilde{q}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) \right) \right) }^{2} + {2d}\left( {{p}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) d\left( {{q}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) \left( {1 - \cos \bar{\measuredangle }\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) {\widetilde{q}}_{k}}\right) }\right) }
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{d\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) d\left( {{\widetilde{q}}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) }{d\left( {{p}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) d\left( {{q}_{k},\gamma \left( m\right) }\right) }
\]

\[
\rightarrow  1
\]

as \( m \rightarrow  \infty \) , where \( \bar{\measuredangle }\left( {{p}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) {q}_{k}}\right) \) and \( \bar{\measuredangle }\left( {{\widetilde{p}}_{k}\gamma \left( m\right) {\widetilde{q}}_{k}}\right) \) are the corresponding angles of the comparison triangles.

Letting \( m \rightarrow  \infty \) , we see that \( {\gamma }^{km} \) has a convergent subsequence whose limit \( {\gamma }^{k} \) is a geodesic ray passing through all \( {N}_{l} \) with \( l > k \) . Let us denote by \( {p}_{j} = \gamma \left( {t}_{j}\right) , j = \; 1,2,\ldots \) From the above computation, we deduce that

\[
d\left( {{p}_{k},{q}_{k}}\right)  \leq  d\left( {\gamma \left( {{t}_{k} + s}\right) ,{\gamma }^{k}\left( s\right) }\right)
\]

for all \( s > 0 \) .

Let \( \varphi \left( x\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{t \rightarrow   + \infty }}\left( {t - d\left( {x,\gamma \left( t\right) }\right) }\right) \) be the Busemann function constructed from the ray \( \gamma \) . Note that the level set \( {\varphi }^{-1}\left( {\varphi \left( {p}_{j}\right) }\right)  \cap  {N}_{j} \) is close to the center sphere \( {S}_{j} \) for any \( j = 1,2,\ldots \) . Now let \( {q}_{k} \) be any fixed point in \( {\varphi }^{-1}\left( {\varphi \left( {p}_{k}\right) }\right)  \cap  {N}_{k} \) . By the definition of Busemann function \( \varphi \) associated to the ray \( \gamma \) , we see that \( \varphi \left( {{\gamma }^{k}\left( {s}_{1}\right) }\right)  - \varphi \left( {{\gamma }^{k}\left( {s}_{2}\right) }\right)  = \; {s}_{1} - {s}_{2} \) for any \( {s}_{1},{s}_{2} \geq  0 \) . Consequently, for each \( l > k \) , by choosing \( s = {t}_{l} - {t}_{k} \) , we see \( {\gamma }^{k}\left( {{t}_{l} - {t}_{k}}\right)  \in  {\varphi }^{-1}\left( {\varphi \left( {p}_{l}\right) }\right)  \cap  {N}_{l} \) . Since \( \gamma \left( {{t}_{k} + {t}_{l} - {t}_{k}}\right)  = {p}_{l} \) , it follows that

\[
d\left( {{p}_{k},{q}_{k}}\right)  \leq  d\left( {{p}_{l},{\gamma }^{k}\left( s\right) }\right) .
\]

with \( s = {t}_{l} - {t}_{k} > 0 \) . This implies that the diameter of \( {\varphi }^{-1}\left( {\varphi \left( {p}_{k}\right) }\right)  \cap  {N}_{k} \) is not greater than the diameter of \( {\varphi }^{-1}\left( {\varphi \left( {p}_{l}\right) }\right)  \cap  {N}_{l} \) for any \( l > k \) , which is a contradiction for \( l \) much larger than \( k \) .

Therefore we have proved the proposition. \( \square \)

nodes.content: Let \( M \) be a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with nonnegative sectional curvature \( K \geq  0 \) . A geodesic ball \( B\left( {p, r}\right) \) of radius \( r \) centered at a point \( p \in  M \) is called a curvature \( \beta \) -bump if sectional curvature \( K \geq  \beta /{r}^{2} \) at all points in the ball. The ball \( B\left( {p, r}\right) \) is called \( \lambda \) -remote from an origin \( O \) if \( d\left( {p, O}\right)  \geq  {\lambda r} \) .

nodes.proof:
Let us denote by \( \left| {OQ}\right|  = d\left( {O, Q}\right) \) the distance between two points \( O, Q \in \; M \) . Without loss of generality, we may assume that for each \( k \) ,

(6.1.1)

\[
1 + 2\left| {P{P}_{k}}\right|  \leq  \left| {P{P}_{k + 1}}\right| .
\]

Draw a minimal geodesic \( {\gamma }_{k} \) from \( P \) to \( {P}_{k} \) and a minimal geodesic \( {\sigma }_{k} \) from \( {P}_{k} \) to \( {P}_{k + 1} \) , both parametrized by arclength. We may further assume

(6.1.2)

\[
{\theta }_{k} = \left| {\measuredangle \left( {{\dot{\gamma }}_{k}\left( 0\right) ,{\dot{\gamma }}_{k + 1}\left( 0\right) }\right) }\right|  < \frac{1}{k}.
\]

By assumption, the sequence \( \left( {M,{\lambda }_{k}^{2}{g}_{ij},{P}_{k}}\right) \) converges (in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology) to a Riemannian manifold \( \left( {\widetilde{M},{\widetilde{g}}_{ij},\widetilde{P}}\right) \) with nonnegative sectional curvature. By a further choice of subsequences, we may also assume \( {\gamma }_{k} \) and \( {\sigma }_{k} \) converge to geodesic rays \( \widetilde{\gamma } \) and \( \widetilde{\sigma } \) starting at \( \widetilde{P} \) respectively. We will prove that \( \widetilde{\gamma } \cup  \widetilde{\sigma } \) forms a line in \( \widetilde{M} \) , and then by the Toponogov splitting theorem [89] the limit \( M \) must be splitted as \( \mathbb{R} \times  N \) .

We argue by contradiction. Suppose \( \widetilde{\gamma } \cup  \widetilde{\sigma } \) is not a line; then for each \( k \) , there exist two points \( {A}_{k} \in  {\gamma }_{k} \) and \( {B}_{k} \in  {\sigma }_{k} \) such that as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) ,

(6.1.3)

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l} {\lambda }_{k}d\left( {{P}_{k},{A}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  A > 0, \\  {\lambda }_{k}d\left( {{P}_{k},{B}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  B > 0, \\  {\lambda }_{k}d\left( {{A}_{k},{B}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  C > 0, \\  \text{ but }A + B > C. \end{array}\right.
\]

![019eb179-47af-757a-baf4-40848a87504b_96_239_759_1071_334_0.jpg](images/019eb179-47af-757a-baf4-40848a87504b_96_239_759_1071_334_0.jpg)

Now draw a minimal geodesic \( {\delta }_{k} \) from \( {A}_{k} \) to \( {B}_{k} \) . Consider comparison triangles \( \bar{\bigtriangleup }{\bar{P}}_{k}\bar{P}{\bar{P}}_{k + 1} \) and \( \bar{\bigtriangleup }{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{A}}_{k}{\bar{B}}_{k} \) in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{2} \) with

\[
\left| {{\bar{P}}_{k}\bar{P}}\right|  = \left| {{P}_{k}P}\right| ,\left| {{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k + 1}}\right|  = \left| {{P}_{k}{P}_{k + 1}}\right| ,\left| {\bar{P}{\bar{P}}_{k + 1}}\right|  = \left| {P{P}_{k + 1}}\right| ,
\]

\[
\text{ and }\left| {{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{A}}_{k}}\right|  = \left| {{P}_{k}{A}_{k}}\right| ,\left| {{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{B}}_{k}}\right|  = \left| {{P}_{k}{B}_{k}}\right| ,\left| {{\bar{A}}_{k}{\bar{B}}_{k}}\right|  = \left| {{A}_{k}{B}_{k}}\right| \text{ . }
\]

By Toponogov's comparison theorem [8], we have

(6.1.4)

\[
\measuredangle {\bar{A}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{B}}_{k} \geq  \measuredangle \bar{P}{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k + 1}.
\]

On the other hand, by (6.1.2) and using Toponogov's comparison theorem again, we have

(6.1.5)

\[
\measuredangle {\bar{P}}_{k}\bar{P}{\bar{P}}_{k + 1} \leq  \measuredangle {P}_{k}P{P}_{k + 1} < \frac{1}{k},
\]

and since \( \left| {{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k + 1}}\right|  > \left| {\bar{P}{\bar{P}}_{k}}\right| \) by (6.1.1), we further have

(6.1.6)

\[
\measuredangle {\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k + 1}\bar{P} \leq  \measuredangle {\bar{P}}_{k}\bar{P}{\bar{P}}_{k + 1} < \frac{1}{k}.
\]

Thus the above inequalities (6.1.4)-(6.1.6) imply that

\[
\measuredangle {\bar{A}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{B}}_{k} > \pi  - \frac{2}{k}.
\]

Hence

(6.1.7)

\[
{\left| {\bar{A}}_{k}{\bar{B}}_{k}\right| }^{2} \geq  {\left| {\bar{A}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k}\right| }^{2} + {\left| {\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{B}}_{k}\right| }^{2} - 2\left| {{\bar{A}}_{k}{\bar{P}}_{k}}\right|  \cdot  \left| {{\bar{P}}_{k}{\bar{B}}_{k}}\right| \cos \left( {\pi  - \frac{2}{k}}\right) .
\]

Multiplying the above inequality by \( {\lambda }_{k}^{2} \) and letting \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) , we get

\[
C \geq  A + B
\]

which contradicts (6.1.3).

Therefore we have proved the proposition. 0

LEMMA 6.1.3. Given a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with bounded curvature and with asymptotic scalar curvature ratio

\[
A = \mathop{\limsup }\limits_{{s \rightarrow   + \infty }}R{s}^{2} =  + \infty
\]

we can find a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \) divergent to infinity, a sequence of radii \( {r}_{j} \) and a sequence of positive numbers \( {\delta }_{j} \rightarrow  0 \) such that

(i) \( R\left( x\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {\delta }_{j}}\right) R\left( {x}_{j}\right) \) for all \( x \) in the ball \( B\left( {{x}_{j},{r}_{j}}\right) \) of radius \( {r}_{j} \) around \( {x}_{j} \) ,

(ii) \( {r}_{j}^{2}R\left( {x}_{j}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) ,

(iii) \( {\lambda }_{j} = d\left( {{x}_{j}, O}\right) /{r}_{j} \rightarrow   + \infty \) ,

(iv) the balls \( B\left( {{x}_{j},{r}_{j}}\right) \) are disjoint,

where \( d\left( {{x}_{j}, O}\right) \) is the distance of \( {x}_{j} \) from the origin \( O \) .

nodes.proof:
Pick a sequence of positive numbers \( {\epsilon }_{j} \rightarrow  0 \) , then choose \( {A}_{j} \rightarrow   + \infty \) so that \( {A}_{j}{\epsilon }_{j}^{2} \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Let \( {\sigma }_{j} \) be the largest number such that

\[
\sup \left\{  {R\left( x\right) d{\left( x, O\right) }^{2} \mid  d\left( {x, O}\right)  \leq  {\sigma }_{j}}\right\}   \leq  {A}_{j}.
\]

Then there exists some \( {y}_{j} \in  M \) such that

\[
R\left( {y}_{j}\right) d{\left( {y}_{j}, O\right) }^{2} = {A}_{j}\;\text{ and }\;d\left( {{y}_{j}, O}\right)  = {\sigma }_{j}.
\]

Now pick \( {x}_{j} \in  M \) so that \( d\left( {{x}_{j}, O}\right)  \geq  {\sigma }_{j} \) and

\[
R\left( {x}_{j}\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{1 + {\epsilon }_{j}}\sup \left\{  {R\left( x\right)  \mid  d\left( {x, O}\right)  \geq  {\sigma }_{j}}\right\}  .
\]

Finally pick \( {r}_{j} = {\epsilon }_{j}{\sigma }_{j} \) . We check the properties (i)-(iv) as follows.

(i) If \( x \in  B\left( {{x}_{j},{r}_{j}}\right)  \cap  \left\{  {d\left( {\cdot , O}\right)  \geq  {\sigma }_{j}}\right\} \) , we have

\[
R\left( x\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {\epsilon }_{j}}\right) R\left( {x}_{j}\right)
\]

by the choice of the point \( {x}_{j} \) ; while if \( x \in  B\left( {{x}_{j},{r}_{j}}\right)  \cap  \left\{  {d\left( {\cdot , O}\right)  \leq  {\sigma }_{j}}\right\} \) , we have

\[
R\left( x\right)  \leq  {A}_{j}/d{\left( x, O\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{{\left( 1 - {\epsilon }_{j}\right) }^{2}}\left( {{A}_{j}/{\sigma }_{j}^{2}}\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{1}{{\left( 1 - {\epsilon }_{j}\right) }^{2}}R\left( {y}_{j}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{\left( 1 + {\epsilon }_{j}\right) }{{\left( 1 - {\epsilon }_{j}\right) }^{2}}R\left( {x}_{j}\right)
\]

since \( d\left( {x, O}\right)  \geq  d\left( {{x}_{j}, O}\right)  - d\left( {x,{x}_{j}}\right)  \geq  {\sigma }_{j} - {r}_{j} = \left( {1 - {\epsilon }_{j}}\right) {\sigma }_{j} \) . Thus we have obtained

\[
R\left( x\right)  \leq  \left( {1 + {\delta }_{j}}\right) R\left( {x}_{j}\right) ,\;\forall x \in  B\left( {{x}_{j},{r}_{j}}\right) ,
\]

where \( {\delta }_{j} = \frac{\left( 1 + {\epsilon }_{j}\right) }{{\left( 1 - {\epsilon }_{j}\right) }^{2}} - 1 \rightarrow  0 \) as \( j \rightarrow   + \infty \) .

(ii) By the choices of \( {r}_{j},{x}_{j} \) and \( {y}_{j} \) , we have

\[
{r}_{j}^{2}R\left( {x}_{j}\right)  = {\epsilon }_{j}^{2}{\sigma }_{j}^{2}R\left( {x}_{j}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {\epsilon }_{j}^{2}{\sigma }_{j}^{2}\left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{1 + {\epsilon }_{j}}R\left( {y}_{j}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
= \frac{{\epsilon }_{j}^{2}}{1 + {\epsilon }_{j}}{A}_{j} \rightarrow   + \infty ,\;\text{ as }j \rightarrow   + \infty .
\]

(iii) Since \( d\left( {{x}_{j}, O}\right)  \geq  {\sigma }_{j} = {r}_{j}/{\epsilon }_{j} \) , it follows that \( {\lambda }_{j} = d\left( {{x}_{j}, O}\right) /{r}_{j} \rightarrow   + \infty \) as \( j \rightarrow   + \infty \) .

(iv) For any \( x \in  B\left( {{x}_{j},{r}_{j}}\right) \) , the distance from the origin

\[
d\left( {x, O}\right)  \geq  d\left( {{x}_{j}, O}\right)  - d\left( {x,{x}_{j}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {\sigma }_{j} - {r}_{j}
\]

\[
= \left( {1 - {\epsilon }_{j}}\right) {\sigma }_{j} \rightarrow   + \infty \text{ , as }j \rightarrow   + \infty \text{ . }
\]

Thus any fixed compact set does not meet the balls \( B\left( {{x}_{j},{r}_{j}}\right) \) for large enough \( j \) . If we pass to a subsequence, the balls will all avoid each other. D

LEMMA 6.1.4. Given a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with unbounded curvature, we can find a sequence of points \( {x}_{j} \) divergent to infinity such that for each positive integer \( j \) , we have \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{j}\right) }\right|  \geq  j \) , and

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( x\right) }\right|  \leq  4\left| {{Rm}\left( {x}_{j}\right) }\right|
\]

for \( x \in  B\left( {{x}_{j},\frac{j}{\sqrt{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {x}_{j}\right) \right| }}}\right) \) .

nodes.proof:
Each \( {x}_{j} \) can be constructed as a limit of a finite sequence \( \left\{  {y}_{i}\right\} \) , defined as follows. Let \( {y}_{0} \) be any fixed point with \( \left| {{Rm}\left( {y}_{0}\right) }\right|  \geq  j \) . Inductively, if \( {y}_{i} \) cannot be taken as \( {x}_{j} \) , then there is a \( {y}_{i + 1} \) such that

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l} \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {y}_{i + 1}\right) }\right|  > 4\left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {y}_{i}\right) }\right| , \\  d\left( {{y}_{i},{y}_{i + 1}}\right)  \leq  \frac{j}{\sqrt{\left| \operatorname{Rm}\left( {y}_{i}\right) \right| }}. \end{array}\right.
\]

Thus we have

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {y}_{i}\right) }\right|  > {4}^{i}\left| {{Rm}\left( {y}_{0}\right) }\right|  \geq  {4}^{i}j
\]

\[
d\left( {{y}_{i},{y}_{0}}\right)  \leq  j\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{k = 1}}^{i}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{4}^{k - 1}j}} < 2\sqrt{j}
\]

Since the manifold is smooth, the sequence \( \left\{  {y}_{i}\right\} \) must be finite. The last element fits. 0

nodes.content: THEOREM 6.2.1 (Perelman [103]). Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) , - \infty  < t < T \) with some \( T > 0 \) , be a nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) . Then there exist a sequence of points \( {q}_{k} \) and a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   - \infty \) such that the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) around \( {q}_{k} \) with factor \( {\left| {t}_{k}\right| }^{-1} \) and with the times \( {t}_{k} \) shifting to the new time zero converge to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton in \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology.

Then there exist a sequence of points \( {q}_{k} \) and a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow - \infty \) such that the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) around \( {q}_{k} \) with factor \( {\left| {t}_{...

nodes.proof:
Clearly, we may assume that the nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is not a gradient shrinking soliton. For the arbitrarily fixed \( \left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right) \) , let \( q\left( \tau \right) \left( {\tau  = {t}_{0} - t}\right) \) be chosen as in (6.2.1) with \( l\left( {q\left( \tau \right) ,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{n}{2} \) . We only need to show that the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) around \( q\left( \tau \right) \) with factor \( {\tau }^{-1} \) converge along a subsequence of \( \tau  \rightarrow   + \infty \) to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology.

We first claim that for any \( A \geq  1 \) , one can find \( B = B\left( A\right)  <  + \infty \) such that for every \( \bar{\tau } > 1 \) there holds

(6.2.6)

\[
l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  \leq  B\text{ and }{\tau R}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right)  \leq  B,
\]

whenever \( \frac{1}{2}\bar{\tau } \leq  \tau  \leq  A\bar{\tau } \) and \( {d}_{{t}_{0} - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}^{2}\left( {q, q\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) }\right)  \leq  A\bar{\tau } \) .

Indeed, by using (6.2.5) at \( \tau  = \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2} \) , we have

(6.2.7)

\[
\sqrt{l\left( {q,\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\right) } \leq  \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sup \{ \left| {\nabla \sqrt{l}}\right| \}  \cdot  {d}_{{t}_{0} - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\left( {q, q\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3}{2\bar{\tau }}} \cdot  \sqrt{A\bar{\tau }}
\]

\[
= \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3A}{2}}\text{ , }
\]

and

(6.2.8)

\[
R\left( {q,{t}_{0} - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\right)  \leq  \frac{{3l}\left( {q,\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\right) }{\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) }
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{6}{\bar{\tau }}{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3A}{2}}\right) }^{2},
\]

for \( q \in  {B}_{{t}_{0} - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\left( {q\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) ,\sqrt{A\bar{\tau }}}\right) \) . Recall that the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality implies that the scalar curvature of the ancient solution is pointwise nondecreasing in time. Thus we know from (6.2.8) that

(6.2.9)

\[
{\tau R}\left( {q,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right)  \leq  {6A}{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3A}{2}}\right) }^{2}
\]

whenever \( \frac{1}{2}\bar{\tau } \leq  \tau  \leq  A\bar{\tau } \) and \( {d}_{{t}_{0} - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}^{2}\left( {q, q\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) }\right)  \leq  A\bar{\tau } \) .

By (6.2.2) and (6.2.3) we have

\[
\frac{\partial l}{\partial \tau } + \frac{1}{2}{\left| \nabla l\right| }^{2} =  - \frac{l}{2\tau } + \frac{R}{2}.
\]

This together with (6.2.9) implies that

\[
\frac{\partial l}{\partial \tau } \leq   - \frac{l}{2\tau } + \frac{3A}{\tau }{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3A}{2}}\right) }^{2}
\]

i.e.,

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial \tau }\left( {\sqrt{\tau }l}\right)  \leq  \frac{3A}{\sqrt{\tau }}{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3A}{2}}\right) }^{2}
\]

whenever \( \frac{1}{2}\bar{\tau } \leq  \tau  \leq  A\bar{\tau } \) and \( {d}_{{t}_{0} - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}^{2}\left( {q, q\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) }\right)  \leq  A\bar{\tau } \) . Hence by integrating this differential inequality, we obtain

\[
\sqrt{\tau }l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  - \sqrt{\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}l\left( {q,\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\right)  \leq  {6A}{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3A}{2}}\right) }^{2}\sqrt{\tau }
\]

and then by (6.2.7),

(6.2.10)

\[
l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  \leq  l\left( {q,\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\right)  + {6A}{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3A}{2}}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
\leq  {7A}{\left( \sqrt{\frac{n}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{3A}{2}}\right) }^{2}
\]

whenever \( \frac{1}{2}\bar{\tau } \leq  \tau  \leq  A\bar{\tau } \) and \( {d}_{{t}_{0} - \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}^{2}\left( {q, q\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) }\right)  \leq  A\bar{\tau } \) . So we have proved claim (6.2.6).

Recall that \( {g}_{ij}\left( \tau \right)  = {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) satisfies \( {\left( {g}_{ij}\right) }_{\tau } = 2{R}_{ij} \) . Let us take the scaling of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution around \( q\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) \) with factor \( {\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) }^{-1} \) , i.e.,

\[
{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( s\right)  = \frac{2}{\bar{\tau }}{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{0} - s\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\right)
\]

where \( s \in  \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) . Claim (6.2.6) says that for all \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {1,{2A}}\right\rbrack \) and all \( q \) such that \( {\operatorname{dist}}_{{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( 1\right) }^{2}\left( {q, q\left( \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}\right) }\right)  \leq  A \) , we have \( \widetilde{R}\left( {q, s}\right)  = \frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}R\left( {q,{t}_{0} - s\frac{\bar{\tau }}{2}}\right)  \leq  B \) . Now taking into account the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing assumption and Theorem 4.2.2, we can use Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5) to obtain a sequence \( {\bar{\tau }}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) such that the marked evolving manifolds \( \left( {M,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) , q\left( \frac{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{2}\right) }\right) \) , with \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right)  = \frac{2}{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{0} - s\frac{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{2}}\right) \) and \( s \in  \lbrack 1, + \infty ) \) , converge to a manifold \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( s\right) ,\bar{q}}\right) \) with \( s \in  \lbrack 1, + \infty ) \) , where \( {\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( s\right) \) is also a solution to the Ricci flow on \( \bar{M} \) .

Denote by \( {\widetilde{l}}_{k} \) the corresponding Li-Yau-Perelman distance of \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) \) . It is easy to see that \( {\widetilde{l}}_{k}\left( {q, s}\right)  = l\left( {q,\frac{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{2}s}\right) \) , for \( s \in  \lbrack 1, + \infty ) \) . From (6.2.5), we also have

(6.2.11)

\[
{\left| \nabla {\widetilde{l}}_{k}\right| }_{{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }}^{2} + {\widetilde{R}}^{\left( k\right) } \leq  6{\widetilde{l}}_{k}
\]

where \( {\widetilde{R}}^{\left( k\right) } \) is the scalar curvature of the metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) } \) . Claim (6.2.6) says that \( {\widetilde{l}}_{k} \) are uniformly bounded on compact subsets of \( M \times  \lbrack 1, + \infty ) \) (with the corresponding origins \( q\left( \frac{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{2}\right) \) ). Thus the above gradient estimate (6.2.11) implies that the functions \( {\widetilde{l}}_{k} \) tend (up to a subsequence) to a function \( \bar{l} \) which is a locally Lipschitz function on \( \bar{M} \) .

We know from (6.2.2)-(6.2.4) that the Li-Yau-Perelman distance \( {\widetilde{l}}_{k} \) satisfies the following inequalities:

(6.2.12)

\[
{\left( {\widetilde{l}}_{k}\right) }_{s} - \Delta {\widetilde{l}}_{k} + {\left| \nabla {\widetilde{l}}_{k}\right| }^{2} - {\widetilde{R}}^{\left( k\right) } + \frac{n}{2s} \geq  0,
\]

(6.2.13)

\[
{2\Delta }{\widetilde{l}}_{k} - {\left| \nabla {\widetilde{l}}_{k}\right| }^{2} + {\widetilde{R}}^{\left( k\right) } + \frac{{\widetilde{l}}_{k} - n}{s} \leq  0.
\]

We next show that the limit \( \bar{l} \) also satisfies the above two inequalities in the sense of distributions. Indeed the above two inequalities can be rewritten as

(6.2.14)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial s} - \bigtriangleup  + {\widetilde{R}}^{\left( k\right) }}\right) \left( {{\left( 4\pi s\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-{\widetilde{l}}_{k}}\right) }\right)  \leq  0,
\]

(6.2.15)

\[
- \left( {4\bigtriangleup  - {\widetilde{R}}^{\left( k\right) }}\right) {e}^{-\frac{{\widetilde{l}}_{k}}{2}} + \frac{{\widetilde{l}}_{k} - n}{s}{e}^{-\frac{{\widetilde{l}}_{k}}{2}} \leq  0,
\]

in the sense of distributions. Note that the estimate (6.2.11) implies that \( {\widetilde{l}}_{k} \rightarrow  \bar{l} \) in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{0,\alpha } \) norm for any \( 0 < \alpha  < 1 \) . Thus the inequalities (6.2.14) and (6.2.15) imply that the limit \( \bar{l} \) satisfies

(6.2.16)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial s} - \bigtriangleup  + \bar{R}}\right) \left( {{\left( 4\pi s\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-\bar{l}}\right) }\right)  \leq  0,
\]

(6.2.17)

\[
- \left( {{4\Delta } - \bar{R}}\right) {e}^{-\frac{\bar{l}}{2}} + \frac{\bar{l} - n}{s}{e}^{-\frac{\bar{l}}{2}} \leq  0,
\]

in the sense of distributions.

Denote by \( {\widetilde{V}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) \) Perelman’s reduced volume of the scaled metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) \) . Since \( {\widetilde{l}}_{k}\left( {q, s}\right)  = l\left( {q,\frac{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{2}s}\right) \) , we see that \( {\widetilde{V}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right)  = \widetilde{V}\left( {\frac{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{2}s}\right) \) where \( \widetilde{V} \) is Perelman’s reduced volume of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. The monotonicity of Perelman’s reduced volume (Theorem 3.2.8) then implies that

(6.2.18)

\[
\mathop{\lim }\limits_{{k \rightarrow  \infty }}{\widetilde{V}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right)  = \bar{V},\text{ for }s \in  \left\lbrack  {1,2}\right\rbrack
\]

for some nonnegative constant \( \bar{V} \) .

(We remark that by the Jacobian comparison theorem (Theorem 3.2.7), (3.2.18) and (3.2.19), the integrand of \( {\widetilde{V}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) \) is bounded by

\[
{\left( 4\pi s\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-{\widetilde{l}}_{k}\left( {X, s}\right) }\right) {\widetilde{\mathcal{J}}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right)  \leq  {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-{\left| X\right| }^{2}}\right)
\]

on \( {T}_{p}M \) , where \( {\widetilde{\mathcal{J}}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) \) is the \( \mathcal{L} \) -Jacobian of the \( \mathcal{L} \) -exponential map of the metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) \) at \( {T}_{p}M \) . Thus we can apply the dominant convergence theorem to get the convergence in (6.2.18). But we are not sure whether the limiting \( \bar{V} \) is exactly Perelman’s reduced volume of the limiting manifold \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( s\right) }\right) \) , because the points \( q\left( \frac{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{2}\right) \) may diverge to infinity. Nevertheless, we can ensure that \( \bar{V} \) is not less than Perelman’s reduced volume of the limit.)

Note by (6.2.5) that

(6.2.19)

\[
{\widetilde{V}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( 2\right)  - {\widetilde{V}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( 1\right)
\]

\[
= {\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{d}{ds}\left( {{\widetilde{V}}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) }\right) {ds}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{1}^{2}{ds}{\int }_{M}\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial s} - \Delta  + {\widetilde{R}}^{\left( k\right) }}\right) \left( {{\left( 4\pi s\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-{\widetilde{l}}_{k}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\left( k\right) }\left( s\right) }.
\]

Thus we deduce that in the sense of distributions,

(6.2.20)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial s} - \Delta  + \bar{R}}\right) \left( {{\left( 4\pi s\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}\exp \left( {-\bar{l}}\right) }\right)  = 0,
\]

and

\[
\left( {{4\Delta } - \bar{R}}\right) {e}^{-\frac{\bar{l}}{2}} = \frac{\bar{l} - n}{s}{e}^{-\frac{\bar{l}}{2}}
\]

or equivalently,

(6.2.21)

\[
{2\Delta }\bar{l} - {\left| \nabla \bar{l}\right| }^{2} + \bar{R} + \frac{\bar{l} - n}{s} = 0,
\]

on \( \bar{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {1,2}\right\rbrack \) . Thus by applying standard parabolic equation theory to (6.2.20) we find that \( \bar{l} \) is actually smooth. Here we used (6.2.2)-(6.2.4) to show that the equality in (6.2.16) implies the equality in (6.2.17).

Set

\[
v = \left\lbrack  {s\left( {{2\Delta }\bar{l} - {\left| \nabla \bar{l}\right| }^{2} + \bar{R}}\right)  + \bar{l} - n}\right\rbrack   \cdot  {\left( 4\pi s\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\bar{l}}.
\]

Then by applying Lemma 2.6.1, we have

(6.2.22)

\[
\left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial s} - \Delta  + \bar{R}}\right) v =  - {2s}{\left| {\bar{R}}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\bar{l} - \frac{1}{2s}{\bar{g}}_{ij}\right| }^{2} \cdot  {\left( 4\pi s\right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-\bar{l}}.
\]

We see from (6.2.21) that the LHS of the equation (6.2.22) is identically zero. Thus the limit metric \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) satisfies

(6.2.23)

\[
{\bar{R}}_{ij} + {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\bar{l} - \frac{1}{2s}{\bar{g}}_{ij} = 0,
\]

so we have shown the limit is a gradient shrinking soliton.

To show that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton is nonflat, we first show that the constant function \( \bar{V}\left( s\right) \) is strictly less than 1 . Consider Perelman’s reduced volume \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right) \) of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. By using Perelman’s Jacobian comparison theorem (Theorem 3.2.7), (3.2.18) and (3.2.19) as before, we have

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = \int {\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-l\left( {X,\tau }\right) }\mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right) {dX}
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{{T}_{p}M}{\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{e}^{-{\left| X\right| }^{2}}{dX}
\]

\[
= 1\text{ . }
\]

Recall that we have assumed the nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is not a gradient shrinking soliton. Thus for \( \tau  > 0 \) , we must have \( \widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  < 1 \) . Since the limiting function \( \bar{V}\left( s\right) \) is the limit of \( \widetilde{V}\left( {\frac{{\bar{\tau }}_{k}}{2}s}\right) \) with \( {\bar{\tau }}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) , we deduce that the constant \( \bar{V}\left( s\right) \) is strictly less than 1, for \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {1,2}\right\rbrack \) .

We now argue by contradiction. Suppose the limiting gradient shrinking soliton \( {\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( s\right) \) is flat. Then by (6.2.23),

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}\bar{l} = \frac{1}{2s}{\bar{g}}_{ij}\text{ and }\Delta \bar{l} = \frac{n}{2s}.
\]

Putting these into the identity (6.2.21), we get

\[
{\left| \nabla \bar{l}\right| }^{2} = \frac{\bar{l}}{s}
\]

Since the function \( \bar{l} \) is strictly convex, it follows that \( \sqrt{4sl} \) is a distance function (from some point) on the complete flat manifold \( \bar{M} \) . From the smoothness of the function \( \bar{l} \) , we conclude that the flat manifold \( \bar{M} \) must be \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . In this case we would have its reduced distance to be \( \bar{l} \) and its reduced volume to be 1 . Since \( \bar{V} \) is not less than the reduced volume of the limit, this is a contradiction. Therefore the limiting gradient shrinking soliton \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) is not flat. \( \square \)

nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content: THEOREM 6.2.2. The only nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solutions to Ricci flow on two-dimensional manifolds are the round sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) and the round real projective plane \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \) .
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 6.2.2. The only nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solutions to Ricci flow on two-dimensional manifolds are the round sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) and the round real projective plane \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \) .

nodes.proof:
Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be a nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution defined on \( M \times  \left( {-\infty , T}\right) \) (for some \( T > 0 \) ), where \( M \) is a two-dimensional manifold. Note that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution satisfies the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5). In particular by Corollary 2.5.8, the scalar curvature of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is pointwise nondecreasing in time. Moreover by the strong maximum principle, the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution has strictly positive curvature everywhere.

By the above Theorem 6.2.1, we know that the scalings of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution along a sequence of points \( {q}_{k} \) in \( M \) and a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   - \infty \) converge to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) with \( - \infty  < t \leq  0 \) .

We first show that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) has uniformly bounded curvature. Clearly, the limiting soliton has nonnegative curvature and is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, and its scalar curvature is still pointwise nondecreasing in time. Thus we only need to show that the limiting soliton has bounded curvature at \( t = 0 \) . We argue by contradiction. Suppose the curvature of the limiting soliton is unbounded at \( t = 0 \) . Of course in this case the limiting soliton \( \bar{M} \) is noncompact. Then by applying Lemma 6.1.4, we can choose a sequence of points \( {x}_{j}, j = 1,2,\ldots \) , divergent to infinity such that the scalar curvature \( \bar{R} \) of the limit satisfies

\[
\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  j\text{ and }\bar{R}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)
\]

for all \( j = 1,2,\ldots \) , and \( x \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{j}, j/\sqrt{R\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }}\right) \) . And then by the nondecreasing (in time) of the scalar curvature, we have

\[
\bar{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  4\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) ,
\]

for all \( j = 1,2,\ldots , x \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{j}, j/\sqrt{R\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }}\right) \) and \( t \leq  0 \) . By combining with Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5) and the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing, we know that a subsequence of the rescaling solutions

\[
\left( {\bar{M},\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) {\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t/\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }\right) ,{x}_{j}}\right) ,\;j = 1,2,\ldots ,
\]

converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a nonflat smooth solution of the Ricci flow. Then Proposition 6.1.2 implies that the new (two-dimensional) limit must be flat. This arrives at a contradiction. So we have proved that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton has uniformly bounded curvature.

We next show that the limiting soliton is compact. Suppose the limiting soliton is (complete and) noncompact. By the strong maximum principle we know that the limiting soliton also has strictly positive curvature everywhere. After a shift of the time, we may assume that the limiting soliton satisfies the following equation

(6.2.24)

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f + {\bar{R}}_{ij} + \frac{1}{2t}{\bar{g}}_{ij} = 0,\;\text{ on } - \infty  < t < 0,
\]

everywhere for some function \( f \) . Differentiating the equation (6.2.24) and switching the order of differentiations, as in the derivation of (1.1.14), we get

(6.2.25)

\[
{\nabla }_{i}\bar{R} = 2{\bar{R}}_{ij}{\nabla }_{j}f.
\]

Fix some \( t < 0 \) , say \( t =  - 1 \) , and consider a long shortest geodesic \( \gamma \left( s\right) ,0 \leq  s \leq  \bar{s} \) . Let \( {x}_{0} = \gamma \left( 0\right) \) and \( X\left( s\right)  = \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \) . Let \( V\left( 0\right) \) be any unit vector orthogonal to \( \dot{\gamma }\left( 0\right) \) and translate \( V\left( 0\right) \) along \( \gamma \left( s\right) \) to get a parallel vector field \( V\left( s\right) ,0 \leq  s \leq  \bar{s} \) on \( \gamma \) . Set

\[
\widehat{V}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} {sV}\left( s\right) , & \text{ for }0 \leq  s \leq  1, \\  V\left( s\right) , & \text{ for }1 \leq  s \leq  \bar{s} - 1, \\  \left( {\bar{s} - s}\right) V\left( s\right) , & \text{ for }\bar{s} - 1 \leq  s \leq  \bar{s}. \end{array}\right.
\]

It follows from the second variation formula of arclength that

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\bar{s}}\left( {{\left| \dot{\widehat{V}}\left( s\right) \right| }^{2} - \bar{R}\left( {X,\widehat{V}, X,\widehat{V}}\right) }\right) {ds} \geq  0.
\]

Thus we clearly have

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\bar{s}}\bar{R}\left( {X,\widehat{V}, X,\widehat{V}}\right) {ds} \leq  \text{ const., }
\]

and then

(6.2.26)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\bar{s}}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} \leq  \text{ const.. }
\]

By integrating the equation (6.2.24) we get

\[
X\left( {f\left( {\gamma \left( \bar{s}\right) }\right) }\right)  - X\left( {f\left( {\gamma \left( 0\right) }\right) }\right)  + {\int }_{0}^{\bar{s}}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} - \frac{1}{2}\bar{s} = 0
\]

and then by (6.2.26), we deduce

\[
\frac{d}{ds}\left( {f \circ  \gamma \left( s\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{s}{2} - \text{ const. },
\]

\[
\text{ and }f \circ  \gamma \left( s\right)  \geq  \frac{{s}^{2}}{4} - \text{ const. } \cdot  s - \text{ const. }
\]

for \( s > 0 \) large enough. Thus at large distances from the fixed point \( {x}_{0} \) the function \( f \) has no critical points and is proper. It then follows from the Morse theory that any two high level sets of \( f \) are diffeomorphic via the gradient curves of \( f \) . Since by (6.2.25),

\[
\frac{d}{ds}\bar{R}\left( {\eta \left( s\right) , - 1}\right)  = \langle \nabla \bar{R},\dot{\eta }\left( s\right) \rangle
\]

\[
= 2{\bar{R}}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f
\]

\[
\geq  0
\]

for any integral curve \( \eta \left( s\right) \) of \( \nabla f \) , we conclude that the scalar curvature \( \bar{R}\left( {x, - 1}\right) \) has a positive lower bound on \( \bar{M} \) , which contradicts the Bonnet-Myers Theorem. So we have proved that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton is compact.

By Proposition 5.1.10, the compact limiting gradient shrinking soliton has constant curvature. This says that the scalings of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) along a sequence of points \( {q}_{k} \in  M \) and a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   - \infty \) converge in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology to the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) or the round \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \) . In particular, by looking at the time derivative of the volume and the Gauss-Bonnet theorem, we know that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) exists on a maximal time interval \( \left( {-\infty , T}\right) \) with \( T <  + \infty \) .

Consider the scaled entropy of Hamilton [60]

\[
E\left( t\right)  = {\int }_{M}R\log \left\lbrack  {R\left( {T - t}\right) }\right\rbrack  d{V}_{t}
\]

We compute

(6.2.27)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}E\left( t\right)  = {\int }_{M}\log \left\lbrack  {R\left( {T - t}\right) }\right\rbrack  {\Delta Rd}{V}_{t} + {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {{\Delta R} + {R}^{2} - \frac{R}{\left( T - t\right) }}\right\rbrack  d{V}_{t}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} + {R}^{2} - {rR}}\right\rbrack  d{V}_{t}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} + {\left( R - r\right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack  d{V}_{t}
\]

where \( r = {\int }_{M}{Rd}{V}_{t}/{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( M\right) \) and we have used \( {\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( M\right)  = \left( {{\int }_{M}{Rd}{V}_{t}}\right)  \cdot  \left( {T - t}\right) \) (by the Gauss-Bonnet theorem).

For a smooth function \( f \) on the surface \( M \) , one can readily check

\[
{\int }_{M}{\left( \Delta f\right) }^{2} = 2{\int }_{M}{\left| {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2}\left( \Delta f\right) {g}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + {\int }_{M}R{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2},
\]

\[
{\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R + R\nabla f\right| }^{2}}{R} = {\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} - 2{\int }_{M}R\left( {\Delta f}\right)  + {\int }_{M}R{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2},
\]

and then

\[
{\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} + {\int }_{M}\left( {\Delta f}\right) \left( {{\Delta f} - {2R}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{\int }_{M}{\left| {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2}\left( \Delta f\right) {g}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + {\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R + R\nabla f\right| }^{2}}{R}.
\]

By choosing \( {\Delta f} = R - r \) , we get

\[
{\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} - {\int }_{M}{\left( R - r\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
= 2{\int }_{M}{\left| {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2}\left( \Delta f\right) {g}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + {\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R + R\nabla f\right| }^{2}}{R} \geq  0.
\]

If the equality holds, then we have

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\Delta f}\right) {g}_{ij} = 0
\]

i.e., \( \nabla f \) is conformal. By the Kazdan-Warner identity [77], it follows that

\[
{\int }_{M}\nabla R \cdot  \nabla f = 0
\]

so

\[
0 =  - {\int }_{M}{R\Delta f}
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{M}{\left( R - r\right) }^{2}.
\]

Hence we have proved the following inequality due to Chow [37]

(6.2.28)

\[
{\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} \geq  {\int }_{M}{\left( R - r\right) }^{2}
\]

and the equality holds if and only if \( R \equiv  r \) .

The combination (6.2.27) and (6.2.28) shows that the scaled entropy \( E\left( t\right) \) is strictly decreasing along the Ricci flow unless we are on the round sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) or its quotient \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \) . Moreover the convergence result in Theorem 5.1.11 shows that the scaled entropy \( E \) has its minimum value at the constant curvature metric (round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) or round \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \) ). We had shown that the scalings of the nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution along a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   - \infty \) converge to the constant curvature metric. Then \( E\left( t\right) \) has its minimal value at \( t =  - \infty \) , so it was constant all along, hence the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution must have constant curvature for each \( t \in  \left( {-\infty , T}\right) \) . This proves the theorem.

LEMMA 6.3.1. Let \( M \) be an \( n \) -dimensional complete noncompact Riemannian manifold. Suppose \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) , x \in  M \) and \( t \in  \left( {-\infty , T}\right) \) with \( T > 0 \) , is a nonflat ancient solution of the Ricci flow with nonnegative curvature operator and bounded curvature. Then the asymptotic volume ratio of the solution metric satisfies

\[
{\nu }_{M}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{r \rightarrow   + \infty }}\frac{{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {O, r}\right) }\right) }{{r}^{n}} = 0
\]

for each \( t \in  \left( {-\infty , T}\right) \) .
