nodes.content:
CLAIM. For the above fixed \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , one can find \( K = K\left( {A,\varepsilon }\right)  <  + \infty \) such that if we have a three-dimensional complete orientable solution with normalized initial metric and satisfying

\[
\left| {Rm}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {r}_{0}^{-2}\text{ for }0 \leq  t \leq  {r}_{0}^{2},{d}_{0}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {r}_{0},
\]

and

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{0}\left( {{B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {A}^{-1}{r}_{0}^{3}
\]

for some \( {x}_{0} \in  M \) and some \( {r}_{0} > 0 \) , then for any point \( x \in  M \) with \( {d}_{{r}_{0}^{2}}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  < {3A}{r}_{0} \) , either

\[
R\left( {x,{r}_{0}^{2}}\right)  < K{r}_{0}^{-2}
\]

or the subset \( \left\{  {\left( {y, t}\right)  \mid  {d}_{{r}_{0}^{2}}^{2}\left( {y, x}\right)  \leq  {\varepsilon }^{-2}R{\left( x,{r}_{0}^{2}\right) }^{-1},{r}_{0}^{2} - {\varepsilon }^{-2}R{\left( x,{r}_{0}^{2}\right) }^{-1} \leq  t \leq  {r}_{0}^{2}}\right\} \) around the point \( \left( {x,{r}_{0}^{2}}\right) \) is \( \varepsilon \) -close to the corresponding subset of an orientable ancient \( \kappa \) - solution.

Notice that in this assertion we don’t impose the restriction of \( {r}_{0} < \alpha \) , so we can consider for the moment \( {r}_{0} > 0 \) to be arbitrary in proving the above claim. Note that the assumption on the normalization of the initial metric is just to ensure the pinching estimate. By scaling, we may assume \( {r}_{0} = 1 \) . The proof of the claim is essentially adapted from that of Theorem 7.1.1. But we will meet the difficulties of adjusting points and verifying a local curvature estimate.

Suppose that the claim is not true. Then there exist a sequence of solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) to the Ricci flow satisfying the assumptions of the claim with the origins \( {x}_{{0}_{k}} \) , and a sequence of positive numbers \( {K}_{k} \rightarrow  \infty \) , times \( {t}_{k} = 1 \) and points \( {x}_{k} \in \; {M}_{k} \) with \( {d}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  < {3A} \) such that \( {Q}_{k} = {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \geq  {K}_{k} \) and the solution in \( \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  {t}_{k} - C\left( \varepsilon \right) {Q}_{k}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{k},{d}_{{t}_{k}}^{2}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right)  \leq  C\left( \varepsilon \right) {Q}_{k}^{-1}}\right\} \) is not, after scaling by the factor \( {Q}_{k},\varepsilon \) -close to the corresponding subset of any orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, where \( {R}_{k} \) denotes the scalar curvature of \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) and \( C\left( \varepsilon \right) \left( { \geq  {\varepsilon }^{-2}}\right) \) is the constant defined in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1. As before we need to first adjust the point \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{k} \geq  \frac{1}{2} \) and \( {d}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  < {4A} \) so that \( {Q}_{k} = {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \geq  {K}_{k} \) and the conclusion of the claim fails at \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , but holds for any \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) satisfying \( {R}_{k}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq \; 2{Q}_{k},{t}_{k} - {H}_{k}{Q}_{k}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{k} \) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  < {d}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  + {H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , where \( {H}_{k} = \; \frac{1}{4}{K}_{k} \rightarrow  \infty \) , as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) .

Indeed, by starting with \( \left( {{x}_{{k}_{1}},{t}_{{k}_{1}}}\right)  = \left( {{x}_{k},1}\right) \) we can choose \( \left( {{x}_{{k}_{2}},{t}_{{k}_{2}}}\right)  \in  {M}_{k} \times \; (0,1\rbrack \) with \( {t}_{{k}_{1}} - {H}_{k}{R}_{k}{\left( {x}_{{k}_{1}},{t}_{{k}_{1}}\right) }^{-1} \leq  {t}_{{k}_{2}} \leq  {t}_{{k}_{1}} \) , and \( {d}_{{t}_{{k}_{2}}}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{2}},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  < {d}_{{t}_{{k}_{1}}}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{1}},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  + \; {H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{R}_{k}{\left( {x}_{{k}_{1}},{t}_{{k}_{1}}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) such that \( {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{2}},{t}_{{k}_{2}}}\right)  \geq  2{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{1}},{t}_{{k}_{1}}}\right) \) and the conclusion of the claim fails at \( \left( {{x}_{{k}_{2}},{t}_{{k}_{2}}}\right) \) ; otherwise we have the desired point. Repeating this process, we can choose points \( \left( {{x}_{{k}_{i}},{t}_{{k}_{i}}}\right) , i = 2,\ldots , j \) , such that

\[
{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{i}},{t}_{{k}_{i}}}\right)  \geq  2{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{i - 1}},{t}_{{k}_{i - 1}}}\right)
\]

\[
{t}_{{k}_{i - 1}} - {H}_{k}{R}_{k}{\left( {x}_{{k}_{i - 1}},{t}_{{k}_{i - 1}}\right) }^{-1} \leq  {t}_{{k}_{i}} \leq  {t}_{{k}_{i - 1}},
\]

\[
{d}_{{t}_{{k}_{i}}}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{i}},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  < {d}_{{t}_{{k}_{i - 1}}}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{i - 1}},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  + {H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{R}_{k}{\left( {x}_{{k}_{i - 1}},{t}_{{k}_{i - 1}}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}},
\]

and the conclusion of the claim fails at the points \( \left( {{x}_{{k}_{i}},{t}_{{k}_{i}}}\right) , i = 2,\ldots , j \) . These inequalities imply

\[
{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{j}},{t}_{{k}_{j}}}\right)  \geq  {2}^{j - 1}{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{1}},{t}_{{k}_{1}}}\right)  \geq  {2}^{j - 1}{K}_{k}
\]

\[
1 \geq  {t}_{{k}_{j}} \geq  {t}_{{k}_{1}} - {H}_{k}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{{j - 2}}\frac{1}{{2}^{i}}{R}_{k}{\left( {x}_{{k}_{1}},{t}_{{k}_{1}}\right) }^{-1} \geq  \frac{1}{2},
\]

and

\[
{d}_{{t}_{{k}_{j}}}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{j}},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  < {d}_{{t}_{{k}_{1}}}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{1}},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  + {H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{i = 0}}^{{j - 2}}\frac{1}{{\left( \sqrt{2}\right) }^{i}}{R}_{k}{\left( {x}_{{k}_{1}},{t}_{{k}_{1}}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} < {4A}.
\]

Since the solutions are smooth, this process must terminate after a finite number of steps to give the desired point, still denoted by \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) .

For each adjusted \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , let \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) be the maximal subinterval of \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - }\right. \; \left. {\frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) so that the conclusion of the claim with \( K = 2{Q}_{k} \) holds on

\[
P\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k},\frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}},{t}^{\prime } - {t}_{k}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  x \in  {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},\frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack  }\right\}
\]

for all sufficiently large \( k \) . We now want to show \( {t}^{\prime } = {t}_{k} - \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-1} \) .

Consider the scalar curvature \( {R}_{k} \) at the point \( {x}_{k} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) . If there is a time \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) satisfying \( {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k},\widetilde{t}}\right)  \geq  2{Q}_{k} \) , we let \( \widetilde{t} \) be the first of such time from \( {t}_{k} \) . Then the solution \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) around the point \( {x}_{k} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-1},\widetilde{t}}\right\rbrack \) is \( \varepsilon \) -close to some orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. Note from the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality that the scalar curvature of any ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is pointwise nondecreasing in time. Consequently, we have the following curvature estimate

\[
{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k}, t}\right)  \leq  2\left( {1 + \varepsilon }\right) {Q}_{k}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) if there is no such time \( \widetilde{t} \) ). By combining with the elliptic type estimate for ancient \( \kappa \) -solutions (Theorem 6.4.3) and the Hamilton-Ivey pinching estimate, we further have

(7.2.1)

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {5\omega }\left( 1\right) {Q}_{k}
\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},{\left( 3{Q}_{k}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) ) and all sufficiently large \( k \) , where \( \omega \) is the positive function in Theorem 6.4.3.

For any point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) with \( \widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{k} \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) ) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right)  \leq \; \frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , we divide the discussion into two cases.

Case (1): \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) .

(7.2.2)

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  \leq  {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right)  + {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} + \frac{3}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{2}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}.
\]

Case (2): \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  > \frac{3}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) .

From the curvature bound (7.2.1) and the assumption, we apply Lemma 3.4.1(ii) with \( {r}_{0} = {Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) to get

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left( {{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right) }\right)  \geq   - {20}\left( {\omega \left( 1\right)  + 1}\right) {Q}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}},
\]

and then for \( k \) large enough,

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  \leq  {d}_{\widehat{t}}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  + {20}\left( {\omega \left( 1\right)  + 1}\right) {\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}
\]

\[
\leq  {d}_{\widehat{t}}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  + \frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}},
\]

where \( \widehat{t} \in  \left( {t,{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) satisfies the property that \( {d}_{s}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  \geq  \frac{3}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) whenever \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {t,\widehat{t}}\right\rbrack \) . So we have

(7.2.3)

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  \leq  {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right)  + {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}} + {d}_{\widehat{t}}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  + \frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}
\]

\[
\leq  {d}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{x}_{k},{x}_{{0}_{k}}}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}},
\]

for all sufficiently large \( k \) . Then the combination of (7.2.2),(7.2.3) and the choice of the points \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) implies \( {t}^{\prime } = {t}_{k} - \frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-1} \) for all sufficiently large \( k \) . (Here we also used the maximality of the subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) in the case that there is no time in \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) with \( {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k}, \cdot  }\right)  \geq  2{Q}_{k} \) .)

Now we rescale the solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) into \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) around the points \( {x}_{k} \) by the factors \( {Q}_{k} = {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) and shift the times \( {t}_{k} \) to the new times zero. Then the same arguments from Step 1 to Step 3 in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1 prove that a subsequence of the rescaled solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a limiting (complete) solution \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) , which is defined on a backward time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-a,0}\right\rbrack \) for some \( a > 0 \) . (The only modification is in Lemma 7.1.2 of Step 1 by further requiring \( {t}_{k} - \frac{1}{4}{\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}_{k}^{-1} \leq  \bar{t} \leq  {t}_{k} \) ).

We next study how to adapt the argument of Step 4 in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1. As before, we have a maximal time interval \( \left( {{t}_{\infty },0}\right\rbrack \) for which we can take a smooth limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) from a subsequence of the rescaled solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) ,{x}_{k}}\right) \) . We want to show \( {t}_{\infty } =  - \infty \) .

Suppose not; then \( {t}_{\infty } >  - \infty \) . Let \( c > 0 \) be a positive constant much smaller than \( \frac{1}{10}{\varepsilon }^{-2} \) . Note that the infimum of the scalar curvature is nondecreasing in time. Then we can find some point \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and some time \( t = {t}_{\infty } + \theta \) with \( 0 < \theta  < \frac{c}{3} \) such that \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty } + \theta }\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) .

Consider the (unrescaled) scalar curvature \( {R}_{k} \) of \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) at the point \( {x}_{k} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) . Since the scalar curvature \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty } \) of the limit on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{3},0}\right\rbrack \) is uniformly bounded by some positive constant \( C \) , we have the curvature estimate

\[
{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k}, t}\right)  \leq  {2C}{Q}_{k}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) and all sufficiently large \( k \) . Then by repeating the same arguments as in deriving (7.2.1), (7.2.2) and (7.2.3), we deduce that the conclusion of the claim with \( K = 2{Q}_{k} \) holds on the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k},\frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}},\left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1}}\right) \) for all sufficiently large \( k \) .

Let \( \left( {{y}_{k},{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{k}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1}}\right) \) be a sequence of associated points and times in the (unrescaled) solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) so that after rescaling, the sequence converges to the \( \left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty } + \theta }\right) \) in the limit. Clearly \( \frac{\theta }{2} \leq  {\theta }_{k} \leq  {2\theta } \) for all sufficiently large \( k \) . Then, by considering the scalar curvature \( {\bar{R}}_{k} \) at the point \( {y}_{k} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{3}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{k}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) , the above argument (as in deriving the similar estimates (7.2.1)-(7.2.3)) implies that the conclusion of the claim with \( K = 2{Q}_{k} \) holds on the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{y}_{k},{t}_{k},\frac{1}{10}{H}_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}{Q}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}},\left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{3}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1}}\right) \) for all sufficiently large \( k \) . In particular, we have the curvature estimate

\[
{R}_{k}\left( {{y}_{k}, t}\right)  \leq  4\left( {1 + \varepsilon }\right) {Q}_{k}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{3}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{k}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) for all sufficiently large \( k \) .

We now consider the rescaled sequence \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) with the marked points replaced by \( {y}_{k} \) and the times replaced by \( {s}_{k} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{4}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{c}{4}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) . By applying the same arguments from Step 1 to Step 3 in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1 and the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality as in Step 4 of Theorem 7.1.1, we conclude that there is some small constant \( {a}^{\prime } > 0 \) such that the original limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) is actually well defined on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{\infty } - {a}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) with uniformly bounded curvature. This is a contradiction. Therefore we have checked the claim.

THEOREM 7.2.2 (Perelman [103]). For any \( w > 0 \) there exist \( \tau  = \tau \left( w\right)  > 0 \) , \( K = K\left( w\right)  <  + \infty ,\alpha  = \alpha \left( w\right)  > 0 \) with the following property. Suppose we have a three-dimensional, compact and orientable solution to the Ricci flow defined on \( M \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with normalized initial metric. Suppose that for some radius \( {r}_{0} > 0 \) with \( {r}_{0} < \alpha \) and a point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  M \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T > {t}_{0} \geq  {4\tau }{r}_{0}^{2} \) , the solution on the ball \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) satisfies

\[
\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq   - {r}_{0}^{-2}\;\text{ on }{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) ,
\]

\[
\text{ and }{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  w{r}_{0}^{3}\text{ . }
\]

Then \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  K{r}_{0}^{-2} \) whenever \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \tau {r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{r}_{0} \) .

nodes.proof:
If we knew that

\[
\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq   - {r}_{0}^{-2}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {r}_{0} \) , then we could just apply Theorem 6.3.3 (ii) and take \( \tau \left( w\right)  = {\tau }_{0}\left( w\right) /2, K\left( w\right)  = C\left( w\right)  + {2B}\left( w\right) /{\tau }_{0}\left( w\right) \) . Now fix these values of \( \tau \) and \( K \) .

We argue by contradiction. Consider a three-dimensional, compact and orientable solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) to the Ricci flow with normalized initial metric, a point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) and some radius \( {r}_{0} > 0 \) with \( {r}_{0} < \alpha \) , for \( \alpha  > 0 \) a sufficiently small constant to be determined later, such that the assumptions of the theorem do hold whereas the conclusion does not. We first claim that we may assume that any other point \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and radius \( {r}^{\prime } > 0 \) with the same property has either \( {t}^{\prime } > {t}_{0} \) or \( {t}^{\prime } < {t}_{0} - {2\tau }{r}_{0}^{2} \) , or \( 2{r}^{\prime } > \; {r}_{0} \) . Indeed, suppose otherwise. Then there exist \( \left( {{x}_{0}^{\prime },{t}_{0}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {r}_{0}^{\prime } \) with \( {t}_{0}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {2\tau }{r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and \( {r}_{0}^{\prime } \leq  \frac{1}{2}{r}_{0} \) , for which the assumptions of the theorem hold but the conclusion does not. Thus, there is a point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) such that

\[
t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}^{\prime } - \tau {\left( {r}_{0}^{\prime }\right) }^{2},{t}_{0}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack   \subset  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {2\tau }{r}_{0}^{2} - \frac{\tau }{4}{r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\text{ and }R\left( {x, t}\right)  > K{\left( {r}_{0}^{\prime }\right) }^{-2} \geq  {4K}{r}_{0}^{-2}\text{ . }
\]

If the point \( \left( {{x}_{0}^{\prime },{t}_{0}^{\prime }}\right) \) and the radius \( {r}_{0}^{\prime } \) satisfy the claim then we stop, and otherwise we iterate the procedure. Since \( {t}_{0} \geq  {4\tau }{r}_{0}^{2} \) and the solution is smooth, the iteration must terminate in a finite number of steps, which provides the desired point and the desired radius.

Let \( {\tau }^{\prime } \geq  0 \) be the largest number such that

(7.2.5)

\[
\operatorname{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq   - {r}_{0}^{-2}
\]

whenever \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\tau }^{\prime }{r}_{0}^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {r}_{0} \) . If \( {\tau }^{\prime } \geq  {2\tau } \) , we are done by Theorem 6.3.3 (ii). Thus we may assume \( {\tau }^{\prime } < {2\tau } \) . By applying Theorem 6.3.3(ii), we know that at time \( {t}^{\prime } = {t}_{0} - {\tau }^{\prime }{r}_{0}^{2} \) , the ball \( {B}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) has

(7.2.6)

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{B}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \xi \left( w\right) {r}_{0}^{3}
\]

for some positive constant \( \xi \left( w\right) \) depending only on \( w \) . We next claim that there exists a ball (at time \( {t}^{\prime } = {t}_{0} - {\tau }^{\prime }{r}_{0}^{2} \) ) \( {B}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}^{\prime },{r}^{\prime }}\right)  \subset  {B}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) with

(7.2.7)

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{B}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {{x}^{\prime },{r}^{\prime }}\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{1}{2}{\alpha }_{3}{\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{3}
\]

and with

(7.2.8)

\[
\frac{{r}_{0}}{2} > {r}^{\prime } \geq  c\left( w\right) {r}_{0}
\]

for some small positive constant \( c\left( w\right) \) depending only on \( w \) , where \( {\alpha }_{3} \) is the volume of the unit ball \( {\mathbb{B}}^{3} \) in the Euclidean space \( {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \) .

Indeed, suppose that it is not true. Then after rescaling, there is a sequence of Riemannian manifolds \( {M}_{i}, i = 1,2,\ldots \) , with balls \( B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right)  \subset  {M}_{i} \) so that

(7.2.5)

\[
{Rm} \geq   - 1\text{ on }B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right)
\]

and

(7.2.6)

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) }\right)  \geq  \xi \left( w\right)
\]

for all \( i \) , but all balls \( B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime }}\right)  \subset  B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) \) with \( \frac{1}{2} > {r}_{i}^{\prime } \geq  \frac{1}{i} \) satisfy

(7.2.9)

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {B\left( {{x}_{i}^{\prime },{r}_{i}^{\prime }}\right) }\right)  < \frac{1}{2}{\alpha }_{3}{\left( {r}_{i}^{\prime }\right) }^{3}.
\]

It follows from basic results in Alexandrov space theory (see for example Theorem 10.7.2 and Theorem 10.10.10 of [9]) that, after taking a subsequence, the marked balls \( \left( {B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) ,{x}_{i}}\right) \) converge in the Gromov-Hausdorff topology to a marked length space \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) with curvature bounded from below by -1 in the Alexandrov space sense, and the associated Riemannian volume forms \( d{\mathrm{{Vol}}}_{{M}_{i}} \) over \( \left( {B\left( {{x}_{i},1}\right) ,{x}_{i}}\right) \) converge weakly to the Hausdorff measure \( \mu \) of \( {B}_{\infty } \) . It is well-known that the Hausdorff dimension of any Alexandrov space is either an integer or infinity (see for example Theorem 10.8.2 of [9]). Then by \( {\left( {7.2.6}\right) }^{\prime } \) , we know the limit \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) is a three-dimensional Alexandrov space of curvature \( \geq   - 1 \) . In the Alexandrov space theory, a point \( p \in  {B}_{\infty } \) is said to be regular if the tangent cone of \( {B}_{\infty } \) at \( p \) is isometric to \( {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \) . It is also a basic result in Alexandrov space theory (see for example Corollary 10.9.13 of [9]) that the set of regular points in \( {B}_{\infty } \) is dense and for each regular point there is a small neighborhood which is almost isometric to an open set of the Euclidean space \( {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \) . Thus for any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there are balls \( B\left( {{x}_{\infty }^{\prime },{r}_{\infty }^{\prime }}\right)  \subset  {B}_{\infty } \) with \( 0 < {r}_{\infty }^{\prime } < \frac{1}{3} \) and satisfying

\[
\mu \left( {B\left( {{x}_{\infty }^{\prime },{r}_{\infty }^{\prime }}\right) }\right)  \geq  \left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) {\alpha }_{3}{\left( {r}_{\infty }^{\prime }\right) }^{3}.
\]

This is a contradiction with (7.2.9).

Without loss of generality, we may assume \( w \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\alpha }_{3} \) . Since \( {\tau }^{\prime } < {2\tau } \) , it follows from the choice of the point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) and the radius \( {r}_{0} \) and (7.2.5),(7.2.7),(7.2.8) that the conclusion of the theorem holds for \( \left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right) \) and \( {r}^{\prime } \) . Thus we have the estimate

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  K{\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{-2}
\]

whenever \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \tau {\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{2},{t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{r}^{\prime } \) . For \( \alpha  > 0 \) small, by combining with the pinching estimate (7.1.1), we have

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {K}^{\prime }{\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{-2}
\]

whenever \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \tau {\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{2},{t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{r}^{\prime } \) , where \( {K}^{\prime } \) is some positive constant depending only on \( K \) . Note that this curvature estimate implies the evolving metrics are equivalent over a suitable subregion of \( \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \tau {\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{2},{t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack  }\right. \) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq \; \left. {\frac{1}{4}{r}^{\prime }}\right\} \) . Now we can apply Theorem 7.2.1 to choose \( \alpha  = \alpha \left( w\right)  > 0 \) so small that

(7.2.10)

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{K}\left( w\right) {\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{-2} \leq  \widetilde{K}\left( w\right) c{\left( w\right) }^{-2}{r}_{0}^{-2}
\]

whenever \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \frac{\tau }{2}{\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{2},{t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}^{\prime }}\right)  \leq  {10}{r}_{0} \) . Then the combination of (7.2.10) with the pinching estimate (7.1.2) would imply

\[
{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq   - \left\lbrack  {{f}^{-1}\left( {R\left( {x, t}\right) \left( {1 + t}\right) }\right) /\left( {R\left( {x, t}\right) \left( {1 + t}\right) }\right) }\right\rbrack  R\left( {x, t}\right)
\]

\[
\geq   - \frac{1}{2}{r}_{0}^{-2}
\]

on the region \( \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \frac{\tau }{2}{\left( {r}^{\prime }\right) }^{2},{t}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack  \text{ and }{d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {r}_{0}}\right\} \) when \( \alpha  = \alpha \left( w\right)  > {r}_{0} \) small enough. This contradicts the choice of \( {\tau }^{\prime } \) . Therefore we have proved the theorem.

We argue by contradiction. Suppose for any \( \rho  > 0 \) , there is a solution and a ball \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{r}_{0}}\right) \) satisfying the assumption of the corollary with \( {r}_{0} < \rho ,{t}_{0} \geq  1 \) , and with

\[

\]

\[
\geq   - \frac{1}{2}{r}_{0}^{-2}
\]

in the region \( \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \tau {\left( {r}_{0}\right) }^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  \text{ and }{d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  2{r}_{0}}\right\} \) . In particular, this would imply

\]

nodes.content: DEFINITION 7.3.1. Suppose we are given a (finite or countably infinite) collection of three-dimensional smooth solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{k}\left( t\right) \) to the Ricci flow defined on \( {M}_{k} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k}^{ - },{t}_{k}^{ + }}\right) \) and go singular as \( t \rightarrow  {t}_{k}^{ + } \) , where each manifold \( {M}_{k} \) is compact and orientable, possibly disconnected with only a finite number of connected components. Let \( \left( {{\Omega }_{k},{\bar{g}}_{ij}^{k}}\right) \) be the limits of the corresponding solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{k}\left( t\right) \) as \( t \rightarrow  {t}_{k}^{ + } \) , as above. Suppose also that for each \( k \) we have \( {t}_{k}^{ - } = {t}_{k - 1}^{ + } \) , and that \( \left( {{\Omega }_{k - 1},{\bar{g}}_{ij}^{k - 1}}\right) \) and \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{ij}^{k}\left( {t}_{k}^{ - }\right) }\right) \) contain compact (possibly disconnected) three-dimensional submanifolds with smooth boundary which are isometric. Then by identifying these isometric submanifolds, we say the collection of solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{k}\left( t\right) \) is a solution to the Ricci flow with surgery (or a surgically modified solution to the Ricci flow) on the time interval which is the union of all \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k}^{ - },{t}_{k}^{ + }}\right) \) , and say the times \( {t}_{k}^{ + } \) are surgery times.

nodes.content:
Canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ). For any given \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exist positive constants \( {C}_{1} \) and \( {C}_{2} \) depending only on \( \varepsilon \) , and a nonincreasing positive function \( r : \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \rightarrow  \left( {0, + \infty }\right) \) such that at each time \( t > 0 \) , every point \( x \) where scalar curvature \( R\left( {x, t}\right) \) is at least \( {r}^{-2}\left( t\right) \) has a neighborhood \( B \) , with \( {B}_{t}\left( {x,\sigma }\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{t}\left( {x,{2\sigma }}\right) \) for some \( 0 < \sigma  < {C}_{1}{R}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( {x, t}\right) \) , which falls into one of the following three categories:

(a) \( B \) is a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck (in the sense \( B \) is the slice at time \( t \) of the parabolic neighborhood \( \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  B,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {t - R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-1}, t}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) , where the solution is well defined on the whole parabolic neighborhood and is, after scaling with factor \( R\left( {x, t}\right) \) and shifting the time to zero, \( \varepsilon \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\varepsilon }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the subset \( \left( {{\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{I}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-1,0}\right\rbrack \) of the evolving standard round cylinder with scalar curvature 1 to \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) and length \( 2{\varepsilon }^{-1} \) to \( \mathbb{I} \) at time zero), or

(b) \( B \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -cap, or

(c) \( B \) is a compact manifold (without boundary) of positive sectional curvature. Furthermore, the scalar curvature in \( B \) at time \( t \) is between \( {C}_{2}^{-1}R\left( {x, t}\right) \) and \( {C}_{2}R\left( {x, t}\right) \) , satisfies the gradient estimates

(7.3.4)

\[
\left| {\nabla R}\right|  < \eta {R}^{\frac{3}{2}}\text{ and }\left| \frac{\partial R}{\partial t}\right|  < \eta {R}^{2},
\]

and the volume of \( B \) in case (a) and case (b) satisfies

\[
{\left( {C}_{2}R\left( x, t\right) \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}} \leq  {\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( B\right)  \leq  \varepsilon {\sigma }^{3}.
\]

Here \( \eta \) is a universal positive constant.

nodes.content:
Lemma 7.3.2 (Perelman [104]). Given \( 0 < \varepsilon  \leq  \frac{1}{100},0 < \delta  < \varepsilon \) and \( 0 < T <  + \infty \) , there exists a radius \( 0 < h < {\delta \rho } \) , depending only on \( \delta \) and \( r\left( T\right) \) , such that if we have a solution to the Ricci flow with surgery, with a normalized metric as initial data, satisfying the a priori assumptions (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ), defined on \( \lbrack 0, T \) ), going singular at time \( T \) and having only a finite number of surgery times on \( \lbrack 0, T) \) , then for each point \( x \) with \( h\left( x\right)  = {\bar{R}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\left( x\right)  \leq  h \) in an \( \varepsilon \) -horn of \( \left( {\Omega ,{\bar{g}}_{ij}}\right) \) with boundary in \( {\Omega }_{\rho } \) , the neighborhood \( {B}_{T}\left( {x,{\delta }^{-1}h\left( x\right) }\right)  \triangleq  \left\{  {y \in  \Omega  \mid  {d}_{T}\left( {y, x}\right)  \leq  {\delta }^{-1}h\left( x\right) }\right\} \) is a strong \( \delta \) -neck (i.e., \( {B}_{T}\left( {x,{\delta }^{-1}h\left( x\right) }\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {T - {h}^{2}\left( x\right) , T}\right\rbrack \) is, after scaling with factor \( {h}^{-2}\left( x\right) ,\delta \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\delta }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the evolving standard round cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-1,0}\right\rbrack \) with scalar curvature 1 at time zero).

nodes.proof:
We argue by contradiction. Suppose that there exists a sequence of solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) , k = 1,2,\ldots \) , to the Ricci flow with surgery, satisfying the a priori assumptions (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ), defined on \( \lbrack 0, T \) ) with limit metrics \( \left( {{\Omega }^{k},{\bar{g}}_{ij}^{k}}\right) , k = 1,2,\ldots \) , and points \( {x}^{k} \) , lying inside an \( \varepsilon \) -horn of \( {\Omega }^{k} \) with boundary in \( {\Omega }_{\rho }^{k} \) , and having \( h\left( {x}^{k}\right)  \rightarrow  0 \) such that the neighborhoods \( {B}_{T}\left( {{x}^{k},{\delta }^{-1}h\left( {x}^{k}\right) }\right)  = \left\{  {y \in  {\Omega }^{k} \mid  {d}_{T}\left( {y,{x}^{k}}\right)  \leq  {\delta }^{-1}h\left( {x}^{k}\right) }\right\} \) are not strong \( \delta \) -necks.

Let \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) be the solutions obtained by rescaling by the factor \( \bar{R}\left( {x}^{k}\right)  = {h}^{-2}\left( {x}^{k}\right) \) around \( {x}^{k} \) and shifting the time \( T \) to the new time zero. We now want to show that a subsequence of \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) , k = 1,2,\ldots \) , converges to the evolving round cylinder, which will give a contradiction.

Note that \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) , k = 1,2,\ldots \) , are solutions modified by surgery. So, we cannot apply Hamilton's compactness theorem directly since it is stated only for smooth solutions. For each (unrescaled) surgical solution \( {\bar{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) , we pick a point \( {z}^{k} \) , with \( \bar{R}\left( {z}^{k}\right)  = 2{C}_{2}^{2}\left( \varepsilon \right) {\rho }^{-2} \) , in the \( \varepsilon \) -horn of \( \left( {{\Omega }^{k},{\bar{g}}_{ij}^{k}}\right) \) with boundary in \( {\Omega }_{\rho }^{k} \) , where \( {C}_{2}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) is the positive constant in the canonical neighborhood assumption. From the definition of \( \varepsilon \) -horn and the canonical neighborhood assumption, we know that each point \( x \) lying inside the \( \varepsilon \) -horn of \( \left( {{\Omega }^{k},{\bar{g}}_{ij}^{k}}\right) \) with \( {d}_{{\bar{g}}_{ij}^{k}}\left( {x,{\Omega }_{\rho }^{k}}\right)  \geq  {d}_{{\bar{g}}_{ij}^{k}}\left( {{z}^{k},{\Omega }_{\rho }^{k}}\right) \) has a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck as its canonical neighborhood. Since \( h\left( {x}^{k}\right)  \rightarrow  0 \) , each \( {x}^{k} \) lies deeply inside an \( \varepsilon \) -horn. Thus for each positive \( A <  + \infty \) , the rescaled (surgical) solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) with the marked origins \( {x}^{k} \) over the geodesic balls \( {B}_{{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\left( {{x}^{k}, A}\right) \) , centered at \( {x}^{k} \) of radii \( A \) (with respect to the metrics \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) \) ), will be smooth on some uniform (size) small time intervals for all sufficiently large \( k \) , if the curvatures of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k} \) at \( t = 0 \) in \( {B}_{{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\left( {{x}^{k}, A}\right) \) are uniformly bounded. In such a situation, Hamilton’s compactness theorem is applicable. Then we can apply the same argument as in the second step of the proof of Theorem 7.1.1 to conclude that for each \( A <  + \infty \) , there exists a positive constant \( C\left( A\right) \) such that the curvatures of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at the new time 0 satisfy the estimate

\[
\left| {\widetilde{R}{m}_{k}}\right| \left( {y,0}\right)  \leq  C\left( A\right)
\]

whenever \( {d}_{{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\left( {y,{x}^{k}}\right)  \leq  A \) and \( k \geq  1 \) ; otherwise we would get a piece of a non-flat nonnegatively curved metric cone as a blow-up limit, which contradicts Hamilton's strong maximum principle. Moreover, by Hamilton's compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5), a subsequence of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) converges to a \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) limit \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) , defined on a spacetime set which is relatively open in the half spacetime \( \{ t \leq  0\} \) and contains the time slice \( t = 0 \) .

By the pinching assumption, the limit is a complete manifold with nonnegative sectional curvature. Since \( {x}^{k} \) was contained in an \( \varepsilon \) -horn with boundary in \( {\Omega }_{\rho }^{k} \) and \( h\left( {x}^{k}\right) /\rho  \rightarrow  0 \) , the limiting manifold has two ends. Thus, by Toponogov’s splitting theorem, the limiting manifold admits a metric splitting \( {\sum }^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) , where \( {\sum }^{2} \) is diffeomorphic to the two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) because \( {x}^{k} \) was the center of a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck.

By combining with the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ), we see that the limit is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-1,0}\right\rbrack \) and is \( \varepsilon \) -close to the evolving standard round cylinder. In particular, the scalar curvature of the limit at time \( t =  - 1 \) is \( \varepsilon \) -close to \( 1/2 \) .

Since \( h\left( {x}^{k}\right) /\rho  \rightarrow  0 \) , each point in the limiting manifold at time \( t =  - 1 \) also has a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck as its canonical neighborhood. Thus the limit is defined at least on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-2,0}\right\rbrack \) and the limiting manifold at time \( t =  - 2 \) is, after rescaling, \( \varepsilon \) -close to the standard round cylinder.

By using the canonical neighborhood assumption again, every point in the limiting manifold at time \( t =  - 2 \) still has a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck as its canonical neighborhood. Also note that the scalar curvature of the limit at \( t =  - 2 \) is not bigger than \( 1/2 + \varepsilon \) . Thus the limit is defined at least on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-3,0}\right\rbrack \) and the limiting manifold at time \( t =  - 3 \) is, after rescaling, \( \varepsilon \) -close to the standard round cylinder. By repeating this argument we prove that the limit exists on the ancient time interval \( ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) .

The above argument also shows that at every time, each point of the limit has a strong \( \varepsilon \) -neck as its canonical neighborhood. This implies that the limit is \( \kappa \) - noncollaped on all scales for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) . Therefore, by Theorem 6.2.2, the limit is the evolving round cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) , which gives the desired contradiction.

nodes.content:
PROPOSITION 7.3.3. Let \( {g}_{ij} \) be a complete Riemannian metric on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n}\left( {n \geq  3}\right) \) with nonnegative curvature operator and positive scalar curvature which is asymptotic to a round cylinder of scalar curvature 1 at infinity. Then there is a complete solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) to the Ricci flow, with \( {g}_{ij} \) as initial metric, which exists on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , has bounded curvature at each time \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , and satisfies the estimate

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{{C}^{-1}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}
\]

for some \( C \) depending only on the initial metric \( {g}_{ij} \) .

nodes.proof:
Since the initial metric has bounded curvature operator and a positive lower bound on its scalar curvature, the Ricci flow has a solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) defined on a maximal time interval \( \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( T < \infty \) which has bounded curvature on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\prime }}\right\rbrack \) for each \( 0 < {T}^{\prime } < T \) . By Proposition 2.1.4, the solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) has nonnegative curvature operator for all \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) . Note that the injectivity radius of the initial metric has a positive lower bound. As we remarked at the beginning of Section 3.4, the same proof of Perelman's no local collapsing theorem I concludes that \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales less than \( \sqrt{T} \) for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) depending only on the initial metric.

We will first prove the following assertion.

CLAIM 1. There is a positive function \( \omega  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) depending only on the initial metric and \( \kappa \) such that

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  R\left( {y, t}\right) \omega \left( {R\left( {y, t}\right) {d}_{t}^{2}\left( {x, y}\right) }\right)
\]

for all \( x, y \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n}, t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) .

The proof is similar to that of Theorem 6.4.3. Notice that the initial metric has nonnegative curvature operator and its scalar curvature satisfies the bounds

(7.3.5)

\[
{C}^{-1} \leq  R\left( x\right)  \leq  C
\]

for some positive constant \( C \) . By the maximum principle, we know \( T \geq  \frac{1}{2nC} \) and \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {2C} \) for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{4nC}}\right\rbrack \) . The assertion is clearly true for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{4nC}}\right\rbrack \) .

Now fix \( \left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( {t}_{0} \geq  \frac{1}{4nC} \) . Let \( z \) be the closest point to \( y \) with the property \( R\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right) {d}_{{t}_{0}}^{2}\left( {z, y}\right)  = 1 \) (at time \( {t}_{0} \) ). Draw a shortest geodesic from \( y \) to \( z \) and choose a point \( \widetilde{z} \) on the geodesic satisfying \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,\widetilde{z}}\right)  = \frac{1}{4}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , then we have

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{{\left( \frac{1}{2}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{2}}\;\text{ on }{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {\widetilde{z},\frac{1}{4}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) .
\]

Note that \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  {C}^{-1} \) everywhere by the evolution equation of the scalar curvature. Then by the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5), for all \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in \; {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {\widetilde{z},\frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\left( \frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) , we have

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \left( \frac{{t}_{0}}{{t}_{0} - {\left( \frac{1}{{8n}\sqrt{C}}\right) }^{2}}\right) \frac{1}{{\left( \frac{1}{2}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
\leq  {\left\lbrack  \frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack  }^{-2}.
\]

Combining this with the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing property, we have

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {\widetilde{z},\frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}
\]

and then

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{8R}{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  \kappa {\left( \frac{1}{64nC}\right) }^{n}{\left( 8R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}.
\]

So by Theorem 6.3.3 (ii), we have

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  C\left( \kappa \right) R\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right) \;\text{ for all }x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{4R}{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) .
\]

Here and in the following we denote by \( C\left( \kappa \right) \) various positive constants depending only on \( \kappa , n \) and the initial metric.

Now by the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5) and local gradient estimate of Shi (Theorem 1.4.2), we obtain

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( \kappa \right) R\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right) \text{ and }\left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}R}\right| \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( \kappa \right) {\left( R\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) \right) }^{2}
\]

for all \( \left. {\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {z,{2R}{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\left( \frac{1}{8nC}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . Therefore by combining with the Harnack estimate (Corollary 2.5.7), we obtain

\[
R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}R\left( {z,{t}_{0} - C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}R{\left( z,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-1}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-2}R\left( {z,{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

Consequently, we have showed that there is a constant \( C\left( \kappa \right) \) such that

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y, R{\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}{\left( R{\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}
\]

and

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  C\left( \kappa \right) R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) \;\text{ for all }x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y, R{\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) .
\]

In general, for any \( r \geq  R{\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , we have

\[
\operatorname{Vol}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y, r}\right) }\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}{\left( {r}^{2}R\left( y,{t}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{n}{2}}{r}^{n}.
\]

By applying Theorem 6.3.3(ii) again, there exists a positive constant \( \omega \left( {{r}^{2}R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) \) depending only on the constant \( {r}^{2}R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) \) and \( \kappa \) such that

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{0}}\right)  \leq  R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) \omega \left( {{r}^{2}R\left( {y,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right) \;\text{ for all }x \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {y,\frac{1}{4}r}\right) .
\]

This proves the desired Claim 1.

Now we study the asymptotic behavior of the solution at infinity. For any \( 0 < \; {t}_{0} < T \) , we know that the metrics \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) with \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) has uniformly bounded curvature. Let \( {x}_{k} \) be a sequence of points with \( {d}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{x}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) . After passing to a subsequence, \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) around \( {x}_{k} \) will converge to a solution to the Ricci flow on \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{n - 1} \) with round cylinder metric of scalar curvature 1 as initial data. Denote the limit by \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) . Then by the uniqueness theorem (Theorem 1.2.4), we have

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  = \frac{\frac{n - 1}{2}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}\;\text{ for all }t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

It follows that \( T \leq  \frac{n - 1}{2} \) . In order to show \( T = \frac{n - 1}{2} \) , it suffices to prove the following assertion.

CLAIM 2. Suppose \( T < \frac{n - 1}{2} \) . Fix a point \( {x}_{0} \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) , then there is a \( \delta  > 0 \) , such that for any \( x \in  M \) with \( {d}_{0}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {\delta }^{-1} \) , we have

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}\;\text{ for all }t \in  \lbrack 0, T),
\]

where \( C \) is the constant in (7.3.5).

In view of Claim 1, if Claim 2 holds, then

\[
\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{M}^{n} \times  \lbrack 0, T)}}R\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  \omega \left( {{\delta }^{-2}\left( {{2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - T}}\right) }\right) \left( {{2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - T}}\right)
\]

\[
< \infty
\]

which will contradict the definition of \( T \) .

To show Claim 2, we argue by contradiction. Suppose for each \( \delta  > 0 \) , there is a point \( \left( {{x}_{\delta },{t}_{\delta }}\right) \) with \( 0 < {t}_{\delta } < T \) such that

\[
R\left( {{x}_{\delta },{t}_{\delta }}\right)  > {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {t}_{\delta }}\text{ and }{d}_{0}\left( {{x}_{\delta },{x}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {\delta }^{-1}.
\]

Let

\[
{\bar{t}}_{\delta } = \sup \left\{  {\left. t\right| \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{{M}^{n} \smallsetminus  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{\delta }^{-1}}\right) }}R\left( {y, t}\right)  < {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}}\right\}  .
\]

Since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{{d}_{0}\left( {y,{x}_{0}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty }}R\left( {y, t}\right)  = \frac{\frac{n - 1}{2}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t} \) and \( \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{M \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{1}{4nC}}\right\rbrack  }}R\left( {y, t}\right)  \leq  {2C} \) , we know \( \frac{1}{4nC} \leq  {\bar{t}}_{\delta } \leq \; {t}_{\delta } \) and there is a \( {\bar{x}}_{\delta } \) such that \( {d}_{0}\left( {{x}_{0},{\bar{x}}_{\delta }}\right)  \geq  {\delta }^{-1} \) and \( R\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\delta },{\bar{t}}_{\delta }}\right)  = {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {\bar{t}}_{\delta }} \) . By Claim

1 and Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5), for \( \delta  \rightarrow  0 \) and after taking a subsequence, the metrics \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) on \( {B}_{0}\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\delta },\frac{{\delta }^{-1}}{2}}\right) \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{\bar{t}}_{\delta }}\right\rbrack \) will converge to a solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) on \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{n - 1} \) with the standard metric of scalar curvature 1 as initial data over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) , and its scalar curvature satisfies

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right)  = {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {\bar{t}}_{\infty }},
\]

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {2C} + \frac{n - 1}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {\bar{t}}_{\infty }},\;\text{ for all }t \in  \left\lbrack  {0,{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

where \( \left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right) \) is the limit of \( \left( {{\bar{x}}_{\delta },{\bar{t}}_{\delta }}\right) \) . On the other hand, by the uniqueness theorem (Theorem 1.2.4) again, we know

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{\bar{x}}_{\infty },{\bar{t}}_{\infty }}\right)  = \frac{\frac{n - 1}{2}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - {\bar{t}}_{\infty }}
\]

which is a contradiction. Hence we have proved Claim 2 and then have verified \( T = \frac{n - 1}{2}. \)

Now we are ready to show

(7.3.6)

\[
R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  \frac{{\widetilde{C}}^{-1}}{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t},\;\text{ for all }\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) ,
\]

for some positive constant \( \widetilde{C} \) depending only on the initial metric.

For any \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,\frac{n - 1}{2}}\right) \) , by Claim 1 and \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing, there is a constant \( C\left( \kappa \right)  > 0 \) such that

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x, R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}{\left( R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}.
\]

Then by the well-known volume estimate of Calabi-Yau (see for example [128] or [112]) for complete manifolds with Ric \( \geq  0 \) , for any \( a \geq  1 \) , we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x,{aR}{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)  \geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}\frac{a}{8n}{\left( R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n}.
\]

On the other hand, since \( \left( {{\mathbb{R}}^{n},{g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) is asymptotic to a cylinder of scalar curvature \( \left( \frac{n - 1}{2}\right) /\left( {\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}\right) \) , for sufficiently large \( a > 0 \) , we have

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x, a\sqrt{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}}\right) }\right)  \leq  C\left( n\right) a{\left( \frac{n - 1}{2} - t\right) }^{\frac{n}{2}}.
\]

Combining the two inequalities, for all sufficiently large \( a \) , we have:

\[
C\left( n\right) a{\left( \frac{n - 1}{2} - t\right) }^{\frac{n}{2}} \geq  {\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x, a\left( \frac{\sqrt{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}}{R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  C{\left( \kappa \right) }^{-1}\frac{a}{8n}\left( \frac{\sqrt{\frac{n - 1}{2} - t}}{R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) {\left( R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{n},
\]

which gives the desired estimate (7.3.6). Therefore the proof of the proposition is complete. \( \square \)

LEMMA 7.3.4 (Justification of the pinching assumption). There are universal positive constants \( {\delta }_{0},{c}_{0} \) and \( {P}_{0} \) such that if we take a \( \delta \) -cutoff surgery at a \( \delta \) -neck of radius \( h \) at time \( T \) with \( \delta  \leq  {\delta }_{0} \) and \( {h}^{-2} \geq  2{e}^{2}\log \left( {1 + T}\right) \) , then we can choose \( c = {c}_{0} \) and \( P = {P}_{0} \) in the definition of \( f\left( z\right) \) such that after the surgery, there still holds the pinching condition

(7.3.9)

\[
\widetilde{R} \geq  \left( {-\widetilde{\nu }}\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\widetilde{\nu }}\right)  + \log \left( {1 + T}\right)  - 3}\right\rbrack
\]

whenever \( \widetilde{\nu } < 0 \) , where \( \widetilde{R} \) is the scalar curvature of the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) and \( \widetilde{\nu } \) is the least eigenvalue of the curvature operator of \( \widetilde{g} \) . Moreover, after the surgery, any metric ball of radius \( {\delta }^{-\frac{1}{2}}h \) with center near the tip (i.e., the origin of the attached cap) is, after scaling with factor \( {h}^{-2},{\delta }^{\frac{1}{2}} \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\delta }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding ball of the standard capped infinite cylinder \( C\left( {{c}_{0},{P}_{0}}\right) \) .

First, we consider the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) on the portion \( \{ 0 \leq  z \leq  2\} \) . Under the conformal change \( \widetilde{g} = {e}^{-{2f}}\bar{g} \) , the curvature tensor \( {\widetilde{R}}_{ijkl} \) is given by

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{ijkl} = {e}^{-{2f}}\left\lbrack  {{\bar{R}}_{ijkl} + {\left| \bar{\nabla }f\right| }^{2}\left( {{\bar{g}}_{il}{\bar{g}}_{jk} - {\bar{g}}_{ik}{\bar{g}}_{jl}}\right)  + \left( {{f}_{ik} + {f}_{i}{f}_{k}}\right) {\bar{g}}_{jl}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+\left( {{f}_{jl} + {f}_{j}{f}_{l}}\right) {\bar{g}}_{ik} - \left( {{f}_{il} + {f}_{i}{f}_{l}}\right) {\bar{g}}_{jk} - \left( {{f}_{jk} + {f}_{j}{f}_{k}}\right) {\bar{g}}_{il}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

If \( \left\{  {{\bar{F}}_{a} = {\bar{F}}_{a}^{i}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal frame for \( {\bar{g}}_{ij} \) , then \( \left\{  {{\widetilde{F}}_{a} = {e}^{f}{\bar{F}}_{a} = {\widetilde{F}}_{a}^{i}\frac{\partial }{\partial {x}^{i}}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal frame for \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) . Let

\[
{\bar{R}}_{abcd} = {\bar{R}}_{ijkl}{\bar{F}}_{a}^{i}{\bar{F}}_{b}^{j}{\bar{F}}_{c}^{k}{\bar{F}}_{d}^{l},
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{abcd} = {\widetilde{R}}_{ijkl}{\widetilde{F}}_{a}^{i}{\widetilde{F}}_{b}^{j}{\widetilde{F}}_{c}^{k}{\widetilde{F}}_{d}^{l},
\]

then

(7.3.10)

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{abcd} = {e}^{2f}\left\lbrack  {{\bar{R}}_{abcd} + {\left| \bar{\nabla }f\right| }^{2}\left( {{\delta }_{ad}{\delta }_{bc} - {\delta }_{ac}{\delta }_{bd}}\right)  + \left( {{f}_{ac} + {f}_{a}{f}_{c}}\right) {\delta }_{bd}}\right.
\]

\[
\left. {+\left( {{f}_{bd} + {f}_{b}{f}_{d}}\right) {\delta }_{ac} - \left( {{f}_{ad} + {f}_{a}{f}_{d}}\right) {\delta }_{bc} - \left( {{f}_{bc} + {f}_{b}{f}_{c}}\right) {\delta }_{ad}}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

and

(7.3.11)

\[
\widetilde{R} = {e}^{2f}\left( {\bar{R} + 4\bar{\bigtriangleup }f - 2{\left| \bar{\nabla }f\right| }^{2}}\right) .
\]

Since

\[
\frac{df}{dz} = c{e}^{-\frac{P}{z}}\frac{P}{{z}^{2}},\;\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}} = c{e}^{-\frac{P}{z}}\left( {\frac{{P}^{2}}{{z}^{4}} - \frac{2P}{{z}^{3}}}\right) ,
\]

then for any small \( \theta  > 0 \) , we may choose \( c > 0 \) small and \( P > 0 \) large such that for \( z \in  \left\lbrack  {0,3}\right\rbrack \) , we have

(7.3.12)

\[
\left| {{e}^{2f} - 1}\right|  + \left| \frac{df}{dz}\right|  + \left| {\left( \frac{df}{dz}\right) }^{2}\right|  < \theta \frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}},\;\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}} < \theta .
\]

On the other hand, by the definition of \( \delta \) -neck of radius \( h \) , we have

\[
{\left| \bar{g} - {h}^{2}{g}_{0}\right| }_{{g}_{0}} < \delta {h}^{2}
\]

\[
{\left| {\nabla }^{j}\bar{g}\right| }_{{g}_{0}} < \delta {h}^{2},\text{ for }1 \leq  j \leq  \left\lbrack  {\delta }^{-1}\right\rbrack  ,
\]

where \( {g}_{0} \) is the standard metric of the round cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Note that in three dimensions, we can choose the orthonormal frame \( \left\{  {{\bar{F}}_{1},{\bar{F}}_{2},{\bar{F}}_{3}}\right\} \) for the metric \( \bar{g} \) so that its curvature operator is diagonal in the orthonormal frame \( \left\{  {\sqrt{2}{\bar{F}}_{2} \land  {\bar{F}}_{3},\sqrt{2}{\bar{F}}_{3} \land  }\right. \; \left. {{\bar{F}}_{1},\sqrt{2}{\bar{F}}_{1} \land  {\bar{F}}_{2}}\right\} \) with eigenvalues \( \bar{\nu } \leq  \bar{\mu } \leq  \bar{\lambda } \) and

\[
\bar{\nu } = 2{\bar{R}}_{2323},\;\bar{\mu } = 2{\bar{R}}_{3131},\;\bar{\lambda } = 2{\bar{R}}_{1212}.
\]

Since \( {h}^{-2}\bar{g} \) is \( \delta \) -close to the standard round cylinder metric \( {g}_{0} \) on the \( \delta \) -neck, we have

(7.3.13)

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l} \left| {\bar{R}}_{3131}\right|  + \left| {\bar{R}}_{2323}\right|  < {\delta }^{\frac{7}{8}}{h}^{-2}, \\  \left| {{\bar{R}}_{1212} - \frac{1}{2}{h}^{-2}}\right|  < {\delta }^{\frac{7}{8}}{h}^{-2}, \\  {\left| {\bar{F}}_{3} - {h}^{-1}\frac{\partial }{\partial z}\right| }_{{g}_{0}} < {\delta }^{\frac{7}{8}}{h}^{-1}, \end{array}\right.
\]

for suitably small \( \delta  > 0 \) . Since \( {\bar{\nabla }}_{a}z = \bar{\nabla }z\left( {\bar{F}}_{a}\right) \) and \( {\bar{\nabla }}_{a}{\bar{\nabla }}_{b}z = {\bar{\nabla }}^{2}z\left( {{\bar{F}}_{a},{\bar{F}}_{b}}\right) \) , it follows that

\[
\left| {{\bar{\nabla }}_{3}z - {h}^{-1}}\right|  < {\delta }^{\frac{7}{8}}{h}^{-1}
\]

\[
\left| {{\bar{\nabla }}_{1}z}\right|  + \left| {{\bar{\nabla }}_{2}z}\right|  < {\delta }^{\frac{7}{8}}{h}^{-1}
\]

and

\[
\left| {{\bar{\nabla }}_{a}{\bar{\nabla }}_{b}z}\right|  < {\delta }^{\frac{7}{8}}{h}^{-2},\text{ for }1 \leq  a, b \leq  3.
\]

By combining with

\[
{\bar{\nabla }}_{a}f = \frac{df}{dz}{\bar{\nabla }}_{a}z,\;{\bar{\nabla }}_{a}{\bar{\nabla }}_{b}f = \frac{df}{dz}{\bar{\nabla }}_{a}{\bar{\nabla }}_{b}z + \frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}{\bar{\nabla }}_{a}z{\bar{\nabla }}_{b}z
\]

and (7.3.12), we get

(7.3.14)

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{ll} \left| {{\bar{\nabla }}_{a}f}\right|  < {2\theta }{h}^{-1}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}, & \text{ for }1 \leq  a \leq  3, \\  \left| {{\bar{\nabla }}_{a}{\bar{\nabla }}_{b}f}\right|  < {\delta }^{\frac{3}{4}}{h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}, & \text{ unless }\;a = b = 3, \\  \left| {{\bar{\nabla }}_{3}{\bar{\nabla }}_{3}f - {h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}}\right|  < {\delta }^{\frac{3}{4}}{h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}. &  \end{array}\right.
\]

By combining (7.3.10) and (7.3.14), we have

(7.3.15)

\[
\left\{  \begin{array}{l} {\widetilde{R}}_{1212} \geq  {\bar{R}}_{1212} - \left( {{\theta }^{\frac{1}{2}} + {\delta }^{\frac{5}{8}}}\right) {h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}, \\  {\widetilde{R}}_{3131} \geq  {\bar{R}}_{3131} + \left( {1 - {\theta }^{\frac{1}{2}} - {\delta }^{\frac{5}{8}}}\right) {h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}, \\  {\widetilde{R}}_{2332} \geq  {\bar{R}}_{2323} + \left( {1 - {\theta }^{\frac{1}{2}} - {\delta }^{\frac{5}{8}}}\right) {h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}, \\  \left| {\widetilde{R}}_{abcd}\right|  \leq  \left( {{\theta }^{\frac{1}{2}} + {\delta }^{\frac{5}{8}}}\right) {h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}},\;\text{ otherwise, } \end{array}\right.
\]

where \( \theta \) and \( \delta \) are suitably small. Then it follows that

\[
\widetilde{R} \geq  \bar{R} + \left\lbrack  {4 - 6\left( {{\theta }^{\frac{1}{3}} + {\delta }^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right\rbrack  {h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}
\]

\[
- \widetilde{\nu } \leq   - \bar{\nu } - \left\lbrack  {2 - 2\left( {{\theta }^{\frac{1}{3}} + {\delta }^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right\rbrack  {h}^{-2}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}}
\]

for suitably small \( \theta \) and \( \delta \) .

If \( 0 <  - \widetilde{\nu } \leq  {e}^{2} \) , then by the assumption that \( {h}^{-2} \geq  2{e}^{2}\log \left( {1 + T}\right) \) , we have

\[
\widetilde{R} \geq  \bar{R}
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}{h}^{-2}
\]

\[
\geq  {e}^{2}\log \left( {1 + T}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {-\widetilde{\nu }}\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\widetilde{\nu }}\right)  + \log \left( {1 + T}\right)  - 3}\right\rbrack  .
\]

While if \( - \widetilde{\nu } > {e}^{2} \) , then by the pinching estimate of \( \bar{g} \) , we have

\[
\widetilde{R} \geq  \bar{R}
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {-\bar{\nu }}\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\bar{\nu }}\right)  + \log \left( {1 + T}\right)  - 3}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {-\widetilde{\nu }}\right) \left\lbrack  {\log \left( {-\widetilde{\nu }}\right)  + \log \left( {1 + T}\right)  - 3}\right\rbrack  .
\]

So we have verified the pinching condition on the portion \( \{ 0 \leq  z \leq  2\} \) .

Next, we consider the metric \( \widetilde{g} \) on the portion \( \{ 2 \leq  z \leq  4\} \) . Let \( \theta \) be a fixed suitably small positive number. Then the constant \( c = {c}_{0} \) and \( P = {P}_{0} \) are fixed. So \( \zeta  = \mathop{\min }\limits_{{z \in  \left\lbrack  {1,4}\right\rbrack  }}\frac{{d}^{2}f}{d{z}^{2}} > 0 \) is also fixed. By the same argument as in the derivation of (7.3.15) from (7.3.10), we see that the curvature of the metric \( \widehat{g} = {e}^{-{2f}}{g}_{0} \) of the standard capped infinite cylinder \( C\left( {{c}_{0},{P}_{0}}\right) \) on the portion \( \{ 1 \leq  z \leq  4\} \) is bounded from below by \( \frac{2}{3}\zeta  > 0 \) . Since \( {h}^{-2}\bar{g} \) is \( \delta \) -close to the standard round metric \( {g}_{0} \) , the metric \( {h}^{-2}\widetilde{g} \) defined by (7.3.8) is clearly \( {\delta }^{\frac{3}{4}} \) -close to the metric \( \widehat{g} = {e}^{-{2f}}{g}_{0} \) of the standard capped infinite cylinder on the portion \( \{ 1 \leq  z \leq  4\} \) . Thus as \( \delta \) is sufficiently small, the curvature operator of \( \widetilde{g} \) on the portion \( \{ 2 \leq  z \leq  4\} \) is positive. Hence the pinching condition (7.3.9) holds trivially on the portion \( \{ 2 \leq  z \leq  4\} \) .

The last statement in Lemma 7.3.4 is obvious from the definition (7.3.8).

LEMMA 7.3.5. Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be the above fixed standard solution to the Ricci flow on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \times  \lbrack 0,1) \) . Then for any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there is a positive constant \( C\left( \varepsilon \right) \) such that each point \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \times  \lbrack 0,1) \) has an open neighborhood \( B \) , with \( {B}_{t}\left( {x, r}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{t}\left( {x,{2r}}\right) \) for some \( 0 < r < C\left( \varepsilon \right) R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , which falls into one of the following two categories: either

(a) \( B \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -cap, or

(b) \( B \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -neck and it is the slice at the time \( t \) of the parabolic neighborhood \( {B}_{t}\left( {x,{\varepsilon }^{-1}R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {t - \min \left\{  {R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-1}, t}\right\}  , t}\right\rbrack \) , on which the standard solution is, after scaling with the factor \( R\left( {x, t}\right) \) and shifting the time \( t \) to zero, \( \varepsilon \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\varepsilon }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the evolving standard cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-\min \{ {tR}\left( {x, t}\right) ,1\} ,0}\right\rbrack \) with scalar curvature 1 at the time zero.

nodes.proof:
The proof of the lemma is reduced to two assertions. We now state and prove the first assertion which takes care of those points with times close to 1 .

Assertion 1. For any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there is a positive number \( \theta  = \theta \left( \varepsilon \right) \) with \( 0 < \theta  < 1 \) such that for any \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \times  \lbrack \theta ,1) \) , the standard solution on the parabolic neighborhood \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {x,{\varepsilon }^{-1}R{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\varepsilon }^{-2}R{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-1},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) is well-defined and is, after scaling with the factor \( R\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,\varepsilon \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\varepsilon }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of some orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution.

We argue by contradiction. Suppose Assertion 1 is not true, then there exist \( \bar{\varepsilon } > 0 \) and a sequence of points \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow  1 \) , such that for each \( k \) , the standard solution on the parabolic neighborhood

\[
{B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{x}_{k},{\bar{\varepsilon }}^{-1}R{\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - {\bar{\varepsilon }}^{-2}R{\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack
\]

is not, after scaling by the factor \( R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) ,\bar{\varepsilon } \) -close to the corresponding subset of any ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. Note that by Proposition 7.3.3, there is a constant \( C > 0 \) (depending only on the initial metric, hence it is universal ) such that \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq \; {C}^{-1}/\left( {1 - t}\right) \) . This implies

\[
{\bar{\varepsilon }}^{-2}R{\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }^{-1} \leq  C{\bar{\varepsilon }}^{-2}\left( {1 - {t}_{k}}\right)  < {t}_{k},
\]

and then the standard solution on the parabolic neighborhood \( {B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{x}_{k}\text{ , }}\right. \; \left. {{\bar{\varepsilon }}^{-1}R{\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - {\bar{\varepsilon }}^{-2}R{\left( {x}_{k},{t}_{k}\right) }^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) is well-defined for \( k \) large. By Claim 1 in the proof of Proposition 7.3.3, there is a positive function \( \omega  : \lbrack 0,\infty ) \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) such that

\[
R\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right)  \leq  R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \omega \left( {R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) {d}_{{t}_{k}}^{2}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right) }\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \) . Now by scaling the standard solution \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) around \( {x}_{k} \) with the factor \( R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) and shifting the time \( {t}_{k} \) to zero, we get a sequence of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {x,\widetilde{t}}\right)  = R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) {g}_{ij}\left( {x,{t}_{k} + \widetilde{t}/R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) }\right) \) to the Ricci flow defined on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \) with \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {-R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) {t}_{k},0}\right\rbrack \) . We denote the scalar curvature and the distance of the rescaled metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k} \) by \( {\widetilde{R}}^{k} \) and \( \widetilde{d} \) . By combining with Claim 1 in the proof of Proposition 7.3.3 and the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality, we get

\[
{\widetilde{R}}^{k}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  \omega \left( {{\widetilde{d}}_{0}^{2}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
{\widetilde{R}}^{k}\left( {x,\widetilde{t}}\right)  \leq  \frac{R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) {t}_{k}}{\widetilde{t} + R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) {t}_{k}}\omega \left( {{\widetilde{d}}_{0}^{2}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right) }\right)
\]

for any \( x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \) and \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left( {-R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) {t}_{k},0}\right\rbrack \) . Note that \( R\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) {t}_{k} \rightarrow  \infty \) by Proposition 7.3.3. We have shown in the proof of Proposition 7.3.3 that the standard solution is \( \kappa \) - noncollapsed on all scales less than 1 for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) . Then from the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing property, the above curvature estimates and Hamilton's compactness theorem, we know \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{k}\left( {x,\widetilde{t}}\right) \) has a convergent subsequence (as \( k \rightarrow  \infty \) ) whose limit is an ancient, \( \kappa \) - noncollapsed, complete and orientable solution with nonnegative curvature operator. This limit must have bounded curvature by the same proof of Step 3 in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1. This gives a contradiction. Hence Assertion 1 is proved.

We now fix the constant \( \theta \left( \varepsilon \right) \) obtained in Assertion 1. Let \( O \) be the tip of the standard capped infinite cylinder \( {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \) (it is rotationally symmetric about \( O \) at time 0, and it remains so as \( t > 0 \) by the uniqueness Theorem 1.2.4).

Assertion 2. There are constants \( {B}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) and \( {B}_{2}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) depending only on \( \varepsilon \) , such that if \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \times  \lbrack 0,\theta ) \) with \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, O}\right)  \leq  {B}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) , then there is a \( 0 < r < {B}_{2}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) such that \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, r}\right) \) is an \( \varepsilon \) -cap; if \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{3} \times  \lbrack 0,\theta ) \) with \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, O}\right)  \geq  {B}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) , then the parabolic neighborhood \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{\varepsilon }^{-1}R{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \min \left\{  {R{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-1},{t}_{0}}\right\}  ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) is after scaling with the factor \( R\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) and shifting the time \( {t}_{0} \) to zero, \( \varepsilon \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\varepsilon }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the corresponding subset of the evolving standard cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-\min \left\{  {{t}_{0}R\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,1}\right\}  ,0}\right\rbrack \) with scalar curvature 1 at time zero.

Since the standard solution exists on the time interval \( \lbrack 0,1) \) , there is a constant \( {B}_{0}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) such that the curvatures on \( \left\lbrack  {0,\theta \left( \varepsilon \right) }\right\rbrack \) are uniformly bounded by \( {B}_{0}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) . This implies that the metrics in \( \left\lbrack  {0,\theta \left( \varepsilon \right) }\right\rbrack \) are equivalent. Note that the initial metric is asymptotic to the standard capped infinite cylinder. For any sequence of points \( {x}_{k} \) with \( {d}_{0}\left( {O,{x}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  \infty \) , after passing to a subsequence, \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) around \( {x}_{k} \) will converge to a solution to the Ricci flow on \( \mathbb{R} \times  {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) with round cylinder metric of scalar curvature 1 as initial data. By the uniqueness theorem (Theorem 1.2.4), the limit solution must be the standard evolving round cylinder. This implies that there is a constant \( {B}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right)  > 0 \) depending on \( \varepsilon \) such that for any \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{0} \leq  \theta \left( \varepsilon \right) \) and \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, O}\right)  \geq  {B}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) , the standard solution on the parabolic neighborhood \( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{\varepsilon }^{-1}R{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - \min \left\{  {R{\left( {x}_{0},{t}_{0}\right) }^{-1},{t}_{0}}\right\}  ,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) is, after scaling with the factor \( R\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,\varepsilon \) -close to the corresponding subset of the evolving round cylinder. Since the solution is rotationally symmetric around \( O \) , the cap neighborhood structures of those points \( {x}_{0} \) with \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0}, O}\right)  \leq  {B}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) follow directly. Hence Assertion 2 is proved.

The combination of these two assertions proves the lemma.

nodes.label: Lemma 7.3.6
nodes.document_title: Huai-Dong Cao and Xi-Ping Zhu - A Complete Proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures
nodes.content:
LEMMA 7.3.6 (Perelman [104]). For any \( 0 < \varepsilon  \leq  1/{100},1 < A <  + \infty \) and \( 0 < \theta  < 1 \) , one can find \( \bar{\delta } = \bar{\delta }\left( {A,\theta ,\varepsilon }\right) \) with the following property. Suppose we have a solution to the Ricci flow with surgery which satisfies the a priori assumptions (with accuracy \( \varepsilon \) ) on \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) and is obtained from a compact orientable three-manifold by a finite number of \( \delta \) -cutoff surgeries with each \( \delta  < \bar{\delta } \) . Suppose we have a cutoff surgery at time \( {T}_{0} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) , let \( {x}_{0} \) be any fixed point on the gluing caps (i.e., the regions affected by the cutoff surgeries at time \( {T}_{0} \) ), and let \( {T}_{1} = \min \left\{  {T,{T}_{0} + \theta {h}^{2}}\right\} \) , where \( h \) is the cutoff radius around \( {x}_{0} \) obtained in Lemma 7.3.2. Then either

(i) the solution is defined on \( P\left( {{x}_{0},{T}_{0},{Ah},{T}_{1} - {T}_{0}}\right)  \triangleq  \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  x \in  {B}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},{Ah}}\right) , t \in  }\right. \; \left. \left\lbrack  {{T}_{0},{T}_{1}}\right\rbrack  \right\} \) and is, after scaling with factor \( {h}^{-2} \) and shifting time \( {T}_{0} \) to zero, \( {A}^{-1} \) -close to a corresponding subset of the standard solution, or

(ii) the assertion (i) holds with \( {T}_{1} \) replaced by some time \( {t}^{ + } \in  \left( {{T}_{0},{T}_{1}}\right) \) , where \( {t}^{ + } \) is a surgery time; moreover, for each point in \( {B}_{{T}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{Ah}}\right) \) , the solution is defined for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{T}_{0},{t}^{ + }}\right) \) but is not defined past \( {t}^{ + } \) (i.e., the whole ball \( {B}_{{T}_{0}}\left( {{x}_{0},{Ah}}\right) \) is cut off at the time \( {t}^{ + } \) ).
