Let \( w > \) 0 and \( 0 < \varepsilon \leq \frac{1}{2}w \) be any small positive constants and let \( \left( {{M}_{t},{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) ,0 < t < \; + \infty \) , be a solution to the Ricci flow with surgery, constructed by Theorem 7.4.3 with the nonincreasing (continuous) positive functions \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) \) a...

nodes.proof:
The proof of the theorem follows, with some modifications, essentially from the same argument of Hamilton as in the proof of Theorem 5.3.4.

Clearly we may assume that the thick part \( {M}_{\text{ thick }}\left( {w, t}\right) \) is not empty for a sequence \( {t}^{\alpha } \rightarrow   + \infty \) , since otherwise we have case (i). If we take a sequence of points \( {x}^{\alpha } \in \; {M}_{\text{ thick }}\left( {w,{t}^{\alpha }}\right) \) , then by Theorem 7.6.3(b) the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) \) around \( {x}^{\alpha } \) with factor \( {\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1} \) converge smoothly, along a subsequence of \( \alpha  \rightarrow   + \infty \) , to a complete hyperbolic manifold of finite volume with constant sectional curvature \( - \frac{1}{4} \) . The limits may be different for different choices of \( \left( {{x}^{\alpha },{t}^{\alpha }}\right) \) . If a limit is compact, we have case (ii). Thus we assume that all limits are noncompact.

Consider all the possible hyperbolic limits of the solution, and among them choose one such complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifold \( \mathcal{H} \) with the least possible number of cusps. Denote by \( {h}_{ij} \) the hyperbolic metric of \( \mathcal{H} \) . For all small \( a > 0 \) we can truncate each cusp of \( \mathcal{H} \) along a constant mean curvature torus of area \( a \) which is uniquely determined; we denote the remainder by \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) . Fix \( a > 0 \) so small that Lemma 5.3.7 is applicable for the compact set \( \mathcal{K} = {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) . Pick an integer \( {l}_{0} \) sufficiently large and an \( {\epsilon }_{0} \) sufficiently small to guarantee from Lemma 5.3.8 that the identity map \( {Id} \) is the only harmonic map \( F \) from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to itself with taking \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to itself, with the normal derivative of \( F \) at the boundary of the domain normal to the boundary of the target, and with \( {d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {F,{Id}}\right)  < {\epsilon }_{0} \) . Then choose a positive integer \( {q}_{0} \) and a small number \( {\delta }_{0} > 0 \) from Lemma 5.3.7 such that if \( \widetilde{F} \) is a diffeomorphism of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into another complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifold \( \left( {\widetilde{\mathcal{H}},{\widetilde{h}}_{ij}}\right) \) with no fewer cusps (than \( \mathcal{H} \) ), of finite volume and satisfying

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{\widetilde{F}}^{ * }{\widetilde{h}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{{q}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } \leq  {\delta }_{0},
\]

then there exists an isometry \( I \) of \( \mathcal{H} \) to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) such that

\[
{d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {\widetilde{F}, I}\right)  < {\epsilon }_{0}.
\]

By Lemma 5.3.8 we further require \( {q}_{0} \) and \( {\delta }_{0} \) to guarantee the existence of a harmonic diffeomorphism from \( \left( {{\mathcal{H}}_{a},{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}}\right) \) to \( \left( {{\mathcal{H}}_{a},{h}_{ij}}\right) \) for any metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) on \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) with \( {\begin{Vmatrix}{\widetilde{g}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{{q}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } \leq  {\delta }_{0}. \)

Let \( {x}^{\alpha } \in  {M}_{\text{ thick }}\left( {w,{t}^{\alpha }}\right) ,{t}^{\alpha } \rightarrow   + \infty \) , be a sequence of points such that the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) \) around \( {x}^{\alpha } \) with factor \( {\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1} \) converge to \( {h}_{ij} \) . Then there exist a marked point \( {x}^{\infty } \in  {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) and a sequence of diffeomorphisms \( {F}_{\alpha } \) from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( {M}_{{t}^{\alpha }} \) such that \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {x}^{\infty }\right)  = {x}^{\alpha } \) and

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }{g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{m}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } \rightarrow  0
\]

as \( \alpha  \rightarrow  \infty \) for all positive integers \( m \) . By applying Lemma 5.3.8 and the implicit function theorem, we can change \( {F}_{\alpha } \) by an amount which goes to zero as \( \alpha  \rightarrow  \infty \) so as to make \( {F}_{\alpha } \) a harmonic diffeomorphism taking \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to a constant mean curvature hypersurface \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) of \( \left( {{M}_{{t}^{\alpha }},{\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right) }\right) \) with the area \( a \) and satisfying the free boundary condition that the normal derivative of \( {F}_{\alpha } \) at the boundary of the domain is normal to the boundary of the target; and by combining with Lemma 7.6.2 (iii), we can smoothly continue each harmonic diffeomorphism \( {F}_{\alpha } \) forward in time a little to a family of harmonic diffeomorphisms \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( {M}_{t} \) with the metric \( {t}^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) , with \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {t}^{\alpha }\right)  = {F}_{\alpha } \) and with the time \( t \) slightly larger than \( {t}^{\alpha } \) , where \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) takes \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into a constant mean curvature hypersurface of \( \left( {{M}_{t},{t}^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) }\right) \) with the area \( a \) and also satisfies the free boundary condition. Moreover, since the surgeries do not take place at the points where the scalar curvature is negative, by the same argument as in Theorem 5.3.4 for an arbitrarily given positive integer \( q \geq  {q}_{0} \) , positive number \( \delta  < {\delta }_{0} \) , and sufficiently large \( \alpha \) , we can ensure the extension \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) satisfies \( {\begin{Vmatrix}{t}^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( t\right) {g}_{ij}\left( t\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } \leq  \delta \) on a maximal time interval \( {t}^{\alpha } \leq  t \leq  {\omega }^{\alpha } \) (or \( {t}^{\alpha } \leq \; t < {\omega }^{\alpha } \) when \( {\omega }^{\alpha } =  + \infty ) \) , and with \( {\begin{Vmatrix}{\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } = \delta \) , when \( {\omega }^{\alpha } <  + \infty \) . Here we have implicitly used the fact that \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) is still strictly concave to ensure the map \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \) is diffeomorphic.

We further claim that there must be some \( \alpha \) such that \( {\omega }^{\alpha } =  + \infty \) ; in other words, at least one hyperbolic piece persists. Indeed, suppose that for each large enough \( \alpha \) we can only continue the family \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) on a finite interval \( {t}^{\alpha } \leq  t \leq  {\omega }^{\alpha } <  + \infty \) with

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right)  - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } = \delta .
\]

Consider the new sequence of manifolds \( \left( {{M}_{{\omega }^{\alpha }},{g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }\right) \) . Clearly by Lemma 7.6.1, the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \) around the new origins \( {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \left( {x}^{\infty }\right) \) with factor \( {\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1} \) converge smoothly (by passing to a subsequence) to a complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifold \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) with the metric \( {\widetilde{h}}_{ij} \) and the origin \( {\widetilde{x}}^{\infty } \) and with finite volume. By the choice of the old limit \( \mathcal{H} \) , the new limit \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) has at least as many cusps as \( \mathcal{H} \) . By the definition of convergence, we can find a sequence of compact subsets \( {\widetilde{U}}_{\alpha } \) exhausting \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) and containing \( {\widetilde{x}}^{\infty } \) , and a sequence of diffeomorphisms \( {\widetilde{F}}_{\alpha } \) of neighborhood of \( {\widetilde{U}}_{\alpha } \) into \( {M}_{{\omega }^{\alpha }} \) with \( {\widetilde{F}}_{\alpha }\left( {\widetilde{x}}^{\infty }\right)  = {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \left( {x}^{\infty }\right) \) such that for each compact subset \( \widetilde{U} \) of \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) and each integer \( m \) ,

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) }^{-1}{\widetilde{F}}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( {g}_{ij}\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right) \right)  - {\widetilde{h}}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{m}\left( \widetilde{U}\right) } \rightarrow  0
\]

as \( \alpha  \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Thus for sufficiently large \( \alpha \) , we have the map

\[
{G}_{\alpha } = {\widetilde{F}}_{\alpha }^{-1} \circ  {F}_{\alpha }\left( {\omega }^{\alpha }\right)  : \;{\mathcal{H}}_{a} \rightarrow  \widetilde{\mathcal{H}}
\]

such that

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{G}_{\alpha }^{ * }{\widetilde{h}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } < \widetilde{\delta }
\]

for any fixed \( \widetilde{\delta } > \delta \) . Then a subsequence of \( {G}_{\alpha } \) converges at least in the \( {C}^{q - 1}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) \) topology to a map \( {G}_{\infty } \) of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) which is a harmonic map from \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) into \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) and takes \( \partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to a constant mean curvature hypersurface \( {G}_{\infty }\left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) of \( \left( {\mathcal{H},{h}_{ij}}\right) \) with the area \( a \) , as well as satisfies the free boundary condition. Clearly, \( {G}_{\infty } \) is at least a local diffeomorphism. Since \( {G}_{\infty } \) is the limit of diffeomorphisms, the only possibility of overlap is at the boundary. Note that \( {G}_{\infty }\left( {\partial {\mathcal{H}}_{a}}\right) \) is still strictly concave. So \( {G}_{\infty } \) is still a diffeomorphism. Moreover by using the standard regularity result of elliptic partial differential equations (see for example [48]), we also have

(7.6.20)

\[
{\begin{Vmatrix}{G}_{\infty }^{ * }{\widetilde{h}}_{ij} - {h}_{ij}\end{Vmatrix}}_{{C}^{q}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) } = \delta .
\]

Now by Lemma 5.3.7 we deduce that there exists an isometry \( I \) of \( \mathcal{H} \) to \( \widetilde{\mathcal{H}} \) with

\[
{d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {{G}_{\infty }, I}\right)  < {\epsilon }_{0}.
\]

Thus \( {I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty } \) is a harmonic diffeomorphism of \( {\mathcal{H}}_{a} \) to itself which satisfies the free boundary condition and

\[
{d}_{{C}^{{l}_{0}}\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{a}\right) }\left( {{I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty },{Id}}\right)  < {\epsilon }_{0}.
\]

However the uniqueness in Lemma 5.3.8 concludes that \( {I}^{-1} \circ  {G}_{\infty } = {Id} \) which contradicts (7.6.20). So we have shown that at least one hyperbolic piece persists and the metric \( {t}^{-1}{F}_{\alpha }^{ * }\left( t\right) {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) , for \( {\omega }^{\alpha } \leq  t < \infty \) , is as close to the hyperbolic metric \( {h}_{ij} \) as we like.

We can continue to form other persistent hyperbolic pieces in the same way as long as there is a sequence of points \( {y}^{\beta } \in  {M}_{\text{ thick }}\left( {w,{t}^{\beta }}\right) ,{t}^{\beta } \rightarrow   + \infty \) , lying outside the chosen pieces. Note that \( V\left( t\right) {\left( t + \frac{3}{2}\right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}} \) is nonincreasing on \( \lbrack 0, + \infty ) \) . Therefore by combining with Margulis lemma (see for example [55] or [76]), we have proved that there exists a finite collection of complete noncompact hyperbolic three-manifolds \( {\mathcal{H}}_{1},\ldots ,{\mathcal{H}}_{m} \) with finite volume, a small number \( a > 0 \) and a time \( T <  + \infty \) such that for all \( t \) beyond \( T \) we can find diffeomorphisms \( {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) \) of \( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{l}\right) }_{a} \) into \( {M}_{t},1 \leq  l \leq  m \) , so that as long as \( t \) is sufficiently large, the metric \( {t}^{-1}{\varphi }_{l}^{ * }\left( t\right) {g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) is as close to the hyperbolic metrics as we like and the complement \( {M}_{t} \smallsetminus  \left( {{\varphi }_{1}\left( t\right) \left( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{1}\right) }_{a}\right)  \cup  \cdots  \cup  {\varphi }_{m}\left( t\right) \left( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{m}\right) }_{a}\right) }\right) \) is contained in the thin part \( {M}_{\text{ thin }}\left( {w, t}\right) \) .

It remains to show the boundary tori of any persistent hyperbolic piece are incompressible. Let \( B \) be a small positive number and assume the above positive number \( a \) is much smaller than \( B \) . Let \( {M}_{a}\left( t\right)  = {\varphi }_{l}\left( t\right) \left( {\left( {\mathcal{H}}_{l}\right) }_{a}\right) \left( {1 \leq  l \leq  m}\right) \) be such a persistent hyperbolic piece of the manifold \( {M}_{t} \) truncated by boundary tori of area at with constant mean curvature, and denote by \( {M}_{a}^{c}\left( t\right)  = {M}_{t} \smallsetminus  {M}_{a}\left( t\right) \) the part of \( {M}_{t} \) exterior to \( {M}_{a}\left( t\right) \) . Thus there exists a family of subsets \( {M}_{B}\left( t\right)  \subset  {M}_{a}\left( t\right) \) which is a persistent hyperbolic piece of the manifold \( {M}_{t} \) truncated by boundary tori of area \( {Bt} \) with constant mean curvature. We also denote by \( {M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right)  = {M}_{t} \smallsetminus  {\overset{ \circ  }{M}}_{B}\left( t\right) \) . By Van Kampen’s Theorem, if \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) }\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {{M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) }\right) \) then it injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {M}_{t}\right) \) also. Thus we only need to show \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) }\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {{M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) }\right) \) .

As before we will use a contradiction argument to show \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {\partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) }\right) \) injects into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {{M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) }\right) \) . Let \( T \) be a torus in \( \partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) \) and suppose \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) does not inject into \( {\pi }_{1}\left( {{M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) }\right) \) . By Dehn’s Lemma we know that the kernel is a cyclic subgroup of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) generated by a primitive element. Consider the normalized metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right)  = {t}^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) on \( {M}_{t} \) . Then by the work of Meeks-Yau [86] or Meeks-Simon-Yau [87], we know that among all disks in \( {M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) \) whose boundary curve lies in \( T \) and generates the kernel of \( {\pi }_{1}\left( T\right) \) , there is a smooth embedded disk normal to the boundary which has the least possible area (with respect to the normalized metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) ). Denote by \( D \) the minimal disk and \( \widetilde{A} = \widetilde{A}\left( t\right) \) its area. We will show that \( \widetilde{A}\left( t\right) \) decreases at a certain rate which will arrive at a contradiction.

We first consider the case that there exist no surgeries at the time \( t \) . Exactly as in Part III of the proof of Theorem 5.3.4, the change of the area \( \widetilde{A}\left( t\right) \) comes from the change in the metric and the change in the boundary. For the change in the metric, we choose an orthonormal frame \( X, Y, Z \) at a point \( x \) in the disk \( D \) so that \( X \) and \( Y \) are tangent to the disk \( D \) while \( Z \) is normal. Since the normalized metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} \) evolves by

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}{\widetilde{g}}_{ij} =  - {t}^{-1}\left( {{\widetilde{g}}_{ij} + 2{\widetilde{R}}_{ij}}\right) ,
\]

the (normalized) area element \( d\widetilde{\sigma } \) of the disk \( D \) around \( x \) satisfies

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}d\widetilde{\sigma } =  - {t}^{-1}\left( {1 + \widetilde{\operatorname{Ric}}\left( {X, X}\right)  + \widetilde{\operatorname{Ric}}\left( {Y, Y}\right) }\right) d\widetilde{\sigma }.
\]

For the change in the boundary, we notice that the tensor \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij} + 2{\widetilde{R}}_{ij} \) is very small for the persistent hyperbolic piece. Then by using the Gauss-Bonnet theorem as before, we obtain the rate of change of the area

(7.6.21)

\[
\frac{d\widetilde{A}}{dt} \leq   - {\int }_{D}\left( {\frac{1}{t} + \frac{\widetilde{R}}{2t}}\right) d\widetilde{\sigma } + \frac{1}{t}{\int }_{\partial D}\widetilde{k}d\widetilde{s} - \frac{2\pi }{t} + o\left( \frac{1}{t}\right) \widetilde{L},
\]

where \( \widetilde{k} \) is the geodesic curvature of the boundary and \( \widetilde{L} \) is the length of the boundary curve \( \partial D \) (with respect to the normalized metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}\left( t\right) \) ). Since \( \widetilde{R} \geq   - {3t}/2\left( {t + \frac{3}{2}}\right) \) for all \( t \geq  0 \) by (7.6.2), the first term on the RHS of (7.6.21) is bounded above by

\[
- {\int }_{D}\left( {\frac{1}{t} + \frac{\widetilde{R}}{2t}}\right) d\widetilde{\sigma } \leq   - \frac{1}{t}\left( {\frac{1}{4} - o\left( 1\right) }\right) \widetilde{A}
\]

while the second term on the RHS of (7.6.21) can be estimated exactly as before by

\[
\frac{1}{t}{\int }_{\partial D}\widetilde{k}d\widetilde{s} \leq  \frac{1}{t}\left( {\frac{1}{4} + o\left( 1\right) }\right) \widetilde{L}.
\]

Thus we obtain

(7.6.22)

\[
\frac{d\widetilde{A}}{dt} \leq  \frac{1}{t}\left\lbrack  {\left( {\frac{1}{4} + o\left( 1\right) }\right) \widetilde{L} - \left( {\frac{1}{4} - o\left( 1\right) }\right) \widetilde{A} - {2\pi }}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Next we show that these arguments also work for the case that there exist surgeries at the time \( t \) . To this end, we only need to check that the embedded minimal disk \( D \) lies in the region which is unaffected by surgery. Our surgeries for the irreducible three-manifold took place on \( \delta \) -necks in \( \varepsilon \) -horns, where the scalar curvatures are at least \( {\delta }^{-2}{\left( \widetilde{r}\left( t\right) \right) }^{-1} \) , and the components with nonnegative scalar curvature have been removed. So the hyperbolic piece is not affected by the surgeries. In particular, the boundary \( \partial D \) is unaffected by the surgeries. Thus if surgeries occur on the minimal disk, the minimal disk has to pass through a long thin neck before it reaches the surgery regions. Look at the intersections of the embedding minimal disk with a generic center two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) of the long thin neck; these are circles. Since the two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) is simply connected, we can replace the components of the minimal disk \( D \) outside the center two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) by some corresponding components on the center two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) to form a new disk which also has \( \partial D \) as its boundary. Since the metric on the long thin neck is nearly a product metric, we could choose the generic center two-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) properly so that the area of the new disk is strictly less than the area of the original disk \( D \) . This contradiction proves the minimal disk lies entirely in the region unaffected by surgery.

Since \( a \) is much smaller than \( B \) , the region within a long distance from \( \partial {M}_{B}\left( t\right) \) into \( {M}_{B}^{c}\left( t\right) \) will look nearly like a hyperbolic cusplike collar and is unaffected by the surgeries. So we can repeat the arguments in the last part of the proof of Theorem 5.3.4 to bound the length \( \widetilde{L} \) by the area \( \widetilde{A} \) and to conclude

\[
\frac{d\widetilde{A}}{dt} \leq   - \frac{\pi }{t}
\]

for all sufficiently large times \( t \) , which is impossible because the RHS is not integrable. This proves that the boundary tori of any persistent hyperbolic piece are incompressible.

Therefore we have proved the theorem. 0

nodes.label: Theorem 7.7.1

nodes.content: THEOREM 7.7.1. Thurston's geometrization conjecture is true.
nodes.content_excerpt: THEOREM 7.7.1. Thurston's geometrization conjecture is true.

nodes.proof:
Let \( M \) be a compact, orientable, and prime three-manifold (without boundary). Without loss of generality, we may assume that the manifold \( M \) is irreducible also.

Recall that the theorem of Thurston (see for example Theorem A and Theorem B in Section 3 of [94], see also [85] and [102]) says that any compact, orientable, and irreducible Haken three-manifold (with or without boundary) is geometrizable. Thus in the following, we may assume that the compact three-manifold \( M \) (without boundary) is atoroidal, and then the fundamental group \( {\pi }_{1}\left( M\right) \) contains no noncyclic, abelian subgroup.

Arbitrarily given a (normalized) Riemannian metric on the manifold \( M \) , we use it as initial data for the Ricci flow. Arbitrarily take a sequence of small positive constants \( {w}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) as \( \alpha  \rightarrow   + \infty \) . For each fixed \( \alpha \) , we set \( \varepsilon  = {w}^{\alpha }/2 > 0 \) . Then by Theorem 7.4.3, the Ricci flow with surgery has a long-time solution \( \left( {{M}_{t}^{\alpha },{g}_{ij}^{\alpha }\left( t\right) }\right) \) on a maximal time interval \( \left\lbrack  {0,{T}^{\alpha }}\right) \) , which satisfies the a priori assumptions (with the accuracy parameter \( \varepsilon  = {w}^{\alpha }/2 \) ) and has a finite number of surgeries on each finite time interval. Since the initial manifold is irreducible, by the surgery procedure, we know that for each \( \alpha \) and each \( t > 0 \) the solution manifold \( {M}_{t}^{\alpha } \) consists of a finite number of components where the essential component \( {\left( {M}_{t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) is diffeomorphic to the initial manifold \( M \) and the others are diffeomorphic to the three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) .

If for some \( \alpha  = {\alpha }_{0} \) the maximal time \( {T}^{{\alpha }_{0}} \) is finite, then the solution \( \left( {{M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{0}},{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{0}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) becomes extinct at \( {T}^{{\alpha }_{0}} \) and the (irreducible) initial manifold \( M \) is diffeomorphic to \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3}/\Gamma \) (the metric quotients of round three-sphere); in particular, the manifold \( M \) is geometrizable. Thus we may assume that the maximal time \( {T}^{\alpha } =  + \infty \) for all \( \alpha \) .

We now apply the long-time behavior theorem (Theorem 7.6.4). If there is some \( \alpha \) such that case (ii) of Theorem 7.6.4 occurs, then for some sufficiently large time \( t \) , the essential component \( {\left( {M}_{t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) of the solution manifold \( {M}_{t}^{\alpha } \) is diffeomorphic to a compact hyperbolic space, so the initial manifold \( M \) is geometrizable. Whereas if there is some sufficiently large \( \alpha \) such that case (iii) of Theorem 7.6.4 occurs, then it follows that for all sufficiently large \( t \) , there is an embedding of a (nonempty) finite number of disjoint unions of incompressible two-tori \( \mathop{\coprod }\limits_{i}{T}_{i}^{2} \) in the essential component \( {\left( {M}_{t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) of \( {M}_{t}^{\alpha } \) . This is a contradiction since we have assumed the initial manifold \( M \) is atoroidal.

It remains to deal with the situation that there is a sequence of positive \( {\alpha }_{k} \rightarrow \; + \infty \) such that the solutions \( \left( {{M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}},{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) always satisfy case (i) of Theorem 7.6.4. That is, for each \( {\alpha }_{k},{M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}} = {M}_{\text{ thin }}\left( {{w}^{{\alpha }_{k}}, t}\right) \) when the time \( t \) is sufficiently large. By the Thick-thin decomposition theorem (Theorem 7.6.3), there is a positive constant, \( 0 < \rho \left( {w}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right)  \leq  1 \) , such that as long as \( t \) is sufficiently large, for every \( x \in  {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}} = \; {M}_{\text{ thin }}\left( {{w}^{{\alpha }_{k}}, t}\right) \) , we have some \( r = r\left( {x, t}\right) \) , with \( 0 < r\sqrt{t} < \rho \left( {w}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) \sqrt{t} \) , such that

(7.7.1)

\[
{Rm} \geq   - {\left( r\sqrt{t}\right) }^{-2}\;\text{ on }{B}_{t}\left( {x, r\sqrt{t}}\right) ,
\]

and

(7.7.2)

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {x, r\sqrt{t}}\right) }\right)  < {w}^{{\alpha }_{k}}{\left( r\sqrt{t}\right) }^{3}.
\]

Clearly we only need to consider the essential component \( {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) . We divide the discussion into the following two cases:

(1) there is a positive constant \( 1 < C <  + \infty \) such that for each \( {\alpha }_{k} \) there is a sufficiently large time \( {t}_{k} > 0 \) such that

(7.7.3)

\[
r\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right) \sqrt{{t}_{k}} < C \cdot  \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{{t}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  {\left( {M}_{{t}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \subset  {M}_{\operatorname{thin}}\left( {{w}^{{\alpha }_{k}},{t}_{k}}\right) \) ;

(2) there are a subsequence \( {\alpha }_{k} \) (still denoted by \( {\alpha }_{k} \) ), and sequences of positive constants \( {C}_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) and times \( {T}_{k} <  + \infty \) such that for each \( t \geq  {T}_{k} \) , we have

(7.7.4)

\[
r\left( {x\left( t\right) , t}\right) \sqrt{t} \geq  {C}_{k} \cdot  \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right)
\]

for some \( x\left( t\right)  \in  {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }, k = 1,2,\ldots \) Here we denote by \( \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) \) the diameter of the essential component \( {\left( {M}_{t}^{\alpha }\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) with the metric \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha }\left( t\right) \) at the time \( t \) .

Let us first consider case (1). For each point \( x \in  {\left( {M}_{{t}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \subset  {M}_{\text{ thin }}\left( {{w}^{{\alpha }_{k}},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , we denote by \( {\rho }_{k}\left( x\right)  = {C}^{-1}r\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right) \sqrt{{t}_{k}} \) . Then by (7.7.1),(7.7.2) and (7.7.3), we have

\[
{\rho }_{k}\left( x\right)  < \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{{t}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) ,
\]

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {x,{\rho }_{k}\left( x\right) }\right) }\right)  \leq  {\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {x, r\left( {x,{t}_{k}}\right) \sqrt{{t}_{k}}}\right) }\right)  < {C}^{3}{w}^{{\alpha }_{k}}{\left( {\rho }_{k}\left( x\right) \right) }^{3},
\]

and

\[
{Rm} \geq   - {\left( r\left( x,{t}_{k}\right) \sqrt{{t}_{k}}\right) }^{-2} \geq   - {\left( {\rho }_{k}\left( x\right) \right) }^{-2}
\]

on \( {B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {x,{\rho }_{k}\left( x\right) }\right) \) . Then it follows from the above Weaker Assertion that \( {\left( {M}_{{t}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) , for sufficiently large \( k \) , are diffeomorphic to graph manifolds. This implies that the (irreducible) initial manifold \( M \) is diffeomorphic to a graph manifold. So the manifold \( M \) is geometrizable in case (1).

We next consider case (2). Clearly, for each \( {\alpha }_{k} \) and the chosen \( {T}_{k} \) , we may assume that the estimates (7.7.1) and (7.7.2) hold for all \( t \geq  {T}_{k} \) and \( x \in  {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) . The combination of (7.7.1) and (7.7.4) gives

(7.7.5)

\[
{Rm} \geq   - {C}_{k}^{-2}{\left( \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) \right) }^{-2}\;\text{ on }{\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) },
\]

for all \( t \geq  {T}_{k} \) . If there are a subsequence \( {\alpha }_{k} \) (still denoted by \( {\alpha }_{k} \) ) and a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \in  \left( {{T}_{k}, + \infty }\right) \) such that

(7.7.6)

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {\left( {M}_{{t}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right)  < {w}_{k}^{\prime }{\left( \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{{t}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) \right) }^{3}
\]

for some sequence \( {w}_{k}^{\prime } \rightarrow  0 \) , then it follows from the Weaker Assertion that \( {\left( {M}_{{t}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) , for sufficiently large \( k \) , are diffeomorphic to graph manifolds which implies the initial manifold \( M \) is geometrizable. Thus we may assume that there is a positive constant \( {w}^{\prime } \) such that

(7.7.7)

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right)  \geq  {w}^{\prime }{\left( \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) \right) }^{3}
\]

for each \( k \) and all \( t \geq  {T}_{k} \) .

In view of the estimates (7.7.5) and (7.7.7), we now want to use Theorem 7.5.2 to get a uniform upper bound for the curvatures of the essential components \( \left( {{\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) },{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) with sufficiently large time \( t \) . Note that the estimate in Theorem 7.5.2 depends on the parameter \( \varepsilon \) and our \( \varepsilon \) ’s depend on \( {w}^{{\alpha }_{k}} \) with \( 0 < \varepsilon  = {w}^{{\alpha }_{k}}/2 \) ; so it does not work in the present situation. Fortunately we notice that the curvature estimate for smooth solutions in Corollary 7.2.3 is independent of \( \varepsilon \) . In the following we try to use Corollary 7.2.3 to obtain the desired curvature estimate.

We first claim that for each \( k \) , there is a sufficiently large \( {T}_{k}^{\prime } \in  \left( {{T}_{k}, + \infty }\right) \) such that the solution, when restricted to the essential component \( \left( {{\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) },{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) , has no surgery for all \( t \geq  {T}_{k}^{\prime } \) . Indeed, for each fixed \( k \) , if there is a \( \delta \left( t\right) \) -cutoff surgery at a sufficiently large time \( t \) , then the manifold \( \left( {{\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) },{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) would contain a \( \delta \left( t\right) \) -neck \( {B}_{t}\left( {y,\delta {\left( t\right) }^{-1}R{\left( y, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) for some \( y \in  {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) with the volume ratio

(7.7.8)

\[
\frac{{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {y,\delta {\left( t\right) }^{-1}R{\left( y, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right) }{{\left( \delta {\left( t\right) }^{-1}R{\left( y, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{3}} \leq  {8\pi \delta }{\left( t\right) }^{2}.
\]

On the other hand, by (7.7.5) and (7.7.7), the standard Bishop-Gromov volume comparison implies that

\[
\frac{{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( {{B}_{t}\left( {y,\delta {\left( t\right) }^{-1}R{\left( y, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) }\right) }{{\left( \delta {\left( t\right) }^{-1}R{\left( y, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }^{3}} \geq  c\left( {w}^{\prime }\right)
\]

for some positive constant \( c\left( {w}^{\prime }\right) \) depending only on \( {w}^{\prime } \) . Since \( \delta \left( t\right) \) is very small when \( t \) is large, this arrives at a contradiction with (7.7.8). So for each \( k \) , the essential component \( \left( {{\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) },{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) has no surgery for all sufficiently large \( t \) .

For each \( k \) , we consider any fixed time \( {\widetilde{t}}_{k} > 3{T}_{k}^{\prime } \) . Let us scale the solution \( {g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( t\right) \) on the essential component \( {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) by

\[
{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( {\cdot , s}\right)  = {\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right) }^{-1}{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( {\cdot ,{\widetilde{t}}_{k}s}\right) .
\]

Note that \( {\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) } \) is diffeomorphic to \( M \) for all \( t \) . By the above claim, we see that the rescaled solution \( \left( {M,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( {\cdot , s}\right) }\right) \) is a smooth solution to the Ricci flow on the time interval \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {\frac{1}{2},1}\right\rbrack \) . Set

\[
{\widetilde{r}}_{k} = {\left( \sqrt{{\widetilde{t}}_{k}}\right) }^{-1}\operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{{\widetilde{t}}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) .
\]

Then by (7.7.4), (7.7.5) and (7.7.7), we have

\[
{\widetilde{r}}_{k} \leq  {C}_{k}^{-1} \rightarrow  0,\;\text{ as }k \rightarrow   + \infty ,
\]

\[
\widetilde{Rm} \geq   - {C}_{k}^{-2}{\left( {\widetilde{r}}_{k}\right) }^{-2},\;\text{ on }\;{B}_{1}\left( {x\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right) ,{\widetilde{r}}_{k}}\right) ,
\]

and

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{1}\left( {{B}_{1}\left( {x\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right) ,{\widetilde{r}}_{k}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {w}^{\prime }{\left( {\widetilde{r}}_{k}\right) }^{3},
\]

where \( \widetilde{Rm} \) is the rescaled curvature, \( x\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right) \) is the point given by (7.7.4) and \( {B}_{1}\left( {x\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right) ,{\widetilde{r}}_{k}}\right) \) is the geodesic ball of rescaled solution at the time \( s = 1 \) . Moreover, the closure of \( {B}_{1}\left( {x\left( {\widetilde{t}}_{k}\right) ,{\widetilde{r}}_{k}}\right) \) is the whole manifold \( \left( {M,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( {\cdot ,1}\right) }\right) \) .

Note that in Theorem 7.2.1, Theorem 7.2.2 and Corollary 7.2.3, the condition about normalized initial metrics is just to ensure that the solutions satisfy the Hamilton-Ivey pinching estimate. Since our solutions \( \left( {{M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}},{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) have already satisfied the pinching assumption, we can then apply Corollary 7.2.3 to conclude

\[
\left| {\widetilde{Rm}\left( {x, s}\right) }\right|  \leq  K\left( {w}^{\prime }\right) {\left( {\widetilde{r}}_{k}\right) }^{-2},
\]

whenever \( s \in  \left\lbrack  {1 - \tau \left( {w}^{\prime }\right) {\left( {\widetilde{r}}_{k}\right) }^{2},1}\right\rbrack  , x \in  \left( {M,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( {\cdot , s}\right) }\right) \) and \( k \) is sufficiently large. Here \( K\left( {w}^{\prime }\right) \) and \( \tau \left( {w}^{\prime }\right) \) are positive constants depending only on \( {w}^{\prime } \) . Equivalently, we have the curvature estimates

(7.7.9)

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right|  \leq  K\left( {w}^{\prime }\right) {\left( \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{{\widetilde{t}}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) \right) }^{-2},\;\text{ on }M,
\]

whenever \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{\widetilde{t}}_{k} - \tau \left( {w}^{\prime }\right) {\left( \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{{\widetilde{t}}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) \right) }^{2},{\widetilde{t}}_{k}}\right. \) ] and \( k \) is sufficiently large.

For each \( k \) , let us scale \( \left( {{\left( {M}_{t}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) },{g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\left( t\right) }\right) \) with the factor \( {\left( \operatorname{diam}\left( {\left( {M}_{{\widetilde{t}}_{k}}^{{\alpha }_{k}}\right) }^{\left( 1\right) }\right) \right) }^{-2} \) and shift the time \( {\widetilde{t}}_{k} \) to the new time zero. By the curvature estimate (7.7.9) and Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5), we can take a subsequential limit (in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology) and get a smooth solution to the Ricci flow on \( M \times  \left( {-\tau \left( {w}^{\prime }\right) ,0}\right\rbrack \) . Moreover, by (7.7.5), the limit has nonnegative sectional curvature on \( M \times  \left( {-\tau \left( {w}^{\prime }\right) ,0}\right\rbrack \) . Recall that we have removed all compact components with nonnegative scalar curvature. By combining this with the strong maximum principle, we conclude that the limit is a flat metric. Hence in case (2), \( M \) is diffeomorphic to a flat manifold and then it is also geometrizable.

Therefore we have completed the proof of the theorem. C

nodes.label: Definition 1-extra-1
nodes.document_title: Zhengnan Chen - Manifolds with Positive Isotropic Curvature of Dimension at Least Nine
nodes.content:
An algebraic curvature operator \( R \) is said to be WPIC (weakly positive isotropic curvature) if for any orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) , we have

\[
{R}_{1313} + {R}_{1414} + {R}_{2323} + {R}_{2424} - 2{R}_{1234} \geq  0. \tag{1.1}
\]

\( R \) is said to be WPIC1 if for any orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and any \( \lambda  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
{R}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{1414} + {R}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{2424} - {2\lambda }{R}_{1234} \geq  0. \tag{1.2}
\]

Moreover \( R \) is said to be WPIC2 if for any orthonormal 4-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) and any \( \lambda ,\mu  \in  \left\lbrack  {0,1}\right\rbrack \) .

\[
{R}_{1313} + {\lambda }^{2}{R}_{1414} + {\mu }^{2}{R}_{2323} + {\lambda }^{2}{\mu }^{2}{R}_{2424} - {2\lambda \mu }{R}_{1234} \geq  0. \tag{1.3}
\]

We call \( {C}_{PIC},{C}_{PIC1},{C}_{PIC2} \) the cones consisting of algebraic curvature operators that satisfy WPIC, WPIC1 or WPIC2 respectively. Moreover, \( R \) is said to be PIC, PIC1 or PIC2 if it’s contained in the interior of \( {C}_{PIC1},{C}_{PIC1} \) or \( {C}_{PIC2} \) respectively. A manifold \( M \) is a PIC, PIC1 or PIC2 manifold if there exists a metric \( g \) on \( M \) such that its curvature operator is PIC, PIC1 or PIC2 respectively.

nodes.label: Theorem 1.1
nodes.document_title: Zhengnan Chen - Manifolds with Positive Isotropic Curvature of Dimension at Least Nine
nodes.content: Theorem 1.1 Let (M, g) be a compact PIC manifold of dimension \( n \geq  9 \) . If \( M \) contains no nontrivial incompressible \( \left( {n - 1}\right) \) -dimensional space forms, then \( M \) is diffeomorphic to a finite connected sum of spaces, each of which is a quotient of \( {S}^{n} \) or \( {S}^{n - 1} \times  \mathbb{R} \) by standard isometries.

nodes.label: Theorem 1.2
nodes.document_title: Zhengnan Chen - Manifolds with Positive Isotropic Curvature of Dimension at Least Nine
nodes.content:
Theorem 1.2 Let \( 9 \leq  n \leq  {11} \) . Then there exist some \( B = B\left( n\right)  > 0 \) , and a family of closed convex cones \( \widehat{C}\left( b\right) ,0 < b < B \) , such that each cone \( \widehat{C}\left( b\right) ,0 < b < B \) is transversally invariant under the Hamiltonian \( {ODE}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}R = Q\left( R\right) \) , and that

1. For any fixed positive reals \( \theta \) and \( N \) , there exists a small \( {\beta }_{0} > 0 \) such that

\[
\left( {\left\{  {R : R - \theta \text{ scalid } \land  \mathrm{{id}} \in  {C}_{PIC}}\right\}   \cap  \left\{  {R : {Ri}{c}_{11} + {Ri}{c}_{22} - \theta \text{ scal } + N \geq  0}\right\}  }\right)
\]

\[
\subset  \left\{  {R : R + N\mathrm{{id}} \land  \mathrm{{id}} \in  \widehat{C}\left( {\beta }_{0}\right) }\right\}
\]

2. Let \( \left\{  {\beta }_{j}\right\} \) be a increasing sequence such that \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow   + \infty }}{\beta }_{j} = B \) , there exists a sequence of positive reals \( \left\{  {\varepsilon }_{j}\right\} \) with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{j \rightarrow   + \infty }}{\varepsilon }_{j} = 0 \) , and

\[
\widehat{C}\left( {\beta }_{j}\right)  \subset  \left\{  {R : R + {\varepsilon }_{j}\text{ scalid } \land  \operatorname{id} \in  {C}_{PIC1}}\right\}  .
\]

As a consequence, we are able to conduct Step 2 of the above pinching estimate in dimension \( 9 \leq  n \leq  {11} \) . Now, we follow the arguments of Step 1 and Step 3 as in [Bre19], and use the family of pinching cones constructed in Theorem 1.2, we are able to deduce suitable pinching estimate for compact \( {PIC} \) manifolds of dimension \( 9 \leq  n \leq  {11} \) . The pinching estimate is formulated as below.

nodes.content:
Corollary 1.3 (Pinching estimate for PIC manifold, cf. Proposition 1.2 of [Bre19]) Let \( 9 \leq  n \leq  {11} \) . Let \( K \subseteq  \operatorname{int}\left( {C}_{PIC}\right) \) be a compact set in the interior of \( {C}_{PIC} \) , and \( T > 0 \) be given. Then there exist a small positive real number \( \theta \) , and a large positive real number \( N \) , an increasing concave function \( f > 0 \) satisfying \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow   + \infty }}\frac{f\left( s\right) }{s} = 0 \) , and a continuous family of closed convex, \( O\left( n\right) \) -invariant sets \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) such that the family \( \left\{  {{\mathcal{F}}_{t} : t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) is invariant under Hamilonian \( {ODE}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}R = Q\left( R\right) \) , \( K \subset  {\mathcal{F}}_{0} \) , and

\[
{\mathcal{F}}_{t} \subseteq  \left\{  {R : R - \theta \text{ scalid } \land  \mathrm{{id}} \in  {C}_{PIC}}\right\}
\]

\[
\cap  \left\{  {R : {Ri}{c}_{11} + {Ri}{c}_{22} - {\theta scal} + N \geq  0}\right\}
\]

\[
\cap  \left\{  {R : R + f\left( {scal}\right) \mathrm{{id}} \land  \mathrm{{id}} \in  {C}_{PIC2}}\right\}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) .

Given this pinching estimate, using Hamilton's maximum principle, we deduce the following pinching estimate for Ricci flow starting from a compact PIC manifolds of dimension \( n \geq  9 \) (cf. Corollary 1.3 of [Bre19]). That is, for any compact PIC manifold \( \left( {M,{g}_{0}}\right) \) of dimension \( n \geq  9 \) , let \( g\left( t\right) \) denote the solution to the Ricci flow starting from \( {g}_{0} \) . Then there exist a small positive real number \( \theta \) , a large positive real number \( N \) , and an increasing concave function satisfying \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{s \rightarrow   + \infty }}\frac{f\left( s\right) }{s} = 0 \) such that the curvature tensor of \( \left( {M, g\left( t\right) }\right) \) satisfies \( R - \theta \) scalid \( \land  \mathrm{{id}} \in  {C}_{PIC},{Ri}{c}_{11} + {Ri}{c}_{22} - \theta \) scal \( + N \geq  0 \) , and \( R + f\left( \text{ scal }\right) \mathrm{{id}} \land  \mathrm{{id}} \in  {C}_{PIC2} \) for all \( t \geq  0 \) . Now, following the arguments of the second part and the third part in [Bre19], i.e. the ancient solution arguments and the surgery arguments, we are able to deduce Theorem 1.1. Hence, it suffices to prove Theorem 1.2.

### 3.1 Definitions of the first family of pinching cones

In this section, we assume \( 9 \leq  n \leq  {11} \) . Let \( {b}_{\max } = \frac{1}{{2n} + 2} \) and \( \varepsilon  = {10}^{-3} \) , for \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } \) , we associate the data \( a,\gamma ,\rho ,\omega , A, P, Q \) by

\[
a = a\left( b\right)  = \frac{{\left( 2 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }b,
\]

\[
\gamma  = \gamma \left( b\right)  = \frac{b}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b},
\]

\[
\rho  = \rho \left( b\right)  = b - \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \gamma \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{{n}^{2}} - \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \left( {{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }\right) }{{n}^{2}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }
\]

\[
\omega  = \omega \left( b\right)  = \left( {1 - \varepsilon }\right) \sqrt{\frac{{27}\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{8}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{{n}^{2}{\rho }^{3}{\left( 2 + \left( n - 3\right) b\right) }^{2}}}, \tag{3.1}
\]

\[
A = A\left( b\right)  = \frac{2 + {8b}}{\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 4}\right) } + \frac{4}{n}\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) ,
\]

\[
P = P\left( b\right)  = \frac{2{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a},
\]

\[
Q = Q\left( b\right)  = \frac{2\left( {{\left( 1 + 2\left( n - 1\right) a\right) }^{2} - {\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }.
\]

In fact, as calculated in Section 2, the data \( P, Q \) satisfies the following: If an algebraic curvature operator \( S \) evolves by the ODE \( \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}S = Q\left( S\right)  + {D}_{a, b}\left( S\right) \) , then

\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)  = P{\left| \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2} + Q{\left( \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \right) }^{2}.
\]

We define the first family of pinching cones as below. One could compare our definition and Definition 3.1 in [Bre19], the fourth condition is different. The advantage of our condition is that we could "push" the cone inside further in the sense that we could let \( {b}_{\max } \) bigger. However, to show that our definition makes sense, we need to use a more precise estimate for \( \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11}}\right) \) (see the proof of Proposition 3.12)

1. \( T \geq  0 \) ,

2. \( S - T \in  {C}_{PIC} \) ,

\[
\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} - \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} \leq  {\omega }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\left( \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}{\left( \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}. \tag{3.2}
\]

We then define \( C\left( b\right)  = {l}_{a, b}\left( {\mathcal{E}\left( b\right) }\right) \) .

Remark 3.2 We write \( {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) for the set of curvature-type tensors that do not necessarily satisfy the first Bianchi identity. For \( T \in  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) , we say \( T \geq  0 \) if \( T \in  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) is nonnegative definite. When \( T \) satisfies the first Bianchi identity, this coincides with the definition of a non-negative curvature operator.

Here we abuse a bit the notation for convenience: For \( T \in  {S}^{2}\left( {\mathfrak{{so}}\left( n\right) }\right) \) , we say \( T \in  {C}_{PIC} \) if \( T\left( {\phi ,\bar{\phi }}\right)  \geq \) 0 for every complex two-form of the form \( \phi  = \left( {{e}_{1} + i{e}_{2}}\right)  \land  \left( {{e}_{3} + i{e}_{4}}\right) \) , where \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) is an orthonormal 4-frame. This is equivalent to say that \( T \in  {C}_{PIC} \) if and only if for any orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) we have

\[
{T}_{1313} + {T}_{1414} + {T}_{2323} + {T}_{2424} + 2{T}_{1342} + 2{T}_{1423} \geq  0.
\]

Notice that if \( T \) satisfies the first Bianchi identity, then the above formula coincides with the definition of WPIC for algebraic curvature operators.

It is clear that \( C\left( b\right) \) is closed, convex, and \( O\left( n\right) \) -invariant for each \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } \) . The following is the main result of this section:

\cdot  \left( {\frac{2\left( {2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) a + n - 3}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{\left( {1 - n}\right) \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}}\right) .
\]

Notice that \( a = \frac{{\left( 2 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }b < \frac{2 + \left( {n + 1}\right) b}{2}b \leq  \frac{5}{4}b \) and \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } = \frac{1}{{2n} + 2} < \frac{1}{2n} \) , we obtain

\[
\frac{2\left( {2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) a + n - 3}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a} - \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }{1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}
\]

\[
> 2\left( {n - 3}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right)  - \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right)
\]

\[
> 2\left( {n - 3}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right)  - \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + \frac{5}{2}\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right)
\]

\[
> \left( {2{\left( n - 3\right) }^{2} - \frac{5}{2}{n}^{2}}\right) b + {3n} - {11}
\]

\[
>  - \frac{n\left( {n + {12}}\right) }{2n} + {3n} - {11}
\]

\[
= \frac{5}{2}n - {17} > 0\text{ . }
\]

For \( h\left( b\right) \) , it suffices to show that \( \frac{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}} \) is strictly increasing in \( b \) , a direct computation gives

\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( \frac{1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}\right)  = \frac{2}{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{3}}\left( {\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) \frac{\mathrm{d}a}{\mathrm{\;d}b} - \left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }\right) .
\]

Notice that \( \frac{2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b} \) increases strictly in \( b \) , hence

\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}a}{\mathrm{\;d}b} = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( {\frac{a}{b} \cdot  b}\right)  = \frac{a}{b} + b\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( \frac{a}{b}\right)  \geq  \frac{a}{b} + b\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( \frac{2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}{2}\right)  = \frac{a}{b} + \frac{\left( {n - 2}\right) b}{2}.
\]

Associating this inequality with the fact that \( \frac{a}{b} = \frac{{\left( 2 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) } > \frac{2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}{2} \) gives us

\[
\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) \frac{\mathrm{d}a}{\mathrm{\;d}b} - \left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \left( {n - 1}\right) \frac{a}{b} + \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) }{2}b + \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{2}{b}^{2} - \left( {n - 2}\right)  - \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) a
\]

\[
\geq  1 + \left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) \left( {b - a}\right)  + \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{2}{b}^{2}.
\]

Using the fact that \( a = \frac{\left( 2 + {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}b\right) }{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }b < \frac{2 + \left( {n + 1}\right) b}{2} \leq  \frac{5}{4}b \) , one checks directly that \( 1 + \left( {n - 1}\right) (n - \) 2) \( \left( {b - a}\right)  + \frac{\left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}}{2}{b}^{2} > 0 \) . The assertion follows.

From the definition of \( \rho \) in (3.1), one immediately sees that \( \rho  < b \) and \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{b \rightarrow  0 + }}\rho  = 0 \) . The following lemma gives a characterization of \( \rho \) from which we can deduce that \( \rho \) is strictly positive for each \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } \)

nodes.proof:
Notice that

\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}\rho }{\mathrm{d}b} = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( {b - \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \gamma \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{{n}^{2}} - \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \left( {{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }\right) }{{n}^{2}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }}\right)
\]

\[
\mathrel{\text{ := }} 1 - {P}_{1} - {P}_{2}
\]

where

\[
{P}_{1} = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \gamma \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{{n}^{2}}\right)  < \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{\mathrm{d}\gamma }{\mathrm{d}b} < \frac{1}{n + 1} \leq  \frac{1}{10},
\]

since the term \( 1 - {2b} \) is positive and decreasing in \( b \) and \( \frac{\mathrm{d}\gamma }{\mathrm{d}b} < \frac{1}{2} \) . Now, for the term \( {P}_{2} \) , we have

\[
{P}_{2} = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \left( {{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }\right) }{{n}^{2}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \left( {\left( {{2n} - 1}\right) {b}^{2} + \left( {{3n} - 2}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{3} + \left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{4}}\right) }{{n}^{2}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }\right) .
\]

Now notice that \( 1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a \) and \( 2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b \) are both positive and increasing in \( b \) , combining with \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } = \frac{1}{{2n} + 2} \) and \( \frac{\mathrm{d}\gamma }{\mathrm{d}b} < \frac{1}{2} \) , we have

\[
{P}_{2} \leq  \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{n}^{2}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( {\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \left( {\left( {{2n} - 1}\right) {b}^{2} + \left( {{3n} - 2}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{3} + \left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{4}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
< \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{n}^{2}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }\left( {\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \left( {2\left( {{2n} - 1}\right) b + 3\left( {{3n} - 2}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} + 4\left( {n - 1}\right) {\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{3}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{n}^{2}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }\left( {{2n}{b}^{2} + 3{n}^{2}{b}^{3} + {n}^{3}{b}^{4}}\right) )
\]

\[
< \frac{4\left( {n - 1}\right) }{{n}^{2}\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) b}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }\left( {{4nb} + 9{n}^{2}{b}^{2} + 4{n}^{3}{b}^{3}}\right)  + \frac{n - 1}{{n}^{2}}\left( {{2n}{b}^{2} + 3{n}^{2}{b}^{3} + {n}^{3}{b}^{4}}\right)
\]

\[
< \frac{4\left( {{4b} + {9n}{b}^{2} + 4{n}^{2}{b}^{3}}\right) }{\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) b}\right) )\left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) } + \left( {2{b}^{2} + {3n}{b}^{3} + {n}^{2}{b}^{4}}\right) \text{ . }
\]

We claim that

\[
\frac{4\left( {{4b} + {9n}{b}^{2} + 4{n}^{2}{b}^{3}}\right) }{\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) b}\right) )\left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) } < \frac{4}{9}.
\]

In fact, the above equation is equivalent to

\[
{36}{n}^{2}{b}^{3} + \left( {{81n} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 3}\right) }\right) {b}^{2} + \left( {{42} - {5n}}\right) b < 2,
\]

and we verify directly that

\[
{36}{n}^{2}{b}^{3} + \left( {{81n} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 3}\right) }\right) {b}^{2} + \left( {{42} - {5n}}\right) b \leq  {36}{n}^{2}{b}_{\max }^{3} + \left( {{81} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 3}\right) }\right) {b}_{\max }^{2} < 2,
\]

hence the claim is true.

Moreover we can check that

\[
2{b}^{2} + {3n}{b}^{3} + {n}^{2}{b}^{4} < \frac{1}{100}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}\rho }{\mathrm{d}b} = 1 - {P}_{1} - {P}_{2} > 1 - \frac{1}{10} - \frac{4}{9} - \frac{1}{100} > \frac{4}{9},
\]

the assertion follows.

nodes.proof:
For the first statement: use the inequality \( a > b \) , it’s clear that

\[
1 + \frac{A}{2}\sqrt{n\left( {n - 2}\right) } > 1 + {2b}\sqrt{n\left( {n - 2}\right) } > 1 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b
\]

\[
> 1 + 2\sqrt{n - 2}b + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} = {\left( 1 + b\sqrt{n - 2}\right) }^{2}\text{ . }
\]

For the second statement: we first calculate that

\[
P + {nQ} = 2 + 4\left( {n - 1}\right) a,
\]

hence the statement is equivalent to the following :

\[
{LHS} \mathrel{\text{ := }} {\left( 1 + \frac{A}{2}\sqrt{n\left( {n - 2}\right) }\right) }^{2} \cdot  \frac{\left( 2 + \left( n - 3\right) b\right) }{\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {1 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) } \leq  \frac{1 - \varepsilon }{2}\sqrt{\frac{{27b}\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{8{n}^{2}{\rho }^{3}}} =  : {RHS}.
\]

(3.4)

For LHS, observe that

\[
{\left( 1 + \frac{A}{2}\sqrt{n\left( {n - 2}\right) }\right) }^{2} \leq  {\left( 1 + \left( \frac{1 + {4a}}{\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {n - 4}\right) } + 2a\right) \left( n - 1\right) \right) }^{2} = {\left( \frac{n - 3}{n - 4}\right) }^{2}{\left( 1 + 2\left( n - 2\right) a\right) }^{2}.
\]

By Lemma 3.4, we obtain

\[
{LHS} \leq  {\left( \frac{n - 3}{n - 4}\right) }^{2}g\left( b\right)  \leq  {\left( \frac{n - 3}{n - 4}\right) }^{2}g\left( {b}_{\max }\right) .
\]

Now we show that RHS is strictly decreasing in \( b \) . Notice that \( \rho  < b \) and by Lemma 3.5, \( \frac{\mathrm{d}\rho }{\mathrm{d}b} > \frac{4}{9} \) , we have

\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}b}\left( \frac{b\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{{\rho }^{3}}\right)  = \frac{1}{{\rho }^{4}}\left( {\left( {2 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) \rho  - 3\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) b\frac{\mathrm{d}\rho }{\mathrm{d}b}}\right)
\]

\[
< \frac{b}{{\rho }^{4}}\left( {\left( {2 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right)  - \frac{4}{3}\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }\right)  = \frac{b}{{\rho }^{4}}\left( {-\frac{2}{3} + \frac{2}{3}\left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right)  < 0.
\]

We can now verify directly that, for \( 9 \leq  n \leq  {11} \) and \( {b}_{max} = \frac{1}{{2n} + 2} \) ,

\[
{LHS} \leq  {\left( \frac{n - 3}{n - 4}\right) }^{2}g\left( {b}_{\max }\right)  < \frac{1 - \varepsilon }{2}\sqrt{\frac{{27}{b}_{\max }\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}\right) }{8{n}^{2}{\left( \rho \left( {b}_{\max }\right) \right) }^{3}}} \leq  {RHS}.
\]

The third statement is equivalent to the following:

\[
{LHS} \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left( {1 + \frac{A}{2}\sqrt{n\left( {n - 2}\right) }}\right)  \cdot  \frac{\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) \left( {2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }{{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{3}} \leq  \frac{1 - \varepsilon }{2}\sqrt{\frac{{27b}\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{8{n}^{2}{\rho }^{3}}} =  : {RHS}.
\]

As above, RHS is strictly decreasing in \( b \) . We now analyze LHS, similarly we have

\[
1 + \frac{A}{2}\sqrt{n\left( {n - 2}\right) } \leq  \frac{\left( {n - 3}\right) \left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 2}\right) a}\right) }{n - 4}.
\]

Hence by Lemma 3.4,

\[
{LHS} \leq  \left( \frac{n - 3}{n - 4}\right) g\left( b\right) h\left( b\right)  \leq  \left( \frac{n - 3}{n - 4}\right) g\left( {b}_{\max }\right) h\left( {b}_{\max }\right) .
\]

It can be verified directly that, for \( 9 \leq  n \leq  {11} \) and \( {b}_{max} = \frac{1}{{2n} + 2} \) ,

\[
{LHS} \leq  \left( \frac{n - 3}{n - 4}\right) g\left( {b}_{\max }\right) h\left( {b}_{\max }\right)  < \frac{1 - \varepsilon }{2}\sqrt{\frac{{27}{b}_{\max }\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}_{\max }}\right) }{8{n}^{2}{\left( \rho \left( {b}_{\max }\right) \right) }^{3}}} \leq  {RHS},
\]

the assertion follows.

nodes.proof:
Recall that

\[
{D}_{a, b}\left( S\right)  = \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) {Ri}{c}_{0}\left( S\right)  \land  {Ri}{c}_{0}\left( S\right)
\]

\[
+ {2a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \land  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  + 2{b}^{2}{Ri}{c}_{0}{\left( S\right) }^{2} \land  \mathrm{{id}}
\]

\[
+ \frac{n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| Ri{c}_{0}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \land  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

Firstly, we have

\[
n{b}^{2}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  - 2\left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b} + n{b}^{2}}\right)  = \frac{{b}^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\left( {2 + \left( {n - 8}\right) b - 2\left( {n + 2}\right) \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - n{\left( n - 2\right) }^{2}{b}^{3}}\right)  > 0
\]

for \( 0 < b \leq  {b}_{\max } \) . It is left to show that

\[
U \mathrel{\text{ := }} \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}\left( S\right)  \land  {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}\left( S\right)  + {2a}\operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  \land  \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right)  + 2{b}^{2}{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }^{2} \land  \mathrm{{id}} \in  {C}_{PIC}.
\]

It suffices to show that for any linearly independent vectors \( \zeta ,\eta \) satisfying \( g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = \; g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = 0 \) , we have \( U\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  \geq  0 \) . As \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) is unitarily diagonalizable on \( {\operatorname{span}}_{\mathbb{C}}\{ \eta ,\zeta \} \) , we can find \( z, w \in  {\operatorname{span}}_{\mathbb{C}}\{ \eta ,\zeta \} \) such that \( g\left( {z,\bar{z}}\right)  = g\left( {w,\bar{w}}\right)  = 2, g\left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = 0 \) and \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = 0 \) . The identities \( g\left( {\zeta ,\zeta }\right)  = g\left( {\zeta ,\eta }\right)  = g\left( {\eta ,\eta }\right)  = 0 \) give \( g\left( {z, z}\right)  = g\left( {w, w}\right)  = g\left( {z, w}\right)  = 0 \) . Consequently, we may write \( z = {e}_{1} + i{e}_{2} \) and \( w = {e}_{3} + i{e}_{4} \) for some orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\}   \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n} \) . Using the identity \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \left( {z,\bar{w}}\right)  = 0 \) , we obtain

\[
U\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)  = 2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {4a}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 4{b}^{2}\left( {{\left( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{11} + {\left( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{22} + {\left( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{33} + {\left( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }^{2}\right) }_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  2\left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) \left( {\mathrm{{{Ri}{c}_{0}}}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \mathrm{{{Ri}{c}_{0}}}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \left( {\mathrm{{{Ri}{c}_{0}}}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + \mathrm{{{Ri}{c}_{0}}}{\left( S\right) }_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
+ {4a}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{44}}\right)
\]

\[
+ 2{b}^{2}\left( {\left( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{22}\right) }^{2}\right)  + {\left( {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + {\operatorname{Ric}}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{44}\right) }^{2}).
\]

Let \( x \mathrel{\text{ := }} \frac{n}{\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\left( {{Ri}{c}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + {Ri}{c}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{22}}\right) \) and \( y \mathrel{\text{ := }} \frac{n}{\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\left( {{Ri}{c}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{33} + {Ri}{c}_{0}{\left( S\right) }_{44}}\right) \) . Recall the third condition in Definition 3.1, we have \( x, y \geq   - {2\gamma } - 2 \) . Let \( D = \left\{  {\left( {x, y}\right)  \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{2} : x, y \geq   - {2\gamma } - 2}\right\} \) , we show that for any \( \left( {x, y}\right)  \in  D \) ,

\[
f\left( {x, y}\right)  = \left( {{2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} - {2a}}\right) {xy} + {2a}\left( {x + 2}\right) \left( {y + 2}\right)  + {b}^{2}\left( {{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

In fact, the Hessian of \( f \) is given by

\[
\text{ Hess }f = \left( \begin{matrix} 2{b}^{2} & {2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} \\  {2b} + \left( {n - 2}\right) {b}^{2} & 2{b}^{2} \end{matrix}\right) .
\]

It follows that Hess \( f \) has two eigenvalues of opposite signs. Since \( f\left( {x, y}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) as \( \left( {x, y}\right)  \in  D \) goes to infinity, \( f \) attains its minimum on \( \partial D \) . Now, one checks directly that

\[
f\left( {-{2\gamma } - 2, y}\right)  = f\left( {-\frac{2\left( {2 + \left( {n - 2}\right) b}\right) }{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}, y}\right)  = {b}^{2}{y}^{2} \geq  0.
\]

As a result, \( U\left( {z, w,\bar{z},\bar{w}}\right)  = \frac{2{\left( \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \right) }^{2}}{{n}^{2}}f\left( {x, y}\right)  \geq  0 \) . Since \( {\operatorname{span}}_{\mathbb{C}}\{ \zeta ,\eta \}  = {\operatorname{span}}_{\mathbb{C}}\{ z, w\} \) , it follows that \( U\left( {\zeta ,\eta ,\bar{\zeta },\bar{\eta }}\right)  \geq  0 \) , and the assertion follows.

nodes.content_excerpt: Proposition 3.9 (cf. Lemma 3.8 in [Bre19]) Suppose \( S \in \mathcal{E}\left( b\right) \smallsetminus \{ 0\} , T \geq 0 \) and \( S - T \in {C}_{PIC} \) . Then \( \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {S - T}\right) \) lies in the interior of the tangent cone \( {T}_{S - T}{C}_{PIC} \) .

nodes.proof:
From the evolution equation of \( S \) and \( T \) , we obtain that

\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {S - T}\right)  = {S}^{\# } + {D}_{a, b}\left( S\right)  - \varepsilon {\left( \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \right) }^{2}\mathrm{{id}} \land  \mathrm{{id}}.
\]

By the definition of \( \varepsilon \) , it is left to show that \( {S}^{\# } \in  {T}_{S - T}{C}_{PIC} \) . Equivalently, given any complex 2-form \( \varphi  \in  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) with the property that \( \varphi  = \left( {{e}_{1} + i{e}_{2}}\right)  \land  \left( {{e}_{3} + i{e}_{4}}\right) \) for some orthonormal four-frame \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2},{e}_{3},{e}_{4}}\right\} \) satisfying \( \left( {S - T}\right) \left( {\varphi ,\bar{\varphi }}\right)  = 0 \) , we show that \( {S}^{\# }\left( {\varphi ,\bar{\varphi }}\right)  \geq  0 \) .

The ideas are from the proof of Theorem 1 in [Wil10]. We know that \( {S}^{\# }\left( {\varphi ,\bar{\varphi }}\right)  =  - \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{\varphi }{\operatorname{Sad}}_{\bar{\varphi }}S}\right) \) . Notice that for any \( \theta  \in  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) , we have

\[
\left( {S - T}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{Ad}}_{\exp \left( {t\theta }\right) }\varphi ,{\operatorname{Ad}}_{\exp \left( {t\bar{\theta }}\right) }\bar{\varphi }}\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Differentiating twice the above equation at \( t = 0 \) , and use the fact that \( {\operatorname{Ad}}_{\exp \left( {t\theta }\right) } = \exp \left( {t{\operatorname{ad}}_{\theta }}\right) \) , we obtain the following:

\[
0 \leq  2\left( {S - T}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{\theta }\varphi ,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\theta }}\bar{\varphi }}\right)  + \left( {S - T}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{\theta }{\operatorname{ad}}_{\theta }\varphi ,\bar{\varphi }}\right)  + \left( {S - T}\right) \left( {\varphi ,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\theta }}{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\theta }}\bar{\varphi }}\right) .
\]

Replace \( \theta \) by \( {i\theta } \) , we see that the first summand in the above inequality is left unchanged while the other two summands change their sign. Therefore we add the two inequalities to obtain that

\[
0 \leq  \left( {S - T}\right) \left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{\theta }\varphi ,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\theta }}\bar{\varphi }}\right) .
\]

Since \( T \) is nonnegative, we have \( 0 \leq  S\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{\theta }\varphi ,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\theta }}\bar{\varphi }}\right)  = S\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{\varphi }\theta ,{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\varphi }}\bar{\theta }}\right) \) for any \( \theta  \in  \mathfrak{{so}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) . This is equivalent to saying that the operator \( - {\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\varphi }}{\operatorname{Sad}}_{\varphi } \) is non-negative Hermitian on \( \mathfrak{{so}}\left( {n,\mathbb{C}}\right) \) . Recall that we want to show that \( - \operatorname{tr}\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{\varphi }S{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\varphi }}S}\right)  =  - \operatorname{tr}\left( {{\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\varphi }}S{\operatorname{ad}}_{\varphi }}\right)  \geq  0 \) , using the spectral decomposition of \( - {\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\varphi }}S{\operatorname{ad}}_{\varphi } \) , it suffices to show that \( S \) is nonnegative on the image of the operator \( {\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\varphi }}S{\operatorname{ad}}_{\varphi } \) . Clearly we have that the image is contained in the image of \( {\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\varphi }} \) and \( S \) is indeed non-negative on the image of \( {\operatorname{ad}}_{\bar{\varphi }} \) . The conclusion follows.

Proposition 3.10 Let \( S \in  \mathcal{E}\left( b\right)  \smallsetminus  \{ 0\} \) and \( \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right)  = 0 \) for some pair of orthonormal vectors \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) , then:

\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)  > 0. \tag{3.5}
\]

nodes.proof:
We may assume that \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) are eigenvectors of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) , and extend \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},{e}_{2}}\right\} \) to an eigenbasis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\cdots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) for \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) . Let \( {\lambda }_{1} \leq  {\lambda }_{2} \leq  \cdots  \leq  {\lambda }_{n} \) denote the eigenvalues for \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) with respect to the basis \( \left\{  {{e}_{1},\cdots ,{e}_{n}}\right\} \) . Following the calculations in [Bre19], we have

\[
\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{p} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{1}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{4\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\left( {a - b}\right) {\operatorname{scal}}^{2}\left( S\right)  + \frac{{2\gamma }\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) {\left( \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \right) }^{2}
\]

\[
- b{\left( {\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{2} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\left( {1 - {2b}}\right) {\left| Ri{c}_{0}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2} \tag{3.7}
\]

\[
+ 2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) \frac{{n}^{2}{b}^{2} - 2\left( {n - 1}\right) \left( {a - b}\right) \left( {1 - {2b}}\right) }{n\left( {1 + 2\left( {n - 1}\right) a}\right) }{\left| Ri{c}_{0}\left( S\right) \right| }^{2}
\]

\[
\geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{p} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{1}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}{\left( \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \right) }^{2} - \rho {\left( {\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{2}.
\]

where in the last inequality we used Lemma 3.11, definition of \( \rho \) , and the identity

\[
2\left( {a - b}\right)  + \gamma \left( {1 - {2b}}\right)  = \frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}.
\]

Observe that \( S \in  {C}_{PIC} \) , we have

\[
\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right)  - 2\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{kk} = \mathop{\sum }\limits_{\substack{{i \neq  k} \\  {j \neq  k} }}{S}_{ijij} \geq  0
\]

for each \( k \in  \{ 1,2,\cdots , n\} \) . It follows that each eigenvalue of \( \operatorname{Ric}\left( S\right) \) is bounded above from the sum of other eigenvalues. Combining with the fact that \( {\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2} \leq  0 \) , this gives us the inequality

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p \in  \{ 3,\cdots , n\} \smallsetminus \{ m\} }}\left( {{\lambda }_{p} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{1}}\right) }\right)  \geq  {\lambda }_{m} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{2} + {\lambda }_{1}}\right) .
\]

As \( S - T \in  {C}_{PIC} \) , it follows that there exists at most one \( m \in  \{ 3,\cdots , n\} \) such that \( {S}_{1m1m} + \; {S}_{2m2m} - {T}_{1m1m} - {T}_{2m2m} < 0 \) . Moreover, for any \( p \in  \{ 3,\cdots , n\}  \smallsetminus  \{ m\} \) we have

\[
\left( {{S}_{1m1m} + {S}_{2m2m} - {T}_{1m1m} - {T}_{2m2m}}\right)  + \left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p} - {T}_{1p1p} - {T}_{2p2p}}\right)  > 0,
\]

so we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} = {S}_{2p2p} - {T}_{1p1p} - {T}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{p} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2}}\right) }\right)  \geq  0.
\]

Since \( T \geq  0 \) , we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{S}_{1p1p} + {S}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{p} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{p} - \frac{1}{2}\left( {{\lambda }_{1} + {\lambda }_{2}}\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}}\right)
\]

It now follows that

\[
\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{1}{2}\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right) \left( {{\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}}\right)
\]

\[
+ \frac{2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}{\operatorname{scal}}^{2}\left( S\right)  - \rho {\left( {\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{2}.
\]

Recall the fourth property in Definition 3.1, we have

\[
\mathop{\sum }\limits_{{p = 3}}^{n}\left( {{T}_{1p1p} + {T}_{2p2p}}\right)  \geq  \frac{{\left( {\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{2}}{\omega \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }.
\]

If \( {\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1} = 0 \) , then clearly we have \( \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {\operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + \operatorname{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right)  > 0}\right) \) . Now assume \( {\lambda }_{2} - \; {\lambda }_{1} > 0 \) , the elementary inequality \( {2x} + y \geq  3{\left( {x}^{2}y\right) }^{\frac{1}{3}} \) for \( x, y \geq  0 \) gives

\[
\frac{{\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}}{{2\omega }\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) } + \frac{2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\frac{{\operatorname{scal}}^{2}\left( S\right) }{{\left( {\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{2}} \geq  3{\left( \frac{1 + \gamma }{8{\omega }^{2}{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}\right) }^{\frac{1}{3}} = {\left( 1 - \varepsilon \right) }^{-\frac{2}{3}}\rho  > \rho ,
\]

where we have used the definition of \( \gamma ,\rho \) and \( \omega \) .

As a consequence,

\[
\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( {{Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{11} + {Ric}{\left( S\right) }_{22} + \frac{2\gamma }{n}\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) }\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \frac{{\left( {\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{3}}{{2\omega }\operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) } + \frac{2\left( {1 + \gamma }\right) }{{n}^{2}}\frac{b{\left( 1 + \left( n - 2\right) b\right) }^{2}}{2 + \left( {n - 3}\right) b}{\left( \operatorname{scal}\left( S\right) \right) }^{2} - \rho {\left( {\lambda }_{2} - {\lambda }_{1}\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
> 0\text{ . }
\]
